act_identification.act_title: THE BENGAL BONDED WAREHOUSE ASSOCIATION ACT, 1838
act_identification.act_short_title: THE BENGAL BONDED WAREHOUSE ASSOCIATION ACT

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Presidency of Fort William in Bengal

act_overview.purpose: This Act incorporates the Bengal Bonded Warehouse Association as a corporate body for the warehousing of goods, both in bond and otherwise. It establishes the Association's capital structure, governance through Directors, and outlines procedures for share management, financial operations, and dissolution. The Act aims to provide a legal framework for the Association's commercial activities related to warehousing.

key_sections.title: Incorporation.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Bengal Bonded Warehouse Association as a corporate body for warehousing goods from March 14, 1838.

key_sections.title: Power to sue and be sued, and to acquire, hold and transfer property.
key_sections.description: Grants the Association the power to sue and be sued, use a common seal, and acquire, hold, and transfer property.

key_sections.title: Capital Stock and shares.
key_sections.description: Defines the initial Capital Stock as Rs. 10,00,000, divided into 2,000 shares of 500 Rupees each.

key_sections.title: Proprietors of shares to be members of Association.
key_sections.description: States that share proprietors are members of the corporation and are subject to the same liabilities as original proprietors.

key_sections.title: First Directors of Association.
key_sections.description: Names the initial six Directors responsible for managing the Association's business.

key_sections.title: Authority of Directors.
key_sections.description: Grants Directors authority to expend money for warehouses, make contracts, appoint servants, manage concerns, and use the Association's seal.

key_sections.title: Power to refuse to register transfer by defaulting proprietor. Power to sell shares to satisfy calls, and issue fresh certificates.
key_sections.description: Allows Directors to refuse transfer registration and sell shares of defaulting proprietors to satisfy unpaid calls and interest.

key_sections.title: Extension of Act 25 of 1836 to warehouses of Association.
key_sections.description: Makes the provisions of Act 25 of 1836, relating to private licensed Warehouses, applicable to the Association's warehouses.

key_sections.title: Certificates of deposit, transferable by endorsement.
key_sections.description: Mandates the issuance of transferable warrants for deposited goods, entitling the holder to receive the goods.

key_sections.title: Suits against Association.
key_sections.description: Specifies that all suits against the Association must be brought in the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William in Bengal.

key_sections.title: Individual members not to be liable.
key_sections.description: Limits the personal liability of individual proprietors, stating that claims can only be recovered from the Association's paid-up capital and assets.

key_sections.title: Increase of Capital Stock.
key_sections.description: Permits the Association to increase its Capital Stock, subject to authorization by two extraordinary general meetings.

key_sections.title: East India Company to have right of pre-emption.
key_sections.description: Grants the East India Company the right of pre-emption for any premises purchased from them by the Association.

key_sections.title: Dissolution of Association by resolution of proprietors.
key_sections.description: Allows for the dissolution of the Association by a resolution passed at two successive extraordinary meetings of proprietors.

key_sections.title: Division of property on dissolution.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for converting the Association's property into money and distributing the surplus among proprietors upon dissolution.

powers_conferred: The Association shall sue and be sued by its corporate name, and shall use such common seal as the Directors shall appoint, and may acquire, hold absolutely, hold by way of pledge, and transfer, any description of property whatever (Section 2).
Directors shall cause names, additions, and places of residence of proprietors, and number of shares, to be registered (Section 4).
Directors shall deliver a certificate signed by three Directors to every proprietor of Capital Stock (Section 5).
Directors shall have authority to expend money for purchasing and erecting warehouses, and of warehousing and bonding goods therein, and to make and fulfil contracts (Section 21).
Directors shall have authority to appoint and remove such servants as may be necessary (Section 21).
Directors shall generally manage all the concerns of the Association, subject to Bye-laws (Section 21).
Directors shall keep the seal of the Association and use it in its affairs, with the presence and consent of three Directors (Section 21).
Directors shall have authority to call on proprietors to pay instalments not exceeding 50 per cent. on each share (Section 22).
Directors may apply any dividend due to a proprietor in satisfaction of unpaid instalments and interest (Section 23).
Directors may refuse to register the transfer of any share belonging to a defaulting proprietor (Section 24).
Directors may sell by public sale the shares of a defaulting proprietor to satisfy unpaid instalments and interest, and issue new certificates (Section 24).
The Association may give general security, by bond, for payment of import duties or due exportation of goods (Section 26).
Directors shall fix the rates at which the Association will Warehouse Goods and receive Goods at its Wharfs (Section 27).
The Secretary of the Association shall deliver a warrant for goods lodged in any Warehouse (Section 28).
The Association may increase its Capital Stock, authorized by two extraordinary general meetings (Section 33).
The Association may be dissolved by a resolution of two-thirds in number and value of proprietors at two successive extraordinary meetings (Section 38).
Directors shall cause all property of the Association to be converted into money and divide the surplus among proprietors upon dissolution (Section 39).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Directors are elected by a general meeting of proprietors (Section 9). A successor Director, when a Director ceases office otherwise than by rotation, is chosen by an extraordinary general meeting of proprietors (Section 11). Directors appoint an officer for share transfer registration (Section 6) and servants (Section 21).

applies_to: persons whose names appear in the Schedule No. 1
proprietors of shares in the Capital Stock
special_provisions: Directors must be resident within the Territories subject to the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal (Section 13).
Suits against the Association must be brought in the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William in Bengal (Section 29).
The East India Company has a right of pre-emption if the Association disposes of premises purchased from the Company (Section 36).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Association, through its Bye-laws, and the Directors (Sections 16, 21).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Directors have the power to refuse to register share transfers and to sell shares of defaulting proprietors to satisfy unpaid calls and interest (Section 24). Suits against the Association are to be brought in the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William in Bengal (Section 29).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William in Bengal

schedules_summary.description: Contains a list of proprietors of shares.
Provides the form for a warrant of deposit for goods lodged in the Association's warehouse.

act_identification.act_title: THE COASTING-VESSELS ACT, 1838

legislative_details.geographical_extent: This Act extends in the first instance to the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in the States of Bombay, Saurashtra and Kutch, but the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, extend it to any other State or part of a State which has a sea-coast.

act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate coasting vessels, fishing vessels, and harbour craft belonging to Indian citizens. It mandates their marking, branding, and registration, and requires owners to obtain and produce certificates of registry. The Act also prescribes fees for registration and penalties for non-compliance with its provisions.

key_sections.title: Extent.
key_sections.description: Defines the geographical extent of the Act, initially covering Bombay, Saurashtra, and Kutch, with power for the Central Government to extend it to other sea-coast states.

key_sections.title: Rules as to coasting and other vessels belonging to any citizen of India.
key_sections.description: Establishes rules for vessels belonging to citizens of India, employed on coasts or in coastwise trading, as well as fishing-vessels and harbour-craft.

key_sections.title: Marking or branding vessels with name of place and number.
key_sections.description: Requires vessels to be marked or branded with the name of their place and a number, and mandates owners to paint this information on the vessel.

key_sections.title: Registry of name, number and burthen.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the registration of vessel name, number, burthen, and owner, specifying the officers responsible for such registry and requiring fresh registration upon changes.

key_sections.title: Owners to apply for registry.
key_sections.description: Obligates owners to apply for registry and ensures information of registry at subordinate ports is forwarded to the Principal Officer, Mercantile Marine Department at Bombay.

key_sections.title: Owner to obtain certificate of registry. Replacing lost certificate.
key_sections.description: Requires owners to obtain a certificate of registry in the specified form and provides for obtaining a renewed certificate if lost or destroyed.

key_sections.title: Fees for certificates.
key_sections.description: Sets out the fee structure for certificates of registry based on the vessel's burthen, with fishing vessels and harbour craft excepted from these fees.

key_sections.title: Production of certificate on demand.
key_sections.description: Mandates owners or commanders to produce the certificate of registry on demand by customs or navy officers.

key_sections.title: Penalty for neglect to comply with rules.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for non-compliance with marking, branding, painting, or certificate requirements, including fines and recovery by sale of the vessel.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to extend the Act to any other State or part of a State which has a sea-coast (Section 1).
Central Government: Power to appoint persons to make registry (Section 4).
Central Government: Power to appoint persons to perform marking, branding, and ascertain burthen (Section 6).
Central Government: Power to appoint officers to receive fees (Section 11).
Central Government: Power to direct compensation for seizing vessels (Section 14).
State Government: Power to appoint officers to receive fees (Section 11 proviso).
Principal Officer, Mercantile Marine Department (Bombay) and Commissioner of Customs (other places): Power to make registry (Section 4).
Principal Officer, Mercantile Marine Department (Bombay) and Commissioner of Customs (other places): Power to perform marking, branding, and ascertain burthen (Section 6).
Registering officers: Power to issue certificates of registry (Section 7).
Officers of the Customs or Navy: Power to demand production of certificate (Section 12).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties are imposed for vessels not being marked or branded as directed, or if the name and number are not painted or maintained. Penalties also apply if a vessel is not furnished with a certificate or if the owner/commander fails to produce it on demand. The fine for vessels for which a fee is payable is ten times the certificate fee, and for fishing-vessels or harbour-craft, it is ten rupees. Fines can be recovered by sale of the vessel, its furniture, ammunition, tackle, and apparel, and are payable for repeated defaults after one month from the last conviction.

related_acts: Bombay Short Titles Act, 1921 (Born. Act 2 of 1921)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint persons for making registry, performing marking and branding duties, and for receiving fees. The State Government also has the power to appoint officers for fee collection under certain conditions.

applies_to: Vessels belonging to any citizen of India
Vessels employed on the coasts or in trading coastwise
Fishing-vessels and harbour-craft
exemptions: Fishing-vessels and harbour-craft are excepted from paying certain certificate fees (Section 10).
special_provisions: The Act initially extends to the territories comprised in the States of Bombay, Saurashtra, and Kutch before 1st November, 1956.
The Central Government has the power to extend the Act to any other State or part of a State which has a sea-coast.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement involves mandatory marking, branding, and registration of vessels, issuance of certificates, and the requirement for owners/commanders to produce these certificates on demand by Customs or Navy officers. Non-compliance leads to fines, recoverable through the sale of the vessel and its equipment.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate having jurisdiction

schedules_summary.description: A form for the certificate of registry, requiring details such as owner's name, occupation, residence, vessel's name, burthen, build location, and port of registration.

act_identification.act_title: THE MADRAS RENT AND REVENUE SALES ACT, 1839
act_identification.act_short_title: THE MADRAS RENT AND REVENUE SALES ACT, 1839.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of the Madras Presidency, except the Scheduled Districts; extended to the Scheduled Districts in Ganjam and Vizagapatam; extended to the Scheduled Districts in Godawari except the Xugar Tahiq

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to empower Tahsildars within the Presidency of Fort St. George to sell property distrained for arrears of rent or revenue. It also establishes that these Tahsildars are subject to the control of the Collector and that all fees from such sales must be credited to the Government.

key_sections.title: Tahsildars empowered to sell property distrained.
key_sections.description: Vests Tahsildars within the Presidency of Fort St. George with the powers of Commissioners for the sale of property distrained for arrears of rent or revenue.

key_sections.title: Control of tahsildars in exercise of such power.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that Tahsildars are subject to the control and superintendence of the Collector, and not the Zila Judge (except in judicial proceedings), when exercising their powers.

key_sections.title: Fees for selling property to be credited to Government.
key_sections.description: Mandates that Tahsildars are not entitled to any fee or commission for selling distrained property, and all such fees must be credited to the Government.

key_sections.title: Delegation of tahsildars powers.
key_sections.description: Grants Tahsildars the authority to delegate their powers under Section 2 to public servants under their authority, subject to the Collector's orders, with Sections 3 and 5 applying to such delegated powers.

powers_conferred: Powers to Tahsildars to sell property distrained for arrears of rent or revenue (Section 2)
Authority to Tahsildars to delegate their powers to any public servants placed under their authority (Section 6)

repealed_acts: Reg. XXVIII of 1802, s. 23

applies_to: Tahsildars within the territories subject to the Presidency of Fort St. George
Commissioners for the sale of property distrained for arrears of rent or of revenue
Public servants to whom Tahsildars' powers are delegated
special_provisions: Applicable to the whole of the Madras Presidency, except the Scheduled Districts
Extended to the Scheduled Districts in Ganjam and Vizagapatam
Extended to the Scheduled Districts in Godawari except the Xugar Tahiq

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through Tahsildars exercising powers of Commissioners for sale of distrained property, under the control and superintendence of the Collector.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Zila Judge (in case of judicial proceedings)

act_identification.act_title: An Act to enable the holders of Revenue which has been alienated to them by the State, to collect that Revenue within the Presidency of Bombay.

legislative_details.enacted_by: Hon’ble the President of the Council of India in Council, on the 28[th] of October, 1842, with the assent of the Right hon’ble the Governor General of India.

act_overview.preamble: I. Whereas it is expedient to authorize the grant by the Governor in Council of Bombay, at his discretion, of Commissions to certain Jageerdars, and others, by virtue of which such persons shall posses increased powers for collecting the Revenue due to them;
act_overview.purpose: This Act enables the Governor in Council of Bombay to grant commissions to holders of alienated revenue, such as Jageerdars, Surinjamdars, and Inamdars. These commissions confer increased powers for the collection of revenue due to them within the Presidency of Bombay.

key_sections.description: Authorizes the Governor in Council of Bombay to grant commissions to holders of alienated revenue for collection, specifying powers.
States that commissions, drawn according to Schedule A, are granted or withheld at Government's pleasure and can be issued to agents.
Confers authority on commission holders to demand security for revenue payment and take precautions similar to a Collector under Regulation XVII, of 1827.
Grants authority to send Mohussuls on defaulters under specific clauses of Regulation XVII of 1827, with limitations on their use.
Authorizes commission holders to attach property of defaulters, report to the Collector, and conduct sales, with exceptions for Jageerdars, Surinjamdars, or Inamdars with civil jurisdiction.
Stipulates that compulsory process ceases upon the defaulter furnishing security to institute a suit within 15 days, and imposes penalties for proceeding after security is provided.
Defines excessive demand for revenue as extortion, entitling the aggrieved party to damages, but allows holders to sue for re-assessment of lands or revenue.
Limits the power conferred by commission to the enforcement of revenue payment for the current and immediately preceding season only.

powers_conferred: Power to the Governor in Council of Bombay to grant commissions for revenue collection.
Power to Jageerdar, Surinjamdar, Inamdar, or other persons holding Lands or Villages to collect alienated revenue.
Power to demand security for the payment of revenue.
Power to send Mohussuls on Defaulters.
Power to attach the property of persons making default in revenue payment.
Power to conduct sales of attached property (with conditions).
Power to institute a suit in a competent Court for the purpose of trying the demand.
Power to institute a suit in any court of competent jurisdiction for the purpose of establishing claim to re-assess the Lands or re-settle the Revenue.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any holder of a commission proceeding with compulsory process after security is furnished or tendered shall forfeit three times the amount of the revenue sought to be recovered. Enforcement of a demand for an excess of rent or Revenue beyond the amount due shall be deemed extortion, and the person against whom such demand was enforced shall obtain three times the amount of any such excessive demand as damages.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Governor in Council of Bombay has the power to grant commissions to Jageerdars, Surinjamdars, Inamdars, or other persons holding Lands or Villages.

applies_to: Jageerdar
Surinjamdar
Inamdar
Other person holding Lands or Villages the Revenue of which has been alienated to him by the State

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through commissions granted by the Governor in Council of Bombay, which empower holders of alienated revenue to demand security, send Mohussuls, attach property, and conduct sales. Legal suits can also be instituted in competent courts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: any court of competent jurisdiction

schedules_summary.description: Form of Commission to be used to a holder of alienated Revenue or his Agent for enabling him to recover such Revenue.

act_identification.act_title: THE REVENUE COMMISSIONERS, BOMBAY ACT, 1842

legislative_details.enacted_by: Hon’ble the President of the Council of India in Council, with the assent of the Right hon’ble the Governor General of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act relative to the number and powers of the Revenue Commissioner under the Presidency of Bombay.
act_overview.purpose: This Act regulates the number and powers of Revenue Commissioners under the Presidency of Bombay. It repeals previous provisions for a single commissioner and allows for the appointment of one or more commissioners with defined jurisdictions and support staff.

key_sections.title: Repeal of part of Regulation V, 180
key_sections.description: Repeals the part of Regulation V, of 180, of the Bombay Code, that provided for a single Revenue Commissioner and excluded the Southern Maharatta Country from his jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Appointment and powers of Revenue Commissioners
key_sections.description: Enacts that one or more Revenue Commissioners shall be appointed for the whole Presidency of Bombay, vested with powers from Regulation V, 1830, and empowered to act within prescribed portions by the Governor in Council.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Deputies and Assistants
key_sections.description: Enacts that each Revenue Commissioner shall have such number of Deputies and Assistants as the Governor in Council deems expedient to appoint.

powers_conferred: Revenue Commissioners: Vested with all powers possessed by the single Revenue Commissioner under Regulation V, 1830.
Revenue Commissioners: Empowered to act within the Presidency of Bombay, or over such portion as the Governor in Council of Bombay may prescribe.
Governor in Council of Bombay: May prescribe portions of the Presidency for Commissioners to act in by Order published in the Gazette.
Governor in Council of Bombay: May appoint Deputies and Assistants for Revenue Commissioners.

repealed_acts: so much of Regulation V, of 180, of the Bombay Code, as provides that one Revenue Commissioner shall be appointed for the Territory subordinate to Bombay, and that the Southern Maharatta Country shall be excluded from his jurisdiction
related_acts: Regulation V, of 180, of the Bombay Code

authorities_established: Deputies and Assistants to Revenue Commissioners
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Governor in Council (for Deputies and Assistants)

applies_to: Revenue Commissioners
Territory composing the Presidency of Bombay
special_provisions: The Governor in Council of Bombay may, from time to time, prescribe by an Order published in the Gazette, the specific portion of the Presidency of Bombay over which a Revenue Commissioner may act.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Governor in Council of Bombay (by Order published in the Gazette)

act_identification.act_title: THE BOUNDARY-MARKS, BOMBAY 1846

legislative_details.enacted_by: Hon’ble the President of the Council of India in Council, with the assent of the Right Hon’ble the Governor General of India
legislative_details.geographical_extent: territories subject to the Presidency of Bombay

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is desirable, with a view to the better definition and security of landed property, the prevention of encroachments and disputes, and the identification of lands assessed to, or exempted from, the public revenue, that provision should be made for the establishment and maintenance of permanent marks to distinguish the boundaries of fields:
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish and maintain permanent boundary marks for fields in the Presidency of Bombay. Its purpose is to better define and secure landed property, prevent encroachments and disputes, and aid in identifying lands for public revenue assessment or exemption.

key_sections.description: Empowers Revenue Officers in the Presidency of Bombay to require owners or occupants to erect and maintain field boundary marks.
Prescribes the method for serving requisition notices for boundary marks, including posting at the Village Chowree if persons are not found.
Allows Revenue Officers to direct the erection and repair of boundary marks if owners/occupants default, with costs apportioned and charged to them or the village revenues.
States that a person out of possession claiming ownership/occupancy cannot have their claim allowed until they repay costs of boundary marks charged to village revenues due to their neglect.
Prescribes a fine not exceeding Fifty Rupees for wilfully erasing, removing, or injuring field boundary marks, with half awarded to the informer and half for restoration costs.

Grants authority for assessment and realization of sums due under the Act to Revenue Officers, to be exercised in conformity with rules for revenue demands, with proceedings subject to appeal to subordinate Revenue Authorities.

powers_conferred: Revenue Officers: to require erection and maintenance of field boundary marks (Section I)
Revenue Officers: to give directions for the erection and repair of field boundary marks (Section III)
Revenue Officers: for the assessment and realization of sums due under the provisions of this Act (Section VI)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person convicted of wilfully erasing, removing, or injuring field boundary marks shall be liable to a fine not exceeding Fifty Rupees for each mark so erased, removed, or injured. One half of the fine may be awarded to the informer, and the other half shall be chargeable with the cost of restoring the mark.

applies_to: Owners or Occupants on the boundaries of fields
Persons possessing a right of ownership or occupancy in such fields
Any person who may be convicted of wilfully erasing, removing, or injuring field boundary marks

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Revenue Officers are empowered to require boundary marks, serve requisitions, direct erection/repair if owners default (recovering costs), and assess/realize sums. Penalties are prescribed for damaging marks. Proceedings are subject to appeal to Revenue Authorities.

schedules_summary.description: A form for requisition to the owner or occupant of a field, requiring them to fix or repair boundary marks within a specified number of days, and stating that default will result in government officers performing the work and recovering the cost under Act III of 1846.

act_identification.act_title: THE BENGAL LAND HOLDER’ ATTENDANCE ACT, 1848
act_identification.act_short_title: THE BENGAL LAND HOLDER’ ATTENDANCE ACT, 1848

legislative_details.enacted_by: Governor General of India in Council
legislative_details.geographical_extent: Presidency of Bengal, excluding the North West Provinces

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS by sundry Regulations of the Bengal Code, provision is made for the imposition of a daily fine, by the Board of Revenue or other authority exercising the powers of that Board, on any proprietor or farmer of land subject to the provisions contained in the said several Regulations, who, when duly summoned by the Collector or other Officer exercising the power of Collector, shall omit or refuse to attend, or to cause his Officer or Agent to attend, or to furnish the accounts or documents required, and shall not shew sufficient cause for such omission ; and it is further provided that the fine, when confirmed by Government, is to be levied by same process as is prescribed for the recovery of arrears of revenue ; and whereas in many cases, by the delay thus occasioned, the whole burden of the penalty is greatly increased beyond what would be necessary, if summary power were given to the Officer by whom the requisition is made, to impose and levy reasonable fines, subject to review by the Commissioner of Revenue and other superior authority, It is enacted as follows:
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to empower Collectors to summarily impose and levy daily fines on land proprietors or farmers in the Presidency of Bengal who fail to attend or furnish required documents when summoned. It seeks to reduce delays in the fine imposition and collection process, making it more efficient.

key_sections.title: If any proprietor or farmer of land shall omit or refuse to attend, or to cause his Officer or Agent to attend, when duly summoned by the Collector, in any case specified in any of the said Regulations, by the time prescribed in the notice issued by the Collector, or shall omit or refuse to furnish the accounts or documents required, and shall not shew sufficient cause for such omission, the Collector may impose of his own authority such daily fine, to be payable daily until compliance with the requisition, as he may think adequate to the situation and circumstances in life or the defaulter, not exceeding in any case the daily fine of fifty Rupees: and the amount of such fine, accruing due from time to time may be levied without further confirmation, by the same process as is prescribed for the recovery of arrears of revenue.
key_sections.description: Grants Collectors summary power to impose and levy daily fines (up to 50 Rupees) on land proprietors/farmers for non-attendance or failure to furnish documents, leviable as arrears of revenue.

key_sections.title: The Collector shall forthwith report the imposition of every such fine, and the amount thereof, and also from time to time the amount levied, to the Commissioner of Revenue, who shall report the same for the information of the local Government.
key_sections.description: Requires Collectors to report fine imposition and amounts levied to the Commissioner of Revenue, who then informs the local Government.

key_sections.title: Every order passed by a Collector under this Act shall be appealable in the usual manner to the Commissioner of Revenue, and other superior authority ; but no such appeal shall avail to prevent the levy of any fine so imposed pending the appeal.
key_sections.description: Establishes that Collector's orders are appealable to the Commissioner of Revenue, but appeals do not stay the levy of fines.

key_sections.title: Whenever the amount levied under any such order, issued for any default by authority of a Collector under this Act, shall have exceeded five hundred Rupees, the Collector shall report the case specially to the Commissioner of Revenue ; and no further levy for such default shall be made otherwise than by authority of the Commissioner of Revenue.
key_sections.description: Mandates a special report to the Commissioner of Revenue if levied fines exceed 500 Rupees, requiring Commissioner's authority for further levies.

key_sections.title: Nothing in this Act contained shall be deemed to repeal the power of imposing daily fines and of levying the fines so imposed in the manner prescribed by the said several Regulations.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that this Act does not repeal existing powers to impose and levy fines under other Regulations.

key_sections.title: The word “Collector” used in this Act shall be taken to mean any person lawfully exercising the powers of a Collector.
key_sections.description: Defines the term 'Collector' for the purposes of this Act.

key_sections.title: This Act shall not extend to the North West Provinces of the Presidency of Bengal.
key_sections.description: Specifies the geographical extent of the Act, excluding the North West Provinces of the Presidency of Bengal.

powers_conferred: Collector: Impose daily fines for non-attendance or failure to furnish documents (Section I)
Collector: Levy fines without further confirmation (Section I)
Collector: Report fine imposition and levy amounts to the Commissioner of Revenue (Section II)
Commissioner of Revenue: Review appeals against Collector's orders (Section III)
Commissioner of Revenue: Authorize further levy of fines if the amount exceeds 500 Rupees (Section IV)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Offence: Proprietor or farmer of land omits or refuses to attend or cause their officer/agent to attend when duly summoned, or omits/refuses to furnish required accounts/documents, without sufficient cause. Penalty: Daily fine not exceeding fifty Rupees, leviable by the same process as prescribed for the recovery of arrears of revenue.

related_acts: sundry Regulations of the Bengal Code

applies_to: proprietor or farmer of land
special_provisions: This Act shall not extend to the North West Provinces of the Presidency of Bengal.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Fines are levied by the same process as prescribed for the recovery of arrears of revenue.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Commissioner of Revenue, and other superior authority (for appeals)

act_identification.act_title: An Act for appointing a Commissioner of Revenue at Madras .

legislative_details.enacted_by: Governor of Fort St. George in Council
legislative_details.geographical_extent: Presidency (Fort St. George Presidency), Districts of that Presidency

act_overview.preamble: Whereas it is expedient that the Governor of Fort St. George in Council should be empowered to depute a Member of the Board of Revenue, to perform in any of the Districts of that Presidency all or any of the duties which, by the General Regulations and Laws of the Presidency, belong to the Board of Revenue collectively, It is enacted as follows:
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to empower the Governor of Fort St. George in Council to depute a Member of the Board of Revenue to perform the collective duties of the Board in any district of the Presidency, thereby streamlining revenue administration.

key_sections.title: The Governor of Fort St. George in Council may, from time to time, whenever he shall see fit, depute a member of the Board of Revenue to perform alone, in any of the Districts of that Presidency, all or any of the duties which, by the General Regulations and Laws of the Presidency, belong to the Board of Revenue collectively.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Governor of Fort St. George in Council to depute a member of the Board of Revenue to perform collective duties in districts.

key_sections.title: When a special Commission shall be given to a Member of the Board of Revenue under this Act, the Member of the Board named therein shall, by virtue thereof, be empowered to exercise, within the limits of his Commission, all the powers and duties which by Law are vested in the Board of Revenue collectively, without exception, or subject to any exceptions or restrictions, which shall be prescribed in such Commission; and all Regulations and Acts concerning the Board of Revenue shall be deemed to apply to the said Commissioner within the limits of his Commission, and with regard to all things concerning the Revenue of the Districts included in it, so far as is necessary to give full effect to his Commission and to this Act.
key_sections.description: Grants the deputed Commissioner all powers and duties of the Board of Revenue collectively, subject to the Commission's limits.

key_sections.title: Every such Commission shall be published in the Fort St. George Gazette, and the Commissioner shall enter on his Office from the date of such publication; and in like manner the revocation or other determination of any such Commission shall be published in the Fort St. George Gazette.
key_sections.description: Requires publication of the Commission in the Fort St. George Gazette for the Commissioner to enter office and for revocation.

key_sections.title: The correspondence and other documents belonging to any such Commission shall be deposited on the determination there of, in the Office of the Board of Revenue, and shall be deemed records of the said Board.
key_sections.description: Mandates depositing correspondence and documents of the Commission with the Board of Revenue, deeming them records.

powers_conferred: Power to the Governor of Fort St. George in Council to depute a member of the Board of Revenue.
Power to the deputed Member (Commissioner) to exercise all powers and duties of the Board of Revenue collectively within the limits of the Commission.

related_acts: General Regulations and Laws of the Presidency
Regulations and Acts concerning the Board of Revenue

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Governor of Fort St. George in Council has the power to depute a member of the Board of Revenue.

applies_to: Governor of Fort St. George in Council
Member of the Board of Revenue
Districts of the Presidency

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act defines the powers and procedures for the deputed Commissioner. Publication of the Commission in the Fort St. George Gazette is required for the Commissioner to enter office.

act_identification.act_title: THE FORFEITED DEPOSITS ACT, 1850

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Districts of Hazaribagh, Ranchi, Palamau and Manbhum and Pargana Dhalbhum and the Kolhan in the District of Singbhum in the Chota Nagpur Division; Sonthal Parganas

act_overview.preamble: An Act for the forfeiture to Government of deposits made on incomplete sales of land under 2Regulation 8, 1819 3***. WHEREAS patnidars [4]*** fraudulently avail themselves of the [5]provision in section 9, Regulation 8, 1819, of the Bengal Code [6]*** that forfeited deposits at sales of land [7]*** for arrears of rent shall be applied as if they were purchase-money.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to regulate the application of deposits forfeited during incomplete sales of land, particularly those related to arrears of rent under Regulation 8, 1819. It directs such deposits to defray sale expenses and forfeits any surplus to the Government, thereby preventing fraudulent practices where these deposits were previously treated as purchase-money.

key_sections.title: Repeals.
key_sections.description: This section originally dealt with repeals, but it was subsequently repealed by the Repealing Act, 1870.

key_sections.title: Application of forfeited deposits.
key_sections.description: Mandates that any forfeited deposit shall be applied to defray the expenses of the sale, and the surplus shall be forfeited to Government.

powers_conferred: Power to Government to forfeit surplus deposits from incomplete land sales.

repealed_acts: Repealing Act, 1870 (14 of 1870)
Act 4, 1846 (by Act 12 of 1891)

applies_to: patnidars
sales of land for arrears of rent
special_provisions: Declared to be in force in the Districts of Hazaribagh, Ranchi, Palamau and Manbhum and Pargana Dhalbhum and the Kolhan in the District of Singbhum in the Chota Nagpur Division.
Declared to be in force in the Sonthal Parganas.

act_identification.act_title: THE IMPROVEMENTS IN TOWNS ACT, 1850

legislative_details.enacted_by: Government of the East India Company
legislative_details.geographical_extent: Presidency of Fort William, not within the Town of Calcutta; Town in the other Presidencies under the Government of the East india Company; any Town or Suburb, not within the Town of Calcutta, Madras, or Bombay

act_overview.preamble: Whereas Act X. 1842, was passed for enabling the inhabitants of any place of public resort or residence, under the Presidency of Fort William, not within the Town of Calcutta, to make better provision for purposes connected with public health and convenience, but the said Act has proved ineffectual for the purpose, and it is expedient to amend the provisions thereof, and to extend the like powers to the inhabitants of Town in the other Presidencies under the Government of the East india Company, It is enacted as follows:
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to enable inhabitants of towns and suburbs (excluding Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay) to make better provision for public health and convenience. It facilitates improvements such as making, repairing, cleaning, lighting, or watching public streets, roads, drains, or tanks, and for the prevention of nuisances.

key_sections.title: Act X. 1842, is repealed.
key_sections.description: Repeals the previous Act X. 1842.

key_sections.title: If it shall appear to the Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governor, of any Presidency or Place within the Territories under the Government of the East India Company, that the inhabitants of any Town or Suburb, not within the Town of Calcutta, Madras, or Bombay, are desirous of making better provision for making, repairing, cleaning, lighting, or watching any public streets, roads, drains, or tanks, or for the prevention of nuisances, or for improving the said Town or Suburb in any other manner, the said Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governor, may order this Act to be put in force within such Town or Suburb.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Governor or Lieutenant Governor to put the Act in force in towns/suburbs (excluding Calcutta, Madras, Bombay) if inhabitants desire improvements.

key_sections.title: Whenever this Act shall come into force in any Town or Suburb, the Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governor, shall appoint the Magistrate and such number of the inhabitants thereof as to him shall appear necessary, to be Commissioners for putting the Act in force, and shall give authority to them to prepare Rules for more effectually accomplishing the purposes for which they are appointed; which Rules, when approved by the Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governors, shall be of the same force within the said Town or Suburb, until altered or rescinded as hereinafter provided, as if they were inserted in this Act.
key_sections.description: Establishes Commissioners (Magistrate and inhabitants) to put the Act in force and prepare rules, subject to approval by the Governor/Lieutenant Governor.

key_sections.title: The Rules to be prepared by the said Commissioners shall provide, among other things, for those following, that is to say: 1. The appointment and management of all necessary Officers and Servants of the Commissioners, and the salaries to be allowed to them. 2. The definition of the persons of property within the Town or Suburb to be taxed for raising the monies necessary for the purpose of this Act, whether by House Assessment or Town Duties, or otherwise, the amount or rate of the taxes to be imposed, the manner of raising and collecting them, and ensuring the safety and due application of them when collected. 3. The manner in which from time to time the Rules in force are to be amended or rescinded, and new Rules are to be made, with the approval in every case of the Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governor. 4. The definition and prohibition of nuisances within the Town or Suburb. 5. The imposition of reasonable penalties for breach of any Rule made by the Commissioners, not exceeding Fifty Rupees, or in the case of continuing nuisance, not exceeding Five Rupees for every day that such nuisance is continued.
key_sections.description: Details the scope of rules to be prepared by Commissioners, including appointment of officers, taxation, amendment of rules, nuisance prohibition, and penalties.

key_sections.title: The Commissioners appointed from time to time shall have full power to make all necessary contracts, for the purposes of this Act, and apply the taxes raised as aforesaid in the necessary works, and in payment of their Officers and Servants, and in the other expenses incident to the execution of this Act within the said Town or Suburb.
key_sections.description: Grants Commissioners power to make contracts and apply collected taxes for works, officer payments, and other expenses.

key_sections.title: No Commissioner shall be personally liable for any contract made by the Commissioners on behalf of the inhabitants of such Town or Suburb ; but every Commissioner shall be laible for any misapplication of the monies collected, to which he shall have been knowingly party or privy, or which shall have happened through gross neglect of his duty and shall be liable to be sued for the same as for money due to, and the suit of the East india Company.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that Commissioners are not personally liable for contracts but are liable for misapplication of funds or gross neglect.

key_sections.title: The powers of Act II. 1839, for the recovery of fines, shall be applied for the recovery of all arrears of taxes and penalties under this Act ; and every Magistrate shall put in force the powers of the said Act II. 1839 for that purpose, whenever thereunto required by the Commissioners, or any of their Officers deputed by them for the purposes of enforcing payment of arrears of taxed imposed under this Act.
key_sections.description: Applies powers of Act II. 1839 for the recovery of taxes and penalties, with Magistrates enforcing these powers upon request by Commissioners.

key_sections.title: The Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governor may, at any time, suspend the operation of this Act in any town or Suburb, and appoint any person or persons to examine and report upon the behavior of the Commissioners, or any of them, or their Officers in the execution of this Act.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Governor or Lieutenant Governor to suspend the Act's operation and investigate the conduct of Commissioners or their officers.

powers_conferred: Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governor: to order this Act to be put in force (Sec II)
Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governor: to make a final order on applications (Sec IV)
Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governor: to appoint Commissioners (Sec VI)
Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governor: to approve rules (Sec VI, VII)
Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governor: to remove any of the Commissioners and appoint others (Sec VI)
Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governor: to suspend the operation of this Act (Sec XIV)
Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governor: to appoint any person or persons to examine and report upon the behavior of the Commissioners (Sec XIV)
Commissioners: to prepare Rules (Sec VI)
Commissioners: to make all necessary contracts (Sec VIII)
Commissioners: to apply the taxes raised in necessary works and expenses (Sec VIII)
Commissioners: to require Magistrates to put in force powers for recovery of arrears of taxes and penalties (Sec X)
Magistrate: to put in force the powers of Act II. 1839 for recovery of fines/taxes (Sec X)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Imposition of reasonable penalties for breach of any Rule made by the Commissioners, not exceeding Fifty Rupees, or in the case of continuing nuisance, not exceeding Five Rupees for every day that such nuisance is continued.

repealed_acts: Act X. 1842

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governor
regulatory_bodies: Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governor

applies_to: inhabitants of any Town or Suburb, not within the Town of Calcutta, Madras, or Bombay
exemptions: Town of Calcutta
Madras
Bombay

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Commissioners, with the approval of the Governor or Governor in Council, or Lieutenant Governor
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Commissioners prepare and enforce rules, collect taxes. Magistrates enforce recovery of taxes and penalties using powers of Act II. 1839.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate (for recovery of fines/taxes); East India Company (for suit against Commissioners for misapplication of monies)

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN TOLLS ACT, 1851

legislative_details.enacted_by: The Governor of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal, the Lieutenant-Governor of North-Western Provinces of Bengal and the Governor of the Presidency of Fort St. George in Council
legislative_details.geographical_extent: This Act extends to the territories administered on the fourth of July, eighteen hundred and fifty-one, by the Governor of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal, the Lieutenant-Governor of North-Western Provinces of Bengal and the Governor of the Presidency of Fort St. George in Council. It has been extended to Ajmer and Merwara, the C.P., the Sonthal Parganas, various Scheduled Districts (Hazaribagh, Lohardaga, Manbhum, Pargana Dhalbhum, Kolhan, Lahaul, Coorg, Ganjam, Vizagapatam, Ducharti and Guditeru Muttahs, Yellavaram taluk, East Godavari Agency, Darjeeling), Madhya Pradesh, and the Union territory of Pondicherry. It also applies to Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, and West Bengal.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to enable Government to levy tolls upon roads and bridges; it is enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to enable the Government to levy tolls on public roads and bridges that have been or will be made or repaired at the expense of the Central or any State Government.

key_sections.title: Extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the geographical areas to which the Act extends.

key_sections.title: Power to cause levy of tolls on roads and bridges within certain rates, and to appoint collectors. Collectors’ responsibilities.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the State Government to levy tolls on public roads and bridges and to appoint collectors, outlining their responsibilities.

key_sections.title: Their powers for recovery of toll. Release of seized property on tender of dues.
key_sections.description: Details the powers of toll collectors to seize property for non-payment of tolls and the procedure for sale or release of seized property.

key_sections.title: Exemptions from payment of toll.
key_sections.description: Lists specific exemptions from toll payment, such as Police-officers on duty.

key_sections.title: Assistance of collectors by Police-officers.
key_sections.description: Mandates Police-officers to assist toll collectors in the execution of the Act.

key_sections.title: Penalty for offences under Act. Compensation to person aggrieved. Saving of his right to sue.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for unlawful levying or demanding of tolls and other related offences, and provides for compensation to aggrieved persons.

key_sections.title: Exhibition of table of tolls, and statement of penalties.
key_sections.description: Requires the display of a table of authorized tolls and penalties at toll-gates.

key_sections.title: Application of proceeds of tolls.
key_sections.description: States that the tolls levied under this Act shall be deemed public revenue.

powers_conferred: Power to cause levy of tolls on roads and bridges (Section 2)
Power to appoint collectors for tolls (Section 2)
Power to seize carriages or animals for non-payment of toll (Section 3)
Power to sell seized property to recover toll and expenses (Section 3)
Power of Police-officers to assist toll-collectors (Section 5)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Offences include levying or demanding unlawful toll, demanding or taking higher toll than lawful, unlawful seizure or sale of property, and unlawfully extorting money. Penalties include imprisonment for up to six calendar months or a fine not exceeding two hundred rupees, with part of the fine potentially awarded to the aggrieved person.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government may place the collection of tolls under the management of such persons as may appear to it proper (Section 2).

applies_to: Territories administered on the fourth of July, eighteen hundred and fifty-one, by the Governor of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal, the Lieutenant-Governor of North-Western Provinces of Bengal and the Governor of the Presidency of Fort St. George in Council (Section 1A)
Any road or bridge which has been, or shall hereafter be, made or repaired at the expense of the Central or any State Government (Section 2)
exemptions: Police-officers on duty
Any person or property in the custody of Police-officers (Section 4)
The State Government Vehicles on Government duty (in Orissa, as per Orissa Act 13 of 1987)
special_provisions: Amendment in Orissa for section 2, allowing levy of tolls for roads/bridges made/repaired by Corporation, Statutory Body, Company, Firm or person authorized by the State Government (Orissa Act 7 of 1999).
Amendment in Orissa for section 4, exempting State Government Vehicles on Government duty (Orissa Act 13 of 1987).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Tolls are collected by appointed officers. In case of non-payment, officers can seize property, which may be sold after 24 hours if the toll remains undischarged. Police-officers are bound to assist toll collectors. Offences under the Act are punishable upon conviction before a Magistrate.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate (for conviction of offences), Civil Court (for redress by suit).

schedules_summary.description: Contained rates of toll, but was repealed by the Devolution Act, 1920 (38 of 1920), s. 2 and the First Schedule.

act_identification.act_title: THE MADRAS CITY LAND REVENUE ACT, 1851

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Madras, within the limits of the Town of Madras as defined in Section XII., Regulation II. of 1802., of the Madras Code

act_overview.preamble: An Act for securing the Land Revenue of Madras. Whereas it is expedient that the land revenue accruing due to the East India Company at Madras, within the limits of the Town of Madras as defined in Section XII., Regulation II. of 1802., of the Madras Code, should be ascertained and collected in as summary a manner as in other parts of the territories under the Government of the East India Company, It is enacted as follows:
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to secure, ascertain, and collect land revenue due to the East India Company within the Town of Madras. It establishes procedures for assessment, collection, and resolution of disputes related to land revenue.

key_sections.title: Assessable lands in Madras not assessed, to be assessed at customary rates.
key_sections.description: Mandates assessment of unassessed lands within Madras City limits at customary rates.

key_sections.title: Lakhiraj tenures of sixty years standing and none of less to be valid.
key_sections.description: Declares Lakiraj tenures with 60 years of uninterrupted possession as valid, unless held under an unexpired British Government grant.

key_sections.title: Collector to determine rate of assessment, subject to an appeal.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Collector to determine assessment rates, with a right to appeal to the Board of Revenue.

key_sections.title: After demand in writing, rent may be recovered by distress and sale of goods and chattels. Collector may appoint bailiffs and appraisers to make and appraise, &c. distresses.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Collector to recover unpaid land assessment or rent by distress and sale of goods, and to appoint officers for this purpose.

key_sections.title: Land revenue or rent of East India Company to have priority over all other claims as respects property liable.
key_sections.description: Establishes the priority of the East India Company's claim for land revenue or rent over all other claims on the land or distrained property.

key_sections.title: Claim to hold land rent free to be referred by Collector to Board, if disallowed by Board, land to be assessed, subject to Civil Suit.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for inquiring into claims of holding land rent-free (lakiraj), involving the Collector and Board of Revenue, with recourse to Civil Courts.

key_sections.title: Obstructing Collector, &c. to be punishable by fine and in default of payment by imprisonment.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for obstructing the Collector or his officers in the execution of their duty.

key_sections.title: Ground rents of East India Company to be deemed revenue within 21 Geo. 3 Cap. 70.
key_sections.description: Declares ground rents payable to the East India Company as revenue under the Act of Parliament, 21 Geo. III. Cap. 70, and limits the civil jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of Judicature at Madras regarding them.

key_sections.title: Actions for trespass or injury committed under color of Act to be tried in East India Company’s Courts, &c. and no action to lie more than 6 months after cause arose.
key_sections.description: Specifies that actions against revenue officers under this Act are to be tried in East India Company's Civil Courts in Chingleput, with a six-month limitation period.

key_sections.title: Interprets the words “Collector” and Board of Revenue.
key_sections.description: Defines 'Collector' and 'Board of Revenue' as persons lawfully appointed to exercise their respective powers under the Act.

powers_conferred: Collector: To assess lands (Section I, III)
Collector: To order measurement of land (Section IV)
Collector: To make proportionate abatement or charge for excess dimensions (Section V, VI)
Collector: To levy rent by distress and sale of goods and chattels (Section VII)
Collector: To appoint officers (Bailiffs, Appraisers, Chief Clerk) for distress and sale (Section VII)
Collector: To inquire into claims to hold land rent-free (Section XII)
Collector: To punish contempts committed in his presence (Section XIV)
Board of Revenue: To hear appeals against assessment rates (Section III)
Board of Revenue: To hear appeals against extra assessment or additional rent (Section VI)
Board of Revenue: To decide on the validity of claims to hold land rent-free (Section XII)
Board of Revenue: To hear appeals against Collector's orders of fine or imprisonment for contempt (Section XIV)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section XIII: Any person obstructing or molesting the Collector or his subordinate officers in their duty is liable to a fine not exceeding five hundred rupees, and in default of payment, imprisonment for up to six months. Section XIV: The Collector may punish contempts committed in his presence by a fine not exceeding two hundred rupees, and in default of payment, imprisonment for up to one month.

related_acts: Regulation II. of 1802., of the Madras Code
Act of Parliament, 21 Geo. III. Cap. 70

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Collector shall have power to appoint any of his Officers to perform the duties of Bailiffs and Appraisers, and of the Chief Clerk of the said Court, as provided by Act VII. of 1847.

applies_to: All assessable lands not the property of the East India Company, within the limits of the Town Madras
Owner of assessed land or any person holding land subject to a rent payable to the East India Company
exemptions: Lakiraj tenures of land in Madras, of which uninterrupted possession has been held under alleged grants, exempt or partially exempt from assessment for sixty years
special_provisions: Applies within the limits of the Town of Madras

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through assessment by the Collector, with appeals to the Board of Revenue. Unpaid rent or assessment can be recovered by distress and sale of goods. Obstruction of officers and contempts are punishable.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate of the Town of Madras (for obstruction/molestation), Civil Courts established by the East India Company in the Zillah of Chingleput (for actions against revenue officers, claims of rent/revenue). The Supreme Court of Judicature at Madras has no civil jurisdiction concerning ground rents.

act_identification.act_title: An Act for the Adjudication of Titles to certain Estates claimed to be wholly or partially Rent-free in the Presidency of Bombay.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Presidency of Bombay; Territories of the Deccan Kandeish, and Southern Mahratta Country, and in other Districts more recently annexed to the Bombay Presidency; any Zillah or other division of the Territories subject to the Presidency of Bombay, which were not brought under the General Regulations of Government by Regulation XXVIII. of 1827

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS in the Territories of the Deccan Kandeish, and Southern Mahratta Country, and in other Districts more recently annexed to the Bombay Presidency, claims against Government on account of Inams and other Estates wholly or partially exempt from payment of Land Revenue are excepted from the cognizance of the ordinary Civil Courts, and incapable of being justly disposed of under the Rules for the determination of Titles, and the Rules of Procedure contained in Chapters IX. and X. of Regulation XVII. of 1827 of the Bombay Code and their Supplements; and whereas it is desirable that the said claims should be tried and determined without further delay. It is declared and enacted as follows:
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide a mechanism for the adjudication of titles to estates claimed as wholly or partially rent-free in specific districts of the Bombay Presidency. It aims to resolve claims against the Government regarding Inams and other revenue-exempt estates, which were previously outside the jurisdiction of ordinary Civil Courts.

key_definitions: Inams already declared permanent by competent authority
uninterruptedly held as wholly or partially exempt from assessment for a period of sixty years
uninterruptedly held as wholly or partially exempt from assessment, for a period of forty years
Land held as wholly exempt from payment of Revenue, or on partial assessment, the possession of which is not continuable under the preceding Rules
Inams apparently permanent by the nature of the objects for which they are held, and not merely personal
lands authorizedly held by an official tenure which it is evident from local usage was meant to be hereditary
Provision for the Widows of the last incumbents of resumed holdings
exception of certain tenures from the application of these Rules
modification and interpretation of these Rules

key_sections.title: The Rules in Chapters IX. and X. of Regulation XVII. of 1827, and in Clause 1 of Regulation VI. of 1833 of the Bombay Code, do not apply to any of the Districts of the Bombay Presidency which were not brought under the General Regulations of Government by Regulation XXVIII. of 1827 of the Bombay Code; and no order hitherto passed regarding the continuance or resumption of lands in any of the said Districts held or claimed from Government as wholly or partially free of assessment, shall be liable to be questioned in any Court of Law, on the grounds of any interpretation nr construction of the Law, which may be inconsistent with the declarations made and the rules prescribed by this enactment.
key_sections.description: Declares certain previous regulations inapplicable to non-regulation districts and prevents questioning of government orders on rent-free lands in courts based on inconsistent interpretations.

key_sections.title: The Governor of Bombay in Council may appoint in any Zillah or other division of the Territories subject to the Presidency of Bombay, which were not brought under the General Regulations of Government by the said Regulation XXVIII. of 1827, an Inam Commissioner with so many Assistants, and such subordinate Establishment, as may be necessary for the purposes hereinafter mentioned.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Governor of Bombay in Council to appoint an Inam Commissioner and assistants in non-regulation districts.

key_sections.title: Each Inam Commissioner sand his Assistants shall have the same authority to procure the attendance of witnesses, and to take evidence, as now is, or from time to time may be, by Law vested in the ordinary Civil Courts; and so far as concerns the penalties for not giving evidence, for false testimony, for resistance of process, contempts, and other like matters, connected with cases under cognizance by any one of the said Officers, his Office shall be held to be a Court of Civil Jurisdiction of the same authority as the superior Civil Court of the Zillah or District in which his Office from time to time shall be established.
key_sections.description: Grants Inam Commissioners and their assistants powers of civil courts for witness attendance, evidence, and penalties, establishing their office as a court of civil jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Bribery, extortion, and generally all acts of abuse, or misapplication of authority, or other misconduct, committed by any Officer belonging to the Establishment of the Inam Commission, or temporarily employed therein under the provisions of this enactment, shall be punishable as criminal offences with fine and ordinary imprisonment without labour for a period not exceeding five years, and the receipt of a present, directly or indirectly, by any such Officer from any person against whom or in whose behalf he may be officially employed, shall be considered extortion.
key_sections.description: Prescribes criminal penalties (fine and imprisonment up to five years) for bribery, extortion, and misconduct by officers of the Inam Commission, without prejudice to civil remedies.

key_sections.title: No decision or order of the Inam Commissioner, or of any of his Assistants, or of the Governor in Council, under the provisions of this enactment, so long as the same shall be in force under such provisions, shall be questioned or avoided in any Court of Law; and no Commissioner or Assistant Commissioner, or other person acting under the provisions of this Act, shall be liable to be sued in any Civil Court for any act bonâ fide done or ordered to be done by him in pursuance of the said provisions.
key_sections.description: Protects decisions of the Inam Commissioner, assistants, or Governor in Council from being questioned in any Court of Law and grants immunity from civil suits for bona fide actions taken under the Act.

key_sections.title: The duty of the Inam Commissioner and his Assistants shall be to investigate, in the manner prescribed by this enactment, the titles of persons holding or claiming against Government the possession or enjoyment of Inams or Jagheers, or any interest therein, or claiming exemption from the payment of Land Revenue, and generally to act according to the instructions of Government in all matters not specifically provided for in this enactment.
key_sections.description: Defines the primary duty of Inam Commissioners and assistants as investigating titles to Inams, Jagheers, or claims for land revenue exemption.

key_sections.title: All orders of the Assistant Commissioners shall be appealable to the Inam Commissioner, who shall also have the authority of revising and of modifying, reversing or annulling, if necessary, their orders and proceedings, and the orders and proceedings of the Inam Commissioner shall be in like manner appealable to, and subject to modification, reversal, or annulment by the Governor of Bombay in Council, whose orders shall in every case be final.
key_sections.description: Establishes an appeal process for orders of Assistant Commissioners to the Inam Commissioner, and from the Inam Commissioner to the Governor of Bombay in Council, whose decisions are final.

key_sections.title: Regarding Inams already declared permanent by competent authority since the introduction of the present Government.—All lands held under a specific and absolute declaration by the British Government, or any competent officer acting under it, that they were to be continued hereditarily or in perpetuity exempt, wholly or partially, from the payment of Revenue, are to be so continued according to the purport of such declaration.
key_sections.description: Mandates the continuation of lands declared permanent by competent British Government authority as wholly or partially revenue-exempt.

key_sections.title: All lands uninterruptedly held as wholly or partially exempt from assessment for a period of sixty years before the introduction of the British Government, and then in the authorized possession of a grandson in male descent, or male heir of the body of such grandson of the original grantee, shall continue to be so held so long as there shall be in existence any male heir of the body of the person who was incumbent at the introduction of the British Government, tracing his lineage from such incumbent through male heirs only.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions for continuing land exemptions based on 60 years of uninterrupted holding before British rule and male lineal descent.

key_sections.title: Regarding claims to Inams apparently permanent by the nature of the objects for which they are held, and not merely personal.—All lands held for the support of Mosques, Temples, or similar Institutions, of the permanent character of which there can be no doubt, are to be continued permanently, even though their permanent continuance may not have been expressly provided for when they were granted.
key_sections.description: Ensures permanent continuation of lands held for the support of Mosques, Temples, or similar permanent institutions, even without explicit grant provisions.

key_sections.title: Regarding the exception of certain tenures from the application of these Rules.—These Rules shall not be necessarily applicable to Jageers, Serinjams, or other tenures for service to Government, or tenures of a Political nature, the titles and continuance of which shall be determined as heretofore under such Rules as Government may find it necessary to issue from time to time.
key_sections.description: Excludes Jageers, Serinjams, and other service or political tenures from these rules, leaving their determination to existing or future government rules.

key_sections.title: Regarding the modification and interpretation of these Rules.—Any of these Rules may be relaxed in favor of claimants under instructions from the Governor of Bombay in Council, in whom shall also be vested the power of interpreting the precise meaning of any of the Rules respecting which a question may arise.
key_sections.description: Grants the Governor of Bombay in Council the power to relax and interpret the rules in favor of claimants.

powers_conferred: Governor of Bombay in Council: appoint Inam Commissioner with Assistants (Section II)
Governor of Bombay in Council: determine competency of officer to make declarations (Schedule B, Rule 1, Provision 1st)
Governor of Bombay in Council: determine precise date of introduction of British Government (Schedule B, Rule 4, Provision 3rd)
Governor of Bombay in Council: prescribe manner of execution of decisions (Schedule A, Rule 13)
Governor of Bombay in Council: relax and interpret rules (Schedule B, Rule 11)
Inam Commissioner and Assistants: investigate titles of persons holding or claiming Inams, Jagheers, or exemption from Land Revenue (Schedule A, Rule 1)
Inam Commissioner and Assistants: procure attendance of witnesses, take evidence, inflict penalties (Section V)
Inam Commissioner: revise, modify, reverse, or annul orders and proceedings of Assistant Commissioners (Schedule A, Rule 2)
Inam Commissioner and Assistants: receive statements and record evidence (Schedule A, Rule 3)
Inam Commissioner and Assistants: ascertain facts and pronounce decisions in absence of claimants (Schedule A, Rule 10)
Collector or Chief Revenue Authority: enforce attachment of land (Schedule A, Rule 8)
Collector or Chief Revenue Authority: remove attachment of land (Schedule A, Rule 11)
Collector or Chief Revenue Authority: carry decisions into execution (Schedule A, Rule 13)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Bribery, extortion, and generally all acts of abuse, or misapplication of authority, or other misconduct committed by any officer of the Inam Commission are punishable as criminal offences with fine and ordinary imprisonment without labour for a period not exceeding five years. Receipt of a present by such officer is considered extortion. These penalties do not preclude other civil prosecutions.

related_acts: Regulation XVII. of 1827 of the Bombay Code
Regulation VI. of 1833 of the Bombay Code
Regulation XXVIII. of 1827 of the Bombay Code

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Governor of Bombay in Council may appoint an Inam Commissioner with Assistants.

applies_to: Territories of the Deccan Kandeish, and Southern Mahratta Country, and in other Districts more recently annexed to the Bombay Presidency
any Zillah or other division of the Territories subject to the Presidency of Bombay, which were not brought under the General Regulations of Government by Regulation XXVIII. of 1827
persons holding or claiming against Government the possession or enjoyment of Inams or Jagheers, or any interest therein, or claiming exemption from the payment of Land Revenue
exemptions: Jageers
Serinjams
other tenures for service to Government
tenures of a Political nature
special_provisions: Rules in Chapters IX. and X. of Regulation XVII. of 1827, and in Clause 1 of Regulation VI. of 1833 of the Bombay Code, do not apply to any of the Districts of the Bombay Presidency which were not brought under the General Regulations of Government by Regulation XXVIII. of 1827 of the Bombay Code.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Governor of Bombay in Council (for prescribing manner of execution, relaxing rules, and interpreting rules)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Investigation of titles by Inam Commissioner and Assistants, receiving statements, taking evidence, issuing notices, attachment of land, collection of rents, and execution of decisions by the Collector. An appeal process is established from Assistant Commissioners to the Inam Commissioner, and then to the Governor of Bombay in Council.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The Office of the Inam Commissioner and his Assistants shall be held to be a Court of Civil Jurisdiction of the same authority as the superior Civil Court of the Zillah or District. Decisions of the Inam Commissioner, Assistants, or Governor in Council cannot be questioned in any other Court of Law.

schedules_summary.description: Contains rules defining the duties of the Inam Commissioner and his assistants, including investigation of titles, appeal procedures, methods for receiving claims and evidence, issuing notices, attaching lands, and the process for delivering and executing decisions.

Contains rules for the adjudication of titles to estates claimed as Inam or exempt from payment of land revenue. These rules cover lands declared permanent, hereditary lands, lands held for specific periods (60 or 40 years) before British rule, lands for religious institutions (Mosques, Temples), lands held under official tenure, provisions for widows, and exceptions for certain tenures like Jageers and Serinjams. It also grants the Governor in Council power to relax and interpret these rules.

act_identification.act_title: An Act for extending the provisions of Acts XXIV.of 1841. and XVII. of 1843, to the Straits Settlement.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the Settlement of Prince of Wales’ Islands, Singapore and Malacca

act_overview.preamble: Whereas doubts have been entertained whether Acts XXIV. of 1841. and XVII. of 1843, are in force in the Settlement of Prince of Wales’ Islands, Singapore and Malacca; It is hereby enacted as follows:
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to clarify and extend the applicability of Acts XXIV of 1841 and XVII of 1843 to the Straits Settlement. It also ensures that provisions relating to Supreme Courts in those Acts are construed as applying to the Court of Judicature of the Straits Settlement.

key_sections.title: Extending Acts 24,1841 and 17,1843 to Straits Settlements.
key_sections.description: The provisions of Acts XXIV. of 1841, and XVII. of 1843, shall be applicable and in force in the said Settlement.

key_sections.title: Extending provisions of above Acts relating to Supreme Court to Court of Judicature of Straits Settlement.
key_sections.description: All provisions contained in Act XXIV. of 1841, and Act XVII. of 1843, relating to Her Majesty’s Supreme Courts shall be applicable to the Court of Judicature of the said Settlement, and shall be construed as if the words 'the Court of Judicature of prince of Wales’ Island, Singapore and Malacca' had been mentioned instead of references to Her Majesty’s Supreme Courts.

applies_to: Straits Settlement
Settlement of Prince of Wales’ Islands, Singapore and Malacca

implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Court of Judicature of prince of Wales’ Island, Singapore and Malacca

act_identification.act_title: THE RENT RECOVERY ACT, 1853

act_overview.preamble: Whereas, by Regulation VIII. 1831 of the Bengal Code, the hearing and decision of Summary Suits or claims relating to arrears or exactions of rents were transferred from the Judges of the Zilah or City Courts to the Collectors of Land Revenue of the several districts; and whereas by Regulation VII. 1832 of the Bengal Code, the conduct of sales of Putnee Talooks and other saleable tenures under Regulations VIII.1819 and I. 1820 of the same Code, and the performance of other acts preparatory to, or connected with, such sales were transferred of the Collector or Deputy Collector, of Land Revenue, or Head Assistant to the Collector or Deputy Collector subject to an appeal as therein provided; and whereas by Act VIII. 1835, the power theretofore vested in the Judge of the Dewanny Adawlut of selling land satisfaction of Summary Decrees for rent was transferred to the Collectors of Land-Revenue, and it was enacted that all sales for the recovery of arrears of rent held under clause 7, section 15, Regulation VII. 1799, should be conducted by the Collector, his Deputy or duty authorized Assistant, and that ten days' notice should be given of such sales by advertisement to be stuck up at the Cutcherry of the Zillah Court or local Adawlut, and that of the Collector ; and whereas it is expedient that Act XXV. 1850, and Section IX. Regulation VIII. 1819, of the Bengal Code, as modified by        Clause I, Section XVI.
