Regulation VII. 1832 of the same Code, and as altered by the said Act XXV. 1850, should be extended to sales under Act VIII. 1835; and whereas doubts may be entertained as to who ought to exercise the jurisdiction transferred by the abovementioned Regulations and Acts, where lands situate within the zillah or other district of one Collector, form part of an entire estate, paying revenue to the Collector of an another Zillah or district;In order therefore to avoid such doubts, and also to define who are the proper Officers to exercise such jurisdictions in cases where lands are situate in a district assigned to an independent Deputy Collector, and also in cases where lands held in putnee, or other tenure, at one entire rent are situate in two or more Collectorates, and to prevent any such decision or sale already made from being held invalid, upon the ground of its having been made by an Officer of a wrong district; It is enacted as follows:
act_overview.purpose: The purpose of this Act is to clarify and define the proper officers and jurisdictions for summary suits relating to arrears of rent and sales of land, especially in cases involving lands across multiple Collectorates or under independent Deputy Collectors. It also aims to validate past decisions and sales made by officers of potentially incorrect districts.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction for sales and suits in single or multiple Collectorates
key_sections.description: Specifies which Collector has jurisdiction to conduct sales or hear suits when lands are entirely within one Collectorate, or when a tenure comprises lands in two or more Collectorates.

key_sections.title: Procedure for doubt regarding Collectorate jurisdiction
key_sections.description: Requires a Collector to report to the Board if there is doubt about jurisdiction, and the Board's order on jurisdiction is conclusive.

key_sections.title: Definition of “Collectorate”
key_sections.description: Defines 'Collectorate' as the zillah or district to which a Collector is appointed, clarifying that lands outside these limits are not part of it even if revenue is paid there.

key_sections.title: Powers of an independent Deputy Collector
key_sections.description: Grants independent Deputy Collectors the same powers and jurisdictions as a Collector within their Deputy Collectorate.

key_sections.title: Definition of independent Deputy Collector and Deputy Collectorate
key_sections.description: Defines an independent Deputy Collector as an officer appointed by Government to act independently, and a Deputy Collectorate as the district where they act.

key_sections.title: Notice of sales by independent Deputy Collector
key_sections.description: Allows notices of sales by an independent Deputy Collector to be stuck up at their Cutcherry instead of the Collector's.

key_sections.title: Exercise of powers by independent Deputy Collector
key_sections.description: Permits an independent Deputy Collector to exercise assigned powers in public Cutcherry anywhere within their Deputy Collectorate.

key_sections.title: Location for sticking up notices at Zillah Court or local Adawlut
key_sections.description: Specifies that notices required at the Zillah Court or local Adawlut should be stuck up within the jurisdiction where the lands to be sold are primarily located.

key_sections.title: Validity of past orders, decisions, or sales
key_sections.description: Prevents disputing or invalidating orders, decisions, or sales made before this Act on the grounds of improper officer or district, unless proceedings to invalidate were already commenced.

key_sections.title: Extension of Act XXV. 1850 and Regulation VIII, 1819
key_sections.description: Extends Act XXV. 1850 and Section IX. Regulation VIII, 1819 of the Bengal Code (as modified) to all sales under Act VIII. 1835.

powers_conferred: Collector: To conduct sales, hear and decide summary suits.
Board (to which Collector is subordinate): To decide on Collector's jurisdiction.
Independent Deputy Collector: To exercise powers and jurisdictions of a Collector.

related_acts: Regulation VIII. 1831 of the Bengal Code
Regulation VII. 1832 of the Bengal Code
Regulation VIII.1819 of the Bengal Code
Regulation I. 1820 of the Bengal Code

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Government

applies_to: lands the subject of sale
summary suits for arrears of rent
sales of Putnee Talooks and other saleable tenures
sales of land in satisfaction of Summary Decrees for rent
special_provisions: If one Talook or tenure shall comprise lands situate in two or more Collectorates, or if any lands situate in two or more Collectorates be held under one lease or engagement or at one entire rent, the Collector, in whose Collectorate the greater part of such lands shall be situate, is the Collector to conduct the sale of such Talook, or tenure or of such lands, and to hear and decide any summary suit relating to arrears or exactions of rent in respect thereof.
Provisions for independent Deputy Collectors regarding their powers and the location of notices.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through Collectors and Deputy Collectors conducting sales and deciding summary suits for rent arrears.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Collectors of Land Revenue, Zillah Court or local Adawlut (for notices)

act_identification.act_title: An Act to facilitate the removal of Nuisances and Encroachments below High-water Mark in the Islands of Bombay and Colaba.
act_identification.act_short_title: THE SHORE NUISANCES (BOMBAY AND KOTABA) ACT, 1853

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Islands of Bombay and Colaba, and the Harbour of Bombay

act_overview.preamble: Whereas there is a large sea-shore in the Islands of Bombay and Colaba, and it is expedient, with a view to the safe Navigation of the Harbour of Bombay, and to the public interests generally, to facilitate the removal of nuisances, obstructions and enroachments below high-water mark in the said Harbour, or upon or about the shores of the said Islands; it is enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to facilitate the removal of nuisances, obstructions, and encroachments below high-water mark in the Harbour of Bombay and on the shores of the Islands of Bombay and Colaba. Its objective is to ensure safe navigation and protect public interests.

key_sections.title: Collector's Power to Require Removal of Nuisances
key_sections.description: Empowers the Collector of Land Revenue at Bombay to issue notice for the removal of nuisances, obstructions, or encroachments below high-water mark in Bombay Harbour or on the shores of Bombay and Colaba, specifying that if not removed within one month, the Collector will abate them.

key_sections.title: Petition to Supreme Court Against Collector's Action
key_sections.description: Allows any person denying the Collector's right to apply to the Supreme Court of Judicature at Bombay by petition within one month to restrain the Collector, with the Court having powers to hear, adjudicate, and issue interim orders.

key_sections.title: Onus of Proof on Petitioner
key_sections.description: States that the burden of proving the alleged right lies with the petitioner during the hearing of any such petition.

key_sections.title: Time Limit for Presenting Petition
key_sections.description: Prohibits the presentation of petitions after one month, unless the petitioner provides satisfactory reasons for the delay to the Court.

key_sections.title: Collector's Power to Abate After Petition Outcome
key_sections.description: Empowers the Collector to proceed with abatement or removal if no petition is presented within one month, or if the petition is dismissed or decided against the petitioner, and grants immunity to the Collector and authorized persons for unavoidable damage during removal.

key_sections.title: Sale of Materials and Application of Proceeds
key_sections.description: Grants the Collector the power to sell materials from removed encroachments or obstructions, apply the proceeds towards removal expenses, and directs that any surplus be forfeited and applied as the Governor of Bombay in Council directs.

key_sections.title: Saving of Rights of East India Company
key_sections.description: States that this Act does not prejudice the rights of the East India Company as trustees for the Crown, nor does it prevent other civil or criminal proceedings for nuisance abatement.

key_sections.title: Definition of 'High-Water Mark'
key_sections.description: Defines the term 'high-water mark' as the ordinary line of high-water at monsoon tides for the purpose of this Act.

powers_conferred: Collector of Land Revenue at Bombay to give notice requiring the removal of any nuisance, obstruction or encroachment
Collector to cause such abatement or removal
Collector to sell the materials of any encroachment or obstruction removed
Supreme Court of Judicature at Bombay to fix a time for hearing and adjudicating upon such petition, and given such directions, and make such orders as the said Court may think just

Supreme Court of Judicature at Bombay to make an order for restraining the alleged nuisance, obstruction or encroachment from being extended, or from being abated or removed by the said Collector, until after adjudication upon the said petition

applies_to: nuisances, obstructions and enroachments below high-water mark in the said Harbour of Bombay, or upon or about the shores of the said Islands
exemptions: rights of the East India Company as trustees for the Crown in any part of the said Harbour, or of the sea-shore of the said Islands
special_provisions: Islands of Bombay and Colaba
Harbour of Bombay

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Collector gives notice for removal; if not removed within one month, Collector abates or removes it. Persons denying the right can petition the Supreme Court. Collector can sell materials to cover costs.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Supreme Court of Judicature at Bombay

schedules_summary.description: Contains Form No. 1 (Notice by Collector for removal of encroachment) and Form No. 2 (Warrant by Collector to authorize removal of encroachment).

act_identification.act_title: THE BENGAL BONDED WAREHOUSE ASSOCIATION ACT, 1854

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend Act No. V. of 1838, relating to the Bengal Bonded Warehouse Association. Whereas the Bengal Bonded Warehouse Association are desirous that the provision of Act No. V. of 1838 should be amended, and it appears reasonable that such amendment should be made; It is enacted as follows:
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to amend specific provisions of Act No. V. of 1838 concerning the Bengal Bonded Warehouse Association. It aims to address the Association's desire for amendments to its operational framework and governance.

key_sections.title: Repeal of sections of Act 5 of 1838
key_sections.description: Repeals Sections XII, XIV, XXXII, and XXXVII of Act No. V. of 1838.

key_sections.title: Management by Directors
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the Association's business shall be managed by six Directors, with three forming a quorum.

key_sections.title: Directors' rotation and re-election
key_sections.description: Details the process for Directors going out of office by rotation in May, new elections at the General Meeting, and the re-eligibility of outgoing Directors.

key_sections.title: Qualification of Director
key_sections.description: Requires a Director to be a proprietor of at least five shares of the Capital Stock in his own right.

key_sections.title: Ordinary General Meetings and Dividends
key_sections.description: Mandates at least two Ordinary General Meetings annually (May and November), where Directors present reports and balance sheets, and dividends may be declared from profits, but not from capital.

key_sections.title: Power to make Bye-laws
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Association to make Bye-laws for its proceedings, binding on members and officers, subject to approval by an extraordinary General Meeting and confirmation by the Governor of Fort William in Bengal.

key_sections.title: Dissolution of Corporation
key_sections.description: Grants the Governor General of India in Council the power to order the dissolution of the Association after 14th March 1860, with dissolution taking effect five years from the date of such order.

powers_conferred: Power to the Association to make Bye-laws for its regulation (Section VI)
Power to the General Meeting of proprietors to declare a dividend out of profits (Section V)
Power to the Governor General of India in Council to direct the dissolution of the Association (Section VII)

repealed_acts: Sections XII, XIV, XXXII, and XXXVII of Act No. V. of 1838

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Directors are chosen by the ordinary General Meeting of proprietors (Section III).
regulatory_bodies: Governor of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal (for confirming Bye-laws)
Governor General of India in Council (for ordering dissolution)

applies_to: The Bengal Bonded Warehouse Association
Proprietors of the Bengal Bonded Warehouse Association
Directors of the Bengal Bonded Warehouse Association
Members and Officers of the Bengal Bonded Warehouse Association

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Bengal Bonded Warehouse Association (for Bye-laws)

act_identification.act_title: THE POLICE, AGRA ACT, 1854

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of the Provinces of Benares, North-Western Provinces

act_overview.preamble:
Whereas the provisions of Section III. and Section VII. of Regulation XI. 1831, have been found
inconvenient, and whereas it is expedient that Regulation XI. 1831, as amended by this Act, should be
extended to the whole of the Provinces of Benares ; It is enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act amends Regulation XI. of 1831 of the Bengal Code by repealing certain sections and extending its provisions, as amended, to the Provinces of Benares. It also clarifies the subordination of Darogahs of Police to Tehseeldars in certain jurisdictions.

key_sections.title: Sections III. and VII., Regulation XI. 1831, repealed.
key_sections.description: Repeals Section III and Section VII of Regulation XI. 1831 of the Bengal Code.

key_sections.title: Darogahs of Police to be subject to Tehseeldars.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that Darogahs of Police appointed within the local limits of a Tehseeldar's police jurisdiction shall be subordinate to and controlled by that Tehseeldar.

key_sections.title: Regulation XI. 1831, as amended, extended to Benares.
key_sections.description: Extends Regulation XI. 1831, as amended by this Act, to the whole of the Province of Benares and allows the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces to exercise powers vested in the Governor General in Council by the said Regulation.

powers_conferred: Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces may exercise all powers vested by Regulation XI. 1831 in the Governor General in Council.

amended_acts: Regulation XI. of 1831 of the Bengal Code
repealed_acts: Regulation XI. 1831 of the Bengal Code (Sections III and VII)

applies_to: Darogah of Police
Tehseeldar
Provinces of Benares
North-Western Provinces
special_provisions: All powers vested by Regulation XI. 1831 in the Governor General in Council, may be exercised by the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces.

act_identification.act_title: THE LEGAL REPRESENTATIVES’ SUITS ACT, 1855

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India, except Part BStates and the Scheduled Districts

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to enable executors, administrators or representatives in certain cases to sue and be sued in respect of certain wrongs which, according to the present law, do not survive to or against such executors, administrators or representatives; It is enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To enable executors, administrators or representatives to sue and be sued for certain wrongs committed in the lifetime of a deceased person, which occasioned pecuniary loss to their estate or for which the deceased would have been subject to an action.

key_sections.title: Executors may sue and be sued in certain cases for wrongs committed in lifetime of deceased.
key_sections.description: Allows actions by executors, administrators, or representatives for wrongs committed in the deceased's lifetime that occasioned pecuniary loss to the estate, provided the wrong was committed within one year before death. Also allows actions against executors, administrators, heirs, or representatives for wrongs committed by the deceased in their lifetime, provided the wrong was committed within one year before death.

key_sections.title: Death of either party not to abate suit. Proviso.
key_sections.description: Ensures that actions commenced under this Act do not abate due to the death of either party and can be continued by or against their representatives. Includes a proviso allowing executors, administrators, or representatives to set up a want of assets as a defence.

powers_conferred: Power to maintain an action by executors, administrators or representatives of any person deceased for wrongs committed in the time of such person.
Power to maintain an action against the executors or administrators or heirs or representatives of any person deceased for wrongs committed by him in his lifetime.

related_acts: Civil Procedure Act, 1833 (3 and 4 Will. 4, c. 42)

applies_to: executors
administrators
representatives of any person deceased
special_provisions: Section 1 of the Act was renumbered as section 1A and a new section 1 (Short title and extent) was inserted for the State of Karnataka by Karnataka 33 of 1978, s. 4, extending the Act to the whole of the State of Karnataka.
The Act came into force in the State of Sikkim on 01/09/1984.
Extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963.
Extended to the Union Territory of Pondicherry by Act 26 of 1968.
Declared in force in the Khondmals District by the Khondmals Laws Regulation, 1936.
Declared in force in the Angul District by the Angul Laws Regulation, 1936.
Declared in force in the Sonthal Parganas by the Sonthal Parganas Settlement Regulation, 1872.
Declared in force in various Scheduled Districts under the Scheduled Districts Act, 1874.
Extended to the New Provinces and Merged States by Act 59 of 1949.
Extended to the States of Tripura, Manipur and Vindhya Pradesh by Act 30 of 1950.

act_identification.act_title: THE FATAL ACCIDENTS ACT, 1855

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS no action or suit is now maintainable in any Court against a person who, by his wrongful act, neglect or default, may have caused the death of another person, and it is often-times right and expedient that the wrong-doer in such case should be answerable in damages for the injury so caused by him. It is enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To provide compensation to families for loss occasioned by the death of a person caused by actionable wrong, addressing the previous lack of legal recourse against wrongdoers in such cases.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical extent.

key_sections.title: Suit for compensation to the family of a person for loss occasioned to it by his death by actionable wrong.
key_sections.description: Establishes the right to sue for compensation for loss to family due to death caused by wrongful act, neglect, or default.

key_sections.title: Not more than one suit to be brought. Claim for loss to estate may be added.
key_sections.description: Limits the number of suits for the same subject-matter and allows claims for pecuniary loss to the deceased's estate to be added.

key_sections.title: Plaintiff shall deliver particulars, etc.
key_sections.description: Requires the plaintiff to provide full particulars of the beneficiaries and the nature of the claim in any suit.

key_sections.title: Interpretation clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms such as 'person', 'parent', and 'child' for the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: the Court may give such damages as it may think proportioned to the loss resulting from such death

applies_to: the family of a person whose death shall have been so caused (wife, husband, parent and child)
executor, administrator or representative of the person deceased
special_provisions: The Act has been extended to Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands by Reg. 8 of 1965, s. 3 and Sch.
The Act has been extended to the Union territory of Pondicherry by Act 26 of 1968, s. 3 and Sch.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through an action or suit for damages in Court.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: any Court

act_identification.act_title: THE BENGAL EMBANKMENT ACT, 1855

legislative_details.enacted_by: Governor General of India in Council
legislative_details.geographical_extent: Territories under the Government of the Lieutenant-Governor of Bengal

act_overview.preamble: Preamble. - Whereas the Regulations now in force for the maintenance embankments in the Territories under the Government of the Lieutenant-Governor of Bengal, have been found ineffectual for the intended purposes thereof, and whereas it is desirable that provision should be made for the better supervision and protection of the same it is enacted as follows:
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the better supervision and protection of embankments in the territories under the Government of the Lieutenant-Governor of Bengal. It aims to address the ineffectiveness of previous regulations concerning embankment maintenance.

key_sections.title: Regulations Repealed.
key_sections.description: Repeals Regulation VI of 1806 and Regulation XI of 1829 in the specified territories, with exceptions for prior acts, offences, and liabilities.

key_sections.title: What is a public embankment within this Act.
key_sections.description: Defines 'embankment' as for excluding or retaining water, and 'public embankment' as any maintained by Government officers at public or private expense.

key_sections.title: Who to have superintendence of public embankments.
key_sections.description: Establishes the position of Superintendent of Embankments to oversee public embankments under general Government orders.

key_sections.title: Superintendent may take charge of any embankment which connecting public embankments, &c.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to the Superintendent to take charge of, remove, change the line of, or enlarge embankments for public protection or drainage.

key_sections.title: Before taking charge of private embankments, &c. Superintendent to give notice to Collector, who shall issue a proclamation.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for the Superintendent to notify the Collector before executing works, including public proclamation, hearing objections, and appeal process.

key_sections.title: Compensation for damages sustained under this Act.
key_sections.description: Provides for compensation claims for damages from embankment works, to be settled by arbitration if admitted, and outlines the arbitration process.

key_sections.title: Penalty for obstructing officer or person in discharge of duty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for wilfully obstructing officers in removing or levelling embankments or buildings.

key_sections.title: Penalty for wilful damage to embankment by cutting, etc.
key_sections.description: Sets penalties for wilfully cutting, destroying, or opening sluices in embankments without authority.

key_sections.title: Penalty for other wilful damage.
key_sections.description: Defines penalties for various other acts causing wilful damage to public embankments, such as making dams, altering banks, or grazing cattle.

key_sections.title: Interpretation.
key_sections.description: Provides interpretation rules for singular/plural, masculine gender, and defines 'Collector'.

powers_conferred: Superintendent of Embankments: to take charge of embankments, remove private embankments, change line of public embankments, make new embankments, enlarge public embankments, pass orders regarding works and applications for sluices.

Collector: to issue proclamations, hear objections, enforce attendance of arbitrators, conduct arbitration, summon witnesses, levy expenses as arrears of Government revenue, value and make compensation for huts, trees, or crops, remove buildings.
Magistrate: to punish offenders for various offences under the Act.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties include imprisonment (simple or with labour) for terms ranging from not exceeding six months to not exceeding seven years, and/or fines not exceeding two hundred rupees, depending on the severity of the offence. Offences include obstructing officers, wilfully cutting or destroying embankments, opening sluices without authority, and other acts causing wilful damage to embankments.

repealed_acts: Regulation VI. of 1806
Regulation XI. of 1829
related_acts: Acts of the Governor General of India in Council

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Collector and claimant each appoint an arbitrator for compensation disputes. The Collector may appoint a third arbitrator if others neglect to do so.

applies_to: Territories under the Government of the Lieutenant-Governor of Bengal
Any person bound to keep up an embankment
Land-holders, farmers, or cultivators desiring sluices
exemptions: Provisions of Section VII do not apply to cases of compensation for huts, trees, or crops.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Collector is responsible for levying expenses as arrears of Government revenue. Magistrates enforce penalties for offences. Darogahs and other Police Officers are empowered to inquire into offences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil Court, Magistrate, Sessions Court

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN BILLS OF LADING ACT, 1856
act_identification.act_short_title: THE INDIAN BILLS OF LADING ACT, 1856

legislative_details.geographical_extent: in force in the whole of India except Part B States and the Scheduled Districts, by the Laws Local Extent Act, 1874 (15 of 1874), s. 3.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS by the custom of merchants a bill of lading of goods being transferable by endorsement, the property in the goods may thereby pass to the endorsee, but nevertheless all rights in respect of the contract contained in the bill of lading continue in the original shipper or owner, and it is expedient that such rights should pass with the property; and whereas it frequently happens that the goods in respect of which bills of lading purport to be signed have not been laden on board, and it is proper that such bills of lading in the hands of a bona fide holder for value should not be questioned by the master or other person signing the same, on the ground of the goods not having been laden as aforesaid: It is enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To amend the law relating to bills of lading, ensuring that rights associated with the contract pass with the property upon endorsement, and to make bills of lading conclusive evidence of shipment in the hands of bona fide holders.

key_sections.title: Rights under bills of lading to vest in consignee or endorsee.
key_sections.description: States that consignees or endorsees of a bill of lading, to whom property in goods passes, acquire all rights of suit and are subject to the same liabilities as if the contract was made with them.

key_sections.title: Not to affect right of stoppage in transitu or claims for freight.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not prejudice the right of stoppage in transit or claims for freight against the original shipper or owner, nor the liability of the consignee or endorsee.

key_sections.title: Bill of lading in hands of consignee, etc., conclusive evidence of the shipment as against master, etc.
key_sections.description: Declares that a bill of lading in the hands of a consignee or endorsee for valuable consideration is conclusive evidence of shipment against the master or signer, unless the holder had actual notice that goods were not shipped, or the misrepresentation was due to fraud of the shipper/holder without default of the signer.

related_acts: Bills of Lading Act, 1855 (18 and 19 Vict., c. 111)

applies_to: Every consignee of goods named in a bill of lading
Every endorsee of a bill of lading to whom the property in the goods therein mentioned shall pass
master or other person signing
special_provisions: Extended to former Part B States by Act 18 of 1949, s. 4.
Extended to Union territory of Pondicherry by Act 26 of 1968, s. 3 and Sch.

Declared to be in force in the following Scheduled Districts: West Jalpaiguri; The Districts of Hazaribagh, Lohardaga (now the Ranchi district), and Manbhum, and Pargana Dhalbhum and the Kolhan in the District of Singhbhum; Assam (except the North Lushai Hills).

act_identification.act_title: AN ACT relating to the administration of the Public Revenues in the Town of Calcutta.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Town of Calcutta, City of Calcutta, Presidency of Fort William in Bengal

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient that the Collector of Calcutta should have charge of the collection of the Stamp Duty within the town of Calcutta, and that he should have power to employ any Deputy Collector subordinate to him, in the performance of any art of the duties of his office: — It is enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to assign the responsibility for collecting Stamp Duty within the town of Calcutta to the Collector of Calcutta. It also grants the Collector the authority to delegate any part of his duties to a subordinate Deputy Collector.

key_sections.title: Regulations modified
key_sections.description: Declares that certain parts of Section VI, Regulation XII, 1826 of the Bengal Code, and Section VI of a Rule Ordinance and Regulation for the Town of Calcutta (1827), which prescribe the special appointment of a Civil Servant for Stamp Duty collection in Calcutta, are subject to modification.

key_sections.title: Collection of Stamp Duty in Calcutta to be ordinarily in charge of the Collector
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the collection of Stamp Duty within the Town of Calcutta shall ordinarily be under the charge of the Collector of Calcutta, unless the Lieutenant Governor of Bengal directs otherwise.

key_sections.title: Collector may entrust any part of his duties to his Deputy
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Collector of Calcutta to employ any subordinate Deputy Collector to perform any part of his official duties under this Act, Regulation XII of 1826, Act XI of 1849, or Act XXIII of 1850, extending the force of Deputy Collector rules to the Town of Calcutta.

powers_conferred: Collector of Calcutta: To employ any Deputy Collector subordinate to him in the performance of any part of the duties of his office.
Lieutenant Governor of Bengal: To direct otherwise regarding the charge of the collection of the Stamp Duty within the Town of Calcutta.

amended_acts: Section VI, Regulation XII, 1826 of the Bengal Code
Section VI of a Rule Ordinance and Regulation for the Town of Calcutta, made and passed on the 14th day of June 1827

applies_to: Collector of Calcutta
Deputy Collectors subordinate to the Collector of Calcutta
Collection of Stamp Duty within the Town of Calcutta
special_provisions: Applicable within the Town of Calcutta.

Rules, Regulations, and Acts relating to the office of Deputy Collector shall be of the same force within the Town of Calcutta as in other parts of the territories subject to the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal.

act_identification.act_title: THE TOBACCO DUTY (TOWN OF BOMBAY) ACT, 1857.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Town of Bombay (including all places within the Islands of Bombay and Colaba)

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to amend the Law relating to the duties payable on Tobacco and the retail sale and warehousing of that article in the Town of Bombay: It is hereby Preamble. enacted as follows : —
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to amend the existing law concerning the duties levied on Tobacco. It also regulates the retail sale and warehousing of Tobacco within the Town of Bombay.

key_sections.title: Laws Repealed.
key_sections.description: Repeals specific chapters of Regulation XXI. 1827 of the Bombay Code and Act XXIV of 1850.

key_sections.title: Municipal Duty on Tobacco intended for consumption in Bombay.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Municipal Duty of seven Rupees and eight annas per maund on Tobacco imported into Bombay for consumption, in addition to Customs Duty.

key_sections.title: Duty if not paid on importation, to be paid on removal from warehouse for consumption. Remission of Municipal Duty on re-exportation.
key_sections.description: Specifies that if Municipal Duty is not paid on importation, Tobacco must be warehoused, and duty paid upon removal for consumption. Duty is remitted on re-exportation.

key_sections.title: Tobacco not to be imported otherwise than by Sea. Landing places to be prescribed.
key_sections.description: Prohibits importing Tobacco into Bombay other than by sea, or landing it at unprescribed places, without permission.

key_sections.title: Permit necessary for removal of Tobacco. Proviso.
key_sections.description: Requires a permit from the Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium for removing Tobacco within the Town or carrying it on thoroughfares/vessels, with exceptions for small quantities for personal use.

key_sections.title: License for retail sale of Tobacco.
key_sections.description: Mandates a license from the Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium for retail sale of Tobacco in the Town, valid for twelve months.

key_sections.title: Monthly returns of stock to be made by retail dealers.
key_sections.description: Requires retail dealers to submit monthly returns of Tobacco stock, with penalties for non-compliance or false returns.

key_sections.title: Confiscation of Tobacco illegally imported, removed, &c. Mitigation of penalty.
key_sections.description: Stipulates confiscation of Tobacco, vessels, vehicles, or animals involved in illegal importation, removal, or possession, with provision for mitigation of penalty.

key_sections.title: Penalty for illegal importation, removal, sale, or possession. Revocation of license.
key_sections.description: Prescribes a fine for illegal importation, removal, sale, or possession of Tobacco, and license revocation for licensed dealers.

key_sections.title: Levy of fines, adjudication, and sale of confiscations.
key_sections.description: Empowers any Magistrate of Police for the Town of Bombay to adjudicate and levy fines and confiscations, with goods sold under warrant.

powers_conferred: Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium, and Officers of Customs: for collecting and enforcing payment of Municipal Duty (Section VI).
Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium, or other Officer empowered by Government: to grant permission for importing Tobacco otherwise than by sea or landing at unprescribed places (Section VII).
Government of Bombay: to prescribe landing places for Tobacco (Section VII).
Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium: to grant Permits for removal of Tobacco (Section IX).
Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium: to give permission to open bales/packages of Tobacco in warehouse (Section X).
Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium, or other Officer duly empowered by Government: to grant licenses for retail sale of Tobacco (Section XI).
Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium, or other Officers: to deprive retail dealers of their license (Section XIV, XV).
Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium, or other Officer: to issue search-warrants (Section XVI).

Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium, or other Officer, or any public Officer authorized by them: to arrest and detain persons and search vessels/vehicles carrying Tobacco liable to confiscation (Section XVII).
Adjudicating Officer: to mitigate the penalty of confiscation (Section XVIII).
Magistrate of Police for the Town of Bombay: to adjudicate and levy all confiscations and fines (Section XX).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Retail dealers refusing or neglecting to make monthly returns, or making false returns, are liable to deprivation of license and a fine not exceeding two hundred Rupees (Section XIV). Retail dealers neglecting or refusing to comply with book entry provisions are liable to deprivation of license and a fine not exceeding two hundred Rupees (Section XV). Any person illegally importing, removing, or selling Tobacco, or knowingly possessing Tobacco subject to confiscation, is liable to a fine not exceeding ten times the value of such Tobacco; if a licensed retail dealer, their license may be revoked (Section XIX). Tobacco illegally imported, removed, or kept, and associated conveyances, are liable to confiscation (Section XVIII).

repealed_acts: Chapters V, VI, VII and VIII of Regulation XXI. 1827 of the Bombay Code
Act XXIV of 1850

regulatory_bodies: Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium

applies_to: All Tobacco imported into the Town of Bombay and intended for consumption therein
Persons selling or offering for sale by retail any Tobacco in the Town of Bombay
exemptions: Small quantities of Tobacco (not exceeding four seers) intended for the private consumption of the importer (Section VIII).
Small quantities of Tobacco (not exceeding four seers) for personal or domestic use, when conveyed without a Permit (Section IX).
special_provisions: Applicable specifically to the Town of Bombay, which includes all places within the Islands of Bombay and Colaba.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Government of Bombay (for prescribing landing places)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out by the Commissioner of Customs, Salt, and Opium, and Officers of Customs, through collection of duties, issuance of permits and licenses, search-warrants, arrest and detention, and confiscation of illegally handled goods. Fines and confiscations are adjudicated and levied by Magistrates of Police.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate of Police for the Town of Bombay

schedules_summary.description: Contains the Form of Permit for the removal of Tobacco.

act_identification.act_title: THE BENGAL GHATWALI LANDS ACT, 1859

act_overview.preamble: Preamble.—WHEREAS it has been held that the Ghatwals of the District of Beerbhoom who pay the revenue of their lands directly to Government under the provisions of Regulation XXIX. 1814 of the Bengal Code have not the power of alienating their lands; and whereas, for the development of the mineral resources of the country in which the said Ghatwalee lands are situate, and for the improvement of the said lands, it is expedient that the power of granting leases for periods not limited by the term of their own possession, should in certain cases be extended to the possessors of such lands; It is enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to empower Ghatwals in the District of Beerbhoom to grant leases for their lands, extending beyond their own possession. This is intended to facilitate the development of mineral resources and general improvement of these lands, addressing a previous limitation on their alienation powers.

key_sections.title: Ghatwals of Beerbhoom to have the same right of granting leases as is allowed to other proprietors of lands.
key_sections.description: Grants Ghatwals in Beerbhoom the power to lease lands for improvement, similar to other proprietors. Leases extending beyond the grantor's lifetime require Commissioner approval and must be for specific development purposes like mining, clearing jungle, or construction.

key_sections.title: Court of Wards and Revenue authorities to have the like power in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Court of Wards or the Commissioner to grant leases for Ghatwalee lands under their superintendence, making such leases valid and binding on future possessors.

powers_conferred: Ghatwals of Beerbhoom: Power to grant leases for any period conducive to the improvement of their tenures, subject to conditions for leases extending beyond their incumbency.
Commissioner of the Division: Power to approve leases of Ghatwalee lands extending beyond the grantor's lifetime or incumbency for specific development purposes.
Court of Wards or Commissioner: Power to grant leases for Ghatwalee lands under their superintendence or direct control of Government Officers.

related_acts: Regulation XXIX. 1814 of the Bengal Code

applies_to: Ghatwals holding lands in the District of Beerbhoom
special_provisions: District of Beerbhoom

act_identification.act_title: THE BENGAL LAND REVENUE SALES ACT, 1859

legislative_details.geographical_extent: such parts of the Lower Provinces in the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal as are or shall be subject to the general Regulations of that Presidency

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to discontinue the practice of obtaining the previous sanction of the Board of Revenue to sales of estates for arrears of revenue, or other demands of Government, in the province of Cuttack: and whereas it is just that a person having a lien upon an estate, and paying the money necessary to protect it from sale for arrears of revenue, should be reasonably secured: and whereas it is expedient to afford sharers in estates, who duly pay their shares of the Sudder jumma of their estates, easy means of protecting their shares from sale by reason of the default of their co-sharers: and whereas it is expedient to afford landholders, particularly absentees, facilities in guarding against the accidental sale of their estates for arrears of revenue by reason of the neglect or fraud of their agents: and whereas it is expedient to provide for the voluntary registration of dependent talooks existing at the time of settlement: and whereas it is expedient to protect the holders of registered under-tenures created since the settlement, and not resumable by the grantors or their representatives, from loss by the avoidance of their tenures on the occasion of a sale of the superior estate for arrears of public revenue, when the arrears can be realized by such sale: and to give absolute security to such tenures by special registry, when shown to be held at rents sufficient for the security of the revenue : and it is therefore proper for the above and other purposes, to improve the law relating to sales of land for arrears of revenue in the Provinces of Bengal, Behar and Orissa: It is enacted as follows :—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to improve the law relating to sales of land for arrears of revenue. It seeks to protect various stakeholders like lien holders, co-sharers, and landholders from arbitrary sales, and provides for the registration of certain tenures to secure them against such sales. The Act also streamlines the process of revenue collection and sales in the Lower Provinces under the Bengal Presidency.

key_sections.title: Laws repealed.
key_sections.description: Repeals Regulation X. 1818 and Act I of 1845, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: What is an arrear of revenue.
key_sections.description: Defines what constitutes an arrear of revenue based on unpaid kist or instalment.

key_sections.title: Latest day of payment.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Board of Revenue to determine payment dates for arrears and demands, and mandates public notification of these dates.

key_sections.title: Notifications of sale to be issued, and no tender after latest day of payment to stop the sale.
key_sections.description: Requires the Collector to issue sale notifications after the latest payment day and states that no late payment will stop the sale.

key_sections.title: Deposits receivable from persons not proprietors.
key_sections.description: Allows non-proprietors to deposit arrears to protect an estate from sale and outlines their rights to recover the amount.

key_sections.title: Separation of shares held in common, by the opening of a separate account.
key_sections.description: Provides a mechanism for recorded sharers of joint estates to pay their revenue shares separately by opening a separate account with the Collector.

key_sections.title: Sale of separate shares.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that if separate accounts are kept, only the share in arrear will be sold, while the excluded shares continue to form one integral estate.

key_sections.title: Deposit for the protection of an estate from sale.
key_sections.description: Allows proprietors to deposit money or government securities as security to protect their estate from sale for arrears.

key_sections.title: Estates under Court of Wards or under attachment.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which estates under the Court of Wards or attachment are exempt from sale for arrears.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Grants the Commissioner of Revenue the power to receive appeals against sales and annul them if not conducted according to the Act.

key_sections.title: Certificate of sales.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Collector to issue a certificate of title to the purchaser once a sale becomes final and conclusive.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of Civil Courts in suits to annul sales.
key_sections.description: Limits the grounds on which Civil Courts can annul sales and sets a one-year limitation period for such suits.

key_sections.title: Rights of a purchaser of a permanently settled estate sold for its own arrears.
key_sections.description: Defines the rights of a purchaser of a permanently settled estate, including the ability to avoid under-tenures, with specific exceptions.

key_sections.title: Common and special registry.
key_sections.description: Establishes two types of registers for tenures and farms, common and special, each offering different levels of security against auction purchasers.

key_sections.title: Rights of a purchaser of an estate not permanently settled sold for its own arrears.
key_sections.description: Outlines the rights of a purchaser of an estate not permanently settled, including the ability to avoid tenures originating with the defaulter, with specific exceptions.

key_sections.title: Punishment for contempt.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Collector to punish contempt committed in their presence with a fine or imprisonment.

powers_conferred: Collector or other Officer: Issue notifications, hold sales, receive deposits, open separate accounts, refer parties to Civil Court, exempt estates from sale, adjourn sales, give certificates of title, order delivery of possession, apply purchase money, notify annulment of sale, punish contempt, purchase for Government, demand fees.
Board of Revenue: Determine payment dates, prescribe place for holding sales, recommend to local Government to annul sale, revise Commissioner's order for special registry.
Commissioner of Revenue: Exempt estates from sale, receive appeals, annul sales, suspend passing of final orders and represent to Board, direct registration, revise orders.
Local Government: Annul sales, issue general instructions to Revenue Authorities, revise Commissioner's order for special registry.
Civil Court: Order temporary possession, determine interest on deposit, determine question at issue, pass final decree for annulment, pass decree pronouncing registration obtained by fraud.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Punishment for contempt (fine not exceeding two hundred Rupees, commutable to imprisonment not exceeding one month). Default in making deposit to be considered a contempt. Defaulting purchaser liable for the difference if the re-sale proceeds are less than the original bid.

repealed_acts: Regulation X. 1818
Act I of 1845

applies_to: proprietors
sharers
landholders
holders of registered under-tenures
exemptions: Estates under the management of the Court of Wards for arrears accrued during that period.
Estates solely owned by minors (until age 18) for arrears accruing after their succession, if duly notified to the Collector.
Estates held under attachment by revenue authorities (not by judicial order) for arrears accruing while under attachment.
Estates held under attachment or managed by a Revenue Officer (by judicial order) for arrears accruing during such period, until after the end of the year in which arrears accrued.
special_provisions: In the district of Sylhet, the Collector may distrain and sell personal property of defaulters first.
The Act's operation is confined to parts of the Lower Provinces in the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal subject to general Regulations.
Specific rights for purchasers of permanently settled estates in Bengal, Behar, and Orissa.
Specific rights for purchasers of estates not permanently settled.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Board of Revenue (for payment dates, sale places); Local Government (for general instructions to subordinate Revenue Authorities).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Public auction of estates for arrears of revenue, issuance of notifications, acceptance of deposits, re-sales, issuance of certificates of sale, delivery of possession, application of purchase money, appeals to Commissioner of Revenue, annulment of sales by Commissioner or Government, jurisdiction of Civil Courts for specific matters, and punishment for contempt.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil Courts, Judge's Court, Moonsiffs' Courts, Magistrate.

schedules_summary.description: Prescribes the format for the certificate of title issued to the purchaser of a mehal or share of a mehal under the Act, including specification details.

Lists the fees demandable by the Collector for various applications under the Act, such as for opening separate accounts, deposits, withdrawals, and registration of under-tenures or farms, based on annual jumma or rent.

act_identification.act_title: THE MADRAS DISTRICT POLICE ACT, 1859

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Territories subject to the Presidency of Fort St. George; Madras Presidency; General Police District

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to make the Police Force throughout the Madras Presidency a more efficient instrument at the disposal of the Magistrate for the prevention and detection of crime, and to re-organize the Police Force and improve the condition of the Village Police: it is enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: To make the Police Force throughout the Madras Presidency a more efficient instrument for the prevention and detection of crime. It also aims to re-organize the Police Force and improve the condition of the Village Police.

key_sections.title: Interpretation.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Laws repealed.
key_sections.description: Details the previous laws and regulations that are repealed or amended by this Act.

key_sections.title: Superintendence vested in Governor in Council.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Governor in Council as the supreme authority for police superintendence.

key_sections.title: Inspector-General of Police, &c.
key_sections.description: Vests police administration in an Inspector-General and Subordinates appointed by the Governor in Council.

key_sections.title: Inspector-General to be appointed a Justice of the Peace. To have the powers of a Magistrate but to exercise such powers under the orders of Government. District Superintendent may be appointed a Magistrate. In what cases he may act in that capacity.
key_sections.description: Confers powers of a Justice of the Peace and Magistrate on the Inspector-General and potentially District Superintendents.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Force.
key_sections.description: Declares the entire Madras Presidency Police establishment as one force and outlines its constitution.

key_sections.title: Inspector-General to control Force and make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Inspector-General to frame rules for the general government and distribution of the Police Force.

key_sections.title: Appointment and dismissal of Police Officers.
key_sections.description: Outlines the authority for appointing and dismissing Police Officers.

key_sections.title: Duties of Police Officers.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the general duties of Police Officers, including crime prevention, apprehension, and intelligence gathering.

key_sections.title: Police Officer may arrest without warrant.
key_sections.description: Specifies circumstances under which a Police Officer can make an arrest without a warrant.

key_sections.title: Penalties for neglect of duty &c.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for Police Officers for various forms of misconduct or neglect of duty.

key_sections.title: Certain duties of Police Officers within the limits of Towns. Obstructions and nuisances in roads.
key_sections.description: Details specific duties of Police Officers regarding public order and nuisances in urban areas.

key_sections.title: Operation of Act.
key_sections.description: States that the Act will take effect in districts notified by the Governor in Council.

powers_conferred: Governor in Council: Superintendence of police; appointment and removal of Inspector-General and Subordinates; sanctioning rules for appointment and dismissal; directing employment of additional police force; passing orders for maintenance of General Police Fund; directing investment of Police Superannuation Fund; extending operation of the Act.

Inspector-General of Police: Administration of police; acting as a Justice of the Peace; exercising powers of a Magistrate; controlling the Police Force and making rules; appointing and dismissing Police Officers; deputing additional Police Officers; directing employment of additional force.
District Superintendent: Appointing and dismissing Police Officers; deputing additional Police Officers; exercising powers of a Magistrate (if vested by Governor in Council).

Police Officers: Exercising powers of a Police Officer throughout the General Police District; arresting without warrant; taking recognizance for appearance of prosecutor or witness; entering and inspecting certain premises without warrant; inspecting weights and measures; laying informations before Magistrate; executing summonses, warrants, and other processes; requiring assistance for arrest.
Magistrate: Appointing special Police Officers; remanding accused persons; issuing summonses and warrants.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties are prescribed for: refusal to serve as special Police Officer or obey orders (fine not exceeding fifty Rupees); unlawful assumption of Police functions, personation, not delivering up certificate/accoutrements (penalty not exceeding two hundred Rupees, or imprisonment not exceeding six months, or both); refusal to assist Police Officer (fine not exceeding fifty Rupees, or imprisonment not exceeding three months, or both); neglect of duty, wilful breach of orders, unauthorized employment, false charge, exceeding powers, neglect to bring person before Magistrate, unwarrantable violence (penalty not exceeding three months' pay, or imprisonment not exceeding three months, or both); receiving unauthorized fees (penalty not exceeding six months' pay, or imprisonment not exceeding six months, or both); extortion, bribery, cowardice (fine not exceeding twelve months' pay, or imprisonment not exceeding twelve months, or both); assaulting/resisting Police Officer, aiding/inciting, false charge against Police Officer (fine not exceeding fifty rupees, or imprisonment not exceeding three months, or both); various offences in streets/roads (e.g., slaughtering cattle, cruelty to animals, obstructing passengers, throwing dirt, public drunkenness, indecent exposure, neglect to protect dangerous places) (fine not exceeding fifty Rupees, or imprisonment not exceeding eight days); opposing/not obeying orders for public processions, music, or violating license conditions (fine not exceeding one hundred Rupees).

repealed_acts: Regulation IX. 1816
Regulation XI. 1816
Regulation IV. 1821
Regulation VI. 1831
Act VII of 1843

authorities_established: Inspector-General of Police for the Presidency of Madras
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Governor in Council appoints Inspector-General and Subordinates. Inspector-General of Police and Deputy Superintendents appoint Police Officers.

applies_to: Police Force throughout the Madras Presidency
Territories subject to the Presidency of Fort St. George
General Police District
exemptions: Supreme Court (for warrant execution)
special_provisions: Charges against Police Officers above the rank of a Private shall only be adjudicated on by European functionaries.
Village Watchers alone shall be liable to conviction by Heads of Villages.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Inspector-General (subject to approval of Governor in Council); Governor in Council (for appointment/dismissal rules and superannuation fund rules).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced by Police Officers through arrest, investigation, and execution of warrants. Magistrates handle convictions, fines, imprisonment, and remands. Fines and penalties are recoverable by distress and sale of goods.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate; any competent Court (for recovery of money).

schedules_summary.description: Lists laws repealed and laws amended by this Act, and includes Form A for the certificate of appointment for a Police Officer.

act_identification.act_title: THE SOCIETIES REGISTRATION ACT, 1860

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India, except the Scheduled Districts. Extended to New Provinces and Merged States, Goa, Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Lakshadweep, and the Union territory of Ladakh. Subject to various State Amendments.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient that provision should be made for improving the legal condition of societies established for the promotion of literature, science, or the fine arts, or for the diffusion of useful knowledge, [2][the diffusion of political education] or for charitable purposes; It is enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to improve the legal condition of societies established for the promotion of literature, science, fine arts, diffusion of useful knowledge, political education, or charitable purposes by providing a framework for their registration and regulation.

key_sections.title: Societies formed by memorandum of association and registration.
key_sections.description: Allows seven or more persons to form a society for literary, scientific, or charitable purposes by subscribing to a memorandum of association and filing it with the Registrar.

key_sections.title: Memorandum of association.
key_sections.description: Specifies the contents of the memorandum of association, including the society's name, objects, and details of the governing body, along with filing rules and regulations.

key_sections.title: Registration and fees.
key_sections.description: Requires the Registrar to certify the registration of a society upon filing the memorandum and certified copy, and specifies the fee payable for registration.

key_sections.title: Annual list of managing body to be filed.
key_sections.description: Mandates the annual filing of a list containing names, addresses, and occupations of the governing body members with the Registrar.

key_sections.title: Property of society how vested.
key_sections.description: States that the property of a registered society, if not vested in trustees, is deemed vested in its governing body for legal proceedings.

key_sections.title: Suits by and against societies.
key_sections.description: Allows societies to sue or be sued in the name of their president, chairman, principal secretary, or trustees, as determined by their rules.

key_sections.title: Societies enabled to alter, extend or abridge their purposes.
key_sections.description: Permits the governing body to alter, extend, or abridge the society's purposes or amalgamate with another society, subject to member approval.

key_sections.title: Provision for dissolution of societies and adjustment of their affairs.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for dissolution of a society by three-fifths of its members and the adjustment of its affairs, with provisions for dispute resolution by the principal Court.

key_sections.title: Upon a dissolution no member to receive profit.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that upon dissolution, any remaining property after satisfying debts shall not be distributed among members but given to another society, with an exception for Joint-stock Companies.

key_sections.title: To what societies Act applies.
key_sections.description: Lists the types of societies that may be registered under the Act, including charitable, literary, scientific, fine arts, and those for diffusion of knowledge or maintenance of libraries/museums.

key_sections.title: Maintenance of accounts and their balancing and auditing.
key_sections.description: Requires governing bodies to keep regular, audited accounts in a prescribed form, balanced annually.

key_sections.title: Registrar's power to cancel registration in certain circumstances.
key_sections.description: Grants the Registrar power to cancel registration on grounds such as contravention of law, subversive activities, fraud, or unlawful activities, after providing an opportunity to be heard.

key_sections.title: Investigations of affairs of society.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Registrar to inspect or investigate the affairs of a society if there is apprehension of mismanagement, breach of fiduciary obligations, or if affairs defeat the objects of the society.

key_sections.title: Disputes regarding election of office-bearers.
key_sections.description: Allows a prescribed authority to summarily decide disputes regarding the election or continuance in office of office-bearers, including setting aside elections for corrupt practices.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Administrator.
key_sections.description: Enables the State Government to appoint an Administrator for a society under specific conditions, such as working against objectives, fraudulent elections, or nominated office-bearers.

powers_conferred: Registrar: Certify registration, refuse registration, issue public notices for objections, register change of name, refuse change of name, direct change of name, cancel registration, call for information, investigate affairs, give directions, call general body meetings, accept composition fees.

State Government: Direct smaller registration fees, appoint Registrar of Societies, appoint Additional Registrars, authorize powers to Additional Registrars, permit use of specific words in society names, make rules, appoint Administrator, extend Administrator's period, appoint advisory committee, dissolve society.

Administration of Union territory of Ladakh: Appoint Registrar of Societies, appoint Additional Registrars, authorize powers to Additional Registrars, fix balancing day for accounts, authorize auditors.
Societies: Form by memorandum, sue and be sued, alter/extend/abridge purposes, amalgamate with other societies, dissolve.
Governing Body: Manage affairs, determine person for suits, make bye-laws, propose alteration/extension/abridgement of purposes, propose amalgamation, propose dissolution, keep accounts.
Members: Determine dissolution, vote on property disposal upon dissolution, create governing body for unregistered societies.
Prescribed Authority (Haryana): Hear and decide election disputes.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Pecuniary penalty for breach of bye-law (Section 9). Members liable to be sued for arrears of subscription, detention/damage/destruction of society property (Section 10). Members guilty of stealing, embezzling, destroying property, or forging instruments of the society are punishable as strangers (Section 11). Failure to comply with provisions regarding annual list or changes in managing body/rules (Assam/Orissa/Ladakh Section 4A/4C, Haryana Section 26) punishable with fine (e.g., up to one hundred/one thousand rupees, or five hundred/five thousand rupees for false entries). Willfully making false entry/alteration or omission in lists/statements/rules (Assam/Orissa/Ladakh Section 4C, Haryana Section 26) punishable with fine (e.g., up to five hundred/two thousand/five thousand rupees). Failure to maintain, balance, and audit accounts (Haryana Section 26). Failure to produce books of accounts or records during investigation (Haryana Section 26). Failure to appear before Registrar or contravention of investigation provisions (Haryana Section 26). Compounding of offences by Registrar (Haryana Section 27).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Administration of Union territory of Ladakh or the State Government (depending on the region) has the power to appoint the Registrar of Societies and Additional Registrars. The State Government (Haryana) has the power to appoint an Administrator.

applies_to: Any seven or more persons associated for any literary, scientific, or charitable purpose, or for any such purpose as is described in section 20 of this Act.

Charitable societies, military orphan funds or societies established at the several presidencies of India, societies established for the promotion of science, literature, or the fine arts, for instruction, the diffusion of useful knowledge, the diffusion of political education, the foundation or maintenance of libraries or reading-rooms for general use among the members or open to the public, or public museums and galleries of paintings and other works of art, collections of natural history, mechanical and philosophical inventions, instruments, or designs.

Any company or society established for a literary, scientific, or charitable purpose, and registered under Act 43 of 1850, or any such society established and constituted previously to the passing of this Act but not registered under the said Act 43 of 1850.
exemptions: Joint-stock Companies (Section 14 proviso).
special_provisions: The Act has been extended and amended with specific provisions for various states and Union Territories including Ladakh, Arunachal Pradesh, Orissa, Uttarakhand, Haryana, Assam, Tripura, C.P. and Berar, Bihar, Punjab, West Bengal, Andhra, Madras, Maharashtra, Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bombay, Pondicherry, and Union territory of Delhi.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through the registration process, annual filing requirements, inspections and investigations by the Registrar, power to issue directions, power to cancel registration, provisions for dissolution, penalties for non-compliance and false statements, compounding of offences, and the appointment of an Administrator.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Principal Court of original civil jurisdiction of the district (for dissolution disputes). Any Court having jurisdiction where the defendant resides or the society is situate (for recovery of penalties). No Court inferior to that of a Magistrate of the First Class (for offences in Assam/Arunachal Pradesh). Prescribed authority (for election disputes in Haryana).

act_identification.act_title: THE POLICE ACT, 1861

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Extendable to any presidency, State or place by order of the State Government. Applied to various regions including Sonthal Parganas, Town of Calcutta and its suburbs, Khondmals District, Angul District, areas transferred to Orissa from Madras Presidency, Scheduled Districts, Kumaon and Garhwal Districts, Coorg, Amindivi Islands, Merged States, Bhopal, Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh, Kutch, Manipur, Tripura, Vindhya Pradesh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Laccadive Minicoy and Amindivi Islands, Madhya Pradesh, Goa, Daman and Diu.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to re-organise the police and to make it a more efficient instrument for the prevention and detection of crime; It is enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: To re-organise the police force and make it a more efficient instrument for the prevention and detection of crime.

key_definitions: subordinate ranks of a police force

key_sections.title: Interpretation clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the force.
key_sections.description: Declares the police-establishment under a State Government as one police force and outlines its constitution.

key_sections.title: Superintendence in the State Government.
key_sections.description: Vests the superintendence of police in the State Government.

key_sections.title: Inspector-General of Police, etc.
key_sections.description: Vests the administration of police in an Inspector-General and other officers, and in District Superintendents under the Magistrate's control.

key_sections.title: Appointment, dismissal, etc., of inferior officers.
key_sections.description: Empowers senior police officers to dismiss, suspend, reduce, or punish subordinate ranks for neglect of duty or unfitness.

key_sections.title: Power of Inspector-General to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Inspector-General power to frame rules for the organization, duties, and efficiency of the police force, subject to State Government approval.

key_sections.title: Quartering of additional police in disturbed or dangerous districts.
key_sections.description: Allows the State Government to declare an area disturbed and quarter additional police, with costs borne by the inhabitants.

key_sections.title: Awarding compensation to sufferers from misconduct of inhabitants or persons interested in land.
key_sections.description: Provides for compensation to victims of misconduct by inhabitants in disturbed areas, assessed by the Magistrate.

key_sections.title: Duties of police-officers.
key_sections.description: Outlines the duties of police officers, including obeying orders, collecting intelligence, preventing crime, detecting offenders, and apprehending persons.

key_sections.title: Penalties for neglect of duty, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for police officers guilty of neglect of duty, breach of rules, unauthorized withdrawal, or misconduct.

key_sections.title: Regulation of public assemblies and processions and licensing of the same.
key_sections.description: Empowers police to regulate public assemblies and processions, prescribe routes and times, and require licenses.

key_sections.title: Punishment for certain offences on roads, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for various public nuisances and offences committed on roads or public places, such as furious riding, cruelty to animals, obstructing passengers, and indecent exposure.

key_sections.title: Scope of Act.
key_sections.description: States that the Act does not take effect by its own operation but can be extended by the State Government to any area, and allows the State Government to make rules.

powers_conferred: Inspector-General of Police: Full powers of a Magistrate throughout the general police-district (Section 5).
Inspector-General of Police: Power to make rules for the organization, classification, distribution, and duties of the police-force (Section 12).
Inspector-General of Police, Deputy Inspector-General, Assistant Inspector-General, or District Superintendent: Power to depute additional police-officers at the cost of individuals (Section 13).
Inspector-General of Police: Power to depute additional police-force for railway, canal, or other public works, or manufactories, with State Government consent (Section 14).
State Government: Superintendence of the police throughout a general police-district (Section 3).
State Government: Power to declare an area disturbed or dangerous and quarter additional police (Section 15).
State Government: Power to exempt persons or classes from liability to bear the cost of additional police (Section 15(5), 15A(3)).
State Government: Power to sanction compensation to sufferers from misconduct of inhabitants (Section 15A(2)).
State Government: Power to extend the whole or any part of this Act to any presidency, State or place (Section 46(1)).
State Government: Power to make rules consistent with this Act to regulate procedure, prescribe conditions for compensation claims, and generally for giving effect to the Act (Section 46(2)).
District Superintendent or Assistant District Superintendent of Police: Power to direct the conduct of public assemblies and processions and license them (Section 30).
Magistrate: Power to appoint special police-officers (Section 17).
Magistrate: Power to detain unclaimed property and issue proclamation (Section 26).
Magistrate: Power to order sale of unclaimed property (Section 27).
Police-officers: Power to lay information before a Magistrate and apply for legal process (Section 24).
Police-officers: Power to take charge of unclaimed property (Section 25).
Police-officers: Power to take into custody, without a warrant, persons committing certain offences on roads (Section 34).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Refusal to serve as special police-officer (Section 19): Fine not exceeding fifty rupees. Refusing to deliver up certificate, clothing, etc., on ceasing to be police-officer (Section 28): Penalty not exceeding two hundred rupees, or imprisonment with or without hard labour for a period not exceeding six months, or both. Neglect of duty, wilful breach of rule/order, unauthorized withdrawal, failure to report for duty, engaging in other employment, cowardice, or unwarrantable personal violence by a police-officer (Section 29): Penalty not exceeding three months’ pay, or imprisonment with or without hard labour for a period not exceeding three months, or both. Disobeying orders issued under sections 30, 30A, 31, or violating license conditions (Section 32): Fine not exceeding two hundred rupees. Certain offences on roads, such as slaughtering cattle, furious riding, cruelty to animals, obstructing passengers, exposing goods for sale, throwing dirt, being found drunk or riotous, indecent exposure, or neglect to protect dangerous places (Section 34): Fine not exceeding fifty rupees, or imprisonment with or without hard labour not exceeding eight days.
