Magistrates have the power to appoint special police-officers (Section 17).

applies_to: All persons enrolled under this Act as police (Section 1)
Inhabitants of areas declared disturbed or dangerous (Section 15, 15A)
Any person committing certain offences on roads or public places (Section 34)
exemptions: State Government may exempt any persons or class or section of inhabitants from liability to bear the cost of additional police (Section 15(5)).
State Government may exempt any persons or class or section of inhabitants from liability to pay any portion of compensation (Section 15A(3)).
special_provisions: The Act does not take effect by its own operation but can be extended by the State Government to any presidency, State or place (Section 46(1)).
Special provisions for police-chaukidars in the Presidency of Fort William (Section 21).
State Amendments for Orissa (Section 15A) and Uttar Pradesh (Section 34A).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Inspector-General of Police (subject to State Government approval) (Section 12) and the State Government (Section 46(2)).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced through duties of police officers (Section 23), powers to lay information before Magistrates (Section 24), recovery of moneys (Section 16), and penalties and fines for various offences and misconduct (Sections 19, 28, 29, 32, 34).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate (Sections 19, 28, 29, 32, 34, 35, 37) and any competent Court for recovery of moneys (Section 16).

act_identification.act_title: THE STAGE-CARRIAGES ACT, 1861

legislative_details.geographical_extent: extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States; but it shall not apply to carriages ordinarily plying for hire within the limits of any municipality or cantonment or other place in which any law for the regulation of carriages is for the time being in force.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to license and to regulate stage-carriages in the Provinces; It is enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish a system for licensing stage-carriages and to regulate their operation. It covers aspects such as safety, passenger capacity, and the welfare of animals used for drawing these carriages, prescribing penalties for non-compliance.

key_sections.title: Definition of stage-carriage.
key_sections.description: Defines what constitutes a stage-carriage for the purposes of this Act.

key_sections.title: Carriages to be licensed.
key_sections.description: Mandates that no carriage shall be used as a stage-carriage unless licensed by a Magistrate or Commissioner of Police.

key_sections.title: Power to refuse license.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the licensing authority to refuse a license if the carriage is unserviceable, unsafe, or unfit, and specifies particulars to be included in a granted license.

key_sections.title: Particulars to be painted on conspicuous part of carriage.
key_sections.description: Requires the proprietor to paint license particulars on a conspicuous part of the licensed stage-carriage.

key_sections.title: Penalty for letting for hire unlicensed carriage.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for letting an unlicensed stage-carriage for hire.

key_sections.title: Penalty for allowing carriage to be drawn by fewer animals or more passengers, etc., to be carried than provided by license.
key_sections.description: Imposes penalties on proprietors, agents, or drivers for violating license conditions regarding the number of animals, passengers, or luggage weight.

key_sections.title: Penalty for ill-treating animals.
key_sections.description: Stipulates penalties for cruelty towards animals employed in drawing stage-carriages or using unfit animals.

key_sections.title: Revocation of license.
key_sections.description: Empowers a Magistrate or Commissioner of Police to cancel a stage-carriage license if the carriage, horse, or harness is unfit.

key_sections.title: Penalty for misconduct on part of drivers.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for drivers whose misconduct endangers passengers or property.

key_sections.title: Penalty when recoverable from proprietor.
key_sections.description: States conditions under which a proprietor can be held liable for offences committed by a driver or horse owner, with a proviso for discharge under certain circumstances.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes, including prescribing license forms, inspection, and regulating animal use.

key_sections.title: Interpretation-clause.
key_sections.description: Defines the term 'Magistrate' and clarifies that provisions applied to horses also apply to other animals used for drawing carriages.

key_sections.title: Extent of Act.
key_sections.description: Specifies the geographical applicability of the Act and its limitations regarding municipal or cantonment areas with existing carriage regulations.

key_sections.title: Power to State Government to exempt.
key_sections.description: Allows the State Government to exempt certain carriages or classes of carriages from the Act's provisions.

powers_conferred: Magistrate or Commissioner of Police: to license carriages (Section 2)
Magistrate or Commissioner of Police: to refuse license (Section 3)
Magistrate or Commissioner of Police: to grant license (Section 3)
State Government: to fix the sum for licenses (Section 4)
Magistrate or Commissioner of Police: to cancel license (Section 10)
Police-officer: to seize stage-carriage with horse (Section 11)
Magistrate: to issue summons (Section 14)
Magistrate or Commissioner of Police: to adjudicate penalties (Section 15)
Magistrate: to levy penalties by distress and sale (Section 16)
Magistrate: to order apprehension and detention of offender (Section 17)
Magistrate: to commit offender to prison (Section 18)
State Government: to make rules (Section 20A)
State Government: to exempt carriages or class of carriages (Section 23)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties include fines for letting a carriage without painted particulars (up to one hundred rupees), letting an unlicensed carriage (up to one hundred rupees for first conviction, up to five hundred rupees for subsequent), violating license conditions regarding animals, passengers, or luggage (up to one hundred rupees for first conviction, up to five hundred rupees for subsequent), ill-treating animals (up to one hundred rupees), and driver misconduct (up to one hundred rupees). Breach of rules made under Section 20A is punishable with a fine up to one hundred rupees. Non-payment of penalties can lead to distress and sale of property, or imprisonment.

applies_to: Every carriage drawn by one or more horses (or other animals) ordinarily used for conveying passengers for hire to or from any place in the States.
exemptions: Carriages ordinarily plying for hire within the limits of any municipality or cantonment or other place in which any law for the regulation of carriages is for the time being in force.
Any carriages or class of carriages exempted by notification by the State Government.
special_provisions: The Act applies to all the States of India, but not so as to supersede or contravene provisions of local laws dealing with the same subject.

Declared to be in force in the Santhal Parganas.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Licensing by Magistrates or Commissioners of Police. Enforcement through penalties, fines, seizure of carriages, distress and sale of movable property, and imprisonment for non-payment of fines. Police officers are empowered to seize non-compliant carriages.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate or Commissioner of Police

act_identification.act_title: THE PARTITION OF REVENUE-PAYING ESTATES ACT, 1863

legislative_details.enacted_by: THE GOVERNER GENERAL OF INDIA IN COUNCIL
legislative_details.geographical_extent: This Act shall extend only to such parts of the North-Western Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal as are subject to the general Regulations of that Presidency; but the Act may be extended, by order of the Local Government, either wholly or in part, to any Non-Regulation Province under such Government.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to the partition of estates paying revenue to Government in the North-Western Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal ; It is enacted as follows :—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws concerning the partition of estates that pay revenue to the Government. It establishes a comprehensive procedure for the division of such estates, including provisions for dispute resolution, cost assessment, and revenue apportionment.

key_sections.title: Future partitions to be made under provisions of Act.
key_sections.description: Mandates that all future partitions of estates ordered by Government officers must follow the provisions of this Act.

key_sections.title: What parties entitled to partition.
key_sections.description: Defines who is entitled to claim partition under the Act, specifically recorded proprietors of joint undivided estates paying revenue to Government.

key_sections.title: Parties desirous of partition to apply to Collector in writing.
key_sections.description: Requires proprietors seeking partition to submit a written application to the Collector of the District.

key_sections.title: Procedure if question of title, or of proprietary right, be raised.
key_sections.description: Outlines the Collector's procedure when objections raise questions of title or proprietary right, including inquiry, evidence taking, and reference to arbitration.

key_sections.title: Decision of Collector equivalent to decision of civil Court, and open to appeal.
key_sections.description: States that the Collector's decisions regarding rights of parties are considered decisions of a Civil Court of first instance and are subject to appeal.

key_sections.title: Civil Court to entertain suits only on appeal from decision of Collector.
key_sections.description: Restricts Civil Courts from entertaining original suits for partition, allowing them only to hear appeals from Collector's decisions.

key_sections.title: Partition may be stayed, and proceedings quashed, by Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Grants the Commissioner the power to stay or quash partition proceedings based on new information or valid reasons, with the decision not being open to revision by a Civil Court.

key_sections.title: Options of settlement by private agreement.
key_sections.description: Allows parties the option of private partition or arbitration for settlement, subject to Collector's confirmation.

key_sections.title: In default of Private agreement, or settlement by arbitration, officer may be appointed to make partition.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of an officer by the Collector to make the partition if private agreement or arbitration fails.

key_sections.title: Division of lands held in common.
key_sections.description: Details the Collector's role in declaring the principle and rule for dividing common lands according to village custom.

key_sections.title: Government may order new allotment of public revenue among estates formed by partition, in case of fraud or error in original allotment being proved.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Government to order a new allotment of public revenue within twelve years if fraud or error in the original apportionment is proven.

key_sections.title: Holder of decree of civil Court, awarding right to portion of estate, may apply for partition, and Collector may proceed thereon under Act.
key_sections.description: Allows a decree-holder from a Civil Court, awarded proprietary right in a portion of an estate, to apply to the Collector for partition under this Act.

key_sections.title: Provisions of Act applied to partition of estates held free from payment of revenue.
key_sections.description: Permits the Local Government to apply the Act's provisions to the partition of estates not paying Government Revenue.

key_sections.title: Territorial scope of Act.
key_sections.description: Defines the geographical areas to which the Act extends, primarily parts of the North-Western Provinces, with provisions for extension by Local Government.

powers_conferred: Collector: To receive applications for partition (Section IV)
Collector: To publish notifications and invite objections (Section VI)
Collector: To refuse applications for valid reasons (Section VII)
Collector: To inquire into questions of title or proprietary right and refer to arbitration (Section VIII)
Collector: To pass decisions on rights of parties, equivalent to a Civil Court (Section IX)
Collector: To fix and assess costs incurred in making partition (Section XIV)

Collector: To direct attachment and khas management of an estate during partition (Section XXVII)

Collector: To exercise powers for measurement and map preparation (Section XXIX)
Collector: To declare the principle and rule for dividing common lands (Section XXX)
Collector: To refuse to declare certain lands a separate mehal (Section XXXI)
Collector: To stop partition with Commissioner's sanction and recover costs (Section XXXIV)

Collector: To give proprietors possession of allotted estates, with Magistrate's assistance if needed (Section XLIV)

Commissioner: To direct division by lot under certain circumstances (Section XLIII)

Board of Revenue: To hear appeals from Commissioner's decisions (Section XLIII)
Local Government: To sanction rules for payment of partition expenses (Section XIV)
Local Government: To order application of Act to estates held free from revenue payment (Section LI)

Officer appointed to make partition: To exercise powers for detailed measurement and map preparation (Section XXIX)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: If any person is guilty of the offence of giving or fabricating false evidence, or of forgery, as defined in the Indian Penal Code, or of abetting any of those offences, the Collector or other Officer exercising jurisdiction under this Act shall have the same powers as a Civil Court under the Code of Criminal Procedure for dealing with such offences.

applies_to: All partitions of estates ordered by Government officers after the passing of this Act (Section II)
Every recorded proprietor of a joint undivided estate paying Revenue to Government, or any portion thereof (Section III)
Partition of any estate held free from the payment of Government Revenue, if ordered by the Local Government (Section LI)
special_provisions: The Act extends only to such parts of the North-Western Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal as are subject to the general Regulations of that Presidency.
The Act may be extended, by order of the Local Government, either wholly or in part, to any Non-Regulation Province under such Government (Section LIX).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Board of Revenue, with the sanction of the Local Government, can lay down rules for the payment of partition expenses (Section XIV). The Board of Revenue is guided by instructions from the Local Government (Section LVII).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Decisions of the Collector regarding rights of parties are considered decisions of a Civil Court (Section IX). Costs and arrears of revenue can be recovered under rules applicable to recovery of arrears of rent or revenue (Section XIV, XLV). The Collector may avail himself of the assistance of the Magistrate in giving possession (Section XLIV).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District or Sadr Court for appeals from Collector's decisions (Section IX, X). Civil Courts are restricted from entertaining original suits for partition but can hear appeals (Section XI).

act_identification.act_title: THE WASTE LANDS (CLAIMS) ACT, 1863

legislative_details.geographical_extent: All part A States except the Scheduled Districts; specific Scheduled Districts including West Jalpaiguri, Hazaribagh, Lohardaga (now Ranchi), Manbhum, Paragana Dhalbhum, Kolhan in Singbhum, Porahat Estate, Kumaon and Garhwal, Mirzapur District (Scheduled portion), Jaunsar Bawar, Lahaul, Kamrup, Naugong Darrang, Sibsagar, Lakhimpur, Goalpara (excluding Eastern Duars), Cachar (excluding North Cachar Hills); extended to Western Duars, The Tarai of the Province of Agra, new Provinces and Merged States, States of Manipur, Tripura and Vindhya Pradesh.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to make special provision for the speedy adjudication of claims which may be preferred to waste lands proposed to be sold, or otherwise dealt with, on account of [3][the Provincial Government], and of objections taken to the sale or other disposition of such lands ; It is enacted as follows :—
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the speedy adjudication of claims to waste lands that the State Government proposes to sell or otherwise deal with. It also addresses objections raised against such sales or dispositions, establishing a specific legal framework for their resolution.

key_sections.title: Provision for inquiry into claims to land, or objections to sale of same.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Collector to inquire into claims or objections regarding waste lands proposed for sale or disposition by the State Government.

key_sections.title: Procedure in such cases.
key_sections.description: Outlines the Collector's procedure for inquiry, including calling for evidence and issuing an order for admission or rejection of claims/objections.

key_sections.title: Procedure after passing of order in the case, Report to Revenue Board, Decision of Board.
key_sections.description: Details the process after the Collector's order, including reporting to the Board of Revenue and the Board's power to confirm, modify, or reverse the order.

key_sections.title: Special Court for trying claims.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Local Government to constitute Special Courts for the investigation and trial of claims under this Act.

key_sections.title: Notice of constitution of Special Courts. Claims not cognizable in other Courts.
key_sections.description: Requires public notice of Special Courts and states that no other court can entertain claims falling under the Special Court's jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Plaintiff and defendant in suit under section V, Proviso, Plaintiff and defendant in suits under section VI.
key_sections.description: Specifies who appears as plaintiff and defendant in suits instituted under Section V and Section VI of the Act.

key_sections.title: No appeal or revision.
key_sections.description: States that decisions or orders passed under this Act are not subject to appeal or revision.

key_sections.title: Reference of question of law, etc., to High Court etc. when reference obligatory in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Allows the Court to refer questions of law, usage, or document construction to the High Court, and makes such reference obligatory for matters of general importance or class rights.

key_sections.title: Limitation as to claims to land sold or dealt with. Provision for such claims if preferred within time.
key_sections.description: Sets a three-year limitation period for claims to land sold or dealt with as waste land by the State Government.

key_sections.title: If claim established, possession not to be given, but compensation.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that if a claim to sold land is established, the claimant receives compensation equal to the sale price plus costs, rather than possession.

key_sections.title: When land has not been absolutely sold, or has been otherwise dealt with.
key_sections.description: Provides for compensation based on the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, if the claimed land was not absolutely sold or was otherwise dealt with by the State Government.

key_sections.title: Exercise of power of the State Government by the Board of Revenue or the Financial Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Allows the Board of Revenue or Financial Commissioner to exercise powers and duties of the State Government under sections 6, 10, 22, and 23 in certain states.

powers_conferred: Collector or other Officer: inquire into claims or objections (Section 1), call for evidence and documents (Section 2), dispose of cases by order (Section 2), postpone sale or disposition of land (Section 3), stop sale or disposition of land (Section 4), report to the Board of Revenue or superior Revenue Authority (Section 5).

Local Government: order a suit to be brought to try a claim or objection (Section 6), constitute Special Courts for investigation and trial of claims (Section 7), appoint an officer to appear as defendant on its behalf (Section 10).
Board of Revenue or other superior Revenue Authority: confirm, modify, or reverse the order of the Collector or other officer (Section 5).

Special Court: make necessary orders prior to the hearing of the suit (Section 7), investigate and try claims (Section 7), fix a day for appearance and hearing (Section 12), require personal attendance of claimant/objector (Section 12), examine parties and witnesses (Section 13), pass orders (Section 13), refer questions of law to High Court (Section 15), award compensation (Section 19, Section 20).
State Government: award compensation for waste land sold (Section 22), award compensation for land sold subject to condition or otherwise disposed of (Section 23).

related_acts: Act VI of 1857 (for the acquisition of lands for public purposes)
U.P. Board of Revenue Act, 1922 (U.P. 12 of 1922)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Local Government has the power to constitute Special Courts and appoint an officer to appear as defendant on its behalf.

applies_to: Claims to waste lands proposed to be sold or otherwise dealt with on account of the State Government.
Objectors to the sale or disposition of such lands.
special_provisions: Declared in force in all part A States except the Scheduled Districts.
Declared in force in specific Scheduled Districts (e.g., West Jalpaiguri, Hazaribagh, Kumaon and Garhwal).
Not in force in Scheduled Districts in Ganjam and Vizagapatam.
Extended to Western Duars, The Tarai of the Province of Agra, new Provinces and Merged States, and States of Manipur, Tripura and Vindhya Pradesh.
Repealed in Bombay by the Waste Lands (Claims) (Bombay Repeal) Act, 1943.
Section 23A has been omitted in its application to the U.P.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Inquiry by the Collector, review by the Board of Revenue or superior Revenue Authority, and adjudication by Special Courts constituted by the Local Government. Proceedings are regulated by the Code of Civil Procedure where applicable.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Special Courts constituted under this Act, High Court (for reference of questions of law).

act_identification.act_title: THE RELIGIOUS ENDOWMENTS ACT, 1863

act_overview.preamble:
Preamble.—Whereas it is expedient to relieve the Boards of Revenue, and the local Agents, in the
Presidency of Fort William in Bengal, and the Presidency of Fort Saint George, from the duties imposed on
them by Regulation XIX, 1810 (Ben. Reg. 19 of 1810), of the Bengal Code (for the due appropriation of the
rents and produce of lands granted for the support of Mosques, Hindu Temples, Colleges and other purposes;
for the maintenance and repair of Bridges, Sarais, Kattras, and other public buildings; and for the custody and
disposal of Nazul Property or Escheats), and Regulation VII, 1817 (Mad. Reg. 7 of 1817), of the Madras
Code (for the due appropriation of the rents and produce of lands granted for the support of Mosques, Hindu
Temples and Colleges or other public purposes; for the maintenance and repair of Bridges, Choultries, or
Chattrams, and other public buildings; and for the custody and disposal of Escheats), so far as those duties
embrace the superintendence of lands granted for the support of Mosques or Hindu Temples and for other
religious uses; the appropriation of endowments made for the maintenance of such religious establishments;
the repair and preservation of buildings connected therewith, and the appointment of trustees or managers
thereof; or involve any connexion with the management of such religious establishments; It is enacted as
follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to divest the Government of India, specifically the Boards of Revenue and local Agents, from the management and superintendence of religious endowments, including those for mosques, Hindu temples, and other religious establishments. It aims to transfer these responsibilities to trustees, managers, or newly appointed committees, thereby ending the Government's direct involvement in the administration of such religious institutions.

key_sections.title: Interpretation-clause.
key_sections.description: Defines 'Civil Court' and 'Court' for the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Government to make special provision respecting mosques, etc.
key_sections.description: Requires the State Government to make special provision for religious establishments where nomination of trustees is vested in or confirmed by the Government.

key_sections.title: Transfer to trustees, etc., of trust-property in charge of Revenue Board.
key_sections.description: Mandates the State Government to transfer trust property from the Board of Revenue or local agents to existing trustees, managers, or superintendents.

key_sections.title: Procedure in case of dispute as to right of succession to vacated trusteeship.
key_sections.description: Allows interested persons to apply to the Civil Court to appoint a manager in case of a dispute over succession to a vacated trusteeship.

key_sections.title: Appointment of committees.
key_sections.description: Requires the State Government to appoint committees to take the place and exercise the powers of the Board of Revenue and local agents.

key_sections.title: Vacancies to be filled.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for filling vacancies in committees, including election by interested persons and intervention by the Civil Court if necessary.

key_sections.title: On appointment of Committee, Board and local agents to transfer property.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that upon appointment of a committee, the Board of Revenue and local agents must transfer all property belonging to the religious establishment to the committee.

key_sections.title: Duty of trustee, etc., as to accounts.
key_sections.description: Imposes a duty on trustees, managers, superintendents, and committees to keep and require regular accounts of receipts and disbursements.

key_sections.title: Persons interested may singly sue in case of breach of trust, etc.
key_sections.description: Allows any interested person to sue trustees, managers, superintendents, or committee members in Civil Court for misfeasance, breach of trust, or neglect of duty, and empowers the Court to direct specific performance, decree damages, and order removal.

key_sections.title: Application for leave to institute suits.
key_sections.description: Requires a preliminary application to the Court for leave to institute suits under the Act, with the Court determining if there are sufficient prima facie grounds.

key_sections.title: Cases in which endowments are partly for religious and partly for secular purposes.
key_sections.description: Provides for the Board of Revenue to determine the portion of property for secular uses versus religious uses when endowments serve both purposes, before transferring management.

key_sections.title: Government not to hold charge henceforth of property for support of any mosque, temple, etc.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the Central or State Government, or any officer, from undertaking or resuming superintendence, management, or appropriation of property for religious establishments, or appointing trustees, except as provided in this Act.

powers_conferred: State Government to make special provision respecting mosques, temples, etc. (Section 3)
State Government to transfer trust-property in charge of Revenue Board to trustees, managers, or superintendents (Section 4)
Civil Court to appoint a manager in case of dispute as to right of succession to vacated trusteeship (Section 5)
Managers appointed by Court to exercise all powers of former trustee, manager, or superintendent (Section 5)
Trustees, managers, or superintendents to whom property is transferred to exercise powers for recovery of rent (Section 6)
State Government to appoint one or more committees to take the place and exercise the powers of the Board of Revenue and local agents (Section 7)
State Government to frame rules for elections to ascertain wishes of persons interested in committee appointments (Section 8)
Civil Court to remove members of committee for misconduct or unfitness (Section 9)
Remaining members of committee to give public notice and fix a day for election of a new member to fill vacancy (Section 10)
Civil Court to appoint a person to fill a vacancy in a committee or order remaining members to do so, if election fails (Section 10)
Committees to exercise powers for recovery of rent of land or other property transferred (Section 12)
Committees of management to require production of accounts from trustees, managers, and superintendents (Section 13)
Civil Court to direct specific performance, decree damages and costs, and direct removal of trustee, manager, superintendent, or committee member in case of breach of trust (Section 14)
Court to order any matter in difference in a suit or proceeding to be referred for decision to arbitrators (Section 16)
Court to grant leave for institution of suits after determining sufficient prima facie grounds (Section 18)
Court to order costs to be paid out of the estate if the suit was for the benefit of the trust and no party was in fault (Section 18)
Court to require accounts of trust to be filed (Section 19)
Board of Revenue to determine what portion of land or property shall remain under its superintendence for secular uses, and what portion shall be transferred for religious uses (Section 21)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for civil remedies in cases of 'misfeasance, breach of trust or neglect of duty' by trustees, managers, superintendents, or committee members. The Civil Court may direct specific performance, decree damages and costs, and order the removal of the offending party. It also mentions 'criminal breach of trust' but clarifies that civil proceedings under this Act do not affect or interfere with criminal proceedings for such offenses.

Madras Regulation 7 of 1817
Repealing Act, 1870 (14 of 1870)
Madras Hindu Religious Endowment Act, 1926 (Mad. Act 2 of 1927)
Orissa Hindu Religious Endowments Act, 1939 (Orissa Act 4 of 1939)
Bihar Act 1 of 1951
Madras Act 22 of 1959
related_acts: Religious Endowments (Extension to Kanara) Act, 1865 (Bom. Act 7 of 1865)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government has the power to appoint committees. The Civil Court has the power to appoint a manager in case of a dispute over trusteeship and to fill vacancies in committees. Interested persons have the power to elect new members to committees.

applies_to: Mosques, temples or other religious establishments
Trustees, managers or superintendents of such establishments
Committees appointed under this Act
Persons interested in any mosque, temple or religious establishment

Extended to Kanara by the Religious Endowments (Extension to Kanara) Act, 1865

Extended to Kumaon and Garhwal, The Tarai of the Province of Agra, Ajmer and Merwara by notifications under s. 5 of the Scheduled Districts Act, 1874

State of Madras (ceased to be in force by Madras Act 22 of 1959)
special_provisions: Section 21 provides for cases where endowments are partly for religious and partly for secular purposes, allowing the Board of Revenue to determine the allocation of property.
A proviso to Section 22 has been added to apply only to Bengal by the Bengal Waqf Act, 1934.
A new Section 23A has been added to apply only to Bengal by the Bengal Waqf Act, 1934.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The State Government has the authority to frame rules for elections of committee members.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced primarily through the Civil Courts, where interested persons can institute suits for breach of trust, misfeasance, or neglect of duty by trustees, managers, superintendents, or committee members. The Courts can direct specific performance, award damages and costs, and order removal. Arbitration is also a mechanism for dispute resolution. Committees are responsible for requiring and keeping accounts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The 'Civil Court', defined as the principal Court of original civil jurisdiction in the district or any other Court empowered by the State Government, has jurisdiction under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: An Act to amend Act 8 of 1851 (for enabling Government to levy Tolls on Public Roads and Bridges)

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Santhal Parganas, C. P. and the Sambalpur District, Districts of Hazaribagh, Lohardaga, Manbhum, Pargana Dhalbhum and the Kolhan in the District of Singbhum, The District of Lahaul, the Scheduled District of Coorg, Ajmer-Merwara, the Scheduled Districts in Vizagapatam and Ganjam, the District of Darjeeling, the Union territory of Pondicherry, the Punjab, Oudh, the C.P., the District of Lakhimpur

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS by Act 8 of 1851 (for enabling Government to levy Tolls on Public Roads and Bridges) authority was given for the levy of certain rates of toll ***; It is enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to amend Act 8 of 1851, which enables the Government to levy tolls on public roads and bridges. It allows collectors of tolls to compound for tolls and grants the State Government the power to extend the Act's applicability to various places.

key_sections.title: Collectors of tolls may compound for tolls leviable under Act 8 of 1851 or this Act.
key_sections.description: Allows any person entrusted with toll collection under Act 8 of 1851 to compound for a fixed sum for a period not exceeding one year, in lieu of regular toll rates.

key_sections.title: Power to extend Act.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the authority to extend this Act to any place where Act 8 of 1851 is in force, and also to extend both Act 8 of 1851 and this Act to places where Act 8 of 1851 is not yet in force.

powers_conferred: Power to Collectors of tolls to compound for tolls leviable under Act 8 of 1851 or this Act (Section 2)
Power to State Government to extend this Act to any place (Section 3)
Power to State Government to extend Act 8 of 1851 and this Act to any place (Section 3)

repealed_acts: Schedule of Act 8 of 1851
related_acts: Tolls on Roads and Bridges Act, 1875 (Bom. 3 of 1875)

applies_to: Any person entrusted with the management of the collection of tolls
State Government
special_provisions: The Act is to be deemed to be and to have been in force in the Punjab, from the 24th March, 1864

schedules_summary.description: Omitted by the Devolution Act, 1920 (38 of 1920), s. 2 and the First Schedule (w.e.f. 14-9-1920).

act_identification.act_title: THE PUBLIC GAMBLING ACT, 1867

legislative_details.geographical_extent: United Provinces, East Punjab, Delhi and the Central Provinces. Sections 13 and 17 extend to the whole of the said States, and other sections can be extended by the State Government to any city, town, suburb, railway-station, house and place within the States.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to make provision for the punishment of public gambling and the keeping of common gaining-houses [5][in the United Provinces, East Punjab, Delhi and the Central Provinces]; It is hereby enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the punishment of public gambling and the keeping of common gaming houses. It defines what constitutes a common gaming-house and outlines penalties for those involved in such activities. The Act also grants powers to authorities for search, seizure, and arrest related to gambling offenses.

key_sections.title: Interpretation-clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, specifically 'Common gaming-house'.

key_sections.title: Power to extend Act.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the State Government to extend the Act's provisions to specific areas.

key_sections.title: Penalty for owning or keeping, or having charge of, a gaming-house.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals who own, occupy, or manage a common gaming-house.

key_sections.title: Penalty for being found in gaming-house.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals found in a common gaming-house for the purpose of gaming.

key_sections.title: Power to enter and authorise police to enter and search.
key_sections.description: Empowers Magistrates and District Superintendents of Police to enter and search suspected common gaming-houses and arrest persons found therein.

key_sections.title: Finding cards, etc., in suspected houses, to be evidence that such houses are common gaming houses.
key_sections.description: States that finding gaming instruments in a suspected house is evidence of it being a common gaming-house.

key_sections.title: Penalty on persons arrested for giving false names and addresses.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalty for persons arrested who give false names or addresses.

key_sections.title: On conviction for keeping a gaming-house, instruments of gaming to be destroyed.
key_sections.description: Allows the Magistrate to order destruction of gaming instruments and forfeiture of money upon conviction.

key_sections.title: Magistrate may require any person apprehended to be sworn and give evidence.
key_sections.description: Empowers Magistrates to require apprehended persons to give evidence on oath, with indemnification for witnesses.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply to certain games.
key_sections.description: Exempts games of mere skill from the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Gaming and setting birds and animals to fight in public streets.
key_sections.description: Allows police officers to apprehend persons gaming or setting animals to fight in public streets and seize instruments.

key_sections.title: Penalty for subsequent offence.
key_sections.description: Prescribes enhanced penalties for repeat offenders under sections 3 or 4.

powers_conferred: State Government: Power to extend the Act to specific areas (Section 2).

Magistrate of a district or other officer invested with full powers of a Magistrate, or the District Superintendent of Police: Power to enter and search suspected common gaming-houses, take persons into custody, and seize instruments of gaming, moneys, and articles of value (Section 5).
Magistrate: Power to order destruction of instruments of gaming, sale and conversion of securities for money, and forfeiture of proceeds/moneys upon conviction (Section 8).
Magistrate: Power to require apprehended persons to be examined on oath or solemn affirmation and give evidence (Section 10).
Police-officer: Power to apprehend without warrant persons found gaming or setting birds/animals to fight in public streets, and to seize instruments of gaming (Section 13).
Magistrate: Power to direct payment of a portion of fine or forfeited moneys/proceeds to an informer (Section 16).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever owns, keeps, or has charge of a common gaming-house, or knowingly permits it to be used as such, or assists in conducting its business, or advances money for gaming, shall be liable to a fine not exceeding two-hundred rupees, or imprisonment not exceeding three months (Section 3). Whoever is found in a common gaming-house for the purpose of gaming shall be liable to a fine not exceeding one hundred rupees, or imprisonment not exceeding one month (Section 4). Persons arrested giving false names or addresses are liable to a penalty not exceeding five hundred rupees plus costs, or imprisonment not exceeding one month (Section 7). Refusal to make oath or answer questions by a witness is punishable as per IPC sections 178 or 179 (Section 10). Gaming or setting birds/animals to fight in public streets is punishable with a fine not exceeding fifty rupees, or imprisonment not exceeding one calendar month (Section 13). Subsequent offences under sections 3 or 4 incur double the punishment, with a maximum fine of six hundred rupees or imprisonment for one year (Section 15).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government has the power to appoint police officers of a certain rank for the purpose of entering and searching gaming-houses (Section 5).

applies_to: Owners, occupiers, or persons having the use of any house, walled enclosure, room or place used as a common gaming-house.
Persons found in a common gaming-house for the purpose of gaming.
Persons found playing for money or other valuable things with instruments of gaming (not being games of mere skill) in public streets, places or thoroughfares.
Persons setting birds or animals to fight in public streets, places or thoroughfares, and those aiding and abetting such fighting.
exemptions: Any game of mere skill wherever played (Section 12).
special_provisions: The Act initially applies to the United Provinces, East Punjab, Delhi and the Central Provinces.
The State Government has the power to extend all or any of the remaining sections of the Act to any city, town, suburb, railway-station, house and place within the States (Section 2).
Uttar Pradesh State Amendment: Insertion of new section 14-A for compounding of offences and abatement of certain trials.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through actions by Magistrates, District Superintendents of Police, and police officers who have powers to enter, search, seize instruments, and arrest offenders. Offences are triable by Magistrates, who can impose fines and imprisonment, and order destruction of gaming instruments or forfeiture of money.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any Magistrate having jurisdiction in the place where the offence is committed (Section 14).

act_identification.act_title: THE SARÁÍS ACT, 1867

legislative_details.enacted_by: GOVERNOR GENERAL OF INDIA IN COUNCIL
legislative_details.geographical_extent: territories under the government of the Lieutenant Governor of the North-West Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal, with power for State Government to extend to other parts of its territories, except Calcutta, Madras and Bombay.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the regulation of public Saráís and Puraos; It is hereby enacted as follows :—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to regulate public Saráís and Puraos. It establishes rules for their registration, maintenance, and the duties of their keepers, aiming to ensure public safety and hygiene.

key_sections.title: Interpretation clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act such as 'Saráí', 'Keeper of a Sarai', and 'Magistrate of the District'.

key_sections.title: Notice of this Act to be given to keepers of Saráís.
key_sections.description: Requires the Magistrate to give written notice of the Act to Saráí keepers and demand registration.

key_sections.title: Registers of Saráís to be kept.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Magistrate of the District to maintain a register of Saráís and their keepers.

key_sections.title: Lodgers, &c., not to be received in Saráís until registered.
key_sections.description: Prohibits Saráí keepers from receiving lodgers or animals until the Saráí is registered.

key_sections.title: Duties of keepers of Saráís.
key_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities of Saráí keepers, including reporting illness/death, allowing inspection, maintaining cleanliness, removing noxious vegetation, keeping structures in repair, providing watchmen, and exhibiting charges.

key_sections.title: Power to shut up, secure, clear, and clean deserted Saráí.
key_sections.description: Grants the Magistrate power to intervene and secure or clean deserted Saráís that become nuisances, recovering expenses from the owner.

key_sections.title: Taking down or repairing ruinous Saráís.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Magistrate to order the repair or demolition of ruinous or dangerous Saráís, with expenses recoverable from the keeper.

key_sections.title: Penalty for permitting Saráís to be filthy or overgrown.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for Saráí keepers who allow their premises to be filthy, unwholesome, or overgrown with vegetation after notice.

key_sections.title: Power for State Government to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the State Government to make, repeal, alter, and add to regulations for the better attainment of the Act's objects.

key_sections.title: Penalty for infringing Act or regulations.
key_sections.description: Sets penalties for Saráí keepers who violate the Act or its regulations, including daily penalties for continuing offences.

key_sections.title: Conviction for third offence to disqualify persons from keeping Saráís.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that a third conviction under the Act disqualifies a person from acting as a Saráí keeper without a special license from the Magistrate.

key_sections.title: Nothing in Act to apply to certain Saráís.
key_sections.description: Exempts Saráís under the direct management of the State Government or Municipal Committee from most provisions of the Act, except Section 8.

key_sections.title: Extent of Act.
key_sections.description: Defines the initial geographical application of the Act and grants the State Government power to extend it to other territories.

key_sections.title: Short title
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Saráís Act, 1867'.

powers_conferred: Magistrate of the District: To give notice of the Act and require registration (Section 3)
Magistrate of the District: To keep a register of Saráís and their keepers (Section 4)
Magistrate of the District: To refuse registration of a keeper without a certificate of character (Section 6)
Magistrate of the District: To require free access and inspection of Saráís (Section 7)
Magistrate of the District: To require cleansing, removal of vegetation, and repair of Saráís (Section 7)
Magistrate of the District: To require provision of watchmen (Section 7)
Magistrate of the District: To direct exhibition of charges (Section 7)
Magistrate of the District: To order reports from keepers about persons resorting to Saráís (Section 8)
Magistrate of the District: To shut up, secure, clear, and clean deserted Saráís and recover expenses (Section 9)
Magistrate of the District: To order taking down or repairing ruinous Saráís and recover expenses (Section 10)
Magistrate of the District: To sell materials of ruinous Saráís to cover expenses (Section 11)
Magistrate of the District: To enter and cleanse/clear filthy Saráís and recover expenses (Section 12 Proviso)
Magistrate of the District: To grant licence for keeping Saráís after a third offence (Section 15)
State Government: To direct the form and signatories for certificates of character (Section 6)
State Government: To prescribe rules for the number of watchmen (Section 7)
State Government: To make regulations for the attainment of the Act's objects (Section 13)
State Government: To extend the Act to other parts of its territories (Section 17)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Receiving lodgers or animals in an unregistered Saráí (Section 5). Failure to perform duties as a keeper (Section 7). Permitting a Saráí to be in a filthy, unwholesome, or overgrown state (Section 12). Infringing any provision of the Act or regulations made thereunder (Section 14). Penalties include a fine not exceeding twenty rupees, and a further penalty not exceeding one Rupee a day for every day the offence continues. A third offence leads to disqualification from keeping a Saráí without a special license (Section 15).

repealed_acts: Bengal Regulation 14 of 1807, section 11. Clause 5.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Magistrate of the District may appoint a person to keep the register of Saráís (Section 4). The State Government may direct the form and signatories for certificates of character for Saráí keepers (Section 6).

applies_to: public Saráís and Puraos
keepers of Saráís
travellers
exemptions: Any Saráí under the direct management of the State Government or of any Municipal Committee (except Section 8)
special_provisions: Initially extends only to the territories under the government of the Lieutenant Governor of the North-West Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal.
State Government has the power to extend the Act to any other part of its territories, except the towns of Calcutta, Madras and Bombay.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Magistrate of the District is responsible for giving notices, maintaining registers, inspecting Saráís, ordering repairs and cleaning, and imposing penalties. Expenses incurred by the Magistrate for cleaning or repairing can be recovered from the keeper or owner. Police stations are to be notified of infectious diseases or deaths.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any Magistrate for conviction (Section 14)

schedules_summary.description: Contains the 'FORM OF NOTICE' to be given to keepers of Saráís, informing them about the Act, the requirement for registration, where to register, and the penalties for non-compliance.

act_identification.act_title: An Act to define the rights of Taluqdárs and others in certain estates in Oudh, and to regulate the succession thereto.

legislative_details.enacted_by: GOVERNOR GENERAL OF INDIA IN COUNCIL
legislative_details.geographical_extent: estates hereinafter referred to in Oudh

act_overview.preamble: Preamble.—WHEREAS, after the re-occupation of Oudh by the British Government in the year 1858, the proprietary right in divers estates in that province was, under certain conditions, conferred by the British Government upon certain Taluqdárs and others; and whereas doubts may arise as to the nature of the rights of the said Taluqdárs and others in such estates, and as to the course of succession thereto; and whereas it is expedient to prevent such doubts, and to regulate such course, and to provide for such other matters connected therewith as are hereinafter mentioned; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to define the rights of Taluqdárs and others in certain estates in Oudh. It also aims to regulate the succession to these estates and prevent doubts regarding the nature of these rights and the course of succession.

chapter_titles: II.— Rights and liabilities of Taluqdárs and Grantees.
III.— Lists of Taluqdárs and Grantees.
IV.— Powers of Taluqdárs and Grantees to transfer and bequeath.

key_sections.title: Short title, Extent of Act.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical extent to the estates referred to within the Act.

key_sections.title: Interpretation–clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Transfer', 'Will', 'Taluqdár', 'Grantee', and 'Estate'.

key_sections.title: Taluqdárs to have heritable and transferable rights in their estates.
key_sections.description: Confers permanent, heritable, and transferable rights to Taluqdárs in their estates, subject to certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Preparation of lists of Taluqdárs and Grantees.
key_sections.description: Mandates the preparation of six lists classifying Taluqdárs and Grantees based on succession rules and other criteria.

key_sections.title: Taluqdárs and Grantees may transfer and bequeath.
key_sections.description: Grants Taluqdárs, Grantees, and their heirs/legatees the power to transfer or bequeath their estates, with conditions regarding mental capacity.

key_sections.title: Rule against perpetuity.
key_sections.description: Establishes a rule against perpetuities for transfers and bequests under the Act, limiting the delay in vesting of property.

key_sections.title: Restriction as to donees and legatees.
key_sections.description: Restricts the power of Taluqdárs/Grantees to give or bequeath estates to persons not in the line of succession, except under specific conditions.

key_sections.title: Sections of Succession Act applied to wills of Taluqdárs.
key_sections.description: Applies specific sections of the Indian Succession Act (No. X of 1865) to wills and codicils made under this Act.

key_sections.title: Special rules of succession to intestate Taluqdárs and Grantees.
key_sections.description: Lays down specific rules for the succession of estates of intestate Taluqdárs and Grantees whose names are in certain lists.

key_sections.title: General rule of succession to intestate Taluqdárs and Grantees.
key_sections.description: States that for cases not covered by section 22, succession to intestate property of Taluqdárs and Grantees will be regulated by the ordinary law of their tribe and religion.

key_sections.title: Maintenance of surviving relatives of Taluqdárs and Grantees.
key_sections.description: Establishes the liability of the person in possession of an estate to pay annuities for the maintenance of certain surviving relatives of the deceased Taluqdár or Grantee.

key_sections.title: Muhammadan Taluqdárs and Grantees empowered to adopt.
key_sections.description: Grants Muhammadan Taluqdárs, Grantees, and their widows the power to adopt a son for the purposes of this Act, under specific conditions.

key_sections.title: Alteration of rules of intestate succession in cases of Taluqdárs and Grantees named in list 3 or list 5.
key_sections.description: Allows Taluqdárs or Grantees in specific lists to declare their desire for succession to be regulated by ordinary law instead of the special rules of the Act.

key_sections.title: Reverter to ordinary law of succession.
key_sections.description: Permits Taluqdárs or Grantees to declare that their estate should be held subject to the ordinary law of succession, thereby making the Act's provisions inapplicable.

key_sections.title: Awards as to compensation and maintenance.
key_sections.description: Makes awards respecting provision for relatives of Taluqdárs legally enforceable if approved by the Financial Commissioner of Oudh.

powers_conferred: Taluqdárs and Grantees, and their heirs and legatees, of sound mind and not a minor, are competent to transfer the whole or any portion of their estate or interest therein during life-time by sale, exchange, mortgage, lease or gift, and to bequeath by will (Section 11).
A married woman may make a bequest under this Act of any property which she could alienate by her own act during her life (Section 11).
The Chief Commissioner of Oudh, subject to instructions from the Governor General of India in Council, shall cause to be prepared six lists of Taluqdárs and Grantees (Section 8).
The Governor General in Council may order the insertion of a name in a proper list if wrongly omitted or entered (Section 9).
Muhammadan Taluqdárs, Grantees, heirs or legatees, and their widows with consent, have power to adopt a son for the purposes of this Act (Section 29).
Any Taluqdár or Grantee in list 3 or 5 may present a declaration to the Chief Commissioner of Oudh to alter rules of intestate succession (Section 30).
Any Taluqdár or Grantee may present a declaration to the Chief Commissioner of Oudh for their estate to revert to ordinary law of succession (Section 31).

applies_to: Taluqdárs and Grantees in Oudh
Heirs and legatees of Taluqdárs and Grantees
Persons whose names are entered in the lists mentioned in section eight
exemptions: Estates for which a declaration has been made under Section 31 to revert to ordinary law of succession.
special_provisions: Special rules of succession for Taluqdárs and Grantees named in the second, third, or fifth lists (Section 22).
Provision for Muhammadan Taluqdárs and Grantees to adopt a son (Section 29).
Provision for Taluqdárs and Grantees in list 3 or 5 to alter rules of intestate succession (Section 30).
Provision for Taluqdárs and Grantees to revert their estate to the ordinary law of succession (Section 31).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Courts shall take judicial notice of the lists of Taluqdárs and Grantees and regard them as conclusive evidence (Section 10). Awards approved by the Financial Commissioner of Oudh and filed in his Court are enforceable as if a Court of competent jurisdiction had passed judgment (Section 33).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Court of an officer engaged in making the first regular settlement of the provinces of Oudh (Section 3), Financial Commissioner of Oudh (Section 33).

schedules_summary.description: Contains orders from the Government of India, Foreign Department, dated 10th and 19th October 1859, regarding the Taluqdárí settlement of Oudh, conferring permanent proprietary rights, and protecting inferior Zamíndárs and village occupants.

Lists names of persons whose lands were specially exempted from confiscation by proclamation in March 1858, and who are deemed to possess specific rights and titles as Taluqdárs for the purposes of this Act.

act_identification.act_title: An Act to amend the law relating to Divorce and Matrimonial Causes

legislative_details.geographical_extent: The whole of India, including the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh (as made applicable by Notification No. S.O. 3912 (E), dated 30th October, 2019).

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to amend the law relating to the divorce of persons professing the Christian religion, and to confer upon certain Courts jurisdiction in matters matrimonial; it is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To amend the law relating to the divorce of persons professing the Christian religion and to confer jurisdiction in matrimonial matters upon certain Courts.

key_sections.title: Short title. Commencement of Act.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Extent of Act. Extent of power to grant relief generally, and to make decrees of dissolution, or of nullity.
key_sections.description: Defines the geographical extent of the Act and the conditions under which courts can grant relief, dissolution, or nullity decrees.

key_sections.title: Interpretation-clause.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Grounds for dissolution of marriage
key_sections.description: Specifies the grounds upon which a marriage may be dissolved by a petition to the District Court.

key_sections.title: Dissolution of marriage by mutual consent.
key_sections.description: Allows for dissolution of marriage by mutual consent of both parties under specified conditions.

key_sections.title: Petition for decree of nullity.
key_sections.description: Enables a husband or wife to petition the District Court for a decree of nullity of marriage.

key_sections.title: Grounds of decree.

key_sections.title: Bar to decree for divorce a mensa et toro; but judicial separation obtainable by husband or wife.

key_sections.title: Deserted wife may apply to court for protection.
key_sections.description: Allows a deserted wife to petition the District Court for an order to protect her property.

key_sections.title: Petition for restitution of conjugal rights.
key_sections.description: Enables a husband or wife to petition the District Court for restitution of conjugal rights if the other party has withdrawn without reasonable excuse.

key_sections.title: Alimony pendente lite.
key_sections.description: Provides for a wife to petition for expenses of proceedings and alimony pending the suit.

key_sections.title: Power to order permanent alimony.
key_sections.description: Grants the District Court power to order permanent alimony to the wife upon dissolution or judicial separation.

key_sections.title: Power to make orders as to custody of children in suit for separation.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Court to make interim orders and provisions regarding the custody, maintenance, and education of minor children in judicial separation suits.

key_sections.title: Code of Civil Procedure to apply.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that proceedings under this Act shall be regulated by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

key_sections.title: Liberty to parties to marry again.
key_sections.description: Grants liberty to parties to marry again after a decree for dissolution or nullity of marriage has become final.

Power to Courts to make decrees of nullity of marriage (Section 2)

act_overview.preamble: Whereas it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to the District and other subordinate Civil Courts in the Presidency of Bombay; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the District and other subordinate Civil Courts in the Presidency of Bombay, establishing their structure, jurisdiction, and administration.

key_sections.title: Short title. Extent of Act.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical extent of application.

key_sections.title: Alteration and creation of Districts.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Governor of Bombay in Council to alter limits of existing districts and create new ones.

key_sections.title: District Judges.
key_sections.description: Establishes a District Court in each District presided over by a District Judge appointed by the Governor of Bombay in Council.

key_sections.title: Original jurisdiction of District Judge.
key_sections.description: Declares the District Court as the principal Court of original civil jurisdiction in the District.

key_sections.title: His appellate jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Defines the District Court as the Court of Appeal from decrees and orders of Subordinate Courts.

key_sections.title: Control and inspection of Courts.
key_sections.description: Grants the District Judge general control over Civil Courts and their establishments within the District, including inspection duties.

key_sections.title: Power to appoint Joint Judges.
key_sections.description: Allows the Governor of Bombay in Council to appoint Joint Judges with co-extensive powers and concurrent jurisdiction with the District Judge.

key_sections.title: Power to appoint Assistant Judges.
key_sections.description: Enables the Governor of Bombay in Council to appoint Assistants to the District Judge.

key_sections.title: Original jurisdiction of Assistant Judge.
key_sections.description: Allows District Judges to refer original suits and miscellaneous applications to Assistant Judges, specifying their jurisdiction limits.

key_sections.title: Number of Subordinate Civil Courts.
key_sections.description: States that each District shall have Subordinate Civil Courts as directed by the Governor of Bombay in Council.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Subordinate Judges.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of Subordinate Judges by the Governor of Bombay in Council and sets qualification criteria.

key_sections.title: Classes of Subordinate Judges.
key_sections.description: Divides Subordinate Judges into two classes and defines their respective jurisdictions.

key_sections.title: Reference of Government suits.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that suits involving the Government or its officers must be referred to the District Judge, not Subordinate Judges or Small Cause Courts.

key_sections.title: Commission of enquiry into alleged misconduct.
key_sections.description: Empowers the High Court to conduct enquiries into alleged misconduct of Subordinate Judges and impose penalties.

key_sections.title: Appointment, etc., of ministerial officers.
key_sections.description: Governs the appointment, fining, suspension, or dismissal of ministerial officers of Civil Courts by the District Judge or Subordinate Judges.

act_identification.act_title: THE OUDH TALUQDARS’ RELIEF ACT, 1870

legislative_details.enacted_by: GOVERNOR GENERAL OF INDIA IN COUNCIL.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS many of the taluqdárs of Oudh are in debt, and their immoveable property is subject to mortgages, charges and liens; and whereas it is expedient to provide for their relief in manner hereinafter appearing; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to provide relief to taluqdars in Oudh whose immoveable properties are burdened with debts, mortgages, charges, and liens. It establishes a mechanism for the management of their estates and the settlement of their financial liabilities through an appointed Manager.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Oudh Taluqdárs' Relief Act.'

key_sections.title: Interpretation-clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'Chief Commissioner', 'taluqdár', and 'heir'.

key_sections.title: Power to vest management of taluqdár's property in an officer appointed by Chief Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Chief Commissioner to appoint a Manager and vest in him the management of a taluqdár's immoveable property upon application, with the Governor General's consent.

key_sections.title: Effect of order.
key_sections.description: Outlines the consequences of the vesting order, including barring pending suits, freeing the taluqdár from arrest for prior debts, exempting moveable and immoveable property from attachment, and rendering the taluqdár incompetent to alienate property.

key_sections.title: Manager to receive rents and profits.
key_sections.description: Details the Manager's duties to receive rents and profits, and to apply them towards government revenue, taluqdár's maintenance, repairs, management costs, and settlement of debts.

key_sections.title: Notice to claimants against taluqdár.
key_sections.description: Requires the Manager to publish a notice calling upon all persons with claims against the taluqdár or his property to notify them within three months.

key_sections.title: Debt or liability not duty notified, to be barred.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that debts or liabilities not duly notified to the Manager within the specified time shall be barred, with a proviso for admission within a further nine-month period.

key_sections.title: Determination of debts and liabilities.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Manager to determine the amount of debts and liabilities owed to creditors and those holding charges on the property, in accordance with rules.

key_sections.title: Scheme for settlement of debts and liabilities.
key_sections.description: Requires the Manager to prepare a scheme for debt settlement, which, upon approval by the Chief Commissioner, shall be implemented.

key_sections.title: Restoration of taluqdár to his property.
key_sections.description: Provides for the restoration of the taluqdár to his property once all debts are discharged, or if the Chief Commissioner decides the Act's provisions should no longer apply, and outlines the revival of barred proceedings and debts in certain cases.

key_sections.title: Manager to have powers of a taluqdar.
key_sections.description: Grants the Manager powers similar to a taluqdar for realizing rents and allows him to apply to the Deputy Commissioner's Court to remove a mortgagee in possession.

key_sections.title: Power to raise money by mortgage or sale.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Manager, with the Chief Commissioner's assent, to raise money for debt settlement by mortgaging or selling parts of the property.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Chief Commissioner to make rules consistent with the Act, which, upon approval by the Governor General in Council and publication, shall have the force of law.

key_sections.title: Bar of suits.
key_sections.description: Prohibits suits or proceedings against any person for actions done bona fide pursuant to this Act.

key_sections.title: Saving of jurisdiction of Courts in Oudh in respect of certain suits.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not preclude Oudh Courts from entertaining suits related to succession or maintenance rights concerning property under the Act, provided the Manager is made a party.

powers_conferred: Chief Commissioner: Power to vest management of taluqdár's property in an officer (Manager) (Section 3).
Chief Commissioner: Power to approve scheme for settlement of debts and liabilities (Section 11).
Chief Commissioner: Power to send back scheme for revision (Section 11).
Chief Commissioner: Power to make rules consistent with the Act (Section 20).
Chief Commissioner: Power to appoint new Managers (Section 21).
Manager: Power to receive and recover rents and profits (Section 5).
Manager: Power to publish notice to claimants (Section 6).
Manager: Power to determine debts and liabilities (Section 9).
Manager: Power to prepare and submit scheme for settlement of debts (Section 11).
Manager: Power to call for further particulars of claims (Section 13).
Manager: Power to summon witnesses and compel production of documents (Section 14).
Manager: Power to administer oaths (Section 15).
Manager: Powers of a taluqdar for realizing rents and profits (Section 17).
Manager: Power to apply to Court of Deputy Commissioner for delivery of property from mortgagee (Section 17).
Manager: Power to lease property for a term not exceeding twenty years (Section 18).
Manager: Power to raise money by mortgage or sale of property (Section 19).
Governor General of India in Council: Power to give previous consent for Manager appointment (Section 3).
Governor General of India in Council: Power to approve rules made by Chief Commissioner (Section 20).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Chief Commissioner appoints the Manager.

applies_to: Taluqdárs in Oudh
Taluqdárs who apply for the provisions of this Act to be applied to their case
exemptions: Debts due, or liabilities incurred, to Government
Moveable property from attachment or sale for prior debts other than debts to Government
Immoveable property from attachment or sale except for debts to Government
Petitions, applications, memoranda of appeal, or other proceedings under this Act from Court fees
special_provisions: Courts of the Province of Oudh retain jurisdiction for suits relating to succession or maintenance from immoveable property under the Act, provided the Manager is made a party.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Chief Commissioner, with approval from the Governor General of India in Council.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the appointment of a Manager who takes over the management of the taluqdár's immoveable property, receives rents and profits, determines and settles debts, and has powers to summon witnesses and compel document production. The Manager's investigations are deemed judicial proceedings.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Court of the Deputy Commissioner (for delivery of property from mortgagee); Courts of the Province of Oudh (for succession/maintenance suits, with Manager as party).

act_identification.act_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Trespasses by Cattle.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India except [3] [the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States], and the presidency-towns and such local areas as the State Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, may from time to time exclude from its operation.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to trespasses by cattle; It is hereby enacted as follows :—
act_overview.purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to trespasses by cattle, including provisions for impounding cattle, levying fines, and addressing damages caused by cattle trespass.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER IV DELIVERY OR SALE OF CATTLE
CHAPTER V COMPLAINTS OF ILLEGAL SEIZURE OR DETENTION

key_sections.title: Title and extent.
key_sections.description: Defines the short title of the Act and its geographical application.

key_sections.title: Interpretation clause.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment of pounds.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of cattle pounds at specified locations.

key_sections.title: Appointment of pound-keepers. Pound-keepers may hold other offices. Pound-keepers to be public servants.
key_sections.description: Details the appointment of pound-keepers, their ability to hold other offices, and their status as public servants.

key_sections.title: Cattle damaging land.
key_sections.description: Empowers cultivators, occupiers, or those with interest in land to seize cattle trespassing and causing damage.

key_sections.title: Cattle damaging public roads, canals and embankments.
key_sections.description: Authorizes persons in charge of public infrastructure to seize cattle causing damage or straying thereon.

key_sections.title: Fines for cattle impounded.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the levy of fines for impounded cattle according to scales set by the State Government.

key_sections.title: Procedure when owner claims the cattle and pays fines and charges.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for the release of impounded cattle upon payment of fines and charges by the owner.

key_sections.title: Procedure when owner refuses or omits to pay the fines and expenses.
key_sections.description: Describes the public auction and sale of cattle if the owner fails to pay fines and expenses.

key_sections.title: Power to make complaints.
key_sections.description: Grants individuals the right to complain to a Magistrate regarding illegal seizure or detention of their cattle.

key_sections.title: Penalty for forcibly opposing the seizure of cattle or rescuing the same.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals who forcibly resist the seizure of cattle or rescue them after seizure.

key_sections.title: Penalty for damage caused to land or crops or public roads by pigs.
key_sections.description: Imposes a fine on owners or keepers of pigs who cause damage by allowing them to trespass.

key_sections.title: Saving of right to sue for compensation.
key_sections.description: Preserves the right of individuals to sue for compensation in a competent court for damage caused by cattle trespass.

key_sections.title: Power for State Government to transfer certain functions to local authority.
key_sections.description: Allows the State Government to transfer its functions or those of the District Magistrate under this Act to local authorities.

powers_conferred: Cultivator or occupier of land, or person with interest in crop/produce, may seize or cause to be seized cattle trespassing on such land and doing damage (Section 10).
Officers of police shall aid in preventing resistance to seizures and rescues (Section 10).

Persons in charge of public roads, pleasure-grounds, plantations, canals, drainage-works, embankments and the like, and officers of police, may seize or cause to be seized cattle doing damage or straying thereon (Section 11).
Pound-keepers shall levy fines for impounded cattle (Section 12).
Magistrate of the District directs establishment of pounds and determines villages to use them (Section 4).
Magistrate of the District controls pounds and fixes/alters rates for feeding and watering (Section 5).
State Government shall appoint pound-keepers (Section 6).
Magistrate may award compensation for illegal seizure or detention (Section 22).
State Government may transfer functions under this Act to any local authority (Section 31).
State Government may make rules for carrying into effect the purposes of this Act (Maharashtra Amendment, Section 32).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever forcibly opposes the seizure of cattle or rescues them after seizure shall be punished with imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months, or with fine not exceeding five hundred rupees, or with both (Section 24). Any fine for mischief by causing cattle to trespass may be recovered by sale of the cattle (Section 25). Any owner or keeper of pigs causing damage by trespass shall be punished with fine not exceeding ten rupees (Section 26). Any pound-keeper failing to perform duties shall be punished with fine not exceeding fifty rupees (Section 27).

related_acts: Cattle-trespass Act, 1871 (Hyd. Act V of 1837, 1 of 1871)
Cattle-trespass (Bombay Extension and Amendment) Act, 1959 (Bom. XIII of 1959)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government shall appoint a pound-keeper for every pound.

applies_to: the whole of India
exemptions: the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States
the presidency-towns
such local areas as the State Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, may from time to time exclude from its operation
special_provisions: Maharashtra State Amendment to sections 1, 10, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 26, 28, 29 and insertion of new sections 12A, 12B, 32.
Assam State Amendment to section 26 and insertion of new section 26A.
Uttar Pradesh Amendment of section 26 and 28.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rule for carrying into effect the purposes of this Act (Maharashtra Amendment, Section 32).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement involves the seizure and impounding of trespassing cattle, levy of fines by pound-keepers, and public auction of cattle if fines and expenses are not paid. Complaints regarding illegal seizure or detention are handled by Magistrates, who can award compensation. Penalties are prescribed for obstructing seizure, rescuing cattle, or causing damage, enforced by Magistrates.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate, Civil Court

act_identification.act_title: THE DEHRA DUN ACT, 1871

legislative_details.geographical_extent: The district under the Superintendent of the Dehra Dun, specifically the district of Dehra Dun, excluding the portion called Jaunsar Bawar.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of High Court and Board of Revenue over Dehra Dun.

key_sections.title: District Court of Saharanpur to be District Court of Dehra Dun.
