key_sections.title: Exemption of Jaunsar Bawar.

act_identification.act_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to pensions and grants by Government of money or land-revenue.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: In so far as it relates to Union pensions, it extends to the whole of India and in so far as it relates to other pensions, it extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. (For the State of Karnataka, it extends to the whole of the State of Karnataka.)

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to pensions and grants by Government of money or land-revenue; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws concerning pensions and grants of money or land-revenue provided by the Government. It regulates claims, mode of payment, and administration of such pensions and grants, and restricts the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in certain matters related to them.

key_sections.title: Short title. Extent of Act.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's short title and its geographical application across India, with a specific amendment for Karnataka.

key_sections.title: Interpretation-section.
key_sections.description: Defines the expression 'grant of money or land-revenue' for the purposes of this Act.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines 'the appropriate Government' in relation to Union and other pensions.

key_sections.title: Bar of suits relating to pensions.
key_sections.description: Prohibits Civil Courts from entertaining suits concerning pensions or grants conferred by the Government, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Claims to be made to Collector, Deputy Commissioner, or other authorized officer.
key_sections.description: Specifies that claims related to pensions or grants must be preferred to designated officers who will dispose of them according to prescribed rules.

key_sections.title: Civil Court empowered to take cognizance of such claims.
key_sections.description: Allows Civil Courts to take cognizance of claims upon receiving a certificate from an authorized officer, but restricts their power to affect Government's liability.

key_sections.title: Payment to be made by Collector, Deputy Commissioner or other authorized officer.
key_sections.description: Mandates that all pensions or grants by Government shall be paid by specified officers, subject to rules prescribed by the Chief Controlling Revenue-Authority.

key_sections.title: Exemption of pension from attachment.
key_sections.description: Exempts certain types of pensions and allowances from seizure, attachment, or sequestration by any Court at the instance of a creditor.

key_sections.title: Assignments, &c., in anticipation of pension, to be void.
key_sections.description: Declares all assignments, agreements, and securities made in anticipation of pension payments as null and void.

key_sections.title: Nomination by pensioner to receive moneys outstanding on account of pension.
key_sections.description: Allows a pensioner to nominate a person to receive unpaid pension moneys after their death, with provisions for a substitute nominee.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the Chief Controlling Revenue Authority in each State to make rules consistent with the Act regarding pension administration.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the Central Government to make rules concerning nominations under section 12A.

key_sections.title: Laying of rules.
key_sections.description: Requires rules made by the Central Government or Chief Controlling Revenue Authority to be laid before each House of Parliament.

powers_conferred: Power to dispose of claims relating to pensions or grants (Collector, Deputy Commissioner, or other authorized officer under Section 5).
Power to order commutation of pensions (appropriate Government under Section 10).
Power to make rules respecting pension administration (Chief Controlling Revenue Authority under Section 14).
Power to make rules regarding nominations (Central Government under Section 15).

repealed_acts: the Repealing Act, 1938 (1 of 1938)
Act 10 of 1914
Act 12 of 1891
Mysore Act 14 of 1955

applies_to: Union pensions
other pensions
persons having a claim relating to any such pension or grant
exemptions: Pensions granted or continued by Government on political considerations, or on account of past services or present infirmities or as a compassionate allowance, and any money due on account of such pension or allowance, are exempt from seizure, attachment or sequestration by process of any Court.
special_provisions: State Amendment for Karnataka modifies sections 1, 5, and 8.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Chief Controlling Revenue Authority (in each State) and Central Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Claims are made to the Collector, Deputy Commissioner, or other authorized officer. Civil Courts can take cognizance of claims upon receiving a certificate. Payments are made by the Collector, Deputy Commissioner, or other authorized officer.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil Courts (with limitations on jurisdiction).

act_identification.act_title: An Act for declaring which of certain rules, laws and regulations have the force of law in the Punjab, and for other purposes.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the territories which immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in the States of Punjab and Delhi

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS certain rules, laws and regulations, made heretofore for the Punjab, acquired the force of law under the provisions of section 25 of the Indian Councils Act, 1861; and whereas it is expedient to declare which of the said rules, laws and regulations shall henceforth be in force in the Punjab, and to amend, consolidate or repeal others of the said rules, orders and regulations; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to declare which existing rules, laws, and regulations previously made for the Punjab shall have the force of law, and to amend, consolidate, or repeal others. It aims to clarify the legal framework in the specified territories.

chapter_titles: Minors and the Court of Wards

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Punjab Laws Act, 1872'.

key_sections.title: Local extent. Commencement.
key_sections.description: Defines the geographical extent of the Act's application and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Enactments in force.
key_sections.description: Declares that Regulations, Acts, and orders specified in the First Schedule are in force to the extent specified.

key_sections.title: Decisions in certain cases to be according to Native law.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the rule of decision for questions regarding succession, personal laws, and religious usages, prioritizing custom, Muhammadan law, or Hindu law.

key_sections.title: Decisions in cases not specially provided for.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that judges shall decide according to justice, equity, and good conscience in cases not otherwise provided for.

key_sections.title: Local customs and mercantile usages when valid.
key_sections.description: Declares local customs and mercantile usages valid unless contrary to justice, equity, good conscience, or previously declared void.

key_sections.title: Power to establish system of village-watchmen and municipal-watchmen, and to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to establish and make rules for village and municipal watchmen systems, covering their appointment, duties, and payment.

key_sections.title: Obligation to assist watchmen and headmen.

key_sections.title: State Government may confer powers of police-officer.

key_sections.title: Trackers may call for assistance in carrying on tracks.

key_sections.title: Penalty for withholding assistance or conniving at offence or escape.

key_sections.title: Control of slaughter of kine and sale of beef.
key_sections.description: Subjects the slaughter of kine and sale of beef to rules prescribed by the State Government.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules as to matters mentioned in sections 43 to 48.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules concerning matters specified in sections 43 to 48.

key_sections.title: Penalties for breach of such rules.
key_sections.description: Allows the State Government to prescribe penalties for breaches of rules made under the Act, including imprisonment or fine.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN CONTRACT ACT, 1872

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to define and amend certain parts of the law relating to contracts;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to define and amend certain parts of the law relating to contracts. It provides a legal framework for the formation, performance, and breach of contracts, as well as specific types of agreements like indemnity, guarantee, bailment, and agency.

chapter_titles: OF THE COMMUNICATION, ACCEPTANCE AND REVOCATION OF PROPOSALS
OF CONTRACTS, VOIDABLE CONTRACTS AND VOID AGREEMENTS
OF CERTAIN RELATIONS RESEMBLING THOSE CREATED BY CONTRACT
OF THE CONSEQUENCES OF BREACH OF CONTRACT

key_sections.title: Short title. Extent. Commencement. Saving.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its geographical extent, and commencement date, along with a saving clause for existing statutes, usages, and customs.

key_sections.title: Interpretation-clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as proposal, promise, consideration, agreement, contract, void, and voidable contract.

key_sections.title: What agreements are contracts.
key_sections.description: States the essential conditions for an agreement to become a contract: free consent, competent parties, lawful consideration, lawful object, and not expressly declared void.

key_sections.title: Who are competent to contract.
key_sections.description: Specifies that persons of majority age, sound mind, and not disqualified by law are competent to contract.

key_sections.title: “Free consent” defined.
key_sections.description: Defines when consent is considered free, listing factors like coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation, and mistake that can vitiate consent.

key_sections.title: What considerations and objects are lawful, and what not.
key_sections.description: Outlines when the consideration or object of an agreement is unlawful, rendering the agreement void.

key_sections.title: Agreement without consideration, void, unless it is in writing and registered, or is a promise to compensate for something done, or is a promise to pay a debt barred by limitation law.
key_sections.description: Establishes the general rule that agreements without consideration are void, with specific exceptions.

key_sections.title: Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings, void.
key_sections.description: States that agreements restricting legal proceedings or limiting the time to enforce rights are void, with exceptions for arbitration agreements and bank/financial institution guarantees.

key_sections.title: “Contingent contract” defined.
key_sections.description: Defines a contingent contract as one to do or not to do something if a collateral event does or does not happen.

key_sections.title: Agreement to do impossible act.
key_sections.description: Declares agreements to do impossible acts as void and addresses contracts that become impossible or unlawful after formation.

key_sections.title: Obligation of person who has received advantage under void agreement, or contract that becomes void.
key_sections.description: Mandates restoration or compensation for advantages received under agreements discovered to be void or contracts that become void.

key_sections.title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract.
key_sections.description: Provides for compensation for loss or damage naturally arising from a breach of contract or known to be likely to result from it.

key_sections.title: “Contract of indemnity” defined.
key_sections.description: Defines a contract of indemnity as one where one party promises to save another from loss caused by the conduct of the promisor or any other person.

key_sections.title: “Contract of guarantee”, “surety”, “principal debtor” and “creditor”.
key_sections.description: Defines a contract of guarantee and the roles of surety, principal debtor, and creditor.

key_sections.title: “Bailment”, “bailor” and “bailee” defined.
key_sections.description: Defines bailment as the delivery of goods by one person to another for some purpose, and identifies the bailor and bailee.

key_sections.title: “Agent” and “principal” defined.
key_sections.description: Defines an agent as a person employed to do any act for another, or to represent another in dealings with third persons, and the principal as the person for whom such act is done.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract (Section 73), including cases where a penalty is stipulated (Section 74). A party rightfully rescinding a contract is entitled to compensation (Section 75). Compensation is also provided for loss through non-performance of acts known to be impossible or unlawful (Section 56). A bailee is liable for compensation for unauthorized use of bailed goods (Section 154). An agent must make compensation to the principal for direct consequences of neglect, want of skill, or misconduct (Section 212) and is not entitled to remuneration for misconducted business (Section 220). A pretended agent is liable to make compensation for loss or damage incurred by a third person (Section 235).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through legal proceedings, primarily by providing for compensation for breach of contract and defining the rights and obligations of parties to various types of contracts. Courts determine reasonable compensation and enforce contractual terms.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to the solemnization in India of the marriages of persons professing the Christian religion; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the solemnization in India of the marriages of persons professing the Christian religion.

chapter_titles: PART I THE PERSONS BY WHOM MARRIAGES MAY BE SOLEMNIZED
PART II TIME AND PLACE AT WHICH MARRIAGES MAY BE SOLEMNIZED
PART III MARRIAGES SOLEMNIZED BY MINISTERS OF RELIGION LICENSED UNDER THIS ACT
PART IV REGISTRATION OF MARRIAGES SOLEMNIZED BY MINISTERS OF RELIGION
PART V MARRIAGES SOLEMNIZED BY, OR IN THE PRESENCE OF, A MARRIAGE REGISTRAR

key_definitions: Registrar General of Births, Deaths and Marriages

key_sections.title: Short title. Extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its geographical extent of application.

key_sections.title: Interpretation clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Church of England', 'minor', 'Christians', and 'Indian Christians'.

key_sections.title: Marriages to be solemnized according to Act.
key_sections.description: States that every marriage between Christians must be solemnized according to the Act's provisions, otherwise it shall be void.

key_sections.title: Persons by whom marriages may be solemnized.
key_sections.description: Lists the authorized persons who can solemnize marriages in India under this Act, including ordained ministers, Clergymen of the Church of Scotland, licensed Ministers of Religion, Marriage Registrars, and licensed persons for Indian Christians.

key_sections.title: Grant and revocation of licenses to solemnize marriages.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to grant and revoke licenses to Ministers of Religion to solemnize marriages.

key_sections.title: Marriage Registrars.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the State Government to appoint Marriage Registrars and Senior Marriage Registrars, and specifies when a Magistrate acts as a Marriage Registrar.

key_sections.title: Time for solemnizing marriage.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the hours between which marriages must be solemnized, with exceptions for special licenses from Anglican or Roman Catholic Bishops, and for Clergymen of the Church of Scotland.

key_sections.title: Consent of father, or guardian, or mother.
key_sections.description: Specifies whose consent is required for the marriage of a minor, prioritizing the father, then guardian, then mother, unless no such person resides in India.

key_sections.title: Solemnization of marriage.
key_sections.description: States that after the certificate is issued, marriage may be solemnized according to the Minister's chosen form or ceremony, in the presence of at least two witnesses.

key_sections.title: On what conditions marriages of [1][Indian] Christians may be certified.
key_sections.description: Outlines the conditions for certifying marriages of Indian Christians, including age requirements (man not under twenty-one, woman not under eighteen), absence of a living spouse, and specific declarations made in the presence of a licensed person and witnesses.

key_sections.title: False oath, declaration, notice or certificate for procuring marriage.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for intentionally making false oaths, declarations, or signing false notices or certificates for procuring a marriage or license.

key_sections.title: Solemnizing marriage without due authority.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for solemnizing or professing to solemnize a Christian marriage without proper authorization under Section 5.

key_sections.title: Non-validation of marriages within prohibited degrees.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not validate any marriage forbidden by the personal law applicable to either party.

powers_conferred: State Government to grant and revoke licenses to Ministers of Religion to solemnize marriages (Section 6).
State Government to appoint Marriage Registrars and Senior Marriage Registrars (Section 7).
State Government to grant and revoke licenses to Christians to grant certificates of marriage between Indian Christians (Section 9).
Anglican Bishop of the Diocese or his Commissary to grant special licenses for solemnizing marriage outside prescribed hours or places (Sections 10, 11).
Roman Catholic Bishop of the Diocese or Vicariate to grant general or special licenses for solemnizing marriage outside prescribed hours (Section 10).
Minister of Religion licensed under the Act to solemnize marriages and issue certificates (Sections 5, 17).
Marriage Registrar to solemnize marriages and issue certificates (Sections 5, 41).
High Court Judge or District Judge to order issuance of certificate in less than fourteen days (Section 43).
High Court Judge or District Judge to examine allegations and declare marriage proper when consent is withheld or person is insane (Section 45).
High Court Judge or District Judge to decide on Marriage Registrar's refusal to issue certificate (Section 46).
High Court Judge or District Judge to declare if a person forbidding a certificate is not authorized (Section 48).
State Government to prescribe fees for various services under the Act (Section 82).
State Government to make rules regarding fees, register-books, and returns of marriages (Section 83).
State Government to declare who shall be the District Judge (Section 85).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Part VII of the Act outlines various offences and penalties. These include: making false oaths, declarations, or signing false notices/certificates for procuring marriage (punishable under IPC Section 193, with imprisonment up to three years and fine); forbidding certificate issuance by false personation (punishable under IPC Section 205); solemnizing marriage without due authority (imprisonment up to ten years, or transportation for seven to ten years, and fine); solemnizing marriage out of proper time or without witnesses (imprisonment up to three years and fine); a Minister of Religion solemnizing marriage without notice or with a minor within fourteen days without consent (imprisonment up to three years and fine); a Marriage Registrar committing offences like issuing certificates or solemnizing marriage without publishing notice, after expiry of notice, with a minor within fourteen days without court authority, or against authorized prohibition (imprisonment up to five years and fine); a Marriage Registrar issuing certificate after expiry of notice, or with a minor within fourteen days, or against authorized prohibition (punishable under IPC Section 166); other authorized persons committing similar offences (imprisonment up to four years and fine); an unlicensed person granting a certificate pretending to be licensed (imprisonment up to five years and fine); a licensed person refusing or neglecting duties (fine up to one hundred rupees); and wilfully destroying, injuring, falsifying register-books or certificates (imprisonment up to seven years and fine). Prosecutions must commence within two years of the offence.

The Act does not apply to the Renoncants of the Union territory of Pondicherry.
special_provisions: The Act does not extend to the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in the States of Travancore-Cochin, Manipur. The words “State of Jammu and Kashmir” were omitted by Act 34 of 2019.
Special licenses can be granted by Anglican Bishops or Roman Catholic Bishops for solemnizing marriages outside prescribed hours or places.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The State Government has the power to make rules by notification in the Official Gazette regarding the disposal of fees, supply of register-books, and preparation and submission of returns of marriages.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the solemnization and registration of marriages by authorized persons and Marriage Registrars. It mandates the keeping of marriage registers, quarterly returns to the Registrar General, and provides for corrections of errors, searches, and certified copies of entries as evidence. Penalties are prescribed for various offences related to solemnization, registration, and false declarations.

act_overview.preamble: Preamble.—WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to the Civil Courts of the Madras Presidency subordinate to the High Court; It is hereby enacted as follows :—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to consolidate and amend the existing law pertaining to the Civil Courts within the Madras Presidency that are subordinate to the High Court. It aims to establish and regulate the constitution, jurisdiction, and administration of these civil courts.

chapter_titles: PART II. ESTABLISHMENT AND CONSTITUTION OF CIVIL COURTS.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its local extent, and the date of its commencement.

key_sections.title: Number of District Courts.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Local Government to fix and alter the number of District Courts, with sanction from the Governor General in Council for increases.

key_sections.title: Number of Subordinate Judges and District Munsifs.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Local Government to fix and alter the number of Subordinate Judges and District Munsifs, with sanction from the Governor General in Council for additions.

key_sections.title: Appointment to vacancy in office of District Munsif.
key_sections.description: Details the appointment process for District Munsifs by the High Court, requiring specific qualifications, and allows the Local Government to annul such appointments.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of District Judge or subordinate Judge in original suits.
key_sections.description: Defines the jurisdiction of District Judges, Subordinate Judges, and District Munsifs in original suits and proceedings of a civil nature, including monetary limits for District Munsifs.

key_sections.title: Appeals from decrees of District Courts.
key_sections.description: Specifies the appellate jurisdiction for decrees and orders from District Courts (to High Court), Subordinate Judges and District Munsifs (to District Court or High Court based on value), and allows for transfer of appeals.

key_sections.title: Law administered by Courts to Natives.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the application of Muhammadan law, Hindu law, or custom in cases involving succession, inheritance, marriage, caste, or religious usage for Natives, and justice, equity, and good conscience otherwise.

key_sections.title: Judges not to try suits in which they are interested;
key_sections.description: Prohibits Judges from trying suits or appeals in which they are personally interested or from appeals against decrees they passed in another capacity.

key_sections.title: Sespension of Judge by Local Government.
key_sections.description: Grants the Local Government the power to suspend or remove any District Judge, Subordinate Judge, or District Munsif for misconduct.

key_sections.title: Suspension of District Munsif by High Court. Commission of Inquiry.
key_sections.description: Empowers the High Court to suspend District Munsifs for alleged misconduct or appoint a commission of inquiry, applying Act XXXVII of 1850.

key_sections.title: Appointment, suspension or removal of Ministerial Officers of District Courts.
key_sections.description: Governs the appointment, suspension, and removal of Ministerial Officers of District Courts by the Judges of such Courts, subject to High Court control.

key_sections.title: District Judge to control Civil Courts of District.
key_sections.description: Vests the general control over all Civil Courts in a District under this Act in the District Judge, subject to High Court rules.

key_sections.title: Investiture of [2][District or] Subordinate Judge with Small Cause jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Allows the Local Government to invest District or Subordinate Judges and District Munsifs with Small Cause jurisdiction up to specified monetary limits.

key_sections.title: Exercise by Subordinate Judge of jurisdiction of District Judge in certain proceedings.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the High Court to allow Subordinate Judges to take cognizance of, or District Judges to transfer to Subordinate Judges, certain proceedings under the Indian Succession Act, 1925.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to amend the law relating to the payment of deposits in Government Savings Banks; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate and channelize public savings into Government Savings Schemes. It amends the law concerning the payment of deposits in Government Savings Banks, particularly addressing nominations, payments on death, and deposits belonging to minors and lunatics, while also providing for the framing and management of various savings schemes.

key_sections.title: Short title. Local extent.
key_sections.description: Defines the short title of the Act and its geographical application.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Framing of Savings Schemes.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to frame, amend, or discontinue Savings Schemes and modify the Schedule.

key_sections.title: Deposit by minor.
key_sections.description: Allows minors aged ten years or more to open and operate accounts, and guardians to do so on behalf of minors.

key_sections.title: Nomination by depositor.
key_sections.description: Enables depositors to designate nominees to receive sums upon their death and specifies conditions for such nominations.

key_sections.title: Payment on death of depositor.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for payment of deposits to nominees or guardians upon the death of a depositor.

key_sections.title: Payment to be discharge. Saving of right of executor. Saving of right of creditor.
key_sections.description: States that payments made under the Act discharge liability and preserves the rights of executors, administrators, and creditors.

key_sections.title: Power to call for information.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to request information, documents, and evidence related to accounts.

key_sections.title: Payment of deposits to minor or guardian.
key_sections.description: Specifies how deposits made by or on behalf of a minor are to be paid.

key_sections.title: Payment of deposits belonging to lunatics.
key_sections.description: Addresses the payment of deposits belonging to depositors who become insane or incapable of managing their affairs.

key_sections.title: Protection against attachment.
key_sections.description: Provides that amounts in the Public Provident Fund Scheme are not liable to attachment under court decrees.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Government Savings Certificates Act, 1959 and the Public Provident Fund Act, 1968, with savings provisions.

act_identification.act_title: THE NORTHERN INDIA CANAL AND DRAINAGE ACT, 1873
act_identification.act_short_title: The Northern India Canal and Drainage Act, 1873

legislative_details.geographical_extent: It extends to [1][Uttar Pradesh and the [2][territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in the States of Punjab and Delhi]] and applies to all lands whether permanently settled, temporarily settled, or free from revenue.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS, throughout the territories to which this Act extends, the State Government is entitled to use and control for public purposes the water of all rivers and streams flowing in natural channels, and of all lakes and other natural collections of still water; and whereas it is expedient to amend the law relating to irrigation, navigation and drainage in the said territories; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the use and control of water resources by the State Government for public purposes, specifically for irrigation, navigation, and drainage. It establishes a framework for the construction and maintenance of canals and drainage works, the supply of water, and the recovery of associated charges.

chapter_titles: PART II: OF THE APPLICATION OF WATER FOR PUBLIC PURPOSES
PART III: OF THE CONSTRUCTION AND MAINTENANCE OF WORKS
PART IV: OF THE SUPPLY OF WATER
PART VIII: OF OBTAINING LABOUR FOR CANALS AND DRAINAGE-WORKS
PART X: OF OFFENCES AND PENALTIES

key_sections.title: Short title. Local extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its geographical application.

key_sections.title: Interpretation clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Canal', 'Water-course', 'Drainage-work', and various 'Canal-officers'.

key_sections.title: Notification to issue when water-supply is to be applied for public purposes.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to declare, by notification, its intention to apply or use water from natural sources for public canal or drainage works.

key_sections.title: Damage for which compensation shall not be awarded. Matters in respect of which compensation may be awarded.
key_sections.description: Specifies types of damage for which compensation will not be awarded and lists the specific matters for which compensation may be granted due to water-supply changes.

key_sections.title: Power to enter and survey, etc. Power to clear land. Power to inspect and regulate water-supply. Notice of intended entry into houses. Compensation for damage caused by entry.
key_sections.description: Grants Canal-officers powers to enter lands for survey, clear land, inspect water-supply, and mandates compensation for damage caused by such entry.

key_sections.title: Application by persons desiring to use canal-water. Contents of application. Liability of applicants for cost of works. Recovery of amount due.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for individuals to apply for canal water use, including application contents, liability for construction costs, and recovery of unpaid amounts.

key_sections.title: In absence of written contract, water-supply to be subject to rules.
key_sections.description: States that without a written contract, canal water supply is governed by rules made by the State Government.

key_sections.title: Conditions as to—power to stop water-supply; claims to compensation in case of failure or stoppage of supply; claims on account of interruption from other causes; duration of supply; sale or sub-letting of right to use canal-water; transfer, with land, of contracts for water; no right acquired by user.
key_sections.description: Sets out various conditions regarding water supply, including the Divisional Canal-officer's power to stop supply, compensation claims, duration of supply, and the non-acquisition of water rights by user.

key_sections.title: Charge on occupier for water, how determined. “Occupier’s rate.”
key_sections.description: Determines that rates for canal water supplied for irrigation to occupiers will be set by State Government rules and defines this as the 'occupier’s rate'.

key_sections.title: “Owner’s rate.”
key_sections.description: Allows for the imposition of an 'owner’s rate' on owners of canal-irrigated lands, in addition to the occupier's rate, based on the benefit derived from irrigation.

key_sections.title: Certified dues recoverable as land-revenue.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that any lawfully due and certified sum under this Part, if unpaid, is recoverable by the Collector as an arrear of land-revenue.

key_sections.title: Power to prohibit obstructions or order their removal.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to prohibit or order the removal/modification of obstructions in rivers, streams, or drainage-channels if they cause injury to land or public health.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction under this Act of Civil Courts.
key_sections.description: Grants Civil Courts jurisdiction over claims against the State Government under this Act, with a specific limitation on orders regarding water supply to crops.

key_sections.title: Offences under Act. Penalty.
key_sections.description: Lists various acts considered offences under the Act, such as damaging canals, interfering with water supply, and neglecting maintenance, and prescribes penalties.

key_sections.title: Power to make, alter and cancel rules. Publication of rules.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the State Government the power to make, alter, and cancel rules for regulating various matters under the Act, requiring their publication in the Official Gazette.

powers_conferred: State Government: To declare water for public purposes (S.5), appoint officers (S.4), make rules (S.75), prohibit/order removal of obstructions (S.55), cause drainage schemes to be drawn up (S.57), direct Collector to ascertain beneficiaries and number of labourers (S.64), fix/alter rates for labourers (S.65).
Canal-officer (general): To enter and survey lands, clear land, inspect/regulate water-supply (S.14), enter for repairs/prevent accidents (S.15).

Divisional Canal-officer: To stop water supply (S.32), issue orders for construction/repair of works for water-course passage (S.18), investigate claims between joint users of water-course (S.19), determine conditions for water supply through existing water-course (S.20), receive applications for new water-courses (S.21) or transfer of existing ones (S.23), seize/detain vessels (S.51), seize cargo/goods (S.52), take possession of abandoned vessels/unclaimed goods (S.54).

Collector: To give public notice for compensation claims (S.7), inquire into claims and determine compensation (S.10), recover amounts as arrears of land-revenue (S.16, S.18, S.19, S.28, S.45, S.47, S.60), inquire into lack of suitable canal crossings (S.17), receive objections to water-course construction/transfer (S.24), place applicant in occupation (S.25, S.27), determine compensation for land/water-course occupation (S.28), determine rent/compensation for land occupation (S.29), deal with compensation claims for drainage works (S.61), require lambardars to collect canal-dues (S.47), ascertain beneficiaries and number of labourers (S.64).
Magistrate: To impose fines and imprisonment for offences (S.70), direct compensation from fine (S.72).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 70 lists various offences including damaging canals, interfering with water supply, neglecting water-course maintenance, corrupting water, navigating canals contrary to rules, failing to supply labourers, destroying marks, passing on banks contrary to rules, and violating rules. The penalty is a fine not exceeding fifty rupees, or imprisonment not exceeding one month, or both.

act_identification.act_title: THE MARRIED WOMEN’S PROPERTY ACT, 1874

legislative_details.geographical_extent: It extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

act_overview.preamble:
Preamble.—WHEREAS it is expedient to make such provision as hereinafter appears for the enjoyment of wages and earnings by women married before the first day of January, 1866, and for insurances on lives by persons married before or after that day:
AND WHEREAS by the Indian Succession Act, 1865 (10 of 1865), section 4, it is enacted that no person shall by marriage acquire any interest in the property of the person whom he or she marries, nor become incapable of doing any act in respect of his or her own property, which he or she could have done, if unmarried:
AND WHEREAS by force of the said Act all women to whose marriages it applies are absolute owners of all property vested in, or acquired by, them, and their husbands do not by their marriage acquire any interest in such property, but the said Act does not protect such husbands from liabilities on account of the debts of their wives contracted before marriage, and does not expressly provide for the enforcement of claims by or against such wives:
It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to clarify and amend the law regarding the separate property rights of married women, particularly concerning their wages, earnings, and life insurance policies. It also addresses their capacity to sue and be sued, and defines the extent of a husband's liability for his wife's debts and breaches of trust.

chapter_titles: IV.—LEGAL PROCEEDINGS BY AND AGAINST MARRIED WOMEN
VI.—HUSBAND’S LIABILITY FOR WIFE’S BREACH OF TRUST OR DEVASTATION

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as The Married Women’s Property Act, 1874.

key_sections.title: Extent and application.
key_sections.description: Defines the geographical extent of the Act and specifies exemptions for married women professing certain religions or whose husbands profess those religions. It also grants power to the State Government to exempt certain groups.

key_sections.title: Married women’s earnings to be their separate property.
key_sections.description: Declares that wages, earnings, and property acquired by a married woman in her own employment, occupation, or trade, or through her skill, shall be her separate property.

key_sections.title: Married woman may effect policy of insurance.
key_sections.description: Allows any married woman to effect a policy of insurance on her own behalf, which shall be her separate property.

key_sections.title: Insurance by husband for benefit of wife.
key_sections.description: States that a policy of insurance effected by a married man for the benefit of his wife or children shall be a trust for their benefit, not subject to the husband's control or creditors, and specifies payment procedures.

key_sections.title: Married women may take legal proceedings.
key_sections.description: Empowers a married woman to maintain a suit in her own name for the recovery and protection of her separate property, with the same remedies as if unmarried.

key_sections.title: Wife’s liability for postnuptial debts.
key_sections.description: Makes a married woman liable to be sued for contracts made with reference to her separate property, to the extent of that property, as if she were unmarried.

key_sections.title: Husband not liable for wife’s antenuptial debts.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that a husband married after December 31, 1865, is not liable for his wife’s debts contracted before marriage, but the wife remains liable to the extent of her separate property.

key_sections.title: Extent of husband’s liability for wife’s breach of trust or devastation.
key_sections.description: Limits a husband's liability for his wife's breach of trust, misapplication, loss, or damage to an estate where she acts as a trustee, executrix, or administratrix, unless he actively participates.

powers_conferred: State Government may from time to time, by order, either retrospectively from the passing of this Act or prospectively, exempt from the operation of all or any of the provisions of this Act the members of any race, sect or tribe or part of a race, sect or tribe
State Government may also revoke any such order
Any married woman may effect a policy of insurance on her own behalf and independently of her husband

A married woman may maintain a suit in her own name for the recovery of property of any description which, by force of the said Indian Succession Act, 1865 (10 of 1865) or of this Act, is her separate property
she shall have, in her own name, the same remedies, both civil and criminal, against all persons, for the protection and security of such property, as if she were unmarried

related_acts: Act No. 17 of 1864 [to constitute an Office of Official Trustee]

applies_to: married women
exemptions: any married woman who at the time of her marriage professed the Hindu, Muhammadan, Buddhist, Sikh or Jaina religion, or whose husband, at the time of such marriage, professed any of those religions
members of any race, sect or tribe or part of a race, sect or tribe, to whom it may consider it impossible or inexpedient to apply such provisions (by State Government order)
special_provisions: The provisions of sub-section (1) of Section 6 shall apply in the case of any policy of insurance effected by any Hindu, Muhammadan, Sikh or Jain in Madras after 31/12/1913, or in any other territory to which this Act extended immediately before the commencement of the Married Women’s Property (Extension) Act, 1959, after 01/04/1923, or in any territory to which this Act extends on and from the commencement of the Married Women’s Property (Extension) Act, 1959.

The provisions of sub-section (1) of Section 6 shall apply in the case of any policy of insurance effected by a Buddhist in any territory to which this Act extends, on or after the commencement of the Married Women’s Property (Extension) Act, 1959.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Married women can maintain suits in their own name for property recovery and protection. Persons can sue married women for postnuptial debts related to their separate property.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: competent court

act_identification.act_title: THE LAWS LOCAL EXTENT ACT, 1874

legislative_details.enacted_by: Governor General of India in Council, the Legislative Council of India, and the Council of the Governor General of India assembled for the purpose of making Laws and Regulations
legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India, with specific provisions for the Presidencies of Fort St. George and Bombay, and the Lower and North-Western Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal, generally excluding Scheduled Districts and certain other specified territories.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to declare the local extent of certain Acts passed by the Governor General of India in Council, the Legislative Council of India, and the Council of the Governor General of India assembled for the purpose of making Laws and Regulations; AND WHEREAS it is also expedient to consolidate the laws relating to the local extent of certain Acts and Regulations in the Presidencies of Fort St. George and Bombay, and in the Lower and the North-Western Provinces of the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal; It is hereby declared and enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to declare the local extent of various Acts and Regulations passed by different legislative bodies in India. It also aims to consolidate existing laws concerning the local extent of these enactments across different presidencies and provinces.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Laws Local Extent Act, 1874'.

key_sections.title: Interpretation clause.
key_sections.description: Defines the expression 'Scheduled Districts' as the territories mentioned in the sixth schedule.

key_sections.title: Local extent of Acts in first schedule.
key_sections.description: Declares that Acts mentioned in the first schedule are in force in the whole of India, with specified exceptions including Scheduled Districts.

key_sections.title: Local extent of enactments in second schedule.
key_sections.description: Declares that enactments in the second schedule are in force throughout the territories subject to the government of Fort St. George, except Scheduled Districts.

key_sections.title: Local extent of enactments in third schedule.
key_sections.description: Declares that enactments in the third schedule are in force throughout the territories subject to the government of Bombay, except Scheduled Districts.

key_sections.title: Local extent of enactments in fourth schedule.
key_sections.description: Declares that enactments in the fourth schedule are in force throughout the territories subject to the Lieutenant-Governor of Bengal, except Scheduled Districts.

key_sections.title: Local extent of enactments in fifth schedule.
key_sections.description: Declares that enactments in the fifth schedule are in force throughout the territories subject to the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces of Fort William, except Scheduled Districts.

key_sections.title: Savings.
key_sections.description: Contains saving clauses, ensuring the Act does not bar certain powers of Central or State Governments, extend certain Acts, affect existing operations, revive repealed enactments, or extend laws to specific towns/parganas.

key_sections.title: Enactments repealed.
key_sections.description: This section, which originally dealt with repealed enactments, was itself repealed by the Repealing Act, 1876 (12 of 1876).

applies_to: Acts mentioned in the first schedule
Enactments mentioned in the second schedule (Madras Presidency)
Enactments mentioned in the third schedule (Bombay Presidency)
Enactments mentioned in the fourth schedule (Lower Provinces of Bengal)
Enactments mentioned in the fifth schedule (North-Western Provinces of Fort William)

the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States
towns of Calcutta, Madras and Bombay
Pargana Bhadohi or Pargana Kera Mangror in the Mirzapur district
Pargana Kaswa Raja in the Benares district

Nothing herein contained shall extend to Pargana Bhadohi or Pargana Kera Mangror in the Mirzapur district, or to Pargana Kaswa Raja in the Benares district, any law not now in force therein.

Lists Madras Regulations and Acts of the Supreme Council relating to the Madras Presidency whose local extent is declared by Section 4.
Lists Bombay Regulations and Acts of the Supreme Council relating to the Bombay Presidency whose local extent is declared by Section 5.

Lists Bengal Regulations (North-Western Provinces) and Acts of the Supreme Council relating to the North-Western Provinces whose local extent is declared by Section 7.

Lists various Scheduled Districts across Madras, Bombay, Bengal, North-Western Provinces, Punjab, Central Provinces, Coorg, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Ajmer and Merwara, and Assam, which are referred to in Section 2 and Sections 3-7 for defining local extent.

act_identification.act_title: THE CHUTIA NAGPUR ENCUMBERED ESTATES ACT, 1876
act_identification.act_short_title: The Chutia Nagpur Encumbered Estates Act, 1876

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the relief of holders of land in Chutia Nagpur who may be in debt, and whose immoveable property may be subject to mortgages, charges and liens; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide relief to landholders in Chutia Nagpur who are burdened by debt. It aims to manage their immoveable property, which is subject to mortgages, charges, and liens, to facilitate the settlement of these debts.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to vest management of property in an officer appointed by Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Allows the Commissioner, with Lieutenant-Governor's consent, to appoint a Manager to vest management of immoveable property of indebted landholders.

key_sections.title: Effect of order.
key_sections.description: Outlines the consequences of the vesting order, including barring pending suits, freeing the holder from arrest, and ceasing the power to alienate property.

key_sections.title: Manager to receive rents and profits, and pay therefrom.
key_sections.description: Details the Manager's duties to collect rents and profits and apply them to government revenue, superior landlord's rent, maintenance, repairs, management costs, and debts.

key_sections.title: Notice to claimants against holder of property.
key_sections.description: Requires the Manager to publish a notice calling upon all claimants to notify their claims within three months.

key_sections.title: Debt not duly notified to be barred.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that debts not notified to the Manager within the specified time will be barred, with a provision for a further nine-month period under certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Determination of debts.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Manager to determine the amount of principal debts, liabilities, and interest due to creditors and those holding mortgages, charges, or liens.

key_sections.title: Scheme for settlement of debts.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Manager to prepare and submit a scheme for debt settlement to the Commissioner for approval and implementation.

key_sections.title: Restoration of owner to his property.
key_sections.description: Provides for the restoration of the owner to their property once all debts are discharged or if the Act's provisions are deemed no longer applicable.

key_sections.title: Manager to have powers of holder of estate.
key_sections.description: Grants the Manager powers similar to the property holder for realizing rents and profits, and the power to remove mortgagees or conditional vendees in possession.

key_sections.title: Power to raise money by mortgage or sale.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Manager, with Commissioner's assent, to raise money for debt settlement by mortgaging or selling parts of the property.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Lieutenant-Governor of Bengal to make rules for various aspects of the Act's implementation, subject to approval by the Governor General in Council.

key_sections.title: Bar of suits.
key_sections.description: Bars suits or proceedings against any person for actions done in good faith pursuant to this Act.
