act_identification.act_title: An Act to limit the jurisdiction of the Civil Courts throughout the Bombay Presidency in matters relating to the Land-revenue, and for other purposes.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS in certain parts of the Presidency of Bombay, the jurisdiction of the Civil Courts in matters connected with the land-revenue is more extensive than it is in the rest of the said Presidency; And whereas it is expedient that the jurisdiction of all the Civil Courts in the said Presidency should be limited in manner hereinafter appearing; And whereas it is also expedient to amend the Bombay Civil Courts Act, section thirty-two, and to revive certain provisions of the thirteenth section of Regulation 17 of 1827 of the Bombay Code, which was repealed by the Land Improvement Act, 1871 (26 of 1871), [1]***; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to limit the jurisdiction of Civil Courts throughout the Bombay Presidency in matters relating to land-revenue. It seeks to standardize jurisdiction, amend the Bombay Civil Courts Act, and revive certain provisions of Regulation 17 of 1827.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title, commencement details, and geographical extent of the Act, along with specific exclusions.

key_sections.title: Interpretation-clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Land', 'Land-revenue', and 'Revenue officer'.

key_sections.title: Bar of certain suits.
key_sections.description: Prohibits Civil Courts from exercising jurisdiction over various matters related to land-revenue, with a proviso for certain cognizable claims.

key_sections.title: Saving of certain suits.
key_sections.description: Specifies types of suits that Civil Courts are not prevented from entertaining, acting as exceptions to the bar imposed by Section 4.

key_sections.title: Bar of certain suits against Revenue officers.
key_sections.description: Protects Revenue officers from being sued for damages in Civil Courts for _bona fide_ acts done in pursuance of law.

key_sections.title: Punishment or prosecution of Revenue officers not a bar to civil remedies.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that departmental punishment or criminal prosecution of Revenue officers does not preclude civil remedies against them.

key_sections.title: Suits not to be entertained unless plaintiff has exhausted right of appeal.
key_sections.description: Mandates that Civil Courts shall not entertain suits against the Government concerning Revenue officers' acts or omissions unless the plaintiff has exhausted all available appeals.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to refer questions for decision of High Court.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to refer questions of law arising in certain suits or investigations to the High Court for decision.

key_sections.title: Power of Civil Judge to refer questions of jurisdiction to High Court.
key_sections.description: Allows a Civil Judge to refer questions of jurisdiction to the High Court if they have doubts about their cognizance of a suit or appeal.

key_sections.title: Privileges of Government in suits in which it is concerned.
key_sections.description: Grants the Government privileges in suits where it is concerned, including the power to require trial by a District Judge and precedence for such trials.

powers_conferred: State Government: To direct the commencement date for a part of Section 4 (Section 1).
State Government: To refer questions for decision of the High Court (Section 12).
State Government: To require certain suits to be tried by the District Judge and given precedence (Section 16).
Civil Judge: To refer questions of jurisdiction to the High Court (Section 13).

related_acts: Regulation 17 of 1827 of the Bombay Code

applies_to: Civil Courts throughout the Bombay Presidency
Revenue officers
persons/entities involved in land-revenue matters
exemptions: Any suit regarding the assessment of revenue on land situate in the City of Bombay, or the collection of such revenue (Section 1(a)).
Any of the provisions of Bombay Acts 5 of 1862 and 6 of 1862, or of Act 21 of 1881 or of Act 23 of 1871 (Section 1(b)).
Claims to hold land wholly or partially exempt from payment of land-revenue under specific enactments, instruments, grants, or judgments (Section 4 Proviso).
Suits against the Government to contest the amount claimed as land-revenue (Section 5(a)).
Suits between private parties for establishing private rights (Section 5(b)).
Suits between superior holders or occupants and inferior holders or tenants regarding dues (Section 5(c)).
Suits for possession of any land being a whole survey number or a recognized share of a survey number (Section 5, clause (g) exception).
Civil Courts in the Districts mentioned in the second schedule for certain claims against the Government (Section 5, added part).
special_provisions: Specific jurisdiction for Civil Courts in the Districts mentioned in the second schedule for certain claims against the Government (Section 5).
Exemptions for land in the City of Bombay (Section 1(a)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the Civil Courts by limiting their jurisdiction in land-revenue matters, allowing for references to the High Court, and protecting Revenue officers for _bona fide_ acts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil Courts, High Court, District Court

schedules_summary.description: This schedule was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1891 (12 of 1891).
Lists specific districts where Civil Courts retain certain jurisdiction over claims against the Government, including Ahmedabad, Kaira, Broach, Surat, Tanna, Colaba, and Kanara.

act_identification.act_title: An Act to declare and amend the laws to be administered in Oudh.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to declare and amend the laws to be administered in Oudh; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to declare and amend the laws to be administered in Oudh. It sets out the statutory laws, customs, and specific rules for matters like dower, pre-emption, and court procedures within the region.

chapter_titles: PART II GENERAL LAWS TO BE ADMINISTERED IN OUDH
CHAPTER III PROCEDURE OF THE COURTS

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title, local extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Statutory law to be administered in Oudh.
key_sections.description: Specifies the laws to be administered by the Courts of Oudh, including customs, Muhammadan and Hindu law, and rules under this Act.

key_sections.title: Muhammadan dower contracts how to be enforced.
key_sections.description: Regulates the enforcement of dower contracts among Muhammadans, allowing courts to award a reasonable amount if the stipulated sum is excessive.

key_sections.title: Right of pre-emption.
key_sections.description: Defines the right of pre-emption as the right of certain persons to acquire immovable property in preference to others.

key_sections.title: Notice to pre-emptors.
key_sections.description: Requires persons proposing to sell or foreclose property to give notice to pre-emptors, specifying the price or amount due.

key_sections.title: Suit to enforce right of pre-emption.
key_sections.description: Outlines the grounds on which a suit to enforce the right of pre-emption may be brought, including lack of notice or bad faith in price/amount.

key_sections.title: Rule of limitation.
key_sections.description: Declares the Judicial Commissioner's Circular No.104 of July, 1860, as a notification under Act 14 of 1859, and deems that Act in force from July 4, 1862.

key_sections.title: Rules of taking evidence.
key_sections.description: Repeals Section 172 of Act No. 8 of 1859 for Oudh and substitutes new rules for taking oral evidence in court.

key_sections.title: Execution-sale of ancestral and acquired property in land.
key_sections.description: Restricts the sale of ancestral land in execution of a decree without the permission of the State Government.

key_sections.title: Right to nominate village-policemen.
key_sections.description: Grants the right to nominate village-policemen to the zamindar or lambardar of the village.

key_sections.title: Duties of village and road police-man.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the duties of village and road policemen, including reporting crimes, keeping police informed of disputes, and arresting offenders.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to make rules regarding the discipline, remuneration, and duties of police, disposal of unclaimed property, public health, and records.

key_sections.title: Publication of rules.
key_sections.description: Mandates the publication of rules made by the State Government and High Court in the Official Gazette, after which they gain the force of law.

key_sections.title: Honorary police-officers.
key_sections.description: Allows the State Government to confer police powers on any person it deems fit and to withdraw such powers.

powers_conferred: State Government: to appoint persons to fill vacancies for village-policemen, to appoint road police, to appoint funds for fines, to make rules, to confer powers on honorary police officers.
High Court: to make rules for custody and sale of attached property, levy of fees, and appointment/remuneration of persons for attachment/investigations.
Magistrate of the district: to appoint or reject nominees for village-policemen, to dismiss village or road policemen.
Courts of Oudh: to administer laws, enforce dower contracts, enforce pre-emption rights, fix time for payment in decrees, take evidence.
Zamindar of the village or lambardar: to nominate village-policemen.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Village-policemen and road-policemen are punishable for willful misconduct, neglect of duty, withdrawing without notice, or unnecessary personal violence, with a fine not exceeding three months' pay or imprisonment not exceeding three months, or both. Breach of rules made under the Act (not by High Court) is punishable with a fine up to fifty rupees or imprisonment up to six months, or both.

repealed_acts: Section 172 of Act No. 8 of 1859
related_acts: Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937 (26 of 1937)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The zamindar or lambardar nominates village-policemen. The State Government appoints or rejects nominees and can appoint persons in default of nomination. The State Government also appoints road police. The Magistrate of the district is involved in the appointment/rejection process.

applies_to: Oudh
Muhammadans (for dower contracts)
Hindus and Muhammadans (for succession, family relations, etc.)
Village-communities (for pre-emption)
Persons having a right of pre-emption
Village-policemen
Road-policemen
special_provisions: Specific rules for Muhammadan dower contracts (Section 5).
Different presumptions for pre-emption rights in village-communities versus towns (Sections 7 and 8).
Requirement of State Government permission for execution-sale of ancestral land (Section 20).
Special provisions for service of process within the jurisdiction of the Lucknow Civil Court (Section 22).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the Courts of Oudh, which administer the specified laws. Suits can be brought to enforce rights like pre-emption. Village and road policemen perform duties including reporting crimes and making arrests. Magistrates are empowered to convict and impose penalties for offenses and breaches of rules.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts of Oudh, Civil Courts, and Magistrates.

schedules_summary.description: Repealed.
Lists Bengal Regulations and Acts of the Governor General in Council, specifying their subjects and modifications for administration in Oudh.

act_identification.act_title: THE BROACH AND KAIRA INCUMBERED ESTATES ACT, 1877
act_identification.act_short_title: The Broach and Kaira Incumbered Estates Act, 1877

legislative_details.enacted_by: GOVERNOR GENERAL OF INDIA IN COUNCIL

act_overview.preamble: Preamble.—WHEREAS many Thakurs in the districts of Broach and Kaira are in debt, and their immoveable property is subject to mortgages, charges and liens; and whereas it is expedient to provide for their relief in manner hereinafter appearing; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide relief to Thakurs in the districts of Broach and Kaira whose estates are encumbered with debts, mortgages, charges, and liens. It establishes a mechanism for the management and liquidation of these debts and liabilities.

chapter_titles: II.—OF THE APPLICATION AND PRELIMINARY INQUIRY.
IV.—PROOF OF DEBTS AND SCHEME FOR LIQUIDATION.
V. OF THE PROCEEDINGS SUBSEQUENT TO SANCTION OF THE LIQUIDATION-SCHEME.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Interpretation-clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Thakur', 'Heir', and 'Commissioner'.

key_sections.title: Application for benefit of Act.
key_sections.description: Allows Thakurs or their heirs to apply for the benefits of the Act if subject to debts or liabilities.

key_sections.title: “Order of management” to what it extends.
key_sections.description: Defines the scope of the 'order of management' over the debtor's immoveable property and liabilities.

key_sections.title: Effect of order of management.
key_sections.description: Outlines the consequences of an order of management, including staying legal proceedings and rendering the debtor incompetent to contract new debts or alienate property.

key_sections.title: Manager to have powers of owner and to receive rents and profits:
key_sections.description: Grants the manager all powers of the owner to manage property and recover rents, including powers of a Collector for recovery.

key_sections.title: Notice to claimants against debtor.
key_sections.description: Requires the manager to publish notices calling for claims against the debtor or property.

key_sections.title: Claim not duly notified to be barred.
key_sections.description: States that claims not notified within the specified time will be deemed discharged, with a proviso for late admission.

key_sections.title: Scheme for liquidation.
key_sections.description: Mandates the manager to prepare a liquidation scheme for paying and discharging debts and liabilities.

key_sections.title: Effects of sanctioning scheme.
key_sections.description: Describes the effects of a sanctioned liquidation scheme, including the permanent barring of certain proceedings and extinguishment of proveable debts.

key_sections.title: Termination of management.
key_sections.description: Details the process for terminating management and restoring the owner to possession of the property.

key_sections.title: Mortgages, &c., made by restored Thakur valid only for his life.
key_sections.description: Limits the validity of mortgages, charges, leases, or alienations made by a restored Thakur to his natural life.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Local Government the power to make rules consistent with the Act for various purposes.

key_sections.title: Bar of suits.
key_sections.description: Prevents suits or proceedings against persons acting bona fide pursuant to the Act.

key_sections.title: Exemption of certain Thakurs from certain provisions of Act.
key_sections.description: Provides specific exemptions for certain named Thakurs from provisions regarding pecuniary liability and alienation.

powers_conferred: Commissioner: to direct an enquiry into debts and liabilities (Section 5)
Commissioner: to dismiss an application or direct management of immoveable property (Section 7)
Commissioner: to send back or sanction liquidation schemes (Section 18)
Commissioner: to relinquish management (Section 19)
Commissioner: to call for proceedings and pass orders thereon (Section 30)
Manager: to have all powers of the owner of the property under management (Section 10)
Manager: to receive and recover all rents and profits, with powers of a Collector for recovery (Section 10)
Manager: to pay costs of management, Government revenue, rent, allowances, and improvement costs (Section 11)
Manager: to publish notices for claimants (Section 12)
Manager: to inquire into claims and determine debts and liabilities (Section 15)
Manager: to rank debts and fix interest (Section 16)
Manager: to prepare and submit a liquidation scheme (Section 17)
Manager: to remove a mortgagee in possession (Section 21)
Manager: to inquire into consideration for leases and set aside or modify them (Section 22)
Manager: to demise property for a term of years (Section 23)
Manager: to raise money by mortgaging or selling property (Section 24)
Manager: to summon and enforce attendance of witnesses and compel production of documents (Section 35)
Local Government: to declare classes of holders as Thakurs (Section 3)
Local Government: to make general rules regarding applications (Section 5)
Local Government: to make rules consistent with the Act (Section 31)
Local Government: to suspend, remove, or appoint new managers (Section 32)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: If a statement submitted under Section 6 contains any averment known or believed to be false, or not known or believed to be true, the person making the verification shall be deemed to have intentionally given false evidence within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code.

repealed_acts: Act No. XV of 1871

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Local Government may suspend or remove any manager and appoint any officer in their stead. The Commissioner directs an enquiry to be made by such officer as he thinks fit.

applies_to: Thakurs in Broach and Kaira
any person who would be sole heir or one of the heirs to such Thakur
exemptions: Thakur of Ahmod (from Section 9 and Section 28)
Thakur of Sarod (from Section 9 and Section 28)
Thakur of Kerwara (from Section 9 and Section 28)
Thakur of Dehej (from Section 9 and Section 28)
Thakur of Janiadra (from Section 9 and Section 28)
special_provisions: The Act specifically applies to Thakurs in Broach and Kaira.

Section 38 provides specific exemptions for certain named Thakurs from the provisions of Section 9 and Section 28, with a proviso allowing the Local Government to remove such exemption under certain conditions.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the appointment of a Manager who takes control of the debtor's immoveable property, liquidates debts according to a sanctioned scheme, and has powers to recover rents, remove mortgagees, lease, mortgage, or sell property. Legal proceedings are stayed or barred during management.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil Courts in British India (for staying/barring proceedings); Courts in Broach and Kaira having jurisdiction in suits relating to succession to immoveable property (for entertaining and disposing of such suits).

act_identification.act_title: An Act to amend the law relating to Treasure-trove.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. Extended to Sonthal Parganas, Khondmals District, Angul District, Scheduled Districts of Hazaribagh, Lohardaga and Manbhum, and Pargana Dhalbhum and the Kolhan in the District of Singbhum, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Goa, Daman and Diu, Lakshadweep, Pondicherry.

act_overview.preamble: Whereas it is expedient to amend the law relating to treasure-trove; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to amend the law relating to treasure-trove. It establishes a procedure for the finder of treasure to report it to the Collector, outlines the process for determining ownership and division of the treasure, and provides for government acquisition and penalties for non-compliance.

key_sections.title: Short title. Extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical extent.

key_sections.title: Interpretation-clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act such as 'Treasure', 'Collector', and 'Owner'.

key_sections.title: Notice by finder of treasure.
key_sections.description: Requires the finder of treasure exceeding ten rupees in value to give notice to the Collector and deposit or secure the treasure.

key_sections.title: Notification requiring claimants to appear.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Collector to publish a notification and serve special notice to potential claimants after receiving a finding report.

key_sections.title: When treasure may be declared ownerless.
key_sections.description: Outlines conditions under which the Collector may declare treasure ownerless and provides for an appeal against such declaration.

key_sections.title: When only one such person claims and his claim is not disputed, treasure to be divided, and shares to be delivered to parties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the procedure for dividing treasure between the finder and a single undisputed claimant, including options for monetary settlement or public auction.

key_sections.title: Power to acquire the treasure on behalf of Government.
key_sections.description: Grants the Collector the power to acquire the treasure for the Government by paying its material value plus one-fifth.

key_sections.title: Decision of Collector final, and no suit to lie against him for acts done bona fide.
key_sections.description: Declares the Collector's decisions under the Act as final and protects the Collector from suits for bona fide actions.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to make rules consistent with the Act to regulate proceedings.

key_sections.title: Penalty on finder failing to give notice, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for finders who fail to give notice, deposit treasure, or attempt to alter its identity, including forfeiture of share and imprisonment or fine.

powers_conferred: Collector: to receive notice of treasure finding
Collector: to make inquiry regarding treasure finding
Collector: to publish notification requiring claimants to appear
Collector: to serve special notice on persons in possession of the finding place
Collector: to cause treasure to be produced
Collector: to determine circumstances of finding and hiding of treasure
Collector: to adjourn hearing for institution of suit in Civil Court
Collector: to declare treasure ownerless
Collector: to deliver treasure to finder
Collector: to divide treasure between finder and owner of place
Collector: to allot whole or more than share of treasure to a party on payment
Collector: to sell treasure by public auction and divide sale-proceeds
Collector: to retain treasure and stay proceedings in case of dispute
Collector: to acquire treasure on behalf of Government
Collector: to exercise powers of a Civil Court for trial of suits during inquiry
State Government: to appoint officers to perform functions of a Collector
State Government: to prescribe manner of publishing notifications
State Government: to make rules to regulate proceedings under the Act
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 20: Finder failing to give notice, not depositing or securing treasure, or altering/attempting to alter treasure to conceal identity, shall have their share vest in Government and be punished with imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both. Section 21: Owner of the place abetting an offence under section 20 shall have their share vest in Government and be punished with imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both.

repealed_acts: enactments (by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1891 (12 of 1891))
The Hyderabad Treasure-Trove Act, 1322F (Hyd. III of 1322F ) (by Bombay Act XXXIII of 1958)
the Indian Treasure-trove Act, 1878, as modified and applied by the State of Saurashtra (Application of Central and Bombay Acts) Ordinance, 1948 (San. Ord. XXV of 1948) (by Bombay Act XXXIII of 1958)
related_acts: The Hyderabad Treasure-Trove Act, 1322F (Hyd. III of 1322F )
State of Saurashtra (Application of Central and Bombay Acts) Ordinance, 1948 (San. Ord. XXV of 1948)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government has the power to appoint any officer to perform the functions of a Collector under this Act.

applies_to: Finders of treasure exceeding ten rupees in value
Owners of the place where treasure is found
exemptions: Treasure not exceeding ten rupees in amount or value
special_provisions: Extension to Sonthal Parganas, Khondmals District, Angul District, Scheduled Districts of Hazaribagh, Lohardaga and Manbhum, Pargana Dhalbhum and the Kolhan in the District of Singbhum, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Goa, Daman and Diu, Lakshadweep, Pondicherry.
Maharashtra State Amendment regarding extension to Hyderabad and Saurashtra area of Bombay State.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Collector conducts inquiries, issues notifications, determines ownership, divides or acquires treasure. Civil Courts resolve disputes over rights. Magistrates enforce penalties for offences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil Court (for establishing rights and resolving disputes), Magistrate (for conviction of offences)

schedules_summary.description: Repealed schedule.

act_identification.act_title: THE NORTHERN INDIA FERRIES ACT, 1878

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, the Central Provinces, Assam, Delhi and Ajmer

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to regulate ferries in [2][Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, the Central Provinces, Assam, Delhi and Ajmer]; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To regulate ferries in Northern India, specifically in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, the Central Provinces, Assam, Delhi and Ajmer.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its local extent, and commencement details.

key_sections.title: Interpretation-clause.
key_sections.description: Defines the term 'ferry' for the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to declare establish, define and discontinue public ferries.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to manage public ferries, including declaring, establishing, defining limits, changing course, and discontinuing them.

key_sections.title: Superintendence of public ferries.
key_sections.description: Vests the immediate superintendence of public ferries in the Magistrate of the district or other appointed officer.

key_sections.title: Letting ferry tolls by auction.
key_sections.description: Describes the process for letting the tolls of public ferries by public auction or otherwise.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the Commissioner of a division or appointed officer to make rules for the control, management, and regulation of public ferries and traffic.

key_sections.title: Private ferry not to ply within two miles of public ferry without sanction.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the establishment or operation of a private ferry within a specified distance of a public ferry without sanction.

key_sections.title: Tolls.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that tolls shall be levied on persons, animals, vehicles, and things crossing by public ferry, and allows for exemptions.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Commissioner of the division to make rules for the maintenance of order and safety at private ferries.

key_sections.title: Penalty for breach of provisions as to table of tolls, list of tolls and return of traffic.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for lessees or other persons who fail to maintain or produce toll tables/lists or furnish traffic returns.

key_sections.title: Penalty for breach of rules made under sections 12 and 19.
key_sections.description: Sets penalties for persons breaching rules made under the Act for public and private ferries.

key_sections.title: Penalty for maintaining private ferry within prohibited limits.
key_sections.description: Imposes penalties for establishing, maintaining, or working a private ferry in contravention of section 13.

key_sections.title: Power to take possession of boats, etc., on surrender or cancellation of lease.
key_sections.description: Allows the Magistrate of the district to take possession of ferry assets upon surrender or cancellation of a lease.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of Civil Courts barred.
key_sections.description: Bars the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in suits to ascertain compensation or abatement of rent under the Act.

key_sections.title: Delegation of powers.
key_sections.description: Enables the State Government to delegate its powers under the Act to various officers.

powers_conferred: State Government: Power to declare, establish, define and discontinue public ferries (S.4); Power to consider and order on claims for compensation (S.5); Power to appoint officers for superintendence of public ferries (S.6); Power to vest management of public ferries in municipality, District Council, District Board or Local Board (S.7, 7A); Power to sanction letting of ferry tolls otherwise than by public auction (S.8); Power to cancel lease of tolls (S.10); Power to fix toll rates (S.15); Power to declare exemptions from tolls (S.15); Power to fix rates for compounding tolls (S.18); Power to sanction rules for private ferries (S.19); Power to direct compensation for use of boats/materials (S.32, 33); Power to delegate its powers (S.35).

Commissioner of a division: Power to make rules for public ferries (S.12); Power to approve lease term (S.8); Power to fix abatement of rent (S.15); Power to sanction cancellation of lease (S.24); Power to make rules for private ferries (S.19); Power to reduce or remit damage amount (S.31).

Magistrate of the district: Power to inquire into claims for compensation (S.5); Power to superintend public ferries (S.6); Power to recover arrears from lessee (S.9); Power to pay compensation for cancelled lease (S.10); Power to receive compensation for surrendered lease (S.11); Power to sign list of tolls (S.16); Power to cancel lease of tolls (S.24); Power to assess damage done by offender (S.31); Power to take possession of boats, etc. (S.32, 33).
Police: Power to arrest without warrant (S.29).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for various offences including: breach of provisions regarding table of tolls, list of tolls, and traffic returns (fine up to fifty rupees); taking unauthorised toll or causing delay (fine up to one hundred rupees); breach of rules made under sections 12 and 19 (imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to two hundred rupees, or both); refusal to pay toll, fraudulent/forcible crossing, obstructing toll-collector, endangering human life/property in ferry-boat, refusing to leave ferry-boat/bridge (fine up to fifty rupees); maintaining private ferry within prohibited limits (fine up to five hundred rupees, and further fine up to one hundred rupees per day); and rash navigation and stacking of timber causing damage to public ferry (imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both).

repealed_acts: Repealing Act, 1938 (1 of 1938)
Repealing and Amending Act, 1891 (12 of 1891)
related_acts: Indian Tolls (Army and Air Force) Act, 1901

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government has the power to appoint officers for superintendence of public ferries (S.6), officers for sanction regarding private ferries (S.13), officers for abatement of rent (S.15), and to whom its powers may be delegated (S.35). The Magistrate of the district may appoint officers for inquiry into compensation claims (S.5) and for signing the list of tolls (S.16).

applies_to: Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, the Central Provinces, Assam, Delhi and Ajmer
All persons, animals, vehicles and other things crossing any river by a public ferry and not employed or transmitted on the public service
exemptions: Persons, animals, vehicles or other things declared by the State Government to be exempt from payment of tolls (S.15)
Boats which do not ply for hire or which the State Government expressly exempts from the operation of section 13 (S.13)
special_provisions: When a river lies between two States, powers regarding public ferries shall be exercised jointly by the State Governments of those States (S.4 proviso).
Alterations in the course or limits of a public ferry due to river changes may be made by the Commissioner of the Division or other appointed officer (S.4 proviso).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Commissioner of a division or other appointed officer (for public ferries under S.12); Commissioner of the division with previous sanction of the State Government (for private ferries under S.19).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is through penalties (fines, imprisonment), cancellation of leases, recovery of arrears, seizure and detention of vessels/timber, and arrest without warrant. Damages caused by offenders can be assessed and recovered.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any Magistrate or Bench of Magistrates having summary jurisdiction under the Code of Criminal Procedure.

act_identification.act_title: THE DEKKHAN AGRICULTURISTS’ RELIEF ACT, 1879

legislative_details.geographical_extent: This section and sections 11, 56, 60 and 62 extend to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. The rest of this Act extends only to the districts of Poona, Satara, Sholapur and Ahmednagar but may, from time to time, be extended wholly or in part by the State Government to any other district or districts in the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in the State of Bombay, or to any part or parts of any other such district or districts.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to relieve the agricultural classes in certain parts of the Dekkhan from indebtedness; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide relief to the agricultural classes in specific regions of the Dekkhan who are burdened by indebtedness. It aims to address the financial difficulties faced by these agriculturists.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its commencement date, and local extent.

key_sections.title: Agriculturists to be sued where they reside.
key_sections.description: Specifies that suits against agriculturists must be instituted and tried in a Court within the local limits of their residence.

key_sections.title: Instruments executed by agriculturist not to be deemed valid unless executed before a Village-registrar.
key_sections.description: Mandates that certain instruments executed by agriculturists are only valid if executed before a Village-registrar, with specific exemptions.

key_sections.title: Registration under this Act to be deemed equivalent to registration under Indian Registration Act, 1877.
key_sections.description: States that instruments registered under this Act are considered duly registered under the Indian Registration Act, 1877, and prohibits other forms of registration for such instruments.

key_sections.title: Exemption of instruments to which the Government or any officer of the Government is a party.
key_sections.description: Exempts instruments involving the Government or its officers from the requirement of being executed before a Village-registrar.

powers_conferred: State Government to extend the Act wholly or in part to other districts (Section 1)
Village-registrar to write, superintend, and attest instruments executed by agriculturists (Section 56)

repealed_acts: Bombay Agricultural Debtors' Relief Act, 1947 (Bom. 28 of 1947)

applies_to: Agriculturists
Agriculturist residing in any local area for which a Village-registrar has been appointed
exemptions: Instruments in any criminal proceeding
Instrument which is executed by an agriculturist merely as a surety
Instrument required by Section 17 of the Indian Registration Act, 1877 (3 of 1877), to be registered under that Act
Instrument to which the Government or any officer of the Government in his official capacity is a party
special_provisions: Sections 1, 11, 56, 60 and 62 extend to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States.
The rest of this Act extends only to the districts of Poona, Satara, Sholapur and Ahmednagar.

The Act may be extended wholly or in part by the State Government to any other district or districts in the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in the State of Bombay, or to any part or parts of any other such district or districts.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced through the requirement of execution before a Village-registrar for certain instruments and through Courts for suits against agriculturists.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Court within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the defendant agriculturist resides

act_identification.act_title: THE LEGAL PRACTITIONERS ACT, 1879

act_overview.purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to Legal Practitioners.

repealed_acts: Chapter VI of Bom. Reg. II of 1827
Acts 1 of 1846

act_identification.act_title: THE KAZIS ACT, 1880

legislative_details.geographical_extent: It extends, in the first instance, only to the territories administered by the Governor of Fort Saint George in Council. But the Government of any other State may, from time to time, by notification in the Official Gazette, extend it to the whole or any part of the territories under its administration.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS by the preamble to Act No. 11 of 1864 (An Act to repeal the law relating to the offices of Hindu and Muhammadan Law officers and to the offices of Kazi’-ul-Kuzaat and of Kazi’, and to abolish the former offices) it was (among other things) declared that it was declared that it was inexpedient that the appointment of the Kazi-ul-Kuzaat, or of City, Town or Pargana Kazi’s should be made by the Government, and by the same Act the enactments relating to the appointment by the Government of the said officers were repealed; and whereas by the usage of the Muhammadan community in some parts of India the presence of Kazi’s appointed by the Government is required at the celebration of marriages and the performance of certain other rites and ceremonies, and it is therefore expedient that the Government should again be empowered to appoint persons to the office of Kazi; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to re-empower the Government to appoint Kazis for local areas where the Muhammadan community requires their presence for marriages and other rites. This reverses a previous policy that had abolished government appointments of such officers.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its initial local extent, with provisions for extension to other territories.

key_sections.title: Power to appoint Kazi’s for any local area.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to appoint Kazis for local areas based on the desire of the Muhammadan residents, and outlines conditions for their suspension or removal.

key_sections.title: Naib Kazi’s.
key_sections.description: Allows appointed Kazis to appoint, suspend, or remove Naib Kazis to act on their behalf, and specifies that suspension/removal of a Kazi also applies to their Naibs.

key_sections.title: Nothing in Act to confer judicial or administrative powers; or to render the presence of Kazi’s necessary; or to prevent any one acting as Kazi’s.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not grant judicial or administrative powers to Kazis, does not make their presence mandatory for ceremonies, and does not restrict others from performing Kazi functions.

powers_conferred: State Government: Power to appoint Kazis for any local area (Section 2)
State Government: Power to suspend or remove Kazis (Section 2)
State Government: Power to extend the Act to other territories (Section 1)
Kazi: Power to appoint one or more persons as Naib Kazis (Section 3)
Kazi: Power to suspend or remove any Naib Kazi (Section 3)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government appoints Kazis. Kazis appoint Naib Kazis.

applies_to: Muhammadans resident in any local area
special_provisions: Initially extends only to the territories administered by the Governor of Fort Saint George in Council.
The Government of any other State may extend it to the whole or any part of the territories under its administration.

act_identification.act_title: THE RELIGIOUS SOCIETIES ACT, 1880

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India except [3][the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States]

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to simplify the manner in which certain bodies of persons associated for the purpose of maintaining religious worship may hold property acquired for such purpose, and to provide for the dissolution of such bodies and the adjustment of their affairs and for the decision of certain questions relating to such bodies; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to simplify the process for religious societies to hold property, manage their dissolution, adjust their affairs, and resolve related questions. It provides a framework for the appointment of trustees and the handling of property upon dissolution.

key_sections.title: Short title. Local extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability, including specific exemptions.

key_sections.title: Appointment of new trustee in cases not otherwise provided for.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for appointing new trustees for religious societies when no other method is prescribed by existing instruments.

key_sections.title: Appointment under section 2 to be recorded in a memorandum under the hand of the chairman of the meeting.
key_sections.description: Requires that the appointment of new trustees under Section 2 be documented in a memorandum, specifying its form and registration requirement.

key_sections.title: Property to vest in new trustees without conveyance.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that property subject to trust automatically vests in new trustees upon their appointment, without the need for a separate conveyance.

key_sections.title: Provision for dissolution of societies and adjustment of their affairs.
key_sections.description: Details the process for the dissolution of religious societies, including the requirement for a three-fifths majority vote and the settlement of property, claims, and liabilities.

key_sections.title: Upon a dissolution no member to receive profit.
key_sections.description: Ensures that upon dissolution, any remaining property after satisfying debts and liabilities is not distributed among members but given to another religious or charitable body.

key_sections.title: Questions may be submitted to High Court.
key_sections.description: Allows interested persons to petition the High Court for an opinion on questions related to membership or the validity of appointments under the Act, with such opinion having the force of a declaratory decree.

powers_conferred: Power to appoint new trustees (by the body of persons or a majority thereof) (Section 2)
Power to determine dissolution of the body (by three-fifths of members) (Section 6)
Power to dispose of and settle property, claims, and liabilities upon dissolution (by the body or as determined at a meeting) (Section 6)
Power of the principal Court of original civil jurisdiction to adjust affairs in case of dispute during dissolution (Section 6)
Power to determine the recipient of remaining property upon dissolution (by three-fifths of members or by Court) (Section 7)
Power of the High Court to give opinion on questions related to membership or appointment validity (Section 9)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The body of persons associated for the purpose of maintaining religious worship, or a majority of not less than two-thirds of its members, has the power to appoint new trustees (Section 2).

applies_to: bodies of persons associated for the purpose of maintaining religious worship
exemptions: any Hindus
Muhammadans or Buddhists
any persons whom the State Government may from time to time, by notification in the Official Gazette, exclude from the operation of this Act
special_provisions: The Act extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through procedures for trustee appointment, property vesting, dissolution, and dispute resolution, with the Principal Court of original civil jurisdiction and the High Court having roles in adjudicating disputes and providing opinions.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court (Section 9)

schedules_summary.description: Contains the form for the Memorandum of the appointment of new trustees, to be executed and attested, as referred to in Section 3.

act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL PROVINCES LAND-REVENUE ACT, 1881

legislative_details.enacted_by: GOVERNOR GENERAL OF INDIA IN COUNCIL
legislative_details.geographical_extent: all the territories for the time being under the administration of the Chief Commissioner of the Central Provinces, except those specified in Part VI of the first schedule of the Scheduled Districts Act 1874

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Land-revenue and the powers of Revenue-officers in the Central Provinces. WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to Land-revenue and to the powers of Revenue-officers in the Central Provinces; It is hereby enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws concerning land-revenue and to define the powers of revenue-officers within the Central Provinces. Its objective is to streamline the administration of land-revenue and related official functions.

chapter_titles: OF REVENUE-OFFICERS: THEIR POWERS AND PROCEDURE.
OF CERTAIN INVESTIGATIONS BY THE SETTLEMENT-OFFICER AND THE PREPARATION OF THE RECORD-OF-RIGHTS.
OF SETTLEMENTS MADE BEFORE THIS ACT COMES INTO FORCE.
OF THE COLLECTION OF LAND REVENUE.
OF CERTAIN ADDITIONAL POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF REVENUE-OFFICERS.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Defines the short title, local extent, and commencement of the Act.

key_sections.title: Interpretation-clause.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Chief controlling Revenue-authority.
key_sections.description: Designates the Chief Commissioner as the Chief Controlling Revenue-authority.

key_sections.title: Revenue-officers.
key_sections.description: Lists the classes of Revenue-officers and their hierarchical structure.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Establishes the appeal structure for decisions and orders under the Act.

key_sections.title: Notification of revenue-survey.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for notifying and conducting a revenue-survey.

key_sections.title: Separate sum to be assessed on every mahal.
key_sections.description: Mandates a separate land-revenue assessment for each mahal, with provisions for reduction.

key_sections.title: Option to accept or refuse assessment.
key_sections.description: Grants proprietors the option to accept or refuse the offered assessment.

key_sections.title: Record-of-rights.
key_sections.description: Requires the Settlement-officer to prepare a record-of-rights for every mahal or group of mahals.

key_sections.title: “Arrear.” “Defaulters.”.
key_sections.description: Defines what constitutes an arrear of revenue and who are considered defaulters.

key_sections.title: Processes for recovery of arrears.
key_sections.description: Lists the various processes available for recovering arrears of revenue payable to Government.

key_sections.title: Correction of record-of-rights.
key_sections.description: Allows for the correction of entries in the record-of-rights by the Deputy Commissioner on specified grounds.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules as to officers.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Chief Commissioner to make rules for the appointment, remuneration, suspension, and removal of lambardars, sub-lambardars, and mukaddams.

key_sections.title: Right to mines and quarries.
key_sections.description: Declares the Government's right to mines, minerals, and quarries unless otherwise provided, with compensation for infringement of surface rights.

key_sections.title: Exclusive jurisdiction of Revenue-authorities.
key_sections.description: Specifies matters over which Civil Courts have no jurisdiction, reserving them for Revenue-authorities.

powers_conferred: Chief Commissioner: To appoint, suspend, remove Commissioners, Deputy Commissioners, Assistant Commissioners, Tahsildars; invest Assistant Commissioner with powers of Deputy Commissioner; alter limits of district or tahsil; invest Revenue-officers with powers; make rules to regulate procedure; powers of revision; publish notification of revenue-survey; issue notification of settlement; appoint Settlement-officers; invest Settlement-officer with powers of Deputy Commissioner; appoint Settlement-commissioner and delegate powers; invest Settlement-officers with Civil Court powers; regulate payment of land-revenue; make rules for guidance of Revenue-officers; make rules as to officers; make rules as to patwaris; empower persons by name or classes; vary or cancel orders; make rules and attach penalty.

Governor General in Council: Control over Chief Commissioner; sanction for additional Commissioners/Deputy Commissioners; sanction for rules; sanction for notification of settlement; sanction for appointment of Settlement-commissioner.

Deputy Commissioner: To distribute work; withdraw and transfer cases; issue notice of demand; execute processes for recovery of arrears; order arrest and imprisonment; manage attached mahal/land; sanction transfer; proclaim annulment of settlement; offer new assessment; correct record-of-rights; revise record-of-rights; exercise Settlement-officers' powers when settlement not in progress; order payment for injuring boundary-marks; make lands separate mahals; alter channel for revenue payment; recover sums as arrears.
Revenue-officers: To enter on land, survey, demarcate boundaries; review orders.

Settlement-officer: To invite claims to unowned lands; form mahals; exclude town/land from settlement; order erection/repair of boundary-marks; assess mahals; offer assessment; make sub-settlement; ascertain proprietors; determine sir-land; decide disputes among shareholders; determine lambardars for revenue payment; ascertain status and rents of tenants; investigate claims to hold free from revenue; decide village-cesses; determine certain disputes; prepare record-of-rights.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties include a sum not exceeding fifty rupees for wilfully erasing, removing, or damaging a boundary-mark (Section 134), a penalty not exceeding two hundred rupees for violation or neglect of rules/customs enforced by Government (Section 123), and a fine up to fifty rupees per day for neglecting to give notice of possession of proprietary rights (Section 127). Arrest and imprisonment are also prescribed for recovery of arrears (Sections 94, 95, 96).

repealed_acts: Act XII of 1841 (For amending the Bengal Code in regard to sales of land for arrear of revenue) - So much as has not been repealed.
Act I of 1847 (For the establishment and maintenance of boundary-marks in the North-Western Provinces of Bengal) - The whole.
Act XXXI of 1858 (To make further provision for the settlement of land gained by alluvion in the Presidency of Fort William in Bengal) - The whole.
related_acts: Act No. XXIII of 1863 (to provide for the adjudication of claims to waste lands)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Chief Commissioner, often with the previous sanction of the Governor General in Council, has the power to appoint, suspend, and remove various Revenue-officers and village-officers.

applies_to: all the territories for the time being under the administration of the Chief Commissioner of the Central Provinces
exemptions: territories specified in Part VI of the first schedule of the Scheduled Districts Act 1874
land purchased free from revenue under any rules for the time being in force to regulate the sale of waste-lands
land in respect of which the revenue has been redeemed under any rules for the time being in force
land excluded from assessment under section forty-four
land in respect of which a claim to hold it free from revenue as against the Government is established
land which the Chief Commissioner, subject to the control of the Governor General in Council, may from time to time exempt from assessment
females, minors, lunatics or idiots from arrest and imprisonment for arrears
special_provisions: In Sambalpur, 'sir-land' includes 'bhogra' land.
Holders of sir-land in Sambalpur are bound to provide for the remuneration of mukaddams.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Chief Commissioner (often with the previous sanction of the Governor General in Council)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through various processes for the recovery of arrears, including arrest and imprisonment, attachment and sale of property, management of mahals, transfer of shares, and annulment of settlement. Revenue-officers are empowered to conduct surveys, demarcate boundaries, assess land-revenue, and maintain records.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Revenue-officers (including those invested with Civil Court powers) have jurisdiction over matters specified in the Act, with Civil Courts having limited jurisdiction as explicitly provided or excluded.

schedules_summary.description: Lists enactments repealed by this Act, including Act XII of 1841, Act I of 1847, and Act XXXI of 1858, specifying the extent of repeal for each.

act_identification.act_title: THE NEGOTIABLE INSTRUMENTS ACT, 1881

act_overview.preamble: An Act to define and amend the law relating to Promissory Notes, Bills of Exchange and Cheques. Preamble.—Whereas it is expedient to define and amend the law relating to promissory notes, bills of exchange and cheques; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To define and amend the law relating to promissory notes, bills of exchange, and cheques.

O F P RESE N TM EN T

key_sections.title: Short title. Local extent, Saving of usages relating to hundis, etc., Commencement.

key_sections.title: Interpretation-clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Banker'.

key_sections.title: “Promissory note.”

key_sections.title: “Bill of exchange.”
key_sections.description: Defines what constitutes a 'Bill of exchange'.

key_sections.title: “Cheque.”

key_sections.title: “Holder in due course.”
key_sections.description: Defines a 'Holder in due course' and the conditions for becoming one.

key_sections.title: “Negotiable instrument.”
key_sections.description: Defines what constitutes a 'Negotiable instrument'.

key_sections.title: Capacity to make, etc., promissory notes, etc. Minor.
key_sections.description: States who has the capacity to make or be bound by negotiable instruments, including provisions for minors.

key_sections.title: Presentment for payment.
key_sections.description: Mandates presentment of promissory notes, bills of exchange, and cheques for payment and outlines consequences of default.

key_sections.title: Effect of material alteration. Alteration by indorsee.
key_sections.description: States that material alteration of a negotiable instrument renders it void against non-consenting parties and discharges indorsers.

key_sections.title: Dishonour by non-acceptance.
key_sections.description: Defines when a bill of exchange is dishonoured by non-acceptance.

key_sections.title: Dishonour by non-payment.
key_sections.description: Defines when a promissory note, bill of exchange, or cheque is dishonoured by non-payment.

key_sections.title: Presumptions as to negotiable instruments.
key_sections.description: Establishes various legal presumptions regarding negotiable instruments, such as consideration, date, and holder in due course status.

key_sections.title: Cheque crossed generally.

key_sections.title: Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency, etc., of funds in the account.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Addresses liability for offences under Section 138 when committed by companies, including directors and other officers.

key_sections.title: Power to direct interim compensation.
key_sections.description: Grants courts the power to order interim compensation to the complainant in cheque dishonour cases.

key_sections.title: Power of Appellate Court to order payment pending appeal against conviction.

powers_conferred: Central Government to declare public holidays (Section 25)
Court to try cases summarily (Section 143)
Court to direct interim compensation (Section 143A)
Appellate Court to order payment pending appeal (Section 148)

Section 141 extends liability for such offences to companies and their responsible officers.

repealed_acts: Enactments repealed (as per Schedule)
related_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)

applies_to: whole of India
Every person capable of contracting
Companies
exemptions: Minors (do not bind themselves)
Local usages relating to instruments in an oriental language (unless excluded by instrument's words)
special_provisions: Nothing herein contained affects the Indian Paper Currency Act, 1871 (3 of 1871), section 21.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN TRUSTS ACT, 1882

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands; but the Central Government may, from time to time, by notification in the Official Gazette, extend it to the, Andaman and Nicobar Islands or to any part thereof.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to define and amend the law relating to private trusts and trustees; It is hereby enacted as follows :—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to define and amend the law relating to private trusts and trustees. It provides a legal framework for the creation, duties, rights, and liabilities associated with private trusts.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II OF THE CREATION OF TRUSTS
CHAPTER III OF THE DUTIES AND LIABILITIES OF TRUSTEES
CHAPTER IV OF THE RIGHTS AND POWERS OF TRUSTEES
CHAPTER V OF THE DISABILITIES OF TRUSTEES
CHAPTER VI OF THE RIGHTS AND LIABILITIES OF THE BENEFICIARY
CHAPTER VII OF VACATING THE OFFICE OF TRUSTEE
CHAPTER VIII OF THE EXTINCTION OF TRUSTS
CHAPTER IX OF CERTAIN OBLIGATIONS IN THE NATURE OF TRUSTS

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title, commencement date, local extent of the Act, and certain savings clauses.

key_sections.title: Interpretation-clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'trust', 'author of the trust', 'trustee', 'beneficiary', 'trust-property', 'breach of trust', 'registered', and 'notice'.

key_sections.title: Lawful purpose.
key_sections.description: States that a trust must be created for a lawful purpose and defines what constitutes an unlawful purpose, rendering such trusts void.

key_sections.title: Trust of immoveable property.
key_sections.description: Specifies the requirements for the validity of trusts relating to immoveable and moveable property, including the need for a written instrument and registration in certain cases.

key_sections.title: Creation of trust.
key_sections.description: Outlines the essential elements required for the creation of a trust, including the intention, purpose, beneficiary, and trust-property.

key_sections.title: Trustee to execute trust.
key_sections.description: Mandates the trustee to fulfil the purpose of the trust and obey the author's directions, with provisions for beneficiary consent and exceptions for impracticable or illegal directions.

key_sections.title: Care required from trustee.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that a trustee must deal with trust-property with the care of an ordinary prudent man, and outlines responsibility for loss.

key_sections.title: Investment of trust-money.
key_sections.description: Governs how trust-money should be invested, subject to directions in the instrument of trust or specified by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Liability for breach of trust.
key_sections.description: Defines the trustee's liability for losses caused by a breach of trust, including conditions for interest payment, unless induced by the beneficiary's fraud or consent.

key_sections.title: Right to apply to Court for opinion in management of trust-property.
key_sections.description: Allows a trustee to seek the Court's opinion, advice, or direction on trust management without instituting a full suit.

key_sections.title: Trustee cannot delegate.
key_sections.description: Prohibits a trustee from delegating their office or duties, with specific exceptions such as provisions in the instrument of trust or necessity.

key_sections.title: Trustee may not use trust-property for his own profit.
key_sections.description: Forbids a trustee from using trust-property for personal profit or purposes unconnected with the trust.

key_sections.title: Right to specific execution.
key_sections.description: Grants the beneficiary the right to specific execution of the trust and, under certain conditions, the right to transfer of possession of the trust-property.

key_sections.title: Appointment of new trustees on death, etc.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of new trustees in cases of disclaimer, death, absence, insolvency, or unfitness of existing trustees.

key_sections.title: Trust how extinguished.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the circumstances under which a trust is extinguished, such as complete fulfilment of purpose, unlawfulness, impossibility of execution, or revocation.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To extend the Act to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands or any part thereof by notification.

Principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction: To grant permission for a minor to create a trust; to give consent for a beneficiary incompetent to contract; to authorize extension of time for sale by a trustee; to give opinion, advice, or direction on trust management; to permit a trustee to lease trust-property for a term exceeding twenty-one years; to permit application of property of minors for maintenance; to control discretionary power of a trustee; to permit a trustee to buy beneficiary's interest; to discharge a trustee; to appoint new trustees.

Trustee: To do all reasonable and proper acts for the realisation, protection, or benefit of trust-property and for the protection or support of a beneficiary not competent to contract; to sell trust-property in lots, by public auction or private contract; to insert special conditions in sale contracts, buy-in, and re-sell; to convey property for sale; to vary investments; to apply property of minors for their maintenance, education, or advancement; to give receipts for money, securities, or moveable property; to compound debts, accept security, allow time for payment, compromise, abandon, or submit to arbitration.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Liability for breach of trust, including making good the loss sustained by the trust-property or beneficiary, and payment of interest in certain cases (e.g., actual receipt of interest, unreasonable delay in payment, failure to invest, employment of trust-property in trade or business).

repealed_acts: The Statute of Frauds (29 Car. II, c. 3)
The Trustees’ and Mortgages’ Powers Act, 1866 (XXVII of 1866)
The Specific Relief Act, 1877 (1 of 1877)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Appointment of new trustees can be made by the person nominated in the instrument of trust, the author of the trust (if alive and competent), surviving or continuing trustees, legal representative of the last surviving trustee, retiring trustees (with Court consent), or by a Principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction.

applies_to: Private Trusts and Trustees
exemptions: Rules of Muhammadan law as to waqf
Mutual relations of the members of an undivided family as determined by any customary or personal law
Public or private religious or charitable endowments
Trusts to distribute prizes taken in war among the captors
Trusts created before the commencement of the Act (specifically Chapter II)
special_provisions: The Central Government may extend the Act to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands or any part thereof.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to define and amend certain parts of the law relating to the transfer of property by act of parties; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To define and amend certain parts of the law relating to the transfer of property by act of parties, covering various aspects of property transactions such as sales, mortgages, leases, and gifts.

chapter_titles: OF TRANSFERS OF PROPERTY BY ACT OF PARTIES
OF MORTGAGES OF IMMOVEABLE PROPERTY AND CHARGES

key_definitions: a person is said to have notice
mercantile document of title to goods

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title, commencement date, and geographical extent of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Acts. Saving of certain enactments, incidents, rights, liabilities, etc.
key_sections.description: Repeals specified enactments in the Schedule and saves certain provisions, contracts, rights, liabilities, and transfers by operation of law or court decrees, and rules of Muhammadan law.

key_sections.title: Interpretation-clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'immoveable property', 'instrument', 'attested', 'registered', 'attached to the earth', 'actionable claim', and 'notice'.

key_sections.title: “Transfer of property” defined.
key_sections.description: Defines 'transfer of property' as an act by which a living person conveys property to one or more other living persons, including companies or associations.

key_sections.title: What may be transferred.
key_sections.description: States that property of any kind may be transferred, with specific exceptions such as chance of an heir, mere right of re-entry, easements apart from dominant heritage, and certain restricted interests.

key_sections.title: Condition restraining alienation.
key_sections.description: Declares conditions absolutely restraining alienation of property as void, with an exception for leases and transfers for the benefit of certain women.

key_sections.title: Rule against perpetuity.
key_sections.description: Sets a rule against creating interests that take effect beyond the lifetime of persons living at the date of transfer and the minority of a person in existence at that period.

key_sections.title: Election when necessary.
key_sections.description: Outlines the doctrine of election, requiring a person to choose between confirming a transfer of property they don't own or relinquishing a benefit conferred by the same transaction.

key_sections.title: Transfer of property pending suit relating thereto.
key_sections.description: Establishes the doctrine of lis pendens, preventing the transfer or dealing of property involved in a pending suit so as to affect the rights of other parties, except with court authority.

key_sections.title: Fraudulent transfer.
key_sections.description: Declares transfers made with intent to defeat or delay creditors as voidable at the option of the creditor, and transfers without consideration with intent to defraud subsequent transferees as voidable.

key_sections.title: Part performance.
key_sections.description: Provides protection to a transferee who has taken possession of immoveable property in part performance of a contract, even if the transfer is not formally completed.

key_sections.title: “Sale” defined.
key_sections.description: Defines 'sale' as a transfer of ownership for a price, specifies how sales are made (registered instrument or delivery), and defines 'contract for sale'.

key_sections.title: “Mortgage”, “mortgagor”, “mortgagee”, “mortgage-money”and “mortgage-deed”defined.
key_sections.description: Defines mortgage as the transfer of an interest in specific immoveable property to secure payment, and categorizes different types of mortgages (simple, conditional sale, usufructuary, English, deposit of title-deeds, anomalous).

key_sections.title: Right of mortgagor to redeem.
key_sections.description: Grants the mortgagor the right to redeem the mortgaged property upon payment or tender of the mortgage-money, requiring the mortgagee to deliver documents and possession, or re-transfer the property.

key_sections.title: Power of sale when valid.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which a mortgagee can sell the mortgaged property without court intervention, particularly for English mortgages or where expressly conferred by deed in certain areas.

key_sections.title: Lease defined.
key_sections.description: Defines 'lease' as a transfer of a right to enjoy immoveable property for a certain time or in perpetuity, in consideration of a price or rent, and defines lessor, lessee, premium, and rent.

key_sections.title: “Gift” defined.
key_sections.description: Defines 'gift' as a voluntary transfer of existing moveable or immoveable property without consideration, by a donor to a donee, accepted during the donor's lifetime.

key_sections.title: Transfer of actionable claim.
key_sections.description: States that the transfer of an actionable claim is effected by a written instrument, vesting rights and remedies in the transferee, with provisions for notice to the debtor.

key_definitions: Dominant and servient heritages and owners

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title, local extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Savings.
key_sections.description: Specifies rights and laws that are not affected by the Act, including government rights over water and customary rights.

key_sections.title: “Easement” defined.
key_sections.description: Defines an easement as a right for beneficial enjoyment of land over another's land, and defines dominant/servient heritages and owners.

key_sections.title: Continuous and discontinuous, apparent and non-apparent, easements.
key_sections.description: Classifies easements based on their continuity and visibility.

key_sections.title: Easements restrictive of certain rights.
key_sections.description: States that easements are restrictions on the exclusive right to enjoy and dispose of property, and rights to natural advantages.

key_sections.title: Easements of necessity and quasi easements.
key_sections.description: Describes how easements of necessity and quasi easements arise upon transfer or bequest of immovable property or partition.

key_sections.title: Acquisition by prescription.
key_sections.description: Outlines the conditions for acquiring easements (light, air, support, way) by peaceable and open enjoyment for twenty years.

key_sections.title: Rights which cannot be acquired by prescription.
key_sections.description: Lists specific rights that cannot be acquired by prescription, such as those leading to total destruction of the subject or rights to surface/underground water not in defined channels.

key_sections.title: Extent of easements.
key_sections.description: Determines the extent and mode of enjoyment for easements, including those of necessity and prescriptive rights.

key_sections.title: Suit for disturbance of easement.
key_sections.description: Allows the owner or occupier of the dominant heritage to sue for compensation if the easement is disturbed and causes substantial damage.

key_sections.title: Injunction to restrain disturbance.
key_sections.description: Provides for granting an injunction to restrain actual or threatened disturbance of an easement.

key_sections.title: Extinction by unity of ownership.
key_sections.description: States that an easement is extinguished when the same person becomes the absolute owner of both the dominant and servient heritages.

key_sections.title: Extinction by non-enjoyment.
key_sections.description: Describes how continuous and discontinuous easements can be extinguished by non-enjoyment for an unbroken period of twenty years.

key_sections.title: “License” defined.
key_sections.description: Defines a license as a right to do something on immovable property that would otherwise be unlawful, without amounting to an easement or interest in the property.

key_sections.title: License when revocable.
key_sections.description: Specifies when a license may be revoked by the grantor, with exceptions for licenses coupled with property transfer or where permanent work has been executed.

Occupiers of immovable property
Dominant owners
Servient owners
Grantors of licenses
Licensees

key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Suits in which Court has no jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: General finality of decrees and orders of Small Cause Court.
key_sections.description: Declares that decrees and orders of the Small Cause Court are generally final and conclusive.

key_sections.title: New trial of contested cases.
key_sections.description: Allows for an application for a new trial in contested cases within a specified period.

key_sections.title: Summons against person occupying property without leave.
key_sections.description: Provides a procedure for an applicant to seek a summons against an occupant refusing to deliver possession of immovable property.

key_sections.title: Application for distress-warrant.
key_sections.description: Describes the process for applying for a distress warrant for arrears of rent.

key_sections.title: Reference when compulsory.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which the Small Cause Court must refer questions of law to the High Court.

key_sections.title: Institution-fee.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the fees payable on plaints and applications under the Act.

key_sections.title: No suit to lie upon decree of Court.
key_sections.description: States that no new suit can be instituted based on a decree of the Small Cause Court.

powers_conferred: State Government: Appoints Chief Judge, other Judges, Additional Chief Judge (Maharashtra), Registrar, Deputy Registrar, clerks, bailiffs, other ministerial officers; directs rank and precedence of Judges; invests Registrar with Judge's powers; prescribes seal; approves holidays; appoints place of imprisonment; varies fees; provides for repayment of fees.

High Court: Exercises superintendence over Small Cause Court; makes rules for procedure and practice; hears appeals; calls for records; approves registers and returns; transfers cases; receives references.

Chief Judge: Distributes business among Judges; directs powers and duties of Registrar and other officers; transfers suits from Judge to Registrar or from Registrar to own file; orders payment for officer default.

Small Cause Court (Judges): Tries suits; tries suits by consent beyond pecuniary limits; suspends execution of decree; orders new trials; issues summons for possession; makes orders for possession; inquires into officer misconduct; summons witnesses; sentences or commits for contempt; receives and registers suits by poor persons.

Registrar: May be invested with powers of a Judge for suits not exceeding twenty rupees; hears and determines suits; executes decrees; receives applications for distress-warrant; issues summons for claims to distrained goods.
Bailiffs and Appraisers: Distrain movable property; force open places for distress; impound distress; make inventory and give notice; appraise property; sell distrained property.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: A Judge or officer practicing or trading in contravention of Section 15 is deemed to have committed an offence under Section 168 of the Indian Penal Code. Any person (except an appointed bailiff) levying or attempting to levy distress for rent illegally is liable to a fine up to five hundred rupees and imprisonment up to three months. A witness refusing to answer or produce documents before the Small Cause Court may be sentenced to simple imprisonment or committed for up to seven days.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The High Court may make rules for procedure and practice, and declare non-judicial and quasi-judicial acts. The State Government may vary fees and provide for repayment of fees. The Chief Judge may make arrangements for the distribution of business and direct the duties of the Registrar and other officers.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through execution of decrees, issuance of distress warrants for rent arrears, orders for possession of immovable property, and enforcement of orders for payment or repayment. Penalties are prescribed for illegal distresses, and imprisonment for contempt of court.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Small Cause Court, High Court (for superintendence, appeals, references, transfers), Madras City Civil Court (for execution in certain cases), Presidency Magistrate (for conviction of illegal distress).
