act_identification.act_title: THE EXPLOSIVES ACT, 1884

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the manufacture, possession, use, sale, [2][transport, import and export] of explosives. WHEREAS it is expedient to regulate the manufacture, possession, use, sale, [2][transport, import and export] of explosives; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to regulate the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport, import, and export of explosives. It establishes a licensing system for these activities and grants powers to the Central Government to make rules, prohibit dangerous explosives, and ensure public safety. The Act also defines offences, prescribes penalties, and outlines procedures for accident inquiries and enforcement.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its local extent to whole India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'aircraft', 'carriage', 'District Magistrate', 'explosive', 'export', 'import', 'master', 'manufacture', 'prescribed', and 'vessel'.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules as to licensing of the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport, import and export of explosives.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for regulating or prohibiting the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport, import, and export of explosives, including provisions for licensing and fees.

key_sections.title: Power for Central Government to prohibit the manufacture, possession or importation of specially dangerous explosives.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to prohibit, absolutely or conditionally, the manufacture, possession, or importation of explosives deemed specially dangerous for public safety.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of manufacture, possession, sale or transport of explosives by young persons and certain other persons.
key_sections.description: Prohibits persons under eighteen, convicted individuals, those bound for peace/good behaviour, or those with cancelled licenses from dealing with explosives, and prohibits selling to such persons or those of unsound mind.

key_sections.title: Grant of licences.
key_sections.description: Outlines the conditions and criteria for the licensing authority to grant licenses for the manufacture or other purposes related to explosives.

key_sections.title: Refusal of licences.
key_sections.description: Specifies the grounds on which the licensing authority shall refuse to grant a licence, including for prohibited explosives, unfit persons, or for public peace/safety.

key_sections.title: Variation, suspension and revocation of licences.
key_sections.description: Details the powers of the licensing authority and courts to vary conditions, suspend, or revoke licenses under various circumstances, such as contravention of conditions or public safety concerns.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Provides for a mechanism for persons aggrieved by licensing authority orders to prefer an appeal to a prescribed appellate authority.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules conferring powers of inspection, search, seizure, detention and removal.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules empowering officers to inspect, search, seize, detain, and remove explosives, and to destroy them if necessary.

key_sections.title: Notice of accidents.
key_sections.description: Mandates immediate notice to authorities (Chief Controller of Explosives and police) in case of accidents involving explosives that result in loss of life, serious injury, or property damage.

key_sections.title: Punishment for certain offences.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for various offences such as contravention of rules, license conditions, notifications, or failure to report accidents.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that when an offence is committed by a company, both the company and the persons in charge, or those whose consent/connivance/neglect led to the offence, shall be deemed guilty.

key_sections.title: Saving and power to exempt.
key_sections.description: Exempts certain activities by Armed Forces and government employees from most provisions of the Act, and empowers the Central Government to grant further exemptions.

key_sections.title: Extension of definition of “explosive” to other explosive substances.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to declare other dangerous substances as 'explosives' under the Act, extending its provisions to them.

key_sections.title: Procedure for making, publication and confirmation of rules.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for making, publishing, and confirming rules under the Act, including public consultation and parliamentary oversight.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To make rules to regulate or prohibit the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport, import and export of explosives (Section 5).
Central Government: To prohibit the manufacture, possession or importation of specially dangerous explosives (Section 6).
Central Government: To make rules conferring powers of inspection, search, seizure, detention and removal of explosives (Section 7).
Central Government: To make rules for regulating procedure at inquiries into accidents (Section 9, 9A).
Central Government: To appoint competent persons to hold inquiries into serious accidents (Section 9A).
Central Government: To suspend or revoke, or direct any licensing authority to suspend or revoke, all or any licences (Section 6E(8)).
Central Government: To exempt any explosive or any person or class of persons from provisions of the Act (Section 14).
Central Government: To declare any substance as an 'explosive' (Section 17).
Central Government: To delegate powers or functions under the Act (Section 17A).
Licensing authority: To grant, refuse, vary, suspend, and revoke licences (Sections 6B, 6C, 6D, 6E).
Officers authorized by rules: To enter, inspect, examine, search, take samples, seize, detain, remove, and destroy explosives (Section 7).
District Magistrate: To hold or direct a Magistrate subordinate to him to hold inquiry into accidents (Section 9).
Naval, military, or air force authority: To hold inquiry into accidents under their control (Section 9).
Person holding an inquiry: To have powers of a Magistrate or Civil Court for enforcing attendance of witnesses and compelling production of documents (Section 9, 9A).
Court: To direct forfeiture of explosives upon conviction (Section 10).
Court: To direct distress and sale of aircraft or vessel for payment of fine (Section 11).

Police-officer, occupier, agent or servant of occupier, railway administration, conservator of the port or officer in charge of the air port: To arrest without warrant persons committing dangerous offences (Section 13).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes punishments for various offences. Contravention of rules or license conditions regarding manufacture, import, or export of explosives is punishable with imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to five thousand rupees, or both. For possession, use, sale, or transport, the punishment is imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to three thousand rupees, or both. Other contraventions incur a fine up to one thousand rupees. Manufacturing, possessing, or importing explosives in contravention of a Central Government notification (Section 6) carries imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to five thousand rupees, or both, with owners/masters of vessels/aircraft also liable for fines for illegal importation. Contravention of prohibitions for young or certain other persons (Section 6A) is punishable with imprisonment up to three years or a fine or both. Failure to give notice of an accident (Section 8) results in a fine up to five hundred rupees, or if attended by loss of human life, imprisonment up to three months or a fine or both. Offences committed by companies hold both the company and responsible individuals liable.

repealed_acts: Act 12 of 1875 (portions)
Act 12 of 1891 (sub-section (2) of Section 2)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government may appoint the Chief Controller of Explosives or any other competent person to hold inquiries into more serious accidents (Section 9A).

applies_to: Whole India
Persons involved in the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport, import, and export of explosives
exemptions: Manufacture, possession, use, transport or importation of any explosive by any of the Armed Forces of the Union, and ordnance factories or other establishments of such Forces in accordance with rules or regulations made by the Central Government (Section 14(1)(a)).
Manufacture, possession, use, transport or importation of any explosive by any person employed under the Central Government or under a State Government in execution of this Act (Section 14(1)(b)).
Any explosive and any person or class of persons, absolutely or subject to conditions, as exempted by the Central Government by notification (Section 14(2)).
special_provisions: The definition of 'District Magistrate' includes the Commissioner of Police, Deputy Commissioner of Police, and Additional District Magistrate in certain areas (Section 4(c)).

Prohibition on manufacture, possession, sale, or transport of explosives by persons under eighteen years of age, those with certain criminal convictions, those bound for keeping the peace or good behaviour, or those whose licenses have been cancelled (Section 6A(a)).
Prohibition on selling, delivering, or despatching explosives to persons prohibited from possessing them or to persons of unsound mind (Section 6A(b)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a comprehensive licensing system for the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport, import, and export of explosives. The Central Government has powers to make rules, prohibit dangerous explosives, and grant exemptions. Authorized officers can inspect, search, seize, and remove explosives. Accidents must be reported and are subject to inquiry. Offences are defined with prescribed penalties, including imprisonment and fines, and provisions exist for forfeiture of explosives and distress of aircraft/vessels for unpaid fines. Arrests without warrant can be made for dangerous offences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts convicting the holder of a licence (Section 6E(6), 10), appellate courts or High Courts exercising revision powers (Section 6E(7)), and Magistrates for inquiries and apprehension (Section 9, 13).

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to amend and declare the law in force in the Punjab with respect to the making and maintenance of records-of-rights in land, the assessment and collection of land-revenue, and other matters relating to land and the liabilities incident thereto; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to amend and declare the existing law in the Punjab concerning the creation and upkeep of land records, the process of assessing and collecting land-revenue, and other related matters concerning land and its associated liabilities.

chapter_titles: RECOVERY OF OTHER DEMANDS BY REVENUE-OFFICERS.
SPECIAL JURISDICTION WITH RESPECT TO LAND.

key_sections.title: Title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application, and commencement provisions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'estate', 'landowner', 'land-revenue', and 'Revenue-officer'.

key_sections.title: Classes of Revenue-officers.
key_sections.description: Establishes the hierarchy and types of Revenue-officers, including Financial Commissioner, Commissioner, Collector, and Assistant Collectors.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Outlines the appeal process for orders made by Revenue-officers to higher authorities like the Collector, Commissioner, and Financial Commissioner.

key_sections.title: Record-of-rights and documents included therein.
key_sections.description: Mandates the creation of a record-of-rights for each estate, detailing its contents such as landowner information, rights, liabilities, and a map.

key_sections.title: Making of that part of the annual record which relates to land-owners, assignees of revenue and occupancy, tenants.
key_sections.description: Requires persons acquiring rights in an estate (landowner, assignee, occupancy tenant) to report their acquisition to the patwari for entry in the annual record.

key_sections.title: Rights of the Government in mines and minerals.
key_sections.description: Declares mines of metal, coal, earth-oil, and gold washing as Government property, granting powers for their enjoyment.

key_sections.title: Presumption in favour of entries in records-of-rights and annual records.
key_sections.description: States that entries in records-of-rights and annual records are presumed true until proven otherwise.

key_sections.title: Assessment of land-revenue.
key_sections.description: Declares all land liable to land-revenue payment, with exceptions, and specifies that assessment can be in cash or kind.

key_sections.title: Security for payment of land-revenue.
key_sections.description: Establishes that the entire estate and its landowners are jointly or severally liable for land-revenue, with certain provisos.

key_sections.title: Processes for recovery of arrears.
key_sections.description: Lists various processes for recovering arrears of land-revenue, including writ of demand, arrest, distress and sale, and transfer or attachment of holdings.

key_sections.title: Sale of estate or holding.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Collector, with Financial Commissioner's sanction, to sell an estate or holding for recovery of land-revenue arrears if other processes are insufficient.

key_sections.title: Effect of partitions of estates and tenancies on joint liability for revenue and rent.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that partitions do not affect joint liability for revenue or rent without express consent of the Financial Commissioner or landlord, respectively.

key_sections.title: Exclusion of jurisdiction of Civil Courts in matters within the jurisdiction of Revenue-officers
key_sections.description: Excludes the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in matters that the Local Government or a Revenue-officer is empowered to dispose of under this Act.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend the Law relating to the Tenancy of Land in the Punjab. WHEREAS it is expedient to amend the law relating to the tenancy of land in the Punjab; It is hereby enacted as follows: —

key_sections.title: Tenants having right of occupancy.
key_sections.description: Outlines the conditions under which a tenant acquires a right of occupancy in land, based on continuous occupation and payment of rent.

key_sections.title: Respective rights of landlord and tenant to produce.
key_sections.description: Defines the rights of landlords and tenants regarding the produce of the tenancy, including the first charge of rent on produce and exclusive possession rights.

key_sections.description: Empowers Revenue Courts to enhance or reduce the rent of occupancy tenants through a suit, subject to certain limitations.

key_sections.title: Grounds of ejectment of occupancy tenant.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the specific grounds upon which a tenant with a right of occupancy can be ejected from their tenancy.

key_sections.title: Restriction on ejectment.
key_sections.description: States that a tenant cannot be ejected except in execution of a decree or in specific cases like unsatisfied rent arrears or non-occupancy tenants.

key_sections.title: Private transfer of right of occupancy under section 5 by tenant.
key_sections.description: Details the conditions and procedure for a tenant with a right of occupancy under section 5 to transfer that right by sale, gift, or mortgage.

key_sections.title: Succession to right of occupancy.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the rules for the devolution of a right of occupancy upon the death of a tenant, including male lineal descendants, widow, and male collateral relatives.

key_sections.title: Improvements by landlords on tenancies of occupancy-tenants.
key_sections.description: Requires landlords to obtain Collector's permission before making improvements on occupancy-tenant tenancies and outlines the application process.

key_sections.title: Title of occupancy-tenant to make improvements.
key_sections.description: Affirms the right of an occupancy tenant to make improvements on their tenancy.

key_sections.title: Determination of compensation by Revenue Court.
key_sections.description: Mandates Revenue Courts to determine compensation for improvements or disturbance in suits related to ejectment or rent enhancement.

key_sections.title: Applications and proceedings cognizable by Revenue-officers.
key_sections.description: Lists various applications and proceedings that are to be exclusively handled by Revenue-officers, precluding other courts from taking cognizance.

key_sections.title: Revenue Court an suit cognizable by them.
key_sections.description: Defines Revenue Courts and specifies the classes of suits that must be instituted, heard, and determined by them, excluding other courts.

key_sections.title: Nullity of certain agreements contrary to the Act.
key_sections.description: Declares certain agreements made between landlords and tenants void if they override provisions of the Act regarding occupancy rights, rent, improvements, or ejectment.
