Persons in possession of land without consent of landlord
Whole of the territories (including the pargana of Spiti) for the time being administered by the Lieutenant – Governor of the Punjab
exemptions: Hazara district
Inferior landowner
Mortgagee of the rights of landowner

Person to whom a holding has been transferred, or an estate or holding has been let in farm, under the Punjab Land-revenue Act, 1887 (XVII of 1887), for the recovery of an arrear of land-revenue or of a sum recoverable as such an arrear
Person who takes from the Government a lease of unoccupied land for the purpose of subletting it
special_provisions: Pargana of Spiti (included in geographical extent)
Hazara district (excluded from geographical extent)
Special provisions for agreements made before November, 1871, and attested by proper officer in a regular settlement record (Section 112)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Local Government (Sections 52, 85, 88, 105); Financial Commissioner (Sections 46, 106); Governor General in Council (Sanction for rules under Sections 61, 88, 107).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a system of Revenue-officers and Revenue Courts, which have jurisdiction over applications and suits related to tenancy matters. It includes procedures for rent adjustment, ejectment, compensation, and appeals, review, and revision of orders and decrees.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Revenue Courts (for specific suits and proceedings); Civil Courts (for questions referred by Revenue Courts, or for validation of proceedings under mistake of jurisdiction by Chief Court); Chief Court (for jurisdiction questions and validation of proceedings).

schedules_summary.description: Lists enactments that are repealed by this Act, specifying their number, year, title, and the extent of repeal.

act_identification.act_title: THE KING OF OUDH’S ESTATE ACT, 1887.

legislative_details.enacted_by: THE GOVERNOR GENERAL OF INDIA IN COUNCIL.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS His late Majesty Wajid Ali Shah, Kind of Oudh, was during his lifetime exempt from the jurisdiction of the Civil Courts, and it is expedient to make provision for the administration of his estate otherwise than under the authority of those Courts; It is hereby enacted as follows :—
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the administration of the estate of His late Majesty the King of Oudh, who was exempt from civil court jurisdiction. It establishes the exclusive authority of the Governor General in Council for settling claims and distributing the estate, overriding normal legal proceedings.

key_sections.title: Administration of the estate of the late king of Oudh by the Governor General in Council.
key_sections.description: Grants exclusive authority to the Governor General in Council for administering the property, settling claims, and distributing the remaining estate of the late King of Oudh, with their acts not being questionable in any Court.

key_sections.title: Indemnity to Agent to the Governor General.
key_sections.description: Indemnifies the Agent to the Governor General and persons acting under his order from liability for acts done since 20th September 1887, in connection with the preservation and administration of the estate.

key_sections.title: Effect of Act.
key_sections.description: States that the Act takes effect notwithstanding any testamentary dispositions or civil court proceedings, and requires any person who has received a portion of the estate to account for it to an officer appointed by the Governor General in Council.

powers_conferred: Exclusive authority to the Governor General in Council to act in the administration of the property of the late King of Oudh (Section 1(1))
Power to the Governor General in Council to make distribution of the remaining property or proceeds (Section 1(1))
Power to the Governor General in Council to appoint an officer for accounting (Section 3)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Governor General in Council has the power to appoint an officer for accounting.

applies_to: The estate of His late Majesty the King of Oudh
exemptions: Acts of the Governor General in Council in connection with the administration or distribution of the property left by His late Majesty shall not be liable to be questioned in any Court (Section 1(2))
The Agent to the Governor General and all persons acting under his order are indemnified and discharged from liability (Section 2)
special_provisions: The Act provides for administration of the estate otherwise than under the authority of Civil Courts, due to the King's exemption from their jurisdiction.
The Act takes effect notwithstanding any testamentary or other disposition made by His late Majesty.
The Act takes effect notwithstanding any proceedings instituted before any Civil Court for administering the estate or collecting debts.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Governor General in Council has exclusive authority for administration, settlement of claims, and distribution. Persons receiving parts of the estate are bound to account to an appointed officer. Acts under this administration are immune from court challenge.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The Act explicitly states that acts of the Governor General in Council cannot be questioned in any Court, and no suit can be instituted against the Agent to the Governor General or the Secretary of State for India in Council regarding these acts.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN RESERVE FORCES ACT, 1888

legislative_details.geographical_extent: beyond the limits of India as well as within those limits

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the Government, discipline and regulation of [2][the] Indian Reserve Fortes; It is hereby enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the Government, discipline, and regulation of the Indian Reserve Forces.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

key_sections.title: Title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Division of Reserve Forces into Regular and Supplementary Reserves.
key_sections.description: Divides the Indian Reserve Forces into Regular Reserve and Supplementary Reserve.

key_sections.title: Locality of service of Reserves.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that members of the Indian Reserve Forces are liable to serve both within and beyond the limits of India.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules for regulation of Reserve Forces.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules and orders for the government, discipline, and regulation of the Indian Reserve Forces, and requires such rules to be laid before Parliament.

key_sections.title: Liability of Reserve Forces to military law.
key_sections.description: Subjects members of the Indian Reserve Forces to military law under rules and orders made under Section 4, similar to persons belonging to the Regular Army.

key_sections.title: Punishment of certain offences by persons belonging to Reserve Forces.
key_sections.description: Defines offences such as failure to attend, non-compliance with rules, or fraudulent pay claims, and prescribes punishments by court-martial or Magistrate.

key_sections.title: Reinstatement in civil employ of persons belonging to Reserve Forces on termination of periods of trailing, muster or Army service.
key_sections.description: Mandates employers to reinstate members of the Indian Reserve Forces after training or army service, with provisions for dispute resolution and penalties for non-compliance.

key_sections.title: Preservation of certain rights of persons belonging to Reserve Forces when called up for training, muster or army service.
key_sections.description: Ensures the preservation of provident fund, superannuation fund, or other employee benefit scheme rights for Reserve Forces members during training or army service.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint commencement date (Section 1)
Central Government: To make rules and orders for government, discipline and regulation of Indian Reserve Forces (Section 4)
Court-martial: To award punishment for offences (Section 6)
Presidency Magistrate or Magistrate of the first class: To award imprisonment for offences (Section 6)
Officer appointed by rule or order: To sign certificates regarding failure to attend (Section 6)
Authority prescribed by rules: To decide on reinstatement matters, exempt employers, require re-employment, or order compensation (Section 7)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Offences include failure to attend when required, failure to comply with rules/orders, or fraudulently obtaining pay by members of the Indian Reserve Forces (Section 6). Penalties for these offences range from punishments by court-martial (other than death, transportation, or imprisonment exceeding one year as per Army Act, 1950) to imprisonment by a Magistrate (up to six months for first offence, one year for subsequent). An employer's failure to obey an order for reinstatement is punishable with a fine up to one thousand rupees, and the court may order payment of compensation equal to six months' remuneration (Section 7).

repealed_acts: Section 7 (by Act 3 of 1958, s. 6)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government has the power to appoint the commencement date of the Act. Rules or orders made under the Act may appoint officers to sign certificates regarding attendance. Rules made under the Act may prescribe an authority to handle reinstatement matters.

applies_to: Persons belonging to the Indian Reserve Forces
Employers of persons belonging to the Indian Reserve Forces
exemptions: Employers may be exempted from reinstatement provisions by an authority prescribed by rules (Section 7)
special_provisions: The Act has been extended to and brought into force in Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963, s. 2 and the First Schedule (w.e.f. 01/07/1965)
The Act has been extended to Lakshadweep by Reg. 8 of 1965, s. 3 and the Schedule (w.e.f. 01/10/1967)
The Act has been extended to Pondicherry by Reg. 7 of 1963, s. 3 and the First Schedule (w.e.f. 01/10/1963)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is through military law for Reserve Forces members (Section 5), conviction by court-martial or Magistrates for specific offences (Section 6), and orders issued by a prescribed authority regarding employer duties, with fines and compensation for non-compliance (Section 7).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Court-martial, Presidency Magistrate, Magistrate of the first class (Section 6)

act_identification.act_title: The City of Bombay Municipal (Supplementary) Act, 1888

legislative_details.enacted_by: GOVERNOR GENERAL OF INDIA IN COUNCIL.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to supplement by legislation in the Council of the Governor General for making Laws and Regulations certain provisions of the City of Bombay Municipal Act, 1888, and of the Calcutta Municipal Consolidation Act, 1889; It is hereby enacted as follows :—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to supplement certain provisions of the City of Bombay Municipal Act, 1888, and the Calcutta Municipal Consolidation Act, 1889. It aims to confirm the validity of jurisdiction conferred upon municipal authorities, magistrates, and courts, and to establish appeal mechanisms to the High Court.

key_sections.title: Confirmation of the City of Bombay Municipal Act, 1888, and the Calcutta Municipal Consolidation Act,1889, so far as regards Benches, Magistrates and Courts of Small Causes
key_sections.description: Confirms the validity of the City of Bombay Municipal Act, 1888, and the Calcutta Municipal Consolidation Act, 1889, regarding jurisdiction of Appellate Benches, Magistrates, and Courts of Small Causes.

key_sections.title: Reference of questions by the Chief Judge of the Bombay Small Cause Court to the Bombay High Court
key_sections.description: Allows the Chief Judge of the Court of Small Causes of Bombay to refer questions of law or construction of documents to the High Court of Judicature at Bombay.

key_sections.title: Appeal to the Bombay High Court from certain orders of the Chief Judge of the Bombay Small Cause Court
key_sections.description: Provides for an appeal to the High Court of Judicature at Bombay from decisions of the Chief Judge of the Court of Small Causes of Bombay under sections 503 or 504 of the City of Bombay Municipal Act, 1888, when the claim exceeds two thousand rupees.

key_sections.title: Appeal to the Bombay High Court from orders of Presidency Magistrates in Bombay
key_sections.description: Establishes an appeal to the High Court of Judicature at Bombay from orders passed by a Presidency Magistrate under section 515 of the City of Bombay Municipal Act, 1888.

key_sections.title: Period of limitation for appeals to the Bombay High Court under the two last foregoing sections
key_sections.description: Specifies the period of limitation for appeals to the High Court under sections 3 and 4, deeming them appeals under the Code of Civil Procedure for limitation purposes.

powers_conferred: Chief Judge of the Court of Small Causes of Bombay: Power to refer questions of law to the High Court (Section 2).

High Court of Judicature at Bombay: Power to decide referred questions (Section 2), hear appeals from Chief Judge (Section 3) and Presidency Magistrates (Section 4), make rules for regulating appeals (Section 4(2)), direct payment of costs (Section 4(5)).
Presidency Magistrate: Power to recover costs as if they were a fine (Section 4(6)).

applies_to: Appellate Benches of Municipal Authorities
Presidency and other Magistrates
Courts of Small Causes or any Judge of such a Court
Chief Judge of the Court of Small Causes of Bombay
High Court of Judicature at Bombay
Municipal Commissioner for the City of Bombay
special_provisions: Provisions specifically for the City of Bombay and Calcutta.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: High Court (for regulating admission of appeals and procedure, Section 4(2)).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Appeals process to the High Court; execution of High Court orders by the Chief Judge of the Court of Small Causes; recovery of costs by Presidency Magistrates.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Court of Small Causes of Bombay, Presidency Magistrates.

act_identification.act_title: An Act to make further provision for the Administration of the Estate of His late Majesty the King of Oudh.

legislative_details.enacted_by: GOVERNOR GENERAL OF INDIA IN COUCIL

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS Act XIX of 1887 (an Act to provide for the Administration of the Estate of His late Majesty the King of Oudh) enacts that the Governor General in Council shall have exclusive authority to act in the administration of the property nature left by His late Majesty the King of Oudh in regard to the settlement and satisfaction of claims against the estate of His late Majesty, and may make distribution of the remaining property or the proceeds thereof in such manner as he deems fit among the family and dependents of His late Majesty; And whereas it is expedient to provide for the mode in which property may be transferred, and suits and other proceedings may be instituted, in the course of the administration of the estate of His late Majesty;
act_overview.purpose: This Act makes further provision for the administration of the estate of His late Majesty the King of Oudh. It specifies the mode for transferring property and instituting legal proceedings by the Agent to the Governor General in Council in connection with the estate.

key_sections.title: Transfers of property by and to the Agent to the Governor General in Council, and institution of legal proceedings by him.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Agent to the Governor General in Council to dispose of moveable and immoveable property, take conveyance of property, and institute legal proceedings in connection with the King of Oudh's estate.

key_sections.title: Consequences ensuring on death, resignation or removal Agent.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that property vested in an Agent passes to their successor, and legal proceedings can be continued by the successor upon the Agent's departure, death, resignation, or removal.

powers_conferred: Power to dispose of any moveable and immoveable property of His late Majesty the King of Oudh
Power to take a conveyance of any moveable or immoveable property in which His late Majesty had a beneficial interest

Power to institute any suit or other proceeding in any Civil, Criminal or Revenue Court in connection with the possession of any moveable or immoveable property belonging to the estate of His late Majesty or the dispossession of any person of any such property, or the recovery of rents, debts or other moneys due to the estate, or otherwise in connection with the administration of the estate.

applies_to: Administration of the Estate of His late Majesty the King of Oudh

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through the Agent to the Governor General in Council instituting suits or other proceedings in various courts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil, Criminal or Revenue Court

act_identification.act_title: THE REVENUE RECOVERY ACT, 1890

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India except *the State of Jammu and Kashmir*

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to make better provision for recovering certain public demands; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The primary purpose of this Act is to establish a legal framework for the efficient recovery of public demands, particularly arrears of land-revenue. It facilitates the recovery of such dues across different districts and from other public officers or local authorities.

key_sections.title: Title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title and geographical extent of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act such as 'district', 'Collector', and 'defaulter'.

key_sections.title: Recovery of public demands by enforcement of processes in other districts than those in which they become payable.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for a Collector to recover arrears of land-revenue or sums recoverable as such, from a defaulter in another district by sending a certificate.

key_sections.title: Remedy available to person denying liability to pay amount recovered under last foregoing section.
key_sections.description: Provides a mechanism for a person to institute a suit in a Civil Court if they deny liability for an amount recovered under Section 3, provided payment was made under protest.

key_sections.title: Recovery by Collectors of sums recoverable as arrears of revenue by other public officers or by local authorities.
key_sections.description: Empowers Collectors to recover sums due to other public officers or local authorities as if they were arrears of land-revenue.

key_sections.title: Property liable to sale under this Act.
key_sections.description: Details the process of issuing a proclamation to prohibit the transfer or charging of immovable property belonging to a defaulter and the conditions under which such property can be sold for recovery.

key_sections.title: Saving of local laws relating to revenue.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not impair existing local laws for revenue recovery or authorize arrest for municipal tax recovery.

key_sections.title: Recovery in India of certain public demands arising beyond India.
key_sections.description: Allows for the recovery in India of arrears of land-revenue or sums recoverable as such, arising in local areas under Central Government administration but outside India.

key_sections.title: Recovery in India of land revenues’ etc., accruing in Burma.
key_sections.description: Enables the Central Government to direct the recovery in India of land revenues and other sums accruing in Burma (and later Pakistan) as arrears of land-revenue, subject to certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Duty of Collectors to remit moneys collected in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Mandates Collectors to remit sums recovered under a certificate from another State or from Pakistan/Burma to the issuing Collector, after deducting expenses.

powers_conferred: Collector: To send certificates for recovery of arrears (Section 3).
Collector: To recover amounts stated in certificates as if they were arrears of land-revenue (Section 3, 5).
Collector: To recover sums for other public officers or local authorities (Section 5).
Collector: To issue a proclamation prohibiting transfer or charging of defaulter's immovable property (Section 6).
Collector: To withdraw such proclamation (Section 6).
Central Government: To direct recovery in India of land revenues accruing in Burma/Pakistan (Section 9).
Collector: To remit collected moneys to the issuing Collector (Section 10).

related_acts: Benares Family Domains Act, 1904 (U.P. Act 3 of 1904)
Bengal Public Demands Recovery Act, 1913 (Bengal Act III of 1913)

applies_to: defaulter (a person from whom an arrear of land-revenue, or a sum recoverable as an arrear of land-revenue, is due, and includes a person who is responsible as surety for the payment of any such arrear or sum)
special_provisions: Modified in its application to the Benares Family Domains by s.15 of the Benares Family Domains Act, 1904 (U.P. Act 3 of 1904).
Extended to Goa, Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Lakshadweep, and Pondicherry with modifications.
Amended in Assam by the Assam Act 16 of 1971, inserting Section 3A.
Now applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh by Notification S.O. 3912 (E), dated 30th October, 2019 (w.e.f. 31-10-2019).
Sub-sections (1) and (2) of Section 9 apply in relation to Pakistan as they apply in relation to Burma.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Recovery by Collectors through certificates, issuance of proclamations prohibiting property transfer, and sale of property.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil Court (for suits under Section 4).

schedules_summary.description: Contains the form of the certificate to be sent by a Collector for the recovery of public demands in other districts.

act_identification.act_title: THE CHARITABLE ENDOWMENTS ACT, 1890

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the vesting and administration of property held in trust for charitable purposes; It is hereby enacted as follows: ––
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the vesting and administration of property held in trust for charitable purposes. It establishes treasurers of Charitable Endowments to hold such property and outlines procedures for settling administration schemes.

key_sections.title: Title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's official title, its geographical application, and the date it came into force.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines 'charitable purpose' to include relief of the poor, education, medical relief, and public utility, excluding religious teaching or worship.

key_sections.title: Appointment and incorporation of treasurer of Charitable Endowments.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central and State Governments to appoint officers as treasurers of Charitable Endowments, who become corporations sole for holding property.

key_sections.title: Definition of “appropriate Government”, etc.
key_sections.description: Defines 'appropriate Government' based on the geographical extent and executive authority over a charitable endowment.

key_sections.title: Orders vesting property in treasurer.
key_sections.description: Allows the appropriate Government to order property held for charitable purposes to be vested in the treasurer of Charitable Endowments.

key_sections.title: Schemes for administration of property vested in the treasurer.
key_sections.description: Enables the appropriate Government to settle or modify schemes for the administration of property vested in the treasurer.

key_sections.title: Mode of applying for vesting orders and schemes.
key_sections.description: Specifies who can make applications for vesting orders and administration schemes.

key_sections.title: Bare trusteeship of treasurer.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the treasurer acts as a bare trustee, not administering the trust directly, and must keep separate accounts.

key_sections.title: Annual publication of list of properties vested in treasurer.
key_sections.description: Requires the treasurer to annually publish a list of vested properties and an abstract of accounts in the Official Gazette.

key_sections.title: Limitation of functions and powers of treasurer.
key_sections.description: States that the treasurer is always a sole trustee and limits their power to take, hold, or transfer property except under specific conditions.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the appropriate Government the power to make rules for prescribing fees, regulating scheme publication, auditing accounts, and generally carrying out the Act's purposes.

key_sections.title: Indemnity to Government and treasurer.
key_sections.description: Provides indemnity to the Government against suits and limits the grounds on which suits can be instituted against a treasurer.

key_sections.title: Saving with respect to Advocate General and Official Trustee.
key_sections.description: Ensures that the Act does not impair the operation of enactments concerning the authority of an Advocate General or the Official Trustees Act, 1913.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint treasurer of Charitable Endowments for India (Section 3(1))
State Government to appoint treasurer of Charitable Endowments for the State (Section 3(1))
Appropriate Government to order vesting of property in treasurer (Section 4(1))
Appropriate Government to settle or modify schemes for administration of property (Section 5(1), (2))
Appropriate Government to appoint a day for scheme operation (Section 5(3))
Appropriate Government to direct annual publication of list of properties (Section 9)
Appropriate Government to issue directions for transfer or disposal of property vested in treasurer (Section 10(1), (2))
Appropriate Government to appoint successor treasurer in contingencies (Section 11)
Central Government to direct transfer of property from one treasurer to another (Section 12)
Appropriate Government to make rules consistent with the Act (Section 13(1))

authorities_established: treasurer of Charitable Endowments for India
treasurer of Charitable Endowments for the State
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government may appoint an officer of the Government by the name of his office to be treasurer of Charitable Endowments for India, and the Government of any State may appoint an officer of the Government by the name of his office to be treasurer of Charitable Endowments for the State.

applies_to: property held in trust for charitable purposes
whole of India
exemptions: a purpose which relates exclusively to religious teaching or worship
any wakf to which the Wakf Act, 1954 (29 of 1954) applies
special_provisions: Declared in force in the Sonthal Parganas by the Sonthal Parganas Settlement Regulation, 1872 (3 of 1872)
Declared in force in the Khondmals District by the Khondmals Laws Regulation, 1936 (4 of 1936)
Declared in force in the Angul District by the Angul Laws Regulation, 1936 (5 of 1936)
Extended to Berar by the Berar Laws Act, 1941 (4 of 1941)
Extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963
Extended to Goa, Daman and Diu by Reg. 11 of 1963
Extended to Lakshadweep by Reg. 8 of 1965
Extended to Pondicherry by Reg. 7 of 1963
Ceased to be in force in the State of Madras by Madras Act 22 of 1959
A proviso to section 5, applicable only to Bengal, has been added by the Bengal Wakf Act, 1934 (Ben. 13 of 1934), section 79.
A new sub-section (3), applicable only to Bengal, has been added by the Bengal Wakf Act, 1934 (Ben. 13 of 1934), s. 80.
Addition of section 6-A in Uttar Pradesh by the Uttar Pradesh Act 37 of 1952
Insertion of new section 12A in Karnataka by Karnataka Act 19 of 1973

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the appointment of treasurers of Charitable Endowments, the vesting of property in them, and the settlement of administration schemes by the appropriate Government. It also provides for legal recourse against treasurers for willful neglect or default.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts have jurisdiction to inquire whether the appropriate Government made a scheme and to hear suits against treasurers for divesting property or for loss/misapplication due to willful neglect or default.

act_identification.act_title: THE GUARDIANS AND WARDS ACT, 1890

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to guardian and ward; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws concerning guardians and wards. Its primary objective is to provide a legal framework for the appointment, declaration, duties, rights, and liabilities of guardians for minors and their property.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II APPOINTMENT AND DECLARATION OF GUARDIANS
CHAPTER III DUTIES, RIGHTS AND LIABILITIES OF GUARDIANS

key_sections.title: Title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Saving of jurisdiction of Courts of Wards and Chartered High Courts.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not derogate from the jurisdiction of Courts of Wards or High Courts.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'minor', 'guardian', and 'ward'.

key_sections.title: Power of the Court to make order as to guardianship.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Court to appoint or declare a guardian for a minor's person or property for the minor's welfare.

key_sections.title: Court having jurisdiction to entertain application.
key_sections.description: Determines which District Court has jurisdiction to hear applications for guardianship of a minor's person or property.

key_sections.title: Matters to be considered by the Court in appointing guardian.
key_sections.description: Outlines the factors the Court must consider when appointing a guardian, primarily the welfare of the minor.

key_sections.title: Guardian not to be appointed by the Court in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Specifies circumstances where the Court cannot appoint a guardian, such as when property is under a Court of Wards or when a parent is fit.

key_sections.title: Fiduciary relation of guardian to ward.
key_sections.description: Establishes the fiduciary duty of a guardian towards their ward, prohibiting profit from the office.

key_sections.title: Duties of guardian of the person.
key_sections.description: Defines the responsibilities of a guardian of the person, including custody, support, health, and education of the ward.

key_sections.title: Duties of guardian of property.
key_sections.description: Outlines the duties of a guardian of property, requiring careful management for the ward's benefit.

key_sections.title: Limitation of powers of guardian of property appointed or declared by the Court.
key_sections.description: Restricts the powers of a court-appointed guardian of property regarding mortgage, charge, transfer, or long-term lease without court permission.

key_sections.title: Removal of guardian.
key_sections.description: Lists the grounds upon which a guardian can be removed by the Court, such as abuse of trust or incapacity.

key_sections.title: Cessation of authority of guardian.
key_sections.description: Details the circumstances under which the authority of a guardian of the person or property ceases.

key_sections.title: Penalty for removal of ward from jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for a guardian who removes a ward from the Court's jurisdiction in contravention of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of High Court to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the High Court the authority to make rules for the effective implementation and guidance of the Act.

powers_conferred: Power of the Court to make order as to guardianship (Section 7)
Power to make interlocutory order for production of minor and interim protection of person and property (Section 12)
Power to award remuneration for auditing accounts (Section 34A)
Power to make orders for regulating conduct or proceedings of guardians, and enforcement of those orders (Section 43)
Power to call upon the Collector or subordinate courts for reports (Section 46)
Power of High Court to make rules (Section 50)
Power to confer jurisdiction on subordinate judicial officers and to transfer proceedings to such officers (Section 4A)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 44 prescribes a penalty for removal of ward from jurisdiction, including a fine not exceeding one thousand rupees or imprisonment up to six months. Section 45 prescribes penalties for contumacy, including a fine not exceeding one hundred rupees (with further daily fines) and detention in civil jail.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Court (District Court, High Court) has the power to appoint or declare guardians.

applies_to: Minors
Guardians of minors (person and property)
exemptions: Jurisdiction of Courts of Wards and Chartered High Courts (Section 3)
Guardianship of a minor whose property is under the superintendence of a Court of Wards (Section 19)
Guardianship of a married female minor whose husband is fit (Section 19(a))
Guardianship of a minor (other than married female) whose father or mother is living and fit (Section 19(b))
special_provisions: Provisions for Collector acting as guardian (Sections 18, 23)
Provisions for simultaneous proceedings in different Courts (Section 14)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Orders can be enforced like injunctions (Section 43(4)). Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance (Sections 44, 45). Suits against guardians for accounting are provided (Sections 35, 36).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District Court, High Court, and subordinate judicial officers empowered by the High Court or District Court.

schedules_summary.description: Contained a list of enactments repealed by this Act, but the schedule itself has been repealed.

act_identification.act_title: An Act to provide for the better administration of the North-Western Provinces and Oudh and to amend certain enactments in force in those Provinces and in Oudh.
act_identification.act_short_title: The North-Western Provinces and Oudh Act, 1890

legislative_details.geographical_extent: North-Western Provinces and Oudh, Jhansi Division

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the better administration of the territories respectively administered by the Lieutenant Governor of the North-Western Provinces and the Chief Commissioner of Oudh, and for that purpose to amend certain enactments which are in force in the said Provinces and in Oudh; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to improve the administration of the North-Western Provinces and Oudh. It achieves this by extending certain laws to the Jhansi Division, establishing a unified Board of Revenue for both regions, and amending various existing enactments to streamline legal and administrative processes.

chapter_titles: PART III THE NORTH-WESTERN PROVINCES AND OUDH

key_sections.title: Title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the North-Western Provinces and Oudh Act, 1890.

key_sections.title: Commencement of Part I.
key_sections.description: Specifies that Part I comes into force on a day directed by the Lieutenant-Governor via notification.

key_sections.title: Laws in force in certain districts of the Allahabad Division to apply to Jhansi.
key_sections.description: Mandates that enactments in force in temporarily-settled districts of Allahabad Division apply to Jhansi, and repeals certain enactments in Jhansi, with exceptions.

key_sections.title: Discharge of functions assigned to Deputy Commissioner and Commissioner by Act 17 of 1886.
key_sections.description: Transfers functions of Deputy Commissioner and Commissioner under the Jhansi and Morar Act, 1886, to the District Judge and High Court, respectively.

key_sections.title: Jhansi Division to cease to be a Scheduled District.
key_sections.description: Declares that the Jhansi Division ceases to be a Scheduled District from a specified day.

key_sections.title: Application of Act 12 of 1887 to Jhansi, and disposal of pending cases.
key_sections.description: Outlines how pending civil cases and proceedings in the Jhansi Division are to be disposed of by various courts after the Act comes into force.

key_sections.title: Commencement of Part II.
key_sections.description: Specifies that Part II comes into force on a day directed by the Chief Commissioner of Oudh via notification.

key_sections.title: Board of Revenue of the North-Western Provinces to be the Board of Revenue of, and Chief Revenue authority in, Oudh.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Board of Revenue of the North-Western Provinces as the Board of Revenue and Chief Revenue-authority for Oudh.

key_sections.title: Pending appeals.
key_sections.description: Provides for the disposal of appeals pending when Part II comes into force, allowing the State Government to transfer certain appeals to the District Judge.

key_sections.title: Commencement of Part III.
key_sections.description: Specifies that Part III comes into force on a day directed by the Lieutenant Governor of the North-Western Provinces and Chief Commissioner of Oudh via notification.

key_sections.title: Place where the Board may sit.
key_sections.description: Allows the Board of Revenue to sit in places in the North-Western Provinces or Oudh as appointed by the State Government for case disposal.

powers_conferred: Lieutenant-Governor to direct the commencement of Part I by notification in the Official Gazette (Section 2)
Chief Commissioner of Oudh to direct the commencement of Part II by notification in the Official Gazette (Section 10)
State Government to transfer pending appeals to the District Judge (Section 54)
Lieutenant Governor of the North-Western Provinces and Chief Commissioner of Oudh to direct the commencement of Part III by notification in the Official Gazette (Section 62)
State Government to appoint places for the Board of Revenue to sit (Section 63)

amended_acts: Bengal, North-Western Provinces and Assam Civil Courts Act, 1887 (12 of 1887)
repealed_acts: Jhansi Courts Act, 1867 (18 of 1867)
Act No. 27 of 1867
related_acts: United Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1901 (U.P. Act 3 of 1901)
Bundelkhand Encumbered Estates Act, 1903 (U.P. Act 1 of 1903)
Bengal, North-Western Provinces and Assam Civil Courts Act, 1887 (12 of 1887)

authorities_established: Board of Revenue of the North-Western Provinces and Oudh
regulatory_bodies: Board of Revenue of the North-Western Provinces and Oudh

applies_to: North-Western Provinces
Oudh
Jhansi Division
exemptions: Jhansi Encumbered Estates Act, 1882 (16 of 1882)
Jhansi and Morar Act, 1886 (17 of 1886)
special_provisions: Specific provisions for the Jhansi Division regarding application and repeal of laws and disposal of pending cases (Part I)
Specific provisions for Oudh regarding the Board of Revenue and disposal of pending appeals (Part II)

implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District Judge, High Court, Munsif, Subordinate Judge, Tahsildar, Assistant Commissioner (for pending cases)

act_identification.act_title: EASEMENTS (EXTENDING ACT V OF 1882)

legislative_details.geographical_extent: to Bombay and the North-Western Provinces and Oudh. Extended Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh by Act 34 of 2019, s. 95 and the fifth schedule (w.e.f. 31-10-2019).

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to extend the Indian Easements Act, 1882 (5 of 1882), to certain areas in which that Act is not in force; It is Hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to extend the Indian Easements Act, 1882, to specific territories where it was not previously in force, namely Bombay and the North-Western Provinces and Oudh.

key_sections.title: Extension of Act V, 1882, to Bombay and the North-Western Provinces and Oudh.
key_sections.description: This section extends the Indian Easements Act, 1882 (V of 1882), to the territories administered by the Governor of Bombay in Council and the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces and Chief Commissioner of Oudh.

applies_to: territories respectively administered by the Governor of Bombay in Council
lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces and Chief Commissioner of Oudh
Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir
Union territory of Ladakh

act_identification.act_title: THE MOORSHEDABAD ACT, 1891

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to confirm and give effect to the indenture which is set forth in the schedule to this Act and which was made the twelfth day of March, 1891, between the Secretary of State for India in Council of the one part and Ihtisham-ul-Mulk Rais-ud Dowlah Amir-ulOmrah Nawab Sir Syud Hussan Ali Khan Bahadoor Mohabat Jung, G.C.I.E., Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabd, eldest son of His late Highness Moontazin-ul-Mulk Mohsenud Dowlah Fureedoon Jah Syud Mansoor Ali Khan Bahadoor Nusrat Jung, late Nawab Nazim of Bengal, Behar and Orissa, of the other part; It is hereby enacted as follows :—
act_overview.purpose: This Act confirms and gives effect to an Indenture made between the Secretary of State for India in Council and the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad, Amir-ul-Omrah, concerning the property, dignity, and succession of the Nawab Bahadoor.

key_sections.title: Title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'the Moorshedabad Act, 1891' and provides for its immediate commencement.

key_sections.title: Confirmation of indenture of March, 1891.
key_sections.description: Confirms the indenture mentioned in the Act.

key_sections.title: Additions to schedule to indenture.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Governor General in Council to add additional immoveable property to the schedules of the indenture, upon the written request of the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad.

key_sections.title: Limitation for claims to scheduled immoveable property.
key_sections.description: Establishes a sixty-year limitation period for acquiring rights to scheduled immoveable property by adverse possession or assertion of title, if such right had not accrued before the passing of this Act.

key_sections.title: Perpetual descent of property.
key_sections.description: Declares that all property mentioned in the indenture or its schedules shall descend and be enjoyed forever by the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad for the time being, subject to the indenture's provisions.

key_sections.title: Relief from stamp and registration Laws.
key_sections.description: Provides that the indenture shall be admissible in evidence and have the same effect as if duly stamped and registered, for all purposes of enactments in force.

powers_conferred: Governor General in Council: Power to add immoveable property to the schedules of the indenture (Section 3).

Secretary of State: Power to enter upon and take possession of immoveable properties, and receive rents/profits and the monthly sum, in case of contravention of terms, extravagance, waste, or mismanagement by the Nawab Bahadoor (as per the indenture).

applies_to: The Secretary of State for India in Council
The Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad, Amir-ul-Omrah, and his lineal heirs male
Immoveable and moveable property mentioned in the indenture and its schedules
special_provisions: Perpetual descent of property to the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad for the time being (Section 5).
Exemption of the indenture from stamp and registration laws (Section 6).

Specific provisions for the maintenance and support of the Nawab Bahadoor and the honour and dignity of his station, including an annual payment and income from specified properties (as detailed in the indenture).
Conditions regarding inalienability of properties, maintenance of buildings, and powers of the Secretary of State in case of mismanagement (as detailed in the indenture).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Governor General in Council (for adding property to schedules under Section 3).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act confirms an indenture which outlines the rights and obligations of the parties. The Secretary of State has powers to intervene in property management in case of mismanagement by the Nawab Bahadoor.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the full text of the Indenture made on 12th March 1891, between the Secretary of State for India in Council and the Nawab Bahadoor of Moorshedabad, detailing agreements regarding property, allowances, succession, and the relinquishment of the Nawab Nazim title.

act_identification.act_title: THE BANKERS’ BOOKS EVIDENCE ACT, 1891

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India [except the State of Jammu and Kashmir]

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to amend the Law of Evidence with respect to Bankers’ books; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to amend the Law of Evidence specifically concerning the use of Bankers' books in legal proceedings, making certified copies admissible as prima facie evidence.

key_sections.title: Title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'company', 'corporation', 'bankers' books', 'legal proceeding', and 'certified copy'.

key_sections.title: Conditions in the printout.
key_sections.description: Specifies the conditions and certifications required for printouts of electronic data to be considered certified copies.

key_sections.title: Power to extend provisions of Act.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to extend the Act's provisions to books of certain partnerships or individual bankers.

key_sections.title: Mode of proof of entries in bankers’ books.
key_sections.description: Establishes that certified copies of entries in bankers' books shall be received as prima facie evidence in legal proceedings.

key_sections.title: Case in which officer of bank not compellable to produce books.
key_sections.description: Protects bank officers from being compelled to produce bankers' books or appear as witnesses, unless ordered by a Court or Judge for special cause.

key_sections.title: Inspection of books by order of Court or Judge.
key_sections.description: Allows a Court or Judge to order inspection and copying of bank entries or the production of certified copies upon application by a party to a legal proceeding.

key_sections.title: Costs.
key_sections.description: Addresses the discretion of the Court or Judge regarding costs incurred for applications or orders under this Act, including payment by or to the bank.

key_sections.title: Order of court to be construed to be order made by specified officer.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that in certain investigations or inquiries, orders of a Court or Judge are to be construed as orders made by a specified officer not lower than a Superintendent of Police.

powers_conferred: State Government: Power to extend the provisions of the Act to the books of any partnership or individual carrying on the business of bankers (Section 3).
Court or Judge: Power to compel an officer of a bank to produce books for special cause (Section 5).
Court or Judge: Power to order inspection and taking copies of entries in a banker’s book (Section 6).
Court or Judge: Power to order the bank to prepare and produce certified copies of entries (Section 6).
Court or Judge: Discretion over costs of applications and actions under the Act (Section 7).

related_acts: State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959 (38 of 1959)

applies_to: Any company or corporation carrying on the business of banking.
Any partnership or individual to whose books the provisions of this Act shall have been extended.
Any post office savings bank or money order office.
exemptions: State of Jammu and Kashmir (historically, as per the text).
special_provisions: Extended in its application to the whole of the Union territory of Lakshadweep.
Extended to the Union territory of Pondicherry.
Applies in relation to the Development Banks as if that were a bank.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the admissibility of certified copies of bankers' books as prima facie evidence in legal proceedings. Courts and Judges have the power to order inspection, production of certified copies, and can compel bank officers to produce books under special circumstances. Costs related to such orders are at the discretion of the Court or Judge.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The Court (person or persons before whom a legal proceeding is held or taken), Judge (Judge of a High Court Division), Court of Civil Judicature (for enforcing cost orders).

act_identification.act_title: An Act for the Regulation of the Bengal Military Police.

legislative_details.enacted_by: GOVERNOR GENERNAL OF INDIA IN COUNCIL
legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of the territories subject to the Lieutenant-Governor of Bengal

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the better regulation of the Bengal Reserve Police, specifically focusing on the Bengal Military Police.

key_sections.title: Title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its geographical extent, and the method for its commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Military Police-officer', 'active service', and 'Commandant'.

key_sections.title: Enrolment and discharge of Military Police-officers.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for the enrolment of Military Police-officers, including signing a statement, and conditions for their discharge.

key_sections.title: More heinous offences.
key_sections.description: Defines serious offences committed by Military Police-officers, such as mutiny, sedition, desertion on active service, and specifies their corresponding severe punishments.

key_sections.title: Less heinous offences.
key_sections.description: Defines less serious offences committed by Military Police-officers, including intoxication on duty, insubordination, and malingering, and prescribes their punishments.

key_sections.title: Minor punishments.
key_sections.description: Authorizes specific officers (District Magistrate, Commandant, Second-in-Command) to award minor punishments for petty disciplinary offences without a formal trial.

key_sections.title: Conferment of magisterial powers on Police-officers.
key_sections.description: Allows the Local Government to invest Police-officers not below the rank of Commandant with magisterial powers for inquiring into or trying offences committed by Military Police-officers.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Local Government the authority to make orders and rules consistent with this Act concerning the Military Police.

powers_conferred: Local Government: To appoint the date of commencement of the Act (Section 1(3)).
Local Government: To direct classes and grades of Military Police-officers (Section 4(1)).
Local Government: To direct the place of imprisonment for sentenced persons (Section 8).
Local Government: To invest Police-officers with magisterial powers (Section 10).
Local Government: To make orders and rules regarding the Military Police (Section 13).
District Magistrate, Commandant or Second-in-Command: To award minor punishments (Section 7(1)).
Commandant or Second-in-Command: To exercise disciplinary powers over certain Police-officers (Section 11).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines 'more heinous offences' (e.g., mutiny, sedition, desertion on active service, using criminal force against a superior) punishable with transportation for life or a term not less than seven years, or imprisonment up to fourteen years, or fine up to three months' pay, or a combination. 'Less heinous offences' (e.g., intoxication on duty, insubordination, malingering, desertion not on active service) are punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to three months' pay, or both. Minor punishments for petty offences against discipline include imprisonment up to seven days or punishment drill/extra duty up to thirty days.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Local Government appoints Commandants and Seconds-in-Command of Military Police (Section 2).

applies_to: Military Police-officer
persons appointed to the Bengal Police Force under section 7 of Act V of 1861

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through the prosecution of offences, awarding of minor punishments by designated officers, and the conferment of magisterial powers on Police-officers for inquiry and trial.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Criminal Court; Police-officer not below the rank of Commandant with magisterial powers.

schedules_summary.description: Contains a statement that Military Police-officers must sign, outlining the conditions for their discharge from service, particularly after three years and when not on active service, and the implications of re-enlistment.

act_identification.act_title: THE MADRAS CITY CIVIL COURT ACT, 1892

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to establish an additional Civil Court for the City of Madras; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The primary purpose of this Act is to establish an additional Civil Court for the City of Madras. This court is vested with jurisdiction to handle civil suits and proceedings of a specific monetary value, thereby augmenting the existing judicial infrastructure in the city.

key_sections.title: Title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and indicates its commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used within the Act, such as 'City Court' and 'High Court'.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the City Court.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Local Government to establish the Madras City Civil Court and defines its jurisdiction and monetary limits for civil suits and proceedings.

key_sections.title: Appointment, suspension and removal of Judges.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Local Government to appoint, suspend, or remove Judges of the City Court by notification.

key_sections.title: Judge of City Court to be Judge of Small Clause Court.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that every City Court Judge also serves as a Judge of the Small Cause Court for cognizable cases and performs duties as required by the Chief Justice of the High Court.

key_sections.title: Powers of Judges when City Court consists of more than one Judge.
key_sections.description: Outlines the powers of individual Judges and the Principal Judge when the City Court has multiple Judges, including distribution of business.

key_sections.title: Appointment, powers, duties and punishment of ministerial officers.
key_sections.description: Details the appointment, powers, duties, and disciplinary actions (suspension, removal, fine) for ministerial officers of the City Court.

key_sections.title: Questions arising in suits, etc., under Act to be dealt with according to law administered by High Court.
key_sections.description: Mandates that all questions in suits or proceedings in the City Court be determined according to the law administered by the High Court in its ordinary original civil jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Receivers.
key_sections.description: Confers powers on the City Court or any Judge thereof to appoint Receivers, similar to High Courts and District Courts under the Code of Civil Procedure.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Designates the High Court as the authority to hear appeals from the City Court and specifies the period of limitation for such appeals.

key_sections.title: Saving of original civil jurisdiction of High Court.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not affect the High Court's original civil jurisdiction, with provisions for costs and transfer of suits.

powers_conferred: Local Government to establish the Madras City Civil Court (Section 3)
Local Government to appoint, suspend, and remove Judges of the City Court (Section 4)
Local Government to appoint a principal Judge when the City Court consists of more than one Judge (Section 6(b))
Local Government to sanction the appointment of clerks, bailiffs, and other ministerial officers (Section 7(1))
Local Government to prescribe the form and dimensions of the City Court's seal (Section 17)
Local Government to approve the list of holidays and vacations (Section 18(1))
Principal Judge to make arrangements for the distribution of the business of the Court among various Judges (Section 6(c))
Judge of the City Court or principal Judge to appoint clerks, bailiffs, and other ministerial officers (Section 7(1))
Judge of the City Court or principal Judge to direct the powers and duties of ministerial officers (Section 7(2))
Judge of the City Court or principal Judge to suspend or remove any appointed officer (Section 7(3)(a))
Judge of the City Court or principal Judge to fine any officer guilty of misconduct or neglect (Section 7(3)(b))
High Court to control the suspension or removal of officers (Section 7(3))
High Court to prescribe fees for serving or executing processes (Section 10)
City Court or any Judge thereof to appoint Receivers (Section 11)
High Court to hear appeals from the City Court (Section 15(1))
High Court Judge to remove for trial any suit from the City Court (Section 14, 16(2))
Judge of the City Court or principal Judge to draw up a list of holidays and vacations (Section 18(1))

related_acts: letters Patent for the High Court, dated the twenty-eight day of December, 1865

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Local Government appoints Judges; Judge of the City Court or principal Judge appoints ministerial officers.
regulatory_bodies: High Court of Judicature at Madras

applies_to: suits and other proceedings of a civil nature not exceeding two thousand five hundred rupees in value and arising within the City of Madras
exemptions: suits or proceedings cognizable by the High Court as a Court of Admiralty or Vice-Admiralty or as a Colonial Court of Admiralty, or as a Court having testamentary, intestate or matrimonial jurisdiction
suits or proceedings cognizable by the Court for the relief of insolvent debtors
suits or proceedings cognizable by the Small Cause Court
special_provisions: Applicable specifically to the City of Madras

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the establishment and functioning of the Madras City Civil Court, its appointed Judges, and ministerial officers. The High Court exercises appellate jurisdiction and control over certain aspects of the City Court's administration.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Madras City Civil Court, High Court of Judicature at Madras, Small Cause Court, Court for the relief of insolvent debtors

act_identification.act_title: THE SIR DINSHAW MANOCKJEE PETIT ACT, 1893
act_identification.act_short_title: THE SIR DINSHAW MANOCKJEE PETIT ACT, 1893

legislative_details.enacted_by: GOVERNOR GENERAL OF INDIA IN COUNCIL
legislative_details.geographical_extent: British India, with specific provisions concerning property in the Island of Bombay and the Presidency of Bombay

act_overview.preamble: An Act for settling Bonds of the Municipal Corporation of the City of Bombay producing an annual income of one lakh and twenty five thousand rupees and a Mansion-house and hereditaments called "Petit Hall" in the Island of Bombay, the property of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit, Baronet, so as to accompany and support the title and dignity of a Baronet lately conferred by Her Present Majesty Queen Victoria on him for and during the term of his natural life, and from and immediately after his decease to hold to his second son, Framjee Dinshaw Petit, Esquire, and the heirs male of his body lawfully begotten, and in default of such issue with remainder to the heirs male of the body of the said Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit, and for other purposes connected therewith. WHEREAS by Letters Patent of Her Majesty Queen Victoria, by the Grace of God of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, Queen, Defender of the Faith, dated at Westminster on or about the first day of September in the fifty-fourth year of Her Reign, and by Warrant under the Queen's sign-manual, Her said Majesty made known that She, of Her special Grace, certain knowledge and more motion, had erected, appointed and created her trusty and well beloved Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit of "Petit Hall,” in the Island of Bombay, Knight, to the dignity, state and degree of a Baronet, and him, the said Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit, for Her Majesty, her heirs and successors, she did erect, appoint and create a Baronet of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland by the said Letters Patent, to hold to him, for and during the term of his natural life, and from and immediately after his decease to hold to Framjee Dinshaw Petit, Esquire, second son of the said Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit, and the heirs male of his body lawfully begotten and to be begotten, and in default of such issue with remainder to the heirs male of the body of the said Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit lawfully begotten and to be begotten; And whereas in fulfilment of an engagement in that behalf made with Her Majesty's Government the said Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit is desirous of settling in perpetuity such property on himself and on the said Framjee Dinshaw Petit and the heirs male of their respective bodies who may succeed to the said Baronetcy as shall be adequate to support the dignity of the title conferred on him and them as aforesaid; And whereas the said Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit is seised of a Mansion-house and hereditaments situate in the Island of Bombay called "Petit Hall," and has an absolute estate of inheritance therein, and is desirous, in fulfilment of the aforesaid engagement, of settling bonds or debentures of the Municipal Corporation of the City of Bombay producing an annual income of one lakh and twenty-five thousand rupees, and the said Mansion-house and hereditaments, to the uses, upon the trusts and for the purposes hereinafter limited and declared, concerning the same respectively;
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to settle specific property, including bonds and a mansion-house ("Petit Hall"), to accompany and support the title and dignity of a Baronet conferred upon Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit and his male heirs. It also mandates that the beneficiaries of the Baronetcy adopt and use the names "Dinshaw Manockjee Petit" to maintain the family's identity associated with the title.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of Trustee.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Corporation with perpetual succession and a common seal, styled "The Trustees of the Dinshaw Manockjee Petit Baronetcy", comprising specific officials and their successors, to execute the Act's powers and purposes.

key_sections.title: Heirs of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit to take his name.
key_sections.description: Mandates that Framjee Dinshaw Petit and all male heirs succeeding to the Baronetcy shall take and use the names "Dinshaw Manockjee Petit" in lieu of any other names.

key_sections.title: Vesting and application of income of settled property.
key_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of Municipal Corporation bonds into the Corporation's name, to be held in trust, with income applied for the benefit of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit, then Framjee Dinshaw Petit, and subsequently the Baronet for the time being.

key_sections.title: Application of income during minority.
key_sections.description: Allows the Corporation to apply income for the maintenance and education of a minor Baronet, investing the residue until the Baronet attains majority.

key_sections.title: Mansion-house limited to the use of the Baronet for the time being.
key_sections.description: Limits the "Petit Hall" Mansion-house and hereditaments to the use of Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit, then Framjee Dinshaw Petit, and subsequently the male heirs succeeding to the Baronetcy, under specific trusts.

key_sections.title: Devolution of interest where beneficiary refuses, neglects or discontinues to use the names Dinshaw Manockjee Petit.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that if a beneficiary refuses or discontinues using the names "Dinshaw Manockjee Petit" for specified periods, their interest in the trust funds and hereditaments shall be suspended and devolve to the next heir.

key_sections.title: Power to charge settled property for jointure of widow.
key_sections.description: Allows the Baronet for the time being to charge the settled property with an annuity for his widow, not exceeding ten thousand rupees, subject to the condition of using the specified names.

key_sections.title: Exclusion of wives from interest in Mansion-house.
key_sections.description: Declares that the "Petit Hall" Mansion-house shall not be subject to any right or interest of the wives of the Baronets under any custom or law of the Parsees.

key_sections.title: Limitation of transfers to life of transferor.
key_sections.description: Restricts the transfer or encumbrance of settled property by beneficiaries to their natural life, and only for the portion of life during which they use the names "Dinshaw Manockjee Petit".

key_sections.title: Addition of stocks, funds or securities to settled property.
key_sections.description: Permits the addition of further stocks, funds, or securities to the settled property by Sir Dinshaw Manockjee Petit or others, with the consent of the Governor of Bombay in Council, up to a total of fifty lakhs of rupees.

key_sections.title: Insurance of Mansion-house, and application of money received in respect of insurance.
key_sections.description: Requires the Corporation to keep the Mansion-house insured against fire, and provides for the application of insurance money for rebuilding or purchasing other suitable hereditaments.

key_sections.title: Power of Corporation to sell or exchange Mansion-house or other hereditaments.
key_sections.description: Grants the Corporation power to sell or exchange the Mansion-house or other hereditaments with the consent of the Baronet and the Governor of Bombay in Council.

key_sections.title: Saving existing rights.

act_identification.act_title: THE PARTITION ACT, 1893

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to amend the law relating to partition; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: An Act to amend the Law relating to Partition.

key_sections.title: Title, extent and saving.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its geographical extent to the whole of India, and a saving clause for local laws concerning immoveable property paying revenue to Government.

key_sections.title: Power to court to order sale instead of division in partition suits.
key_sections.description: Empowers the court to order a sale of property and distribution of proceeds instead of division if division is not reasonable or beneficial, upon request of shareholders.

key_sections.title: Procedure when sharer undertakes to buy.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for a shareholder to buy the share of a party requesting a sale at a court-determined valuation, including provisions for multiple bidders.

key_sections.title: Partition suit by transferee of share in dwelling-house.
key_sections.description: Provides that if a non-family member transferee of a share in a dwelling-house belonging to an undivided family sues for partition, a family member shareholder can undertake to buy that share at a court-determined valuation.

key_sections.title: Representation of parties under disability.
key_sections.description: Allows a person authorized to act on behalf of a party under disability to make requests for sale or applications to buy, subject to the court's opinion on benefit to the disabled party.

key_sections.title: Reserved bidding and bidding by shareholders.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that sales under Section 2 are subject to reserved bidding fixed by the court, and allows shareholders to bid with special terms regarding payment or setting off purchase-money.

key_sections.title: Procedure to be followed in case of sales.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the procedure for sales, referring to the Registrar's procedure for High Courts and rules prescribed by High Courts or the Code of Civil Procedure for other courts.

key_sections.title: Orders for sale to be deemed decrees.
key_sections.description: Declares that any court order for sale under sections 2, 3, or 4 shall be considered a decree within the meaning of section 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

key_sections.title: Saving of power to order partly partition and partly sale.
key_sections.description: Allows the court in a partition suit to decree a partition of part of the property and a sale of the remainder under this Act.

key_sections.title: Application of Act to pending suits.
key_sections.description: States that the Act applies to suits instituted before its commencement where no scheme for partition has been finally approved by the court.

powers_conferred: Power to court to order sale instead of division in partition suits (Section 2)
Power to court to order valuation and offer to sell shares to a shareholder (Section 3)
Power to court to direct sale of share to a family member in dwelling-house cases (Section 4)
Power to court to fix and vary reserved bidding (Section 6)
Power to High Court to prescribe rules for sales (Section 7(b))
Power to court to order partly partition and partly sale (Section 9)
