act_identification.act_title: THE PRISONS ACT, 1894

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. Nothing in this Act shall apply to civil jails in the State of Bombay as it existed immediately before the 1st November, 1956 outside the city of Bombay.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend the law relating to Prisons. [22nd March, 1894] WHEREAS, it is expedient to amend the law relating to prisons in [2][India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States], and to provide rules for the regulation of such prison; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To amend the law relating to prisons and to provide rules for the regulation of such prisons.

chapter_titles: ADMISSION, REMOVAL AND DISCHARGE OF PRISONERS
FOOD, CLOTHING AND BEDDING OF CIVIL AND UNCONVICTED CRIMINAL PRISONERS

key_sections.title: Title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent of application, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'prison', 'criminal prisoner', 'civil prisoner', and 'prohibited article'.

key_sections.title: Inspector General.
key_sections.description: Mandates the appointment of an Inspector General for each State Government's territories to control and superintend prisons.

key_sections.title: Officers of prisons.
key_sections.description: Outlines the mandatory officers for every prison, including Superintendent, Medical Officer, Medical Subordinate, and Jailer.

key_sections.title: Superintendent.
key_sections.description: Defines the Superintendent's role in managing prison discipline, labour, expenditure, punishment, and control, subject to Inspector General's orders.

key_sections.title: Prisoners to be examined on admission.
key_sections.description: Requires searching and medical examination of prisoners upon admission, with records kept of their health and physical condition.

key_sections.title: Separation of prisoners.
key_sections.description: Details the requirements for separating different categories of prisoners, including females from males, young prisoners from adults, unconvicted from convicted, and civil from criminal prisoners.

key_sections.title: Prisoners under sentence of death.
key_sections.description: Prescribes special confinement and guarding arrangements for prisoners under sentence of death.

key_sections.title: Penalty for introduction or removal of prohibited articles into or from prison and communication with prisoners.
key_sections.description: Establishes penalties for introducing or removing prohibited articles from prison or communicating with prisoners contrary to rules.

key_sections.title: Prison-offences.
key_sections.description: Lists specific acts that constitute prison-offences when committed by a prisoner, such as disobedience, assault, or wilful damage.

key_sections.title: Punishment of such offences.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Superintendent to award various punishments for prison-offences, including formal warnings, change of labour, loss of privileges, and different forms of confinement.

key_sections.title: Procedure on committal of heinous offence.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for referring serious prison-offences to a Magistrate for inquiry and trial, with potential for additional imprisonment.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules for various aspects of prison administration, discipline, and prisoner treatment.

powers_conferred: State Government: Power to provide accommodation for prisoners (Section 4), appoint officers for prisons (Section 6), direct temporary shelter and custody for prisoners (Section 7), make rules for prison administration (Section 59).
Inspector General: General control and superintendence of all prisons (Section 5), sanction for Jailer's other employment (Section 16), sanction for retention of fetters on prisoners (Section 57).

Superintendent: Manage prison in matters of discipline, labour, expenditure, punishment, and control (Section 11), keep records (Section 12), award punishments for prison-offences (Section 48), confine prisoners in irons (Section 56).
Medical Officer: Charge of sanitary administration of the prison (Section 13), report on prisoner's health (Section 14), certify fitness of prisoner for punishment (Section 50).

Jailer: Reside in prison (Section 16), give notice of death of prisoner (Section 17), responsible for safe custody of records and prisoner's effects (Section 18), search visitors (Section 41), arrest persons committing offences under Section 42 (Section 43).
Deputy and Assistant Jailers: Perform duties and responsibilities of a Jailer under Superintendent's orders (Section 20).
Magistrate: Inquire into and try heinous prison-offences referred by Superintendent (Section 52).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Offences include introduction or removal of prohibited articles into or from prison, and communication with prisoners (Section 42), punishable with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to two hundred rupees, or both. Various acts are declared as prison-offences when committed by a prisoner (Section 45), punishable by the Superintendent with formal warnings, change of labour, loss of privileges, substitution of clothing, imposition of handcuffs/fetters, separate confinement, penal diet, cellular confinement, or whipping (Section 46). Heinous prison-offences can be referred to a Magistrate, who may sentence the prisoner to imprisonment up to one year (in addition to existing sentence) or to punishments under Section 46 (Section 52). Offences by prison-subordinates (e.g., violation of duty, unauthorized absence) are punishable with fine not exceeding two hundred rupees, or imprisonment not exceeding three months, or both (Section 54).

repealed_acts: Enactments listed in THE SCHEDULE (which was repealed by the Repealing Act, 1938 (1 of 1938))

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government has the power to appoint the Inspector General and other officers of prisons. The Superintendent has the power to select and appoint prisoners as officers of prisons.

applies_to: Whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States.
Criminal prisoners
Civil prisoners
Convicted criminal prisoners
Unconvicted criminal prisoners
exemptions: Civil jails in the State of Bombay as it existed immediately before the 1st November, 1956 outside the city of Bombay.
Female prisoners are not liable to the imposition of handcuffs or fetters, or to whipping.
Civil prisoners are not liable to the imposition of handcuffs or fetters, or to whipping.
special_provisions: Nothing in this Act shall apply to civil jails in the State of Bombay as it existed immediately before the 1st November, 1956 outside the city of Bombay, and those jails shall continue to be administered under the provisions of sections 9 and 16 (both inclusive) of Bombay Act 2 of 1874, as amended by subsequent enactments.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the duties and powers conferred upon prison officers (Superintendent, Inspector General, Jailer, Medical Officer) and by prescribing penalties for offences committed by prisoners, prison-subordinates, and others in relation to prisons. Magistrates have jurisdiction to try heinous prison-offences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate, Court of the District Magistrate, Magistrate of the first class, Presidency Magistrate, Court of Justice.

schedules_summary.description: Contains a list of enactments that were repealed by this Act. This Schedule itself was later repealed by the Repealing Act, 1938.

act_identification.act_title: THE EPIDEMIC DISEASES ACT, 1897

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the better prevention of the spread of Dangerous Epidemic Diseases. WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the better prevention of the spread of dangerous epidemic disease; It is hereby enacted as follows :—
act_overview.purpose: To provide for the better prevention of the spread of dangerous epidemic disease.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical extent.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms such as 'act of violence', 'healthcare service personnel', and 'property' for the purpose of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to take special measures and prescribe regulations as to dangerous epidemic disease.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to take special measures and prescribe temporary regulations to prevent the outbreak or spread of dangerous epidemic diseases.

key_sections.title: Powers of Central Government.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government powers to take measures and prescribe regulations for inspection and detention of conveyances and persons at entry/exit points during an epidemic.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of violence against healthcare service personnel and damage to property.
key_sections.description: Prohibits any person from indulging in violence against healthcare service personnel or causing damage to property during an epidemic.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for disobeying regulations/orders, committing acts of violence against healthcare service personnel, and causing grievous hurt during such acts.

key_sections.title: Cognizance, investigation and trial of offences.
key_sections.description: Outlines procedures for cognizance, investigation, and trial of offences under the Act, including making certain offences cognizable and non-bailable.

key_sections.title: Compensation for acts of violence.
key_sections.description: Mandates compensation to be paid by convicted persons for causing hurt or grievous hurt to healthcare service personnel and for damage to property.

key_sections.title: Protection to persons acting under Act.
key_sections.description: Provides legal protection to persons acting in good faith under the provisions of this Act.

powers_conferred: State Government to take special measures and prescribe regulations as to dangerous epidemic disease.
State Government to require or empower any person to take such measures.
State Government to determine in what manner and by whom any expenses incurred (including compensation) shall be defrayed.
State Government to take measures and prescribe regulations for inspection of persons travelling and segregation of suspected infected persons.
State Government to declare any person as healthcare service personnel by notification in the Official Gazette.

Central Government to take measures and prescribe regulations for the inspection and detention of any bus or train or goods vehicle or ship or vessel or aircraft leaving or arriving at any land port or aerodrome, and for detention of persons intending to travel therein or arriving thereby.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Disobeying any regulation or order made under this Act is an offence punishable under section 188 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860). Committing or abetting an act of violence against a healthcare service personnel, or abetting or causing damage or loss to any property, is punishable with imprisonment for a term of not less than three months but which may extend to five years, and with a fine of not less than fifty thousand rupees but which may extend to two lakh rupees. Causing grievous hurt to a healthcare service personnel while committing an act of violence is punishable with imprisonment for a term of not less than six months but which may extend to seven years, and with a fine of not less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees. Additionally, convicted persons are liable to pay compensation for hurt or grievous hurt and for property damage (twice the fair market value).

related_acts: Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010 (23 of 2010)
Land Ports Authority of India Act, 2010 (31 of 2010)

persons travelling by railway or otherwise
healthcare service personnel
any person

Amended in its application to the C. P. and Berar by the C. P. and Berar Epidemic Diseases (Amendment) Act, 1945 (C. P. and Berar Act 4 of 1945).

Extended to Lakshadweep (w.e.f. 1-10-1967) : vide Reg. 8 of 1965, s. 3 and Sch.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced through penalties for disobedience, specific punishments for violence against healthcare personnel and property damage, and provisions for cognizance, investigation, and trial of offences by police officers not below the rank of Inspector. Compensation for acts of violence is also prescribed.

act_identification.act_title: THE GENERAL CLAUSES ACT, 1897

act_overview.preamble:
An Act to consolidate and extend the General Clauses Act, 1868 and 1887.

[11th March, 1897.]

WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and extend the General Clauses Acts, 1868 (1 of 1868) and

1887 (1 of 1887); it is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to consolidate and extend the General Clauses Acts of 1868 and 1887, providing general rules for the construction and interpretation of Central Acts and Regulations.

chapter_titles: PROVISIONS AS TO ORDERS, RULES, ETC., MADE UNDER ENACTMENTS

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as The General Clauses Act, 1897.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for numerous terms used in this Act and other Central Acts and Regulations.

key_sections.title: Application of foregoing definitions to previous enactments.
key_sections.description: Specifies which definitions from Section 3 apply to Central Acts and Regulations made after certain dates.

key_sections.title: Application of certain definitions to Indian Laws.
key_sections.description: Extends the application of certain definitions from Section 3 to all Indian laws.

key_sections.title: Coming into operation of enactments.
key_sections.description: Defines when a Central Act or Regulation comes into operation, especially when no specific date is mentioned.

key_sections.title: Effect of repeal.
key_sections.description: Outlines the general effects of repealing an enactment, ensuring that previous operations, rights, liabilities, and ongoing proceedings are not affected unless a different intention appears.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Act making textual amendment in Act or Regulation.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the repeal of an Act that made textual amendments to another Act or Regulation does not affect the continuance of those amendments.

key_sections.title: Construction of references to repealed enactments.
key_sections.description: Provides rules for interpreting references to repealed provisions when those provisions have been re-enacted with or without modification.

key_sections.title: Computation of time.
key_sections.description: Establishes rules for computing time periods, especially when a court or office is closed on the last day of a prescribed period.

key_sections.title: Gender and number.
key_sections.description: States that words importing the masculine gender include females, and singular words include plural, and vice versa, unless repugnant to the context.

key_sections.title: Power to appoint to include power to suspend or dismiss.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the power to make an appointment includes the power to suspend or dismiss the appointed person, unless a different intention appears.

key_sections.title: Power to issue, to include power to add to, amend, vary or rescind notifications, orders, rules or bye-laws.
key_sections.description: Ensures that the power to issue notifications, orders, rules, or bye-laws also includes the power to modify or cancel them.

key_sections.title: Continuation of orders, etc., issued under enactments repealed and re-enacted.
key_sections.description: Provides for the continuation of orders, rules, etc., made under a repealed enactment if it is re-enacted, ensuring legal continuity.

key_sections.title: Provision as to offences punishable under two or more enactments.
key_sections.description: States that an offender cannot be punished twice for the same offence, even if it constitutes an offence under multiple enactments.

key_sections.title: Meaning of service by post.
key_sections.description: Defines how service by post is deemed to be effected, including proper addressing, pre-paying, and posting by registered post.

powers_conferred: Power to appoint any person to fill any office or execute any function (interpreted by Section 15)
Power to suspend or dismiss any person appointed (interpreted by Section 16)
Power to issue, add to, amend, vary or rescind notifications, orders, rules or bye-laws (interpreted by Section 21)
Power to make rules or bye-laws and issue orders between passing and commencement of enactment (interpreted by Section 22)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides rules for the prosecution and punishment of offences defined in other enactments, ensuring that an offender is not punished twice for the same offence (Section 26). It also applies provisions for the recovery of fines from the Indian Penal Code and Code of Criminal Procedure (Section 25).

act_identification.act_title: THE LIVE-STOCK IMPORTATION ACT, 1898

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to make better provision for the regulation of the importation or live stock which is liable to be affected by infectious or contagious disorders; It is hereby enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to regulate the importation of live-stock and live-stock products into India. Its primary objective is to prevent the spread of infectious or contagious disorders among animals and to safeguard human and animal health from potentially harmful live-stock products.

key_sections.title: Short title and local extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its geographical extent.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'infectious or contagious disorders', 'live-stock', 'import', and 'live-stock products'.

key_sections.title: Power to regulate importation of live-stock.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to regulate, restrict, or prohibit the import of live-stock and related items liable to infectious disorders.

key_sections.title: Power to regulate Importation of live-stock products.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to regulate, restrict, or prohibit the import of live-stock products that may affect human or animal health.

key_sections.title: Power for State Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to make rules for the detention, inspection, disinfection, or destruction of imported live-stock and related items.

key_sections.title: Protection to persons acting under Act.
key_sections.description: Provides protection against legal proceedings for actions done in good faith under the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government to regulate, restrict or prohibit importation of live-stock (Section 3)
Central Government to regulate, restrict or prohibit importation of live-stock products (Section 3A)
State Government to make rules for detention, inspection, disinfection or destruction of imported live-stock and related items (Section 4)
Officers of customs to have powers regarding regulated imports (Section 3(2))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Breach of rules made by State Government may be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees (Section 4(2)).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government may appoint officers for detention, inspection, disinfection, etc. (Section 4(1))

applies_to: Importation of live-stock
Importation of live-stock products
special_provisions: Extended to Goa, Daman and Diu by Reg. 12 of 1962
Extended to Pondicherry by Reg. 7 of 1963

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for regulation, restriction, prohibition of import); State Government (for detention, inspection, disinfection, destruction)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Notifications issued by Central Government operate as if issued under section 11 of the Customs Act, 1962; officers of customs have powers similar to those for customs regulation; enactments relating to customs apply (Section 3(2)).

act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL PROVINCES TENANCY ACT, 1898

legislative_details.enacted_by: THE GOVERNOR GENERAL OF INDIA IN COUNCIL
legislative_details.geographical_extent: all the territories for the time being administered by the Chief Commissioner of the Central Provinces

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the Law relating to Agricultural Tenancies in the Central Provinces. WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to agricultural tenancies in the Central Provinces ; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws concerning agricultural tenancies within the Central Provinces. Its primary objective is to provide a comprehensive legal framework for the rights and obligations of landlords and tenants in agricultural land.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and immediate commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'arrear', 'holding', 'improvement', 'landlord', 'rent', and 'tenant'.

key_sections.title: Classes of tenants.
key_sections.description: Classifies tenants into five categories: absolute occupancy-tenants, occupancy-tenants, village-service-tenants, sub-tenants, and ordinary tenants.

key_sections.title: Penalty for levy of anything in excess of rent by landlord.
key_sections.description: Prescribes a penalty for landlords who levy anything in excess of legally payable rent.

key_sections.title: Right to make improvements.
key_sections.description: Grants tenants the right to make improvements on their holdings and outlines conditions under which landlords may also make improvements.

key_sections.title: Liability to pay to tenant on ejectment compensation for improvements.
key_sections.description: Ensures tenants receive compensation for improvements made to their holdings upon ejectment, with provisions for assessment and payment.

key_sections.title: Surrender of holdings.
key_sections.description: Details the conditions and liabilities associated with a tenant's surrender of their holding.

key_sections.title: Definition of “absolute occupancy-tenant”.
key_sections.description: Defines who qualifies as an absolute occupancy-tenant based on historical records.

key_sections.title: Right heritable and transferable after notice to landlord, who may claim to purchase.
key_sections.description: Outlines the heritable and transferable rights of absolute occupancy-tenants, including the landlord's right to purchase.

key_sections.title: Definition of “Occupancy-tenant”.
key_sections.description: Defines who qualifies as an occupancy-tenant based on continuous occupation and specific conditions.

key_sections.title: Devolution of occupancy-right.
key_sections.description: Governs the inheritance and transferability of occupancy-rights, including prohibitions on sale and certain transfers.

key_sections.title: Grounds for ejectment.
key_sections.description: Specifies the limited grounds on which an occupancy-tenant may be ejected by their landlord.

key_sections.title: Definition of “ordinary tenant”.
key_sections.description: Defines an ordinary tenant as any tenant not falling into other specified categories.

key_sections.title: Obligation of landlord to confer occupancy-rights on ordinary tenant.
key_sections.description: Mandates landlords to confer occupancy-rights upon ordinary tenants under certain conditions, including tender of a sum equal to two and-a-half times the annual rent.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of Civil Courts barred in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Restricts the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in matters specifically assigned to Revenue-officers or Settlement-officers by this Act.

powers_conferred: Local Government: To prescribe instalments and dates for rent payment (Section 6).
Local Government: To make rules regarding rent payment to multiple landlords (Section 7).
Revenue-officer: To receive deposits of rent in certain cases (Section 8).
Revenue-officer: To impose penalties on landlords for levying excess rent (Section 10).
Revenue-officer: To impose penalties on landlords for refusing or giving defective receipts (Section 12).
Revenue-officer: To enhance rent when productive power of holding increased by landlord (Section 13).
Revenue-officer: To reduce rent when effect of improvement ceases (Section 14).
Revenue-officer: To alter rent when holding is increased, diminished or deteriorated (Section 15).
Revenue-officer: To alter rent in case of new assessment (Section 16).
Settlement-officer/Revenue-officer: To commute rent payable in kind to fixed money-rent (Section 17).
Revenue-officer: To remit or suspend rent consequent on like treatment of land-revenue (Section 18).

A village-service-tenant attempting to transfer their interest in contravention of the Act is liable to ejectment (Section 56(2)).

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the exemption from the operation of municipal building laws of certain buildings and lands which are the property, or in the occupation, of the Government and situate within the limits of a municipality. WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the exemption from the operation of municipal building laws of certain buildings and lands which are the property, or in the occupation, of the Government and situate within the limits of a municipality;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to exempt certain buildings and lands owned or occupied by the Government, and located within municipal limits, from the application of municipal building laws. It also establishes a procedure for municipal authorities to raise objections or suggestions regarding such government constructions.

key_sections.description: Exempts Government buildings used for public service or purpose from municipal building laws, with a proviso requiring reasonable notice to the municipal authority for proposed works, unless connected with defence or deemed confidential.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act provides a mechanism where municipal authorities can submit objections or suggestions regarding government building works, which the State Government must consider and pass orders on, ensuring compliance with those orders (Section 4).

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who demands and receives any toll in contravention of the provisions of section 3 or section 4 shall be punishable with fine which may extend to fifty rupees.

the carriages, horses, and baggage, and persons employed in driving/carrying, of any exempted persons

all animals accompanying any body of troops (intended for food or provisioning)
all persons in charge of any exempted carriage, horse or animal

act_identification.act_title: THE WORKS OF DEFENCE ACT, 1903

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for imposing restrictions upon the use and enjoyment of land in the vicinity of works of defence in order that such land may be kept free from buildings and other obstructions, and for determining the amount of compensation to be made on account of such imposition. WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for imposing restrictions upon the use and enjoyment of land in the vicinity of works of defence in order that such land may be kept free from buildings and other obstructions and for determining the amount of compensation to be made on account of such imposition; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for imposing restrictions on the use and enjoyment of land near works of defence to ensure it remains free from buildings and obstructions. It also establishes a framework for determining compensation for such imposed restrictions.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

chapter_titles: REFERENCE TO COURT AND PROCEDURE THEREON

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical extent.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Declaration and notice that restrictions will be imposed.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for declaring and notifying the public about the imposition of restrictions on land use near works of defence.

key_sections.title: Further powers exercisable after publication of notice under section 3, sub-section (2).
key_sections.description: Grants powers to authorized officers to demolish constructions, cut trees, and clear land after public notice, with provisions for emergency exercise of powers.

key_sections.title: Restrictions.
key_sections.description: Details the specific types of restrictions that can be imposed on land within different boundaries around works of defence.

key_sections.title: Notice to persons interested.
key_sections.description: Requires the Collector to give public notice for claims to compensation and to persons interested in the land.

key_sections.title: Inquiry and award by Collector.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Collector to inquire into objections, assess decrease in land value, and make an award for compensation and its apportionment.

key_sections.title: Reference to Court.
key_sections.description: Allows persons who have not accepted the Collector's award to request a reference to the Court for determination of objections.

key_sections.title: Matters to be considered in determining compensation.
key_sections.description: Specifies the factors the Court must consider when determining the amount of compensation, including market value decrease and damages.

key_sections.title: Matters not to be considered in determining compensation.
key_sections.description: Lists factors that the Court shall not take into consideration when determining compensation.

key_sections.title: Payment of compensation or deposit of same in Court.
key_sections.description: Describes the process for tendering and paying compensation, or depositing it in Court in case of refusal, incompetence, or dispute.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for willfully obstructing authorized acts, damaging works, or contravening restrictions.

key_sections.title: Completion of imposition of restrictions not compulsory, but compensation to be awarded when not completed.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to withdraw from imposing restrictions and mandates compensation for damage suffered due to notice or proceedings.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for the enforcement of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to declare necessity for restrictions (Section 3)
Central Government: to authorise officers for preliminary acts (Section 4)
Central Government: to authorise officers for further powers (Section 6)
Central Government: to declare emergency for exercising powers (Section 6(3))
Central Government: to declare specific restrictions (Section 7)
Central Government: to direct period for notice (Section 9)
Central Government: to sanction arrangements instead of money compensation (Section 31(3))
Central Government: to withdraw from the imposition of declared restrictions (Section 38)
Central Government: to make rules for enforcement (Section 44)
Officer authorised by Central Government: to enter, survey, take levels, dig, bore, set out boundaries, mark levels, cut and clear crops/fences (Section 4)
Officer authorised by Central Government: to enter, demolish buildings, cut trees, remove banks, make drains, fill excavations, level and clear land (Section 6)
Collector: to cause public notice of declaration (Section 3)
Collector: to refer dispute regarding damage payment (Section 5)
Collector: to cause land to be marked out, measured, registered, and planned (Section 8)
Collector: to cause public notice for claims to compensation (Section 9)
Collector: to require statements as to names and interests (Section 10)
Collector: to inquire into objections and make an award (Section 12)
Collector: to adjourn inquiry (Section 14)
Collector: to summon and enforce attendance of witnesses and production of documents (Section 15)
Collector: to refer dispute as to apportionment to the Court (Section 30)
Collector: to tender payment of compensation or deposit in Court (Section 31)
Collector: to determine compensation for withdrawal of restrictions (Section 38)
Collector: to refer questions regarding building parts to the Court (Section 39)
Court: to determine objections referred by Collector (Section 18)
Court: to determine compensation (Section 23)
Court: to direct Collector to pay interest on excess compensation (Section 28)
Court: to order investment of money deposited (Section 32, Section 33)
Magistrate/Commissioner of Police: to enforce compliance if Collector/officer is opposed (Section 37)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever willfully obstructs any person in acts authorized by sections 4, 6, or 8, or destroys/damages/alters any work done under section 6, or contravenes section 7 or conditions thereunder, shall be punishable with imprisonment up to one month or fine up to fifty rupees, or both. For continuing offences, an additional fine up to five rupees per day may be imposed, and expenses for removing effects of the offence may be recovered.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government has the power to appoint a special judicial officer to perform functions of the Court (Section 2(g)) and any officer specially to perform functions of a Collector (Section 2(f)).

applies_to: use and enjoyment of land in the vicinity of works of defence
the whole of India
exemptions: Road-ballast, manure and agricultural produce may be exempted from stacking/storing prohibitions with written approval (Section 7(a)(ii) Proviso).
Huts, fences or other constructions of wood or other easily destroyed/removed materials may be maintained/erected/altered with written approval (Section 7(b)(i) Proviso).
Open railings and dry brush-wood fences may be exempted from prohibitions on buildings/excavations with written approval (Section 7(c) Proviso).
special_provisions: The Act has been extended to Goa, Daman and Diu by Reg. 12 of 1962, s. 3 and the Schedule (w.e.f. 31-1-1963) and to Pondicherry (w.e.f. 1-10-1963) by Reg. 7 of 1963, s. 3 and the First Schedule.
Land beyond two thousand yards from the crest of the outer parapet of the work may be included in the outer boundary under certain conditions (Section 39(4)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Collector conducts inquiries, makes awards, and manages compensation. The Court handles references, determines compensation, and hears appeals. Authorized officers carry out preliminary acts and exercise further powers including demolition. Magistrates or Commissioners of Police enforce compliance if officers are opposed. Penalties are prescribed for contraventions.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: A principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction, or a special judicial officer appointed by the Central Government. Appeals lie to the High Court.

act_identification.act_title: THE VICTORIA MEMORIAL ACT, 1903

act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the erection, maintenance, and management of the Victoria Memorial at Calcutta. It establishes a permanent body of Trustees to oversee the memorial, which commemorates the life and reign of Her late Majesty Victoria.
act_overview.act_category: Institutions of Natural and Cultural Importance

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Victoria Memorial Act, 1903.

key_sections.title: Trustees.
key_sections.description: Defines the constitution of the Trustees of the Victoria Memorial, their ex officio and nominated members, and establishes them as a body corporate with perpetual succession and powers to acquire property, contract, sue and be sued.

key_sections.title: Property vested in Trustees.
key_sections.description: States that all moneys and property, movable or immovable, for the Memorial shall vest in the Trustees.

key_sections.title: Officers and servants to be public servants.
key_sections.description: Declares that all officers and servants employed by the Trustees are deemed public servants under the Indian Penal Code, with an exception for contractors' employees.

key_sections.title: Rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes, including appointment of Trustees, meeting procedures, committee powers, management of the Memorial, fees, and accounts.

key_sections.title: Power of Trustees to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Trustees, with Central Government approval, to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules, for discharging their functions, including conditions for loaning articles and recruitment of employees.

Central Government: make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act (Section 5(1))
Trustees: make regulations, with previous approval of the Central Government, for discharging functions (Section 6(1))

authorities_established: The Trustees of the Victoria Memorial
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government nominates three persons to the Trustees. Trustees nominate four persons to the Trustees with Central Government approval. Trustees may appoint a Secretary.
regulatory_bodies: The Trustees of the Victoria Memorial

Officers and servants employed by the Trustees
exemptions: persons in the service of any contractor employed by the Trustees (regarding public servant status)
special_provisions: The Act specifically concerns the Victoria Memorial at Calcutta.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through rules made by the Central Government and regulations made by the Trustees. The Trustees, as a body corporate, can sue and be sued.

act_identification.act_title: THE ANCIENT MONUMENTS PRESERVATION ACT, 1904

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble:
WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the preservation of ancient monuments, for the exercise of control
over traffic in antiquities and over excavation in certain places, and for the protection and acquisition in
certain cases of ancient monuments and of objects of archaeological, historical or artistic interest; It is hereby
enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to preserve ancient monuments and objects of archaeological, historical, or artistic interest. It also seeks to control traffic in antiquities and regulate archaeological excavations in specific areas, including provisions for their protection and acquisition.
act_overview.act_category: Institutions of Natural and Cultural Importance

chapter_titles: Protection of Sculptures, Carvings, Images, Bas-reliefs, Inscriptions or like objects

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its geographical application.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'ancient monument' and 'antiquities'.

key_sections.title: Protected monuments.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to declare an ancient monument as a protected monument.

key_sections.title: Acquisition of rights in or guardianship of an ancient monument.
key_sections.description: Allows the Collector to purchase, lease, accept gifts/bequests, or the Commissioner to accept guardianship of protected monuments.

key_sections.title: Preservation of ancient monument by agreement.
key_sections.description: Enables the Collector to enter into agreements with owners for the preservation of protected monuments.

key_sections.title: Compulsory purchase of ancient monument.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to direct the acquisition of protected monuments under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, for preservation.

key_sections.title: Power Central Government to control mining, etc., near ancient monument.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make rules restricting or regulating mining and similar operations near ancient monuments.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for destroying, removing, injuring, altering, defacing, or imperiling protected monuments or contravening orders.

key_sections.title: Power to Central Government to control traffic in antiquities.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to prohibit or restrict the import or export of antiquities.

key_sections.title: Power to Central Government to control moving of sculptures, carvings or like objects.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to regulate the movement of sculptures, carvings, and similar objects.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to notify areas as protected.
key_sections.description: Enables the Central Government to declare areas as protected for archaeological excavation, making buried antiquities government property.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules regulating Archaeological excavation in protected areas.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for licensing and regulating archaeological excavations in protected areas.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers general rule-making power upon the Central Government for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

Collector: fix reasonable period for owner to enter into agreement (Section 10)
Collector: give notice to the owner for compulsory purchase of objects (Section 19)
Commissioner: accept guardianship of a monument (Section 4)

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person committing a breach of rules made under Section 10A shall be punishable with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees. A breach of rules made under Section 15 shall be punishable with fine which may extend to twenty rupees. Any person other than the owner who destroys, removes, injures, alters, defaces or imperils a protected monument, and any owner who does so to a monument maintained by the Central Government or under agreement, or contravenes an order under Section 7(1), shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with imprisonment which may extend to three months, or with both (Section 16). Any person who brings or takes or attempts to bring or take antiquities into or out of territories in contravention of a notification under Section 17(1) shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, and antiquities shall be liable to confiscation. Any person who moves any object in contravention of a notification under Section 18(1) shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees. Rules made under Section 20B may provide that any person committing a breach thereof or of any condition of a licence shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, and may further provide for the licensee's punishment if the breach is by an agent or servant.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN RAILWAY BOARD ACT, 1905

act_identification.act_title: THE CODE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE, 1908

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India except the State of Nagaland and the tribal areas. State Government may extend to Nagaland or tribal areas. Application to Amindivi Islands, East Godavari, West Godavari and Visakhapatnam Agencies in Andhra Pradesh and Union Territory of Lakshadweep is without prejudice to existing rules/regulations. act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the laws relating to the procedure of the Courts of Civil Judicature. WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the laws relating to the procedure of the Courts of Civil Judicature: It is hereby enacted as follows :
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to consolidate and amend the laws that govern the procedure of Civil Courts in India. It aims to provide a comprehensive framework for the conduct of civil suits and proceedings.

chapter_titles: PART IV SUITS IN PARTICULAR CASES
PART VIII REFERENCE, REVIEW AND REVISION
PART IX SPECIAL PROVISIONS RELATING TO THE HIGH COURTS NOT BEING THE COURT OF A JUDICIAL COMMISSIONER

key_sections.title: Short title, commencement and extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the official title, effective date, and geographical applicability of the Code.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'decree', 'judgment', 'public officer', etc.

key_sections.title: Courts to try all civil suits unless barred.
key_sections.description: Establishes the general jurisdiction of civil courts to try all suits of a civil nature unless expressly or impliedly barred.

key_sections.title: Stay of suit.
key_sections.description: Provides for the stay of a suit if the matter in issue is also directly and substantially in issue in a previously instituted suit between the same parties.

key_sections.title: Res judicata.
key_sections.description: Prevents a court from trying any suit or issue that has been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties and finally decided.

key_sections.title: General power of transfer and withdrawal.
key_sections.description: Grants the High Court or District Court the power to transfer or withdraw suits, appeals, or other proceedings.

key_sections.title: Power of Supreme Court to transfer suits, etc.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Supreme Court to transfer suits, appeals, or other proceedings from one High Court or Civil Court to another across States.

key_sections.title: Institution of suits.
key_sections.description: Specifies that every suit shall be instituted by the presentation of a plaint or in such other prescribed manner.

key_sections.title: Interest.
key_sections.description: Allows courts to award interest on the principal sum adjudged in a money decree, from the date of suit to payment.

key_sections.title: Compensatory costs in respect of false or vexatious claims or defences.
key_sections.description: Enables courts to award compensatory costs against a party for false or vexatious claims or defences.

key_sections.title: Execution of decrees passed by Courts in reciprocating territory.
key_sections.description: Provides for the execution of decrees passed by superior courts in reciprocating territories as if they were passed by a District Court in India.

key_sections.title: Questions to be determined by the Court executing decree.
key_sections.description: Mandates that all questions between parties relating to the execution, discharge, or satisfaction of a decree shall be determined by the executing court, not by a separate suit.

key_sections.title: Powers of Court to enforce execution.
key_sections.description: Outlines the various methods a court may use to enforce the execution of a decree, including delivery of property, attachment and sale, arrest and detention, or appointing a receiver.

key_sections.title: Property liable to attachment and sale in execution of decree.
key_sections.description: Specifies what types of property are liable to attachment and sale in execution of a decree, and lists exemptions.

key_sections.title: Suits by or against Government.
key_sections.description: Determines the authority to be named as plaintiff or defendant in suits involving the Central or State Government.

key_sections.title: Notice.
key_sections.description: Requires prior notice to be given before instituting a suit against the Government or a public officer in their official capacity.

key_sections.title: Settlement of disputes outside the Court.
key_sections.description: Empowers the court to refer disputes for arbitration, conciliation, judicial settlement (including Lok Adalat), or mediation.

key_sections.title: Public charities.
key_sections.description: Governs suits concerning alleged breaches of trust for public charitable or religious purposes, or where court direction is needed for trust administration.

key_sections.title: Appeal from original decree.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals from every decree passed by a court exercising original jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Second appeal.
key_sections.description: Allows for a second appeal to the High Court from an appellate decree if it involves a substantial question of law.

key_sections.title: Revision.
key_sections.description: Grants the High Court revisional jurisdiction over cases decided by subordinate courts where no appeal lies, to correct jurisdictional errors or material irregularities.

key_sections.title: Saving of inherent powers of Court.
key_sections.description: Preserves the inherent power of the court to make orders necessary for the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of process.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties:

Section 95: Compensation for obtaining arrest, attachment or injunction on insufficient grounds, not exceeding fifty thousand rupees.
Order XXXIX, Rule 2A: Disobedience or breach of injunction may lead to attachment of property and detention in civil prison for up to three months.
Order XI, Rule 21: Non-compliance with discovery orders may result in dismissal of suit (for plaintiff) or striking out of defence (for defendant).
Order VIII, Rule 10: Failure to present written statement may lead to judgment against the defaulting party.
Order IX, Rule 12: Non-attendance of a party ordered to appear in person subjects them to rules applicable to non-appearing parties.
Order XVI, Rule 20: Refusal of a party to give evidence when required by the Court may lead to judgment against them.
Order XXI, Rule 41(3): Disobedience of an order to make an affidavit of assets may result in detention in civil prison for up to three months.
Order XXI, Rule 71: Defaulting purchaser at a sale is answerable for loss on re-sale.
Order XXI, Rule 72(3): Decree-holder purchasing property without court permission may be liable for costs and deficiency on re-sale.
Order XXI, Rule 78: Irregularity in publishing or conducting sale of movable property does not vitiate sale, but injured person may sue for compensation or recovery.
Order XV-A, Rule 8: Non-compliance with orders in Case Management Hearing may lead to condonation with costs, foreclosure of rights (e.g., to file affidavits, cross-examine), or dismissal of plaint/allowing of suit.
