act_identification.act_title: THE EXPLOSIVE SUBSTANCES ACT, 1908

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India and applies also to citizens of India outside India

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is necessary further to amend the law relating to explosive substances; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: An Act further to amend the law relating to explosive substances.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and application.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its geographical extent to the whole of India and its application to citizens outside India.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines 'explosive substance' and 'special category explosive substance'.

key_sections.title: Punishment for causing explosion likely to endanger life or property.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for unlawfully and maliciously causing an explosion with explosive or special category explosive substances.

key_sections.title: Punishment for attempt to cause explosion, or for making or keeping explosive with intent to endanger life or property.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for attempting to cause an explosion or possessing explosives with intent to endanger life or property.

key_sections.title: Punishment for making or possessing explosives under suspicious circumstances.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for making or possessing explosives under circumstances that raise reasonable suspicion of unlawful object.

key_sections.title: Punishment of abettors.
key_sections.description: States that abettors of any offence under this Act shall be punished with the same punishment as provided for the offence.

key_sections.title: Restriction on trial of offences.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that no court shall proceed to trial for an offence against this Act without the consent of the District Magistrate.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to specify additional substances as 'special category explosive substance' by notification (Section 2(b)).
District Magistrate: Power to consent to the trial of offences under this Act (Section 7).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Punishment for causing explosion likely to endanger life or property (Section 3): imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment (not less than ten years) and fine for explosive substance; death, or rigorous imprisonment for life and fine for special category explosive substance. Punishment for attempt to cause explosion, or for making or keeping explosive with intent to endanger life or property (Section 4): imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years and fine for explosive substance; rigorous imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment up to ten years and fine for special category explosive substance. Punishment for making or possessing explosives under suspicious circumstances (Section 5): imprisonment up to ten years and fine for explosive substance; rigorous imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment up to ten years and fine for special category explosive substance. Punishment of abettors (Section 6): same punishment as for the offence abetted.

applies_to: whole of India
citizens of India outside India
special_provisions: Extended to Goa, Daman and Diu with modifications by Reg. 12 of 1962, s. 3 and Sch., (w.e.f. 1-2-1965).
Comes into force in Pondicherry vide Reg. of 1963, s. 3 and First Schedule (w.e.f. 1-10-1963).
Brought into force in Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963, s. 2 and Sch. 1 (w.e.f. 1 -7-1965).
Extended to the whole of territory of Lakshadweep vide Keg. 8 of 1965, s. 3 and Sch. (w.e.f. 1-10-1967).
Extended to the State of Sikkim vide Notification No. G.S.R. 201, dated 30-1-1976 (w.e.f. 1-2-1976).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Trial of offences requires the consent of the District Magistrate.

act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL PROVINCES FINANCIAL COMMISSIONER’S ACT, 1908

legislative_details.enacted_by: GOVERNOR GENERAL OF INDIA IN COUNCIL

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the appointment of a Financial Commissioner for the Central Provinces and further to amend the Central Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1881. WHEREAS it is expedient to appoint a Financial Commissioner for the Central Provinces and further to amend the Central Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1881 (XVIII of 1881); It is hereby enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the appointment of a Financial Commissioner for the Central Provinces. It also amends the Central Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1881, to redefine Revenue-officers and their subordination, and to assign powers to the newly appointed Financial Commissioner.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies the conditions for its commencement.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Financial Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Establishes the position of a Financial Commissioner for the Central Provinces and outlines the appointment, suspension, and removal process.

key_sections.title: Assignment of powers to Financial Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Chief Commissioner, with sanction, to assign powers and functions to the Financial Commissioner.

key_sections.title: Substitution of new sections for sections 5 and 6, Act XVIII, 1881.
key_sections.description: Substitutes new sections 5 and 6 in the Central Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1881, defining classes of Revenue-officers and their subordination.

key_sections.title: Amendment of sections 17 and 25 Act XVIII, 1881.
key_sections.description: Amends sections 17 and 25 of the Central Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1881, by adding 'or the Financial Commissioner' after 'Chief Commissioner'.

key_sections.title: Amendment of sections 22 and 23 Act XVIII, 1881.
key_sections.description: Amends sections 22 and 23 of the Central Provinces Land-revenue Act, 1881, by substituting 'Chief Commissioner' with 'Financial Commissioner'.

powers_conferred: Chief Commissioner, with previous sanction of the Governor General in Council, may appoint, suspend or remove the Financial Commissioner (Section 2).
Chief Commissioner, with previous sanction of the Governor General in Council, may assign powers or functions to the Financial Commissioner (Section 3).
Chief Commissioner may invest an officer in charge of a village-survey with the powers of a Revenue-officer of any class (Section 4, new section 6(4)).

authorities_established: Financial Commissioner for the Central Provinces
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Chief Commissioner, with the previous sanction of the Governor General in Council

applies_to: Central Provinces

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN PORTS ACT, 1908

legislative_details.geographical_extent: to the ports mentioned in the first schedule, and to such parts of the navigable rivers and channels leading to such ports respectively as have been declared to be subject to Act XXII of 1855 (for the Regulation of Ports and Port-dues) or to the Indian Ports Act, 1875 (12 of 1875), or to the Indian Ports Act, 1889 (10 of 1889); to the other ports or parts of navigable rivers or channels to which the Government, in exercise of the power hereinafter conferred, extends this Act.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate the enactments relating to ports and port-charges; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act consolidates existing enactments related to ports and port-charges. Its primary objective is to regulate the administration, safety, and financial aspects of ports, including the levy of port-dues and the powers and duties of port officials.

chapter_titles: PORT-OFFICIALS AND THEIR POWERS AND DUTIES
RULES FOR THE SAFETY OF SHIPPING AND THE CONSERVATION OF PORTS

key_sections.title: Title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability to various ports and navigable waters.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Magistrate', 'master', 'pilot', 'port', 'vessel', and 'Government'.

key_sections.title: Power to extend or withdraw the Act or certain portions thereof.
key_sections.description: Grants the Government the authority to extend or withdraw the application of the Act or specific sections to any port or part of a navigable river/channel.

key_sections.title: Power to make port-rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Government to make rules for regulating various aspects of port operations, including vessel movement, berths, cargo handling, safety, and public health.

key_sections.title: Appointment of conservator.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Government to appoint a conservator for every port, outlining their role and subordination.

key_sections.title: Removal of obstructions within limits of port.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the conservator to remove obstructions to navigation or lawful use of port facilities and recover expenses from the owner.

key_sections.title: Raising or removal of wreck impeding navigation within limits of port.
key_sections.description: Details the conservator's power to require or undertake the raising, removal, or destruction of wrecks impeding navigation, and the recovery of associated costs.

key_sections.title: Improperly discharging ballast.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the improper discharge of ballast, rubbish, oil, or water mixed with oil into ports, prescribing penalties and expense recovery.

key_sections.title: Moving of vessels without pilot or permission of harbour-master.
key_sections.description: Regulates the movement of vessels of certain measurements within specified ports, requiring a pilot or permission, with exceptions.

key_sections.title: Levy of port-dues.
key_sections.description: Establishes the framework for levying port-dues on vessels entering ports, specifying rates and frequency of payment as per the First Schedule.

key_sections.title: Receipt, expenditure and account of port-charges.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for receiving and expending port-charges, requiring the maintenance of a distinct port fund account and pilotage account.

key_sections.title: Distraint and sale on refusal to pay port-charges.
key_sections.description: Provides for the distraint or arrest and subsequent sale of a vessel and its tackle if port-dues, fees, or other charges are not paid on demand.

key_sections.title: No port-clearance to be granted until port-charges are paid.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that port-clearance shall not be granted until all applicable port-dues, fees, charges, fines, penalties, and expenses are paid or secured.

key_sections.title: Power to impose hospital port-dues.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to impose additional hospital port-dues on vessels for the support of public hospitals or dispensaries for seamen.

key_sections.title: Application of certain provisions of the Act to aircraft.
key_sections.description: Extends specific provisions of the Act to aircraft making use of any port while on water, treating them similarly to vessels.

key_sections.title: Maritime security.
key_sections.description: Requires port facilities in India to comply with maritime security requirements outlined in Chapter IXB of the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958.

powers_conferred: Government: To extend or withdraw the Act or portions thereof (Section 4).
Government: To alter the limits of any port (Section 5).
Government: To make rules for regulating port operations, safety, and public health (Section 6).
Government: To appoint a conservator for every port (Section 7).
Government: To appoint a health-officer at any port (Section 17).
Government: To vary rates of port-dues and grant exemptions (Section 34).
Government: To impose hospital port-dues (Section 49).
Conservator: To give and enforce directions for vessel movement and safety (Section 8).
Conservator: To cut warps and ropes in case of urgent necessity (Section 9).
Conservator: To remove obstructions within port limits and recover expenses (Section 10).
Conservator: To raise or remove wrecks impeding navigation and sell property to recover costs (Section 14).
Conservator: To board vessels and enter buildings to investigate offences or perform duties (Section 15).
Conservator/Port-officer: To require crews to prevent or extinguish fire (Section 16).
Authority appointed to receive port-charges: To distrain and sell vessels for unpaid charges (Section 42).
Magistrate: To try offences, levy fines by distress and sale of vessel, and recover expenses/damages (Sections 55, 57, 59).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes various penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for offences such as disobeying port rules or conservator's directions (e.g., fine up to 100 rupees for disobeying conservator's direction under S.8(2)), causing obstructions (fine up to 100 rupees under S.10(2)), improperly discharging ballast or oil (fine up to 5 lakh rupees under S.21(2), and imprisonment up to 1 year and fine up to 5 lakh rupees for continuing offence under S.21(3)), injuring buoys or moorings (fine up to 2000 rupees or imprisonment up to 2 years under S.19(2)), loosening vessels from moorings (fine up to 200 rupees or imprisonment up to 6 months under S.20), and evading payment of port-charges (fine up to five times the amount under S.45(1)).

related_acts: Act XXII of 1855 (for the Regulation of Ports and Port-dues)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Government (Central or State) has the power to appoint the Conservator (Section 7), the Health-officer (Section 17), and the officer or body responsible for receiving port-charges (Section 36).
regulatory_bodies: Authority constituted under section 47A of the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963

applies_to: Ports mentioned in the first schedule
Parts of navigable rivers and channels leading to such ports
Other ports or parts of navigable rivers or channels to which the Government extends this Act
All aircraft making use of any port, while on water
exemptions: Vessels belonging to, or in the service of, the Central Government or a State Government
Vessels of war belonging to any Foreign Prince or State
Pleasure yacht
Any vessel compelled to re-enter a port by stress of weather or damage
Any vessel leaving a port within forty-eight hours without discharging or taking in any passengers or cargo
Sailing vessels of any measurement not exceeding a specified measurement in certain ports (as per Government notification)
Any vessel or class of vessels from payment of port-dues (by Government exemption)
Any class of vessels from hospital port-dues (by Central Government notification)
special_provisions: Sections 31 or 32 shall not apply to any port, river or channel unless specially extended by the Government (Section 1(3)).

The State Government may direct that for the purposes of Section 36, any number of ports in the State (not being major ports) shall be regarded as constituting a single port, forming a common port fund account (Section 37).
Special provisions for port-due chargeability for vessels in ballast (Section 46) and vessels not discharging or taking in cargo (Section 47).
Specific exemption for vessels in ports in the territories of Madras and Andhra, or the Port of Gopalpur in Orissa, leaving within 48 hours (Section 48(c)).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Government (Central or State) (Section 6(1)); State Government (for rules made by it, to be laid before State Legislature) (Section 6(2A)); Central Government (for rules made by it, to be laid before Parliament) (Section 6(2B)).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through various mechanisms including the conservator's power to remove obstructions and recover expenses (Section 10, 11, 14), the authority to distrain and sell vessels for unpaid port-charges (Section 42), withholding port-clearance (Section 43), and the jurisdiction of Magistrates to try offences and levy fines or recover expenses by distress and sale of vessels (Sections 55, 57).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate

schedules_summary.description: Lists ports, vessels chargeable, rate of port-dues, and frequency of payment, categorized into Major Ports and various State-controlled ports (West Bengal, Orissa, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Pondicherry, Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Daman and Diu, Maharashtra, Gujarat).
This schedule was repealed by the Repealing Act, 1938.

act_identification.act_title: THE REGISTRATION ACT, 1908

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate the enactments relating to the Registration of Documents. WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate the enactments relating to the registration of documents; it is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To consolidate the existing laws relating to the registration of documents, ensuring legal validity and public record of transactions.

chapter_titles: PART IV: OF THE TIME OF PRESENTATION
PART V: OF THE PLACE OF REGISTRATION
PART VI: OF PRESENTING DOCUMENTS FOR REGISTRATION
PART VII: OF ENFORCING THE APPEARANCE OF EXECUTANTS AND WITNESSES
PART VIII: OF PRESENTING WILLS AND AUTHORITIES TO ADOPT
PART IX: OF THE DEPOSIT OF WILLS
PART X: OF THE EFFECTS OF REGISTRATION AND NON-REGISTRATION
PART XI: OF THE DUITES AND POWERS OF REGISTERING OFFICERS
PART XII: OF REFUSAL TO REGISTER
PART XIII: OF THE FEES FOR REGISTRATION, SEARCHES AND COPIES

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its geographical application to the whole of India, and its effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Immovable Property' and 'Lease'.

key_sections.title: Documents of which registration is compulsory.
key_sections.description: Lists categories of documents, including instruments of gift of immovable property and certain leases, for which registration is mandatory.

key_sections.title: Documents of which registration is optional.
key_sections.description: Outlines types of documents, such as instruments relating to movable property or wills, for which registration is not compulsory but may be done.

key_sections.title: Time for presenting documents.
key_sections.description: Sets a four-month time limit for presenting documents (other than wills) for registration after their execution.

key_sections.title: Place for registering documents relating to land.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that documents concerning land must be presented for registration in the sub-district where the property is located.

key_sections.title: Persons to present documents for registration.
key_sections.description: Identifies who is authorized to present documents for registration, including executing parties, their representatives, or agents.

key_sections.title: Compulsory affixing of photograph, etc.
key_sections.description: Requires persons presenting documents to affix their passport size photograph and fingerprints to the document, especially for immovable property transfers.

key_sections.title: Enquiry before registration by registering officer.
key_sections.description: Mandates an inquiry by the registering officer to verify execution, identity of parties, and the right of representatives before registration.

key_sections.title: Procedure on admission and denial of execution respectively.
key_sections.description: Details the process for registration when execution is admitted and the procedure for refusal when execution is denied or the party is incapacitated.

key_sections.title: Time from which registered document operates.
key_sections.description: States that a registered document operates from the time it would have commenced operation, not from the time of its registration.

key_sections.title: Effect of non-registration of documents required to be registered.
key_sections.description: Specifies that unregistered documents required to be registered will not affect immovable property or be received as evidence, with certain provisos.

key_sections.title: Register-books to be kept in the several offices.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the types of register-books (e.g., Book 1 for non-testamentary documents, Book 3 for wills) to be maintained in registration offices.

key_sections.title: Power of Inspector-General to superintend registration offices and make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Inspector-General general superintendence over registration offices and the power to make rules for various procedural matters.

key_sections.title: Reasons for refusal to register to be recorded.
key_sections.description: Requires Sub-Registrars to record reasons for refusing to register a document in Book No. 2 and provide a copy to the applicant.

key_sections.title: Suit in case of order of refusal by Registrar.
key_sections.description: Allows a person aggrieved by a Registrar's refusal to register a document to file a suit in a Civil Court to direct registration.

key_sections.title: Fees to be fixed by State Government.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to prepare a table of fees for registration, searches, copies, and other related services.

key_sections.title: Penalty for incorrectly endorsing, copying, translating or registering documents with intent to injure.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for registering officers or their employees who intentionally make incorrect entries or copies with intent to cause injury.

key_sections.title: Penalty for making false statements, delivering false copies or translations, false personation, and abetment.
key_sections.description: Imposes penalties for making false statements, delivering false documents or translations, false personation, or abetting such acts.

powers_conferred: State Government: To appoint Inspector-General of Registration (S.3), form districts and sub-districts (S.5), appoint Registrars and Sub-Registrars (S.6), establish offices (S.7), appoint Inspectors of Registration offices (S.8), fill vacancies in Registrar's or Sub-Registrar's office (S.10, S.12), allow proper establishments (S.14), provide register-books and fire-proof boxes (S.16), exempt certain leases from compulsory registration (S.17), require description of houses and land by reference to Government maps or surveys (S.22), fix fees for registration, searches, and copies (S.78), approve rules made by the Inspector-General (S.69).

Inspector-General of Registration: To appoint persons to act as Registrar during absence or vacancy (S.10), prescribe forms for register-books (S.16), prescribe safeguards for keeping books in electronic form (S.16A), exercise general superintendence over registration offices and make rules (S.69), remit fines (S.70).

Registrar: To appoint persons to act as Sub-Registrar during absence or vacancy (S.12), receive and register any document registrable by a subordinate Sub-Registrar (S.30), direct registration of documents where presentation was delayed (S.34), order registration after appeal (S.75), superintend and control Sub-Registrars (S.68), issue orders for rectification of errors (S.68), summon and enforce attendance of witnesses (S.75).
Registering Officer: To administer oaths and record substance of statements (S.63), commence prosecutions for offences under the Act (S.83).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 81 prescribes punishment (imprisonment up to seven years, or fine, or both) for registering officers or their employees who incorrectly endorse, copy, translate, or register documents with intent to injure. Section 82 prescribes punishment (imprisonment up to seven years, or fine, or both) for making false statements, delivering false copies or translations, false personation, or abetment of such acts. State amendments (e.g., Gujarat Act 4 of 2020, S.89C) may prescribe additional penalties, such as imprisonment for failure to file notice under section 89B.

repealed_acts: Acts mentioned in the repealed Schedule of the Act, which was repealed by the Repealing Act, 1938 (1 of 1938).
related_acts: State Bank of India (Subsidiary Bank) Act, 1959
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertaking) Act, 1970

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government appoints the Inspector-General of Registration, Registrars, Sub-Registrars, and Inspectors of Registration offices. The Inspector-General appoints persons to act as Registrar during absence or vacancy. The Registrar appoints persons to act as Sub-Registrar during absence or vacancy.

applies_to: Whole of India
Documents of which registration is compulsory (S.17)
Documents of which registration is optional (S.18)
exemptions: Leases executed in any district or part of a district where terms do not exceed five years and annual rents do not exceed fifty rupees (S.17 proviso).

Documents specified in Section 17(2) (e.g., composition deeds, shares in joint stock companies, certain debentures, specific court decrees/orders, grants of immovable property by Government, partition instruments by Revenue-Officer, loan orders under specific acts, mortgage endorsements/receipts, certificates of sale by Civil/Revenue-Officer).
Persons exempt from appearance at registration-office due to bodily infirmity, being in jail, or legal exemption from personal appearance in Court (S.38).
Certain documents executed by or in favour of Government (S.90).
special_provisions: The State Government may exclude any districts or tracts of country from the Act's operation (S.1(2) proviso).
Various State Amendments exist, modifying sections for specific states like Karnataka, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Orissa, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Tripura, Kerala, and Haryana.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Inspector-General of Registration (S.69) with the sanction/approval of the State Government. The State Government also has direct rule-making powers (e.22, S.89A, S.91).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a system of registration offices, with procedures for presenting documents, inquiries, admission or refusal of registration, appeals against refusal, and suits in Civil Courts. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance or fraudulent acts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District Court, High Court (in its ordinary original civil jurisdiction), Civil Court.

schedules_summary.description: Contained a list of Repeal of Enactments, but the Schedule itself has been repealed by the Repealing Act, 1938.

act_identification.act_title: THE PRESIDENCY-TOWNS INSOLVENCY ACT, 1909

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Presidency-towns (Calcutta, Madras and Bombay) and the States as defined in Section 2(j)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend the Law of Insolvency in the Presidency towns *** WHEREAS it is expedient to amend the law relating to insolvency in the Presidency-towns ***; It is hereby enacted as follows :––
act_overview.purpose: To amend the law relating to insolvency in the Presidency-towns, providing for the administration of property of insolvents and the process of discharge.

chapter_titles: PART I CONSTITUTION AND POWERS OF COURT
PART II PROCEEDINGS FROM ACT OF INSOLVENCY TO DISCHARGE

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the official short title of the Act and its date of commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'creditor', 'debt', 'official assignee', and 'property'.

key_sections.title: Courts having jurisdiction in insolvency.
key_sections.description: Specifies the High Courts at Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay as having jurisdiction under this Act.

key_sections.title: Acts of insolvency .
key_sections.description: Enumerates various actions or circumstances that constitute an act of insolvency by a debtor.

key_sections.title: Power to adjudicate.
key_sections.description: Grants the Court power to make an order of adjudication, declaring a debtor insolvent, upon a petition by a creditor or the debtor.

key_sections.title: Effect of order of adjudication.
key_sections.description: States that upon adjudication, the insolvent's property vests in the official assignee and becomes divisible among creditors, restricting other remedies against the property.

key_sections.title: Power for Court to annul adjudication in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Allows the Court to annul an adjudication if the debtor should not have been adjudged insolvent or if debts are paid in full.

key_sections.title: Discharge of insolvent.
key_sections.description: Enables an insolvent to apply for an order of discharge, which the Court may grant absolutely, suspend, or grant conditionally.

key_sections.title: Effect of order of discharge.
key_sections.description: Specifies the debts from which an insolvent is released by an order of discharge and those from which they are not, such as government debts or debts incurred by fraud.

key_sections.title: Debts provable in insolvency.
key_sections.description: Defines which debts and liabilities are provable in insolvency, excluding unliquidated damages not arising from contract or breach of trust.

key_sections.title: Priority of debts.
key_sections.description: Establishes the order of priority for payment of debts in the distribution of the insolvent's property, including debts due to Government and wages.

key_sections.title: Description of insolvents property divisible amongst creditors.
key_sections.description: Describes the property of the insolvent that is divisible among creditors, excluding property held in trust and certain personal necessities.

key_sections.title: Appointment and removal of official assignees of insolvents estate.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for appointing and removing official assignees and deputy official assignees for insolvents' estates.

key_sections.title: Undischarged insolvent obtaining credit.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for an undischarged insolvent who obtains credit of fifty rupees or upwards without disclosing their status.

key_sections.title: Rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Courts having jurisdiction to make rules for carrying into effect the objects of the Act, covering various procedural and administrative aspects.

Power of Court to review, rescind or vary any order (Section 8)

Discharged insolvent failing to assist in realization of property is contempt of Court (Section 43).

act_identification.act_title: THE ANAND MARRIAGE ACT, 1909

act_overview.preamble: An Act to remove doubts as to the validity of the marriage ceremony common among the Sikhs called Anand. WHEREAS it expedient to remove any doubts as to the validity of the marriage ceremony common among the Sikhs called Anand; it is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The primary purpose of this Act is to remove doubts and validate marriages solemnized according to the Sikh marriage ceremony called Anand. It also provides for the optional registration of such marriages to facilitate proof.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the official name of the Act and specifies its geographical application.

key_sections.title: Validity of Anand marriages.
key_sections.description: Declares all past and future Anand marriages, solemnized according to the Sikh marriage ceremony, as good and valid in law.

key_sections.title: Exemption of certain marraiges from Act.
key_sections.description: Specifies marriages not covered by the Act, such as those between non-Sikhs or judicially declared null and void.

key_sections.title: Saving of marriages solemnized according to other ceremonies.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not affect the validity of any marriage duly solemnized according to other customary Sikh marriage ceremonies.

key_sections.title: Non-validation of marriages within prohibited degrees.
key_sections.description: States that the Act does not validate marriages between persons related within prohibited degrees of consanguinity or affinity according to Sikh customary law.

key_sections.title: Registration of marriages.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to make rules for the optional registration of Anand marriages, outlining the process, inspection, and evidentiary value of the Marriage Register.

powers_conferred: State Government shall make rules providing that the parties to any such marriage may have the particulars relating to their marriage entered in a Marriage Register.
Registrar to give certified extracts from the Marriage Register to the parties to the marriage on payment of fees.
State Government to lay every rule made under this section before the State Legislature.

authorities_established: officer of the State Government or of a local authority authorised by the State Government
important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government to authorise officers of the State Government or of a local authority to keep a Marriage Register.

applies_to: Marriages solemnized according to the Sikh marriage ceremony called Anand
Parties to such marriages
exemptions: any marriage between persons not professing the Sikh religion
any marriage which has been judicially declared to be null and void
marriages between persons who are related to each other in any degree of consanguinity or affinity which would, according to the customary law of the Sikhs, render a marriage between them illegal
special_provisions: The Act has extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963, s. 2 and first Schedule (w.e.f. 1-7-1965).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: State Governments are to make rules for the optional registration of Anand marriages in a Marriage Register kept by authorized officers. The register is open for inspection, and certified extracts serve as evidence.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN MUSEUM ACT, 1910

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry concerned with matters relating to the Indian Museum

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to the Indian Museum; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing law concerning the Indian Museum, establishing its governance and defining the powers and duties of its Trustees.
act_overview.act_category: Institutions of Natural and Cultural Importance

chapter_titles: PROPERTY AND POWERS OF THE TRUSTEES

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Constitution and incorporation of the Trustees of the Indian Museum.
key_sections.description: Defines the composition of the Trustees, their corporate status, and powers.

key_sections.title: Property vested in or placed under the control of the Trustees.
key_sections.description: Specifies that all property of the Indian Museum vests in the Trustees and grants them exclusive possession and control of the land and buildings.

key_sections.title: Power to Trustees to exchange, sell and destroy articles in collections.
key_sections.description: Grants Trustees powers to loan, exchange, sell, present, remove, and destroy articles in their collections, subject to bye-laws.

key_sections.title: Power to Trustees to make bye-laws.
key_sections.description: Empowers Trustees to make bye-laws for the execution of their trust, with Central Government sanction, covering various aspects of museum management.

key_sections.title: Power of Trustees to appoint officers and servants.
key_sections.description: Authorizes Trustees to appoint officers and servants for the care and management of trust-property and determine their functions.

key_sections.title: Budget
key_sections.description: Requires Trustees to submit an annual budget to the Central Government for approval.

key_sections.title: Annual report and accounts.
key_sections.description: Mandates Trustees to submit annual reports and accounts to the Central Government and an appointed auditor, and to publish them.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to issue directions to Trustees.
key_sections.description: Binds Trustees to follow directions from the Central Government on policy matters, after being given an opportunity to express their views.

key_sections.title: Officers under Act to be public servants.
key_sections.description: Declares officers and servants appointed under this Act as public servants under the Indian Penal Code.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, covering recruitment, conditions of service, accounts, and custody of collections.

key_sections.title: Property in collections on determination of trust.
key_sections.description: Specifies the ownership of collections if the trust constituted by this Act is determined, distinguishing between Asiatic Society collections and others.

powers_conferred: Power to Trustees to acquire and hold property, enter into contracts, sue and be sued (Section 2(2))
Power to Trustees to exchange, sell, and destroy articles in collections (Section 7)
Power to Trustees to make bye-laws (Section 8)
Power to Trustees to appoint officers and servants (Section 9)
Power to Trustees to keep collections not belonging to them (Section 14)
Power to Trustees to part with certain property in their possession (Section 15)
Power to Central Government to specify commencement date (Section 1(2))
Power to Central Government to sanction bye-laws (Section 8(1))
Power to Central Government to specify budget submission date (Section 10)
Power to Central Government to appoint auditor (Section 10A(1)(b))
Power to Central Government to issue directions to Trustees on policy matters (Section 12A)
Power to Central Government to sanction custody and administration of other collections (Section 14)
Power to Central Government to approve conditions for parting with property (Section 15)
Power to Central Government to make rules (Section 15A)

authorities_established: The Trustees of the Indian Museum
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The authority which nominated a Trustee has the power to nominate a new Trustee in case of vacancy (Section 4). The Trustees have the power to appoint officers and servants (Section 9(1)). The Central Government has the power to appoint an auditor (Section 10A(1)(b)).

applies_to: The Indian Museum
The Trustees of the Indian Museum
Officers and servants appointed under this Act

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Trustees, with the previous sanction of the Central Government, can make bye-laws (Section 8). The Central Government can make rules (Section 15A).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act establishes a body corporate (The Trustees of the Indian Museum) to manage the museum. The Central Government exercises oversight through approval of budgets, sanctioning bye-laws, issuing directions, and making rules. Officers and servants are deemed public servants.

schedules_summary.description: Describes the specific land boundaries and appurtenances (buildings, roads, tanks, easements) that are vested in or placed under the control of the Trustees for the purposes of the Indian Museum.

act_identification.act_title: THE CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES ACT, 1912

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India except [2][the territories which, immediately before the 1[st ] November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States]

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient further to facilitate the formation of Co-operative Societies for the promotion of thrift and self-help among agriculturists, artisans and persons of limited means, and for that purpose to amend the law relating to Co-operative Societies; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to facilitate the formation of Co-operative Societies. It aims to promote thrift and self-help among agriculturists, artisans, and persons of limited means by amending the law relating to Co-operative Societies.

chapter_titles: PROPERTY AND FUNDS OF REGISTERED SOCIETIES

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: The Registrar.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to appoint a Registrar of Co-operative Societies and assistants, conferring powers upon them.

key_sections.title: Societies which may be registered.
key_sections.description: Outlines the types of societies that can be registered under the Act, focusing on promotion of economic interests and co-operative principles.

key_sections.title: Registration.
key_sections.description: Grants the Registrar the power to register a society and its by-laws if satisfied with compliance to the Act and rules.

key_sections.title: Societies to be bodies corporate.
key_sections.description: Declares that registration confers corporate body status with perpetual succession, common seal, and powers to hold property, contract, and sue.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt from income-tax, stamp-duty and registration fees.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government and State Government to remit income-tax, stamp-duty, and registration fees for registered societies.

key_sections.title: Restrictions on loans.
key_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on registered societies regarding lending to non-members and lending on security of moveable or immoveable property.

key_sections.title: Inquiry by Registrar.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Registrar to conduct or direct inquiries into the constitution, working, and financial condition of a registered society.

key_sections.title: Dissolution.
key_sections.description: Grants the Registrar power to cancel the registration of a society after inquiry or application, leading to its dissolution.

key_sections.title: Winding-up.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of a liquidator upon cancellation of registration and outlines the liquidator's powers for winding-up the society's affairs.

key_sections.title: Rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, specifying various matters for which rules can be made.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of the use of the word “co-operative”.
key_sections.description: Prohibits any person other than a registered society from using the word 'co-operative' in their trade name without State Government sanction.

key_sections.title: Indian Companies Act, 1882, not to apply.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of the Indian Companies Act, 1882, shall not apply to registered societies.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever contravenes the provisions of Section 47 (Prohibition of the use of the word “co-operative”) shall be punishable with fine which may extend to fifty rupees, and in the case of a continuing offence with further fine of five rupees for each day on which the offence is continued after conviction therefor.

repealed_acts: Co-operative Credit Societies Act, 1904 (10 of 1904)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government has the power to appoint a Registrar of Co-operative Societies and persons to assist the Registrar. The Registrar has the power to appoint a competent person to be liquidator of a society.

applies_to: Societies having as their object the promotion of the economic interests of their members in accordance with co-operative principles
Societies established with the object of facilitating the operations of such societies
Societies consisting of at least ten persons above the age of eighteen years (with exceptions for societies where a member is a registered society)
exemptions: Any society may be exempted by the State Government from any of the requirements of this Act as to registration by special order.
Any registered society may be exempted by the State Government from any of the provisions of this Act or have provisions applied with modifications by general or special order.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the powers of the Registrar, including registration, audit, inquiry, inspection, and cancellation of registration. implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate having jurisdiction (for recovery of costs), Civil Court (for enforcement of liquidator's orders), Court of the District Judge (for appeals from liquidator's orders).

act_identification.act_title: THE OFFICIAL TRUSTEES ACT, 1913

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the Law constituting the office of Official Trustee.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to consolidate and amend the existing laws related to the establishment and functioning of the office of Official Trustee. It defines the powers, duties, and liabilities of the Official Trustee in managing trusts and properties.

chapter_titles: PART II: THE OFFICE OF OFFICIAL TRUSTEE
PART III: RIGHTS, POWERS, DUTIES AND LIABILITIES OF OFFICIAL TRUSTEE

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Interpretation clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, such as 'Government' and 'prescribed'.

key_sections.title: Official Trustees.
key_sections.description: Mandates the appointment of an Official Trustee by the Government for each State.

key_sections.title: Official Trustee to be corporation sole, to have perpetual succession and official seal, and to sue and be sued in his corporate name.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Official Trustee as a corporation sole with perpetual succession and the ability to sue and be sued.

key_sections.title: General powers and duties of Official Trustee.
key_sections.description: Outlines the general powers and duties of the Official Trustee, including acting as an ordinary trustee and conditions for accepting trusts.

key_sections.title: Power of High Court to appoint Official Trustee to be trustee of property.
key_sections.description: Grants the High Court the power to appoint the Official Trustee as a trustee of property under certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Liability of Government.
key_sections.description: Stipulates the Government's liability to cover sums for the Official Trustee's personal liabilities, with specific exceptions.

key_sections.title: Fees.
key_sections.description: Provides for the charging of fees for the duties performed by the Official Trustee, to be prescribed by the Government.

key_sections.title: Auditors to be appointed to examine Official Trustees’s accounts, etc., and to report to Government.

key_sections.title: Rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Government to make rules for the effective implementation of the Act and regulation of the Official Trustee's duties.

powers_conferred: Official Trustee: act as an ordinary trustee, be appointed trustee by a Court, decline trusts, accept trusts (with conditions), sue and be sued in corporate name, incur expenditure for property care and management.
High Court: appoint Official Trustee as trustee of property, make orders respecting trust property, make orders regarding payment of transferred moneys.

Government: appoint Official Trustees, appoint Deputy Official Trustees, prescribe fees, make rules for the Act's objects and Official Trustee's proceedings, direct transfer of property between Official Trustees.
Auditor: summon witnesses, examine persons on oath, issue commissions for examination, summon for production of documents.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who, when summoned by an auditor, refuses or neglects to attend, produce documents, be sworn, or be examined, shall be deemed to have committed an offence punishable under section 188 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).

related_acts: Bihar and West Bengal (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1956 (40 of 1956)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Government shall appoint an Official Trustee for each State. The Government may appoint a Deputy or Deputies to assist the Official Trustee.

applies_to: the whole of India
persons intending to create a trust
executors of wills
administrators of estates
private trustees
minors entitled to gift, legacy or share
lunatics entitled to gift, legacy or share
exemptions: Official Trustee shall not accept any trust under any composition or scheme of arrangement for the benefit of creditors.
Official Trustee shall not accept any trust of any estate known or believed by him to be insolvent.

Official Trustee shall not administer the estate of a deceased person, unless he is expressly appointed sole executor of, and sole trustee under, the will of such person.
special_provisions: Amendments to this Act coming into force on 26th January, 1950, shall not affect pending legal proceedings or automatically transfer property from one Official Trustee to another.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the actions of the Official Trustee, oversight by the High Court, and regular audits of the Official Trustee's accounts. Non-compliance with auditor summons can lead to penalties under the Indian Penal Code.

act_identification.act_title: THE WHITE PHOSPHORUS MATCHES PROHIBITION ACT, 1913

key_sections.title: Prohibition of use of white phosphorus in manufacture of matches.

key_sections.title: Power of Inspector of Factories to take samples of material used in manufacture.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of sale.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the sale, offer for sale, or possession for sale of matches made with white phosphorus, and provides for forfeiture of such matches.

Magistrate: Power to order forfeiture and destruction of matches made with white phosphorus (Section 6(2)).

Contravention of the prohibition on sale may lead to forfeiture of matches (Section 6(2)).

applies_to: Persons involved in the manufacture of matches

act_identification.act_title: THE SIR JAMSETJEE JEJEEBHOY BARONETCY ACT, 1915
act_identification.act_short_title: The Sir Jamsetjee Jejeebhoy Baronetcy Act, 1915

legislative_details.enacted_by: Legislative Council of the Governor General of India

act_overview.preamble:
An Act for repealing Act No. 20 of 1860 entitled An “Act for settling Promissory Notes of the Government of India, producing an annual income of one lakh of rupees and a Mansion House and hereditaments called Mazagon Castle, in the Island of Bombay, late the property of Sir Jamsetjee Jejeebhoy, Baronet, deceased, so as to accompany and support the title and dignity of a Baronet, lately conferred on him and the heirs male of his body, by Her present Majesty Queen Victoria, and for other purposes connected therewith,” and for resettling the said Promissory Notes, Mansion House and hereditaments and for other purposes connected therewith.
WHEREAS by Letters Patent of Her late Majesty Queen Victoria, by the Grace of God of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland Queen, Defender of the Faith, dated at Westminster on or about the 6th day of August in the 21st year of Her said late Majesty’s reign, and by Warrant under Her said late Majesty’s sign-manual, Her said late Majesty made known that she, of her special grace, certain knowledge and mere motion had erected, appointed and created Sir Jamsetjee Jejeebhoy, then of Bombay, Knight, but then deceased (a man eminent for family inheritance, estate and integrity of manner), to and into the dignity, state, and degree of a Baronet, and him, the said Sir Jamsetjee Jejeebhoy for Her said late Majesty, her heirs, and successors, she did erect, appoint, constitute and create a Baronet, by the said Letters Patent, to hold to him and the heirs male of his body lawfully begotten, and to be begotten for ever:
And whereas in fulfilment of an engagement in that behalf made with Her said late Majesty’s Government, during the lifetime of the said Sir Jamsetjee Jejeebhoy, deceased, the said Sir Jamsetjee Jejeebhoy was desirous of settling in perpetuity such property on himself and the heirs male of his body who might succeed to the said Baronetcy, as should be adequate to support the dignity of the title conferred on him and them as aforesaid:
And whereas the said Sir Jamsetjee Jejeebhoy was seized of a Mansion House and hereditaments situate in the Island of Bombay called Mazagon Castle, and had an absolute estate of inheritance therein, and was desirous, in fulfilment of the aforesaid engagement, of settling Promissory Notes of the Government of India, producing an annual income of one lakh of rupees and the said Mansion House and the purposes in the said Act No. 20 of 1860 limited and declared, concerning the same respectively:
act_overview.purpose: The Act repeals Act No. 20 of 1860 and resettles the Government Promissory Notes and Mazagon Castle property associated with the Sir Jamsetjee Jejeebhoy Baronetcy. Its main purpose is to provide for the financial support and maintenance of the Baronetcy, including new powers for investment, sale of existing property, and purchase of new residential property, while ensuring the succession and naming conventions for future Baronets.

act_identification.act_title: THE KING OF OUDH’S ESTATE VALIDATION ACT, 1917
act_identification.act_short_title: The King of Oudh’s Estate Validation Act, 1917

act_overview.preamble: An Act to validate certain deeds of conveyance and a trust deed relating to certain properties of His late Majesty, Wajid Ali Shah, King of Oudh, and for other purposes. WHEREAS doubts have arisen as to the validity of three deeds of conveyance, all dated the 23rd November 1901, and a deed of declaration of trust of the same date, copies of which are set out in the Schedule to this Act, and all of which deeds purport to relate to certain properties then or formerly of His late Majesty, Wajid Ali Shah, King of Oudh (hereinafter, in this Act, called the late King), and in the case of the said trust deed to declare the trusts of a certain Emambarra, mosque and burial ground, and for the up-keep and maintenance thereof to constitute a certain Endowment Fund hereinafter in this Act referred to as the Sibtainabad Endowment Fund; And Whereas by the said trust deed it was recited or assumed inter alia that a share amounting to rupees two hundred thousand in a certain Government Promissory Note No. 018878 for rupees five hundred thousand standing in the name of Malkai Kisshore and deposited in the Government Treasury at Lucknow belonged to the estate of the late King, and that the said share was to form a part of the Sibtainabad Endowment Fund, and the interest thereon to be applied with the interest of certain other securities in the said trust deed referred to for the up-keep and maintenance of the said Emambarra, mosque and burial ground; And Whereas all interest from the 1st of March 1901 to the 31st of December 1913 payable in respect of the said share of rupees two hundred thousand in the said Note has been paid and credited to the Sibtainabad Endowment Fund along with the interest of the said other securities and the said Emambarra, mosque and burial ground have been kept up and maintained thereout; And Whereas it now appears that the said share of rupees two hundred thousand did not, in fact, belong to the estate of the late King, and that on his death the interest thoreon was or was intended to be payable to certain of the issue of the said Malkai Kisshore, and that the inclusion of the interest of the said share in the Sibtainabad Endowment Fund was due to a misapprehension; And Whereas there is now standing to the credit of the Sibtainabad Endowment Fund the sum of rupees seventy-seven thousand eight hundred and fifty-six being the accumulated balance after providing for the up-keep and maintenance of the said Emambarra, mosque and burial ground; And Whereas it is expedient that the said deeds of conveyance and the said trust deed and all acts and things done thereunder should be validated, and that at the same time it should be formally declared that the said share of rupees two hundred thousand no longer forms a part of the Sibtainabad Endowment Fund, and that the interest thereon shall be made available as from the 1st of January 1914, for the persons who may hereafter be deemed entitled thereto under the provisions hereinafter appearing; And Whereas it is just and equitable that the said sum of rupees seventy-seven thousand eight hundred and fifty-six should be released from the trusts of the said trust deed and should also be made available for distribution amongst the persons so entitled; And Whereas it is also expedient to provide for the future management and distribution of the said share of rupees two hundred thousand and of the interest accrued due since, the 1st of January 1914, and hereafter accruing due for time to time in respect thereof and also for the distribution of any future surplus monies which may accrue to the said Sibtainabad Endowment Fund after providing for the up-keep and maintenance of the said Emambarra mosque and burial ground;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to validate certain deeds of conveyance and a trust deed related to the estate of the late King of Oudh, Wajid Ali Shah. It also aims to clarify the status of a specific share in a Government Promissory Note within the Sibtainabad Endowment Fund and to provide for the distribution of certain funds and future management of the endowment.

act_identification.act_title: THE USURIOUS LOANS ACT, 1918

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to give additional powers to Courts to deal in certain cases with usurious loans of money or in kind; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to provide additional powers to Courts to address usurious loans. It enables Courts to re-open transactions, adjust excessive interest, and modify securities to ensure fairness in loan agreements.

key_definitions: Suit to which this Act applies

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical application, along with the power of State Government to exempt certain areas or transactions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Interest', 'Loan', and 'Suit to which this Act applies'.

key_sections.title: Re-opening of transactions.
key_sections.description: Grants Courts powers to re-open loan transactions, relieve debtors of excessive interest, and revise or alter securities if the interest is excessive and the transaction was substantially unfair.

key_sections.title: Insolvency proceedings.
key_sections.description: Extends the powers granted to Courts under Section 3 to applications relating to the admission or amount of a proof of a loan in insolvency proceedings.

powers_conferred: Courts may re-open transactions, take an account between parties, and relieve the debtor of all liability in respect of any excessive interest.
Courts may re-open any account already taken and order the creditor to repay any sum in respect of excessive interest.
Courts may set aside either wholly or in part or revise or alter any security given or agreement made in respect of any loan, and order the creditor to indemnify the debtor.
The State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, direct that the Act shall not apply to any area, class of persons, or class of transactions.

applies_to: Suits for the recovery of a loan made after the commencement of this Act
Suits for the enforcement of any security taken or any agreement made after the commencement of this Act, in respect of any loan
Suits for the redemption of any security given after the commencement of this Act in respect of any loan
exemptions: The territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States
Any area, class of persons, or class of transactions specified by State Government notification

Rights of any transferee for value who satisfies the Court that the transfer to him was bona fide, and that he had at the time of such transfer no notice of any fact which would have entitled the debtor as against the lender to relief under Section 3
special_provisions: The State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, direct that the Act shall not apply to any area, class of persons, or class of transactions which it may specify in its notification.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through Courts exercising powers in suits to which this Act applies and in insolvency proceedings.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts in general, and specifically in insolvency proceedings.

act_identification.act_title: THE POISONS ACT, 1919

legislative_details.geographical_extent: extends to the whole of India: Provided that it shall not apply to the State of Jammu and Kashmir* except to the extent to which the provisions of this Act relate to the importation into India of any specified poison.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law regulating the importation, possession and sale of poisons *** WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law regulating the importation, possession and sale of poisons ***; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To consolidate and amend the law regulating the importation, possession and sale of poisons.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical extent.

key_sections.title: Power of the State Government to regulate possession for sale and sale of any poison.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the State Government to regulate the possession for sale and sale of specified poisons through rules, including licensing, sales conditions, and safe custody.

key_sections.title: Power to prohibit importation into the States of any poison except under licence.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to prohibit the importation of specified poisons without a licence and to regulate the grant of such licences.

key_sections.title: Power to regulate possession of any poison in certain areas.
key_sections.description: Allows the State Government to regulate the possession of specified poisons in local areas where their use for committing murder or mischief by poisoning cattle is frequent, and prescribes penalties for breaches.

key_sections.title: Presumption as to specified poisons.
key_sections.description: States that any substance specified as a poison in a rule or notification under this Act is deemed a poison for the Act's purposes.

key_sections.title: Penalty for unlawful importation, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for breaches of rules under section 2, unlawful importation without a licence, or breaking licence conditions, including imprisonment, fine, and confiscation.

key_sections.title: Power to issue search warrants.
key_sections.description: Authorizes District Magistrates, Sub-divisional Magistrates, and Commissioners of Police to issue search warrants for places suspected of possessing or selling poison in contravention of the Act.

key_sections.title: Rules.
key_sections.description: Confers general rule-making power on the State Government and Central Government to carry out the Act's purposes, subject to previous publication and legislative oversight.

key_sections.title: Savings.
key_sections.description: Provides exemptions for medical or veterinary practitioners acting in good faith and allows the State Government or rule-making authority to exempt certain articles, classes of articles, or persons from the Act's provisions.

powers_conferred: State Government: regulate possession for sale and sale of any specified poison (Section 2)
State Government: grant licences to possess any specified poison for sale (Section 2)
State Government: regulate possession of any specified poison in certain local areas (Section 4)
State Government: make rules generally to carry out the purposes and objects of this Act (Section 8)
State Government: declare that provisions of this Act shall be deemed not to apply to any article or class of articles or any poison or class of poisons (Section 9)

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Breach of any rule made under section 2, unlawful importation without a licence, or breaking any condition of an importation licence is punishable. For a first conviction, imprisonment may extend to three months or a fine up to five hundred rupees, or both. For a second or subsequent conviction, imprisonment may extend to six months or a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both. Any poison involved is liable to confiscation. Breach of rules made under section 4(1) is punishable with imprisonment for up to one year, or a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both, along with confiscation of the poison.

Persons dealing with poisons

Any article or class of articles of commerce specified by State Government order (Section 9(2))
Any poison or class of poisons used for any purpose specified by State Government order (Section 9(2))
Any person or class of persons exempted by the rule-making authority (Section 9(3))
special_provisions: It shall not apply to the State of Jammu and Kashmir* except to the extent to which the provisions of this Act relate to the importation into India of any specified poison.

implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District Magistrate, Sub-divisional Magistrate, Commissioner of Police (for search warrants)

act_identification.act_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the Law relating to Insolvency as administered by Courts having jurisdiction outside the Presidency-towns.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States and the Scheduled Districts

act_overview.preamble:
An Act to consolidate and amend the Law relating to Insolvency [1]*** as administered by Courts having jurisdiction outside the Presidency-towns [2]***.

WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to insolvency [1]*** as

administered by Courts having jurisdiction outside the Presidency-towns [2]*** ;

It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws related to insolvency. Its primary objective is to provide a structured legal framework for the administration of insolvency proceedings by courts outside the Presidency-towns, ensuring fair distribution of a debtor's property among creditors and regulating the discharge of debtors.

chapter_titles:
PART I
CONSTITUTION AND POWERS OF COURT

PART II
PROCEEDINGS FROM ACT OF INSOLVENCY TO DISCHARGE

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'creditor', 'debtor', 'property', and 'secured creditor'.

key_sections.title: Insolvency jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Establishes District Courts as having insolvency jurisdiction and allows State Governments to invest subordinate courts with concurrent jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Act of insolvency.
key_sections.description: Defines various actions or inactions by a debtor that constitute an act of insolvency, leading to potential proceedings.

key_sections.title: Petition and adjudication.
key_sections.description: Outlines the conditions under which a creditor or debtor may present an insolvency petition, leading to an order of adjudication.

key_sections.title: Effect of an order of adjudication.
key_sections.description: Describes the legal consequences of an order of adjudication, including the vesting of the insolvent's property in the Court or receiver and restrictions on creditors' remedies.

key_sections.title: Power to annul adjudication of insolvency.
key_sections.description: Grants the Court the power to annul an adjudication of insolvency if it was improperly made or if the debts have been paid in full.

key_sections.title: Discharge.
key_sections.description: Details the process for a debtor to apply for an order of discharge and the Court's authority to grant, suspend, or refuse it, possibly with conditions.

key_sections.title: Cases in which Court must refuse an absolute discharge.
key_sections.description: Specifies various grounds, such as insufficient assets or fraudulent conduct, upon which the Court is required to refuse an absolute order of discharge.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Receiver.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of a receiver for the insolvent's property, which thereupon vests in the receiver, and outlines conditions for their appointment and removal.

key_sections.title: Duties and powers of receiver.
key_sections.description: Lays out the responsibilities and authorities of the receiver, including realizing the debtor's property, distributing dividends, and carrying on business with court leave.

key_sections.title: Priority of debts.
key_sections.description: Establishes the order of priority for the payment of different types of debts, such as government debts and wages, from the insolvent's property.

key_sections.title: Offences by debtors.
key_sections.description: Defines various offences committed by debtors, such as willful failure to perform duties or fraudulent concealment of property, and prescribes penalties.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Outlines the provisions for appeals against decisions and orders made by subordinate courts and District Courts in insolvency matters.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the High Court, with the sanction of the State Government, the power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.

Court: To exercise general powers and follow civil procedure (Section 5)
Court: To appoint an interim receiver (Section 20)

Court: To order release of debtor from arrest or imprisonment (Section 23)
Court: To award compensation against a creditor for frivolous petition (Section 26)

Court: To annul adjudication of insolvency (Section 35)
Court: To cancel one of concurrent orders of adjudication (Section 36)
Court: To approve or refuse compositions and schemes of arrangement (Section 38, Section 39)
Court: To re-adjudge debtor insolvent (Section 40)
Court: To grant, suspend, or refuse an order of discharge (Section 41)
Court: To redeem a secured creditor's security (Section 47)
Court: To expunge or reduce entries in the schedule (Section 50)
Court: To appoint a receiver for the property of the insolvent (Section 56)
Court: To remove persons from possession or custody of property (Section 56)
Court: To direct attachment and sale of receiver's property for default (Section 56)
Court: To exercise all rights and powers of a receiver if none is appointed (Section 58)
Court: To grant leave for receiver to carry on business, institute suits, etc. (Section 59)

Court: To make allowance to the insolvent out of his property (Section 66)
Court: To authorize creditors to appoint a committee of inspection (Section 67A)
Court: To confirm, reverse, or modify acts or decisions of the receiver (Section 68)
Court: To record a finding and make a complaint for offences by debtors (Section 70)
Court: To send cases for trial to a Magistrate (Section 72)
Court: To grant or refuse a certificate regarding the cause of insolvency (Section 73)
State Government: To invest subordinate courts with jurisdiction (Section 3)
State Government: To appoint Official Receivers (Section 57)
State Government: To fix remuneration for Official Receivers (Section 57)
State Government: To empower Court or officer to require information (Section 59A)
State Government: To bar application of certain provisions to certain Courts (Section 81)
High Court: To make rules for carrying into effect the Act (Section 79)
High Court: To direct Official Receiver's powers (Section 80)
Receiver: To realize the property of the debtor and distribute dividends (Section 59)
Receiver: To sell all or any part of the property of the insolvent (Section 59)
Receiver: To give receipts for money received (Section 59)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 69 defines offences by debtors, including willful failure to perform duties, fraudulent concealment or destruction of documents, keeping false books, making false entries, concealing debts, or making away with property. The penalty for these offences is imprisonment which may extend to one year. Section 72 makes it an offence for an undischarged insolvent to obtain credit of fifty rupees or upwards without informing the creditor of their status, punishable with imprisonment for up to six months, or fine, or both.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Court has the power to appoint a receiver (Section 56) and an interim receiver (Section 20). The State Government has the power to appoint Official Receivers (Section 57). Creditors who have proved their debts may be authorized by the Court to appoint a committee of inspection (Section 67A).

applies_to: debtor
creditor
insolvent
exemptions: any corporation or against any association or company registered under any enactment for the time being in force (Section 8)
cases to which Chapter IV of the Dekkan Agriculturists Relief Act, 1879 (17 of 1879), is applicable (Section 82)
special_provisions: The Act extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States and the Scheduled Districts (Section 1(2)).
The State Government may invest any Court subordinate to a District Court with jurisdiction in any class of cases (Section 3).
Special provisions apply in local areas where a declaration under section 68 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, is in force regarding sale of immovable property (Section 60).
Provisions for summary administration apply when the debtor's property is not likely to exceed five hundred rupees, with specific modifications to the Act's procedures (Section 74).
The State Government may, by notification, declare that certain provisions of the Act specified in Schedule II shall not apply to insolvency proceedings in certain Courts (Section 81).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The High Court, with the previous sanction of the State Government, may make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act (Section 79).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through District Courts and subordinate courts exercising insolvency jurisdiction. Receivers and Official Receivers are appointed to realize and distribute the insolvent's property. The Court oversees the entire process, including adjudication, discharge, and penalizing offences. Criminal liability for certain offences is handled by Magistrates of the first class.

act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to provide facilities for obtaining information about trusts created for public charitable or religious purposes. It also enables trustees of such trusts to seek directions from a Court on certain matters and makes special provisions for the payment of expenditure in suits against these trustees.

key_sections.title: Procedure on petition.
