act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN RED CROSS SOCIETY ACT, 1920

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India, including specific Union Territories like Goa, Daman and Diu, Lakshadweep, and Pondicherry, and various States and Union territories as listed in the Second Schedule.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the future administration of the various monies and gifts received from the public for the purpose of medical and other aid to the sick and wounded, and other purposes of a like nature during the late war, and more especially for the administration of the monies and property held by a Committee known as the Joint War Committee, Indian Branch, of the Order of St. John of Jerusalem in England and the British Red Cross Society; AND WHEREAS it is expedient to constitute an Indian Red Cross Society with a view to the continuation in peace time, on a wider basis and with a wider purpose, of the work carried on by the said Committee during the war, and to provide for the affiliation therewith of other societies and bodies having similar objects; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to administer funds and gifts received for medical aid during the late war, particularly those held by the Joint War Committee. It constitutes the Indian Red Cross Society to continue this work in peacetime on a wider basis and purpose. The Act also provides for the affiliation of other societies with similar objectives.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act as the Indian Red Cross Society Act, 1920.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Indian Red Cross Society.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Indian Red Cross Society and outlines the nomination process for its first members by the Joint War Committee.

key_sections.title: Incorporation.
key_sections.description: Constitutes the members of the Society as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and powers to hold property and sue/be sued.

key_sections.title: President of the Society.
key_sections.description: Declares the President of India as the President of the Indian Red Cross Society.

key_sections.title: Composition of Managing Body.
key_sections.description: Details the composition of the Managing Body, including nominated and elected members, and provisions for its reconstitution.

key_sections.title: Powers of the President to supersede the Managing Body.
key_sections.description: Grants the President of India the power to supersede the Managing Body under specific conditions of mismanagement or prejudice to the Society's objectives.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Managing Body to make rules for the management, functions, control, and procedure of the Society, with the President's approval.

key_sections.title: Dissolution and transfer of property of Joint War Committee.
key_sections.description: Provides for the dissolution of the Joint War Committee and the vesting of its property, debts, and liabilities in the newly constituted Indian Red Cross Society.

key_sections.title: Purposes to which funds of Society may be applied.
key_sections.description: Specifies the purposes for which the Managing Body may apply the funds and income of the Society, including relief of sickness and suffering due to war or other causes.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Branch Committees.
key_sections.description: Outlines the constitution of Branch Committees in States and the annual distribution of income to them for specified objects.

key_sections.title: Affiliation of other Societies.
key_sections.description: Allows the Managing Body to affiliate other societies or bodies with similar objects, both within India and internationally.

key_sections.title: Transfer of property to Pakistan.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Managing Body to transfer specified funds to the Pakistan Red Cross Society as per the Third Schedule.

powers_conferred: Managing Body: to make rules for the management, functions, control and procedure of the Society (Section 5)
Managing Body: to apply the corpus or income of property for relief of sickness, suffering or distress (Section 7)
Managing Body: to affiliate other societies or bodies (Section 9)
Managing Body: to determine what matters fall within the scope of clause (b) of section 7 (Section 10)
Managing Body: to receive and hold gifts and apply them to purposes (Section 11)
Managing Body: to transfer property to the Pakistan Red Cross Society (Section 13)
President of India: to nominate Chairman and six members of the Managing Body (Section 4B)
President of India: to approve the appointment of Secretary-General and Treasurer (Section 4C)
President of India: to supersede the Managing Body (Section 4E)
Chairman of Managing Body: to preside over meetings, re-appropriate budgetary allocations, authorize expenditure, institute disciplinary proceedings (Section 4D)
Vice-Chairman of Managing Body: to exercise powers of Chairman in his absence, act as ex officio member in committees (Section 4D)
Branch Committees: to receive gifts and expend monies for its purposes (Section 12)
Central Government: to amend the Second Schedule by notification (Section 8(2))

related_acts: Indian Red Cross Society (Amendment) Act, 1992 (14 of 1992)
Indian Red Cross Society (Amendment) Act, 1956 (22 of 1956)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The President of India nominates the Chairman and six members of the Managing Body. The Managing Body, with the previous approval of the President, appoints the Secretary-General and Treasurer of the Society. The first members of the Society and the Managing Body were nominated by the Joint War Committee.

applies_to: Indian Red Cross Society
Joint War Committee, Indian Branch
State Branch Committees
other societies or bodies having similar objects
special_provisions: The Act has been extended with modifications to Goa, Daman and Diu, Lakshadweep, and Pondicherry.
Provisions for the transfer of property to the Pakistan Red Cross Society are detailed in Section 13 and the Third Schedule.
Provisions for the constitution of Branch Committees in States and the distribution of income to them are outlined in Section 8 and the Second Schedule.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Managing Body (with previous approval of the President)

schedules_summary.description: Lists the objects to which the funds of the Society may be applied, including aid to sick and wounded armed forces, maternity and child welfare, relief for disasters, and promotion of peace.
Provides a statement showing the approximate percentage of claim of various States and Union territories to the income of the property vested in the Society.
Details the share of the Pakistan Red Cross Society in specified funds, including amounts advanced and balances payable, for transfer from the Indian Red Cross Society.

act_identification.act_title: THE PASSPORT (ENTRY INTO INDIA) ACT, 1920

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to take power to require passports of persons entering [2][India]; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: An Act to take power to require passports of persons entering India.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, such as 'entry', 'passport', and 'prescribed'.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make rules requiring passports for entry into India, including provisions for prohibitions, prescribing authorities, exemptions, and penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Punishment for subsequent offences.
key_sections.description: Prescribes double the penalty for persons convicted of a subsequent offence under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of arrest.
key_sections.description: Authorizes police officers (sub-inspector and above) and empowered Customs Department officers to arrest without warrant persons contravening or suspected of contravening rules made under Section 3.

key_sections.title: Power of removal.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to direct the removal of persons who have entered India in contravention of rules made under Section 3.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to make rules requiring passports for persons entering India (Section 3(1))
Central Government: Power to empower officers of the Customs Department for arrest (Section 4(1))
Central Government: Power to direct the removal of persons from India (Section 5)
Rules made under Section 3: Power to prohibit entry into India without a passport (Section 3(2)(a))
Rules made under Section 3: Power to prescribe authorities for passport issuance/renewal and conditions (Section 3(2)(b))
Rules made under Section 3: Power to provide for exemption of persons or classes of persons (Section 3(2)(c))
Officer of police (not below the rank of a sub-inspector) and empowered officer of the Customs Department: Power to arrest without warrant (Section 4(1))
Officer of the Government: Power to enforce direction for removal (Section 5)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of rules or orders made under Section 3 is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees, or with both (Section 3(3)). Subsequent offences are punishable with double the penalty provided for the later offence (Section 3A).

applies_to: persons entering India
exemptions: Any person or class of persons from any provision of such rules, either absolutely or on any condition, as provided by rules made under Section 3(2)(c).
special_provisions: Extended to Goa, Daman and Diu with modifications by Regulation 12 of 1962, s. 3 and Sch.
Extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Regulation 6 of 1963, s. 2 and Sch. 1
Extended to Lakshadweep by Regulation 8 of 1965, s. 3 and Sch.
Extended to Sikkim (w.e.f. 20-0-1976): vide Notifin. No. S. O. 3392, dated 3-9-1976.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government makes rules requiring passports for entry. Police and Customs officers have powers of arrest for contravention. The Central Government can direct removal of persons who entered in contravention of rules.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate having jurisdiction in the case (Section 4(2))

act_identification.act_title: THE ALIGARH MUSLIM UNIVERSITY ACT, 1920

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to [1]*** incorporate a teaching and residential Muslim University at Aligarh, and to dissolve the Societies registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (21 of 1860), which are respectively known as the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh, and the Muslim University Association, and to transfer to and vest in the said University all properties and rights of the said Societies and of the Muslim University Foundation Committee;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to incorporate a teaching and residential Muslim University at Aligarh. It also aims to dissolve the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College and the Muslim University Association, transferring their properties and rights to the newly established University.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that its commencement date will be appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act and in Statutes made thereunder.

key_sections.title: Incorporation.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Aligarh Muslim University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

key_sections.title: Dissolution of the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, Aligarh, and the Muslim University Association, and transfer of all property to the University.
key_sections.description: Mandates the dissolution of the specified societies and the transfer of all their properties, rights, and liabilities to the University.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the various powers of the University, including instruction, research, granting degrees, establishing institutions, and managing its affairs.

key_sections.title: University open to all persons.
key_sections.description: Declares the University open to all persons regardless of sex, race, religion, creed, caste, or class, with a proviso for religious instruction.

key_sections.title: The Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President as the Visitor of the University and defines the Visitor's powers of inspection, inquiry, and annulment of proceedings.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the principal officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and others.

key_sections.title: The Vice-Chancellor.
key_sections.description: Describes the appointment, powers, and functions of the Vice-Chancellor as the principal executive and academic officer.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities governing the University, such as the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council.

key_sections.title: The Court.
key_sections.description: Defines the constitution and powers of the Court as the supreme governing body of the University, including its power to make Statutes.

key_sections.title: The Executive Council.
key_sections.description: Identifies the Executive Council as the principal executive body of the University and states its constitution, term, powers, and duties are prescribed by Statutes.

key_sections.title: Power to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Details the matters for which Statutes may provide, covering the constitution of authorities, appointments, conditions of service, and other administrative aspects.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Ordinances may provide, including admission, courses of study, examinations, fees, and student residence.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employee.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that employees shall be appointed on written contracts and provides for arbitration in case of disputes.

powers_conferred: To provide for instruction in such branches of learning as the University may think fit, and to make provision for research and for the advancement and dissemination of knowledge (University)
To promote Oriental and Islamic studies and give instruction in Muslim theology and religion and to impart moral and physical training (University)
To promote the study of the religions, civilisation and culture of India (University)
To promote especially the educational and cultural advancement of the Muslims of India (University)
To hold examinations and to grant diplomas or certificates to, and confer degrees and other academic distinctions on, persons (University)
To confer honorary degrees or other distinctions (University)
To institute professorships, readerships, lectureships and other teaching or academic posts (University)
To institute and award fellowships (including travelling fellowships), scholarships, studentships, exhibitions and prizes (University)
To institute and maintain Halls for the students of the University (University)
To establish within a radius of twenty-five kilometres of the University Mosque such Special Centres, Specialised Laboratories or other units for research and instruction (University)
To demand and receive such fees and other charges (University)
To supervise and control the residence and to regulate the discipline of students (University)
To make special arrangements in respect of the residence, discipline and teaching of women students (University)
To create administrative, ministerial and other posts and to make appointments thereto (University)
To regulate and enforce discipline among the employees of the University (University)
To acquire, hold, manage and dispose of property, movable or immovable (University)
To borrow, with the approval of the Central Government, on the security of the property of the University, money (University)
To declare a Department of Studies to be an autonomous Department (University)
To cause an inspection to be made of the University, its buildings, laboratories, and equipment, and of any institution maintained by the University (Visitor)
To cause an inquiry to be made in respect of any matter connected with the administration or finances of the University (Visitor)
To issue directions to the Executive Council (Visitor)
To annul any proceeding of the University which is not in conformity with this Act, the Statutes or the Ordinances (Visitor)
To make Statutes and to amend or repeal the same (Court)
To consider Ordinances (Court)
To consider and pass resolutions on the annual report, the annual accounts and the financial estimates (Court)
To elect such persons to serve on the authorities of the University and to appoint such officers (Court)
To make Ordinances (Executive Council)
To appoint examiners (Executive Council)
To prepare the Annual Report of the University (Executive Council)
To prepare the annual accounts and balance sheet of the University (Executive Council)
To make Regulations consistent with this Act, the Statutes and the Ordinances (Authorities of the University)
To appoint the date of commencement of the Act (Central Government)
To audit the annual accounts and balance sheet of the University (Comptroller and Auditor-General of India)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Vice-Chancellor. The Court elects the Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor, and Honorary Treasurer. The Executive Council appoints examiners, Registrar, and Finance Officer.

applies_to: all persons (including the teachers and taught) of either sex and of whatever race, religion, creed, caste or class
exemptions: religious instruction being given in the manner prescribed by the Ordinances to those who have consented to receive it
special_provisions: special arrangements in respect of the residence, discipline and teaching of women students

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Court has the power to make Statutes. The Executive Council has the power to make Ordinances. The authorities of the University have the power to make Regulations.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor has powers of inspection, inquiry, issuing directions, and annulling proceedings. The Executive Council is the principal executive body. Disputes between the University and employees/students are referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No suit shall lie in any Civil Court in respect of matters decided by the Tribunal of Arbitration.

schedules_summary.description: Refers to the Statutes of the University, to be found in the University Calendar.

act_identification.act_title: THE MAINTENANCE ORDERS ENFORCEMENT ACT, 1921

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to facilitate the enforcement in [2][India] of Maintenance Orders made [3][[4]*** in [5][reciprocating territories]], [6]*** and vice versa; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to facilitate the enforcement of maintenance orders made in India in reciprocating territories and vice versa, ensuring that such orders can be legally recognized and enforced across different jurisdictions.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Court of summary jurisdiction', 'dependants', 'maintenance order', and 'reciprocating territory'.

key_sections.title: Declaration of reciprocal arrangements.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to declare countries or territories as reciprocating territories if legal provisions exist for enforcing Indian maintenance orders there.

key_sections.title: Registration in India of maintenance orders made in the reciprocating territories.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for registering maintenance orders made in reciprocating territories within Indian Courts (High Court or Court of summary jurisdiction).

key_sections.title: Transmission of maintenance orders made in India.
key_sections.description: Details the procedure for transmitting maintenance orders made by Indian Courts to reciprocating territories for enforcement.

key_sections.title: Power of summary Courts to make provisional maintenance orders against persons resident in reciprocating territories.
key_sections.description: Grants Courts of summary jurisdiction the power to make provisional maintenance orders against persons residing in reciprocating territories, subject to confirmation by a competent Court in that territory.

key_sections.title: Power of Court of summary jurisdiction to confirm maintenance order made out of India.
key_sections.description: Describes the process by which a Court of summary jurisdiction in India can confirm provisional maintenance orders made in reciprocating territories.

key_sections.title: Enforcement of maintenance orders.
key_sections.description: Specifies that registered or confirmed maintenance orders shall have the same force and effect as if originally obtained in the High Court or a Civil Court, and outlines the enforcement powers of Courts.

key_sections.title: Rule-making power.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying into effect the purposes of the Act, including for the levy of costs and charges.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To declare reciprocal arrangements (Section 3).
Central Government: To send copies of maintenance orders for registration in India (Section 4).
Central Government: To receive and transmit certified copies of maintenance orders to reciprocating territories (Section 5).
Central Government: To receive and transmit depositions and provisional orders to reciprocating territories (Section 6).
Central Government: To send documents for confirmation of provisional orders made out of India (Section 7).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying into effect the purposes of the Act (Section 12).
Court in India: To register maintenance orders made in reciprocating territories (Section 4).
Court in India: To send certified copies of maintenance orders to the Central Government for transmission (Section 5).
Court of summary jurisdiction in India: To make provisional maintenance orders against persons resident in reciprocating territories (Section 6).
Court of summary jurisdiction in India: To take further evidence for provisional orders remitted from reciprocating territories (Section 6).
Court of summary jurisdiction in India: To rescind provisional orders (Section 6).
Court of summary jurisdiction in India: To vary or rescind confirmed orders (Section 6).
Court of summary jurisdiction in India: To confirm provisional maintenance orders made in reciprocating territories (Section 7).
Court of summary jurisdiction in India: To vary or rescind confirmed orders (Section 7).
High Court or Civil Court: To enforce registered maintenance orders (Section 8).
Court of summary jurisdiction: To enforce registered or confirmed maintenance orders (Section 8).
Court: To direct payment of charges for transmission of sums awarded as maintenance (Section 9).

applies_to: Persons against whom maintenance orders are made
Courts in India
Reciprocating territories
exemptions: State of Jammu and Kashmir (as per Section 1(2) of the Act)
Orders of affiliation (excluded from 'maintenance order' definition)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Maintenance orders made in reciprocating territories are registered in Indian Courts (High Court or Court of summary jurisdiction) and then enforced as if they were original Indian orders. Similarly, Indian maintenance orders are transmitted to reciprocating territories for enforcement. Provisional orders can be made by Indian Courts against residents of reciprocating territories, subject to confirmation, and vice versa.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court, Court of summary jurisdiction (Court of a Chief Presidency Magistrate or of a District Magistrate)

act_identification.act_title: THE DELHI UNIVERSITY ACT, 1922

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to establish and incorporate a [1][teaching and affiliating University] at Delhi; It is hereby enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University at Delhi. It aims to provide for instruction, research, and the advancement and dissemination of knowledge, and to cultivate and promote arts, science and other branches of learning.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: The University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the University of Delhi as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the various powers of the University, including providing instruction, granting degrees, conducting research, and managing colleges.

key_sections.title: Territorial exercise of powers.
key_sections.description: Defines the geographical limits of the University's powers, primarily the Union territory of Delhi, with some exceptions.

key_sections.title: University open to all classes, castes and creeds.
key_sections.description: Ensures the University is open to all persons without discrimination based on sex, race, creed, caste or class.

key_sections.title: Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor and outlines their powers of inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the various officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and Registrar.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities of the University, such as the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council.

key_sections.title: The Court.
key_sections.description: Declares the Court as the supreme authority of the University with review powers over the Executive Council and Academic Council.

key_sections.title: The Executive Council.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Executive Council as the executive body of the University.

key_sections.title: The Academic Council.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Academic Council as the academic body responsible for standards of instruction, education, and examination.

key_sections.title: Statutes.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Statutes may provide, including constitution of bodies, appointment of officers, and conditions for colleges.

key_sections.title: Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Ordinances may provide, including student admission, courses of study, fees, and examinations.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of officers and teachers.
key_sections.description: Mandates written contracts for salaried officers and teachers and provides for arbitration of disputes.

powers_conferred: University: provide instruction, research, advance knowledge, hold examinations, grant degrees, confer honorary degrees, grant diplomas, co-operate with other Universities, institute teaching posts, appoint teachers, institute fellowships, scholarships, exhibitions and prizes, maintain colleges and halls, admit colleges to privileges, demand fees, supervise student residence and discipline, make grants for extramural teaching, make special arrangements for women students, acquire, hold, manage and dispose of property, borrow money, create administrative and ministerial posts, make appointments.
Visitor: cause inspection and inquiry, address Vice-Chancellor with results, issue directions, annul proceedings of the University.
Court: review acts of the Executive Council and Academic Council, exercise all powers of the University not otherwise provided.
Executive Council: make, amend or repeal Statutes, make Ordinances, manage colleges and institutions, supervise and inspect colleges.
Academic Council: control and general regulation of standards of instruction, education and examination, advise the Executive Council on academic matters.
Chancellor: decide disputes regarding constitution of University authorities and bodies.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Chancellor (for disputes), Executive Council (for arbitration tribunal members), Visitor (for umpire in arbitration).

applies_to: persons of either sex and of whatever race, creed, caste or class
students of the University
non-collegiate women students
teachers in educational institutions
external candidates
exemptions: educational institution beyond the limits of the Union territory of Delhi (unless directed by Central Government)
educational institutions within the Union territory of Delhi associated with any other University (with exceptions for specific institutions like Indraprastha Vishwavidyalaya)
special_provisions: non-collegiate women students
teachers in educational institutions
students pursuing a course of study by correspondence
external candidates
special arrangements for women students
institutions situated outside India (if directed by Central Government)
educational institutions affiliated to the Indraprastha Vishwavidyalaya

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Executive Council (Statutes, Ordinances), Academic Council (proposes Ordinances), University authorities (Regulations), Visitor (approves Statutes, disallows Ordinances).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Inspection and inquiry by the Visitor, audit of accounts by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, dispute resolution by the Chancellor, arbitration for service disputes of officers and teachers.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Tribunal of Arbitration (for disputes between University and officers/teachers).

schedules_summary.description: Refers to the Statutes of the University, which are to be found in the University Calendar.

act_identification.act_title: THE BOILERS ACT, 1923

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to steam-boilers. WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to steam-boilers; It is hereby enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to steam-boilers. The Act provides for the registration, inspection, and certification of boilers and boiler components, and establishes authorities for their regulation and safety.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its geographical extent, and the date of its commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as "accident", "boiler", "owner", "steam pipe", and various authorities.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of use of unregistered or uncertificated boiler.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the use of boilers that are not registered or do not have a valid certificate, or are used at higher than permitted pressure.

key_sections.title: Registration.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for registration of boilers, including application, inspection, and issuance of a certificate for use.

key_sections.title: Renewal of certificate.
key_sections.description: Details the conditions under which a boiler certificate ceases to be in force and the procedure for its renewal.

key_sections.title: Alterations and renewals to boilers.
key_sections.description: Requires written sanction from the Chief Inspector for any structural alteration, addition, or renewal to a registered boiler, with an exception for supervision by a Competent Person.

key_sections.title: Report of accidents.
key_sections.description: Mandates the owner or person in charge to report accidents involving boilers or boiler components to the Inspector within twenty-four hours.

key_sections.title: Penalties for illegal use of boiler.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for illegal use of boilers, including using unregistered or uncertified boilers, or operating them at excessive pressure.

key_sections.title: Central Boilers Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Central Boilers Board to exercise powers related to regulations under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Boilers Board the power to make regulations concerning the material, design, construction, inspection, and certification of boilers and boiler components.

key_sections.title: Exemptions. Power to suspend in case of emergency.
key_sections.description: Provides the State Government with powers to exempt certain boilers or classes of boilers from the operation of the Act under specified conditions or in emergencies.

powers_conferred: State Government: Power to limit extent of the Act (Section 4)
State Government: Power to appoint Chief Inspector, Deputy Chief Inspectors, and Inspectors (Section 5)
State Government: Power to make rules (Section 29)
State Government: Power to exempt boilers or classes of boilers (Section 34)
Central Government: Power to appoint Technical Adviser (Section 4A)
Central Government: Power to make rules (Section 28A)
Central Government: Power to give directions to State Governments (Section 31A)
Central Boilers Board: Power to make regulations (Section 28)
Chief Inspector: Power to register boilers and assign register numbers (Section 7)
Chief Inspector: Power to order issue of certificates (Section 7)
Chief Inspector: Power to withdraw or revoke certificates or provisional orders (Section 11)
Chief Inspector: Power to sanction structural alterations, additions, or renewals to boilers (Section 12)
Inspector: Power to fix date for examination of boilers (Section 7)
Inspector: Power to inspect boilers (Section 7)
Inspector: Power to grant provisional orders (Section 9)
Inspector: Powers of entry for inspection or examination (Section 17)
Competent Authority: Power to issue Welders certificate (Section 4B)
Inspecting Authority: Power to carry out inspection during manufacture and erection (Section 4D, Section 4E)
Inspecting Authority: Power to issue certificate of inspection (Section 4D, Section 4E)
Competent Person: Power to inspect and renew certificates (Section 8)
Competent Person: Power to supervise structural alteration, addition or renewal (Section 12)
Competent Person: Power to approve repairs (Section 4F)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Minor penalties (Section 22) for refusing to surrender provisional order, produce certificate, make over certificate, or report accident, with penalty up to five thousand rupees. Penalties for illegal use of boiler (Section 23) including using unregistered/uncertified boilers, using at higher pressure, using transferred boiler without reporting, or failing to mark register number, with penalty up to one lakh rupees and additional one thousand rupees per day for continuing contravention. Other penalties (Section 24) for making alterations without sanction, tampering with safety valve, or allowing person inside boiler without disconnection, punishable with imprisonment up to two years or fine up to one lakh rupees, or both. Penalty for tampering with register mark (Section 25) for removing/altering mark (penalty up to one lakh rupees) or fraudulently marking (imprisonment up to two years or fine up to one lakh rupees or both). Penalty for breach of rules (Section 30) with penalty up to one thousand rupees for first contravention and up to one lakh rupees for subsequent contravention.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government appoints Chief Inspector, Deputy Chief Inspectors, and Inspectors. Central Government appoints Technical Adviser.

applies_to: Owners of boilers
Persons undertaking welding work connected with boilers
Manufacturers of boilers or boiler components
Persons repairing boilers or boiler components
Boilers and boiler components belonging to the Government
exemptions: Locomotive boilers belonging to or under the control of the railways
Any boiler or boiler component in any vessel propelled wholly or in part by the agency of steam
Any boiler or boiler component belonging to, or under the control of, the Army, Navy or Air Force
Any boiler appertaining to a sterilizer disinfector used in hospitals or nursing homes, if the boiler does not exceed one hundred liters in capacity
Any specified area from the operation of all or any specified provisions of this Act, by State Government notification
Any boilers or classes or types of boilers used exclusively for the heating of buildings or the supply of hot water, by State Government notification
Any boilers or steam-pipes or any class of boilers or steam-pipes or any boiler or steam-pipe from the operation of all or any of the provisions of this Act, by State Government in case of emergency
Any boiler or boiler components in the whole or any part of the State, by State Government notification, based on material, design, construction, and need for rapid industrialisation
special_provisions: Extends to the whole of India.
State Government may, by notification, exclude any specified area from the operation of all or any specified provisions of this Act.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Boilers Board (for regulations), Central Government (for rules), State Government (for rules).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a system of registration, inspection, and certification of boilers and boiler components by Inspectors and Competent Persons. It includes provisions for reporting accidents, appeals against orders, adjudication of penalties, and trials of offences. The Central Government can issue directions to State Governments for implementation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate of the first class

act_identification.act_title: THE EMPLOYEE’S COMPENSATION ACT, 1923

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the payment by certain classes of employers to their [2][employees] of compensation for injury by accident. WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the payment by certain classes of employers to their 3[employees] of compensation for injury by accident; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the payment of compensation by certain classes of employers to their employees for injuries sustained by accident arising out of and in the course of their employment. It also covers occupational diseases and sets out procedures for claiming and distributing compensation.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Commissioner', 'compensation', 'dependant', 'employee', 'employer', and types of disablement.

key_sections.title: Employer’s liability for compensation.
key_sections.description: Establishes the employer's liability to pay compensation for personal injury by accident or occupational disease arising out of and in the course of employment, with certain provisos.

key_sections.title: Amount of compensation.
key_sections.description: Details the calculation of compensation amounts for death, permanent total disablement, permanent partial disablement, and temporary disablement.

key_sections.title: Compensation to be paid when due and penalty for default.
key_sections.description: Mandates timely payment of compensation and prescribes penalties, including interest and additional sums, for default.

key_sections.title: Distribution of compensation.
key_sections.description: Governs the process of depositing compensation with the Commissioner and its distribution to dependants, especially in cases of death or legal disability.

key_sections.title: Notice and claim.
key_sections.description: Outlines requirements for giving notice of accidents and filing claims for compensation, including time limits and exceptions.

key_sections.title: Contracting.
key_sections.description: Addresses the liability of a principal employer for compensation to employees of a contractor, and the right to indemnity.

key_sections.title: Insolvency of employer.
key_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of employer's rights against insurers to the employee in case of employer's insolvency.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for various failures by employers, such as not maintaining records, sending statements/reports, or informing employees of their rights.

key_sections.title: Reference to Commissioners.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that questions regarding compensation liability, amount, or duration are to be settled by a Commissioner, excluding Civil Court jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Commissioners.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to appoint Commissioners for Workmen’s Compensation and defines their qualifications.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Allows appeals to the High Court against specific orders of a Commissioner, provided a substantial question of law is involved.

key_sections.title: Power of the State Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering various procedural and administrative matters.

powers_conferred: State Government: make rules (Section 32), appoint Commissioners (Section 20), require employers to maintain notice-books (Section 10(3)), direct returns as to compensation (Section 16), add employments to Schedule III (Section 3(3)).

Central Government: specify monthly wages (Section 4(1B)), enhance compensation amounts (Section 4 proviso), make rules for transfer of money to other countries (Section 35), add employments to Schedule III (Section 3(3)).

Commissioner: settle questions of liability/amount/duration of compensation (Section 19), require statements regarding fatal accidents (Section 10A), make awards for deficiency (Section 22A), exercise powers of a Civil Court (Section 23), recover arrears (Section 31), submit questions of law to High Court (Section 27), register agreements (Section 28), entertain claims with delayed notice/filing for sufficient cause (Section 10(1) proviso).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Employers are liable to pay simple interest at 12% per annum (or higher rate specified by Central Government) on compensation not paid within one month, and a further sum not exceeding 50% of the amount as penalty if there is no justification for delay (Section 4A). Penalties for failing to maintain a notice-book, send statements/reports/returns, or inform employees of their rights include a fine not less than fifty thousand rupees but which may extend to one lakh rupees (Section 18A).

related_acts: War Pensions and Detention Allowances (Mercantile Marine, etc.) Scheme, 1939
War Pensions and Detention Allowances (Indian Seamen, etc.)Scheme, 1941
Pensions (Navy, Army, Air Force and Mercantile Marine) Act, 1939 (2 & 3 Geo.)
War Pensions and Detention Allowances (Indian Seamen) Scheme, 1942
Working Journalists and Other Newspaper Employees (Conditions of Service) and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1955

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government has the power to appoint Commissioners for Workmen’s Compensation (Section 20(1)).

applies_to: certain classes of employers to their employees
employees as defined in Section 2(1)(dd) and Schedule II
masters and seamen (Section 15)
captains and other members of crew of aircrafts (Section 15A)
employees abroad of companies and motor vehicles (Section 15B)
exemptions: any person working in the capacity of a member of the Armed Forces of the Union (Section 2(1)(dd)(iii))
factories to which the Employees’ State Insurance Act, 1948 (34 of 1948), applies (Section 10B(3))
special_provisions: Extended to Goa, Daman and Diu by Reg. 12 of 1962, s. 3 and Sch. (w.e.f. 15-8-1963)
Extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963, s. 2 and Sch. I
Extended to Pondicherry by Reg. 7 of 1963, s. 3 and Sch. I
Extended to Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands by Reg. 8 of 1965, s. 3 and Sch.
Modified in its application to apprentices under the Apprentices Act, 1961 (52 of 1961) by s. 16
Special provisions relating to masters and seamen (Section 15)
Special provisions relating to captains and other members of crew of aircrafts (Section 15A)
Special provisions relating to employees abroad of companies and motor vehicles (Section 15B)
Uttar Pradesh Amendment to section 22 regarding filing of applications by authorized officers and clubbing of applications.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The State Government (Section 32) and the Central Government (Section 35) have the power to make rules.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Commissioners settle disputes regarding compensation (Section 19) and can recover amounts as arrears of land-revenue (Section 31). Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance by employers (Section 18A).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court for appeals (Section 30). Civil Courts do not have jurisdiction over matters to be settled by a Commissioner (Section 19(2)).

schedules_summary.description: Lists injuries deemed to result in permanent total disablement (Part I) and permanent partial disablement (Part II), along with the percentage of loss of earning capacity for each injury.
Lists categories of persons who are included in the definition of 'employees' for the purposes of this Act, covering various occupations and industries.
Lists occupational diseases (Parts A, B, and C) that are deemed to be injuries by accident under the Act, along with the employments where there is a risk of contracting them.
Provides factors for working out the lump sum equivalent of compensation amounts in cases of permanent disablement and death, based on the employee's age.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN NAVAL ARMAMENT ACT, 1923

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States

act_overview.preamble: AN ACT to give effect *** to the Treaty for the Limitation of Naval Armament. WHEREAS it is expedient to give effect *** to the [Treaty for the Limitation of Naval Armament and for the Exchange of Information concerning Naval Construction signed in London on behalf of His Majesty on the twenty-fifth day of March, 1936]; It is hereby enacted as follows:
act_overview.purpose: The primary purpose of this Act is to implement the Treaty for the Limitation of Naval Armament and for the Exchange of Information concerning Naval Construction. It restricts the building, altering, arming, or equipping of vessels of war without a proper licence. The Act establishes procedures for licensing, seizure, forfeiture, and penalties to ensure compliance with these international obligations.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used within the Act, such as 'competent Court', 'ship', 'States', and 'the Treaty'.

key_sections.title: Restriction on building or equipping vessels of war.
key_sections.description: Prohibits persons from building, altering, arming, or equipping vessels of war, or despatching such ships, except under a licence granted by the Act.

key_sections.title: Licences.
key_sections.description: Details the process for granting licences by the Central Government for activities restricted under Section 3, and conditions for such licences.

key_sections.title: Offences against the Act.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravening Section 3 or failing to comply with Section 4(3), including imprisonment and fine, and addresses liability for companies/corporations.

key_sections.title: Liability of ships to forfeiture.
key_sections.description: States that any ship built, altered, armed, or equipped as a vessel of war in contravention of Section 3 or similar laws, if found in the States, is liable to forfeiture.

key_sections.title: Seizure, detention and search of ships.
key_sections.description: Empowers specific officers (Magistrates, Armed Forces officers, customs/police officers) to seize and detain ships liable to forfeiture and outlines reporting requirements to the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Procedure in forfeiture of ships.
key_sections.description: Outlines the judicial procedure for applying for and ordering the forfeiture of ships, including notice to interested parties and powers of the Court.

key_sections.title: Special proof of relevant facts.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that questions regarding whether a ship is a vessel of war or adapted for such use shall be referred to and determined by the Central Government, whose decision is final.

key_sections.title: Penalties for proceeding to sea after seizure.
key_sections.description: Imposes penalties on the master, owner, and sender of a ship that proceeds to sea after being seized or detained under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to enter dock-yards, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to authorized persons to enter dock-yards and other places to make inquiries and search ships believed to be liable to forfeiture.

key_sections.title: Courts by which and conditions subject to which offences may be tried.
key_sections.description: Specifies the minimum court level for trying offences under the Act and requires a complaint made by or under authority from the Central Government.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Grant licences under Section 4.
Central Government: Appoint date of commencement under Section 1(3).
Central Government: Declare competent Courts for the purposes of this Act under Section 2(a).
Central Government: Require designs and particulars for licence applications or compliance under Section 4(2) and 4(3).
Central Government: Receive reports of ship seizures under Section 7(2).
Central Government: Order release or application for forfeiture of seized ships and make temporary disposal orders under Section 7(3).
Central Government: Direct the disposal of forfeited ships under Section 9.
Central Government: Determine questions regarding a ship being a vessel of war or its adaptation under Section 10.
Central Government: Authorize complaints for the trial of offences under Section 13.
Presidency Magistrate or Magistrate of the first class: Seize and detain ships liable to forfeiture under Section 7(1)(a).
Commissioned officer on full pay in the Armed Forces of the Union: Seize and detain ships liable to forfeiture under Section 7(1)(a).
Officer of customs or police officer (of designated rank): Seize and detain ships liable to forfeiture under Section 7(1)(b).
Officers empowered to seize and detain: Enter dock-yards, ship-yards, or other places, make inquiries, and search ships under Section 12(1).
Competent Court: Hear applications for forfeiture, pass orders of forfeiture, and make other orders regarding ships or sale proceeds under Section 8.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person contravening Section 3 or failing to comply with Section 4(3) is punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both. Directors and managers of companies/corporations are liable unless they prove lack of knowledge/consent. If a seized or detained ship proceeds to sea, the master is punishable with a fine up to one thousand rupees, and the owner and sender are likewise punishable unless they prove lack of knowledge/consent. If an officer is taken to sea, the owner and master are further liable for expenses and a daily fine up to one hundred rupees.

applies_to: Any person involved in building, altering, arming, or equipping vessels of war or despatching such ships.
Any ship built, altered, armed, or equipped as a vessel of war in the States or His Majesty’s Dominions in contravention of law.
special_provisions: The Act extends to the whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a licensing system for building/equipping vessels of war. Contraventions lead to seizure and detention of ships by designated officers (Magistrates, Armed Forces, customs, police), followed by judicial forfeiture proceedings in competent Courts. Penalties, including imprisonment and fines, are prescribed for offences. Officers also have powers to enter and search dock-yards.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court or such other Court having unlimited original civil jurisdiction as the Central Government may declare for forfeiture proceedings. Presidency Magistrate or Magistrate of the first class for trial of offences.

schedules_summary.description: The Schedule was repealed by the Indian Naval Armament (Amendment) Act, 1937 (2 of 1937), s. 6.

act_identification.act_title: THE OFFICIAL SECRETS ACT, 1923

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India and applies also to servants of the Government and to citizens of India outside India.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law [2]*** relating to official secrets. WHEREAS it is expedient that the law relating to official secrets [2]*** should be consolidated and amended; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: to consolidate and amend the law relating to official secrets.

key_definitions: communication of any sketch, plan, model, article, note or document

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its geographical reach, and to whom it applies.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'prohibited place' and 'munitions of war'.

key_sections.title: Penalties for spying.
key_sections.description: Outlines actions considered spying, such as approaching prohibited places or communicating secret information, and prescribes penalties.

key_sections.title: Communications with foreign agents to be evidence of commission of certain offences.
key_sections.description: Establishes that communication with foreign agents can be used as evidence in proceedings for spying offences.

key_sections.title: Wrongful communication, etc., of information.
key_sections.description: Defines offences related to the unauthorized communication, retention, or use of secret official information or documents.

key_sections.title: Unauthorised use of uniforms; falsification of reports, forgery, personation, and falsedocuments.
key_sections.description: Addresses offences involving the misuse of official uniforms, falsification of documents, personation, and related acts prejudicial to state safety.

key_sections.title: Duty of giving information as to commission of offences.
key_sections.description: Imposes a duty on individuals to provide information about offences under the Act to police officers or armed forces members upon demand.

key_sections.title: Attempts, incitements, etc.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that attempts to commit or abet the commission of an offence under the Act are punishable in the same manner as the offence itself.

key_sections.title: Penalty for harbouring spies.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for knowingly harbouring individuals who are about to commit or have committed spying offences.

key_sections.title: Search-warrants.
key_sections.description: Authorizes magistrates to issue search warrants for premises where offences under the Act are suspected to have been or are about to be committed.

key_sections.title: Restriction of trial of offences.
key_sections.description: Sets limitations on which courts can try offences under the Act and specifies conditions for taking cognizance of such offences.

key_sections.title: Exclusion of public from proceedings.
key_sections.description: Allows for the exclusion of the public from court proceedings if the publication of evidence would be prejudicial to the safety of the State.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Defines liability for offences committed by companies, extending responsibility to individuals in charge and officers under certain conditions.

powers_conferred: Central Government to declare places as 'prohibited places' by notification in the Official Gazette (Section 2(8)(c), (d)).
Central Government to confer powers of a Superintendent of Police for the purposes of this Act (Section 2(10)).
Presidency Magistrate, Magistrate of the first class, or Sub-divisional Magistrate to grant search-warrants (Section 11(1)).
Police officer not below the rank of Superintendent to issue written orders for search in cases of great emergency (Section 11(2)).
Inspector-General or Commissioner of Police to empower police officers to demand information (Section 8(1), 10(2)).
Appropriate Government to specially empower a Magistrate of the first class to try offences (Section 13(1)).
Appropriate Government to order or authorize complaints for taking cognizance of offences (Section 13(3)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties for spying (Section 3) range from imprisonment up to 3 years, or up to 14 years for offences related to defence establishments or secret official codes. Wrongful communication of information (Section 5), unauthorized use of uniforms/falsification (Section 6), interfering with officers (Section 7), failing to give information (Section 8), and harbouring spies (Section 10) are punishable with imprisonment up to 3 years, or with fine, or with both. Attempts and incitements (Section 9) carry the same punishment as the main offence.

repealed_acts: Repealing Act, 1927 (12 of 1927)

applies_to: whole of India
servants of the Government
citizens of India outside India

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement involves police officers, Superintendents of Police, and Magistrates. It includes powers of search and seizure through search-warrants issued by Magistrates or written orders by Superintendents in emergencies. Trials are conducted by empowered Magistrates or Courts of Session, with restrictions on cognizance requiring complaints from the appropriate Government. Public can be excluded from proceedings for national security reasons.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate of the first class specially empowered, District or Presidency Magistrate, Court of Session.

act_identification.act_title: THE MUSSALMAN WAKF ACT, 1923
act_identification.date_of_commencement: Section 1 came into force at once (05/08/1923); remaining provisions to come into force on such date as the State Government may appoint by notification.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India except the territories which immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make provision for the better management of wakf property and for ensuring the keeping and publication of proper accounts in respect of such properties WHEAREAS it is expedient to make provision for the better management of wakf property and for ensuring the keeping and publication of proper accounts in respect of such properties;
act_overview.purpose: To make provision for the better management of wakf property and for ensuring the keeping and publication of proper accounts in respect of such properties.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, geographical extent, and commencement dates for its provisions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'benefit', 'Court', 'Mutwalli', 'prescribed', and 'wakf'.

key_sections.title: Obligation to furnish particulars relating to wakf.
key_sections.description: Requires mutwallis to furnish detailed statements of wakf property particulars to the Court within specified periods.

key_sections.title: Publication of particulars and requisition of further particulars.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Court to publish furnished particulars and allows for requisition of further details or documents from mutwallis.

key_sections.title: Statement of accounts.
key_sections.description: Requires mutwallis to prepare and furnish annual statements of accounts to the Court, with provisions for extension of time.

key_sections.title: Audit of account.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that every statement of accounts must be audited by a certified auditor or a person authorized by the Court, depending on the wakf's income.

key_sections.title: Mutawalli entitled to pay cost of audit, etc., from wakf funds.
key_sections.description: Allows mutwallis to use wakf income to cover expenses incurred for furnishing particulars, documents, or audit costs as required by the Act.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for mutwallis who fail to furnish required statements or documents, or who provide false, misleading, untrue, or unaudited statements.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including specifying particulars, fees, forms, and audit procedures.

key_sections.title: Savings.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not affect other enactments for control of religious/charitable endowments and specifies cases where the Act does not apply, such as wakfs administered by official trustees or under court-approved schemes.

key_sections.title: Exemption.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to exempt specific wakfs or sections of the Mussalman community from the operation of the Act or any of its provisions.

powers_conferred: State Government: to direct commencement of provisions (S.1(4))
State Government: to designate Courts (S.2(b))
State Government: to make rules (S.11)
State Government: to exempt wakfs (S.13)
Court: to require mutwalli to furnish particulars (S.4(2))
Court: to extend time for furnishing accounts (S.5)
Court: to authorize auditors for certain wakfs (S.6(b))
Court: to permit inspection and copies of documents (S.9)
Mutwalli: to pay cost of audit and other expenses from wakf funds (S.7)

amended_acts: Bihar and Orissa Mussalman Wakf (Amendment) Act, 1926 (B. & O., 1 of 1926)
Mussalman Wakf, Bombay Public Trusts Registration and Parsi Public Trusts Registration (Amendment) Act, 1944 (Bombay 10 of 1944)
repealed_acts: Bengal Wakf Act, 1934 (Bengal 13 of 1934) (in its application to Bengal)
United Provinces Muslim Wakf Act, 1936 (U.P. 13 of 1936) (in part in United Provinces)
Wakf Act, 1954 (29 of 1954) (superseded this Act in general application)

applies_to: Mussalman Wakfs
Mutwallis of Mussalman Wakfs
exemptions: Wakfs where benefit is claimable by the creator or their family/descendants (S.2(e))
Wakfs administered by the Treasurer of Charitable Endowments, Administrator General, or Official Trustee (S.12(b)(i))
Wakfs administered by a receiver appointed by any Court or under a scheme settled/approved by any Court or authority (S.12(b)(ii))
Wakfs to which the Wakf Act, 1954 (29 of 1954) applies
Any wakf or wakfs created or administered for the benefit of any specified section of the Mussalman community, if exempted by State Government notification (S.13)
special_provisions: State Government may direct specific provisions to come into force in specified parts of a State (S.1(4))
State Government may exempt specific wakfs or sections of the Mussalman community from the Act (S.13)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Mutwallis are required to furnish particulars and accounts to the Court, which are subject to publication and audit. Non-compliance is subject to penalties.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Court of the District Judge or, within the limits of the ordinary original civil jurisdiction of a High Court, such Court, subordinate to the High Court, as the State Government may designate (S.2(b))

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN SOLDIERS (LITIGATION) ACT, 1925

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law to provide for the special protection in respect of civil and revenue litigation of Indian soldiers serving under special conditions. WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law to provide for the special protection in respect of civil and revenue litigation of Indian soldiers serving under special conditions; It is hereby enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to consolidate and amend the law to provide special protection for Indian soldiers in civil and revenue litigation. It addresses situations where soldiers are serving under special conditions, ensuring their legal interests are safeguarded.

key_definitions: decree or order of a Court

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's official name, its geographical application, and the date it came into force.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Court', 'Indian soldier', and 'proceeding'.

key_sections.title: Circumstances in which an Indian soldier shall be deemed to be serving under special conditions.
key_sections.description: Outlines the conditions under which an Indian soldier is considered to be serving under 'special conditions' or 'war conditions' for the purposes of this Act.

key_sections.title: Particulars to be furnished in plaints, applications or appeals to Court.
key_sections.description: Requires persons presenting legal documents to state if an adverse party is an Indian soldier serving under special conditions.

key_sections.title: Power of Collector to intervene in case of unrepresented Indian soldier.
key_sections.description: Grants the Collector the power to certify facts to the Court if an unrepresented Indian soldier is a party to a proceeding.

key_sections.title: Notice to be given in case of unrepresented Indian soldier.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Court to suspend proceedings and give notice to the prescribed authority if an unrepresented Indian soldier is a party, with certain provisos.

key_sections.title: Postponement of proceedings.
key_sections.description: Requires the Court to postpone proceedings for a soldier if the prescribed authority certifies it is necessary due to special conditions.

key_sections.title: Power to set aside decrees and orders, passed against an Indian soldier serving under war or special conditions.
key_sections.description: Allows a Court to set aside decrees or orders passed against an Indian soldier serving under special conditions, upon application.

key_sections.title: Modification of law of limitation where Indian soldier or his legal representative is a party.
key_sections.description: Excludes the period of service under special conditions from the computation of limitation periods for suits, appeals, or applications involving an Indian soldier.

key_sections.title: Rule making power.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for various matters related to the Act's implementation, including notices, postponement periods, and prescribed authorities.

key_sections.title: Power to apply the provisions of the Act to other persons in the service of the Government.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government (and State Government for State Public Services) to extend the Act's provisions to other classes of government servants.

Power of Court to suspend and postpone proceedings (Sections 6, 7, 9)
Power of Court to set aside decrees and orders passed against an Indian soldier (Section 10)
Power of Court to refer questions to prescribed authorities (Section 12)
Power of Central Government to specify tribunals or authorities (Section 2(a))
Power of Central Government to declare war conditions or specify places within India (Section 3)
