repealed_acts: Acts IX of 1918
Acts XII of 1924

applies_to: Indian soldiers
other class of persons in the service of Government (if notified)
special_provisions: Provisions regarding agricultural land and village immovable property in specific areas as notified by the Central Government (Section 11 proviso)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government (Section 13), and State Government for State Public Services (Section 14(2))
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through Courts, Collectors, and prescribed authorities by providing for postponement of proceedings, setting aside of decrees, and modification of limitation periods for Indian soldiers.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: A Court other than a Criminal Court, and includes any tribunal or authority specified by the Central Government empowered to receive evidence and determine rights and obligations.

act_identification.act_title: THE PROVIDENT FUNDS ACT, 1925

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble:
An Act to amend and consolidate the law relating to Government and other Provident Funds.
WHEARES it is expedient to amend and consolidate the law relating to Government and other
Provident Funds;
It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To amend and consolidate the law relating to Government and other Provident Funds.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'compulsory deposit', 'Provident Fund', and 'dependant'.

key_sections.title: Protection of compulsory deposits.
key_sections.description: Protects compulsory deposits in Government or Railway Provident Funds from assignment, charge, attachment, and claims by insolvency officials.

key_sections.title: Provisions regarding re-payments.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for making payments from Provident Funds to subscribers, depositors, or their dependants/nominees upon the sum becoming payable.

key_sections.title: Rights of nominees.
key_sections.description: Establishes the rights of nominees to receive sums from Provident Funds upon the death of the subscriber or depositor, overriding other laws or dispositions.

key_sections.title: Power to make deductions.
key_sections.description: Allows for deductions from contributory Provident Funds for amounts due to the Government or Railway administration, subject to certain limits and conditions.

key_sections.title: Withholding or recovery of Government contributions in case of Central Government officers taking up, without prior permission, commercial employment within two years of their retirement.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which Government contributions to a contributory provident fund may be withheld or recovered from retired Central Government officers who take up commercial employment without permission.

key_sections.title: Protection for acts done in good faith.
key_sections.description: Grants immunity from legal proceedings for actions performed in good faith under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to apply the Act to other Provident Funds.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to extend the provisions of this Act to Provident Funds established by local authorities or specified institutions.

key_sections.title: Savings as to estates of soldiers.
key_sections.description: States that Sections 4 and 5 do not apply to money belonging to estates covered by the Regimental Debts Act, 1893.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint the date of commencement of the Act (Section 1(3)).
Central Government: To make rules (Section 6A(1)(d)).
Central Government: To grant or refuse permission for Central Government officers to take up commercial employment after retirement (Section 6A(3)).
Central Government: To declare non-entitlement to or direct refund of Government contributions (Section 6A(7)).
Central Government: To lay rules before Parliament (Section 6A(11)).
Appropriate Government: To direct the application of the Act to Provident Funds of local authorities (Section 8(1)).
Appropriate Government: To direct the application of the Act to Provident Funds of institutions specified in the Schedule (Section 8(2)).
Appropriate Government: To add names of public institutions to the Schedule (Section 8(3)).
Officer whose duty is to make payment: To pay sums or balances from Provident Funds (Section 4(1)).
Authority specified in the rules of the fund: To direct deductions from contributory Provident Funds (Section 6).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Withholding or recovery of Government contributions from Central Government officers who take up commercial employment without prior permission or breach conditions (Section 6A(7)).

related_acts: Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948 (9 of 1948)
State Bank of India Act, 1955 (23 of 1955)
Unit Trust of India Act, 1963 (52 of 1963)

applies_to: Government Provident Funds
Railway Provident Funds
Provident Funds established by local authorities (if notified by appropriate Government)
Provident Funds established for the benefit of employees of institutions listed in the Schedule (if notified by appropriate Government)
Central Government officers (for provisions related to commercial employment after retirement)
exemptions: Estates for the administration of which the Regimental Debts Act, 1893 applies (from Sections 4 and 5)
Central Government officers appointed under a contract of service for a specified term (from definition of 'Central Government officer' in Section 6A(1)(a))
special_provisions: Provisions for Central Government officers regarding commercial employment after retirement (Section 6A).
Provisions for application to local authorities and scheduled institutions (Section 8).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Payment by designated officers (Section 4); withholding or recovery of Government contributions by Central Government (Section 6A(7), 6A(8)); decisions by competent Civil Courts (Section 4(1) Proviso (ii)).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil, Revenue or Criminal Court (Section 3); competent Civil Court (Section 4(1) Proviso (ii)).

schedules_summary.description: Contains a list of various institutions (e.g., Pasteur Institute of India, Calcutta Improvement Tribunal, Indian Central Cotton Committee, Reserve Bank of India, Universities, Port Trusts, etc.) to whose Provident Funds the Act may be applied by the appropriate Government under Section 8(2).

act_identification.act_title: THE SIKH GURDWARAS (SUPPLEMENTARY) ACT, 1925

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to supplement, by legislation in the Indian Legislature, certain provisions of the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925, for the purposes hereinafter appearing; It is hereby enacted as follows:
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to supplement certain provisions of the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925. Specifically, it validates provisions of the said Act concerning the jurisdiction and procedure of the High Court.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Validation of certain provisions of Punjab Act 8 of 1925.
key_sections.description: Validates certain provisions of the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925 (referred to as Punjab Act 8 of 1925), particularly those affecting the jurisdiction or procedure of the High Court of Punjab.

key_sections.title: [Repealed].
key_sections.description: This section, which previously dealt with the amendment of section 12 of Punjab Act 8 of 1925, was repealed by the Repealing Act, 1938.

implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court of Punjab

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN CARRIAGE OF GOODS BY SEA ACT, 1925
act_identification.act_short_title: THE INDIAN CARRIAGE OF GOODS BY SEA ACT, 1925

act_overview.purpose: To amend the law with respect to the carriage of goods by sea and to establish the responsibilities, liabilities, rights and immunities attaching to carriers under bills of lading.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its geographical extent to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Application of Rules.
key_sections.description: States that the Rules set out in the Schedule shall apply to the carriage of goods by sea from any port in India to any other port.

key_sections.title: Absolute warranty of sea worthiness not to be implied in contracts to which Rules apply.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that no absolute undertaking of seaworthiness is implied in contracts to which the Rules apply.

key_sections.title: Statement as to application of Rules to be included in bills of lading.
key_sections.description: Requires bills of lading issued in India for contracts covered by the Rules to include an express statement of their application.

key_sections.title: Responsibilities and Liabilities - Carrier's duty to exercise due diligence
key_sections.description: Outlines the carrier's obligation to exercise due diligence to make the ship seaworthy, properly man, equip, and supply it, and make holds fit for goods.

key_sections.title: Responsibilities and Liabilities - Issuance of bill of lading
key_sections.description: Mandates the carrier to issue a bill of lading on demand, showing identification marks, quantity/weight, and apparent order/condition of goods.

key_sections.title: Responsibilities and Liabilities - Notice of loss or damage and time limit for suit
key_sections.description: Specifies requirements for giving notice of loss or damage and sets a one-year limitation period for bringing suit against the carrier.

key_sections.title: Responsibilities and Liabilities - Clauses relieving carrier from liability
key_sections.description: Declares any clause in a contract of carriage relieving the carrier from liability for negligence or lessening liability contrary to the Rules as null and void.

key_sections.title: Rights and Immunities - Causes for which carrier is not responsible
key_sections.description: Lists various causes of loss or damage for which neither the carrier nor the ship shall be responsible, such as act of God, act of war, perils of the sea, etc.

key_sections.title: Rights and Immunities - Limitation of liability
key_sections.description: Sets limits on the carrier's liability for loss or damage to goods, based on Special Drawing Rights per package/unit or per kilogram, unless value is declared.

key_sections.title: Special Conditions
key_sections.description: Allows carriers and shippers to agree on special terms for particular goods, provided no bill of lading is issued and the agreement is embodied in a non-negotiable receipt.

powers_conferred: Central Government to notify ports in the Official Gazette for specific application of Article VI (Section 5(b))
Central Government to appoint the day of commencement of the Rules by notification in the Official Gazette (Section 7(2))

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government to appoint the day of commencement of the Rules (Section 7(2))

applies_to: carriage of goods by sea in ships carrying goods from any port in India to any other port whether in or outside India
contracts of carriage covered by a bill of lading or any similar document of title
exemptions: charterparties (unless bills of lading are issued under them)
goods carried in sailing ships (subject to modification of Article VI)
bulk cargoes (subject to modification of Rules 4 and 5 of Article III)
contracts for the carriage of goods by sea before 01/01/1926
ordinary commercial shipments (for special conditions under Article VI)
special_provisions: Extension to Goa, Daman and Diu, Pondicherry, and Lakshadweep
Modification of Article VI for carriage of goods from a port in India to a port in Ceylon as notified by the Central Government

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for notifying ports and commencement date)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Liability discharged unless suit is brought within one year after delivery of goods or the date when goods should have been delivered.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the 'RULES RELATING TO BILLS OF LADING', which are divided into nine Articles (I-IX). These Articles define key terms, outline the responsibilities and liabilities of carriers, specify rights and immunities, and detail special conditions for the carriage of goods by sea.

act_identification.act_title: THE MADRAS, BENGAL AND BOMBAY CHILDREN (SUPPLEMENTARY) ACT, 1925
act_identification.act_short_title: Madras, Bengal and Bombay Children (Supplementary) Act, 1925

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to supplement by legislation in the Indian Legislature certain provisions of the Madras Children Act, 1920 (Mad. Act IV of 1920.), of the Bengal Children Act, 1922 (Ben. Act II of 1922.), and of the Bombay Children Act, 1924 (Bom. Act XIII of 1924.), for the purpose hereinafter appearing; It is hereby enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to supplement certain provisions of the Madras Children Act, 1920, the Bengal Children Act, 1922, and the Bombay Children Act, 1924. Its primary objective is to validate the appellate and revisional jurisdiction conferred by these provincial Children Acts on the respective High Courts, ensuring their legal standing as if enacted by the Indian Legislature.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Madras, Bengal and Bombay Children (Supplementary) Act, 1925.

key_sections.title: Validation of certain provisions of Madras Children Act, 1920, Bengal Children Act, 1922, and Bombay Children Act, 1924.
key_sections.description: Validates the appellate and revisional jurisdiction conferred by the Madras Children Act, 1920, Bengal Children Act, 1922, and Bombay Children Act, 1924, on the High Courts of Judicature at Madras, Fort William in Bengal and Bombay, respectively, as if these Acts had been passed by the Indian Legislature.

implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Courts of Judicature at Madras, at Fort William in Bengal and at Bombay

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN SUCCESSION ACT, 1925

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Territory of India excluding the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate the law applicable to intestate and testamentary succession. WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate the law applicable to intestate and testamentary succession. It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to consolidate the law applicable to intestate and testamentary succession.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II.—Rules in cases of Intestates other than Parsis
CHAPTER III.—Of the Execution of unprivileged Wills
CHAPTER V.—Of the Attestation, Revocation, Alteration and Revival of Wills
CHAPTER VI.—Of the construction of Wills
CHAPTER VIII.—Of the vesting of Legacies
CHAPTER XII.—Of Bequests with Directions as to Application or Enjoyment
CHAPTER XIII.—Of Bequests to an Executor
CHAPTER XVII—Of the payment of liabilities in respect of the subject of a bequest.
CHAPTER XVIII.—Of Bequests of Things described in General Terms
CHAPTER XIX.—Of Bequests of the Interest or Produce of a Fund
CHAPTER XXI.—Of Legacies to creditors and Portioners
CHAPTER XXIII.—Of Gifts in Contemplation of Death
REPRESENTATIVE TITLE TO PROPERTY OF DECEASED ON SUCCESSION
PROBATE, LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION AND ADMINISTRATION OF ASSETS OF DECEASED
CHAPTER I.—Of Grant of Probate and Letters of Administration
CHAPTER III.—Alteration and Revocation of Grants
CHAPTER IV.—Of the Practice in granting and revoking Probates and Letters of Administration
CHAPTER V.—Of Executors of their own Wrong
CHAPTER VI.—Of the Powers of an Executor or Administrator
CHAPTER VII.—Of the Duties of an Executor or Administrator
CHAPTER VIII.—Of assent to a legacy by Executor or Administrator
CHAPTER IX,—Of the Payment and Apportionment of Annuities
CHAPTER X.—Of the Investment of Funds to Provide for Legacies
CHAPTER XL.—Of the Produce and Interest of Legacies
CHAPTER XII.—Of the Refunding of Legacies
CHAPTER XIII.—Of the Liability of an Executor or Administrator for Devastation

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Law regulating succession to deceased person’s immoveable and moveable property, respectively.
key_sections.description: Defines how succession to immoveable and moveable property is regulated based on domicile.

key_sections.title: Acquisition of new domicile.
key_sections.description: Explains the conditions under which a person acquires a new domicile.

key_sections.title: Application of Part.
key_sections.description: Specifies the applicability of the Part concerning intestate succession, including exemptions.

key_sections.title: As to what property deceased considered to have died intestate.
key_sections.description: Defines when a person is deemed to have died intestate regarding their property.

key_sections.title: Where intestate has left widow and lineal descendants, or widow and kindred only, or widow and no kindred.
key_sections.description: Outlines the distribution of property when an intestate leaves a widow and various combinations of lineal descendants or kindred.

key_sections.title: General principles relating to intestate succession.
key_sections.description: Establishes general principles for intestate succession among Parsis.

key_sections.title: Application of certain provisions of Part to a class of wills made by Hindus, etc.
key_sections.description: Specifies which provisions of Part VI apply to wills and codicils made by Hindus, Buddhists, Sikhs, or Jainas.

key_sections.title: Person capable of making wills.
key_sections.description: Defines who is capable of making a will, including conditions of sound mind and age.

key_sections.title: Execution of unprivileged wills.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the rules for the execution of unprivileged wills, including signing and attestation requirements.

key_sections.title: Privileged wills.
key_sections.description: Defines privileged wills and who can make them (soldiers, airmen, mariners).

key_sections.title: Revocation of will by testator’s marriage.
key_sections.description: States that a will is generally revoked by the testator's marriage, with an exception for powers of appointment.

key_sections.title: Bequest to person not in existence at testator's death subject to prior bequest.
key_sections.description: Declares certain bequests to persons not in existence at the testator's death as void unless they comprise the whole remaining interest.

key_sections.title: Rule against perpetuity.
key_sections.description: Establishes the rule against perpetuities, limiting the delay in vesting of bequeathed property.

key_sections.title: Bequest to religious or charitable uses.
key_sections.description: Sets conditions for bequests to religious or charitable uses, especially when the testator has close relatives.

key_sections.title: Property transferable by gift made in contemplation of death.
key_sections.description: Defines gifts made in contemplation of death (donatio mortis causa) and their conditions.

key_sections.title: Character and property of executor or administrator as such.
key_sections.description: States that the executor or administrator is the legal representative and that the deceased's property vests in them.

key_sections.title: Right as executor or legatee when established.
key_sections.description: Requires probate or letters of administration to establish rights as an executor or legatee in court, with exceptions.

key_sections.title: Probate only to appointed executor.
key_sections.description: Specifies that probate can only be granted to an executor appointed by the will, either expressly or by implication.

key_sections.title: Revocation or annulment for just cause.
key_sections.description: Outlines the conditions under which a grant of probate or letters of administration may be revoked or annulled for just cause.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of District Judge in granting and revoking probates, etc.
key_sections.description: Confers jurisdiction on the District Judge for granting and revoking probates and letters of administration within their district.

key_sections.title: Power of executor or administrator to dispose of property.
key_sections.description: Grants power to executors and administrators to dispose of the deceased's property, subject to certain restrictions for specific communities.

key_sections.title: Inventory and account.
key_sections.description: Mandates executors and administrators to exhibit an inventory and account of the estate to the court.

key_sections.title: Restriction on grant of certificates under this part.
key_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on the grant of succession certificates for certain debts or securities.

powers_conferred: State Government: To exempt any race, sect or tribe from operation of Act (Section 3). To appoint public curators (Section 210). To make rules for companies to be granted probate/administration (Section 223, 236). To invest inferior courts with District Judge powers (Section 388).

District Judge: To inquire into succession claims (Section 193). To appoint curators (Section 195). To authorize curators (Section 196). To grant and revoke probates/letters of administration (Section 264). To order production of testamentary papers (Section 267). To interfere for protection of property (Section 269). To examine petitioner on oath, require evidence, issue citations (Section 283). To grant succession certificates (Section 371). To require security from certificate grantee (Section 375). To extend/amend certificates (Section 376, 378).

High Court: To appoint delegates of District Judge (Section 265). Concurrent jurisdiction with District Judge (Section 300). To suspend, remove, discharge executor/administrator (Section 301). To give directions to executor/administrator (Section 302). To prescribe form for inventory/account (Section 317). To authorize securities for investment (Section 148, 341).

Executor/Administrator: To dispose of property (Section 307). To incur expenditure for property management (Section 308). To sue/be sued (Section 305, 306). To collect property and debts (Section 319). To assent to legacies (Section 332).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Punishment for false averment in petition or declaration under Section 193 of the Indian Penal Code (Section 282, 372(2)). Punishment for intentionally omitting to comply with requisition for inventory/account under Section 176 of the Indian Penal Code (Section 317). Punishment for intentionally false inventory/account under Section 193 of the Indian Penal Code (Section 317). Punishment for wilful omission to deliver up revoked probate/letters of administration (fine up to 1000 rupees or imprisonment up to 3 months, or both) (Section 296(2)). Punishment for wilful omission to deliver up superseded/invalid certificates (fine up to 1000 rupees or imprisonment up to 3 months, or both) (Section 389(2)).

repealed_acts: Indian Succession Act, 1865 (10 of 1865)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: District Judge appoints curators. High Court appoints District Delegates. State Government appoints public curators.

applies_to: General application to intestate and testamentary succession.
Specific provisions apply to Hindus, Buddhists, Sikhs, Jainas.
Specific provisions for Parsis.
Indian Christians.
exemptions: State Government can exempt any race, sect or tribe from certain provisions (Section 3).
Part II (Domicile) does not apply if deceased was Hindu, Muhammadan, Buddhist, Sikh or Jaina (Section 4).

Part III (Marriage) does not apply to marriages contracted before 1st January, 1866, or to marriages where one or both parties professed Hindu, Muhammadan, Buddhist, Sikh or Jaina religion (Section 20(2)).

Part IV (Consanguinity) does not apply to any will made or intestacy occurring before 1st January, 1866, or to intestate or testamentary succession to the property of any Hindu, Muhammadan, Buddhist, Sikh, Jaina or Parsi (Section 23).
Part V (Intestate Succession) does not apply to any intestacy occurring before 1st January, 1866, or to the property of any Hindu, Muhammadan, Buddhist, Sikh or Jaina (Section 29(1)).
Chapter II of Part V does not apply to Parsis (Section 31).

Section 33A does not apply to Indian Christians, children or grandchildren of male Indian Christians, or persons professing Hindu, Buddhist, Sikh or Jaina religion whose succession is regulated by the Special Marriage Act, 1872 (Section 33A(5)).

Part VI (Testamentary Succession) does not apply to testamentary succession to the property of any Muhammadan nor, save as provided by section 57, to testamentary succession to the property of any Hindu, Buddhist, Sikh or Jaina; nor shall they apply to any will made before 1st January, 1866 (Section 58(1)).
Section 118 (Bequest to religious or charitable uses) does not apply to a Parsi (Proviso to Section 118).
Section 324 (Application of moveable property to payment of debts) does not apply where the deceased was a Hindu, Muhammadan, Buddhist, Sikh or Jaina or an exempted person (Section 324(3)).
Section 345 (Investment of residue bequeathed for life) does not apply if the deceased was a Hindu, Muhammadan, Buddhist, Sikh or Jaina or an exempted person (Section 345(2)).

Section 269 (District Judge to interfere for protection of property) does not apply when the deceased is a Hindu, Muhammadan, Buddhist, Sikh or Jaina or an exempted person, nor shall it apply to any part of the property of an Indian Christian who has died intestate (Section 269(2)).
special_provisions: Special rules for Parsi intestates (Chapter III of Part V, Sections 50-56).
Special mode of acquiring domicile in India (Section 11).
Special provision where intestate has left widow and no lineal descendants (Section 33A).
Provisions of Part VI applicable to certain wills and codicils made by Hindus, etc. (Section 57).
State amendments for Kerala and Karnataka regarding specific sections.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: State Government (for company conditions, public curators, inferior courts). High Court (for investment securities, notice publication, creditor notices, inventory/account forms).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced through applications to District Courts for probate, letters of administration, and succession certificates; involving summary proceedings and regular suits.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District Judge, High Court, District Delegates, and inferior courts invested with the powers of a District Judge.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the Table of Consanguinity for computing degrees of kindred.
Contains Part I: Order of next-of-kin in case of Parsi intestates referred to in Section 54, and Part II: Order of next-of-kin in case of Parsi intestates referred to in Section 55.
Lists the provisions of Part VI (Testamentary Succession) applicable to certain wills and codicils made by Hindus, Buddhists, Sikhs, or Jainas, along with restrictions and modifications.
Provides the form for a certificate issued by the High Court or District Judge regarding probate or letters of administration.
Provides the form for a caveat against the grant of probate or administration.
Provides the form for a grant of probate.
Provides the form for letters of administration.
Provides the forms for succession certificates and extended certificates.
Indicates enactments that were repealed.

act_identification.act_title: THE TRADE UNIONS ACT, 1926

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the registration of Trade Unions and in certain respects to define the law relating to registered Trade Unions ***. WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the registration of Trade Unions and in certain respects to define the law relating to registered Trade Unions ***; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the registration of Trade Unions. It also defines the law relating to registered Trade Unions in certain respects, covering their rights, liabilities, and operational procedures.

chapter_titles: RIGHTS AND LIABILITIES OF REGISTERED TRADE UNIONS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides for the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'appropriate Government', 'executive', 'office-bearer', 'Registrar', 'trade dispute', and 'Trade Union'.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Registrars.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to appoint Registrars, Additional, and Deputy Registrars of Trade Unions.

key_sections.title: Mode of registration.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for registration of a Trade Union, including minimum membership requirements for workmen's unions.

key_sections.title: Application for registration.
key_sections.description: Specifies the particulars required in an application for registration of a Trade Union.

key_sections.title: Provisions to be contained in the rules of a Trade Union.
key_sections.description: Details the mandatory provisions that must be included in the rules of a Trade Union for it to be eligible for registration.

key_sections.title: Registration.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Registrar to register a Trade Union upon satisfaction of compliance with the Act's requirements.

key_sections.title: Certificate of registration.
key_sections.description: Requires the Registrar to issue a certificate of registration, which serves as conclusive evidence of due registration.

key_sections.title: Cancellation of registration.
key_sections.description: Lays down the grounds and procedure for the withdrawal or cancellation of a Trade Union's registration certificate by the Registrar.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Provides for an appeal mechanism against the Registrar's refusal to register or cancellation of registration, specifying the appellate courts.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of registered Trade Unions.
key_sections.description: Confers corporate status on registered Trade Unions, granting them perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire property and sue/be sued.

key_sections.title: Objects on which general funds may be spent.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the specific objects on which the general funds of a registered Trade Union may be lawfully spent.

key_sections.title: Constitution of a separate fund for political purposes.
key_sections.description: Allows a registered Trade Union to constitute a separate fund for political purposes, detailing the permissible objects for such expenditure.

key_sections.title: Criminal conspiracy in trade disputes.
key_sections.description: Grants immunity to office-bearers and members of registered Trade Unions from criminal conspiracy charges in trade disputes, unless the agreement is to commit an offence.

key_sections.title: Immunity from civil suit in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Provides immunity to registered Trade Unions and their office-bearers/members from civil suits in certain cases related to acts done in furtherance of a trade dispute.

key_sections.title: Disqualifications of office-bearers of Trade Unions.
key_sections.description: Specifies disqualifications for individuals to be chosen as or to remain office-bearers of Trade Unions, such as age and conviction for moral turpitude.

key_sections.title: Proportion of office-bearers to be connected with the industry.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the proportion of office-bearers who must be connected with the industry, with special provisions for unorganised sectors.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the appropriate Government to make regulations for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Failure to submit returns.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for failure to submit returns or for making false entries in required statements.

key_sections.title: Supplying false information regarding Trade Unions.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for supplying false information regarding Trade Unions with intent to deceive.

powers_conferred: Registrar: To appoint Additional and Deputy Registrars (S.3), to call for further information for registration (S.7), to refuse registration (S.7), to register Trade Unions (S.8), to issue certificate of registration (S.9), to withdraw or cancel registration (S.10), to divide funds on dissolution (S.27), to inspect documents (S.28(4)).

Appropriate Government: To appoint Registrars of Trade Unions (S.3), to appoint date of commencement (S.1(3)), to notify other objects on which general funds may be spent (S.15(k)), to make regulations (S.29).
Trade Union: To apply for registration (S.4), to change its name (S.23), to amalgamate with other Trade Unions (S.24), to constitute a separate fund for political purposes (S.16).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Failure to submit returns or making false entries in statements/rules (Section 31) punishable with fine up to fifty rupees (for continuing default, additional fine up to five rupees per week, aggregate not exceeding fifty rupees for S.31(1)) or up to five hundred rupees (for S.31(2)). Supplying false information regarding Trade Unions with intent to deceive (Section 32) punishable with fine up to two hundred rupees.

authorities_established: Additional and Deputy Registrars of Trade Unions
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The appropriate Government has the power to appoint the Registrar of Trade Unions and Additional and Deputy Registrars of Trade Unions.

applies_to: Trade Unions
Registered Trade Unions
Workmen
Employers
exemptions: Any agreement between partners as to their own business (S.2 Proviso (i))
Any agreement between an employer and those employed by him as to such employment (S.2 Proviso (ii))
Any agreement in consideration of the sale of the goodwill of a business or of instruction in any profession, trade or handicraft (S.2 Proviso (iii))
Registered Trade Unions are exempt from the application of The Societies Registration Act, 1860, The Co-operative Societies Act, 1912, and The Companies Act, 1956 (S.14).

Amended in its application to Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.
Special provisions for the State of Jammu and Kashmir (S.16(2), S.21A(3), S.9 State Amendment).
Special provisions for Ladakh (UT) (S.9 State Amendment).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The appropriate Government has the power to make regulations for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is primarily through the Registrar of Trade Unions, who handles registration, cancellation, and inspection of documents. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance. Appeals against the Registrar's decisions can be made to specified courts. In Maharashtra, the Industrial Court handles certain disputes.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court, Labour Court or Industrial Tribunal, Court not inferior to an additional or assistant Judge of a principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction (for appeals); Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class (for offences); Industrial Court constituted under the Bombay Industrial Relations Act, 1946 (for certain disputes in Maharashtra).

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN FOREST ACT, 1927

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States. It applies to the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in the States of Bihar, Bombay, Coorg, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh, Orissa, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal; but the Government of any State may by notification in the Official Gazette bring this Act into force in the whole or any specified part of that State to which this Act extends and where it is not in force.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate the law relating to forests, the transit of forest-produce and the duty leviable on timber and other forest-produce; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To consolidate the law relating to forests, the transit of forest-produce and the duty leviable on timber and other forest-produce.

chapter_titles: OF THE CONTROL OVER FORESTS AND LANDS NOT BEING THE PROPERTY OF GOVERNMENT
OF THE DUTY ON TIMBER AND OTHER FOREST-PRODUCE
OF THE CONTROL OF TIMBER AND OTHER FOREST-PRODUCE IN TRANSIT
OF THE COLLECTION OF DRIFT AND STRANDED TIMBER

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title and the geographical extent of the Act's application.

key_sections.title: Interpretation clause.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to reserve forests.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government power to constitute forest-land or waste-land as reserved forests.

key_sections.title: Notification by State Government.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for the State Government to issue notifications for constituting reserved forests and appointing a Forest Settlement-officer.

key_sections.title: Notification declaring forest reserved.
key_sections.description: Details the conditions under which the State Government shall publish a notification declaring a forest as reserved.

key_sections.title: Acts prohibited in such forests.
key_sections.description: Lists acts prohibited in reserved forests and prescribes penalties for their contravention.

key_sections.title: Formation of village-forests.
key_sections.description: Allows the State Government to assign rights over reserved forests to village-communities, forming village-forests.

key_sections.title: Protected forests.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to declare forest-land or waste-land as protected forests.

key_sections.title: Protection of forests for special purposes.
key_sections.description: Enables the State Government to regulate or prohibit certain activities in forests for specific protective purposes.

key_sections.title: Power to impose duty on timber and other forest-produce.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to levy duty on timber and other forest-produce.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules to regulate transit of forest produce.
key_sections.description: Vests control of timber and forest-produce in transit with the State Government and allows it to make rules for regulation.

key_sections.title: Seizure of property liable to confiscation.
key_sections.description: Authorizes Forest-officers or Police-officers to seize property believed to be involved in a forest-offence.

key_sections.title: Power to compound offences and impose penalties.
key_sections.description: Empowers Forest-officers to accept compensation for certain forest-offences and release seized property.

key_sections.title: Presumption that forest-produce belongs to Government.
key_sections.description: Establishes a presumption of Government ownership for forest-produce in legal proceedings under the Act.

key_sections.title: Recovery of money due to Government.
key_sections.description: Provides for the recovery of money due to the Government under the Act as arrears of land-revenue.

powers_conferred: State Government: To constitute reserved forests (S.3), issue notifications (S.4, S.20, S.29, S.30), make rules (S.5, S.16, S.28, S.32, S.41, S.51, S.76), declare forests no longer reserved (S.27), regulate/prohibit activities in forests (S.35), assume management of forests (S.36), apply Act provisions to lands (S.38), invest Forest-officers with powers (S.72), empower Forest-officers to compound offences (S.68).
Central Government: To levy duty on timber and forest-produce (S.39), make rules for timber movement across customs frontiers (S.41A).

Forest Settlement-officer: To inquire into and determine rights (S.7), exercise powers of a Civil Court (S.8), acquire land (S.11), pass orders on claims (S.12), record claims (S.13, S.14), ensure continued exercise of rights (S.15), commute rights (S.16).

Forest-officer: To stop ways and water-courses (S.25), seize property liable to confiscation (S.52), release seized property on bond (S.53), arrest without warrant (S.64), release arrested persons on bond (S.65), prevent commission of forest-offences (S.66), accept compensation for offences and release property (S.68).

Magistrate: To take measures for arrest and trial of offenders and disposal of property (S.54), order confiscation of property (S.57), direct sale of perishable property (S.58), try forest-offences summarily (S.67).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines various offences related to reserved forests (e.g., setting fire, felling trees, clearing land, hunting - S.26), protected forests (e.g., felling reserved trees, quarrying stone, clearing land, setting fire - S.33), breach of transit rules (S.42), counterfeiting marks or altering boundary-marks (S.63), and general breach of rules (S.77). Penalties generally include imprisonment for terms ranging from one month to two years, fines ranging from two hundred to five hundred rupees (with provisions for higher fines in state amendments), or both, in addition to compensation for damage. Double penalties may be inflicted in certain circumstances (S.42). Wrongful seizure by officers is also punishable (S.62). Failure to assist Forest-officers is an offence (S.79).

repealed_acts: Enactments listed in The Schedule (which is repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1948)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government appoints Forest-officers, Forest Settlement-officers, officers to hear appeals, and members of the Forest Court.

applies_to: Whole of India except the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States.
Territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in the States of Bihar, Bombay, Coorg, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh, Orissa, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.

Any forest-land or waste-land which is the property of Government, or over which the Government has proprietary rights, or to the whole or any part of the forest-produce of which the Government is entitled.
Village-community (for village-forests).
Owner of any land (for protection of forests at their request).
exemptions: Territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States.
Any class of timber from the provisions of section 45 (by State Government notification).
special_provisions: The Government of any State may by notification in the Official Gazette bring this Act into force in the whole or any specified part of that State to which this Act extends and where it is not in force (S.1(3)).

If inquiry and record for protected forests would take too long, endangering Government rights, the State Government may declare land a protected forest, but without abridging existing rights (S.29(3) Proviso).
State Government may continue to levy duties lawfully levied before the commencement of the Constitution, subject to non-discrimination (S.39(4)).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: State Government (for various matters including reserved forests, village-forests, protected forests, transit of forest-produce, collection of drift timber, and general provisions); Central Government (for duty on timber and forest-produce, and movements of timber across customs frontiers).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out by Forest-officers and Police-officers through powers of seizure, arrest, and prevention of offences. Magistrates have jurisdiction to try offences, dispose of seized property, and order confiscation. Offences can be compounded by empowered Forest-officers. Money due to the Government is recoverable as arrears of land-revenue.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate having jurisdiction, Appellate Court, District Magistrate or Magistrate of the first class (for summary trials), Civil Courts (for claims to drift timber), Forest Court (for appeals).

schedules_summary.description: Lists enactments repealed by the Act (this Schedule itself was later repealed).

act_identification.act_title: THE SALE OF GOODS ACT, 1930

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to define and amend the law relating to the sale of goods; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to define and amend the law relating to the sale of goods. It establishes the legal framework governing contracts of sale, including the formation of contracts, transfer of property and risk, performance of the contract, and remedies for breach.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II FORMATION OF THE CONTRACT
CHAPTER III EFFECTS OF THE CONTRACT
CHAPTER IV PERFORMANCE OF THE CONTRACT
CHAPTER V RIGHTS OF UNPAID SELLER AGAINST THE GOODS
CHAPTER VI SUITS FOR BREACH OF THE CONTRACT

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'buyer', 'seller', 'goods', 'delivery', and 'price'.

key_sections.title: Sale and agreement to sell.
key_sections.description: Distinguishes between a 'sale' (where property is transferred immediately) and an 'agreement to sell' (where transfer occurs in the future or upon conditions).

key_sections.title: Condition and warranty.
key_sections.description: Defines and differentiates between 'condition' (essential to the contract) and 'warranty' (collateral to the main purpose) in a contract of sale.

key_sections.title: Implied conditions as to quality or fitness.
key_sections.description: Outlines implied conditions regarding the quality or fitness of goods for a particular purpose, subject to certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Property passes when intended to pass.
key_sections.description: States that the property in specific or ascertained goods is transferred to the buyer at the time the parties intend it to be transferred, based on contract terms and conduct.

key_sections.title: Risk prima facie passes with property.
key_sections.description: Establishes the general rule that goods remain at the seller's risk until property is transferred to the buyer, after which they are at the buyer's risk.

key_sections.title: Sale by person not the owner.
key_sections.description: Deals with the principle that a non-owner cannot pass a better title than they possess, with exceptions for mercantile agents and estoppel.

key_sections.title: Duties of seller and buyer.
key_sections.description: Stipulates the fundamental duties of the seller to deliver goods and the buyer to accept and pay for them according to the contract.

key_sections.title: “Unpaid seller” defined.
key_sections.description: Defines an 'unpaid seller' as one who has not received the full price or whose negotiable instrument for payment has been dishonoured.

key_sections.title: Unpaid seller’s rights.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the rights of an unpaid seller against the goods, including lien, stoppage in transit, and re-sale.

key_sections.title: Right of stoppage in transit.
key_sections.description: Grants the unpaid seller the right to stop goods in transit if the buyer becomes insolvent, allowing the seller to resume possession.

key_sections.title: Suit for price.
key_sections.description: Allows the seller to sue the buyer for the price of goods if the property has passed and the buyer wrongfully neglects or refuses to pay.

key_sections.title: Damages for non-delivery.
key_sections.description: Enables the buyer to sue the seller for damages if the seller wrongfully neglects or refuses to deliver the goods.

key_sections.title: Specific performance.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Court to order specific performance of a contract to deliver specific or ascertained goods in certain circumstances.

powers_conferred: Court's power to direct specific performance (Section 58)
Seller's right to add or deduct taxes in contracts of sale (Section 64A)
Unpaid seller's rights including lien, stoppage in transit, and re-sale (Section 46)

applies_to: contracts for the sale of goods
persons who buy or agree to buy goods
persons who sell or agree to sell goods
exemptions: actionable claims and money
transaction in the form of a contract of sale which is intended to operate by way of mortgage, pledge, charge or other security

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through suits for breach of contract in a court of law.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Court

act_identification.act_title: THE HINDU GAINS OF LEARNING ACT, 1930
act_identification.act_short_title: The Hindu Gains of Learning Act, 1930

act_overview.preamble: An Act to remove doubt as to the rights of a member of a Hindu undivided family in property acquired by him by means of his learning. WHEREAS it is expedient to remove doubt, and to provide an uniform rule, as to the rights of a member of a Hindu undivided family in property acquired by him by means of his learning; It is hereby enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to clarify and establish a uniform rule regarding the rights of a member of a Hindu undivided family concerning property acquired through their learning. It ensures that such gains are considered the exclusive and separate property of the acquirer.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its geographical application.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'acquirer', 'gains of learning', and 'learning'.

key_sections.title: Gains of learning not to be held, not to be separate property of acquirer merely for certain reasons.
key_sections.description: Declares that gains of learning are the exclusive and separate property of the acquirer, regardless of whether learning was imparted by family members, or if the acquirer or family was maintained by joint funds during the learning period.

key_sections.title: Savings.
key_sections.description: Ensures that the Act does not affect past transfers of property, validity of actions, rights or liabilities from partitions, or ongoing legal proceedings that occurred before the commencement of the Act.

applies_to: a member of a Hindu undivided family
special_provisions: extended in its application to Dadra and Nagar Haveli (w.e.f. 1-7-19651 by Reg. 6 of 1963, s. 2 and the First schedule and to the Union territory of Pondicherry by Act 26 of 1968, s. 3 and Sch.
made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN PARTNERSHIP ACT, 1932

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to define and amend the law relating to partnership; it is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act defines and amends the law relating to partnership. Its main objective is to provide a comprehensive legal framework for the formation, conduct, and dissolution of partnership firms.

chapter_titles: RELATIONS OF PARTNERS TO THIRD PARTIES

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application to the whole of India, and commencement dates for its provisions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms such as 'act of a firm', 'business', 'prescribed', and 'third party' for the purpose of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definition of “partnership”, “partner”, “firm” and “firm name”.
key_sections.description: Defines partnership as a relation between persons sharing profits of a business, and identifies partners, firm, and firm name.

key_sections.title: Partner to be agent of the firm.
key_sections.description: Establishes that a partner acts as an agent of the firm for business purposes.

key_sections.title: Liability of a partner for acts of the firm.
key_sections.description: States that every partner is jointly and severally liable for all acts of the firm done while they are a partner.

key_sections.title: Minors admitted to the benefits of partnership.
key_sections.description: Outlines the conditions under which a minor may be admitted to the benefits of a partnership and their rights and liabilities.

key_sections.title: Dissolution of a firm.
key_sections.description: Defines dissolution of a firm as the dissolution of partnership between all partners.

key_sections.title: Dissolution by the Court.
key_sections.description: Enumerates grounds on which a Court may order the dissolution of a firm at the suit of a partner.

key_sections.title: Mode of settlement of accounts between partners.
key_sections.description: Prescribes rules for settling accounts of a firm after dissolution, including payment of losses and distribution of assets.

key_sections.title: Application for registration.
key_sections.description: Details the process and requirements for applying for the registration of a firm, including required particulars and fees.

key_sections.title: Effect of non-registration.
key_sections.description: Specifies the legal disabilities and limitations on suits for firms that are not registered under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the State Government to make rules for prescribing fees, forms, and regulating procedures under the Act.

related_acts: Presidency Small Cause Courts Act, 1882 (15 of 1882)
Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887 (9 of 1887)

firms

firms or partners in firms which have no place of business in the territories to which this Act extends (Section 69(4)(a))
firms whose places of business are in areas exempted by notification under section 56 (Section 69(4)(a))
any suit or claim of set-off not exceeding one hundred rupees in value (Section 69(4)(b))
special_provisions: State Amendment for Goa, Daman and Diu (Sections 3, 57, 58, 59)
State Amendment for Uttarakhand (Sections 58, 67, 68)
State Amendment for Rajasthan (Section 58, Schedule I)
State Amendment for Karnataka (Section 59A, Schedule I)
State Amendment for Maharashtra (Section 59A-1, Section 69A)

State Amendment for Gujarat (Schedule I)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is primarily through the registration of firms by Registrars, penalties for false particulars, and legal proceedings in competent Courts for matters such as dissolution or rights enforcement.

schedules_summary.description: Specifies the maximum fees payable for various documents and acts under the Act, such as statements for registration, intimations, notices, applications, and inspections.

act_identification.act_title: THE MURSHIDABAD ESTATE ADMINISTRATION ACT, 1933

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except [the territories which, immediately before the 1st November 1956, were comprised in Part B States]

act_overview.purpose: The Act provides for the appointment of a Manager for the properties of the Nawab Bahadur of Murshidabad. Its objectives include defining the Manager's powers and duties, applying the estate's income and a monthly sum for debt settlement, and protecting the Nawab Bahadur from financial difficulties while ensuring the maintenance of his position and dignity.

key_definitions: issues and profits of the immoveable properties of the estate

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Immoveable properties of the estate', 'Manager', and 'Nawab Bahadur'.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Manager.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government of West Bengal to appoint an officer as Manager for the Murshidabad Estate properties and income.

key_sections.title: Effect of order under section 3.
key_sections.description: Outlines the legal consequences upon the appointment of a Manager, including barring of pending proceedings, immunity from suits, and restrictions on the Nawab Bahadur's property dealings.

key_sections.title: Application by Manager of sums received.
key_sections.description: Details how the Manager shall apply the received sums, including payments to the Nawab Bahadur, government dues, estate expenses, and debt settlement.

key_sections.title: Notice to claimants.
key_sections.description: Requires the Manager to publish a notice calling for claims against the Nawab Bahadur within a specified period.

key_sections.title: Debt not duly notified to be barred.
key_sections.description: States that debts not notified to the Manager within the prescribed time will be barred, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Determination of debts.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Manager to determine the principal and interest of debts and liabilities and to reduce interest rates.

key_sections.title: Power to inquire into consideration for leases, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants the Manager power to inquire into the sufficiency of consideration for certain transactions and to set aside or modify them.

key_sections.title: Scheme for settlement of debts.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Manager to prepare and submit a scheme for the settlement of determined debts and liabilities to the Board of Revenue.

key_sections.title: Power to order production of accounts, papers, etc., and evidence of title .
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Collector of Murshidabad to order production of documents and titles related to the estate and impose fines for non-compliance.

key_sections.title: Manager to be deemed a public servant.
key_sections.description: Declares the Manager to be a public servant within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board of Revenue, with State Government sanction, the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions.

powers_conferred: State Government of West Bengal: appoint Manager (Section 3)
State Government of West Bengal: fix monthly sum for Nawab Bahadur (Section 7)
State Government of West Bengal: sanction expenditure (Section 7)
State Government of West Bengal: make orders to facilitate restoration of properties (Section 26)
Manager: receive and recover rents, issues and profits (Section 6)
Manager: receive monthly sum from Government Treasury (Section 6)
Manager: apply sums received for payments and debt settlement (Section 7)
Manager: publish notice for claims (Section 8)
Manager: determine amount of debts and liabilities (Section 11)
Manager: inquire into consideration for leases and set aside/modify them (Section 12)
Manager: call for further particulars of claims (Section 15)
Manager: summon and enforce attendance of witnesses and compel production of documents (Section 16)
Manager: have same powers as Nawab Bahadur for realising rents (Section 19)
Manager: make settlement of properties and execute leases (Section 20)
Manager: enter into contracts and take action for estate benefit (Section 21)
Collector of Murshidabad: order production of accounts, papers, etc. (Section 18)
Collector of Murshidabad: punish non-compliance with fine (Section 18)
Collector of Murshidabad: cause delivery of property to Manager from mortgagee/vendee (Section 19)
Board of Revenue: approve scheme for settlement of debts (Section 14)
Board of Revenue: approve repairs and improvements (Section 7)
Board of Revenue: hear appeals against Manager's orders (Section 13, Section 18)
Board of Revenue: supervise and control Manager's orders/proceedings (Section 22)
Board of Revenue: make rules with State Government sanction (Section 28)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who refuses to comply with an order under sub-section (1) of Section 18 may be punished by the Collector of Murshidabad with fine not exceeding five hundred rupees. Fines imposed under this Act are recoverable as a public demand (Section 24).

related_acts: Government of India Act, 1935 (26 Geo. 5, e. 2.)
Indian Independence (Rights, Property and Liabilities) Order, 1947

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government of West Bengal has the power to appoint the Manager.

applies_to: Properties of the Nawab Bahadur of Murshidabad
Nawab Bahadur
exemptions: Debts due or liabilities incurred to the Government or to any local authority
Rent due to a superior landlord from the Nawab Bahadur as tenant of any property
special_provisions: The Act specifically applies to the Murshidabad Estate and the Nawab Bahadur of Murshidabad.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Board of Revenue, with the previous sanction of the State Government, has the power to make rules.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Manager is responsible for receiving and applying funds, determining debts, and managing properties. Appeals against Manager's orders lie with the Board of Revenue. Fines can be imposed by the Collector of Murshidabad and are recoverable as public demands. Manager's orders regarding leases, etc., have the force of a Civil Court decree.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil Courts are mentioned in relation to pending proceedings being barred and Manager's orders having the force of a decree. The Act does not explicitly name specific courts with jurisdiction for enforcement beyond this.

act_identification.act_title: THE RESERVE BANK OF INDIA ACT, 1934
act_identification.act_short_title: the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
act_identification.date_of_commencement: Section 1 came into force at once; Sections 2 to 19, 47, 50 to 52, 55 to 58 and 61 came into force on 01/01/1935; other sections on 01/04/1935.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to constitute a Reserve Bank for India to regulate the issue of Bank notes and the keeping of reserves with a view to securing monetary stability in [2][India] and generally to operate the currency and credit system of the country to its advantage; 3[AND WHEREAS it is essential to have a modern monetary policy framework to meet the challenge of an increasingly complex economy; AND WHEREAS the primary objective of the monetary policy is to maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth; AND WHEREAS the monetary policy framework in India shall be operated by the Reserve Bank of India;]
act_overview.purpose: To establish a Reserve Bank for India to regulate the issuance of bank notes, maintain monetary stability, and manage the currency and credit system. It also aims to create a modern monetary policy framework to ensure price stability while supporting economic growth, with the Reserve Bank of India operating this framework.

CHAPTER IIID: REGULATION OF TRANSACTIONS IN DERIVATIVES, MONEY MARKET INSTRUMENTS, SECURITIES, ETC.

National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development
business of a non-banking financial institution

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter V (Sections 58B to 58G) details penalties for various offenses. These include imprisonment up to three years and fines for wilfully making false statements or omitting material statements. Fines up to one lakh rupees (and further daily fines) are prescribed for failing to produce documents or furnish information. Contravention of Section 31 (issue of demand bills/notes) incurs a fine equal to the bill amount. Unauthorised disclosure of credit information (Section 45E) can lead to imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both. Contravention of NBFC registration requirements (Section 45-IA) carries imprisonment from one to five years and fines from one lakh to twenty-five lakh rupees. Auditors failing to comply with Bank directions (Section 45MA) face fines up to ten lakh rupees. Non-compliance with Company Law Board orders (Section 45QA) can result in imprisonment up to three years and daily fines. Receiving unauthorized deposits or issuing non-compliant advertisements can lead to imprisonment up to three years and fines up to twice the deposit amount. Contravention of Section 45S (deposits by unincorporated bodies) can lead to imprisonment up to two years and fines up to twice the deposit amount or two thousand rupees, whichever is more. General contraventions or defaults are punishable with fines up to one lakh rupees and further daily fines for continuing offenses. The Bank also has the power to impose fines on non-banking financial companies.

act_overview.purpose: To make better provision for the control of the manufacture, possession, use, operation, sale, import and export of aircraft.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.

act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws concerning the import, transport, storage, production, refining, and blending of petroleum. Its objective is to regulate these activities to ensure safety and control.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to amend the law relating to marriage and divorce among Parsis; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to amend the existing law concerning marriage and divorce specifically for Parsis. It aims to provide a comprehensive legal framework for Parsi marriages and their dissolution.

key_sections.title: Applicability of provisions of the Act.
