Any district with few Parsi inhabitants may be included within the jurisdiction of the Parsi Chief Matrimonial Court by the State Government.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the registration of marriages and divorces by appointed Registrars, the constitution of Parsi Matrimonial Courts (Chief and District) for hearing matrimonial suits, and the imposition of penalties for non-compliance with certain provisions. The High Court exercises superintendence and appellate jurisdiction over these Courts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Parsi Chief Matrimonial Courts, Parsi District Matrimonial Courts, High Court (for appeals and superintendence)

schedules_summary.description: Contains a table of prohibited degrees of consanguinity and affinity for Parsi marriages.
Provides the form for the Certificate of Marriage.

act_identification.act_title: THE PAYMENT OF WAGES ACT, 1936

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the payment of wages of certain classes to employed persons. WHEREAS it is expedient to regulate the payment of wages to certain classes of employed persons.
act_overview.purpose: To regulate the payment of wages to certain classes of employed persons, ensuring timely payment and controlling deductions from their wages.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical reach, effective date, and the categories of employment and wage limits to which it applies.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'employed person', 'employer', 'factory', 'industrial or other establishment', 'wages', etc.

key_sections.title: Responsibility for payment of wages.
key_sections.description: Assigns responsibility for wage payment to the employer and specifies who is responsible in different types of establishments like factories, industrial establishments, and railways.

key_sections.title: Time of payment of wages.
key_sections.description: Mandates the timeframes within which wages must be paid after the end of a wage-period, and for payment upon termination of employment.

key_sections.title: Wages to be paid in current coin or currency notes or by cheque or crediting in bank account.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the modes of wage payment, allowing for current coin, currency notes, cheque, or bank account credit, with provisions for government specification.

key_sections.title: Deductions which may be made from wages.
key_sections.description: Lists the only authorized deductions from wages, prohibiting any other deductions, and clarifies what constitutes a deduction.

key_sections.title: Fines.
key_sections.description: Regulates the imposition of fines on employed persons, including conditions for imposition, maximum limits, and application of fine proceeds.

key_sections.title: Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of Inspectors and outlines their powers to examine, inspect, search, supervise wage payments, and seize documents to ensure compliance with the Act.

key_sections.title: Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment of wages and penalty for malicious or vexatious claims.
key_sections.description: Establishes authorities to hear and decide claims regarding unauthorized deductions or delayed wage payments, and allows for compensation and penalties for malicious claims.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Grants the right to appeal against orders or directions made under Section 15 to specified courts, subject to certain conditions and monetary thresholds.

key_sections.title: Penalty for offences under the Act.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, primarily fines, for various contraventions of the Act's provisions by employers or other responsible persons, including enhanced penalties for repeat offenders.

key_sections.title: Rule-making power.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, including procedural rules, record maintenance, and other specific matters.

powers_conferred: Appropriate Government: extend provisions of the Act (Section 1(5)), exempt from time of payment of wages (Section 5(3)), specify industrial or other establishments (Section 2(ii)(h)), approve rules for deductions (Section 7(2)(ff), 7(2)(fff), 7(2)(i), 7(2)(ii), 7(2)(j), 7(2)(k), 7(2)(kk), 7(2)(kkk)), approve acts and omissions for fines (Section 8(1)), make rules regarding deductions for absence from duty (Section 9(2)), make rules regulating advances and loans (Section 12(b), 12A), impose conditions for deductions (Section 13), appoint Inspectors (Section 14(2), 14(3)), appoint authorities for claims (Section 15(1)), make rules to regulate procedure and for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act (Section 26).
Inspectors: make examination and inquiry, enter, inspect and search premises, supervise payment of wages, require production of records, seize documents (Section 14(4)).

Authorities appointed under section 15: hear and decide claims, direct refund of deducted amounts, direct payment of delayed wages, award compensation, impose penalties for malicious/vexatious claims (Section 15(3), 15(4)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for various contraventions. For violating sections related to wage payment, deductions, or fines (e.g., sections 5, 7-13), the penalty is a fine not less than one thousand five hundred rupees but which may extend to seven thousand five hundred rupees. For contravening sections like 4, 5(4), 6, 8(8), 10(2), or 25, the fine may extend to three thousand seven hundred fifty rupees. Failure to nominate a responsible person under section 3 can result in a fine up to three thousand rupees. Offences related to record keeping, furnishing information, or obstructing Inspectors carry fines not less than one thousand five hundred rupees but which may extend to seven thousand five hundred rupees. Repeat offenders face enhanced fines, and failure to pay wages by the fixed date incurs an additional daily fine.

authorities_established: Authorities to hear and decide claims (Section 15(1)): Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation, Regional Labour Commissioner, Assistant Labour Commissioner, presiding officer of any Labour Court or Industrial Tribunal, officer with experience as a Judge of a Civil Court or a Judicial Magistrate.
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Appropriate Government (for Inspectors and Section 15 authorities).

applies_to: Persons employed in any factory.
Persons employed upon any railway by a railway administration (otherwise than in a factory).
Persons employed (either directly or through a sub-contractor) by a person fulfilling a contract with a railway administration.
Persons employed in an industrial or other establishment specified in sub-clauses (a) to (g) of clause (ii) of section 2.
Any class of persons employed in any establishment or class of establishments specified by appropriate Government under sub-clause (h) of clause (ii) of section 2.
Employed persons whose wages for a wage period do not exceed twenty four thousand rupees per month or such other higher sum specified by the Central Government.
exemptions: Appropriate Government may exempt persons employed upon any railway (otherwise than in a factory) or daily-rated workers in the Public Works Department from Section 5 (Time of payment of wages) (Section 5(3)).
special_provisions: In relation to any establishment owned by the Central Government, extension of provisions requires concurrence of that Government (Proviso to Section 1(5)).
Specific payment deadlines for persons employed on a dock, wharf, jetty or in a mine (Proviso to Section 5(1)).
Specific payment deadlines for termination due to establishment closure (Proviso to Section 5(2)).
Consultation with Central Government for exemption orders concerning daily-rated workers in PWD (Proviso to Section 5(3)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Inspectors monitor compliance, conduct inquiries, and supervise wage payments (Section 14). Authorities appointed under Section 15 adjudicate claims for unpaid wages or illegal deductions. Penalties are prescribed for contraventions, enforced through courts (Section 20, 21). Appeals against decisions of authorities can be made to specified courts (Section 17).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Court of Small Causes (for appeals in Presidency-towns) (Section 17(1)). District Court (for appeals elsewhere) (Section 17(1)). High Court (for questions of law submitted by the appellate court) (Section 17(4)). Courts taking cognizance of offences under the Act (Section 21).

act_identification.act_title: THE AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE (GRADING AND MARKING) ACT, 1937
act_identification.act_short_title: The Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to establish a framework for the grading and marking of agricultural and other produce. It aims to ensure quality control and prevent misrepresentation in the trade of such articles. This is intended to protect consumers and serve the public interest by standardizing produce quality.

key_definitions: marked with a grade designation mark

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical extent.

key_sections.title: Explanations.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'agricultural produce', 'grade designation', and 'migraded'.

key_sections.title: Prescription of grade designations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for fixing grade designations, defining quality, specifying marks, and authorizing persons for marking, along with other related matters.

key_sections.title: Powers of entry, inspection and search.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to authorised officers of the Central or State Government to enter, inspect, and search premises for contraventions of the Act or rules.

key_sections.title: Powers of the authorised officer to seize agricultural produce.
key_sections.description: Authorises officers to seize and detain agricultural produce involved in or likely to be used in an offence under the Act.

key_sections.title: Penalty for unauthorised marking with grade designation mark.
key_sections.description: Prescribes a penalty for marking scheduled articles with a grade designation mark without proper authorization.

key_sections.title: Penalty for counterfeiting grade designation mark.
key_sections.description: Prescribes a penalty for counterfeiting a grade designation mark or possessing instruments for such counterfeiting.

key_sections.title: Penalty for selling migrated articles.
key_sections.description: Prescribes a penalty for selling scheduled articles that are 'migraded'.

key_sections.title: Power to prescribe compulsory grade designations in respect of certain articles.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to declare certain scheduled articles or classes of articles to be sold or distributed only with a grade designation mark, and prescribes a penalty for contravention.

key_sections.title: Adjudicating officer.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of an adjudicating officer to hold inquiries and impose penalties under sections 4, 5, 5A, and 5B.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Establishes an appeal mechanism against orders of the adjudicating officer to the Agricultural Marketing Adviser.

key_sections.title: Recovery.
key_sections.description: Specifies that unpaid penalties imposed under the Act shall be recovered as arrears of land revenue.

key_sections.title: Extension of application of Act.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to extend the application of the Act to articles not initially included in the Schedule.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, including fixing grade designations, defining quality, specifying marks, and authorizing persons/bodies to mark articles (Section 3).
Central Government: To declare compulsory grade designations for certain articles in the public interest or for consumer protection (Section 5B).
Central Government: To appoint adjudicating officers for determining and imposing penalties (Section 5C).
Central Government: To extend the application of the Act to articles not included in the Schedule (Section 6).

Officer of the Central Government or a State Government (gazetted rank or equivalent) authorised by the Central Government: To enter any premises, inspect, and search for agricultural produce if a contravention is believed (Section 3A).
Authorised officer: To seize and detain agricultural produce related to an offence under the Act (Section 3B).
Adjudicating officer: To summon and enforce attendance of persons, hold inquiry, and impose penalties (Section 5C).
Agricultural Marketing Adviser, Government of India: To hear and dispose of appeals against orders of the adjudicating officer (Section 5D).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for several offences: unauthorised marking with a grade designation mark (penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees under Section 4), counterfeiting a grade designation mark (penalty not exceeding fifteen lakh rupees under Section 5), selling migraded articles (penalty not exceeding three lakh rupees under Section 5A), and contravening provisions related to compulsory grade designations (penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees under Section 5B).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint adjudicating officers.

applies_to: agricultural produce
horticulture produce
articles of food or drink wholly or partly manufactured from such produce
fleeces and skins of animals
other produce as declared by the Central Government

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement involves powers of entry, inspection, search, and seizure by authorised officers. Penalties for contraventions are determined and imposed by an adjudicating officer, with an appeal mechanism to the Agricultural Marketing Adviser. Unpaid penalties are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

schedules_summary.description: Lists 63 specific articles of agricultural produce, horticulture, and other items to which the provisions of the Act apply, including fruits, vegetables, dairy produce, tobacco, coffee, oilseeds, spices, and various grains.

act_identification.act_title: THE ARYA MARRIAGE VALIDATION ACT, 1937

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India except [the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States] and applies also to citizens of India wherever they may be.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to recognise and remove doubts as to the validity of inter-marriages current among Arya Samajists. WHEREAS it is expedient to recognise and place beyond doubt the validity of inter-marriages of a class of Hindus known as Arya Samajists; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to legally recognize and validate marriages between individuals who are Arya Samajists. It aims to remove any doubts regarding the validity of such inter-marriages, specifically addressing concerns related to parties belonging to different castes, sub-castes, or having different religious backgrounds before marriage.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Establishes the official name of the Act and defines its geographical applicability and scope.

key_sections.title: Marriage between Arya Samajists not to be invalid.
key_sections.description: Declares that marriages between Arya Samajists are valid, irrespective of caste differences or prior religious affiliations, overriding Hindu Law, usage, or custom.

applies_to: Arya Samajists
citizens of India wherever they may be
exemptions: the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States

act_identification.act_title: THE MUSLIM PERSONAL LAW (SHARIAT) APPLICATION ACT, 1937
act_identification.act_short_title: THE MUSLIM PERSONAL LAW (SHARIAT) APPLICATION ACT, 1937

act_overview.preamble:
WHEREAS it is expedient to make provision for the application of the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat)
to Muslims***; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act makes provision for the application of the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) to Muslims in India. It aims to ensure that in matters such as intestate succession, marriage, divorce, maintenance, dower, guardianship, gifts, trusts, and wakfs, the rule of decision for Muslims shall be the Shariat, overriding any contrary custom or usage.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the official short title of the Act and specifies its geographical applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Application of Personal Law to Muslims.
key_sections.description: Mandates the application of Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) to Muslims for various personal matters, including succession, marriage, divorce, maintenance, and wakfs, overriding customs, with exceptions for agricultural land and certain endowments.

key_sections.title: Power to make a declaration.
key_sections.description: Allows a Muslim individual to declare their desire to obtain the benefit of the Act's provisions, extending its application to adoption, wills, and legacies for themselves and their descendants.

key_sections.title: Rule-making power.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including prescribing forms for declarations and fees.

key_sections.title: Repeals.
key_sections.description: Repeals specific provisions of several older Acts and Regulations that are inconsistent with the provisions of this Act.

powers_conferred: State Government: Power to make rules to carry into effect the purposes of this Act (Section 4)
Prescribed authority: To accept declarations under Section 3
Officer appointed by State Government: To hear appeals against refusal to accept a declaration (Section 3)

repealed_acts: Section 5 of THE MUSLIM PERSONAL LAW (SHARIAT) APPLICATION ACT, 1937 by the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 (8 of 1939)
Section 26 of the Bombay Regulation IV of 1827
Section 16 of the Madras Civil Courts Act, 1873 (3 of 1873)
Section 3 of the Oudh Laws Act, 1876 (18 of 1876)
Section 5 of the Punjab Laws Act, 1872 (4 of 1872)
Section 5 of the Central Provinces Laws Act, 1875 (20 of 1875)
Section 4 of the Ajmere Laws Regulation, 1877 (3 of 1877)
related_acts: Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 (8 of 1939)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government may appoint an officer to hear appeals regarding declarations (Section 3)

applies_to: Muslims
Declarant and all his minor children and their descendants (for benefits under Section 3)
exemptions: Questions relating to agricultural land (Section 2)
Charities and charitable institutions and charitable and religious endowments (from wakfs in Section 2)
Renoncants of the Union territory of Pondicherry
special_provisions: Substitution of a new section for section 2 for Kerala by Kerala Act 42 of 1963
Proviso for Pondicherry stating nothing in this Act shall apply to the Renoncants of the Union territory of Pondicherry
Act has been extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963
Act has been extended to the whole of the Union territory of Lakshadweep by Reg. 8 of 1965

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the application of Muslim Personal Law by courts and through administrative processes for declarations and rule-making by the State Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts applying the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat)

act_identification.act_title: THE INSURANCE ACT, 1938

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the business of insurance. WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to the business of insurance ; It is hereby enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to consolidate and amend the law relating to the business of insurance in India. It aims to regulate and govern various aspects of insurance operations, ensuring sound practices and protecting policyholders' interests.

chapter_titles: PART II: PROVISIONS APPLICABLE TO INSURERS
PART IIA: LIFE INSURANCE COUNCIL AND GENERAL INSURANCE COUNCIL AND COMMITTEES THEREOF
PART IIB: TARIFF ADVISORY COMMITTEE AND CONTROL OF TARIFF RATES
PART IIC: SOLVENCY MARGIN, ADVANCE PAYMENT OF PREMIUM AND RESTRICTIONS ON THE OPENING OF A NEW PLACE OF BUSINESS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Registration.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration for carrying on insurance business and outlines the registration process and conditions.

key_sections.title: Requirements as to capital.
key_sections.description: Sets minimum paid-up equity capital requirements for insurers.

key_sections.title: Separation of accounts and funds.
key_sections.description: Requires insurers to maintain separate accounts and funds for different classes of insurance business.

key_sections.title: Accounts and balance-sheet.
key_sections.description: Mandates the preparation of annual financial statements by insurers.

key_sections.title: Actuarial report and abstract.
key_sections.description: Requires life insurers to conduct annual actuarial investigations and submit reports.

key_sections.title: Investment of assets.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the manner and limits for investment of assets by insurers.

key_sections.title: Power of investigation and inspection by Authority.
key_sections.description: Grants the Authority powers to investigate and inspect the affairs of insurers and intermediaries.

key_sections.title: Power of the Authority to issue directions.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Authority to issue directions to insurers in the public interest or for policyholder protection.

key_sections.title: Assignment and transfer of insurance policies.
key_sections.description: Lays down rules for the assignment and transfer of insurance policies.

key_sections.title: Nomination by policyholder.
key_sections.description: Specifies procedures and effects of nomination by policyholders for policy proceeds.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of rebates.
key_sections.description: Prohibits offering or accepting rebates on insurance premiums.

key_sections.title: Appointment of insurance agents.
key_sections.description: Governs the appointment of insurance agents and lists disqualifications.

key_sections.title: Policy not be called in question on ground of misstatement after three years.
key_sections.description: Sets a time limit for insurers to question life insurance policies based on misstatements or fraud.

key_sections.title: Winding up by the Court.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for winding up insurance companies by the Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Sufficiency of assets.
key_sections.description: Requires insurers and re-insurers to maintain a specified solvency margin.

key_sections.title: No risk to be assumed unless premium is received in advance.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that no risk can be assumed without prior receipt of premium.

key_sections.title: Penalty for default in complying with, or act in contravention of, this Act.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for various defaults and contraventions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of Authority to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Authority power to make regulations to carry out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to apply provisions to Special Economic Zones (SEZs), exempt certain persons/insurers, sanction amalgamation schemes, make rules, exempt from certain requirements, publish summary of returns.

Authority (IRDAI): Appointment of Controller, permission for foreign insurance, registration of insurers, certification of soundness of terms, power to order revaluation, power of investigation and inspection, power to appoint staff, power to issue directions, approval for appointments/remuneration of managerial persons, power to remove managerial persons, power to appoint additional directors, further powers, power to issue directions regarding re-insurance treaties, power to prepare Scheme of Amalgamation, power to accept/decline transfer/assignment, power to specify percentages for re-insurance, power to constitute Advisory Committee, power to examine re-insurance treaties, power to adjudicate, power to make regulations, power to exempt.
Courts/Tribunal: Winding up, reduce contracts of insurance, order restoration of property or compensation.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties are prescribed for various contraventions including: insuring properties with foreign insurers without permission (up to five crore rupees); general defaults in complying with the Act, rules, regulations, directions, solvency margin, or re-insurance treaties (one lakh rupees per day or one crore rupees, whichever is less); carrying on insurance business without registration (up to twenty-five crore rupees and imprisonment up to ten years); failure to comply with investment provisions (up to twenty-five crore rupees); wrongfully obtaining or withholding property (up to one crore rupees); failure to comply with rural/social sector obligations or motor third-party risk requirements (up to twenty-five crore rupees); contravention of orders regarding removal of managerial persons (one lakh rupees per day or one crore rupees, whichever is less); unauthorized acting as or appointing insurance agents/intermediaries (up to ten thousand rupees for agent, up to one crore rupees for insurer/appointing person); failure to deliver documents/property to Administrator (ten thousand rupees per day or ten lakh rupees, whichever is less).

related_acts: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999 (41 of 1999)
Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (15 of 2002)
Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 (15 of 1992)
International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019

authorities_established: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Authority)
Executive Committee of the Life Insurance Council
Executive Committee of the General Insurance Council
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints Controller of Insurance. Authority appoints Investigating Officer, staff, additional directors, Administrator, and adjudicating officer. Executive Committees appoint their respective Secretaries.
regulatory_bodies: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Authority)

applies_to: Insurers carrying on insurance business in India
Indian insurance companies, statutory bodies, insurance co-operative societies, foreign companies engaged in re-insurance
Insurance agents, intermediaries, insurance intermediaries
Policy-holders
exemptions: Certain persons/insurers for specific business (by Central Government notification)
Any insurer from provisions of Act (by Central Government notification)
Any trade union registered under the Indian Trade Unions Act, 1926
Any provident fund to which the provisions of the Provident Funds Act, 1925, apply
Any insurance business carried on by the Central Government or a State Government or a Government company (if Central Government orders)
Any approved superannuation fund
Any fund for mutual benefit of Government servants or pensioners
Any mutual or provident insurance society of Government or railway servants exempted from Provident Insurance Societies Act, 1912
Any fund in existence in the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu on 20th December, 1961
International Financial Services Centre
special_provisions: Central Government can apply provisions with exceptions/modifications to Special Economic Zones.
Specific provisions for insurers incorporated outside India regarding filing particulars and keeping books.
Provisions applicable to State Governments and Government companies for general insurance business.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government and the Authority (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through investigation and inspection by the Authority, power to issue directions, removal of managerial persons, search and seizure, imposition of penalties for contraventions, adjudication by the Authority, and recovery of penalties as arrears of land revenue. Winding up of insurance companies is handled by the Tribunal, and courts have powers to order restoration of property or compensation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction, High Court, National Company Law Tribunal (Tribunal), National Company Law Appellate Tribunal, Securities Appellate Tribunal.

schedules_summary.description: Contains rules for the valuation of liabilities of an insurer in insolvency or liquidation, specifying methods and basis for calculation by an actuary approved by the Court, considering the purpose of valuation, interest rates, mortality/sickness rates, and court directions.

act_identification.act_title: THE MANOEUVRES FIELD FIRING AND ARTILLERY PRACTICE ACT, 1938
act_identification.act_short_title: Manoeuvres, Field Firing and Artillery Practice Act, 1938

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to provide facilities for military manoeuvres and for field firing and artillery practice; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to provide facilities for military manoeuvres and for field firing and artillery practice. It outlines the powers exercisable by military forces during such activities, establishes a compensation mechanism for damages, and defines offences related to obstruction.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical extent.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to authorise manoeuvres.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to authorize military manoeuvres in specified areas for a limited period, with prior notice.

key_sections.title: Powers exercisable for purposes of maneuvers.
key_sections.description: Details the powers of military forces during manoeuvres, including passing over land, encampment, constructing temporary works, and water supply, with certain restrictions on sacred places and private properties.

key_sections.title: Right to compensation for damage caused by manoeuvres.
key_sections.description: Establishes the right to compensation from Defence Estimates for damage to person or property or interference with rights due to manoeuvres.

key_sections.title: Method of assessing compensation.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for assessing and disbursing compensation, including the role of Revenue Officers and a commission for appeals.

key_sections.title: Offences.
key_sections.description: Defines offences related to obstructing manoeuvres or unauthorized entry/interference and prescribes penalties.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to authorise field firing and artillery practice.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to define areas for field firing and artillery practice and authorize such practices with prior notice.

key_sections.title: Powers exercisable for purposes of field firing and artillery practice.
key_sections.description: Details the powers of forces during field firing and artillery practice, including the use of lethal missiles and declaring danger zones, with provisions for warning and exclusion of persons/animals.

key_sections.title: Compensation.
key_sections.description: Extends compensation provisions of sections 5 and 6 to field firing and artillery practice, including compensation for exclusion from danger zones and loss of employment/crop deterioration.

key_sections.title: Offences.
key_sections.description: Defines offences related to obstructing field firing/artillery practice or unauthorized entry/interference and prescribes penalties.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules for publishing notices, regulating land use, and governing compensation procedures.

powers_conferred: State Government to authorise military manoeuvres (Section 2)
State Government to authorise field firing and artillery practice (Section 9)
State Government to make rules (Section 13)
Military forces to pass over, encamp, construct military works, execute manoeuvres, and supply water (Section 3)
Forces engaged in field firing or artillery practice to carry out practice with lethal missiles (Section 10)
Officer in Command of military forces to restore lands (Section 4)
Officer Commanding forces to declare an area a danger zone (Section 10)
Collector to depute Revenue Officers (Section 6)
Collector to constitute a commission for compensation appeals (Section 6)
Collector to prohibit entry into and secure removal from danger zones (Section 10)
Revenue Officer to consider claims, determine, and disburse compensation (Section 6)
Commission to decide appeals regarding compensation (Section 6)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Offences include wilfully obstructing manoeuvres or field firing/artillery practice, unauthorized entry into camps or danger zones, and unauthorized interference with military apparatus or targets. Penalties for such offences may extend to a fine of ten rupees.

related_acts: Ancient Monuments Preservation Act, l904 (7 of 1904)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Collector of the district shall depute Revenue Officers (Section 6). The Collector of the district shall constitute a commission, with himself as chairman, a person nominated by the Officer Commanding the forces, and two persons nominated by the District Board (Section 6).

applies_to: military forces engaged in the manoeuvres
persons as are included in the forces engaged in field firing or artillery practice
any person (in relation to offences)
exemptions: any well or tank held sacred by any religious community
any place of worship or ground attached thereto
any place or building reserved or used for the disposal of the dead
any dwelling house or premises attached thereto
any educational institution
factory
workshop or store
any premises used for the carrying on of any trade, business or manufacture
any garden or pleasure ground
any ancient monument as defined in section 2 of the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act, l904 (7 of 1904)
special_provisions: The Act has been extended in its application to Goa, Daman and Diu by Reg. 12 of 1962, s. 3 and Sch., (w.e.f. 31-1-1963)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through notifications issued by the State Government, actions taken by military forces, a compensation mechanism involving Revenue Officers and a commission, and penalties for specified offences. act_identification.act_title: THE CUTCHI MEMONS ACT, 1938

legislative_details.geographical_extent: The Act has been applied to the Sonthal Parganas district and the Chota Nagpur division, and to all the partially-excluded areas of the Province of Orissa.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient that all Cutchi Memons be governed in matters of succession and inheritance by the Muhammadan Law; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide that all Cutchi Memons shall be governed in matters of succession and inheritance by the Muhammadan Law. It aims to standardize the legal framework for these specific personal law matters for the community.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Cutchi Memons Act, 1938, and specifies its commencement date as 1st November, 1938.

key_sections.title: Cutchi Memons to be governed in certain matters by Muhammadan Law.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that all Cutchi Memons shall be governed by the Muhammadan Law in matters of succession and inheritance, subject to the provisions of section 3.

key_sections.title: Savings.
key_sections.description: Ensures that the Act does not affect any right or liability acquired or incurred before its commencement, or any legal proceeding or remedy related to such rights or liabilities.

repealed_acts: Repealing and Amending Act, 1942 (25 of 1942)

applies_to: all Cutchi Memons
exemptions: any right or liability acquired or incurred before its commencement
any legal proceeding or remedy in respect of any such right or liability
special_provisions: Applied to the Sonthal Parganas district and the Chota Nagpur division
Applied to all the partially-excluded areas of the Province of Orissa

act_identification.act_title: THE DISSOLUTION OF MUSLIM MARRIAGES ACT, 1939
act_identification.act_short_title: The Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and clarify the provisions of Muslim law relating to suits for dissolution of marriage by women married under Muslim law and to remove doubts as to the effect of the renunciation of Islam by a married Muslim woman on her marriage tie; It is hereby enacted as follows: ––
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to consolidate and clarify the provisions of Muslim law relating to suits for dissolution of marriage by women married under Muslim law. It also aims to remove doubts regarding the effect of a married Muslim woman's renunciation of Islam on her marriage tie.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical extent.

key_sections.title: Grounds for decree for dissolution of marriage
key_sections.description: Enumerates the specific grounds upon which a Muslim woman can obtain a decree for dissolution of her marriage.

key_sections.title: Notice to be served on heirs of the husband when the husband’s whereabouts are not known.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the procedure for serving notice on the husband's heirs in cases where his whereabouts are unknown.

key_sections.title: Effect of conversion to another faith.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that renunciation of Islam or conversion by a Muslim woman does not automatically dissolve her marriage, but allows her to seek dissolution on other grounds.

key_sections.title: Rights to dower not to be affected.
key_sections.description: Ensures that the dissolution of marriage under this Act does not affect a married woman's right to her dower under Muslim law.

powers_conferred: Power to the Court to grant a decree for the dissolution of marriage

repealed_acts: section 5 of Act 26 of 1937

applies_to: A woman married under Muslim law
exemptions: woman converted to Islam from some other faith who re-embraces her former faith
Renoncants of the Union territory of Pondicherry
special_provisions: In its application to Pondicherry, nothing contained in this Act shall apply to the Renoncants of the Union territory of Pondicherry.
The Act has been extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963, s. 2 and Sch. I.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through suits filed in Court for a decree of dissolution of marriage.

act_identification.act_title: THE REGISTRATION OF FOREIGNERS ACT, 1939

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the registration of foreigners entering, being present in, and departing form, [1][India]; It is hereby enacted as follows: ––
act_overview.purpose: To provide for the registration of foreigners entering, being present in, and departing from India.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical extent to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'foreigner' and 'prescribed'.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for the registration and regulation of foreigners, including reporting requirements and identity proof.

key_sections.title: Burden of proof.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the onus of proving non-foreign status or a particular class/description of foreigner lies upon the person concerned.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention or attempted contravention of rules made under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt from application of Act.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to exempt individuals or classes of foreigners from the application of the Act or its rules.

key_sections.title: Protection to persons acting under this Act.
key_sections.description: Provides protection against legal proceedings for actions done in good faith under the Act.

key_sections.title: Application of other laws not barred.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act's provisions are in addition to, and not in derogation of, other laws like the Foreigners Act, 1946.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to make rules with respect to foreigners for various purposes (Section 3)
Central Government: Power to declare exemptions from the application of the Act or rules (Section 6)
Prescribed authority: Power to demand proof of identity from foreigners (Section 3(d))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who contravenes, or attempts to contravene, or fails to comply with, any provision of any rule made under this Act shall be punished, if a foreigner, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees or with both, or if not a foreigner, with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees.

applies_to: foreigners entering, or being present in, India
any person having the management of any hotel, boarding-house, sarai or any other premises of like nature
any person having the management or control of any vessel or aircraft
exemptions: Any individual foreigner or any class or description of foreigner, as declared by the Central Government by order
special_provisions: Extended to Goa, Daman and Diu with modifications by Reg. 12 of 1962, s. 3 and Sch.
Extended to Pondicherry with modification vide Notification No. G.S.R. 1557, dated 24-11-1962
Brought into force in Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963, s. 2 and Sch. I. (w.e.f. 1-7-1965)
Extended to Lakshadweep vide Reg. 8 of 1965, s. 3 and Sch. (w.e.f. 1-10-1967)
Extended to the State of Sikkim vide Notification No. G.S.R. 41 (E), dated 27-1-1976 (w.e.f. 1-2-1976)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through rules made by the Central Government requiring reporting, identity proof, and information from managers of premises/vessels; enforced with penalties for contravention.

act_identification.act_title: THE COMMERCIAL DOCUMENTS EVIDENCE ACT, 1939

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India except [2][the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States]

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend the Law of Evidence with respect to certain commercial documents. WHEREAS it is expedient to amend the Law of Evidence with respect to certain commercial documents;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to amend the Law of Evidence concerning certain commercial documents. It aims to make statements within these documents relevant facts and establish presumptions about their genuineness.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Commercial Documents Evidence Act, 1939, and defines its geographical extent.

key_sections.title: Statements of relevant facts in scheduled documents to be themselves relevant facts.
key_sections.description: Declares that statements of facts in issue or relevant facts made in any document included in the Schedule are themselves relevant facts within the meaning of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.

key_sections.title: Presumption as to genuineness of documents.
key_sections.description: Empowers courts to presume the genuineness and accuracy of statements in documents included in Part I (shall presume) and Part II (may presume) of the Schedule, for the purposes of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines the term 'recognised Chamber of Commerce' as used in the Schedule.

powers_conferred: Power to the Court to presume the genuineness and accuracy of statements contained in documents included in the Schedule.

related_acts: States Re-organisation Act, 1956 (Central Act XXXVII of 1956)
International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea, 1929

applies_to: the whole of India except [2][the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States]
exemptions: the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States

implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: a Court

schedules_summary.description: Lists various commercial documents (e.g., Lloyd’s Register of Shipping, shipping certificates, marine insurance documents, consular certificates, customs duty receipts, railway tariffs, company documents) in relation to which the Court 'SHALL presume' their genuineness and accuracy.

Lists other commercial documents (e.g., survey reports, foreign ship log books, dock certificates, export applications, weight/measurement certificates, aircraft documents, customs/excise passes, warehouse warrants, railway/steamship receipts, P&T receipts, survey awards, company balance sheets) in relation to which the Court 'MAY presume' their genuineness and accuracy.

act_identification.act_title: THE DRUGS AND COSMETICS ACT, 1940

legislative_details.enacted_by: Legislatures of all the Provinces have passed resolutions in terms of section 103 of the Government of India Act, 1935

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the import, manufacture, distribution and sale of drugs and cosmetics. WHEREAS it is expedient to regulate the import, manufacture, distribution and sale of drugs and cosmetics; AND WHEREAS the Legislatures of all the Provinces have passed resolutions in terms of section 103 of the Government of India Act, 1935 (26 Geo. 5, c. 2), in relation to such of the above-mentioned matters and matters ancillary thereto as are enumerated in List II of the Seventh Schedule to the said Act:
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to regulate the import, manufacture, distribution, and sale of drugs and cosmetics in India. It aims to ensure the quality, safety, and efficacy of these products and to prevent the sale of misbranded, adulterated, or spurious items.

chapter_titles: THE DRUGS TECHNICAL ADVISORY BOARD, THE CENTRAL DRUGS LABORATORY AND THE DRUGS CONSULTATIVE COMMITTEE
MANUFACTURE. SALE AND DISTRIBUTSION OF DRUGS AND COSMETICS
PROVISIONS RELATING TO AYURVEDIC, SIDDHA AND UNANI DRUGS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the official name, geographical applicability, and effective date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani drug', 'cosmetic', 'drug', 'Government Analyst', 'Inspector', and 'manufacture'.

key_sections.title: The Drugs Technical Advisory Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Drugs Technical Advisory Board to advise the Central and State Governments on technical matters related to the Act.

key_sections.title: The Central Drugs Laboratory.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of a Central Drugs Laboratory for testing and analysis of drugs and cosmetics.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of import of certain drugs or cosmetics.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the import of drugs or cosmetics that are not of standard quality, misbranded, adulterated, spurious, or imported without a license.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to prohibit import of drugs and cosmetics in public interest.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to prohibit import of drugs or cosmetics if they pose a risk to human/animal health or lack therapeutic value.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of manufacture and sale of certain drugs and cosmetics.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the manufacture, sale, stock, or distribution of drugs and cosmetics that are not of standard quality, misbranded, adulterated, spurious, or without a valid license.

key_sections.title: Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Empowers Central and State Governments to appoint Inspectors for enforcing the Act.

key_sections.title: Powers of Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Outlines the powers of Inspectors, including inspection, taking samples, searching premises, and seizing articles.

key_sections.title: Powers of Central Government to regulate, restrict or prohibit manufacture, etc., of drug and cosmetic in public interest.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to regulate, restrict, or prohibit manufacture, sale, or distribution of drugs or cosmetics in public interest.

key_sections.title: Penalty for manufacture, sale, etc., of drugs in contravention of this Chapter.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for various offences related to the manufacture, sale, and distribution of drugs, including severe penalties for adulterated or spurious drugs causing harm or death.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government broad powers to make rules for implementing the provisions of Chapter IV.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Specifies liability for offences committed by companies, including directors, managers, and other officers.

key_sections.title: Special Courts.
key_sections.description: Provides for the designation of Special Courts for the trial of offences related to adulterated or spurious drugs.

powers_conferred: Power of Central Government to prohibit import of drugs and cosmetics in public interest (Section 10A)
Power of Central Government to make rules (Section 12, 33, 33N)
Powers of Inspectors (Section 22)
Power of Central Government to regulate, restrict or prohibit manufacture, etc., of drug and cosmetic in public interest (Section 26A)
Power of Central Government to regulate or restrict, manufacture, etc., of drug in public interest (Section 26B)
Power of Court to implead the manufacturer, etc. (Section 32A)
Power of Central Government to give directions to State Governments (Section 33P)
Magistrate’s power to impose enhanced penalties (Section 36)
Power to amend First Schedule (Section 33-O)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines various offences related to the import, manufacture, sale, and distribution of drugs and cosmetics, including importing/manufacturing/selling non-standard, misbranded, adulterated, or spurious products. Penalties range from imprisonment (up to life imprisonment for serious drug offences) and fines (up to ten lakh rupees or three times the value of confiscated drugs, whichever is more, for serious drug offences; up to fifty thousand rupees or three times the value for cosmetic offences) to confiscation of goods and implements. Subsequent offences attract enhanced penalties.

amended_acts: notification No. S.O. 820, dated the 6th June, 1978
related_acts: Government of India Act, 1935 (26 Geo. 5, c. 2)

authorities_established: Ayurvedic and Unani Drugs Technical Advisory Board
The Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani Drugs Consultative Committee
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government and State Government appoint Government Analysts and Inspectors. Central Government appoints Secretary of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board and Ayurvedic and Unani Drugs Technical Advisory Board. Central Government or State Government designates Special Courts.
regulatory_bodies: Ayurvedic and Unani Drugs Technical Advisory Board
The Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani Drugs Consultative Committee

applies_to: whole of India
drugs and cosmetics
Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani drugs
exemptions: small quantities of any drug for the purpose of examination, test or analysis or for personal use
Vaidyas and Hakims who manufacture Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani drug for the use of their own patients
manufacture, subject to the prescribed conditions, of small quantities of any Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani drug for the purpose of examination, test or analysis
special_provisions: in relation to the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh)
Application of provisions to Government departments

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through Inspectors and Government Analysts who have powers of inspection, sampling, search, and seizure. Offences are tried in competent courts, including Special Courts, with prescribed penalties and provisions for confiscation of goods.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class, Court of Session, Special Courts

schedules_summary.description: Lists authoritative books for Ayurvedic, Siddha, and Unani Tibb systems of medicine, which define the formulae for Ayurvedic, Siddha, or Unani drugs.

Specifies the standards of quality to be complied with by imported drugs and by drugs manufactured for sale, sold, stocked, exhibited for sale, or distributed, including patent/proprietary medicines, vaccines, biological products, substances affecting human body structure/function, and Homoeopathic medicines.

act_identification.act_title: THE COFFEE ACT, 1942

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act [1][to provide for the development under the control of the Union of the coffee industry]. WHEREAS it is expedient [1][to provide for the development under the control of the Union of the coffee industry] ;
act_overview.purpose: To provide for the development of the coffee industry under the control of the Union. It establishes the Coffee Board to regulate the cultivation, curing, marketing, and sale of coffee, both domestically and for export, and to manage funds for the industry's growth.

chapter_titles: Duties of Customs and of Excise
Control of Sale, Export and Re-import of Coffee

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and duration.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and duration.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to expediency of Union control.
key_sections.description: Declares the expediency of Union control over the coffee industry in the public interest.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Coffee Board and outlines its composition.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of the Board.
key_sections.description: Declares the Board as a body corporate with perpetual succession and powers to acquire property and sue/be sued.

key_sections.title: Registration of owners of coffee estates.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration for owners of coffee estates with the State Government.

key_sections.title: Fixation of prices for sale of coffee.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to fix wholesale or retail prices for coffee in the Indian market.

key_sections.title: Export of coffee.
key_sections.description: Regulates the export of coffee from India, generally requiring it to be done by or under authorization from the Board.

key_sections.title: Free sale quota.
key_sections.description: Provides for the allotment of a free sale quota to registered estates by the Board.

key_sections.title: Surplus coffee and surplus pool.
key_sections.description: Mandates delivery of surplus coffee to the Board for inclusion in the surplus pool and outlines its management.

key_sections.title: General fund.
key_sections.description: Details the credits and application of the Board's general fund.

key_sections.title: Pool fund.
key_sections.description: Details the credits and application of the Board's pool fund, primarily for payments to registered owners.

key_sections.title: Failure to register.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for owners who fail to register their coffee estates.

key_sections.title: Cognizance of offences.
key_sections.description: Specifies which courts can take cognizance of offences under the Act and conditions for complaints.

key_sections.title: Power of the Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Fix prices for coffee (Section 16)
Central Government: Appoint Chairman, Chief Coffee Marketing Officer, Secretary, Deputy Secretary, Marketing Officers (Sections 4, 9)
Central Government: Specify quantity of coffee for export and grant exemptions (Section 20)
Central Government: Sanction transfer of funds between general and pool funds (Section 32)
Central Government: Make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (Section 48)
Central Government: Control acts of the Board, cancel, suspend or modify actions (Section 42)
Central Government: Hear appeals against Board orders (Section 43)
Board: Appoint committees, staff, and agents (Section 7)
Board: Allot free sale quotas to registered estates (Section 22)
Board: Issue licences for curing establishments (Section 28)
Board: Maintain separate general and pool funds (Section 30)
Board: Borrow on the security of funds or coffee (Section 33)
Board: Make payments to registered owners from the pool fund (Section 34)
Board: Seize coffee withheld from inclusion in the surplus pool (Section 38B)
Board: Inspect records and obtain copies (Section 46)
State Government: Make rules for registration of coffee estates (Section 15)
State Government: Appoint registering officers (Section 14)
Chairman: Allow owner to retain coffee for consumption and seed purposes (Section 25)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties include fines for failure to register (up to 1000 rupees, plus 500 rupees/month), contraventions of sale regulations (up to 1000 rupees), operating an unlicensed curing establishment (up to 500 rupees), failure to furnish returns (up to 1000 rupees), making false returns (up to 1000 rupees), contravention of coffee delivery to surplus pool (up to 1000 rupees and confiscation), and obstruction (up to 1000 rupees). Offences by companies hold both the company and responsible individuals liable.

repealed_acts: Indian Coffee Cess Act, 1935 (14 of 1935)
related_acts: Indian Coffee Market Expansion Ordinance, 1940 (13 of 1940)
Cess Laws (Repealing and Amending) Act, 2006 (24 of 2006)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairman, Chief Coffee Marketing Officer, Secretary, Deputy Secretary, Marketing Officers, and auditors. The State Government appoints registering officers. The Board may appoint committees, staff, and agents.

applies_to: Owners of land planted with coffee plants
Registered owners
Licensed curers
Dealers
Curing establishments
Companies
exemptions: Coffee shipped as stores on board any vessel or aircraft in reasonable quantity (Section 20)
Coffee carried as personal baggage of a passenger, not exceeding specified quantities (Section 20)
Coffee exported for such purposes and in such quantities as the Central Government may specify (Section 20)
Export of coffee from India to the State of Jammu and Kashmir or to any foreign settlement bounded by India, if exempted by Central Government (Section 20)
Classes of owners producing small quantities of coffee or in remote localities, exempted by Central Government from delivering coffee to surplus pool (Section 25)
special_provisions: The Act extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
The Central Government may exempt the export of coffee from India to the State of Jammu and Kashmir or to any foreign settlement bounded by India.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through mandatory registration of coffee estate owners, licensing of curing establishments, fixation of coffee prices, regulation of sale, export, and re-import of coffee, allotment of free sale quotas, management of a surplus pool, and requiring returns from registered owners. The Board has powers of inspection and seizure. Penalties are prescribed for various contraventions, and the Central Government exercises overall control and hears appeals.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class.

act_identification.act_title: An Act to make provisions on a basis of reciprocity in regard to entry into, travel, residence, the acquisition, holding or disposal of property, the enjoyment of educational facilities, the holding of public office, or the carrying on of any occupation, trade, business or profession in India by, and the franchise in India of, persons domiciled in British Possessions.

act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to enable the Central Government to impose reciprocal disabilities on persons domiciled in British Possessions in India, mirroring the disabilities faced by persons of Indian origin in those British Possessions regarding various rights and activities.

key_sections.title: Definitions.

key_sections.title: Burden of proof on person claiming exemption.

key_sections.title: Direction imposing disabilities in respect of entry, travel and residence not to apply to armed forces.

members of armed forces domiciled in a British Possession (for entry, travel, and residence disabilities, until six months after the termination of present hostilities)

key_sections.description: Outlines the process for appealing decisions or orders of Central Excise Officers to the Commissioner (Appeals).

key_sections.title: Appeals to the Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Details the procedure for appealing certain orders to the Appellate Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers broad powers on the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Levy and collect duty (Section 3), charge excise duty on capacity (Section 3A), increase duty of excise (Section 3B), amend Fourth Schedule (Section 3C), specify goods for retail sale price valuation (Section 4A), grant exemption from duty (Section 5A), establish Consumer Welfare Fund (Section 12C), make rules (Section 37), delegate powers (Section 37A), issue orders/instructions/directions for appeals (Section 35R), annul or modify orders (Section 35EE).

Central Excise Officer: Recover sums due to Government (Section 11), recover duties not levied/paid/short-levied/short-paid/erroneously refunded (Section 11A), exercise powers and discharge duties of subordinate officers (Section 12E), search and seize (Section 12F), arrest persons (Section 13), summon persons to give evidence and produce documents (Section 14), direct special audit (Section 14A, 14AA), determine amount due (Section 11D).
Courts: Order forfeiture of goods, receptacles, vehicles, implements (Section 10), publish name, place of business, etc., of convicted persons (Section 9B).
Settlement Commission: Order provisional attachment to protect revenue (Section 32G), grant immunity from prosecution and penalty (Section 32K).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 9 defines offences such as contravention of Section 8 or rules, evasion of duty, improper removal of excisable goods, acquiring excisable goods liable to confiscation, contravention related to CENVAT credit, failure to supply information, supplying false information, and abetment. Penalties include imprisonment for terms up to seven years (with a minimum of six months for duty exceeding fifty lakh rupees) or up to three years (or fine or both for other cases), and fines. Section 9A specifies that most offences are non-cognizable, but those involving duty exceeding fifty lakh rupees are cognizable and non-bailable. Offences by companies are addressed in Section 9AA, making persons in charge and directors liable. Section 10 allows courts to order forfeiture of goods, receptacles, vehicles, and implements. Vexatious search or seizure by a Central Excise Officer (Section 22) is punishable with a fine up to two thousand rupees. Failure of a Central Excise Officer in duty (Section 23) is punishable with imprisonment up to three months or a fine up to three months' pay, or both. Rules made under Section 37 may also provide for penalties, including confiscation of goods and penalties not exceeding the duty leviable or five thousand rupees, whichever is greater.

act_identification.act_title: THE PUBLIC DEBT ACT, 1944

WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to Government securities *** and to the management by the Reserve Bank of India of the public debt of [the Government].
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to consolidate and amend the law relating to Government securities. It also aims to regulate the management of the public debt of the Government by the Reserve Bank of India.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Securities to which this Act applies.
key_sections.description: Defines the scope of the Act's applicability to Government securities issued by Central or State Governments.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'the Bank', 'the Government', and 'Government security'.

key_sections.title: Transfer of Government securities.
key_sections.description: Outlines the prescribed manner for transferring Government securities and conditions for their validity.

key_sections.title: Notice of trust not receivable.
key_sections.description: States that the Government will not receive or be bound by notice of any trust in respect of Government securities.

key_sections.title: Persons whose title to a Government security of a deceased sole holder may be recognised by the Bank.
key_sections.description: Specifies who may be recognized by the Bank as having title to a deceased sole holder's Government security, including provisions for Hindu undivided families.

key_sections.title: Nominations by holders of Government securities.
key_sections.description: Allows holders of Government securities to make nominations for payment on their death, overriding other dispositions.

key_sections.title: Issue of duplicate securities and of new securities on conversion, consolidation, sub-division or renewal.

key_sections.title: Summary determination by the Bank of title to Government security in case of dispute.
key_sections.description: Grants the Bank power to determine title to a Government security in case of dispute and make vesting orders.

key_sections.title: Law applicable in regard to Government securities.
key_sections.description: Declares that the rights relating to Government securities shall be determined by the law and Courts of India.

key_sections.title: Legal effect of orders made by the Bank.
key_sections.description: States that the Bank's recognition of a holder or its orders cannot be questioned by any Court regarding the Bank's or Government's relations with the holder.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including specific matters.

Bank to make orders vesting Government securities (Sections 9, 10, 12)
Bank to issue duplicate or new securities (Section 11)
Bank to request District Magistrate to record evidence (Section 14)
Bank to suspend payment of interest or postpone registration of transfers (Section 15)
Bank to require bonds or security (Section 16)
Central Government to declare public offices to which Section 5 applies (Section 5(1))
Central Government to specify classes of Government securities for application of Sections 9B and 9C (Section 9A)
Central Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (Section 28)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: null

Holders of Government securities

Provisions for Hindu undivided family governed by Mitakshara Law regarding title recognition (Section 7 proviso)
Provisions for securities created and issued by the Government of Hyderabad, Saurashtra or Travancore-Cochin on or before 31st March, 1953 (Section 29 proviso)

act_identification.act_title: THE INTERNATIONAL MONETARY FUND AND BANK ACT, 1945
act_identification.act_short_title: The International Monetary Fund and Bank Act, 1945

act_overview.preamble: An [2][Act] to implement the International Monetary Fund and Bank Agreements. WHEREAS, at the United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference held at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, in July, 1944, Articles of the following agreements were drawn up, and set out in the Final Act of the said Conference that is to say,— (a) an agreement (hereinafter referred to as the Fund Agreement) for the establishment and operation of an international body to be called the International Monetary Fund (hereinafter referred to as the International Fund), and (b) an agreement (hereinafter referred to as the Bank Agreement) for the establishment and operation of an international body to be called the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (hereinafter referred to as the International Bank);
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to implement the agreements for the establishment and operation of the International Monetary Fund and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, as drawn up at the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944. It provides for payments, information sharing, and grants legal force to certain provisions of these agreements in India.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Payments to International Fund and Bank.
key_sections.description: Mandates payments from the Consolidated Fund of India for subscriptions, charges, and other sums required by the International Fund and Bank.

key_sections.title: Reserve Bank to be depository for International Fund and Bank.
key_sections.description: Designates the Reserve Bank of India as the depository for the Indian currency holdings of the International Fund and Bank.

key_sections.title: Reserve Bank to use, receive, acquire, etc., special drawing rights on behalf of Central Government.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Reserve Bank to manage special drawing rights for the Central Government in the International Fund.

key_sections.title: Power to call for information.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government or Reserve Bank power to compel individuals to furnish information required by the International Fund.

key_sections.title: Certain provisions of Agreements to have force of law.
key_sections.description: States that specific provisions of the Fund and Bank Agreements, as set out in the Schedule, shall have the force of law in India.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for implementing the Act and the scheduled provisions.

powers_conferred: Central Government to make payments to International Fund and Bank.
Central Government to create and issue non-interest bearing and non-negotiable notes or other obligations.
Central Government to call for information from any person.
Central Government to make rules for giving effect to the Act.
Reserve Bank of India to be depository for International Fund and Bank.
Reserve Bank to use, receive, acquire, hold, transfer or operate special drawing rights on behalf of the Central Government.
Reserve Bank to call for information from any person.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Prosecution under section 176 or section 177 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) for failure to furnish information as required under this Act.

repealed_acts: section 6 of The International Monetary Fund and Bank Act, 1945 (by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1952 (48 of 1952))

any person (for furnishing information)

Salaries and emoluments paid by the Fund to non-local nationals from tax.
Obligations or securities issued by the Fund from certain types of taxation.

Certain provisions of international agreements are given force of law. The Central Government is empowered to make rules for implementation.
