act_identification.act_title: THE INDUSTRIAL EMPLOYMENT (STANDING ORDERS) ACT, 1946

act_overview.preamble:
An Act to require employers in industrial establishments formally to define conditions of employment under them.
WHEREAS it is expedient to require employers in industrial establishments to define with sufficient
precision the conditions of employment under them and to make the said conditions known to workmen
employed by them;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to require employers in industrial establishments to formally define the conditions of employment for their workmen. It aims to ensure that these conditions are precise and made known to the workmen employed by them.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical reach, and to which industrial establishments it applies, including exemptions.

key_sections.title: Interpretation.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appellate authority', 'appropriate Government', 'employer', 'industrial establishment', and 'standing orders'.

key_sections.title: Submission of draft standing orders.
key_sections.description: Requires employers to submit draft standing orders for adoption, covering matters in the Schedule and conforming to model orders where prescribed.

key_sections.title: Conditions for certification of standing orders.
key_sections.description: Outlines the requirements for standing orders to be certifiable, including covering all Schedule matters and conformity with the Act, and assigns the Certifying Officer/appellate authority to adjudicate fairness/reasonableness.

key_sections.title: Certification of standing orders.
key_sections.description: Details the process for certifying standing orders, including inviting objections, hearing parties, making necessary modifications, and issuing certified copies.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Allows aggrieved parties to appeal the Certifying Officer's order to the appellate authority, whose decision is final regarding the certification of standing orders.

key_sections.title: Date of operation of standing orders.
key_sections.description: Specifies when certified standing orders come into effect, either after a period from certification or after an appellate decision.

key_sections.title: Posting of standing orders.
key_sections.description: Mandates employers to prominently display the certified standing orders in English and the local language at the industrial establishment.

key_sections.title: Duration and modification of standing orders.
key_sections.description: Sets conditions for the duration and modification of certified standing orders, generally not allowing modification for six months without agreement.

key_sections.title: Payment of subsistence allowance.
key_sections.description: Requires employers to pay subsistence allowance to workmen suspended pending inquiry into misconduct, at specified rates.

key_sections.title: Certifying Officers and appellate authorities to have powers of civil court.
key_sections.description: Grants Certifying Officers and appellate authorities powers of a Civil Court for receiving evidence, administering oaths, and compelling document production.

key_sections.title: Penalties and procedure.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for employers who fail to submit or improperly modify standing orders, or contravene certified standing orders, and outlines prosecution procedures.

key_sections.title: Interpretation, etc., of standing orders.
key_sections.description: Allows employers or workmen to refer questions regarding the application or interpretation of certified standing orders to a Labour Court for a final decision.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply to certain industrial establishments.
key_sections.description: Exempts industrial establishments where workmen are governed by specific government service rules or regulations.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including prescribing additional matters for the Schedule and model standing orders.

powers_conferred: Appropriate Government: to apply provisions to industrial establishments (S.1(3))
Appropriate Government: to appoint appellate authorities (S.2(a))
Appropriate Government: to appoint Certifying Officers (S.2(c))
Appropriate Government: to decide if an industrial establishment is under Central Government control (S.2(b) proviso)
Appropriate Government: to sanction prosecution for offences (S.13(3))
Appropriate Government: to exempt industrial establishments from provisions (S.14)
Appropriate Government: to delegate its powers (S.14A)
Appropriate Government: to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (S.15)
Certifying Officer: to certify draft standing orders (S.5)
Certifying Officer: to have powers of a Civil Court for receiving evidence, administering oaths, enforcing attendance of witnesses, and compelling discovery and production of documents (S.11)
Appellate Authority: to hear appeals against Certifying Officer's orders and confirm or amend standing orders (S.6)
Appellate Authority: to have powers of a Civil Court for receiving evidence, administering oaths, enforcing attendance of witnesses, and compelling discovery and production of documents (S.11)
Labour Court: to decide disputes regarding subsistence allowance (S.10A(2))
Labour Court: to decide questions regarding the application or interpretation of standing orders (S.13A)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: An employer who fails to submit draft standing orders or modifies them improperly is punishable with a fine up to five thousand rupees, and a further fine of two hundred rupees per day for continuing offence. An employer contravening certified standing orders is punishable with a fine up to one hundred rupees, and a further fine of twenty-five rupees per day for continuing offence. Prosecution requires prior sanction of the appropriate Government.

related_acts: Bombay Industrial Relations Act, 1946 (Bombay Act 11 of 1947)
Madhya Pradesh Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1961 (Madhya Pradesh Act 26 of 1961)
Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules
Civilians in Defence Service (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The appropriate Government has the power to appoint Certifying Officers and appellate authorities.

applies_to: Every industrial establishment wherein one hundred or more workmen are employed, or were employed on any day of the preceding twelve months.
Any industrial establishment employing such number of persons less than one hundred as may be specified by the appropriate Government by notification.
exemptions: Any industry to which the provisions of Chapter VII of the Bombay Industrial Relations Act, 1946 (Bombay Act 11 of 1947) apply.

Any industrial establishment to which the provisions of the Madhya Pradesh Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1961 (Madhya Pradesh Act 26 of 1961) apply (with a proviso for Central Government establishments).

Industrial establishments in respect of which the appropriate Government is the Government of the State of Gujarat or the Government of the State of Maharashtra (for temporary application of model standing orders under S.12A(2)).

Any industrial establishment or class of industrial establishments exempted by the appropriate Government by notification (S.14).
special_provisions: State amendments for Karnataka and Maharashtra reducing the threshold of workmen for applicability from one hundred to fifty (S.1(3)).

Proviso in S.1(4)(ii) stating that the Act shall apply to all industrial establishments under the control of the Central Government, notwithstanding the Madhya Pradesh Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1961.
Proviso in S.2(b) allowing the Central Government to decide if an industrial establishment is under its control, with such decision being final and binding.

S.10(4) stating that sub-section (2) (modification application) shall not apply to an industrial establishment in respect of which the appropriate Government is the Government of the State of Gujarat or the Government of the State of Maharashtra (though Maharashtra later deleted this exemption for itself).
S.10A(3) provides that if State laws offer more beneficial subsistence allowance provisions, those shall apply.
S.12A(2) states that temporary application of model standing orders does not apply to industrial establishments where the appropriate Government is Gujarat or Maharashtra.
Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh (UTs) amendment inserting section 13C for compounding of offences.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a certification process for standing orders by Certifying Officers and appellate authorities. Employers are required to submit draft standing orders, which are then certified after review and potential modifications. Certified orders must be posted prominently. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance, failure to submit, or improper modification of standing orders. Labour Courts are empowered to interpret standing orders and resolve disputes.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Labour Courts (for subsistence allowance disputes and interpretation of standing orders), Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the second class (for trying offences under the Act).

schedules_summary.description: Lists the matters to be provided in standing orders under this Act, including classification of workmen, hours of work, holidays, pay-days, wage rates, shift working, attendance, leave, entry/search requirements, closing/re-opening of sections, termination of employment, suspension/dismissal for misconduct, means of redress, and age for retirement/superannuation (Maharashtra amendment), and employment/re-employment of probationers/badlis/temporary/casual workmen (Maharashtra amendment).

act_identification.act_title: THE DELHI SPECIAL POLICE ESTABLISHMENT ACT, 1946

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India; Union territories; any State (not being a Union territory); Railway areas

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make provision for the constitution of a special police force [2][in Delhi for the investigation of certain offences in [3] [the Union territories]] for the superintendence and administration of the said force and for the extension to other areas [4]* * * of the powers and jurisdiction of members of the said force in regard to the investigation of the said offences. WHEREAS it is necessary to constitute a special police force [2][in Delhi for the investigation of certain offences in [3][the Union territories]] and to make provision for the superintendence and administration of the said force and for the extension to other area [4]*** of the powers and jurisdiction of the members of the said force in regard to the investigation of the said offences;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to constitute a special police force, known as the Delhi Special Police Establishment, for the investigation of certain offences in Union territories. It also provides for the superintendence and administration of this force and allows for the extension of its powers and jurisdiction to other areas.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946' and states its geographical applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Interpretation section.
key_sections.description: States that words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003, shall have the meanings assigned to them in that Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution and powers of special police establishment.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to constitute the Delhi Special Police Establishment for investigating notified offences in Union territories and defines the powers, duties, privileges, and liabilities of its members.

key_sections.title: Offences to be investigated by special police establishment.—
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to specify, by notification, the offences or classes of offences to be investigated by the Delhi Special Police Establishment.

key_sections.title: Superintendence and administration of Special Police Establishment.—
key_sections.description: Vests the superintendence of the Delhi Special Police Establishment in the Commission for Prevention of Corruption Act offences and in the Central Government for other matters, and vests administration in a Director.

key_sections.title: Committee for appointment of Director.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Committee comprising the Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition, and Chief Justice of India (or nominee) to recommend the appointment of the Director.

key_sections.title: Terms and conditions of service of Director.—
key_sections.description: Specifies that the Director shall hold office for a minimum period of two years, with provisions for extension and transfer requiring Committee consent.

key_sections.title: Director of Prosecution.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of a Directorate of Prosecution, headed by a Director, for conducting prosecutions under this Act, functioning under the Director's supervision.

key_sections.title: Appointment for posts of Superintendent of Police and above, extension and curtailment of their tenure, etc.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for appointing officers at the level of Superintendent of Police and above, and for extending or curtailing their tenure, based on the recommendation of a specified committee.

key_sections.title: Extension of powers and jurisdiction of special police establishment to other areas.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to extend the powers and jurisdiction of the Delhi Special Police Establishment to areas in States (not Union territories) and Railway areas for investigating specified offences.

key_sections.title: Consent of State Government to exercise of powers and jurisdiction.—
key_sections.description: Stipulates that members of the Delhi Special Police Establishment cannot exercise powers and jurisdiction in any State (not being a Union territory or railway area) without the consent of that State Government.

key_sections.title: Approval of Central Government to conduct, inquiry or investigation.—
key_sections.description: Requires prior approval of the Central Government for inquiry or investigation into certain offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, concerning high-ranking Central Government officials, with an exception for on-the-spot arrests.

powers_conferred: Central Government to constitute a special police force called the Delhi Special Police Establishment (Section 2).

Central Government to extend powers and jurisdiction of the Delhi Special Police Establishment to other areas (Section 5).
Central Government to approve inquiry or investigation into certain offences for specified officials (Section 6A).

Director of Prosecution to conduct prosecution of cases under this Act (Section 4BA).

Committee (Central Vigilance Commissioner, Vigilance Commissioners, Secretaries of Home and Personnel) to recommend appointment, extension, or curtailment of tenure for officers of SP rank and above (Section 4C).

The Directorate of Prosecution conducts prosecution of cases under this Act. act_identification.act_title: THE FOREIGNERS ACT, 1946
