key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, such as 'foreigner', 'prescribed', and 'specified'.

key_sections.title: Power to make orders.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make orders for prohibiting, regulating, or restricting the entry, presence, and departure of foreigners in India.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt citizens of Commonwealth Countries and other persons from application of Act in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to exempt certain Commonwealth citizens or other foreigners from the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Obligations of masters of vessels, etc.
key_sections.description: Mandates masters of vessels and pilots of aircraft to furnish particulars of foreign passengers and crew, and to provide accommodation for removal of foreigners.

key_sections.title: Obligation of hotel keepers and others to furnish particulars.
key_sections.description: Requires keepers of lodging premises to provide information about accommodated foreigners and maintain records.

key_sections.title: Determination of nationality.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for determining the nationality of a foreigner when it is uncertain or multiple nationalities are claimed.

key_sections.title: Burden of proof.
key_sections.description: Places the onus of proving non-foreign status or specific class of foreigner on the person concerned.

key_sections.title: Power to give effect to orders, directions, etc.
key_sections.description: Empowers authorities and police officers to take necessary steps and use force to ensure compliance with orders and directions under the Act.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of provisions of the Act, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for remaining in India beyond the visa period, violating visa conditions, or general contravention of the Act or orders.

key_sections.title: Penalty for entry in restricted areas, etc.
key_sections.description: Specifies penalties for entering or staying in restricted areas or without valid documents.

key_sections.title: Penalty for using forged passport.
key_sections.description: Imposes penalties for knowingly using a forged passport to enter or remain in India.

key_sections.title: Penalty for abetment.
key_sections.description: Provides for punishment for abetment of offences under sections 14, 14A, or 14B.

key_sections.title: Application of other laws not barred.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act's provisions are in addition to, and not in derogation of, other relevant laws.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to make orders for prohibiting, regulating or restricting entry, presence and departure of foreigners (Section 3)
Central Government: Power to exempt citizens of Commonwealth Countries and other persons from application of Act (Section 3A)
Central Government: Power to determine conditions for detention/confinement of internees and persons on parole (Section 4)
Central Government: Power to grant licence or permission for change of name (Section 5)
Central Government: Power to direct provision of accommodation for removal of foreigners (Section 6(5))
Central Government: Power to revise decisions on nationality (Section 8(2))
Prescribed authority: Power to make orders under clause (e) or (f) of sub-section (2) of section 3 (Section 3(3))
Prescribed authority: Power to control places frequented by foreigners (Section 7A)
Prescribed authority: Power to determine nationality (Section 8(1))
District Magistrate, Commissioner of Police, Superintendent of Police: Power to require information from masters of vessels or pilots of aircraft (Section 6(2))
Any authority empowered by or under the Act: Power to take steps and use force for securing compliance with directions or effective exercise of power (Section 11(1))
Police officer: Power to take steps and use force for securing compliance with orders or directions (Section 11(2))
Any authority upon which power is conferred by Act: Power to delegate authority in writing (Section 12)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 13 defines attempts, abetment, and contravention by masters/pilots as deemed contraventions. Section 14 prescribes imprisonment up to five years and fine for remaining beyond visa period, violating visa conditions, or general contravention. Section 14A mandates imprisonment not less than two years (up to eight years) and fine not less than ten thousand rupees for entry in restricted areas or without valid documents. Section 14B imposes imprisonment not less than two years (up to eight years) and fine not less than ten thousand rupees (up to fifty thousand rupees) for using a forged passport. Section 14C provides for the same punishment for abetment as for the abetted offence.

applies_to: foreigners
exemptions: Citizens of any specified Commonwealth Country (Section 3A)
Any other individual foreigner or class or description of foreigner as specified by Central Government order (Section 3A)
Assumption or use of any name in pursuance of a licence or permission granted by the Central Government (Section 5(5)(a))
By any married woman, of her husband’s name (Section 5(5)(b))
special_provisions: The Act has been extended to Goa, Daman and Diu, Pondicherry, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Lakshadweep, Minicoy and Amindivi Island, and the State of Sikkim with modifications.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government makes orders to regulate foreigners. Authorities and police officers are empowered to take steps and use force to ensure compliance. Masters of vessels, pilots of aircraft, and hotel keepers have obligations to furnish particulars. Contraventions are subject to penalties including imprisonment and fines.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: any Court

act_identification.act_title: THE INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ACT, 1947

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make provision for the investigation and settlement of industrial disputes, and for certain other purposes. WHEREAS it is expedient to make provision for the investigation and settlement of industrial disputes, and for certain other purposes hereinafter appearing; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to provide a framework for the investigation and settlement of industrial disputes. It establishes authorities like Conciliation Officers, Boards, Courts, and Tribunals to facilitate amicable resolution and adjudication of such disputes, and addresses related matters like strikes, lock-outs, lay-off, retrenchment, and unfair labour practices.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II AUTHORITIES UNDER THIS ACT
CHAPTER IIB REFERENCE OF CERTAIN INDIVIDUAL DISPUTES TO GRIEVANCE SETTLEMENT AUTHORITIES
CHAPTER III REFERENCE OF DISPUTES TO BOARDS, COURTS OR TRIBUNALS
CHAPTER IV PROCEDURE, POWERS AND DUTIES OF AUTHORITIES
CHAPTER VB SPECIAL PROVISIONS RELATING TO LAY-OFF, RETRENCHMENT AND CLOSURE IN CERTAIN ESTABLISHMENTS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines various terms used throughout the Act, crucial for its interpretation.

key_sections.title: Dismissal, etc., of an individual workman to be deemed to be an industrial dispute.
key_sections.description: Specifies that dismissal, discharge, retrenchment, or termination of an individual workman can be considered an industrial dispute.

key_sections.title: Works Committee.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of Works Committees in certain industrial establishments to promote good relations between employers and workmen.

key_sections.title: Labour Courts.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution and qualifications of presiding officers of Labour Courts for adjudication of industrial disputes related to matters in the Second Schedule.

key_sections.title: Tribunals.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution and qualifications of presiding officers of Industrial Tribunals for adjudication of industrial disputes related to matters in the Second or Third Schedule.

key_sections.title: National Tribunals.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution and qualifications of presiding officers of National Industrial Tribunals for disputes of national importance or affecting multiple states.

key_sections.title: Notice of change.
key_sections.description: Requires employers to give notice before changing conditions of service applicable to workmen in respect of matters specified in the Fourth Schedule.

key_sections.title: Setting up of Grievance Redressal Machinery.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of Grievance Redressal Committees in industrial establishments employing twenty or more workmen for individual grievances.

key_sections.title: Reference of disputes to Boards, Courts or Tribunals.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to refer existing or apprehended industrial disputes to various authorities for settlement or adjudication.

key_sections.title: Voluntary reference of disputes to arbitration.
key_sections.description: Allows employers and workmen to voluntarily refer industrial disputes to arbitration before they are referred to a Labour Court, Tribunal, or National Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Powers of Labour Courts, Tribunals and National Tribunals to give appropriate relief in case of discharge or dismissal of workmen.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to Labour Courts, Tribunals, and National Tribunals to set aside discharge/dismissal orders and direct reinstatement or other relief if the order was not justified.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of strikes and lock-outs.
key_sections.description: Prohibits strikes and lock-outs in public utility services without proper notice and during conciliation proceedings.

key_sections.title: General prohibition of strikes and lock-outs.
key_sections.description: Imposes general prohibitions on strikes and lock-outs during the pendency of proceedings before various authorities or during the operation of settlements/awards.

key_sections.title: Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen.
key_sections.description: Lays down conditions, including notice and compensation, that must be fulfilled by an employer before retrenching a workman who has completed one year of continuous service.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of lay-off.
key_sections.description: Prohibits lay-off of workmen in certain industrial establishments without prior permission from the appropriate Government, with exceptions for specific reasons.

key_sections.title: Conditions precedent to retrenchment of workmen.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions for retrenchment in certain industrial establishments, including a three-month notice and prior permission from the appropriate Government.

key_sections.title: Procedure for closing down an undertaking.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for closing down an undertaking in certain industrial establishments, requiring a ninety-day prior application for permission from the appropriate Government.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of unfair labour practice.
key_sections.description: Prohibits employers, workmen, or trade unions from engaging in any unfair labour practice as specified in the Fifth Schedule.

key_sections.title: Penalty for committing unfair labour practices.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for any person who commits an unfair labour practice.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service, etc., to remain unchanged under certain circumstances during pendency of proceedings.
key_sections.description: Prevents employers from altering conditions of service or taking punitive action against workmen during the pendency of conciliation or adjudication proceedings without express permission.

key_sections.title: Recovery of money due from an employer.
key_sections.description: Provides a mechanism for workmen to apply to the appropriate Government for the recovery of money or benefits due from employers under a settlement, award, or specific chapters of the Act.

key_sections.title: Representation of parties.
key_sections.description: Specifies the manner in which workmen and employers can be represented in proceedings under the Act, including restrictions on legal practitioners.

powers_conferred: Appropriate Government: Appoint conciliation officers (S.4), constitute Boards of Conciliation (S.5), Courts of Inquiry (S.6), Labour Courts (S.7), Tribunals (S.7A), National Tribunals (S.7B - Central Govt), exempt from notice of change (S.9B), refer disputes to Boards, Courts, Tribunals (S.10), prohibit strikes/lock-outs (S.10(3), S.10A(4A)), extend/reduce period of operation of awards (S.19), make rules (S.38), delegate powers (S.39), amend Schedules (S.40), grant/refuse permission for lay-off (S.25M), retrenchment (S.25N), closure (S.25O), direct restarting of undertakings (S.25P), exempt from provisions (S.36B).
Conciliation Officers: Mediate and promote settlement of industrial disputes (S.4), investigate disputes (S.12), enforce attendance and production of documents (S.11(4)).

Boards, Courts, Labour Courts, Tribunals, National Tribunals: Investigate and inquire into matters (S.11(1)), powers of a Civil Court (S.11(3)), appoint assessors (S.11(5)), give appropriate relief in discharge/dismissal cases (S.11A), adjudicate disputes (S.10, S.15), execute awards (S.11(9), S.11(10)).
Labour Courts: Decide questions regarding money value of benefits (S.33C(2)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties are prescribed for various offences including illegal strikes and lock-outs (S.26), instigation of illegal strikes/lock-outs (S.27), financial aid to illegal strikes/lock-outs (S.28), breach of settlement or award (S.29), disclosing confidential information (S.30), closure without notice (S.30A), contravention of Section 33 (S.31(1)), other contraventions (S.31(2)), lay-off and retrenchment without previous permission (S.25Q), closure without complying with S.25-O or contravening related orders (S.25R), and committing unfair labour practices (S.25U). Penalties range from imprisonment up to one month to one year, and fines from fifty rupees to five thousand rupees, with provisions for continuing fines for ongoing breaches.

repealed_acts: 25-I. [Recovery of moneys due from employres under this chapter.] Rep. by the Industrial Disputes (Amendment and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1956 (36 of 1956), s. 19 (w.e.f. 10-3-1957).
related_acts: Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948 (9 of 1948)
Coal Mines Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1948 (46 of 1948)
Employees’ Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (19 of 1952)
Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation Act, 1961 (47 of 1961)
Unit Trust of India Act, 1963 (52 of 1963)
Airports Authority of India Act, 1994 (55 of 1994)
Small Industries Development Bank of India Act, 1989 (39 of 1989)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 (5 of 1970)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980 (40 of 1980)
State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959 (38 of 1959)
Khadi and Village Industries Commission Act, 1956 (61 of 1956)
Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957 (67 of 1957)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The appropriate Government appoints conciliation officers, members of Boards/Courts, and presiding officers of Labour Courts/Tribunals. The Central Government appoints presiding officers of National Tribunals.

applies_to: Whole of India (S.1(2)).
Industrial establishments employing one hundred or more workmen for Works Committee (S.3).
Industrial establishments employing twenty or more workmen for Grievance Redressal Committee (S.9C).
Industrial establishments (not seasonal/intermittent) employing not less than one hundred workmen for Chapter VB (S.25K(1)).
Workmen (defined in S.2(s)).
Employers (defined in S.2(g)).
exemptions: No notice of change required if change is pursuant to settlement/award or for workmen covered by specific government service rules (S.9A Proviso).
Government can exempt classes of industrial establishments/workmen from S.9A (S.9B).
Workmen subject to Air Force Act, Army Act, Navy Act, police service, prison officers, managerial/administrative capacity, supervisory capacity drawing high wages are not "workman" (S.2(s)).
Sections 25C to 25E do not apply to establishments where Chapter VB applies, or those with less than fifty workmen, or seasonal/intermittent establishments (S.25A).
Undertakings for construction of buildings, bridges, roads, canals, dams, or other construction work are exempt from S.25FFA notice for closure (S.25FFA(1) Proviso (b)).
Undertakings with less than fifty workmen are exempt from S.25FFA notice for closure (S.25FFA(1) Proviso (a)).
Government can exempt from S.25FFA notice in exceptional circumstances (S.25FFA(2)).
Government can exempt from S.25M (lay-off) in exceptional circumstances (S.25M(9)).
Government can exempt from S.25N (retrenchment) in exceptional circumstances (S.25N(8)).
Government can exempt from S.25-O (closure) in exceptional circumstances (S.25-O(7)).
Government can exempt industrial establishments/undertakings from all or any provisions of the Act if adequate provisions exist for dispute settlement (S.36B).
special_provisions: State Amendments for Kerala, Assam, Orissa, Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, Meghalaya, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat are mentioned, modifying definitions, penalties, and applicability thresholds.
Provisions for public utility services (S.10(2) Proviso, S.22).
Special provisions for certain establishments in Chapter VB (S.25K onwards).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through conciliation proceedings, adjudication by Labour Courts, Tribunals, and National Tribunals, and voluntary arbitration. Awards become enforceable after 30 days of publication. Money due from employers can be recovered as arrears of land revenue (S.33C(1)), and awards/orders/settlements can be executed as Civil Court decrees (S.11(9), S.11(10)). Penalties are prescribed for contraventions of the Act.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Labour Courts, Tribunals, National Tribunals (for adjudication and certain enforcement), Civil Courts (for execution of awards/orders/settlements and enforcing rights under S.35), and Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class (for trying offences under the Act, S.34(2)).

schedules_summary.description: Lists industries which may be declared to be public utility services under sub-clause (vi) of clause (n) of Section 2.
Specifies matters within the jurisdiction of Labour Courts.
Specifies matters within the jurisdiction of Industrial Tribunals.
Lists conditions of service for which notice of change is required to be given by employers.
Defines and lists various unfair labour practices on the part of employers and trade unions of employers, and on the part of workmen and trade unions of workmen.

act_identification.act_title: THE ARMED FORCES (EMERGENCY DUTIES) ACT, 1947

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Extended to the new Provinces and merged States, States of Manipur, Tripura and Vindhya Pradesh, Pondicherry, Lakshdeep, Goa, Daman and Diu, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to enable duties in connection with vital services to be imposed in an emergency on an Armed Forces * * *. WHEREAS it is expedient to enable duties in connection with vital services to be imposed in the emergency on the Armed Forces * * *.
act_overview.purpose: This Act enables the Central Government to declare certain services as vital to the community during an emergency. It then mandates personnel of the Armed Forces to obey commands related to these vital services.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

key_sections.title: Short title and extend.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'the Armed Forces (Emergency Duties) Act, 1947'.

key_sections.title: Emergency duties of Armed Forces.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to declare services as vital and mandates Armed Forces personnel to obey commands related to such services, deeming them lawful under respective service acts.

key_sections.title: Validation of certain past commands.
key_sections.description: Validates commands given to Armed Forces personnel between 30th September 1946 and the commencement of this Act, deeming them lawful, but exempts individuals from punishment for not obeying such past commands.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To declare any specified service to be a service of vital importance to the community (Section 2(1)).
Central Government: To extend notifications declaring vital services (Section 2(1) Proviso).
Central Government: To specify services for the validation of past commands (Section 3).
Superior officers: To give commands to Armed Forces personnel in relation to employment upon or in connection with vital services (Section 2(2)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Disobedience to commands given by superior officers in relation to vital services, declared under Section 2, is deemed a violation of lawful commands under the Army Act, 1950, Air Force Act, 1950, or Navy Act, 1957. However, no person shall be punished solely for not having obeyed certain commands given between 30th September 1946 and the commencement of this Act, which are validated under Section 3.

applies_to: Every person subject to the Army Act, 1950 (46 of 1950)
Every person subject to the Air Force Act, 1950 (45 of 1950)
Every person subject to the Navy Act, 1957 (62 of 1957)
exemptions: No person shall be punished by reason only of his not having obeyed any command given between 30th September 1946 and the commencement of this Act, even if such command is validated under Section 3.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced through commands issued by superior officers, which are deemed lawful commands under the respective service acts (Army Act, Air Force Act, Navy Act).

act_identification.act_title: THE RUBBER ACT, 1947

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the development [2][under the control of the Union] of the rubber industry 3***. WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the development [2][under the control of the Union] of the rubber industry 3***;
act_overview.purpose: To provide for the development of the rubber industry under the control of the Union.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the official name of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to expediency of Union control.
key_sections.description: Declares that Union control over the rubber industry is in the public interest.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Rubber Board and outlines its composition.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Board.
key_sections.description: Details the duties and responsibilities of the Rubber Board for developing the rubber industry.

key_sections.title: Power of the Board to import rubber for sale, or to purchase rubber in the internal market.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board power to import or purchase rubber with previous Central Government approval.

key_sections.title: Funds of the Board.
key_sections.description: Deals with the dissolution of the previous board and the establishment of funds for the new Board.

key_sections.title: Power to prohibit or control imports and exports of rubber.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to regulate the import and export of rubber.

key_sections.title: Imposition of new rubber cess.
key_sections.description: Provides for the levy and collection of an excise duty (cess) on rubber produced in India.

key_sections.title: Power to fix maximum and minimum prices for sale of rubber.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to fix price controls for rubber.

key_sections.title: Licensing of transactions in rubber.
key_sections.description: Requires licences for selling, disposing of, buying, or acquiring rubber.

key_sections.title: Control by the Central Government.
key_sections.description: States that all acts of the Board are subject to the control of the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to issue directions to Board.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue policy directions to the Board.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government authority to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contraventions of the Act or rules, false statements, obstruction, and failure to produce records.

key_sections.title: Adjudication of penalties.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for adjudging penalties, including the appointment of an adjudicating officer and appeal mechanism.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Prohibit, restrict or control imports and exports of rubber (Section 11)
Central Government: Fix maximum and minimum prices for sale of rubber (Section 13)
Central Government: Make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act (Section 25)
Central Government: Control all acts of the Board, and cancel, suspend or modify any action taken by the Board (Section 22)
Central Government: Issue directions on questions of policy to the Board (Section 22A)
Central Government: Appoint Chairman, Executive Director, Rubber Production Commissioner, and Secretary to the Board (Section 4, 6A)
Board: Promote the development of the rubber industry (Section 8)
Board: Import rubber for sale, or purchase rubber in the internal market (Section 8A)
Board: Levy fees for the issue and renewal of special licences (Section 19)
Board: Issue general or special licences for transactions in rubber (Section 14)
Board: Issue special licences for planting or replanting rubber (Section 17)
Board: Make regulations to carry out its functions (Section 25A)
Board: Compound offences punishable under this Act (Section 26A)
Executive Director: Appoint an adjudicating officer for holding an inquiry and imposing penalty (Section 26B)
Executive Director: Hear appeals against orders of the adjudicating officer (Section 26B)
Adjudicating Officer (Secretary to the Board or other authorized officer): Hold inquiry and impose penalty (Section 26B)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of import/export orders under Section 11(1) is punishable with penalty up to one lakh rupees or cancellation of licence, or both (Section 11(3)). General contraventions of the Act or rules, making false statements, obstructing officers, or failing to produce records are liable to penalty which may extend to fifty thousand rupees (Section 26(1)).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the Chairman, Executive Director, Rubber Production Commissioner, and Secretary to the Board. The Central Government also nominates members to the Board.

applies_to: Every person owning land planted with rubber plants
Dealers in rubber
Manufacturers using rubber
Holders of special licences for transactions in rubber
exemptions: The Central Government may exempt or reduce the duty of excise on rubber exported.
special_provisions: The Act extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
Provisions for estates situated only partly in India regarding rubber production returns.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the levy and collection of cess by the Board, licensing of transactions and planting, inspections of land and premises, imposition and adjudication of penalties, and prosecution for offences. The Central Government exercises control over the Board and can issue directions.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District Judge for appeals against cess assessment (Section 12(6)). No Court inferior to that of a Presidency Magistrate or of Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act (Section 27A).

act_identification.act_title: THE UNITED NATIONS (PRIVILEGES AND IMMUNITIES) ACT, 1947
act_identification.act_short_title: The United Nations (Privileges and Immunities) Act, 1947

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to give effect to the Convention on the Privileges and Immunities of the United Nations, and to enable similar privileges and immunities to be enjoyed by other international organisations and their representatives and officials;
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to give legal effect to the Convention on the Privileges and Immunities of the United Nations in India. It also enables the conferment of similar privileges and immunities on other international organizations and their representatives and officials.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Conferment on United Nations and its representatives and officers and certain privileges and immunities.
key_sections.description: Grants the provisions of the Convention on Privileges and Immunities, as set out in the Schedule, the force of law in India for the United Nations and its representatives and officers, and allows the Central Government to amend the Schedule.

key_sections.title: Power to confer certain privileges and immunities on other international organisations and their representatives and officers.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to extend similar privileges and immunities to other international organizations and their representatives and officers by notification.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, with such rules to be laid before Parliament.

powers_conferred: Central Government to amend the Schedule in conformity with amendments to the Convention (Section 2(2))
Central Government to declare application of Schedule provisions to other international organisations (Section 3)
Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act (Section 4(1))
United Nations to possess juridical personality, contract, acquire and dispose of property, and institute legal proceedings (Schedule, Article I, Section 1)
United Nations to transfer funds, gold or currency and operate accounts in any currency (Schedule, Article II, Section 5)
United Nations to use codes and despatch and receive correspondence by courier or in bags (Schedule, Article III, Section 10)
Secretary-General to specify categories of officials for privileges and immunities (Schedule, Article V, Section 17)
Secretary-General to waive immunity of any official (Schedule, Article V, Section 20)
Security Council to waive immunity of the Secretary-General (Schedule, Article V, Section 20)
Secretary-General to waive immunity of any expert (Schedule, Article VI, Section 23)
United Nations to issue United Nations Laissez-passer to its officials (Schedule, Article VII, Section 24)
United Nations to make provisions for appropriate modes of settlement of disputes (Schedule, Article VIII, Section 29)

related_acts: Convention on the Privileges and Immunities of the United Nations
Article 65 of the Statute of the Court

applies_to: United Nations and its representatives and officers
Other international organisations and their representatives and officers
exemptions: Representatives of Members are not exempt from customs duties on goods imported (otherwise than as part of their personal baggage) or from excise duties or sales taxes (Schedule, Article IV, Section 11(g))
United Nations will not claim exemption from taxes which are, in fact, no more than charges for public utility services (Schedule, Article II, Section 7(a))
special_provisions: Extended to the Union territory of Pondicherry
Extended to the State of Sikkim

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The provisions of the Schedule have the force of law in India. Rules made by the Central Government are laid before each House of Parliament.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: International Court of Justice (for interpretation or application of the convention)

schedules_summary.description: Contains the provisions of the Convention on the Privileges and Immunities, adopted by the General Assembly of the United Nations on 13th February, 1946. It details the juridical personality, property, funds and assets, facilities in respect of communications, privileges and immunities of representatives of Members, officials, experts on missions, United Nations Laissez-passer, and settlement of disputes for the United Nations and related personnel.

act_identification.act_title: THE UNITED NATIONS (SECURITY COUNCIL) ACT, 1947

act_overview.preamble: An Act to enable effect to be given to certain provisions of the Charter of the United Nations. WHEREAS it is expedient to enable effect to be given to certain provisions of the Charter of the United Nations; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to empower the Central Government to implement measures, not involving armed force, as called for by the United Nations Security Council under Article 41 of the UN Charter. It allows the government to make necessary provisions, including those with extra-territorial operation and for the punishment of offenders, to effectively apply these measures.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as 'The United Nations (Security Council) Act, 1947'.

key_sections.title: Measures under Art 41 of the Charter of the United Nations.
key_sections.description: This section empowers the Central Government to make provisions, by order published in the Official Gazette, to apply measures called for by the UN Security Council under Article 41 of the UN Charter, not involving armed force. Such provisions may include extra-territorial operation and punishment for offenders.

powers_conferred: Central Government may, by order published in the Official Gazette, make such provisions (including provisions having extra-territorial operation) as appear to it necessary or expedient for enabling those measures to be effectively applied.
Provision may be made for the punishment of persons offending against the order.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act empowers the Central Government to make provisions for the punishment of persons offending against any order issued under Section 2.

related_acts: Charter of the United Nations signed at San Francisco on the 26th day of June 1945

applies_to: Central Government

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through orders published in the Official Gazette by the Central Government, which can include provisions for punishment of offenders.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN NURSING COUNCIL ACT, 1947

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to constitute an Indian Nursing Council in order to establish a uniform standard of training for nurses, midwives and health visitors;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to constitute an Indian Nursing Council. This Council is established to ensure a uniform standard of training for nurses, midwives, and health visitors across India.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its geographical extent to the whole of India, and its immediate commencement.

key_sections.title: Interpretation.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'the Council', 'prescribed', 'State Council', and 'State register'.

key_sections.title: Constitution and composition of the Council.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to constitute the Indian Nursing Council and details its membership composition, including elected and ex officio members.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of the Council.
key_sections.description: Declares the Indian Nursing Council as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to acquire property and to sue and be sued.

key_sections.title: Recognition of qualifications.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for recognising nursing, midwifery, and health visitor qualifications, including those listed in the Schedule, and provisions for reciprocity with other territories or countries.

key_sections.title: Effect of recognition.
key_sections.description: States that recognised qualifications are sufficient for enrolment in State registers and sets conditions for enrolment, including provisions for citizens with foreign qualifications and temporary enrolment for non-citizens.

key_sections.title: Inspections.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Executive Committee to appoint inspectors to assess training institutions and examinations, and requires reports to be submitted to relevant authorities.

key_sections.title: Withdrawal of recognition.
key_sections.description: Provides the Council with the power to withdraw recognition of qualifications or institutions if training standards or conditions are not met, following a report from the Executive Committee and consultation with State Governments.

key_sections.title: Indian Nurses Register.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Indian Nurses Register, to be maintained by the Council's Secretary, containing names from all State registers, and declares it a public document.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Council the authority to make regulations for carrying out the Act's provisions, covering aspects like management, elections, meetings, functions of committees, and prescribing standards for training and examinations.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To constitute the Council, nominate the President for the first five years, decide disputes regarding certain elections, sanction fees and allowances, and amend the Schedule.

Council: To elect its President and Vice-President, constitute an Executive Committee and other committees, appoint a Secretary and other officers/servants, acquire property, sue and be sued, declare qualifications as recognised, enter into negotiations for reciprocity, maintain the Indian Nurses Register, and make regulations.
Executive Committee: To appoint inspectors, report on the suitability of institutions and adequacy of training/examinations, and exercise powers conferred by the Council's regulations.

repealed_acts: Ordinance 13 of 1947

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to constitute the Council, nominate the President for the first five years, and appoint the Secretary for the first three years. The Council elects its President and Vice-President, and appoints the Secretary (after the initial period) and other officers and servants. The Executive Committee appoints inspectors.

applies_to: Nurses, midwives, and health visitors seeking uniform training standards and registration.
Persons seeking enrolment in any State register.
Citizens of India holding foreign nursing/midwifery qualifications (with Council approval).

Persons not being citizens of India employed as nurse, midwife, auxiliary nurse-midwife, teacher or administrator in hospitals for teaching, research or charitable work (with President's approval, for temporary enrolment).
exemptions: Persons already enrolled in any State register before the commencement of this Act.
Persons entitled to be enrolled in any State register immediately before the commencement of this Act, if they apply within two years.
special_provisions: Reciprocal arrangements for recognition of qualifications with authorities in other territories of India or foreign countries.
Temporary enrolment in State Register for non-citizens employed in hospitals for teaching, research or charitable work, with practice limited to the attached hospital or institution.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Council has the power to make regulations. For the first constitution of the Council, the President may make regulations with the previous sanction of the Central Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is primarily through the recognition and withdrawal of qualifications, inspections of training institutions and examinations, and the maintenance of the Indian Nurses Register and State registers. Disputes regarding elections are referred to the State Government or Central Government.

schedules_summary.description: This Schedule is divided into two parts. Part I lists 'Recognised qualifications' for General Nursing, Midwifery, Auxiliary Nursing-Midwifery, and Health Visitors, specifying various examination boards, councils, universities, and other authorities that issue these qualifications. Part II lists 'Recognised higher qualifications', detailing specific diplomas and degrees in advanced nursing fields (e.g., Sister Tutor Course, Psychiatric Nursing, Public Health Nursing, Nursing Administration) and the authorities that issue them.

act_identification.act_title: THE DOCK WORKERS (REGULATION OF EMPLOYMENT) ACT, 1948

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for regulating the employment of dock workers; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: An Act to provide for regulating the employment of dock workers.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its geographical extent.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Board', 'cargo', 'dock worker', 'employer', 'Government', and 'scheme'.

key_sections.title: Scheme for ensuring regular employment of workers.
key_sections.description: Empowers the creation of schemes for registration and regulation of dock workers and employers to ensure regular employment, and specifies what such schemes may provide for, including penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Making, variation and revocation of schemes.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for the Government to make, vary, or revoke schemes for ports or groups of ports, subject to previous publication.

key_sections.title: Advisory Committees.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of Advisory Committees to advise the Government on matters arising from the administration of the Act or any scheme.

key_sections.title: Dock Labour Boards.
key_sections.description: Enables the Government to establish Dock Labour Boards for ports, defining them as corporate bodies with perpetual succession and a common seal.

key_sections.title: Functions of a Board.
key_sections.description: Specifies that a Board is responsible for administering the scheme for its designated port(s) and must follow directions from the Government.

key_sections.title: Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Government to appoint Inspectors for the Act, defines their status as public servants, and outlines their powers to enter premises, examine documents, and take evidence.

key_sections.title: Power to supersede a Board.
key_sections.description: Grants the Government power to supersede a Dock Labour Board under certain conditions, such as grave emergency or persistent default, and outlines the consequences of supersession.

key_sections.title: Cognizance of offences.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that courts can only take cognizance of offences under a scheme based on a report from an Inspector or authorized person, and specifies the competent courts for trial.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Addresses offences committed by companies, holding persons in charge and the company liable, with provisions for due diligence and liability of directors/managers in certain cases.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Government to make rules to give effect to the Act's provisions, including rules for the composition and functioning of Advisory Committees and Boards.

powers_conferred: Government: make schemes for ports (Section 4(1))
Government: add to, amend, vary or revoke schemes (Section 4(1))
Government: direct port authority to prepare draft schemes (Section 4(3))
Government: constitute Advisory Committee (Section 5(1))
Government: appoint members of Advisory Committee (Section 5(2))
Government: establish Dock Labour Boards (Section 5A(1))
Government: appoint Chairman and members of Dock Labour Boards (Section 5A(3))
Government: give directions to a Board (Section 5B(2))
Government: appoint auditors for Board accounts (Section 5C(2))
Government: appoint Inspectors (Section 6(1))
Government: prescribe manner for complaints to Inspectors (Section 6(4))
Government: appoint person to investigate or inquire into working of a Board (Section 6A(1))
Government: supersede a Board (Section 6B(1))
Government: extend period of supersession or re-establish Board (Section 6B(3))
Government: make rules to give effect to the Act (Section 8(1))
Dock Labour Boards: administer schemes (Section 5B(1))
Dock Labour Boards: acquire, hold and dispose of property and to contract (Section 5A(2))
Inspectors: enter premises or vessel (Section 6(3)(a))
Inspectors: require production and examine documents (Section 6(3)(b))
Inspectors: take evidence (Section 6(3)(c))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of any provision of a scheme is punishable with imprisonment up to three months for a first contravention or six months for subsequent contraventions, or with a fine up to five hundred rupees for a first contravention or one thousand rupees for subsequent contraventions, or with both. Offences by companies are also addressed, holding persons in charge and the company liable.

related_acts: Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Amendment Act, 1962 (8 of 1962)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Government has the power to appoint members of the Advisory Committee, the Chairman and members of Dock Labour Boards, and Inspectors.

applies_to: Dock workers
Employers of dock workers
special_provisions: The Act was initially extended to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir, but later made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh by notification.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through schemes made by the Government, administered by Dock Labour Boards, and monitored by Inspectors. Offences under schemes are cognizable by specific courts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class

act_identification.act_title: THE PHARMACY ACT, 1948

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to make better provision for the regulation of the profession and practice of pharmacy and for that purpose to constitute Pharmacy Councils;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to regulate the profession and practice of pharmacy. It also aims to constitute Pharmacy Councils for this purpose.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical extent, and commencement details, including conditional commencement for certain chapters.

key_sections.title: Interpretation.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution and composition of Central Council.
key_sections.description: Outlines the formation and membership of the Pharmacy Council of India.

key_sections.title: Education Regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Council to make regulations prescribing minimum standards for pharmacy education.

key_sections.title: The Central Register.
key_sections.description: Mandates the maintenance of a Central Register of pharmacists by the Central Council.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Council power to make regulations for Chapter II, subject to Central Government approval.

key_sections.title: Constitution and composition of State Councils.
key_sections.description: Details the formation and membership of State Pharmacy Councils.

key_sections.title: Preparation and maintenance of register.
key_sections.description: Requires the preparation and maintenance of a register of pharmacists for each State.

key_sections.title: Qualifications for entry on first register.
key_sections.description: Sets out the eligibility criteria for individuals to be entered on the initial register of pharmacists.

key_sections.title: Qualifications for subsequent registration.
key_sections.description: Defines the qualifications required for registration after the first register is prepared and after Education Regulations take effect.

key_sections.title: Special provisions for registration of certain persons.
key_sections.description: Provides special conditions for the registration of displaced persons, citizens from outside India, and others.

key_sections.title: Removal from register.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Executive Committee to remove a registered pharmacist's name from the register under specified conditions.

key_sections.title: Penalty for falsely claiming to be registered.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals who falsely claim to be registered pharmacists.

key_sections.title: Dispensing by unregistered persons.
key_sections.description: Prohibits unregistered persons from compounding, preparing, mixing, or dispensing medicine, with exceptions, and specifies penalties.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government power to make rules to carry out the purposes of Chapters III, IV, and V.

powers_conferred: Central Council: make Education Regulations (Section 10), approve courses of study and examinations (Section 12), declare qualifications granted outside India (Section 14), maintain the Central Register (Section 15A), appoint Inspectors (Section 16), make regulations for Chapter II (Section 18).

State Government: appoint date for Chapters III, IV and V to take effect (Section 1(3)), constitute State Councils (Section 19), enter into inter-State agreements (Section 20), appoint Registrar for State Council (Section 26 proviso), sanction appointment of Inspectors (Section 26A), cause preparation of first register (Section 29), constitute Registration Tribunal (Section 30), direct renewal fees (Section 34), appoint Commission of Enquiry (Section 45), make rules for Chapters III, IV and V (Section 46).
State Council: maintain the register (Section 29(2)), approve entry of names in the register (Section 33(2) proviso), restore names to the register (Section 37).

Executive Committee (Central/State): report on efficacy of Education Regulations (Section 10(5)), consider withdrawal of approval for courses/examinations (Section 13), appoint Inspectors (Section 16), order removal of names from the register (Section 36).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 26A(3): Wilfully obstructing an Inspector is liable to penalty which may extend to one lakh rupees. Section 41(1): Falsely claiming to be registered is punishable on first conviction with fine up to one lakh rupees, and on subsequent conviction with imprisonment up to three months or fine up to two lakh rupees, or both. Section 42(2): Contravention of dispensing by unregistered persons is punishable with imprisonment up to three months, or with fine up to two lakh rupees, or with both. Section 43(1): Failure to surrender certificate of registration is punishable with fine up to fifty rupees.

related_acts: Jammu and Kashmir Pharmacy Act, 2011 (1955 A.D.)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government nominates members to Central Council, sanctions remuneration, sanctions President's regulations, appoints Commission of Enquiry. Central Council appoints Registrar and other officers/servants, elects President/Vice-President and Executive Committee members. State Government appoints date for chapters, nominates members to State Council, appoints Registrar, sanctions Inspector appointment, constitutes Registration Tribunal, appoints authority for appeals, appoints Commission of Enquiry, makes rules. State Council appoints Registrar and other officers/servants, elects President/Vice-President and Executive Committee members.

applies_to: Profession and practice of pharmacy
Pharmacists
Persons residing or carrying on the business or profession of pharmacy in the State
Displaced persons, repatriates, and other specific categories for registration under special provisions
exemptions: Medical practitioners dispensing medicine for their own patients.
Medical practitioners dispensing medicine for patients of another medical practitioner with the general or special sanction of the State Government.
special_provisions: Conditional commencement of Chapters III, IV and V in a particular State from a date appointed by the State Government.
Provisions for territorial changes due to reorganisation of States on 1st November, 1956.
Proviso for Union territories regarding Central Council representation for five years from the commencement of the Pharmacy (Amendment) Act, 1976.
Conditions for qualifications granted outside India, particularly for non-citizens of India.
Inter-State agreements for the constitution or shared services of State Councils.
Special provisions for registration of certain persons (Section 32A, 32B, 32C).
Special provision for the President of the State Council for the first five years from its constitution.
Special provision for the Registrar of the State Council for the first four years from its constitution.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Council (with Central Government approval) for regulations under Chapter II. President of Central Council (with Central Government sanction) for initial regulations. State Government for rules under Chapters III, IV and V.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Inspection by Inspectors appointed by the Executive Committee (Central Council) or State Council. Registration and removal of pharmacists from the register. Penalties for falsely claiming registration, dispensing by unregistered persons, and failure to surrender certificates. Adjudication of penalties by an adjudicating officer appointed by the Central Government. Appeals against adjudication orders to the President, Central Council. Appointment of a Commission of Enquiry by Central or State Government for non-compliance.

act_identification.act_title: THE MINIMUM WAGES ACT, 1948

act_overview.preamble:
An Act to provide for fixing minimum rates of wages in certain employments. 
WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for fixing minimum rates of wages in certain employments;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the fixing of minimum rates of wages in certain employments. It aims to ensure that employees in specified sectors receive a fair minimum remuneration for their work.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Interpretation.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'adolescent', 'adult', 'appropriate Government', 'employer', 'employee', 'scheduled employment', and 'wages'.

key_sections.title: Fixing of minimum rates of wages.
key_sections.description: Mandates the appropriate Government to fix and periodically review/revise minimum rates of wages for scheduled employments.

key_sections.title: Minimum rate of wages.
key_sections.description: Specifies the components that may constitute the minimum rate of wages, including basic rate, special allowance (cost of living allowance), and cash value of concessions.

key_sections.title: Procedure for fixing and revising minimum wages.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for fixing and revising minimum wages, either through committees or by publishing proposals.

key_sections.title: Central Advisory Board.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of a Central Advisory Board to advise Central and State Governments on minimum wage matters and coordinate Advisory Boards.

key_sections.title: Payment of minimum rates of wages.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that employers must pay wages not less than the fixed minimum rates to employees in scheduled employments.

key_sections.title: Fixing hours for a normal working day, etc.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to fix working hours, provide for a day of rest, and payment for work on rest days.

key_sections.title: Maintenance of registers and records.
key_sections.description: Requires employers to maintain registers and records of employees, work, and wages, and to exhibit notices.

key_sections.title: Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the appropriate Government to appoint Inspectors with powers to enter premises, examine records, and seize relevant documents.

key_sections.title: Claims.
key_sections.description: Establishes an authority to hear and decide claims arising from payment of less than minimum wages or other dues, and empowers it to direct payment and compensation.

key_sections.title: Penalties for certain offences.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for employers who pay less than minimum wages or contravene rules regarding working hours.

key_sections.title: Exemptions and exceptions.
key_sections.description: Allows the appropriate Government to grant exemptions from the Act's provisions for certain classes of employees, localities, or establishments under specific conditions.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to add to Schedule.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the State Government to add new employments to the Schedule, thereby bringing them under the purview of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of appropriate Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering various aspects like term of office, procedure, wage computation, and enforcement.

powers_conferred: Appropriate Government: fix minimum rates of wages (Sec 3), review and revise minimum rates of wages (Sec 3), fix different minimum rates of wages (Sec 3), fix minimum rates of wages by wage-periods (Sec 3), appoint committees and sub-committees (Sec 5), publish proposals for fixing/revising wages (Sec 5), appoint an Advisory Board (Sec 7), authorise payment of minimum wages wholly or partly in kind (Sec 11), authorise provision of essential commodities at concession rates (Sec 11), fix number of hours for a normal working day (Sec 13), provide for a day of rest (Sec 13), provide for payment for work on a day of rest (Sec 13), appoint Inspectors (Sec 19), appoint Authority to hear and decide claims (Sec 20), direct non-application of Act to disabled employees (Sec 26), direct non-application of Act to certain employees/localities (Sec 26), add to Schedule (Sec 27), make rules (Sec 30).
Central Government: appoint a Central Advisory Board (Sec 8), give directions to a State Government (Sec 28), make rules (Sec 29).
Inspectors: enter premises, examine persons, require information, seize or take copies of records (Sec 19).
Authority (appointed under Sec 20): hear and decide claims, direct payment of amounts and compensation, recover amounts as fine, exercise powers of a Civil Court.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 22 prescribes penalties for employers who pay less than the minimum rates of wages or contravene rules/orders under section 13, with imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to five hundred rupees, or both. Section 22A provides for a general punishment of a fine up to five hundred rupees for other contraventions of the Act or rules/orders. Section 20(4) allows for a penalty not exceeding fifty rupees against an applicant if a claim is found to be malicious or vexatious.

amended_acts: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Central Act 2 of 1974)
Rajasthan Panchayat Samitis And Zila Parishads Act, 1959 (Rajasthan Act 37 of 1959)

authorities_established: Authority to hear and decide claims
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The appropriate Government appoints committees, sub-committees, Advisory Boards, Inspectors, and the Authority for claims. The Central Government appoints the Central Advisory Board.

applies_to: Employees employed in scheduled employments in respect of which minimum rates of wages have been fixed.
exemptions: Employees in scheduled employment where there are less than one thousand employees in the whole State (unless the number rises to one thousand or more).

Employees engaged on urgent work, or in any emergency, or in preparatory/complementary work, or whose employment is essentially intermittent, or engaged in work dependent on irregular natural forces (for provisions related to normal working day hours).
Disabled employees (if the appropriate Government directs).
Any class of employees employed in any scheduled employment or to any locality where there is carried on a scheduled employment (if the appropriate Government directs for special reasons).
Employees in a scheduled employment or establishment who are in receipt of wages exceeding a prescribed limit (if the appropriate Government directs).
Members of the employer's family who are living with him and are dependent on him.
Members of the Armed Forces of the Union.
special_provisions: State amendments for Kerala, Assam, Karnataka, and Rajasthan regarding specific sections.

Minimum rates of wages fixed or revised shall not apply to employees during the pendency of industrial dispute proceedings or operation of an award under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Sec 3(2A)).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government (Sec 29) and the appropriate Government (Sec 30) have the power to make rules under this Act.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the appointment of Inspectors (Sec 19) who can inspect premises and records. Claims for underpayment of minimum wages are heard and decided by an appointed Authority (Sec 20). Penalties, including imprisonment and fines, are prescribed for various offences (Sec 22, 22A), with cognizance of offences taken by courts (Sec 22B). The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, can also be applied to scheduled employments for enforcement (Sec 22F).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrates have jurisdiction for recovery of amounts as fines and for imposing penalties. The Authority appointed under Section 20 has the powers of a Civil Court for taking evidence and enforcing attendance of witnesses.

schedules_summary.description: Part I lists various industrial and mining employments such as carpet making, rice mills, tobacco manufactory, plantations, oil mills, construction, stone breaking, and different types of mines (e.g., gypsum, barytes, bauxite, manganese, china clay, copper, clay, magnesite, white clay, stone, steatite, ochre, asbestos, fire clay, chromite, quartzite, quartz, silica, graphic, feldspar, laterite, dolomite, redoxide, wolfram, iron ore, granite mines). Part II lists employment in agriculture, encompassing cultivation, tillage, dairy farming, production of agricultural/horticultural commodities, raising livestock/bees/poultry, and related farm operations.

act_identification.act_title: THE REHABILITATION FINANCE ADMINISTRATION ACT, 1948

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish the Rehabilitation Finance Administration. WHEREAS it is expedient to establish a Rehabilitation Finance Administration for the purpose of giving financial assistance on reasonable terms to displaced persons to enable them to settle in business or industry;
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish a Rehabilitation Finance Administration. Its main purpose is to provide financial assistance on reasonable terms to displaced persons, enabling them to settle in business or industry.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Administration', 'borrower', and 'displaced person'.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Rehabilitation Finance Administration as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Administration.
key_sections.description: Outlines the composition of the Administration, including the Chairman and appointed/nominated members.

key_sections.title: Funds of the Administration.
key_sections.description: Details how the Administration is funded by the Central Government, including limits on advances for loans and guarantees.

key_sections.title: Business of the Administration.
key_sections.description: Describes the core functions of the Administration, including advancing loans and guaranteeing losses for scheduled banks.

key_sections.title: Loans.
key_sections.description: Sets out the terms and conditions for advancing loans, including limits, interest rates, period, and security.

key_sections.title: Mode of recovery.
key_sections.description: Provides methods for the Administration to recover unpaid loans, such as treating them as arrears of land revenue or taking charge of the borrower's business.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Mandates proper accounts and annual audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, with reports laid before Parliament.

key_sections.title: Power of inspection.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to the Chief Administrator or authorized officers to inspect borrower's records and imposes penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to give direction.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue general or special directions to the Administration.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for implementing the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Administration, with Central Government sanction, to make regulations for various operational matters.

powers_conferred: Administration: To acquire, hold and transfer property (Section 3)
Administration: To open branches (Section 3)
Administration: To appoint a Deputy Chief Administrator and other officers and servants (Section 10)
Administration: To fix salary and allowances for staff and members (Section 10)
Administration: To advance loans (Section 12, 13)
Administration: To guarantee losses of scheduled banks (Section 12)
Administration: To call for repayment before agreed period (Section 14)
Administration: To recover loans as arrears of land revenue or take charge of business (Section 15)
Administration: To inspect books of accounts and documents (Section 17)
Administration: To make regulations (Section 24)
Administration: To delegate powers or duties (Section 22)
Central Government: To constitute the Rehabilitation Finance Administration (Section 3)
Central Government: To appoint Chairman, officials, and nominate non-officials to the Administration (Section 4)
Central Government: To constitute an Advisory Board (Section 5)
Central Government: To advance money to the Administration (Section 11)
Central Government: To give general or special directions to the Administration (Section 19)
Central Government: To order liquidation of the Administration (Section 21)
Central Government: To make rules (Section 23)
Central Government: To sanction regulations made by the Administration (Section 24)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person contravening the provisions of sub-section (1) or sub-section (3) of Section 17 (regarding furnishing information, producing documents, or communicating information) shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees or with both.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairman, officials, and nominates non-officials to the Administration and members to the Advisory Board. The Administration appoints the Deputy Chief Administrator and other officers and servants.

applies_to: displaced persons
individual, company, association or body of individuals (borrowers)
special_provisions: Initially extended to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir. Later made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Administration can recover unpaid loans as arrears of land revenue or by taking charge of the borrower's business or industry. It also has powers of inspection over borrowers' records.

act_identification.act_title: THE DAMODAR VALLEY CORPORATION ACT, 1948

legislative_details.geographical_extent: States of Bihar and West Bengal; Damodar Valley and its area of operation

act_overview.preamble:
An Act to provide for the establishment and regulation of a Corporation for the development of the Damodar Valley in the Provinces of Bihar and West Bengal. 
WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the establishment and regulation of a Corporation for the development of the Damodar Valley in the Provinces of Bihar and West Bengal:
AND WHEREAS in pursuance of section 103 of the Government of India Act, 1935, (26 Geo. 5, c. 2.) resolutions have been passed by all the Chambers of the Provincial Legislatures of the said Provinces to the effect that certain matters dealt with in this Act which are enumerated in the Provincial Legislative List should be regulated in those Provinces by Act of the Dominion Legislature; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to establish and regulate a Corporation for the comprehensive development of the Damodar Valley. This includes promoting and operating schemes for irrigation, water-supply, drainage, generation and distribution of electrical energy, flood control, navigation, afforestation, soil erosion control, public health, and the general well-being of the region.

chapter_titles: PART II ESTABLISHMENT OF THE CORPORATION
PART III FUNCTIONS AND POWERS OF THE CORPORATION
PART IV FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT

key_sections.title: Incorporation.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Damodar Valley Corporation as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Corporation.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Corporation.
key_sections.description: Details the primary functions of the Corporation, including schemes for irrigation, water-supply, electrical energy, flood control, navigation, afforestation, soil erosion, public health, and general well-being.

key_sections.title: Supply and generation of electrical energy.
key_sections.description: Regulates the generation, transmission, and sale of electrical energy within the Damodar Valley, overriding certain provisions of the Indian Electricity Act, 1910.

key_sections.title: General powers of the Corporation.
key_sections.description: Grants the Corporation broad powers necessary for carrying out its functions, including acquiring property, constructing works, preventing pollution, and undertaking resettlement.

key_sections.title: Fund of the Corporation.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Corporation's own fund for all receipts and payments, with provisions for depositing moneys in the Reserve Bank of India.

key_sections.title: Liabilities of participating Governments to provide capital to the Corporation.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that participating Governments are responsible for providing the entire capital required by the Corporation for its projects.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Mandates that the Corporation's accounts be maintained and audited in a prescribed manner, in consultation with the Auditor-General of India.

key_sections.title: Directions by the Central Government.
key_sections.description: States that the Corporation must be guided by the Central Government's policy directions, with the Central Government's decision being final on matters of policy.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of provisions in sections 17 and 18 or any rules made thereunder.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for various matters, including conditions of service for members, budget forms, and account maintenance.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Corporation, with Central Government sanction, to make regulations for carrying out its functions, covering appointments, service conditions, and water/energy charges.
