implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (Section 95), State Government (Section 96), and the Corporation (makes regulations, Section 97).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement involves the collection of contributions, determination and recovery of contributions by authorized officers and Recovery Officers, inspections by Social Security Officers, adjudication of disputes by Employees' Insurance Courts, and penalties for non-compliance. Amounts due can be recovered as arrears of land revenue.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Employees’ Insurance Court, High Court (for appeals and questions of law), and Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the First Class (for trying offences).

schedules_summary.description: Lists injuries deemed to result in permanent total disablement and permanent partial disablement, used for calculating disablement benefits.
Lists occupational diseases, categorized into Parts A, B, and C, which are deemed to be 'employment injury' for benefit purposes.

act_identification.act_title: THE COAL MINES PROVIDENT FUND AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS ACT, 1948
act_identification.act_short_title: the Coal Mines Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act 1948

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make provisions for the framing of a Provident Fund Scheme [, a [2][Pension Scheme]] 3[, a Deposit linked Insurance Scheme] and a Bonus Scheme for persons employed in Coal Mines.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish schemes for provident fund, pension, deposit-linked insurance, and bonus for persons employed in coal mines.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Interpretation.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'bonus', 'coal mine', 'employee', 'employer', and various fund/scheme related terms.

key_sections.title: Coal Mines Provident Fund Scheme.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to frame a provident fund scheme for employees in coal mines and specifies that the Fund shall vest in and be administered by the Board of Trustees.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Board of Trustees.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a Board of Trustees by the Central Government to administer the Fund.

key_sections.title: Coal Mines Pension Scheme.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to frame a pension scheme for coal mine employees, providing for various types of pensions and life assurance benefits, and establishes a Pension Fund.

key_sections.title: Coal Mines Deposit-linked Insurance Scheme.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to frame a deposit-linked insurance scheme for employees covered by the Provident Fund Scheme and establishes an Insurance Fund.

key_sections.title: Coal Mines Bonus Schemes.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to frame a bonus scheme for employees in coal mines.

key_sections.title: Determination of moneys due from employers.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Coal Mines Provident Fund Commissioner or other authorized officer to determine amounts due from employers under the Act or any scheme, with powers similar to a Civil Court.

key_sections.title: Protection against attachment.
key_sections.description: Protects provident fund amounts, family pension, and insurance amounts from assignment, charge, or attachment by any court decree or order.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of the Act or any scheme framed thereunder, including imprisonment and fine, with enhanced penalties for repeat offences.

key_sections.title: Mode of recovery of money due from an employer.
key_sections.description: Specifies that amounts due from an employer (contributions, bonus, transferred accumulations, damages, charges) can be recovered by the Central Government as an arrear of land revenue.

key_sections.title: Payment of contribution by employers and recovery thereof from members.
key_sections.description: Mandates employers to pay both employer's and employee's contributions, allowing recovery of employee's share from wages but prohibiting deduction of employer's contribution or charges from wages.

key_sections.title: Priority of payment of contributions and bonus over other debts.
key_sections.description: Grants priority to the payment of contributions, bonus, and administration charges over other debts in cases of insolvency or company winding-up.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to exempt coal mines or classes of persons from the Insurance Scheme under certain conditions, particularly if existing benefits are more favourable.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Ordinance 7 of 1948.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Coal Mines Provident Fund and Bonus Schemes Ordinance, 1948, and provides for the deemed validity of actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Frame Coal Mines Provident Fund Scheme, Coal Mines Pension Scheme, Coal Mines Deposit-linked Insurance Scheme, and Coal Mines Bonus Schemes.
Central Government: Specify coal mines to which schemes apply.
Central Government: Constitute a Board of Trustees.
Central Government: Appoint Chairman and members of the Board of Trustees.
Central Government: Appoint Coal Mines Provident Fund Commissioner and other officers.
Central Government: Specify method of recruitment, salary, allowances, discipline, and other conditions of service for the Coal Mines Provident Fund Commissioner.
Central Government: Make special grants to the Family Pension Fund.
Central Government: Determine employer contributions to the Insurance Fund.
Central Government: Modify schemes framed under the Act.
Central Government: Lay schemes before Parliament.
Central Government: Authorize officers to determine moneys due from employers.
Central Government: Appoint Inspectors and define their jurisdiction.
Central Government: Recover amounts due from employers as arrears of land revenue.
Central Government: Delegate powers under the Act or schemes.
Central Government: Recover damages from employers for default in payment.
Central Government: Remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act or schemes.
Central Government: Exempt coal mines or persons from the Insurance Scheme.
Board of Trustees: Administer the Fund, Pension Fund, and Insurance Fund.
Board of Trustees: Perform other functions as required by schemes.
Board of Trustees: Appoint other officers and employees for administration of schemes.
Board of Trustees: Specify method of recruitment, salary, allowances, discipline, and other conditions of service for its officers and employees (with Central Government approval).
Board of Trustees: Delegate powers and functions to its Chairman, Commissioner, or other officers.
Coal Mines Provident Fund Commissioner: Act as chief executive officer of the Board.
Coal Mines Provident Fund Commissioner: Determine the amount due from any employer.
Inspectors: Require information and production of documents from employers or contractors.
Inspectors: Enter and search coal mines.
Inspectors: Examine employers, agents, servants, or employees.
Inspectors: Make copies of, or take extracts from, documents.
Inspectors: Seize documents if an offence is believed to have been committed.
Inspectors: Exercise other powers as provided by schemes.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person contravening provisions of the Act or any scheme thereunder is punishable with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both. For a repeat offence within two years of a previous conviction, the punishment is imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to two thousand rupees, or both. No court inferior to a Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class shall try such offences.

repealed_acts: The Coal Mines Provident Fund and Bonus Schemes Ordinance, 1948
related_acts: Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (19 of 1952)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 (5 of 1970)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairman and members of the Board of Trustees, and the Coal Mines Provident Fund Commissioner and other officers. The Board may appoint other officers and employees.

applies_to: persons employed in Coal Mines
employees
coal mines to which the said scheme shall apply
exemptions: employees or class of employees from joining the Fund or from payment of contributions (as per First Schedule)
any coal mine from the operation of all or any of the provisions of the Insurance Scheme (by Central Government notification)
any person or class of persons employed in any coal mine and covered by the Insurance Scheme from its operation (if benefits are more favourable)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government is empowered to frame schemes (Provident Fund, Pension, Deposit-linked Insurance, Bonus) and to add to, amend, or vary them.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the administration of schemes by the Board of Trustees, determination of dues by the Coal Mines Provident Fund Commissioner, appointment of Inspectors with powers to investigate and seize documents, recovery of dues as arrears of land revenue, and penalties for contraventions.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No Court inferior to that of a Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class shall try offences under the Act. Orders determining amounts due from employers are final and cannot be questioned in any Court of law.

schedules_summary.description: Specifies matters to be provided for in the Coal Mines Provident Fund Scheme, including contributions, administration costs, committee constitution, accounts, withdrawals, interest rates, nominations, and records.

Specifies matters to be provided for in the Coal Mines Pension Scheme, covering applicability, contributions, qualifying service, protection against default, accounts, pension scales, disbursement, and nominations.

Specifies matters to be provided for in the Coal Mines Deposit-linked Insurance Scheme, including coverage, accounts, employee particulars, nominations, registers, insurance amounts, minimum balance, and payment mode.

Specifies matters to be provided for in the Coal Mines Bonus Scheme, including bonus payment based on attendance, eligibility, calculation, conditions for debarment, setting apart sums, records, and transfer of unpaid bonus.

act_identification.act_title: THE DIPLOMATIC AND CONSULAR OFFICERS (OATHS AND FEES) ACT, 1948
act_identification.act_short_title: The Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948

legislative_details.geographical_extent: any State, Union territory of Pondicherry

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the administration of oaths by diplomatic and consular officers and to prescribe the fees leviable in respect of certain of their official duties. WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the administration of oaths by diplomatic and consular officers and for the levy of fees in respect of certain official duties performed by them;
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for diplomatic and consular officers to administer oaths and perform notarial acts in foreign countries. It also establishes provisions for the Central Government to prescribe and regulate fees for their official duties.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as The Diplomatic and Consular Officers (Oaths and Fees) Act, 1948.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'consular officer', 'diplomatic officer', and 'prescribed'.

key_sections.title: Powers as to oaths and notarial acts abroad.
key_sections.description: Empowers diplomatic and consular officers to administer oaths, take affidavits, and perform notarial acts in foreign countries, making such acts as effectual as if done in a State in India.

key_sections.title: Punishment for offences under this Act.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for false swearing in oaths or affidavits and for forging or fraudulently altering seals or signatures related to acts under this Act.

key_sections.title: Trial of offences.
key_sections.description: Specifies that offences under this Act may be inquired into, dealt with, tried, and punished in any State where the accused person was apprehended or is in custody.

key_sections.title: Power to prescribe fees.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to prescribe fees for matters or things done by diplomatic or consular officers in the execution of their office.

key_sections.title: Publication and issue of tables of fees.
key_sections.description: Mandates the publication and gratuitous issue of tables of fees and requires consular and diplomatic officers to exhibit these tables in their offices for public inspection.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including prescribing fee scales, remuneration, registers, and publication methods.

powers_conferred: Diplomatic or consular officer: Administer any oath, take any affidavit, and do any notarial act in any foreign country or place where he is exercising his functions.
Central Government: Prescribe the fees to be levied in respect of any matter or thing done by a diplomatic or consular officer.
Central Government: Make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever swears falsely in any oath or affidavit shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. Whoever forges or fraudulently alters the seal or signature of any person authorised to administer an oath, or uses such forged documents, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.

applies_to: Diplomatic officers
Consular officers
special_provisions: Extended to Union territory of Pondicherry by Act 26 of 1968, s. 3 and the Schedule.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Offences under this Act are inquired into, dealt with, tried, and punished in any State where the person charged was apprehended or is in custody. The Central Government prescribes fees and makes rules for the Act's implementation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any State in which the person charged with the offence was apprehended or is in custody

act_identification.act_title: THE CENSUS ACT, 1948

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for certain matters in connection with the taking of census. WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the taking of census in * * * India or any part thereof whenever necessary or desirable and to provide for certain matters in connection with the taking of such census;
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the taking of census in India or any part thereof whenever necessary or desirable. It also addresses various matters connected with the conduct and administration of such census.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Defines the official short title of the Act and its geographical application.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'premises', 'prescribed', and 'vehicle'.

key_sections.title: Central Government to take census.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to declare its intention to take a census in the whole or any part of the territories to which the Act extends.

key_sections.title: Appointment of census staff.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to appoint a Census Commissioner and Directors of Census Operations, and State Governments to appoint census-officers.

key_sections.title: Staff of every local authority to be made available for taking census.
key_sections.description: Requires local authorities to make their staff available for census duties when directed by the Central Government or its authorized authority.

key_sections.title: Requisitioning premises, of vehicles, etc., for taking of a census.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to requisition premises, vehicles, vessels, or animals for the purpose of taking a census.

key_sections.title: Payment of compensation.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for determining and paying compensation to persons interested in requisitioned premises, vehicles, vessels, or animals.

key_sections.title: Asking of questions and obligation to answer.
key_sections.description: Empowers census officers to ask questions and legally obliges individuals to answer to the best of their knowledge or belief, with certain exceptions for female names.

key_sections.title: Occupier or manager to fill up schedule.
key_sections.description: Requires occupiers of dwelling-houses or managers of establishments to fill up census schedules with particulars regarding inmates or employees.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for various offences such as refusal to perform duties, making false returns, disclosing information, or hindering census operations.

key_sections.title: Records of census not open to inspection of admissible in evidence.
key_sections.description: Ensures that census records are not open to public inspection and are generally inadmissible as evidence in civil or criminal proceedings, except for prosecutions under this Act.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Provides legal protection to census authorities and staff for actions done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act or rules.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including appointment of officers and service of orders.

powers_conferred: Central Government to take census (Section 3)
Central Government to appoint Census Commissioner and Directors of Census Operations (Section 4)
State Government to appoint census-officers (Section 4)
State Government to delegate power of appointing census-officers (Section 4)
District Magistrate or State Government appointed authority to direct officers to perform census duties (Section 6)
District Magistrate or State Government appointed authority to call upon persons to give assistance (Section 7)
Central Government to requisition premises, vehicles, vessels, or animals for census (Section 7A)
Central Government to obtain information for requisitioning or compensation (Section 7C)
Central Government authorized person to enter and inspect premises for requisitioning (Section 7D)
Officer empowered by Central Government to summarily evict from requisitioned premises (Section 7E)
Central Government to delegate functions regarding requisitioning (Section 7G)
Census officer to ask questions (Section 8)
Census officer to access premises and affix numbers (Section 9)
Census officer to leave schedules for filling (Section 10)
Central Government to extend provisions of Act to other operations (Section 17A)
Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act (Section 18)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 11 outlines various offences including refusal to perform duty, hindering operations, intentionally putting offensive questions, making false returns, disclosing information without sanction, damaging census documents, local authority failing to comply with orders, giving false answers, refusing access, removing marks, not filling schedules, and trespassing into a census office. Penalties include a fine up to one thousand rupees, and for certain offences (a, b, or c), also imprisonment up to three years. Abetment of any offence under sub-section (1) is punishable with a fine up to one thousand rupees. Section 7H prescribes imprisonment up to one year or fine or both for contravention of any order regarding requisitioning under Section 7A or 7C.

amended_acts: the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization (Adaptation of Central Laws) Order, 2020
Union Territory of Ladakh Reorganisation (Adaptation of Central Laws) Order, 2020

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government may appoint a Census Commissioner and Directors of Census Operations. The State Government may appoint persons as census-officers and may delegate this power to such authority as it thinks fit.

applies_to: whole of India
officers in command of naval, military or air forces or vessels of war
persons having charge or control of a vessel (except pilot or harbourmaster)
persons in charge of lunatic asylums, hospitals, workhouses, prisons, reformatories, lock-ups, or public/charitable/religious/educational institutions
keepers, secretaries or managers of any sarai, hotel, boarding-house, lodging-house, immigration depot or club
managers or officers of a railway or any commercial or industrial establishment
occupants of immovable property where persons are living
owners and occupiers of land, tenure-holders, farmers and assignees of land revenue, or their agents
members of district, municipal, panchayat and other local authorities and officers and servants of such authorities
officers and members of staff of any factory, firm or establishment
persons occupying any house, enclosure, vessel or other place
exemptions: Pilot or harbourmaster (from duties under Section 6(1)(b))
No person shall be bound to state the name of any female member of his household
No woman shall be bound to state the name of her husband or deceased husband or of any other person whose name she is forbidden by custom to mention
special_provisions: The Act has been extended to Goa, Daman and Diu, Lakshadweep, and the State of Sikkim.
Temporary suspension of other laws as to mode of taking census in municipalities (Section 16).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the appointment of census staff, delegation of duties, requisitioning powers, obligation to answer questions and fill schedules, and penalties for non-compliance. Prosecutions require prior sanction, and certain offences are cognizable and triable summarily. Actions taken in good faith by census staff are protected.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No Court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall try offences under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE OILFIELDS (REGULATION AND DEVELOPMENT) ACT, 1948

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient in the public interest to provide for the regulation of [2]* * * oilfields and for the development of [3][mineral oil resources] [4]* * *; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To provide for the regulation of oilfields and for the development of mineral oil resources in the public interest.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used within the Act, such as 'lessor', 'lessee', 'mine', 'mineral oils', 'mining lease', and 'oilfield'.

key_sections.title: No mining lease to be valid unless it is in accordance with this Act.
key_sections.description: Declares that any mining lease granted after the Act's commencement must conform to its rules, otherwise it is void.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules as respects mining leases.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make rules for regulating the grant of mining leases, including application procedures, terms, conditions, area, period, and rent.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules as respects mineral development.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for the conservation and development of mineral oils, covering aspects like drilling, production methods, storage, and submission of returns.

key_sections.title: Royalties in respect of mineral oils.
key_sections.description: Mandates the payment of royalties on mineral oils as specified in the Schedule, allows the Central Government to amend royalty rates, and provides for exemptions.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules for modification of existing leases.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for modifying existing mining leases to bring them into conformity with the Act, including provisions for notice, compensation, and determination principles.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for contravention of rules made under the Act, and enhanced fines for continuing offences.

key_sections.title: Laying of rules and notifications.
key_sections.description: Requires rules and certain notifications to be laid before each House of Parliament for review and potential modification or annulment.

key_sections.title: Power of inspection.
key_sections.description: Confers powers on authorized officers of the Central Government to enter, inspect mines, demand documents, and examine persons for ascertaining working conditions or other purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Act to be binding on the Government.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act are binding on the Government.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to appoint commencement date (Section 1(3)).
Central Government: Power to make rules for regulating the grant of mining leases (Section 5).
Central Government: Power to make rules for the conservation and development of mineral oils (Section 6).
Central Government: Power to amend the Schedule to enhance or reduce royalty rates (Section 6A(4)).
Central Government: Power to exempt mineral oil from royalty (Section 6A(5)).
Central Government: Power to make rules for modifying or altering terms and conditions of existing mining leases (Section 7).
Central Government: Power to delegate any power exercisable under this Act to an officer or authority (Section 8).
Central Government: Power to authorize officers for inspection purposes (Section 11(1)).
Central Government: Power to authorize the granting of mining leases or working of mines on terms and conditions different from rules in special cases (Section 12).
Officer authorized by Central Government: Right to enter and inspect any mine (Section 11(1)(a)).
Officer authorized by Central Government: Right to order the production of any document, book, register or record (Section 11(1)(b)).
Officer authorized by Central Government: Right to examine any person having control of, or connected with, any mine (Section 11(1)(c)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Rules made under the Act may provide for punishment for contravention with imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both. Continuing offences after first conviction are punishable with a daily fine up to one hundred rupees.

amended_acts: Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957 (67 of 1957)
Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Act, 1969 (39 of 1969)
related_acts: Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government

applies_to: Whole of India
Holders of a mining lease
Owners or lessees of mines
exemptions: No royalty payable in respect of crude oil, casing-head condensate or natural gas which is unavoidably lost or returned to the reservoir or used for drilling/production operations (Section 6A(3)).
Central Government may exempt mineral oil produced from off-shore areas from whole or part of royalty (Section 6A(5)).
special_provisions: Concessional rates of royalty for early commercial production from contract areas awarded under Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (Schedule 1(5), 2(5), 3(4)).
Different royalty rates based on production areas (e.g., on land, shallow water, deep water, ultra deep water) and categories of basins (Category-I, II, III) (Schedule).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Rules made under the Act can prescribe penalties. Authorized officers of the Central Government have powers of inspection, demanding documents, and examining persons.

schedules_summary.description: Details the rates of royalty for Crude Oil, Casing Head Condensate, and Natural Gas. It specifies rates based on production areas (e.g., nomination blocks, NELP regime, Discovered Small Field Policy, Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy), water depths (on land, shallow, deep, ultra deep), and provides for concessional rates for early commercial production. It also includes notes on the calculation of well-head price, post well head cost, and the categorization of sedimentary basins in India.

act_identification.act_title: THE TERRITORIAL ARMY ACT, 1948

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution of a Territorial Army. WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the constitution of Territorial Army;
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the constitution and maintenance of a Territorial Army. It outlines the eligibility, service conditions, and liabilities of its personnel.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and application.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's name, geographical reach, and to whom it applies.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used within the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Territorial Army.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Territorial Army and empowers the Central Government to constitute and manage its units.

key_sections.title: Liability of certain persons for compulsory service in the Territorial Army.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which government or public utility service employees may be compulsorily liable for service.

key_sections.title: Liability for military service.
key_sections.description: Outlines the conditions and circumstances under which officers and enrolled persons are liable to perform military service.

key_sections.title: Reinstatement in civil employ of persons required to perform military service.
key_sections.description: Mandates employers to reinstate persons returning from military service and provides for compensation in case of failure.

key_sections.title: Application of the Army Act, 1950.
key_sections.description: States that officers and enrolled persons are subject to the provisions of the Army Act, 1950, under certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Punishment for failure to lodge forms duly filled up, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for non-compliance with requisitions for service or examination.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Constitute, disband or reconstitute units of the Territorial Army (Section 3)
Central Government: Declare public utility service by notification (Section 2(dd))
Central Government: Issue general or special order for military service beyond India (Section 7)
Central Government: Make adaptations and modifications to the Army Act, 1950 (Section 9)
Central Government: Exempt persons from the operation of this Act by notification (Section 6A Explanation (e))
Central Government: Make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act (Section 14)
President: Grant commissions to officers in the Territorial Army (Section 5)
Prescribed authority: Call upon persons for compulsory service in the Territorial Army (Section 6A(2))
Prescribed authority: Require persons to fill up and lodge forms (Section 6A(4))
Prescribed authority: Require management of public utility service to furnish particulars (Section 6A(5))
Prescribed authority: Summarily punish enrolled persons (Section 10)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Employers failing to obey reinstatement orders are punishable with a fine up to one thousand rupees and may be ordered to pay six months' remuneration (Section 7A(2)). Enrolled persons contravening the Act or rules, or committing offences under the Army Act, 1950, may be punished with a fine up to one hundred rupees (Section 10). Failure to comply with requisitions, report for service, or submit to examination is punishable with imprisonment up to three months, or a fine up to two hundred rupees, or both (Section 10A).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The President grants commissions to officers in the Territorial Army (Section 5). The Central Government constitutes units of the Territorial Army (Section 3).

applies_to: all classes of persons in the Territorial Army, wherever they may be
Any person who is a citizen of India (for enrolment)
every person employed under the Government or in a public utility service who has attained the age of twenty years but has not completed the age of forty years (for compulsory service)
exemptions: a woman (from compulsory service)
a member of the Regular Army, the Navy or the Air Force or a member of any Reserve Force (from compulsory service)
a person who is not a citizen of India (from compulsory service)
a person employed under the Government in any country or place outside India (from compulsory service)
any other persons as may be exempted from the operation of this Act by the Central Government
special_provisions: This Act has been extended to Goa, Daman and Diu, Pondicherry, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and the Union territory of Lakshadweep.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Offences may be tried by criminal courts or summarily by order of the prescribed authority. Persons may be taken into and kept in military custody, tried and punished under the Army Act, 1950. Fines imposed by courts are recoverable as such. Employers failing to reinstate employees are subject to fines and orders to pay compensation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No Court inferior to that of a Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence made punishable by or under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL SILK BOARD ACT, 1948

act_overview.purpose: To provide for the development of the silk industry under Central control and to establish a Central Silk Board for that purpose.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical extent.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to expediency of Union control.
key_sections.description: Declares the expediency of Union control over the silk industry in the public interest.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Central Silk Board as a body corporate and outlines its composition.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Board.
key_sections.description: Details the duties and functions of the Board to promote the development of the silk industry.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Central Silk-worm Seed Committee.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of the Central Silk-worm Seed Committee.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Committee.
key_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities, powers, and functions of the Central Silk-worm Seed Committee.

key_sections.title: Power to notify kinds or varieties of silk-worm seeds.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to notify specific kinds or varieties of silk-worm seeds for regulation.

key_sections.title: Registration Committee.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Registration Committee and mandates registration for silk-worm seed producers and dealers.

key_sections.title: Funds of the Board.
key_sections.description: Describes the funding mechanism and expenditure rules for the Board.

key_sections.title: Imposition of cess on certain kinds of silk.
key_sections.description: Provides for the levy and collection of a cess on filature raw silk and spun silk.

key_sections.title: Control by the Central Government.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Central Government's control over the acts and orders of the Board.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Silk-worm Seed Committee the power to make regulations.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for making false statements, obstructing officers, or failing to produce records.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of sections 8C and 8E.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravening provisions related to notified silk-worm seeds and registration.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To make nominations for Board members (Sec 5), to control the Board (Sec 11), to make rules (Sec 13), to notify kinds or varieties of silk-worm seeds (Sec 8C), to specify terms for export and import of silk-worm seed (Sec 8-I), to permit import for research purposes (Sec 8-I), to restrict export or import of silk-worm seed (Sec 8-I).

Board: To acquire, hold, and dispose of property, to contract, to sue and be sued (Sec 4(2)), to constitute a Standing Committee (Sec 6(2)), to promote the development of the silk industry (Sec 8(1)), to undertake, assist or encourage scientific, technological and economic research (Sec 8(2)(a)), to devise means for improved methods of mulberry cultivation, rearing, developing and distributing healthy silkworm seeds, reeling or spinning of silkworm cocoons and silk waste (Sec 8(2)(b)), to improve marketing of raw silk (Sec 8(2)(d)), to collect statistics (Sec 8(2)(e)), to advise the Central Government on matters relating to silk industry (Sec 8(3)(a)), to prepare and furnish reports (Sec 8(3)(c)).

Central Silk-worm Seed Committee: To implement the Act (Sec 8B(1)), to lay down quality standards for silk-worm seed (Sec 8B(2)(i), (iii)), to authorise silk-worm races and hybrids (Sec 8B(2)(ii)), to lay down conditions for production facilities (Sec 8B(2)(iv)), to lay down certification and testing procedures (Sec 8B(2)(v)), to undertake registration of producers and dealers (Sec 8B(2)(vi)), to lay down conditions for export and import (Sec 8B(2)(vii)), to program and plan silk-worm seed production (Sec 8B(2)(viii)), to advise governments (Sec 8B(2)(ix)), to make regulations (Sec 13A).
Hybrid Authorisation Committee: To recommend kinds or varieties of silk-worm seed, hybrid seeds and races for notification (Sec 8D(2)).
Registration Committee: To register silk-worm seed of notified kind or variety (Sec 8E(3)(a)), to register silk-worm seed producers (Sec 8E(3)(b)), to register silk-worm dealers (Sec 8E(3)(c)).
Silk-worm Seed Certification Agencies: To conduct inspection for registration of producers and dealers (Sec 8F).
Central Seed Testing Laboratories: To carry out functions entrusted by the Committee (Sec 8G(2)).
Seed Officers: To inspect seeds and facilities of producers and dealers (Sec 8H(2)), to take samples of silk-worm seed (Sec 8H(3)(a)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 14 prescribes penalties for making false statements in returns, obstructing officers, or failing to produce account books or records, punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both. Section 14A prescribes a fine of five thousand to twenty-five thousand rupees, besides suspension or cancellation of registration, for contravention of sections 8C and 8E or related regulations/notifications concerning silk-worm seed.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson of the Board, nominates officials and other members to the Board, and makes nominations in default of other governments. The Committee appoints Seed Analysts and Seed Officers.

applies_to: whole of India
persons involved in the silk industry
producers of silk-worm seed
dealers of silk-worm seed
reelers of filature raw silk or spun silk

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for rules), Central Silk-worm Seed Committee (for regulations).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the functions of the Central Silk Board and its committees, including inspection by Seed Officers, imposition of cess, and penalties for contraventions. The Central Government exercises control over the Board's acts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District Judge or such other civil judicial officer for appeals against cess assessment.

act_identification.act_title: THE FACTORIES ACT, 1948

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law regulating labour in factories. WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law regulating labour in factories; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To consolidate and amend the law regulating labour in factories.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER IVA PROVISION RELATING TO HAZARDOUS PROCESSES
CHAPTER VI WORKING HOURS OF ADULTS
CHAPTER VII EMPLOYMENT OF YOUNG PERSONS
CHAPTER VIII ANNUAL LEAVE WITH WAGES

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Interpretation.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'adult', 'child', 'factory', and 'occupier'.

key_sections.title: Approval, licensing and registration of factories.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to make rules for the approval, licensing, and registration of factories.

key_sections.title: General duties of the occupier.
key_sections.description: Outlines the occupier's responsibility for the health, safety, and welfare of workers in the factory.

key_sections.title: Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of Inspectors and Chief Inspectors by the State Government to enforce the Act.

key_sections.title: Cleanliness.
key_sections.description: Mandates that every factory must be kept clean and free from effluvia, specifying cleaning procedures.

key_sections.title: Fencing of machinery.
key_sections.description: Requires secure fencing for moving parts of machinery to ensure worker safety.

key_sections.title: Precautions in case of fire.
key_sections.description: Requires measures to prevent fire outbreaks, provide means of escape, and equip for fire extinguishing.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Site Appraisal Committees.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of committees to advise on applications for factories involving hazardous processes.

key_sections.title: Compulsory disclosure of information by the occupier.
key_sections.description: Mandates occupiers of factories with hazardous processes to disclose information regarding dangers and safety measures.

key_sections.title: First-aid appliances.
key_sections.description: Requires the provision and maintenance of first-aid boxes and ambulance rooms in factories.

key_sections.title: Creches.
key_sections.description: Mandates the provision of suitable rooms for children of women workers in factories employing a certain number of women.

key_sections.title: Weekly hours.
key_sections.description: Sets the maximum weekly working hours for adult workers in a factory.

key_sections.title: Extra wages for overtime.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that workers are entitled to double their ordinary rate of wages for overtime work.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of employment of young children.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the employment of children below the age of fourteen years in any factory.

key_sections.title: Annual leave with wages.
key_sections.description: Details the entitlement of workers to annual leave with wages based on days worked.

key_sections.title: Dangerous operations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to make rules for manufacturing processes or operations that pose serious risks to workers.

key_sections.title: General penalty for offences.
key_sections.description: Prescribes general penalties for contraventions of the Act or rules made thereunder.

powers_conferred: State Government may declare different departments to be separate factories or two or more factories to be a single factory (Section 4)
State Government may exempt any factory or class or description of factories from provisions during public emergency (Section 5)
State Government may make rules for approval, licensing and registration of factories (Section 6)
State Government may appoint Inspectors and Chief Inspectors (Section 8)
Inspectors have powers to enter, examine, inquire, seize documents, and direct actions (Section 9)
State Government may appoint certifying surgeons (Section 10)
State Government may make rules prescribing arrangements for disposal of wastes and effluents (Section 12)
State Government may prescribe standards for ventilation and temperature (Section 13)
State Government may make rules for artificial humidification (Section 15)
Chief Inspector may exempt workrooms from overcrowding provisions (Section 16)
State Government may make rules for drinking water (Section 18)
State Government may prescribe number of latrines and urinals (Section 19)
State Government may make rules for spittoons (Section 20)
State Government may prescribe further precautions for machinery or exempt certain machinery (Section 21)
State Government may prohibit cleaning/lubricating of machinery parts in motion (Section 22)
State Government may prescribe machines dangerous for young persons (Section 23)
State Government may make rules specifying further safeguards for machinery (Section 26)
Chief Inspector may permit continued use of non-compliant hoists/lifts (Section 28)
State Government may make rules for lifting machines, chains, ropes and lifting tackles (Section 29)
State Government may make rules for pressure plant (Section 31)
State Government may exempt factories from pit/sump covering provisions (Section 33)
State Government may make rules prescribing maximum weights to be lifted (Section 34)
State Government may make rules for protection of eyes (Section 35)
State Government may exempt factories from dangerous fumes/gas provisions (Section 37)
Chief Inspector may require additional fire precautions (Section 38)
Inspector may require specifications of defective parts or tests of stability (Section 39)
Inspector may serve orders regarding safety of buildings and machinery (Section 40)
Inspector may serve orders regarding maintenance of buildings (Section 40A)
State Government may make rules to supplement safety chapter (Section 41)
State Government may constitute Site Appraisal Committees (Section 41A)
Central Government may appoint Inquiry Committee (Section 41D)
Central Government may direct laying down of emergency standards (Section 41E)
Central Government may make changes in the Second Schedule (Section 41F)
State Government may make rules for washing facilities (Section 42)
State Government may make rules for storing and drying clothing (Section 43)
Chief Inspector may require seating arrangements (Section 44)
State Government may make rules for canteens (Section 46)
State Government may make rules for shelters, rest rooms and lunch rooms (Section 47)
State Government may make rules for creches (Section 48)
State Government may prescribe duties, qualifications and conditions of service of Welfare Officers (Section 49)
State Government may make rules to supplement welfare chapter (Section 50)
Chief Inspector may approve exceeding daily maximum hours for shift changes (Section 54)
State Government or Chief Inspector may exempt from intervals for rest (Section 55)
Chief Inspector may increase spread over hours (Section 56)
State Government or Chief Inspector may exempt from prohibition of overlapping shifts (Section 58)
State Government may make rules for computing cash equivalent of concessional sales (Section 59)
State Government may make rules defining persons in supervision/management and exempt them from certain provisions (Section 64)
State Government may make exempting orders for adult workers (Section 65)
State Government may vary limits for women's working hours (Section 66)
State Government may make rules for exemption of women in fish-curing/canning factories (Section 66)
Certifying surgeon may grant/renew/revoke certificates of fitness (Section 69)
State Government may vary limits for female adolescent/male adolescent working hours (Section 70)
State Government may make rules for certificates of fitness and other duties of certifying surgeons (Section 76)
State Government may exempt factories from annual leave with wages provisions (Section 84)
State Government may apply the Act to certain premises (Section 85)
State Government may exempt public institutions (Section 86)
State Government may make rules for dangerous operations (Section 87)
Inspector may prohibit employment on account of serious hazard (Section 87A)
State Government may make rules for regulating procedure at inquiries into accidents (Section 88)
Central Government may add to or alter the Third Schedule (Section 89)
State Government may appoint competent person to inquire into accidents or diseases (Section 90)
Inspector may take samples (Section 91)

Chief Inspector, Director General of Factory Advice Service and Labour Institutes, Director General of Health Services, or authorized officers may undertake safety and occupational health surveys (Section 91A)
Court may require occupier/manager to remedy matters for which offence was committed (Section 102)
State Government may make rules prescribing manner of service of orders (Section 109)
State Government may make rules requiring submission of returns (Section 110)
State Government may make rules for any matter to be prescribed (Section 112)
Central Government may give directions to State Governments (Section 113)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: General penalty for offences (Section 92) includes imprisonment up to two years or fine up to one lakh rupees, with further fine for continuing contravention. Enhanced penalty after previous conviction (Section 94) includes imprisonment up to three years or fine not less than ten thousand rupees up to two lakh rupees. Specific penalties for obstructing Inspector (Section 95), wrongfully disclosing analysis results (Section 96), contravention of hazardous process provisions (Section 96A) with imprisonment up to seven years and fine up to two lakh rupees, offences by workers (Section 97) with fine up to five hundred rupees, using false certificate of fitness (Section 98) with imprisonment up to two months or fine up to one thousand rupees, and permitting double employment of child (Section 99) with fine up to one thousand rupees. Workers contravening obligations under Section 111 are punishable with imprisonment up to three months or fine up to one hundred rupees.

related_acts: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 (6 of 1974)
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 (14 of 1981)
Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867 (25 of 1867)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government appoints Inspectors, Chief Inspector, Additional Chief Inspectors, Joint Chief Inspectors, Deputy Chief Inspectors, other officers to assist Chief Inspector, and Certifying Surgeons. Central Government appoints Inquiry Committee.
regulatory_bodies: Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution
Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution
State Board (Water Prevention and Control of Pollution)
State Board (Air Prevention and Control of Pollution)
Meteorological Department of the Government of India
Town Planning Department of the State Government
Director-General of Factory Advice Service and Labour Institutes

applies_to: Factories
Labour in factories
Whole of India
exemptions: State Government may exempt any factory or class or description of factories from all or any provisions during public emergency (Section 5).
State Government may exempt factories from cleanliness provisions (Section 11(2)).
State Government may exempt any particular machinery or part thereof from fencing provisions (Section 21(2)).
Chief Inspector may permit continued use of non-compliant hoists/lifts installed before commencement of Act (Section 28(3)).
State Government may exempt class or description of hoist or lift from certain requirements (Section 28(4)).
State Government may exempt any factory or class or description of factories from dangerous fumes/gas provisions (Section 37(5)).
State Government may exempt any factory or class or description of factories from welfare provisions (Section 50(a)).
State Government may make rules for exemption of workers from weekly holidays, daily hours, intervals for rest, spread over (Section 64).
State Government may make exempting orders for adult workers from certain working hour provisions (Section 65).
State Government may make rules for exemption of women working in fish-curing or fish-canning factories from restrictions on employment hours (Section 66(2)).
State Government may exempt factories from annual leave with wages provisions (Section 84).
State Government may exempt public institutions from all or any provisions of the Act (Section 86).
Chief Inspector may exempt occupier of any factory or class of factories from setting up a Safety Committee (Section 41G).
special_provisions: State amendments for Maharashtra, Ladakh, Jammu and Kashmir, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan regarding the definition of 'factory' by altering the number of workers for applicability (Section 2(m)).
State amendment for Arunachal Pradesh inserting Section 5A allowing exemption for new factories to create economic activities and employment opportunities.
State amendment for Tamil Nadu inserting Section 7-AA requiring occupier of Match or Fire Works Factory to insure workers.
State amendment for Karnataka reducing the worker threshold for first-aid appliances (Section 45) and welfare officers (Section 49).
State amendments for Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh altering the maximum overtime hours in a quarter (Section 64(4)(iv) and Section 65(3)(iv)).
State amendments for Maharashtra, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, and Uttar Pradesh regarding the employment of women during night shifts (Section 66(1)(b)).
State amendment for Maharashtra altering the number of days for annual leave with wages eligibility (Section 79(1)).
State amendments for Maharashtra, Arunachal Pradesh, and Rajasthan altering the number of persons for applying the Act to certain premises (Section 85(1)(i)).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: State Government (for various provisions including licensing, health, safety, welfare, working hours, employment of young persons, annual leave, special provisions, and general matters). Central Government (for changes in the Second Schedule and directing emergency standards).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced by Inspectors and Chief Inspectors appointed by the State Government, who have powers of entry, examination, inquiry, and seizure. Certifying surgeons are appointed for medical examinations. Penalties are prescribed for contraventions, and courts can issue orders for compliance. Appeals against Inspector's orders can be made to prescribed authorities or the High Court.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No Court below that of a Presidency Magistrate or of a Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act. High Court for appeals against Inspector's order under Section 87A.

schedules_summary.description: Lists industries involving hazardous processes, including various metallurgical, chemical, and manufacturing industries.
Specifies permissible levels of certain chemical substances in the work environment, including time-weighted average concentrations and short-term exposure limits.
Lists notifiable diseases, which are occupational diseases that must be reported, such as various poisonings, skin conditions, and respiratory diseases.

act_identification.act_title: THE RESERVE BANK (TRANSFER TO PUBLIC OWNERSHIP) ACT, I948
act_identification.act_short_title: the Reserve Bank (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948

act_overview.preamble: An Act to bring the share capital of the Reserve Bank of India into public ownership and to make consequential amendments in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. WHEREAS it is expedient to bring the share capital of the Reserve Bank of India into public ownership, to make provisions with respect to the relations between the Central Government and the Bank and to make consequential amendments in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to transfer the share capital of the Reserve Bank of India into public ownership. It also aims to make provisions regarding the relations between the Central Government and the Bank and to introduce consequential amendments to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'the Reserve Bank (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948'.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Bank', and 'principal Act'.

key_sections.title: Transfer of Bank shares.
key_sections.description: Mandates the transfer of all shares in the capital of the Bank to the Central Government on the appointed day and outlines the compensation mechanism for shareholders.

key_sections.title: Vacation of office by existing office bearers.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that existing Directors and Local Board members (excluding Governor/Deputy Governor) vacate office on the appointed day, and new boards are constituted as per the principal Act.

key_sections.title: Interim arrangements.
key_sections.description: Provides for the Governor or a nominated Deputy Governor to exercise the Bank's powers, subject to Central Government conditions, pending the constitution of the Central Board.

key_sections.title: Rule-making power.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make rules for implementing the Act, particularly concerning compensation payment and determination of beneficiaries.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to appoint the 'appointed day'.
Central Government: to issue promissory notes as compensation to shareholders.
Central Government: to specify the repayment date for promissory notes.
Central Government: to impose restrictions and conditions on the Governor or Deputy Governor regarding interim arrangements.
Central Government: to make rules for the purpose of giving effect to the objects of this Act.
Central Government: to make rules for the manner and authority by which compensation shall be paid.
Central Government: to make rules for the determination of persons to whom compensation is payable.

Governor of the Bank (or nominated Deputy Governor): to exercise all powers and do all acts and things which may be exercised or done by the Bank, pending the constitution of the Central Board, subject to Central Government restrictions and conditions.

applies_to: all shares in the capital of the Bank
every person who, immediately before the appointed day, is registered as the holder of any such shares
any Director of the Bank

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government appoints the 'appointed day' for share transfer and compensation, and makes rules for implementation. The Governor or a nominated Deputy Governor can make interim arrangements.

schedules_summary.description: This schedule was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1950 (35 of 1950) with effect from 10-04-1950.

act_identification.act_title: THE DELHI AND AJMER-MERWARA LAND DEVELOPMENT ACT, 1948
act_identification.act_short_title: the Delhi and Ajmer-Merwara Land Development Act, 1948

act_overview.preamble:
An Act to provide for the preparation and execution of land development schemes, the
 reclamation of waste-land and the control of private forests and grass-land, in the Provinces of Delhi and Ajmer-Merwara.
WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the preparation and execution of land development schemes,
the reclamation of waste-land and the control of private forests and grass-land in the Provinces of Delhi
and Ajmer-Merwara;
It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to facilitate the preparation and execution of land development schemes, including the reclamation of waste-land. It also aims to control private forests and grass-land in the States of Delhi and Ajmer to promote public welfare and agricultural improvement.

chapter_titles: Land Development Boards and Land Development Schemes
Control over Forests and Lands not being the Property of Government

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its geographical extent to Delhi and Ajmer, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Chief Commissioner.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Board', 'owner', 'prescribed', 'reclamation', and 'tenant'.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Land Development Boards.
key_sections.description: Mandates the appointment of a Land Development Commissioner and the constitution of a Land Development Board by the Chief Commissioner.

key_sections.title: Matters for which land development schemes may provide.
key_sections.description: Outlines the various matters, such as soil preservation, erosion prevention, water supply improvement, and land reclamation, that land development schemes can address.

key_sections.title: Inquiry into, and sanctioning of, schemes.
key_sections.description: Details the process for inquiry into and sanctioning of land development schemes by the Chief Commissioner and the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of specified provisions of schemes or regulations, including imprisonment or fine.

key_sections.title: Works to be carried out by Government at owner’s expense.
key_sections.description: Allows the Land Development Commissioner to carry out works at the owner's expense if the owner fails to do so, with recovery as arrears of land revenue.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals against certain determinations of the Board or orders of the Land Development Commissioner or Revenue Officer to a prescribed authority.

key_sections.title: Order for taking possession of waste-land.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Board to direct the Land Development Commissioner to take temporary possession of waste-land for reclamation purposes.

key_sections.title: Compensation for period of possession.
key_sections.description: Establishes the mechanism for determining and paying compensation to owners and tenants for the period during which waste-land is under government possession for reclamation.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Act XVI of 1927 in Delhi.
key_sections.description: Specifies amendments to the Indian Forest Act, 1927, as it applies to the State of Delhi, particularly concerning control over forests and waste-land.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including specific matters.

powers_conferred: Chief Commissioner: Appoint Land Development Commissioner, constitute Land Development Board, remove Board members, invest Commissioner with powers of Deputy Commissioner or Collector, appoint Inquiry Officer, remit contributions, hear appeals.
Land Development Commissioner: Make grants or advance loans, carry out works at owner's expense, take temporary possession of waste-land, arrange for reclamation, determine compensation.
Land Development Board: Prepare land development schemes, make regulations, determine contributions, approve statements and maps, decide amount of net expenditure to be recovered.
Central Government: Sanction land development schemes, call for reports and give directions to the Board, make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of specified provisions of a scheme or regulations made under Section 7 may be punishable with simple imprisonment for up to one month, or a fine up to fifty rupees, or both. Prosecution requires a complaint in writing by the Land Development Commissioner.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Chief Commissioner appoints the Land Development Commissioner and constitutes the Land Development Board.

applies_to: States of Delhi and Ajmer
Owners of land
Tenants of land
special_provisions: Amendment of the Indian Forest Act, 1927, in its application to the State of Delhi (Section 30).
Application of Chapter V of the Indian Forest Act, 1927, to the State of Ajmer (Section 31).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Land development schemes are prepared by the Board, sanctioned by the Central Government, and executed by the Land Development Commissioner. Expenses and contributions are recoverable as arrears of land revenue. An appeals mechanism is provided for aggrieved persons. The Land Development Commissioner initiates prosecutions for contraventions.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Decisions of the prescribed appeal authorities are final and cannot be questioned in any court. Claims for arrears of rent cannot be enforced against the Government or persons holding land under the Government. Prosecutions for contraventions are initiated by the Land Development Commissioner, implying jurisdiction of criminal courts. Suits against the Government for actions taken in good faith under the Act are barred.

act_identification.act_title: THE MANGROL AND MANAVADAR (ADMINISTRATION OF PROPERTY) ACT, 1949
act_identification.act_short_title: the Mangrol and Manavadar (Administration of Property) Act, 1949

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Properties belonging to the States of Mangrol and Manavadar in Kathiawar

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS the administration of the States of Mangrol and Manavadar has been taken over by the Central Government; AND WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the vesting of certain properties belonging to the said States in the Managers thereof appointed by or on behalf of the Central Government and for certain matters incidental thereto;
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the vesting of certain properties belonging to the States of Mangrol and Manavadar in Kathiawar in the Managers of the said States. Its main objective is to facilitate the administration of these properties by Managers appointed by or on behalf of the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Mangrol and Manavadar (Administration of Property) Act, 1949.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines 'Manager' as the Manager for the time being of the State of Mangrol or Manavadar, appointed by or on behalf of the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Vesting of property in Manager.
key_sections.description: States that properties described in the Schedule, standing in the name of the Sheikh of Mangrol, Khan of Manavadar, Begum Sahiban Fatma, or any officer, are deemed to have vested in the Manager of the respective State from 1st November, 1947.

key_sections.title: Powers of Manager.
key_sections.description: Grants the Manager all rights, powers, and authority of a full owner over properties vested in him, with a proviso that he is bound by the terms of any lawfully created trust.

key_sections.title: Issue of duplicate securities.
key_sections.description: Allows the Manager to apply to the Reserve Bank of India for duplicate Government securities described in the Schedule if the originals are not in his custody, and mandates the Reserve Bank to issue them.

key_sections.title: Transfers otherwise than by Manager void.
key_sections.description: Declares any transfer or disposition of scheduled property made on or after 1st November, 1947, by any person other than the Manager or without his consent, as void and of no effect.

key_sections.title: Power to call for information.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to require information from any person in possession of property belonging to the States and prescribes penalties for non-compliance.

key_sections.title: Bar of jurisdiction of Court.
key_sections.description: Bars courts from entertaining civil or criminal proceedings related to scheduled properties, except at the instance of the Manager, and makes the Central Government's decision on claims final.

key_sections.title: Power of the Central Government to add to the Schedule.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to amend, alter, or add items of property to the Schedule by notification in the Official Gazette.

key_sections.title: Bar of legal proceedings.
key_sections.description: Protects the Central Government, Reserve Bank of India, banks, companies, the Manager, and other persons from legal proceedings for actions done in good faith under the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Mangrol and Manavadar (Administration of Property) Ordinance, 1948, and retrospectively validates actions taken under the Ordinance as if taken under this Act from 16th August, 1948.

powers_conferred: Manager: To have and exercise all rights, powers and authority which a full owner has or exercises in relation to his own property (Section 4).
Manager: To make an application to the Reserve Bank of India for the issue of a duplicate security (Section 6(1)).
Central Government: To require any person to furnish information regarding property belonging to the State of Mangrol or Manavadar (Section 8(1)).
Central Government: To amend or alter the Schedule by notification in the Official Gazette (Section 10(1)).

legislative_details.geographical_extent: West Godavari District of the Province of Madras, specifically the Eluru Taluk and the scheduled area within it

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS by virtue of the Madras Partially Excluded Area (Cesser) Order, 1948, made under section 91 of the Government of India Act, 1935, the area comprised in the villages specified in Article 2 of the said Order ceased, as from the 1st day of July, 1948, to be part of a partially excluded area in the West Godavari District of the Province of Madras; AND WHEREAS it is expedient that the laws in force in the said area with respect to the matters enumerated in List I in the Seventh Schedule to the Government of India Act, 1935 (25 and 26 Geo. 5, c. 2), should be assimilated to the laws in force with respect to the said matters in the rest of the said district; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to assimilate laws in force in a specific 'partially excluded area' (scheduled area) of the West Godavari District with the laws in force in the rest of the district, specifically concerning matters enumerated in List I of the Seventh Schedule to the Government of India Act, 1935. This ensures uniformity of laws in the region.

key_sections.title: Provision for removal of difficulties.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government, leading to the automatic assimilation of laws. The Central Government can issue orders to resolve transitional difficulties.

powers_conferred: Council: manage affairs of the Institute and discharge functions assigned under the Act (Sec 9(1)); approve academic courses and their contents; prescribe fees for examination; grant or refuse registration of a firm; prescribe qualifications for entry in the Register of members; recognize foreign qualifications and training; prescribe guidelines for grant or refusal of certificates of practice; issue guidelines for carrying out the objects of the Act; levy fees from members, examinees and other persons; regulate and maintain status and standard of professional qualifications; carry out research in accountancy; conduct investor education and awareness programmes; enter into memorandum or arrangement with foreign agencies (with Central Government approval); enable functioning of disciplinary bodies and Quality Review Board; consider recommendations of Quality Review Board; ensure functioning of the Institute (Sec 15).

Central Government: nominate members to the Council (Sec 9(2)(b), 11); specify conditions for foreign qualifications (Sec 4(1)(v)); remove disability for convicted persons (Sec 8(v)); establish a Tribunal for election disputes (Sec 10B); make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act (Sec 29A); direct the Council to make, amend or revoke regulations (Sec 30A); frame first regulations (Sec 30(4)); issue general or special directions to the Council (Sec 30C); dissolve the Council in case of persistent default (Sec 30C(2)); appoint Chairperson and members of Appellate Authority (Sec 22A); appoint Chairperson and members of Quality Review Board (Sec 28A).
Director (Discipline): make investigations in respect of information or complaints and form a prima facie opinion on alleged misconduct (Sec 21).
Board of Discipline: reprimand a member, remove name from Register up to three months, impose fine up to one lakh rupees (Sec 21A(3)).
Disciplinary Committee: reprimand a member, remove name from Register permanently or for a period, impose fine up to five lakh rupees (Sec 21B(3)).
Appellate Authority: confirm, modify or set aside orders; impose, set aside, reduce, or enhance penalties; remit cases for further enquiry; pass other orders (Sec 22G(2)).

Quality Review Board: make recommendations to the Council regarding quality of services; review quality of services; guide members to improve quality; forward cases of non-compliance to Disciplinary Directorate (Sec 28B).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalty for falsely claiming to be a member or practicing without a certificate: fine up to one lakh rupees on first conviction, and imprisonment up to six months or fine up to five lakh rupees or both on subsequent conviction (Sec 24). Penalty for using the name of the Council, awarding degrees of chartered accountancy, or regulating the profession: imprisonment up to six months or fine not less than one lakh rupees but up to five lakh rupees or both on first conviction, and imprisonment up to one year or fine not less than two lakh rupees but up to ten lakh rupees or both on subsequent conviction (Sec 24A). Companies practicing as chartered accountants: fine not less than two lakh rupees but up to ten lakh rupees on first conviction, and fine not less than four lakh rupees but up to twenty lakh rupees on subsequent conviction (Sec 25). Unqualified persons signing documents: fine not less than one lakh rupees but up to five lakh rupees on first conviction, and imprisonment up to one year or fine not less than two lakh rupees but up to ten lakh rupees or both on second or subsequent conviction (Sec 26). Professional misconduct under the First Schedule: reprimand, removal of name from Register up to three months, or fine up to one lakh rupees (Sec 21A(3)). Professional misconduct under the Second Schedule or both Schedules: reprimand, permanent or temporary removal of name from Register, or fine up to five lakh rupees (Sec 21B(3)).
