act_identification.act_short_title: The Industrial Disputes (Banking and Insurance Companies) Act, 1949

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the adjudication of industrial disputes concerning banking and insurance companies having branches or other establishments in more than one State; It is hereby enacted as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To provide for the adjudication of industrial disputes concerning banking and insurance companies. Specifically, it addresses disputes involving companies with branches or establishments in more than one State.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms by referencing Section 2 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of references by State Governments of certain industrial disputes for adjudication, inquiry or settlement.
key_sections.description: Prohibits State Governments or their subordinate authorities from referring industrial disputes concerning banking or insurance companies for adjudication, inquiry, or settlement.

key_sections.title: Abatement of proceedings relating to disputes pending before State tribunals and reference of such disputes to tribunals constituted by the Central Government.
key_sections.description: Provides for the abatement of proceedings related to banking and insurance company disputes pending before State tribunals and mandates their reference to Industrial Tribunals constituted by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Powers of Central Government to refer disputes in respect of which awards or decisions have been made for adjudication.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to refer disputes for adjudication even if previous awards or decisions exist, and to stay or declare such awards inoperative.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Ordinance 28 of 1949.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Industrial Disputes (Banking and Insurance Companies) Second Ordinance, 1949, while saving actions taken under it.

powers_conferred: Central Government to refer industrial disputes to an Industrial Tribunal for adjudication (Section 5(2))
Central Government to refer disputes for adjudication even if awards or decisions have been made (Section 6(1))
Central Government to stay the implementation of awards or decisions (Section 6(1))
Central Government to declare previous awards or decisions inoperative (Section 6(2))

repealed_acts: The Industrial Disputes (Banking and Insurance Companies) Second Ordinance, 1949 (28 of 1949)

applies_to: industrial disputes concerning banking or insurance companies
banking and insurance companies having branches or other establishments in more than one State
exemptions: State of Jammu and Kashmir (as per original enactment)
special_provisions: The Act has been extended to the Scheduled Areas of the State of Orissa by Orissa Reg. 1 of 1956
The Act has been amended in U.P. by U.P. Act 25 of 1951
The Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh by Notification No. S.O. 3912 (E), dated 30th October, 2019

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Adjudication of industrial disputes by Industrial Tribunals constituted under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, with the Central Government having powers to refer disputes and manage awards.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Industrial Tribunal constituted under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947

act_identification.act_title: THE POLICE ACT, 1949
act_identification.date_of_commencement: It shall come into force in a [4][Union territory] on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint in this behalf for [5][such territory].

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution of a general police-district embracing two or more [2][Union territories] and for the establishment of a police force therefor. WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the constitution of a general police-district embracing two or more [2][Union territories] and for the establishment of a police force therefor;
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the constitution of a general police-district encompassing two or more Union territories. Its main objective is to establish a unified police force for such a district.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its geographical extent to Union territories, and that its commencement date will be appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines the term 'general police-district' as constituted under section 3 of this Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution of general police-district embracing two or more Union territories.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to constitute a general police-district covering two or more Union territories, notwithstanding the Police Act, 1861.

key_sections.title: Constitution of one police force for general police-district.
key_sections.description: States that the police establishment in a general police-district shall form a single police force, with its composition and constitution directed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Superintendence and administration of police.
key_sections.description: Vests the superintendence of the police in the Central Government and the administration in an officer appointed by the Central Government, who exercises powers similar to an Inspector-General of Police under the Police Act, 1861.

key_sections.title: Application of the Police Act, 1861.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the provisions of the Police Act, 1861, apply to the police force constituted under this Act, granting its members powers, duties, privileges, and liabilities as if it were a State police force.

key_sections.title: Saving.
key_sections.description: Ensures that nothing in this Act affects the provisions of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint commencement date for Union territories (Section 1(3))
Central Government to constitute a general police-district (Section 3)
Central Government to direct the number of officers and men and the manner of constitution of the police force (Section 4)
Central Government to exercise superintendence of the police (Section 5(1))
Central Government to appoint an officer for the administration of the police force (Section 5(2))
Central Government to specify powers exercisable by the appointed officer (Section 5(2))

related_acts: the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946 (25 of 1946)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (for an officer to administer the police force)

applies_to: all the [3][Union territories]
special_provisions: Extended to Goa, Daman and Diu with modifications by Reg. 12 of 1962, s. 3 and the Schedule.
Comes into force in Pondicherry on 01/10/1963 vide Reg. 7 of 1963, s. 3 and First Schedule.
Comes into force in Dadra and Nagar Haveli (w.e.f. 01/07/1965) by Reg. 6 of 1963, s. 2 and Schedule.
Comes into force in Lakshadweep vide Reg. 8 of 1965, s. 3 and Schedule (w.e.f. 01/10/1967).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced through the police force constituted for the general police-district, under the superintendence and administration of the Central Government and an officer appointed by it.

act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL RESERVE POLICE FORCE ACT, 1949

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed Central Reserve Police Force.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

chapter_titles: GENERAL DUTIES OF MEMBERS OF THE FORCE
SUPERINTENDENCE CONTROL AND ADMINISTRATION OF THE FORCE

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical extent of application.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Force.
key_sections.description: Establishes the continuation of the Central Reserve Police Force and its constitution.

key_sections.title: Resignation and withdrawal from the Force.
key_sections.description: Lays down conditions under which a member of the Force may resign or withdraw from duties.

key_sections.title: General duties of members of the Force.
key_sections.description: Outlines the general duties and liabilities of members of the Force, including serving within and beyond India.

key_sections.title: Superintendence, control and administration of the Force.
key_sections.description: Vests superintendence and control in the Central Government and specifies administration details.

key_sections.title: More heinous offences.
key_sections.description: Defines serious offences committed by members of the Force and prescribes their punishments.

key_sections.title: Less heinous offences.
key_sections.description: Defines less serious offences committed by members of the Force and prescribes their punishments.

key_sections.title: Minor punishments.
key_sections.description: Details the types of minor punishments that can be awarded by various officers for disobedience or misconduct.

key_sections.title: Powers and duties conferrable and imposable on members of the Force.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to confer police officer powers and invest officers with Magistrate powers for certain offences.

key_sections.title: Protection for acts of members of the Force.
key_sections.description: Provides protection to members of the Force for acts done in pursuance of warrants or orders, and sets limitation periods for legal proceedings.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes, including specific matters.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint Commandant, assistant commandants and company officers (Section 4(1))
Central Government: Superintendence and control over the Force (Section 8(1))
Central Government: Specify headquarters of the Force (Section 8(2))
Central Government: Confer or impose powers or duties of a police officer on members of the Force (Section 16(1))
Central Government: Invest Commandant or assistant commandant with powers of a Magistrate (Section 16(2))
Central Government: Make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 18(1))
Commandant: Appoint persons to the Force (Section 2(d))
Commandant: Grant permission for resignation or withdrawal from the Force (Section 6(b))
Commandant: Award minor punishments (Section 11(1))
Commandant: Order forfeiture of pay, allowance and other moneys (Section 12(1))
Commandant: Direct confinement in quarter-guard or other suitable place (Section 12(2))
Commandant: Impose collective fines (Section 14)
Officers appointed under Section 4(1): Exercise powers and authority as provided by or under the Act (Section 4(2))
Gazetted officer (in command of detachment away from headquarters): Award specific minor punishments (Section 11(2))
Assistant commandant, company officer or subordinate officer (subedar or inspector) commanding a separate detachment or outpost: Award specific minor punishments (Section 11(3))
Jemadar or sub-inspector (temporarily in command of a detachment or outpost): Award specific minor punishments (Section 11(4))
Company officer: Make penal deductions from pay and allowances (Section 13)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 9 defines 'More heinous offences' such as mutiny, assault on superior officers, desertion, and cowardice, punishable with transportation for life (not less than seven years) or imprisonment (up to fourteen years) or fine (up to three months' pay) or both. Section 10 defines 'Less heinous offences' including intoxication on duty, insubordination, and absence without leave, punishable with imprisonment (up to one year) or fine (up to three months' pay) or both. Section 11 outlines 'Minor punishments' like reduction in rank, fines, and confinement, which can be awarded for disobedience, neglect of duty, or other misconduct.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government may appoint a Commandant, assistant commandants, and company officers to the Force. The Commandant appoints members to the Force.

applies_to: members of the Force, wherever they may be
special_provisions: Offences committed by a member of the Force may, under certain conditions (offender on leave, offence not connected with duties, or petty offence), be inquired into or tried by an ordinary criminal Court having jurisdiction, if the prescribed authority so directs (Section 16(2) proviso).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the Central Government's superintendence and control, administration by appointed officers, and a system of offences, punishments, and disciplinary actions within the Force. Members of the Force have powers of arrest, and the Commandant or assistant commandant can be invested with Magistrate powers for certain offences. Ordinary criminal courts may also have jurisdiction in specific cases.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrates (invested with powers under Section 16(2)); ordinary criminal Courts (under conditions specified in Section 16(2) proviso)

schedules_summary.description: Contains the 'RECRUITING ROLL' which outlines the statement to be read out and signed by a person before appointment to the Force, detailing conditions for discharge and resignation from service.

act_identification.act_title: THE HIGH COURTS (SEALS) ACT, 1950

legislative_details.geographical_extent: High Courts in the States and Courts of Judicial Commissioner for Union territories

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the use of seals of common form and design by the High Courts in the States.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to standardize the design and form of seals to be used by High Courts in the States and Courts of Judicial Commissioner for Union territories. It mandates a common design featuring the Asoka capital and specific inscriptions.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Establishes the short title of the Act as 'The High Courts (Seals) Act, 1950'.

key_sections.title: Seals of High Courts.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the common form, design, and inscriptions for seals to be used by High Courts in States and Courts of Judicial Commissioner for Union territories, superseding any contrary existing provisions.

key_sections.title: [Repeal of Ordinance 13 of 1950.]
key_sections.description: Repeals Ordinance 13 of 1950.

repealed_acts: Ordinance 13 of 1950
related_acts: direction or other law relating to the use of seals by High Courts

applies_to: Every High Court in a [1][State]
Every Court of the Judicial Commissioner for a [2][Union territory]

act_identification.act_title: THE EMBLEMS AND NAMES (PREVENTION OF IMPROPER USE) ACT, 1950
act_identification.act_short_title: The Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act, 1950

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India and also applies to citizens of India outside India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to prevent the improper use of certain emblems and names for professional and commercial purposes.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to prevent the misuse of specific emblems and names for professional and commercial activities. It prohibits the unauthorized use of these identifiers in trade, business, or as part of company registrations, trademarks, or patents.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's official name, its geographical reach, applicability to citizens abroad, and the date it comes into force.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'emblem', 'competent authority', and 'name'.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of improper use of certain emblems and names.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the unauthorized use of specified emblems and names for trade, business, profession, or in patents, trademarks, or designs without Central Government permission.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of registration of certain companies, etc.
key_sections.description: Prevents competent authorities from registering companies, firms, trademarks, designs, or granting patents if their names or emblems contravene Section 3.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the punishment for contravening the provisions of Section 3, which is a fine.

key_sections.title: Previous sanction for prosecution.
key_sections.description: Requires prior sanction from the Central Government or an authorized officer before initiating any prosecution under this Act.

key_sections.title: Savings.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not exempt any person from other legal proceedings that could be brought against them.

key_sections.title: Power of the Central Government to amend the Schedule.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to add to or alter the Schedule by notification in the Official Gazette.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act and specifies parliamentary oversight for such rules.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to prescribe cases and conditions for use of emblems/names (Section 3)
Central Government: to authorise officers for granting permission (Section 3)
Central Government: to decide questions regarding emblems (Section 4(2))
Central Government: to sanction prosecution (Section 6)
Central Government: to amend the Schedule (Section 8)
Central Government: to make rules (Section 9)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who contravenes the provisions of section 3 shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government has the power to authorise officers for granting permission (Section 3) and for sanctioning prosecution (Section 6).

applies_to: the whole of India
citizens of India outside India
any person
exemptions: cases and conditions as may be prescribed by the Central Government (Section 3)

pictorial use of Mahatma Gandhi, Shrimati Indira Gandhi, Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj or the Prime Minister of India or the words ‘Gandhi’ ‘Nehru’ or ‘Shivaji’ on calendars where only the name of the manufacturers and printers of the calendars are given and the calendars are not used for advertising goods (Schedule 9A)
special_provisions: Extended to Goa, Daman and Diu with modifications by Reg. 12 of 1962
Brought into force in Pondicherry by Reg. 7 of 1963
Brought into force in Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963
Brought into force in Sikkim by S.O. 4292 dated 16-9-1975
The words “except the State of Jammu and Kashmir” omitted by the Jammu and Kashmir (Extension of Laws) Act, 1956 (62 of 1956)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through prohibitions on improper use and registration, with penalties for contravention. Prosecution requires prior sanction from the Central Government or an authorized officer.

schedules_summary.description: Lists specific names, emblems, seals, flags, insignia, coat-of-arms, and pictorial representations whose improper use is prohibited. This includes symbols of international organizations (UN, WHO, UNESCO, ICAO, Interpol, WMO), national symbols (Indian National Flag, Government of India/State, President, Governor, Rashtrapati Bhavan, Ashoka Chakra, Parliament, Supreme Court), names of national figures (Mahatma Gandhi, Indira Gandhi, Shivaji, Prime Minister, Lal Bahadur Shastri), and emblems of various other organizations and institutions (St. John’s Ambulance, Tuberculosis Association, IAEA, Rama Krishna Math and Mission, Sri Sarda Math and Ramakrishna Sarda Mission, Bharat Scouts and Guides, International Olympic Committee, National Youth Emblem, Auroville, Sri Sathya Sai Central Trust, Sri Sathya Sai, NHRC, FIFA).

act_identification.act_title: THE IMMIGRANTS (EXPULSION FROM ASSAM) ACT, 1950

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the expulsion of certain immigrants from Assam.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides the Central Government with the power to order the expulsion of certain immigrants from Assam if their stay is deemed detrimental to the interests of the general public of India or any section thereof, or of any Scheduled Tribe in Assam.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its geographical applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Power to order expulsion of certain immigrants.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to order the expulsion of persons or classes of persons from India or Assam if their stay is detrimental to public interest or Scheduled Tribes in Assam, with a proviso for certain displaced persons from Pakistan.

key_sections.title: Delegation of power.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to delegate its powers and duties under section 2 to subordinate officers or the Government of Assam, Meghalaya, or Nagaland.

key_sections.title: Power to give effect to orders, etc.
key_sections.description: Empowers authorities to take necessary steps and use reasonable force to give effect to orders made under the Act.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravening, attempting to contravene, abetting contravention of, or failing to comply with orders made under section 2, or harbouring such persons.

key_sections.title: Protection to persons acting under this Act.
key_sections.description: Provides legal protection against suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings for actions done in good faith under this Act.

key_sections.title: [Repealed.]
key_sections.description: Indicates that this section, originally titled '[Repeal and saving.]', has been repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1957.

powers_conferred: Power to order expulsion of certain immigrants (Central Government)
Power to delegate expulsion powers (Central Government)
Power to take steps and use force to give effect to orders (Empowered authorities)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who contravenes or attempts to contravene or abets the contravention of any order made under section 2, or fails to comply with any direction given by such order, or harbours any person who has contravened such an order, shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.

repealed_acts: Repealing and Amending Act, 1957 (36 of 1957)

applies_to: Any person or class of persons, having been ordinarily resident in any place outside India, who has or have come into Assam and whose stay is detrimental to the interests of the general public of India or of any section thereof or of any Scheduled Tribe in Assam.
exemptions: Any person who on account of civil disturbances or the fear of such disturbances in any area now forming part of Pakistan has been displaced from or has left his place of residence in such area and who has been subsequently residing in Assam.
special_provisions: Specific focus on immigrants in Assam.
Protection of interests of Scheduled Tribes in Assam.
Delegation of powers to the Government of Assam, Meghalaya, or Nagaland.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government issues expulsion orders. Empowered authorities can take steps and use force to give effect to these orders. Non-compliance is subject to penalties including imprisonment and fine.

act_identification.act_title: THE SPECIAL CRIMINAL COURTS (JURISDICTION) ACT, 1950

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India except [1] [the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States]

act_overview.preamble: An Act to confer upon special criminal courts, constituted by or under certain State laws, jurisdiction to try offences against laws with respect to any of the matters enumerated in the Union List.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to confer jurisdiction upon special criminal courts, established by or under various State laws, to try offences related to matters enumerated in the Union List of the Constitution. It ensures that these courts can handle such cases despite other existing laws.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines the term 'special criminal court' for the purposes of this Act.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of special criminal courts to try offences with respect to matters in the Union List.
key_sections.description: Confers jurisdiction on special criminal courts to try offences against laws related to matters in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution.

key_sections.title: Power to add to Schedule.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to add other State laws concerning special criminal courts to the Schedule by notification.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Ordinance VII of 1950.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Special Criminal Courts (Jurisdiction) Ordinance, 1950, and provides for the validation of actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Power to Central Government to add State laws to the Schedule by notification in the Official Gazette (Section 4).

repealed_acts: The Special Criminal Courts (Jurisdiction) Ordinance, 1950 (7 of 1950)
related_acts: The Bombay Public Security Measures Act, 1947
The Central Provinces and Berar Public Safety Act, 1948
The West Bengal Special Courts Ordinance, 1949
The West Bengal Special Courts Act, 1950
The West Bengal Criminal Law Amendment (Special Courts) Act, 1949
The Tribunals of Criminal Jurisdiction Ordinance, 952 (West Bengal Ordinance. (1 of 1952)

applies_to: special criminal courts constituted by or under certain State laws
offences against laws with respect to any of the matters enumerated in List I in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution
exemptions: the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States

implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: special criminal courts

schedules_summary.description: Lists various State laws (e.g., The Bombay Public Security Measures Act, 1947; The Central Provinces and Berar Public Safety Act, 1948; The West Bengal Special Courts Ordinance, 1949; The West Bengal Special Courts Act, 1950; The Assam Special Courts Act, 1950; The West Bengal Criminal Law Amendment (Special Courts) Act, 1949; The Tribunals of Criminal Jurisdiction Ordinance, 952) that constitute special criminal courts for the purpose of this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE TRANSFER OF PRISONERS ACT, 1950

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the removal from one State to another of persons confined in a prison.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to facilitate the transfer of prisoners from a prison in one State to a prison in another State within India. It outlines the conditions under which such transfers can occur, requiring consent from both State Governments involved.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the official short title of the Act and specifies its geographical applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, including 'court', 'Government' or 'State Government', and 'prison'.

key_sections.title: Removal of prisoners from one State to another.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Government of a State to order the removal of a confined prisoner to a prison in another State, with the consent of that other State's Government, under specified conditions of confinement.

key_sections.title: [Repealed.]
key_sections.description: Notes the repeal of a section that originally dealt with the amendment of section 29 of Act III of 1900.

powers_conferred: The Government of a State may, with the consent of the Government of any other State, by order, provide for the removal of a prisoner from that prison to any prison in the other State.

applies_to: persons confined in a prison in a State
persons under sentence of death
persons under, or in lieu of, a sentence of imprisonment or transportation
persons in default of payment of a fine
persons in default of giving security for keeping the peace or for maintaining good behaviour
special_provisions: The Act has been extended to Kohima and Mokakchung Districts by Reg. 7 of 1961.
The Act has been extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963.
The Act has been extended to Goa, Daman and Diu by notification No. GSR 430, dated 9-3-1965.
The words “extends to the State of Jammu and Kashmir” omitted by Act 25 of 1968, s. 2 and the Schedule (w.e.f. 15-8-1968).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: State Governments issue orders for prisoner removal with mutual consent. The officer in charge of the receiving prison is mandated to detain the prisoner according to court orders.

act_identification.act_title: THE UNION TERRITORIES (LAWS) ACT 1950

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Union territory of Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, Manipur or Tripura or to any part of such territory, States of Tripura and Vindhya Pradesh

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the extension of laws to certain [1][Union territories.]
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides the legal framework for the Central Government to extend existing laws to various Union territories. It also specifically extends certain Acts and Ordinances to Tripura, Vindhya Pradesh, and Manipur, ensuring their application and adaptation in these regions.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its date of commencement.

key_sections.title: Power to extend enactments to certain Union territories.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the Central Government to extend any enactment in force in a State to specified Union territories with restrictions and modifications.

key_sections.title: Extension of laws to Tripura, Vindhya Pradesh and Manipur.
key_sections.description: Extends specific Acts and Ordinances to the States of Tripura, Vindhya Pradesh, and Manipur, including special provisions and amendments for Manipur.

key_sections.title: Repeals and Savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals certain existing laws, including Section 7 of the Delhi Laws Act, 1912, and the Ajmer Merwara (Extension of Laws) Act, 1947, while providing savings for past operations, penalties, and actions taken under the repealed laws.

powers_conferred: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, extend to the Union territory of Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, Manipur or Tripura or to any part of such territory, with such restrictions and modifications as it thinks fit, any enactment which is in force in a State at the date of the notification.

Any Court or other authority may construe the Act or Ordinance with such alterations not affecting the substance as may be necessary or proper to adapt it to the matter before the Court or other authority.

repealed_acts: Section 7 of the Delhi Laws Act, 1912 (13 of 1912)
The Ajmer Merwara (Extension of Laws) Act, 1947 (52 of 1947)

any law which immediately before the coming into force of any Act or Ordinance extended by this Act to any of the States of Manipur, Tripura and Vindhya Pradesh is in force in that State and corresponds to the Act or Ordinance as so extended
related_acts: Ajmer Merwara (Extension of Laws) Act, 1947 (52 of 1947)

applies_to: Central Government
Union territory of Delhi
Himachal Pradesh
Manipur
Tripura
States of Tripura
Vindhya Pradesh
exemptions: The Converts’ Marriage Dissolution Act, 1866 (not extended to Manipur)
The Indian Christian Marriage Act, 1872 (not extended to Manipur)
The Legal Practitioners Act, 1879 (not extended to Manipur)
special_provisions: Proviso to Section 3(2) modifies the application of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) in the State of Manipur regarding age limits in sections 361 and 375.
Section 3(2A) specifies that Acts in Part A of the Schedule shall not extend to Manipur, and Acts in Part B shall extend to Manipur from a specific date with specified amendments.
Section 3(3) allows any Court or other authority to construe extended Acts or Ordinances with necessary alterations to adapt them.
Explanation to Section 3 and 4 clarifies that references to the State of Manipur or Tripura after 31st October, 1956, are to be construed as references to the Union territory of Manipur or Tripura.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government extends laws by notification in the Official Gazette. Courts and other authorities are empowered to construe and adapt the extended laws for their application.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any Court or other authority

schedules_summary.description: This Schedule is divided into two parts. Part A lists Acts that are not extended to Manipur by this Act (e.g., The Converts’ Marriage Dissolution Act, 1866). Part B lists Acts that are extended to Manipur from the commencement of the Union Territories’ (Laws) Amendment Act, 1956, along with specific amendments to their application (e.g., The Indian Oaths Act, 1873, The Transfer of Property Act, 1882).

act_identification.act_title: THE ARMY AND AIR FORCE (DISPOSAL OF PRIVATE PROPERTY) ACT, 1950.

key_sections.title: Definitions.

key_sections.title: Property of deceased persons and deserters other than officers.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for commanding officers to secure, inventory, and dispose of movable property and moneys of deceased or deserting non-officer personnel, including payment of debts and handling of surplus.

key_sections.title: Property of officers who die or desert.
key_sections.description: Extends the provisions of Section 3 to officers who die or desert, with modifications for the performing authority (Committee of Adjustment) and disposal of surplus.

key_sections.title: Decision of questions as to regimental and other debts in camp or quarters.
key_sections.description: Grants the prescribed person final authority to decide doubts or differences regarding regimental and other debts of deceased or deserter personnel.

key_sections.title: Representative powers of commanding officer or Committee.
key_sections.description: Confers rights and powers similar to a legal representative on the commanding officer or Committee for the purpose of administering the estate of the deceased.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to hand over estate or deceased person to the Administrator General.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to direct the transfer of a deceased person's estate to the Administrator General of a State for administration under specific conditions.

key_sections.title: Disposal of surplus by prescribed persons.
key_sections.description: Details the process for the prescribed person to handle surplus funds, including payment to representatives, publication of notices, and deposit with the Central Government if no claim is established.

key_sections.title: Disposal of certain property without production of probate, etc.
key_sections.description: Permits the delivery or payment of property or money up to a specified value to entitled persons without requiring formal legal documents like probate or succession certificates.

key_sections.title: Discharge of commanding officer, Committee, prescribed person and the Central Government.
key_sections.description: Provides legal discharge and protection from further liability for actions taken in good faith by the commanding officer, Committee, prescribed person, or Central Government under the Act.

key_sections.title: Application of sections 3 to 13 to persons of unsound mind or to persons reported missing on active service.
key_sections.description: Extends the applicability of sections 3 to 13 to persons subject to the Army or Air Force Act who are ascertained to be of unsound mind or officially reported missing on active service.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for the effective implementation and administration of the Act.

powers_conferred: Commanding officer: secure movable property, make inventory, draw pay and allowances, make provision for regimental debts, collect moneys from banking companies, sell or convert movable property into money.

Central Government: direct handing over estate to Administrator General.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 73 (Penalty for not issuing proper receipt) and Section 75 (Penalty for non-production of receipt book) create presumptions against the landholder. Section 76(2) makes a landholder interfering with crops liable for compensation up to Rs. 100. Section 110 deems collection of lag or neg by a landholder or agent as extortion under the Indian Penal Code. Section 111 imposes compensation up to Rs. 100 for landholders compelling service or for false complaints by tenants. Section 112 states that habitual infringement of tenant rights can lead to the landlord's property being taken under the Court of Wards. Section 113 deems illegal entry on a holding (by tenant or landholder) as criminal trespass under the Indian Penal Code. Section 203(3) allows for rules to prescribe fines not exceeding fifty rupees for contravention.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter VI details various offences, including those in relation to the enemy (Sections 34, 35), mutiny (Section 37), desertion (Section 38), absence without leave (Section 39), striking/threatening superior officer (Section 40), insubordination (Section 42), fraudulent enrolment (Section 43), unbecoming conduct (Section 45), disgraceful conduct (Section 46), ill-treating subordinate (Section 47), intoxication (Section 48), permitting escape (Section 49), irregularity in arrest (Section 50), escape from custody (Section 51), offences relating to property (Section 52), extortion/corruption (Section 53), making away with equipment (Section 54), injury to property (Section 55), false accusation (Section 56), falsifying documents (Section 57), offences relating to courts-martial (Section 59), false evidence (Section 60), unlawful detention of pay (Section 61), offences relating to aircraft and flying (Sections 62, 63, 64), violation of good order (Section 65), miscellaneous offences (Section 66), attempt (Section 67), abetment (Sections 68, 69, 70), and civil offences (Section 71). Punishments (Chapter VII) include death, transportation for life or 7+ years, imprisonment (rigorous or simple) up to 14 years, detention up to 2 years (for airmen), cashiering (for officers), dismissal from service, reduction in rank, forfeiture of seniority/service/pay/allowances, severe reprimand or reprimand, fine, stoppage of pay and allowances, and field punishment. Specific penalties vary by offence and whether on active service.

repealed_acts: Repealing and Amending Act, 1957 (36 of 1957)
related_acts: Reserve and Auxiliary Air Forces Act, 1952 (62 of 1952)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: President (commission officers, appoint warrant officers), Chief of the Air Staff (appoint Provost-marshals, empower officers to convene courts-martial), Central Government (empower officers to convene summary general courts-martial), Officer having power to convene a general court-martial (convene district court-martial).

applies_to: Officers and warrant officers of the Air Force (Section 2(a))
Persons enrolled under this Act (Section 2(b))

Persons belonging to the Regular Air Force Reserve or the Air Defence Reserve or the Auxiliary Air Force, in the circumstances specified in section 26 of the Reserve and Auxiliary Air Forces Act, 1952 (62 of 1952) (Section 2(c))

Persons not otherwise subject to air force law, who, on active service, in camp, on the march, or at any frontier post specified by the Central Government by notification in this behalf, are employed by, or are in the service of, or are followers of, or accompany any portion of the Air Force (Section 2(d))
exemptions: Aliens, except with the consent of the Central Government signified in writing (Section 11).
Females, except in such corps, department, branch or other body forming part of, or attached to any portion of, the Air Force as the Central Government may specify (Section 12).
special_provisions: Application of Act to certain forces under the Central Government (Section 5).
Special provision as to rank in certain cases (Section 6).
Power to declare persons to be on active service (Section 9).
Nothing in Section 11 shall bar the enrolment of the subjects of Nepal in the Air Force.
Act extended to Goa, Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Pondicherry, Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir, and Union territory of Ladakh (footnotes).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced through trials by courts-martial, punishments awarded by commanding officers or other specified officers, arrest and custody by air force authorities, and aid from civil authorities for apprehension of offenders/deserters. Execution of sentences is detailed in Chapter XIII.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts-martial (General, District, Summary General) and Criminal courts (with shared jurisdiction in certain cases).

act_identification.act_title: THE ARMY ACT, 1950

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Wherever persons subject to this Act may be; at any place in or beyond India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the Government of the regular Army.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws governing the regular Army. It establishes the legal framework for the administration, discipline, and service conditions of military personnel.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

chapter_titles: SPECIAL PROVISIONS FOR THE APPLICATION OF ACT IN CERTAIN CASES

key_definitions: all words (except the word “India”) and expressions used but not defined in this Act and defined in the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860)

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Persons subject to this Act.
key_sections.description: Defines the categories of persons, including officers, enrolled persons, and reserve forces, who are subject to the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'active service', 'civil offence', 'Chief of the Army Staff', and 'regular Army'.

key_sections.title: Ineligibility of females for enrolment or employment.
key_sections.description: States that females are generally ineligible for enrolment or employment in the regular Army, with exceptions specified by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power to modify certain fundamental rights in their application to persons subject to this Act.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to restrict certain fundamental rights for persons subject to the Act, such as joining trade unions or communicating with the press.

key_sections.title: Offences in relation to the enemy and punishable with death.
key_sections.description: Lists severe offences related to the enemy, such as abandoning post, aiding the enemy, or mutiny, which are punishable by death.

key_sections.title: Civil offences.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that persons subject to the Act who commit civil offences in or beyond India can be tried by court-martial and specifies the applicable punishments.

key_sections.title: Civil offence not triable by court-martial.
key_sections.description: Exempts certain civil offences like murder or rape against non-military persons from court-martial jurisdiction, unless committed under specific circumstances like active service or outside India.

key_sections.title: Punishments awardable by courts-martial.
key_sections.description: Outlines the scale of punishments that can be inflicted by courts-martial, ranging from death to forfeiture of pay and allowances.

key_sections.title: Kinds of courts-martial.
key_sections.description: Identifies the four types of courts-martial established under the Act: general, district, summary general, and summary.

key_sections.title: Period of limitation for trial.
key_sections.description: Sets a limitation period of three years for the commencement of trials by court-martial, with exceptions for certain offences like desertion or fraudulent enrolment.

key_sections.title: Choice between criminal court and court-martial.
key_sections.description: Grants discretion to the commanding officer to decide whether an offence with concurrent jurisdiction should be tried by a criminal court or a court-martial.

key_sections.title: Form of sentence of death.
key_sections.description: Specifies that a court-martial, when awarding a death sentence, shall direct whether the offender suffers death by hanging or by being shot.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act, covering various aspects like court-martial procedure and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Mandates that all rules and regulations made under the Act must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To apply provisions of the Act to certain forces, declare persons on active service, dismiss or remove persons from service, modify fundamental rights, specify additional punishments, order withholding of pay and allowances, make rules for military prisons, pardon, remit, commute sentences, suspend sentences, annul court-martial proceedings, make rules and regulations.
President: To grant commission as an officer or junior commissioned officer, or appoint as warrant officer.

Chief of the Army Staff: To dismiss, remove or reduce persons from service (other than officers), specify additional punishments, appoint provost-marshals, convene general courts-martial, confirm findings and sentences, annul court-martial proceedings, pardon, remit, commute sentences, suspend sentences.

Officer commanding army, army corps, division or independent brigade: To impose collective fines, decide jurisdiction between criminal court and court-martial, order detention of lunatic accused, pardon, remit, commute sentences.

Commanding officer: To order persons into military custody, ensure timely investigation of charges, inquire into absence without leave, hold summary courts-martial, award punishments to persons other than officers, junior commissioned officers and warrant officers, and to junior commissioned officers.
Courts-martial (General, District, Summary General, Summary): To try persons subject to the Act for offences and award authorized punishments.
Provost-marshals: To arrest and detain persons for offences, carry into effect punishments awarded by court-martial or authorized officers.

Officer having power not less than a brigade or equivalent commander: To dismiss or remove persons (other than officers or junior commissioned officers), reduce warrant officers or non-commissioned officers, award punishments to officers below field officer rank, junior commissioned officers or warrant officers.

Officer having power not less than an area commander or equivalent commander or officer empowered to convene a general court-martial: To award punishments to officers below lieutenant-colonel rank, junior commissioned officers or warrant officers.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines a wide range of offences, categorized into: offences in relation to the enemy (punishable with death or imprisonment up to 14 years), offences punishable more severely on active service, mutiny (punishable by death), desertion and aiding desertion (punishable by death or imprisonment up to 7 years), absence without leave (imprisonment up to 3 years), striking or threatening superior officers (imprisonment up to 14 years), insubordination and obstruction (imprisonment up to 10 years), fraudulent enrolment (imprisonment up to 5 years), false answers on enrolment (imprisonment up to 5 years), unbecoming conduct (cashiering or dismissal), disgraceful conduct (imprisonment up to 7 years), ill-treating a subordinate (imprisonment up to 7 years), intoxication (cashiering or imprisonment up to 2 years), permitting escape of person in custody (imprisonment up to 14 years), irregularity in connection with arrest or confinement (imprisonment up to 2 years), escape from custody (imprisonment up to 5 years), offences in respect of property (imprisonment up to 10 years), extortion and corruption (imprisonment up to 10 years), making away with equipment (imprisonment up to 10 years), injury to property (imprisonment up to 14 years), false accusations (imprisonment up to 5 years), falsifying official documents and false declaration (imprisonment up to 14 years), signing in blank and failure to report (imprisonment up to 7 years), offences relating to courts-martial (imprisonment up to 3 years), false evidence (imprisonment up to 7 years), unlawful detention of pay (imprisonment up to 10 years), offences in relation to aircraft and flying (imprisonment up to 14 years), violation of good order and discipline (imprisonment up to 7 years), miscellaneous offences (imprisonment up to 7 years), attempt, and abetment. Penalties include death, transportation for life or for any period not less than seven years, imprisonment (rigorous or simple, up to fourteen years), cashiering (for officers), dismissal from service, reduction to lower rank/grade, forfeiture of seniority/service/pay, severe reprimand or reprimand, and fines.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The President may grant commissions as officers or junior commissioned officers, or appoint warrant officers. The Central Government or the Chief of the Army Staff may appoint provost-marshals. The Central Government or the Chief of the Army Staff, or officers empowered by them, may convene various types of courts-martial.

applies_to: Officers, junior commissioned officers and warrant officers of the regular Army
Persons enrolled under this Act
Persons belonging to the Indian Reserve Forces
Persons belonging to the Indian Supplementary Reserve Forces when called out for service or when carrying out the annual test
Officers of the Territorial Army, when doing duty as such officers, and enrolled persons of the said Army when called out or embodied or attached to any regular forces
Persons holding commissions in the Army in India Reserve of Officers, when ordered on any duty or service
Officers appointed to the Indian Regular Reserve of Officers, when ordered on any duty or service

Persons not otherwise subject to military law who, on active service, in camp, on the march or at any frontier post, are employed by, or are in the service of, or are followers of, or accompany any portion of, the regular Army
exemptions: Females are generally ineligible for enrolment or employment in the regular Army, except in specified corps/departments by Central Government notification.
Persons not citizens of India are ineligible for enrolment, except with Central Government consent, but subjects of Nepal are not barred.

Civil offences of murder, culpable homicide not amounting to murder, or rape against persons not subject to military, naval or air force law are not triable by court-martial, unless committed on active service, outside India, or at a frontier post.
special_provisions: The Central Government may apply provisions of this Act, with or without modifications, to any force raised and maintained in India under its authority.
Subjects of Nepal are not barred from enrolment in the regular Army.
Females may be eligible for enrolment or employment in specific corps, departments, branches, or bodies as specified by the Central Government.

Persons who have ceased to be subject to this Act may still be taken into military custody, tried, and punished for offences committed while they were subject to the Act, subject to certain limitations.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government has the power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act and to make regulations for other purposes of the Act.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through military custody, detention, and a system of courts-martial (general, district, summary general, and summary) which try offences and award punishments. Provost-marshals are appointed to maintain order and discipline and execute punishments. Civil authorities are required to aid in the apprehension and delivery of offenders to military custody. Sentences are executed through confinement in military or civil prisons, with provisions for pardons, remissions, and suspensions.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts-martial (General, District, Summary General, and Summary) have jurisdiction over offences under this Act. Criminal Courts also have jurisdiction over civil offences, with a choice of forum determined by the commanding officer, subject to reference to the Central Government.

act_identification.act_title: THE CONTINGENCY FUND OF INDIA ACT, 1950

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Finance

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment and maintenance of Contingency Fund.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the establishment and maintenance of the Contingency Fund of India. Its main objective is to enable withdrawals for meeting unforeseen expenditure pending authorization by Parliament.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950.

key_sections.title: Establishment of the Contingency Fund of India.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Contingency Fund of India as an imprest, into which a specified sum (initially fifty crores, later enhanced) shall be paid from the Consolidated Fund of India.

key_sections.title: Custody of the Contingency Fund and withdrawals therefrom.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the Contingency Fund shall be held by a Secretary to the Government of India in the Ministry of Finance on behalf of the President, and outlines conditions for withdrawals.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for regulating matters connected with the custody, payment into, and withdrawal of moneys from the Contingency Fund of India.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to make rules for regulating the Contingency Fund of India (Section 4).

applies_to: Central Government
Parliament
special_provisions: The Act has been extended to Goa, Daman and Diu by Reg. 12 of 1962, s. 3 and Schedule.
The Act has been extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963, s. 2 and Schedule I.
The Act has been extended to Pondicherry by Reg. 7 of 1963, s. 3 and Schedule I.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government makes rules, which are laid before each House of Parliament. Withdrawals from the fund are for unforeseen expenditure pending authorization by Parliament.

act_identification.act_title: THE ROAD TRANSPORT CORPORATIONS ACT, 1950

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the incorporation and regulation of Road Transport Corporations.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the incorporation and regulation of Road Transport Corporations. It aims to facilitate the establishment and management of these corporations to provide efficient and economical road transport services.

chapter_titles: SPECIAL PROVISIONS APPLICABLE TO THE UNION TERRITORY OF DELHI

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its geographical extent, and commencement provisions for certain territories.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Road Transport Corporations in the States.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to establish Road Transport Corporations by notification in the Official Gazette.

key_sections.title: Management of Corporation and Board of Directors.
key_sections.description: Details the vesting of management in a Board of Directors, its composition, and appointment of members.

key_sections.title: Establishment of subsidiary corporations.
key_sections.description: Allows a parent Corporation to establish subsidiary corporations with the concurrence of State and Central Governments.

key_sections.title: General duty of Corporation.
key_sections.description: Outlines the general duty of a Corporation to provide efficient, adequate, economical, and coordinated road transport services.

key_sections.title: Powers of Corporation.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers of a Corporation, including operating services, acquiring property, and entering contracts.

key_sections.title: Capital of the Corporation.
key_sections.description: Describes how the capital of a Corporation is provided by the State Government and how additional capital can be raised through shares.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Mandates proper accounts and records, annual audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, and submission of reports.

key_sections.title: Directions by the State Government.
key_sections.description: Allows the State Government to issue general instructions to Corporations regarding their operations, employees, and finances.

key_sections.title: Power to supersede a Corporation.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government power to supersede a Corporation under certain conditions, such as inability to perform duties or abuse of powers.

key_sections.title: Liquidation of a Corporation.
key_sections.description: Specifies that no law relating to winding up of companies applies, and liquidation is by order of the State Government with Central Government approval.

key_sections.title: Compensation for acquisition of road transport undertakings.
key_sections.description: Lays down the procedure for determining and paying compensation when a Corporation acquires an undertaking.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.

Corporation to operate road transport services (Section 19)
Corporation to provide ancillary services (Section 19)

act_identification.act_title: THE KHADDAR (PROTECTION OF NAME) ACT, 1950

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the use of the words “Khaddar” and “Khadi” when applied as a trade description of woven materials.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to regulate the use of the words “Khaddar” and “Khadi” as a trade description for woven materials. key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the official short title of the Act and specifies its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: The words “Khaddar” and “Khadi” to be trade description.
key_sections.description: Deems the words “Khaddar” and “Khadi” as a trade description for woven materials, indicating they are handloom cloth from hand-spun yarns in India.

key_sections.title: [Repealed].
key_sections.description: This section was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1957.

applies_to: woven materials
special_provisions: Vide Notification No. S.O. 3912 (E), dated 30th October, 2019, this Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

act_identification.act_title: THE JALLIANWALA BAGH NATIONAL MEMORIAL ACT, 1951

act_overview.purpose: The Act provides for the establishment and management of the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial. act_overview.act_category: Institutions of Natural and Cultural Importance

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial Act, 1951.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Memorial', 'Trust', and 'Trustees'.

key_sections.title: Objects of the Trust.
key_sections.description: Outlines the objectives of the Trust, such as erecting and maintaining structures, acquiring properties, and raising funds for the Memorial.

key_sections.title: Trustees of the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial.
key_sections.description: Specifies the composition of the Trustees, including the Prime Minister as Chairperson, and establishes the Trustees as a body corporate with perpetual succession.

key_sections.title: Term of office of nominated Trustees.
key_sections.description: Sets the term of office for nominated Trustees and provides for their eligibility for renomination or termination by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Property vested in Trustees.
key_sections.description: Declares that all property and funds listed in the Schedule, and any future acquisitions, shall vest in the Trustees.

key_sections.title: Power of Trustees to appoint committee of management.
key_sections.description: Grants the Trustees the power to appoint a committee of management and delegate powers, duties, and functions to it.

key_sections.title: Power to approve audited accounts.
key_sections.description: Requires the Trust to meet at least annually to approve its audited accounts.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Mandates the audit of the Trust's accounts by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and requires the audit report to be laid before Parliament.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.

key_sections.title: Power of Trustees to make regulations.

key_sections.title: Rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament.

powers_conferred: Trustees of the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial: To acquire and hold property, enter into contracts, sue and be sued (Section 4(2)); to appoint a committee of management and entrust powers to it (Section 7); to make regulations (Section 10).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (for nominated Trustees); Trustees (for committee of management members, officers and servants).

applies_to: Trust for the erection and management of the Memorial
Trustees of the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial

act_identification.act_title: THE VISVA-BHARATI ACT, 1951

key_sections.title: Declaration of Visva-Bharati as an institution of national importance.
