key_sections.description: Defines the Acharya (Chancellor) as the Head of the University, detailing appointment, term, and powers.

key_sections.title: The Upacharya (Vice-Chancellor).
key_sections.description: Establishes the Upacharya (Vice-Chancellor) as the principal executive and academic officer, outlining appointment, powers, and functions.

key_sections.title: The Samsad (Court).
key_sections.description: Describes the constitution, powers, and functions of the Samsad (Court), including reviewing policies and considering annual reports.

key_sections.title: The Karma-Samiti (Executive Council).
key_sections.description: Identifies the Karma-Samiti (Executive Council) as the principal executive body, responsible for management, administration, and appointments.

key_sections.title: The Siksha-Samiti (Academic Council).
key_sections.description: Designates the Siksha-Samiti (Academic Council) as the principal academic body, responsible for standards of learning, education, and examinations.

key_sections.title: Statutes.
key_sections.description: Lists the matters for which Statutes may provide, covering governance, appointments, and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Matters to be provided for in the Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Ordinances may provide, including student admission, courses of study, and examination conduct.

key_sections.title: Adhyapakas of the University to be appointed under a written contract.
key_sections.description: Mandates written contracts for the appointment of adhyapakas to permanent posts and details provisions for existing contracts.

key_sections.title: Tribunal of Arbitration.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Tribunal of Arbitration for resolving disputes arising from employment contracts of adhyapakas.

key_sections.title: Authorities by whom order for removal or dismissal or adhyapaka, etc., may be made and the procedure therefor.
key_sections.description: Outlines the authority and procedure for the dismissal or removal of adhyapakas and academic staff.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Paridarsaka (Visitor) the power to issue orders to remove difficulties in the establishment or functioning of the University or its authorities.

powers_conferred: University: To provide facilities for studies, instruction, socially useful productive work, community service and research; to undertake educational experiments; to make provision for research and advisory services; to co-operate, collaborate or associate with other institutions; to approve institutions of higher learning; to establish and maintain Bhavanas, Schools of Studies and Research, Chatravasas, Gymnasia and other institutions; to establish campuses, special centres, laboratories; to organise application of learning to village problems; to undertake promotion of adult education, rural reconstruction, social welfare, cottage industries; to establish examination centres; to grant diplomas, certificates, degrees; to confer honorary degrees; to determine admission standards; to supervise student residences; to make special arrangements for women students; to regulate student conduct; to create teaching and academic posts; to appoint Visiting Professors, Emeritus Professors, Fellows, Scholars, Resident Artists, Resident Writers; to appoint or recognise adhyapakas; to approve persons for instruction or research; to undertake publication; to create administrative posts; to provide for terms and conditions of service of employees; to regulate conduct and duties of employees; to regulate and enforce discipline among employees; to make arrangements for health and welfare of employees; to demand and receive fees; to institute and award fellowships, scholarships, studentships, medals and prizes; to receive benefactions, donations and gifts; to acquire, hold, manage and dispose of property; to borrow money with Central Government approval; to establish campuses within territorial limits; to admit students from other universities; to do all necessary or incidental acts.

Paridarsaka (Visitor): To cause an inspection or inquiry of the University; to address the Upacharya (Vice-Chancellor) with views and advice; to issue directions to the Karma-Samiti (Executive Council); to annul any proceeding of the University not in conformity with the Act, Statutes or Ordinances; to assent to Statutes; to direct suspension or disallow Ordinances; to remove difficulties.

Upacharya (Vice-Chancellor): To exercise general supervision and control over academic affairs; to exercise any power conferred on any authority of the University in immediate action (reporting to the authority); to place adhyapakas or academic staff under suspension.

Karma-Samiti (Executive Council): To manage and administer the revenue and property of the University; to conduct all administrative affairs; to create teaching and academic posts; to define duties and conditions of service; to appoint Professors, Readers, Lecturers, adhyapakas and academic staff; to provide for appointment of Visiting Professors, etc.; to manage and regulate finances, accounts, investments; to invest money; to make Statutes; to make Ordinances; to remove persons from membership of any authority or board.
Samsad (Court): To review broad policies and programmes of the University; to consider and pass resolutions on annual reports and accounts; to advise the Paridarsaka (Visitor).

Siksha-Samiti (Academic Council): To control and generally regulate, and be responsible for the maintenance of standards of learning, education, instruction, evaluation and examination; to advise the Karma-Samiti (Executive Council) on all academic matters.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for disciplinary actions against adhyapakas and academic staff, including dismissal or removal from service, for reasons such as unsound mind, being a deaf-mute, suffering from contagious leprosy, being an undischarged insolvent, or conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude. It also allows for the removal of any person from membership of a University authority or board, and the withdrawal of degrees or diplomas, for serious offences involving moral turpitude or scandalous conduct.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the first Acharya (Chancellor) and Upacharya (Vice-Chancellor). The Paridarsaka (Visitor) appoints the Acharya (Chancellor) and Upacharya (Vice-Chancellor), and the umpire for the Tribunal of Arbitration. The Karma-Samiti (Executive Council) appoints Professors, Readers, Lecturers, other adhyapakas, academic staff, Visiting Professors, Emeritus Professors, Fellows, Scholars, Resident Artists, and Resident Writers. The University creates and makes appointments to teaching, academic, administrative, ministerial, and other posts. Casual vacancies are filled by the person or body who appointed, elected, or co-opted the original member.

applies_to: The institution known as Visva-Bharati.
All persons irrespective of sex, nationality, race, creed, caste or class (for admission or appointment).
Students of the University (for residence).
Adhyapakas and other employees of the University.
exemptions: No test or condition as to religious belief or profession, except for specific benefactions with such conditions.
Religious instruction may be given with consent.
Students of its Loka Shiksha Samsad (People’s Education Council) are exempt from residing in a Chatravasa.
special_provisions: The territorial jurisdiction of the University is restricted to the area specified in the Second Schedule (Santiniketan, Birbhum, West Bengal).
The University may establish and maintain examination centres outside its territorial limits for home study courses.
Special arrangements may be made for women students regarding residence, discipline, and teaching.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Karma-Samiti (Executive Council) has the power to make Statutes and Ordinances. The authorities of the University may make Regulations.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Paridarsaka (Visitor) has powers of inspection, inquiry, issuing directions, and annulling proceedings. The Karma-Samiti (Executive Council) manages administration, finances, and discipline. The Upacharya (Vice-Chancellor) exercises general supervision and control. A Tribunal of Arbitration is established for employment disputes. Disciplinary measures are prescribed for students and employees. Annual reports and accounts are submitted to Parliament.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: A Tribunal of Arbitration has jurisdiction over disputes arising from employment contracts of adhyapakas, and no other court proceedings shall lie in such matters. The Act does not specify other competent courts for general disputes.

schedules_summary.description: Repealed.
Specifies the territorial limits of the University, describing the area known as Santiniketan in the District of Birbhum in West Bengal.

act_identification.act_title: THE PRESIDENT’S EMOLUMENTS AND PENSION ACT, 1951
act_identification.act_short_title: THE PRESIDENT’S EMOLUMENTS AND PENSION ACT, 1951

act_overview.preamble: An act to provide [1][for the emoluments of the President and for] pensions to retiring Presidents.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the emoluments payable to the President of India and the pensions and other facilities to be provided to retiring Presidents and their spouses, including family pension and free medical attendance.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Emoluments of the President.
key_sections.description: Specifies the monthly emoluments payable to the President.

key_sections.title: Pension to retiring Presidents.
key_sections.description: Details the pension and other post-retirement benefits (residence, staff, medical, travel) for former Presidents and their spouses, with conditions for Vice-Presidents and re-elected Presidents.

key_sections.title: Family pension to spouse of President.
key_sections.description: Provides for family pension to the spouse of a President who dies in office or after retirement.

key_sections.title: Free medical attendance and treatment to spouse of President dying in office.
key_sections.description: Ensures free medical attendance and treatment for the spouse of a President who dies while holding office.

key_sections.title: Free Accommodation to spouse of President.
key_sections.description: Grants free accommodation and other benefits (secretarial staff, telephone, car, travel) to the spouse of a President who dies in office or after retirement.

key_sections.title: Sums to be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
key_sections.description: States that all sums payable under this Act shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, as amended by the 2008 Amendment Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act (Section 5)
Central Government: Power to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of this Act (Section 6)

related_acts: Salaries and Allowances of Ministers Act, 1952 (58 of 1952)
President’s Emoluments and Pension (Amendment) Act, 2008 (28 of 2008)

applies_to: President
retiring Presidents
spouse of President
exemptions: Any person before assuming the office of President, who has held the office of the Vice-President, shall not be entitled to any pension and other benefits under the provisions of the Vice-President’s Pension Act, 1997 (30 of 1997).

Where any such person is re-elected to the office of President, such person or the spouse of such person shall not be entitled to any benefit under this section for the period during which such person again holds that office.

act_identification.act_title: THE FINANCE COMMISSION (MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS) ACT, 1951

act_overview.preamble: An Act to determine the qualifications requisite for appointment as members of the Finance Commission and the manner in which they shall be selected, and to prescribe their powers.
act_overview.purpose: This Act defines the qualifications and selection process for members of the Finance Commission. It also prescribes the powers and procedures to be followed by the Commission.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as The Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines 'the Commission' as the Finance Commission constituted by the President under Article 280(1) of the Constitution.

key_sections.title: Qualifications for appointment as, and the manner of selection of, members of the Commission.
key_sections.description: Outlines the qualifications for the Chairman and other four members of the Commission, including experience in public affairs, legal background, financial knowledge, and economics.

key_sections.title: Personal interest to disqualify members.
key_sections.description: Requires the President to ensure that prospective and existing members of the Commission do not have financial or other interests that could prejudicially affect their functions.

key_sections.title: Disqualifications for being a member of the Commission.
key_sections.description: Lists conditions under which a person is disqualified from being a member, such as unsound mind, insolvency, conviction for moral turpitude, or prejudicial financial interest.

key_sections.title: Term of office of members and eligibility for reappointment.
key_sections.description: Specifies that members hold office for a period determined by the President and are eligible for reappointment, with a provision for resignation.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service and salaries and allowances of members.
key_sections.description: States that members render whole-time or part-time service as specified by the President, and their fees, salaries, and allowances are determined by the Central Government through rules.

key_sections.title: Procedure and powers of the Commission.
key_sections.description: Grants the Commission powers of a civil court for summoning witnesses, requiring documents, and requisitioning public records, and the power to require information from any person.

powers_conferred: Power of the President to satisfy himself regarding financial or other interests of members (Section 4)
Power of the President to specify the period of office for members (Section 6)
Power of the Central Government to determine fees, salaries, and allowances of members by rules (Section 7)
Power of the Commission to determine its own procedure (Section 8(1))
Powers of a civil court for summoning and enforcing attendance of witnesses (Section 8(1)(a))
Powers of a civil court for requiring the production of any document (Section 8(1)(b))
Powers of a civil court for requisitioning any public record from any court or office (Section 8(1)(c))
Power of the Commission to require any person to furnish information (Section 8(2))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Failure to furnish information when required by the Commission is deemed to be legally bound within the meaning of section 176 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: President

applies_to: Chairman of the Commission
members of the Commission
any person required to furnish information by the Commission

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for determining fees, salaries, and allowances)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Commission has powers of a civil court for specific matters and can require information, with non-compliance being an offence under the Indian Penal Code.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil court (for purposes of Section 8(1)); Civil court for purposes of sections 480 and 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (for purposes of Section 8(3))

act_identification.act_title: THE SCHEDULED AREAS (ASSIMILATION OF LAWS) ACT, 1951
act_identification.act_short_title: THE SCHEDULED AREAS (ASSIMILATION OF LAWS) ACT, 1951

legislative_details.geographical_extent: The areas specified in the Schedule, which are assimilated to the laws in force in the districts of Darrang and Lakhimpur of the State of Assam.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to assimilate certain laws in force in the scheduled areas to the laws in force in the districts of Darrang and Lakhimpur of the State of Assam.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to unify the legal framework by replacing existing laws in specific "scheduled areas" with the laws currently in force in the Darrang and Lakhimpur districts of Assam. This ensures legal consistency across these regions.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'law', and 'scheduled areas'.

key_sections.title: Assimilation of laws.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that existing laws in scheduled areas will cease to be in force and laws from Darrang and Lakhimpur districts of Assam will extend to these areas.

key_sections.title: Transitional provisions.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government or the State of Assam to issue orders for temporary application or non-application of laws during the transition period.

key_sections.title: Savings.
key_sections.description: Provides an exception for legal proceedings involving Scheduled Tribes, allowing them to continue under the Assam Frontier (Administration of Justice) Regulation, 1945.

key_sections.title: Provision for removal of difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make provisions by order to remove any difficulties arising from the transition of laws.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint the date of commencement of the Act.
Central Government: To direct transitional provisions for a specified period.
Central Government of the State of Assam: To direct transitional provisions for a specified period.
Central Government: To make provisions for the removal of difficulties arising from the transition of laws.

related_acts: Assam Frontier (Administration of Justice) Regulation, 1945 (Regulation 1 of 1945)

applies_to: scheduled areas
exemptions: All suits, cases and other legal proceedings between the parties all of whom belong to the Scheduled Tribes specified in Item 2 of Part I—Assam, of the Schedule to the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, or such other tribe or tribes, as may be specified in this behalf.
special_provisions: Transitional provisions for a period not exceeding twelve months from the appointed day (Section 4).
Savings for legal proceedings involving Scheduled Tribes (Section 5).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government; Central Government of the State of Assam
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through the cessation of existing laws and extension of new laws, and by orders issued by the Central Government or the State of Assam for transitional provisions and removal of difficulties.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts operating under the Assam Frontier (Administration of Justice) Regulation, 1945, for specific cases involving Scheduled Tribes.

schedules_summary.description: Specifies the geographical areas that constitute the 'scheduled areas' by providing detailed boundary descriptions for parts of the Balipara Frontier Tract, Abor Hills and Mishmi Hills districts (Sadiya Frontier Tract), and Tirap Frontier Tract.

act_identification.act_title: THE MARKING OF HEAVY PACKAGES ACT, 1951
act_identification.act_short_title: The Marking of Heavy Packages Act, 1951

act_overview.preamble: An Act to give effect to the International Convention drawn up in Geneva on the 30th day of May, 1929, for the marking of weight on heavy packages transported by sea or inland water- ways.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to implement an international convention by mandating the marking of gross weight on heavy packages transported by sea or inland waterways from India. It establishes provisions for inspectors to ensure compliance and prescribes penalties for violations.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, its application across India, and the date it comes into force.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'heavy package' and 'inland water-way'.

key_sections.title: Obligation to mark weight on heavy packages.
key_sections.description: Mandates that persons consigning heavy packages for transport by sea or inland waterway must plainly, durably, and conspicuously mark their gross weight.

key_sections.title: Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint inspectors for the purposes of the Act and defines their status as public servants.

key_sections.title: Powers of inspectors.
key_sections.description: Grants inspectors powers to enter, inspect, examine packages, and direct or cause the marking of packages not in compliance with Section 3.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including fines, for contravention of Section 3, non-compliance with inspector's directions, or wilful obstruction of an inspector.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Stipulates liability for offences committed by companies, extending responsibility to the company itself and individuals in charge, as well as directors, managers, or officers in certain circumstances.

key_sections.title: Cognizance of offences.
key_sections.description: Specifies the courts competent to try offences under the Act and the requirement for a written complaint by an inspector within six months.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Provides legal protection against suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings for actions done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules regarding the marking and packing of heavy packages, circumstances for approximate weight marking, and other related matters.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint inspectors (Section 4(1))
Central Government: To make rules (Section 10(1))
Inspectors: To enter, inspect, and examine any place or vessel and packages (Section 5(a))
Inspectors: To direct that a heavy package not marked in accordance with Section 3 shall not be transported (Section 5(b))
Inspectors: To cause a package to be marked and recover expenses as arrears of land revenue (Proviso to Section 5(b))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person contravening Section 3 or an inspector's direction under Section 5(b) shall be punishable with a fine up to five hundred rupees. Any person wilfully obstructing an inspector shall be punishable with a fine up to two hundred rupees. For offences by companies, the company and every person in charge and responsible for its business, as well as directors, managers, secretaries, or other officers involved by consent, connivance, or neglect, shall be deemed guilty and punished accordingly.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (for Inspectors)

applies_to: Every person consigning a heavy package for transport by sea or inland water-way from any place in India
Companies committing offences under the Act
exemptions: Cases or circumstances specified by rules where it is difficult to determine the correct weight, allowing only approximate weight to be marked (Proviso to Section 3)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced by Inspectors appointed by the Central Government, who have powers of inspection and direction. Offences are tried by specific courts based on a written complaint by an inspector, and penalties are prescribed for non-compliance and obstruction.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class

act_identification.act_title: THE RAJGHAT SAMADHI ACT, 1951

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the administration and control of the Rajghat Samadhi in Delhi.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the administration and control of the Rajghat Samadhi in Delhi. It establishes a Committee to manage its affairs, maintain it, and organize functions related to the Samadhi.
act_overview.act_category: Institutions of Natural and Cultural Importance

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Committee' and 'Samadhi'.

key_sections.title: The Rajghat Samadhi Committee.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Rajghat Samadhi Committee as a body corporate for the administration and control of the Samadhi.

key_sections.title: Composition of the Committee.
key_sections.description: Details the members constituting the Committee, including ex officio, nominated, and elected members, and provisions for the Chairman.

key_sections.title: Powers and duties of the Committee.
key_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities of the Committee, including administering the Samadhi, maintaining it, and organizing functions.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the Act's objects and regulating access to the Samadhi.

key_sections.title: Power of Committee to make bye-laws.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Committee to make bye-laws for its meetings, appointment of staff, and other administrative matters.

key_sections.title: Rules and bye-laws to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Mandates that all rules and bye-laws made under the Act must be laid before each House of Parliament.

key_sections.title: Validity of acts of Committee not to be questioned by reason of vacancy, etc.
key_sections.description: Ensures that the acts or proceedings of the Committee remain valid despite any vacancy or defect in its constitution.

powers_conferred: Central Government to make rules to carry out the objects of this Act, and to regulate access to the Samadhi or to any portion thereof.
Central Government to appoint any person to be the Chairman of the Committee.
Central Government to nominate officials and non-officials to the Committee.
Committee to administer the affairs of the Samadhi and to keep the Samadhi in proper order and in a state of good repair.
Committee to organise and regulate periodical functions at the Samadhi.
Committee to do such other things as may be incidental or conducive to the efficient administration of the affairs of the Samadhi.
Committee to make bye-laws consistent with this Act and the rules made thereunder for various purposes.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (for Chairman and nominated members of the Committee)

applies_to: The Rajghat Samadhi in Delhi

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Administration and control vested in the Rajghat Samadhi Committee, with rules made by the Central Government and bye-laws by the Committee.

schedules_summary.description: Describes the Samadhi premises, admeasuring 44.35 acres, with its boundaries on the north, south, east, and west.

act_identification.act_title: THE REPRESENTATION OF THE PEOPLE ACT, 1951
act_identification.act_short_title: the Representation of the People Act, 1951

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the conduct of elections to the Houses of Parliament and to the House or Houses of the Legislature of each State, the qualifications and disqualifications for membership of those Houses, the corrupt practices and other offences at or in connection with such elections and the decision of doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with such elections.
act_overview.purpose: This Act regulates the conduct of elections to the Parliament and State Legislatures in India. It lays down qualifications and disqualifications for membership, defines corrupt practices and electoral offences, and establishes procedures for resolving election disputes.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER I.—Qualifications for Membership of Parliament
CHAPTER II.—Qualifications for Membership of State Legislatures
CHAPTER III.—Disqualifications for Membership of Parliament and State Legislatures
CHAPTER VII.—Publication of Election Results and Nominations
CHAPTER VIIA.—Declaration of Assets and Liabilities
CHAPTER II.—Presentation of Election Petitions to High Court
CHAPTER IV.—Withdrawal and Abatement of Election Petitions
CHAPTER V.—Costs and Security for Costs
CHAPTER IV.—Powers of Election Commission in connection with inquiries as to disqualifications of Members

key_sections.title: Short title
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as The Representation of the People Act, 1951.

key_sections.title: Interpretation
key_sections.description: Defines various terms used throughout the Act, including 'appropriate authority', 'election', 'elector', and 'political party'.

key_sections.title: Qualification for membership of the Council of States
key_sections.description: Lays down the qualification for membership in the Council of States, requiring a person to be an elector for a Parliamentary constituency in India.

key_sections.title: Disqualification on conviction for certain offences
key_sections.description: Specifies various offences that lead to disqualification for membership, including those under the Indian Penal Code, Protection of Civil Rights Act, Customs Act, etc., with varying periods of disqualification based on sentence.

key_sections.title: Disqualification on ground of corrupt practices
key_sections.description: Outlines disqualification based on being found guilty of corrupt practices, with the President determining the period after consulting the Election Commission.

key_sections.title: Registration with the Election Commission of associations and bodies as political parties
key_sections.description: Mandates registration of political parties with the Election Commission to avail provisions of the Act, detailing application requirements and the Commission's decision-making process.

key_sections.title: Presentation of nomination paper and requirements for a valid nomination
key_sections.description: Details the procedure for filing nomination papers, including requirements for proposers, declarations for reserved seats, and conditions for dismissal from government service.

key_sections.title: Right to information
key_sections.description: Requires candidates to furnish information regarding criminal accusations (charges framed for offences punishable with 2+ years imprisonment) and convictions (sentenced to 1+ year imprisonment) in an affidavit.

key_sections.title: Right to vote
key_sections.description: Establishes who is entitled to vote, disqualifications for voting, and rules against multiple voting in the same or different constituencies.

key_sections.title: Declaration of assets and liabilities
key_sections.description: Mandates elected members of Parliament to declare their assets and liabilities, and those of their spouse and dependent children, to the Chairman of the Council of States or Speaker of the House of the People.

key_sections.title: Account of election expenses and maximum thereof
key_sections.description: Requires candidates to keep a separate and correct account of election expenses, specifying that certain expenses by political party leaders are not counted towards the candidate's limit.

key_sections.title: High Court to try election petitions
key_sections.description: Designates the High Court as the court with jurisdiction to try election petitions, usually by a single Judge.

key_sections.title: Corrupt practices
key_sections.description: Defines various corrupt practices for the purposes of the Act, including bribery, undue influence, appeals on grounds of religion/race/caste, publication of false statements, illegal hiring of conveyances, and booth capturing.

key_sections.title: Penalty for filing false affidavit, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for candidates who fail to furnish required information, give false information, or conceal information in their nomination papers or affidavits.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules, in consultation with the Election Commission, for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: President: To issue notifications for elections (Sections 12, 12A, 14), determine disqualification period (Section 8A), make provisions for curtailing term of office of Council of States members (Section 154).

Election Commission: To recommend dates for notifications (Sections 12, 12A, 14, 14A, 15, 15A, 16), delegate functions (Section 19A), supervise elections (Section 20), nominate observers (Section 20B), designate/nominate returning officers (Section 21), approve polling stations (Section 25), register political parties (Section 29A), appoint dates for nominations/scrutiny/withdrawal/poll (Section 30, 39), allocate equitable sharing of time on media (Section 39A), fix hours for poll (Section 56), declare poll void or issue directions in case of destruction/loss of ballot boxes (Section 58, 64A), declare poll void or countermand election in case of booth capturing (Section 58A), remove or reduce period of disqualification (Section 11, 11B), call upon constituencies to fill remaining seats (Section 53), call for bye-elections (Sections 147, 149, 150, 151), extend time for completion of election (Section 153), make rules (Section 169).

State Government: To issue notifications for State Legislative Assembly elections (Section 15), requisition premises/vehicles for election purposes (Section 160), determine compensation for requisitioned property (Section 161), obtain information (Section 162), delegate functions regarding requisitioning (Section 166).

Returning Officer: To give public notice of election (Section 31), receive nomination papers (Section 33), inform about scrutiny dates (Section 35), scrutinize nominations (Section 36), publish list of contesting candidates (Section 38), preside over elections (Section 29), count votes (Section 64), declare results (Section 66), report results (Section 67).

High Court: To try election petitions (Section 80A), dismiss petitions (Section 86), allow amendment of particulars of corrupt practice (Section 86), decide election petitions (Section 98), make orders regarding corrupt practices and costs (Section 99), declare election void or candidate duly elected (Sections 100, 101), decide by lot in case of equality of votes (Section 102), grant leave for withdrawal of petitions (Section 109), grant further security for costs (Section 117).
Chairman of Council of States/Speaker of House of People: To make rules for declaration of assets and liabilities (Section 75A).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines various corrupt practices (e.g., bribery, undue influence, promoting enmity, publishing false statements, illegal hiring of conveyances, booth capturing) and electoral offences. Penalties for electoral offences include imprisonment ranging from three months to five years, fines, or both, depending on the nature of the offence and the person involved (e.g., election official vs. general public). Specific penalties are prescribed for acts like filing false affidavits, disturbing election meetings, printing unauthorized pamphlets, breaches of official duty, and going armed to polling stations.

Political parties.

act_identification.act_title: THE ASSAM (ALTERATION OF BOUNDARIES) ACT, 1951

act_overview.preamble: An Act to alter the boundaries of the State of Assam consequent on the cession of a strip of territory comprised in that State to the Government of Bhutan.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to alter the boundaries of the State of Assam by ceding a specific strip of territory to the Government of Bhutan. It also amends the First Schedule to the Constitution to reflect this territorial change.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'the Assam (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1951'.

key_sections.title: Alteration of the boundaries of Assam.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that upon commencement, the specified territory in the Schedule ceases to be part of Assam and is ceded to Bhutan, thereby altering Assam's boundaries.

key_sections.title: Amendment of the First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Directs the insertion of specific words into the First Schedule to the Constitution, under 'TERRITORIES OF STATES', to exclude the ceded territories from Assam.

amended_acts: the First Schedule to the Constitution

applies_to: State of Assam

schedules_summary.description: Describes the strip of territory measuring 32.81 square miles, located south of Bhutan, defined by specific latitudes, longitudes, and boundary pillars erected in 1930-31 and 1950.

act_identification.act_title: THE COMPANIES (DONATIONS TO NATIONAL FUNDS) ACT, 1951

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to enable companies to make donations to National funds.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to empower companies to make donations to specific national funds, such as the Gandhi National Memorial Fund or the Sardar Vallabhbhai National Memorial Fund, and other charitable funds approved by the Central Government. This power is granted irrespective of existing company law or the company's memorandum or articles of association, provided an extraordinary resolution is passed.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, specifically 'company' and 'the Companies Act'.

key_sections.title: Power of companies to make donations to certain National Funds.
key_sections.description: Grants companies the authority to make donations to specified national and approved charitable funds, overriding other legal restrictions or company articles, subject to an extraordinary resolution.

key_sections.title: [Repeal of Act 35 of 1948.]
key_sections.description: Repeals Act 35 of 1948.

powers_conferred: Power of companies to make donations to certain National Funds

repealed_acts: Act 35 of 1948

applies_to: companies
whole of India
exemptions: State of Jammu and Kashmir (initially)
special_provisions: Extended to the Union territory of Pondicherry by Act 26 of 1968, s. 3 and Schedule.
Made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh by notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019.

act_identification.act_title: THE ALL-INDIA SERVICES ACT, 1951

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the recruitment, and the conditions of service of persons appointed, to the All-India Services common to the Union and the States.
act_overview.purpose: The primary purpose of this Act is to regulate the recruitment processes and establish the conditions of service for individuals appointed to the All-India Services, which are common to both the Union and the States.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines the expression 'an All-India Service'.

key_sections.title: Other All-India Services.
key_sections.description: Constitutes additional All-India Services like Indian Service of Engineers, Indian Forest Service, and Indian Medical and Health Service.

key_sections.title: Regulation of recruitment and conditions of service.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for recruitment and conditions of service, including retrospective effect, and requires rules to be laid before Parliament.

key_sections.title: Continuance of existing rules.
key_sections.description: Ensures that existing rules applicable to an All-India Service continue in force and are deemed made under this Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint a date for the constitution of other All-India Services (Section 2A).
Central Government: To make rules for the regulation of recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to an All-India Service (Section 3(1)).
Central Government: To give retrospective effect to rules, provided it does not prejudicially affect interests (Section 3(1A)).

related_acts: Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Adaptation of Central Laws) Order, 2020
Union Territory of Ladakh Reorganisation (Adaptation of Central Laws) Order, 2020

applies_to: persons appointed, to the All-India Services common to the Union and the States
Indian Administrative Service
Indian Police Service
Indian Service of Engineers (Irrigation, Power, Buildings and Roads)
Indian Forest Service
Indian Medical and Health Service
special_provisions: The words “including the State of Jammu and Kashmir” omitted by the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Adaptation of Central Laws) Order, 2020.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Rules made by the Central Government are laid before each House of Parliament for a specified period, allowing for modification or annulment by both Houses.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDUSTRIES (DEVELOPMENT AND REGULATION) ACT, 1951

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the development and regulation of certain industries.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the development and regulation of certain industries. It declares that it is expedient in the public interest for the Union to control industries specified in the First Schedule, aiming to foster their growth and orderly functioning.

chapter_titles: THE CENTRAL ADVISORY COUNCILAND DEVELOPMENT COUNCILS
DIRECT MANAGEMENT OR CONTROL OF INDUSTRIAL UNDERTAKINGS BY CENTRAL GOVERNMENT IN CERTAIN CASES
MANAGEMENT OR CONTROL OF INDUSTRIAL UNDERTAKINGS OWNED BY COMPANIES IN LIQUIDATION
POWER TO PROVIDE RELIEF TO CERTAIN INDUSTRIAL UNDERTAKINGS
CONTROL OF SUPPLY, DISTRIBUTION, PRICE, ETC., OF CERTAIN ARTICLES

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to expediency of control by the Union.
key_sections.description: Declares that it is in the public interest for the Union to control industries listed in the First Schedule.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Advisory Council', 'industrial undertaking', and 'scheduled industry'.

key_sections.title: Establishment and constitution of Central Advisory Council and its functions.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to establish a Central Advisory Council to advise on scheduled industries' development and regulation.

key_sections.title: Establishment and constitution of Development Councils and their functions.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to establish Development Councils for scheduled industries to perform functions aimed at increasing efficiency and productivity.

key_sections.title: Imposition of cess on scheduled industries in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the levy and collection of a cess on goods manufactured or produced in specified scheduled industries for the Act's purposes.

key_sections.title: Registration of existing industrial undertakings.
key_sections.description: Mandates the registration of existing industrial undertakings within a specified period and the issuance of registration certificates.

key_sections.title: Licensing of new industrial undertakings.
key_sections.description: Requires a licence from the Central Government to establish any new industrial undertaking after the Act's commencement.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to specify the requirements which shall be complied with by small scale industrial undertakings.
key_sections.description: Enables the Central Government to specify requirements for industrial undertakings to be regarded as ancillary or small scale, for supportive measures.

key_sections.title: Power to cause investigation to be made into scheduled industries or industrial undertakings.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to investigate scheduled industries or industrial undertakings under specific circumstances, such as production fall or detrimental management.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to assume management or control of an industrial undertaking in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to take over management or control of an industrial undertaking if directions are not complied with or if it's managed detrimentally.

key_sections.title: Power to take over industrial undertakings without investigation under certain circumstances.
key_sections.description: Provides for the Central Government to take over industrial undertakings without prior investigation in urgent situations like reckless investments or prolonged closure.

key_sections.title: Power to control supply, distribution, price, etc., of certain articles.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to regulate the supply, distribution, and price of articles relatable to scheduled industries for equitable distribution and fair prices.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, up to twenty-five lakh rupees, for contravention of specified provisions, directions, or rules, including provisions for company liability.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt in special cases.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to exempt certain industrial undertakings or classes of industries from the Act's provisions, especially to encourage small undertakings.

scheduled industries
industrial undertakings

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through investigations into industrial undertakings, issuance of directions, assumption of management or control by the Central Government, control over supply, distribution, and prices of articles, powers of inspection, and imposition of penalties through adjudication and appeal processes.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court, any court having jurisdiction

schedules_summary.description: Lists various industries and articles whose manufacture or production falls under the purview of this Act, including metallurgical, fuels, electrical equipment, transportation, industrial machinery, chemicals, textiles, and more.

act_identification.act_title: THE STATE FINANCIAL CORPORATIONS ACT, 1951
act_identification.date_of_commencement: on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of State Financial Corporations.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the establishment of State Financial Corporations to facilitate the financing of industrial concerns. It outlines their capital structure, management, powers, and duties, including the ability to grant loans, guarantee payments, and underwrite shares for industrial development.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application, and commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Financial Corporation' and 'industrial concern'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of State Financial Corporations.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to establish Financial Corporations as corporate bodies.

key_sections.title: Share capital and share-holders.
key_sections.description: Details the authorized capital, division into shares, and distribution among various entities including the State Government and Small Industries Bank.

key_sections.title: Additional capital of Financial Corporation and its borrowing powers.
key_sections.description: Outlines the Financial Corporation's ability to issue bonds, debentures, and borrow money from various sources.

key_sections.title: Managements.
key_sections.description: Vests the general superintendence, direction, and management of the Financial Corporation in a Board of directors.

key_sections.title: Board of directors.
key_sections.description: Specifies the composition of the Board of directors, including nominated and elected members.

key_sections.title: Business which Financial Corporation may transact.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the types of business the Financial Corporation can undertake, such as guaranteeing loans, underwriting shares, and granting advances to industrial concerns.

key_sections.title: Rights of Financial Corporation in case of default.
key_sections.description: Grants the Financial Corporation rights to take over management or possession of industrial concerns and realize property in case of default.

key_sections.title: Special provisions for enforcement of claims by Financial Corporation.
key_sections.description: Allows the Financial Corporation to apply to a district judge for enforcement of claims, including sale of property or transfer of management.

key_sections.title: Power of Financial Corporation to appoint directors or administrators of an industrial concern when management is taken over.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Financial Corporation to appoint directors or administrators for an industrial concern whose management has been taken over.

key_sections.title: Recovery of amounts due to the Financial Corporation as an arrear of land revenue.
key_sections.description: Provides a mechanism for the Financial Corporation to recover outstanding amounts as arrears of land revenue.

key_sections.title: Power to give instructions to Financial Corporation on questions of policy.
key_sections.description: Allows the State Government to issue policy instructions to the Board and to supersede the Board if instructions are not followed.

key_sections.title: Offences.
key_sections.description: Defines offences related to false statements and unauthorized use of the Corporation's name, and prescribes penalties.

key_sections.title: Power of Board to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board the power to make regulations for the effective implementation of the Act.

Section 42(2) prescribes imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both, for using the name of the Financial Corporation in any prospectus or advertisement without written consent.

act_identification.act_title: THE PLANTATIONS LABOUR ACT, 1951

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India (excluding the State of Jammu and Kashmir initially, but now applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the welfare of labour, and to regulate the conditions of work, in plantations.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to ensure the welfare of workers in plantations. It also aims to regulate their conditions of work, covering aspects like health, safety, hours of employment, and leave.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical reach, effective date, and the types of plantations it applies to based on area and number of employees.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'adolescent', 'adult', 'child', 'employer', 'plantation', and 'worker'.

key_sections.title: Registration of plantations.
key_sections.description: Mandates the registration of plantations with a registering officer and outlines the application and certificate process.

key_sections.title: Chief inspector and inspectors.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to appoint a chief inspector and inspectors of plantations to oversee compliance with the Act.

key_sections.title: Drinking water.
key_sections.description: Requires employers to provide and maintain a sufficient supply of wholesome drinking water for all workers in plantations.

key_sections.title: Medical facilities.
key_sections.description: Mandates the provision and maintenance of prescribed medical facilities for workers and their families in every plantation.

key_sections.title: Creches.
key_sections.description: Requires employers to provide suitable rooms for the children of women workers in plantations meeting certain employment thresholds.

key_sections.title: Housing facilities.
key_sections.description: Makes it the duty of every employer to provide and maintain necessary housing accommodation for workers and their families.

key_sections.title: Liability of employer in respect of accidents resulting from collapse of houses provided by him.
key_sections.description: Establishes employer liability for compensation in case of death or injury due to the collapse of provided housing, unless solely due to occupant fault or natural calamity.

key_sections.title: Safety.
key_sections.description: Requires employers to make effective arrangements for worker safety concerning insecticides, chemicals, and toxic substances, including training, medical examination, and protective gear.

key_sections.title: Weekly hours.
key_sections.description: Sets limits on weekly working hours for adult and adolescent workers and provides for overtime wages.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of employment of children.
key_sections.description: Explicitly prohibits the employment of children in any plantation.

key_sections.title: Annual leave with wages.
key_sections.description: Outlines the entitlement of workers to annual leave with wages, calculated based on days worked, and provisions for accumulated leave.

key_sections.title: Sickness and maternity benefits.
key_sections.description: Entitles workers to sickness allowance and women workers to maternity allowance, subject to prescribed rules.

key_sections.title: Compensation.
key_sections.description: Requires employers to provide compensation to workers in case of accidents, to be registered with the Commissioner as per the Workmen’s Compensation Act, 1923.
