key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for various offences, including obstruction of an inspector (imprisonment up to six months, fine up to ten thousand rupees), use of false certificate of fitness (imprisonment up to two months, fine up to one thousand rupees), contravention of employment provisions (imprisonment up to six months, fine up to ten thousand rupees), and other general contraventions (imprisonment up to six months, fine up to ten thousand rupees). Enhanced penalties apply for repeat offenders (imprisonment up to one year, fine not less than ten thousand rupees but up to one lakh rupees).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government has the power to appoint registering officers, the chief inspector, inspectors, additional inspectors, certifying surgeons, and Commissioners. The chief inspector may declare local areas for inspectors.

applies_to: Land used or intended to be used for growing tea, coffee, rubber, cinchona or cardamom, which admeasures 5 hectares or more and employs fifteen or more persons.

Land used or intended to be used for growing any other plant, which admeasures 5 hectares or more and employs fifteen or more persons, if so directed by the State Government with Central Government approval.
Any land, regardless of size or number of employees, if the State Government declares the Act's provisions applicable.
Workers as defined in Section 2(k).
Employers as defined in Section 2(e).
exemptions: Any factory on the premises to which the provisions of the Factories Act, 1948 apply (Section 2(f)).
Midwives and nurses from night work restrictions (Section 25).

The State Government may, with previous approval of the Central Government (except for Section 19 exemptions), exempt any employer or class of employers from all or any provisions of the Act (Section 42).
special_provisions: The Act initially excluded the State of Jammu and Kashmir but is now applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.
State Government may extend applicability to smaller plantations (less than 5 hectares or less than fifteen persons) by notification (Section 1(5)).
State-specific amendments are noted for Kerala and Assam regarding certain sections.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The State Government is the primary authority for making rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, including specific rules for registration, inspecting staff, health, welfare, safety, hours of work, leave, accidents, and general matters. The Central Government's approval is required for certain exemptions.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through registering officers for plantation registration, a Chief Inspector and Inspectors who conduct examinations and inquiries, and certifying surgeons for medical examinations. The Act also provides for penalties for non-compliance and establishes Commissioners to determine compensation for accidents. The Chief Inspector can also cause facilities to be provided and recover costs from defaulting employers.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act. Appeals against decisions of the Commissioner regarding compensation for house collapse can be made to the High Court.

act_identification.act_title: THE EMPLOYEES’ PROVIDENT FUNDS AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS ACT, 1952
act_identification.act_short_title: the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the institution of provident funds [[3]pension fund] and deposit-linked insurance fund] for employees in factories and other establishments.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to provide for the institution of provident funds, pension funds, and deposit-linked insurance funds for employees in factories and other establishments. Its primary purpose is to ensure social security benefits for employees, covering aspects like superannuation, retirement, permanent disablement, and life insurance.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and application.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's name, geographical reach, and to which establishments it applies.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Employees’ Provident Fund Schemes.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to frame the Employees' Provident Fund Scheme and establish the Fund.

key_sections.title: Central Board.
key_sections.description: Constitutes the Central Board of Trustees to administer the Fund.

key_sections.title: Contributions and matters which may be provided for in Schemes.
key_sections.description: Specifies the rates of employer and employee contributions to the Fund.

key_sections.title: Employees’ Pension Scheme.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to frame the Employees' Pension Scheme and establish the Pension Fund.

key_sections.title: Employees’ Deposit-linked Insurance Scheme.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to frame the Employees' Deposit-linked Insurance Scheme and establish the Insurance Fund.

key_sections.title: Determination of moneys due from employers.
key_sections.description: Grants power to officers to determine amounts due from employers and resolve disputes regarding applicability.

key_sections.title: Appeals to Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals against certain orders to a Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Mode of recovery of moneys due from employers.
key_sections.description: Outlines methods for recovering arrears from employers.

key_sections.title: Protection against attachment.
key_sections.description: Protects provident fund, pension, and insurance amounts from attachment.

key_sections.title: Priority of payment of contributions over other debts.
key_sections.description: Establishes priority for payment of contributions in cases of insolvency or winding up.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for false statements, non-compliance with contribution payments, and other contraventions.

key_sections.title: Power to recover damages.
key_sections.description: Grants power to recover damages from employers for defaults in payments.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply to certain establishments.
key_sections.description: Specifies establishments to which the Act does not apply and provides for exemptions.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the appropriate Government to exempt establishments or classes of persons from the Schemes under certain conditions.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to apply Act to establishments (Sec 1(3), 1(4)), add industries to Schedule I (Sec 4), frame Schemes (Sec 5, 6A, 6C), modify Schemes (Sec 7), constitute Central Board (Sec 5A), constitute Executive Committee (Sec 5AA), constitute State Board (Sec 5B), appoint officers (Sec 5D), give directions to Central Board (Sec 20), make rules (Sec 21), remove difficulties (Sec 22).
Appropriate Government: Appoint Inspectors (Sec 13(1)), exempt establishments (Sec 17(1), 17(2)), delegate powers (Sec 19).

Central Provident Fund Commissioner/Authorised Officer: Determine moneys due (Sec 7A), issue certificate to Recovery Officer (Sec 8B), recover damages (Sec 14B), exempt establishments from Insurance Scheme (Sec 17(2A)).
Inspectors: Inquire, enter and search establishments, examine persons, make copies/take extracts, seize documents (Sec 13(2)).
Central Board: Administer Fund (Sec 5A(3)), appoint officers (Sec 5D(3)), delegate powers (Sec 5E).
Tribunal: Regulate procedure, exercise powers of officers under 7A, pass orders on appeals (Sec 7J, 7L).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties are prescribed for making false statements/representations (imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both), contravention or default in paying contributions or charges (imprisonment up to three years, with minimums and fines depending on the nature of default), and general contravention of Act/Scheme provisions (imprisonment up to six months, with minimums and fines). Enhanced punishment applies for subsequent convictions. Offences by companies hold both the company and responsible individuals liable. Courts can also order payment or transfer of accumulations in addition to punishment.

related_acts: Working Journalists (Conditions of Service) and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1955 (45 of 1955)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and certain members of the Central Board, as well as the Central Provident Fund Commissioner and Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officers. The Central Board appoints other officers and employees. State Boards appoint staff with State Government approval.

applies_to: Every establishment which is a factory engaged in any industry specified in Schedule I and employs twenty or more persons.
Any other establishment employing twenty or more persons or class of such establishments specified by the Central Government.
Establishments where the employer and majority of employees agree to apply the Act.
Establishments continue to be governed even if the employee count falls below twenty.
exemptions: Co-operative Societies registered under Co-operative Societies Act, 1912, or similar State law, employing less than fifty persons and working without aid of power.
Establishments belonging to or under the control of Central/State Government whose employees are entitled to contributory provident fund or old age pension benefits under government schemes/rules.
Establishments set up under Central/Provincial/State Act whose employees are entitled to contributory provident fund or old age pension benefits under schemes/rules framed under that Act.
Any class of establishments, by Central Government notification, based on financial position or other circumstances.
Establishments whose provident fund rules are not less favourable than Section 6 and other benefits are not less favourable.
Establishments whose employees enjoy provident fund, pension, or gratuity benefits not less favourable than those under the Act/Scheme.
Any person or class of persons employed in an establishment if entitled to provident fund, gratuity, or old age pension benefits not less favourable than those under the Act/Scheme.
Establishments from the Insurance Scheme if employees enjoy more favourable life insurance benefits without separate contribution.
Any person or class of persons from the Insurance Scheme if life insurance benefits are more favourable.
Establishments or class of establishments from the Pension Scheme if employees are members of another pension scheme with equal or more favourable benefits.
special_provisions: Central Government can apply Act to establishments employing less than twenty persons.
Provisions for transfer of accounts when employees move between establishments to which Act applies/does not apply.
Liability in case of transfer of establishment.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement involves determination of moneys due by authorised officers, review of orders, appeals to a Tribunal, and recovery of arrears through various modes including attachment, sale, arrest, and appointment of receivers. Inspectors conduct inquiries and compliance checks. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance, and courts have powers to order payments.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Industrial Tribunal for appeals. No court inferior to a Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class shall try offences.

schedules_summary.description: Lists industries to which the Act applies, including various manufacturing sectors like cement, textiles, chemicals, food products, and others.

Specifies matters for which provision may be made in the Employees' Provident Fund Scheme, such as employee eligibility, contributions, administration costs, accounts, withdrawals, interest rates, nominations, and inspection powers.

Specifies matters for which provision may be made in the Employees' Pension Scheme, including employee applicability, contribution crediting, qualifying service, pension scales, and administration of the Pension Fund.
Specifies matters to be provided for in the Employees' Deposit-linked Insurance Scheme, such as employee coverage, investment of funds, nominations, insurance benefits, and payment methods.

act_identification.act_title: THE INFLAMMABLE SUBSTANCES ACT, 1952

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare certain substances to be dangerously inflammable and to provide for the regulation of their import, transport, storage and production by applying thereto the Petroleum Act, 1934, and the rules thereunder, and for certain matters connected with such regulation.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to declare specific substances as dangerously inflammable and to regulate their import, transport, storage, and production. It achieves this by applying the provisions of the Petroleum Act, 1934, and its associated rules to these substances, and addresses related regulatory matters.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Inflammable Substances Act, 1952.

key_sections.title: Definitions.—In this Act,—
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'dangerously inflammable substance' and 'Petroleum Act'.

key_sections.title: Declaration of certain substances to be dangerously inflammable.
key_sections.description: Declares specific liquids and substances, such as acetone, calcium phosphide, and ethyl alcohol, to be dangerously inflammable.

key_sections.title: Power to apply Petroleum Act to dangerously inflammable substances.—(1) The Central
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to apply provisions of the Petroleum Act, 1934, and its rules to dangerously inflammable substances and to make rules for their testing.

key_sections.title: Operation of certain notifications and rules.—Notifications or rules issued or purporting to have
key_sections.description: Deems certain notifications and rules issued under section 30 of the Petroleum Act between April 1, 1937, and the commencement of this Act to be valid under this Act.

key_sections.title: Validation of certain acts and indemnity in respect thereof.—All acts of executive authority,
key_sections.description: Validates past executive acts, proceedings, and sentences related to inflammable substances carried out before the Act's commencement and provides indemnity against legal proceedings.

key_sections.title: [Repeal of section 30,
key_sections.description: Repeals section 30 of the Petroleum Act, 1934, and notes its own repeal by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1957.

powers_conferred: Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, apply any or all of the provisions of the Petroleum Act and of the rules made thereunder, with such modifications as it may specify, to any dangerously inflammable substance.
Central Government may make rules providing specially for the testing of any dangerously inflammable substance.

repealed_acts: Section 30 of the Petroleum Act, 1934 (30 of 1934)

applies_to: any dangerously inflammable substance

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: By applying provisions of the Petroleum Act, 1934, and its rules; validation of past executive acts by government officers.

act_identification.act_title: THE REQUISITIONING AND ACQUISITION OF IMMOVABLE PROPERTY ACT, 1952
act_identification.act_short_title: The Requisitioning and Acquisition of Immovable Property Act, 1952

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the requisitioning and acquisition of immovable property for the purposes of the Union.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes legal provisions for the Central Government to temporarily take over (requisition) or permanently purchase (acquire) private immovable property. This is done when such property is deemed necessary for public purposes related to the Union.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and duration.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and duration of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'award', 'competent authority', 'landlord', and 'property'.

key_sections.title: Power to requisition immovable property.
key_sections.description: Grants the competent authority the power to requisition immovable property for public purposes of the Union, with certain exemptions.

key_sections.title: Power to take possession of requisitioned property.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for the competent authority to take possession of property that has been requisitioned.

key_sections.title: Release from requisitioning
key_sections.description: Details the conditions and procedures under which requisitioned property may be released by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power to acquire requisitioned property.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to acquire requisitioned property for a public purpose by publishing a notice in the Official Gazette.

key_sections.title: Principles and method of determining compensation.
key_sections.description: Lays down the principles and methods for determining the amount of compensation payable for requisitioned or acquired property, including the role of an arbitrator.

key_sections.title: Appeals from orders of requisitioning.
key_sections.description: Provides for persons aggrieved by a requisition order to prefer an appeal to the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Appeals from awards in respect of compensation.
key_sections.description: Allows persons aggrieved by an arbitrator's award regarding compensation to appeal to the High Court.

key_sections.title: Competent authority and arbitrator to have certain powers of civil courts.
key_sections.description: Confers powers of a civil court, such as summoning witnesses and requiring document production, on the competent authority and arbitrator.

key_sections.title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts.
key_sections.description: States that civil courts generally do not have jurisdiction over matters that the competent authority or arbitrator is empowered to determine under this Act.

key_sections.title: Penalty for offences.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions, rules, or orders, or for obstructing the exercise of powers.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeals and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals specific previous acts and includes savings provisions for actions taken under those acts.

powers_conferred: Power to requisition immovable property (Competent authority)
Power to take possession of requisitioned property (Competent authority)
Power to acquire requisitioned property (Central Government)
Power to obtain information (Central Government or competent authority)
Power to enter and inspect (Competent authority or empowered officer)
Power to make rules (Central Government)
Power to delegate powers (Central Government)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever contravenes any provision of this Act, or any rule made thereunder, or any order made or direction given under this Act, or obstructs the lawful exercise of any power conferred by or under this Act, shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.

repealed_acts: The Requisitioned Land (Continuance of Powers) Act, 1947 (17 of 1947)
The Delhi Premises (Requisition and Eviction) Act, 1947 (49 of 1947)
The Requisitioning and Acquisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1952 (3 of 1952)
related_acts: State Bank of India Act, 1955 (23 of 1955)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the competent authority and arbitrator.

applies_to: immovable property for the purposes of the Union
exemptions: Property bona fide used by the owner as the residence of himself or his family.

Property exclusively used either for religious worship by the public or as a school, hospital, public library or an orphanage or for the purpose of accommodation of persons connected with the management of such place of worship or such school, hospital, library or orphanage.
special_provisions: Extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963, s. 2 and Sch. I.
Extended to Goa, Daman and Diu by Notification. No. G.S.R. 388, dated the 15th March. 1967.
Brought into force in the State of Sikkim (w.e.f. 1-12-1976) by Notification. No. S.O. 4514, dated 27th November, 1976.
Made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh by notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019.
Special provision as to certain requisitions under Act 51 of 1962 (Defence of India Act, 1962).
Special provision as to certain requisitions under Act 42 of 1971 (Defence of India Act, 1971).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The competent authority is empowered to requisition and take possession of property. The Central Government can acquire or release property. Appeals against orders and awards can be made to the Central Government and High Courts, respectively. The competent authority and arbitrator have powers of civil courts for inquiries.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court (for appeals from awards)

act_identification.act_title: THE PRESIDENTIAL AND VICE-PRESIDENTIAL ELECTIONS ACT, 1952
act_identification.act_short_title: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate certain matters relating to or connected with elections to the offices of President and Vice-President of India.
act_overview.purpose: This Act regulates the conduct of elections for the offices of President and Vice-President of India. It covers aspects from nominations and voting procedures to the resolution of election disputes.

chapter_titles: PART II CONDUCT OF PRESIDENTIAL AND VICE-PRESIDENTIAL ELECTIONS

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Returning Officer and his assistants.
key_sections.description: Mandates the appointment of a Returning Officer and assistants by the Election Commission for each election.

key_sections.title: Appointment of dates for nominations, etc.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Election Commission to appoint dates for nominations, scrutiny, withdrawal, and polling for elections.

key_sections.title: Presentation of nomination papers and requirements for a valid nomination.
key_sections.description: Details the procedure for presenting nomination papers and the conditions for a valid nomination, including proposer/seconder requirements.

key_sections.title: Scrutiny of nominations.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for scrutinizing nomination papers and the grounds for their rejection.

key_sections.title: Procedure in contested and uncontested elections.
key_sections.description: Specifies the procedure for declaring results in uncontested elections and for conducting polls in contested ones.

key_sections.title: Manner of voting at elections.
key_sections.description: States that votes shall be given by ballot in a prescribed manner, prohibiting proxy voting.

key_sections.title: Report of the result.
key_sections.description: Requires the Returning Officer to report election results to the Central Government and Election Commission for official publication.

key_sections.title: Authority to try election petitions.
key_sections.description: Designates the Supreme Court as the sole authority to try election petitions challenging Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections.

key_sections.title: Presentation of petition.
key_sections.description: Specifies who can present an election petition to the Supreme Court and the time limit for its presentation.

key_sections.title: Grounds for declaring the election of a returned candidate to be void.
key_sections.description: Lists the specific grounds upon which the Supreme Court may declare an election void, such as bribery, undue influence, or non-compliance with the Constitution/Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, in consultation with the Election Commission.

key_sections.title: Maintenance of secrecy of voting.
key_sections.description: Mandates all election officials to maintain the secrecy of voting and prescribes penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of civil courts barred.
key_sections.description: Bars the jurisdiction of civil courts from questioning the legality of actions or decisions made under this Act, except as provided in Part III.

powers_conferred: Election Commission: To appoint Returning Officers and Assistant Returning Officers (Section 3).
Election Commission: To appoint dates for nominations, scrutiny, withdrawal, and polling (Section 4).
Election Commission: To cancel notifications and issue new ones for fresh elections (Section 8).
Election Commission: To issue instructions for the transfer of ballot papers (Rule 22).
Election Commission: To fix place and time for counting of votes (Rule 27).
Election Commission: To furnish statements showing the number of votes each elector has (Rule 30).
Election Commission: To direct the custody of ballot boxes and election papers (Rule 36).
Election Commission: To direct conditions for public inspection of election papers (Rule 37).
Election Commission: To maintain lists of members of the electoral college (Rule 40).
Central Government: To cause the publication of election results in the Official Gazette (Section 12).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 21).
Returning Officer: To give public notice of intended elections (Section 5).
Returning Officer: To accept or reject nomination papers (Section 5B, 5E).
Returning Officer: To declare a candidate duly elected in uncontested elections (Section 8).
Returning Officer: To publish lists of contesting candidates (Section 8).
Returning Officer: To count votes (Section 10).
Returning Officer: To declare election results (Section 11).
Returning Officer: To report election results to the Central Government and Election Commission (Section 12).
Returning Officer: To conduct the poll at each place of polling (Rule 9).
Returning Officer: To prepare ballot paper accounts (Rule 20).
Returning Officer: To seal ballot boxes and packets (Rule 21).
Returning Officer: To determine the result of voting (Rule 33).
Returning Officer: To recount votes (Rule 34).
Returning Officer: To announce and report the final result (Rule 35).
Supreme Court: To try election petitions (Section 14).
Supreme Court: To make orders dismissing petitions, declaring elections void, or declaring other candidates elected (Section 17).
Supreme Court: To declare elections void on specified grounds (Section 18).
Supreme Court: To declare a candidate other than the returned candidate as duly elected (Section 19).
Supreme Court: To send copies of orders to the Central Government for publication (Section 20).
Presiding Officer: To appoint polling officers (Rule 9(2)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person contravening the provisions for maintaining secrecy of voting (Section 22(1)) shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine, or with both (Section 22(2)). The Act also refers to the offences of bribery and undue influence as defined in Chapter IXA of the Indian Penal Code (Section 18(2)).

repealed_acts: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Election Rules, 1952
related_acts: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections (Amendment) Act, 1977 (20 of 1977)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Election Commission appoints the Returning Officer and Assistant Returning Officers (Section 3). The Presiding Officer may appoint polling officers (Rule 9(2)).

applies_to: Elections to the offices of President of India
Elections to the offices of Vice-President of India
Candidates for Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections
Electors (members of the electoral college)
special_provisions: Specific provisions for the first Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections (Section 4(2)).
Specific provisions for elections to fill vacancies caused by expiration of term (Section 4(3)).
Specific provisions for elections to fill vacancies caused by death, resignation, or removal (Section 4(4)).
Provision for voting by electors under preventive detention via postal ballot (Rule 26).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government, after consulting the Election Commission (Section 21). The Supreme Court for rules regarding election petitions (Section 14(3), 15).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the Election Commission, Returning Officers, and other appointed officials who conduct the elections. Disputes are resolved by the Supreme Court. Penalties are prescribed for specific violations like breach of voting secrecy.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The Supreme Court has jurisdiction to try election petitions (Section 14(2)). Civil courts are barred from questioning election-related actions or decisions under this Act (Section 23).

schedules_summary.description: Contains detailed instructions for the determination of election results, including definitions of terms like 'continuing candidate', 'first preference', 'next available preference', 'unexhausted paper', and 'exhausted paper', as well as procedures for counting votes, calculating the quota for election, and excluding candidates.

act_identification.act_title: THE MINES ACT, 1952

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend and consolidate the law relating to the regulation of labour and safety in mines.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to amend and consolidate existing laws concerning the regulation of labour and safety within mines. Its primary objective is to ensure the well-being and safety of persons employed in mining operations.

chapter_titles: MINING OPERATIONS AND MANAGEMENT OF MINES
PROVISIONS AS TO HEALTH AND SAFETY

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Chief Inspector and Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint Chief Inspector and Inspectors of Mines and outlines their public servant status.

key_sections.title: Powers of Inspectors of Mines.
key_sections.description: Details the powers of Inspectors to examine, inquire, enter, inspect, search, and seize documents in mines.

key_sections.title: Committees.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of Committees by the Central Government for the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Duties and responsibilities of owners, agents and managers.
key_sections.description: Outlines the financial, compliance, and overall management responsibilities of owners, agents, and managers.

key_sections.title: Powers of Inspectors when causes of danger not expressly provided against exist or when employment of persons is dangerous.
key_sections.description: Grants Inspectors powers to issue notices and prohibit employment in cases of danger to human life or safety.

key_sections.title: Notice to be given of accidents.
key_sections.description: Requires owners, agents, or managers to report accidents causing loss of life, serious injury, or other specified occurrences.

key_sections.title: Extra wages for overtime.
key_sections.description: Stipulates the rate of extra wages for overtime work performed by persons in mines.

key_sections.title: Employment of persons below eighteen years of age.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the employment of persons below eighteen years of age in mines, with exceptions for apprentices and trainees.

key_sections.title: Employment of women.
key_sections.description: Restricts the employment of women in mines, particularly below ground and during certain hours above ground.

key_sections.title: Annual leave with wages.
key_sections.description: Defines the entitlement to annual leave with wages based on completed service and attendance.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make regulations for various aspects of mine safety and operations.

key_sections.title: Obstruction.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for obstructing Inspectors or authorized persons in their duties.

key_sections.title: Special provision for contravention of law with dangerous results.
key_sections.description: Sets out enhanced penalties for contraventions of the Act, regulations, rules, or bye-laws that result in loss of life, serious bodily injury, or other danger.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt from operation of Act, regulations, etc.,
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to exempt certain areas, mines, or persons from the Act's provisions under specified conditions.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint Chief Inspector and Inspectors (Section 5), appoint certifying surgeons (Section 11), constitute Committees (Section 12), appoint Court of inquiry (Section 24), direct investigation of causes of disease (Section 26), make regulations (Section 57), make rules (Section 58), exempt from operation of Act (Section 83), alter or rescind orders (Section 84), decide questions on mine applicability (Section 82).

Chief Inspector and Inspectors: Make examination and inquiry (Section 7), enter, inspect and examine any mine (Section 7), search and take possession of material/records (Section 7), give notice and require remedy for danger (Section 22), prohibit employment (Section 22, 22A), authorize special officers for surveying/leveling/measuring (Section 8), authorize qualified medical practitioners to exercise powers of certifying surgeon (Section 11), authorize Inspectors to exercise Chief Inspector's powers (Section 6).
Committees: Exercise powers of an Inspector (Section 14), have powers of a civil court for discovery, inspection, enforcing attendance, compelling production of documents (Section 14).
Manager: Permit persons to be employed in contravention of certain provisions in case of emergency (Section 38).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties:
The Act prescribes various offences and penalties, including:
- Obstruction of Chief Inspector, Inspector, or authorized person: Imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both (Section 63).
- Refusal to produce registers/documents: Fine up to three hundred rupees (Section 63).
- Falsification of records, false statements, or use of false certificates: Imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both (Section 64).
- Use of false certificates of fitness: Imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to two hundred rupees, or both (Section 65).
- Omission to furnish plans, returns, notices, etc.: Fine up to one thousand rupees (Section 66).
- Contravention of provisions regarding employment of labour: Imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both (Section 67).
- Employment of persons below eighteen years of age: Fine up to five hundred rupees (Section 68).
- Failure to appoint manager: Imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to two thousand five hundred rupees, or both (Section 69).
- Failure to give notice of accidents: Imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both (Section 70).
- Contravention of certain regulations (specified in Section 57): Imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to two thousand rupees, or both (Section 72A).
- Contravention of orders under Section 22 or 22A: Imprisonment up to two years, and fine up to five thousand rupees (minimum two thousand rupees in absence of special reasons) (Section 72B).
- Contravention of law with dangerous results:
  - Resulting in loss of life: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both (minimum three thousand rupees in absence of special reasons) (Section 72C).
  - Resulting in serious bodily injury: Imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to three thousand rupees, or both (Section 72C).
  - Otherwise causing injury or danger: Imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both (Section 72C).
- General provision for disobedience of orders (where no other penalty is provided): Imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both (Section 73).
- Enhanced penalty for previous conviction for the same offence within two years (Section 74).
- Medical practitioner failing to report notified disease: Fine up to fifty rupees (Section 25(4)).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the Chief Inspector of Mines, Inspectors of Mines, Certifying Surgeons, members of Committees, and competent persons to hold Courts of inquiry. Owners or agents of mines are responsible for appointing managers.

applies_to: whole of India
mines belonging to the Government
exemptions: Any mine or part thereof in which excavation is being made for prospecting purposes only, under certain conditions (Section 3(1)(a)).

Any mine engaged in the extraction of kankar, murrum, laterite, boulder, gravel, shingle, ordinary sand, ordinary clay, building stone, slate, road metal, earth, fullers earth, marl, chalk and lime stone, under certain conditions (Section 3(1)(b)).

The Central Government may exempt, absolutely or conditionally, any local area, mine, group or class of mines, or class of persons from all or any provisions of the Act, regulations, rules or bye-laws (Section 83(1)).

The Chief Inspector or any other authority may exempt, subject to restrictions, any mine or part thereof from regulations, rules or bye-laws if compliance is unnecessary or impracticable (Section 83(2)).
Persons holding positions of supervision or management or employed in a confidential capacity are exempt from certain provisions regarding hours and limitation of employment (Section 37).
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for commencement of different provisions of the Act and for different States (Section 1(3)).
Apprentices and other trainees, not below sixteen years of age, may be allowed to work under proper supervision in a mine or part thereof (Section 40(2)).
The Central Government may direct that provisions of Chapters III and IV of the Factories Act, 1948, shall apply to all mines and their precincts (Section 86).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government has the power to make regulations (Section 57) and rules (Section 58). The owner, agent, or manager of a mine may frame bye-laws, and shall do so if called upon by the Chief Inspector or Inspector (Section 61).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through inspections by the Chief Inspector and Inspectors, who have powers to examine, inquire, enter, inspect, search, and seize. They can issue notices to remedy dangerous conditions and prohibit employment. The Act also provides for the constitution of Committees and Courts of Inquiry to investigate accidents and diseases. Contraventions of the Act, regulations, rules, or bye-laws are subject to penalties, including imprisonment and fines. Prosecutions are instituted at the instance of the Chief Inspector, District Magistrate, or an authorized Inspector. Courts have the power to order remedial measures.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No Court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence under this Act which is alleged to have been committed by any owner, agent or manager of a mine or any offence which is punishable with imprisonment (Section 80).

act_identification.act_title: THE CINEMATOGRAPH ACT, 1952

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Parts I, II and IV extends to the whole of India and Part III extends to the Union territories only.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make provision for the certification of cinematograph films for exhibition and for regulating exhibitions by means of cinematographs.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish provisions for the certification of cinematograph films before public exhibition. It also seeks to regulate the exhibition of films through cinematographs.

chapter_titles: PART II CERTIFICATION OF FILMS FOR PUBLIC EXHIBITION
PART III REGULATION OF EXHIBITIONS BY MEANS OF CINEMATOGRAPHS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Board of film Certification.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Board of Film Certification for sanctioning films for public exhibition.

key_sections.title: Examination of films.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for examining films and the types of certificates that can be granted.

key_sections.title: Certification of films.
key_sections.description: Details the types of certificates ('U', 'UA', 'A', 'S') granted by the Board and their implications.

key_sections.title: Principles of guidance in certifying films.
key_sections.description: Lays down the principles that guide the certification authority in sanctioning films.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals against orders of the Board to the High Court.

key_sections.title: Suspension and revocation of certificate.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to suspend or revoke film certificates under certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Revisional powers of the Central Government.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government powers to deem certified films uncertified or change certificate types, or suspend exhibition.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of unauthorised recording.
key_sections.description: Prohibits unauthorized recording of films in exhibition places with intent to create infringing copies.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of unauthorised exhibition of films.
key_sections.description: Prohibits unauthorized exhibition of infringing copies of films for profit.

key_sections.title: Penalties for contraventions of this Part.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for various contraventions related to film certification and exhibition.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of Part II.

key_sections.title: Cinematograph exhibitions to be licensed.
key_sections.description: Mandates licensing for cinematograph exhibitions.

key_sections.title: Penalties for contravention of this Part.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contraventions related to licensing and exhibition regulations under Part III.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To constitute the Board of Film Certification (Section 3).
Central Government: To determine salary and allowances for the Chairman and members of the Board (Section 3).
Central Government: To establish advisory panels (Section 5).
Central Government: To issue directions setting out principles for certifying films (Section 5B).
Central Government: To suspend and revoke certificates (Section 5E).
Central Government: To review its own orders under Section 5E (Section 5F).
Central Government: To exercise revisional powers over film certification (Section 6).
Central Government: To make rules for Part II and Part III of the Act (Sections 8, 16).
Central Government: To exempt films or classes of films from provisions of Part II or Part III (Sections 9, 17).
Central Government: To issue directions to licensees for regulating exhibition of films (Section 12(4)).
Central Government: To confirm or discharge orders of suspension of film exhibition made by local authorities (Section 13(2)).
Board of Film Certification: To sanction films for public exhibition (Section 3, 4).
Board of Film Certification: To grant certificates ('U', 'UA', 'A', 'S') for films (Section 5A).
Board of Film Certification: To consult advisory panels (Section 5(3)).
Licensing authority (District Magistrate or State Government specified authority): To grant licences for cinematograph exhibitions (Section 11, 12).
Licensing authority: To revoke or suspend licences (Section 15).
Lieutenant-Governor/Chief Commissioner/District Magistrate: To suspend exhibition of films likely to cause a breach of peace (Section 13).
Police officer: To enter, search, and seize films in cases of contravention (Section 7A).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties for contraventions under Part II (Section 7) include imprisonment up to three years, fines up to ten lakh rupees (with further fines for continuing offences), and specific penalties for exhibiting 'A' or 'S' films to unauthorized persons (penalty not exceeding ten thousand rupees per person). Contravention of Section 6AA (unauthorized recording) or Section 6AB (unauthorized exhibition) is punishable with imprisonment from three months to three years and a fine from three lakh rupees to five percent of the audited gross production cost. Penalties for contraventions under Part III (Section 14) include a penalty of one lakh rupees and a further penalty of ten thousand rupees for each day of continuing contravention.

repealed_acts: The Cinematograph Act, 1918 (2 of 1918)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairman and other members of the Board of Film Certification and members of advisory panels.

applies_to: Any person desiring to exhibit any film
Owner or person in charge of a cinematograph
Owner or occupier of any place used for exhibition
exemptions: The Central Government may exempt any film or class of films from provisions of Part II or Part III.
Exhibition of 'A' or 'S' certified films to children below the age of three years accompanying their parents or guardians is not deemed an offence.
special_provisions: Parts I, II and IV extend to the whole of India, while Part III extends only to the Union territories.
State amendments for Ladakh (UT) regarding Section 1(3) proviso.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a certification process by the Board of Film Certification, licensing of exhibitions by designated authorities, imposition of penalties for contraventions, power of seizure by police officers, and provisions for appeals to the High Court and review by the Central Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Metropolitan Magistrate, Judicial Magistrate of the First Class (for certain offences), High Court (for appeals and certain powers).

key_sections.title: Registers.

act_identification.act_title: THE SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES OF MINISTERS ACT, 1952
act_identification.act_short_title: The Salaries and Allowances of Ministers Act, 1952

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the salaries and allowances of Ministers.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the salaries, allowances, and perquisites of Ministers, including their residence, medical treatment, and advances for motor-cars. It also specifies that Ministers shall not draw salary or allowances as Members of Parliament and includes provisions for income-tax exemption on certain perquisites. The Act empowers the Central Government to make rules for its implementation.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as The Salaries and Allowances of Ministers Act, 1952.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines 'Minister' as a member of the Council of Ministers, by whatever name called, and includes a Deputy Minister.

key_sections.title: Salaries and daily constituency allowances.
key_sections.description: Entitles each Minister to a monthly salary and daily allowance, and a constituency allowance, at rates specified for Members of Parliament.

key_sections.title: Residence of Ministers.
key_sections.description: Entitles Ministers to rent-free furnished residence during their term and for a period thereafter, with provisions for their families in case of death.

key_sections.title: Sumptuary allowance to Ministers.
key_sections.description: Prescribes sumptuary allowances for the Prime Minister, Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers, with a temporary reduction for COVID-19.

key_sections.title: Travelling and daily allowances to Ministers.
key_sections.description: Outlines entitlements for travelling allowances for Ministers and their families for official duties and personal travel within India.

key_sections.title: Medical treatment, etc., to Ministers.
key_sections.description: Grants Ministers and their families free medical treatment and accommodation in government hospitals.

key_sections.title: Advances to Ministers for purchase of motor-cars.
key_sections.description: Allows for repayable advances to Ministers for the purchase of motor-cars to facilitate their official duties.

key_sections.title: Ministers not to draw salary or allowances as Members of Parliament.
key_sections.description: Prohibits persons receiving salary or allowances under this Act from concurrently drawing salary or allowances as Members of Parliament.

key_sections.title: Exemption from liability to pay income-tax on certain perquisites received by a Minister.
key_sections.description: Exempts the value of rent-free furnished residence provided to a Minister from income-tax computation under the Income-tax Act, 1961.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act and mandates parliamentary approval for such rules.

powers_conferred: Central Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act.

repealed_acts: Act 53 of 1947
related_acts: Salaries, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 (30 of 1954)
Salaries and Allowances of Ministers (Amendment) Act, 1977

Deputy Ministers
Prime Minister
Minister of State
Members of the Cabinet

special_provisions: Sumptuary allowance payable to each Minister shall be reduced by thirty per cent. for a period of one year commencing from the 1st April, 2020, to meet the exigencies arising out of Corona Virus (COVID-19) pandemic.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Notification respecting appointment, etc., of Ministers to be published in the Official Gazette, which shall be conclusive evidence.

act_identification.act_title: THE COMMISSIONS OF INQUIRY ACT, 1952

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the appointment of Commissions of Inquiry and for vesting such Commissions with certain powers.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to enable the appropriate Government to appoint Commissions of Inquiry. It also vests these Commissions with specific powers necessary for conducting their inquiries effectively.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official name, geographical applicability, and effective date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'Commission', and 'prescribed'.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Commission.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to appoint Commissions of Inquiry for matters of public importance, and outlines conditions for such appointments.

key_sections.title: Powers of Commission.
key_sections.description: Grants the Commission powers of a civil court for summoning, examining, requiring document production, receiving evidence, and requisitioning public records.

key_sections.title: Additional powers of Commission.
key_sections.description: Allows the appropriate Government to confer additional powers on the Commission, including requiring information, entering and seizing documents, and treating proceedings as judicial.

key_sections.title: Power of Commission to utilise the services of certain officers and investigation agencies for conducting investigation pertaining to inquiry.
key_sections.description: Enables the Commission to use services of government officers or investigation agencies for inquiry-related investigations.

key_sections.title: Persons not obliged to disclose secret process of manufacture of goods in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Provides an exemption from disclosing secret manufacturing processes unless specifically required by the inquiry.

key_sections.title: Commission to cease to exist when so notified.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to declare when a Commission shall cease to exist.

key_sections.title: Persons likely to be prejudicially affected to be heard.
key_sections.description: Mandates that persons whose conduct is inquired into or whose reputation may be affected must be given a reasonable opportunity to be heard and produce evidence.

key_sections.title: Right of cross-examination and representation by legal practitioner.
key_sections.description: Grants the right to cross-examine witnesses and be represented by a legal practitioner to specified persons.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Provides legal protection against suits or proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

key_sections.title: Penalty for acts calculated to bring the Commission or any member thereof into disrepute.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for acts or statements intended to bring the Commission or its members into disrepute.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the appropriate Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Power to appoint Commissions of Inquiry (appropriate Government)
Powers of a civil court (Commission)
Power to require any person to furnish information (Commission)
Power to enter any building or place and seize documents (Commission or authorized officer)
Power to utilise the services of officers and investigation agencies (Commission)
Power to appoint assessors (Commission)
Power to regulate its own procedure (Commission)
Power to make rules (appropriate Government)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act refers to offences under the Indian Penal Code, 1860, for failure to furnish information (sections 176, 177), and for acts committed in the view or presence of the Commission (sections 175, 178, 179, 180, 228). Section 10A specifically defines an offence for acts calculated to bring the Commission or any member thereof into disrepute, punishable with simple imprisonment for up to six months, or with fine, or with both.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The appropriate Government has the power to appoint members of the Commission.

applies_to: whole of India
Commissions of Inquiry
other inquiring authorities (by notification)
exemptions: Persons not obliged to disclose secret process of manufacture of goods in certain cases
special_provisions: Extended to Goa, Daman and Diu by Reg. 12 of 1962
Extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963
Extended to Pondicherry by Reg. 7 of 1963
Made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Commissions have powers of a civil court. They can require information, seize documents, and forward cases of certain offences to magistrates. Penalties are prescribed for acts bringing the Commission into disrepute, with cognizance taken by the High Court.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate having jurisdiction (for forwarded cases), High Court (for offences under Section 10A), Supreme Court (for appeals from High Court judgments under Section 10A)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution and regulation of certain Air Force Reserve and also an Auxiliary Air Force and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the constitution and regulation of various Air Force Reserves, including the Regular Air Force Reserve and the Air Defence Reserve, as well as an Auxiliary Air Force. It also covers matters connected with their establishment, service, and discipline.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

chapter_titles: LIABILITY AND DISCIPLINE OF MEMBERS OF RESERVE AND AUXILIARY AIR FORCES

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, and the staggered commencement dates for its provisions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Air Force Reserve', 'competent authority', and 'prescribed'.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government may appoint an air officer or a committee of air officers as the competent authority. Citizens of India with specific aviation qualifications or experience
Officers and airmen of the Air Force
Employers of persons called up for service under the Act

implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts are empowered to impose fines and imprisonment for offences under the Act. A 'prescribed authority' handles disputes regarding employer reinstatement.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the regulation of certain matters relating to forward contracts, the prohibition of options in goods and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: To regulate certain matters relating to forward contracts, prohibit options in goods, and address matters connected therewith.

chapter_titles: FORWARD CONTRACTS AND OPTIONS IN GOODS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment and constitution of the Forward Markets Commission.
key_sections.description: Establishes and outlines the constitution of the Forward Markets Commission.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Commission.
key_sections.description: Details the responsibilities and duties of the Forward Markets Commission.

key_sections.title: Powers of the Commission.
key_sections.description: Confers powers of a civil court on the Commission for specific matters.

key_sections.title: Grant of recognition to association.
key_sections.description: Governs the process and conditions for granting recognition to associations by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power of recognised association to make bye-laws.
key_sections.description: Empowers recognised associations to make bye-laws for the regulation and control of forward contracts.

key_sections.title: Power of Commission to suspend member of recognised association or to prohibit him from trading.
key_sections.description: Grants the Commission power to suspend members of recognised associations or prohibit them from trading.

key_sections.title: Certificate of registration to be obtained by all associations.
key_sections.description: Mandates all associations dealing with forward contracts to obtain a certificate of registration from the Commission.

key_sections.title: Forward contracts in notified goods illegal or void in certain circumstances.
key_sections.description: Declares forward contracts in notified goods illegal or void under specified conditions.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of options in goods.
key_sections.description: Prohibits options in goods, making them illegal or void after the section comes into force.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for various offences under the Act.

key_sections.title: Penalty for owning or keeping place used for entering into forward contracts in goods.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for persons owning or managing places used for illegal forward contracts.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying into effect the objects of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Forward Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1952 itself and provides for savings and transitional provisions.

key_sections.title: Transfer and vesting of undertaking of Commission.
key_sections.description: Details the transfer and vesting of the Commission's undertaking to the Securities and Exchange Board of India upon the Act's repeal.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To establish the Forward Markets Commission (Section 3).
Central Government: To grant or withdraw recognition to associations (Sections 6, 7).
Central Government: To call for periodical returns or direct inquiries (Section 8).
Central Government: To direct rules to be made or to make rules for recognised associations (Section 10).
Central Government: To make or amend bye-laws of recognised associations (Section 12).
Central Government: To supersede the governing body of a recognised association (Section 13).
Central Government: To suspend business of a recognised association (Section 14).
Central Government: To declare sections applicable to goods and areas, making certain forward contracts illegal (Section 15).
Central Government: To prohibit forward contracts in certain cases (Section 17).
Central Government: To exempt contracts or classes of contracts from the Act's operation (Section 27).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the objects of the Act (Section 28).
Central Government: To delegate its powers under the Act (Section 26).
Forward Markets Commission: To perform functions as assigned by or under the Act (Section 4).
Forward Markets Commission: To exercise powers of a civil court (Section 4A).
Forward Markets Commission: To inspect accounts and other documents (Section 8).
Forward Markets Commission: To grant or refuse certificates of registration to associations (Section 14B).
Forward Markets Commission: To suspend members of recognised associations or prohibit them from trading (Section 12B).
Recognised associations: To make rules respecting grouping of members, restricting voting rights, etc. (Section 9A).
Recognised associations: To make bye-laws for the regulation and control of forward contracts (Section 11).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 20 prescribes penalties (imprisonment up to one year, fine not less than one thousand rupees, or both; for second/subsequent offences, imprisonment up to one year and fine) for making false statements, failing to furnish information, entering contracts during suspension, being a member of an unregistered association, publishing contravening information, organizing associations in contravention of Section 18, or entering into prohibited forward contracts/options. Section 21 prescribes penalties (imprisonment up to two years, fine not less than one thousand rupees, or both; for second/subsequent offences, imprisonment up to two years and fine) for owning/keeping places used for illegal forward contracts, organizing illegal associations, managing such places, falsely representing membership, canvassing illegally, gathering for illegal bids/offers, or manipulating prices. Section 21A allows courts to order forfeiture of property related to the offence.

repealed_acts: Any law corresponding to this Act or any provision contained therein, in force in any State, applicable to goods or classes of goods, immediately before this Act or its provision is made applicable to those goods or classes of goods (Section 29).
related_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 (5 of 1970)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints members of the Forward Markets Commission (Section 3). The Central Government may appoint persons to exercise powers of a superseded governing body of a recognised association (Section 13).
regulatory_bodies: Securities and Exchange Board of India (as a successor/related body upon repeal)

applies_to: Whole of India (Section 1)
Associations concerned with the regulation and control of forward contracts (Sections 5, 14A)
Persons entering into forward contracts or options in goods
exemptions: Central Government may exempt any contract or class of contracts from the operation of all or any provisions of this Act (Section 27).
Non-transferable specific delivery contracts are generally exempt from Chapter III or Chapter IV (Section 18(1)).
special_provisions: Different dates of commencement may be appointed for different provisions, States or areas, and for different goods or classes of goods (Section 1(3)).
Provisions for Pondicherry, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Goa, Daman and Diu (footnotes).
Historical exclusion and later inclusion of the State of Jammu and Kashmir (footnotes).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the functions and powers of the Forward Markets Commission (Sections 4, 4A), powers of the Central Government (e.g., recognition, prohibition, supersession, suspension), penalties for contraventions (Sections 20, 21), forfeiture of property (Section 21A), powers of search and seizure (Section 22A), and presumptions in certain cases (Section 22B).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a presidency magistrate or a magistrate of the first class shall take cognizance of or try any offence punishable under this Act (Section 24).

act_identification.act_title: THE SCHEDULED AREAS (ASSIMILATION OF LAWS) ACT, 1953

legislative_details.geographical_extent: scheduled areas (as specified in the Schedule) and districts of Nowgong and Sibsagar in the State of Assam

act_overview.preamble: An Act to assimilate certain laws in force in the scheduled areas to the laws in force in the districts of Nowgong and Sibsagar in the State of Assam.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to assimilate the laws in force in the scheduled areas to the laws in force in the districts of Nowgong and Sibsagar in the State of Assam. It aims to standardize the legal framework in these scheduled areas by replacing their existing laws with those of the specified districts.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and provides for its commencement date to be appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'law', and 'scheduled areas'.

key_sections.title: Assimilation of laws.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that existing laws in scheduled areas cease to be in force from the appointed day, and laws from Nowgong and Sibsagar districts of Assam will extend to or come into force in the scheduled areas.

key_sections.title: Transitional provisions.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government or the Government of Assam to direct that certain laws continue or do not extend to scheduled areas for a period not exceeding twelve months.

key_sections.title: Savings.
key_sections.description: Provides an exception for legal proceedings involving Scheduled Tribes, allowing them to be tried under existing rules for the Administration of Justice and Police in specific Mikir Hills Tracts.

key_sections.title: Provision for removal of difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties arising from the transition of laws under this Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint the date of commencement of the Act (Section 1(2))
Central Government or the Government of the State of Assam to issue orders for transitional provisions (Section 4)
Central Government to make orders for removal of difficulties (Section 6)

applies_to: scheduled areas (as specified in the Schedule)
districts of Nowgong and Sibsagar in the State of Assam (for laws being extended)
exemptions: suits, cases and other legal proceedings between parties all of whom belong to the Scheduled Tribes specified in item 2 of Part I—Assam, of the Schedule annexed to the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950 or such other tribe or tribes, as may be specified in this behalf
special_provisions: Transitional provisions for a period not exceeding twelve months (Section 4)
Savings for legal proceedings involving Scheduled Tribes (Section 5)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for commencement and removal of difficulties)
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Rules for the Administration of Justice and Police in the Sibsagar and Nowgong Mikir Hills Tracts (for specific cases involving Scheduled Tribes)

schedules_summary.description: Specifies the geographical areas that constitute the 'scheduled areas' for the purpose of this Act, including portions of Gobha Mauza, Kholahat Reserved Forest, Lumding Reserved Forest, Dabaka Reserved Forest, Suang Reserved Forest, Diju Valley South Reserved Forest, Bagser Reserved Forest, Panbari Reserved Forest, Upper Daigurung Reserved Forest, Lower Daigurung Reserved Forest, Village lands of Ghatiani Pathar, Dokhara Pathar and Murphuloni, and portions of Barpathar, Ghiladhari and Sarupathar Mauzas.

act_identification.act_title: THE SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES OF OFFICERS OF PARLIAMENT ACT, 1953
act_identification.act_short_title: Salaries and Allowances of Officers of Parliament Act, 1953

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the salaries and allowances of certain officers of Parliament.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the salaries, allowances, residence, medical facilities, and other perquisites for the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines 'officer of Parliament' for the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Salaries, etc., of officers of Parliament.
key_sections.description: Specifies the salaries and allowances payable to the Chairman, Deputy Chairman, Speaker, and Deputy Speaker.

key_sections.title: Residence for officers of Parliament.
key_sections.description: Entitles officers of Parliament to rent-free furnished residence and provisions for their families in case of death.

key_sections.title: Sumptuary allowance.
key_sections.description: Prescribes sumptuary allowances for the Speaker, Deputy Chairman, and Deputy Speaker.

key_sections.title: Travelling and daily allowances to officers of Parliament.
key_sections.description: Details entitlements for travelling and daily allowances for officers and their families.

key_sections.title: Medical facilities to officers of Parliament.
key_sections.description: Grants free medical facilities to officers of Parliament and their families.

key_sections.title: Family pension, etc., to spouse of Speaker dying in office.
key_sections.description: Provides for family pension and residence to the spouse of a Speaker who dies in office.

key_sections.title: Advances to officers of Parliament for purchase of motor-cars.
key_sections.description: Allows for repayable advances to officers for the purchase of motor-cars.

key_sections.title: Officers of Parliament not to draw salary or allowances as Members of Parliament.
key_sections.description: Prohibits officers from drawing additional salary or allowances as Members of Parliament.

key_sections.title: Exemption from liability to pay income-tax on daily allowance received by the Chairman and certain perquisites received by an officer of Parliament.
key_sections.description: Exempts certain allowances and perquisites from income-tax.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes.

powers_conferred: Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act (Section 11)

related_acts: Salaries, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 (30 of 1954)
Salaries and Allowances of Ministers Act, 1952 (58 of 1952)

applies_to: officers of Parliament
the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States
the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the House of the People

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government, in consultation with the Chairman and the Speaker

act_identification.act_title: THE TEA ACT, 1953

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India: Provided that it shall not apply to the State of Jammu and Kashmir* except to the extent to which the provisions of this Act relate to the control of the export of tea from, and the cultivation of tea in, India. *Vide notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019, this Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the control by the Union of the Tea industry, including the control, in pursuance of the International Agreement now in force, of the cultivation of tea in, and of the export of tea from, India and for that purpose to establish a Tea Board and levy a duty of excise on tea produced in India.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the control by the Union over the tea industry in India. This includes regulating the cultivation and export of tea, establishing a Tea Board, and levying an excise duty on tea produced in India.

chapter_titles: MANAGEMENT OR CONTROL OF TEA UNDERTAKINGS OR TEA UNITS BY THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES
CONTROL OVER THE EXPORT OF TEA AND TEA SEED

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its geographical extent, and the date of its commencement.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to expediency of control by the Union.
key_sections.description: Declares that it is expedient in the public interest for the Union to control the tea industry.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment and constitution of the Tea Board.
key_sections.description: Details the establishment of the Tea Board as a body corporate and its composition.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the duties and measures the Tea Board can undertake to promote the development of the tea industry.

key_sections.title: Method of control of extension of tea cultivation.
key_sections.description: Establishes the requirement for permission from the Board to plant tea on new land or replace tea areas.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to assume management or control of tea undertaking or tea unit in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to take over management or control of tea undertakings or units under specified conditions.

key_sections.title: Control of export of tea and tea seed.
key_sections.description: Mandates that tea and tea seed exports must be covered by a licence or permit.

key_sections.title: Imposition of Cess on Tea Produced In India.
key_sections.description: Provides for the levy and collection of an excise duty (cess) on all tea produced in India.

key_sections.title: Power to control price and distribution of tea or tea waste.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to fix prices, regulate distribution, and prohibit disposal of tea or tea waste.

key_sections.title: Penalty for illicit export.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for breaches related to the export of tea or tea seed without proper documentation.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeals and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals previous acts related to tea control and includes savings provisions for continuity.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint members and officers of the Board, issue directions to the Board, dissolve the Board, determine export allotment, assume management or control of tea undertakings/units, cancel or vary contracts, make declarations regarding tea undertakings/units, call for reports, control price and distribution of tea, cancel/suspend/modify Board actions, make rules, delegate powers, suspend operation of the Act, sanction prosecution.

Tea Board: To promote tea industry development, regulate production and cultivation, improve quality, promote co-operative efforts, undertake research, control pests, regulate sale and export, train in tea testing, increase consumption, register and license manufacturers/brokers/dealers, improve marketing, collect statistics, secure better working conditions, grant permission to plant tea, determine export quotas, issue export licences, maintain accounts of quotas, borrow funds, write off losses, make by-laws.
Adjudicating Officer (Secretary to the Board or other authorized officer): To hold inquiry and impose penalty for contraventions.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 36 penalizes illicit export of tea or tea seed as an offence under the Sea Customs Act, 1878. Section 37 imposes a fine up to one thousand rupees for making false returns. Section 41 imposes a penalty up to fifty thousand rupees and forfeiture of property for contravention of orders relating to price and distribution control. Section 42 imposes a penalty up to fifty thousand rupees for other contraventions of the Act or rules, and up to one lakh rupees for subsequent contraventions.
