Adjudication of these penalties is handled by an adjudicating officer appointed by the Deputy Chairman of the Board, with an appeal to the Deputy Chairman.

repealed_acts: The Indian Tea Control Act, 1938 (8 of 1938)
The Central Tea Board Act, 1949 (13 of 1949)
related_acts: Central Excises and Salt Act, 1944 (1 of 1944)
Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023 (18 of 2023)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairman, other members (not exceeding forty), Deputy Chairman, Secretary, and other officers of the Board. The Board may appoint other officers and employees.

applies_to: Whole of India (with specific provisions for Jammu and Kashmir)
Owners of tea estates and gardens
Persons employed in tea estates and gardens
Manufacturers of tea
Dealers (exporters and internal traders of tea)
Brokers of tea
Persons engaged in blending tea
exemptions: State of Jammu and Kashmir (except for control of export and cultivation of tea, though later made applicable to UT of J&K and Ladakh)
Tea imported into India from outside India
Tea shipped as stores on board vessels or aircraft (within reasonable quantity)
Tea exported by post in packages not exceeding five kilograms
Tea exported with previous sanction of Central Government by Red Cross Society or organizations for troops overseas
Tea taken as part of personal luggage of a passenger
special_provisions: The Act's application to the State of Jammu and Kashmir was initially limited but later extended to the Union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh by notification.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government has the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act. The Tea Board has the power to make by-laws consistent with the Act and rules.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement involves inspection powers for authorized persons, the Board's power to call for returns, imposition of penalties for contraventions (e.g., illicit export, false returns, price control violations), and adjudication of these penalties by an adjudicating officer. The Central Government exercises general control over the Board's acts and proceedings and can issue directions.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No Court inferior to that of a Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the First Class shall try any offence punishable under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE ANDHRA STATE ACT, 1953

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Territories comprising the States of Andhra, Madras, and Mysore, as affected by the formation of Andhra State and transfer of territory.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the formation of the State of Andhra, the increasing of the area of the State of Mysore and the diminishing of the area of the State of Madras, and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to facilitate the formation of the State of Andhra, adjust the boundaries of the State of Mysore by increasing its area, and consequently diminish the area of the State of Madras. It also addresses various connected matters arising from this reorganization, including legislative representation, High Courts, financial provisions, and administrative arrangements.

chapter_titles: PART II: FORMATION OF ANDHRA STATE AND TRANSFER OF TERRITORY FROM MADRAS TO MYSORE
PART III: REPRESENTATION IN THE LEGISLATURES
PART VII: ADMINISTRATIVE AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies the commencement dates for different parts and sections.

key_sections.title: Formation of Andhra State.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Part A State of Andhra from specified territories of the Madras State.

key_sections.title: Transfer of territory from Madras to Mysore.
key_sections.description: Adds specified territories from the Madras State to the State of Mysore.

key_sections.title: Amendment of the First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule of the Constitution to reflect the formation of Andhra and changes in Madras and Mysore territories.

key_sections.title: Representation in the House of the People.
key_sections.description: Adjusts the number of seats allotted to Madras, Mysore, and Andhra in the House of the People.

key_sections.title: Strength of Legislative Assemblies.
key_sections.description: Determines the total number of seats in the Legislative Assemblies of Andhra, Madras, and Mysore.

key_sections.title: High Court for Andhra.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of a separate High Court for the State of Andhra.

key_sections.title: Apportionment of assets and liabilities.
key_sections.description: Outlines how the assets and liabilities of the State of Madras are to be apportioned between Madras, Andhra, and Mysore.

key_sections.title: Power to adapt laws.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the appropriate Government to adapt and modify existing laws for application in the new or altered states.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to the Indian Administrative Service and the Indian Police Service.
key_sections.description: Addresses the creation of separate cadres for the Indian Administrative Service and Indian Police Service for Andhra and Madras, and allocation of officers.

key_sections.title: Special provisions with regard to Tungabhadra Project.
key_sections.description: Details the rights and liabilities of Andhra and Mysore concerning the Tungabhadra Project.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the President to issue orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions.

powers_conferred: President: To appoint an earlier date for the High Court of Andhra (S.28).
President: To determine Judges of the Andhra High Court (S.29).
President: To order allocation or adjustment of property/benefits/liability between states (S.51).
President: To determine strength, composition, and allocation of officers for Indian Administrative Service and Indian Police Service cadres (S.61).
President: To determine allocation of officers for Indian Civil Service, Indian Police, Indian Service of Engineers, and Indian Forest Service (S.62).
President: To require persons to serve in connection with affairs of Andhra or Mysore (S.63).
President: To give directions to States of Madras, Andhra, and Mysore for division of services (S.64).
President: To determine allowances and privileges of the Governor of Andhra (S.67).
President: To remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act (S.69).
Governor of Madras: To authorise expenditure from Consolidated Fund of Andhra and Madras (S.43).
Governor of Andhra: To appoint the principal seat of the High Court of Andhra (S.28).
Governor of Andhra: To authorise further expenditure from Consolidated Fund of Andhra (S.43).
Rajpramukh of Mysore: To authorise expenditure from Consolidated Fund of Mysore (S.43).
Appropriate Government (Central/State): To make adaptations and modifications to laws (S.54).
Governor (Andhra) and Rajpramukh (transferred territory): To name authorities for exercising statutory functions (S.56).
Chief Justice of Madras High Court: To certify proceedings for transfer to Andhra or Mysore High Courts (S.38, S.41, S.58).
Chief Justice of Andhra High Court: To appoint place(s) of sitting for Judges and Division Courts (S.36).
High Court of Andhra: To approve, admit, enrol, remove, and suspend advocates and attorneys, and make rules (S.31, S.32).

amended_acts: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
related_acts: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
The Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies (Madras) Order, 1951
The Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies (Mysore) Order, 1951
The Delimitation of Council Constituencies (Madras) Order, 1951
The Delimitation of Council Constituencies (Mysore) Order, 1951
The Madras Co-operative Societies Act, 1932 (6 of 1932)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: President appoints Judges of the Andhra High Court (S.29). Governor of Andhra appoints the principal seat of the High Court (S.28). Governor or Rajpramukh of a State determines corresponding court, tribunal, authority or officer in case of doubt regarding transfer of proceedings (S.58).

applies_to: The State of Andhra
The State of Madras (as diminished)
The State of Mysore (as increased)
Legislative bodies of these states
High Courts of these states
Government services and personnel in these states
Financial assets and liabilities of these states
special_provisions: Special provisions for detention in certain jails and institutions (S.59).
Continuance of facilities in certain State institutions (S.60).
Special provisions with regard to Tungabhadra Project (S.66).
Allowances and privileges of the Governor of Andhra (S.67).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The High Court of Andhra has power to make rules with respect to advocates, attorneys, practice and procedure (S.31, S.32). The President has power to make orders for allocation/adjustment (S.51), give directions (S.64), remove difficulties (S.69), and determine allowances (S.67). The appropriate Government has power to adapt laws (S.54). The Governor/Rajpramukh has power to name authorities for statutory functions (S.56).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through its statutory provisions, orders issued by the President, Governors, and Rajpramukh, and through the jurisdiction and transfer mechanisms of the High Courts of Madras, Andhra, and Mysore. It provides for the legal framework for state reorganization, including transfer of assets, liabilities, personnel, and judicial proceedings.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court of Andhra, High Court at Madras, High Court of Mysore, Supreme Court.

schedules_summary.description: Lists Andhra Members and Madras Members of the Council of States, specifying their terms of office.
Details modifications to the Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies (Madras) Order, 1951 and (Mysore) Order, 1951.
Specifies modifications to the Delimitation of Council Constituencies (Madras) Order, 1951.
Lists members of the Madras Legislative Council and provides for determining their terms of office.
Outlines modifications to the Delimitation of Council Constituencies (Mysore) Order, 1951.
Contains modifications to the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 and the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950.
Details provisions for the apportionment of assets and liabilities between the States of Madras, Andhra, and Mysore.
Lists jails and other institutions in the State of Madras and the transferred territory for use by the Government of Andhra.
Lists institutions in the State of Madras and the transferred territory where facilities are to be continued for the State of Andhra.

act_identification.act_title: THE CALCUTTA HIGH COURT (EXTENSION OF JURISDICTION) ACT, 1953
act_identification.act_short_title: The Calcutta High Court (Extension of Jurisdiction) Act, 1953

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Chandernagore and Andaman and Nicobar Islands

act_overview.preamble: An Act to extend the jurisdiction of the High Court at Calcutta to Chandernagore and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to extend the jurisdiction of the High Court at Calcutta to Chandernagore and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, making it the High Court for these territories.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as The Calcutta High Court (Extension of Jurisdiction) Act, 1953.

key_sections.title: Extension of jurisdiction of Calcutta High Court to Chandernagore and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
key_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the High Court at Calcutta to Chandernagore and Andaman and Nicobar Islands, retrospectively for Chandernagore from 2nd May, 1950.

key_sections.title: Effect of certain orders.
key_sections.description: Specifies that orders made by the highest court of appeal for Chandernagore before 2nd May, 1950, or by the Chief Commissioner of Andaman and Nicobar Islands before the commencement of this Act, shall be deemed orders of the High Court at Calcutta.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the High Court at Calcutta the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act and effectively exercise its jurisdiction in Chandernagore and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

powers_conferred: Power to make rules (to the High Court at Calcutta)

applies_to: Chandernagore
Andaman and Nicobar Islands

implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court at Calcutta

act_identification.act_title: THE COIR INDUSTRY ACT, 1953

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Board for the development of the Coir Industry and for that purpose to levy a customs duty on coir fiber, coir yarn and coir products exported from India and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the establishment of the Coir Board to promote the development of the Coir Industry. It also enables the levy of a customs duty on the export of coir fiber, coir yarn, and coir products to fund these development activities.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER III CONTROL OVER THE EXPORT OF COIR FIBRE COIR YARD AND PRODUCTS
CHAPTER IV FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT
CHAPTER V CONTROL BY THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to expediency of control by the Union.
key_sections.description: Declares the Union's control over the coir industry as expedient in public interest.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment and constitution of the Coir Board.
key_sections.description: Details the establishment, corporate nature, and composition of the Coir Board.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the duties and measures the Board can undertake for coir industry development, including promoting exports, regulating production, research, and marketing.

key_sections.title: Control of export of coir fibre, coir yarn and coir products.
key_sections.description: Mandates that export of coir products requires a licence issued by the Board.

key_sections.title: Imposition of a duty of customs on export of coir fibre, coir yarn and coir products.
key_sections.description: Provides for the levy and collection of a customs duty (cess) on exported coir products.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Coir Fund and specifies sources of its funding and application of funds.

key_sections.title: General control over acts and proceedings of the Board.
key_sections.description: Subjects all acts and proceedings of the Board to the control of the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of Section 12 regarding export control.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes.

key_sections.title: Power of Board to make by-laws.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board power to make by-laws consistent with the Act and rules.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint members of the Coir Board
Coir Board to acquire, hold and dispose of property, both movable and immovable, and to contract, and to sue and be sued
Board to elect a Vice-Chairman
Board to constitute Executive and other Committees
Central Government to appoint a Secretary to the Board
Board to appoint officers and employees
Board to promote development of the coir industry

Board to regulate production, license exporters, undertake research, collect statistics, fix grade standards, improve marketing, promote co-operative organisation, ensure remunerative returns, license retting places and warehouses
Central Government to dissolve the Board
Board to issue licences for export of coir fibre, coir yarn or coir products
Central Government to levy and collect a duty of customs (cess) on exported coir products
Central Government to pay proceeds of cess to the Board
Central Government to grant sums of money to the Board
Board to borrow on the security of the Fund or any other asset
Central Government to control acts and proceedings of the Board
Central Government to delegate any power exercisable by it under this Act
Central Government to suspend or relax the operation of all or any of the provisions of this Act
Central Government to make rules
Board to make by-laws
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person contravening the provisions of section 12 (control of export) shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees. Attempts or abetment of contravention are also deemed contraventions. If the offence is by a company, persons in charge and the company are liable, and directors/managers/secretaries/officers are also liable if the offence was committed with their consent, connivance, or neglect.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (for Chairman, Board members, Secretary)

applies_to: Whole of India
exemptions: any coir product dispatched out of the territories to which this Act extends by post or carried in a passenger’s luggage for his personal use
export of any coir fibre, coir yarn or coir product to any foreign settlement bounded by India (if exempted by Central Government)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Control of export through licensing by the Board (Section 12), imposition of customs duty (cess) on exports (Section 13), general control and directions by the Central Government over the Board (Section 18), and penalties for contravention (Section 20).

act_identification.act_title: THE LUSHAI HILLS DISTRICT (CHANGE OF NAME) ACT, 1954
act_identification.act_short_title: Lushai Hills District (Change of Name) Act, 1954

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the tribal area in Assam now known as the Lushai Hills District

act_overview.preamble: An Act to change the name of the Lushai Hills District.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to change the official name of the Lushai Hills District to the Mizo District. It also makes necessary amendments to the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution to reflect this change and ensures that all future references to the Lushai Hills District are construed as references to the Mizo District.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date, to be appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Lushai Hills District to be known as Mizo District.
key_sections.description: Declares that the Lushai Hills District in Assam shall be known as the Mizo District from the Act's commencement.

key_sections.title: Amendment of the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Amends paragraph 20 of the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution to reflect the change of name to Mizo District.

key_sections.title: Reference to Lushai Hills District to be construed as reference to Mizo District.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that any reference to the Lushai Hills District in any legal document shall be interpreted as a reference to the Mizo District.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint the date of commencement of the Act

amended_acts: the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (for commencement date)

applies_to: the tribal area in Assam now known as the Lushai Hills District

act_identification.act_title: THE DRUGS AND MAGIC REMEDIES (OBJECTIONABLE ADVERTISEMENTS) ACT, 1954
act_identification.act_short_title: Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisement) Act, 1954

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India, and applies also to persons domiciled in the territories to which this Act extends who are outside the said territories

act_overview.preamble: An Act to control the advertisement of drugs in certain cases, to prohibit the advertisement for certain purposes of remedies alleged to possess magic qualities and to provide for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to control the advertisement of drugs in specific cases and to prohibit the advertisement of remedies claiming magic qualities for certain purposes. It also provides for related matters concerning these prohibitions and their enforcement.

key_definitions: taking any part in the publication of any advertisement

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's name, geographical reach, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms like 'advertisement', 'drug', and 'magic remedy'.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of advertisement of certain drugs for treatment of certain diseases and disorders.
key_sections.description: Prohibits advertisements for drugs related to specific conditions like miscarriage, sexual pleasure, menstrual disorders, and diseases listed in the Schedule.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of misleading advertisements relating to drugs.
key_sections.description: Prohibits advertisements that give a false impression, make false claims, or are otherwise false or misleading about drugs.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of advertisement of magic remedies for treatment of certain diseases and disorders.
key_sections.description: Prohibits advertisements for magic remedies claiming efficacy for conditions specified in Section 3.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of import into, and export from, India of certain advertisements.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the import and export of documents containing advertisements prohibited under Sections 3, 4, or 5.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of the Act or rules, including imprisonment and/or fine.

key_sections.title: Powers of entry, search, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants Gazetted Officers powers to enter, search, and seize materials related to offenses under the Act.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Specifies liability for offenses committed by companies, including persons in charge and directors/managers.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable.
key_sections.description: Declares offenses under the Act as cognizable.

key_sections.title: Forfeiture.
key_sections.description: Allows courts to order forfeiture of documents or articles involved in contravention.

key_sections.title: Savings.
key_sections.description: Lists specific advertisements and materials that are exempt from the Act's provisions, such as those by registered medical practitioners or government publications.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt from application of Act.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to exempt certain drugs or advertisements from the Act's application in public interest.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government authority to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to appoint commencement date, to make rules, to exempt from application of Act
State Government: to authorize Gazetted Officers for entry, search, seizure
Gazetted Officer: powers of entry, search, seizure
Courts: to try offences, to direct forfeiture
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of the Act or rules made thereunder is punishable. First conviction carries imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both. Subsequent convictions carry imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both.

amended_acts: Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Amendment Act, 1963 (42 of 1963)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (for commencement date, rules, exemptions); State Government (for authorizing Gazetted Officers)

applies_to: whole of India
persons domiciled in the territories to which this Act extends who are outside the said territories
exemptions: any signboard or notice displayed by a registered medical practitioner on his premises indicating that treatment for any disease, disorder or condition specified in section 3, the Schedule or the rules made under this Act is undertaken in those premises
any treatise or book dealing with any of the matters specified in section 3 from a bonafide scientific or social standpoint
any advertisement relating to any drug sent confidentially in the manner prescribed under section 16 only to a registered medical practitioner
any advertisement relating to a drug printed or published by the Government

any advertisement relating to a drug printed or published by any person with the previous sanction of the Government granted prior to the commencement of the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Amendment Act, 1963 (42 of 1963)
special_provisions: Extended to Pondicherry by Reg. 7 of 1963
Extended to the State of Sikkim, vide S.O. 949 (E), dated 20th October, 1988

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Prohibition of objectionable advertisements; penalties for contravention; powers of entry, search, and seizure by authorized Gazetted Officers; provisions for offences by companies; offences are cognizable; forfeiture of materials involved in contravention.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No Court inferior to that of a Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class

schedules_summary.description: Lists 54 diseases, disorders, or conditions for which advertisements of certain drugs and magic remedies are prohibited, including Appendicitis, Cancer, Diabetes, Heart diseases, Sexual impotence, Tuberculosis, and Venereal diseases.

act_identification.act_title: THE DELIVERY OF BOOKS AND NEWSPAPERS (PUBLIC LIBRARIES) ACT, 1954
act_identification.act_short_title: Delivery of Books and Newspapers (Public Libraries) Act, 1954

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for delivery of books to the National Library and other public libraries.
act_overview.purpose: This Act mandates the delivery of copies of all published books and newspapers to the National Library at Calcutta and other specified public libraries. Its primary purpose is to ensure the preservation of these publications for public access and national heritage.
act_overview.act_category: Institutions of Natural and Cultural Importance

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'book', 'newspaper', and 'public libraries'.

key_sections.title: Delivery of books of public libraries.
key_sections.description: Mandates publishers to deliver copies of books to the National Library and other public libraries within thirty days of publication.

key_sections.title: Delivery of newspapers to public libraries.
key_sections.description: Requires publishers to deliver copies of each issue of newspapers to specified public libraries as soon as published.

key_sections.title: Receipt for books delivered.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the person in charge of a public library must provide a written receipt for delivered books.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including fines, for publishers who contravene the provisions of the Act or rules made thereunder.

key_sections.title: Cognizance of offences.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for taking cognizance of offences and specifies the courts competent to try such offences.

key_sections.title: Application of Act to books and newspapers published by Government.
key_sections.description: Extends the Act's applicability to government publications, with an exemption for books meant for official use only.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act and specifies parliamentary oversight for such rules.

powers_conferred: Central Government to specify three other public libraries by notification in the Official Gazette (Section 2(b))
Central Government to notify public libraries for newspaper delivery (Section 3A)
Central Government to empower officers for cognizance of offences (Section 6(1))
Central Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act (Section 8(1))
Court trying the offence may direct that the whole or any part of the fine realised shall be paid, by way of compensation, to the public library (Section 5)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any publisher who contravenes any provision of this Act or of any rule made thereunder shall be punishable with fine which may extend to fifty rupees and, if the contravention is in respect of a book, shall also be punishable with fine which shall be equivalent to the value of the book.

related_acts: Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867 (XXV of 1867)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government to empower officers for cognizance of offences (Section 6(1))

applies_to: publisher of every book published in the territories to which this Act extends
publisher of every newspaper, published in the territories to which this Act extends
books and newspapers published by or under the authority of the Government
exemptions: newspaper published in conformity with the provisions of section 5 of the Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867 (from definition of 'book')
any second or subsequent edition of a book in which no additions or alterations have been made and a copy of a preceding edition has been delivered (Section 3(4))
books meant for official use only (Section 7)
special_provisions: Extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Cognizance of offences taken on complaint made by an officer empowered by the Central Government; trial by presidency magistrate or magistrate of the first class.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: presidency magistrate or a magistrate of the first class

act_identification.act_title: THE HIGH COURT JUDGES (SALARIES AND CONDITIONS OF SERVICE) ACT, 1954
act_identification.act_short_title: High Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Act, 1954

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India (for High Courts in States)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate salaries and certain conditions of service of the Judges of High Courts
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to regulate the salaries and various conditions of service for Judges of High Courts in India. It covers aspects such as leave, pensions, allowances, and other perquisites.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'acting Chief Justice', 'Judge', 'High Court', and 'actual service'.

key_sections.title: Kinds of leave admissible to a judge.
key_sections.description: Outlines the different types of leave that can be granted to a Judge, including leave on full allowances, half allowances, and casual leave.

key_sections.title: Salaries of the Judges.
key_sections.description: Specifies the monthly salaries payable to the Chief Justice and other Judges of a High Court.

key_sections.title: Pension payable to Judges.
key_sections.description: Establishes the entitlement of Judges to a pension upon retirement, subject to conditions specified in the First Schedule.

key_sections.title: Family pensions and gratuities.
key_sections.description: Details the provisions for family pensions and gratuities payable upon the death of a Judge.

key_sections.title: Facility of rent-free houses.
key_sections.description: Grants Judges the entitlement to a rent-free official residence or an allowance in lieu thereof.

key_sections.title: Exemption from liability to pay income-tax on certain perquisites received by a Judge.
key_sections.description: Provides for exemption from income-tax on specific perquisites like rent-free residence, conveyance facilities, sumptuary allowance, and leave travel concession.

key_sections.title: Facilities for medical treatment and other conditions of service.
key_sections.description: Ensures medical treatment facilities for Judges and their families and states that other conditions of service will be determined by rules.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: President of India: To add to the service for pension for special reasons (Section 16).
President of India: To fix vacation periods for High Courts (Section 23A).
Governor of the State: To grant or refuse leave to a Judge, or revoke or curtail leave (Section 13).
Central Government: To make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (Section 24).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Governor of the State, after consultation with the Chief Justice of that High Court, is competent to grant or refuse leave to a Judge (Section 13). The President of India is competent to grant pension to a Judge (Section 21).

applies_to: Judges of High Courts
Chief Justice of a High Court
acting Chief Justice
acting Judge
additional Judge
special_provisions: Special provisions in respect of Judges transferred from the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir (Section 23C).

schedules_summary.description: Details the scales and provisions for pensions payable to Judges, categorized into Part I (for Judges not holding other pensionable posts or electing this part) and Part III (for Judges holding other pensionable posts and not electing Part I).
Contains tables for Injury Gratuities and Pensions, and Family Gratuities and Pensions, specifying amounts for Chief Justices and other Judges, and for their widows and children.

act_identification.act_title: THE SALARY, ALLOWANCES AND PENSION OF MEMBERS OF PARLIAMENT ACT, 1954
act_identification.act_short_title: Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the [1][salary, allowances and pension] of Members of Parliament.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the salaries, daily allowances, travelling allowances, and pension for Members of Parliament. It also outlines various facilities and benefits, including free transit, constituency allowances, and provisions for family pension and advances.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'committee', 'dependent', and 'member'.

key_sections.title: Salaries and daily allowances.
key_sections.description: Outlines the entitlement of members to salaries and daily allowances, including provisions for reduction during specific periods and future increases.

key_sections.title: Travelling allowances.
key_sections.description: Details the travelling allowances payable to members for journeys undertaken for parliamentary duties, covering various modes of transport.

key_sections.title: Travelling allowances for intermediate journeys.
key_sections.description: Specifies travelling allowances for members who are absent for short periods during sessions or committee sittings, including air travel facilities.

key_sections.title: Free transit by railway.
key_sections.description: Provides for free non-transferable railway passes for members and details their usage and validity.

key_sections.title: Free transit by Steamer.
key_sections.description: Grants special free steamer transit and airfare facilities for members representing the Union territories of Andaman and Nicobar Islands or Lakshadweep.

key_sections.title: Constituency allowance and amenities.
key_sections.description: Entitles members to constituency allowance, office expense allowance, medical facilities, and housing/utility facilities.

key_sections.title: Pension.
key_sections.description: Establishes pension for former members of Parliament, including additional pension for longer service and conditions for its payment.

key_sections.title: Family pension.
key_sections.description: Provides for family pension to the spouse or dependents of a deceased member of Parliament.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power on a Joint Committee of both Houses of Parliament to make rules for regulating various allowances, facilities, and pension matters under the Act.

powers_conferred: Power to make rules for regulating payment of daily and travelling allowances and pension (Joint Committee of both Houses of Parliament under Section 9)

related_acts: Salaries and Allowances of Ministers Act, 1952 (58 of 1952)
Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act, 1977 (33 of 1977)
Salaries and Allowances of Officers of Parliament Act, 1953 (20 of 1953)
Representation of the People Act, 1951 (43 of 1951)

authorities_established: Joint Committee of both Houses of Parliament
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Chairman of the Council of States and Speaker of the House of the People nominate members to the Joint Committee.

applies_to: Members of Parliament
Ex-Members of Parliament
Spouse of a Member
Dependents of a Member
Companion or relatives of a Member (for travel facilities)
exemptions: Ministers (as defined in the Salaries and Allowances of Ministers Act, 1952)
Leaders of the Opposition (as defined in the Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act, 1977)
Officers of Parliament (as defined in the Salaries and Allowances of Officers of Parliament Act, 1953)
special_provisions: Special air travel facilities for members from Ladakh area of the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
Free steamer transit and airfare for members from Andaman and Nicobar Islands or Lakshadweep.
Special facilities for blind and physically incapacitated Members for travel.
Air travel facilities in certain circumstances where usual routes are inaccessible due to climatic conditions.
Provisions for members residing within 300 kilometers from Delhi or in specific North-Eastern states regarding road mileage allowance.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Joint Committee of both Houses of Parliament

act_identification.act_title: THE HIMACHAL PRADESH AND BILASPUR (NEW STATE) ACT, 1954
act_identification.act_short_title: Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur (New State) Act, 1954

legislative_details.geographical_extent: The new State of Himachal Pradesh, formed by uniting the existing States of Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the formation of the new State of Himachal Pradesh by uniting the existing States of Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur, and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the formation of a new Part C State named Himachal Pradesh by merging the existing States of Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur. It also addresses consequential changes in legislative representation, judicial administration, and the continuity of existing laws, authorities, and taxes.

chapter_titles: PART II FORMATION OF THE NEW STATE OF HIMACHAL PRADESH
PART III REPRESENTATION IN THE LEGISLATURES
PART V ADMINISTRATIVE AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'article', 'existing States', 'law', and 'sitting member'.

key_sections.title: Formation of the new State of Himachal Pradesh.
key_sections.description: Establishes the formation of a new Part C State, Himachal Pradesh, by uniting the existing States of Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur.

key_sections.title: Amendment of the First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule of the Constitution to reflect the omission of Bilaspur and the new territory of Himachal Pradesh.

key_sections.title: Representation in the Council of States.
key_sections.description: Allots one seat to the new State in the Council of States and specifies the status of the sitting member.

key_sections.title: Representation in the House of the People.
key_sections.description: Allots 4 seats to the new State in the House of the People until further provision is made by law.

key_sections.title: Parliamentary constituencies of the new State and their delimitation.
key_sections.description: Defines the initial Parliamentary constituencies for the new State and refers to modifications in the Delimitation Order.

key_sections.title: Court of the Judicial Commissioner for the new State.
key_sections.description: Amalgamates the existing Courts of Judicial Commissioner for Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur into a single Court for the new State, detailing its jurisdiction, officers, and procedure.

key_sections.title: Existing laws to continue.
key_sections.description: Ensures that all laws in force in the areas forming the new State continue until repealed or amended by a competent authority.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the President power to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions for a period of one year.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint the commencement date of the Act (Section 1(2)).
Delimitation Commission to amend, vary or rescind its final orders regarding constituencies (Section 23).
The new Court of the Judicial Commissioner to admit, suspend and remove advocates, vakils and pleaders and to make rules (Section 25(e)).
The new Court of the Judicial Commissioner to make modifications to practice and procedure (Section 25(f)).
The President to make orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act (Section 32).

amended_acts: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
related_acts: Delimitation of Parliamentary Constituencies (Part C States) Order, 1951
Judicial Commissioners’ Courts (Declaration as High Courts) Act, 1950 (15 of 1950)
Government of Part C States Act, 1951

authorities_established: Court of the Judicial Commissioner for the new State

applies_to: The existing States of Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur
The new State of Himachal Pradesh
special_provisions: Saving of the powers of the Central Government in relation to the Bhakra-Nangal Project (Section 31).
Provisions for the continuity of sitting members of the Council of States and House of the People (Sections 5, 11).
Continuity of existing authorities, officers, laws, and taxes in the new State (Sections 27, 28, 30).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for commencement date); New Court of the Judicial Commissioner (for advocates, practice, and procedure); President (to remove difficulties).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Court of the Judicial Commissioner for the new State; Subordinate Courts.

schedules_summary.description: Contains modifications to the Delimitation of Parliamentary Constituencies (Part C States) Order, 1951, specifically regarding Bilaspur and the new Himachal Pradesh.
Details amendments to the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) (Part C States) Order, 1951, including the omission of Bilaspur and additions to the list of Scheduled Castes for Himachal Pradesh.

act_identification.act_title: THE SHILLONG (RIFILE RANGE AND UMLONG) CANTONMENTS ASSIMILATION OF LAWS ACT, 1954
act_identification.act_short_title: Shillong (Rifle Range and Umlong) Cantonments Assimilation of Laws Act, 1954

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Fifth Year of the Republic of India
legislative_details.geographical_extent: scheduled areas (The Shillong (Rifle Range) Cantonment and The Shillong (Umlong) Cantonment) and Khasi and Jaintia Hills District

act_overview.preamble: An Act to assimilate certain laws in force in the scheduled areas to the laws in force in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills District.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to assimilate laws in force in the Shillong (Rifle Range and Umlong) Cantonments (referred to as 'scheduled areas') with the laws in force in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills District. It aims to ensure that the same legal framework applies across these regions.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's short title and specifies that its commencement date will be appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'law', and 'scheduled areas'.

key_sections.title: Assimilation of laws.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that laws previously in force in the scheduled areas will cease, and laws from the Khasi and Jaintia Hills District will extend to and be in force in these areas.

key_sections.title: Removal of difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make provisions to remove any difficulties arising from the transition of laws under Section 3.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint the commencement date of the Act (Section 1(2))
Central Government to make provisions for the removal of difficulties arising from the transition of laws (Section 4)

applies_to: The Shillong (Rifle Range) Cantonment
The Shillong (Umlong) Cantonment

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act directly assimilates laws by ceasing existing ones in scheduled areas and extending laws from the Khasi and Jaintia Hills District to them. The Central Government is empowered to resolve transitional difficulties.

schedules_summary.description: Specifies the 'scheduled areas' referred to in the Act, which include The Shillong (Rifle Range) Cantonment and The Shillong (Umlong) Cantonment, providing detailed geographical descriptions and boundary coordinates for each.

act_identification.act_title: THE SPECIAL MARRIAGE ACT, 1954

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India, and applies also to citizens of India domiciled in the territories to which this Act extends

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide a special form of marriage in certain cases, for the registration of such and certain other marriages and for divorce.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides a special legal framework for solemnizing marriages between any two persons, facilitating the registration of such marriages and other forms of marriages, and establishing procedures for judicial separation and divorce.

chapter_titles: REGISTRATION OF MARRIAGES CELEBRATED IN OTHER FORMS
CONSEQUENCES OF MARRIAGE UNDER THIS ACT
RESTITUTION OF CONJUGAL RIGHTS AND JUDICIAL SEPARATION

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, its geographical application to India and citizens domiciled therein, and its effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'degrees of prohibited relationship', 'district', and 'district court'.

key_sections.title: Marriage Officers.
key_sections.description: Empowers State and Central Governments to appoint Marriage Officers for the purposes of this Act.

key_sections.title: Conditions relating to solemnization of special marriages.
key_sections.description: Outlines the essential conditions for solemnizing a special marriage, including age, mental capacity, and not being within prohibited degrees of relationship.

key_sections.title: Notice of intended marriage.
key_sections.description: Requires parties intending to marry under this Act to give written notice to the Marriage Officer.

key_sections.title: Certificate of marriage.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Marriage Officer to issue a certificate of marriage after solemnization, which serves as conclusive evidence of the marriage.

key_sections.title: Registration of marriages celebrated in other forms.
key_sections.description: Allows for the registration of marriages celebrated in other forms, provided certain conditions are met.

key_sections.title: Restitution of conjugal rights.
key_sections.description: Enables an aggrieved party to petition the district court for restitution of conjugal rights if the other party has withdrawn from society without reasonable excuse.

key_sections.title: Judicial separation.
key_sections.description: Permits either spouse to petition the district court for judicial separation on specified grounds, including those for divorce or non-compliance with a restitution decree.

key_sections.title: Void marriages.
key_sections.description: Declares marriages solemnized in contravention of certain conditions of Section 4 or where a party was impotent as null and void.

key_sections.title: Voidable marriages.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which a marriage may be annulled by a decree of nullity, such as non-consummation, pre-marital pregnancy by another, or consent obtained by coercion or fraud.

key_sections.title: Divorce.
key_sections.description: Lays down various grounds upon which a petition for divorce may be presented to the district court by either the husband or the wife.

key_sections.title: Divorce by mutual consent.
key_sections.description: Provides for divorce by mutual consent of both parties, subject to conditions regarding separation period and agreement to dissolve the marriage.

key_sections.title: Penalty on married person marrying again under this Act.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that a person already married who solemnizes another marriage under this Act commits an offence under the Indian Penal Code, rendering the new marriage void.

key_sections.title: Punishment of bigamy.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties under the Indian Penal Code for bigamy committed by a person whose marriage was solemnized under this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central and State Governments the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: State Government may appoint one or more Marriage Officers (Section 3(1))
Central Government may specify officers as Marriage Officers (Section 3(2))
Marriage Officer to inquire into objections (Section 8(1))
Marriage Officer shall have all the powers vested in a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for inquiries (Section 9(1))
Marriage Officer may impose costs by way of compensation (Section 9(2))
Central Government shall give its decision on objections from abroad (Section 10)
District court to decide appeals from orders of Marriage Officer (Section 8(2), Section 17)
Court to pass decrees for restitution of conjugal rights, judicial separation, nullity, or divorce (Section 22, 23, 24, 25, 27, 28, 34)
Court to order alimony pendente lite (Section 36)
Court to order permanent alimony and maintenance (Section 37)
Court to pass interim orders and make provisions for custody, maintenance and education of minor children (Section 38)
High Court to make rules regulating procedure (Section 41)
Central Government and State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act (Section 50)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person printing or publishing in camera proceedings without permission is punishable with fine up to one thousand rupees (Section 33(2)). A married person marrying again under this Act commits an offence under section 494 or 495 of the Indian Penal Code (Section 43). A person whose marriage is solemnized under this Act and contracts another marriage during the lifetime of spouse is subject to penalties under section 494 and 495 of the Indian Penal Code (Section 44). Any person signing a false declaration or certificate is guilty of an offence under section 199 of the Indian Penal Code (Section 45). A Marriage Officer who knowingly and wilfully solemnizes a marriage in contravention of the Act is punishable with simple imprisonment up to one year, or with fine up to five hundred rupees, or both (Section 46).

repealed_acts: The Special Marriage Act, 1872 (3 of 1872)
related_acts: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 (78 of 1956)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government and Central Government have the power to appoint Marriage Officers.

applies_to: Whole of India
Citizens of India domiciled in the territories to which this Act extends
Any two persons
special_provisions: Where the marriage is solemnized in the State of Jammu and Kashmir, both parties must be citizens of India domiciled in the territories to which this Act extends (Section 4(e)).

Section 19 and section 21 shall not apply, and so much of section 20 as creates a disability shall also not apply, where the marriage is solemnized under this Act between two persons who both profess the Hindu, Buddhist, Sikh or Jaina religion (Section 21A).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government, State Government, and High Court
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through Marriage Officers who solemnize and register marriages, and through district courts which handle petitions for restitution of conjugal rights, judicial separation, nullity, divorce, alimony, child custody, and appeals. Proceedings are regulated by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District court, High Court, Supreme Court

schedules_summary.description: Lists the 'Degrees of prohibited relationship' for both men (Part I) and women (Part II).
Provides the form for the 'NOTICE OF INTENDED MARRIAGE'.
Contains the forms for 'DECLARATION TO BE MADE BY THE BRIDEGROOM' and 'DECLARATION TO BE MADE BY THE BRIDE', to be signed by parties and witnesses before solemnization.
Presents the form for the 'CERTIFICATE OF MARRIAGE' to be issued by the Marriage Officer after solemnization.
Outlines the form for the 'CERTIFICATE OF MARRIAGE CELEBRATED IN OTHER FORMS' for registration under Chapter III.

act_identification.act_title: THE ESSENTIAL COMMODITIES ACT, 1955

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Sixth Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide, in the interest of the general public, for the control of the production, supply and distribution of, and trade and commerce, in certain commodities.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to ensure the availability and equitable distribution of essential commodities at fair prices. It grants powers to the Central Government to control their production, supply, distribution, and trade and commerce for the general public interest.

key_definitions: reasonable return on the capital employed

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used within the Act.

key_sections.title: Essential commodities declaration, etc.
key_sections.description: Defines 'essential commodity' and empowers the Central Government to amend the Schedule of essential commodities.

key_sections.title: Powers to control production, supply, distribution, etc., of essential commodities.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government powers to regulate or prohibit production, supply, distribution, trade, and commerce of essential commodities.

key_sections.title: Confiscation of essential commodity.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Collector to order confiscation of seized essential commodities, packages, and conveyances for contravention of orders.

key_sections.title: Issue of show cause notice before confiscation of food grains, etc.
key_sections.description: Mandates a show cause notice and opportunity for hearing before any confiscation order is made.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Allows appeals against confiscation orders to a judicial authority appointed by the State Government.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for contravention of orders made under Section 3, and forfeiture of property.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to recover certain amounts as arrears of land revenue.
key_sections.description: Enables the Central Government to recover unpaid amounts under Section 3 orders as arrears of land revenue.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Stipulates liability for offences committed by companies, including persons in charge and other officers.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable.
key_sections.description: Declares all offences under this Act to be cognizable.

key_sections.title: Power to try summarily.
key_sections.description: Allows for summary trial of certain offences related to essential commodities, especially foodstuffs and drugs.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken under Act.
key_sections.description: Provides protection against legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeals and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Essential Commodities Ordinance, 1955, and other similar state laws, with savings for existing orders.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to control production, supply, distribution, trade, and commerce of essential commodities (Sec 3(1))
Central Government: to amend the Schedule of essential commodities (Sec 2A(2))
Central Government: to authorize persons to exercise control over undertakings engaged in production and supply (Sec 3(4))
Central Government: to recover certain amounts as arrears of land revenue (Sec 7A)
Central Government: to specify orders for summary trial (Sec 12A(1))
State Government: to have duties imposed by orders under Section 3 (Sec 4)
State Government: to exercise powers to make orders or issue notifications under Section 3 (if delegated by Central Government, Sec 5)
Collector: to inspect and order confiscation of essential commodities, packages, and conveyances (Sec 6A)
Collector: to order the sale of seized essential commodities, especially those subject to speedy decay (Sec 6A(2))
Courts: to publish the name, place of business, etc., of companies convicted under the Act (Sec 10B)
Courts: to try certain offences summarily (Sec 12A)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person contravening an order made under Section 3 is punishable. For orders related to information or records (Sec 3(2)(h) or (i)), imprisonment may extend to one year and fine. For other orders, imprisonment is not less than three months but may extend to seven years, along with a fine. Property, packages, and conveyances involved in the contravention may be forfeited. Failure to comply with directions under Section 3(4)(b) carries similar penalties. Repeat offenders face enhanced penalties, with imprisonment not less than six months. Making false statements is punishable with imprisonment up to five years, or fine, or both. Companies and responsible individuals are liable for offences committed by the company.

amended_acts: Essential Commodities (Uttar Pradesh Second Amendment) Act, 1975
repealed_acts: Essential Commodities Ordinance, 1955 (1 of 1955)

any other law in force in any State immediately before the commencement of this Act in so far as such law controls or authorises the control of the production, supply and distribution of, and trade and commerce in, any essential commodity
related_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 (5 of 1970)

applies_to: whole of India
any person contravening orders
companies
public servants
exemptions: No confiscation of foodgrains or edible oilseeds from a producer if the seized items were produced by him (Sec 6A Proviso)
Owner of an animal, vehicle, vessel, or other conveyance used for hire may pay a fine instead of confiscation if used without their knowledge or connivance (Sec 6A Proviso 2, Sec 6B(2))
special_provisions: Extended to Goa, Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Lakshadweep and Amindivi Islands, and Sikkim.
Specific amendments for the State of Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh are detailed within the Act text.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (by order under Section 3); State Government (if powers are delegated by the Central Government under Section 5)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through orders issued by the Central Government to regulate or prohibit production, supply, distribution, trade, and commerce of essential commodities. Contraventions lead to penalties, including imprisonment, fines, and forfeiture of property. Confiscation of seized commodities is handled by the Collector, with provisions for appeal. Amounts due under orders can be recovered as arrears of land revenue. Certain offences can be tried summarily.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Judicial authority appointed by the State Government (for appeals against confiscation under Section 6C); Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class (for passing sentences under Section 12 and summary trials under Section 12A); Civil courts (jurisdiction barred for injunctions against government actions without prior notice under Section 12B).

schedules_summary.description: Lists the commodities declared as 'Essential Commodities' for the purposes of the Act, including drugs, fertilizer, foodstuffs (with edible oilseeds and oils), hank yarn made wholly from cotton, petroleum and petroleum products, raw jute and jute textiles, various seeds (food-crops, fruits, vegetables, cattle fodder, jute, cotton), masks, and hand sanitizers.

act_identification.act_title: THE PROTECTION OF CIVIL RIGHTS ACT, 1955
act_identification.act_short_title: the Protection of Civil Rights Act

act_overview.preamble: An Act to prescribe punishment for the [2][preaching and practice of “Untouchability”] for the enforcement of any disability arising therefrom and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to prescribe punishment for the practice of "Untouchability" and the enforcement of any disability arising from it. It seeks to abolish "untouchability" and ensure that civil rights accruing from this abolition are available to and availed of by concerned persons.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'civil rights' and 'Scheduled Castes'.

key_sections.title: Punishment for enforcing religious disabilities.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for preventing access to public worship places or religious services on grounds of 'untouchability'.

key_sections.title: Punishment for enforcing social disabilities.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for enforcing various social disabilities related to public access, services, and customs on grounds of 'untouchability'.

key_sections.title: Punishment for other offences arising out of “untouchability”.
key_sections.description: Covers offences like preventing exercise of civil rights, molesting, inciting, or insulting Scheduled Caste members on grounds of 'untouchability'.

key_sections.title: Unlawful compulsory labour when to be deemed to be a practice of “untouchability”.
key_sections.description: Defines and punishes compulsory labour like scavenging or carcass removal, if enforced on grounds of 'untouchability'.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to impose collective fine.
key_sections.description: Grants State Governments power to impose collective fines on inhabitants of an area involved in or abetting offences under the Act.

key_sections.title: Enhanced penalty on subsequent conviction.
key_sections.description: Stipulates increased penalties for repeat offenders convicted under this Act.

key_sections.title: Presumption by Courts in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Establishes a presumption that acts against Scheduled Caste members were committed on grounds of 'untouchability' unless proven otherwise.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable and triable summarily.
key_sections.description: Declares offences under the Act as cognizable and allows for summary trials by Judicial or Metropolitan Magistrates.

key_sections.title: Duty of State Government to ensure that the rights accruing from the abolition of “untouchability” may be availed of by the concerned persons.
key_sections.description: Mandates State Governments to take measures to ensure civil rights are made available and availed of, including legal aid, special courts, and surveys.

key_sections.title: Act to override other laws.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in other laws, customs, or court orders.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal.
key_sections.description: Repeals specific enactments listed in the Schedule to the extent they correspond or are repugnant to this Act.

powers_conferred: Court to cancel or suspend licences in certain cases (Section 8)
Government to resume or suspend grants made to public worship places or educational institutions (Section 9)
State Government to impose collective fine (Section 10A)
State Government to ensure that the rights accruing from the abolition of “untouchability” may be availed of by the concerned persons (Section 15A)
Central Government to make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act (Section 16B)
Central Government to coordinate measures taken by State Governments (Section 15A(3))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines various offences related to the practice of 'untouchability', including enforcing religious or social disabilities, refusing admission to public institutions, refusing to sell goods or render services, inciting 'untouchability', insulting Scheduled Caste members, and unlawful compulsory labour. Penalties generally range from not less than one month to not more than six months imprisonment, and a fine of not less than one hundred rupees to not more than five hundred rupees for initial offences. Enhanced penalties are prescribed for subsequent convictions, with imprisonment terms increasing up to two years and fines up to one thousand rupees.

act_identification.act_title: THE STATE BANK OF INDIA ACT, 1955
act_identification.act_short_title: The State Bank of India Act, 1955

act_overview.preamble: An Act to constitute a State Bank for India, to transfer to it the undertaking of the Imperial Bank of India and to provide for other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEAEAS for the extension of banking facilities on a large scale, more particularly in the rural and semi-urban areas, and for diverse other public purposes it is expedient to constitute a State Bank for India, and to transfer to it the undertaking of the Imperial Bank of India and to provide for other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto;
act_overview.purpose: This Act constitutes the State Bank of India to extend banking facilities, especially in rural and semi-urban areas, and for other public purposes. It facilitates the transfer of the undertaking of the Imperial Bank of India to the newly constituted State Bank.

chapter_titles: INCORPORATION AND SHARE CAPITAL OF STATE BANK
TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKING OF THE IMPERIAL BANK TO STATE BANK

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment of the State Bank.
key_sections.description: Constitutes the State Bank of India as a body corporate to carry on banking business and take over the Imperial Bank's undertaking.

key_sections.title: Transfer of assets and liabilities of the Imperial Bank to the State Bank.
key_sections.description: Mandates the transfer of all assets and liabilities of the Imperial Bank to the State Bank on the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Transfer of service of existing officers and employees of the Imperial Bank to the State Bank.

key_sections.title: Compensation to be given to shareholders of Imperial Bank.

key_sections.title: Management.

key_sections.title: Central Board to be guided by directions of Central Government.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the Central Board must follow directions from the Central Government on matters of public interest.

key_sections.title: Composition of the Central Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the composition of the Central Board, including appointed and elected directors.

key_sections.title: State Bank to act as agent of the Reserve Bank.
key_sections.description: Requires the State Bank to act as an agent of the Reserve Bank for government business at its branches in India.

key_sections.title: Other business which the State Bank may transact.
key_sections.description: Specifies the types of banking and other business the State Bank is authorized to conduct.

key_sections.title: State Bank may acquire the business of other Banks.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Bank to acquire the business of other banking institutions with the sanction of the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Audit.
key_sections.description: Details the audit process for the State Bank, including auditor qualifications, appointment, duties, and reporting.

key_sections.title: Obligation as to fidelity and secrecy.
key_sections.description: Imposes an obligation on the State Bank and its personnel to observe fidelity and secrecy regarding its affairs and constituents.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for implementing the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Board to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Board to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules for its effective implementation.

State Bank: To acquire and hold property; to establish branches; to carry on banking business; to acquire business of other banks; to appoint officers and employees; to make regulations.
Central Board: To exercise general superintendence and direction; to increase issued capital; to constitute committees; to make regulations.

act_identification.act_title: THE HINDU MARRIAGE ACT, 1955

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India, and applies also to Hindus domiciled in the territories to which this Act extends who are outside the said territories.

act_overview.preamble: An act to amend and codify the law relating to marriage among Hindus.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to amend and codify the law relating to marriage among Hindus, establishing uniform conditions, ceremonies, and procedures for Hindu marriages, as well as provisions for restitution of conjugal rights, judicial separation, nullity of marriage, and divorce.

chapter_titles: RESTITUTION OF CONJUGAL RIGHTS AND JUDICIAL SEPARATION

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical application to the whole of India and to domiciled Hindus outside these territories.

key_sections.title: Application of Act.
key_sections.description: Defines the categories of persons to whom the Act applies, including Hindus, Buddhists, Jainas, Sikhs, and others not being Muslim, Christian, Parsi or Jew, with an explanation for who is considered Hindu, Buddhist, Jaina or Sikh.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act such as 'custom', 'usage', 'district court', 'full blood', 'half blood', 'uterine blood', 'prescribed', 'sapinda relationship', and 'degrees of prohibited relationship'.

key_sections.title: Overriding effect of Act.
key_sections.description: States that the Act overrides existing Hindu law, custom, usage, and other inconsistent laws in matters covered by the Act.

key_sections.title: Conditions for a Hindu marriage.
key_sections.description: Lays down the essential conditions for a valid Hindu marriage, including monogamy, mental capacity, minimum age for bride and bridegroom, and absence of prohibited relationships or sapinda relationships unless custom permits.

key_sections.title: Ceremonies for a Hindu marriage.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that a Hindu marriage may be solemnized according to customary rites and ceremonies, and specifies that Saptapadi completes the marriage if included in the rites.

key_sections.title: Registration of Hindu marriages.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to make rules for the registration of Hindu marriages for proof purposes, and allows for compulsory registration with penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Restitution of conjugal right.
key_sections.description: Allows an aggrieved party to petition the district court for restitution of conjugal rights if the other party has withdrawn from society without reasonable excuse.

key_sections.title: Judicial separation.
key_sections.description: Enables either party to a marriage to petition for a decree of judicial separation on grounds specified in Section 13, making cohabitation non-obligatory.

key_sections.title: Void marriages.
key_sections.description: Declares marriages solemnized after the commencement of the Act to be null and void if they contravene conditions specified in clauses (i), (iv), and (v) of section 5.

key_sections.title: Voidable marriages.
key_sections.description: Specifies grounds on which a marriage can be annulled by a decree of nullity, such as impotence, contravention of mental capacity conditions, consent obtained by force or fraud, or pregnancy by another person at the time of marriage.

key_sections.title: Divorce.
key_sections.description: Outlines the grounds on which a marriage may be dissolved by a decree of divorce, including adultery, cruelty, desertion, conversion, unsoundness of mind, venereal disease, renunciation of the world, or not being heard of for seven years.

key_sections.title: Divorce by mutual consent.
key_sections.description: Provides for dissolution of marriage by a decree of divorce upon a joint petition by both parties, based on living separately for one year or more and mutual agreement for dissolution.

key_sections.title: Punishment of bigamy.
key_sections.description: Declares bigamous marriages among Hindus solemnized after the Act's commencement as void and applies provisions of sections 494 and 495 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

key_sections.title: Permanent alimony and maintenance.
key_sections.description: Empowers the court to order the respondent to pay permanent alimony and maintenance to the applicant, considering income, property, and conduct of the parties.

key_sections.title: Custody of children.
key_sections.description: Allows the court to pass interim orders and make provisions in the decree regarding the custody, maintenance, and education of minor children, consistent with their wishes.

powers_conferred: State Government to make rules for registration of Hindu marriages (Section 8(1))
State Government to make registration of Hindu marriages compulsory (Section 8(2))
District court to grant restitution of conjugal rights (Section 9)
Court to grant decree for judicial separation (Section 10)
Court to declare void marriages by decree of nullity (Section 11)
Court to annul voidable marriages by decree of nullity (Section 12)
Court to dissolve marriage by decree of divorce (Section 13, 13A, 13B)
High Court to make rules regarding presentation of petitions for divorce (Section 14)
Court or Government to transfer petitions in certain cases (Section 21A)
Court to order maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings (Section 24)
Court to order permanent alimony and maintenance (Section 25)
Court to pass orders for custody, maintenance and education of minor children (Section 26)
Court to make provisions for disposal of property (Section 27)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of rules for compulsory registration of Hindu marriages (Section 8(2)) is punishable with fine up to twenty-five rupees. Bigamy (Section 17) is punishable under sections 494 and 495 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860. Contravention of marriage conditions in Section 5(iii) (age) is punishable with rigorous imprisonment up to two years or fine up to one lakh rupees, or both. Contravention of conditions in Section 5(iv) or (v) (prohibited relationship, sapinda) is punishable with simple imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both (Section 18). Printing or publishing in-camera proceedings without permission (Section 22(2)) is punishable with fine up to one thousand rupees.

related_acts: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 (78 of 1956)

applies_to: any person who is a Hindu by religion in any of its forms or developments, including a Virashaiva, a Lingayat or a follower of the Brahmo, Prarthana or Arya Samaj
any person who is a Buddhist, Jaina or Sikh by religion

any other person domiciled in the territories to which this Act extends who is not a Muslim, Christian, Parsi or Jew by religion, unless it is proved that any such person would not have been governed by the Hindu law or by any custom or usage as part of that law in respect of any of the matters dealt with herein if this Act had not been passed
any child, legitimate or illegitimate, both of whose parents are Hindus, Buddhists, Jainas or Sikhs by religion

any child, legitimate or illegitimate, one of whose parents is a Hindu, Buddhist, Jaina or Sikh by religion and who is brought up as a member of the tribe, community, group or family to which such parent belongs or belonged
