any person who is a convert or re-convert to the Hindu, Buddhist, Jaina or Sikh religion
exemptions: members of any Scheduled tribe within the meaning of clause (25) of article 366 of the Constitution unless the Central Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, otherwise directs
special_provisions: Extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli (w.e.f. 1-7-1965) by Reg. 6 of 1963, s. 2 and Schedule I
Extended to Pondicherry (w.e.f 1-10-1963) with modifications by Reg. 7 of 1963, s. 3 and the Schedule I
State Amendment for Uttar Pradesh regarding grounds for divorce in Section 13(1)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: State Government (for Hindu Marriage Register, Section 8); High Court (for rules regarding petitions, Section 14, 21)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Proceedings are initiated by petition to the District Court. The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, applies to proceedings. Decrees and orders are enforced in the same manner as those of a court exercising original civil jurisdiction.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District Court (for original petitions); High Court (for appeals and rule-making); Supreme Court (for appeals)

act_identification.act_title: THE PRISONERS (ATTENDANCE IN COURTS) ACT, 1955

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Sixth Year of the Republic of India
legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the attendance in courts of persons confined in prisons for obtaining their evidence or for answering a criminal charge.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the attendance of persons confined in prisons in civil or criminal courts. Its main objective is to enable courts to obtain evidence from prisoners or to allow them to answer criminal charges. It also outlines conditions and procedures for such attendance.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, such as 'confinement in a prison', 'prison', and 'State Government'.

key_sections.title: Power of courts to require appearance of prisoners to give evidence or answer a charge.
key_sections.description: Grants civil and criminal courts the power to order the appearance of confined persons for evidence or to answer charges, subject to certain conditions and countersignatures.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to exempt certain persons from operation of section 3.
key_sections.description: Allows the State Government to exempt certain persons or classes of persons from being removed from prison, considering factors like public order and interest.

key_sections.title: Prisoners to be brought up.
key_sections.description: Mandates the officer in charge of a prison to produce the prisoner in court as required by an order under section 3 and ensure their custody.

key_sections.title: Officer in charge of prison when to abstain from carrying out order.
key_sections.description: Outlines specific circumstances under which a prison officer may abstain from carrying out a court order for a prisoner's appearance, such as sickness or proximity to trial expiry.

key_sections.title: Commissions for examination of prisoners.
key_sections.description: Provides for the issuance of commissions under the Code of Civil Procedure for examining prisoners in prison, especially when their court attendance is not feasible.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including procedures for countersignature, declarations of unfitness, and escort arrangements.

key_sections.title: Repeal.
key_sections.description: Repeals Part IX and the First and Second Schedules of the Prisoners Act, 1900, and corresponding laws in Part B States.

powers_conferred: Power of civil or criminal courts to require appearance of prisoners to give evidence or answer a charge (Section 3)
Power of State Government to exempt certain persons from operation of section 3 (Section 4)
Power of State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act (Section 9)

repealed_acts: Part IX of the Prisoners Act, 1900 (3 of 1900)
First and Second Schedules to the Prisoners Act, 1900
any law corresponding to the provisions of this Act in any Part B State

applies_to: persons confined in prisons
exemptions: any person or class of persons exempted by State Government order under section 4
prisoners declared unfit to be removed from prison due to sickness or infirmity (Section 6)
prisoners under committal for trial or remand pending trial/investigation, where conditions in Section 6(b), (c), (d) apply
special_provisions: This Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh vide notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019.
This Act has been extended in its application to the Union territory Goa, Daman and Diu by the Act 11 of 1963, s. 3 and the Schedule (w.e.f 1-2-1965).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Courts issue orders for prisoner attendance (Section 3). Officer in charge of prison is responsible for producing the prisoner (Section 5), with provisions for abstaining under specific conditions (Section 6). Commissions can be issued for examination (Section 7).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any civil or criminal court

schedules_summary.description: Contains the form for a court order requiring the production of a prisoner to give evidence in a civil or criminal matter.
Contains the form for a court order requiring the production of a prisoner to answer a criminal charge.

act_identification.act_title: THE DURGAH KHAWAJA SAHEB ACT, 1955

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make provision for the proper administration of the Durgah and the Endowment of the Durgah of Khawaja Moin-ud-din Chishti, generally known as Durgah Khawaja Saheb, Ajmer.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the proper administration, control, and management of the Durgah and its Endowment, specifically the Durgah of Khawaja Moin-ud-din Chishti, also known as Durgah Khawaja Saheb, located in Ajmer.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: The Committee.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Committee for the administration, control, and management of the Durgah Endowment as a body corporate.

key_sections.title: Composition of Committee.
key_sections.description: Details the number and qualifications of members for the Committee and their appointment by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to appoint Nazim.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to appoint a Nazim for the Durgah, who also serves as the Committee's secretary.

key_sections.title: Powers and duties of the Committee.
key_sections.description: Outlines the various powers and duties of the Committee, including administration, financial management, and regulation of Durgah affairs.

key_sections.title: Succession to the office of Sajjadanashin.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the procedure for filling vacancies in the office of Sajjadanashin, including dispute resolution by the Judicial Commissioner.

key_sections.title: Power to solicit or receive offerings on behalf of the Durgah.
key_sections.description: Grants the Nazim or authorized persons the exclusive right to solicit and receive offerings for the Durgah and prescribes penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Committee to observe Muslim Law and tenets of the Chishti Saint.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Committee to follow Muslim Law applicable to Hanafi Muslims and conduct rites according to the Chishti Saint's tenets.

key_sections.title: Board of Arbitration.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of a Board of Arbitration to resolve certain disputes between the Committee and other parties, making its award final.

key_sections.title: Enforcement of final orders of Committee.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that final orders of the Committee can be enforced by civil courts as if they were court decrees.

key_sections.title: Bye-laws.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Committee to make bye-laws for carrying out the Act's purposes, subject to Central Government approval.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint Nazim (Section 9)
Central Government to remove members of the Committee (Section 6)
Central Government to supersede the Committee (Section 8)
Central Government to constitute an Advisory Committee (Section 10)
Central Government to approve and confirm bye-laws (Section 20)
Committee to administer, control and manage the Durgah Endowment (Section 4, 11)
Committee to elect a president and a vice-president (Section 7)
Committee to determine the privileges of the Khadims (Section 11(f))
Committee to define the powers and duties of the Advisory Committee (Section 11(g))
Committee to determine the functions and powers of the Sajjadanashin (Section 11(h))
Committee to appoint, suspend or dismiss servants of the Durgah Endowment (Section 11(i))
Committee to make provision for the education and maintenance of indigent descendants and Khadims (Section 11(j))
Committee to delegate powers and functions to the Nazim (Section 11(k))
Committee to make bye-laws (Section 20)
Nazim or any person authorised by him to solicit and receive nazars or offerings on behalf of the Durgah (Section 14)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever solicits or receives any nazars or offerings in contravention of the provisions of sub-section (1) of Section 14, shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.

repealed_acts: The Durgah Khawaja,Saheb Act, 1936 (XXIII of 1936)
The Durgah Khawaja Saheb (Emergency Provisions) Act, 1950 (XVII of 1950)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints Committee members, Nazim, Advisory Committee members, and a member of the Board of Arbitration. The Committee appoints servants of the Durgah Endowment.

applies_to: The Durgah and the Endowment of the Durgah of Khawaja Moin-ud-din Chishti, generally known as Durgah Khawaja Saheb, Ajmer
Hanafi Muslims (for Committee and Advisory Committee members)
Khadims
Sajjadanashin
Descendants of Khawaja Moin-ud-din Chishti
special_provisions: Advisory Committee members to be chosen from among the residents of the State of Ajmer or any of the neighbouring States (Section 10)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Committee, with approval and confirmation from the Central Government, has the power to make bye-laws.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Final orders of the Committee are enforceable by civil courts. Disputes between the Committee and other parties can be referred to a Board of Arbitration.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil courts (for enforcing Committee orders), Judicial Commissioner of Ajmer (for Sajjadanashin succession disputes).

act_identification.act_title: THE PRIZE COMPETITIONS ACT, 1955

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in the States of Andhra, Bombay, Madras, Orissa, Uttar Pradesh, Hyderabad, Madhya Bharat, Patiala and East Punjab States Union and Saurashtra and all Part C States.

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the control and regulation of prize Competitions; AND WHEREAS the Legislatures of the States of Andhra, Bombay, Madras, Orissa, Uttar Pradesh, Hyderabad, Madhya Bharat, Patiala and East Punjab States Union and Saurashtra have passed resolutions in terms of clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution in relation to the above-mentioned matter and matters ancillary thereto in so far as such matters are matters enumerated in List II in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution; BE it enacted by Parliament in the Sixth Year of the Republic of India as follows:―
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the control and regulation of prize competitions across specified territories in India. It establishes a licensing system for competitions offering prizes below a certain monetary threshold and prohibits those exceeding it, aiming to prevent misuse and ensure fair conduct.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, the geographical areas to which it extends, and the date it comes into force.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'licensing authority', 'money', 'prescribed', and 'prize competition'.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of prize competitions where the prize offered exceeds one thousand rupees a month.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the promotion or conduct of prize competitions where the total prize value exceeds one thousand rupees per month and limits the number of entries.

key_sections.title: Licensing of prize competitions where the prize offered does not exceed one thousand rupees a month.
key_sections.description: Requires a licence for promoting or conducting prize competitions where the total prize value does not exceed one thousand rupees per month.

key_sections.title: Licences for prize competitions.
key_sections.description: Outlines the application process for obtaining a licence, the power of the licensing authority to grant or refuse licences, and the conditions for granting them.

key_sections.title: Penalty for promoting or conducting any prize competition in contravention of the provisions of sections 4 and 5.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals who promote or conduct prize competitions in violation of the prohibitions or licensing requirements.

key_sections.title: Offences by Corporations.
key_sections.description: Addresses the liability of companies and their officers when an offence under the Act is committed by a corporation.

key_sections.title: Power of entry and search.
key_sections.description: Grants police officers the authority to enter, search premises, take persons into custody, and seize items suspected of being involved in illegal prize competitions.

key_sections.title: Forfeiture newspapers and publications containing prize competitions.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to declare forfeiture of newspapers or publications containing prize competitions or advertisements that contravene the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the State Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including details regarding licences, accounts, and appeals.

powers_conferred: Power to State Government to appoint licensing authority (Section 2(a))
Power to licensing authority to grant or refuse licences (Section 6(2))
Power to licensing authority to cancel or suspend licences (Section 8)
Power to licensing authority to call for and inspect accounts and documents (Section 13)
Power to police-officer (not below Sub-inspector, authorized by State Government) for entry and search (Section 14)
Power to State Government to declare forfeiture of newspapers and publications (Section 15)
Power to State Government to make rules (Section 20)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for various offences, including promoting or conducting prize competitions in contravention of the Act's provisions (imprisonment up to three months or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both), failure to keep or submit accounts (imprisonment up to one month or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both), and other related offences such as printing/selling tickets or advertising illegally (imprisonment up to three months or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both). Special provisions exist for offences committed by corporations.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government

applies_to: Any person who promotes or conducts a prize competition
special_provisions: Extends to the territories which, immediately before the 1st November, 1956, were comprised in the States of Andhra, Bombay, Madras, Orissa, Uttar Pradesh, Hyderabad, Madhya Bharat, Patiala and East Punjab States Union and Saurashtra and all Part C States.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a licensing system for prize competitions, with powers granted to the licensing authority to grant, refuse, suspend, or cancel licences. It mandates the keeping and submission of accounts, and provides for penalties for contraventions. Police officers are empowered with entry and search, and the State Government can order forfeiture of publications. Appeals against licensing authority decisions can be made to the State Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No Court inferior to that of a Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class

act_identification.act_title: THE WORKING JOURNALISTS AND OTHER NEWSPAPER EMPLOYEES (CONDITIONS OFSERVICE) AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS ACT, 1955
act_identification.act_short_title: The Working Journalists and other Newspaper Employees (Conditions of Service) and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1955

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate certain conditions of service of working journalists and other persons employed in newspaper establishments.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the conditions of service for working journalists and other employees in newspaper establishments. It covers aspects such as wages, gratuity, hours of work, and leave, and establishes mechanisms for fixing and revising wage rates.

chapter_titles: APPLICATION OF CERTAIN ACTS TO NEWSPAPER EMPLOYEES

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Names the Act and specifies its territorial application to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms such as 'Board', 'newspaper employee', 'newspaper establishment', 'wages', and 'working journalist'.

key_sections.title: Act 14 of 1947 to apply to working journalists.
key_sections.description: Applies provisions of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, to working journalists with specific modifications for retrenchment notice periods.

key_sections.title: Payment of gratuity.
key_sections.description: Lays down conditions and calculation for gratuity payment to working journalists upon termination, retirement, resignation, or death.

key_sections.title: Hours of work.
key_sections.description: Prescribes maximum working hours and mandatory rest periods for working journalists.

key_sections.title: Fixation or revision of rates of wages.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to fix or revise wage rates for working journalists.

key_sections.title: Procedure for fixing and revising rates of wages.
key_sections.description: Outlines the constitution and composition of a Wage Board for working journalists.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Tribunal for fixing or revising rates of wages in respect of working journalists.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a Tribunal by the Central Government if the Wage Board for working journalists cannot function effectively.

key_sections.title: Fixation or revision of rates of wages of non-journalist newspaper employees.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to fix or revise wage rates for non-journalist newspaper employees.

key_sections.title: Effect of laws and agreements inconsistent with this Act.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over inconsistent laws or agreements, unless the latter are more favourable to the employee.

key_sections.title: Employer not to dismiss, discharge, etc., newspaper employees.
key_sections.description: Prohibits employers from dismissing, discharging, or retrenching newspaper employees due to liability for wage payments under the Act.

key_sections.title: Recovery of money due from an employer.
key_sections.description: Provides a mechanism for newspaper employees or their nominees/family to recover amounts due from employers through the State Government.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including fines, for employers contravening the provisions of the Act or rules made thereunder, with provisions for company offenses.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering various aspects like gratuity, hours of work, and procedures.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To notify classes of periodical work as 'newspaper' (S.2(b)).
Central Government: To fix or revise wage rates for working journalists (S.8) and non-journalist newspaper employees (S.13B).
Central Government: To constitute Wage Boards for working journalists (S.9) and non-journalist newspaper employees (S.13C).
Central Government: To enforce recommendations of the Wage Board (S.12).
Central Government: To fix interim rates of wages (S.13A).
Central Government: To constitute Tribunals for fixing or revising wage rates for working journalists (S.13AA) and non-journalist newspaper employees (S.13DD).
Central Government: To make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (S.20).
State Government: To appoint Inspectors (S.17B).
State Government: To refer questions regarding amounts due to Labour Courts (S.17(2)).
Inspectors: To require information, enter premises, examine persons, make copies of documents, and exercise other prescribed powers (S.17B(2)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any employer contravening the Act or rules is punishable with a fine up to two hundred rupees. Subsequent convictions for the same offense can lead to a fine up to five hundred rupees. Specific provisions address offenses committed by companies, holding responsible those in charge and the company itself, with exceptions for lack of knowledge or due diligence, and additional liability for directors/managers in cases of consent, connivance, or gross negligence.

repealed_acts: Act 1 of 1955
related_acts: Working Journalists (Fixation of Rates of Wages) Act, 1958 (29 of 1958)
Employees’ Provident Funds [and Miscellaneous Provisions] Act, 1952
Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules
Civilians in Defence Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints members of the Wage Boards and the person constituting the Tribunals.

applies_to: working journalists
other persons employed in newspaper establishments
every newspaper establishment wherein twenty or more newspaper employees are employed (for Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act)
every newspaper establishment in which twenty or more persons are employed (for Employees’ Provident Funds Act)
exemptions: Any person employed mainly in a managerial or administrative capacity (S.2(dd)(ii), S.2(f)(i)).
Any person employed in a supervisory capacity performing mainly managerial functions (S.2(dd)(iii), S.2(f)(ii)).
Any newspaper employee who is an employee of the Government to whom specific government service rules or regulations apply (S.19B).
special_provisions: Section 3(2) modifies Section 25F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, for working journalists, specifying different notice periods for retrenchment (six months for an editor, three months for other working journalists).
Section 4 provides special provisions for retrenchment of working journalists that occurred between 14th July, 1954, and 12th March, 1955.

The proviso to Section 5(1) specifies different gratuity calculation rates for working journalists employed in newspaper establishments with not more than six working journalists before the commencement of the Act.

The Schedule specifies conditions under which two or more newspaper establishments are deemed to be one for the purposes of clause (d) of section 2, based on common control, ownership by spouses, or similar titles.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Money due to newspaper employees can be recovered by application to the State Government, which issues a certificate to the Collector for recovery as an arrear of land revenue. Disputes regarding amounts due can be referred by the State Government to Labour Courts. State Governments appoint Inspectors to ascertain compliance with the Act, who have powers to require information, enter premises, and examine records. Contraventions of the Act are subject to penalties.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No Court inferior to that of a Presidency Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under Section 18. Labour Courts constituted under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, or corresponding state laws, have jurisdiction over disputes regarding amounts due to newspaper employees.

schedules_summary.description: Defines criteria for deeming two or more newspaper establishments as a single establishment for the purpose of clause (d) of section 2, including common control, ownership by spouses, or publishing newspapers with the same or similar titles.

act_identification.act_title: THE MANIPUR (COURTS) ACT, 1955

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of the Union territory of Manipur

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Judicial Commissioner’s Court and other Courts in Manipur.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the establishment of a Judicial Commissioner's Court and other subordinate civil courts in the Union territory of Manipur. It defines their jurisdiction, powers, and administrative control, aiming to establish a structured judicial system for the region.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment of the Court of the Judicial Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of the Court of the Judicial Commissioner for Manipur.

key_sections.title: Civil and criminal jurisdiction of the Court of the Judicial Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Declares the Court of the Judicial Commissioner as the highest court of appeal, revision, or reference for civil and criminal proceedings in Manipur.

key_sections.title: Superintendence and control of subordinate courts.
key_sections.description: Vests general superintendence and control of all courts in Manipur in the Court of the Judicial Commissioner.

key_sections.title: Court of the Judicial Commissioner to be a court of record.
key_sections.description: Declares the Court of the Judicial Commissioner as a court of record with powers to punish for contempt.

key_sections.title: Classes of subordinate civil courts.
key_sections.description: Outlines the classes of subordinate civil courts, including district courts, subordinate judge courts, and munsiff courts.

key_sections.title: District court to be principal civil court of original jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Designates the district court as the principal civil court of original jurisdiction in a district.

key_sections.title: Appeals from original decrees.
key_sections.description: Specifies the courts to which appeals from original decrees or orders shall lie based on the value of the suit.

key_sections.title: Revisional powers of the Court of the Judicial Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Confers revisional powers on the Court of the Judicial Commissioner for cases where no appeal lies, particularly on questions of law or custom.

key_sections.title: Power to confer powers of civil courts on officers in Hill Areas and procedure before the courts of such officers.
key_sections.description: Allows the Chief Commissioner to invest officers in hill areas with civil court powers and specifies procedural adaptations for such courts.

key_sections.title: Power of the Judicial Commissioner to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Judicial Commissioner to make rules for various administrative and procedural matters concerning courts.

key_sections.title: Repeals and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Manipur State Courts Act 1947 and includes savings provisions for actions taken under the repealed Act.

key_sections.title: Declaration of the Judicial Commissioner's Court as a High Court for certain purposes.
key_sections.description: Declares the Court of the Judicial Commissioner as a High Court for the purposes of specific articles of the Constitution.

powers_conferred: Chief Commissioner: appoint district judges (S.17), fix number of subordinate judges and munsiffs (S.19), make rules for qualifications of subordinate judges and munsiffs (S.19), determine jurisdiction of subordinate judges and munsiffs (S.22), define local limits of jurisdiction (S.23), fix place of sittings of courts (S.26), prescribe seals (S.29), invest officers in hill areas with civil court powers (S.39).

Judicial Commissioner: appoint Registrar and ministerial officers (S.9), make rules for delegating powers to Registrar (S.9), make rules and issue general directions for subordinate courts (S.10), make rules for recording evidence and judgments (S.12), admit and remove advocates, vakils and pleaders (S.13), confer small causes jurisdiction (S.24), authorize subordinate judges and munsiffs for certain proceedings (S.25), make rules for ministerial officers (S.30), sanction delegation of powers by district judge (S.31), make rules for various matters (S.40), prepare list of holidays (S.43).

District Judge: assign functions to additional district judges (S.18), distribute business among courts (S.28), appoint ministerial officers (S.30), delegate powers to judges of courts under administrative control (S.31), empower subordinate judge or munsiff for temporary vacancy (S.38).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Court of the Judicial Commissioner has the power to punish for contempt of itself (S.14).

repealed_acts: The Manipur State Courts Act 1947, as amended by the Manipur State Courts (Amendment) Order, 1950
related_acts: Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887 (9 of 1887)
Judicial Commissioners' Courts (Declaration as High Courts) Act, 1950 (15 of 1950)

authorities_established: Court of the Judicial Commissioner for Manipur
important_authorities.appointment_powers: President (Judicial Commissioner, Additional Judicial Commissioner - S.4); Judicial Commissioner (Registrar, ministerial officers of the Court of the Judicial Commissioner - S.9); Chief Commissioner (District Judges - S.17, Additional District Judges - S.18, Subordinate Judges and Munsiffs - S.19); District Judge (Ministerial officers of the district court and civil courts under administrative control - S.30).

applies_to: whole of the Union territory of Manipur
civil suits
criminal proceedings
special_provisions: Power to confer powers of civil courts on officers in Hill Areas and procedure before the courts of such officers (S.39).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Chief Commissioner (for commencement date, civil districts, jurisdiction, seals, court fees, investing officers in hill areas); Judicial Commissioner (for delegating powers to Registrar, regulating practice/procedure of subordinate courts, recording evidence/judgments, admitting/removing advocates, small causes jurisdiction, rules for ministerial officers, general rules for courts).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Court of the Judicial Commissioner has general superintendence and control over all subordinate courts (S.10). The District Judge has administrative control over civil courts within his jurisdiction (S.27).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Court of the Judicial Commissioner, District Court, Court of a Subordinate Judge, Court of a Munsiff.

act_identification.act_title: An Act to provide for the acquisition and determination of Indian citizenship.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the acquisition and determination of Indian citizenship.
act_overview.purpose: This Act lays down the legal framework for how individuals can acquire Indian citizenship, including by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, or incorporation of territory. It also defines the conditions and procedures for the termination and deprivation of Indian citizenship.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Citizenship Act, 1955.

key_sections.title: Interpretation.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'illegal migrant', 'minor', and 'Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder'.

key_sections.title: Citizenship by birth.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which a person born in India acquires Indian citizenship by birth, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Citizenship by descent.
key_sections.description: Outlines the criteria for a person born outside India to acquire Indian citizenship by descent, based on the citizenship of their parents.

key_sections.title: Citizenship by registration.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to register certain categories of persons, not being illegal migrants, as citizens of India, subject to conditions.

key_sections.title: Citizenship by naturalisation.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to grant a certificate of naturalisation to qualified persons, not being illegal migrants, who meet the conditions in the Third Schedule.

key_sections.title: Special provisions as to citizenship of persons covered by the Assam Accord.
key_sections.description: Provides special rules for persons of Indian origin who came to Assam from specified territory before or after 1st January, 1966, under the Assam Accord.

key_sections.title: Special provisions as to citizenship of person covered by proviso to clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 2.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to grant citizenship to certain persons from specific communities and countries who entered India on or before 31st December, 2014.

key_sections.title: Registration of Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder.
key_sections.description: Details the conditions and categories of persons eligible for registration as an Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder.

key_sections.title: Conferment of rights on Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder.
key_sections.description: Specifies the rights conferred upon Overseas Citizen of India Cardholders, excluding certain constitutional and electoral rights.

key_sections.title: Renunciation of citizenship.
key_sections.description: Allows a citizen of India of full age and capacity to renounce their Indian citizenship by making a declaration.

key_sections.title: Termination of citizenship.
key_sections.description: States that a citizen of India who voluntarily acquires the citizenship of another country shall cease to be a citizen of India.

key_sections.title: Deprivation of citizenship.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to deprive certain citizens of their Indian citizenship under specified grounds, such as fraud or disloyalty.

key_sections.title: Issue of national identity cards.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to compulsorily register every citizen and issue national identity cards, and to maintain a National Register of Indian Citizens.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, covering various procedural and administrative matters.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Grant certificate of naturalisation (Section 6)
Central Government: Register as citizen (Section 5)
Central Government: Register minor as citizen (Section 5(4))
Central Government: Specify persons for citizenship by incorporation of territory (Section 7)
Central Government: Register Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder (Section 7A)
Central Government: Specify rights of Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder (Section 7B)
Central Government: Cancel registration as Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder (Section 7D)
Central Government: Register renunciation of citizenship (Section 8)
Central Government: Determine acquisition of foreign citizenship (Section 9(2))
Central Government: Deprive citizenship (Section 10)
Central Government: Certify citizenship in case of doubt (Section 13)
Central Government: Grant or refuse applications under sections 5, 6 and 7A (Section 14)
Central Government: Revise orders (Section 15)
Central Government: Review orders (Section 15A)
Central Government: Issue national identity cards and maintain National Register of Indian Citizens (Section 14A)
Central Government: Make rules (Section 18)
Central Government: Delegate powers (Section 16)
Prescribed authority: Register renunciation of citizenship (Section 8)
Prescribed authority: Grant or refuse applications under sections 5, 6 and 7A (Section 14)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person making false representation for procuring anything under this Act is punishable with imprisonment up to five years, or fine up to fifty thousand rupees, or both (Section 17). Breach of rules made under the Act may be punishable with fine up to one thousand rupees, or for rules related to compulsory registration of citizens, with imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both (Section 18(3) and proviso).

related_acts: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
Representation of the People Act, 1951 (43 of 1951)
Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 (18 of 1969)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government has the power to appoint members of the Committee of Inquiry (Section 10(5)) and officers and staff to assist the Registrar General of Citizen Registration (Section 14A(4)).

applies_to: Persons born in India (Section 3)
Persons born outside India (Section 4)
Persons of Indian origin (Section 5)
Persons married to a citizen of India (Section 5)
Minor children of citizens of India (Section 5)
Persons whose parents are registered as citizens of India (Section 5)
Persons who were earlier citizens of independent India (Section 5)
Overseas Citizen of India Cardholders (Section 5, Section 7A)
Persons covered by the Assam Accord (Section 6A)
Persons covered by proviso to clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 2 (Section 6B)
Persons connected with incorporated territory (Section 7)
Citizens of India of full age and capacity (Section 8, Section 9, Section 10)
exemptions: Persons whose parent possesses immunity as envoy of foreign sovereign power (Section 3(2)(a))
Persons whose parent is an enemy alien and birth occurs in occupied territory (Section 3(2)(b))

No person, who or either of whose parents or grandparents or great grandparents is or had been a citizen of Pakistan, Bangladesh or such other country as the Central Government may specify, shall be eligible for registration as an Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder (Section 7A(1) proviso).

Tribal area of Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram or Tripura as included in the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution and the area covered under “The Inner Line” notified under the Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation, 1873 (Reg. 5 of 1873) are exempt from Section 6B.
special_provisions: Special provisions for persons covered by the Assam Accord (Section 6A).
Special provisions for persons covered by proviso to clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 2 (Section 6B).
Central Government may relax the residential period for registration (Section 5(1A)).
Central Government may grant exemption from the residential requirement for registration (Section 5(6)).
Central Government may waive naturalisation conditions for distinguished service (Section 6(1) proviso).
Central Government may relax the period for naturalisation (Third Schedule, proviso to (c)).
Reduced aggregate period for naturalisation for certain communities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh or Pakistan (Third Schedule, proviso to (d)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through registration by prescribed authorities, grant of certificates by the Central Government, inquiries by a Committee of Inquiry, maintenance of a National Register of Indian Citizens, and provisions for revision and review of orders. Penalties are prescribed for false representations.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the form for the Oath of Allegiance to be taken by persons acquiring citizenship by registration or naturalisation.
Lays down the qualifications and conditions that a person must meet to be eligible for naturalisation as a citizen of India.

act_identification.act_title: THE UNIVERSITY GRANTS COMMISSION ACT, 1956

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make provision for the co-ordination and determination of standards in Universities and for that purpose, to establish a University Grants Commission.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to coordinate and determine standards in Universities across India. Its primary objective is to establish the University Grants Commission to achieve these goals and regulate higher education.

chapter_titles: POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE COMMISSION

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Commission', 'University', and 'member'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of the Commission.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of the University Grants Commission as a body corporate with perpetual succession.

key_sections.title: Composition of the Commission.
key_sections.description: Details the composition of the Commission, including the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and other members, and their appointment by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Commission.
key_sections.description: Outlines the general duties and specific functions of the Commission, including promoting and coordinating university education, determining standards, and disbursing grants.

key_sections.title: Regulation of fees and prohibition of donations in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Commission to regulate fees and prohibit donations in colleges providing specified courses of study, to ensure merit-based admissions.

key_sections.title: Consequences of failure of Universities to comply with recommendations of the Commission.
key_sections.description: Specifies that the Commission may withhold grants from Universities that fail to comply with its recommendations or contravene rules/regulations.

key_sections.title: Right to confer degrees.
key_sections.description: Restricts the right to confer or grant degrees exclusively to established Universities or institutions deemed as such, or specially empowered by Parliament.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of the use of the word “University” in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Prohibits any institution, other than a legally established University, from using the word 'University' in its name.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including fines, for contravention of provisions related to conferring degrees or using the word 'University'.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, covering various administrative and functional aspects.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Commission to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules, covering aspects like meetings, association of persons, service conditions, and academic standards.

powers_conferred: Central Government may declare institutions for higher education (other than Universities) to be deemed Universities for the purposes of this Act (Section 3).
Central Government appoints the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and other members of the Commission (Section 5).
Commission may associate persons for particular purposes (Section 9).
Commission may appoint a Secretary and other employees (Section 10).
Commission has the general duty to promote and co-ordinate University education and determine/maintain standards (Section 12).
Commission may inquire into financial needs of Universities (Section 12(a)).
Commission may allocate and disburse grants to Universities and deemed Universities (Section 12(b), (c), (cc)).
Commission may establish and maintain institutions for common facilities for Universities (Section 12(ccc)).
Commission may recommend measures for improvement of University education and advise Universities (Section 12(d)).
Commission may advise Central or State Governments on grant allocation to Universities (Section 12(e)).
Commission may advise on establishment of new Universities or expansion of activities (Section 12(f)).
Commission may advise Central Government, State Government or University on referred questions (Section 12(g)).
Commission may collect and make available information on University education (Section 12(h)).
Commission may require Universities to furnish information (Section 12(i)).
Commission may perform other functions for advancing higher education (Section 12(j)).
Commission may specify by regulations the matters and scale of fees to be charged by colleges and prohibit donations (Section 12A).
Commission may prohibit colleges from presenting students for qualification if they contravene fee regulations (Section 12A(4)).
Commission may cause inspection of University departments (Section 13).
Commission may withhold grants from Universities failing to comply with recommendations or contravening rules/regulations (Section 14).
Central Government may pay sums to the Commission for its functions (Section 15).
Commission may spend sums from its Fund for performing its functions (Section 16(3)).
Central Government may give directions to the Commission on policy relating to national purposes (Section 20).
Commission has the right to specify degrees by notification (Section 22(3)).
Central Government has the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (Section 25).
Commission has the power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules (Section 26).
Commission may delegate powers to its Chairman, Vice-Chairman or officers (Section 27).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever contravenes the provisions of section 22 (Right to confer degrees) or section 23 (Prohibition of the use of the word “University”) shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees. If the contravening person is an association or body of individuals, every member who knowingly or wilfully authorises or permits the contravention shall be punishable with fine up to one thousand rupees.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and other members of the Commission. The Commission appoints its Secretary and other employees.

applies_to: Universities established or incorporated by or under a Central Act, a Provincial Act or a State Act
Institutions for higher education, other than a University, declared by the Central Government to be deemed Universities
Colleges providing courses of study for obtaining qualifications from a university
exemptions: For a period of two years from the commencement of this Act, institutions which immediately before such commencement had the word “University” associated with their name are exempt from the prohibition of using the word “University”.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (Section 25) and the Commission (for regulations, Section 26).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Commission enforces the Act through its functions, including allocating and disbursing grants, making recommendations, conducting inspections, and withholding grants for non-compliance. It also regulates fees and prohibits donations. Penalties are prescribed for specific contraventions.

act_identification.act_title: THE ALL-INDIA INSTITUTES OF MEDICAL SCIENCES ACT, 1956
act_identification.act_short_title: All-India Institutes of Medical Sciences Act, 1956

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Union territory Goa, Daman and Diu

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of [1][All-India Institutes of Medical Sciences]. BE it enacted by Parliament in the Seventh Year of the Republic of India as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to establish All-India Institutes of Medical Sciences to develop high standards of medical education, provide top-tier training facilities in health activities, and achieve self-sufficiency in post-graduate medical education across India.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'corresponding Institute', 'existing Institute', 'Fund', 'Governing Body', and 'Institute'.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of the Institute.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment and incorporation of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences as a body corporate with perpetual succession.

key_sections.title: Declaration of Institutes as institution of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares existing and newly established Institutes as institutions of national importance.

key_sections.title: Objects of the Institute.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary objectives of the Institute, including developing high standards of medical education, providing top-tier training, and achieving self-sufficiency in post-graduate medical education.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Institute.
key_sections.description: Details the various functions the Institute may undertake to promote its objects, such as providing teaching, research facilities, establishing colleges and hospitals, and granting degrees.

key_sections.title: Recognition of Medical, dental and nursing qualifications granted by the Institute.
key_sections.description: Ensures that medical, dental, and nursing qualifications granted by the Institute are recognized under relevant national acts.

key_sections.title: Control by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the Institute must follow directions issued by the Central Government for efficient administration.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of Institute registered as society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
key_sections.description: Provides for the incorporation of specific Institutes previously registered as societies under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, into bodies corporate under this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, after consultation with the Institutes.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers every Institute to make regulations, with the Central Government's approval, consistent with the Act and rules, for its administration and functioning.

powers_conferred: Institute: acquire, hold and dispose of property, both movable and immovable, and to contract, and shall by the said name sue and be sued (Section 3(2))
Institute: provide for under-graduate and post-graduate teaching in the science of modern medicine and other allied sciences (Section 14(a))
Institute: provide facilities for research in the various branches of such sciences (Section 14(b))
Institute: provide for the teaching of humanities in the under graduate courses (Section 14(c))
Institute: conduct experiments in new methods of medical education (Section 14(d))
Institute: prescribe courses and curricula for both under-graduate and post graduate studies (Section 14(e))

Institute: establish and maintain medical colleges, hospitals, dental college, nursing college, rural and urban health organisations, and other institutions for training health workers (Section 14(f))
Institute: train teachers for the different medical colleges in India (Section 14(g))
Institute: hold examinations and grant degrees, diplomas and other academic distinctions and titles (Section 14(h))
Institute: institute, and appoint persons to, professorships, readerships, lectureships and posts of any description (Section 14(i))
Institute: receive grants from the Government and gifts, donations, benefactions, bequests and transfers of properties (Section 14(j))
Institute: deal with any property belonging to, or vested in, the Institute (Section 14(k))
Institute: demand and receive such fees and other charges (Section 14(l))
Institute: construct quarters for its staff and allot such quarters (Section 14(m))
Institute: borrow money, with the prior approval of the Central Government, on the security of the property (Section 14(n))
Institute: constitute pension and provident funds for the benefit of its officers, teachers and other employees (Section 20(1))
Institute: make regulations consistent with this Act and the rules (Section 29)
Central Government: appoint date for commencement of the Act (Section 1(2))
Central Government: establish other All-India Institutes of Medical Sciences (Section 3(1) proviso)
Central Government: nominate members to the Institute (Section 4(d), (e), (f))
Central Government: nominate President for every Institute (Section 7(1))
Central Government: appoint the first Director of every Institute (other than the existing Institute) (Section 11(1) proviso)
Central Government: specify locations for Institutes (other than existing and corresponding Institutes) (Section 12(3))
Central Government: pay sums of money to every Institute under appropriation made by Parliament (Section 15)
Central Government: approve investment decisions of the Institute's Fund (Section 16(2))
Central Government: prescribe form and time for budget preparation (Section 17)
Central Government: prescribe form for annual statement of accounts (Section 18(1))
Central Government: cause audit report and accounts to be laid before Parliament (Section 18(4))
Central Government: require reports, returns and other information from the Institute (Section 19, 27)
Central Government: declare that the provisions of the Provident Funds Act, 1925, shall apply to pension or provident funds constituted by the Institute (Section 20(2))
Central Government: issue directions to the Institute for efficient administration (Section 25)
Central Government: decide disputes between the Institute and the Central Government (Section 26)
Central Government: make transitory provisions for Institutes (other than existing Institute) (Section 27D)
Central Government: make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act (Section 28)
Central Government: make regulations until the Institute is established (Section 29(2))

authorities_established: All India Institute of Medical Sciences
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government nominates the President and certain members, and appoints the first Director for new Institutes. The Institute appoints its Director and other officers/employees. Members of Parliament are elected by their respective Houses.

applies_to: All-India Institutes of Medical Sciences
Officers, teachers and other employees of the Institute
Medical, dental and nursing students of the Institute
special_provisions: Specific provisions for the existing Institute located at New Delhi and other corresponding Institutes.
Provisions for Institutes established on and after the commencement of the All-India Institute of Medical Sciences (Amendment) Act, 2012.
Incorporation and effects of incorporation for Institutes registered as societies under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
Transitory provisions for Institutes other than the existing Institute.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government exercises control over the Institutes, issues directions, and receives reports and information. Accounts are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, and reports are laid before Parliament.

act_identification.act_title: THE HINDU SUCCESSION ACT, 1956

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Seventh Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend and codify the law relating to intestate succession among Hindus.
act_overview.purpose: To amend and codify the law relating to intestate succession among Hindus, ensuring a structured and uniform system of inheritance for the Hindu community.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Application of Act.
key_sections.description: Defines the categories of persons to whom the Act applies, including Hindus, Buddhists, Jainas, and Sikhs, and certain exemptions.

key_sections.title: Definitions and interpretation.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms such as 'agnate', 'cognate', 'heir', 'intestate', and various traditional laws.

key_sections.title: Overriding effect of Act.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall override existing Hindu law, customs, usages, and other inconsistent laws.

key_sections.title: Devolution of interest in coparcenary property.
key_sections.description: Grants daughters equal rights as sons in Mitakshara coparcenary property by birth, making them coparceners.

key_sections.title: General rules of succession in the case of males.
key_sections.description: Outlines the order of succession for the property of a male Hindu dying intestate, prioritizing Class I heirs, then Class II, agnates, and cognates.

key_sections.title: Property of a female Hindu to be her absolute property.
key_sections.description: Declares that any property possessed by a female Hindu, however acquired, shall be held by her as full owner.

key_sections.title: General rules of succession in the case of female Hindus.
key_sections.description: Sets out the rules for the devolution of property of a female Hindu dying intestate, specifying different orders based on the source of property.

key_sections.title: Murderer disqualified.
key_sections.description: Disqualifies a person who commits or abets murder from inheriting the property of the murdered person.

key_sections.title: Failure of heirs.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that if an intestate leaves no qualified heir, the property shall devolve on the Government (escheat).

key_sections.title: Testamentary succession.
key_sections.description: Confers upon any Hindu the right to dispose of property by will or other testamentary disposition.

powers_conferred: Central Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, otherwise directs (regarding Scheduled Tribes)
Court to determine consideration for property transfer in absence of agreement
State Government to specify courts by notification in the Official Gazette
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: A person who commits murder or abets the commission of murder shall be disqualified from inheriting the property of the person murdered, or any other property in furtherance of the succession to which he or she committed or abetted the commission of the murder.

amended_acts: Hindu Succession (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 1990 (Karnataka Act 23 of 1994)
Hindu Succession (Tamil Nadu Amendment) Act, 1989 (Tamil Nadu Act 1 of 1990)
related_acts: Madras Nambudri Act, 1932 Madras Act (21 of 1933)

applies_to: Any person who is a Hindu by religion in any of its forms or developments, including Virashaiva, Lingayat, or a follower of Brahmo, Prarthana or Arya Samaj
Any person who is a Buddhist, Jaina or Sikh by religion
Any other person who is not a Muslim, Christian, Parsi or Jew by religion, unless it is proved that any such person would not have been governed by Hindu law or custom
Children (legitimate or illegitimate) of Hindu, Buddhist, Jaina or Sikh parents
Converts or reconverts to the Hindu, Buddhist, Jaina or Sikh religion
exemptions: Members of any Scheduled Tribe within the meaning of clause (25) of article 366 of the Constitution, unless Central Government directs otherwise
Property succession regulated by the Indian Succession Act, 1925, due to the Special Marriage Act, 1954
Any estate descending to a single heir by covenant or agreement with a Ruler of an Indian State or pre-commencement enactment
The Valiamma Thampuran Kovilagam Estate and the Palace Fund administered by the Palace Administration Board
Partitions of coparcenary property effected before 20th December, 2004 (for Section 6)
Daughters married prior to or partitions effected before the commencement of Hindu Succession (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 1990 (for Karnataka Amendment 6A(d))
Daughters married before the date of the commencement of the Hindu Succession (Tamil Nadu Amendment) Act, 1989 (for Tamil Nadu Amendment 29-A(iv))
Partitions effected before the date of the commencement of the Hindu Succession (Tamil Nadu Amendment) Act, 1989 (for Tamil Nadu Amendment 29-A(v))
special_provisions: Special provisions respecting persons governed by marumakkattayam and aliyasantana laws (Section 17)
State Amendments for Karnataka (Sections 6A, 6B, 6C) and Tamil Nadu (Sections 29-A, 29-B, 29-C) regarding equal rights to daughters in coparcenary property and devolution by survivorship.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act defines the rules for succession and devolution of property. Courts are empowered to determine consideration in property transfer disputes.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The court within the limits of whose jurisdiction the immovable property is situate or the business is carried on, and includes any other court which the State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify in this behalf.

schedules_summary.description: Lists the heirs in Class I and Class II for the purpose of succession under the Act, as referred to in Section 8.

act_identification.act_title: THE LIFE INSURANCE CORPORATION ACT, 1956

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the nationalisation of life insurance business in India by transferring all such business to a Corporation established for the purpose and to provide for the regulation and control of the business of the Corporation and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to nationalise the life insurance business in India. It achieves this by transferring all existing life insurance businesses to a newly established Corporation. The Act also provides for the regulation and control of the Corporation's business and related matters.

chapter_titles: ESTABLISHMENT OF LIFE INSURANCE CORORATION OF INDIA
TRANSFER OF EXISTING LIFE INSURANCE BUSINESS TO THE CORPORATION

key_definitions: Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title and commencement details of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Life Insurance Corporation of India.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Life Insurance Corporation of India as a body corporate.

key_sections.title: Board of Directors.
key_sections.description: Details the constitution, powers, and composition of the Board of Directors of the Corporation.

key_sections.title: Capital of Corporation.
key_sections.description: Specifies the authorised share capital of the Corporation and provisions for its increase, reduction, and share issuance.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Corporation.
key_sections.description: Outlines the general duty and specific powers of the Corporation in carrying on life insurance business.

key_sections.title: Transfer of assets and liabilities of existing insurers carrying on controlled business.
key_sections.description: Mandates the transfer of assets and liabilities of existing insurers' controlled business to the Corporation.

key_sections.title: Transfer of service of existing employees of insurers to the Corporation.
key_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of employees of existing insurers to the Corporation, maintaining their terms of service.

key_sections.title: Compensation for acquisition of controlled business.
key_sections.description: States that compensation will be given to insurers for acquired controlled business according to the First Schedule.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Tribunals.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to constitute Tribunals for the purposes of the Act, outlining their composition and powers.

key_sections.title: Corporation to be guided by the directions of Central Government.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the Corporation must follow Central Government directions on policy matters involving public interest.

key_sections.title: Appointment of auditors.
key_sections.description: Details the appointment, term, and conditions for auditors of the Corporation.

key_sections.title: Corporation to have the exclusive privilege of carrying on life insurance business.
key_sections.description: Grants the Corporation exclusive privilege of carrying on life insurance business in India from the appointed day, subject to later cessation by Section 30A.

key_sections.title: Policies to be guaranteed by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Guarantees payment of sums assured by policies issued by the Corporation and transferred policies by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power on the Central Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Confers power on the Board to make regulations with Central Government approval.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint date for establishment (Sec 3), appoint Chairperson/Managing Directors (Sec 4), increase/reduce authorised share capital (Sec 5), give directions on policy (Sec 21), constitute Tribunals (Sec 17), make rules (Sec 48), approve regulations (Sec 49), remove difficulties (Sec 51).

Corporation: Acquire, hold, dispose of property (Sec 3), carry on life insurance business (Sec 6), invest funds (Sec 6), acquire/hold/dispose of property for business (Sec 6), transfer business outside India (Sec 6), advance/lend money (Sec 6), borrow/raise money (Sec 6), carry on other business (Sec 6), modify contracts of life insurance (Sec 14), seek relief for certain transactions (Sec 15), determine compensation (Sec 16), establish offices/branches/agencies (Sec 18), constitute committees (Sec 19, 19A, 19B, 19C, 19D), employ persons (Sec 23), declare dividend (Sec 28B), have official seal (Sec 32), make regulations (Sec 49).

Board of Directors: General superintendence and direction of affairs (Sec 4), exercise powers of Corporation (Sec 4), appoint directors (Sec 4), specify senior management for disclosures (Sec 4B), formulate policy on related party transactions (Sec 4C), determine terms of issue of partly paid-up shares (Sec 5), increase issued share capital (Sec 5), reduce paid-up equity share capital (Sec 5), entrust powers to Chief Executive/Managing Directors (Sec 20), maintain funds (Sec 24), prepare books of account/financial statements (Sec 24A, 24B), prepare Board's report (Sec 24C), appoint auditors (Sec 25), appoint internal auditor (Sec 25C), cause actuarial investigation (Sec 26), approve surplus utilization (Sec 28), publish surplus distribution policy (Sec 28).
Tribunal: Decide matters referred to it (Sec 10, 16), powers of a civil court (Sec 17), exclusive jurisdiction in certain matters (Sec 41).
Adjudicating Officer: Adjudge penalties (Sec 4D).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 4B(5) imposes a penalty up to one lakh rupees on directors or employees contravening disclosure provisions. Section 4C(6) imposes a penalty up to twenty-five lakh rupees on directors or employees violating related party transaction provisions. Section 4D(5) specifies double the penalty for repeat contraventions within three years. Section 24D imposes a penalty from fifty thousand to five lakh rupees on specified officers for contravening financial reporting provisions. Section 40 prescribes imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both, for wilfully withholding or misapplying property.

related_acts: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999 (41 of 1999)
Coal Mines Provident Fund, Family Pension and Bonus Schemes Act, 1948 (46 of 1948)
Employees Provident Funds and Family Pension Fund Act, 1952 (19 of 1952)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director, Managing Directors, adjudicating officer, appellate authority, and special auditor. The Board of Directors appoints directors and fills casual vacancies of auditors and internal auditors. Members at a general meeting approve the appointment of directors and appoint auditors. The Nomination and Remuneration Committee recommends independent directors and their appointment/removal.
regulatory_bodies: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
Institute of Chartered Accountants of India

applies_to: life insurance business in India
existing insurers carrying on controlled business
whole-time employee of an insurer whose controlled business has been transferred
whole-time salaried employee of a chief agent of an insurer
Corporation
exemptions: any insurer whose business is being voluntarily wound up or is being wound up under the orders of the Court
any insurer to whom the Insurance Act does not apply by reason of the provisions contained in section 2E thereof
any composite insurer in respect of the management of whose affairs an Administrator has been appointed under section 52A of the Insurance Act
the scheme run by the Central Government known as the Post Office Life Insurance Fund
any approved superannuation fund as defined in clause (a) of section 58N of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922 (11 of 1922), which is in existence on the appointed day

any scheme in existence on the appointed day or any scheme framed after the appointed day with the approval of the Central Government whereby, in consideration of certain compulsory deductions made by Government from the salaries of its employees as part of the conditions of service, the payment of money is assured by Government on the death of the employee concerned or on the happening of any contingency dependent on his life

any Family Pension Scheme Framed under the Coal Mines Provident Fund, Family Pension and Bonus Schemes Act, 1948 (46 of 1948), or the Employees Provident Funds and Family Pension Fund Act, 1952 (19 of 1952), for the purpose of providing family pension and life assurance benefits to the employees covered by the said Scheme.
special_provisions: Exception in the case of insurance business in respect of persons residing outside India
Revesting of certain shares vested in the Administrator General
Repatriation of assets and liabilities in the case of foreign insurers in certain cases
Special provisions regarding transfer of controlled business of certain composite insurer

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Penalties are adjudicated by an officer appointed by the Central Government, with provisions for appeal. Tribunals constituted under the Act have powers of a civil court and exclusive jurisdiction in certain matters, with their decisions enforceable in civil courts. Specific penalties are prescribed for withholding property or contravening financial reporting requirements.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Tribunals, civil courts, and National Company Law Tribunal (for director disqualification).

schedules_summary.description: Details the methods and principles for calculating compensation to be given by the Corporation to insurers whose controlled business is acquired, including provisions for insurers with share capital, those who have allocated bonuses, and displaced insurers.
Outlines methods (Method A and Method B) for calculating the total amount of liabilities of an insurer incorporated outside India for the purposes of Section 35.
Specifies how compensation is to be calculated for chief agents and special agents whose contracts terminate due to the Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE HINDU MINORITY AND GUARDIANSHIP ACT, 1956
act_identification.act_short_title: The Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India and applies also to Hindus domiciled in the territories to which this Act extends who are outside the said territories

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend and codify certain parts of the law relating to minority and guardianship among Hindus.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to amend and codify the law relating to minority and guardianship among Hindus. It establishes clear provisions for natural and testamentary guardians, their powers, and emphasizes the welfare of the minor as the paramount consideration in guardianship matters.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Act to be supplemental to Act 8 of 1890.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act's provisions are in addition to, and not in derogation of, the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890.

key_sections.title: Application of Act.
key_sections.description: Defines the categories of persons to whom the Act applies, including Hindus, Buddhists, Jains, Sikhs, and certain other domiciled persons, with specific exemptions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms such as 'minor', 'guardian', and 'natural guardian'.

key_sections.title: Over-riding effect of Act.
key_sections.description: States that the Act overrides any inconsistent Hindu Law, custom, usage, or other laws in force before its commencement.

key_sections.title: Natural guardians of a Hindu minor.
key_sections.description: Identifies who can be a natural guardian for a Hindu minor, specifying conditions and exclusions.

key_sections.title: Powers of natural guardian.
key_sections.description: Outlines the powers of a natural guardian, including restrictions on disposing of immovable property without court permission.

key_sections.title: Testamentary guardians and their powers.
key_sections.description: Details the provisions for appointing guardians by will and their subsequent powers.

key_sections.title: De facto guardian not to deal with minor’s property.
key_sections.description: Prohibits de facto guardians from dealing with a minor's property after the Act's commencement.

key_sections.title: Welfare of minor to be paramount consideration.
key_sections.description: Establishes that the welfare of the minor is the primary consideration in the appointment or declaration of any person as guardian by a court.

powers_conferred: Power of natural guardian to do acts for the benefit of the minor or minor's estate (Section 8(1))
Power of natural guardian to mortgage, charge, transfer, or lease immovable property with court permission (Section 8(2))
Power of Hindu father/mother to appoint a guardian by will (Section 9)
Power of Central Government to direct application of Act to Scheduled Tribes (Section 3(2))

repealed_acts: any text, rule or interpretation of Hindu Law or any custom or usage as part of that law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act
any other law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act (in so far as it is inconsistent with any of the provisions contained in this Act)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Hindu father or mother by will (Section 9); Court (Section 13)

applies_to: any person who is a Hindu by religion in any of its forms or developments, including a Virashaiva, a Lingayat or a follower of the Brahmo, Prarthana or Arya Samaj
any person who is a Buddhist, Jain or Sikh by religion
any other person domiciled in the territories to which this Act extends who is not a Muslim, Christian, Parsi or Jew by religion (unless proved otherwise)
Hindus domiciled in the territories to which this Act extends who are outside the said territories
exemptions: members of any scheduled Tribe within the meaning of clause (25) of article 366 of the Constitution (unless Central Government directs otherwise)
Renoncants of the Union Territory of Pondicherry
special_provisions: Nothing contained in this Act shall apply to the members of any scheduled Tribe within the meaning of clause (25) of article 366 of the Constitution unless the Central Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, otherwise directs (Section 3(2))
Nothing contained in this Act shall apply to the Renoncants of the Union Territory of Pondicherry (Section 3(2A))

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through court proceedings for permission regarding property disposal (Section 8) and for appointment/declaration of guardians (Section 13).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: city civil court or a district court or a court empowered under section 4A of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890

act_identification.act_title: THE INTER-STATE RIVER WATER DISPUTES ACT, 1956

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the adjudication of disputes relating to waters of inter-State rivers and river valleys.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes a framework for the adjudication of disputes concerning the waters of inter-State rivers and river valleys. It empowers the Central Government to constitute Water Disputes Tribunals to investigate and decide on such disputes between State Governments, ensuring their decisions are final and binding.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used within the Act, such as 'prescribed', 'Tribunal', and 'water dispute'.

key_sections.title: Complaints by State Governments as to water disputes.
