key_sections.description: Outlines the process for State Governments to request the Central Government to refer a water dispute to a Tribunal for adjudication.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to constitute a Water Disputes Tribunal for adjudication when a request is received and negotiations fail.

key_sections.title: Adjudication of water disputes.
key_sections.description: Details the process by which the Tribunal investigates and forwards its report and decision on water disputes to the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Filling of vacancies.
key_sections.description: Provides for the filling of vacancies in the office of the Chairman or any other member of a Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Publication of decision of Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to publish the Tribunal's decision in the Official Gazette, making it final, binding, and enforceable as a Supreme Court order.

key_sections.title: Power to make schemes to implement decision of Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to frame schemes for the effective implementation of the Tribunal's decisions, including establishing authorities.

key_sections.title: Powers of Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the Tribunal powers similar to a civil court for summoning, discovery, investigation, and regulating its own procedure.

key_sections.title: maintenance of date bank and information.
key_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to maintain a national data bank and information system for river basins, with State Governments supplying necessary data.

key_sections.title: Bar of jurisdiction of Supreme Court and other courts.
key_sections.description: Explicitly bars the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts in respect of water disputes referred to a Tribunal under this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, after consulting with State Governments.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Ravi and Beas Waters Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a specific Tribunal for the verification and adjudication of matters related to the Ravi and Beas waters as per the Punjab Settlement.

powers_conferred: Central Government to constitute a Water Disputes Tribunal (Section 4)
Central Government to refer water disputes to the Tribunal (Section 5)
Central Government to publish the decision of the Tribunal (Section 6)
Central Government to make schemes to implement the decision of the Tribunal (Section 6A)
Central Government to maintain a data bank and information system (Section 9A)
Central Government to verify data supplied by State Governments (Section 9A)
Central Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (Section 13)
Central Government to dissolve the Tribunal (Section 12)
Tribunal to investigate and adjudicate water disputes (Section 5)
Tribunal to have powers of a civil court (Section 9)
Tribunal to require State Governments to carry out surveys and investigations (Section 9)
Tribunal to regulate its practice and procedure (Section 9)
State Governments to request the Central Government to refer water disputes (Section 3)

authorities_established: any authority (whether described as such or as a committee or other body) for the implementation of the decision or directions of the Tribunal
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Chief Justice of India nominates the Chairman and other members of the Tribunal. Central Government appoints assessors.

applies_to: State Governments
two or more State Governments
special_provisions: Extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963, s. 2 and First Schedule.
Extended to Pondicherry by Reg. 7 of 1973, s. 3 and First Schedule.
Constitution of Ravi and Beas Waters Tribunal for specific matters related to the Punjab Settlement.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government, after consultation with the State Governments
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Decisions of the Tribunal, once published in the Official Gazette by the Central Government, are final and binding and have the same force as an order or decree of the Supreme Court. The Central Government may frame schemes to implement these decisions. Tribunal decisions regarding expenses can be enforced as if they were orders made by the Supreme Court.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Water Disputes Tribunals (Supreme Court and other courts are barred from exercising jurisdiction over referred water disputes)

act_identification.act_title: THE STATES REORGANISATION ACT, 1956

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India (affecting its States and Union territories)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the reorganisation of the States of India and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the reorganisation of the States of India by altering their territories, forming new states, and making consequential provisions for their administration, legislatures, high courts, and financial matters. It aims to restructure the political and administrative map of India.

chapter_titles: PART II TERRITORIAL CHANGES AND FORMATION OF NEW STATES
PART III ZONES AND ZONAL COUNCILS
PART IV REPRESENTATION IN THE LEGISLATURES
PART VII APPORTIONMENT OF ASSETS AND LIABILITIES OF CERTAIN PART A AND PART B STATES
PART VIII APPORTIONMENT OF CERTAIN ASSETS AND LIABILITIES OF THE UNION
PART IX PROVISIONS AS TO CERTAIN CORPORATIONS AND INTER-STATE AGREEMENTS AND ARRANGEMENTS
PART X PROVISIONS AS TO SERVICES
PART XI LEGAL AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act as The States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'existing State', 'new State', and 'successor State'.

key_sections.title: Transfer of territory from Hyderabad to Andhra and alteration of name.
key_sections.description: Details the transfer of specific territories from Hyderabad to Andhra and renames Andhra as Andhra Pradesh from the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Formation of Kerala State.
key_sections.description: Outlines the formation of the new State of Kerala by combining territories from Travancore-Cochin and Madras.

key_sections.title: Amendment of the First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Specifies the substitution of Parts A, B, and C in the First Schedule to the Constitution to reflect the new state structure.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Zonal Councils.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of Zonal Councils for five specified zones from the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Councils.
key_sections.description: Defines the advisory functions of the Zonal Councils, including discussing economic planning, border disputes, linguistic minorities, and matters arising from state reorganisation.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Delimitation Commission.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a Delimitation Commission by the Central Government to determine constituencies and seat allocations.

key_sections.title: High Courts for the new States.
key_sections.description: Establishes High Courts for the new States of Kerala, Mysore, and Rajasthan, and designates existing High Courts for new Bombay, Madhya Pradesh, and Punjab.

key_sections.title: Application of Part.
key_sections.description: Specifies that Part VII governs the apportionment of assets and liabilities of existing Part A or Part B States affected by territorial changes.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to All-India Services.
key_sections.description: Details the constitution of State cadres for All-India Services in new States and the allocation of members to these cadres.

key_sections.title: Power to adapt laws.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the appropriate Government to make adaptations and modifications to existing laws for their application to the newly formed or territorially altered States or Union territories.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the President to issue orders to remove any difficulties arising in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Act 49 of 1951.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Government of Part C States Act, 1951, with effect from the appointed day, while saving laws made under it.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to specify population ratio, to order allocation or adjustment of assets and liabilities, to give directions to State Governments, to make rules, to remove difficulties, to nominate members to Zonal Councils, to approve rules of procedure for Zonal Councils, to make rules for joint meetings of Zonal Councils, to constitute Delimitation Commission, to appoint judges, to appoint principal seat of High Court, to issue directions for State Electricity Boards, to give directions for power and water supply arrangements, to make orders for inter-state agreements, to issue directions for statutory corporations, to add or amend conditions for road transport permits, to authorize levy of tolls, to establish Advisory Committees for services, to approve changes in service conditions, to specify authorities for exercising statutory functions.

President: to nominate Union Minister to Zonal Council, to nominate members from Union territories to Zonal Councils, to nominate members if no Council of Ministers in a State, to make provisions for terms of office of members of Council of States, to make modifications in Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Orders, to appoint judges of High Courts, to appoint principal seat of High Court, to remove difficulties.
Governor/Rajpramukh: to authorize expenditure from Consolidated Fund of new States, to determine allowances and privileges.
Zonal Councils: to appoint Committees, to discuss matters and advise Central and State Governments.
Chief Justice of High Court: to certify proceedings for transfer between High Courts, to appoint places of sitting for Judges and division courts, to specify advocates entitled to practice.
Delimitation Commission: to determine number of seats, constituencies, and revise orders for parliamentary and assembly constituencies.
High Courts: to approve, admit, enrol, remove and suspend advocates and attorneys, to make rules with respect to practice and procedure.

amended_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
Union Duties of Excise (Distribution) Act, 1953 (3 of 1953)
repealed_acts: Government of Part C States Act, 1951 (49 of 1951)
Section 14 of this Act (by Adaptation of Laws (No. 1) Order, 1956)
Section 126 of this Act (by the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958 (24 of 1958))
related_acts: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
Representation of the People Act, 1951 (43 of 1951)
Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur (New State) Act, 1954

important_authorities.appointment_powers: President, Central Government, Chairman of Zonal Council, Chief Justice of High Court, Governor of new State, Chief Justice of India.

applies_to: Existing States of India
New States formed under the Act
Union territories formed or affected by the Act
Government servants
Statutory corporations
Co-operative societies
Commercial or industrial undertakings
exemptions: Jammu and Kashmir (from certain provisions like allocation of seats in House of People and revenue distribution)
Specific territories or entities may be excluded from certain provisions as detailed in the Act (e.g., certain districts from new state formations).
special_provisions: Formation of Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands as a Union territory.
Special provisions for elections to the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.
Specific arrangements for High Courts, including jurisdiction and transfer of proceedings.
Detailed apportionment of assets and liabilities for various existing and new states.
Provisions for certain State Financial Corporations, State Electricity Boards, and inter-state agreements.
Special provisions relating to retrenchment compensation in certain cases.
Establishment of Devaswom Fund in Madras for territories transferred from Travancore-Cochin.
Continuance of facilities in specified State institutions for adjoining states.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government, Zonal Councils (with Central Government approval), High Courts.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through orders issued by the President or Central Government, directions given by the Central Government to State Governments, orders of the Delimitation Commission having the force of law, and enforcement by courts, tribunals, and authorities.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Courts (for new States and transferred proceedings), Supreme Court (for appeals), and other courts, tribunals, or authorities as specified or empowered to enforce laws.

schedules_summary.description: Specifies the constituencies and states for the transfer of sitting members of Legislative Assemblies from existing states to new or altered states.
Details modifications to be made in the Delimitation of Council Constituencies (Madras) Order, 1951, affecting the Madras Legislative Council.
Outlines the allocation of seats in the House of the People and the assignment of seats to State Legislative Assemblies for the reorganised states and Union territories.

Contains modified forms of Section 3 of the Union Duties of Excise (Distribution) Act, 1953, and paragraphs 3 and 5 of the Constitution (Distribution of Revenues) Order, 1953, for the financial year 1956-57.
Prescribes the method for apportionment of liability in respect of pensions among successor states, including adjustments and allocation ratios.

Lists categories of institutions (e.g., Engineering Colleges, Medical Colleges, Hospitals, Research Institutes, Jails) for which the Central Government may direct facilities to be provided to adjoining states.

act_identification.act_title: THE BIHAR AND WEST BENGAL (TRANSFER OF TERRITORIES) ACT, 1956
act_identification.act_short_title: The Bihar and West Bengal (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1956.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: States of Bihar and West Bengal, specifically the transferred territories between them.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the transfer of certain territories from Bihar to West Bengal and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act facilitates the transfer of specific territories from the State of Bihar to the State of West Bengal. It also addresses consequential matters such as representation in legislatures, high court jurisdiction, apportionment of assets and liabilities, and administrative provisions arising from this territorial transfer.

chapter_titles: PART III REPRESENTATION IN THE LEGISLATURES
PART VI APPORTIONMENT OF ASSETS AND LIABILITIES
PART VIII LEGAL AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'appointed day' and 'transferred territories'.

key_sections.title: Transfer of territories from Bihar to West Bengal.
key_sections.description: Specifies the territories to be transferred from Bihar to West Bengal and their inclusion in West Bengal districts.

key_sections.title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule of the Constitution to reflect the territorial changes of Bihar and West Bengal.

key_sections.title: Allocation of seats in the House of the People and assignment of seats to State Legislative Assemblies.
key_sections.description: Modifies the number of seats allocated to Bihar and West Bengal in the House of the People and their respective Legislative Assemblies.

key_sections.title: Extension of jurisdiction of, and transfer of proceedings to, Calcutta High Court.
key_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the Calcutta High Court to the transferred territories and provides for the transfer of pending proceedings from Patna High Court.

key_sections.title: Land and goods.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that land and goods in the transferred territories belonging to Bihar shall pass to West Bengal, with provisions for division of unissued stores.

key_sections.title: Public debt.
key_sections.description: Outlines the apportionment of public debt between Bihar and West Bengal, including loans raised by government securities and from central/other banks.

key_sections.title: Pensions.
key_sections.description: States that the liability for pensions shall be apportioned between Bihar and West Bengal in accordance with the provisions in the Schedule.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to services.
key_sections.description: Governs the provisional and final allotment of government servants between Bihar and West Bengal following the territorial transfer.

key_sections.title: Power to adapt laws.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the appropriate Government to adapt and modify laws for their application in Bihar or West Bengal.

key_sections.title: Transfer of pending proceedings.
key_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of pending legal proceedings (other than High Court) between the courts, tribunals, authorities, or officers of Bihar and West Bengal.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the President to issue orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint an authority for demarcation of boundary line (Section 3(1))
State Government to alter name, extent and boundaries of any district or division in West Bengal (Section 3(4))
President to make provisions regarding terms of office of members of the Council of States (Section 7)
President to make modifications in the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, and the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950 (Section 14)
Central Government to appoint an authority to determine seats for Scheduled Castes and Tribes and revise delimitation orders (Section 16(1))
Governor of West Bengal to authorise expenditure from the Consolidated Fund (Section 20(2))
President to specify modifications for distribution of revenues (Section 21)
Central Government to order allocation or adjustment of property, benefits, or liabilities between States (Section 37)
Central Government to give directions to either State Government regarding services (Section 41(5))
Appropriate Government to adapt and modify laws (Section 44)
Government of West Bengal to specify authority, officer or person for exercising statutory functions (Section 46)
President to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act (Section 51)
Central Government to make rules to give effect to the provisions of the Act (Section 52(1))

related_acts: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
Delimitation of Council Constituencies (West Bengal) Order, 1951
Union Duties of Excise (Distribution) Act, 1953 (3 of 1953)

authorities_established: Authority appointed by the Central Government for demarcation of boundary line (Section 3(1))
Authority appointed by the Central Government for delimitation of constituencies (Section 16(1))
important_authorities.appointment_powers: President appoints Election Commission (Section 2(d)). Central Government appoints authority for demarcation (Section 3(1)). President makes provisions for terms of office of Council of States members (Section 7). Central Government appoints authority for delimitation (Section 16(1)). Government of West Bengal names authorities for exercising statutory functions (Section 46).
regulatory_bodies: State Transport Authority of West Bengal
Regional Transport Authority in West Bengal

applies_to: States of Bihar and West Bengal
Transferred territories
Sitting members of the House of the People and State Legislative Assemblies
Government servants serving in connection with the affairs of Bihar
State Financial Corporations constituted for Bihar and West Bengal
Road transport permits issued by State Transport Authorities in Bihar
special_provisions: Specific demarcation rules for the boundary line in Purnea district (Section 3(2))
Inclusion of transferred territory in Darjeeling district and formation of Purulia district (Section 3(3))
Continuance of certain sitting members of the Bihar Legislative Assembly despite territorial changes (Section 9)
Temporary provisions for the continuance of existing road transport permits in transferred territories (Section 40)
Conditions of service for provisionally or finally allotted persons not to be varied to their disadvantage without Central Government approval (Section 41(4) Proviso)
Continuance of officers in the same posts in West Bengal after transfer (Section 42)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through various mechanisms including orders by the President and Central Government, directions from the Central Government to State Governments, adaptation and construction of laws by appropriate authorities and courts, and notifications by the Government of West Bengal for exercising statutory functions.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court at Calcutta, High Court at Patna, Supreme Court, any Court, tribunal or authority (for transfer of proceedings and construction of laws).

schedules_summary.description: Details the apportionment of liability in respect of pensions between the States of Bihar and West Bengal. It covers pensions granted before the appointed day, outstanding claims, and pensions of officers retiring on or after the appointed day, including adjustments based on population ratio and qualifying service.

act_identification.act_title: THE SECURITIES CONTRACTS (REGULATION) ACT, 1956

act_overview.preamble: An Act to prevent undesirable transactions in securities by regulating the business of dealing therein, by [1]*** providing for certain other matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to prevent undesirable transactions in securities by regulating the business of dealing in them and providing for other related matters.

chapter_titles: LISTING OF SECURITIES BY PUBLIC COMPANIES

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical extent, and commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Grant of recognition to stock exchanges.
key_sections.description: Outlines conditions and procedure for granting recognition to stock exchanges by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Corporatisation and demutualisation of stock exchanges.
key_sections.description: Mandates corporatisation and demutualisation of recognised stock exchanges.

key_sections.title: Power of recognised stock exchanges to make bye-laws.
key_sections.description: Grants recognised stock exchanges the power to make bye-laws for regulating contracts, subject to SEBI approval.

key_sections.title: Power to issue directions.
key_sections.description: Empowers SEBI to issue directions to stock exchanges, clearing corporations, or other persons in the securities market.

key_sections.title: Contracts in notified areas illegal in certain circumstances.
key_sections.description: Declares certain contracts in securities illegal in notified areas if not entered into through recognised stock exchanges.

key_sections.title: Contracts in derivatives.
key_sections.description: Declares contracts in derivatives legal and valid if traded on recognised stock exchanges and settled through clearing houses.

key_sections.title: Conditions for listing.
key_sections.description: Requires compliance with listing agreement conditions for securities listed on a recognised stock exchange.

key_sections.title: Delisting of securities.
key_sections.description: Provides for delisting of securities by recognised stock exchanges and the right of appeal.

key_sections.title: Right of appeal to Securities Appellate Tribunal against refusal of stock exchange to list securities of public companies.
key_sections.description: Grants companies the right to appeal to the Securities Appellate Tribunal against refusal to list securities.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for various contraventions of the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Power to adjudicate.
key_sections.description: Empowers SEBI to appoint adjudicating officers for imposing penalties.

key_sections.title: power to delegate.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to delegate its powers (except rule-making) to SEBI or RBI.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make rules for carrying out the Act's objects.

key_sections.title: Power of Securities and Exchange Board of India to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers SEBI to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Grant recognition to stock exchanges (Section 4), withdraw recognition (Section 5), call for periodical returns or direct inquiries (Section 6), direct rules to be made or make rules (Section 8), supersede governing body of a recognised stock exchange (Section 11), suspend business of recognised stock exchanges (Section 12), prohibit contracts in certain cases (Section 16), license dealers in securities (Section 17), specify non-application of Act (Section 28), delegate powers (Section 29A), make rules (Section 30), grant immunity (Section 23-O), establish Special Courts (Section 26A).
Recognised Stock Exchange: Make rules restricting voting rights (Section 7A), make bye-laws (Section 9), establish additional trading floor (Section 13A), delist securities (Section 21A).

Securities and Exchange Board of India: Make or amend bye-laws of recognised stock exchanges (Section 10), issue directions (Section 12A), approve schemes for corporatisation and demutualisation (Section 4B), approve transfer of clearing house functions (Section 8A), make regulations (Section 31), appoint adjudicating officers (Section 23-I), settle administrative and civil proceedings (Section 23JA).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for various contraventions, including failure to comply with requisitions, entering into illegal contracts, contravening provisions related to licensing or stock exchanges, operating illegal trading places, and misrepresenting ability to trade. Penalties range from imprisonment up to ten years or fines up to twenty-five crore rupees, or both, for serious offences. Specific penalties are also provided for failures such as furnishing information, entering client agreements, redressing investor grievances, segregating client funds/securities, complying with listing conditions, excess dematerialisation, and furnishing periodical returns, with fines ranging from one lakh rupees to twenty-five crore rupees. Failure to pay imposed penalties or comply with directions also attracts imprisonment and/or fines.

related_acts: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002
International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints judges for Special Courts (Section 26A). Central Government appoints persons to exercise powers of superseded governing body of a recognised stock exchange (Section 11). Securities and Exchange Board of India appoints adjudicating officers (Section 23-I).
regulatory_bodies: Securities and Exchange Board of India

applies_to: Whole of India
persons dealing in securities
stock exchanges
public companies
collective investment schemes
mutual funds
pooled investment vehicles
exemptions: Government
Reserve Bank of India
any local authority
any corporation set up by a special law
any person who has effected any transaction with or through the agency of any such authority
any convertible bond or share warrant or any option or right in relation thereto
classes of contracts specified by Central Government
non-transferable specific delivery contracts (unless specified otherwise)
International Financial Services Centre (for SEBI powers)
special_provisions: Special provisions related to commodity derivatives (Section 30A)
Special provisions related to pooled investment vehicle (Section 30B)
Establishment of Special Courts for speedy trial of offences (Section 26A)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (Section 30), Recognised stock exchanges (Section 7A, Section 9), Securities and Exchange Board of India (Section 31)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced through penalties, adjudication by officers appointed by SEBI, recovery of amounts, and prosecution in Special Courts. SEBI also issues directions and approves schemes for stock exchanges.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Securities Appellate Tribunal, High Court, Special Courts, Civil Courts (jurisdiction excluded for matters determinable by SAT)

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL HIGHWAYS ACT, 1956

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Seventh Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the declaration of certain highways to be national highways and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: The primary purpose of this Act is to declare specific highways as national highways. It also provides for the acquisition of land, development, maintenance, and management of these national highways, along with provisions for levying fees and addressing related matters.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its applicability to the whole of India, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Declaration of certain highways to be national highways.
key_sections.description: Declares highways specified in the Schedule as national highways and empowers the Central Government to add or omit highways from the Schedule.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'competent authority' and 'land'.

key_sections.title: Power to acquire land, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to declare its intention to acquire land for national highway purposes through notification.

key_sections.title: Determination of amount payable as compensation.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for determining compensation for acquired land, including public notice, hearing claims, and arbitration if the amount is not acceptable.

key_sections.title: National highways to vest in the Union.
key_sections.description: States that all national highways, including appurtenant lands and structures, vest in the Union.

key_sections.title: Responsibility for development and maintenance of national highways.
key_sections.description: Assigns responsibility for development and maintenance of national highways to the Central Government, with power to delegate functions to State Governments or other authorities.

key_sections.title: Fees for services or benefits rendered on national highways.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to levy and collect fees for services or benefits rendered on national highways, such as for use of ferries, bridges, and tunnels.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to enter into agreements for development and maintenance of national highways.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to enter into agreements with persons for the development and maintenance of national highways, enabling them to collect fees.

key_sections.title: Punishment for mischief by injury to national highway.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for individuals who cause mischief by injuring a national highway, rendering it impassable or less safe.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including specific matters like fee rates and inspection reports.

key_sections.title: Laying of notifications, rules, etc., before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Requires all notifications, rules, and agreements made under the Act to be laid before both Houses of Parliament.

powers_conferred: Central Government: declare highways to be national highways (Section 2)
Central Government: omit any highway from the Schedule (Section 2)
Central Government: authorize competent authority to perform functions (Section 3)
Central Government: declare intention to acquire land for national highways (Section 3A)
Central Government: authorize persons to enter land for survey, measurement, etc. (Section 3B)
Central Government: declare acquisition of land (Section 3D)
Central Government: enter and do acts necessary upon vested land (Section 3F)
Central Government: appoint arbitrator for compensation disputes (Section 3G)
Central Government: deposit amount for compensation (Section 3H)
Central Government: give directions to State Governments (Section 6)
Central Government: levy fees for services or benefits on national highways (Section 7)
Central Government: enter into agreements for development and maintenance of national highways (Section 8A)
Central Government: make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 9)
Competent authority: perform functions as authorized by Central Government (Section 3)
Competent authority: cause publication of notification substance (Section 3A)
Competent authority: hear objections to land use (Section 3C)
Competent authority: submit report to Central Government regarding acquisition (Section 3D)
Competent authority: direct owner/person in possession to surrender land (Section 3E)
Competent authority: apply to Commissioner of Police/Collector to enforce surrender of land (Section 3E)
Competent authority: determine amount payable as compensation (Section 3G)
Competent authority: give public notice inviting claims for compensation (Section 3G)
Competent authority: determine persons entitled to receive compensation (Section 3H)
Competent authority: refer apportionment disputes to civil court (Section 3H)
Competent authority: have powers of a civil court for certain matters (summoning, discovery, evidence, etc.) (Section 3I)
Person (under agreement with Central Government): collect and retain fees (Section 8A)
Person (under agreement with Central Government): regulate and control traffic (Section 8A)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 8B prescribes punishment for mischief by injury to a national highway. The punishment is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with a fine, or with both.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government authorizes the 'competent authority' and appoints the 'arbitrator' for compensation disputes.

applies_to: Whole of India
Highways declared as national highways
Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir
Union territory of Ladakh
exemptions: Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for acquisitions under this Act)
special_provisions: The Act was made applicable to Goa, Daman and Diu by Regulation 11 of 1963, s. 3 and Sch. (w.e.f. 01/02/1965).
The Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh vide notification NO. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through notifications by the Central Government, actions of the competent authority (including land acquisition, compensation determination, and taking possession), arbitration for compensation disputes, and penalties for mischief. The Commissioner of Police or Collector may be involved in enforcing possession.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Principal civil court of original jurisdiction (for apportionment disputes)

schedules_summary.description: Lists numerous National Highways by their National Highway Number and provides a description of their routes, connecting various cities and regions across India, and sometimes extending to international borders.

act_identification.act_title: THE RIVER BOARDS ACT, 1956

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Inter-State rivers and river valleys across India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of River Boards for the regulation and development of inter-State rivers and river valleys.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the establishment of River Boards. These Boards are tasked with the regulation and development of inter-State rivers and river valleys, with the Central Government taking control in the public interest.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II ESTABLISHMENT OF RIVER BOARDS
CHAPTER III POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE BOARD

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date as appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to expediency of control by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Declares that it is expedient in the public interest for the Central Government to control the regulation and development of inter-State rivers and river valleys.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'Board', 'Governments interested', 'member', and 'prescribed'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Boards.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to establish River Boards for advising Governments interested on matters concerning inter-State rivers or river valleys.

key_sections.title: Matters in respect of which a Board may be authorised to tender advice.
key_sections.description: Outlines the specific matters on which a Board may be empowered to tender advice, including conservation, irrigation, power development, flood control, navigation, afforestation, soil erosion, and pollution prevention.

key_sections.title: Functions of Board.
key_sections.description: Specifies that the Central Government, after consultation, may empower the Board to perform functions under section 13 within its area of operation, requiring consultation with interested Governments.

key_sections.title: Preparation of schemes by Board and their execution.
key_sections.description: Details the process for the Board to prepare, confirm, modify, or reject schemes for regulating or developing inter-State rivers, including consultation and cost allocation.

key_sections.title: General Powers of Board.
key_sections.description: Grants general powers to the Board for efficiently performing its functions, including acquiring property, conducting investigations, inspecting works, conducting research, collecting data, and publishing information.

key_sections.title: Arbitration.
key_sections.description: Provides for arbitration in case of disputes or differences between two or more Governments interested regarding advice tendered by the Board, measures undertaken, or financial liabilities.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering various administrative and procedural matters.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Board, with Central Government approval, to make regulations for its meetings, advisory committees, association of persons, and terms of service for members and officers.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Establish River Boards (Sec 4)
Central Government: Appoint Chairman and members of the Board (Sec 5)
Central Government: Empower the Board to perform functions (Sec 14)
Central Government: Pay sums to the Board (Sec 17)
Central Government: Dissolve the Board (Sec 27)
Central Government: Make rules (Sec 28)
Board: Tender advice to Governments interested on regulation/development of inter-State rivers (Sec 13)
Board: Prepare and execute schemes for regulating or developing inter-State rivers (Sec 15)
Board: Acquire, hold and dispose of property (Sec 16(a))
Board: Undertake investigations, surveys, research (Sec 16(b), (d))
Board: Inspect works (Sec 16(c))
Board: Collect data and publish information (Sec 16(e), (f))
Board: Require information from Governments interested (Sec 16(g))
Board: Delegate powers (Sec 24)
Board: Make regulations (Sec 29)

applies_to: inter-State rivers and river valleys
Governments interested

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through the establishment of River Boards, tendering advice, preparation and execution of schemes, and arbitration for disputes between interested Governments. The Central Government may assist in scheme execution.

act_identification.act_title: THE LOK SAHAYAK SENA ACT, 1956

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution of Lok Sahayak Sena for imparting military training to citizens of India.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the constitution of the Lok Sahayak Sena. Its main objective is to impart military training to citizens of India.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, such as 'camp', 'Force', 'prescribed', 'superior officer', and 'volunteer'.

key_sections.description: Provides for the raising and maintenance of the Lok Sahayak Sena by the Central Government through the enrolment of volunteers.

key_sections.title: Enrolment.
key_sections.description: Outlines the eligibility criteria (citizen of India, age 18-40 years) and process for enrolment as a volunteer in the Force.

key_sections.title: Offences and penalties.
key_sections.description: Details various offences committed by volunteers (e.g., failure to attend, insubordination, disobedience) and prescribes summary penalties like fines or confinement to barracks.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering aspects like enrolment, training, discipline, and discharge.

powers_conferred: Central Government to raise and maintain the Lok Sahayak Sena
Central Government to establish, close down, or re-establish camps
Central Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act
Prescribed authority to enrol volunteers
Prescribed authority to direct duties of volunteers
Prescribed authority to discharge volunteers
Prescribed authority to summarily punish volunteers for offences
Prescribed authority to order recovery of loss or damage to Government property
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Volunteers committing offences such as failure to attend, absence without leave, using criminal force or insubordinate language to a superior officer, disobeying lawful commands, neglecting orders, assaulting others, or acts prejudicial to good order/military discipline, shall be punishable summarily by the prescribed authority with a fine up to fifty rupees or confinement to barracks for up to seven days.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The prescribed authority has the power to enroll volunteers.

applies_to: Any citizen of India not below the age of eighteen years and not above the age of forty years who offers for enrolment as a volunteer

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Offences are punishable summarily by the prescribed authority. Fines can be recovered by a magistrate. Loss or damage to Government property can be recovered as an arrear of land revenue by the Collector.

Central Government to make provisions or give directions by order to remove difficulties in giving effect to the extended laws (Section 6(1))

act_identification.act_title: THE KHADI AND VILLAGE INDUSTRIES COMMISSION ACT, 1956
act_identification.act_short_title: The Khadi and Village Industries Commission Act, 1956
