act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL SALES TAX ACT, 1956

act_overview.preamble: An Act to formulate principles for determining when a sale or purchase of goods takes place in the course of inter-State trade or commerce or outside a State or in the course of import into or export from India, to provide for the levy, collection and distribution of taxes on sales of goods in the course of inter-State trade or commerce and to declare certain goods to be of special importance in inter-State trade or commerce and specify the restrictions and conditions to which State laws imposing taxes on the sale or purchase of such goods of special importance shall be subject.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish principles for identifying inter-State, outside-State, import, or export sales/purchases of goods. It also provides for the levy, collection, and distribution of taxes on inter-State sales and declares certain goods as specially important, setting conditions for State taxation on them.

chapter_titles: FORMULATION OF PRINCIPLES FOR DETERMINING WHEN A SALE OR PURCHASE OF GOODS TAKES PLACE IN THE COURSE OF INTER-STATE TRADE OR COMMERCE OR OUTSIDE A STATE OR IN THE COURSE OF IMPORT OR EXPORT
GOODS OF SPECIAL IMPORTANCE IN INTER-STATE TRADE OR COMMERCE
APPEALS TO THE HIGHEST APPELLATE AUTHORITY OF THE STATE
AUTHORITY TO SETTLE DISPUTES IN COURSE OF INTER -STATE TRADE OR COMMERCE

key_definitions: crossing the customs frontiers of India

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application, and commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appropriate State', 'business', 'dealer', 'goods', 'sale', and 'turnover'.

key_sections.title: When is a sale or purchase of goods said to take place in the course of inter-State trade or commerce.
key_sections.description: Formulates principles for determining when a sale or purchase occurs in inter-State trade or commerce.

key_sections.title: Liability to tax on inter-State sales.
key_sections.description: Establishes the liability of dealers to pay tax on inter-State sales, with certain exemptions.

key_sections.title: Burden of proof, etc., in case of transfer of goods claimed otherwise than by way of sale.
key_sections.description: Places the burden of proof on dealers claiming goods movement was not a sale and outlines the declaration process.

key_sections.title: Registration of dealers.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration for dealers liable to pay tax and outlines the process, conditions, and cancellation of registration.

key_sections.title: Rates of tax on sales in the course of inter-State trade or commerce.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the rates of tax applicable to inter-State sales, including provisions for reduced rates and exemptions.

key_sections.title: Levy and collection of tax and penalties.
key_sections.description: Details how tax and penalties are levied by the Government of India and collected by State authorities.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Specifies various offences under the Act and the corresponding punishments, including imprisonment and fines.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to the Central and State Governments to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Company in liquidation.
key_sections.description: Outlines the duties and liabilities of liquidators regarding tax payments for companies in liquidation.

key_sections.title: Liability of directors of private company in liquidation.
key_sections.description: Establishes the joint and several liability of directors for unpaid tax of a private company in liquidation.

key_sections.title: Appeals to highest appellate authority of State.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals against orders of the assessing authority to the highest appellate authority of the State.

key_sections.title: Central Sales Tax Appellate Authority.
key_sections.description: Establishes and defines the composition of the Central Sales Tax Appellate Authority to settle inter-State disputes.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Details the process and conditions for filing appeals to the Central Sales Tax Appellate Authority.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint commencement date (Section 1(3)), exempt tax on sales to diplomatic missions (Section 6(3)), specify designated Indian carrier (Section 5(5) Explanation), make rules (Section 13(1)), constitute Central Sales Tax Appellate Authority (Section 19(1)), provide officers and staff to Authority (Section 19(4)), reduce rate of tax under sub-section (1) of section 8 (Section 8(1) proviso).
State Government: Make rules (Section 13(3), 13(4)), exempt or reduce tax on certain inter-State sales (Section 8(5)).

Assessing Authority (or authority granting registration): Assess, re-assess, collect, and enforce payment of tax, interest, penalty (Section 9(2)), impose security as condition for registration (Section 7(2A)), require additional security (Section 7(3A)), forfeit security (Section 7(3D)), refuse to issue forms (Section 7(3F)), order refund of security (Section 7(3G)), impose penalty in lieu of prosecution (Section 10A(1)).

Central Sales Tax Appellate Authority: Settle inter-State disputes (Section 19(1)), adjudicate appeals (Section 20(2)), regulate its own procedure (Section 23), grant stay of operation of order (Section 22(1A)), issue direction for refund of tax or transfer refundable amount (Section 22(1B)), have powers of a court (Section 22(1)).
Highest Appellate Authority of the State: Hear and decide appeals (Section 18A(3)), grant stay (Section 18A(5)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 10 defines offences such as furnishing false declarations, failing to register or comply with security orders, falsely representing registration status, failing to use goods for specified purposes, possessing unauthorized forms, and collecting tax in contravention of Section 9A. Penalties include simple imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both, with a daily fine for continuing offences. Section 10A allows for a penalty not exceeding one-and-a-half times the tax that would have been levied, in lieu of prosecution for certain offences.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairman and Members of the Central Sales Tax Appellate Authority (Section 19(2)).

applies_to: Every dealer liable to pay tax under this Act
Any person who carries on the business of buying, selling, supplying or distributing goods
exemptions: Sales in the course of export of goods out of the territory of India (Section 6(1) proviso, Section 5(3))
Subsequent sales during movement of goods to a registered dealer, under certain conditions (Section 6(2))
Sales to foreign diplomatic missions, consulates, the United Nations, or similar international bodies, subject to Central Government notification (Section 6(3))
Sales of goods to a registered dealer for use in a unit located in any special economic zone or for development, operation and maintenance of special economic zone by the developer (Section 8(6))
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act to come into force (Section 1(3)).
State Governments may, in public interest, exempt or reduce tax rates on certain inter-State sales (Section 8(5)).
Special provisions for sales to units or developers in Special Economic Zones (Section 8(6), 8(7), 8(8)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Authorities empowered under the general sales tax law of the appropriate State assess, re-assess, collect, and enforce payment of tax, interest, and penalties on behalf of the Government of India, applying the provisions of such State law (Section 9(2)).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a presidency magistrate or a magistrate of the first class shall try any offence under this Act (Section 11(1)).

act_identification.act_title: THE HINDU ADOPTIONS AND MAINTENANCE ACT, 1956
act_identification.act_short_title: THE HINDU ADOPTIONS AND MAINTENANCE ACT, 1956

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend and codify the law relating to adoptions and maintenance among Hindus.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to amend and codify the law relating to adoptions and maintenance among Hindus. It aims to provide a comprehensive legal framework for adoptions and maintenance obligations within the Hindu community.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official name of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Application of Act.
key_sections.description: Defines the categories of persons to whom the Act applies, including Hindus, Buddhists, Jainas, Sikhs, and certain other persons, with specific exemptions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'custom', 'usage', 'maintenance', and 'minor'.

key_sections.title: Overriding effect of Act.
key_sections.description: States that the Act overrides existing Hindu law, custom, usage, and other inconsistent laws regarding matters covered by the Act.

key_sections.title: Adoptions to be regulated by this Chapter.
key_sections.description: Mandates that all adoptions by or to a Hindu after the Act's commencement must comply with its provisions, rendering non-compliant adoptions void.

key_sections.title: Requisites of a valid adoption.
key_sections.description: Outlines the essential conditions for an adoption to be legally valid, concerning the capacity of persons adopting, giving, and being adopted.

key_sections.title: Capacity of a male Hindu to take in adoption.
key_sections.description: Defines the capacity of a male Hindu to adopt, including requirements for sound mind, age, and spousal consent.

key_sections.title: Capacity of a female Hindu to take in adoption.
key_sections.description: Defines the capacity of a female Hindu to adopt, including requirements for sound mind, age, and spousal consent.

key_sections.title: Persons capable of giving in adoption.
key_sections.description: Specifies who can give a child in adoption, primarily the father, mother, or guardian, and conditions for their consent or court permission.

key_sections.title: Persons who may be adopted.
key_sections.description: Sets forth the conditions for a person to be eligible for adoption, including religious affiliation, marital status, and age.

key_sections.title: Other conditions for a valid adoption.
key_sections.description: Lists additional conditions for a valid adoption, such as the absence of existing children of the same gender, age difference requirements, and the actual giving and taking of the child.

key_sections.title: Effects of adoption.
key_sections.description: Describes the legal consequences of adoption, including the severance of ties with the birth family and the creation of new ties with the adoptive family, with certain provisos.

key_sections.title: Valid adoption not to be cancelled.
key_sections.description: States that a validly made adoption cannot be cancelled by adoptive parents or the adopted child.

key_sections.title: Maintenance of wife.
key_sections.description: Establishes the right of a Hindu wife to be maintained by her husband during her lifetime, including conditions for separate residence and maintenance.

key_sections.title: Maintenance of children and aged parents.
key_sections.description: Outlines the obligation of a Hindu to maintain legitimate or illegitimate children and aged or infirm parents.

key_sections.title: Amount of maintenance.
key_sections.description: Grants discretion to the court to determine the amount of maintenance, considering factors like the parties' status, needs, property, and income.

powers_conferred: Central Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, otherwise directs (regarding application to Scheduled Tribes) (Section 2(2))
Court to grant permission to a guardian for adoption (Section 9(4))
Court to sanction payments or rewards in consideration of adoption (Section 9(5))
Court to determine whether any, and if so what, maintenance shall be awarded (Section 23(1))
State Government or an officer authorised by the State Government to sanction prosecution under Section 17 (Section 17(3))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 17 prohibits receiving or giving any payment or reward in consideration of adoption. Contravention is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.

applies_to: any person, who is a Hindu by religion in any of its forms or developments, including a Virashaiva, a Lingayat or a follower of the Brahmo, Prarthana or AryaSamaj
any person who is a Buddhist, Jaina or Sikh by religion

any other person who is not a Muslim, Christian, Parsi or Jew by religion, unless it is proved that any such person would not have been governed by the Hindu law or by any custom or usage as part of that law in respect of any of the matters dealt with herein if this Act had not been passed
any child, legitimate or illegitimate, both of whose parents are Hindus, Buddhists, Jainas or Sikhs by religion

any child, legitimate or illegitimate, one of whose parents is a Hindu, Buddhist, Jaina or Sikh by religion and who is brought up as a member of the tribe, community, group or family to which such parent belongs or belonged
any child, legitimate or illegitimate, who has been abandoned both by his father and mother or whose parentage is not known and who in either case is brought up as a Hindu, Buddhist, Jaina or Sikh
any person who is a convert or re-convert to the Hindu, Buddhist, Jaina or Sikh religion
exemptions: Muslim, Christian, Parsi or Jew by religion (unless specific conditions are met)
members of any Scheduled Tribe within the meaning of clause (25) of article 366 of the Constitution unless the Central Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, otherwise directs
special_provisions: Extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963, s. 2 and First Schedule.
Amended in U.P. Act 57 of 1976.
In Pondicherry, nothing contained in this Act shall apply to the renoncants of the Union territory of Pondicherry.
The words “except the State of Jammu and Kashmir” omitted by Act 34 of 2019, s. 95 and the Fifth Schedule (w.e.f. 31-10- 2019).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through legal proceedings in courts, which determine the validity of adoptions, award maintenance, and impose penalties for prohibited acts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: city civil court or a district court within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the child to be adopted ordinarily resides

act_identification.act_title: THE MANIPUR (VILLAGE AUTHORITIES IN HILL AREAS) ACT, 1956
act_identification.act_short_title: The Manipur (Village Authorities in Hill Areas) Act, 1956

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of the hill areas of the Union territory of Manipur

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the constitution and functions of Village Authorities in the hill areas of the Union territory of Manipur.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws governing the constitution and functions of Village Authorities in the hill areas of the Union territory of Manipur. It establishes village courts and defines their jurisdiction for both criminal and civil cases, ensuring local administration of justice.

chapter_titles: CONSTITUTION AND FUNCTIONS OF VILLAGE AUTHORITIES
ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE BY VILLAGE AUTHORITIES

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Village Authorities.
key_sections.description: Outlines the criteria and process for constituting Village Authorities based on the number of tax-paying houses.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of Village Authorities.
key_sections.description: Declares Village Authorities as corporate bodies with perpetual succession and the power to sue and be sued.

key_sections.title: Functions of Village Authorities.
key_sections.description: Details the duties of Village Authorities, including maintaining law and order, powers of arrest, and providing information to magistrates.

key_sections.title: Constitution of village courts.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Chief Commissioner to appoint members of Village Authorities to form village courts.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of village courts in criminal cases.
key_sections.description: Grants village courts concurrent jurisdiction with criminal courts for specific offences listed in the Schedule.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of village courts in civil cases.
key_sections.description: Defines the types of civil suits and monetary limits within which village courts have concurrent jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Procedure before village courts.
key_sections.description: States that certain major procedural codes (Court Fees Act, CrPC, CPC, Evidence Act) do not apply to village courts, and their procedure will be prescribed by rules.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Chief Commissioner to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Manipur State Hill Peoples (Administration) Regulation, 1947, with savings for past actions and rights.

powers_conferred: Chief Commissioner: to declare hill areas (Section 2(d))
Chief Commissioner: to nominate members of Village Authorities (Section 3(3))
Chief Commissioner: to call for records of proceedings (Section 18)
Chief Commissioner: to appoint members of village courts (Section 19)
Chief Commissioner: to make rules for the Act (Section 57)
Deputy Commissioner: to remove members of Village Authorities (Section 8)
Deputy Commissioner: to decide election disputes (Section 12)
Deputy Commissioner: to control Village Authorities (Section 15)
Deputy Commissioner: to transfer criminal cases (Section 29)
Deputy Commissioner: to cancel or modify village court orders or direct retrial (Section 25)
Village Authorities: to maintain law and order (Section 16(1)(a))
Village Authorities: to arrest persons for heinous offences or other specified reasons (Section 16(1)(b))
Village Authorities: to give immediate information of deaths, heinous offences, and disputes (Section 16(1)(c))
Village Authorities: to supply information to police officers or magistrates (Section 16(1)(d))
Village Courts: to dismiss or refuse to entertain complaints (Section 22)
Village Courts: to impose fine or award compensation (Section 26)
Village Courts: to release offenders after admonition or on probation (Section 27)
Village Courts: to permit compounding of offences (Section 28)
Village Courts: to determine necessary parties in suits (Section 39)
Village Courts: to summon witnesses and require production of documents (Section 51(1))
District Judge: to cancel or modify village court decrees or order retrial in civil cases (Section 43)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for refusal to assist Village Authorities (fine up to 200 rupees by a village court or 500 rupees by a sub-divisional magistrate) and for failure to obey witness summons (fine not exceeding 25 rupees by a village court). Village courts are empowered to impose fines not exceeding 200 rupees or imprisonment up to one month for convicted offenders, and can also award compensation or release offenders on admonition or probation. The Schedule lists specific offences under various Acts (e.g., Cattle Trespass Act, Police Act, Indian Penal Code) that village courts have jurisdiction to try.

repealed_acts: The Manipur State Hill Peoples (Administration) Regulation, 1947

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Chief Commissioner nominates members of Village Authorities and appoints members of village courts. The chairman of a Village Authority is elected by its members if there is no Chief Khulakpa.

applies_to: the whole of the hill areas of the Union territory of Manipur
every person who is a citizen of India and who is ordinarily resident in the village
exemptions: Certain suits are not triable by village courts, including those on a balance of partnership account, for a share under intestacy or legacy, by or against the Government or public officers, by or against minors or persons of unsound mind, for assessment/recovery of rent of immovable property, for recovery of immovable property, or for enforcement/redemption of a mortgage of immovable property (Section 31).
Village courts shall not try any criminal case or civil suit in which the Village Authority or any member thereof is a party or is interested (Section 50).
No woman shall, against her will, be compelled to appear in person before a village court as an accused, party, or witness (Section 53).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Village Authorities are responsible for maintaining law and order, making arrests, and providing information. Village courts try criminal and civil cases, impose fines, and award compensation. Decrees of village courts can be executed with the assistance of the Munsiff court.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Village courts, sub-divisional magistrate, Deputy Commissioner, court of session, district judge, munsiff court

schedules_summary.description: Lists specific offences triable by a village court, including offences under the Cattle Trespass Act, 1871, other enactments punishable with fine only up to two hundred rupees, offences under Section 34 of the Police Act, 1861, and certain sections of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, with specific value limits for property-related offences.

act_identification.act_title: THE FARIDABAD DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION ACT, 1956

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the town of Faridabad, in the district of Gurgaon in the State of Haryana (as described in the Schedule)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment and regulation of a trading Corporation for the purpose of carrying on and promoting trade and industry in the town of Faridabad, assisting in the rehabilitation of displaced persons settled therein and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish and regulate a trading Corporation for promoting trade and industry in Faridabad. It also seeks to assist in the rehabilitation of displaced persons settled in the town and manage related matters.

chapter_titles: POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE CORPORATION

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Faridabad Development Corporation Act, 1956.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Corporation', 'displaced person', and 'Faridabad'.

key_sections.title: Incorporation.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Faridabad Development Corporation as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Corporation.
key_sections.description: Outlines the composition of the Corporation, including a Chairman and other members appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: General duty of the Corporation.
key_sections.description: Defines the primary duties of the Corporation, including promoting trade and industry, assisting displaced persons, and managing Union property.

key_sections.title: Powers of the Corporation.
key_sections.description: Details the powers of the Corporation, such as acquiring and holding property, promoting trade, providing financial assistance, constructing buildings, and advancing loans.

key_sections.title: Vesting of property in the Corporation.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that all property, assets, and funds related to Faridabad's development shall vest in the Corporation upon its establishment.

key_sections.title: Mode of recovery of moneys due to the Corporation.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the method for recovering moneys due to the Corporation, allowing recovery as an arrear of land revenue.

key_sections.title: Members and officers of the Corporation to be public servants.
key_sections.description: Declares that all members and officers of the Corporation are deemed public servants under the Indian Penal Code when acting under this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Corporation: acquire and hold property, make improvements, transfer property by sale, lease or otherwise
Corporation: carry on or promote any trade, business or industry
Corporation: give financial or other assistance to persons to enable them to carry on trade, business or industry in Faridabad
Corporation: construct or cause to be constructed residential or other buildings and to sell or let such buildings
Corporation: advance loans on prescribed terms and purposes
Corporation: supply or cause to be supplied electrical energy for domestic and industrial purposes
Corporation: take measures for the rehabilitation of displaced persons settled in Faridabad
Corporation: take steps for improving the economic and social conditions of the inhabitants of Faridabad
Central Government: appoint date for establishment of Corporation
Central Government: appoint Chairman and other members of the Corporation
Central Government: determine term of office and conditions of service of Chairman and members
Central Government: appoint another person to act in place of a temporarily absent member
Central Government: appoint Administrator of the Corporation
Central Government: declare non-recurring expenditure as capital provided to the Corporation
Central Government: make grants and advance loans to the Corporation
Central Government: direct vesting of property in the Corporation
Central Government: determine intervals and terms for repayment of capital and loans with interest
Central Government: direct provision for depreciation and reserve and other funds
Central Government: give general or special directions to the Corporation
Central Government: require returns, statistics, accounts and other information from the Corporation
Central Government: remove difficulties by order or direction
Central Government: make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act
Corporation: constitute committees for general or special purposes
Corporation: appoint other officers for efficient performance of functions
Corporation: delegate powers and duties to Chairman, any other member or officer

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints Chairman, members, and Administrator. The Corporation appoints other officers.

applies_to: Faridabad Development Corporation
Persons carrying on trade, business or industry in Faridabad
Displaced persons settled in Faridabad
Inhabitants of Faridabad
special_provisions: The Act applies to the specific geographical area of Faridabad as described in the Schedule.
The office of a member of the Corporation shall not disqualify its holder for being chosen as, or for being, a member of either House of Parliament.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government may give directions to the Corporation. Moneys due to the Corporation can be recovered by the Collector as an arrear of land revenue. The Corporation is required to submit budgets, annual reports, and accounts to the Central Government.

schedules_summary.description: Describes the geographical boundaries and area of Faridabad, including specific landmarks and villages.

act_identification.act_title: THE SLUM AREAS (IMPROVEMENT AND CLEARANCE) ACT, 1956
act_identification.act_short_title: The Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act, 1956

legislative_details.geographical_extent: all Union territories except the Union territories of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and the Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the improvement and clearance of slum areas in certain Union territories and for the protection of tenants in such areas from eviction.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to provide for the improvement and clearance of slum areas in certain Union territories. It also includes provisions for the protection of tenants in such areas from eviction, ensuring their rights during redevelopment.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER IV SLUM CLEARANCE AND RE-DEVELOPMENT
CHAPTER VI PROTECTION OF TENANTS IN SLUM AREAS FROM EVICTION

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its geographical application to Union territories (with exceptions), and how its commencement date is determined.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Administrator', 'building', 'competent authority', 'land', 'occupier', 'owner', 'slum clearance', and 'work of improvement'.

key_sections.title: Declaration of slum areas.
key_sections.description: Empowers the competent authority to declare an area as a slum area if buildings are unfit for human habitation or detrimental to safety, health, or morals.

key_sections.title: Power of competent authority to require improvement of buildings unfit for human habitation.
key_sections.description: Grants the competent authority power to issue notices to owners requiring improvements to buildings deemed unfit for human habitation in slum areas.

key_sections.title: Power of competent authority to order demolition of buildings unfit for human habitation.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the competent authority to order the demolition of buildings in slum areas that are unfit for human habitation and cannot be rendered fit at a reasonable expense.

key_sections.title: Power to declare any slum area to be a clearance area.
key_sections.description: Enables the competent authority to declare a slum area as a clearance area if demolition of all buildings is the most satisfactory method of dealing with conditions.

key_sections.title: Slum clearance order.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for making and confirming slum clearance orders, requiring demolition and vacation of buildings, and allowing owners to re-develop land.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to acquire land.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to acquire land within, adjoining, or surrounded by slum or clearance areas for improvement or re-development purposes.

key_sections.title: Basis for determination of compensation.
key_sections.description: Establishes the method for calculating compensation for acquired land, based on net average monthly income, and provides for appeals to the Administrator.

key_sections.title: Proceedings for eviction of tenants not to be taken without permission of the competent authority.
key_sections.description: Prohibits eviction proceedings against tenants in slum areas without the prior written permission of the competent authority, considering factors like alternative accommodation and slum improvement.

key_sections.title: Rent of buildings in slum areas.
key_sections.description: Provides for the determination of rent for buildings in slum areas after improvement or re-erection, especially for tenants restored to possession.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for non-compliance with notices/orders, contravention of restrictions, and obstruction of authorized persons, including provisions for company offenses.

key_sections.title: Act to override other laws.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, covering various procedural and administrative matters.

powers_conferred: Competent authority to declare slum areas (Section 3)
Competent authority to require improvement of buildings (Section 4)
Competent authority to order demolition of buildings (Section 7)
Competent authority to declare clearance areas (Section 9)
Competent authority to make slum clearance orders (Section 10)
Competent authority to re-develop clearance areas (Section 11)
Central Government to acquire land (Section 12)
Competent authority to determine compensation (Section 15)
Competent authority to grant or refuse permission for eviction (Section 19)
Competent authority to direct restoration of possession of premises (Section 20A)
Competent authority to determine rent of buildings (Section 20B)
Competent authority to authorise entry, inspection, and survey (Sections 22, 23, 24, 25)
Competent authority to order eviction of occupants (Section 28)
Competent authority to order removal of offensive or dangerous trades (Section 29)
Central Government to make rules (Section 40)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever fails to comply with any notice, order or direction issued or given under this Act shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. Whoever commences or causes to be commenced any work in contravention of any restriction or condition imposed under sub-section (7) of section 10 or any plan for the re-development of a clearance area shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. Whoever obstructs the entry of any person authorised under this Act or molests such person shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees. Provisions are also made for offences committed by companies, holding persons in charge and directors liable.

amended_acts: Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Amendment Act, 1964

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Administrator of a Union territory appoints the 'competent authority'. The Central Government may delegate powers of the Administrator to the Chief Secretary or other officers.

applies_to: All Union territories except the Union territories of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and the Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands
Owners and occupiers of buildings and land in slum areas
Tenants in slum areas
exemptions: Union territories of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and the Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands
Eviction of tenants from buildings belonging to the Government, the Delhi Development Authority, or any local authority
special_provisions: Different commencement dates may be appointed for different Union territories by the Central Government
Extended to Pondicherry Act 26 of 1968

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The competent authority issues notices, orders, and directions. It can execute works itself if owners fail, recover expenses as arrears of land revenue, demolish buildings, and evict occupants using force if necessary. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance and obstruction. Appeals against orders lie with the Administrator.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a magistrate of the first class shall try an offence punishable under this Act. Civil courts have barred jurisdiction except as expressly provided.

schedules_summary.description: Outlines the principles for the determination of the net average monthly income for land acquired under the Act, including methods for calculating gross rent, deductions for expenses, and provisions for unoccupied land.

act_identification.act_title: THE WOMEN’S AND CHILDREN’S INSTITUTIONS (LICENSING) ACT, 1956
act_identification.act_short_title: THE WOMEN’S AND CHILDREN’S INSTITUTIONS (LICENSING) ACT, 1956

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the licensing of institutions for women and children and for matters incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate and license institutions established for the reception, care, protection, and welfare of women and children. It mandates that such institutions operate under a valid licence and adhere to prescribed conditions to ensure the well-being of their inmates.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its geographical application (whole of India except Jammu and Kashmir), and that it comes into force in a State on a date appointed by the State Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'child', 'institution', 'licensing authority', 'prescribed', and 'woman'.

key_sections.title: Licensing of institutions.
key_sections.description: Mandates that no person shall establish or maintain an institution after the Act's commencement without a licence granted under this Act.

key_sections.title: Application for licence.
key_sections.description: Outlines the requirement for persons desiring to establish an institution to apply for a licence to the licensing authority in the prescribed form.

key_sections.title: Grant of licence.
key_sections.description: Details the process for granting, refusing, and renewing licences, including the requirement for written orders and communication of refusal grounds.

key_sections.title: Licence not transferable.
key_sections.description: States that a licence granted under this Act cannot be transferred.

key_sections.title: Revocation of licence.
key_sections.description: Provides for the revocation of a licence by the licensing authority under certain conditions, such as breach of conditions or unsatisfactory management, and outlines the consequences of revocation.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Establishes the right to appeal to the State Government against an order of the licensing authority refusing or revoking a licence.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions, rules, or licence conditions, including imprisonment or fine.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply to certain institutions.
key_sections.description: Specifies institutions to which the Act does not apply, such as certain hostels, boarding houses, and protective homes under another specific Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering various aspects like application forms, management, and inspection.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Provides for the repeal of corresponding State Acts upon the commencement of this Act in a State and includes savings provisions for actions taken under such repealed Acts.

powers_conferred: State Government: To appoint the date of commencement of the Act in a State (Section 1).
State Government: To act as licensing authority or prescribe an officer or authority as such (Section 2).
State Government: To hear appeals against orders of the licensing authority (Section 8).
State Government: To make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 11).
Licensing authority: To grant, refuse, or renew licences (Section 5).
Licensing authority: To revoke licences (Section 7).
Licensing authority: To direct the restoration or transfer of women or children from an institution upon licence revocation (Section 7).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who contravenes any of the provisions of this Act or of any rule made thereunder, or any of the conditions of a licence shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to two hundred and fifty rupees, or with both.

related_acts: the Suppression of Immoral Traffic in Women and Girls Act, 1956 (104 of 1956)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government

applies_to: institutions established and maintained for the reception, care, protection and welfare of women or children
exemptions: hostels, or boarding houses attached to, or controlled or recognised by educational institutions
any protective home established under the Suppression of Immoral Traffic in Women and Girls Act, 1956 (104 of 1956)
special_provisions: Extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
Shall come into force in a State on such date as the State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a licensing system managed by a licensing authority, which grants, renews, and revokes licences. Contravention of the Act's provisions, rules, or licence conditions can lead to penalties including imprisonment or fine.

act_identification.act_title: THE IMMORAL TRAFFIC (PREVENTION) ACT, 1956

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide in pursuance of the International Convention signed at New York on the 9th day of May, 1950, for the Prevention of Immoral Traffic.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to prevent immoral traffic, specifically the sexual exploitation or abuse of persons for commercial purposes. It aims to suppress prostitution, particularly in public places and involving children or minors, and provides for the rescue, rehabilitation, and protection of victims through corrective institutions and protective homes.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, its application to the whole of India, and its commencement dates.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'brothel', 'child', 'prostitution', 'protective home', and 'special police officer'.

key_sections.title: Punishment for keeping a brothel or allowing premises to be used as a brothel.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals who keep, manage, or allow premises to be used as a brothel.

key_sections.title: Punishment for living on the earnings of prostitution.
key_sections.description: Outlines penalties for persons living on the earnings of prostitution, with enhanced punishment if a child or minor is involved.

key_sections.title: Procuring, inducing or taking person for the sake of prostitution.
key_sections.description: Details punishments for procuring, inducing, or taking a person for prostitution, with severe penalties for offenses against the will of the person or involving children/minors.

key_sections.title: Detaining a person in premises where prostitution is carried on.
key_sections.description: Specifies penalties for detaining a person in a brothel or premises for sexual intercourse, including presumptions for children or minors found in brothels.

key_sections.title: Prostitution in or in the vicinity of public places.
key_sections.description: Prohibits prostitution in or near public places and prescribes penalties for those carrying on or permitting such activities, with enhanced penalties for child or minor involvement.

key_sections.title: Seducing or soliciting for purpose of prostitution.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishments for seducing or soliciting for prostitution in public places.

key_sections.title: Seduction of a person in custody.
key_sections.description: Details severe punishments for persons in custody or authority who cause or aid the seduction of a person for prostitution.

key_sections.title: Detention in a corrective institution.
key_sections.description: Allows courts to order detention in a corrective institution for female offenders of sections 7 or 8, in lieu of imprisonment, based on character and circumstances.

key_sections.title: Special police officer and advisory body.
key_sections.description: Mandates the appointment of special police officers and permits the formation of advisory bodies to deal with offences under the Act.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable.
key_sections.description: Declares offences under the Act as cognizable and outlines procedures for arrest without warrant by special police officers.

key_sections.title: Search without warrant.
key_sections.description: Empowers special police officers or trafficking police officers to conduct searches without a warrant under specific conditions, including removal and medical examination of persons found.

key_sections.title: Rescue of person.
key_sections.description: Authorizes magistrates to direct police officers to enter brothels, remove persons, and produce them before the magistrate.

key_sections.title: Intermediate custody of persons removed under section 15 or rescued under section 16.
key_sections.description: Provides for the safe custody, inquiry, and potential detention in protective homes for persons removed or rescued under the Act.

key_sections.title: Closure of brothel and eviction of offenders from the premises.
key_sections.description: Empowers magistrates to order the closure of brothels and eviction of offenders, making leases void.

key_sections.title: Protective homes.
key_sections.description: Governs the establishment, licensing, maintenance, and management of protective homes and corrective institutions by the State Government or licensed authorities.

key_sections.title: Power to establish special courts.
key_sections.description: Enables State Governments to establish Special Courts for the speedy trial of offences under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering various aspects like custody, maintenance, and management of institutions.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals existing State Acts relating to suppression of immoral traffic upon the commencement of this Act and includes savings provisions for actions taken under those repealed acts.

powers_conferred: State Government: To appoint special police officers (Section 13(1)).
State Government: To associate non-official advisory bodies with special police officers (Section 13(3)(b)).
State Government: To establish and maintain protective homes and corrective institutions (Section 21(1)).
State Government: To issue and revoke licenses for protective homes and corrective institutions (Section 21(3), (7)).
State Government: To transfer inmates between protective homes or corrective institutions (Section 21(9A)).

Central Government: To establish special courts for inter-State offences (Section 22AA).
Magistrate: To direct police officers to enter brothels and remove persons (Section 16(1)).
Magistrate: To pass orders for safe custody of removed/rescued persons (Section 17(1), (3)).
Magistrate: To order detention of persons in protective homes or other suitable custody (Section 17(4)).
Magistrate: To summon a panel of respectable persons to assist in inquiries (Section 17(5)).
Magistrate: To issue notice and inquire into the use of premises as brothels and order closure/eviction (Section 18(1)).
Magistrate: To receive applications for being kept in a protective home or provided care (Section 19(1)).
Magistrate: To order removal of prostitutes from any place and prohibit re-entry (Section 20(3)).
Magistrate: To try cases summarily (Section 22B).
Special Police Officer: To deal with offences under the Act (Section 13(1)).

Special Police Officer: To search premises without warrant (Section 15(1)).
Special Police Officer: To remove persons from premises during search (Section 15(4)).
Trafficking Police Officer: To investigate inter-State offences (Section 13(4)).
Trafficking Police Officer: To search premises without warrant (Section 15(1)).
Trafficking Police Officer: To remove persons from premises during search (Section 15(4)).
District Magistrate: To confer powers of special police officer on retired police/military officers (Section 13(2A)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines various offences including keeping a brothel (Section 3), living on the earnings of prostitution (Section 4), procuring, inducing, or taking persons for prostitution (Section 5), detaining persons in brothels (Section 6), prostitution in public places (Section 7), seducing or soliciting for prostitution (Section 8), and seduction of a person in custody (Section 9). Penalties range from imprisonment for terms of up to three months to life imprisonment, along with fines. Enhanced penalties are prescribed for offences involving children or minors. Other offences include failure to comply with removal orders (Section 20) and establishing/maintaining protective homes without a license (Section 21).

repealed_acts: All State Acts relating to suppression of immoral traffic in persons or to the prevention of prostitution, in force in any State immediately before the commencement of this Act.
related_acts: International Convention signed at New York on the 9th day of May, 1950

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government appoints special police officers and officers for investigation of licence applications. The Central Government appoints trafficking police officers. The District Magistrate may confer powers of a special police officer on retired police or military officers.

applies_to: The whole of India

Persons involved in immoral traffic, brothel keeping, living on earnings of prostitution, procuring, inducing, or taking persons for prostitution, detaining persons in brothels, prostitution in public places, seducing or soliciting for prostitution, seduction of a person in custody.
special_provisions: The Act has been extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Goa, Daman and Diu, and the Union Territory of Pondicherry.
The State Government may, by notification, direct that prostitution shall not be carried on in specified areas.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out by special police officers and trafficking police officers, who have powers of arrest and search. Magistrates and Special Courts try offences. The Act provides for rescue operations, intermediate custody, and detention in protective homes or corrective institutions for rehabilitation. Brothels can be closed and offenders evicted by magisterial orders.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class, District Magistrate, Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Executive Magistrate specially empowered by the State Government, Special Courts established by State or Central Government, and the Court of Session for appeals.

schedules_summary.description: Lists the magistrates competent to exercise powers conferred by various sections of the Act, including Section 7(1), 11(4), 15(5), 16, 18, 19, 20, and 22B.

act_identification.act_title: THE COPYRIGHT ACT, 1957

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend and consolidate the law relating to copyright.
act_overview.purpose: To amend and consolidate the law relating to copyright in India.

chapter_titles: OWNERSHIP OF COPYRIGHT AND THE RIGHTS OF THE OWNER
RIGHTS OF BROADCASTING ORGANISATION AND OF PERFORMERS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its geographical extent to the whole of India, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Interpretation.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Works in which copyright subsists.
key_sections.description: Outlines the classes of works (literary, dramatic, musical, artistic, cinematograph films, sound recordings) in which copyright subsists in India, subject to certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Meaning of copyright.
key_sections.description: Defines copyright as the exclusive right to do or authorise specific acts in respect of a work, varying by type of work (literary, dramatic, musical, artistic, computer programme, cinematograph film, sound recording).

key_sections.title: First owner of copyright.
key_sections.description: States that the author is generally the first owner of copyright, with specific provisions for works made in employment, commissioned works, Government works, and public undertakings.

key_sections.title: Assignment of copyright.
key_sections.description: Allows the owner of copyright to assign their rights wholly or partially, for the whole term or part thereof, with specific conditions for future works and royalties for authors of literary/musical works in films/sound recordings.

key_sections.title: Compulsory licence in works withheld from public.
key_sections.description: Provides for compulsory licensing if a copyright owner unreasonably withholds a published or performed work from the public, or refuses communication to the public on reasonable terms.

key_sections.title: Registration of Copyright society.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration for any person or association carrying on the business of issuing or granting licences for copyright works, with provisions for conditions, renewal, and cancellation.

key_sections.title: Broadcast reproduction right.
key_sections.description: Establishes a special 'broadcast reproduction right' for broadcasting organisations, subsisting for twenty-five years, and defines acts constituting infringement.

key_sections.title: Performer’s right.
key_sections.description: Grants a special 'performer’s right' to performers in relation to their performances, subsisting for fifty years.

key_sections.title: When copyright infringed.
key_sections.description: Defines when copyright in a work is deemed to be infringed, including doing exclusive acts without licence or importing infringing copies.

key_sections.title: Certain acts not to be infringement of copyright.
key_sections.description: Lists various acts that do not constitute an infringement of copyright, such as fair dealing, reproduction for judicial proceedings, educational use, and certain uses by libraries.

key_sections.title: Offences of infringement of copyright or other rights conferred by this Act.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for knowingly infringing copyright or other rights conferred by the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of police to seize infringing copies.
key_sections.description: Empowers police officers (not below sub-inspector rank) to seize infringing copies and plates without warrant, to be produced before a Magistrate.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering various procedural and administrative matters.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint Registrar and Deputy Registrars of Copyrights (Section 10).
Central Government: To extend copyright to foreign works (Section 40).
Central Government: To apply Chapter VIII to broadcasting organisations and performers in certain other countries (Section 40A).
Central Government: To restrict rights in works of foreign authors (Section 42).
Central Government: To restrict rights of foreign broadcasting organisations and performers (Section 42A).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 78).
Appellate Board: To decide certain disputes (Section 6).
Appellate Board: To regulate its own procedure (Section 12).
Appellate Board: To grant compulsory licences (Sections 31, 31A, 31B, 31C, 31D, 32, 32A).
Appellate Board: To revoke assignment of copyright (Section 19A).
Appellate Board: To fix tariff schemes for copyright societies (Section 33A).
Appellate Board: To fix resale share right (Section 53A).
Registrar of Copyrights: To maintain Register of Copyrights (Section 44).
Registrar of Copyrights: To enter particulars of work in Register (Section 45).
Registrar of Copyrights: To amend or alter Register (Section 49).
Registrar of Copyrights: To publish entries in Official Gazette (Section 50A).
Police Officer (not below Sub-Inspector): To seize infringing copies without warrant (Section 64).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who knowingly infringes copyright or other rights conferred by the Act (except Section 53A) is punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than six months but which may extend to three years, and with a fine not less than fifty thousand rupees but which may extend to two lakh rupees. Enhanced penalties apply for second and subsequent convictions (imprisonment not less than one year but up to three years, fine not less than one lakh rupees but up to two lakh rupees). Knowing use of an infringing copy of a computer programme is an offence punishable with imprisonment for seven days to three years and a fine of fifty thousand rupees to two lakh rupees. Possession of plates for making infringing copies is punishable with imprisonment up to two years and fine. Circumvention of technological measures and tampering with Rights Management Information are punishable with imprisonment up to two years and fine. Making false entries in the register or producing false entries is punishable with imprisonment up to one year or fine or both. Publishing sound recordings or video films in contravention of Section 52A is punishable with imprisonment up to three years and fine.

act_identification.act_title: THE COAL BEARING AREAS (ACQUISITION AND DEVELOPMENT) ACT, 1957
act_identification.act_short_title: the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India, except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish in the economic interest of India greater public control over the coal mining industry and its development by providing for the acquisition by the State of unworked land containing or likely to contain coal deposits or of rights in or over such land, for the extinguishment or modification of such rights accruing by virtue of any agreement, lease, licence or otherwise, and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to establish greater public control over the coal mining industry and its development. It provides for the acquisition by the State of unworked land containing or likely to contain coal deposits or rights over such land, and for the extinguishment or modification of existing rights, to facilitate coal prospecting and mining.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'competent authority', 'Government company', and 'Tribunal'.

key_sections.title: Appointment of competent authority.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint any person as a competent authority for the purposes of this Act, potentially for different provisions or areas.

key_sections.title: Preliminary notification respecting intention to prospect for coal in any area and powers of competent authorities thereupon.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to issue a preliminary notification of its intention to prospect for coal and outlines the powers of the competent authority for survey and related activities.

key_sections.title: Power to acquire land or rights in or over land notified under section 4.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to acquire land or rights over land previously notified under Section 4 if coal is found to be obtainable.

key_sections.title: Declaration of acquisition.
key_sections.description: Details the process for the Central Government to make a declaration of acquisition after considering objections to the acquisition of land or rights.

key_sections.title: Vesting of land or rights in Central Government.
key_sections.description: States that upon publication of the acquisition declaration, the land or rights vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from encumbrances.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of land or rights in a Government company.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to direct that acquired land or rights, instead of vesting in itself, vest in a Government company under specified terms and conditions.

key_sections.title: Compensation for prospecting licences ceasing to have effect, rights under mining leases being acquired, etc.
key_sections.description: Specifies the method for determining compensation payable for prospecting licences that cease to have effect, for acquired rights under mining leases, and for acquired land.

key_sections.title: Method of determining compensation.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for determining compensation, including the constitution of a Tribunal and its powers to make awards.

key_sections.title: Prospecting and mining to be done by Central Government in conformity with the Mineral Concession Rules.
key_sections.description: Mandates that prospecting and mining operations conducted by the Central Government or a Government company conform to the Mineral Concession Rules.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals against awards of the Tribunal to the High Court and against orders of a competent authority to the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for obstructing authorized acts, damaging marks, or failing to comply with orders under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering inquiry procedures, Tribunal proceedings, and appeals.

key_sections.title: Notifications under Act 1 of 1894 in which proceedings are pending to be treated as notifications under this Act.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that certain notifications issued under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, before the commencement of this Act, shall be treated as notifications under this Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint competent authority (Sec 3)
Central Government: To issue preliminary notification for prospecting (Sec 4)
Central Government: To acquire land or rights in or over land (Sec 7)
Central Government: To make declaration of acquisition (Sec 9)
Central Government: To direct vesting of land or rights in a Government company (Sec 11)
Central Government: To constitute a Tribunal for determining compensation (Sec 14)
Central Government: To delegate its powers or duties (Sec 19)
Central Government: To obtain information relating to property (Sec 21)
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Sec 27)
