Competent Authority: To enter and inspect property (Sec 22)
Tribunal: To determine the amount of compensation (Sec 14(5))
Tribunal: To apportion compensation among persons entitled (Sec 14(6))
Tribunal: To exercise powers of a civil court for certain matters (Sec 14(8))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever wilfully obstructs any person in doing any of the acts authorised by sub-section (3) of section 4 or wilfully fills up, destroys, damages or displaces any mark made under section 4, or wilfully obstructs the lawful exercise of any other power conferred by or under this Act, or fails to comply with any order made or direction given under this Act, shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

related_acts: Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1948 (53 of 1948)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the competent authority and constitutes the Tribunal.

applies_to: Whole of India, except the State of Jammu and Kashmir
Land containing or likely to contain coal deposits
Persons interested in such land or rights over it
exemptions: Portion of any land in which coal mining operations are actually being carried on
Premises on which any process ancillary to the getting, dressing or preparation for sale of coal is being carried on
special_provisions: No declaration of acquisition for land/rights belonging to a State Government (if not leased out) without previous consultation with the State Government (Section 9 proviso).

Notifications issued under section 4 or 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, before the commencement of this Act, relating to coal prospecting/development, are to be treated as notifications under this Act (Section 28).
Objections preferred under section 5A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, are deemed objections under section 8 of this Act (Section 28(3)).

Where no objection was preferred under section 5A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, it is deemed that a notification under section 7 of this Act was issued and no objection was preferred under section 8 (Section 28(3A)).
Vide notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019, this Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the actions of the competent authority (e.g., taking possession of land), the determination of compensation by a Tribunal, and the imposition of penalties for non-compliance or obstruction. Appeals against orders and awards are provided. Notices and orders are served as prescribed.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court (for appeals against Tribunal awards); civil courts have no jurisdiction except as expressly provided in the Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE RAILWAY PROTECTION FORCE ACT, 1957

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed Force of the Union for the better protection and security of railway property, passenger area and passengers and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the constitution and regulation of an armed Force of the Union. Its main purpose is the better protection and security of railway property, passenger areas, and passengers, along with related matters.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Force', 'Director-General', 'railway property', 'passenger', and 'passenger area'.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Force.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution and maintenance of the Railway Protection Force as an armed Force of the Union.

key_sections.title: Appointment and powers of superior officers.
key_sections.description: Outlines the appointment process for superior officers, including the Director-General, and their powers and authority.

key_sections.title: Dismissal, removal, etc., of members of the force.
key_sections.description: Details the disciplinary actions, including dismissal, suspension, reduction in rank, and other punishments, that can be taken against enrolled members of the Force.

key_sections.title: Officers and members of the Force to be deemed to be railway servants.
key_sections.description: States that the Director-General and every member of the Force are considered railway servants under the Indian Railways Act, 1890.

key_sections.title: Duties of members of the Force.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the duties of superior officers and members of the Force, including protecting railway property, passenger areas, and passengers.

key_sections.title: Power to arrest without warrant.
key_sections.description: Grants members of the Force the power to arrest individuals without a warrant under specified circumstances related to their duties and railway security.

key_sections.title: Power to search without warrant.
key_sections.description: Authorizes members of the Force (not below the rank of Senior Rakshak) to conduct searches without a warrant under certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Procedure to be followed after arrest.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the procedure for handling arrested persons, requiring them to be handed over to a police officer or taken to the nearest police station.

key_sections.title: Restrictions respecting right to Form association, etc.
key_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on members of the Force regarding forming associations, communicating with the press, or participating in political activities.

key_sections.title: Surrender of certificate, arms, etc., by persons ceasing to be members of the Force.
key_sections.description: Requires individuals ceasing to be members of the Force to surrender their certificates, arms, and other articles, and prescribes penalties for non-compliance.

key_sections.title: Penalties for neglect of duty, etc.
key_sections.description: Defines offences related to neglect of duty, wilful breach of orders, unauthorized absence, and cowardice by enrolled members, and prescribes penalties including imprisonment.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering various aspects of the Force's administration and service conditions.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint Director-General and other superior officers (S.4), make rules (S.21), superintendence of the Force (S.8), invest officers with powers of Magistrate (S.17(3)).
Superior officers: Exercise powers and authority over members (S.4(2)), dismiss, suspend, reduce rank, award punishments (S.9), receive surrendered articles (S.16A).
Members of the Force: Arrest without warrant (S.12), search without warrant (S.13), deemed railway servants (S.10).
Inspector-General, Additional Inspector-General, Deputy Inspector-General: Appoint enrolled members (S.6), command, supervise, administer Force (S.8).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 16A(2) prescribes imprisonment up to one month or fine up to two hundred rupees or both for wilful neglect or refusal to surrender certificate, arms, etc., upon ceasing to be a member of the Force. Section 17(1) prescribes imprisonment up to one year for enrolled members guilty of violation of duty, wilful breach or neglect of rules/orders, unauthorized withdrawal from duties, failure to report for duty after leave, unauthorized employment, or cowardice.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (Director-General, superior officers); Inspector-General, Additional Inspector-General, or Deputy Inspector-General (enrolled members of the Force).

applies_to: Members of the Railway Protection Force
Persons committing offences related to railway property, passenger area and passengers
exemptions: Members of the Force are exempt from the application of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, and the Factories Act, 1948.
special_provisions: Extended to Goa, Daman and Diu with modifications, by Reg. 12 of 1962.
Comes into force in Pondicherry on 01/10/1963.
Extended to and brought into force in Dadra and Nagar Haveli (w.e.f. 01/07/1965) by Reg. 6 of 1963.
Provisions for the existing Force and their deemed appointments to new offices (S.22).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the powers conferred upon members of the Force (arrest, search), disciplinary actions by superior officers, and prescribed penalties for offences. The Central Government makes rules for its administration.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Ordinary criminal courts; Assistant Inspector-General, Senior Commandant or Commandant invested with powers of a Magistrate of any class for certain offences.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the form of certificate issued to a member of the Railway Protection Force, vesting them with the powers, functions, and privileges of a member of the Force.

act_identification.act_title: THE WEALTH-TAX ACT, 1957

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the levy of wealth-tax.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the levy of wealth-tax. It defines what constitutes wealth, how it is to be assessed, and the authorities responsible for its administration and collection.

key_definitions: Chief Commissioner, Director-General, Commissioner, Commissioner (Appeals), Director, Additional Director of Income-tax, Additional Commissioner of Income-tax, Joint Director, Joint Commissioner of Income-tax, Deputy Director, Deputy Commissioner, Assistant Commissioner, Assistant Director, Income-tax Officer, Inspector of Income-tax and Tax Recovery Officer

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Charge of wealth-tax .
key_sections.description: Establishes the levy of wealth-tax on net wealth of individuals, HUFs, and companies at specified rates.

key_sections.title: Net wealth to include certain assets.
key_sections.description: Details specific assets to be included in computing an individual's net wealth, such as assets transferred to spouse or minor child.

key_sections.title: Exemptions in respect of certain assets.
key_sections.description: Lists assets that are exempt from wealth-tax and are not included in the net wealth of the assessee.

key_sections.title: Value of assets, how to be determined.
key_sections.description: Outlines the method for determining the value of assets for the purposes of the Act, referring to Schedule III.

key_sections.title: Return of wealth.
key_sections.description: Mandates persons whose net wealth exceeds the non-chargeable amount to furnish a return of wealth by the due date.

key_sections.title: Assessment.
key_sections.description: Describes the process of assessment of net wealth by the Assessing Officer, including intimation, inquiry, and determination of tax payable.

key_sections.title: Wealth escaping assessment.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Assessing Officer to assess or reassess wealth that has escaped assessment under certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Penalty for failure to furnish returns, to comply with notices and concealment of assets, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for non-compliance with notices, failure to furnish returns, and concealment or inaccurate particulars of assets.

key_sections.title: Application for settlement of cases.
key_sections.description: Allows an assessee to apply to the Settlement Commission for settlement of cases by making a full and true disclosure of wealth.

key_sections.title: Appeal to the Deputy Commissioner (Appeals) from orders of Assessing Officer.
key_sections.description: Grants assessees the right to appeal against assessment orders, penalties, and other specified orders to the Deputy Commissioner (Appeals).

key_sections.title: Mode of recovery.
key_sections.description: Applies provisions of the Income-tax Act for the recovery of wealth-tax, penalties, fines, and interest.

key_sections.title: Registration of valuers.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Register of Valuers and outlines the process and qualifications for registration as a valuer.

key_sections.title: Power of search and seizure.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to wealth-tax authorities to conduct searches and seizures of books, documents, money, bullion, and other valuable articles under specified circumstances.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Specifies entities and organizations whose net wealth is exempt from wealth-tax.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Board to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including valuation methods and return forms.

powers_conferred: Board: Issue orders, instructions and directions for proper administration of the Act (Section 10).
Board: Make rules for dispensing with furnishing documents with return of wealth (Section 14A).
Board: Make rules for filing of return in electronic form (Section 14B).
Board: Approve retention of books of account or other documents beyond 180 days (Section 37A(6)).
Board: Make rules in relation to searches or seizure (Section 37A(12)).
Board: Hear appeals against orders/directions disqualifying representatives (Section 44(2)).
Board: Make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act (Section 46).
Assessing Officer: Assess net wealth and determine sum payable (Section 16).
Assessing Officer: Issue notices for wealth escaping assessment (Section 17).
Assessing Officer: Amend orders of assessment or refund or any other order (Section 35).
Assessing Officer: Serve notice of demand (Section 30).
Assessing Officer: Extend time for payment or allow payment by instalments (Section 31(3)).
Assessing Officer: Treat assessee as not being in default in respect of amount in dispute in appeal (Section 31(6)).
Assessing Officer: Refund amounts due to assessee (Section 34A).
Assessing Officer: Set off refund amount against sum payable (Section 34A(5)).
Assessing Officer: Require statements or information from individuals, companies, firms, HUFs (Section 38).
Assessing Officer: Make order for seized assets (Section 37A(5A)).
Valuation Officer: Estimate value of assets (Section 16A).
Valuation Officer: Serve notice to assessee for objections (Section 16A(4)).
Valuation Officer: Pass order estimating value of asset (Section 16A(5)).
Valuation Officer: Amend any order passed by him (Section 35).
Valuation Officer: Enter land/building, inspect assets, require facilities, inspect books of account (Section 38A).
Commissioner/Chief Commissioner/Director General: Control wealth-tax authorities (Section 9).
Commissioner/Chief Commissioner/Director General: Make enquiries (Section 13A).
Commissioner/Chief Commissioner/Director General: Reduce or waive penalty in certain cases (Section 18B).
Commissioner/Chief Commissioner/Director General: Grant immunity from penalty (Section 18BA).
Commissioner/Chief Commissioner/Director General: Revise orders of subordinate authorities (Section 25).
Commissioner/Chief Commissioner/Director General: Sanction prosecution for offences (Section 35-I).
Commissioner/Chief Commissioner/Director General: Compound offences (Section 35-I).
Commissioner/Chief Commissioner/Director General: Grant immunity from prosecution (Section 35GA).
Commissioner/Chief Commissioner/Director General: Approve provisional attachment of property (Section 34C).
Commissioner/Chief Commissioner/Director General: Authorise search and seizure (Section 37A(1)).
Commissioner/Chief Commissioner/Director General: Authorise requisition of books of account (Section 37B(1)).
Commissioner/Chief Commissioner/Director General: Furnish information respecting assessees (Section 42B).
Settlement Commission: Settle cases (Chapter VA).
Settlement Commission: Order provisional attachment to protect revenue (Section 22DD).
Settlement Commission: Reopen completed proceedings (Section 22E).
Settlement Commission: Regulate its own procedure and the procedure of Benches (Section 22F(7)).
Settlement Commission: Grant immunity from prosecution (Section 22H).
Central Government: Appoint Valuation Officers (Section 12A).
Central Government: Appoint Chairman, Vice-Chairman and other members of Settlement Commission (Section 22B).
Central Government: Enter into agreements for avoidance or relief of double taxation (Section 44A).
Central Government: Make exemption, reduction in rate or other modification in Union territories (Section 46A).
Central Government: Remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act (Section 47).
Central Government: Pay interest on refunds (Section 34A(3), (3A), (4)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties are prescribed for failure to furnish returns, comply with notices, and concealment of assets (Section 18), ranging from Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 25,000 for failure to comply with notices, and 1 to 5 times the tax sought to be evaded for concealment. Penalties for failure to answer questions, sign statements, furnish information, or allow inspection (Section 18A) range from Rs. 500 to Rs. 10,000 for each default, and Rs. 100 to Rs. 200 per day for failure to furnish statements/information. Wilful attempt to evade tax (Section 35A) carries rigorous imprisonment from 3 months to 7 years and fine, depending on the amount evaded. Failure to furnish returns (Section 35B) carries similar imprisonment and fine. Failure to produce accounts (Section 35C) is punishable with rigorous imprisonment up to 1 year or fine (Rs. 4-10 per day) or both. False statements in verification (Section 35D, 35E) also carry imprisonment and fine. Failure to furnish particulars under Section 34ACC (Section 35EE) and contravention of orders under Section 37A (Section 35EEE) are punishable with rigorous imprisonment up to 2 years and fine. Abetment of false returns (Section 35F) carries imprisonment and fine. Second and subsequent offences (Section 35G) carry rigorous imprisonment from 6 months to 7 years and fine.

The Settlement Commission provides a mechanism for settlement of cases (Chapter VA).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court (for references and appeals, Sections 27, 27A), Supreme Court (for appeals, Section 29), and no court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class for trying offences under the Act (Section 35L).

act_identification.act_title: THE INTER-STATE CORPORATIONS ACT, 1957

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the reorganisation of certain corporations functioning in two or more States by virtue of section 109 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides a legal framework for the reorganisation or dissolution of certain inter-State corporations. It enables State Governments to propose schemes and empowers the Central Government to approve and implement these schemes, including the transfer of assets, liabilities, and employees.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Inter-State Corporations Act, 1957'.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines 'inter-State corporation' as a body corporate constituted under Acts specified in the Schedule and functioning in two or more States by virtue of section 109 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, or other reorganisation enactments.

key_sections.title: Power of State Governments to frame schemes.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to frame schemes for the reconstitution, reorganisation, or dissolution of inter-State corporations, including proposals for asset, liability, and employee transfers, and forward them to the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Reorganisation of certain inter-State corporations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to approve, with or without modifications, schemes forwarded by State Governments and to make orders to give effect to such schemes, covering dissolution, reconstitution, transfer of assets/liabilities, and employee matters.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to add to the Schedule.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to add Acts to the Schedule by notification, thereby expanding the scope of 'inter-State corporation' under this Act.

powers_conferred: Power of State Governments to frame schemes for reconstitution, reorganisation or dissolution of inter-State corporations (Section 3)
Power of Central Government to approve schemes and make orders for reorganisation of inter-State corporations (Section 4)
Power of Central Government to add Acts to the Schedule (Section 5)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: State Governments frame schemes, which are then approved and given effect by the Central Government through orders published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.

JUDGE ADVOCATE GENERAL OF THE NAVY AND OFFICERS OF HIS DEPARTMENT
DISPOSAL OF THE PRIVATE PROPERTY OF PERSONS DECEASED, MISSING, ETC.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Persons subject to naval law.
key_sections.description: Defines the categories of persons who are subject to naval law, including members of the Indian Navy, Reserve Forces, and certain other individuals.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'active service', 'civil offence', 'Court-martial', 'Indian Navy', and 'sailor'.

key_sections.title: Fundamental rights to apply to persons subject to naval law with modifications.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that fundamental rights under the Constitution apply to persons subject to naval law with certain restrictions or abrogations as provided by the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to raise and maintain naval forces.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to establish and maintain regular, reserve, and auxiliary naval forces.

key_sections.title: Restrictions respecting right to form associations, freedom of speech, etc.
key_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on persons subject to naval law regarding forming associations, freedom of speech, and communication with the press.

key_sections.title: Misconduct by officers or persons in command.
key_sections.description: Defines various forms of misconduct by officers in command, such as failing to engage the enemy or surrendering, and prescribes punishments.

key_sections.title: Mutiny defined.
key_sections.description: Provides a comprehensive definition of mutiny within the context of naval, army, and air forces.

key_sections.title: Desertion.
key_sections.description: Defines desertion and specifies the severe punishments, including forfeiture of pay and benefits, for those found guilty.

key_sections.title: Civil offences.
key_sections.description: States that persons subject to naval law who commit civil offences will be punished under this Act, with specific provisions for capital offences.

key_sections.title: Punishments.
key_sections.description: Lists the various types of punishments that can be inflicted under the Act, ranging from death to minor disciplinary actions.

key_sections.title: Power of court-martial and commanding officers to try offences.
key_sections.description: Outlines the authority of courts-martial and commanding officers to try and punish offences under the Act, including limitations on commanding officers' powers.

key_sections.title: Constitution of courts-martial.
key_sections.description: Details the process for constituting and convening courts-martial, including eligibility criteria for members and the president.

key_sections.title: Powers of Central Government and the Chief of the Naval Staff in respect of findings and sentences.
key_sections.description: Confers powers upon the Central Government and the Chief of the Naval Staff to set aside, alter, reduce, commute, pardon, or remit sentences.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make regulations for the governance, discipline, recruitment, and conditions of service of the naval forces.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To raise and maintain naval forces (Sec 5), appoint Chief of Naval Staff (Sec 3), grant commissions (Sec 10), dismiss/discharge/retire officers/sailors (Sec 15), make regulations (Sec 184, 159), confirm death sentences (Sec 82), change place of confinement (Sec 153), discharge/remove prisoners (Sec 154), remove insane prisoners (Sec 156), set apart naval prisons/detention quarters (Sec 157), impose forfeiture of time/seniority (Sec 94), pardon/remit/suspend sentences (Sec 163, 164).

Chief of the Naval Staff: To give directions for execution of death sentences (Sec 149), impose forfeiture of time/seniority (Sec 94), appoint provost-marshals (Sec 89), order courts-martial (Sec 97), consider judicial review reports (Sec 161), pardon/remit/suspend sentences (Sec 163, 164).

Commanding Officers: To summarily try and punish non-officers (Sec 93), delegate punishment powers (Sec 93), make deductions from pay (Sec 28, 29), secure/dispose of property of deceased sailors (Sec 171).

Courts-martial: To try and punish offences (Sec 93), award punishments (Sec 81), order compensation from fine (Sec 138), impose summary punishment for contempt (Sec 139, 140), exercise powers of a criminal court (Sec 141, 142).
Provost-marshals: To arrest and detain for trial (Sec 89).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines a wide range of offences, including misconduct by officers (Sec 34), misconduct by others (Sec 35), delaying or discouraging action (Sec 36), disobedience in action (Sec 37), spying (Sec 38), correspondence with the enemy (Sec 39), improper communication with the enemy (Sec 40), deserting post and neglect of duty (Sec 41), mutiny (Sec 42, 43), seducing naval personnel (Sec 44), striking superior officers (Sec 45), ill-treating subordinates (Sec 46), disobedience and insubordination (Sec 47), quarrelling, fighting and disorderly behavior (Sec 48), desertion (Sec 49), inducing desertion (Sec 50), absence without leave (Sec 51), drunkenness (Sec 52), uncleanness or indecent acts (Sec 53), cruelty and conduct unbecoming an officer (Sec 54), losing ship or aircraft (Sec 55), dangerous unauthorised flying (Sec 55A), inaccurate certificate (Sec 55B), low flying and annoyance by flying (Sec 55C), disobedience of lawful command of captain of an aircraft (Sec 55D), offences by officers in charge of convoy (Sec 56), taking unauthorised goods on board ship (Sec 57), offences in respect of property (Sec 58), arson (Sec 59), falsifying official documents and false declarations (Sec 60), malingering (Sec 61), endeavouring to stir up disturbance (Sec 62), offences in respect of papers relating to prize (Sec 63), offences in respect of prize (Sec 64), offences in respect of persons on board a prize ship (Sec 65), unlawful taking or ransoming a prize (Sec 66), breaking bulk on board a prize ship (Sec 67), violation of the Act, regulations and orders (Sec 68), offences in relation to Court-martial (Sec 69), fraudulent entry (Sec 70), escape from custody (Sec 71), failure to assist in detention of offenders (Sec 72), failure to attend by members of reserve forces (Sec 73), offences against good order and naval discipline (Sec 74), attempts (Sec 75), abetment of offences (Sec 76), and civil offences (Sec 77). Penalties include death, imprisonment (life or lesser term), dismissal with disgrace from naval service, detention, dismissal from naval service, forfeiture of seniority/time for promotion, reduction in rank, fine, mulcts of pay and allowances, severe reprimand or reprimand, and forfeiture of pay, benefits, medals, and decorations.

authorities_established: Judge Advocate General of the Navy
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Judge Advocate General of the Navy and Deputy Judge Advocate General of the Navy. The President appoints the Chief of the Naval Staff and grants commissions to officers. The Chief of the Naval Staff appoints provost-marshals and empowers officers to order courts-martial. The convening officer appoints the trial judge advocate and the president of a court-martial.

applies_to: Every person belonging to the Indian Navy during service liability (Sec 2(1)(a))
Every person belonging to the Indian Naval Reserve Forces under specified conditions (Sec 2(1)(b))
Members of the regular Army and the Air Force when embarked on Indian Navy ships or aircraft (Sec 2(1)(c))
Every person entering into an engagement with the Central Government to serve (Sec 2(1)(d), 6)
Every person belonging to any auxiliary forces raised under this Act (Sec 2(1)(e))
Every person made subject to naval law by any other Act or regulations during active service (Sec 2(1)(f))
Every person ordered to be received, or being a passenger, on board any ship or aircraft of the Indian Navy (Sec 2(2)(a))
Every person sentenced under this Act to imprisonment or detention, during the term of his sentence (Sec 2(2)(b))
exemptions: Persons not citizens of India, except with Central Government consent or subjects of Nepal (Sec 9(1))
Women, except in such department, branch or other body and subject to such conditions as specified by the Central Government (Sec 9(2))
Cadets whilst under training in a joint service institution (from definition of 'subordinate officer' Sec 3(23))
Prosecutor, commanding officer of the accused's ship, and the officer investigating the offence are not qualified to sit on a court-martial for that accused (Sec 97(8), (9))
special_provisions: The Act was extended to Goa, Daman and Diu by Regulation 11 of 1963.
The Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.
Officers retired or permitted to resign are liable to recall to naval service in an emergency (Sec 14(4)).
Officers of the Royal Navy attached to or serving with the Indian Navy may exercise powers and be eligible for commissions/appointments as if they were officers of the Indian Navy (Sec 188).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through naval tribunals, including courts-martial and disciplinary courts, which try and punish offences. Commanding officers also have powers for summary trials and punishments. Arrests can be made with or without warrants by authorized officers and provost-marshals. The Act provides for investigation after arrest and detailed procedures for trials. Sentences are executed under specific provisions, and there is a system for judicial review by the Judge Advocate General of the Navy. The Central Government and Chief of the Naval Staff have powers to modify findings and sentences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts-martial, Disciplinary Courts, Criminal Courts (for civil offences and certain enforcement actions), Magistrates (for summoning witnesses, executing fines, and property disposal).

act_identification.act_title: THE DELHI DEVELOPMENT ACT, 1957

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of the National Capital Territory of Delhi

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the development of Delhi according to plan and for matters ancillary thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the planned development of Delhi. It establishes the Delhi Development Authority to prepare master and zonal development plans, acquire and dispose of land, and carry out various development operations, including providing essential services and amenities.

chapter_titles: THE DELHI DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY AND ITS OBJECTS
MASTER PLAN AND ZONAL DEVELOPMENT PLANS
MODIFICATIONS TO THE MASTER PLAN AND THE ZONAL DEVELOPMENT PLAN

key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, geographical extent, and commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: The Delhi Development Authority.
key_sections.description: Establishes and outlines the constitution of the Delhi Development Authority.

key_sections.title: Objects of the Authority.
key_sections.description: Defines the primary objectives and powers of the Delhi Development Authority.

key_sections.title: Civic survey of, and master plan for, Delhi.

key_sections.title: Zonal development plans.

key_sections.title: Declaration of development areas and development of land in those and other areas.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to declare development areas and regulates land development within and outside these areas.

key_sections.title: Compulsory acquisition of land.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for compulsory acquisition of land for development purposes.

key_sections.title: Disposal of land by the Authority or the local authority concerned.
key_sections.description: Governs the disposal of acquired land by the Authority or local authorities.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for various offences under the Act, including unauthorised development.

key_sections.title: Order of demolition of building.
key_sections.description: Grants power to order demolition of buildings constructed in contravention of plans or without permission.

key_sections.title: Power to stop development.
key_sections.description: Provides authority to issue orders to discontinue unauthorised development.

key_sections.title: Power to seal unauthorised development.
key_sections.description: Allows for the sealing of unauthorised development to enforce the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Appellate Tribunal for deciding appeals under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of Authority to levy betterment charges.
key_sections.description: Enables the Authority to levy charges on properties that benefit from development.

key_sections.title: Control by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Central Government's control and power to issue directions to the Authority.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Authority the power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.

key_sections.title: Repeal, etc., and savings.
key_sections.description: Specifies acts repealed by this Act and includes savings clauses for continuity.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Undertaking development in contravention of plans or without permission is punishable with rigorous imprisonment up to three years (for setting up a colony without a layout plan) or simple imprisonment up to six months or fine up to five thousand rupees or both (for other cases). Using land or building in contravention of plans is punishable with a fine up to five thousand rupees, with an additional fine of two hundred and fifty rupees per day for continuing offences. Obstructing authorised entry is punishable with imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to one thousand rupees or both. Failure to comply with an order to stop development is punishable with a fine up to two hundred rupees for every day of non-compliance.

the Delhi (Control of Building Operations) Act, 1955 (53 of 1955)
related_acts: Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act, 1956 (6 of 1956)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Vice-Chairman, Finance and Accounts Member, Engineer Member, and three other persons to the Delhi Development Authority. It also appoints the Secretary and Chief Accounts Officer of the Authority, and nominates members to the Advisory Council and arbitrators for betterment charges.

Any person or body (including a department of Government) undertaking development of land
Owners of property in development areas or other areas benefited by development (for betterment charges)
exemptions: Works for maintenance, improvement, or alteration of building affecting only interior or not materially affecting external appearance
Works by local authority or government department for inspecting, repairing, renewing drains, sewers, mains, pipes, cables
Erection of non-dwelling agricultural buildings
Erection of places of worship, tombs, cenotaphs, or walls enclosing such on land already occupied for such purpose
Excavations (including wells) in ordinary agricultural operations
Construction of unmetalled roads for agricultural access

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government, after consultation with the Authority
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through requirements for development permission, penalties for contravention, orders for demolition and stopping unauthorised development, sealing of unauthorised development, and appeals to the Appellate Tribunal and Lieutenant Governor. Fines and moneys due are recoverable as arrears of land revenue. The Authority has default powers to carry out development and provide amenities. The Central Government exercises control and issues directions.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate shall try an offence punishable under this Act. Appeals are heard by the Appellate Tribunal and the Lieutenant Governor.

act_identification.act_title: THE DELHI MUNICIPAL CORPORATION ACT, 1957

legislative_details.geographical_extent: The entire area of the Union territory of Delhi except New Delhi and Delhi Cantonment, as defined in the Act.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the Municipal Government of Delhi.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the laws governing the municipal administration of Delhi. Its primary objective is to establish a Municipal Corporation for Delhi, define its constitution, powers, and functions, and regulate various aspects of urban governance including taxation, public health, building regulations, and public safety.

key_sections.title: Taxes to be imposed by the Corporation under this Act.

key_sections.title: Self assessment and submission of return.

key_sections.title: Appeal against assessment, etc.

key_sections.title: Order of demolition and stoppage of buildings and works in certain cases and appeal.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines various offences including corrupt practices in elections, breaches of voting secrecy, disorderly conduct at polling stations, removal of ballot papers, booth capturing, and sale of liquor on polling day. Penalties range from fines (e.g., up to Rs. 250 for canvassing, Rs. 300 per day for sitting while disqualified, Rs. 100 for general contraventions) to imprisonment (e.g., up to 3 months for secrecy breaches, up to 6 months for electoral officers influencing votes, 1-3 years for booth capturing, up to 2 years for electoral offences by officers). Specific penalties are also prescribed for wilful default in property tax payment, acquiring interest in Corporation contracts, terminal tax evasion, and contraventions listed in the Twelfth Schedule.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement includes recovery of taxes through distress and sale of property, seizure of vehicles and animals, recovery from occupiers, and institution of suits. Building regulations are enforced through orders for demolition, stoppage, and sealing of unauthorized constructions. The Act also provides for prosecutions for various offences, composition of offences, and arrest of offenders by police. The Central Government can issue directions to the Corporation and even dissolve it for non-compliance.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The court of the district judge of Delhi, the Municipal Taxation Tribunal, the Appellate Tribunal, and Municipal Magistrates have jurisdiction under this Act for election disputes, tax appeals, building regulation appeals, and trial of offences, respectively.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the [1][development and regulation of mines and minerals] under the control of the Union.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to provide for the development and regulation of mines and minerals under the control of the Union. It declares the expediency of Union control over the regulation of mines and the development of minerals in the public interest.

key_sections.title: Power of State Governments to make rules in respect of minor minerals.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to make rules for regulating the grant of concessions for minor minerals.

key_sections.title: Penalties.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of Section 4(1) or 4(1A) is punishable with imprisonment up to five years and a fine up to five lakh rupees per hectare. Contravention of rules made under the Act is punishable with imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to five lakh rupees, or both, with additional fines for continuing contraventions. Trespassers can be evicted, and minerals, tools, equipment, or vehicles used in illegal mining are liable to be seized and confiscated. The State Government can recover the value of illegally mined minerals and associated rent, royalty, or tax.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act provides for penalties including imprisonment and fines for contraventions, eviction of trespassers, seizure and confiscation of illegally mined minerals and equipment. It also allows for the recovery of the value of illegally mined minerals, rent, royalty, or tax. Enforcement is facilitated through authorized persons making complaints, powers of search and seizure, and powers of entry and inspection. State Governments are empowered to make rules to prevent illegal mining, transportation, and storage.

act_identification.act_title: THE PROBATION OF OFFENDERS ACT, 1958
act_identification.date_of_commencement: in a State on such date as the State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different parts of the State

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the release of offenders on probation or after due admonition and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the release of certain offenders on probation of good conduct or after due admonition. It aims to facilitate the rehabilitation of offenders by avoiding immediate imprisonment in suitable cases, especially for younger individuals, and provides for their supervision by probation officers.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, its geographical application to the whole of India, and that its commencement date will be appointed by State Governments.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, such as 'Code', 'probation officer', and 'prescribed'.

key_sections.title: Power of court to release certain offenders after admonition.
key_sections.description: Grants courts the power to release certain offenders, found guilty of minor offences and with no previous convictions, after due admonition instead of sentencing them.

key_sections.title: Power of court to release certain offenders on probation of good conduct.
key_sections.description: Empowers courts to release offenders, not punishable with death or life imprisonment, on probation of good conduct, requiring them to enter into a bond and potentially be under supervision.

key_sections.title: Power of court to require released offenders to pay compensation and costs.
key_sections.description: Allows courts to order offenders released under section 3 or 4 to pay compensation for loss or injury and cover the costs of proceedings.

key_sections.title: Restrictions on imprisonment of offenders under twenty-one years of age.
key_sections.description: Restricts courts from sentencing offenders under twenty-one years of age to imprisonment unless specific conditions are met and reasons are recorded, encouraging release under section 3 or 4.

key_sections.title: Courts competent to make order under the Act, appeal and revision and powers of courts in appeal and revision.
key_sections.description: Specifies which courts can make orders under the Act, and outlines the provisions for appeal and revision of such orders.

key_sections.title: Removal of disqualification attaching to conviction.
key_sections.description: States that a person dealt with under section 3 or 4 shall not suffer disqualification attached to a conviction, with a proviso for subsequent sentencing.

key_sections.title: Probation officers.
key_sections.description: Defines who can be a probation officer, including those appointed by the State Government or recognised societies, or other fit persons appointed by the court.

key_sections.title: Duties of probation officers.
key_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities of probation officers, such as inquiring into circumstances of accused persons, supervising probationers, and assisting offenders.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government, with Central Government approval, the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering aspects like appointment and duties of probation officers.

powers_conferred: Power of court to release certain offenders after admonition (Section 3)
Power of court to release certain offenders on probation of good conduct (Section 4)
Power of court to require released offenders to pay compensation and costs (Section 5)
Power of court to vary conditions of probation (Section 8)
Power of court to sentence offender for original offence if bond conditions are violated (Section 8, Section 9)

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act does not define new offences but applies to existing offences under the Indian Penal Code (e.g., sections 379, 380, 381, 404, 420) or any other law punishable with imprisonment for not more than two years, or with fine, or with both. Penalties prescribed include a fine not exceeding fifty rupees for failure to observe bond conditions (Section 9(3)(b)), or sentencing for the original offence if bond conditions are violated or a penalty is not paid.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government appoints probation officers or recognises societies providing them. In exceptional cases, the court may appoint a person to act as a probation officer. A court or district magistrate may also appoint a probation officer in place of a person named in a supervision order.

applies_to: Persons found guilty of offences punishable under specific sections of the Indian Penal Code (379, 380, 381, 404, 420) or other laws with imprisonment not exceeding two years, or fine, or both, with no previous conviction (Section 3)
Persons found guilty of offences not punishable with death or imprisonment for life (Section 4)
Offenders under twenty-one years of age (Section 6)
exemptions: Offences punishable with death or imprisonment for life (Section 4)
special_provisions: Special restrictions on imprisonment for offenders under twenty-one years of age (Section 6)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The State Government, with the approval of the Central Government
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through court orders for release on admonition or probation, requiring offenders to enter into bonds, and placing them under the supervision of probation officers. Courts can also order compensation and costs. Procedures are outlined for dealing with offenders who fail to observe bond conditions, including sentencing for the original offence or imposing a penalty.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any court empowered to try and sentence the offender to imprisonment, the High Court, or any other court when the case comes before it on appeal or in revision.

act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to preserve ancient and historical monuments and archaeological sites and remains of national importance. It also regulates archaeological excavations and provides for the protection of sculptures, carvings, and similar objects.
