key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties include imprisonment up to two years or fine up to one lakh rupees, or both, for destroying, removing, injuring, altering, defacing, imperiling, or misusing a protected monument, contravening orders, removing sculptures, or contravening restrictions in protected areas (Section 30(1)). Moving antiquities in contravention of notification carries similar penalties (Section 30(2)). Construction in prohibited or regulated areas without permission is punishable with imprisonment not exceeding two years or fine up to one lakh rupees, or both (Sections 30A, 30B). Government officers conniving at such constructions face imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both (Section 30C). Breach of rules may also lead to imprisonment or fines (Section 38(3)).

repealed_acts: The Ancient and Historical Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (Declaration of National Importance) Act, 1951 (71 of 1951)
section 126 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (37 of 1956)
The Ancient Monuments Preservation Act, 1904 (7 of 1904)
related_acts: Ancient and Historical Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (Declaration of National Importance) Act, 1951 (71 of 1951)
Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (Amendment and Validation) Bill, 2010
Antiquities and Art Treasures Act, 1972 (52 of 1972)
Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (Amendment and Validation) Act, 2010 (10 of 2010)
Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Rules, 1959

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Chairperson of National Monuments Authority appointed by the President. Members of National Monuments Authority appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of the Selection Committee.

applies_to: the whole of India
Owners and occupiers of protected monuments/areas
Persons carrying out excavations
State Governments (for archaeological excavations)
exemptions: Use of protected monument for customary religious observances (Section 5(6))
Construction of drains, public latrines, water supply, electricity supply (not considered 'construction' for certain purposes) (Section 2(dc))
Cultivation not involving digging more than one foot of soil in protected areas (Section 19(1) proviso)
Compulsory acquisition power does not extend to images/symbols used for bona fide religious observances (Section 26(3))
special_provisions: Extended to Goa, Daman and Diu with modifications by Reg. 12 of 1962, S. 3 and Sch. (w.e.f. 22-11-1962). Extended to Dadra and Nagar Haveli by Reg. 6 of 1963, s. 2 and Sch. I (w.e.f. 11-7-1965) and Pondicherry by Reg. 7 of 1963, s. 3 and Sch. I (w.e.f. 1-10-1963).
Made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.
Special provisions for permissions granted between 16th June 1992 and the assent of the 2010 Amendment Bill (Section 20A(3) proviso, 20B proviso).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through agreements for monument maintenance, orders by the Director-General, acquisition of monuments/areas, and prescribed penalties for contraventions. Amounts due to the Government can be recovered as land revenue arrears. The Director-General conducts surveys and identifies unauthorised constructions. The Competent Authority grants/refuses permissions, and the National Monuments Authority oversees these processes.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a presidency magistrate or a magistrate of the first class

act_identification.act_title: An Act to enable certain special powers to be conferred upon members of the armed forces in disturbed areas in the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura

act_overview.preamble: An Act to enable certain special powers to be conferred upon members of the armed forces in disturbed areas in the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to enable the Central Government, State Governors, or Union Territory Administrators to declare areas as 'disturbed areas'. It then confers special powers upon members of the armed forces operating in these areas to maintain public order and aid civil power, including powers of arrest, search, and use of force.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its geographical application to certain states.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'armed forces' and 'disturbed area'.

key_sections.title: Power to declare areas to be disturbed areas.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Governor of a State, Administrator of a Union territory, or the Central Government to declare an area as 'disturbed' if public order requires the aid of armed forces.

key_sections.title: Special powers of the armed forces.
key_sections.description: Grants specific powers to armed forces personnel in disturbed areas, including the power to use force (even to cause death), destroy structures, arrest without warrant, and enter and search premises.

key_sections.title: Arrested persons to be made over to the police.
key_sections.description: Mandates that any person arrested under the Act must be handed over to the nearest police station with a report of the circumstances of the arrest.

key_sections.title: Protection to persons acting under Act.
key_sections.description: Provides protection from prosecution, suit, or other legal proceedings for actions taken under the Act, requiring prior sanction from the Central Government.

powers_conferred: Power to declare areas to be disturbed areas (Governor of State, Administrator of Union territory, Central Government)

Power to fire upon or otherwise use force, even to the causing of death, against persons acting in contravention of law (commissioned officer, warrant officer, non-commissioned officer or equivalent rank in armed forces)

Power to destroy arms dumps, prepared or fortified positions, shelters, training camps, or hide-outs (commissioned officer, warrant officer, non-commissioned officer or equivalent rank in armed forces)

Power to arrest, without warrant, any person who has committed or is about to commit a cognizable offence (commissioned officer, warrant officer, non-commissioned officer or equivalent rank in armed forces)

Power to enter and search without warrant any premises for arrest, recovery of wrongfully restrained persons, stolen property, or unlawful arms/ammunition (commissioned officer, warrant officer, non-commissioned officer or equivalent rank in armed forces)

applies_to: members of the armed forces
disturbed areas in the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura
any person who has committed a cognizable offence or against whom a reasonable suspicion exists that he has committed or is about to commit a cognizable offence

any person who is acting in contravention of any law or order for the time being in force in the disturbed area prohibiting the assembly of five or more persons or the carrying of weapons or of things capable of being used as weapons or of fire-arms, ammunition or explosive substances

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced by members of the armed forces who are granted special powers, including the authority to use force, arrest without warrant, and conduct searches in disturbed areas. Persons arrested under the Act must be handed over to the nearest police station. Protection is provided to those acting under the Act, requiring Central Government sanction for prosecution.

act_identification.act_title: THE SUGAR EXPORT PROMOTION ACT, 1958

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the export of sugar in the public interest and for the levy and collection in certain circumstances of an additional duty of excise on sugar produced in India.
act_overview.purpose: The Act provides for the export of sugar in the public interest. It establishes a mechanism for fixing export quotas for sugar factories and levies an additional excise duty on sugar if an owner fails to meet their export quota.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as The Sugar Export Promotion Act, 1958, and states its applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'export', 'export agency', 'factory', and 'owner'.

key_sections.title: Export agency.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to specify an export agency for the purposes of the Act, which can be a company or other body corporate.

key_sections.title: Fixation of quantity of sugar for purposes of export.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to fix the quantity of sugar for export, considering factors like available stock, domestic consumption, and foreign exchange earnings.

key_sections.title: Export quotas for factories.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to apportion the fixed export quantity among factory owners based on their production, establishing their export quotas.

key_sections.title: Liability of owner to deliver export quota to export agency.
key_sections.description: Obligates owners to deliver their export quota of sugar to the export agency upon demand, losing all rights to the sugar except payment.

key_sections.title: Levy of additional excise duty on sugar.
key_sections.description: Imposes an additional excise duty on sugar dispatched for consumption in India if an owner fails to deliver their full export quota, and specifies penalties for non-payment.

key_sections.title: Sale by export agency of sugar delivered.
key_sections.description: Requires the export agency to take measures to export delivered sugar, with a proviso allowing it to sell sugar in India or purchase sugar for export under certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Payments to owners in respect of sugar delivered.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for the export agency to make payments to owners for delivered sugar, based on total sale proceeds minus expenses, and allows for on-account payments.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to give directions.
key_sections.description: States that the export agency must comply with general or special directions issued by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including provisions for returns, accounts, inspections, and penalties for breach of rules.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Notes that this section, and thus the Act, was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1960.

powers_conferred: Central Government to specify an export agency (Section 3)
Central Government to fix the quantity of sugar for export (Section 4)
Central Government to apportion export quotas among owners (Section 5)
Export agency to demand delivery of sugar from owners (Section 6)
Export agency to sell delivered sugar, including in India under certain conditions (Section 8)
Export agency to make payments to owners for delivered sugar (Section 9)
Central Government to give general or special directions to the export agency (Section 10)
Central Government to delegate its powers under the Act (Section 11)
Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 13)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Failure by an owner to pay the additional excise duty within the specified period may result in a penalty of up to ten percent of the outstanding duty for every thirty days of default. Breach of rules made under the Act may be punishable with a fine up to five thousand rupees.

related_acts: Central Excises and Salt Act, 1944 (1 of 1944)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government may specify an export agency (company or body corporate)

applies_to: owners of factories producing sugar by the vacuum pan process

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government fixes export quantities and quotas, and specifies an export agency. The export agency demands sugar delivery and manages sales. An additional excise duty is levied for shortfalls in export quota delivery, with penalties for non-payment. The Central Government issues directions and makes rules for implementation.

act_identification.act_title: THE WORKING JOURNALISTS (FIXATION OF RATES OF WAGES) ACT, 1958
act_identification.act_short_title: The Working Journalists (Fixation of Rates of Wages) Act, 1958

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the fixation of rates of wages in respect of working journalists and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the fixation of rates of wages for working journalists. It establishes a Committee to make recommendations for wage fixation and outlines the process for the Central Government to enforce these recommendations, ensuring fair remuneration for journalists.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Committee.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of a Committee by the Central Government to fix wage rates for working journalists.

key_sections.title: Functions of Committee.
key_sections.description: Outlines the functions of the Committee, including calling for representations and making recommendations for wage fixation.

key_sections.title: Powers of Committee.
key_sections.description: Grants the Committee powers similar to an industrial tribunal for inquiry and evidence collection.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to enforce recommendations of Committee.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to enforce the recommendations of the Committee, with or without modifications.

key_sections.title: Working journalists entitled to wages at rates not less than those specified in the order.
key_sections.description: Ensures working journalists are entitled to wages at rates not less than those specified in the Central Government's order.

key_sections.title: Recovery of money due to working journalists.
key_sections.description: Provides a mechanism for working journalists to recover money due to them from employers, including referral to a Labour Court.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for employers who contravene the provisions regarding wage payment.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to constitute a Committee under section 3.
Central Government: to enforce recommendations of the Committee under section 6.
Central Government: to make rules under section 13.
Committee: to call upon newspaper establishments and working journalists for representations under section 4.
Committee: to make recommendations to the Central Government for fixation of rates of wages under section 4.
Committee: to exercise powers of an industrial tribunal under section 5.
Committee: to regulate its own procedure under section 5.
Committee: to authorise officers for examination of accounts/documents or obtaining statements under section 5.
Authorised officer: to examine accounts or documents or obtain statements under section 5.
State Government: to recover money due to working journalists under section 9.
State Government: to refer questions regarding amount due to a Labour Court under section 9.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Employers contravening Section 7 (payment of wages) are punishable with a fine which may extend to two hundred rupees. For a subsequent conviction, the fine may extend to five hundred rupees. Provisions are also made for offences committed by companies, holding responsible those in charge of the company's business, and potentially directors, managers, or secretaries in cases of consent, connivance, or gross negligence.

related_acts: Working Journalists (Conditions of Service) and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1955 (45 of 1955)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint members of the Committee, including the Chairman, and to appoint a Secretary and other staff to the Committee.

applies_to: working journalists
newspaper establishments
employers
special_provisions: Where a working journalist is entitled to more favourable benefits under any award, agreement, or contract of service than those under this Act, they shall continue to receive the more favourable benefits.
Nothing in this Act precludes a working journalist from entering into agreements for more favourable rights or privileges than those provided by this Act.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government enforces the recommendations of the Committee by making an order. Money due to working journalists can be recovered by the State Government as an arrear of land revenue, or by referral to a Labour Court. Contravention of wage payment provisions by employers is subject to penalties.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Labour Court

act_identification.act_title: THE SUPREME COURT JUDGES (SALARIES AND CONDITIONS OF SERVICE) ACT, 1958
act_identification.act_short_title: the Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Act, 1958

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate [1][salaries and certain conditions of service] of the Judges of the Supreme Court.
act_overview.purpose: This Act regulates the salaries, leave, pensions, and other conditions of service for Judges of the Supreme Court of India. It ensures their financial well-being and provides for their post-retirement benefits.

key_definitions: service as a Judge in India

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'the Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Act, 1958'.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Judge', 'Chief Justice', 'actual service', and 'service for pension'.

key_sections.title: Kinds of leave admissible to a Judge.
key_sections.description: Outlines the types of leave a Judge may be granted, including leave on full allowances, half allowances, and casual leave.

key_sections.title: Leave encashment.
key_sections.description: Entitles a Judge to claim cash equivalent of leave salary on retirement, calculated on full allowances basis, up to the maximum period prescribed under the All India Service (Leave) Rules, 1955.

key_sections.title: Salaries of the Judges.
key_sections.description: Specifies the monthly salaries payable to the Chief Justice of India and other Judges of the Supreme Court.

key_sections.title: Pension payable to Judges.
key_sections.description: Sets out the conditions under which a pension is payable to a Judge upon retirement, referring to Part I of the Schedule.

key_sections.title: Benefit of added years of service.
key_sections.description: Grants an additional period of ten years to a Judge's service for pension purposes if they qualified under sub-clause (b) of clause (3) of article 124 of the Constitution.

key_sections.title: Family pension and gratuity.
key_sections.description: Details the provisions for family pension and death-cum-retirement gratuity for Judges and their families, including calculation rates and eligibility.

key_sections.title: Additional quantum of pension or family pension.
key_sections.description: Provides for an additional quantum of pension or family pension based on the age of the retired Judge or family pensioner, with a specified scale.

key_sections.title: Facilities for rent-free houses and other conditions of service.
key_sections.description: Ensures Judges are entitled to rent-free official residences, medical treatment facilities, and other conditions of service, including an allowance if an official residence is not availed.

key_sections.title: Exemption from liability to pay Income-tax on certain perquisites received by a Judge.
key_sections.description: Exempts certain perquisites like rent-free residence, allowance in lieu thereof, conveyance facilities, sumptuary allowance, and leave travel concession from income tax for Judges.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, covering various aspects like leave, pension, and conditions of service.

powers_conferred: President: To grant or refuse leave to a Judge or to revoke or curtail the leave already granted to a Judge (Section 12).
President: To add to the service for pension of a Judge for special reasons (Section 15).
President: To grant pension to a Judge (Section 21).
Central Government: To make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act (Section 24).

related_acts: High Court Judges (Conditions of Service) Act, 1954 (28 of 1954)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: President (for granting leave and pension to Judges)

applies_to: Judges of the Supreme Court
special_provisions: Special provisions for pension in respect of Judges who are members of service (Section 14).
Special disability leave may be granted to a Judge (Section 7).
Exemption from liability to pay Income-tax on certain perquisites received by a Judge (Section 23D).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is implemented through rules made by the Central Government and powers exercised by the President regarding leave and pension.

schedules_summary.description: Contains provisions for pensions of Judges, divided into Part I (for Judges not holding other pensionable posts or who elected this part) and Part III (for Judges holding other pensionable posts and not electing Part I).

act_identification.act_title: THE INTERNATIONAL FINANCE CORPORATION (STATUS, IMMUNITIES AND PRIVILEGES) ACT, 1958
act_identification.act_short_title: International Finance Corporation (Status, Immunities and Privileges) Act, 1958

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India. The Act has now been extended by Act 26 of 1968 to the Union territory Pondicherry, comprising the former French Establishments in India, (w.e.f 1-8-1968).

act_overview.preamble: An Act to implement the international agreement for the establishment and operation of the International Finance Corporation in so far as it relates to the status, immunities and privileges of that Corporation, and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to give legal effect in India to the international agreement establishing the International Finance Corporation. It specifically outlines the status, immunities, and privileges granted to the Corporation, its officers, and employees within India, ensuring the Corporation can fulfill its functions.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, namely 'Agreement' and 'Corporation'.

key_sections.title: Conferment of status and certain immunities and privileges on the Corporation and conferment of certain immunities and privileges on its officers and employees.
key_sections.description: Grants the provisions of the Agreement, as set out in the Schedule, the force of law in India, with specific provisos regarding customs duties and taxes.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act and mandates parliamentary oversight for such rules.

key_sections.title: Financing Operations
key_sections.description: States that the Corporation may make investments of its funds in productive private enterprises in the territories of its members.

key_sections.title: Status of the Corporation
key_sections.description: Declares the Corporation to possess full juridical personality, including the capacity to contract, acquire and dispose of property, and institute legal proceedings.

key_sections.title: Position of the Corporation with regard to Judicial Process
key_sections.description: Outlines conditions under which actions may be brought against the Corporation and grants immunity from seizure, attachment, or execution of its property before final judgment.

key_sections.title: Immunity of Assets from Seizure
key_sections.description: Ensures the Corporation's property and assets are immune from search, requisition, confiscation, expropriation, or any other form of seizure by executive or legislative action.

key_sections.title: Immunities and Privileges of Officers and Employees
key_sections.description: Grants immunity from legal process for official acts, and certain immunities and facilities for non-local nationals among its officers and employees.

key_sections.title: Immunities from Taxation
key_sections.description: Provides immunity from all taxation and customs duties for the Corporation, its assets, income, operations, and certain salaries/obligations, with specific conditions.

powers_conferred: Central Government may, from time to time, by notification in the Official Gazette, amend the Schedule
Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act.

applies_to: the International Finance Corporation
its officers and employees
exemptions: immune from legal process with respect to acts performed by them in their official capacity (Officers and Employees)
immune from immigration restrictions, alien registration requirements and national service obligations (Officers and Employees, not local nationals)
immune from all taxation and from all customs duties (Corporation, its assets, property, income, operations, transactions)
immune from liability for the collection or payment of any tax or duty (Corporation)

No tax shall be levied on or in respect of salaries and emoluments paid by the Corporation to Directors, Alternates, officials or employees of the Corporation who are not local citizens, local subjects, or other local nationals.
No taxation of any kind shall be levied on any obligation or security issued by the Corporation
No taxation of any kind shall be levied on any obligation or security guaranteed by the Corporation
immune from all forms of seizure, attachment or execution before the delivery of final judgment against the Corporation (Property and assets of the Corporation)
immune from search, requisition, confiscation, expropriation or any other form of seizure by executive or legislative action (Property and assets of the Corporation)
The archives of the Corporation shall be inviolable.
special_provisions: nothing in Section 9 of Article VI of the Agreement shall be construed as— (a) entitling the Corporation to import into India goods free of any duty of customs without any restriction on their subsequent sale therein; or (b) conferring on the Corporation any exemption from duties or taxes which form part of the price of goods sold; or (c) conferring on the Corporation any exemption from duties or taxes which are in fact no more than charges for services rendered.
The Act has now been extended by Act 26 of 1968 to the Union territory Pondicherry, comprising the former French Establishments in India, (w.e.f 1-8-1968).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: the provisions of the Agreement set out in the Schedule shall have the force of law in India
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: a court of competent jurisdiction in the territories of a member in which the Corporation has an office, has appointed an agent for the purpose of accepting service or notice of process, or has issued or guaranteed securities.

schedules_summary.description: Contains provisions of the Agreement for the establishment and operation of the International Finance Corporation, which are given the force of law in India. It details financing operations, applicability of foreign exchange restrictions, and comprehensive status, immunities, and privileges for the Corporation, its assets, archives, communications, officers, and employees, including immunities from judicial process and taxation.

act_identification.act_title: THE MERCHANT SHIPPING ACT, 1958
act_identification.date_of_commencement: Parts I and II came into force w.e.f. 15th December, 1958; Part IV came into force w.e.f. 17th March, 1959; Sections 7, 405 to 414 (both inclusive), 436 (in so far as it relates to offences mentioned against S. Nos. 122 to 125), 437 to 442, 447, 448, 456 to 460 and so much of section 461 and of Part I of the Schedule as relate to the Control of Shipping Act, 1947 (26 of 1947), came into force on the 1st April, 1960; The remaining provisions came into force w.e.f. 1st January, 1961.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Applies to any vessel registered in India or required to be registered, or owned wholly by persons meeting Section 21 criteria, wherever the vessel may be. For other vessels, it applies only while within India, including its territorial waters.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to foster the development and ensure the efficient maintenance of an Indian mercantile marine in a manner best suited to serve the national interests and for that purpose to establish a National Shipping Board to provide for the registration, certification, safety and security of Indian ships and generally to amend and consolidate the law relating to merchant shipping.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to foster the development and efficient maintenance of an Indian mercantile marine. It aims to serve national interests by establishing a National Shipping Board and providing for the registration, certification, safety, and security of Indian ships, while also consolidating and amending existing merchant shipping laws.

chapter_titles: PART V REGISTRATION OF INDIAN SHIPS
PART VIA OBLIGATION OF CERTAIN CERTIFICATE HOLDERS TO SERVE GOVERNMENT OR IN INDIAN SHIPS
PART IXB SECURITY OF SHIPS AND PORT FACILITIES
PART X COLLISIONS, ACCIDENTS AT SEA AND LIABILITY
PART XB CIVIL LIABILITY FOR OIL POLLUTION DAMAGE
PART XC INTERNATIONAL OIL POLLUTION COMPENSATION FUND
PART XIA PREVENTION AND CONTAINMENT OF POLLUTION OF THE SEA BY OIL
PART XIB CONTROL OF HARMFUL ANTI-FOULING SYSTEMS OF SHIPS
PART XIII WRECK AND SALVAGE WRECK
PART XIV CONTROL OF INDIAN SHIPS AND SHIPS ENGAGED IN COASTING TRADE

key_definitions: country to which the Load Line Convention applies
country to which the Safety Convention applies

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Establishes the official short title of the Act and specifies that its commencement date(s) will be appointed by the Central Government via notification.

key_sections.title: Application of Act.
key_sections.description: Defines the territorial and jurisdictional scope of the Act, specifying its application to Indian vessels wherever they may be and to other vessels only within Indian territorial waters.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides a comprehensive list of definitions for key terms and expressions used throughout the Act to ensure clarity and consistent interpretation.

key_sections.title: Establishment of National Shipping Board.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of a National Shipping Board to advise the Central Government on matters related to Indian shipping.

key_sections.title: Obligation to register.
key_sections.description: Requires every Indian ship, with certain exceptions, to be registered under this Act to be recognized as an Indian ship.

key_sections.title: Certificates of competency to be held by officers of ships.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that Indian ships must be provided with officers holding duly certificated competency in accordance with prescribed manning scales.

key_sections.title: Business of seamen's employment offices.
key_sections.description: Outlines the functions of seamen's employment offices, including licensing, regulating recruitment, and maintaining registers of seamen.

key_sections.title: Agreements with crew.
key_sections.description: Requires the master of every Indian ship (with exceptions) to enter into a formal agreement with every seaman engaged in India.

key_sections.title: Misconduct endangering life or ship.
key_sections.description: Prohibits masters, seamen, or apprentices from knowingly committing acts or omissions that endanger the ship or life on board.

key_sections.title: No ship to carry passengers without a certificate of survey.
key_sections.description: Prohibits ships from carrying more than twelve passengers without a valid certificate of survey under this Part.

key_sections.title: Construction rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules prescribing requirements for the hull, equipment, and machinery of Indian passenger or cargo ships.

key_sections.title: Collision regulations.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make regulations for the prevention of collisions at sea, applicable to Indian and foreign ships.

key_sections.title: Submersion of load lines.
key_sections.description: Prohibits Indian ships from being loaded to submerge the appropriate load line, ensuring safe loading practices.

key_sections.title: Unseaworthy ship not to be sent to sea.
key_sections.description: Makes it an offence to send or attempt to send an Indian ship to sea in an unseaworthy state that endangers human life.

key_sections.title: Limitation of liability for damages in respect of certain claims.
key_sections.description: Allows ship owners, salvors, and related parties to limit their liability for certain claims arising from maritime incidents, as per the Convention.

key_sections.title: Application.
key_sections.description: Defines the scope of application for Part XIA, covering oil tankers, other ships, and offshore installations, and incidents of marine casualty causing pollution.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for various contraventions and failures to comply with the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeals and savings.
key_sections.description: Specifies the enactments repealed by this Act and includes saving provisions for existing notifications, rules, appointments, and certificates.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official name of the Act, its geographical application, and the date it came into force.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'basic rent', 'Controller', 'landlord', 'premises', 'standard rent', and 'tenant'.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply to certain premises.
key_sections.description: Outlines specific types of premises to which the provisions of this Act do not apply, including government-owned premises and those with monthly rent exceeding a certain amount.

key_sections.title: Rent in excess of standard rent not recoverable.
key_sections.description: States that tenants are not liable to pay rent exceeding the standard rent, except for lawful increases, and any agreement to the contrary is construed as an agreement for standard rent only.

key_sections.title: Unlawful charges not to be claimed or received.
key_sections.description: Prohibits claiming or receiving rent in excess of standard rent, or any premium/pugree, or advance rent exceeding one month's rent without Controller's permission, in connection with tenancy.

key_sections.title: Standard rent.
key_sections.description: Defines how 'standard rent' is to be calculated for residential and non-residential premises based on various factors like construction date, previous rent fixation, and cost of construction.

key_sections.title: Protection of tenant against eviction.
key_sections.description: Provides protection to tenants against eviction, specifying the limited grounds on which a landlord can obtain an order for recovery of possession from the Controller.

key_sections.title: Right to recover immediate possession of premises to accrue to certain persons.
key_sections.description: Grants a right to landlords, who are government allottees required to vacate their accommodation due to owning property in Delhi, to recover immediate possession of premises let out by them.

key_sections.title: Right to recover immediate possession of premises to accrue to members of the armed forces, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants a right to released/retired armed forces personnel or dependents of those killed in action to recover immediate possession of premises for their residence.

key_sections.title: Right to recover immediate possession of premises to accrue to Central Government and Delhi Administration employees.
key_sections.description: Grants a right to retired or soon-to-be retired Central Government or Delhi Administration employees to recover immediate possession of premises for their residence.

key_sections.title: Right to recover immediate possession of premises to accrue to a widow.
key_sections.description: Grants a right to a widow to recover immediate possession of premises let out by her or her husband for her own residence.

key_sections.title: Special procedure for the disposal of applications for eviction on the ground of bona fide requirement.
key_sections.description: Outlines a summary procedure for the Controller to deal with eviction applications based on bona fide requirement, including specific summons forms and conditions for tenants to contest.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Controllers and additional Controllers.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint Controllers and Additional Controllers, define their jurisdiction, and specifies their qualification requirements.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for various contraventions of the Act, such as claiming unlawful charges, sub-letting without consent, or cutting off essential services.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of civil courts barred in respect of certain matters.
key_sections.description: Bars the jurisdiction of civil courts in matters related to standard rent fixation, eviction, and other issues that the Controller is empowered to decide under this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, covering various procedural and administrative matters.

act_identification.act_title: THE PARLIAMENT (PREVENTION OF DISQUALIFICATION) ACT, 1959

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare that certain offices of profit under the Government shall not disqualify the holders thereof for being chosen as, or for being, members of Parliament.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to specify certain offices of profit under the Government that will not lead to disqualification for individuals serving as members of Parliament. It aims to prevent such offices from being a barrier to parliamentary membership by explicitly listing non-disqualifying positions.
