key_sections.description: Allows members aggrieved by orders of the Board of Discipline or Disciplinary Committee to appeal to the Appellate Authority.

key_sections.title: Penalty for falsely claiming to be a member, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for persons falsely representing themselves as members or practicing without a certificate.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Quality Review Board.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of a Quality Review Board by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Council the power to make regulations for carrying out the objects of the Act.

powers_conferred: Council: management of the affairs of the Institute and for discharging the functions assigned to it by or under this Act; approve academic courses and their contents; prescribe fees for examination; prescribe qualifications for entry in the Register of members; recognise foreign qualifications and training; prescribe guidelines for granting or refusal of certificates of practice; grant or refuse registration of a firm; levy fees from members, examinees and other persons; regulate and maintain the status and standard of professional qualifications; carry out research in accountancy; enable functioning of disciplinary bodies and Appellate Authority; enable functioning of Quality Review Board; issue guidelines; conduct investor education and awareness programmes; enter into MOUs with foreign agencies; consider recommendations of Quality Review Board; ensure functioning of the Institute; appoint Secretary, Director (Discipline), other officers and employees; fix allowances of President, Vice-President and other members; constitute Standing Committees and other Committees; invest money; keep proper accounts; prepare and approve annual financial statement; borrow from scheduled bank or Central Government; remove names from Register of members; restore names to Register of members; make regulations.

Central Government: nominate members to Council; establish Tribunal; appoint Presiding Officer and Members of Tribunal; nominate members to Disciplinary Committee; establish Quality Review Board; appoint Chairperson and members of Quality Review Board; issue directions to the Council; dissolve the Council; authorise persons to take over management of Institute; make rules; frame first regulations; specify countries for reciprocity.

Institute: examine candidates for enrolment; regulate training of students; maintain and publish a Register of persons qualified to practice as cost accountants; maintain and publish a Register of firms; collect fees from members, examinees and other persons; remove names from the Register of members and firms; restore names to the Register of members and firms; maintain a library and publish books and periodicals; conduct elections to the Council; grant or refuse certificates of practice.

Authority, Disciplinary Committee, Board of Discipline and Director (Discipline): powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in respect of summoning and enforcing attendance, examining on oath, discovery and production of documents, and receiving evidence on affidavit.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalty for falsely claiming to be a member or practicing without a certificate (Section 24): Fine up to one lakh rupees for first conviction, and imprisonment up to six months or fine up to five lakh rupees or both for subsequent conviction. Penalty for using name of the Council, awarding degrees of cost accountancy, etc. (Section 25): Imprisonment up to six months or fine not less than one lakh rupees but up to five lakh rupees for first conviction, and imprisonment up to one year or fine not less than two lakh rupees but up to ten lakh rupees or both for subsequent conviction. Companies not to engage in cost accountancy (Section 26): Fine not less than two lakh rupees but up to ten lakh rupees for first conviction, and not less than four lakh rupees but up to twenty lakh rupees for subsequent conviction. Unqualified persons not to sign documents (Section 27): Fine not less than one lakh rupees but up to five lakh rupees for first conviction, and imprisonment up to one year or fine not less than two lakh rupees but up to ten lakh rupees or both for subsequent conviction. Offences by companies (Section 28): Company and responsible persons deemed guilty and punishable. Professional or other misconduct (Sections 21, 21A, 21B, 22 and Schedules I & II) can lead to reprimand, removal from Register (temporary or permanent), or fine (up to one lakh rupees by Board of Discipline, up to five lakh rupees by Disciplinary Committee).

related_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)

authorities_established: Institute of Cost Accountants of India
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government: nominates members to the Council, appoints Presiding Officer and Members of the Tribunal, nominates members to the Disciplinary Committee, appoints Chairperson and members of the Quality Review Board. Council: elects President and Vice-President, appoints Secretary, Director (Discipline), other officers and employees, elects members to the Board of Discipline and Disciplinary Committee, nominates members to the Quality Review Board.

applies_to: Members of the Institute of Cost Accountants of India
Persons engaged in the practice of cost accountancy in India
exemptions: Persons not permanently residing in India (may have further conditions for entry to Register)
Whole-time salaried employees (not deemed to be in practice)
Companies (prohibited from practicing as cost accountants)
special_provisions: Reciprocity: Provisions for preventing subjects of certain countries from becoming members or practicing in India if Indian domiciliaries face discrimination in those countries.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the Disciplinary Directorate, Board of Discipline, Disciplinary Committee, and Appellate Authority for professional misconduct. Penalties are prescribed for various offences, and prosecution requires sanction from the Council or Central Government. The Quality Review Board reviews service quality and can forward non-compliance cases to the Disciplinary Directorate.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil courts (for powers of inquiry), High Court (for appeals prior to 2006 amendment), any civil or criminal court (for offences and misconduct).

schedules_summary.description: Defines professional misconduct in relation to cost accountants in practice (Part I), professional misconduct in relation to members of the Institute in service (Part II), professional misconduct in relation to members of the Institute generally (Part III), and other misconduct in relation to members of the Institute generally (Part IV).

Defines professional misconduct in relation to cost accountants in practice (Part I), professional misconduct in relation to members of the Institute generally (Part II), and other misconduct in relation to members of the Institute generally (Part III).

act_identification.act_title: THE EMPLOYMENT EXCHANGES (COMPULSORY NOTIFICATION OF VACANCIES) ACT, 1959
act_identification.act_short_title: The Employment Exchanges (Compulsory Notification of Vacancies) Act, 1959

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the compulsory notification of vacancies to employment exchanges.
act_overview.purpose: This Act mandates employers in the public sector, and potentially the private sector, to compulsorily notify employment exchanges of available vacancies. It aims to streamline the process of employment by requiring employers to furnish information and returns regarding these vacancies.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official name of the Act, its geographical applicability to the whole of India, and provisions for its commencement date in different states or areas.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'employee', 'employer', 'employment exchange', 'establishment', and 'establishment in public/private sector'.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply in relation to certain vacancies.
key_sections.description: Outlines specific types of vacancies and employments to which the Act does not apply, including certain agricultural employments, domestic service, short-duration employments, unskilled office work, and parliamentary staff.

key_sections.title: Notification of vacancies to employment exchanges.
key_sections.description: Mandates employers in the public sector to notify vacancies to prescribed employment exchanges and empowers the appropriate Government to extend this requirement to the private sector. It also clarifies that notification does not impose an obligation to recruit through the exchange.

key_sections.title: Employers to furnish information and returns in prescribed form.
key_sections.description: Requires employers in the public sector, and potentially the private sector, to furnish prescribed information and returns regarding vacancies to employment exchanges.

key_sections.title: Right of access to records or documents.
key_sections.description: Grants prescribed government officers or their authorized persons the right to access and inspect relevant records or documents of employers to verify information required under the Act.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including fines, for employers who fail to notify vacancies, refuse or furnish false information/returns, refuse to answer questions, or impede access to records.

key_sections.title: Cognizance of offences.
key_sections.description: States that no prosecution for an offence under this Act can be instituted without the sanction of a prescribed government officer or an authorized person.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Provides legal protection against suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings for actions done or intended to be done in good faith under this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including specifying the manner of notification, furnishing information, and exercising access rights.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint commencement date for States/areas (Section 1(3))
Central Government: To declare certain routine or unskilled work as 'unskilled office work' (Section 2(i)(8))
Central Government: To direct non-application of the Act in relation to certain vacancies (Section 3(2))
Appropriate Government: To require employers in the private sector to notify vacancies (Section 4(2))
Appropriate Government: To require employers in the private sector to furnish information and returns (Section 5(2))
Prescribed Government officer or authorized person: Right of access to records or documents and right of entry (Section 6)
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 10)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties are prescribed for employers who fail to notify vacancies (fine up to five hundred rupees for first offence, one thousand for subsequent), or who fail to furnish information/returns, furnish false information, refuse to answer questions, or impede access to records (fine up to two hundred and fifty rupees for first offence, five hundred for subsequent).

applies_to: Employers in every establishment in public sector
Employers in every establishment in private sector (if required by appropriate Government notification)
exemptions: Vacancies in employment in agriculture (including horticulture) in private sector (other than agricultural or farm machinery operatives)
Vacancies in employment in domestic service
Vacancies in employment with total duration less than three months
Vacancies in employment to do unskilled office work
Vacancies in employment connected with the staff of Parliament
Vacancies proposed to be filled through promotion or by absorption of surplus staff
Vacancies proposed to be filled on the result of examination/interview by independent agencies (e.g., Union/State Public Service Commission)
Vacancies in an employment which carries a remuneration of less than sixty rupees in a month
special_provisions: The Act shall come into force in a State on such date as the Central Government may appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different States or for different areas of a State (Section 1(3)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Employers are required to notify vacancies and furnish information to employment exchanges. Government officers have access to records for verification. Non-compliance is subject to penalties, and prosecution requires sanction from a prescribed officer.

act_identification.act_title: THE RAJASTHAN AND MADHYA PRADESH (TRANSFER OF TERRITORIES) ACT, 1959
act_identification.act_short_title: The Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1959

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the transfer of certain territories from the State of Rajasthan to the State of Madhya Pradesh and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to facilitate the transfer of specific territories from the State of Rajasthan to the State of Madhya Pradesh. It also addresses various connected matters arising from this territorial transfer, such as amendments to the Constitution and other laws, and the management of assets and liabilities.

key_definitions: corresponding court, tribunal, authority or officer

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as The Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1959.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'transferred territories', and 'sitting member'.

key_sections.title: Transfer of territories from Rajasthan to Madhya Pradesh.
key_sections.description: Mandates the transfer of specified territories from Rajasthan to Madhya Pradesh as of the appointed day and their inclusion in Mandsaur district.

key_sections.title: Amendment of the First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Directs the amendment of the First Schedule to the Constitution to reflect the territorial changes between Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.

key_sections.title: Amendments of Delimitation Orders.
key_sections.description: Specifies that Delimitation Orders related to parliamentary and assembly constituencies will be modified according to the Second Schedule.

key_sections.title: Extension of jurisdiction of Madhya Pradesh High Court.
key_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the Madhya Pradesh High Court to the transferred territories and removes the jurisdiction of the Rajasthan High Court, with provisions for pending proceedings.

key_sections.title: Assets and liabilities.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that all land, stores, articles, goods, rights, liabilities, and obligations in the transferred territories belonging to Rajasthan shall pass to Madhya Pradesh.

key_sections.title: Extension of laws.
key_sections.description: Provides for the extension of laws in force in Mandsaur district to the transferred territories and the cessation of Rajasthan laws in those territories.

key_sections.title: Transfer of pending proceedings.
key_sections.description: Details the transfer of pending legal proceedings (other than High Court cases) exclusively related to the transferred territories from Rajasthan to corresponding authorities in Madhya Pradesh.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the President the power to issue orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Power of the State Government to alter the name, extent or boundaries of any district in the State of Madhya Pradesh (Section 3(3))
Power of the High Court of Rajasthan to hear and dispose of pending proceedings relatable to the transferred territories (Section 7(2))
Power of any court, tribunal or authority to construe laws for facilitating their application in relation to the transferred territories (Section 12)
Power of the President to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act (Section 16)
Power of the Central Government to make rules to give effect to the provisions of the Act (Section 17(1))

amended_acts: The Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1956
The Constitution of Council Constituencies (Madhya Pradesh) Order, 1957
related_acts: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)

applies_to: States of Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh
Territories specified in the First Schedule
special_provisions: Pending proceedings relatable to transferred territories in the High Court of Rajasthan shall be heard and disposed of by that High Court (Section 7(2))
Nothing in sub-section (2) of Section 3 shall be deemed to affect the power of the State Government to alter district boundaries in Madhya Pradesh after the appointed day (Section 3(3))

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act itself dictates the transfer of territories, assets, liabilities, and legal jurisdiction. The President is empowered to remove difficulties, and courts/authorities are to construe laws for proper application.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court of Rajasthan, High Court of Madhya Pradesh, other courts, tribunals, and authorities as defined in Section 14

schedules_summary.description: Specifies the exact territories, including villages, sheet numbers, khasara numbers, and area measurements, that are transferred from Bhensrorgarh tahsil of Chittor district in Rajasthan to the State of Madhya Pradesh.

Details modifications to the Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1956, and the Delimitation of Council Constituencies (Madhya Pradesh) Order, 1957, to account for the territorial changes, specifically regarding references to districts, tahsils, and divisions as they existed on the appointed day.

act_identification.act_title: THE ARMS ACT, 1959

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Arms and Ammunition.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to consolidate and amend the existing laws concerning arms and ammunition. It aims to regulate the acquisition, possession, manufacture, sale, import, export, and transport of arms and ammunition to ensure public safety and peace.

chapter_titles: ACQUISITION, POSSESSION, MANUFACTURE, SALE, IMPORT, EXPORT AND TRANSPORT OF ARMS AND AMMUNITION

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its territorial application to the whole of India, and that its commencement date is to be appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions and interpretation.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'acquisition', 'ammunition', 'arms', 'firearms', 'licence', 'prohibited arms', and 'prohibited ammunition'.

key_sections.title: Licence for acquisition and possession of firearms and ammunition.
key_sections.description: Mandates a licence for acquiring, possessing, or carrying firearms and ammunition, and limits the number of firearms a person can possess to two.

key_sections.title: Licence for manufacture, sale, etc., of arms and ammunition.
key_sections.description: Requires a licence for manufacturing, selling, transferring, converting, repairing, testing, or proving arms and ammunition.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of acquisition or possession, or of manufacture or sale of prohibited arms or prohibited ammunition.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the acquisition, possession, manufacture, or sale of prohibited arms or ammunition unless specially authorised by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of acquisition or possession by, or of sale or transfer to, young persons and certain other persons of firearms, etc.
key_sections.description: Prohibits persons under twenty-one years, those convicted of certain offences, or of unsound mind from acquiring or possessing firearms, and prohibits selling to such persons.

key_sections.title: Licence for import and export of arms, etc.
key_sections.description: Requires a licence for bringing into or taking out of India any arms or ammunition, with certain exceptions for private use or bona fide tourists.

key_sections.title: Grant of licences.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for granting licences, including application requirements, police reports, and conditions for granting licences for different purposes.

key_sections.title: Refusal of licences.
key_sections.description: Specifies the grounds on which a licensing authority shall refuse to grant a licence, such as for prohibited arms, or if the applicant is unfit or poses a risk to public peace or safety.

key_sections.title: Variation, suspension and revocation of licences.
key_sections.description: Details the powers of the licensing authority to vary, suspend, or revoke licences under specified conditions, including for contravention of conditions or public interest.

key_sections.title: Deposit of arms, etc., on possession ceasing to be lawful.
key_sections.description: Mandates the deposit of arms or ammunition with police or licensed dealers when their possession becomes unlawful, with provisions for return or forfeiture.

key_sections.title: Punishment for certain offences.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishments for various offences, including unlicensed manufacture, sale, possession of prohibited arms, illicit trafficking, and contravention of other provisions, with varying terms of imprisonment and fines.

key_sections.title: Punishment for using arms, etc.
key_sections.description: Specifies punishments for using arms or prohibited arms/ammunition in contravention of the Act, with severe penalties, including imprisonment for life or death, if such use results in death.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to exempt any person or class of persons, or specific arms/ammunition, or parts of India from the operation of the Act in public interest.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering aspects like licensing authorities, application forms, fees, and conditions for licences.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint commencement date (S.1(3)); To regulate acquisition/possession of non-firearms (S.4); To prohibit import/export of arms (S.11); To restrict/prohibit transport of arms (S.12); To order seizure and detention of arms (S.24); To issue notifications for disturbed areas (S.24A, S.24B); To suspend/revoke licences (S.17(9)); To exempt persons/arms/areas from the Act (S.41); To direct census of firearms (S.42); To delegate powers/functions (S.43); To make rules (S.44).
Licensing Authority: To grant, refuse, vary, suspend, and revoke licences (S.13, S.14, S.17).
Police Officer/Specially empowered officer: To demand production of licence, seize arms, and arrest without warrant (S.19).
Magistrate/Police Officer/Public Servant/Railway/Aircraft/Vessel/Vehicle employee: To arrest persons conveying arms under suspicious circumstances and seize arms (S.20).
Magistrate: To cause search and seizure of arms/ammunition (S.22); To search vessels, vehicles for arms (S.23).
Court (convicting/appellate/High Court): To suspend or revoke licences (S.17(7), S.17(8)); To confiscate arms or ammunition (S.32).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines numerous offences, primarily related to the unlicensed acquisition, possession, manufacture, sale, import, export, or transport of arms and ammunition, especially prohibited items. Penalties range from imprisonment for six months and/or fine for minor contraventions (e.g., failure to deliver licence, false information, contravention of licence conditions) to imprisonment for life or death for using prohibited arms/ammunition resulting in death. Specific penalties are prescribed for involvement with organized crime syndicates and illicit trafficking, often with minimum imprisonment terms of seven or ten years, extending to imprisonment for life. Using firearms in a rash or negligent manner or in celebratory gunfire is punishable with imprisonment up to two years or fine up to one lakh rupees, or both. Confiscation of arms, ammunition, and related conveyances is also possible upon conviction. Punishment for subsequent offences is double the penalty for the latter offence.

repealed_acts: The Indian Arms Act, 1878 (11 of 1878)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint officers for taking census of firearms and to delegate its powers or functions under the Act. The licensing authority is empowered to grant or renew licences.

applies_to: Whole of India
Persons acquiring, possessing, manufacturing, selling, importing, exporting, or transporting arms and ammunition
exemptions: Arms or ammunition on board any sea-going vessel or aircraft forming part of its ordinary armament or equipment.
Acquisition, possession, carrying, manufacture, repair, conversion, test, proof, sale, transfer, import, export, or transport of arms or ammunition by or under orders of the Central Government.
Acquisition, possession, carrying, manufacture, repair, conversion, test, proof, sale, transfer, import, export, or transport of arms or ammunition by a public servant in the course of his duty.

Acquisition, possession, carrying, manufacture, repair, conversion, test, proof, sale, transfer, import, export, or transport of arms or ammunition by a member of the National Cadet Corps, Territorial Army, or other specified forces in the course of his duty.
Any weapon of an obsolete pattern or of antiquarian value or in disrepair which is not capable of being used as a firearm.
Acquisition, possession, or carrying by a person of minor parts of arms or ammunition not intended to be used with complementary parts.
special_provisions: Extension to Goa, Daman and Diu, Pondicherry, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Sikkim.
Special provisions for disturbed areas regarding possession and carrying of notified arms (Sections 24A, 24B).
Provisions for bona fide tourists to bring arms and ammunition into India for sport (Section 10(1)(b)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a system of licensing for arms and ammunition, with prohibitions on certain types of arms and persons. It grants powers of search, seizure, and arrest to police officers, magistrates, and other empowered officials. Contraventions are met with penalties, including imprisonment and fines, and provisions for confiscation of arms. Offences are cognizable, and previous sanction of the district magistrate is required for prosecution in certain cases.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate, Convicting court, Appellate court, High Court

act_identification.act_title: THE ANDHRA PRADESH AND MADRAS (ALTERATION OF BOUNDARIES) ACT, 1959
act_identification.act_short_title: the Andhra Pradesh and Madras (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1959

legislative_details.geographical_extent: States of Andhra Pradesh and Madras

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the alteration of boundaries of the States of Andhra Pradesh and Madras and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the alteration of the boundaries between the States of Andhra Pradesh and Madras. It addresses consequential matters such as changes in territorial divisions, representation in legislatures, jurisdiction of High Courts, apportionment of assets and liabilities, and administrative provisions.

chapter_titles: PART III REPRESENTATION IN THE LEGISLATURES
PART VI APPORTIONMENT OF ASSETS AND LIABILITIES
PART VIII LEGAL AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Transfer of territories.
key_sections.description: Mandates the transfer of specified territories between the States of Andhra Pradesh and Madras from the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule to the Constitution to reflect the altered territories of Andhra Pradesh and Madras.

key_sections.title: Strength of Legislative Assemblies.
key_sections.description: Adjusts the total number of seats in the Legislative Assemblies of Andhra Pradesh and Madras.

key_sections.title: Extension of jurisdiction of, and transfer of proceedings to, Andhra Pradesh High Court.
key_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the Andhra Pradesh High Court to newly acquired territories and provides for the transfer of relevant legal proceedings.

key_sections.title: Extension of jurisdiction of, and transfer of proceedings to, Madras High Court.
key_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the Madras High Court to newly acquired territories and provides for the transfer of relevant legal proceedings.

key_sections.title: Land and goods.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that land, stores, articles, and cash balances in transferred territories pass to the recipient State.

key_sections.title: Pensions.
key_sections.description: Provides for the apportionment of pension liabilities between Andhra Pradesh and Madras.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to services.
key_sections.description: Governs the continuance and allotment of government servants between the two States following territorial changes.

key_sections.title: Power to adapt laws.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the appropriate Government to adapt and modify laws for their application in the altered States.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the President to issue orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for the purpose of giving effect to the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint commencement date (Section 1(2))
State Government to alter names, extent or boundaries of districts, taluks, firkas or villages (Section 7)
Central Government to order allocation or adjustment of property, benefits or liabilities between States (Section 36)
President to specify manner of pension apportionment (Section 31)
President to specify modifications for distribution of revenues (Section 24)
Central Government to give directions for services (Section 43(5))
Appropriate Government to adapt laws (Section 46)
State Government to name authorities for exercising statutory functions (Section 48)
President to remove difficulties (Section 53)
Central Government to make rules (Section 54)

amended_acts: The Constitution (First Schedule and Fourth Schedule)
Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1956
Delimitation Commission’s Final Order No. 19, dated the 4th October, 1954
related_acts: Union Duties of Excise (Distribution) Act, 1957 (55 of 1957)
Estate Duty and Tax on Railway Passenger Fares (Distribution) Act, 1957 (57 of 1957)
Additional Duties of Excise (Goods of Special Importance) Act, 1957 (58 of 1957)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government, President, State Government

applies_to: States of Andhra Pradesh and Madras
territories transferred between these States
persons serving in connection with the affairs of Andhra Pradesh or Madras
special_provisions: Special provisions with regard to Araniar Project (Section 41)
Temporary provisions as to the continuance of certain existing road transport permits (Section 42)
Provisions as to the continuance of officers in the same posts (Section 44)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through orders issued by the Central Government, State Governments, and the President; adaptation and construction of existing laws; transfer of legal proceedings and jurisdiction of High Courts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court of Andhra Pradesh, High Court at Madras, Supreme Court, other courts, tribunals, authorities

schedules_summary.description: Territories transferred from the State of Madras to the State of Andhra Pradesh.
Territories transferred from the State of Andhra Pradesh to the State of Madras.
Villages of Nagari firka in Puttur taluk, referenced in Section 4(1).
Modifications of the First Schedule to the Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1956.
Modifications of the Second Schedule to the Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1956.
Modifications of the Delimitation Commission’s Final Order No. 19 dated the 4th October, 1954.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN STATISTICAL INSTITUTE ACT, 1959

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare the institution known as the Indian Statistical Institute having at present its registered office in Calcutta to be an institution of national importance and to provide for certain matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act declares the Indian Statistical Institute as an institution of national importance. It provides for the Institute's power to grant degrees and diplomas, its financial support from the Central Government, and establishes mechanisms for government oversight, audit, and control to ensure its efficient functioning in areas like research, education, and national development planning.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, such as 'Institute', 'memorandum', and 'rules and regulations'.

key_sections.title: Declaration of the Indian Statistical Institute as an institution of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the Indian Statistical Institute as an institution of national importance due to its objects.

key_sections.title: Grant of degrees and diplomas by Institute.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Institute to hold examinations and grant degrees and diplomas in specified subjects, notwithstanding other laws.

key_sections.title: Grants, loans, etc., by Central Government to the Institute.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to provide financial assistance to the Institute for its functions, including research and education.

key_sections.title: Audit of accounts of the Institute.
key_sections.description: Mandates the audit of the Institute's accounts by qualified auditors selected by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Prior approval of Central Government necessary for certain action by Institute.
key_sections.description: Requires the Institute to obtain prior approval from the Central Government for significant actions like altering purposes, amending rules, or disposing of certain property.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Committees by Central Government for preparing programme of work by the Institute, etc.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to constitute committees to prepare work programmes and financial estimates for the Institute.

key_sections.title: Review of work done, Inspection of assets, etc.
key_sections.description: Enables the Central Government to constitute committees for reviewing the Institute's work, inspecting assets, evaluating performance, and advising the Government.

key_sections.title: Power to issue directions to Institute.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the Institute in the public interest, including directions to amend its memorandum or rules.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to assume functions of control.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to assume control of the Institute or any part thereof under specific circumstances, such as default in following directions or abuse of power.

powers_conferred: Institute: Grant degrees and diplomas (Section 4)
Central Government: Pay grants, loans or otherwise to the Institute (Section 5)
Central Government: Select auditors for the Institute (Section 6)
Central Government: Issue directions to auditors (Section 6)
Central Government: Grant prior approval for certain actions by the Institute (Section 7)
Central Government: Constitute committees for preparing programme of work (Section 8)
Central Government: Constitute committees for reviewing work, inspecting assets, and evaluating the Institute (Section 9)
Central Government: Issue directions to the Institute (Section 11)
Central Government: Assume functions of control over the Institute (Section 12)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government

applies_to: The Indian Statistical Institute

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government exercises oversight through financial grants, audit requirements, approval for significant actions, constitution of committees for work programmes and reviews, power to issue directions, and the power to assume control of the Institute.

act_identification.act_title: THE GENEVA CONVENTIONS ACT, 1960

act_overview.preamble: An Act to enable effect to be given to certain international Conventions done at Geneva on the twelfth day of August, 1949, to which India is a party, and for purposes connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to implement the provisions of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 in India. It provides for the punishment of grave breaches of these conventions and regulates the use of Red Cross and other emblems, ensuring legal protection for persons covered by the conventions.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II PUNISHMENT OF OFFENDERS AGAINST CONVENTIONS
CHAPTER III LEGAL PROCEEDINGS IN RESPECT OF PROTECTED PERSONS
CHAPTER IV ABUSE OF THE RED CROSS AND OTHER EMBLEMS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Act's name, territorial application, and provides for its commencement date by Central Government notification.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Conventions', 'court', 'protected internee', 'protecting power', and 'protected prisoner of war'.

key_sections.title: Punishment of grave breaches of conventions.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions, including death or imprisonment for life for wilful killing, and imprisonment up to fourteen years for other cases, applicable within or without India regardless of nationality.

key_sections.title: Liability of persons for offences committed outside India.
key_sections.description: Extends the Act's jurisdiction to offences committed outside India, allowing such persons to be dealt with as if the offence occurred within India.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of court.
key_sections.description: Specifies that no court inferior to that of a chief presidency magistrate or a Court of Session shall try offences punishable under Chapter II.

key_sections.title: Notice of trial of protected persons to be served on protecting power, etc.
key_sections.description: Mandates that courts must serve notice of trial to the protecting power and the accused for protected prisoners of war and internees, with specific particulars and timeframes.

key_sections.title: Legal re-presentation of certain persons.
key_sections.description: Ensures legal representation for persons on trial for offences under Section 3 or for protected prisoners of war, with provisions for assigned legal practitioners.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of use of Red Cross and other emblems.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the unauthorized use of the Red Cross, Red Crescent, Red Lion and Sun, Swiss Confederation emblems, and similar designs or wordings.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes a fine up to five hundred rupees and forfeiture of goods for contravention of the prohibition on emblem use.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that both the company and responsible individuals are liable for offences committed by a company under Chapter IV, with a proviso for due diligence.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Geneva Convention Implementing Act, 1936, and states that The Geneva Convention Act, 1911, ceases to have effect as part of Indian law.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint commencement date (Section 1(3)).
Central Government: To approve the use of Red Cross and other emblems (Section 12).
Central Government: To specify officers for cognizance of offences (Section 17).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act (Section 18).
Courts: To try offences (Section 5).
Courts: To adjourn trials and authorize detention of the accused (Section 8(5), 9(1)).
Courts: To direct that a legal practitioner be assigned to watch over the interests of the accused (Section 9(3)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Grave breaches of Conventions are punishable with death or imprisonment for life (for wilful killing) or imprisonment up to fourteen years (for other cases) (Section 3). Unauthorized use of Red Cross and other emblems is punishable with a fine up to five hundred rupees and forfeiture of goods (Section 13). Companies and their responsible officers are liable for offences committed by companies (Section 14).

repealed_acts: The Geneva Convention Implementing Act, 1936 (14 of 1936)
The Geneva Convention Act, 1911 (1 and 2 Geo. 5, C. 20)
related_acts: Geneva Convention for the Amelioration of the Condition of the Wounded and Sick in Armed Forces in the Field of August 12, 1949
Geneva Convention for the Amelioration of the Condition of Wounded, Sick and Shipwrecked Members of Armed Forces at Sea of August 12, 1949
Geneva Convention Relative to the Treatment of Prisoners of War of August 12, 1949
Geneva Convention Relative to the Protection of Civilian Persons in Time of War of August 12, 1949

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to specify officers for cognizance of offences under this Act (Section 17).

applies_to: The whole of India (Section 1(2)).
Persons committing or attempting to commit grave breaches of conventions, within or without India, regardless of nationality or citizenship (Section 3(1), 3(2)).
Indian ships or aircraft for the use of emblems (Section 16).
exemptions: Trade marks registered before the coming into force of this Act, for certain uses of emblems or designations (Section 15).
special_provisions: Special provisions for legal proceedings in respect of protected persons, including notice of trial and legal representation (Chapter III).
Special provisions for offences committed by companies (Section 14).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Offences are tried by courts (Section 5), with specific procedures for protected persons (Chapter III). The Central Government has the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions (Section 18).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a chief presidency magistrate or a Court of Session shall try any offence punishable under Chapter II (Section 5).

schedules_summary.description: Contains the text of the Geneva Convention for the Amelioration of the Condition of the Wounded and Sick in Armed Forces in the Field of August 12, 1949.
Contains the text of the Geneva Convention for the Amelioration of the Condition of Wounded, Sick and Shipwrecked Members of Armed Forces at Sea of August 12, 1949.
Contains the text of the Geneva Convention Relative to the Treatment of Prisoners of War of August 12, 1949.
Contains the text of the Geneva Convention Relative to the Protection of Civilian Persons in Time of War of August 12, 1949.

act_identification.act_title: THE ORPHANAGES AND OTHER CHARITABLE HOMES (SUPERVISION AND CONTROL) ACT, 1960
act_identification.act_short_title: Orphanages and Other Charitable Homes (Supervision and Control) Act, 1960

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the supervision and control of orphanages, homes for neglected women or children and other like institutions and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish a framework for the supervision and control of orphanages, homes for neglected women or children, and similar institutions. It seeks to ensure the proper management, care, protection, and welfare of women and children residing in such homes.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II THE BOARD OF CONTROL AND ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS
CHAPTER IV MANAGEMENT OF RECOGNISED HOMES

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its geographical extent, and how its commencement date will be determined by State Governments.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Board', 'certificate', 'child', 'home', 'manager', 'managing committee', 'recognised home', 'prescribed', and 'woman'.

key_sections.title: Board of Control, its constitution, etc.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to establish a Board of Control for supervising homes and details its composition, including members from the State Legislature, managing committees, and government nominees.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary duty of the Board to supervise and control matters related to the management of homes, subject to directions from the State Government.

key_sections.title: Homes not to be run without certificate.
key_sections.description: Mandates that no person shall maintain or conduct a home without a certificate of recognition granted under this Act.

key_sections.title: Grant or refusal of certificate.
key_sections.description: Describes the process for granting or refusing a certificate of recognition, including inquiry by the Board, opportunity for hearing, and non-transferability of certificates.

key_sections.title: Revocation of certificate.
key_sections.description: Details the conditions under which the Board may revoke a certificate, such as non-compliance with conditions or unsatisfactory management, and the procedure for such revocation.

key_sections.title: Managing committee.
key_sections.description: Requires every recognised home to have a managing committee responsible for its management, which appoints a manager for the home.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for non-compliance with the Act, rules, regulations, directions, or certificate conditions.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, covering various administrative and procedural matters.

key_sections.title: Power of the Board to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Board, with State Government approval, to make regulations for performing its functions, including supervision, inspection, and inmate care.

key_sections.title: Repeals and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Women's and Children's Institutions (Licensing) Act, 1956, and similar State Acts, while providing for savings of actions taken under the repealed Acts.

powers_conferred: State Government: establish Board of Control (Section 5), give directions to Board (Section 7), exempt homes (Section 28), make rules (Section 29), approve Board regulations (Section 30).
Board: supervise and control homes (Section 7), give directions to managers (Section 8), inspect homes (Section 9), make regulations (Section 30), grant/refuse/revoke certificates (Sections 15, 17).
Manager: discharge inmates (Section 22), send reports on deaths (Section 23).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who fails to comply with any provision of this Act or its rules, regulations, directions, orders, or certificate conditions shall be punishable for a first offence with imprisonment up to three months or a fine up to two hundred and fifty rupees or both. For a second or subsequent offence, imprisonment may extend to six months or a fine up to one thousand rupees or both.

repealed_acts: Women's and Children's Institutions (Licensing) Act, 1956 (105 of 1956)
related_acts: Suppression of Immoral Traffic in Women and Girls Act, 1956 (104 of 1956)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government nominates members to the Board of Control and the Chairman for its first constitution. The Board appoints its own officers and employees. The managing committee appoints the manager of a home.

applies_to: Orphanages
Homes for neglected women or children
Other like institutions maintained for the reception, care, protection and welfare of women or children
exemptions: Any hostel or boarding house attached to, or controlled or recognised by, an educational institution
Any protective home established under the Suppression of Immoral Traffic in Women and Girls Act, 1956 (104 of 1956)
Any reformatory, certified or other school, or any home or workhouse, governed by any enactment for the time being in force
special_provisions: Extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh).
Comes into force in a State on such date as the State Government may appoint by notification.
State-specific amendments for Maharashtra regarding the constitution of the Board of Control and term of office of members.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Board of Control supervises and controls homes, issues directions to managers, and conducts inspections. Homes require a certificate of recognition to operate. Non-compliance is subject to penalties, and prosecutions require sanction from the District Magistrate or Chief Presidency Magistrate.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District Magistrate or the Chief Presidency Magistrate (for sanctioning prosecutions)

act_identification.act_title: THE BOMBAY REORGANISATION ACT, 1960

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Territories of the former State of Bombay, now Maharashtra and Gujarat

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the reorganisation of the State of Bombay and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the reorganisation of the State of Bombay into the new States of Maharashtra and Gujarat. It addresses the division of territories, legislative representation, high courts, apportionment of assets and liabilities, services, and other connected matters to facilitate this reorganisation.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act as 'The Bombay Reorganisation Act, 1960'.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'law', 'population ratio', and 'transferred territory'.

key_sections.title: Formation of Gujarat State.
key_sections.description: Establishes the new State of Gujarat from specified territories of the State of Bombay, and renames the residuary State of Bombay as the State of Maharashtra.

key_sections.title: Amendment of the First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule of the Constitution to reflect the formation of Gujarat and Maharashtra as new states.

key_sections.title: Amendment of the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Amends the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution to allocate seats in the Council of States to the new States of Maharashtra and Gujarat.

key_sections.title: Representation in the House of the People.
key_sections.description: Allocates seats in the House of the People to the States of Maharashtra and Gujarat and amends the Representation of the People Act, 1950 accordingly.

key_sections.title: Strength of Legislative Assemblies.
key_sections.description: Determines the total number of seats in the Legislative Assemblies of Maharashtra and Gujarat and amends the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

key_sections.title: High Court for Gujarat.
key_sections.description: Establishes a separate High Court for the State of Gujarat and designates the High Court of Bombay as the High Court for the State of Maharashtra.

key_sections.title: Application of Part.
key_sections.description: States that Part VI of the Act governs the apportionment of assets and liabilities of the State of Bombay immediately before the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Public debt.
key_sections.description: Details the apportionment of the public debt of the State of Bombay between the States of Maharashtra and Gujarat.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to All-India Services.
key_sections.description: Provides for the creation of separate cadres for All-India Services for Maharashtra and Gujarat and the allocation of existing members.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to other services.
key_sections.description: Outlines the provisional and final allocation of other government servants between the States of Maharashtra and Gujarat.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the President the power to issue orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government to issue directions regarding functioning and apportionment of bodies corporate (Sections 68, 70, 74)
Central Government to issue directions for maintenance of arrangements for electric power and water supply (Section 69)
Central Government to specify securities for transfer to Gujarat (Section 51, 52)
Central Government to order allocation or adjustment of assets or liabilities (Section 66)
Central Government to give directions to State Governments of Maharashtra and Gujarat (Section 83)
Central Government to determine State for service and approve service conditions (Section 81)
Central Government to make rules (Section 96)
President to appoint principal seat of Gujarat High Court (Section 28)
President to determine allowances and privileges of Governor of Gujarat (Section 44)
President to remove difficulties (Section 95)
Governor of Bombay/Gujarat to authorise expenditure from Consolidated Fund of Gujarat (Section 42)
Chief Justice of High Court of Bombay to certify proceedings for transfer to Gujarat High Court (Section 37)
Chief Justice of High Court of Bombay to nominate Judges for Permanent Bench at Nagpur (Section 41)
Chief Justice of High Court of Gujarat to appoint member to perform Speaker duties (Section 17)
Chief Justice of High Court of Gujarat to nominate members of first Bar Council (Section 72)
Election Commission to determine number of seats, constituencies, and make orders for Gujarat Legislative Assembly (Section 19)
State Government to alter name, extent or boundaries of any district, taluka or village (Section 5)
State Government of Gujarat to name authorities for exercising statutory functions (Section 90)
High Court of Gujarat to make rules and orders with respect to practice and procedure (Section 32)

amended_acts: The First Schedule to the Constitution
The Fourth Schedule to the Constitution
Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1956
related_acts: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1956
Representation of the People Act, 1951 (43 of 1951)
Union Duties of Excise (Distribution) Act, 1957 (55 of 1957)
Estate Duty and Tax on Railway Passenger Fares (Distribution) Act, 1957 (57 of 1957)
Additional Duties of Excise (Goods of Special Importance) Act, 1957 (58 of 1957)
Bombay Sales Tax Act, 1959 (Bom. Act LI of 1959)
Agricultural Produce (Development and Warehousing) Corporations Act, 1956 (28 of 1956)

authorities_established: High Court for the State of Gujarat
Special Revenue Reserve Fund in Gujarat
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The President determines Judges of Gujarat High Court, principal seat of Gujarat High Court, and allowances/privileges of Governor of Gujarat. The Governor of Gujarat may appoint a member to perform Speaker duties. The Chief Justice of the High Court of Bombay nominates Judges for the Nagpur bench and certifies proceedings for transfer. The Chief Justice of the High Court of Gujarat nominates members of the first Bar Council. The Central Government specifies associate members for the Election Commission and determines the State for service.
regulatory_bodies: National Co-operative Development and Warehousing Board
Bar Council for the High Court of Bombay

applies_to: State of Bombay (before reorganisation)
States of Maharashtra and Gujarat (after reorganisation)
Sitting members of Council of States, House of the People, Legislative Assembly of Bombay, Legislative Council of Bombay
Judges of the High Court of Bombay
Advocates and attorneys entitled to practise in the High Court of Bombay
Government servants of the State of Bombay
Bodies corporate, cooperative societies, commercial or industrial undertakings of the State of Bombay
Persons enrolled as pleaders in subordinate courts in the State of Bombay
special_provisions: Special provisions in relation to Gujarat Legislative Assembly (Section 19)
Special provision as to biennial elections (Section 24)
Permanent Bench of Bombay High Court at Nagpur (Section 41)
Special provision for Bar Council of Gujarat (Section 72)
Special provision relating to retrenchment compensation in certain cases (Section 77)
Special provision as to income-tax (Section 78)
Continuance of facilities in certain State institutions (Section 79)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (Section 96), High Court of Gujarat (Section 32), Election Commission (Section 19)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through orders issued by the President or Central Government, directions given by the Central Government to State Governments and authorities, and amendments to existing laws and constitutional schedules. The Election Commission is empowered to make orders regarding constituencies. Courts have jurisdiction to interpret and enforce laws, with specific provisions for transfer of proceedings and finality of certain orders.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court at Bombay, High Court of Gujarat, Supreme Court, any court, tribunal, or authority empowered to enforce laws.

schedules_summary.description: Lists the specific villages and talukas transferred from the State of Bombay to form part of the State of Gujarat.
Specifies the sitting members of the Council of States who are allocated to Maharashtra and Gujarat.
Details amendments to the First Schedule of the Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1956, concerning parliamentary constituencies.
Details amendments to the Second Schedule of the Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1956, concerning assembly constituencies.
Specifies amendments to the Delimitation of Council Constituencies (Bombay) Order, 1951.
Lists the sitting members who shall cease to be members of the Bombay Legislative Council.
Outlines amendments to the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, defining Scheduled Castes in Gujarat and Maharashtra.
Outlines amendments to the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1960, defining Scheduled Tribes in Gujarat and Maharashtra.

Contains modified forms of sections from various Acts and Orders related to the distribution of Union duties of excise, estate duty, tax on railway passenger fares, and additional duties of excise, reflecting the reorganisation.
Provides rules for the division of stores (e.g., for specific purposes, Sachivalaya, unissued stores) between the States of Maharashtra and Gujarat.
Details the apportionment of liability in respect of pensions between Maharashtra and Gujarat.
Lists specific multi-unit cooperative societies to which transitional provisions apply.
Lists State institutions in Maharashtra and Gujarat where facilities are to be continued for the people of the other State.

act_identification.act_title: THE DELHI LAND HOLDINGS (CEILING) ACT, 1960

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of the Union territory of Delhi

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the imposition of a ceiling on land holdings in the Union territory of Delhi and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: To impose a ceiling on land holdings in the Union territory of Delhi and to address related matters, including the determination, vesting, and allotment of excess land.

chapter_titles: CEILING ON HOLDINGS AND VESTING AND ALLOTMENT OF EXCESS LAND

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title, geographical extent, and commencement details of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'ceiling limit', 'family', 'minor', 'orchard', 'person', and 'person under disability'.

key_sections.title: Ceiling on holding.
key_sections.description: Establishes the maximum land area a person or family can hold, with different limits based on irrigation and crop yield, and provisions for conversion between land categories.

key_sections.title: Submission of returns.
key_sections.description: Mandates persons holding land in excess of the ceiling limit to submit returns with particulars of land and desired retention.

key_sections.title: Procedure for determination of excess land.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for the competent authority to determine excess land, including inquiry, publication of lists, and treatment of certain transfers.

key_sections.title: Excess land to vest in Government.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which excess land of a Bhumidhar or Asami vests in the Government.

key_sections.title: Publication of the final list and consequences thereof.
key_sections.description: Details the process for publishing the final list of excess land, handling objections, and the legal consequences of such publication, including vesting of land.

key_sections.title: Compensation.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the rates and manner of compensation payable by the Government for excess land that vests in it, including provisions for apportionment and structures.

key_sections.title: Limit of future acquisition of land.
key_sections.description: Prohibits acquisition of land that would cause holdings to exceed the ceiling limit and specifies how such excess land will be treated.

key_sections.title: Allotment of excess land.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Chief Commissioner to allot excess land vesting in the Government to specified persons, with preference to landless agricultural labourers.

key_sections.title: Act to override contract and other laws.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over contrary provisions in other laws, customs, or agreements.

key_sections.title: Offences and penalties.
key_sections.description: Defines offences related to non-submission or false submission of returns and obstruction, prescribing penalties.

key_sections.title: Finality of orders and bar of jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Declares orders made under the Act as final and bars civil courts from jurisdiction over matters decidable by competent authorities.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Chief Commissioner the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, detailing specific matters for which rules can be made.

powers_conferred: Chief Commissioner: To appoint the date of commencement of the Act (Section 1(3)); to authorize competent authorities (Section 2(c)); to declare areas for goshala or breeding/feeding horses (Section 1(2)(d)); to reserve excess land for public purposes (Section 15); to allot excess land (Section 16); to call for records for revision (Section 20(1)); to make rules (Section 27).
Competent authority: To determine excess land (Section 6); to make orders determining amount payable as compensation (Section 10(6)).
Deputy Commissioner: To entertain objections to the published list (Section 9(1)); to approve or modify the list (Section 9(2)); to take possession of excess land (Section 14).
Officers/Authorities holding inquiries: To enforce attendance, require discovery of documents, receive evidence on affidavit (Section 21).
Officer entrusted with duty: To enter upon and survey land (Section 22).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Failure to submit a return or submitting a false return is punishable with imprisonment for up to six months and a fine up to one thousand rupees. Contravention of lawful orders or obstruction of possession is punishable with a fine up to one thousand rupees.

related_acts: State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Chief Commissioner has the power to authorize any person or authority to perform the functions of the competent authority under this Act (Section 2(c)).

applies_to: Whole of the Union territory of Delhi
Persons holding land in the Union territory of Delhi
exemptions: Areas included in a municipality or notified area under the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911, or in a cantonment under the Cantonments Act, 1924.
Areas owned and held by the Central Government or any State Government or any local authority.
Areas owned and held by any corporation owned or controlled by the Central Government.
Areas acquired under any law relating to the acquisition of land for a public purpose.
Areas held and occupied for the purpose of a goshala or for breeding/feeding horses, declared as such by the Chief Commissioner (subject to conditions).
Areas owned and held by any agricultural co-operative land mortgage bank, any State or Central Co-operative Bank or any other bank (as defined in the Act).
special_provisions: Provisions for land held by a person whose family members exceed five, allowing for increased holding up to twice the ceiling limit (Section 3(5)).
Provisions for major sons of a person representing a family to hold land not exceeding the ceiling limit (Section 3(7)).
Provisions for joint submission of returns by co-sharers in case of a joint holding (Section 4).
Provisions for restoration of excess land to a Bhumidhar under certain conditions (Section 8 proviso).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the determination of excess land by competent authorities, vesting of such land in the Government, payment of compensation, and subsequent allotment. It includes provisions for submission of returns, inquiries, appeals, and revisions. The Deputy Commissioner is empowered to take possession of excess land. Sums due to the Government can be recovered as arrears of land revenue.

act_identification.act_title: THE INTERNATIONAL DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATION (STATUS, IMMUNITIES AND PRIVILEGES) ACT, 1960
act_identification.act_short_title: International Development Association (Status, Immunities and Privileges) Act, 1960

act_overview.preamble: An Act to implement the international agreement for the establishment and operation of the International Development Association in so far as it relates to the status, immunities and privileges of that Association, and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act implements the international agreement for the establishment and operation of the International Development Association. Its primary objective is to confer specific status, immunities, and privileges upon the Association and its personnel within India, as detailed in the agreement.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, specifically 'Agreement' and 'Association'.

key_sections.title: Conferment of status and certain immunities and privileges on the Association and conferment of certain immunities and privileges on its officers and employees.
key_sections.description: Grants the provisions of Article VIII of the Agreement the force of law in India, conferring status, immunities, and privileges, with certain provisos regarding taxation and duties.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Notifications under section 3 and rules under section 4 to be placed before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Mandates that notifications and rules made under the Act be laid before each House of Parliament for review and potential modification or annulment.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to appoint the date of commencement of the Act
Central Government: to amend the Schedule in conformity with amendments to the Agreement
Central Government: to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (for commencement date)

act_identification.act_title: THE MANIPUR LAND REVENUE AND LAND REFORMS ACT, 1960
act_identification.act_short_title: The Manipur Land Revenue and Land Reforms Act, 1960

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of the Union territory of Manipur except the hill areas thereof

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to land revenue in the Union territory of Manipur and to provide for certain measures of land reform.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws concerning land revenue in the Union territory of Manipur. It also seeks to introduce and implement various measures for land reform within the territory.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II.—REVENUE DIVISIONS, REVENUE OFFICERS AND THEIR APPOINTMENT
CHAPTER IV.—SURVEY AND SETTLEMENT OF LAND REVENUE
CHAPTER VII.—REALISATION OF LAND REVENE AND OTHER PUBLIC DEMANDS
CHAPTER VIII.—PROCEDURE OF REVENUE OFFICERS: APPEALS AND REVISIONS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, its geographical application (Union territory of Manipur except hill areas), and that its commencement date will be appointed by notification.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Administrator', 'agriculture', 'basic holding', 'competent authority', 'deputy commissioner', 'family', 'land owner', 'personal cultivation', 'rent', and 'tenant'.

key_sections.title: Title of Government to lands, etc.
key_sections.description: Declares all unowned lands, public roads, water bodies, and rights therein as Government property, and vests rights to mines and minerals in the Government.

key_sections.title: Liability of land to land revenue.
key_sections.description: States that all lands are liable to pay land revenue to the Government, with provisions for exemption by the Administrator.

key_sections.title: Preparation of record of rights.
key_sections.description: Mandates the survey officer to prepare a record of rights for each village, detailing survey numbers and other particulars.

key_sections.title: Accrual of rights of landowners.
key_sections.description: Grants ownership rights to persons holding land from the Government for agricultural purposes at the Act's commencement, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Rights of landowners.
key_sections.description: Outlines the rights of landowners, including permanent, heritable, and transferable rights, and the entitlement to make improvements and plant trees.

key_sections.title: Interest of tenants.
key_sections.description: Declares the interest of a tenant in land as heritable but generally non-transferable, and prohibits eviction except as provided by the Act.

key_sections.title: Maximum rent.
key_sections.description: Sets limits on the rent payable by a tenant, specifying proportions of produce or multiples of land revenue.

key_sections.title: Eviction of tenant.
key_sections.description: Lists the specific grounds under which a tenant may be evicted from land, such as reservation for personal cultivation or failure to pay rent.

key_sections.title: Transfer of ownership of land to tenant.
key_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of ownership of non-resumable land from the landowner to the tenant, making the tenant the owner liable for land revenue.

key_sections.title: Ceiling on holdings.
key_sections.description: Establishes a ceiling limit on land holdings for individuals and families, with provisions for additional acreage based on family size.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of civil courts excluded.
key_sections.description: Excludes the jurisdiction of civil courts over matters arising under the Act, unless expressly provided, with an exception for title disputes.

key_sections.title: Act to override contract and other laws.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any contrary provisions in other laws, customs, usages, agreements, or court orders.
