act_identification.act_title: THE DELHI PRIMARY EDUCATION ACT, 1960

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for free and compulsory Primary education for children in the Union territory of Delhi.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish free and compulsory primary education for children residing in the Union territory of Delhi. It outlines the duties of local authorities and parents to ensure children attend approved schools and provides for enforcement mechanisms.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its application to the Union territory of Delhi, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'child', 'approved school', 'local authority', and 'primary education'.

key_sections.title: Schemes for primary education.
key_sections.description: Mandates local authorities to provide for compulsory primary education and submit schemes to the State Government for sanction.

key_sections.title: Primary education to be compulsory in areas covered by schemes.
key_sections.description: Requires local authorities to declare primary education compulsory in specified areas upon sanction of a scheme.

key_sections.title: Responsibility of parent to cause his child to attend school.
key_sections.description: Places the duty on parents to ensure their child attends an approved school, unless there is a reasonable excuse.

key_sections.title: Reasonable excuse for non-attendance.
key_sections.description: Lists circumstances that are considered reasonable excuses for a child's non-attendance at an approved school.

key_sections.title: Attendance orders.
key_sections.description: Empowers attendance authorities to issue orders directing parents to cause their child to attend an approved school if there is no reasonable excuse for non-attendance.

key_sections.title: Children not to be employed so as to prevent them from attending school.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the employment of children in a manner that prevents them from attending an approved school.

key_sections.title: Primary education to be free.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that no fee shall be levied for attending approved schools managed by the State Government or a local authority, and ensures free education in private approved schools under attendance orders.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of section 13.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for parents failing to comply with attendance orders or to furnish required information.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of section 14.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for persons contravening the prohibition on employing children to prevent school attendance.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, covering various aspects of implementation.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Punjab Primary Education Act.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Punjab Primary Education Act, 1940, in areas where primary education becomes compulsory under this Act.

powers_conferred: State Government: to sanction schemes, determine cost sharing for schemes, call upon local authorities to submit schemes, appoint persons to prepare/implement schemes, make rules, and delegate powers.

Local authority: to provide for compulsory primary education, prepare schemes, give effect to sanctioned schemes, prepare and revise lists of children, appoint attendance authorities, and take steps to ensure free education.

Attendance authority: to put questions and require information from parents, notify parents of their obligations, require children to attend special schools, hold inquiries, and pass attendance orders.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Parents failing to comply with an attendance order under section 13 are punishable with a fine not exceeding two rupees, and an additional fine of fifty naye paise per day for continuing contravention, with a yearly maximum of fifty rupees per child. Failure to furnish information under section 13(4) incurs a fine up to twenty-five rupees. Any person contravening section 14 (employing a child to prevent school attendance) is punishable with a fine up to twenty-five rupees, and an additional fine of one rupee per day for continuing contravention.

repealed_acts: Punjab Primary Education Act, 1940 (Punjab Act XVIII of 1940)
related_acts: Delhi Panchayat Raj Act, 1954 (Delhi Act III of 1955)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The local authority may appoint attendance authorities. The State Government may appoint any person to prepare or give effect to a scheme if a local authority fails to do so.

applies_to: children in the Union territory of Delhi
children ordinarily resident within the jurisdiction of a local authority
children within a specified age group (not less than six or more than fourteen)
exemptions: Children for whom there is no approved school within the prescribed distance from residence.
Children receiving satisfactory instruction in some other manner.
Children who have completed primary education up to the specified class or standard.
Children suffering from a physical or mental defect preventing attendance.
Children with other compelling circumstances certified by the attendance authority.
special_provisions: Provision for special schools for physically or mentally deficient children.
Provision for part-time education in certain cases due to economic or family circumstances.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Local authorities prepare and implement schemes for compulsory primary education. Attendance authorities are appointed to notify parents, issue attendance orders, and ensure compliance. Offences are tried by competent courts, and penalties are prescribed for non-compliance with attendance orders or employment prohibitions.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Panchayati Adalat (in rural areas to which the Delhi Panchayat Raj Act, 1954 extends) and the court of a magistrate having jurisdiction (in other areas).

act_identification.act_short_title: The Tripura Land Revenue and Land Reforms Act, 1960

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to land revenue in the Union territory of Tripura and to provide for the acquisition of estates and for certain other measures of land reform.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend existing laws concerning land revenue in the Union territory of Tripura. It also provides for the acquisition of estates and introduces various land reform measures.

CHAPTER VII.—REALISATION OF LAND REVENUE AND OTHER PUBLIC DEMANDS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application to the Union territory of Tripura, and that its commencement date will be appointed by notification.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Administrator', 'agriculture', 'Collector', 'raiyat', 'under-raiyat', and 'personal cultivation'.

key_sections.title: Title of Government to lands, etc.
key_sections.description: Declares that all unowned lands, public roads, water bodies, and rights therein are the property of the Government, including mines and minerals.

key_sections.title: Unauthorised occupation of land.
key_sections.description: Defines unauthorized occupation as trespass, allowing summary eviction and forfeiture of constructions, with penalties recoverable as land revenue arrears.

key_sections.title: Liability of land to land revenue.
key_sections.description: States that all lands are liable to land revenue, with the Administrator having power to grant exemptions.

key_sections.title: Preparation of record of rights.
key_sections.description: Mandates the preparation of a record of rights for each village by the survey officer, detailing survey numbers and other particulars.

key_sections.title: Land revenue to be first charge.
key_sections.description: Establishes land revenue as the primary charge on land, crops, rents, and profits.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Outlines the hierarchy and process for filing appeals against orders passed by various revenue officers.

key_sections.title: Rights of raiyats.
key_sections.description: Declares the rights of raiyats in their land as permanent, heritable, and transferable, including rights to make improvements and plant trees.

key_sections.title: “Permissible limit” defined.
key_sections.description: Defines the maximum area of land a raiyat may resume from under-raiyats for personal cultivation, varying based on disability and existing holdings.

key_sections.title: Maximum rent.
key_sections.description: Sets the maximum rent payable by an under-raiyat, either as a share of produce or a multiple of land revenue.

key_sections.title: Transfer of ownership of land to under-raiyats.
key_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of ownership of non-resumable land from raiyats to under-raiyats, making the under-raiyat the owner liable for land revenue.

key_sections.title: Notification vesting estates in the State.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Administrator to declare that estates and intermediary rights therein shall vest in the Government, free from encumbrances.

key_sections.title: Compensation payable to intermediary.
key_sections.description: Specifies the formula for calculating compensation payable to intermediaries based on a multiple of their net income from the estate.

key_sections.title: Ceilings on holdings.
key_sections.description: Imposes a ceiling limit on land holdings for individuals and families, generally 25 standard acres, with provisions for larger families.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of civil courts excluded.
key_sections.description: Excludes the jurisdiction of civil courts over matters arising under this Act, unless expressly provided, with an exception for questions of title.

key_sections.title: Act to over-ride contracts and other laws.
key_sections.description: States that the Act's provisions shall prevail over contrary provisions in other laws, customs, usages, agreements, or court orders.

act_identification.act_title: THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS ACT, 1960
act_identification.act_short_title: THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS ACT, 1960

act_overview.preamble: An Act to prevent the infliction of unnecessary pain or suffering on animals and for that purpose to amend the law relating to the prevention of cruelty to animals.
act_overview.purpose: The primary objective of this Act is to prevent the infliction of unnecessary pain or suffering upon animals. It also serves to amend the existing legal framework concerning the prevention of cruelty to animals.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II ANIMAL WELFARE BOARD OF INDIA
CHAPTER III CRUELTY TO ANIMALS GENERALLY

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its geographical application to the whole of India, and that its commencement date will be appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'animal', 'Board', 'captive animal', and 'domestic animal'.

key_sections.title: Duties of persons having charge of animals.
key_sections.description: Establishes the duty of every person caring for an animal to ensure its well-being and prevent unnecessary pain or suffering.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Animals Welfare Board of India.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of the Animal Welfare Board of India by the Central Government for the promotion of animal welfare.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the various functions of the Animal Welfare Board, including advising the Government, encouraging animal welfare activities, and providing veterinary assistance.

key_sections.title: Treating animals cruelly.
key_sections.description: Defines various acts of cruelty towards animals and prescribes penalties for such offences.

key_sections.title: Penalty for practising phooka or doom dev.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for performing or permitting the operation of 'phooka' or 'doom dev' on milch animals.

key_sections.title: Experiments on animals.
key_sections.description: States that experiments on animals for scientific advancement are not unlawful under this Act, provided they are for specific beneficial purposes.

key_sections.title: Committee for control and supervision of experiments on animals.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a Committee by the Central Government to control and supervise experiments on animals.

key_sections.title: Restriction on exhibition and training of performing animals.
key_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on the exhibition and training of performing animals, requiring registration and prohibiting certain animals from being used.

key_sections.title: Saving as respects manner of killing prescribed by religion.
key_sections.description: Exempts the killing of animals in a manner required by the religion of any community from being considered an offence under this Act.

key_sections.title: Power of court to deprive person convicted of ownership of animal.
key_sections.description: Grants courts the power to forfeit an animal to the Government and prohibit a convicted person from having custody of animals.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, covering various aspects of animal welfare and treatment.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Act 11 of 1890.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines various offences related to cruelty to animals, including beating, overloading, employing unfit animals, administering injurious drugs, improper confinement, neglect, abandonment, mutilation, animal fighting, and unapproved exhibition/training of performing animals. Penalties range from fines (e.g., Rs. 10-50 for first cruelty offence, up to Rs. 1000 for phooka) to imprisonment (up to 3 months for repeat cruelty offences or performing animal offences, up to 2 years for phooka), or both. Animals involved in 'phooka' may be forfeited to the Government. Contravention of Committee orders or rules made under the Act also carries penalties.

The Board and the Committee have powers to appoint their respective officers and employees.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government has the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (S.38). The Animal Welfare Board of India can make regulations for its affairs (S.10), and the Committee for control and supervision of experiments on animals can make rules relating to experiments (S.17). The State Government also has power to make rules (Maharashtra Act 45 of 2017, S.38B).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement involves penalties for various acts of cruelty, powers of search and seizure by police officers and authorized persons, and the issuance of search warrants by magistrates. Courts can order the destruction of suffering animals, deprive convicted persons of animal ownership, and prohibit them from having custody of animals. The Act also provides for the establishment of infirmaries for the treatment and care of animals involved in offences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrates (including First or Second Class, Presidency, Sub-divisional) and general 'courts' are competent to hear cases, issue orders for destruction, prohibit activities, and impose penalties under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE ACQUIRED TERRITORIES (MERGER) ACT, 1960

legislative_details.geographical_extent: States of Assam, Punjab and West Bengal, and the territories acquired from Pakistan that are merged into these states

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the merger into the States of Assam, Punjab and West Bengal of certain territories acquired in pursuance of the agreements entered into between the Governments of India and Pakistan and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the merger of certain territories, acquired through agreements between India and Pakistan, into the Indian States of Assam, Punjab, and West Bengal. It also addresses related matters concerning these mergers, including administration, property, and laws.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Acquired Territories (Merger) Act, 1960.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'acquired territories', 'appointed day', and 'Indo-Pakistan agreements'.

key_sections.title: Merger of acquired territories.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that acquired territories will be included in and form part of the States of Assam, Punjab, and West Bengal from the appointed day, and provides for their administration.

key_sections.title: Amendment of the First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Mandates amendments to the First Schedule of the Constitution to reflect the inclusion of the acquired territories into the States of Assam, Punjab, and West Bengal.

key_sections.title: Construction of references to existing constituencies.
key_sections.description: Provides how references to existing parliamentary, assembly, and council constituencies in various delimitation orders shall be construed after the merger of acquired territories.

key_sections.title: Provisions as to sitting members.
key_sections.description: Ensures that sitting members of Parliament and State Legislatures whose constituencies are altered due to the Act are deemed to have been elected to the altered constituencies.

key_sections.title: Property and assets.
key_sections.description: Specifies that property and assets within the acquired territories, previously vested in Pakistan, shall vest in the Union or the State concerned, depending on their purpose.

key_sections.title: Appropriation of moneys for expenditure in acquired territories.
key_sections.description: Allows for the appropriation of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of the State concerned for expenditure in the acquired territories and permits the Governor to authorize interim expenditure.

key_sections.title: Extension of laws.
key_sections.description: Declares that laws in force in the acquired territories shall cease to be in force, and laws of the State concerned shall extend to these territories from the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Power to name authorities for exercising statutory functions.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government concerned the power to specify authorities, officers, or persons competent to exercise statutory functions in the acquired territories.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government and the State Government concerned to make orders to remove difficulties arising from the transition of laws or the administration of acquired territories.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint the 'appointed day' for merger (Section 2(b))

Central Government: To make orders to remove difficulties in relation to the transition of laws (Section 11(1))
State Government concerned: To provide for the administration of acquired territories (Section 3(2))

State Government concerned: To specify authorities, officers, or persons for exercising statutory functions (Section 10)
State Government concerned: To make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act or in administration (Section 11(2))

act_identification.act_title: THE ADVOCATES ACT, 1961

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend and consolidate the law relating to the legal practitioners and to provide for the constitution of Bar Councils and an All-India Bar.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to amend and consolidate the law governing legal practitioners in India. It also provides for the establishment and constitution of Bar Councils at both state and all-India levels to regulate the legal profession.

chapter_titles:
CHAPTER III
ADMISSION AND ENROLMENT OF ADVOCATES

CHAPTER VII
TEMPORARY AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its geographical extent to the whole of India, and that different provisions may come into force on different dates.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'advocate', 'Bar Council', 'High Court', and 'legal practitioner'.

key_sections.title: State Bar Councils.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of State Bar Councils for various states and Union territories, outlining their composition including ex officio and elected members.

key_sections.title: Bar Council of India.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Bar Council of India, detailing its composition with ex officio members like the Attorney-General and Solicitor-General, and elected members from State Bar Councils.

key_sections.title: Functions of State Bar Councils.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the responsibilities of State Bar Councils, including admitting advocates, maintaining rolls, handling misconduct cases, promoting law reform, and providing legal aid.

key_sections.title: Functions of Bar Council of India.
key_sections.description: Outlines the functions of the Bar Council of India, such as laying down professional conduct standards, supervising State Bar Councils, promoting legal education, and recognising law degrees.

key_sections.title: Senior and other advocates.
key_sections.description: Classifies advocates into senior advocates and other advocates, and specifies the criteria for designation as a senior advocate by the Supreme Court or a High Court.

key_sections.title: State Bar Councils to maintain roll of advocates.
key_sections.description: Requires every State Bar Council to prepare and maintain a roll of advocates, categorised into senior and other advocates, with provisions for seniority determination.

key_sections.title: Persons who may be admitted as advocates on a State roll.
key_sections.description: Sets out the qualifications required for a person to be admitted as an advocate on a State roll, including citizenship, age, law degree, and payment of fees.

key_sections.title: Advocates to be the only recognised class of persons entitled to practise law.
key_sections.description: Declares that advocates are the sole recognised class of persons entitled to practise law from the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Right of advocates to practise.
key_sections.description: Grants every advocate whose name is on the State roll the right to practise in all courts, tribunals, and before any legally authorised person or authority throughout India.

key_sections.title: Punishment of advocates for misconduct.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Bar Councils to refer cases of professional or other misconduct by advocates to disciplinary committees, which can reprimand, suspend, or remove an advocate from the roll.

key_sections.title: Appeal to the Supreme Court.
key_sections.description: Allows any person aggrieved by an order of the disciplinary committee of the Bar Council of India to appeal to the Supreme Court within sixty days.

key_sections.title: Penalty for persons illegally practising in courts and before other authorities.
key_sections.description: Prescribes imprisonment for up to six months for any person who illegally practises in courts or before authorities without being entitled to do so under the Act.

key_sections.title: General power of the Bar Council of India to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers general rule-making power on the Bar Council of India for discharging its functions, covering aspects like voting conditions, professional conduct, legal education standards, and fees.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who practises in any court or before any authority or person without being entitled to do so under this Act shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months (Section 45). An advocate found guilty of professional or other misconduct may be reprimanded, suspended from practice for a period, or have their name removed from the State roll of advocates (Section 35). implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through disciplinary committees of State Bar Councils and the Bar Council of India, which investigate and punish professional misconduct (Sections 35, 36). The Bar Council of India exercises general supervision and control over State Bar Councils (Section 48B).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Supreme Court (for appeals and rule-making), High Courts (for rule-making, sanction for attendance of presiding officers, execution of costs orders), Civil courts (for enforcing process of disciplinary committees), District Judge, Sessions Judge, District Magistrate, and Revenue-officer (for framing tout lists).

schedules_summary.description: Lists specific enactments that are repealed by this Act, including The Legal Practitioners (Women) Act, 1923; The Legal Practitioners (Fees) Act, 1926; Section 53 of The States Reorganisation Act, 1956; and Section 31 of The Bombay Reorganisation Act, 1960.

act_identification.act_title: THE DOWRY PROHIBITION ACT, 1961

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Twelfth Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to prohibit the giving or taking of dowry.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to prohibit the practice of giving or taking dowry. It aims to prevent the exchange of property or valuable security in connection with marriage and to ensure that any dowry received benefits the wife or her heirs.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its application to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definition of “dowry”.
key_sections.description: Defines 'dowry' as any property or valuable security given or agreed to be given in connection with a marriage, excluding dower or mahr under Muslim Personal Law.

key_sections.title: Penalty for giving or taking dowry.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for giving, taking, or abetting dowry, with imprisonment for not less than five years and a fine.

key_sections.title: Penalty for demanding dowry.
key_sections.description: Stipulates punishment for demanding dowry, directly or indirectly, from parents, relatives, or guardians of a bride or bridegroom.

key_sections.title: Ban on advertisement.
key_sections.description: Prohibits advertisements offering property, money, or business interests as consideration for marriage and prescribes penalties for such acts.

key_sections.title: Agreement for giving or taking dowry to be void.
key_sections.description: Declares any agreement for the giving or taking of dowry to be void.

key_sections.title: Dowry to be for the benefit of the wife or her heirs.
key_sections.description: Mandates that any dowry received by a person other than the woman must be transferred to her within a specified period, or to her heirs if she dies.

key_sections.title: Cognizance of offences.
key_sections.description: Specifies which courts can try offences under the Act and the conditions under which a court can take cognizance of such offences.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable for certain purposes and to be bailable and non-compoundable.
key_sections.description: States that offences under this Act are cognizable for investigation purposes, non-bailable, and non-compoundable.

key_sections.title: Dowry Prohibition Officers.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of Dowry Prohibition Officers by the State Government and outlines their powers and functions.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of the State Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, particularly concerning Dowry Prohibition Officers.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to appoint the date of commencement of the Act (Section 1(3)).
Central Government: Power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 9).
State Government: Power to appoint Dowry Prohibition Officers and specify their jurisdiction and powers (Section 8B(1)).
State Government: Power to confer police officer powers on Dowry Prohibition Officers (Section 8B(3)).
State Government: Power to appoint an advisory board to assist Dowry Prohibition Officers (Section 8B(4)).
State Government: Power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 10).
Dowry Prohibition Officers: Power to ensure compliance with the Act, prevent dowry, collect evidence, and perform additional functions (Section 8B(2)).
Courts (Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class): Power to try offences and pass sentences under the Act (Section 7(1)(a), (c)).
Courts: Power to direct the transfer of property to the woman or her heirs/parents/children if not transferred before conviction (Section 6(3A)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines several offences: giving or taking dowry (Section 3), demanding dowry (Section 4), advertising for dowry (Section 4A), and failing to transfer dowry to the woman or her heirs (Section 6(2)). Penalties include imprisonment ranging from not less than six months up to five years, and fines ranging from five thousand rupees up to fifteen thousand rupees or the value of the dowry, whichever is more. Courts may impose lesser sentences for adequate and special reasons.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government has the power to appoint Dowry Prohibition Officers and members of the advisory board.

applies_to: Whole of India
Any person who gives, takes, or abets the giving or taking of dowry
Any person who demands dowry
Any person who advertises for dowry
exemptions: Dower or mahr in the case of persons to whom the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) applies.

Presents given at the time of marriage to the bride or bridegroom without any demand, provided they are entered in a list maintained under the rules and, if from the bride's side, are customary and not excessive.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government and the State Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the appointment of Dowry Prohibition Officers who ensure compliance, prevent dowry, and collect evidence. Offences are cognizable for investigation purposes. Courts take cognizance based on police reports or complaints from aggrieved persons or recognized welfare organizations. Penalties are prescribed for various offences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No Court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class.

act_identification.act_title: THE MOTOR TRANSPORT WORKERS ACT, 1961
act_identification.date_of_commencement: such date not being later than the 31st day of March, 1962, as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint and different dates may be appointed for different States

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the welfare of motor transport workers and to regulate the conditions of their work.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to ensure the welfare of motor transport workers by establishing regulations concerning their working conditions, including hours of work, rest intervals, and facilities. It also provides for the registration of motor transport undertakings and enforcement mechanisms.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical extent, commencement date, and to which undertakings it applies.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'adolescent', 'employer', 'motor transport undertaking', and 'motor transport worker'.

key_sections.title: Registration of motor transport undertaking.
key_sections.description: Mandates the registration of motor transport undertakings under this Act and outlines the application process.

key_sections.title: Chief inspector and inspectors.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to appoint a Chief Inspector and Inspectors for the State to enforce the Act.

key_sections.title: Powers of the inspectors.
key_sections.description: Details the powers of inspectors, including examination, inquiry, entry, inspection, search, and seizure of documents.

key_sections.title: Canteens.
key_sections.description: Allows the State Government to make rules requiring employers to provide and maintain canteens for workers in certain undertakings.

key_sections.title: Medical facilities.
key_sections.description: Requires employers to provide and maintain readily available medical facilities for motor transport workers at operating centers and halting stations.

key_sections.title: Hours of work for adult motor transport workers.
key_sections.description: Sets limits on daily and weekly working hours for adult motor transport workers, with provisions for exceptions.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of employment of children.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the employment of children in any capacity in motor transport undertakings.

key_sections.title: Act 4 of 1936 to apply to payment of wages to motor transport workers.
key_sections.description: Extends the applicability of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, to motor transport workers.

key_sections.title: Extra wages for overtime.
key_sections.description: Stipulates the rates for extra wages payable to motor transport workers for overtime work or work on rest days.

key_sections.title: Annual leave with wages.
key_sections.description: Provides for annual leave with wages for motor transport workers based on their period of work.

key_sections.title: Obstructions.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for obstructing inspectors or refusing to provide facilities or documents.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Addresses the liability of companies and their responsible persons for offences committed under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, specifying various aspects that can be covered by such rules.

powers_conferred: State Government: Appoint Chief Inspector and Inspectors (Section 4)
State Government: Declare local limits for inspectors' powers (Section 4)
Chief Inspector/Inspector: Make examination and inquiry, require transport vehicle to stop (Section 5)
Chief Inspector/Inspector: Enter, inspect, and search premises (Section 5)
Chief Inspector/Inspector: Examine motor transport workers, require production of documents, take statements (Section 5)
Chief Inspector/Inspector: Seize or take copy of registers or documents (Section 5)
State Government: Appoint qualified medical practitioners as certifying surgeons (Section 7)
State Government: Make rules requiring provision and maintenance of canteens (Section 8)
State Government: Delegate power to Chief Inspector to make rules for canteen foodstuffs and charges (Section 8)
State Government: Prescribe standards for rest rooms or alternative accommodation (Section 9)
State Government: Make rules requiring employers to provide uniforms, raincoats, or other amenities (Section 10)
State Government: Prescribe medical facilities for motor transport workers (Section 11)
Central Government: Give directions to State Governments regarding implementation of the Act (Section 39)
State Government: Make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (Section 40)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines offences such as obstructing inspectors, using false certificates of fitness, contravening provisions regarding employment of motor transport workers, and other wilful disobedience or contraventions. Penalties include imprisonment ranging from one month to six months, or fines ranging from fifty rupees to one thousand rupees, or both. Continuing contraventions may incur additional daily fines. Enhanced penalties apply for repeat offenders, and provisions are made for offences committed by companies.

amended_acts: Act 51 of 1970 (Central Labour Laws (Extension to Jammu and Kashmir) Act, 1970)
Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Adaptation of Central Laws) Order, 2020
Union Territory of Ladakh Reorganisation (Adaptation of Central Laws) Order, 2020

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government has the power to appoint the Chief Inspector, Inspectors, and Certifying Surgeons.

applies_to: Every motor transport undertaking employing five or more motor transport workers
exemptions: Transport vehicles used for the transport of sick or injured persons
Transport vehicles used for any purpose connected with the security of India, or the security of a State, or the maintenance of public order
Motor transport workers holding positions of supervision or management (by State Government notification)
Part-time motor transport workers (by State Government notification)
Any class of employers (by State Government notification)
special_provisions: The State Government may, by notification, apply all or any provisions of this Act to any motor transport undertaking employing less than five motor transport workers.
The Act came into force in the State of Jammu and Kashmir on the commencement of the Central Labour Laws (Extension to Jammu and Kashmir) Act, 1970.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The State Government, and the Chief Inspector (under delegation for specific canteen rules).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a system of Chief Inspectors and Inspectors who have powers to examine, inquire, inspect, search, and seize documents. Contraventions are subject to penalties, and offences by companies are also addressed.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Presidency magistrate or a magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE DELHI (URBAN AREAS) TENANTS’ RELIEF ACT, 1961

legislative_details.geographical_extent: areas in the Union territory of Delhi which, immediately before the 1st day of November, 1956, were included in a municipality or in a notified area under the provisions of the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911 (Punjab Act 3 of 1911), or in a cantonment under the provisions of the Cantonments Act, 1924 (2 of 1924)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide relief to the tenants of land in the urban areas of the Union territory of Delhi.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to provide relief to tenants of land in urban areas of the Union territory of Delhi by defining grounds for their ejectment, providing for the abatement of certain pending proceedings, and enabling the restoration of land to tenants in specific circumstances.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'Chief Commissioner,' 'family,' 'land-holder,' 'person under disability,' 'tenant,' and 'tenancy'.

key_sections.title: Grounds of ejectment of tenant.
key_sections.description: Specifies the limited grounds on which a tenant can be ejected from land, including non-payment of rent, failure to cultivate, sub-letting, or misuse of land. It also includes special grounds for religious/charitable institutions and persons under disability.

key_sections.title: Abatement of proceedings.
key_sections.description: States that certain pending ejectment proceedings that would be inconsistent with this Act shall abate upon its commencement.

key_sections.title: Restoration of land to tenant in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Provides for the restoration of land to a tenant if a land-holder (person under disability or institution) fails to use the land for the stated purpose after ejectment, or for tenants ejected before the Act's commencement under conditions inconsistent with the Act.

key_sections.title: Rent.
key_sections.description: Caps the rent payable by a tenant at one-fifth of the produce or its money equivalent, or the agreed lower rent.

key_sections.title: Act to override contracts, etc.
key_sections.description: Declares that the Act's provisions generally override other laws, customs, agreements, or court orders.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Chief Commissioner the authority to make rules for implementing the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal.
key_sections.description: Repeals inconsistent provisions of certain other tenancy acts as they apply to the areas covered by this Act.

powers_conferred: Chief Commissioner to appoint commencement date
Chief Commissioner to specify officer for restoration of land
Chief Commissioner to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act
Officer specified by Chief Commissioner to restore possession of land

repealed_acts: Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887
Agra Tenancy U.P. Act, 1901
Punjab Tenants (Security of Tenure) Act, 1950
related_acts: Agra Tenancy Act, 1901 (U.P. Act II of 1901)

applies_to: areas in the Union territory of Delhi which, immediately before the 1st day of November, 1956, were included in a municipality or in a notified area under the provisions of the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911 (Punjab Act 3 of 1911), or in a cantonment under the provisions of the Cantonments Act, 1924 (2 of 1924)
exemptions: areas owned by the Central Government
areas owned by the Delhi Development Authority constituted under the Delhi Development Act, 1957 (61 of 1957)
areas owned by any local authority
special_provisions: Definitions of 'land' and 'tenant' for areas to which the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887, applies, are from that Act.
Definitions of 'land' and 'tenant' for areas to which the Agra Tenancy Act, 1901, applies, are from that Act.
Special grounds for ejectment and restoration of land for 'person under disability' and 'religious or charitable institution'.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act defines specific grounds for ejectment of tenants and provides for the abatement of certain pending ejectment proceedings. It also outlines conditions for the restoration of land to tenants in cases of improper ejectment.

act_identification.act_title: THE UNION TERRITORIES (STAMP AND COURT-FEES LAWS) ACT, 1961
act_identification.act_short_title: Union Territories (Stamp and Court-fees Laws) Act, 1961

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Union territory of Himachal Pradesh, Union territory of Manipur, Union territory of Tripura

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the amendment and repeal of certain laws relating to stamp duties and court-fees as in force in certain Union territories.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to amend and repeal existing laws related to stamp duties and court-fees in the Union territories of Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, and Tripura. It facilitates the substitution or repeal of local versions of these laws with those in force in neighboring states like Punjab and Assam, and validates past stamp duty collections in Manipur.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Union Territories (Stamp and Court-fees Laws) Act, 1961.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Indian Stamp Act, 1899, as in force in Himachal Pradesh.
key_sections.description: Provides for the substitution of Schedule I-A of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, in Himachal Pradesh with the Punjab version, on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Court-fees Act, 1870, as in force in Himachal Pradesh.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Court-fees Act, 1870, in Himachal Pradesh upon the extension of the Punjab version of the Act to that Union territory.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Court-fees Act, 1870, as in force in Manipur and Tripura.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Court-fees Act, 1870, in Manipur and Tripura upon the extension of the Assam version of the Act to those Union territories.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Indian Stamp Act, 1899, as in force in Manipur and Tripura.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, in Manipur and Tripura upon the extension of the Assam version of the Act to those Union territories.

key_sections.title: Validation of levy of stamp duties in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Validates stamp duties levied and collected in Manipur between April 16, 1950, and the date of extension of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (Assam version), deeming them to have been lawfully collected.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint a date for the substitution of Schedule I-A of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, in Himachal Pradesh (Section 2).
Central Government: To extend the Court-fees Act, 1870, to Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, and Tripura by notification under section 2 of the Union Territories (Laws) Act, 1950 (Sections 3, 4).
Central Government: To extend the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, to Manipur and Tripura by notification under section 2 of the Union Territories (Laws) Act, 1950 (Section 5).

repealed_acts: Court-fees Act, 1870 (7 of 1870)
Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (2 of 1899)

applies_to: Union territory of Himachal Pradesh
Union territory of Manipur
Union territory of Tripura
special_provisions: Validation of stamp duties levied in the Union territory of Manipur during the period commencing on the 16th day of April, 1950, and ending on the date on which the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (as in force in Assam) is extended to that Union territory (Section 6).

act_identification.act_title: THE DADRA AND NAGAR HAVELI ACT, 1961
act_identification.act_short_title: the Dadra and Nagar Haveli Act, 1961

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Twelfth Year of the Republic of India
legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of the Union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make provision for the representation of the Union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli in Parliament and for the administration of that Union territory and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the representation of the Union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli in the House of the People and establishes provisions for its administration. It also addresses related matters concerning the territory's governance and legal framework.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its geographical extent, and the date from which it is deemed to have come into force.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used within the Act, such as 'Administrator', 'appointed day', 'Dadra and Nagar Haveli', and 'Varishta Panchayat'.

key_sections.title: Representation in the House of the People.
key_sections.description: Allots one seat to the Union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli in the House of the People and amends the Representation of the People Acts of 1950 and 1951 accordingly.

key_sections.title: Varishta Panchayat.
key_sections.description: Grants the Varishta Panchayat the right to discuss and make advisory recommendations to the Administrator on administrative and development matters, and prescribes an oath for its members.

key_sections.title: Other functionaries.
key_sections.description: Ensures the continuance of existing judges, magistrates, and other officers exercising lawful functions in Dadra and Nagar Haveli until new provisions are made.

key_sections.title: Property and assets.
key_sections.description: Declares that all property and assets previously vested in the Varishta Panchayat or Administrator of Free Dadra and Nagar Haveli shall vest in the Union from the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Rights and obligations.
key_sections.description: Transfers all rights, liabilities, and obligations of the Varishta Panchayat or Administrator of Free Dadra and Nagar Haveli to the Central Government from the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Continuance of existing laws.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that all laws in force in Free Dadra and Nagar Haveli before the appointed day shall continue until repealed or amended by Parliament or competent authority.

key_sections.title: Continuance of existing taxes.
key_sections.description: Ensures the continued levy and application of all existing taxes, duties, cesses, or fees until new provisions are made by Parliament or competent authority.

key_sections.title: Power to extend enactments to Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to extend any enactment in force in a State to Dadra and Nagar Haveli, with restrictions or modifications, via notification.

key_sections.title: Extension of the jurisdiction of Bombay High Court to Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
key_sections.description: Provides for the extension of the jurisdiction of the High Court at Bombay to Dadra and Nagar Haveli from a date specified by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Powers of courts and other authorities for purposes of facilitating the application of laws.
key_sections.description: Authorizes courts and other authorities to construe laws with necessary alterations to adapt them for application in Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove any difficulties arising in giving effect to the Act's provisions or in the administration of Dadra and Nagar Haveli, with retrospective effect.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including matters related to the Varishta Panchayat.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to appoint officers and authorities for administration (Section 5)
Central Government: to extend enactments to Dadra and Nagar Haveli (Section 10)
Central Government: to specify date for extension of Bombay High Court jurisdiction (Section 11)
Central Government: to remove difficulties in implementing the Act (Section 13)
Central Government: to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (Section 14)
Varishta Panchayat: right to discuss and make recommendations to the Administrator (Section 4)
Courts or other authorities: to construe laws with alterations for application in Dadra and Nagar Haveli (Section 12)

amended_acts: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
Representation of the People Act, 1951 (43 of 1951)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (to appoint officers and authorities for administration)

applies_to: the Union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli

implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court at Bombay

key_definitions: company in which the public are substantially interested
person who has a substantial interest in the company

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official title, geographical applicability, and effective date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Charge of income-tax.
key_sections.description: Establishes the chargeability of income-tax on total income for each assessment year.

key_sections.title: Scope of total income.
key_sections.description: Defines what constitutes the total income for residents and non-residents, including income received, accrued, or deemed to accrue in India or outside India.

key_sections.title: Residence in India.
key_sections.description: Lays down criteria for determining the residential status of individuals, Hindu undivided families, firms, companies, and other persons for tax purposes.

key_sections.title: Income deemed to accrue or arise in India.
key_sections.description: Specifies categories of income that are deemed to accrue or arise in India, regardless of where they are actually received.

key_sections.title: Incomes not included in total income.
key_sections.description: Lists various incomes that are exempt from being included in the total income for tax computation.

key_sections.title: Income from property held for charitable or religious purposes.
key_sections.description: Provides for exemptions for income derived from property held under trust for charitable or religious purposes, subject to certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Heads of income.
key_sections.description: Classifies all income into specific heads for the purpose of charge of income-tax and computation of total income.

key_sections.title: Salaries.
key_sections.description: Defines what income is chargeable under the head 'Salaries'.

key_sections.title: Income from house property.
key_sections.description: Specifies that the annual value of property owned by the assessee, other than for business use, is chargeable under this head.

key_sections.title: Profits and gains of business or profession.
key_sections.description: Defines various types of income chargeable under the head 'Profits and gains of business or profession'.

key_sections.title: Depreciation.
key_sections.description: Allows deductions for depreciation on tangible and intangible assets used for business or profession.

key_sections.title: Expenditure on scientific research.
key_sections.description: Provides for deductions for expenditure incurred on scientific research, including capital and revenue expenditure, and payments to research institutions.

key_sections.title: Other deductions.
key_sections.description: Lists various other deductions allowed in computing income from business or profession, such as insurance premiums, bonus, interest on capital, and bad debts.

key_sections.title: General.
key_sections.description: Allows deduction for any expenditure (not capital or personal) laid out wholly and exclusively for business or profession, if not covered by specific sections.

key_sections.title: Amounts not deductible.
key_sections.description: Specifies certain amounts that are not deductible in computing income from business or profession, such as certain interest, taxes, and payments to related parties.

key_sections.title: Profits chargeable to tax.
key_sections.description: Deems certain receipts or benefits as profits and gains chargeable to tax, especially those related to previous allowances or deductions.

key_sections.title: Definitions of certain terms relevant to income from profits and gains of business or profession.

act_identification.act_title: THE VOLUNTARY SURRENDER OF SALARIES (EXEMPTION FROM TAXATION) ACT, 1961

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for exempting from taxes on income a portion of the salary or allowances payable to any person who has in the public interest volunteered to forego it.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to provide income tax and super tax exemption for individuals who voluntarily surrender a portion of their salary or allowances in the public interest. This applies to salaries from the Consolidated Fund of India or a State, or those surrendered to the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Voluntary Surrender of Salaries (Exemption from Taxation) Act, 1961.

key_sections.title: Exemption from taxes on income in respect of salaries surrendered in favour of Government.
key_sections.description: Provides for exemption from income-tax or super-tax on salaries voluntarily foregone in the public interest, whether from Consolidated Funds or surrendered to the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Provisions of section 2 to apply to allowances.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.

key_sections.title: Repeal.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of a corporation for the purpose of insurance of deposits and guaranteeing of credit facilities and for other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes a corporation to provide insurance for deposits held in banks and to guarantee credit facilities. It also covers other related and incidental matters concerning the operation and management of this corporation.

chapter_titles: ESTABLISHMENT AND MANGEMENT OF THE DEPOSIT INSURANCE CORPORATION

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.

key_sections.title: Definition.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Deposit Insurance Corporation.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Deposit Insurance Corporation as a body corporate.

key_sections.title: Premium.
key_sections.description: Outlines the liability of insured banks to pay premium to the Corporation and rules for its calculation and payment.

key_sections.title: Liability of Corporation in respect of insured deposits.

key_sections.title: Manner of payment by Corporation in case of winding up of insured banks.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to give directions.

act_identification.act_title: THE APPRENTICES ACT, 1961
act_identification.date_of_commencement: such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint; and different dates may be appointed for different States

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the regulation and control of training of apprentices and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate and control the training of apprentices across various trades and industries. It establishes a framework for apprenticeship contracts, training standards, and the rights and obligations of both employers and apprentices.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II APPRENTICES AND THEIR TRAINING

key_definitions: Board or State Council of Technical Education

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical reach, effective date, and conditions under which it applies or does not apply to certain areas, industries, or schemes.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'apprentice', 'designated trade', 'employer', 'establishment', and various councils and advisers.

key_sections.title: Qualifications for being engaged as an apprentice.
key_sections.description: Outlines the minimum age and other standards of education and physical fitness required for a person to be engaged as an apprentice.

key_sections.title: Reservation of training places for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes in designated trades.
key_sections.description: Mandates employers to reserve training places for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in designated trades, with numbers to be prescribed based on population.

key_sections.title: Contract of apprenticeship.
key_sections.description: Requires a contract of apprenticeship between the apprentice (or guardian) and the employer, detailing its commencement, terms, and registration process with the Apprenticeship Adviser.

key_sections.title: Termination of apprenticeship contract.
key_sections.description: Governs the termination of apprenticeship contracts, including termination upon expiry, by application to the Apprenticeship Adviser, and provisions for compensation or refund in case of breach.

key_sections.title: Number of apprentices for a designated trade.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to prescribe the number of apprentices an employer must engage for designated and optional trades, and allows employers to join together for training.

key_sections.title: Practical and basic training of apprentices.
key_sections.description: Obligates employers to arrange practical training, outlines inspection facilities, mandates basic training for certain trade apprentices, and specifies cost-sharing for training.

key_sections.title: Obligations of employers.
key_sections.description: Lists the duties of employers, including providing training, ensuring qualified instructional staff, and fulfilling contract obligations.

key_sections.title: Obligations of apprentices.
key_sections.description: Details the responsibilities of apprentices, such as diligent learning, regular attendance, obedience to lawful orders, and adherence to contract terms.

key_sections.title: Payment to apprentices.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that employers must pay apprentices a stipend at a rate not less than the prescribed minimum, and prohibits payment on a piece-work basis or participation in bonus schemes.

key_sections.title: Apprentices are trainees and not workers.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that apprentices are trainees, not workers, and that general labor laws do not apply to them, except as otherwise provided in this Act.

key_sections.title: Settlement of disputes.
key_sections.description: Establishes a mechanism for resolving disagreements or disputes between employers and apprentices by referring them to the Apprenticeship Adviser, with an appeal process to the Apprenticeship Council.

key_sections.title: Holding of test and grant of certificate and conclusion of training.
key_sections.description: Provides for trade apprentices to undergo tests conducted by the National Council or authorized agencies and receive certificates of proficiency upon successful completion, with similar provisions for graduate/technician apprentices.

key_sections.title: Offences and penalties.
key_sections.description: Defines various offenses, such as contravening the required number of apprentices, refusing information, obstructing inspection, or violating contract terms, and prescribes corresponding penalties.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including retrospective application and penalties for rule contraventions.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint commencement date, specify areas or industries for application, notify special apprenticeship schemes, specify designated trades, prescribe number of apprentices, approve syllabus and equipment for training, approve training programs, make rules.
State Government: Appoint commencement date, appoint State Apprenticeship Adviser, determine members of State Apprenticeship Council, delegate powers.

Apprenticeship Adviser: Verify and register contracts of apprenticeship, convey objections regarding contracts, approve novation of contracts, approve overtime work for apprentices, settle disputes between employer and apprentice, revise period or remuneration in employment offers.
Central Apprenticeship Adviser: Authorize other persons (not below Assistant Apprenticeship Adviser rank) for inspection, specify period for related instruction.
State Apprenticeship Adviser: Authorize other persons (not below Assistant Apprenticeship Adviser rank) for inspection.
Employer: Determine weekly and daily hours of work for apprentices (subject to training duration), formulate policy for recruiting apprentices after training.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: If an employer contravenes provisions relating to the number of apprentices, they receive a month's notice; failure to reply or unsatisfactory reasons lead to a fine of five hundred rupees per shortfall of apprenticeship month for the first three months, and one thousand rupees per month thereafter. Other offenses, such as refusing information, obstructing inspection, requiring unauthorized overtime, employing apprentices on unrelated work, paying piecework, involving in bonus schemes, engaging unqualified persons, or failing to carry out contract terms, are punishable with a fine of one thousand rupees for every occurrence. For contraventions where no specific penalty is provided, the fine shall not be less than one thousand rupees but may extend to three thousand rupees.

act_identification.act_title: THE MATERNITY BENEFIT ACT, 1961

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the employment of women in certain establishments for certain periods before and after child-birth and to provide for maternity benefit and certain other benefits.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the employment of women in various establishments during periods before and after childbirth. It provides for the payment of maternity benefits and other related benefits to ensure the well-being of women employees during pregnancy and after delivery.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official name, geographical applicability, and effective date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Application of Act.
key_sections.description: Details the types of establishments and conditions under which the Act applies, including factories, mines, plantations, and shops with ten or more employees.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'employer', 'establishment', 'maternity benefit', and 'woman'.

key_sections.title: Employment of, or work by, women prohibited during certain periods.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the employment of women during the six weeks following delivery, miscarriage, or medical termination of pregnancy, and restricts arduous work during pregnancy.

key_sections.title: Right to payment of maternity benefit.
key_sections.description: Establishes the right of women to maternity benefit, the rate of payment, qualifying period of employment, and maximum period for which benefit is payable, including provisions for adoption and commissioning mothers.

key_sections.title: Notice of claim for maternity benefit and payment thereof.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for women to give notice of their claim for maternity benefit and the employer's obligation to pay it.

key_sections.title: Payment of medical bonus.
key_sections.description: Entitles women to a medical bonus if pre-natal, confinement, and post-natal care are not provided free of charge by the employer.

key_sections.title: Leave for miscarriage, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants women leave with wages for a period of six weeks following miscarriage or medical termination of pregnancy.

key_sections.title: Nursing breaks.
key_sections.description: Provides for two nursing breaks of prescribed duration for women returning to duty after childbirth, until the child is fifteen months old.

key_sections.title: Crèche facility.
key_sections.description: Mandates crèche facilities for establishments with fifty or more employees and allows women four visits a day to the crèche.

key_sections.title: Dismissal during absence of pregnancy.
key_sections.description: Prohibits dismissal or discharge of a woman during or on account of her absence due to pregnancy, and specifies conditions under which maternity benefit may be deprived for gross misconduct.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to appoint Inspectors for the purposes of enforcing the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of Inspector to direct payments to be made.
key_sections.description: Grants Inspectors the power to inquire into complaints of withheld maternity benefits or wrongful dismissal and direct payments or appropriate orders.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of Act by employer.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for employers who fail to pay maternity benefits or wrongfully discharge/dismiss women.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the appropriate Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering various administrative and procedural matters.

powers_conferred: Central Government to give directions to State Governments regarding execution of the Act (Section 25)
Appropriate Government to appoint Inspectors (Section 14)

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Employers failing to pay maternity benefit or discharging/dismissing women during absence due to pregnancy are punishable with imprisonment (not less than three months, up to one year) and fine (not less than two thousand rupees, up to five thousand rupees). Other contraventions of the Act or rules are punishable with imprisonment (up to one year) or fine (up to five thousand rupees) or both. Obstructing an Inspector or failing to produce documents is punishable with imprisonment (up to one year) or fine (up to five thousand rupees) or both.

special_provisions: The qualifying period of eighty days for maternity benefit does not apply to a woman who has immigrated into the State of Assam and was pregnant at the time of immigration.
Maximum period of maternity benefit for a woman having two or more surviving children is twelve weeks, of which not more than six weeks shall precede the date of her expected delivery.
A woman who legally adopts a child below the age of three months or a commissioning mother is entitled to maternity benefit for twelve weeks from the date the child is handed over.
Employers may allow women to work from home after availing maternity benefit, based on mutual agreement.
