implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through Inspectors appointed by the appropriate Government, who have powers to inspect establishments, investigate complaints, and direct payments. Penalties are prescribed for contraventions by employers and obstruction of Inspectors. Aggrieved women, trade unions, or voluntary organizations, or Inspectors, can file complaints in competent courts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE INSTITUTES OF TECHNOLOGY ACT, 1961

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry concerned with technical education

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare certain institutions of technology to be institutions of national importance and to provide for certain matters connected with such institutions and the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur.
act_overview.purpose: This Act declares various institutions of technology as institutions of national importance. It provides for their incorporation, powers, governance, and other related matters. The Act also establishes a central Council to coordinate the activities of these Institutes.

key_definitions: Institute of Technology, Banaras Hindu University

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Declaration of certain institutions as institutions of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares various Indian Institutes of Technology as institutions of national importance.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of institutes.
key_sections.description: Establishes each Institute as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

key_sections.title: Effect of incorporation of institutes.
key_sections.description: Details the legal consequences of incorporation, including transfer of property, rights, liabilities, and employees from societies to the corresponding Institutes.

key_sections.title: Powers of Institutes.
key_sections.description: Outlines the powers and duties of each Institute, including instruction, research, granting degrees, managing funds, and making appointments.

key_sections.title: Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of every Institute and defines the Visitor's powers to review and issue directions.

key_sections.title: Authorities of Institutes.
key_sections.description: Lists the primary authorities of an Institute: the Board of Governors and the Senate.

key_sections.title: Functions of Board.
key_sections.description: Describes the responsibilities of the Board of Governors, including general superintendence, policy decisions, and making Statutes.

key_sections.title: Functions of Senate.
key_sections.description: Defines the Senate's role in controlling and regulating instruction, education, and examination standards.

key_sections.title: Director.
key_sections.description: Outlines the appointment and responsibilities of the Director as the principal academic and executive officer.

key_sections.title: Grants by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Provides for financial grants from the Central Government to the Institutes.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Council.
key_sections.description: Establishes a central body called the Council and specifies its composition.

key_sections.title: Functions of Council.
key_sections.description: Details the Council's duties, including coordinating activities, advising on academic matters, and reviewing development plans and budgets.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Indian Institute of Technology (Kharagpur) Act, 1956, while saving certain provisions.

powers_conferred: Institutes: To provide for instruction and research, hold examinations and grant degrees, confer honorary degrees, fix fees, establish and manage halls and hostels, supervise and control students, institute academic and other posts, frame Statutes and Ordinances, deal with property, receive gifts/grants/donations, cooperate with other institutions, institute and award fellowships/scholarships/prizes, meet technological needs of States and Union territories in its zone.
Visitor: To appoint persons to review work and progress of any Institute, hold inquiries, issue directions, assent to Statutes.

Board of Governors: To exercise general superintendence, direction and control of Institute affairs, take policy decisions, institute courses of study, make Statutes, appoint persons to academic and other posts, consider and modify or cancel Ordinances, consider annual reports/accounts/budget, appoint committees.
Senate: To control and generally regulate standards of instruction, education and examination, make Ordinances.
Director: To be the principal academic and executive officer, responsible for administration, imparting instruction, and maintaining discipline.
Central Government: To make rules for Chapter III, remove difficulties, pay grants to Institutes.
Council: To coordinate activities of Institutes, advise on academic matters, lay down policy, examine development plans and budget estimates, recommend allocation of funds, advise the Visitor.

repealed_acts: The Indian Institute of Technology (Kharagpur) Act, 1956 (5 of 1956)
related_acts: Indian Institute of Technology (Kharagpur) Act, 1956 (5 of 1956)
Roorkee University Act, 1947 (U.P. Act IX of 1948)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor nominates the Chairman of the Board and appoints the umpire for the Tribunal of Arbitration. The Council appoints the Director and nominates persons to the Board. The Central Government appoints persons to the Council and nominates the Secretary of the Council. State Governments nominate persons to the Board. The Chairman of the Board nominates persons to the Senate. The Board makes appointments to academic and other posts. The Director makes appointments in other cases. Members of Parliament are elected to the Council by the House of the People and the Council of States.
regulatory_bodies: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research

applies_to: Institutions declared as institutions of national importance (listed in Section 2)
Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur
Societies related to the declared institutions
Employees of the Institutes
special_provisions: Specific provisions for the Indian Institute of Technology, Roorkee regarding incorporation effects and transitional arrangements.
Specific provisions for the Indian Institute of Technology (Banaras Hindu University), Varanasi regarding incorporation effects, Board and Senate composition, and transitional arrangements.
Specific provisions for the Indian Institute of Technology, Guwahati regarding commencement of amendments.
Specific provisions for new IITs established by the 2012 and 2016 Amendment Acts regarding commencement of amendments and transitional arrangements.
Institutes may strive to meet the technological needs of the States and Union territories included in its zone.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government has the power to make rules for Chapter III. The Board has the power to make Statutes. The Senate has the power to make Ordinances.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor can issue directions which Institutes are bound to comply with. The Chairman of the Board and Council are responsible for ensuring implementation of decisions. Accounts are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India. Disputes between an Institute and its employees are referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The decision of the Tribunal of Arbitration is final and cannot be questioned in any court. No suit or proceeding shall lie in any court in respect of matters required to be referred to the Tribunal of Arbitration.

schedules_summary.description: Contains provisions of the Indian Institute of Technology (Kharagpur) Act, 1956, that are continued in force. These provisions include the declaration of IIT Kharagpur as an institution of national importance, definitions specific to it, its incorporation details, and the transfer of service of its existing employees.

act_identification.act_title: THE GOA, DAMAN AND DIU (ADMINISTRATION) ACT, 1962

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the administration of the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the administration of the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu. It ensures the continuance and adaptation of existing laws, establishes representation in the House of the People, and validates past administrative actions.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its deemed date of commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used within the Act, such as 'Administrator' and 'appointed day'.

key_sections.title: Representation in the House of the People.
key_sections.description: Allots two seats to the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu in the House of the People and amends related Acts.

key_sections.title: Officers and functionaries in relation to Goa, Daman and Diu.
key_sections.description: Ensures the continuance of existing judges, magistrates, and other officers and authorities in their functions.

key_sections.title: Continuance of existing laws and their adaptation.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that all existing laws in Goa, Daman and Diu shall continue in force and grants power to the Central Government to adapt them.

key_sections.title: Power to extend enactments to Goa, Daman and Diu.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to extend enactments in force in a State to Goa, Daman and Diu.

key_sections.title: Power to construe laws.
key_sections.description: Allows Courts or other authorities to construe laws to facilitate their application in Goa, Daman and Diu.

key_sections.title: Validation of certain action and indemnity of officers for certain acts.
key_sections.description: Validates actions taken by the Administrator or officers before the Act's commencement and provides indemnity against legal proceedings for such actions.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Goa, Daman and Diu (Administration) Ordinance, 1962, while saving actions taken under it.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to appoint officers and authorities for administration (Section 4)
Central Government: to direct continuance of existing officers (Section 4)
Central Government: to make adaptations and modifications to existing laws (Section 5(2))
Central Government: to extend enactments to Goa, Daman and Diu (Section 6)
Central Government: to make orders to remove difficulties (Section 10)
Judges, magistrates and other officers: to continue to exercise their functions (Section 4)
Court or other authority: to construe laws for facilitating application (Section 8)

amended_acts: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
Representation of the People Act, 1951 (43 of 1951)
repealed_acts: Goa, Daman and Diu (Administration) Ordinance, 1962 (2 of 1962)
related_acts: Goa, Daman and Diu Judicial Commissioner's Court (Declaration asHigh Court) Act, 1964 (16 of 1964)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: President (for Administrator under Article 239 of the Constitution); Central Government (for officers and authorities for administration)

applies_to: Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through the continued exercise of functions by existing officers and authorities, the continuance and adaptation of existing laws, and the Central Government's power to extend enactments and remove difficulties.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any Court of law; any Court or other authority

act_identification.act_title: THE HINDI SAHITYA SAMMELAN ACT, 1962

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare the institution known as the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan having its head office at Allahabad to be an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act declares the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, an institution with its head office at Allahabad, to be of national importance. It provides for its incorporation as a body corporate and outlines its functions, primarily focusing on the promotion, development, and advancement of the Hindi language and literature.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Declaration of the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan as an institution of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, with its head office at Allahabad, as an institution of national importance due to its objects.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'prescribed', 'Sammelan', and 'Society'.

key_sections.title: Incorporation.
key_sections.description: Constitutes the Sammelan as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and powers to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and to sue and be sued. Specifies its head office and initial members.

key_sections.title: Effect of incorporation of Sammelan.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that upon incorporation, references to the Society become references to the Sammelan, all property, rights, and liabilities of the Society transfer to the Sammelan, and employees continue their service under the Sammelan.

key_sections.title: Functions of Sammelan.
key_sections.description: Outlines the various functions of the Sammelan, including promoting Hindi language and literature, holding examinations, conferring degrees, establishing institutions, awarding prizes, and managing its property.

key_sections.title: Governing Body.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Governing Body for the general superintendence, direction, and management of the Sammelan's affairs, specifying its composition and powers.

key_sections.title: First Governing Body and its duties.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a First Governing Body by the Central Government and details its duties, including performing Sammelan functions, making rules, determining first members, and arranging for the constitution of the permanent Governing Body.

key_sections.title: Rules to be made by the first Governing Body.
key_sections.description: Mandates the First Governing Body to make rules concerning membership, powers of the Governing Body, elections, committees, accounts, employee conditions, legal proceedings, affiliation of institutions, and award of degrees/prizes.

key_sections.title: Fund of the Sammelan.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Fund for the Sammelan, detailing sources of credit (fees, grants, donations) and its application towards meeting expenses and allowances.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Requires the Sammelan to maintain proper accounts, prepare annual statements, and have its accounts audited annually by a chartered accountant.

key_sections.title: Power to make rule.
key_sections.description: Grants the Governing Body the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes, subject to Central Government approval and publication.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make provisions or give directions to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the Act, provided they are consistent with its purposes.

powers_conferred: Sammelan: acquire, hold and dispose of property and to contract and may by that name sue and be sued (Section 4(2))
Sammelan: promote the spread of Hindi language and to develop it and secure its enrichment (Section 6(a))
Sammelan: work for the promotion, development and advancement of Hindi literature (Section 6(b))
Sammelan: work for the promotion, development and advancement of Devanagari script (Section 6(c))
Sammelan: arrange for the holding of examinations through the medium of Hindi language and to confer degrees, diplomas and other academic distinctions (Section 6(d))

Sammelan: establish and maintain schools, colleges and other institutions for instruction in Hindi language and Hindi literature and also to affiliate schools, colleges and other institutions (Section 6(e))
Sammelan: affiliate institutions having for their object the promotion of Hindi language and Hindi literature (Section 6(f))
Sammelan: award honorary degrees and other academic distinctions (Section 6(g))
Sammelan: institute and award prizes (Partioshiks) to distinguished scholars in Hindi (Section 6(h))
Sammelan: promote and encourage research in Hindi language and Hindi literature (Section 6(i))
Sammelan: co-operate with other institutions having similar objects (Section 6(j))
Sammelan: receive gifts, grants, donations or benefactions from the Government and receive bequests, donations or transfers of moveable and immoveable properties (Section 6(k))
Sammelan: deal with any property belonging to or vested in the Sammelan (Section 6(l))
Sammelan: borrow on the security of the property of the Sammelan with Central Government approval (Section 6(m))
Sammelan: perform such other functions as may be deemed necessary for advancing the cause of Hindi language and Hindi literature (Section 6(n))
Central Government: appoint date of commencement (Section 1(2))
Central Government: determine number of persons in Governing Body (Section 7(2))
Central Government: nominate members to Governing Body (Section 7(2))
Central Government: constitute the first Governing Body (Section 8(1))
Central Government: approve rules made by First Governing Body (Section 8(3)(b), 12(2), 12(3))
Central Government: specify allowances for First Governing Body members (Section 9(4))
Central Government: give instructions for preparing list of first members (Section 11(1))
Central Government: direct manner of publication of list of first members (Section 11(2))
Central Government: specify further period for elections to Governing Body (Section 13)
Central Government: approve rules made by Governing Body (Section 17(2))
Central Government: remove difficulties by order published in Official Gazette (Section 19)
First Governing Body: perform all functions of the Sammelan and carry on administration (Section 8(3)(a))
First Governing Body: make rules with the approval of the Central Government (Section 8(3)(b))
First Governing Body: determine the first members of the Sammelan (Section 8(3)(c))
First Governing Body: take all necessary steps for the constitution of the Governing Body (Section 8(3)(d))
First Governing Body: take over the management, control and administration of all properties vested in the Sammelan (Section 10)
First Governing Body: cause to be prepared a list of all persons who are to be considered as first members (Section 11(1))
First Governing Body: order insertion or omission of names from the list of first members (Section 11(3))
Governing Body: general superintendence, direction and management of the affairs of the Sammelan (Section 7(1))
Governing Body: make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act (Section 17(1))

authorities_established: Hindi Sahitya Sammelan (as a body corporate)
executive committee or any other committee
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints Chairman, Secretary, and thirteen other members of the First Governing Body (Section 8(1)). Sammelan appoints chartered accountant as auditor (Section 16(2)).

applies_to: The institution known as the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan
Members of the Sammelan
Employees of the Society/Sammelan
Properties of the Society/Sammelan

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: First Governing Body (Section 12) and Governing Body (Section 17), with Central Government approval.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The general superintendence, direction, and management of the Sammelan's affairs vest in a Governing Body. The Sammelan is required to maintain proper accounts and records, which are subject to annual audit by a chartered accountant. The Central Government has powers to approve rules and remove difficulties.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL CO-OPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION ACT, 1962
act_identification.act_short_title: The National Co-operative Development Corporation Act, 1962

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the incorporation and regulation of a corporation for the purpose of planning and promoting programmes for the production, processing, marketing, storage, export and import of agricultural produce, foodstuffs industrial goods, livestock, certain other commodities and services on co-operative principles and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: To incorporate and regulate a corporation for planning and promoting programmes for the production, processing, marketing, storage, export and import of agricultural produce, foodstuffs, industrial goods, livestock, certain other commodities and services on co-operative principles.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment of the National Co-operative Development Corporation.
key_sections.description: Establishes the National Co-operative Development Corporation as a body corporate and outlines its structure including the General Council.

key_sections.title: Functions of Corporation.
key_sections.description: Details the primary functions of the Corporation, including planning, promoting, and financing programmes through co-operative societies.

key_sections.title: Board of Management of the Corporation.
key_sections.description: Constitutes the Board of Management of the Corporation and defines its composition and powers.

key_sections.title: Grants by the Central Government to Corporation.
key_sections.description: Outlines the provisions for grants and loans from the Central Government to the Corporation.

key_sections.title: Power of Corporation to borrow money.
key_sections.description: Grants the Corporation the power to borrow money from various sources with Central Government approval.

key_sections.title: Corporation to maintain fund.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Corporation to maintain the National Co-operative Development Fund and specifies its sources and application.

key_sections.title: Directions by Central Government.
key_sections.description: States that the Corporation shall be guided by directions from the Central Government on all matters, including policy.

key_sections.title: Dissolution of Corporation.
key_sections.description: Provides for the dissolution of the Corporation by the Central Government under certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of Corporation to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Corporation to make regulations with the previous sanction of the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.

powers_conferred: Power to acquire, hold and dispose of property and to contract, and to sue and be sued (Corporation)
Power to plan, promote and finance programmes through co-operative societies (Corporation)
Power to advance loans or grant subsidies to State Governments for financing co-operative societies (Corporation)
Power to provide funds to State Governments for financing co-operative societies for purchase of agricultural produce, foodstuffs, etc. (Corporation)
Power to plan and promote programmes through co-operative societies for supply of seeds, manures, fertilizers, etc. (Corporation)
Power to provide loans and grants directly to national level co-operative societies and other co-operative societies (Corporation)
Power to participate in the share capital of national level co-operative societies and other co-operative societies (Corporation)
Power to borrow money (Corporation)
Power to receive gifts, grants, donations or benefactions (Corporation)
Power to nominate President, Vice-President, and members of the General Council (Central Government)
Power to remove members from office (Central Government)
Power to appoint the managing director (Central Government)
Power to give directions to the Corporation (Central Government)
Power to dissolve the Corporation (Central Government)
Power to make rules (Central Government)
Power to make regulations (Corporation)

repealed_acts: Agricultural Produce (Development and Warehousing) Corporations Act, 1956 (28 of 1956)
related_acts: Industrial Development Bank of India Act, 1964 (18 of 1964)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 (5 of 1970)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980 (40 of 1980)
Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
State Bank of India Act, 1955 (23 of 1955)
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981 (61 of 1981)
Khadi and Village Industries Commission Act, 1956 (61 of 1956)

authorities_established: Board of Management of the Corporation
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government has the power to nominate the President, Vice-President, and various members of the General Council, and to appoint the managing director.

applies_to: Whole of India
Co-operative societies
State Governments
special_provisions: Applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh (as per notification S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Corporation's functions are carried out through planning, promoting, and financing programmes for co-operative societies, with the Central Government providing grants, loans, and issuing directions. The Corporation is required to submit returns and reports to the Central Government.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the form for the Declaration of Fidelity and Secrecy to be made by members, officers, employees, or auditors of the National Co-operative Development Corporation.

act_identification.act_title: THE STATE OF NAGALAND ACT, 1962

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the formation of the State of Nagaland and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the formation of the State of Nagaland by carving out the Naga Hills-Tuensang Area from Assam. It also addresses the necessary amendments to the Constitution and other laws, establishes a common High Court, and outlines financial and administrative provisions for the new state.

chapter_titles: FORMATION OF THE STATE OF NAGALAND

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the State of Nagaland Act, 1962.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'law', and 'Naga Hills-Tuensang Area'.

key_sections.title: Formation of State of Nagaland.
key_sections.description: Establishes the new State of Nagaland comprising the Naga Hills-Tuensang Area, which ceases to be part of Assam, and defines its initial districts.

key_sections.title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule of the Constitution to include Nagaland as a new state.

key_sections.title: Strength of Legislative Assembly.
key_sections.description: Determines the total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland, including special provisions for the Tuensang district.

key_sections.title: Common High Court for Assam and Nagaland.
key_sections.description: Establishes a common High Court for Assam and Nagaland and specifies the status of existing judges.

key_sections.title: Authorisation of expenditure pending its sanction by Legislature.
key_sections.description: Allows the President and Governor to authorize expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of Nagaland pending legislative sanction.

key_sections.title: Property, assets, rights, liabilities and obligations.
key_sections.description: Transfers property, assets, rights, liabilities, and obligations from the Union to the State of Nagaland.

key_sections.title: Continuance of existing laws and their adaptation.
key_sections.description: Ensures the continuance of existing laws in the Naga Hills-Tuensang Area in the new State of Nagaland, with provisions for adaptation.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the President power to issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint the 'appointed day' by notification
Central Government to make rules to give effect to the Act's provisions
President to determine grants-in-aid and share in Union duties of excise, estate duty and taxes on income for Nagaland
President to authorise expenditure from Consolidated Fund of Nagaland pending legislative sanction
President to determine allowances and privileges of the Governor of Nagaland
President to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions
Governor of Nagaland to authorise further expenditure from Consolidated Fund of Nagaland
Governor to specify manner for filling seats allocated to Tuensang district in Legislative Assembly
Election Commission to delimit assembly constituencies and amend Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1961
Appropriate Government to make adaptations and modifications to laws
Courts, tribunals or authorities to construe laws for facilitating application

amended_acts: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
Representation of the People Act, 1951 (43 of 1951)
Union Duties of Excise (Distribution) Act, 1962 (3 of 1962)
Additional Duties of Excise (Goods of Special Importance) Act, 1957 (58 of 1957)
repealed_acts: Nagaland (Transitional Provisions) Regulation, 1961 (Regulation 2 of 1961)

Bar Council of Assam and Nagaland

regulatory_bodies: Bar Council of Assam and Nagaland

Naga Hills-Tuensang Area

Provisions for the 'appointed day' to be notified by the Central Government
Continuance of existing laws and courts until altered or inconsistent with the Act

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through its provisions, including the continuance and adaptation of existing laws, the establishment of a common High Court, and the powers conferred upon the Central Government, President, Governor, and Election Commission.

act_identification.act_title: THE ATOMIC ENERGY ACT, 1962

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the development, control and use of atomic energy for the welfare of the people of India and for other peaceful purposes and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to facilitate the development, control, and utilization of atomic energy for the welfare of the Indian populace and for other peaceful applications, along with addressing related matters.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application across India, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions and interpretation.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'atomic energy', 'fissile material', and 'prescribed substance'.

key_sections.title: General powers of the Central Government.
key_sections.description: Outlines the broad powers of the Central Government regarding atomic energy, including production, research, control of substances, and declaration of restricted information/prohibited areas.

key_sections.title: Notification of discovery of uranium or thorium.
key_sections.description: Requires reporting of any discovery of uranium or thorium in India to the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Control over mining or concentration of substances containing uranium.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government powers to regulate or prohibit mining and treatment of uranium-containing substances, with provisions for compensation.

key_sections.title: Compulsory acquisition of prescribed substances, minerals and plants.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to compulsorily acquire prescribed substances, minerals, and plants related to atomic energy, with provisions for notice and compensation.

key_sections.title: Control over production and use of atomic energy.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to prohibit certain activities related to atomic energy without a licence and specifies conditions for licensing.

key_sections.title: Special provisions as to safety.
key_sections.description: Enables the Central Government to make rules for safety in premises handling radioactive substances or radiation generating plants, including preventing hazards and safe waste disposal.

key_sections.title: Restriction on disclosure of information.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to restrict the disclosure of sensitive information related to atomic energy plants and processes.

key_sections.title: Special Provisions as to inventions.
key_sections.description: Prohibits patents for inventions related to atomic energy and grants the Central Government powers over such inventions and patent applications.

key_sections.title: Principles relating to payment of compensation.
key_sections.description: Establishes the principles and process for determining and paying compensation for compulsory acquisitions or other actions under the Act.

key_sections.title: Offences and penalties.
key_sections.description: Defines various offences under the Act and prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government broad powers to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering various aspects of atomic energy regulation.

powers_conferred: To produce, develop, use and dispose of atomic energy and carry out research (Section 3(a))
To manufacture, acquire, store, transport, and dispose of prescribed or radioactive substances and related articles (Section 3(b), (bb))
To declare information as 'restricted information' (Section 3(c))
To declare any area or premises as 'prohibited area' (Section 3(d))
To control radioactive substances or radiation generating plant for safety (Section 3(e))
To provide for production and supply of electricity from atomic energy (Section 3(f))
To require reporting of discovery of uranium or thorium (Section 4)
To control or prohibit mining or concentration of substances containing uranium (Section 5)
To compulsorily acquire minerals, concentrates, or other materials containing uranium (Section 6)
To obtain information regarding materials, plant, or processes (Section 7)
To authorize entry and inspection (Section 8)
To do work for discovering minerals (Section 9)
To compulsorily acquire exclusive rights to work minerals (Section 10)
To compulsorily acquire prescribed substances, minerals, and plants (Section 11)
To serve notice for novation of certain contracts (Section 13)
To prohibit production and use of atomic energy except under a licence (Section 14)
To requisition any substance for extracting uranium or plutonium (Section 15)
To prohibit manufacture, possession, use, transfer, export, import, transport, and disposal of radioactive substances (Section 16)
To make rules for special safety provisions (Section 17)
To restrict disclosure of information (Section 18)
To prohibit entry into prohibited areas (Section 19)
To inspect patent applications and refuse them if related to atomic energy (Section 20)
To appoint arbitrators for compensation determination (Section 21)
To develop national policy for atomic power, fix rates, and enter arrangements for electricity supply (Section 22)
To administer the Factories Act, 1948, for certain factories (Section 23)
To delegate its powers (Section 27)
To make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act (Section 30)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of orders or licence conditions under Section 14, rules under Section 17, obstruction of authorized persons, or contravention of Section 18(2) are punishable with imprisonment up to five years, or fine, or both. Other offences, such as failing to comply with notices under Section 5 or 7, making untrue statements, obstructing powers under Section 8 or 9, or contravening other provisions, are punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both (Section 24).

repealed_acts: Act 29 of 1948
related_acts: Indian Patents and Designs Act, 1911 (2 of 1911)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints arbitrators (Section 21(1)(b)); Central Government appoints persons for hearings related to objections (Sections 9(3), 11(6), 13(2)); Central Government authorizes persons for entry and inspection (Sections 8(1), 17(4)).

applies_to: whole of India
every person who discovers uranium or thorium
any person mining or treating substances containing uranium
any person in possession or control of prescribed substances or plants
companies
Government
exemptions: disclosure of information regarding plants of a type in use for purposes other than atomic energy, unless it reveals atomic energy use (Section 18(3)(i))
subsequent disclosure of information already made public (Section 18(3)(ii))
use of small quantities of natural uranium for examination, test or analysis (Section 15(2))
special_provisions: Arrangements with the Electricity Board of the State where an atomic power station is situated for transmission of electricity to any other State (Section 22(1)(c)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the Central Government's authority to issue notices, impose conditions, grant or revoke licenses, prohibit activities, conduct inspections, and compulsorily acquire property. Contraventions are subject to penalties, and offences are cognizable under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court for appeals against arbitrator's awards (Section 21(3)). Offences are cognizable under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Section 26).

act_identification.act_title: THE EXTRADITION ACT, 1962

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the extradition of fugitive criminals and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws concerning the extradition of individuals accused or convicted of crimes, known as fugitive criminals, from India to foreign states and vice versa. It also addresses related and incidental matters concerning such extraditions.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II EXTRADITION OF FUGITIVE CRIMINALS TO FOREIGN STATE TO WHICH CHAPTER III DOES NOT APPLY
CHAPTER III RETURN OF FUGITIVE CRIMINALS TO FOREIGN STATES WITH EXTRADITION ARRANGEMENTS
CHAPTER IV SURRENDER OR RETURN OF ACCUSED OR CONVICTED PERSONS FROM FOREIGN STATES

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'extradition offence' and 'fugitive criminal'.

key_sections.title: Application of Act.
key_sections.description: Outlines how the Central Government applies the Act's provisions to foreign states, including treaty states and those without treaties.

key_sections.title: Procedure before magistrate.
key_sections.description: Details the procedure a magistrate must follow when inquiring into a requisition for surrender, including taking evidence and determining a prima facie case.

key_sections.title: Surrender of fugitive criminal.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue a warrant for the custody and surrender of a fugitive criminal after a magisterial inquiry.

key_sections.title: Endorsed warrant for apprehension of fugitive criminal.
key_sections.description: Describes the process for apprehending a fugitive criminal in India using an endorsed warrant issued by a foreign state.

key_sections.title: Provisional warrant for apprehension of fugitive criminal.
key_sections.description: Allows a magistrate to issue a provisional warrant for the apprehension of a fugitive criminal from a foreign state under urgent circumstances.

key_sections.title: Accused or convicted person surrendered or returned by foreign State not to be tried for certain offence.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that a person surrendered or returned by a foreign state cannot be tried in India for offences other than those for which they were surrendered, or related lesser offences, or with the foreign state's consent.

key_sections.title: Liability of fugitive criminals to be arrested and surrendered or returned.
key_sections.description: Establishes the general liability of fugitive criminals to be arrested and surrendered or returned under the Act, regardless of when the offence was committed or Indian court jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to discharge any fugitive criminal.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to discharge a fugitive criminal if surrender is deemed unjust, inexpedient, or for political reasons.

key_sections.title: Restrictions on surrender.
key_sections.description: Sets out restrictions on the surrender or return of a fugitive criminal, including cases of political offences, time-barred prosecutions, and conditions regarding trial for other offences.

key_sections.title: Extra territorial jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Extends jurisdiction to treat extradition offences committed in a foreign state as if committed in India, allowing for prosecution in India.

key_sections.title: Prosecution on refusal to extradition.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to prosecute a fugitive criminal in India if extradition to a foreign state is refused.

key_sections.title: Provision of life imprisonment for death penalty.
key_sections.description: Provides that a fugitive criminal surrendered from a foreign state that does not have the death penalty for an offence punishable by death in India shall be liable only for life imprisonment.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Direct application of Act (S.3)
Central Government: Issue order for magisterial inquiry (S.5)
Central Government: Issue warrant for surrender (S.8)
Central Government: Endorse warrant (S.15)
Central Government: Discharge apprehended person (S.16(2))
Central Government: Issue warrant for return (S.18)
Central Government: Make requisition for surrender to India (S.19)
Central Government: Discharge fugitive criminal (S.29)
Central Government: Decide simultaneous requisitions (S.30)
Central Government: Add or omit offences from Schedule (S.31(3))
Central Government: Request provisional arrest (S.34B)
Central Government: Make rules (S.36)
Magistrate: Inquire into case (S.5, S.7)
Magistrate: Issue warrant for arrest (S.6, S.9, S.16)
Magistrate: Commit to prison (S.7(4), S.17(1))
Magistrate: Discharge fugitive criminal (S.7(3))
Magistrate: Report to Central Government (S.9(2), S.16(2), S.17(3))
Magistrate: Release on bail (S.17(2))
Magistrate: Exercise jurisdiction for offences at sea or in air (S.23)
High Court: Order discharge if not surrendered within two months (S.24)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines 'extradition offence' and includes abetment, conspiracy, attempt, incitement, or participation as an accomplice in such offences. While it does not prescribe specific penalties, it refers to offences punishable with imprisonment for at least one year under Indian or foreign law, and provides for life imprisonment in certain cases where the death penalty is not applicable in the surrendering foreign state.

repealed_acts: The Indian Extradition Act, 1903 (15 of 1903)

any law corresponding thereto in force at the commencement of this Act in the territories which, immediately before the 1st day of November, 1956, were comprised in Part B States and the North East Frontier Agency and Tuensang District (Extradition) Regulation, 1961 (3 of 1961)
The Extradition Acts, 1870 to 1932 (33 and 34 Vict. c. 52; 36 and 37 Vict. c. 60; 6 Edw. 7, c. 15; 22 and 23 Geo. 5, c. 39, 44 and 45 Vict. c. 69)
the Fugitive Offenders Act, 1881
related_acts: the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974)
Suppression of Unlawful Acts against Safety of Civil Aviation Act, 1982 (66 of 1982)
Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, 1987 (28 of 1987)

applies_to: fugitive criminal of a foreign State
any person who is accused or convicted of an extradition offence committed in India and who is or is suspected to be, in any foreign State
exemptions: offence of political character
prosecution for the offence in respect of which his surrender is sought is according to the law of that State barred by time

if he has been accused of some offence in India, not being the offence for which his surrender or return is sought, or is undergoing sentence under any conviction in India until after he has been discharged
special_provisions: Application can be restricted to such part of India as may be specified in the order (S.3(2))
Modifications, exceptions, conditions for treaty states (S.3(3)(c), S.12(2))

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through requisitions from foreign states or by the Central Government, followed by magisterial inquiries, issuance of warrants for arrest, custody, and eventual surrender or return of fugitive criminals.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate, High Court, court of session

schedules_summary.description: Lists offences which are not to be regarded as offences of a political character, including specific sections of the Indian Penal Code and other Acts like the Anti-Hijacking Act, Suppression of Unlawful Acts against Safety of Civil Aviation Act, Explosive Substances Act, Arms Act, and Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE FOREIGNERS LAW (APPLICATION AND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1962

act_overview.preamble: An Act to apply the Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939 and the Foreigners Act, 1946 to certain persons to whom they do not at present apply and further to amend the Foreigners Act, 1946.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to extend the application of the Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939, and the Foreigners Act, 1946, to individuals whose parents or grandparents were citizens or subjects of countries at war with, or committing aggression against, India. It also aims to amend the Foreigners Act, 1946.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Foreigners Law (Application and Amendment) Act, 1962.

key_sections.title: Application of Act 16 of 1939 and Act 31 of 1946 to certain persons.
key_sections.description: Mandates that the provisions of the Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939, and the Foreigners Act, 1946, apply to persons whose parents or grandparents were citizens or subjects of countries at war with or committing aggression against India, or assisting such countries.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Foreigners Law (Application and Amendment) Ordinance, 1962, and saves actions taken under the repealed Ordinance, deeming them to have been done under this Act as if it commenced on 26th October, 1962.

repealed_acts: The Foreigners Law (Application and Amendment) Ordinance, 1962 (5 of 1962)

applies_to: any person who, or either of whose parents, or any of whose grand-parents was at any time a citizen or subject of any country at war with, or committing external aggression against, India or of any other country assisting the country at war with, or committing such aggression against, India

act_identification.act_title: THE PONDICHERRY (ADMINISTRATION) ACT, 1962

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the administration of Pondicherry and for matters connected therewith. BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirteenth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the legal and administrative framework for the Union territory of Pondicherry following its cession to India. It ensures the continuance and adaptation of existing laws, establishes the jurisdiction of the Madras High Court, and clarifies the status of property, assets, rights, and obligations.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its geographical extent to the whole of Pondicherry, and its deemed commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Administrator', 'appointed day', 'Pondicherry', and 'High Court'.

key_sections.title: Officers and functionaries in relation to Pondicherry.
key_sections.description: Ensures the continuance of existing courts, tribunals, authorities, and officers in Pondicherry, exercising their functions as before the appointed day, unless otherwise directed by the Central Government or Administrator.

key_sections.title: Continuance of existing laws and their-adaptation.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that all laws in force in the former French Establishments before the appointed day shall continue in Pondicherry, with powers for the Central Government to make adaptations and modifications.

key_sections.title: Property and assets.
key_sections.description: Declares that all property and assets within Pondicherry that vested in the Government of the French Republic before the appointed day shall vest in the Union.

key_sections.title: Rights and obligations.
key_sections.description: States that all rights, liabilities, and obligations of the Government of the French Republic related to the administration of the former French Establishments shall become those of the Central Government from the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Extension of the jurisdiction of Madras High Court to Pondicherry.
key_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the High Court at Madras to Pondicherry from the 6th day of November, 1962.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of High Court.
key_sections.description: Details the jurisdiction of the High Court over Pondicherry, including powers previously exercisable by French courts and the transfer of pending appeals and proceedings.

key_sections.title: Power of High Court to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the High Court the power to make rules concerning matters such as translation of papers, court-fees, procedure, and the approval and enrolment of advocates from Pondicherry.

key_sections.title: Validation of certain orders and decrees.
key_sections.description: Validates orders and decrees made by certain French courts during a specified period and provides for the handling of decisions where respondents lacked opportunity to appear.

key_sections.title: Limitation for appeals.
key_sections.description: Sets out the periods of limitation for various types of appeals to the High Court, including civil, criminal, and labour appeals.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove any difficulties arising in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, with retrospective effect in certain cases.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Pondicherry (Administration) Ordinance, 1962, while saving actions taken under the said Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint officers and authorities for the administration of Pondicherry (Section 3)
Central Government or Administrator to direct continuance of courts, tribunals, authorities or officers (Section 3)
Central Government to make adaptations and modifications to laws (Section 4(2))
Central Government to extend enactments to Pondicherry (Section 8)
High Court to make rules (Section 12)
Central Government to remove difficulties (Section 19)

repealed_acts: The Pondicherry (Administration) Ordinance, 1962 (8 of 1962)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government to appoint from time to time such officers and authorities as may be necessary for the administration of Pondicherry

applies_to: whole of Pondicherry
special_provisions: Decisions rendered after 17th March, 1960, by any court in France where the respondent had no opportunity to appear for want of service of summons shall be deemed never to have been rendered and transferred to the High Court or corresponding court in Pondicherry (Section 13(2)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Continuance of existing courts, tribunals, authorities and officers; Central Government's power to adapt laws and remove difficulties.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court at Madras

act_identification.act_title: THE PETROLEUM AND MINERALS PIPELINES (ACQUISITION OF RIGHT OF USER IN LAND) ACT, 1962
act_identification.act_short_title: Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962

legislative_details.geographical_extent: It extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir. It applies in the first instance to the whole of the States of West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar-Pradesh and Gujarat and the Union territory of Delhi, and the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, declare that this Act shall also apply to such other State of Union territory and with effect from such date as may be specified in that notification.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the acquisition of right of user in land for laying pipelines for the transport of petroleum and minerals and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the acquisition of the right of user in land for the purpose of laying pipelines for the transport of petroleum and minerals. It also covers matters connected with such acquisition and the subsequent use and maintenance of these pipelines.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and application.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's name, geographical scope, and initial areas of application.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms such as 'competent authority', 'corporation', 'minerals', and 'petroleum'.

key_sections.title: Publication of notification for acquisition.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for the Central Government to publish a notification of its intention to acquire the right of user in land for laying pipelines.

key_sections.title: Declaration of acquisition of right of user.
key_sections.description: Describes the formal declaration of the acquisition of the right of user in land and its vesting in the Central Government, State Government, or corporation.

key_sections.title: Central Government or State Government or corporation to lay pipelines.
key_sections.description: Grants authority to lay pipelines and specifies restrictions on the types of land where pipelines cannot be laid.

key_sections.title: Restrictions regarding the use of land.
key_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on the owner or occupier of land regarding construction, excavation, or planting trees after the declaration of acquisition.

key_sections.title: Compensation.
key_sections.description: Details the procedure for determining and paying compensation for damages, loss, or injury sustained due to pipeline activities and for the acquisition of the right of user.

key_sections.title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts.
key_sections.description: States that civil courts generally do not have jurisdiction over matters that the competent authority is empowered to determine under this Act.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes various penalties for obstructing authorized acts, damaging pipelines, making unauthorized connections, or causing destruction to pipelines.

key_sections.title: Certain offences to be cognizable.
key_sections.description: Declares specific offences under sub-sections (2), (3), and (4) of Section 15 to be cognizable and non-bailable.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To declare intention to acquire right of user (Sec 3), declare acquisition of right of user (Sec 6), direct vesting of right of user (Sec 6), authorize persons to lay pipelines (Sec 7), authorize persons for inspection (Sec 8), make rules (Sec 17).
State Government: To lay pipelines (Sec 7), authorize persons for inspection (Sec 8).
Corporation: To lay pipelines (Sec 7), authorize persons for inspection (Sec 8).

Competent authority: To publish notification substance (Sec 3), hear objections (Sec 5), make reports to Central Government (Sec 6), decide disputes (Sec 7), determine compensation (Sec 10), determine persons entitled to compensation (Sec 11), refer apportionment disputes to District Judge (Sec 11), powers of a civil court (Sec 12).
District Judge: To determine compensation if not acceptable (Sec 10), determine market value (Sec 10), decide apportionment disputes (Sec 11), cause removal of structures/trees (Sec 9(3)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 15 prescribes penalties for: wilfully obstructing authorized acts, filling up/destroying trenches/marks, or doing prohibited acts under Section 9 (imprisonment up to six months or fine or both); wilfully making unauthorized connections, removing/destroying/damaging pipelines, inserting devices to extract petroleum/minerals, disrupting supplies (rigorous imprisonment up to ten years and fine); repeat offenders for the latter (rigorous imprisonment not less than three years but up to ten years); causing damage/destruction to pipelines with intent to commit sabotage or with knowledge of causing death/bodily injury (rigorous imprisonment not less than ten years but may extend to life imprisonment or death).

amended_acts: Act 13 of 1977 (Petroleum Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Amendment Act, 1977)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government authorizes the 'competent authority' by notification in the Official Gazette.

applies_to: Whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (initially)
States of West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar-Pradesh and Gujarat and the Union territory of Delhi (in the first instance)
Such other State or Union territory as declared by the Central Government by notification
exemptions: Land used for residential purposes immediately before the date of notification under Section 3(1)
Land on which there stands any permanent structure which was in existence immediately before the said date
Land which is appurtenant to a dwelling house
Land at a depth which is less than one metre from the surface (for laying pipelines)
special_provisions: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, declare that this Act shall also apply to such other State or Union territory and with effect from such date as may be specified in that notification.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through notifications by the Central Government for acquisition, objection hearings by the competent authority, determination and payment of compensation by the competent authority or District Judge, and penalties for violations. The competent authority is vested with certain powers of civil courts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District Judge (for compensation disputes, market value, apportionment, removal of structures); Civil courts (jurisdiction barred for matters determined by competent authority); High Court (special powers regarding bail under Section 439 CrPC, 1973, are not affected).

act_identification.act_title: THE MANIPUR (SALES OF MOTOR SPIRIT AND LUBRICANTS) TAXATION ACT, 1962
act_identification.act_short_title: The Manipur (Sales of Motor Spirit and Lubricants) Taxation Act, 1962

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of the Union territory of Manipur

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the levy of a tax on sales of motor spirit and lubricants in the Union territory of Manipur.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws concerning the imposition of tax on the sale of motor spirit and lubricants within the Union territory of Manipur.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Levy of tax.
key_sections.description: Establishes the levy and collection of tax on sales of specified goods by dealers and outlines tax rates and exemptions.

key_sections.title: Taxing authorities.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Chief Commissioner to appoint a Commissioner of Taxes and other assisting personnel.

key_sections.title: Registration of dealers.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration for dealers and outlines the process for obtaining and amending registration certificates.

key_sections.title: Assessment.
key_sections.description: Details the procedure for assessing tax payable by dealers based on returns or best judgment.

key_sections.title: Power to grant exemption from tax.
key_sections.description: Grants the Chief Commissioner power to exempt dealers or classes of dealers from tax in public interest.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for dealers failing to furnish returns, comply with notices, concealing sales, or evading tax.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals against assessment or penalty orders to the prescribed authority.

key_sections.title: Offences and penalties.
key_sections.description: Defines various offences under the Act and specifies corresponding punishments.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Chief Commissioner to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Assam Act 4 of 1939 as extended to Manipur.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Assam Sales of Motor Spirit and Lubricants Taxation Act, 1939, as extended to Manipur.

powers_conferred: Chief Commissioner: Appoint Commissioner of Taxes and other assistants (Section 4), grant exemption from tax (Section 12), make rules (Section 36).

Commissioner: Register dealers (Section 5), cancel registration certificates (Section 6), assess tax (Sections 8, 10, 11), impose penalties (Sections 13, 17), revise orders (Section 15), refund tax (Section 19), order production of accounts (Section 21), conduct entry, inspection, search and seizure (Section 22), compound offences (Section 29), delegate powers (Section 32).
Central Government: Fix rates of tax (Section 3).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines offences such as carrying on business in contravention of the Act, failure to submit returns or submitting false returns, failure to keep accounts, failure to produce documents, evading tax, obstructing inspection, and charging higher sales-tax. Penalties for these offences include imprisonment up to six months or a fine not exceeding one thousand rupees, or both, with daily fines for continuing offences. False statements in declarations are also punishable with simple imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both. Officers conducting vexatious searches are liable to a fine up to five hundred rupees. Dealers may face penalties up to 1.5 times the tax for failures related to returns, compliance, concealment of sales, or tax evasion. Failure to pay sums due can incur a penalty not exceeding fifty percent of the demanded sum.

repealed_acts: The Assam Sales of Motor Spirit and Lubricants Taxation Act, 1939
related_acts: The Central Sales Tax Act, 1956 (74 of 1956)
The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (5 of 1898)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Chief Commissioner of Manipur has the power to appoint a Commissioner of Taxes and other persons to assist him.

applies_to: Every dealer

Any person who sells taxable goods manufactured, made or processed by him in, or brought by him into, the Union territory from any place outside that territory for the purpose of sale in that territory.
exemptions: Sales taking place outside the Union territory.
Sales in the course of import into or export out of the territory of India.
Sales in the course of inter-State trade or commerce as laid down in section 3 of the Central Sales Tax Act, 1956.
Classes of dealers or specific dealers exempted by the Chief Commissioner in the public interest.
special_provisions: The Act extends to the whole of the Union territory of Manipur.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through assessment of tax by the Commissioner, imposition of penalties for non-compliance or evasion, recovery of sums due as arrears of land revenue, and powers of entry, inspection, search, and seizure. Offences are investigated by prescribed officers, and criminal proceedings can be initiated, subject to the Commissioner's sanction. The Commissioner also has powers to compound offences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence under this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to grant exemption from duty.

key_sections.title: Recovery of duties not levied or not paid or short-levied or short-paid or erroneously refunded.

key_sections.title: Drawback on imported materials used in the manufacture of goods which are exported.

key_sections.title: Penalty for improper importation of goods, etc.

key_sections.title: Confiscation of goods attempted to be improperly exported, etc.

key_sections.title: Penalty for attempt to export goods improperly, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for improper exportation and related acts.

key_sections.title: Appeals to Commissioner (Appeals).
key_sections.description: Allows appeals against decisions of lower-ranking customs officers to the Commissioner (Appeals).

key_sections.title: Appeals to the Appellate Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Evasion of duty or prohibitions.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines various offences related to improper importation/exportation, evasion of duty, false declarations, and obstruction of customs officers. Penalties include confiscation of goods and conveyances (Sections 111, 113, 115, 118, 119, 120, 121), fines (Sections 112, 114, 114A, 114AA, 114AB, 116, 117, 125), and imprisonment (Sections 132, 133, 134, 135, 135A, 135AA, 136). Penalties vary based on the nature and value of the goods or the severity of the offence, with higher penalties for serious offences like large-scale duty evasion or dealing in prohibited goods, and for repeat offenders. Officers of customs can also be penalized for certain offences.

act_identification.act_short_title: The Delhi Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1962

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of the Union territory of Delhi

act_overview.preamble: An Act to impose a tax on motor vehicles in the Union territory of Delhi and for other matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to impose a tax on motor vehicles operating or kept for use within the Union territory of Delhi. It also covers related provisions concerning the collection, payment, and enforcement of this tax.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the Union territory of Delhi, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Administrator', 'taxation authority', and 'registered owner'.

key_sections.title: Levy of tax.
key_sections.description: Establishes the levy and collection of tax on motor vehicles used or kept for use in Delhi, based on rates specified in Schedule I.

key_sections.title: Declaration and payment of tax.
key_sections.description: Mandates registered owners to file a declaration and pay the prescribed tax within specified times and manners.

key_sections.title: Issue of token.
key_sections.description: Requires the taxation authority to issue a token upon tax payment or confirmation of no tax payable, to be displayed on the vehicle.

key_sections.title: Refund of tax.
key_sections.description: Outlines conditions and rates for refund of tax when a vehicle is not used, removed from Delhi, or its registration is cancelled.

key_sections.title: Penalty payable when tax not paid.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the taxation authority to impose a penalty, not exceeding the annual tax, for default in tax payment.

key_sections.title: Arrears of tax and penalty recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that unpaid tax and penalties can be recovered as arrears of land revenue, including by distraint and sale of the motor vehicle.

key_sections.title: Exemptions.
key_sections.description: Details specific exemptions from tax payment, including for agriculturists' vehicles and vehicles not in use, and allows the Administrator to grant further exemptions.

key_sections.title: Effect of payment of tax in other States with respect to motor vehicles brought into Delhi.
key_sections.description: Provides for non-payment of tax under this Act for vehicles already taxed in another State, for a limited period.

key_sections.title: Penalty for incomplete and untrue declaration, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for submitting false declarations or obstructing officers in their duties.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Administrator the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including forms, payment methods, and appeal procedures.

key_sections.title: Repeal.
key_sections.description: Repeals several previous Motor Vehicles Taxation Acts as extended to Delhi, while preserving past actions and rights.

act_identification.act_title: THE WAREHOUSING CORPORATIONS ACT, 1962

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the incorporation and regulation of corporations for the purpose of warehousing of agricultural produce and certain other commodities and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish and regulate corporations specifically for the warehousing of agricultural produce and other specified commodities. It covers the formation, management, functions, and financial aspects of both Central and State Warehousing Corporations.

key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its geographical extent, and the date of its commencement.

key_sections.title: Functions of Central Warehousing Corporation.
key_sections.description: Outlines the powers and duties of the Central Warehousing Corporation, including building godowns, running warehouses, and acting as a government agent.

key_sections.title: State Warehousing Corporations.
key_sections.description: Allows State Governments to establish State Warehousing Corporations as bodies corporate.

key_sections.title: Functions of the State Warehousing Corporation.
key_sections.description: Details the functions of State Warehousing Corporations, such as acquiring and building warehouses within the State and acting as agents.

key_sections.title: Borrowing powers of Warehousing Corporation.
key_sections.description: Grants Warehousing Corporations powers to borrow funds by issuing bonds and debentures or from specified banks and financial institutions.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit of Warehousing Corporation.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the maintenance of accounts, annual statements, and the audit process for Warehousing Corporations, involving the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

key_sections.description: Confers power upon the appropriate Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of Warehousing Corporations to make regulations.

key_sections.description: Repeals the Agricultural Produce (Development and Warehousing) Corporations Act, 1956, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under the repealed Act.

State Warehousing Corporation: acquire and build godowns and warehouses, run warehouses for storage, arrange transport, act as an agent of the Central Warehousing Corporation or Government, enter into joint ventures, carry out other prescribed functions.

act_identification.act_title: THE MARINE INSURANCE ACT, 1963

act_overview.preamble: An Act to codify the law relating to marine insurance.
act_overview.purpose: This Act codifies the law relating to marine insurance. It defines marine insurance contracts, insurable interests, and various types of losses, and outlines the rights and liabilities of insurers and assured parties.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'contract of marine insurance', 'freight', 'insurable property', 'marine adventure', and 'maritime perils'.

key_sections.title: Marine insurance defined.
key_sections.description: Defines a contract of marine insurance as an agreement where the insurer indemnifies the assured against losses incidental to marine adventure.

key_sections.title: Avoidance of wagering contracts.
key_sections.description: Declares marine insurance contracts by way of wagering as void and specifies conditions under which a contract is deemed a wagering contract.

key_sections.title: Insurable interest defined.
key_sections.description: Defines insurable interest, stating that a person has an insurable interest if they are interested in a marine adventure and may benefit by its safety or be prejudiced by its loss.

key_sections.title: Insurance is uberrimae fidei.
key_sections.description: States that a contract of marine insurance is based on utmost good faith, and failure to observe it by either party may lead to the contract being avoided.

key_sections.title: Contract must be embodied in policy.
key_sections.description: Mandates that a contract of marine insurance must be embodied in a marine policy to be admitted in evidence.

key_sections.title: Double insurance.
key_sections.description: Addresses situations where an assured is over-insured by two or more policies on the same adventure, outlining the assured's claims and insurers' contributions.

key_sections.title: Nature of warranty.
key_sections.description: Defines a promissory warranty in marine insurance, stating it must be exactly complied with, and non-compliance discharges the insurer from liability.

key_sections.title: Warranty of seaworthiness of ship.
key_sections.description: Establishes an implied warranty in voyage policies that the ship must be seaworthy at the commencement of the voyage for the insured adventure.

key_sections.title: Included and excluded losses.
key_sections.description: Specifies the insurer's liability for losses proximately caused by insured perils and lists certain losses for which the insurer is not liable.

key_sections.title: Partial and total loss.
key_sections.description: Classifies losses into total or partial, and further divides total loss into actual total loss and constructive total loss.

key_sections.title: Constructive total loss defined.
key_sections.description: Defines constructive total loss as when the subject-matter is reasonably abandoned due to unavoidable actual total loss or excessive expenditure to preserve it.

key_sections.title: Right of subrogation.
key_sections.description: Grants the insurer the right to take over the assured's interest and rights/remedies in the subject-matter after paying for a total or partial loss.

key_sections.title: Power to apply Act with modifications, etc., in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to apply the Act with conditions, exceptions, and modifications to contracts relating to ships used in inland navigation.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint date of commencement
Central Government to apply Act with modifications, conditions, and exceptions in certain cases

exemptions: contracts of insurance other than a contract of marine insurance as by this Act defined
wagering contracts
special_provisions: contracts of marine insurance relating to any class of ships exclusively used in inland navigation
