act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for Legislative Assemblies and Councils of Ministers for certain Union territories and for certain other matters.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the establishment of Legislative Assemblies and Councils of Ministers in certain Union territories. It also addresses various other matters related to their governance, legislative powers, and financial administration.

chapter_titles:
PART V
MISCELLANEOUS AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions and interpretation.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms and provides rules for interpretation used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Legislative Assemblies for Union territories and their composition.
key_sections.description: Establishes Legislative Assemblies for Union territories and outlines their composition, including seat allocation and reservation.

key_sections.title: Qualification for membership of Legislative Assembly.
key_sections.description: Specifies the eligibility criteria for individuals to become members of a Legislative Assembly.

key_sections.title: Extent of legislative power.
key_sections.description: Defines the scope of legislative power of the Legislative Assembly to make laws for the Union territory.

key_sections.title: Inconsistency between laws made by Parliament and laws made by Legislative Assembly.
key_sections.description: Addresses situations where there is a conflict between laws made by Parliament and those made by the Legislative Assembly.

key_sections.title: Assent to Bills.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for obtaining assent to Bills passed by the Legislative Assembly, including reservation for the President's consideration.

key_sections.title: Annual financial statement.
key_sections.description: Requires the Administrator to lay an annual financial statement before the Legislative Assembly.

key_sections.title: Rules of procedure.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Legislative Assembly to make rules for regulating its procedure and conduct of business.

key_sections.title: Council of Ministers.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Council of Ministers with a Chief Minister to aid and advise the Administrator in the exercise of functions.

key_sections.title: Other provisions as to Ministers.
key_sections.description: Details the appointment, tenure, collective responsibility, and oaths for Ministers.

key_sections.title: Consolidated Fund of the Union territory.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Consolidated Fund for each Union territory and regulates its operation.

key_sections.title: Provision in case of failure of constitutional machinery.
key_sections.description: Grants the President power to suspend the Act's operation in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a Union territory.

key_sections.title: Power of President to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the President to issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals certain previous laws and includes savings provisions for actions taken under those repealed laws.

act_identification.act_title: THE OFFICIAL LANGUAGES ACT, 1963
act_identification.date_of_commencement: Section 3 shall come into force on the 26th day of January, 1965 and the remaining provisions of this Act shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the languages which may be used for the official purposes of the Union, for transaction of business in Parliament, for Central and State Acts and for certain purposes in High Courts.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the continued use of the English language for official purposes of the Union and in Parliament, alongside Hindi. It also makes provisions for the use of Hindi in Central and State Acts, and optionally in High Courts' judgments.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and specifies the commencement dates for different sections.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'appointed day' and 'Hindi'.

key_sections.title: Continuance of English language for official purposes of the Union and for use in Parliament.
key_sections.description: Mandates the continued use of English alongside Hindi for official purposes of the Union and in Parliament, with provisions for communication between the Union and States, and between States.

key_sections.title: Committee on Official Language.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a Committee on Official Language to review the progress of Hindi's use and submit recommendations to the President.

key_sections.title: Authorised Hindi translations of Central Acts, etc.
key_sections.description: Declares Hindi translations of Central Acts, Ordinances, rules, regulations, and bye-laws published under Presidential authority as authoritative texts, and requires Hindi translations for Bills in Parliament.

key_sections.title: Authorised Hindi translation of State Acts in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Allows for authoritative Hindi translations of State Acts and Ordinances to be published by the Governor's authority in certain cases.

key_sections.title: Optional use of Hindi or other official language in judgments, etc., of High Courts.
key_sections.description: Permits the Governor of a State, with Presidential consent, to authorize the use of Hindi or the State's official language in High Court judgments, decrees, or orders, requiring an English translation.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, subject to parliamentary review.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint commencement dates for provisions of the Act (Section 1(2))
Central Government to provide for the language or languages to be used for official purposes of the Union by rules (Section 3(4))

Governor of a State, with previous consent of the President, to authorize the use of Hindi or the official language of the State in judgments, decrees or orders of High Courts (Section 7)
Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act (Section 8(1))

act_identification.act_title: THE EXPORT (QUALITY CONTROL AND INSPECTION) ACT, 1963
act_identification.act_short_title: THE EXPORT (QUALITY CONTROL AND INSPECTION) ACT, 1963

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the sound development of the export trade of India through quality control and inspection and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to foster the robust growth of India's export trade by implementing quality control and inspection mechanisms for commodities intended for export, along with addressing related matters.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application across India, and its effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'adjudicating authority', 'export', 'inspection', and 'quality control'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Export Inspection Council.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the Export Inspection Council, its composition, and corporate status.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Council.
key_sections.description: Outlines the advisory, programmatic, and grant-making functions of the Export Inspection Council.

key_sections.title: Powers of the Central Government in regard to quality control and inspection.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government powers to notify commodities for quality control, specify inspection types, set standards, and prohibit export without certification.

key_sections.title: Machinery for quality control and inspection.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to establish or recognise agencies for quality control and inspection, and details their examination and certification processes.

key_sections.title: Power to enter and inspect.
key_sections.description: Authorises the Director of Inspection and Quality Control or an authorised officer to enter and inspect premises for commodities or documents related to the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to seize commodities, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants authorised officers the power to seize commodities, packages, and documents liable to confiscation under the Act.

key_sections.title: Confiscation.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which commodities, packages, and other goods are liable to confiscation, particularly in cases of fraud or contravention of the Act.

key_sections.title: Liability to penalty.
key_sections.description: Establishes penalties for persons involved in acts or omissions that render commodities liable to confiscation, or for dealing with such commodities.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for contravening specific orders, fraudulently obtaining certificates, or affixing marks/seals.

key_sections.title: Suspension, etc., of operation of the provisions of the Act.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to suspend or relax the operation of the Act's provisions in public interest for specific commodities, areas, or periods.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Act to over-ride other enactments.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over other enactments concerning quality control and inspection of export commodities.

powers_conferred: Central Government: establish Export Inspection Council (Section 3), appoint Director of Inspection and Quality Control (Section 4), give directions to the Council (Section 5), notify commodities for quality control/inspection (Section 6), specify type of quality control/inspection (Section 6), establish/adopt/recognise standard specifications (Section 6), prohibit export without certificate/mark (Section 6), establish/recognise agencies for quality control/inspection (Section 7), recognise/establish marks or seals (Section 8), require information from exporters (Section 9), pay grants/loans to the Council (Section 10), delegate powers (Section 13), authorise prosecution (Section 14), suspend or relax operation of provisions (Section 16A), make rules (Section 17).

Export Inspection Council: advise Central Government on quality control and inspection for exports (Section 5), draw up programmes (Section 5), make grants-in-aid to agencies (Section 5), perform other assigned functions (Section 5), co-opt members (Section 5), constitute specialist committees (Section 5), appoint officers and employees (Section 3(5)).

Director of Inspection and Quality Control: exercise prescribed powers and duties (Section 4), enter and inspect premises (Section 10A), search premises (Section 10B), seize commodities, packages, documents (Section 10C), stop and seize conveyances (Section 10D), adjudicate confiscation or impose penalty (Section 10K).

Agencies for quality control or inspection: hold examinations relating to quality control/inspection (Section 7), issue certificates (Section 7), amend, suspend or cancel certificates (Section 7(3A)).
Adjudicating authority: adjudicate confiscation, impose penalty (Section 10K), exercise powers of a civil court (Section 10-O).
Appellate authority: hear appeals against decisions/orders (Section 10M), exercise powers of a civil court (Section 10-O).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person contravening an order under Section 6(d), fraudulently obtaining a certificate under Section 7, or fraudulently affixing a mark/seal under Section 8(1) is punishable for the first offence with imprisonment up to two years or fine up to five thousand rupees or both; for subsequent offences, imprisonment up to three years and fine up to five thousand rupees (with a minimum of three months imprisonment). Attempt or abetment of such offences is also punishable. Contravention of any other provision, rule, or order incurs a fine up to one thousand rupees (Section 11). Failure to pay penalty or comply with an order of adjudicating/Appellate authority is punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both (Section 11A). Officers/employees of the Council/agency/testing house involved in contravention or searching without reason, or unlawfully disclosing information, are subject to imprisonment and/or fines (Section 11B). Persons liable to penalty under Section 10-I face a penalty not exceeding five times the commodity's value or five thousand rupees, whichever is more. Commodities and conveyances are liable to confiscation (Sections 10F, 10G).

authorities_established: Director of Inspection and Quality Control
agencies for quality control or inspection
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairman and nominates other members of the Export Inspection Council, and appoints the Director of Inspection and Quality Control. The Council may appoint its own officers and other employees.
regulatory_bodies: agencies for quality control or inspection

applies_to: export trade of India
commodities intended for export
persons manufacturing, dealing in or exporting notified commodities
special_provisions: The Central Government may suspend or relax the operation of the Act's provisions for specific notified commodities, generally or in respect of any area and for such period as specified, in the public interest (Section 16A).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the establishment of the Export Inspection Council and agencies for quality control and inspection. The Central Government has powers to notify commodities, specify inspection types, and prohibit export without certification. Enforcement includes powers of entry, inspection, search, and seizure by authorised officers, leading to confiscation of goods and conveyances, and imposition of penalties. Adjudication is carried out by the Director of Inspection and Quality Control or subordinate officers, with provisions for appeals and revisions. Prosecutions are instituted by or with the consent of an officer authorised by the Central Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts of law (for questioning decisions), civil courts (for adjudicating and appellate authorities' powers), and Civil Courts for purposes of sections 345 and 346 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

act_identification.act_title: THE LIMITATION ACT, 1963

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law for the limitation of suits and other proceedings and for purposes connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to consolidate and amend the law relating to the limitation of suits, appeals, and applications. It sets out the time periods within which legal proceedings must be initiated to ensure timely justice and prevent stale claims.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official name of the Act, its geographical applicability to the whole of India, and that it came into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'applicant', 'application', 'defendant', 'plaintiff', 'period of limitation', 'suit', and 'trustee'.

key_sections.title: Bar of limitation.
key_sections.description: States that any suit, appeal, or application filed after the prescribed period shall be dismissed, even if limitation is not raised as a defence, and defines when a suit is deemed instituted.

key_sections.title: Extension of prescribed period in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Allows for the extension of the prescribed period for appeals or applications (with exceptions) if the appellant or applicant can demonstrate sufficient cause for the delay.

key_sections.title: Legal disability.
key_sections.description: Provides for an extension of the limitation period for persons under legal disability (minor, insane, or idiot) at the time the period is to be reckoned.

key_sections.title: Suits against trustees and their representatives.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that suits against trustees for specific purposes or their representatives to recover trust property or its proceeds are not barred by any length of time.

key_sections.title: Exclusion of time in legal proceedings.
key_sections.description: Details how time spent in obtaining copies of judgments, decrees, or orders, or the day from which the period is reckoned, should be excluded when computing the period of limitation.

key_sections.title: Exclusion of time of proceeding bona fide in court without jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Allows for the exclusion of time spent prosecuting a civil proceeding in good faith in a court that lacked jurisdiction, when computing the limitation period for a subsequent suit or application.

key_sections.title: Effect of fraud or mistake.
key_sections.description: Provides that the period of limitation does not begin to run until the plaintiff or applicant discovers fraud or mistake, or could have discovered it with reasonable diligence.

key_sections.title: Effect of acknowledgment in writing.
key_sections.description: States that a fresh period of limitation is computed from the time an acknowledgment of liability in writing is signed before the expiration of the prescribed period.

key_sections.title: Acquisition of easements by prescription.
key_sections.description: Outlines the conditions under which easements (like access to light, air, way, or watercourse) can be acquired by peaceable and open enjoyment for a specified period (20 or 30 years).

key_sections.title: Extinguishment of right to property.
key_sections.description: Declares that if a person fails to institute a suit for possession of property within the limited period, their right to that property shall be extinguished.

key_sections.title: Savings.
key_sections.description: Specifies that the Act does not affect Section 25 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, and clarifies the applicability of its provisions to special or local laws and laws relating to marriage and divorce.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint the date of commencement of the Act (Section 1(3)).
Courts to admit appeals or applications after the prescribed period if sufficient cause is shown (Section 5).
Courts to treat a suit or appeal as if court fees had been paid in the first instance, after rejection of pauper application (Section 13).
Courts to grant permission for a fresh suit in certain circumstances (Section 14(3)).
Courts to extend the period for execution of a decree or order in cases of fraud or force by the judgment-debtor (Section 17(2)).

repealed_acts: Indian Limitation Act, 1908
Limitation Act, Samvat 1995

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government has the power to appoint the date of commencement of the Act.

applies_to: Whole of India
Suits
Appeals
Applications
exemptions: Suits or other proceedings under any law for the time being in force with respect to marriage and divorce (Section 29(3)).
Cases arising in territories to which the Indian Easements Act, 1882, extends, for Sections 25 and 26 and the definition of “easement” in Section 2 (Section 29(4)).
special_provisions: Special provisions for suits, etc., for which the prescribed period is shorter than the period prescribed by the Indian Limitation Act, 1908 (Section 30).
Special provisions for suits, etc., for which the prescribed period is shorter than the period prescribed by the Limitation Act, Samvat 1995, for Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh (UTs) (Section 30A).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced by courts dismissing any suit, appeal, or application instituted, preferred, or made after the prescribed period of limitation (Section 3).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil courts, High Courts, Supreme Court, Courts of Session (as referenced in the Schedule for appeals and applications).

schedules_summary.description: This Schedule, titled 'PERIODS OF LIMITATION', is divided into three main divisions: First Division for Suits, Second Division for Appeals, and Third Division for Applications. It lists various types of legal actions, their corresponding periods of limitation, and the specific time from which each period begins to run. The First Division (Suits) is further categorized into parts such as 'Suits relating to Accounts', 'Suits relating to Contracts', 'Suits relating to Declarations', 'Suits relating to Decrees and Instruments', 'Suits relating to Immovable Property', 'Suits relating to Movable Property', 'Suits relating to Tort', 'Suits relating to Trusts and Trust Property', and 'Suits relating to Miscellaneous Matters', along with a general category for 'Suits for which there is no prescribed period'. The Second Division (Appeals) covers appeals under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, and the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. The Third Division (Applications) covers applications in specified cases under various Acts and general 'Other Applications'.

act_identification.act_title: THE TEXTILES COMMITTEE ACT, 1963

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Committee for ensuring the quality of textiles and textile machinery and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the establishment of a Committee to ensure standard qualities of textiles and textile machinery for both internal marketing and export purposes. It also covers related matters such as inspection, cess imposition, and regulation of the textile industry.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Textiles Committee.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of the Textiles Committee as a body corporate and outlines its composition.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Committee.
key_sections.description: Details the general and specific functions of the Committee, primarily to ensure standard qualities of textiles and textile machinery.

key_sections.title: Powers of the Committee.
key_sections.description: Grants the Committee necessary powers to carry out its functions under the Act.

key_sections.title: Imposition of cess on textiles and textile machinery manufactured in India.
key_sections.description: Provides for the levy and collection of a cess on textiles and textile machinery manufactured in India, with certain exemptions.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to constitute a Tribunal for hearing appeals related to cess assessments.

key_sections.title: Inspection.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Committee to direct officers to examine the quality of textiles or suitability of textile machinery and submit reports.

key_sections.title: Levy of fees for inspection and examination.
key_sections.description: Allows the Committee to levy fees for inspection, examination, and special services, with provisions for exemption.

key_sections.title: Power to prohibit exports and internal marketing of textiles and textile machinery.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to prohibit the export or internal sale of textiles or textile machinery that do not conform to specified standards.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Committee to make regulations with the previous sanction of the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Repeal and Saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Cotton Textiles Fund Ordinance, 1944, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of an order prohibiting export or sale of textiles or textile machinery under Section 17(1) is punishable. For the first offence, imprisonment up to one year or fine or both. For the second or subsequent offence, imprisonment up to one year and also with fine, with a minimum of three months imprisonment in the absence of special reasons. Courts may also direct forfeiture of the textiles or textile machinery. Offences by companies are also addressed, holding persons in charge and the company liable, with provisions for proving lack of knowledge or due diligence.

act_overview.purpose: This Act consolidates and amends the law concerning the office and responsibilities of Administrators-General. act_identification.act_title: THE SPECIFIC RELIEF ACT, 1963

act_overview.preamble: An Act to define and amend the law relating to certain kinds of specific relief.
act_overview.purpose: The Act defines and amends the law relating to specific relief, providing for the recovery of property, specific performance of contracts, rectification of instruments, rescission of contracts, cancellation of instruments, declaratory decrees, and preventive relief through injunctions.

key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used within the Act, such as 'obligation', 'settlement', 'trust', and 'trustee'.

key_sections.title: Specific relief to be granted only for enforcing individual civil rights and not for enforcing penal laws.
key_sections.description: States that specific relief is granted solely for enforcing individual civil rights, not penal laws.

key_sections.title: Recovery of specific immovable property.
key_sections.description: Outlines the manner in which a person entitled to possession of specific immovable property may recover it.

key_sections.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property.
key_sections.description: Allows a person dispossessed of immovable property without consent to sue for recovery, with certain limitations.

key_sections.title: Recovery of specific movable property.
key_sections.description: Describes the process for recovering specific movable property.

key_sections.title: Specific performance in respect of contracts.
key_sections.description: Stipulates when the specific performance of a contract shall be enforced by the court.

key_sections.title: Contracts not specifically enforceable.
key_sections.description: Lists types of contracts that cannot be specifically enforced, such as those involving continuous duty or personal qualifications.

key_sections.title: Power of court to engage experts.
key_sections.description: Grants the court power to engage experts to assist on specific issues in a suit under this Act.

key_sections.title: Personal bars to relief.
key_sections.description: Enumerates conditions under which specific performance of a contract cannot be enforced in favour of a person.

key_sections.title: Substituted performance of contract.
key_sections.description: Provides for substituted performance of a contract through a third party or own agency when a contract is broken, allowing recovery of expenses.

key_sections.title: Special provisions for contract relating to infrastructure project.

key_sections.title: When instrument may be rectified.

key_sections.title: When rescission may be adjudged or refused.
key_sections.description: Specifies the circumstances under which a contract may be rescinded by the court or when rescission may be refused.

key_sections.title: When cancellation may be ordered.
key_sections.description: Empowers the court to order the cancellation of a written instrument that is void or voidable and may cause serious injury if left outstanding.

key_sections.title: Discretion of court as to declaration of status or right.

key_sections.title: Preventive relief how granted.

key_sections.title: Injunction when refused.
key_sections.description: Lists the specific cases in which an injunction cannot be granted by the court.

Court's power to direct specific performance of part of a contract and award compensation (Section 12)
Court's power to engage experts to assist on specific issues (Section 14A)

Court's power to grant relief for possession, partition, or refund of earnest money (Section 22)
Court's power to rectify instruments (Section 26)
Court's power to adjudge or refuse rescission of contracts (Section 27)
Court's power to order cancellation of instruments (Section 31)
Court's power to make declaratory decrees regarding status or right (Section 34)
Court's power to grant preventive relief through injunctions (Section 36, 38, 39)
Central Government's power to amend the Schedule relating to infrastructure projects (Section 20A(2))
State Government's power to designate Special Courts for infrastructure projects (Section 20B)

act_identification.act_title: THE COMPANIES (PROFITS) SURTAX ACT, 1964

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to impose a special tax, known as surtax, on the profits of certain companies. It defines chargeable profits, outlines the assessment and collection procedures, and provides for appeals and penalties related to this tax.

key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Definitions.

key_sections.title: Tax authorities.
key_sections.description: Designates income-tax authorities as authorities for this Act and outlines the Board's power to issue instructions.

key_sections.title: Charge of tax.
key_sections.description: Establishes the levy of surtax on chargeable profits of companies for specified assessment years.

key_sections.title: Return of chargeable profits.
key_sections.description: Mandates companies to furnish returns of chargeable profits and empowers the Assessing Officer to require such returns.

key_sections.title: Assessment.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for the Assessing Officer to assess chargeable profits and the amount of surtax payable.

key_sections.title: Advance payment of surtax.

key_sections.title: Penalties.

key_sections.title: Appeals to the Commissioner (Appeals).
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals against assessment orders, penalties, interest levies, or refusal of relief to the Commissioner (Appeals).

key_sections.title: Appeals to Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Allows assessees and the Chief Commissioner or Commissioner to appeal orders to the Appellate Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Application of provisions of Income-tax Act.
key_sections.description: Specifies sections and schedules of the Income-tax Act that apply to this Act with necessary modifications.

key_sections.title: Failure to deliver returns, etc.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board, subject to Central Government control, the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes.

Board: Make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 25(1)).

Assessing Officer: Serve notice to furnish returns (Section 5(2)).

Assessing Officer: Assess chargeable profits and surtax (Section 6(2)).

Assessing Officer: Direct payment of interest in case of underestimate (Section 7D).

Appellate Tribunal: Admit an appeal or permit the filing of a memorandum of cross objections after the expiry of the relevant period (Section 12(5)).

Chief Commissioner or Commissioner: Revise orders (Section 17(1)).
Chief Commissioner or Commissioner: Institute proceedings and compound offences (Section 23).
Central Government: Make exemption, reduction in rate or other modification in respect of surtax for certain Union territories (Section 24).
Central Government: Enter into agreements with foreign countries for relief, avoidance of double taxation, exchange of information, or recovery of tax (Section 24A).
Central Government: Make exemption, reduction in rate or other modification in respect of surtax for certain foreign companies in mineral oil business (Section 24AA).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 9 prescribes penalties for failure to furnish returns, produce documents, conceal particulars, or furnish inaccurate particulars of chargeable profits, with penalties up to the amount of surtax chargeable or avoided. Section 9A imposes penalties for false estimates or failure to pay advance surtax, ranging from ten percent to one and a half times the shortfall. Section 20 makes failure to deliver returns or produce documents punishable with a fine up to five hundred rupees, and a further fine of ten rupees per day of default. Sections 21 and 22 make false statements or abetment of false returns punishable with simple imprisonment up to six months, or a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.

Foreign companies involved in prospecting for, extraction, etc., of mineral oils (Section 24AA)

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS, in pursuance of clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution, resolutions have been passed by the Legislatures of certain State to the effect that storage of commodities other than those covered by the Warehousing Corporations Act, 1962 (58 of 1962), in warehouses run by the corporations established under that Act, shall be regulated in those States by Parliament by law. act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to supplement the Warehousing Corporations Act, 1962, by extending its provisions to cover the storage of commodities not originally included in the 1962 Act. act_identification.act_title: THE RAILWAYS (EMPLOYMENT OF MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES) ACT, 1965
act_identification.act_short_title: The Railways (Employment of Members of the Armed Forces) Act, 1965

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make certain provisions relating to the employment of members of the Armed Forces of the Union in the working and management of railways.
act_overview.purpose: This Act makes provisions for the employment of members of the Armed Forces of the Union in the working and management of railways. It defines their powers, duties, and liabilities when assisting a railway administration and outlines conditions when they replace it.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and specifies its territorial application to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Interpretation.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that words and expressions used in this Act, if defined in the Indian Railways Act, 1890, shall carry the same meanings as in that Act.

key_sections.title: Employment of members of Armed Forces of the Union to assist a railway administration in connection with the service of a railway.
key_sections.description: Details that when Armed Forces members assist a railway, provisions of the Indian Railways Act, 1890, regarding powers, status, immunity, duties, or liabilities of railway servants, apply to them, without affecting railway administration's liability or Chapter VIA of the 1890 Act.

key_sections.title: Employment of members of Armed Forces of the Union to replace railway administration in working a railway.
key_sections.description: Provides that if the Armed Forces assume the entire working, management, and maintenance of a railway, the Central Government may notify this, and the Indian Railways Act, 1890, will cease to apply to that railway for the duration of such assumption.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Railways (Employment of Members of the Armed Forces) Ordinance, 1965, and saves actions taken under it as if they were done under this Act from 29th September, 1965.

powers_conferred: Power to Central Government to notify the assumption of railway working, management, and maintenance by the Armed Forces of the Union (Section 4).

Powers, status, or immunity conferred upon a railway servant under the Indian Railways Act, 1890, are conferred upon members of the Armed Forces of the Union when employed to assist a railway administration (Section 3(1)(a)).

repealed_acts: The Railways (Employment of Members of the Armed Forces) Ordinance, 1965 (Ord. 4 of 1965)

applies_to: Members of the Armed Forces of the Union when employed to assist a railway administration in connection with the service of a railway (Section 3).
Members of the Armed Forces of the Union when assuming the whole of the working, management and maintenance of a railway (Section 4).
exemptions: Provisions of Chapter VIA of the Indian Railways Act, 1890, are not applicable to members of the Armed Forces of the Union employed to assist a railway administration (Section 3(2)).
The Indian Railways Act, 1890, ceases to be applicable to a railway or its portion/section when its working, management, and maintenance is assumed by the Armed Forces of the Union (Section 4).

key_sections.title: Reserve Bank to be depository for Bank.

key_sections.title: Conferment of status and certain immunities, exemptions and privileges on Bank and conferment of certain immunities, exemptions and privileges on its officers and employees.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.

key_sections.title: Notifications issued under section 5 and rules made under section 6 to be laid before Parliament.

act_identification.act_title: THE DELHI HIGH COURT ACT, 1966

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Seventeenth Year of the Republic of India
legislative_details.geographical_extent: Union territory of Delhi, Union territory of Himachal Pradesh

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution of a High Court for the Union territory of Delhi, for the extension of the jurisdiction of that High Court to the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the establishment of a High Court for the Union territory of Delhi. It also extends the jurisdiction of this High Court to the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh. The Act addresses various matters connected with the constitution and functioning of the High Court.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date, with a special provision for Section 17.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, such as 'appointed day' and 'notified order'.

key_sections.title: High Court.
key_sections.description: Establishes the High Court for the Union territory of Delhi, specifies its principal seat, and allows for Judges and Division Courts to sit at other places.

key_sections.title: Salaries and allowances or Judges to be expenditure charged on Consolidated Fund of India.
key_sections.description: Declares that the expenditure for salaries and allowances of High Court Judges shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

key_sections.title: Exceptions and modifications subject to which the provisions of Chapter V of Part VI of the Constitution apply to the High Court of Delhi.
key_sections.description: Outlines specific exceptions and modifications to the application of Chapter V of Part VI of the Constitution for the High Court of Delhi.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of High Court of Delhi.
key_sections.description: Defines the original, appellate, and other jurisdictions of the High Court of Delhi over the Union territory of Delhi, including ordinary original civil jurisdiction for suits exceeding a specified value.

key_sections.title: Power to enrol legal practitioners, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants the High Court of Delhi powers to approve, admit, enrol, remove, and suspend legal practitioners, and to make rules concerning them, similar to the High Court of Punjab.

key_sections.title: Practice and procedure in the High Court of Delhi.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the practice and procedure of the High Court of Punjab shall apply to the High Court of Delhi, with necessary modifications, and grants rule-making powers to the Delhi High Court.

key_sections.title: Transfer of proceedings from the High Court of Punjab to the High Court of Delhi.
key_sections.description: Details the transfer of pending proceedings from the High Court of Punjab to the High Court of Delhi and defines the jurisdiction of both courts regarding such transfers.

key_sections.title: Extension of the jurisdiction of the High Court of Delhi.
key_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the High Court of Delhi to the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh, abolishes the Court of the Judicial Commissioner for Himachal Pradesh, and provides for the transfer of proceedings.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make provisions by notified order to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Power to adapt laws.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to adapt and modify laws to facilitate their application in relation to the Union territories of Delhi and Himachal Pradesh.

act_identification.act_title: THE RAILWAY PROPERTY (UNLAWFUL POSSESSION) ACT, 1966

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Seventeenth Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to unlawful possession of railway property. BE it enacted by Parliament in the Seventeenth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to unlawful possession of railway property.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, such as 'Force', 'railway property', and 'superior officer'.

key_sections.title: Penalty for theft, dishonest misappropriation or unlawful possession of railway property].—[3][Whoever commits theft, or dishonestly misappropriates or is found, or is proved] to have been, in possession of any railway property reasonably suspected of having been stolen or unlawfully obtained shall, unless he proves that the railway property came into his possession lawfully, be punishable—
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for theft, dishonest misappropriation, or unlawful possession of railway property, including imprisonment and fine, with enhanced penalties for subsequent offences.

key_sections.title: [1][Punishment for abetment, conspiracy or connivance at offences.]—[2][Whoever abets or conspires in the commission of an offence punishable under this Act, or any owner] or occupier of land or building, or any agent of such owner or occupier in charge of the management of that land or building, who wilfully connives at an offence against the provisions of this Act, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both.
key_sections.description: Stipulates punishment for abetment, conspiracy, or wilful connivance at offences under this Act.

key_sections.title: Offences under the Act not to be cognizable.
key_sections.description: Declares that offences under this Act are not cognizable, notwithstanding the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.

key_sections.title: Power to arrest without warrant.
key_sections.description: Grants superior officers or members of the Force the power to arrest persons without a warrant for offences under this Act.

key_sections.title: [4][Inquiry how to be made].—(1) [5][When an officer of the Force receives information about the commission of an offence punishable under this Act, or when any person is arrested] by an officer of the Force for an offence punishable under this Act or is forwarded to him under section 7, he shall proceed to inquire into the charge against such person.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for inquiry into charges by an officer of the Force, including powers similar to a police-station in-charge and provisions for bail or forwarding to a Magistrate.

key_sections.title: Power to summon persons to give evidence and produce documents.
key_sections.description: Confers power on officers of the Force to summon persons for evidence or document production during an inquiry.

key_sections.title: Issue of search warrant.
key_sections.description: Details the process for an officer of the Force to apply for and a Magistrate to issue a search warrant for places suspected of holding stolen or unlawfully obtained railway property.

key_sections.title: Power of courts to order forfeiture of vehicles, etc.
key_sections.description: Empowers courts to order the forfeiture of property, receptacles, packages, coverings, animals, vehicles, or other conveyances used in committing an offence under this Act.

key_sections.title: Act to override other laws.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in any other law.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Railway Stores (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1955, and includes savings clauses regarding past offences and the General Clauses Act, 1897.

Officer of the Force shall proceed to inquire into the charge (Section 8(1))

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 3 defines offences of theft, dishonest misappropriation, or unlawful possession of railway property, punishable with imprisonment up to five years, or fine, or both, with minimum penalties for first and subsequent offences. Section 4 defines offences of abetment, conspiracy, or wilful connivance at offences, punishable with imprisonment up to five years, or fine, or both.

repealed_acts: The Railway Stores (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1955 (51 of 1955)
related_acts: Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization (Adaptation of Central Laws) Order, 2020
Union Territory of Ladakh Reorganisation (Adaptation of Central Laws) Order, 2020

applies_to: Persons who commit theft, dishonestly misappropriate or are found in possession of railway property
Persons who abet or conspire in the commission of an offence
Owners or occupiers of land or building, or their agents, who wilfully connive at an offence
exemptions: Exemptions under sections 132 and 133 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, are applicable to requisitions for attendance under section 9.
special_provisions: Section 15, titled 'Construction of references to laws not in force in Jammu and Kashmir', which was later omitted by specific Reorganisation Orders.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced through arrest without warrant by superior officers or members of the Force, inquiry by officers of the Force, issuance of search warrants by Magistrates, and assistance from Government and village officers. Courts have the power to order forfeiture of property.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate having jurisdiction; Any court trying an offence punishable under this Act

act_identification.act_title: THE PUNJAB REORGANISATION ACT, 1966

legislative_details.geographical_extent: The existing State of Punjab and its successor States (Punjab, Haryana) and Union territories (Chandigarh, Himachal Pradesh)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the reorganisation of the existing State of Punjab and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the reorganisation of the existing State of Punjab by forming the new State of Haryana, creating the Union territory of Chandigarh, and transferring certain territories to the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh. It also addresses consequential matters such as representation in legislatures, High Court jurisdiction, apportionment of assets and liabilities, provisions for corporations and services, and other legal and miscellaneous provisions.

key_sections.title: Formation of Haryana State.
key_sections.description: Establishes the new State of Haryana from specified territories of the existing State of Punjab, effective from the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Formation of Union territory of Chandigarh.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Union territory of Chandigarh from specified territories of the existing State of Punjab, effective from the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Transfer of territory from Punjab to Himachal Pradesh.

key_sections.title: Common High Court for Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh.
key_sections.description: Establishes a common High Court for the States of Punjab and Haryana and the Union territory of Chandigarh, to be called the High Court of Punjab and Haryana.

key_sections.title: Application of Part.

key_sections.title: Rights and liabilities in regard to Bhakra-Nangal and Beas Projects.

key_sections.title: Bhakra Management Board.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to All-India Services.
key_sections.description: Outlines the creation of separate cadres for the Indian Administrative Service and Indian Police Service for Punjab and Haryana, and the allocation of existing members.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to other Services.
key_sections.description: Details the provisional and final allocation of persons serving in connection with the affairs of the existing State of Punjab to the successor States.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, including specific matters related to the Bhakra Management Board and Beas Construction Board.

act_identification.date_of_commencement: It shall come into force in a State on such date as the State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint and different dates may be appointed by the State Government for different areas and for different provisions of this Act.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the welfare of the workers in beedi and cigar establishments and to regulate the conditions of their work and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to ensure the welfare of workers employed in beedi and cigar manufacturing establishments. It seeks to regulate their working conditions, including aspects like working hours, leave, and workplace amenities, and addresses related matters.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and commencement procedure.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'adult', 'child', 'employee', 'employer', and 'industrial premises'.

key_sections.title: Industrial premises to be licensed.
key_sections.description: Mandates that all industrial premises used for beedi and cigar manufacturing must hold a valid license.

key_sections.title: Licences.
key_sections.description: Outlines the application, grant, renewal, and cancellation process for licenses, and factors considered by the competent authority.

key_sections.title: Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to appoint Inspectors and a Chief Inspector for the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Powers of Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Details the powers of Inspectors, including examination, inquiry, requiring document production, and entering premises.

key_sections.title: Working hours.
key_sections.description: Sets limits on daily and weekly working hours for employees and provides for overtime work.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of employment of children.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the employment of children in any industrial premises.

key_sections.title: Annual leave with wages.
key_sections.description: Establishes provisions for annual leave with wages for adult and young persons, including accumulation and payment upon termination.

key_sections.title: Notice of dismissal.
key_sections.description: Requires employers to give one month's notice or wages in lieu thereof before dismissing an employee, and provides for appeals against dismissal.

key_sections.title: General penalty for offence.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for general contraventions of the Act or rules, and for failure to reinstate employees.

key_sections.title: Application of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 and the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961.
key_sections.description: Specifies the applicability of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act and the Maternity Benefit Act to industrial premises and establishments under this Act.

key_sections.title: Effect of laws and agreements inconsistent with this Act.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over inconsistent laws or agreements, while allowing for more favourable benefits to employees.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply to self-employed persons in private dwelling houses.
key_sections.description: Exempts self-employed persons working with family assistance in private dwelling houses from the Act's provisions, provided they are not employees.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, detailing specific matters for which rules can be made.

Central Government: To give directions to a State Government regarding execution of the Act (Section 42)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties are prescribed for obstructing an Inspector (imprisonment up to six months, fine up to five thousand rupees, or both). General contraventions of the Act or rules, or failure to pay wages/compensation, are punishable with a fine up to two hundred and fifty rupees for the first offence, and for subsequent offences, imprisonment for one to six months, a fine of one hundred to five hundred rupees, or both. Failure to reinstate an employee carries a fine up to two hundred and fifty rupees, with a daily fine of twenty rupees for continuing default. Offences by companies also hold persons in charge and, in certain cases, directors/managers, liable.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government has the power to appoint the competent authority, Inspectors, and the Chief Inspector. The State Government also specifies the appellate authority.

applies_to: Workers in beedi and cigar establishments
Employees (including home workers) in any establishment or industrial premises
Industrial premises where manufacturing process connected with beedi or cigar is carried on
exemptions: Self-employed persons in private dwelling houses who carry on manufacturing with the assistance of family members living with and dependent on them, provided the owner/occupier is not an employee of an employer to whom this Act applies (Section 43).

Classes of industrial premises, employers, or employees may be exempted by the State Government, except for women employees regarding annual leave with wages, maternity benefits, creches, wages, rejection of beedi/cigar, and night work (Section 41).
special_provisions: The Act initially extended to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir, but was later made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.
The Act may come into force on different dates in different States, areas, and for different provisions as appointed by the State Government.
Special provisions are made for 'home workers' who receive raw materials for making beedi or cigar at home.
Prohibition of employment of children and restrictions on employment of women or young persons during certain hours.

Specific disputes between employer and employee regarding raw materials, rejection of beedi/cigar, and payment of wages for rejected items shall be referred for settlement as specified by State Government rules.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a licensing system for industrial premises, appointment of Inspectors with powers to ensure compliance, and penalties for contraventions. The State Government can issue rules for implementation and the Central Government can give directions. Provisions of other labour laws like the Payment of Wages Act, Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, Maternity Benefit Act, and Industrial Disputes Act are also applied or adapted for enforcement.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No Court inferior to that of a presidency magistrate or a magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE POLICE-FORCES (RESTRICTION OF RIGHTS) ACT, 1966
act_identification.date_of_commencement: on such date as may be appointed in this behalf by notification in the Official Gazette

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the restriction of certain rights conferred by Part III of the Constitution in their application to the members of the Forces charged with the maintenance of public order so as to ensure the proper discharge of their duties and the maintenance of discipline among them.
act_overview.purpose: This Act restricts certain fundamental rights of members of police forces, including the right to form associations and freedom of speech, to ensure the proper discharge of their duties and maintain discipline within forces responsible for public order.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title, geographical extent, and commencement provisions for the Act, allowing for different dates for Union territories and States.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'member of a police-force', 'police-force', and 'prescribed'.

key_sections.title: Restrictions respecting right to form association, freedom of speech, etc.
key_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on members of police forces regarding forming associations, communicating with the press, and participating in political activities without express sanction.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of the restrictions laid down in section 3, including imprisonment or fine or both.

key_sections.title: Power to amend Schedule.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.

Central Government: to amend the Schedule
Central Government: to make rules

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person contravening section 3 shall be punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or with fine up to two thousand rupees, or with both.

member of a police-force

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through penalties for contravention of restrictions and rules made by the Central Government.

act_identification.act_title: THE POST-GRADUATE INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH, CHANDIGARH ACT, 1966
act_identification.act_short_title: The Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, Act 1966

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Union territory of Chandigarh (where the Institute is located)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare the institution known as the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, to be an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act declares the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, as an institution of national importance. Its purpose is to incorporate this institution, provide for its administration, and enable it to develop high standards of medical education, research, and training in various health activities to meet national needs for specialists and medical teachers.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Declaration of Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, as an institution of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, as an institution of national importance.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Fund', 'Governing Body', and 'Institute'.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of Institute.
key_sections.description: Constitutes the Institute as a body corporate with perpetual succession, common seal, and powers to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.

key_sections.title: Objects of Institute.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary objectives of the Institute, including developing high standards of medical education, providing top-tier educational facilities, and achieving self-sufficiency in post-graduate medical education.

key_sections.title: Functions of Institute.
key_sections.description: Details the various functions the Institute may undertake to promote its objects, such as providing teaching and research facilities, establishing colleges and hospitals, granting degrees, and receiving grants.

key_sections.title: Grant of medical degrees, diplomas, etc., by Institute.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Institute to grant medical degrees, diplomas, and other academic distinctions.

key_sections.title: Recognition of medical qualifications granted by Institute.
key_sections.description: Ensures that medical degrees and diplomas granted by the Institute are recognized medical qualifications under the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956.

key_sections.title: Control by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the Institute shall comply with directions issued by the Central Government for the efficient administration of the Act.

key_sections.title: Transfer of service of existing employees.
key_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of employees of the existing Post-Graduate Institute to the newly incorporated Institute, maintaining their terms and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Continuance of facilities at Institute.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Institute to continue providing facilities to the Governments and people of Haryana, Punjab, Chandigarh, and Himachal Pradesh under specified terms.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, after consultation with the Institute.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulation.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Institute, with Central Government approval, to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules for its administration.

authorities_established: The Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government nominates members to the Institute, including representatives from various ministries and other persons, and also nominates the President of the Institute and appoints the first Director.
