Officers, teachers and other employees of the Institute
special_provisions: The first Director of the Institute shall be appointed by the Central Government (Sec 11(1) Proviso).

The Institute shall continue to provide facilities to the Governments of the States of Haryana and Punjab and the Central Government in relation to the Union territories of Chandigarh and Himachal Pradesh (Sec 29).
The first regulations under this Act shall be made by the Central Government (Sec 32(2)).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government, after consultation with the Institute (Sec 31(1)).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the Central Government's power to issue directions (Sec 25), make rules (Sec 31), and approve regulations (Sec 32). The Institute itself is responsible for carrying out its functions and administering its affairs in accordance with the Act, rules, and regulations.

act_identification.act_title: THE JAWAHARLAL NEHRU UNIVERSITY ACT, 1966

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Union territory of Delhi and potentially outside that territory for specific institutions or bodies, subject to local laws and University rules.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate a university in Delhi.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Jawaharlal Nehru University in Delhi. Its primary purpose is to disseminate and advance knowledge through teaching and research, promoting principles like national integration, social justice, secularism, and international understanding. It aims to foster Indian culture, facilitate diverse student and teacher participation, and promote inter-disciplinary studies.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'College', 'Hall', 'University', 'Statutes', 'Ordinances', and 'Regulations'.

key_sections.title: The University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Jawaharlal Nehru University as a body corporate in the Union territory of Delhi with perpetual succession and a common seal.

key_sections.title: Objects.
key_sections.description: Outlines the main objectives of the University, including disseminating knowledge, wisdom, and understanding, and promoting principles like national integration and international understanding as detailed in the First Schedule.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers of the University, such as providing instruction, conducting research, granting degrees, establishing colleges, regulating discipline, and managing property.

key_sections.title: Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University, granting powers to review work, inspect, issue directions, and annul proceedings.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the key officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Rectors, Deans, Registrar, and Finance Officer, and outlines their general roles.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Identifies the main authorities governing the University, such as the Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Schools of Studies, and Finance Committee.

key_sections.title: The Court.
key_sections.description: Declares the Court as the supreme authority of the University, with powers to review acts of other councils and exercise residual powers.

key_sections.title: The Executive Council.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Executive Council as the executive body responsible for the general management and administration of the University.

key_sections.title: The Academic Council.
key_sections.description: Constitutes the Academic Council as the academic body responsible for controlling and regulating standards of instruction, education, and examination.

key_sections.title: Statutes.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters that the Statutes may provide for, including the constitution and powers of authorities, appointment of officers, and administration of the University.

key_sections.title: Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Outlines the matters that the Ordinances may provide for, such as student admission, courses of study, fees, examinations, and student discipline.

key_sections.title: Removal of difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make provisions to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, provided they are not inconsistent with its purposes.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Act 8 of 1922.
key_sections.description: Amends the Delhi University Act, 1922, by inserting a clause regarding the provisions of the Jawaharlal Nehru University Act, 1966.

powers_conferred: University: To provide for instruction and research, establish Special Centres and Specialised Laboratories, organize extra-mural teaching, hold examinations and grant degrees, confer honorary degrees, create and appoint to teaching/administrative posts, appoint/recognise teachers, institute awards, establish/maintain/recognise Colleges and Halls, regulate student/employee discipline, promote health/welfare of students/employees, determine admission examinations, recognise institutions, co-operate with other bodies, enter agreements for incorporation of institutions, demand fees, receive donations, acquire/hold/manage/dispose of property, invest funds, provide research/advisory services, print/publish research, borrow money with Central Government approval, and do all necessary things for its objects.

Visitor (President of India): To appoint persons to review University work, inspect University facilities and work, cause inquiries, issue directions, and annul proceedings not in conformity with the Act/Statutes/Ordinances.

Executive Council: To appoint teaching and administrative staff, fix emoluments and conditions of service, regulate discipline among staff, manage finances/accounts/investments/property, accept/transfer property, provide infrastructure, enter contracts, adjudicate grievances, appoint/remove examiners/moderators, select common seal, institute awards, and delegate powers.

Academic Council: To report on matters, propose establishment of departments/colleges, formulate schemes for Schools of Studies, promote research, recommend creation/abolition of teaching posts, recognise diplomas/degrees of other universities, appoint admission committees, publish textbooks/syllabuses, arrange examinations, recommend honorary degrees, confer/grant degrees/academic distinctions, propose/award fellowships/scholarships, and promote student health/welfare.

Vice-Chancellor: To maintain and promote efficiency and good order, ensure observance of Act/Statutes/Ordinances/Regulations, convene meetings, take immediate action in emergencies, and delegate powers.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for disciplinary actions against students for misconduct, which may include expulsion from any college or institution, rustication for a stated period, debarment from admission to courses, fines, debarment from taking examinations for one or more years, or cancellation of examination results. These actions are taken by the Vice-Chancellor or delegated authorities.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Vice-Chancellor (from a panel) and members of the Academic Advisory Committee. The Court elects the Chancellor. The Executive Council appoints Rectors (on VC's recommendation), Registrar, Finance Officer, Dean of Students (on VC's recommendation), Chief Proctor (on VC's recommendation), Librarian, Professors, Readers, Lecturers, and other administrative/ministerial staff. The Vice-Chancellor appoints Deans of Schools of Studies.

applies_to: Jawaharlal Nehru University
Colleges maintained by the University
Recognised institutions
Students of the University
Employees of the University
special_provisions: The University's jurisdiction over institutions already recognized by the University of Delhi requires Central Government authorization after consultation with the University of Delhi.
Powers and jurisdiction extend to institutions/bodies outside the Union territory of Delhi subject to local laws and University rules.
Transitional provisions for the initial nomination/appointment and terms of office for the first Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and members of the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Statutes are made by the Executive Council with the Visitor's approval (first Statutes are in the Second Schedule). Ordinances are made by the Executive Council (first Ordinances by the Vice-Chancellor with Central Government approval). Regulations are made by the authorities of the University.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act establishes a governance structure including the Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, and various officers (e.g., Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer) responsible for administration, academic standards, financial management, and discipline. The Visitor (President of India) exercises oversight, review, and directive powers.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Disputes regarding the constitution of University authorities or bodies are referred to the Visitor, whose decision is final. Disputes arising from contracts with teachers, officers, or employees are referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration.

schedules_summary.description: Outlines the specific objects of the University, focusing on promoting principles like national integration, social justice, secularism, democratic way of life, international understanding, and scientific approach, and detailing actions such as fostering Indian culture, facilitating diverse student/teacher participation, promoting social awareness, integrated courses, inter-disciplinary studies, and international studies.

Contains the Statutes of the University, which provide detailed provisions for definitions, the constitution, powers, and duties of various officers (Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Rectors, Deans, Registrar, Finance Officer, Dean of Students, Chief Proctor, Librarian) and authorities (Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Academic Advisory Committee, Schools of Studies, Finance Committee), selection committees, conditions of service, procedures for removal of teachers and employees, maintenance of student discipline, and the Alumni Association, as well as procedures for making Ordinances and Regulations.

act_identification.act_title: THE SEEDS ACT, 1966
act_identification.date_of_commencement: on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for regulating the quality of certain seeds for sale, and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the quality of seeds of certain kinds or varieties intended for sale. It establishes a framework for the notification of seed varieties, specification of quality standards, and a system for certification and testing. The Act also provides for the appointment of Seed Analysts and Inspectors to ensure compliance and prescribes penalties for contraventions.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Central Seed Committee.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Central Seed Committee to advise Central and State Governments on matters related to the Act's administration.

key_sections.title: Power to notify kinds or varieties of seeds.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to notify specific kinds or varieties of seeds for quality regulation.

key_sections.title: Regulation or sale of seeds of notified kinds or varieties.
key_sections.description: Sets conditions for the sale, keeping for sale, or supply of notified seeds, including conformity to standards and proper labeling.

key_sections.title: The Central Seed Certification Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Central Seed Certification Board to advise on certification matters and coordinate certification agencies.

key_sections.title: Grant of certificate by certification agency.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for applying for and granting certificates for seeds by a certification agency.

key_sections.title: Powers of Seed Inspector.
key_sections.description: Details the powers of Seed Inspectors, including taking samples, entering premises, and seizing materials.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contraventions of the Act or rules, or for obstructing a Seed Inspector.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Specifies liability for offences committed by companies and their officers.

key_sections.title: Exemption.
key_sections.description: Provides an exemption for seeds grown and sold directly by a person on their own premises for sowing or planting.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to notify kinds or varieties of seeds (Section 5)
Central Government: Power to specify minimum limits of germination and purity (Section 6)
Central Government: Power to establish Central Seed Laboratory (Section 4)
Central Government: Power to constitute Central Seed Committee (Section 3)
Central Government: Power to establish Central Seed Certification Board (Section 8A)
Central Government: Power to appoint Secretary and staff for Committee and Board (Sections 3, 8E)
Central Government: Power to recognise seed certification agencies of foreign countries (Section 18)
Central Government: Power to give directions to State Governments (Section 23)
Central Government: Power to make rules (Section 25)
State Government: Power to establish State Seed Laboratory (Section 4)
State Government: Power to establish certification agency (Section 8)
State Government: Power to appoint Seed Analysts (Section 12)
State Government: Power to appoint Seed Inspectors (Section 13)
State Government: Power to specify appellate authority (Section 11)
Certification agency: Power to grant certificates (Section 9)
Certification agency: Power to revoke certificates (Section 10)
Seed Inspector: Power to take samples of seeds (Section 14(1)(a))
Seed Inspector: Power to send samples for analysis (Section 14(1)(b))
Seed Inspector: Power to enter and search premises (Section 14(1)(c))
Seed Inspector: Power to seize stock of seeds (Section 14(1)(c))
Seed Inspector: Power to examine and seize records, registers, documents (Section 14(1)(d))
Seed Inspector: Power to break-open containers or doors (Section 14(3))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for contravening its provisions or rules, or for obstructing a Seed Inspector. For a first offence, the penalty is a fine which may extend to five hundred rupees. For subsequent convictions, the penalty is imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or a fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or both. Additionally, seeds involved in a contravention may be forfeited to the Government.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints Chairman and members of Central Seed Committee, Secretary of Committee, Chairman and members of Central Seed Certification Board, and Secretary and staff of Board. State Government appoints Seed Analysts and Seed Inspectors.

applies_to: Any person selling, keeping for sale, offering to sell, bartering or otherwise supplying any seed of any notified kind or variety
Any person exporting or importing any seed of any notified kind or variety
exemptions: Any seed of any notified kind or variety grown by a person and sold or delivered by him on his own premises direct to another person for being used by that person for the purpose of sowing or planting.
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act, and for different States or for different areas thereof.
Different kinds or varieties may be notified for different States or for different areas thereof.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through Seed Inspectors who can take samples, conduct searches, and seize materials. Seed Analysts perform laboratory analysis. Certification agencies grant and revoke certificates. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance, and property may be forfeited.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrates and courts for prosecution.

act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the issuance of passports and travel documents. Its main objective is to regulate the departure of Indian citizens and other individuals from India, along with addressing related and incidental matters.

key_sections.description: Outlines the process for applying for passports and travel documents, including fees, particulars, and the passport authority's power to issue or refuse them.

key_sections.title: Refusal of passports, travel documents, etc.
key_sections.description: Specifies the grounds on which a passport authority may refuse to issue or endorse a passport or travel document, including national security and public interest.

key_sections.title: Variation, impounding and revocation of passports and travel documents.
key_sections.description: Grants the passport authority powers to vary, impound, or revoke passports and travel documents under specified conditions, such as wrongful possession, false information, or public interest.

key_sections.title: Suspension of passports or travel documents in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government or a designated officer to suspend passports or travel documents for a limited period in public interest, pending impounding or revocation proceedings.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Provides for an appeal mechanism for persons aggrieved by orders of the passport authority, specifying the appellate authority and procedure.

key_sections.title: Offences and penalties.
key_sections.description: Defines various offences related to passports and travel documents, such as contravention of provisions, furnishing false information, or using another's passport, and prescribes corresponding penalties.

key_sections.title: Power to arrest.
key_sections.description: Empowers officers of customs, police, or emigration to arrest without warrant persons suspected of committing offences under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of search and seizure.
key_sections.description: Grants officers of customs, police, or emigration the power to search places and seize passports or travel documents from suspected offenders.

key_sections.title: Previous sanction of Central Government necessary.
key_sections.description: Requires the prior sanction of the Central Government or an authorized officer for instituting any prosecution under the Act.

key_sections.title: Passports and travel documents to be property of Central Government.
key_sections.description: Declares that all passports and travel documents issued under this Act remain the property of the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering various aspects like appointment of authorities, application forms, fees, and conditions.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To prescribe classes of persons for passports/travel documents (S.4(3))
Central Government: To specify named foreign countries (S.5 Explanation)
Central Government: To approve conditions for passports/travel documents (S.9)
Central Government: To approve variation/cancellation of conditions (S.10(1), S.10(2))
Central Government: To impound/revoke passports/travel documents (S.10(6))
Central Government: To suspend passports/travel documents (S.10A)
Central Government: To designate officers for suspension (S.10A Explanation)
Central Government: To grant previous sanction for prosecution (S.15)
Central Government: To issue passports/travel documents to non-citizens (S.20)
Central Government: To delegate powers (S.21)
Central Government: To exempt persons or classes of persons from the Act (S.22)
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes (S.24)
Passport Authority: To issue/refuse passports/travel documents (S.5)
Passport Authority: To vary/cancel endorsements/conditions (S.10(1), S.10(2))
Passport Authority: To impound/revoke passports/travel documents (S.10(3), S.10(4))
Officers of customs/police/emigration officer: To arrest without warrant (S.13)
Officers of customs/police/emigration officer: To search and seize passports/travel documents (S.14)

Appellate court/High Court: To revoke passport/travel document (S.10(8))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 12 outlines offences and penalties. Contravention of Section 3, furnishing false information, altering entries, using another's passport, or allowing another to use one's passport is punishable with imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to five thousand rupees or both. Non-citizens obtaining passports by suppressing nationality or holding forged passports face imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of ten to fifty thousand rupees. Abetment carries the same punishment as the abetted offence. Contravention of passport/travel document conditions or rules, for which no other punishment is provided, is punishable with imprisonment up to three months or a fine up to five hundred rupees or both. Repeat offenders face double the penalty for the latter offence.

repealed_acts: The Passports Ordinance, 1967 (4 of 1967)
related_acts: Trading with the Enemy (Continuance of Emergency Provisions) (16 of 1947)
Foreigners Law (Application and Amendment) Act, 1962 (42 of 1962)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government empowers the 'passport authority' and 'appellate authorities', designates officers for sanctioning prosecution, and designates officers or authorities for delegation of powers.

applies_to: whole of India
citizens of India who are outside India
citizens of India and other persons
exemptions: any person or class of persons (by Central Government notification)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through powers of arrest, search, and seizure by customs, police, or emigration officers. Prosecution requires prior sanction from the Central Government. Appeals against orders of the passport authority are provided. Courts can revoke passports upon conviction.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate, criminal court, appellate court, High Court

act_identification.act_title: THE UNLAWFUL ACTIVITIES (PREVENTION) ACT, 1967

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the more effective prevention of certain unlawful activities of individuals and associations [, and for dealing with terrorist activities,] and for matters connected therewith. WHEREAS the Security Council of the United Nations in its 4385th meeting adopted Resolution 1373 (2001) on 28th September, 2001, under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations requiring all the States to take measures to combat international terrorism; AND WHEREAS Resolutions 1267 (1999), 1333 (2000), 1363 (2001), 1390 (2002), 1455 (2003), 1526 (2004), 1566 (2004), 1617 (2005), 1735 (2006) and 1822 (2008) of the Security Council of the United Nations require the States to take action against certain terrorists and terrorist organisations, to freeze the assets and other economic resources, to prevent the entry into or the transit through their territory, and prevent the direct or indirect supply, sale or transfer of arms and ammunitions to the individuals or entities listed in the Schedule; AND WHEREAS the Central Government, in exercise of the powers conferred by section 2 of the United Nations (Security Council) Act, 1947 (43 of 1947) has made the Prevention and Suppression of Terrorism (Implementation of Security Council Resolutions) Order, 2007; AND WHEREAS it is considered necessary to give effect to the said Resolutions and the Order and to make special provisions for the prevention of, and for coping with, terrorist activities and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the more effective prevention of certain unlawful activities of individuals and associations, and for dealing with terrorist activities. It also aims to give effect to United Nations Security Council Resolutions concerning international terrorism, including freezing assets and preventing support to terrorists and terrorist organizations.

chapter_titles: FORFEITURE OF PROCEEDS OF TERRORISM OR ANY PROPERTY INTENDED TO BE USED FOR TERRORISM

key_definitions: cession of a part of the territory of India
secession of a part of the territory of India from the Union

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, and its extraterritorial jurisdiction over Indian citizens and government personnel.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'association', 'terrorist act', 'unlawful activity', and 'proceeds of terrorism'.

key_sections.title: Declaration of an association as unlawful.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to declare an association unlawful by notification, subject to confirmation by a Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of an 'Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Tribunal' consisting of a High Court Judge, with powers of a civil court for inquiry.

key_sections.title: Penalty for being member of an unlawful association, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for membership, participation, or assistance to an unlawful association, with enhanced penalties for involvement with weapons leading to loss of life or injury.

key_sections.title: Punishment for unlawful activities.
key_sections.description: Stipulates punishment for individuals who take part in, commit, advocate, abet, advise, or incite unlawful activities.

key_sections.title: Terrorist act.
key_sections.description: Defines 'terrorist act' broadly to include acts intended to threaten India's unity, integrity, security, or sovereignty, or to strike terror, using various means including explosives, hazardous substances, or causing economic damage.

key_sections.title: Punishment for terrorist act.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for committing a terrorist act, including death or life imprisonment if the act results in death.

key_sections.title: Punishment for raising funds for terrorist act.
key_sections.description: Penalizes individuals who raise or provide funds for terrorist acts, whether directly or indirectly, knowing such funds are likely to be used for terrorism.

key_sections.title: Forfeiture of proceeds of terrorism.
key_sections.description: Declares that proceeds of terrorism, regardless of who holds them, are liable to be forfeited to the Central or State Government.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Schedule, etc.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to add, remove, or amend entries in the Schedules related to terrorist organizations and individuals.

key_sections.title: Modified application of certain provisions of the Code.
key_sections.description: Modifies provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, including making all offences cognizable, extending investigation periods, and imposing restrictions on bail for accused persons.

key_sections.title: Cognizance of offences.
key_sections.description: Requires prior sanction from the Central or State Government for courts to take cognizance of offences under certain chapters of the Act.

key_sections.title: Certain powers of the Central Government.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government powers to freeze, seize, or attach funds and financial assets of individuals or entities involved in terrorism, and to prevent their entry into India.

powers_conferred: Central Government to declare associations unlawful (Section 3)
Central Government to constitute Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Tribunal (Section 5)
Central Government to prohibit the use of funds of an unlawful association (Section 7)
Central Government to notify places used for the purpose of an unlawful association (Section 8)
Central Government to amend Schedules related to terrorist organizations and individuals (Section 35)
Central Government to delegate powers to State Governments (Section 42)
Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act (Section 52)
Central Government to freeze, seize or attach funds and other financial assets of individuals or entities involved in terrorism (Section 51A)
Tribunal to adjudicate on declarations of unlawful associations and regulate its own procedure (Section 4, 5)
Tribunal to have powers of a civil court for inquiry (Section 5)
Investigating officer and Designated Authority to seize or attach proceeds of terrorism (Section 25)
Court to order forfeiture of proceeds of terrorism (Section 26)
Court to pass orders for attachment or forfeiture of property of accused persons (Section 33)
District Magistrate to make list of movable properties and prohibit their use in notified places (Section 8)
Police officers to arrest, search, etc. (Section 43A)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines various offences including being a member of an unlawful association (Section 10), dealing with its funds (Section 11), contravening orders regarding notified places (Section 12), engaging in unlawful activities (Section 13), committing terrorist acts (Section 15, 16), raising funds for terrorist acts (Section 17), conspiracy (Section 18), organizing terrorist camps (Section 18A), recruiting for terrorist acts (Section 18B), harbouring terrorists (Section 19), being a member of a terrorist gang or organization (Section 20), holding proceeds of terrorism (Section 21), and threatening witnesses (Section 22). Penalties range from imprisonment for terms up to life, death penalty for terrorist acts resulting in death, and fines. Enhanced penalties are prescribed for certain offences involving explosives or other lethal weapons (Section 23). Offences committed by companies, societies, or trusts also carry specific punishments (Section 22C).

related_acts: Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946 (25 of 1946)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints the presiding officer of the Tribunal (Section 5) and members of the Review Committees (Section 37).

applies_to: Whole of India
Every person guilty in India
Any person committing an offence beyond India
Citizens of India outside India
Persons in the service of the Government, wherever they may be
Persons on ships and aircrafts, registered in India, wherever they may be
exemptions: Spouse of the offender for harbouring or concealing a terrorist (Section 19 proviso)
Treaties, agreements, or conventions entered into between the Government of India and any other country, or negotiations thereof (Section 13(3))
special_provisions: Nothing contained in sub-clause (ii) of Section 2(p) (defining unlawful association) shall apply to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through investigation by police officers (Section 43), powers of arrest and search (Section 43A), cognizance of offences by courts (Section 45), admissibility of intercepted communications as evidence (Section 46), and forfeiture of proceeds of terrorism (Chapter V). Sanction from the Central or State Government is required for prosecution under certain chapters (Section 45).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Criminal courts having jurisdiction under the Code of Criminal Procedure (Section 2(d)), including Special Courts under the National Investigation Agency Act. High Courts hear appeals against forfeiture orders (Section 28). Courts of District Judges handle applications related to prohibitory orders on funds and notified places (Sections 7(4), 8(8)).

schedules_summary.description: Lists various terrorist organisations.
Lists international conventions and treaties for the suppression of unlawful acts, which define offences constituting terrorist acts under the Act.
Specifies security features used to define high quality counterfeit Indian currency notes.
Lists names of individuals identified as terrorists.

act_identification.act_title: THE JAMMU AND KASHMIR REPRESENTATION OF THE PEOPLE (SUPPLEMENTARY) ACT, 1968

act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to supplement the Jammu and Kashmir Representation of the People Act, 1957. It applies specific sections of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, to orders made by the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir with certain modifications.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.

act_identification.act_title: THE BIHAR AND UTTAR PRADESH (ALTERATION OF BOUNDARIES) ACT, 1968

legislative_details.geographical_extent: States of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the alteration of boundaries of the States of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the alteration of the boundaries between the States of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. It also addresses various connected matters such as representation in legislatures, jurisdiction of High Courts, apportionment of assets and liabilities, and other legal and miscellaneous provisions arising from these boundary changes.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Transfer of territories.
key_sections.description: Details the specific territories to be transferred between the States of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh and the process of demarcation.

key_sections.title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Specifies the amendments to be made to the First Schedule of the Constitution of India due to the territorial changes.

key_sections.title: Extension of jurisdiction of, and transfer of proceedings to, High Court at Patna.
key_sections.description: Outlines the extension of jurisdiction of the Patna High Court and the transfer of legal proceedings to it from the Allahabad High Court.

key_sections.title: Extension of jurisdiction of, and transfer of proceedings to, High Court at Allahabad.
key_sections.description: Outlines the extension of jurisdiction of the Allahabad High Court and the transfer of legal proceedings to it from the Patna High Court.

key_sections.title: Land and goods.
key_sections.description: Stipulates the transfer of land, stores, articles, and other goods belonging to the States in the transferred territories.

key_sections.title: Contracts.
key_sections.description: Addresses how contracts made by the States before the appointed day are to be treated after the territorial transfer.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to order allocation or adjustment in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to order allocation or adjustment of property, benefits, or liabilities between the States.

key_sections.title: Construction of boundary pillars, etc.
key_sections.description: Provides for the construction and maintenance of boundary pillars and prescribes penalties for their removal or injury.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the President to issue orders to remove any difficulties in implementing the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint the 'appointed day', specify authority for deep stream determination, appoint authority for boundary demarcation, cause maps to be published, order allocation or adjustment of assets/liabilities, make rules, and remove difficulties (through the President).

State Governments of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh: To agree on deep stream determination, administer transferred territories, spend moneys from Consolidated Fund, authorize expenditure, construct and maintain boundary pillars.
Governor of Bihar or Uttar Pradesh: To authorize expenditure from the Consolidated Fund, and cause reports of the Comptroller and Auditor-General to be laid before the Legislature.
High Court at Patna / High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Chief Justice): To certify proceedings for transfer, order transfer of proceedings, and specify advocates entitled to practice.

Authority appointed by the Central Government: To demarcate the fixed boundary, rationalize boundary alignment, decide on interpretation of the Schedule, determine location and responsibility for boundary pillars, enter and survey areas, and prepare maps of transferred territories.
Appropriate Government: To make adaptations and modifications to laws for facilitating their application.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever wilfully removes or injures any boundary pillar shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both. An offence under this provision may be inquired into and tried by a court in either of the States of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.

related_acts: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
Bihar and West Bengal (Transfer of Territories) Act, 1956

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the 'appointed day' and the authority for boundary demarcation. The Chief Justices of the High Courts have the power to specify advocates entitled to practice.

applies_to: States of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh
Territories transferred between the States of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the demarcation of boundaries by an authority appointed by the Central Government, administration of transferred territories by State Governments, transfer of legal proceedings between High Courts, and penalties for damaging boundary pillars. The Central Government also has powers to resolve difficulties and make rules.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court at Patna, High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, and courts in either of the States of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh for specific offences.

schedules_summary.description: Contains an Explanatory Note regarding village boundaries and names, and detailed geographical descriptions for the 'Ganga Sector' and 'Ghaghra Sector' to define the fixed boundary between Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.

act_identification.act_title: THE PONDICHERRY (EXTENSION OF LAWS) ACT, 1968

act_overview.preamble: An Act to extend certain Central Acts to the Union territory of Pondicherry.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to extend various Central Acts to the Union territory of Pondicherry. It specifies how these Acts, along with their rules and orders, will come into force and be construed in Pondicherry, including provisions for modifications and the repeal of corresponding local laws. The Act also grants powers to the Administrator and the Central Government to manage the implementation and address any difficulties.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Pondicherry (Extension of Laws) Act, 1968.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Act', 'Administrator', and 'Pondicherry'.

key_sections.title: Extension with amendments of certain laws to Pondicherry and their commencement therein.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that specified Acts in the Schedule will extend to Pondicherry with modifications, and their commencement date will be appointed by the Administrator.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Provides for the repeal of existing laws in Pondicherry corresponding to the extended Acts, while including saving provisions for past operations, rights, and liabilities.

key_sections.title: Extension of rules, orders, etc., under certain laws.
key_sections.description: Ensures that rules, notifications, orders, regulations, and bye-laws made by the Central Government under the extended Acts will also extend to Pondicherry.

key_sections.title: Rules of construction.
key_sections.description: Lays down rules for construing references to laws or functionaries not in force or existence in Pondicherry, and for interpreting references to the State Government.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make orders or give directions to remove difficulties in giving effect to the extended Acts in Pondicherry.

powers_conferred: Administrator to appoint commencement dates for extended Acts (Section 3(2))
Administrator to decide corresponding functionary if a question arises or none exists (Section 6(1)(a))
Central Government to make provisions or give directions to remove difficulties (Section 7)

related_acts: Madras Court-fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955

applies_to: Union territory of Pondicherry
exemptions: Renoncants of the Union territory of Pondicherry
special_provisions: Specific modifications for the application of various Central Acts in Pondicherry as detailed in the Schedule.
Exemption of 'Renoncants' from certain provisions of extended Acts.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Administrator (for commencement dates); Central Government (for removing difficulties); Legislative Assembly of Pondicherry (for rules under Indian Stamp Act, 1899 as modified)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The extended Acts come into force in Pondicherry on dates appointed by the Administrator, and their rules, orders, etc., also extend. The Central Government can issue orders to remove difficulties in implementation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any court, tribunal or other authority (Section 7); High Court of Madras (for certain matters under Indian Stamp Act, 1899 as modified)

schedules_summary.description: Lists Central Acts (divided into Part I and Part II) that are extended to the Union territory of Pondicherry, along with specific modifications for their application in that territory. Part I lists acts generally in force, and Part II lists acts as they were in force in specific states or Union territories on August 1, 1966.

act_identification.act_title: THE CIVIL DEFENCE ACT, 1968

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make provision for civil defence and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to make comprehensive provisions for civil defence. It covers the constitution of a Civil Defence Corps and outlines the powers of the Central and State Governments regarding civil defence measures.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

chapter_titles: POWER OF CENTRAL GOVERNMENT TO MAKE RULES FOR CIVIL DEFENCE

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement procedure of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'civil defence', 'Civil Defence Corps', and 'hostile attack'.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules for civil defence.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for securing civil defence, covering various matters like prevention, instruction, and protection.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Civil Defence Corps.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to constitute Civil Defence Corps and appoint a Controller to command them.

key_sections.title: Dismissal of members of Civil Defence Corps.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for dismissal of members from the Civil Defence Corps by the Controller for unsatisfactory duty or misconduct.

key_sections.title: Functions of members of Civil Defence Corps.
key_sections.description: Describes the functions of Corps members in carrying out civil defence measures and their deployment for training or service.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for members of the Corps who neglect or refuse to obey orders, and for any person failing to obey orders under the Act or rules.

key_sections.title: Effect of Act and rules, etc., inconsistent with other enactments.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act and its rules shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in other enactments.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply to measures taken for the protection of the Armed Forces.
key_sections.description: Exempts the Armed Forces of the Union and measures taken for their protection or their installations from the application of this Act.

key_sections.title: Power of the Central Government to delegate.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to delegate its powers or duties under the Act to subordinate officers or authorities.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Provides legal protection against suits or prosecutions for actions taken in good faith under the Act by government, Director, Controller, or authorised persons.

key_sections.title: Authorised persons and members of the Corps to be public servants.
key_sections.description: Declares authorised persons and members of the Corps as public servants within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code.

key_sections.title: Rules and regulations to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Requires all rules and regulations made by the Central Government under the Act to be laid before Parliament.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to make rules for civil defence (Section 3)
Central Government: to make regulations for carrying out purposes of Chapter III (Section 9)
Central Government: to delegate any power or duty under the Act (Section 16A)
State Government: to constitute Civil Defence Corps (Section 4)
State Government: to appoint members and officers of the Corps (Section 5)
State Government: to appoint a Director of Civil Defence (Section 4(2))
State Government: to call out members of the Corps for training or functions (Section 8(2))
State Government: to delegate its powers under the Act (Section 17)
Controller: to command the Civil Defence Corps (Section 4)
Controller: to appoint members to office or command in the Corps (Section 5)
Controller: to dismiss members of the Civil Defence Corps (Section 6)
Controller: to call out members of the Corps for training or functions (Section 8(2))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Members of the Corps neglecting or refusing to obey orders or discharge functions are punishable with a fine up to five hundred rupees, with a further fine of fifty rupees per day for continuing contravention. Any person neglecting or failing to obey orders or directions under the Act or rules is similarly punishable with a fine up to five hundred rupees, and a further fine of fifty rupees per day for continuing contravention.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government appoints members of the Corps and Director of Civil Defence. Controller appoints members to office or command within the Corps.

applies_to: Whole of India
Any person, property, place or thing in India or any part of the territory thereof
Members of the Civil Defence Corps
exemptions: Armed Forces of the Union
Measures taken by authorities in control of the Armed Forces for securing civil defence or safety of such forces or for the protection of any naval, military or air force installations or stores
special_provisions: The Act shall come into force in a State or part thereof on such date as the Central Government may appoint, with different dates possible for different States or parts.
A member of the Corps of any State may be required to discharge functions in relation to civil defence in any other State.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for rules and regulations); State Government (may make orders under rules made by Central Government).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced through rules and regulations made by the Central Government, orders made by State Government or Controller, and penalties for non-compliance. Prosecutions require consent of the Controller.

act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL LAWS (EXTENSION TO JAMMU AND KASHMIR) ACT, 1968

key_sections.description: States that the Acts mentioned in the Schedule, along with their rules, orders, and regulations, are extended to and shall be in force in the State of Jammu and Kashmir, and shall be amended as specified in the Schedule.

key_sections.title: Construction of references to laws not in force in Jammu and Kashmir.
key_sections.description: Directs that references in the extended Acts to laws not in force in Jammu and Kashmir shall be construed as references to corresponding laws in force in that State.

key_sections.title: Construction of references to authorities where new Authorities have been constituted.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that references to existing authorities in laws in force in Jammu and Kashmir shall be construed as references to corresponding new authorities constituted under the extended laws.

key_sections.title: Repeals and savings.
key_sections.description: Provides for the repeal of any corresponding law in force in Jammu and Kashmir immediately before the commencement of this Act, with savings for previous operations, rights, liabilities, penalties, and legal proceedings.

key_sections.title: Powers to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to issue orders or directions to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of any Act extended to Jammu and Kashmir, including specifying authorities, transferring matters, and recognizing past actions.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint the commencement date of the Act (Section 1(2))
Central Government to make provisions or give directions to remove difficulties in giving effect to the extended Acts (Section 6(1))
Central Government to specify corresponding authorities (Section 6(2)(a))
Central Government to provide for transfer of pending matters before courts, tribunals, or other authorities (Section 6(2)(b))
Central Government to specify areas, circumstances, extent, or conditions for recognizing actions taken under repealed laws (Section 6(2)(c))
Central Government to direct non-application or modified application of Companies Act provisions to companies in Jammu and Kashmir (Section 620C of the Companies Act, as inserted by this Act)

amended_acts: THE COST AND WORKS ACCOUNTANTS ACT, 1959
related_acts: THE COST AND WORKS ACCOUNTANTS ACT, 1959

applies_to: State of Jammu and Kashmir
Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir
Union territory of Ladakh
special_provisions: The Act itself is a special provision for the extension of Central Laws to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
The Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh vide notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019.
Section 620C, inserted into the Companies Act, 1956, allows the Central Government to apply provisions of that Act to companies in Jammu and Kashmir with exceptions or modifications.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for removing difficulties and issuing directions)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through the extension and amendment of specified Central Laws, repeal of corresponding State laws, and powers granted to the Central Government to resolve implementation difficulties.

schedules_summary.description: Lists various Central Acts (e.g., The Official Trustees Act, 1913; The Motor Vehicles Act, 1939; The Companies Act, 1956) and specifies the amendments to be made to their sections, primarily to remove clauses that previously excluded the State of Jammu and Kashmir from their applicability, thereby extending them to the State.

act_identification.act_title: THE ENEMY PROPERTY ACT, 1968

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India and it applies also to all citizens of India outside India and to branches and agencies outside India of companies or bodies corporate registered or incorporated in India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the continued vesting of enemy property vested in the Custodian of Enemy Property for India under the Defence of India Rules, 1962 [1][and the Defence of India Rules, 1971], and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the continued vesting of enemy property in the Custodian of Enemy Property for India. It outlines the powers of the Custodian to manage, preserve, and dispose of such property, and establishes rules for its administration, including provisions for sale, transfer, and legal proceedings.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical and personal extent, and commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Custodian', 'enemy', 'enemy subject', 'enemy firm', and 'enemy property'.

key_sections.title: Property vested in the Custodian of Enemy Property for India under the Defence of India Rules, 1962, and the Defence of India Rules, 1971 to continue to vest in Custodian.
key_sections.description: Ensures that enemy property vested under previous Defence of India Rules continues to vest in the Custodian under this Act.

key_sections.title: Law of succession or any custom or usage not to apply to enemy property.
key_sections.description: States that laws of succession, custom, or usage do not apply to enemy property, and no person has rights over such property.

key_sections.title: Prohibition to transfer any property vested in Custodian by an enemy, enemy subject or enemy firm.
key_sections.description: Prohibits enemies, enemy subjects, or enemy firms from transferring vested property, declaring such transfers void.

key_sections.title: Power of Custodian in respect of enemy property vested in him.
key_sections.description: Outlines the extensive powers of the Custodian to manage, preserve, and deal with enemy property, including carrying on business, recovering debts, and disposing of property.

key_sections.title: Sale of Property by Custodian.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Custodian to dispose of enemy properties by sale or otherwise with Central Government approval, and deposit proceeds into the Consolidated Fund of India.

key_sections.title: Exemption from attachment, etc.
key_sections.description: Declares that enemy property vested in the Custodian is exempt from attachment, seizure, or sale in execution of civil court decrees or other authority orders.

key_sections.title: Transfer of property vested as enemy property in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to direct the transfer of property back to the original owner if it determines the property was not enemy property.

key_sections.title: Exclusion of jurisdiction of civil courts.
key_sections.description: Excludes the jurisdiction of civil courts or authorities over matters concerning enemy property under this Act.

key_sections.title: Appeal to High Court.
key_sections.description: Provides for an appeal to the High Court against orders of the Central Government under section 18.

key_sections.title: Effect of laws inconsistent with the Act.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws, including laws of succession or custom.

key_sections.title: Validation.
key_sections.description: Validates the provisions of the Act as amended by the Enemy Property (Amendment and Validation) Act, 2017, and ensures continued vesting of divested property in the Custodian.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint Custodian, Deputy Custodian, Assistant Custodian (Sec 3)
Central Government: Appoint Inspectors (Sec 4)
Central Government: Direct Custodian on money/property dealing (Sec 7(3))
Central Government: Approve Government securities for investment (Sec 8(viii))
Central Government: Direct payments (Sec 8(xi))
Central Government: Specify time for disposal of property (Sec 8A(1))
Central Government: Issue directions to Custodian on disposal (Sec 8A(5))
Central Government: Make guidelines for disposal (Sec 8A(6))
Central Government: Direct other authority/Ministry/Department for disposal (Sec 8A(7))
Central Government: Deal with or utilise enemy property (Sec 8A(8))
Central Government: Reduce or remit fees (Sec 17 Proviso)
Central Government: Review vesting orders (Sec 18)
Central Government: Make rules (Sec 23)
Custodian: Take measures for preserving property (Sec 8(1))
Custodian: Carry on the business of the enemy (Sec 8(2)(i))
Custodian: Fix and collect rent, standard rent, lease rent, licence fee or usage charges (Sec 8(2)(ia))
Custodian: Take action for recovering any money due to the enemy (Sec 8(2)(ii))
Custodian: Make any contract and execute any document (Sec 8(2)(iii))
Custodian: Institute, defend or continue any suit or other legal proceeding, refer any dispute to arbitration and compromise any debts, claims or liabilities (Sec 8(2)(iv))
Custodian: Secure vacant possession of the enemy property by evicting unauthorised occupants (Sec 8(2)(iva))
Custodian: Raise loans on the security of the property (Sec 8(2)(v))
Custodian: Incur expenditure out of the property (Sec 8(2)(vi))
Custodian: Transfer by way of sale, mortgage or lease or otherwise dispose of any of the properties (Sec 8(2)(vii))
Custodian: Invest any moneys held by him on behalf of enemies (Sec 8(2)(viii))
Custodian: Make payments to the enemy and his dependents (Sec 8(2)(ix))
Custodian: Make payments on behalf of the enemy to persons other than enemies (Sec 8(2)(x))
Custodian: Make such other payments as directed by the Central Government (Sec 8(2)(xi))
Custodian: Issue certificate of sale (Sec 10A)
Custodian: Summon persons and call for documents (Sec 11)
Custodian: Declare property vests in him and issue certificate (Sec 5A)
Custodian: Dispose of property by sale or otherwise (Sec 8A(1))
Custodian: Requisition services of any police officer (Sec 8A(2))
Custodian: Deposit sale proceeds into the Consolidated Fund of India (Sec 8A(3))
Custodian: Send a report to the Central Government (Sec 8A(4))
Custodian: Call for returns (Sec 15(1))
Custodian: Levy fees (Sec 17(1))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties are prescribed for making payments in contravention of Section 7(1) (imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both), contravening Section 10(2) (imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both), failing to comply with a requisition under Section 11 (fine up to ten thousand rupees), and failing to submit returns or furnishing false returns under Section 15(2) (fine up to ten thousand rupees). Offences by companies are also covered, holding responsible persons and the company liable.

repealed_acts: The Enemy Property Ordinance, 1968 (7 of 1968)

authorities_established: Custodian of Enemy Property for India
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the Custodian of Enemy Property for India, Deputy Custodians, Assistant Custodians, and Inspectors of Enemy Property.

applies_to: whole of India
all citizens of India outside India
branches and agencies outside India of companies or bodies corporate registered or incorporated in India

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the Custodian of Enemy Property for India, Deputy Custodians, Assistant Custodians, and Inspectors of Enemy Property, who are empowered to manage, preserve, dispose of, and investigate enemy property. It includes provisions for summoning persons, calling for documents, and imposing penalties for non-compliance.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court (for appeals under Section 18C). Civil courts' jurisdiction is excluded in matters pertaining to this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE ANDHRA PRADESH AND MYSORE (TRANSFER OF TERRITORY) ACT, 1968
act_identification.act_short_title: The Andhra Pradesh and Mysore (Transfer of Territory) Act, 1968

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the transfer of certain territory from the State of Mysore to the State of Andhra Pradesh and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the transfer of specific territory from the State of Mysore to the State of Andhra Pradesh. It also addresses various connected matters arising from this territorial transfer, including constitutional amendments, jurisdiction of High Courts, and management of assets and liabilities.

key_definitions: corresponding court, tribunal, authority or officer

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'appointed day' and 'transferred territory'.

key_sections.title: Transfer of territory from Mysore to Andhra Pradesh.
key_sections.description: Stipulates the transfer of specified territory from the State of Mysore to the State of Andhra Pradesh from the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Details the amendments to the First Schedule of the Constitution of India to reflect the territorial transfer.

key_sections.title: Extension of jurisdiction of Andhra Pradesh High Court.
key_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the High Court of Andhra Pradesh to the transferred territory and addresses pending proceedings in the High Court of Mysore.

key_sections.title: Assets and liabilities.
key_sections.description: Specifies the transfer of land, stores, articles, goods, rights, liabilities, and obligations from the State of Mysore to the State of Andhra Pradesh in relation to the transferred territory.

key_sections.title: Extension of laws.
key_sections.description: Provides for the extension of laws in force in Hindupur taluk to the transferred territory and the cessation of laws previously in force in the transferred territory.

key_sections.title: Transfer of pending proceedings.
key_sections.description: Mandates the transfer of pending legal proceedings (other than High Court cases) relating exclusively to the transferred territory from Mysore to Andhra Pradesh.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the President the power to issue orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Power of the State Government (Andhra Pradesh) to alter the name, extent or boundaries of any district or taluk in the State of Andhra Pradesh (Section 3(3))
Power of the High Court of Mysore to hear and dispose of proceedings relatable to the transferred territory pending before the appointed day (Section 9(2))
Power of any court, tribunal or authority to construe laws for facilitating their application in relation to the transferred territory (Section 14)
Power of the President to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act (Section 18)
Power of the Central Government to make rules to give effect to the provisions of the Act (Section 19(1))

Delimitation of Council Constituencies (Andhra Pradesh) Order, 1957

State of Andhra Pradesh
transferred territory (Area comprised in survey number 19 of “Abakavaripalli” village of Bagepallitaluk in Kolar district)
special_provisions: Proceedings relatable to the transferred territory pending in the High Court of Mysore immediately before the appointed day shall be heard and disposed of by that High Court (Section 9(2)).
Any court, tribunal or authority may construe laws to facilitate their application in the transferred territory (Section 14).

implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court of Andhra Pradesh, High Court of Mysore, other courts, tribunals, authorities or officers as per transferred proceedings

schedules_summary.description: Specifies the territory transferred from the State of Mysore to the State of Andhra Pradesh, specifically survey number 19 of “Abakavaripalli” village of Bagepallitaluk in Kolar district.

act_identification.act_title: THE INSECTICIDES ACT, 1968
act_identification.date_of_commencement: It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint and different dates may be appointed for different States and for different provisions of this Act. (1st March, 1971 for sections 4, 7, 8 and 36; 1st August, 1971 for remaining provisions)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the import, manufacture, sale, transport, distribution and use of insecticides with a view to prevent risk to human beings or animals, and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the import, manufacture, sale, transport, distribution, and use of insecticides. Its primary objective is to prevent risks posed by these substances to human beings and animals, and to address related matters.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its application throughout India, and the process for its commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'animals', 'insecticide', 'misbranded', and various officers.

key_sections.title: The Central Insecticides Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Central Insecticides Board to advise Central and State Governments on technical matters related to insecticides and their safety.

key_sections.title: Registration Committee.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of a Registration Committee responsible for registering insecticides after scrutinizing their efficacy and safety.

key_sections.title: Registration of insecticides.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for applying for and obtaining registration for insecticides, including conditions and refusal grounds.

key_sections.title: Grant of licence.
key_sections.description: Details the process for applying for and granting licenses to manufacture, sell, stock, exhibit for sale, distribute, or use insecticides for commercial pest control.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of import and manufacture of certain insecticides.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the import or manufacture of misbranded, prohibited, or unregistered insecticides, or those not in accordance with licence conditions.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of sale, etc., of certain insecticides.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the sale, stocking, distribution, transport, or use of unregistered, prohibited, or unlicensed insecticides.

key_sections.title: Insecticide Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Empowers Central or State Governments to appoint Insecticide Inspectors for specified areas to ensure compliance with the Act.

key_sections.title: Powers of Insecticide Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Grants Insecticide Inspectors powers to enter, search, inspect, seize, stop distribution, and take samples of insecticides.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of sale, etc., of insecticides for reasons of public safety.
key_sections.description: Allows Central or State Governments to prohibit the sale, distribution, or use of insecticides if they pose a risk to human beings or animals.

key_sections.title: Offences and punishment.
key_sections.description: Defines various offences under the Act, such as dealing in misbranded or unregistered insecticides, and prescribes corresponding punishments including imprisonment and fines.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for implementing the provisions of the Act, covering various aspects like packing, labelling, and registration.

key_sections.title: Exemption.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which certain uses of insecticides or certain organizations are exempt from the Act's provisions.

powers_conferred: Central Government to constitute the Central Insecticides Board (Section 4)
Central Government to constitute a Registration Committee (Section 5)
Board to appoint other committees (Section 6)
Central Government to appoint Secretary and other officers for the Board and Registration Committee (Section 8)
Registration Committee to register insecticides (Section 9)
Central Government to hear appeals against non-registration or cancellation (Section 10)
Central Government to revise decisions of the Registration Committee (Section 11)
State Government to appoint licensing officers (Section 12)
Licensing officer to grant, revoke, suspend, and amend licences (Sections 13, 14)
Central Government to establish Central Insecticides Laboratory (Section 16)
Central Government or a State Government to appoint Insecticide Analysts (Section 19)
Central Government or a State Government to appoint Insecticide Inspectors (Section 20)
Insecticide Inspectors to enter, search, inspect, seize, stop distribution, and take samples (Section 21)
State Government to require notification of poisoning (Section 26)
Central Government or State Government to prohibit sale/use of insecticides for public safety (Section 27)
Central Government to give directions to State Governments (Section 34)
Central Government to make rules (Section 36)
State Governments to make rules (Section 37)
Central Government to grant exemptions (Section 38)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 29 outlines offences such as importing, manufacturing, selling, stocking, or distributing misbranded or unregistered insecticides, or doing so without a licence, or contravening prohibitions under Section 27, or obstructing an Insecticide Inspector. Punishments for the first offence include imprisonment up to two years or a fine of ten thousand to fifty thousand rupees, or both. Subsequent offences carry imprisonment up to three years or a fine of fifteen thousand to seventy-five thousand rupees, or both. Using an insecticide in contravention of the Act or rules is punishable with a fine of five hundred to five thousand rupees, or imprisonment up to six months, or both. Other contraventions of the Act, rules, or licence conditions are punishable with imprisonment up to one year or a fine of five thousand to twenty-five thousand rupees for the first offence, and up to two years or a fine of ten thousand to fifty thousand rupees for subsequent offences.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Secretary of the Board, staff for the Board and Registration Committee, and the Director of the Central Insecticides Laboratory. State Governments appoint licensing officers, Insecticide Analysts, and Insecticide Inspectors.

applies_to: Any person desiring to import or manufacture any insecticide
Any person engaged in the business of import or manufacture of any insecticide
Any person desiring to manufacture or to sell, stock or exhibit for sale or distribute any insecticide or to undertake commercial pest control operations with the use of any insecticide
exemptions: The use of any insecticide by any person for his own household purposes or for kitchen garden or in respect of any land under his cultivation

Any substance specified or included in the Schedule or any preparation containing any one or more such substances, if such substance or preparation is intended for purposes other than preventing, destroying, repelling or mitigating any insects, rodents, fungi, weeds and other forms of plant or animal life not useful to human beings
Any educational, scientific or research organisation engaged in carrying out experiments with insecticides
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different States for the commencement of the Act or its provisions
Special Courts may be notified by State Governments for speedy trial of offences in any district or metropolitan area

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a system of registration and licensing of insecticides, appointment of Insecticide Analysts and Inspectors with powers to inspect, seize, and take samples. It includes provisions for reporting poisoning, prohibiting sale/use for public safety, and prescribes penalties for offences, with trials conducted by specific courts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Metropolitan magistrate or a judicial magistrate of the first class, and Special Courts

schedules_summary.description: Contains a comprehensive list of insecticides, including their chemical names and common names, that fall under the purview of the Act as per section 3(e).

act_identification.act_title: THE BORDER SECURITY FORCE ACT, 1968

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India, including the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh, and also outside India. Specific powers may be exercised within local limits adjoining the borders of India.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution and regulation of an Armed Force of the Union for ensuring the security of the borders of India and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the constitution and regulation of the Border Security Force, an armed force of the Union. Its primary objective is to ensure the security of the borders of India and to address matters connected with the functioning, discipline, and administration of its members.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

chapter_titles: CONSTITUTION OF THE FORCE AND CONDITIONS OF SERVICE OF THE MEMBERS OF THE FORCE
EXECUTION OF SENTENCE, PARDONS, REMISSIONS, ETC.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Persons subject to this Act.
key_sections.description: Specifies who is subject to the Act, including officers, subordinate officers, under-officers, and other enrolled persons.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Force.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Border Security Force as an armed force of the Union for border security.

key_sections.title: Control, direction.
key_sections.description: Vests general superintendence, direction, and control of the Force in the Central Government and command in the Director-General.

key_sections.title: Restrictions respecting right to form association, freedom of speech, etc.
key_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on members of the Force regarding associations, political activities, and communication with the press.

key_sections.title: Offences in relation to the enemy and punishable with death.
key_sections.description: Defines severe offences related to the enemy, punishable by death or lesser punishment.

key_sections.title: Mutiny.
key_sections.description: Defines offences related to mutiny and their severe punishments.

key_sections.title: Punishments awardable by Security Force Courts.
key_sections.description: Lists the scale of punishments that can be inflicted by Security Force Courts, including death, imprisonment, and dismissal.

key_sections.title: Kinds of Security Force Courts.
key_sections.description: Establishes three kinds of Security Force Courts: General, Petty, and Summary.

key_sections.title: Choice between criminal court and Security Force Court.
key_sections.description: Grants discretion to the Director-General or other specified officers to decide whether an offence is tried by a criminal court or a Security Force Court.

key_sections.title: Remedy against order, finding or sentence of Security Force Court.
key_sections.description: Allows aggrieved persons to petition against orders, findings, or sentences of Security Force Courts to confirming authorities or the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Pardon and remission.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government, Director-General, or other officers to pardon, remit, mitigate, or commute punishments.

key_sections.title: Powers and duties conferrable and imposable on members of the Force.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to confer specific powers and duties on members of the Force for law enforcement purposes.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: General superintendence, direction and control of the Force (Section 5); dismiss or remove persons (Section 10); appoint Director-General, Inspectors-General, Deputy Inspectors-General (Section 5); make rules (Section 141); confer powers and duties on members of the Force (Section 139); confirm findings and sentences of General Security Force Courts (Section 108); pardon, remit, mitigate, or commute punishments (Section 128); suspend sentences (Section 130); annul proceedings of Security Force Courts (Section 118).

Director-General: Command and supervision of the Force (Section 5); dismiss, remove or reduce persons (Section 11); convene General Security Force Courts (Section 65); decide choice of court between criminal and Security Force Court (Section 80); pardon, remit, mitigate, or commute punishments (Section 128); suspend sentences (Section 130); annul proceedings of Security Force Courts (Section 118).
