Commandant: Duty in regard to detention of offenders (Section 58); impose collective fines (Section 56); award minor punishments (Section 53); hold Summary Security Force Courts (Section 70).
Security Force Courts: Try persons subject to the Act for offences and award punishments (Sections 72, 73, 74).
Deputy Inspector-General: Dismiss or remove persons (Section 11); award punishments to subordinate officers and below (Section 55); decide choice of court (Section 80).
Force police officers: Take charge of confined persons, preserve order and discipline, prevent breaches, arrest and detain for trial (Section 63).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter III (Sections 14-47) defines a wide range of offences, including those in relation to the enemy (punishable with death or imprisonment up to 14 years), mutiny (punishable with death), desertion (punishable with death or imprisonment up to 7 years), absence without leave (imprisonment up to 3 years), striking or threatening superior officers (imprisonment up to 14 years), insubordination, disgraceful conduct, intoxication, offences against property (imprisonment up to 10 years), false accusations, falsifying documents, and civil offences. Chapter IV (Sections 48-56) outlines the punishments awardable by Security Force Courts, which include death, imprisonment (life or lesser terms), dismissal from service, reduction in rank, forfeiture of seniority, fines, severe reprimand, and forfeiture of pay and allowances. Minor punishments can also be awarded by Commandants or other officers without a Security Force Court.

related_acts: Central Excises and Salt Act, 1944 (1 of 1944)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints Director-General, Inspectors-General, Deputy Inspectors-General (Section 5). Director-General or any prescribed officer appoints Force police (Section 63).

applies_to: officers and subordinate officers
under-officers and other persons enrolled under this Act
Every member of the Force
special_provisions: References to any law not in force in the State of Jammu and Kashmir shall be construed as references to the corresponding law in force in that State (Section 2(2)).
This Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh (Footnote to Section 2(2)).
Powers and duties may be conferred on members of the Force within local limits of such area adjoining the borders of India (Section 139(1)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the establishment of the Border Security Force, defining offences and prescribing punishments, and setting up Security Force Courts for trials. It also includes provisions for arrest, detention, investigation, and execution of sentences, with powers vested in the Central Government, Director-General, Commandants, and other officers.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Security Force Courts (General, Petty, Summary) and criminal courts.

act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL INDUSTRIAL SECURITY FORCE ACT, 1968

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed force of the Union for the better protection and security of industrial undertakings owned by the Central Government, certain other industrial undertakings, employees of all such undertakings and to provide technical consultancy services to industrial establishments in the private sector and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the constitution and regulation of the Central Industrial Security Force, an armed force of the Union. Its main objectives are to ensure the protection and security of industrial undertakings owned by the Central Government, other specified industrial undertakings, and their employees, and to offer technical consultancy services to private sector industrial establishments.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Director-General', 'Force', 'industrial undertaking', and 'supervisory officer'.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Force.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution and maintenance of the Central Industrial Security Force as an armed force of the Union for the protection and security of industrial undertakings.

key_sections.title: Appointment and powers of supervisory officers.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint the Director-General and other supervisory officers, outlining their powers and authority.

key_sections.title: Duties of members of the Force.
key_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities of Force members, including obeying orders, protecting industrial undertakings and employees, and providing technical consultancy services.

key_sections.title: Power to arrest without warrant.
key_sections.description: Grants members of the Force the authority to arrest persons without a warrant under specific circumstances, such as causing hurt to employees or committing cognizable offences related to property.

key_sections.title: Power to search without warrant.
key_sections.description: Allows Force members of a prescribed rank to conduct searches without a warrant if there is reason to believe an offence has been committed and a warrant cannot be obtained promptly.

key_sections.title: Deputation of the Force to industrial undertakings in public sector, joint venture or private sector.
key_sections.description: Permits the Director-General to depute Force members for the protection and security of industrial undertakings in public sector, joint ventures, or private sector upon request.

key_sections.title: Technical Consultancy Service to industrial establishments.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Director-General to provide technical consultancy services relating to security to private sector industrial establishments for a fee.

key_sections.title: Restrictions respecting right to form association, etc.
key_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on Force members regarding their right to form associations, join unions, or communicate with the press without prior sanction.

key_sections.title: Penalties for neglect of duty, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment, for Force members found guilty of neglect of duty, wilful breach of rules, unauthorized absence, or cowardice.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering aspects like conditions of service, duties, punishments, and deputation terms.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint Director-General and supervisory officers (Section 4).
Central Government: To entrust other duties to the Force (Section 3).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 22).
Director-General: To appoint enrolled members of the Force (Section 5).
Director-General: To command, supervise, and administer the Force (Section 7).
Director-General: To depute Force members to industrial undertakings (Section 14).
Director-General: To provide technical consultancy services (Section 14A).
Supervisory officers: To exercise powers and authority as provided by the Act (Section 4).
Supervisory officers: To administer the Force within prescribed local limits (Section 7).
Supervisory officers: To dismiss, remove, or punish enrolled members (Section 8).
Members of the Force: To arrest without warrant (Section 11).
Members of the Force: To search without warrant (Section 12).
Members of the Force: To remove trespassers from premises (Section 11(2)).
Members of the Force: To protect and safeguard industrial undertakings, installations, and employees (Section 10).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties are prescribed for wilfully neglecting or refusing to surrender certificate, arms, etc., by persons ceasing to be members of the Force (imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to two hundred rupees, or both - Section 17(2)). Penalties are also prescribed for neglect of duty, wilful breach of rules, unauthorized withdrawal from duty, failure to report after leave, unauthorized employment, or cowardice (Force custody and imprisonment up to one year - Section 18(1)).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Director-General and other supervisory officers. The Director-General appoints enrolled members of the Force, with a proviso that other specified supervisory officers may also exercise this power.

applies_to: Members of the Central Industrial Security Force
Industrial undertakings owned by the Central Government
Joint venture industrial undertakings
Private industrial undertakings (for deputation and technical consultancy services)
Employees of the aforementioned industrial undertakings
Organisations owned or funded by the Government
exemptions: Members of the Force are not subject to the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, or the Factories Act, 1948, or any corresponding State laws relating to industrial disputes.
special_provisions: Consent of the State Government is required before specifying installations not owned or controlled by the Central Government for protection (Section 10(b) proviso).

For deputation to undertakings owned, controlled, or managed by a Government company (where Central Government is not a member) or a corporation established by a Provincial or State Act, the request must be made with the consent of the State Government (Section 14 proviso).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the command, supervision, and administration of the Force by the Director-General and supervisory officers. It includes powers of arrest and search without warrant for Force members, and provisions for penalties for neglect of duty. The Central Government may also invest a Commandant with the powers of a Magistrate for certain offences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Ordinary criminal courts have jurisdiction. Additionally, a Commandant, if invested with the powers of a Magistrate by the Central Government, can inquire into or try certain offences committed by enrolled members of the Force.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the form of the certificate issued to an enrolled member of the Central Industrial Security Force, vesting them with the powers, functions, and privileges of such a member.

act_identification.act_title: THE JUDGES (INQUIRY) ACT, 1968

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Nineteenth Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the procedure for the investigation and proof of the misbehaviour or incapacity of a judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court and for the presentation of an address by Parliament to the President and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes a procedure for the investigation and proof of misbehaviour or incapacity of a Judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court. It also regulates the process for Parliament to present an address to the President for the removal of such a Judge.

key_sections.title: Short title and Commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, such as 'Chairman', 'Committee', 'Judge', 'prescribed', and 'Speaker'.

key_sections.title: Investigation into misbehaviour or incapacity of Judge by Committee.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for initiating an investigation into a Judge's misbehaviour or incapacity, including the constitution of a Committee, framing of charges, and medical examination.

key_sections.title: Report of Committee.
key_sections.description: Details the Committee's power to regulate its procedure, ensure fair opportunity to the Judge, and submit a report with findings on the charges.

key_sections.title: Powers of Committee.
key_sections.description: Confers on the Committee the powers of a civil court for investigation purposes, including summoning witnesses, requiring document production, and receiving evidence.

key_sections.title: Consideration of report and procedure for presentation of an address for removal of Judge.
key_sections.description: Specifies the parliamentary procedure for considering the Committee's report and presenting an address to the President for the removal of a Judge if misbehaviour or incapacity is proved.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a Joint Committee of both Houses of Parliament to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Speaker or Chairman may admit or refuse a motion for removal of a Judge (Section 3(1))
Speaker or Chairman shall constitute a Committee for investigation (Section 3(2))
Committee shall frame definite charges and communicate them to the Judge (Section 3(3), 3(4))
Committee may arrange for medical examination of the Judge (Section 3(5))
Central Government may appoint an advocate to conduct the case (Section 3(9))
Committee shall have powers of a civil court (Section 5)
Joint Committee of both Houses of Parliament has power to make rules (Section 7)

authorities_established: Joint Committee of both Houses of Parliament
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Speaker or Chairman appoints Committee members and Medical Board members; Central Government appoints advocate; Speaker and Chairman nominate members for the Joint Committee.

applies_to: Judge of the Supreme Court
Judge of a High Court
Chief Justice of India
Chief Justice of a High Court

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Joint Committee of both Houses of Parliament
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Investigation by a Committee, report to Parliament, consideration by Houses of Parliament, and presentation of an address to the President for removal.

act_identification.act_title: THE LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY OF NAGALAND (CHANGE IN REPRESENTATION) ACT, 1968
act_identification.act_short_title: The Legislative Assembly of Nagaland (Change in Representation) Act, 1968

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for a change in representation in the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland and for that purpose to make consequential amendments in the State of Nagaland Act, 1962 and the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to modify the representation in the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland by increasing the total number of seats and altering the method of filling seats for the Tuensang district. It also makes consequential amendments to the State of Nagaland Act, 1962 and the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Establishes the short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Change in representation in the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland.
key_sections.description: Increases the total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland and specifies the method of filling seats, particularly for the Tuensang district.

key_sections.title: Saving as to present Legislative Assembly.
key_sections.description: Ensures that the changes introduced by this Act do not affect the composition of the present Legislative Assembly of Nagaland until its dissolution.

powers_conferred: Governor of Nagaland to specify the manner of choosing persons for seats in the Tuensang district by notification in the Official Gazette

applies_to: Legislative Assembly of Nagaland
Tuensang district
State of Nagaland
special_provisions: Provisions for the period referred to in clause (2) of article 371A of the Constitution
Special method for filling seats allotted to the Tuensang district

act_identification.act_title: THE PRESIDENT (DISCHARGE OF FUNCTIONS) ACT, 1969

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the discharge of the functions of the President in certain contingencies.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the discharge of the functions of the President in specific situations where both the President and Vice-President's offices are vacant or they are unable to perform their duties. It designates the Chief Justice of India or the seniormost Supreme Court Judge to temporarily assume these functions.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969'.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines the terms 'President', 'Vice-President' and 'Second Schedule' as referring to the President of India, the Vice-President of India and the Second Schedule to the Constitution respectively.

key_sections.title: Discharge of President’s functions in certain contingencies.
key_sections.description: Specifies that in the event of vacancies in the offices of both the President and Vice-President, or their inability to discharge functions, the Chief Justice of India or the seniormost Judge of the Supreme Court shall discharge the President's functions, and outlines their powers and entitlements.

powers_conferred: The person discharging the functions of the President under this section shall, during, and in respect of, the period while he is so discharging the said functions, have all the powers and immunities of the President.

applies_to: President
Vice-President
Chief Justice of India
seniormost Judge of the Supreme Court of India

act_identification.act_title: THE REGISTRATION OF BIRTHS AND DEATHS ACT, 1969
act_identification.act_short_title: the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
act_identification.date_of_commencement: It shall come into force in a State on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the regulation of registration of births and deaths and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the registration of births and deaths across India. It establishes a system for recording vital events and addresses related matters to ensure accurate demographic data.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER III REGISTRATION OF BIRTHS AND DEATHS
CHAPTER IV MAINTENANCE OF RECORDS AND STATISTICS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on dates appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions and interpretation.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'birth', 'death', 'Aadhaar number', 'database', 'adoption', etc.

key_sections.title: Registrar General of India.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of the Registrar General of India by the Central Government, outlines their functions, and mandates maintaining a national database of births and deaths.

key_sections.title: Chief Registrar.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of a Chief Registrar for each State by the State Government, outlining their executive authority and responsibility for coordinating registration work.

key_sections.title: Registrars.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to appoint Registrars for local areas, detailing their duties to register births and deaths and maintain records.

key_sections.title: Persons required to register births and deaths.
key_sections.description: Identifies various individuals and authorities responsible for providing information for the registration of births and deaths, including Aadhaar numbers of parents and informants.

key_sections.title: Duty of certain persons to notify births and deaths and to certify cause of death.
key_sections.description: Mandates medical professionals and other specified persons to notify births and deaths and to issue certificates of the cause of death.

key_sections.title: Delayed registration of births and deaths.
key_sections.description: Outlines procedures and fees for registering births and deaths after the specified period, including requirements for permission from District Registrars or orders from Magistrates for significant delays.

key_sections.title: Search of births and deaths register
key_sections.description: Allows individuals to search registers and obtain birth or death certificates, specifying that these certificates are admissible as evidence and can be used for various official purposes like admission, driving license, passport, and Aadhaar.

key_sections.title: Special provision as to registration of births and deaths of citizens outside India.
key_sections.description: Addresses the registration of births and deaths of Indian citizens occurring outside India, handled by the Registrar General of India or upon their return to India.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for failure to provide information, providing false information, or neglecting duties by Registrars or other specified persons.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Establishes an appeal mechanism for persons aggrieved by actions or orders of Registrars or District Registrars.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government, with Central Government approval, the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes, covering various procedural aspects.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint Registrar General of India (Section 3(1)), give directions to State Governments (Section 22), approve State Government rules (Section 30(1)).

Registrar General of India: Appoint other officers (Section 3(2)), issue general directions, coordinate activities, maintain national database (Section 3(3), 3(4)), make database available to other authorities (Section 3(5)).

State Government: Appoint Chief Registrar (Section 4(1)), appoint other officers (Section 4(2)), divide territory into registration divisions (Section 5), appoint District Registrars (Section 6(1)), appoint Registrars (Section 7(1)), specify persons to give information (Section 8(2)), specify persons to notify births/deaths (Section 10(iii)), make rules (Section 30(1)), delegate powers (Section 27), remove difficulty (Section 32).

Chief Registrar: Authorise officers to discharge functions (Section 4(2)), issue instructions, coordinate, supervise registration work (Section 4(4)), maintain state-level database (Section 4(5)), make database available (Section 4(6)), authorise officers for inspection (Section 18), authorise officers for compounding offences (Section 24), authorise officers for prosecution (Section 25).
District Registrar: Superintend registration, execute Act provisions (Section 6(2)), grant written permission for delayed registration (Section 13(2)), decide appeals (Section 25A(2)).

Registrars: Enter information (Section 7(2)), inspect registration offices (Section 18), obtain information (Section 21), correct or cancel entries (Section 15), give certificates (Section 12), appoint Sub-Registrars (Section 7(5)).
District Magistrate/Sub-Divisional Magistrate/Executive Magistrate: Order registration for delayed information after one year (Section 13(3)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person (except those specified in 8(1A)) failing to give information, giving false information, or refusing to sign/thumb mark is punishable with a fine up to two hundred and fifty rupees (Section 23(1)). Persons specified in Section 8(1)(b), (c), (d), (da), (db), (dc), (e) committing similar offences are punishable with a fine up to one thousand rupees per birth/death (Section 23(1A)). A Registrar or Sub-Registrar neglecting duties is punishable with a fine up to two hundred and fifty rupees (Section 23(2)). Persons neglecting to provide or issue certificates under Section 10(2) or (3) are punishable with a fine up to fifty rupees (Section 23(3)). General contraventions without specific penalties are punishable with a fine up to two hundred and fifty rupees (Section 23(4)) or one thousand rupees per birth/death for persons specified in Section 8(1A) (Section 23(4A)). Offences are tried summarily by a magistrate (Section 23(5)).

repealed_acts: so much of any law in force therein as relates to the matters covered by this Act
related_acts: Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016 (18 of 2016)
Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (2 of 2016)
Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act, 1886 (Act 6 of 1886)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Registrar General of India. The State Government appoints the Chief Registrar, District Registrars, and Registrars. Registrars, with the Chief Registrar's approval, appoint Sub-Registrars and Special Sub-Registrars.

applies_to: the whole of India
citizens of India outside India
special_provisions: Different commencement dates may be appointed for different parts of a State (Proviso to Section 1(3)).
Special provisions regarding births and deaths in a plantation (Section 9).
Special provision as to registration of births and deaths of citizens outside India (Section 20).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: State Government, with the approval of the Central Government (Section 30(1)).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a hierarchical registration establishment (Registrar General, Chief Registrar, District Registrars, Registrars). Duties are imposed on various persons to report births and deaths, and penalties are prescribed for non-compliance. An appeal mechanism is also provided.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: A magistrate for summary trial of offences (Section 23(5)).

act_identification.act_title: THE UNION TERRITORIES (SEPARATION OF JUDICIAL AND EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONS) ACT, 1969
act_identification.act_short_title: the Union territories (Separation of Judicial and Executive Functions) Act, 1969
act_identification.date_of_commencement: It shall come into force in a Union territory to which it extends on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint in respect thereof

legislative_details.geographical_extent: all Union territories except the Union territory of Chandigarh

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the separation of judicial and executive functions in Union Territories.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to separate judicial and executive functions in Union Territories by amending the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. It redefines the roles and powers of Judicial and Executive Magistrates to ensure that functions involving appreciation of evidence and punishment are handled by Judicial Magistrates, while administrative functions are handled by Executive Magistrates.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Defines the short title, geographical extent, and commencement procedure of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines the term 'Union territory' for the purpose of sections 3 to 9 of the Act.

key_sections.title: Amendments to Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
key_sections.description: States that the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, shall be amended as specified in the Schedule for the separation of judicial and executive functions.

key_sections.title: Functions exercisable by Judicial and Executive Magistrates.
key_sections.description: Delineates the types of functions to be exercised by Judicial Magistrates (involving appreciation of evidence, punishment, detention) and Executive Magistrates (administrative functions like licensing, sanctioning prosecution).

key_sections.title: Repeal of laws in transferred areas in Himachal Pradesh.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Punjab Separation of Judicial and Executive Functions Act, 1964, and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, in transferred areas of Himachal Pradesh upon the commencement of this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions, in consultation with the High Court.

key_sections.title: Power of Legislative Assembly of Union territory to amend this Act.
key_sections.description: Allows the Legislative Assembly of a Union territory to amend this Act in its application to that Union territory.

key_sections.title: For section 6, the following sections shall be substituted, namely:— “6. Classes of Criminal Courts.—Besides the High Court and the Courts constituted under any law other than this Code for the time being in force, there shall to be two classes of Criminal Courts, namely:— I. Courts of Session. II. Courts of Magistrates. A1.—Classes of Magistrates 6A. Classes of Magistrates.—There shall be the following classes of Magistrates, namely:— I. Judicial Magistrates: (1) Chief Judicial Magistrate (2) Judicial Magistrates of the first class. (3) Judicial Magistrates of the second class. II. Executive Magistrates: (1) District Magistrates. (2) Sub-divisional Magistrates. (3) Executive Magistrates of the first class. (4) Executive Magistrates of the second class. (5) Special Executive Magistrates.”.
key_sections.description: Substitutes Section 6 of the CrPC, 1898, to establish distinct classes of Criminal Courts and, crucially, introduces and defines the classes of Judicial and Executive Magistrates.

key_sections.title: For section 12, the following section shall be substituted, namely:— “12. Executive Magistrates and Chief Judicial Magistrates.—(1) The State Government may appoint as many persons as it thinks fit, besides the District Magistrate, to be Executive Magistrates of the first or second class in any district, and the State Government or the District Magistrate, subject to the control of the State Government, may, from time to time, define local areas within which such persons may exercise all or any of the powers with which they may, respectively, be invested under this Code. (2) The State Government, in consultation with the High Court, may confer on any person who is a civil Judge or a member of the Judicial Service of a Union territory or a group of such territories, the powers of any class of Judicial Magistrates in any district; and the State Government, in consultation with the High Court, or the Chief Judicial Magistrate, subject to the control of the High Court, may, from time to time, define local areas within which he may exercise all or any of the powers with which he may be invested under this Code. (3) The State Government, in consultation with the High Court, may, for such period not exceeding three years from the commencement of the Union Territories (Separation of Judicial and Executive Functions) Act, 1969, as it may think fit, appoint as many persons, who are members of a civil service in any Union territory or in any State and who are or have been exercising the powers of a Magistrate in such territory or state at or before the commencement of the said Act, as may be considered necessary to be Judicial Magistrates in any district; and the State Government, in consultation with the High Court, may define local areas within which such persons may exercise all or any of the powers with which they may, respectively, be invested under this Code. (4) Except as otherwise provided by any such definition as is referred to in sub-sections (1), (2) or (3), the jurisdiction and powers of such persons shall extend throughout such district.”.
key_sections.description: Substitutes Section 12 of the CrPC, 1898, detailing the appointment and powers of Executive Magistrates and Chief Judicial Magistrates, including the role of the State Government and High Court in conferring powers.

key_sections.title: For section 17, the following sections shall be substituted, namely:— “17. Subordination of Judicial Magistrates and Benches to Chief Judicial Magistrates and of Chief Judicial Magistrates and Assistant Sessions Judges to Sessions Judge.—(1) All Judicial Magistrates appointed under sub-sections (2) and (3) of section 12 and all Benches constituted under section 15, shall, subject to the control of the Sessions Judge, be subordinate to the Chief Judicial Magistrate, and the Chief Judicial Magistrate may, from time to time, make rules or give special orders consistent with this Code as to the distributions of business among such Magistrates and Benches. (2) All Chief Judicial Magistrates shall be subordinate to the Sessions Judge. (3) All Assistant Sessions Judge shall be subordinate to the Sessions Judge in whose Court they exercise jurisdiction, and the sessions Judge may, from time to time, make rules consistent with this Code as to the distribution of business among such Assistant Sessions Judges. (4) The Sessions Judge may also, when he himself is unavoidably absent or incapable of acting, make provision for the disposal of any urgent application by an Additional or Assistant Sessions Judge, or, if there be no Additional or Assistant Sessions Judge, by the Chief Judicial Magistrate, and such Judge or Magistrate shall have jurisdiction to deal with any such application. 17A. Subordination of Executive Magistrates.—(1) All Executive Magistrates appointed under sub-section (1) of section 12, section 13 and section 14 shall be subordinate to the District Magistrate and every Executive Magistrate (other than a Sub-divisional Magistrate) exercising powers in a sub-division shall also be subordinate to the Sub-divisional Magistrate, subject, however, to the general control of the District Magistrate. (2) The District Magistrate may, from time to time, make rules or give special orders consistent with this Code as to the distribution of business among Executive Magistrates subordinate to him and as to allocation of business to an Additional District Magistrate. 17B. Courts inferior to High Court and Court of Session.—Courts of Session and Courts of Judicial and Executive Magistrates shall be Criminal Courts inferior to the High Court and Courts of Judicial and Executive Magistrates shall be Criminal Courts inferior to the Court of Session.”.
key_sections.description: Substitutes Section 17 of the CrPC, 1898, to define the subordination structure for Judicial Magistrates (to Chief Judicial Magistrate and Sessions Judge) and Executive Magistrates (to District Magistrate and Sub-divisional Magistrate).

key_sections.title: For sections 37 and 38, the following sections shall be substituted, namely:— “37. Additional powers conferable on Magistrates.—In addition to the ordinary powers,— (i) the State Government, in consultation with the High Court, may invest any Judicial Magistrate with any of the Powers specified in Part IA of Schedule IV; (ii) a Chief Judicial Magistrate may invest any Judicial Magistrate within his local jurisdiction with the powers specified in Part IB of Schedule IV; (iii) the State Government may invest any Executive Magistrate with any of the powers specified in Part IIA of Schedule IV; and (iv) a District Magistrate may invest any Executive Magistrate within his local jurisdiction with the powers specified in Part IIB of Schedule IV. 38. Exercise of powers under section 37 by Chief Judicial Magistrate or District Magistrate to be subject to control of High Court or State Government.—The power conferred on the Chief Judicial Magistrate under clause (ii) of section 37 shall be exercised subject to the control of the High Court and the power conferred on the District Magistrate under clause (iv) of that section shall be exercised subject to the control of the State Government. 38A. Power on Judicial Magistrates to be conferred in consultation with High Court.—Whenever under any provisions of this Code or of any other law for the time being in force relating to any of the matters specified in Lists II and III of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, any judicial powers are to be conferred on a Sessions Judge, or an Additional or Assistant Sessions Judge or a Chief Judicial Magistrate or any other Judicial Magistrate or any such Magistrate is to be specially empowered to exercise such powers the orders conferring such powers or empowering the exercise of such powers shall be made by the State Government in consultation with the High Court notwithstanding that such provision may not expressly so provide. Explanation —For the purposes of this section, the question whether any powers are judicial shall be decided by the State Government in consultation with the High Court and such decision shall be final”.
key_sections.description: Substitutes Sections 37 and 38 of the CrPC, 1898, to specify how additional powers can be conferred upon Judicial and Executive Magistrates by the State Government, Chief Judicial Magistrate, or District Magistrate, emphasizing consultation with the High Court for judicial powers.

key_sections.title: For section 435, the following section shall be substituted, namely:— “435. Power to call for records of inferior Courts.—(1) The High Court or any Sessions Judge may call for and examine the record of any proceeding before any inferior Criminal Court situate within the local limits of its or his jurisdiction and any Chief Judicial Magistrate may call for and examine the record of any proceedings before any Judicial Magistrate under his Jurisdiction for the purpose of satisfying itself or himself as to the correctness, legality or propriety of any finding, sentence or order recorded or passed, and as to the regularity of any proceedings of such inferior Court or such Magistrate, as the case may be, and may, when calling for such record, direct that the execution of any sentence or order be suspended and, if the accused is in confinement, that he be released on bail or on his own bond pending the examination of the record. (2) The District Magistrate or any Sub-divisional Magistrate empowered by the State Government in this behalf, may call for and examine the record of any proceeding before any Subordinate Executive Magistrate for the purpose of satisfying himself as to the correctness, legality or propriety of any order recorded or passed, and as to the regularity of any proceedings of such Subordinate Magistrate and may, when calling for such record, direct that the execution of any order be suspended and, if the person is in confinement, that he be released on bail or on his own bond pending the examination of the record. (3) If any Sub-divisional Magistrate acting under sub-section (2) considers that any such proceeding or order is illegal or improper or that any such proceeding is irregular, he shall forward the record, with such remarks thereon as he thinks fit to the District Magistrate. (4) The High Court may call for and examine the record of any proceeding under section 118, 122, 143, 144 or 145, notwithstanding the fact that such proceeding was before an Executive Magistrate. (5) If an application in respect of any proceeding before any Judicial Magistrate other than the Chief Judicial Magistrate has been made under sub-section (1) either to the Sessions Judge or the Chief Judicial Magistrate, no further application shall be entertained by the other of them and if an application in respect of any proceeding before any Executive Magistrate has been made to the Sessions Judge under sub-section (1) or to the District Magistrate under sub-section (2), no further application shall be entertained by the other of them.”.
key_sections.description: Substitutes Section 435 of the CrPC, 1898, detailing the power of the High Court, Sessions Judge, Chief Judicial Magistrate, District Magistrate, and Sub-divisional Magistrate to call for and examine records of inferior courts, distinguishing between judicial and executive proceedings.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to appoint commencement date (Section 1), power to remove difficulties (Section 8).

State Government: Power to alter limits of divisions/districts (Schedule, Section 7(2) CrPC), power to appoint Executive Magistrates (Schedule, Section 12(1) CrPC), power to confer powers on Judicial Magistrates (Schedule, Section 12(2), (3) CrPC), power to appoint Special Executive Magistrates (Schedule, Section 14 CrPC), power to direct Benches of Judicial Magistrates (Schedule, Section 15 CrPC), power to invest Judicial/Executive Magistrates with additional powers (Schedule, Section 37 CrPC), power to empower Judicial Magistrates (Schedule, Section 38A CrPC), power to confer/withdraw powers on Judicial Magistrates (Schedule, Section 39, 41 CrPC), power to empower Magistrates to record statements/confessions (Schedule, Section 40(1), (1A) CrPC), power to authorize Benches of Magistrates (Schedule, Section 265 CrPC).

High Court: Power to be consulted by State Government for various appointments and power conferrals (Schedule, Section 7(2), 9, 10(2A), 10(2B), 12(2), 12(3), 15, 16, 37(i), 38A, 39, 40, 41(i), 40(1), 186, 206, 260, 261, 265, 562 CrPC), power to control Chief Judicial Magistrate (Schedule, Section 38 CrPC), power to call for records of inferior courts (Schedule, Section 435(1), (4) CrPC).

Chief Judicial Magistrate: Power to make rules/orders for distribution of business among Judicial Magistrates (Schedule, Section 17(1) CrPC), power to invest Judicial Magistrates with powers (Schedule, Section 37(ii) CrPC), power to withdraw powers (Schedule, Section 41(2) CrPC), power to transfer cases (Schedule, Section 192 CrPC), power to entertain complaints/police reports (Schedule, Section 190 CrPC), power to try summarily (Schedule, Section 260 CrPC), power to tender pardon (Schedule, Section 337 CrPC), power to hear appeals (Schedule, Section 406A CrPC), power to call for records (Schedule, Section 435(1) CrPC), power to order inquiry/commitment (Schedule, Section 436, 437 CrPC), power to report case to High Court (Schedule, Section 438 CrPC), power to withdraw/refer cases (Schedule, Section 528 CrPC).

District Magistrate: Power to define local areas for Executive Magistrates (Schedule, Section 12(1) CrPC), power to make rules/orders for distribution of business among Executive Magistrates (Schedule, Section 17A(2) CrPC), power to invest Executive Magistrates with powers (Schedule, Section 37(iv) CrPC), power to withdraw powers (Schedule, Section 41(2) CrPC), power to call for records of subordinate Executive Magistrates (Schedule, Section 435(2) CrPC), power to direct further inquiry (Schedule, Section 436(2) CrPC), power to report cases to High Court (Schedule, Section 438(3) CrPC), power to hear appeals (Schedule, Section 406A CrPC), power to withdraw/recall cases (Schedule, Section 528(2B) CrPC).
Legislative Assembly of a Union territory: Power to amend this Act in its application to that Union territory (Section 9).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act reassigns the functions related to offences and penalties under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, by specifying whether they are to be exercised by Judicial or Executive Magistrates, based on the nature of the function (judicial or administrative).

repealed_acts: Punjab Separation of Judicial and Executive Functions Act, 1964

authorities_established: Judicial Magistrates (Chief Judicial Magistrate, Judicial Magistrates of the first class, Judicial Magistrates of the second class)
Executive Magistrates (District Magistrates, Sub-divisional Magistrates, Executive Magistrates of the first class, Executive Magistrates of the second class, Special Executive Magistrates)
important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government, High Court, Chief Judicial Magistrate, District Magistrate

applies_to: all Union territories except the Union territory of Chandigarh
exemptions: Union territory of Chandigarh
special_provisions: transferred areas in the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government, State Government, High Court
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through amendments to the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, which reassign judicial and executive functions to distinct classes of Magistrates. The Central Government can issue notifications for commencement, and the State Government, in consultation with the High Court, makes rules and orders for the exercise of powers.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court, Courts of Session, Courts of Magistrates (Judicial and Executive Magistrates)

schedules_summary.description: Details extensive amendments to the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, primarily by establishing distinct classes of Judicial and Executive Magistrates, defining their ordinary and additional powers, and specifying their subordination and jurisdiction. It replaces sections 6, 12, 14, 17, 29, 30, 37, 38, 406A, 435, 515, and 528 of the CrPC, and amends numerous other sections to reflect the separation of judicial and executive functions.

act_identification.act_title: THE FOREIGN MARRIAGE ACT, 1969

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Relates to marriages of citizens of India outside India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make provision relating to marriages of citizens of India outside India.
act_overview.purpose: This Act makes provisions for the solemnization and registration of marriages involving citizens of India outside India. It sets conditions for such marriages, provides for matrimonial reliefs, and prescribes penalties for contraventions.

chapter_titles: REGISTRATION OF FOREIGN MARRIAGES SOLEMNIZED UNDER OTHER LAWS
MATRIMONIAL RELIEF IN RESPECT OF FOREIGN MARRIAGES

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as The Foreign Marriage Act, 1969.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'degrees of prohibited relationship', 'foreign country', and 'Marriage Officer'.

key_sections.title: Marriage Officers.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint diplomatic or consular officers as Marriage Officers for foreign countries.

key_sections.title: Conditions relating to solemnization of foreign marriages.
key_sections.description: Lays down the essential conditions for solemnizing a foreign marriage under this Act, including age, marital status, and prohibited relationships.

key_sections.title: Notice of intended marriage.
key_sections.description: Requires parties intending to marry under this Act to give written notice to the Marriage Officer.

key_sections.title: Certificate of marriage.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Marriage Officer to issue a certificate of marriage upon solemnization, which serves as conclusive evidence of the marriage.

key_sections.title: Validity of foreign marriages in India.
key_sections.description: Declares marriages solemnized according to this Act as good and valid in law in India.

key_sections.title: Registration of foreign marriages.
key_sections.description: Provides for the registration of foreign marriages solemnized under the law of other countries, provided certain conditions are met.

key_sections.title: Matrimonial reliefs to be under Special Marriage Act, 1954.
key_sections.description: Applies provisions of the Special Marriage Act, 1954, concerning matrimonial reliefs to marriages solemnized under this Act or other foreign marriages involving Indian citizens.

key_sections.title: Punishment for bigamy.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for bigamy committed by persons whose marriage is solemnized or deemed solemnized under this Act, referring to the Indian Penal Code.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Indian Foreign Marriage Act, 1903.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint Marriage Officers (Section 3).
Central Government: To give decisions on objections to marriage (Section 10).
Central Government: To decide appeals against refusal to solemnize or register marriage (Sections 11, 17).
Central Government: To declare recognition of marriages solemnized under laws of other countries (Section 23).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 28).
Marriage Officer: To solemnize marriages (Section 4).
Marriage Officer: To keep records and Marriage Notice Book (Section 6).
Marriage Officer: To publish notices of intended marriage (Section 7).
Marriage Officer: To inquire into objections to marriage (Section 10).
Marriage Officer: To refuse to solemnize marriage under certain conditions (Section 11).
Marriage Officer: To issue certificate of marriage (Section 14).
Marriage Officer: To register foreign marriages (Section 17).
Marriage Officer: To certify documents of marriages solemnized in accordance with local law in a foreign country (Section 24).
Marriage Officer: To correct errors in the Marriage Certificate Book (Section 26).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for bigamy (referencing IPC sections 494 and 495), contravention of certain marriage conditions (simple imprisonment up to 15 days or 1 month, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both), making false declarations (imprisonment up to three years and fine), and wrongful action by a Marriage Officer (simple imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both).

repealed_acts: The Indian Foreign Marriage Act, 1903 (14 of 1903)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government may appoint diplomatic or consular officers to be Marriage Officers.

applies_to: Citizens of India outside India
Marriages where at least one party is a citizen of India
exemptions: The Act does not affect the validity of marriages solemnized in a foreign country otherwise than under this Act.
special_provisions: A marriage between parties within prohibited relationship may be solemnized if personal law or custom governing at least one party permits it (Proviso to Section 4(d)).
Specific conditions for courts to grant matrimonial relief based on domicile or residence (Section 18(3)).

Amendments to the Special Marriage Act, 1954, regarding its application to citizens of India domiciled in territories to which that Act extends, particularly concerning the State of Jammu and Kashmir (Section 29).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through Marriage Officers who solemnize and register marriages, publish notices, and inquire into objections. The Central Government provides oversight and appellate review. Penalties are prescribed for contraventions.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District court for matrimonial reliefs.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the form for the Notice of Intended Marriage.
Contains the declaration forms to be made by the bridegroom and the bride before marriage.
Contains the form for the Certificate of Marriage.

act_identification.act_title: THE KHUDA BAKHSH ORIENTAL PUBLIC LIBRARY ACT, 1969
act_identification.act_short_title: The Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library Act, 1969

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare the Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library at Patna to be an institution of national importance and to provide for its administration and certain other connected matters.
act_overview.purpose: This Act declares the Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library at Patna as an institution of national importance. It provides for the establishment of a Board for its administration, management, and development on modern scientific lines.
act_overview.act_category: Institutions of Natural and Cultural Importance

chapter_titles: THE KHUDA BAKHSH ORIENTAL PUBLIC LIBRARY BOARD
PROPERTY, LIABILITIES AND FUNCTIONS OF THE BOARD

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Declaration of Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library as an institution of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library at Patna in Bihar as an institution of national importance.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Board', 'Chairman', 'library', and 'State Government'.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library Board as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

key_sections.title: Composition of Board.
key_sections.description: Details the composition of the Board, including ex officio members and nominated persons by the Central and State Governments.

key_sections.title: Transfer of service of existing employees to Board.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that existing employees of the library become employees of the Board with similar tenure, remuneration, and terms of service.

key_sections.title: Property and liabilities of Board.
key_sections.description: Specifies that all properties, funds, and liabilities of the library's trustees shall vest in or be enforceable against the Board upon its establishment.

key_sections.title: Duties of Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the general duty of the Board to manage the library, promote its development, and perform other assigned functions, including instruction and research.

key_sections.title: Grants by Central Government to Board.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to provide grants, loans, or other sums of money to the Board for its efficient functioning.

key_sections.title: Fund of Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Fund for the Board, detailing sources of credit including moneys from Central and State Governments, fees, gifts, and other sources.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Board to maintain proper accounts and specifies that accounts shall be audited annually by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to issue directions to Board.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the Board on questions of policy, with the Board having an opportunity to express its views.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules to give effect to the Act's provisions, including matters related to term of office, allowances, and disqualifications.

key_sections.title: Power of Board to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Board, with Central Government approval, to make regulations for discharging its functions, covering aspects like use of manuscripts, meetings, and staff conditions.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint date of commencement (Section 1)
Central Government to appoint date of establishment of Board (Section 4)
Central Government to nominate members to the Board (Section 5)
State Government to nominate members to the Board (Section 5)
Board to acquire, hold, and dispose of property and contract (Section 4)
Board to sue and be sued (Section 4)
Board to associate persons for particular purposes (Section 10)
Board to appoint officers and other employees (Section 12)
Board to manage the library and plan, promote, organise and implement programmes for its development (Section 16)
Board to provide for instruction and research relating to libraries (Section 16)
Board to purchase or acquire manuscripts, books, articles or things for preservation (Section 17)
Board to expend sums from its Fund for performing functions (Section 19)
Board to sanction reappropriation of expenditure (Section 20)
Board to delegate powers and duties (Section 24)
Board to make regulations (Section 28)

related_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)

authorities_established: Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library Board
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government nominates members to the Board and approves the Board's regulations. The State Government also nominates members. The Board appoints its own officers and employees.

applies_to: Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library at Patna
Employees of the library
Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library Board

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library Board, which manages the library and performs functions as directed by the Central Government. The Central Government provides grants, approves budgets, and issues policy directions. Accounts are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India. Rules are made by the Central Government and regulations by the Board.

act_identification.act_title: THE BIHAR LAND REFORMS LAWS (REGULATING MINES AND MINERALS) VALIDATION ACT, 1969
act_identification.act_short_title: Bihar Land Reforms Laws (Regulating Mines and Minerals) Validation Act, 1969

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Twentieth Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to validate certain provisions contained in the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950, and the Bihar Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 1964, and action taken and things done in connection therewith.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to legally validate specific sections of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950, and a rule from the Bihar Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 1964. It also validates all past actions, rules, notifications, and collection of rents or royalties under these laws, overriding any contrary court judgments.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Bihar Land Reforms Laws (Regulating Mines and Minerals) Validation Act, 1969.

key_sections.title: Validation of certain Bihar State laws and action taken and things done connected therewith.
key_sections.description: Validates specific Bihar State laws listed in the Schedule, and all actions, rules, notifications, and collection of rents or royalties made under them, overriding any court judgments. It also clarifies that claims for refund of excess payments are not prevented.

powers_conferred: Validation of power to collect rents/royalties under specified Bihar State laws

related_acts: Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950 (Bihar Act XXX of 1950)
Bihar Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1964 (Bihar Act IV of 1965)
Bihar Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1965 (Bihar Act VI of 1965)
Bihar Minor Mineral Concession (First Amendment) Rules, 1964

schedules_summary.description: Lists specific provisions of the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950 (Sections 10, 10-A, 31), and sub-rule (2) of Rule 20 of the Bihar Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 1964, that are validated by this Act.

act_identification.act_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to judicial oaths and for certain other purposes.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to judicial oaths and for certain other purposes.
act_overview.purpose: The primary purpose of this Act is to consolidate and amend the existing laws concerning judicial oaths. It regulates the administration of oaths and affirmations in legal proceedings, ensuring that witnesses, interpreters, and jurors are bound to state the truth.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Oaths Act, 1969' and specifies its geographical application to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Saving of certain oaths and affirmations.
key_sections.description: Exempts proceedings before courts martial and oaths/affirmations prescribed by the Central Government for Armed Forces members from the Act's application.

key_sections.title: Power to administer oaths.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon courts and persons authorized to receive evidence, as well as commanding officers, to administer oaths and affirmations. Also allows High Courts and State Governments to empower for affidavits.

key_sections.title: Oaths or affirmations to be made by witnesses, interpreter and jurors.
key_sections.description: Mandates oaths or affirmations for witnesses, interpreters, and jurors, with specific exceptions for child witnesses and accused persons in criminal proceedings.

key_sections.title: Affirmation by persons desiring to affirm.
key_sections.description: Allows a witness, interpreter, or juror to make an affirmation instead of an oath.

key_sections.title: Forms of oaths and affirmations.
key_sections.description: Prescribes that oaths and affirmations under Section 4 shall be administered according to the forms in the Schedule, with a proviso for alternative forms if desired by the witness and deemed appropriate by the court.

key_sections.title: Proceedings and evidence not invalidated by omission of oath or irregularity.
key_sections.description: States that an omission to take an oath, substitution, or irregularity in administration shall not invalidate proceedings or render evidence inadmissible, nor affect the obligation to state the truth.

key_sections.title: Persons giving evidence bound to state the truth.
key_sections.description: Obligates every person giving evidence before an authorized court or person to state the truth on the subject.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Indian Oaths Act, 1873, but includes a saving clause for agreements made under section 8 of the repealed Act in pending proceedings.

powers_conferred: Power to courts and persons having authority to receive evidence to administer oaths and affirmations (Section 3(1)).
Power to commanding officers of military, naval, or air force stations to administer oaths (Section 3(1)(b)).
Power to High Court or State Government to empower courts/persons to administer oaths and affirmations for affidavits (Section 3(2)).
Power to courts to allow witnesses to give evidence on alternative forms of oath or affirmation (Section 6(1) Proviso).

repealed_acts: The Indian Oaths Act, 1873 (10 of 1873)

applies_to: Whole of India.
All courts and persons having by law or consent of parties authority to receive evidence.
Commanding officers of military, naval, or air force stations.
All witnesses, interpreters, and jurors.
exemptions: Proceedings before courts martial.
Oaths, affirmations, or declarations prescribed by the Central Government for members of the Armed Forces of the Union.
Child witnesses under twelve years of age who do not understand the nature of an oath or affirmation.
Accused persons in criminal proceedings, unless examined as a witness for the defence.
Official interpreters of any court, after entering on the execution of their duties.
special_provisions: Provisions for child witnesses under twelve years of age, where absence of oath does not render evidence inadmissible (Section 4 Proviso).
Provisions allowing witnesses to use alternative forms of oath or affirmation common to their class, if not repugnant to justice or decency (Section 6(1) Proviso).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the administration of oaths and affirmations by courts and authorized persons, binding individuals to state the truth in legal proceedings.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: All courts, including the Supreme Court, High Courts, and Benches of Judges or Magistrates, as well as persons having authority to receive evidence.

schedules_summary.description: Contains four forms of oaths or affirmations: Form No. 1 for Witnesses, Form No. 2 for Jurors, Form No. 3 for Interpreters, and Form No. 4 for Affidavits.

act_identification.act_title: THE ASSAM REORGANISATION (MEGHALAYA) ACT, 1969

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the formation within the State of Assam of an autonomous State to be known as Meghalaya and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the creation of Meghalaya as an autonomous State within the State of Assam. It defines its executive and legislative powers, financial provisions, and the apportionment of assets and liabilities between Assam and the newly formed Meghalaya, along with other connected matters.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Establishes the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Formation of Meghalaya.
key_sections.description: Details the formation of Meghalaya as an autonomous State within Assam and specifies its territorial composition.

key_sections.title: Executive power of Meghalaya.
key_sections.description: Vests the executive power of Meghalaya in the Governor.

key_sections.title: Council of Ministers.
key_sections.description: Mandates a Council of Ministers with a Chief Minister to aid and advise the Governor.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Legislature of Meghalaya.
key_sections.description: Constitutes the Legislature of Meghalaya, comprising the Governor and the Legislative Assembly.

key_sections.title: Extent of Legislative power.
key_sections.description: Defines the exclusive and concurrent legislative powers of Meghalaya.

key_sections.title: Inconsistency between laws made by Parliament and laws made by the Legislature of Meghalaya.
key_sections.description: Addresses the issue of inconsistency between laws made by Parliament and the Legislature of Meghalaya.

key_sections.title: Consolidated Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Consolidated Fund of Meghalaya.

key_sections.title: Apportionment of assets and liabilities.
key_sections.description: Mandates the apportionment of assets and liabilities between Assam and Meghalaya.

key_sections.title: Obligation of Meghalaya, the State of Assam and the Union.
key_sections.description: Outlines the obligations of Meghalaya, Assam, and the Union regarding compliance with laws and executive power.

key_sections.title: Continuance of existing laws and their adaptations.
key_sections.description: Ensures the continuance of existing laws in Meghalaya and provides for their adaptation.

key_sections.title: Amendment of the Sixth Schedule.
key_sections.description: Specifies that the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution shall be amended as per the Fourth Schedule of this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to implement the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint commencement date, fix seats in Legislative Assembly, nominate members to Legislative Assembly, determine proportion of revenue distribution, make rules, remove difficulties.

Governor: Appoint Chief Minister and Ministers, administer oaths, determine salaries, appoint Advocate-General, make rules for business, summon/prorogue/dissolve Legislative Assembly, address Legislative Assembly, appoint Speaker/Deputy Speaker, make rules for secretariat, promulgate Ordinances, authorise expenditure.

Legislature of Meghalaya: Make laws, determine salaries/allowances of Ministers, members, Speaker/Deputy Speaker, regulate recruitment/conditions of service for secretariat, establish Contingency Fund, regulate custody of funds.
Election Commission: Delimit constituencies, maintain delimitation orders.

President: Assent to Bills, make orders for elections, determine number of persons for Provisional Legislative Assembly, suspend provisions of Act, make orders for allocation/adjustment of assets/liabilities.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 30 prescribes a penalty of five hundred rupees for sitting and voting as a member of the Legislative Assembly before making an oath or affirmation, or when not qualified or disqualified.

related_acts: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
Representation of the People Act, 1951 (43 of 1951)
Union Duties of Excise (Distribution) Act, 1962 (3 of 1962)
Additional Duties of Excise (Goods of Special Importance) Act, 1957 (58 of 1957)

authorities_established: Special Committee for development of Shillong
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Governor appoints the Chief Minister and other Ministers, and may appoint the Advocate-General. The Governor also nominates members to the Legislative Assembly and associate members to the Election Commission. The Legislative Assembly chooses its Speaker and Deputy Speaker. The Central Government nominates persons to the Provisional Legislative Assembly.

applies_to: Autonomous State of Meghalaya
Persons qualified for membership of Legislative Assembly
Members of Legislative Assembly
Government of Meghalaya
exemptions: Property of the Union from taxes imposed by Meghalaya or any authority within Meghalaya.
Property of the State of Assam from taxes imposed by Meghalaya or any authority within Meghalaya.
Vehicles registered in Assam transiting through Meghalaya from taxes under laws enacted by the Legislature of Meghalaya.
special_provisions: Provisions for the United Khasi Jaintia Hills District and Garo Hills District to form part of Meghalaya.
Provision for North Cachar Hills or Mikir Hills District to form part of Meghalaya upon resolution.
Special provisions regarding legislative power for the area comprised within the municipality of Shillong.
Special Committee for development of Shillong.
Provisions for a Provisional Legislative Assembly until the regular Legislative Assembly is constituted.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government, Governor, Legislature of Meghalaya, Election Commission.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The executive power of Meghalaya must ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament and the State of Assam. The Union and Assam Governments can issue directions to Meghalaya. Existing courts and tribunals continue to function. The appropriate Government can adapt existing laws.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court of Assam (for certain references), Supreme Court (mentioned in context of restrictions on discussion and jurisdiction).

schedules_summary.description: Contains the forms of oaths or affirmations to be made by candidates for election, members of the Legislative Assembly, and members of the Council of Ministers (oath of office and oath of secrecy).

Lists matters with respect to which the Legislative Assembly of Meghalaya has exclusive power to make laws (Part A), and matters where Meghalaya and Assam Legislatures have concurrent power (Part C). It also includes matters from the Concurrent List (Part B).

Details the apportionment of assets and liabilities between the State of Assam and Meghalaya, covering lands, goods, treasury balances, arrears of taxes, loans, investments, public debt, and other financial obligations.
Specifies the amendments to be made to the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution, particularly concerning District Councils, their powers, and the application of laws in Meghalaya.

act_identification.act_title: THE BANKING COMPANIES (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKINGS) ACT, 1970
act_identification.act_short_title: the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of certain banking companies, having regard to their size, resources, coverage and organisation, in order to control the heights of the economy and to meet progressively, and serve better, the needs of development of the economy in conformity with national policy and objectives and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to nationalize certain large banking companies by acquiring and transferring their undertakings to new corresponding banks. The objective is to control key economic sectors and better serve the developmental needs of the economy in line with national policy.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II TRANSFER OF THE UNDERTAKINGSOF EXISTING BANKS AND SHARE CAPITALS OF THE CORRESPONDING NEW BANKS
CHAPTER IV MANAGEMENT OF CORRESPONDING NEW BANKS

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement dates.

key_sections.title: Definitions
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as "appointed day", "banking company", "corresponding new bank", and "existing bank".

key_sections.title: Establishment of corresponding new banks and business thereof
key_sections.description: Constitutes new banks corresponding to existing ones, details their capital structure, and outlines their banking business.

key_sections.title: Undertaking of existing banks to vest in corresponding new banks
key_sections.description: States that the undertakings of existing banks are transferred to and vested in the corresponding new banks upon commencement of the Act.

key_sections.title: General effect of vesting
key_sections.description: Describes what the undertaking includes (assets, liabilities, rights, etc.) and how pending proceedings are handled.

key_sections.title: Payment of compensation
key_sections.description: Details the compensation to be paid by the Central Government to existing banks for the transfer of their undertakings, including payment options and interest rates.

key_sections.title: Head office and management
key_sections.description: Specifies the location of the head office and the vesting of general superintendence, direction, and management in a Board of Directors or a Custodian.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make scheme
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make schemes for carrying out the Act's provisions, including capital structure, Board constitution, and amalgamation.

key_sections.title: Closure of accounts and disposal of profits
key_sections.description: Mandates the closing and balancing of accounts, appointment of auditors, and disposal of profits for corresponding new banks.

key_sections.title: Removal of Chairman from office
key_sections.description: Deals with the transition of the Chairman of an existing bank to Custodian and the terms of service for other employees.

key_sections.title: Obligations as to fidelity and secrecy
key_sections.description: Requires corresponding new banks and their personnel to observe fidelity and secrecy customary among bankers.

act_identification.act_title: THE HARYANA AND PUNJAB AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITIES ACT, 1970
act_identification.act_short_title: The Haryana and Punjab Agricultural Universities Act, 1970

legislative_details.geographical_extent: States of Haryana and Punjab, and temporarily the Union territory of Himachal Pradesh for the Punjab Agricultural University

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of two independent Agricultural Universities in place of the Punjab Agricultural University constituted by the Punjab Agricultural University Act, 1961, and for matters consequential on, or connected with the establishment of those independent Agricultural Universities. WHEREAS, for the development of agriculture in the States of Haryana and Punjab, it is expedient to provide for the establishment of two independent Agricultural Universities in place of the Punjab Agricultural University constituted by the Punjab Agricultural University Act, 1961; AND WHEREAS, the Legislatures of the States of Haryana and Punjab have passed resolutions in terms of clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution in relation to the above-mentioned matter and matters ancillary thereto in so far as such matters are matters enumerated in List II in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution;
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the dissolution of the existing Punjab Agricultural University and the establishment of two independent agricultural universities, namely the Haryana Agricultural University and the Punjab Agricultural University. Its main objective is to facilitate the development of agriculture in the States of Haryana and Punjab through dedicated educational, research, and extension institutions.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to enlarge the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in regard to criminal matters.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to enlarge the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in criminal matters. It specifies conditions under which appeals can be made to the Supreme Court from judgments, final orders, or sentences of High Courts in criminal proceedings.
