act_identification.act_title: THE CONTRACT LABOUR (REGULATION AND ABOLITION) ACT, 1970
act_identification.act_short_title: The Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the employment of contract labour in certain establishments and to provide for its abolition in certain circumstances and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the employment of contract labour in specific establishments and to provide for its abolition under certain circumstances. It also addresses various matters connected with contract labour.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER III REGISTRATION OF ESTABLISHMENTS EMPLOYING CONTRACT LABOUR
CHAPTER V WELFARE AND HEALTH OF CONTRACT LABOUR

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical reach, effective date, and the types of establishments and contractors it applies to, including exemptions for intermittent or casual work.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'contract labour', 'contractor', 'establishment', 'principal employer', and 'workman'.

key_sections.title: Central Advisory Board.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of a Central Advisory Contract Labour Board to advise the Central Government on matters related to the Act's administration.

key_sections.title: Registration of certain establishments.
key_sections.description: Requires principal employers of applicable establishments to register with a registering officer in the prescribed manner.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of employment of contract labour.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to prohibit the employment of contract labour in any process, operation, or work in an establishment after consultation with the relevant advisory board.

key_sections.title: Licensing of contractors.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that no contractor to whom the Act applies shall undertake work through contract labour without a valid license issued by the licensing officer.

key_sections.title: Canteens.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the appropriate Government to make rules requiring contractors to provide and maintain canteens for contract labour in certain establishments.

key_sections.title: Liability of principal employer in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Establishes that if a contractor fails to provide required amenities (like canteens, rest-rooms, first-aid), the principal employer must provide them and can recover expenses from the contractor.

key_sections.title: Responsibility for payment of wages.
key_sections.description: Makes the contractor responsible for paying wages to contract labour, with the principal employer becoming liable if the contractor defaults, and allows recovery of such payments.

key_sections.title: Contravention of provisions regarding employment of contract labour.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for contravening provisions of the Act or rules related to contract labour employment or license conditions.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Specifies that if an offence is committed by a company, both the company and persons in charge of its business are deemed guilty, with provisions for proving lack of knowledge or due diligence.

key_sections.title: Inspecting staff.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to appoint inspectors and defines their powers, including entering premises, examining persons, and seizing documents.

key_sections.title: Effect of laws and agreements inconsistent with this Act.
key_sections.description: States that the Act's provisions shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in other laws or agreements, while preserving more favourable benefits for contract labour.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the appropriate Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, detailing specific matters such rules may cover.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Obstruction of an inspector or refusal to afford facilities is punishable with imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both. Refusal to produce documents or preventing examination by an inspector carries the same penalty. Contravention of provisions regarding employment of contract labour or license conditions is punishable with imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both, with an additional fine of one hundred rupees per day for continuing contravention. Other offences for which no specific penalty is provided are punishable with imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both. For offences by companies, the company and every person in charge and responsible for its business are deemed guilty and liable to punishment.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairman and members of the Central Advisory Contract Labour Board. The State Government appoints the Chairman and members of the State Advisory Contract Labour Board. The appropriate Government appoints registering officers, licensing officers, appellate officers, and inspectors.

applies_to: Every establishment in which twenty or more workmen are employed or were employed on any day of the preceding twelve months as contract labour.
Every contractor who employs or who employed on any day of the preceding twelve months twenty or more workmen.
exemptions: Establishments in which work only of an intermittent or casual nature is performed.
special_provisions: The appropriate Government may, by notification, apply the provisions of this Act to any establishment or contractor employing such number of workmen less than twenty as may be specified.

State amendments exist for Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Union Territory Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, Rajasthan, and Gujarat, altering the threshold of workmen from 'twenty' to 'fifty' or 'forty' for applicability.
The appropriate Government may, in special cases or emergencies, exempt establishments or contractors from all or any provisions of the Act for specified periods.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the registration of establishments, licensing of contractors, and provisions for welfare and health of contract labour. Inspecting staff are appointed to monitor compliance, and principal employers and contractors are required to maintain registers and records. Penalties are prescribed for contraventions, and a system of appeals is in place.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Presidency Magistrate or a magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE PATENTS ACT, 1970

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend and consolidate the law relating to patents.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to amend and consolidate the law relating to patents in India. It aims to encourage inventions, ensure they are worked in India on a commercial scale, promote technological innovation, and ensure patent rights do not impede public health or lead to anti-competitive practices, making patented inventions available at affordable prices.

chapter_titles: OPPOSITION PROCEEDINGS TO GRANT OF PATENTS
PROVISIONS FOR SECRECY OF CERTAIN INVENTIONS
GRANT OF PATENTS AND RIGHTS CONFERRED THEREBY

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its geographical applicability to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions and interpretation.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act, such as 'assignee', 'Controller', 'invention', 'patent', 'patentee', and 'patent office'.

key_sections.title: What are not inventions.
key_sections.description: Lists specific categories of subject matter that are not considered 'inventions' within the meaning of this Act and are therefore not patentable, including frivolous inventions, discoveries of scientific principles, methods of treatment, and traditional knowledge.

key_sections.title: Persons entitled to apply for patents.
key_sections.description: Outlines who can apply for a patent, including the true and first inventor, their assignee, or the legal representative of a deceased inventor.

key_sections.title: Contents of specifications.
key_sections.description: Details the requirements for provisional and complete specifications, including describing the invention, disclosing the best method, and defining the scope of claims.

key_sections.title: Publication of applications.
key_sections.description: Governs the publication of patent applications, specifying when they are opened to the public and the rights conferred upon publication.

key_sections.title: Request for examination.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that an application will not be examined unless a request for examination is made within a prescribed period, and outlines consequences for failure to do so.

key_sections.title: Opposition to patent.
key_sections.description: Describes the process and grounds for opposing the grant of a patent (pre-grant opposition) and for opposing a patent after its grant (post-grant opposition).

key_sections.title: Secrecy directions relating to inventions relevant for defence purposes.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Controller to issue directions prohibiting or restricting the publication of information about inventions relevant for defence purposes.

key_sections.title: Residents not to apply for patents outside India without prior permission.
key_sections.description: Prohibits Indian residents from applying for patents outside India without prior permission from the Controller, unless certain conditions are met.

key_sections.title: Grant of patents.
key_sections.description: Details the conditions and process for the grant of a patent once an application is found to be in order.

key_sections.title: Rights of patentees.
key_sections.description: Defines the exclusive rights conferred upon a patentee, including preventing third parties from making, using, selling, or importing the patented product or using the patented process.

key_sections.title: Term of patent.
key_sections.description: Establishes the term of a patent as twenty years from the date of filing the application and specifies conditions under which a patent ceases to have effect.

key_sections.title: Revocation of Power patents.
key_sections.description: Outlines the grounds on which a patent may be revoked by the High Court, including wrongful obtainment, lack of novelty, obviousness, or non-disclosure of information.

key_sections.title: Compulsory licences.
key_sections.description: Provides for the grant of compulsory licences after three years from the patent grant date if public requirements are not met, the invention is not available at an affordable price, or is not worked in India.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Specifies that suits for infringement or declarations related to patents must be instituted in a district court or High Court, with provisions for transfer to the High Court if a counter-claim for revocation is made.

key_sections.title: Certain acts not to be considered as infringement.
key_sections.description: Lists specific acts, such as making or importing a patented invention for regulatory approval purposes or importation of patented products by authorized persons, that are not considered infringement.

key_sections.title: Contravention of Secrecy provisions relating to certain inventions.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment or fine, for contravening secrecy directions or applying for patents outside India without permission.

key_sections.title: Qualifications for registration as patent agents.
key_sections.description: Sets out the eligibility criteria for individuals to be registered as patent agents, including citizenship, age, educational qualifications, and passing a qualifying examination.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering various procedural and administrative matters.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for various offences. Contravention of secrecy provisions (Section 118) or applying for patents outside India without permission (Section 39) is punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both. Falsification of entries in the register (Section 119) carries similar penalties. Unauthorised claim of patent rights (Section 120) incurs a penalty up to ten lakh rupees, with a further penalty of one thousand rupees per day for continuing claims. Refusal or failure to supply information (Section 122) results in a penalty up to one lakh rupees, with a further penalty of one thousand rupees per day for continuing refusal/failure; furnishing false information incurs a penalty equal to one half percent of total sale/turnover or five crore rupees, whichever is less. Practice by non-registered patent agents (Section 123) is punishable with a penalty up to five lakh rupees, with a further penalty of one thousand rupees per day for continuing default. Failure to comply with an order of the adjudicating officer or appellate authority (Section 124B(6)) within ninety days is punishable with a fine of one lakh rupees or imprisonment up to one year, or both.

Provisions for protection of security of India (Section 157A)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the Controller of Patents, who has powers to examine applications, grant or refuse patents, and manage the patent register. Infringement of patents is addressed through civil suits in District Courts or High Courts, which can grant injunctions, damages, or accounts of profits. The Act also provides for adjudication of penalties by the Controller for certain contraventions, with an appeal mechanism to an appellate authority.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District Court and High Court (Section 104).

schedules_summary.description: Contains amendments to The Indian Patents and Designs Act, 1911. These amendments primarily involve omitting sections and clauses related to patents from the 1911 Act, updating definitions, and making consequential changes to ensure that the 1911 Act deals only with designs, while patent matters are governed by The Patents Act, 1970.

act_identification.act_title: THE STATE OF HIMACHAL PRADESH ACT, 1970
act_identification.act_short_title: The State of Himachal Pradesh Act, 1970

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of the State of Himachal Pradesh and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the establishment of the State of Himachal Pradesh. It addresses various matters connected with the formation of the new state, including its representation in legislatures, high court, financial provisions, and services.

chapter_titles:
PART II
ESTABLISHMENT OF THE STATE OF HIMACHAL PRADESH

PART III
REPRESENTATION IN THE LEGISLATURES

PART V
AUTHORISATION OF EXPENDITURE AND DISTRIBUTION OF REVENUES

PART VII
PROVISIONS AS TO SERVICES

PART VIII
LEGAL AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

key_definitions: existing Union territory of Himachal Pradesh

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as The State of Himachal Pradesh Act, 1970.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Administrator', 'appointed day', 'Election Commission', and 'existing Union territory of Himachal Pradesh'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of State of Himachal Pradesh.
key_sections.description: Establishes a new State, to be known as the State of Himachal Pradesh, comprising the territories of the existing Union territory of Himachal Pradesh from the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule to the Constitution to include Himachal Pradesh as the 18th State and omits its entry from Union Territories.

key_sections.title: Provision as to Legislative Assembly as constituted on the appointed day.
key_sections.description: Specifies the total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of Himachal Pradesh, reservation for Scheduled Castes and Tribes, and deems the existing territorial constituencies and sitting members to be part of the new State's Assembly.

key_sections.title: Delimitation of constituencies.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Election Commission to delimit parliamentary and assembly constituencies for Himachal Pradesh based on census figures, considering geographical compactness, administrative units, and reservation for Scheduled Castes and Tribes.

key_sections.title: High Court for Himachal Pradesh.
key_sections.description: Establishes a separate High Court for the State of Himachal Pradesh with its principal seat at Simla.

key_sections.title: Special provision relating to Advocates and Bar Council.
key_sections.description: Addresses the right of advocates to practice in the new High Court and amends the Advocates Act, 1961, to establish a Bar Council of Himachal Pradesh.

key_sections.title: Transfer of proceedings from High Court of Delhi to High Court of Himachal Pradesh.
key_sections.description: Outlines the transfer of pending legal proceedings from the High Court of Delhi to the High Court of Himachal Pradesh, defining jurisdiction and exceptions.

key_sections.title: Property, assets, rights, liabilities, obligations, etc.
key_sections.description: Details the transfer of property, assets, rights, liabilities, and obligations from the Union (in relation to the existing Union territory) to the State of Himachal Pradesh.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to All-India Services.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of State cadres for the Indian Administrative Service, Indian Police Service, and Indian Forest Service for Himachal Pradesh and the allocation of members to these cadres.

key_sections.title: Continuance of existing laws and their adaptation.
key_sections.description: Ensures the continuance of existing laws in the new State and provides for their adaptation and modification by the appropriate Government.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the President the power to issue orders to remove any difficulties arising in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules by notification to give effect to the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: President: Authorise expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Himachal Pradesh (Section 33)
President: Determine allowances and privileges of the Governor of Himachal Pradesh (Section 35)
President: Determine grants-in-aid of the revenues of the State of Himachal Pradesh and its share in Union duties and taxes (Section 36)
President: Remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act (Section 53)
President: Direct Judges of the High Court of Delhi to become Judges of the High Court of Himachal Pradesh (Section 22)
Central Government: Appoint the 'appointed day' (Section 2(b))
Central Government: Give directions to the Government of the State of Himachal Pradesh (Section 45)
Central Government: Make rules to give effect to the provisions of the Act (Section 54)

Central Government: Establish advisory committees (Section 44)

Election Commission: Maintain delimitation orders up-to-date (Section 18)

act_identification.act_title: THE MEDICAL TERMINATION OF PREGNANCY ACT, 1971
act_identification.act_short_title: The Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the termination of certain pregnancies by registered medical practitioners and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to legalize and regulate the termination of certain pregnancies by qualified medical practitioners, ensuring the procedure is performed safely and under specified conditions. It also addresses related matters such as the places where terminations can occur, consent requirements, and penalties for violations.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Short title, extent and commencement of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act.

key_sections.title: When pregnancies may be terminated by registered medical practitioners.
key_sections.description: Outlines the conditions under which registered medical practitioners may terminate pregnancies, including gestational limits and required medical opinions.

key_sections.title: Place where pregnancy may be terminated.
key_sections.description: Specifies the approved places where pregnancy terminations can be carried out.

key_sections.title: Sections 3 and 4 when not to apply.
key_sections.description: Details exceptions to Sections 3 and 4, particularly for life-saving terminations, and prescribes penalties for illegal terminations.

key_sections.title: Protection of privacy of a woman.
key_sections.description: Ensures the protection of privacy for women undergoing pregnancy termination.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make regulations for specific procedural aspects and information disclosure.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Provides protection for registered medical practitioners acting in good faith under the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to appoint commencement date (Section 1(3))
Central Government: Power to make rules (Section 6)
State Government or Union territory: Power to constitute a Medical Board (Section 3(2C))
State Government: Power to make regulations (Section 7)
Registered medical practitioners: Power to terminate pregnancies under specified conditions (Section 3)
District Level Committee: Power to approve places for pregnancy termination (Section 4(b))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes rigorous imprisonment for a term of not less than two years but which may extend to seven years for termination of pregnancy by a person who is not a registered medical practitioner, termination in a place other than that mentioned in section 4, or for any person being owner of a place not approved under section 4(b). Disclosure of a woman's particulars (Section 5A) is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both. Contravention of regulations (Section 7(3)) is punishable with a fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the date of commencement of the Act. State Governments or Union territories have the power to constitute Medical Boards and specify members for District Level Committees.

applies_to: Registered medical practitioners
Pregnant women
Guardians of minors or mentally ill persons
Owners of places where pregnancy termination is performed
exemptions: The provisions of section 4, and so much of the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 3 as relate to the length of the pregnancy and the opinion of not less than two registered medical practitioners, shall not apply to the termination of a pregnancy by a registered medical practitioner in a case where he is of opinion, formed in good faith, that the termination of such pregnancy is immediately necessary to save the life of the pregnant woman.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through rules made by the Central Government and regulations made by State Governments, with penalties prescribed for contraventions of its provisions and regulations.

act_identification.act_title: THE PUBLIC PREMISES (EVICTION OF UNAUTHORISED OCCUPANTS) ACT, 1971
act_identification.act_short_title: The Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the eviction of unauthorised occupants from public premises and for certain incidental matters.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes a legal framework for the eviction of individuals who are in unauthorised occupation of public premises. It empowers estate officers to issue eviction notices, order removal of unauthorised constructions, and recover rent or damages, while also providing for appeals and penalties for non-compliance.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official name, territorial application, and effective date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'estate officer', 'premises', 'public premises', 'rent', and 'unauthorised occupation'.

key_sections.title: Appointment of estate officers.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint estate officers and define their jurisdiction for the purposes of this Act.

key_sections.title: Issue of notice to show cause against order of eviction.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for estate officers to issue notices to persons in unauthorised occupation, requiring them to show cause against eviction.

key_sections.title: Eviction of unauthorised occupants.
key_sections.description: Details the process for estate officers to make and enforce eviction orders against unauthorised occupants, including the use of force if necessary.

key_sections.title: Power to remove unauthorised constructions, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants estate officers the power to remove unauthorised constructions, goods, or animals from public premises and recover costs.

key_sections.title: Order of demolition of unauthorised construction.
key_sections.description: Authorises estate officers to order the demolition of unauthorised constructions on public premises after providing notice.

key_sections.title: Power to require payment of rent or damages in respect of public premises.
key_sections.description: Enables estate officers to require payment of arrears of rent or damages for unauthorised occupation, including compound interest.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Establishes the right to appeal against orders of the estate officer to an appellate officer (District Judge or designated judicial officer).

key_sections.title: Offences and penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for unlawful occupation of public premises and re-occupation after eviction.

key_sections.title: Bar of jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Restricts the jurisdiction of courts from entertaining suits or proceedings related to eviction, removal, demolition, or recovery of dues under this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1958.

key_sections.title: Validation.
key_sections.description: Validates actions taken under the repealed 1958 Act, deeming them effective under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint estate officers, make rules, delegate powers.

Estate Officers: Issue notices, order eviction, remove unauthorised constructions, order demolition, seal unauthorised constructions, dispose of property, require payment of rent/damages, exercise powers of a civil court for inquiry, recover arrears as land revenue, obtain information.
Appellate Officer: Hear appeals, stay enforcement of orders.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Unlawfully occupying public premises is punishable with simple imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both. Re-occupying premises after eviction is punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both. A Magistrate can order summary eviction for re-occupation.

repealed_acts: The Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1958 (32 of 1958)
related_acts: Metro Railway (Operation and Maintenance) Act, 2002 (60 of 2002)
New Delhi Municipal Council Act, 1994 (44 of 1994)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints estate officers. The District Judge designates appellate officers.

applies_to: Persons in unauthorised occupation of public premises, including premises belonging to the Central Government, certain companies, corporations, universities, institutes, boards, State Governments/Union Territories, Cantonment Boards, municipal bodies in Delhi, Delhi Development Authority, and enemy property.
special_provisions: Specific provisions for premises in the National Capital Territory of Delhi.
Specific provisions for eviction from temporary occupation.
Specific provisions for eviction from residential accommodation.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Eviction orders by estate officers, use of force for eviction, removal/demolition/sealing of unauthorised constructions, recovery of rent/damages/costs as arrear of land revenue, and penalties for offences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Appellate officer (District Judge or designated judicial officer) for appeals. Magistrates for offences. Civil courts have barred jurisdiction for most matters under this Act, but may resolve property disputes referred by estate officers.

act_identification.act_title: THE COMPTROLLER AND AUDITOR-GENERAL’S (DUTIES, POWERS AND CONDITIONS OF SERVICE) ACT, 1971
act_identification.act_short_title: Comptroller and Auditor-General’s (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Union, States, and Union territories having a Legislative Assembly

act_overview.preamble: An Act to determine the conditions of service of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and to prescribe his duties and powers and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to define the conditions of service, including salary, term of office, leave, and pension, for the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India. It also prescribes the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General concerning the compilation and audit of accounts for the Union, States, and Union Territories.

chapter_titles: SALARY AND OTHER CONDITIONS OF SERVICE OF THE COMPTROLLER AND AUDITOR-GENERAL
DUTIES AND POWERS OF THE COMPTROLLER AND AUDITOR-GENERAL

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, such as 'accounts', 'appropriation accounts', 'Comptroller and Auditor-General', 'State', and 'Union'.

key_sections.title: Salary.
key_sections.description: Determines the salary of the Comptroller and Auditor-General, equating it to that of a Supreme Court Judge, with provisions for pension adjustments.

key_sections.title: Term of office.
key_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for the Comptroller and Auditor-General as six years or until attaining the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier.

key_sections.title: Pension.
key_sections.description: Outlines the pension entitlements for the Comptroller and Auditor-General upon demitting office, with various provisions based on prior service and amendments.

key_sections.title: Comptroller and Auditor-General to compile accounts of Union and States.
key_sections.description: Assigns responsibility to the Comptroller and Auditor-General for compiling accounts of the Union and States, with provisions for relieving this responsibility.

key_sections.title: Comptroller and Auditor-General to prepare and submit accounts to the President, Governors of States and Administrators of Union territories having Legislative Assemblies.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Comptroller and Auditor-General to prepare and submit annual accounts to the President, Governors, or Administrators, as applicable.

key_sections.title: General provisions relating to audit.
key_sections.description: Defines the general duties of the Comptroller and Auditor-General regarding the audit of expenditure, transactions, and accounts of the Union, States, and Union Territories.

key_sections.title: Audit of receipts and expenditure of bodies or authorities substantially financed from Union or State Revenues.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Comptroller and Auditor-General to audit bodies or authorities substantially financed by government grants or loans.

key_sections.title: Powers of Comptroller and Auditor-General in connection with audit of accounts.
key_sections.description: Grants specific powers to the Comptroller and Auditor-General for conducting audits, including inspection, requiring documents, and seeking information.

key_sections.title: Audit of Government companies and corporations.
key_sections.description: Specifies the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General regarding the audit of Government companies and corporations, in accordance with relevant laws.

key_sections.title: Laying of reports in relation to accounts of Government companies and corporations.
key_sections.description: Requires the Comptroller and Auditor-General's reports on Government companies and corporations to be laid before Parliament or State Legislatures.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act related to account maintenance.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Comptroller and Auditor-General to make regulations concerning the scope and extent of audit and principles of government accounting.

key_sections.title: Repeal.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Comptroller and Auditor-General (Conditions of Service) Act, 1953.

act_identification.act_title: THE NAVAL AND AIRCRAFT PRIZE ACT, 1971
act_identification.act_short_title: the Naval and Aircraft Prize Act, 1971

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Territory of India and localities in the temporary or permanent possession of, or occupied by, the Armed Forces of the Union

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment and procedure of Prize Courts and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The Act provides for the establishment and procedure of Prize Courts in India. It defines their jurisdiction over captured ships, aircraft, and goods during war or armed conflict, and outlines procedures for adjudication, appeals, and the disposition of prize property.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Naval and Aircraft Prize Act, 1971.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'aircraft', 'Armed Forces', 'prize', 'Prize Court', and 'ship-of-war'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Prize Courts.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to constitute Prize Courts and specifies the qualifications for their members.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of Prize Courts in prize cases.
key_sections.description: Grants exclusive jurisdiction to Prize Courts over prize cases, including those where prize is brought into India or areas occupied by Armed Forces, or where prize property is lost or cannot be brought in.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Allows persons aggrieved by a Prize Court order to appeal to the Central Government within ninety days.

key_sections.title: General powers of Prize Courts.
key_sections.description: Confers powers on Prize Courts similar to those of a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for summoning, discovery, evidence, etc.

key_sections.title: Procedure on capture of prize.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for delivering captured ships and aircraft to the Marshal of the Court or an appointed person.

key_sections.title: Prize proceedings not to apply to enemy warships and military aircraft.
key_sections.description: Exempts enemy warships, military aircraft, and other enemy-owned ships/aircraft or goods therein from prize proceedings.

key_sections.title: Capture to belong to Central Government.
key_sections.description: Declares that all prizes captured by the Armed Forces of the Union and condemned by a Prize Court shall be the exclusive property of the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Prize salvage.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions for restoration of retaken ships, goods, or aircraft belonging to Indian citizens, subject to payment of prize salvage to the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Offences in respect of prize.
key_sections.description: Defines 'prize offence' by reference to specific sections of the Navy Act, 1957, and prescribes punishment of imprisonment up to two years or fine or both.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for regulating the practice and procedure of Prize Courts and for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeals.
key_sections.description: Repeals several historical Naval Prize and Prize Courts Acts in so far as they apply in India.

key_sections.title: Savings.
key_sections.description: Contains savings clauses regarding claims to prize, existing treaties, and the Central Government's power to enter into new treaties.

powers_conferred: Central Government to constitute Prize Courts
Central Government to determine conditions of service for Prize Court members
Central Government to purchase military or victualling stores from captured foreign ships/aircraft
Central Government to make grants from prize proceeds to benevolent funds of Armed Forces
Central Government to make rules for practice and procedure of Prize Courts
Central Government to dissolve Prize Courts
Central Government to enter into treaties or conventions with foreign States
Prize Courts to have exclusive jurisdiction in prize cases
Prize Courts to take cognizance of and judicially proceed upon captures, seizures, prizes, and reprisals
Prize Courts to apply principles of International Law where no provision or insufficient provision is made
Prize Courts to have powers of a Civil Court under Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
Prize Courts to enforce orders or decrees of other Prize Courts or Central Government
Prize Courts to direct unlading, inventory, and warehousing of goods taken as prize
Prize Courts to award prize salvage and enforce payment thereof
Prize Courts to determine compensation to owners of retaken ships/aircraft used by enemy
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Every person guilty of a prize offence (as defined by reference to sections 63, 64, 65, 66 or 67 of the Navy Act, 1957) shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to two years or with fine or both.

the Prize Act, 1939

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government has the power to appoint members of Prize Courts.

applies_to: ships, vessels, aircrafts and goods that are captured or seized during a war or as a measure of reprisal during an armed conflict or in the exercise of the right of self-defence
Indian citizen (for prize salvage)
exemptions: ship-of-war or military aircraft of the enemy or any other ship or aircraft owned by the enemy whether or not registered in the territory of the enemy or goods carried therein
special_provisions: Application of principles of International Law for matters not provided for or insufficiently provided for by the Act
Right of unhindered passage may be allowed to a ship or aircraft within the territory of India on the outbreak of hostilities or an armed conflict on the basis of reciprocity

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Prize Courts exercise exclusive jurisdiction over prize cases, with powers similar to Civil Courts. Appeals can be made to the Central Government. Captured prize is delivered to a Marshal or appointed person for custody. Rules made by the Central Government regulate practice and procedure.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Prize Courts established under section 3 of this Act

act_identification.act_title: THE PREVENTION OF INSULTS TO NATIONAL HONOUR ACT, 1971
act_identification.act_short_title: Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971

act_overview.preamble: An Act to prevent insults to national honour.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to prevent insults to the Indian National Flag and the Constitution of India. It also aims to prevent disturbances to the singing of the Indian National Anthem, thereby upholding national honour.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its geographical applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Insults to Indian National Flag and Constitution of India.
key_sections.description: Defines various acts constituting insult or disrespect to the Indian National Flag or the Constitution of India in public view, and prescribes punishment.

key_sections.title: Prevention of singing of Indian National Anthem, etc.
key_sections.description: Defines the offence of intentionally preventing the singing of the Indian National Anthem or causing disturbance during such singing, and prescribes punishment.

key_sections.title: Enhanced penalty on second and subsequent convictions.
key_sections.description: Prescribes an enhanced minimum imprisonment for individuals convicted of a second or subsequent offence under Section 2 or Section 3.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 2 prescribes punishment for insults to the Indian National Flag and Constitution of India with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. Section 3 prescribes punishment for preventing the singing of the Indian National Anthem or causing disturbance with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. Section 3A mandates an enhanced penalty for second and subsequent convictions under Section 2 or 3, with imprisonment for a term not less than one year.

applies_to: Whoever
exemptions: Comments expressing disapprobation or criticism of the Constitution or of the Indian National Flag or of any measures of the Government with a view to obtain an amendment of the Constitution of India or an alteration of the Indian National Flag by lawful means

act_identification.act_title: THE CONTEMPT OF COURTS ACT, 1971

act_overview.preamble: An Act to define and limit the powers of certain courts in punishing contempts of courts and to regulate their procedure in relation thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act defines and limits the powers of certain courts in punishing contempts of courts. It also regulates the procedure to be followed in relation to such contempts.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as 'The Contempt of Courts Act, 1971' and states its applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'contempt of court', 'civil contempt', 'criminal contempt', and 'High Court'.

key_sections.title: Power of High Court to punish contempts of subordinate courts.
key_sections.description: Grants High Courts jurisdiction, powers, and authority to punish contempts of courts subordinate to them.

key_sections.title: Punishment for contempt of court.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the punishment for contempt of court, including simple imprisonment, fine, or both, and provisions for apology and detention in civil prison for civil contempt.

key_sections.title: Contempts not punishable in certain cases.
key_sections.description: States conditions under which contempts are not punishable, such as when they do not substantially interfere with justice, and allows justification by truth as a defence in public interest.

key_sections.title: Procedure where contempt is in the face of the Supreme Court or a High Court.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for dealing with contempt committed in the presence or hearing of the Supreme Court or a High Court.

key_sections.title: Cognizance of criminal contempt in other cases.
key_sections.description: Details how the Supreme Court or High Court may take action for criminal contempt not covered by Section 14, either on its own motion or on motion by the Advocate-General or other specified Law Officer.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals against orders or decisions of the High Court in contempt cases, specifying the appellate forums and time limits.

key_sections.title: Limitation for actions for contempt.
key_sections.description: Sets a limitation period of one year for initiating contempt proceedings from the date the contempt is alleged to have been committed.

key_sections.title: Repeal.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Contempt of Courts Act, 1952.

powers_conferred: Power of High Court to punish contempts of subordinate courts (Section 10)
Power of High Court to try offences committed or offenders found outside jurisdiction (Section 11)
Power of Supreme Court and High Courts to make rules (Section 23)
Power of courts to punish for contempt (Section 12)
Power of appellate court to suspend execution of punishment or order, and release appellant on bail (Section 19(2))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contempt of court (civil or criminal) is punishable with simple imprisonment for up to six months, or a fine up to two thousand rupees, or both. For civil contempt, detention in a civil prison for up to six months may be ordered if a fine is insufficient. Companies and responsible officers can also be held liable for contempt.

repealed_acts: The Contempt of Courts Act, 1952 (32 of 1952)
related_acts: Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867 (25 of 1867)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government may specify Law Officer for Union territory of Delhi or in relation to the court of a Judicial Commissioner (Section 15).

applies_to: Whole of India
Courts (Supreme Court, High Courts, subordinate courts)
Judges, magistrates or other persons acting judicially
Companies and their officers
exemptions: Nyaya Panchayats or other village courts
special_provisions: Special provisions for the Union territory of Delhi regarding Law Officer (Section 15(1)(c))
Special provisions for the Court of a Judicial Commissioner (Section 18(2), Section 19 Proviso)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Supreme Court or any High Court
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act provides procedures for taking cognizance of contempt, issuing notices, attaching property, conducting hearings (including by Benches for criminal contempt), and allowing for appeals. Punishments include imprisonment and fines.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Supreme Court, High Courts, and subordinate courts (in relation to contempt against them)

act_identification.act_title: THE MANIPUR (HILL AREAS) DISTRICT COUNCILS ACT, 1971

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of the Union territory of Manipur

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of District Councils in the Hill Areas in the Union territory of Manipur.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the establishment of District Councils in the Hill Areas of the Union territory of Manipur. It defines their constitution, functions, financial powers, and the procedures for their operation and control.

chapter_titles: PROCEDURE AND STAFF OF DISTRICT COUNCILS
FINANCE OF DISTRICT COUNCILS AND VESTING OF PROPERTY

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's official name and its geographical application to the Union territory of Manipur.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Administrator', 'autonomous district', and 'Hill Areas'.

key_sections.title: Division of Hill Areas into autonomous districts.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Administrator to divide the Hill Areas into autonomous districts and outlines powers to alter these districts.

key_sections.title: Constitution of District Councils and their composition.
key_sections.description: Establishes District Councils for each autonomous district and specifies their composition, including elected and nominated members.

key_sections.title: Disputes as to elections.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for challenging election results of District Council members through an election petition to the District Judge.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of District Councils.
key_sections.description: Declares each District Council as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and powers to acquire property and sue/be sued.

key_sections.title: Functions of District Councils.
key_sections.description: Details the various matters under the control and administration of District Councils, including property, roads, schools, markets, and land management.

key_sections.title: Powers of taxation.
key_sections.description: Grants District Councils the authority to levy specific taxes within their autonomous districts, such as taxes on professions, animals, and for maintenance of services.

key_sections.title: Council Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the 'Council Fund' for all moneys received by the District Council and provides for its management and audit.

key_sections.title: Supersession of District Council.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Administrator to supersede a District Council under certain conditions, such as incompetence or abuse of powers, and outlines the effects of such supersession.

key_sections.title: Power of Administrator to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers general and specific powers upon the Administrator to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make bye-laws.
key_sections.description: Authorizes District Councils to make bye-laws for various matters within their autonomous districts, subject to Administrator's confirmation.

powers_conferred: District Councils: Levy taxes (Section 33), fix and levy fees (Section 34), manage property, institutions, roads, schools, dispensaries, markets, water supply, soil preservation, livestock, public health, ferries, relief works, land allotment, non-reserved forests, regulation of Jhum cultivation (Section 29). Make bye-laws (Section 52).

Administrator: Divide Hill Areas into autonomous districts (Section 3), appoint date for District Council constitution (Section 4), nominate members (Section 4), delimit constituencies (Section 5), alter delimitation orders (Section 6), make rules for elections (Section 21), nominate first Chairman (Section 23), fix salary/allowances for Chairman (Section 23), determine allowances for members (Section 26), make exceptions/conditions for District Council functions (Section 29), appoint Chief Executive Officer (Section 32), approve appointment of officers/staff (Section 32), sanction tax proposals (Section 35), abolish/reduce taxes (Section 36), appoint persons for assessment/collection of taxes (Section 38), appoint appellate authority for taxes (Section 39), approve instalments for taxes/fees (Section 40), approve remission/reduction/exemption from taxes (Section 41), make rules for Council Fund management (Section 43), modify/rescind Deputy Commissioner's orders (Section 46), supersede District Council (Section 47), make rules for carrying out Act (Section 51), confirm bye-laws (Section 52).

Deputy Commissioner: Convene meetings for Chairman removal (Section 23), sanction suits against members (Section 27), give directions regarding schools (Section 46), suspend resolutions/orders of District Council (Section 46), report to Administrator for supersession (Section 47).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalty for obstruction of District Council or its officers/servants with a fine up to fifty rupees (Section 49). Penalty for member/officer/employee entering into contract with Council, deemed an offence under Section 168 of the Indian Penal Code (Section 50). Penalty for infringement of rules or bye-laws with a fine up to one hundred rupees, and for continuing breach, a further fine up to ten rupees per day, with imprisonment up to fifteen days for default of payment (Section 53).

related_acts: Government of Union Territories Act, 1963 (20 of 1963)
Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Administrator has powers to appoint the Chief Executive Officer (Section 32(1)), nominate members to District Councils (Section 4(3)), appoint the Deputy Commissioner (Section 2(e)), and nominate the first Chairman (Section 23). District Councils appoint their own officers and staff, subject to rules framed by the Administrator (Section 32(3), (4)).

applies_to: the whole of the Union territory of Manipur
Hill Areas
persons chosen by direct election on the basis of adult suffrage
members of a District Council
exemptions: mechanically propelled vehicle (from 'vehicle' definition)
body of persons (from 'person' definition)
land acquired for any public purpose or land which is a reserved forest (from land allotment by District Council)
special_provisions: Special provisions regarding the effect of certain sections (Section 3, Section 29(xvii), Section 47(1) proviso) during periods when the Hill Areas Committee is not functioning (Section 48).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Administrator has the power to make rules for regulating elections (Section 21), managing the Council Fund (Section 43(3)), and generally for carrying out the provisions of the Act (Section 51). District Councils have the power to make bye-laws (Section 52). The Deputy Commissioner can make rules regarding the notice for a resolution to remove the Chairman (Section 23(3)).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement includes recovery of taxes and fees as public dues (Section 37), recovery of moneys claimable by the Council through distress and sale of property by a Magistrate (Section 42), and penalties for obstruction, entering into contracts with the Council, and infringement of rules or bye-laws (Sections 49, 50, 53). The Deputy Commissioner and Administrator exercise control, including suspension of resolutions and supersession of District Councils (Sections 46, 47).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The court of the District Judge has jurisdiction over election disputes (Section 14) and questions regarding disqualification of members (Section 25(4)). A Magistrate has jurisdiction for the recovery of moneys claimable by the Council (Section 42).

act_identification.act_title: THE NORTH-EASTERN AREAS (REORGANISATION) ACT, 1971

legislative_details.geographical_extent: The territories comprising the North-Eastern areas of India, specifically the existing State of Assam, and the newly established States of Manipur, Tripura, Meghalaya, and Union territories of Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of the States of Manipur and Tripura and to provide for the formation of the State of Meghalaya and of the Union territories of Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh by reorganisation of the existing State of Assam and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to reorganize the North-Eastern region of India by establishing new states (Manipur, Tripura) and forming a new state (Meghalaya) and union territories (Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh) out of the existing State of Assam. It also addresses related matters concerning their legislatures, high courts, finances, and services.

chapter_titles: PART II: ESTABLISHMENT OF THE STATES OF MANIPUR AND TRIPURA AND FORMATION OF THE STATE OF MEGHALAYA AND OF THE UNION TERRITORIES OF MIZORAM AND ARUNACHAL PRADESH
PART III: REPRESENTATION IN THE LEGISLATURES
PART V: AUTHORISATION OF EXPENDITURE AND DISTRIBUTION OF REVENUES
PART VII: PROVISIONS AS TO CERTAIN CORPORATIONS
PART VIII: PROVISIONS AS TO SERVICES
PART IX: LEGAL AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment of the State of Manipur.
key_sections.description: Establishes the new State of Manipur from the existing Union territory.

key_sections.title: Formation of the State of Meghalaya.
key_sections.description: Provides for the formation of the new State of Meghalaya.

key_sections.title: Formation of the Union territory of Mizoram.
key_sections.description: Provides for the formation of the new Union territory of Mizoram.

key_sections.title: Amendment of first Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Amends the First Schedule of the Constitution to reflect the new states and union territories.

key_sections.title: Delimitation of constituencies.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for delimiting constituencies for the Legislative Assemblies of the new states.

key_sections.title: Common High Court for Assam, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Manipur and Tripura.
key_sections.description: Establishes a common High Court for several North-Eastern states, abolishing the High Court of Assam and Nagaland.

key_sections.title: Establishment of separate High Courts for the States of Meghalaya, Manipur and Tripura.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of separate High Courts for Meghalaya, Manipur, and Tripura through an amendment.

key_sections.title: Property, assets, rights, liabilities, obligations, etc., of the States of Manipur and Tripura.
key_sections.description: Details the transfer of property, assets, rights, liabilities, and obligations to the new States of Manipur and Tripura.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to All-India Services.
key_sections.description: Addresses the constitution of joint cadres and allocation of members for All-India Services in the reorganized states.

key_sections.title: Amendment of articles 210, 239A, 244, 244A, 275, 332, 371B and Fifth and Sixth Schedules to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Specifies various amendments to the Constitution necessitated by the reorganization.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the President power to issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: President: Appoint Administrator, appoint Election Commission, nominate persons to fill seats in Council of States, authorise expenditure, determine allowances and privileges of Governors, determine grants-in-aid and share in Union duties, provide for establishment of permanent bench of common High Court, determine Judges of High Courts, direct application of Acts of Parliament.

Central Government: Appoint 'appointed day', issue directions to State Electricity Board/Warehousing Corporation, determine apportionment of assets/liabilities of corporations, make orders for transfer/re-employment of employees, give directions for maintenance of previous arrangements for power/water supply, issue directions to Assam State Financial Corporation, sanction scheme for reconstitution of Financial Corporation, refer scheme to High Court Judge, issue directions to inter-State body corporate, authorise levy of tolls, make rules for apportionment of losses/profits for income-tax, fix terms for continuance of facilities in State institutions, determine initial strength and composition of joint cadres, allocate members of All-India Services, determine position in Select List, direct allocation of persons for service in Manipur/Tripura, direct members of Central Health Service, determine persons serving in existing State of Assam to serve in Meghalaya/Mizoram, give directions to State Governments/Administrator, establish Advisory Committees, specify authority for statutory functions, remove difficulties, make rules.
Election Commission: Distribute seats and delimit constituencies, maintain delimitation orders up-to-date.

Governor: Authorise expenditure, cause reports to be laid before Legislative Assembly, declare expenditure duly authorised, provide for action on reports, make modifications/adaptations to Rules of Procedure.

Chief Justice of common High Court: Consulted by President for permanent bench, appoint places for Judges/division courts to sit, nominate Judge for Financial Corporation scheme, certify proceedings for transfer, order transfer of proceedings.
State Government: Define local limits of jurisdiction of subordinate judges/munsiffs.

amended_acts: Additional Duties of Excise (Goods of Special Importance) Act, 1957
repealed_acts: High Court of Assam and Nagaland
Courts of the Judicial Commissioners for Manipur and Tripura
related_acts: Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1966

authorities_established: Gauhati High Court (common High Court for Assam, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Manipur and Tripura)
important_authorities.appointment_powers: President, Central Government, Chief Justice of common High Court, Governor.
regulatory_bodies: Bar Council of Assam, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Manipur and Tripura
Public Service Commission for the State of Assam

applies_to: Existing State of Assam
States of Manipur, Tripura, Meghalaya
Union territories of Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh
Persons serving in connection with affairs of these states/UTs
Corporations and institutions operating in these areas
exemptions: Property held by Union for Union purposes
Institutions/undertakings where expenditure met from Consolidated Fund of India
Property placed by Union at disposal of administration with ownership vesting in Union
Amounts payable by Union to existing State of Assam for internal disturbances in Mizo District
special_provisions: Provisional Legislative Assembly of Meghalaya
Special provisions for advocates and Bar Council
Special provisions for retrenchment compensation
Special provisions for income-tax
Continuance of facilities in certain State institutions
Special provisions relating to members of Central Health Service
Special provisions for Shillong cantonment and municipality
Provisions for Mizo District

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Orders and notifications by President and Central Government; directions by Central Government to State Governments and Administrator; delimitation by Election Commission; legal proceedings and transfers of cases by High Courts and other courts/tribunals; agreements between States for asset/liability apportionment, or determination by Central Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Common High Court (Gauhati High Court), High Court of Meghalaya, High Court of Manipur, High Court of Tripura, Supreme Court, District Courts and other subordinate courts/tribunals.

schedules_summary.description: Contains amendments to the Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1966, affecting parliamentary constituencies like Cachar, Diphu, Dhubri, and omitting certain assembly constituencies.
Details amendments to the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, by substituting figures and adding new Parts for Manipur, Meghalaya, and Tripura, listing their respective Scheduled Castes.

Outlines amendments to the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) (Union Territories) Order, 1951, by substituting paragraphs, omitting existing Parts, and inserting new Parts for Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh, listing their Scheduled Castes.

Specifies amendments to the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, including the omission of a paragraph for Assam and the insertion of new Parts for Manipur, Meghalaya, and Tripura, listing their Scheduled Tribes.

Contains amendments to the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) (Union Territories) Order, 1951, by substituting paragraphs, omitting existing Parts, and inserting new Parts for Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh, listing their Scheduled Tribes.

Provides for the apportionment of assets and liabilities between the States of Assam and Meghalaya, covering land, stores, taxes, loans, investments, public debt, contracts, and other financial obligations.

Lists specific institutions (e.g., training schools, hospitals, colleges, press) located in Assam, Meghalaya, or Mizoram where existing facilities are to be continued for the benefit of the people of the reorganized states and union territories.

Details amendments to the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution, concerning tribal areas, application of Acts of Parliament and State Legislatures to autonomous districts and regions in Assam, Meghalaya, and Mizoram.

Specifies amendments to the Manipur (Courts) Act, 1955, primarily replacing references to 'Chief Commissioner' and 'Judicial Commissioner' with 'State Government' and 'High Court' respectively, and omitting certain judicial provisions.

Outlines amendments to the Tripura (Courts) Order, 1950, similar to the Ninth Schedule, replacing references to 'Chief Commissioner' and 'Judicial Commissioner' with 'State Government' and 'High Court' respectively, and omitting certain judicial provisions.

act_identification.act_title: THE NORTH-EASTERN COUNCIL ACT, 1971

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the setting up of a Council for the north-eastern areas of India to be called the North-Eastern Council and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the establishment of the North-Eastern Council to serve as a regional planning body for the north-eastern areas of India. Its purpose includes formulating regional plans, prioritizing schemes benefiting multiple States, and reviewing measures for security and public order in the region.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Council' and 'north-eastern area'.

key_sections.title: Setting up and composition of the North-Eastern Council.
key_sections.description: Establishes the North-Eastern Council and specifies its composition, including Governors, Chief Ministers, and Presidential nominees.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Council.
key_sections.description: Outlines the Council's role as a regional planning body, its responsibilities in formulating and reviewing schemes, and its power to recommend measures for coordination and security.

key_sections.title: Meetings of the Council.
key_sections.description: Details the frequency and procedure for the Council's meetings, including who presides and the forwarding of proceedings.

key_sections.title: Nomination of certain officers to attend the meetings of the Council.
key_sections.description: Provides for the nomination of officers from various Central Government Ministries to assist the Council.

key_sections.title: Officers and staff of the Council.
key_sections.description: Describes the secretarial staff of the Council, their functioning, office location, and administrative expenses.

key_sections.title: Repeal.
key_sections.description: Repeals the previous North-Eastern Council Act, 1970.

powers_conferred: Council shall function as a regional planning body for the north-eastern area.
Council shall formulate specific projects and schemes for Sikkim.
Council shall review implementation of projects and schemes and recommend measures for co-ordination.
Council shall recommend the manner of execution, management, sharing of benefits, or expenditure for multi-State projects.
Council shall recommend undertaking of necessary surveys and investigation of projects.
Council shall review measures for maintenance of security and public order and recommend further measures.
Council shall have such power as may be delegated to it by the Central Government.

repealed_acts: The North-Eastern Council Act, 1970 (26 of 1970)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: President (for members, Chairman, Vice-Chairman of the Council); Central Government (for secretarial staff)

applies_to: north-eastern areas of India
States of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura
special_provisions: in case or Sikkim, the Council shall formulate specific projects and schemes for that State including the review of implementation of such projects and schemes.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Council (for rules of procedure); Central Government (delegation of powers)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Council reviews implementation of projects and schemes, recommends measures for coordination among State Governments, and reviews security and public order measures. Proceedings of meetings are forwarded to the Central Government and State Governments.

act_identification.act_title: THE DELHI SIKH GURDWARAS ACT, 1971

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of the Union territory of Delhi

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the proper management of the Sikh Gurdwaras and Gurdwara property in Delhi and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the proper management and control of Sikh Gurdwaras and their associated properties in Delhi. It establishes a management committee and outlines its powers, functions, and financial regulations, along with procedures for elections and dispute resolution.

chapter_titles: POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
SETTLEMENT OF ELECTIONS AND OTHER DISPUTES

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its application to the Union territory of Delhi, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Committee', 'Gurdwaras', 'Gurdwara property', and 'Sikh'.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of the Committee.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee as a body corporate for the management of Gurdwaras and Gurdwara property.

key_sections.title: Composition of the Committee.
key_sections.description: Details the composition of the Committee, including elected and co-opted members.

key_sections.title: Qualifications of elector.
key_sections.description: Outlines the eligibility criteria for persons to be registered as voters for Committee elections, including age, residency, and religious practices.

key_sections.title: Qualifications of member.
key_sections.description: Sets forth the qualifications and disqualifications for individuals to be chosen or co-opted as members of the Committee.

key_sections.title: Director Gurdwara Elections.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of a Director Gurdwara Elections by the Central Government to oversee electoral rolls and conduct elections.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of the Committee.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the responsibilities and duties of the Committee, including religious rites, property management, education, and social welfare.

key_sections.title: Gurdwara Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Gurdwara Fund for all receipts and income of Gurdwaras and Gurdwara property, specifying its use in trust for the Act's purposes.

key_sections.title: Prohibition regarding making of contributions for political purposes.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the Committee from contributing any amount for political purposes or to any political party.

key_sections.title: Audit of Accounts.
key_sections.description: Mandates the audit of the Committee's accounts by qualified auditors and specifies the audit process and reporting requirements.

key_sections.title: Election disputes, electoral offences etc.
key_sections.description: Applies provisions of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957, for settling disputes, corrupt practices, and electoral offences related to Committee elections.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including electoral procedures and other matters.

key_sections.title: Power of Committee to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Committee to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules for its functions, covering administrative and operational aspects.

key_sections.title: Repeal and Saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Delhi Sikh Gurdwaras (Management) Act, 1971, and includes saving provisions for continuity of appointments, assets, liabilities, and legal proceedings.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to appoint the date of commencement of the Act (Section 1(3))
Central Government: to appoint a Director Gurdwara Elections (Section 13(1))
Central Government: to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (Section 39(1))
Director Gurdwara Elections: to determine the number and extent of wards (Section 6(2))
Director Gurdwara Elections: to alter or amend orders regarding wards (Section 6(3))
Director Gurdwara Elections: to conduct elections of members (Section 11)
Director Gurdwara Elections: to publish election and co-option results (Section 12)
Director Gurdwara Elections: to summon the first meeting of elected members and the Committee (Sections 14, 15)
Director Gurdwara Elections: to summon another meeting for election of office-bearers if initial election fails (Section 16A)
Committee: to control, direct, and superintend Gurdwaras and Gurdwara property (Section 24)
Committee: to elect office bearers and members of the Executive Board (Section 16)
Committee: to appoint officers and other employees (Section 23(1))
Committee: to make regulations (Section 40(1))
Executive Board: to exercise all powers conferred on the Committee not expressly reserved (Section 21(1))
Executive Board: to constitute sub-committees (Section 20(1))
President (of the Committee): to revise orders passed by delegated authorities (Section 21(3))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: A person sitting or voting as a member of the Committee when unqualified is liable to a penalty of three hundred rupees recoverable as an arrear of land revenue (Section 10(2)). Contravention of rules made by the Central Government may be punishable with imprisonment for up to six months or with fine or with both (Section 39(3)). The Act also refers to electoral offences as per the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957 (Section 31).

repealed_acts: the Delhi Sikh Gurdwaras (Management) Act, 1971 (24 of 1971)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the Director Gurdwara Elections (Section 13(1)). The Committee has the power to appoint its officers and other employees (Section 23(1)) and auditors (Section 29(1)).

applies_to: Sikh Gurdwaras and Gurdwara property in Delhi
persons who profess the Sikh religion
members of the Committee
registered Singh Sabhas in Delhi

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee, which has control and superintendence over Gurdwaras. Elections are conducted by the Director Gurdwara Elections. Financial oversight is ensured through budget approval and mandatory audits. Disputes related to elections and other matters are settled by the District Court and High Court.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District Court in Delhi (Section 32), High Court at Delhi (Section 33)

schedules_summary.description: Contains the form of oath to be made and subscribed by members of the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee before taking their seat.

act_identification.act_title: THE MARINE PRODUCTS EXPORT DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY ACT, 1972
act_identification.act_short_title: Marine Products Export Development Authority Act, 1972

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Authority for the development of the marine products industry under the control of the Union and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish the Marine Products Export Development Authority to promote and develop the marine products industry, with a special focus on exports. It seeks to bring the marine products industry under the control of the Union for public interest.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to expediency of control by the Union.
key_sections.description: Declares the expediency of Union control over the marine products industry in public interest.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment and constitution of the Authority.
key_sections.description: Details the establishment, corporate status, and composition of the Marine Products Export Development Authority.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Authority.
key_sections.description: Outlines the duties and measures the Authority can undertake to promote the marine products industry, especially exports.

key_sections.title: Registration of fishing vessel, processing plant, etc.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration for owners of fishing vessels, processing plants, storage premises, or conveyances for marine products.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Marine Products Export Development Fund and specifies sources of credit and application of funds.

key_sections.title: Power to prohibit or control imports and exports of marine products.
