key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of an adjudicating officer by the Central Government to determine and impose penalties under the Act.

key_sections.title: Offences for failure to comply with provisions of section 25 or 26 and for failure to pay penalty.
key_sections.description: Specifies imprisonment and fine as penalties for failure to comply with restrictions on new outlets/discharges and for failure to pay imposed penalties.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for various matters concerning the Central Board and the implementation of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to make rules for matters concerning the State Board and the implementation of the Act within its jurisdiction.

powers_conferred: Central Board: Advise Central Government on water pollution, coordinate State Boards, provide technical assistance, conduct research, organize training, run mass media programs, perform State Board functions (if directed), collect data, lay down standards for streams/wells, plan nationwide programs, establish/recognize laboratories (Section 16).

State Board: Plan comprehensive programs for pollution control, advise State Government, collect/disseminate information, conduct research, collaborate with Central Board, inspect sewage/trade effluents, lay down effluent standards, evolve treatment methods, advise on industry location, make/vary/revoke orders for pollution control, establish/recognize laboratories (Section 17).

Boards (Central/State): Give directions to persons, officers, or authorities (Section 18, 33A), make applications to courts for restraining apprehended pollution (Section 33), carry out certain works if conditions are not met (Section 30), borrow money (Section 37A).
State Government: Restrict the application of the Act to certain areas (Section 19), supersede State Board (Section 62), make rules (Section 64).
Central Government: Supersede the Central Board and Joint Boards (Section 61), make rules (Section 63), appoint adjudicating officers (Section 45B).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties:
The Act prescribes penalties for various contraventions:
- Failure to comply with directions to furnish information (Section 20): Penalty not less than ten thousand rupees, up to fifteen lakh rupees, with an additional penalty of ten thousand rupees per day for continuing contravention (Section 41).
- Failure to comply with emergency orders (Section 32(1)(c)), court directions (Section 33(2)), or Board directions (Section 33A): Penalty not less than ten thousand rupees, up to fifteen lakh rupees, with an additional penalty of ten thousand rupees per day for continuing contravention (Section 41A).
- Destroying Board property, obstructing officers, damaging works, failing to furnish required information, making false statements for consent: Penalty not less than ten thousand rupees, up to fifteen lakh rupees, with an additional penalty of ten thousand rupees per day for continuing contravention (Section 42).
- Contravention of prohibition on using streams/wells for polluting matter (Section 24): Penalty not less than ten thousand rupees, up to fifteen lakh rupees, with an additional penalty of ten thousand rupees per day for continuing contravention (Section 43).
- Altering or interfering with monitoring devices for consent under Section 25 or 26: Penalty not less than ten thousand rupees, up to fifteen lakh rupees (Section 44).
- Contravention of any provision or order/direction for which no specific penalty is provided: Penalty not less than ten thousand rupees, up to fifteen lakh rupees, with an additional penalty up to ten thousand rupees per day for continuing contravention (Section 45A).
- Failure to comply with provisions of Section 25 or 26 (new outlets/discharges): Imprisonment for 1.5 to 6 years and fine; additional fine of fifty thousand rupees per day for continuing failure after conviction. If failure continues beyond one year, imprisonment for 2 to 7 years and fine (Section 45E(1) & (2)).
- Failure to pay imposed penalty or additional penalty within ninety days: Imprisonment up to three years, or fine up to twice the penalty, or both (Section 45E(3)).
- Contravention by Government Department: Head of Department liable to pay penalty equal to one month of basic salary, unless proven without knowledge or due diligence exercised. Other officers also liable for neglect (Section 48).

Central Government nominates Chairman, officials, non-officials, company representatives, and appoints member-secretary for the Central Board (Section 3). It also nominates Chairman for Joint Boards (Section 14), appoints Government analysts (Section 53(1)), and adjudicating officers (Section 45B).
State Government nominates Chairman, officials, local authority members, non-officials, company representatives, and appoints member-secretary for the State Board (Section 4). It also appoints Government analysts (Section 53(2)).
Central Board or State Board may appoint officers, employees (Section 12(3)), and consulting engineers (Section 12(4)).

Joint Boards can be constituted by agreement between two or more contiguous States, or by the Central Government and one or more contiguous States for Union territories (Section 13).
For the State of Jammu and Kashmir (now Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh), provisions of corresponding law apply to search or seizure under Section 23(2).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the powers and functions of the Central and State Boards, including their ability to obtain information, take samples, inspect premises, issue directions, and impose restrictions on polluting activities. It also includes provisions for emergency measures, applications to courts for restraining pollution, and a system of penalties and adjudicating officers for non-compliance.

any other offence, which under the provisions of that Code, may be tried along with such offence

schedules_summary.description: Lists various enactments (e.g., Income Tax Act, Customs Act, Foreign Exchange Regulation Act) to whose offences Chapter XXXVI of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, shall not apply.

act_identification.act_title: THE UNIVERSITY OF HYDERABAD ACT, 1974

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of the State of Andhra Pradesh

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate a teaching University in the State of Andhra Pradesh and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The Act establishes a teaching University in the State of Andhra Pradesh. Its primary purpose is to disseminate and advance knowledge through instructional and research facilities, with a special focus on integrated courses in humanities and science, and inter-disciplinary studies.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that its commencement date will be appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act and its Statutes.

key_sections.title: The University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the University of Hyderabad as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, located in Andhra Pradesh.

key_sections.title: Objects.
key_sections.description: Outlines the University's objectives, including knowledge dissemination, research, integrated courses, and inter-disciplinary studies.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers of the University, such as granting degrees, instituting posts, establishing campuses, and managing property.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Specifies the geographical extent of the University's jurisdiction as the whole of the State of Andhra Pradesh.

key_sections.title: University open to all classes, castes and creed.
key_sections.description: Declares the University open to all persons regardless of sex, race, creed, caste, or class, prohibiting religious tests, while allowing special provisions for weaker sections.

key_sections.title: Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor, outlining powers of inspection, inquiry, and annulment of University proceedings.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the official officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellors, Deans, Registrar, and Finance Officer.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities of the University, such as the Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, and Boards of Schools.

key_sections.title: Statutes.
key_sections.description: Details the matters for which the Statutes of the University may provide, covering constitution of authorities, appointments, conditions of service, and academic matters.

key_sections.title: Statutes how made.
key_sections.description: Describes the process for making, amending, or repealing Statutes, including the role of the Executive Council and the Visitor's approval.

key_sections.title: Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Ordinances may provide, such as student admission, courses of study, examinations, and conditions of award.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees.
key_sections.description: Mandates written contracts for employees and provides for arbitration in disputes between the University and employees.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make provisions to remove difficulties in implementing the Act for a period of three years from commencement.

powers_conferred: To provide for instructions in such branches of learning as the University may, from time to time, determine and to make provision for research and for the advancement and dissemination of knowledge (Section 5(1))

To grant, subject to such conditions as the University may determine, diplomas or certificates to, and confer degrees and other academic distinctions on the basis of examinations, evaluation or any other method of testing, on persons, and to withdraw any such diplomas, certificates, degrees or other academic distinctions for good and sufficient cause (Section 5(2))

To institute Principalships, Professorships, Readerships, Lecturerships, and other teaching or academic posts required by the University and to appoint persons to such Principalships, Professorships, Readerships, Lecturerships or other posts (Section 5(6))
To create administrative, ministerial and other posts and to make appointments thereto (Section 5(10))
To co-operate or collaborate or associate with any other University or authority or institution of higher learning (Section 5(11))
To establish such campuses, special centres, specialised laboratories or other units for research and instruction (Section 5(12))
To institute and award fellowships, scholarships, studentships, medals and prizes (Section 5(13))
To establish and maintain Colleges, Institutions and Halls (Section 5(14))
To declare a College an Institution or a Department as an autonomous College or Institution or Department (Section 5(16))
To regulate and enforce discipline among the employees and students of the University (Section 5(21))
To acquire, hold, manage and dispose of any property, movable or immovable, including trust and endowment properties (Section 5(23))
To borrow, with the approval of the Central Government, on the security of the property of the University, money for the purposes of the University (Section 5(24))
Visitor shall have the right to cause an inspection or inquiry to be made of the University (Section 8(2))
Visitor may, by order in writing, annul any proceeding of the University which is not in conformity with this Act, the Statutes or Ordinances (Section 8(9))
Vice-Chancellor may exercise any power conferred on any authority of the University if immediate action is necessary (Section 12(3))
Executive Council shall have the management and administration of the revenue and property of the University and the conduct of all administrative affairs (Statute 13(1))
Executive Council to create teaching and academic posts, determine emoluments and conditions of service (Statute 13(i))
Executive Council to appoint Professors, Readers, Lecturers and other academic staff (Statute 13(ii))

Academic Council to exercise general supervision over the academic policies of the University and to give directions regarding methods of instruction, evaluation of research or improvements in academic standards (Statute 15(a))
Vice-Chancellor to have all powers relating to discipline and disciplinary action in relation to students (Statute 31(1))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for disciplinary action against employees, including suspension, censure, withholding of increment, and removal for misconduct or other specified reasons (Statute 4(4), Statute 27, Statute 28). It also outlines procedures for disciplinary cases against students, including removal from rolls, debarment from examinations, fines, and cancellation of results (Section 31, Statute 31). Degrees, diplomas, certificates, and other academic distinctions can be withdrawn for good and sufficient cause (Section 5(2), Statute 30).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and members of the Planning Board. The Executive Council appoints Pro-Vice-Chancellors (on Vice-Chancellor's recommendation), Librarians, Professors, Readers, Lecturers, other academic staff, Principals, and administrative/ministerial posts. The Vice-Chancellor appoints Deans of Schools.

applies_to: Persons of either sex and of whatever race, creed, caste, or class
Employees of the University
Students of the University
exemptions: No test whatsoever of religious belief or profession shall be adopted or imposed to entitle a person to be admitted as a teacher or student, or to hold any office, or to graduate, or to enjoy any privilege.
special_provisions: Special provisions for admission of students of the weaker sections of the people and, in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Section 7 Proviso)
Special arrangements in respect of women students (Section 5(20), Statute 13(xv))

Transitional provisions for the appointment of the first Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, and the constitution of the first Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council (Section 41)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Executive Council, with Visitor's approval, makes, amends, or repeals Statutes. The Vice-Chancellor makes the first Ordinances, which can then be amended by the Executive Council. Authorities of the University may make Regulations consistent with the Act, Statutes, and Ordinances.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Vice-Chancellor is responsible for ensuring the observance of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations. The Visitor has powers of inspection, inquiry, and annulment of University proceedings. Disputes between the University and employees or students regarding disciplinary action are referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration. Employees and students have a right to appeal to the Executive Council against decisions of officers or authorities.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil Courts are explicitly excluded from jurisdiction over matters decided by the Arbitration Tribunal concerning employee disputes (Section 30(2)) and over the Visitor's decision regarding disqualifications for membership in University authorities (Statute 35(2)).

schedules_summary.description: Contains the initial Statutes of the University, detailing the Vice-Chancellor's role, powers, and duties, appointment and functions of other officers (Pro-Vice-Chancellors, Registrar, Finance Officer, Deans, Heads of Departments, Deans of Students' Welfare, Proctors, Librarians), constitution and powers of authorities (Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Planning Board, Schools of Studies, Boards of Studies, Finance Committee, Selection Committees), terms and conditions of service for teachers, procedures for removal of staff, conferment and withdrawal of degrees, student discipline, and general provisions for meetings, resignations, disqualifications, and delegation of powers.

act_identification.act_title: THE INTEREST-TAX ACT, 1974

act_overview.preamble: An Act to impose a special tax on interest in certain cases.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to impose a special tax on interest in certain cases, specifically on interest accruing or arising to credit institutions. It provides for the charge, computation, assessment, and collection of this interest-tax.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Interest-tax Act, 1974, and specifies its territorial application to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'assessee', 'chargeable interest', 'credit institution', and 'interest'.

key_sections.title: Tax authorities.
key_sections.description: Designates income-tax authorities as interest-tax authorities and outlines their jurisdiction and control.

key_sections.title: Charge of tax.
key_sections.description: Imposes interest-tax on scheduled banks and credit institutions at specified rates on their chargeable interest for assessment years, with provisions for cessation of tax after 31st March, 2000.

key_sections.title: Scope of chargeable interest.
key_sections.description: Defines chargeable interest as the total amount of interest accruing or arising to a credit institution, with specific exclusions and provisions for bad or doubtful debts.

key_sections.title: Computation of chargeable interest.
key_sections.description: Details the method for computing chargeable interest, allowing deductions for bad debts and specifying periods for which interest is not taken into account.

key_sections.title: Return of chargeable interest.
key_sections.description: Mandates credit institutions to furnish returns of chargeable interest in the prescribed form and manner, and allows for revised returns.

key_sections.title: Assessment.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Assessing Officer to assess chargeable interest and interest-tax payable, including best judgment assessments in cases of non-compliance.

key_sections.title: Self-assessment.
key_sections.description: Requires assessees to pay interest-tax and any associated interest before furnishing their return, with provisions for default.

key_sections.title: Advance payment of interest-tax.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that interest-tax is payable in advance in three instalments during the financial year, with specified due dates and amounts.

key_sections.title: Penalty for concealment of chargeable interest.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for concealing particulars of chargeable interest or furnishing inaccurate particulars.

key_sections.title: Appeals to the Commissioner (Appeals).
key_sections.description: Allows assessees to appeal against assessments, penalties, or other orders of the Assessing Officer to the Commissioner (Appeals).

key_sections.title: Appeals to Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals to the Appellate Tribunal against orders of the Commissioner or Commissioner (Appeals).

key_sections.title: Application of provisions of Income-tax Act.
key_sections.description: Specifies that certain sections and schedules of the Income-tax Act and Income-tax (Certificate Proceedings) Rules, 1962, apply with modifications to this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Board of Direct Taxes the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including prescribing forms and procedures.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to exempt credit institutions or categories of interest from interest-tax, subject to the recommendation of the Reserve Bank of India.

powers_conferred: Assessing Officer to serve notices and assess chargeable interest (Section 8, 10)
Commissioner (Appeals) to hear and determine appeals (Section 15)
Appellate Tribunal to hear and make orders on appeals (Section 16)
Commissioner to revise orders prejudicial to revenue (Section 19)
Commissioner to revise orders not prejudicial to assessee (Section 20)
Board to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 27)
Central Government to exempt credit institutions or interest from tax (Section 28)
Central Government to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act (Section 29)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties include a sum not less than, but not exceeding three times, the interest-tax sought to be evaded for concealment of chargeable interest (Section 13). Failure to comply with notices incurs a penalty of not less than one thousand rupees, up to twenty-five thousand rupees (Section 23). False statements, wilful attempt to evade tax, and abetment of false returns are punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term of not less than three months but which may extend to seven years and with fine (Sections 24, 25, 26).

related_acts: Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963 (54 of 1963)
Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)

applies_to: every scheduled bank
every credit institution
assessee
exemptions: chargeable interest accruing or arising after the 31st day of March, 2000
interest on loans and advances made to other credit institutions or to any co-operative society engaged in carrying on the business of banking
interest which accrues or arises before the 1st day of August, 1974
interest which accrues or arises during the period commencing on the 1st day of April, 1985 and ending with the 30th day of September, 1991
any credit institution or any class of credit institutions or any interest on any category of loans or advances (by Central Government notification)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Board (Central Board of Direct Taxes), subject to the control of the Central Government
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through assessment by the Assessing Officer, self-assessment, advance payment of tax, and provisions for interest, penalties, and prosecution for non-compliance or evasion. Appeals can be made to the Commissioner (Appeals) and the Appellate Tribunal. The Act also applies relevant provisions of the Income-tax Act.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court or Supreme Court (in relation to orders and appeals)

act_identification.act_title: THE OIL INDUSTRY (DEVELOPMENT) ACT, 1974

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Board for the development of oil industry and for that purpose to levy a duty of excise on crude oil and natural gas and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to establish a Board for the development of the oil industry. It also provides for the levy of a duty of excise on crude oil and natural gas to fund this development and addresses related matters.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II THE OIL INDUSTRY DEVELOPMENT BOARD
CHAPTER III FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT
CHAPTER IV CONTROL BY THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Board', 'oil industry', 'crude oil', and 'natural gas'.

key_sections.title: Establishment and constitution of the Board.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of the Oil Industry Development Board as a body corporate and outlines its composition and appointment of members.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Board.
key_sections.description: Details the Board's functions, including rendering financial and other assistance for the development of the oil industry through grants, loans, guarantees, and underwriting.

key_sections.title: Special provisions for enforcement of claims by the Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedures for the Board to enforce its claims against defaulting oil industrial concerns or persons, including applying to court for sale of property, injunctions, or transfer of management.

key_sections.title: Power of Board to appoint Directors of oil industrial concern.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board the power to appoint Directors to an oil industrial concern when its management is taken over, overriding provisions of the Companies Act, 1956 regarding director qualifications.

key_sections.title: Duties of excise.
key_sections.description: Establishes the levy and collection of a cess in the form of a duty of excise on crude oil and natural gas produced in India, specifying rates and application of the Central Excises and Salt Act, 1944.

key_sections.title: Oil Industry Development Fund.
key_sections.description: Provides for the formation of the Oil Industry Development Fund, detailing the sources of its funds and how it shall be applied for the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for persons who fail to produce records, furnish false information, or obstruct officers of the Board or Central Government.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other enactments.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, specifying various matters that such rules may cover.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint members, Chairman, and Secretary of the Board (Section 3, 5)
Board to render financial and other assistance for oil industry development (Section 6)
Board to call for repayment of assistance before agreed period under certain conditions (Section 8)
Board to apply to court for enforcement of claims, including sale of property, injunctions, or transfer of management (Section 9)
Board to appoint Directors of an oil industrial concern when its management is taken over (Section 10)
Central Government to require persons in oil industry to maintain and produce books, accounts, and records (Section 21)
Central Government to issue directions to the Board for efficient administration of the Act (Section 22)
Central Government to sanction prosecution for offences under the Act (Section 27)
Central Government to dissolve the Board in public interest (Section 29)
Central Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (Section 31)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person failing to produce books/records, furnishing false information, or obstructing officers is punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both (Section 23). Other contraventions of the Act or rules are punishable with imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both (Section 24). Offences by companies hold both the company and persons in charge liable, with provisions for directors, managers, etc. (Section 25).

related_acts: The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (4 of 1882)
The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908)
The Central Excises and Salt Act, 1944 (1 of 1944)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairman and members of the Board, and the Secretary to the Board. The Board may appoint consultants, other officers, and employees. The Board may also appoint Directors of an oil industrial concern when its management is taken over.

applies_to: Oil industrial concerns
Other persons engaged in any activity referred to in clause (k) of section 2 (oil industry activities)
Persons engaged in oil industry

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Board can enforce claims through court orders (attachment, sale of property, injunctions, transfer of management). The Central Government can issue directions to the Board and require persons in the oil industry to maintain and produce records. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance and obstruction.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court or the Court of Judicial Commissioner, or any civil court empowered by notification. For offences, no court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class.

schedules_summary.description: Specifies the items (Crude oil, Natural gas) on which duty of excise is levied under Section 15(1) and the maximum rates at which this duty may be collected.

act_identification.act_title: THE CONSERVATION OF FOREIGN EXCHANGE AND PREVENTION OF SMUGGLING ACTIVITIES ACT, 1974
act_identification.act_short_title: THE CONSERVATION OF FOREIGN EXCHANGE AND PREVENTION OF SMUGGLING ACTIVITIES ACT, 1974

act_overview.preamble:
An Act to provide for preventive detention in certain cases for the purposes of conservation and augmentation of Foreign Exchange and prevention of smuggling activities and for matters connected therewith.

WHEREAS violations of foreign exchange regulations and smuggling activities are having an
increasingly deleterious effect on the national economy and thereby a serious adverse effect on the
security of the State;

AND WHEREAS having regard to the persons by whom and the manner in which such activities or

violations are organised and carried on, and having regard to the fact that in certain areas which are highly
vulnerable to smuggling, smuggling activities of a considerable magnitude are clandestinely organised
and carried on, it is necessary for the effective prevention of such activities and violations to provide for
detention of persons concerned in any manner therewith;
act_overview.purpose: To provide for preventive detention to conserve and augment foreign exchange and prevent smuggling activities. It addresses the adverse effects of foreign exchange violations and smuggling on the national economy and security by enabling the detention of persons involved in such activities.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application across India, and its effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'detention order', and 'smuggling'.

key_sections.title: Power to make orders detaining certain persons.
key_sections.description: Grants power to Central or State Governments or their empowered officers to issue detention orders to prevent individuals from engaging in activities prejudicial to foreign exchange conservation or smuggling.

key_sections.title: Grounds of detention severable.
key_sections.description: States that a detention order made on multiple grounds shall be deemed separate on each ground, preventing invalidation if some grounds are found vague or invalid.

key_sections.title: Powers in relation to absconding persons.
key_sections.description: Outlines powers of the appropriate Government to deal with persons absconding or concealing themselves to avoid detention, including reporting to magistrates and directing appearance.

key_sections.title: Advisory Boards.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of Advisory Boards to review detention cases and report on the sufficiency of cause for detention, with provisions for confirmation or revocation of orders.

key_sections.title: Cases in which and circumstances under which persons may be detained for periods longer than three months without obtaining the opinion of Advisory Board.
key_sections.description: Provides for extended detention periods without Advisory Board opinion in specific cases related to smuggling in highly vulnerable areas, subject to Central Government declaration.

key_sections.title: Maximum period of detention.
key_sections.description: Sets the maximum period for which a person may be detained under the Act, varying based on whether Section 9 provisions apply.

key_sections.title: Revocation of detention orders.
key_sections.description: Allows for the revocation or modification of detention orders by the Central Government or State Government, and clarifies that revocation does not bar a new order.

key_sections.title: Temporary release of persons detained.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central or State Government to direct temporary release of detained persons, with or without conditions, and specifies penalties for non-compliance.

key_sections.title: Special provisions for dealing with emergency.
key_sections.description: Introduces special provisions for detention during a Proclamation of Emergency, allowing for detention without disclosing grounds or providing representation in certain circumstances.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Grants immunity from legal proceedings to the Central Government, State Government, and individuals for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Maintenance of Internal Security (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974, and causes its amendments to the Maintenance of Internal Security Act, 1971, to cease effect.

powers_conferred: Power to make orders detaining certain persons to the Central Government, State Government, or specially empowered officers (Section 3).
Power to regulate place and conditions of detention to the appropriate Government (Section 5).
Power to make a report to a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class regarding absconding persons and direct their appearance to the appropriate Government (Section 7).
Power to constitute Advisory Boards to the Central Government and each State Government (Section 8(a)).
Power to confirm or revoke detention orders based on Advisory Board reports to the appropriate Government (Section 8(f)).
Power to make a declaration for detention longer than three months without Advisory Board opinion in specific cases to the Central Government or empowered officers (Section 9).
Power to revoke or modify detention orders to the appropriate Government (Section 10 proviso, Section 11).
Power to direct temporary release of detained persons and cancel such release to the Central Government or State Government (Section 12).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Failure to comply with a direction to appear under Section 7(1)(b) is punishable with imprisonment up to one year or fine or both. Failure to surrender after temporary release under Section 12(3) is punishable with imprisonment up to two years or fine or both. Failure to fulfill conditions of release or bond under Section 12(5) results in forfeiture of the bond and liability to pay the penalty.

repealed_acts: The Maintenance of Internal Security (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974 (11 of 1974)
related_acts: Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1988
Jammu and Kashmir Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Ordinance, 1988 (J & K Ordinance 1 of 1988)
Maintenance of Internal Security Act, 1971 (20 of 1971)
Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of Smuggling Activities (Amendment) Act, 1976
Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of Smuggling Activities (Amendment) Act, 1975

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government and each State Government have the power to constitute Advisory Boards and appoint their Chairman and two other persons.

applies_to: whole of India
any person (including a foreigner)
special_provisions: For the State of Jammu and Kashmir, a reference to a law not in force there shall be construed as a reference to the corresponding law in force in that State (Section 2(g)).
Special provisions for dealing with emergency during a Proclamation of Emergency (Section 12A).
Provisions for detention longer than three months without Advisory Board opinion in specific circumstances related to smuggling in 'area highly vulnerable to smuggling' (Section 9).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Detention orders are made by the Central or State Government or their empowered officers. These orders are executed in India following the manner for warrants of arrest under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. The appropriate Government regulates the place and conditions of detention. Absconding persons can be reported to Magistrates. Advisory Boards review detention cases, and the appropriate Government confirms or revokes orders based on their reports. Temporary release of detained persons can be directed by the Central or State Government.

act_identification.act_title: THE EAST PUNJAB URBAN RENT RESTRICTION ACT (EXTENSION TO CHANDIGARH) ACT, 1974
act_identification.act_short_title: East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act (Extension to Chandigarh) Act, 1974

act_overview.preamble: An Act to extend the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, to the Union territory of Chandigarh.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to extend the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, to the Union territory of Chandigarh. It also provides for specific modifications to the extended Act's application in Chandigarh and validates actions previously taken under it.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act (Extension to Chandigarh) Act, 1974.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines 'the Act' as the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, as it was in force in certain areas before 1st November 1966.

key_sections.title: Extension of East Punjab Act III of 1949 to Chandigarh.
key_sections.description: Extends the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, with specified modifications, to the Union territory of Chandigarh, with retrospective effect from 4th November 1972.

key_sections.title: Validation and saving.
key_sections.description: Validates past actions taken under the extended Act as if this Act had been in force, and provides a saving clause against offences committed before its commencement.

powers_conferred: Central Government to declare other areas as urban for the purposes of the Act (by notification).
Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

amended_acts: East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949
related_acts: East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949 (East Punjab Act III of 1949)
Capital of Punjab (Development and Regulation) Act, 1952 (Punjab Act XXVII of 1952)

applies_to: Union territory of Chandigarh
all the urban areas in the Union territory of Chandigarh

schedules_summary.description: Contains modifications to the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, including substituting 'State Government' with 'Central Government', defining the Act's extent to urban areas of Chandigarh, adding a definition for 'notification', modifying the definition of 'urban area', and substituting the power to make rules to the Central Government.

act_identification.act_title: THE SICK TEXTILE UNDERTAKINGS (NATIONALISATION) ACT, 1974
act_identification.date_of_commencement: 1st April, 1974 (retrospective for most provisions); 21st December, 1974 (for sections 32 and 33)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the acquisition and transfer of the sick textile undertakings, and the right, title and interest of the owners in respect of the sick textile undertakings, specified in the First Schedule with a view to re-organising and rehabilitating such sick textile undertakings so as to subserve the interests of the general public by the augmentation of the production and distribution, at fair prices, of different verieties of cloth and yarn, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of sick textile undertakings and the rights of their owners, with the aim of re-organising and rehabilitating them. This is intended to serve the public interest by increasing the production and distribution of cloth and yarn at fair prices.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II ACQUISITION OF THE RIGHTS OF OWNERS OF SICK TEXTILE UNDERTAKINGS
CHAPTER IV MANAGEMENT, ETC., OF SICK TEXTILE UNDERTAKINGS
CHAPTER V PROVISIONS RELATING TO EMPLOYEES OF SICK TEXTILE UNDERTAKINGS

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement dates for different provisions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Acquisition of rights of owners in respect of sick textile undertakings.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that sick textile undertakings and the rights of their owners are transferred to and vested in the Central Government, and subsequently in the National Textile Corporation.

key_sections.title: General effect of vesting.
key_sections.description: Details what is included in the vested undertakings (assets, rights, liabilities) and how existing encumbrances are discharged.

key_sections.title: Owner to be liable for certain prior liabilities.
key_sections.description: Specifies which liabilities remain with the original owner and which are assumed by the Central Government/National Textile Corporation.

act_identification.act_title: An Act to give effect to the Convention on offences and certain other acts committed on board aircraft.

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of the Central Government dealing with Civil Aviation

act_overview.preamble: An Act to give effect to the Convention on offences and certain other acts committed on board aircraft. WHEREAS a Convention on offences and certain other acts committed on board aircraft was on the Fourteenth day of September, 1963, signed at Tokyo; AND WHEREAS it is expedient that India should accede to the said Convention and should make provisions for giving effect thereto; BE it enacted by Parliament in the Twenty-sixth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to give effect to the Tokyo Convention on offences and certain other acts committed on board aircraft. It aims to enable India to accede to the Convention and make necessary provisions for its implementation.

key_definitions: country or to the territorial limits thereof

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Act's short title, territorial extent, and the date of its commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'aircraft', 'commander', 'Convention country', and 'Tokyo Convention'.

key_sections.title: Application of criminal law to aircraft.
key_sections.description: Extends the application of Indian criminal law to acts or omissions taking place on Indian registered aircraft while in flight outside India.

key_sections.title: Provisions as to Extradition Act.
key_sections.description: Deems aircraft registered in a Convention country to be within that country's jurisdiction for the purpose of applying the Extradition Act, 1962.

key_sections.title: Powers of commander of aircraft.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to the commander of an aircraft to take reasonable measures, including restraint, against persons jeopardizing safety or committing offences on board.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Clarifies the jurisdiction of Indian courts for offences and other acts committed on board an aircraft, deeming offences committed in flight to have occurred where the offender may be found.

key_sections.title: Provisions as to evidence in connection with aircraft.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which depositions made outside India can be admissible as evidence in Indian courts for offences committed on aircraft.

key_sections.title: Provisions as to documentary evidence.
key_sections.description: States that certain publications and messages from the Ministry of Civil Aviation shall be evidence of the matters appearing therein in legal proceedings.

key_sections.title: Power to apply the provisions of Act with modifications to certain aircraft.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to apply the Act's provisions with modifications to certain types of aircraft by notification.

key_sections.title: Contracting parties to Convention.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to certify, by notification, who are the contracting parties to the Tokyo Convention and the extent of their adherence.

key_sections.title: Power to treat certain aircraft to be registered in Convention country.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to direct that certain aircraft be treated as registered in a Convention country for the purposes of this Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint the date of commencement of the Act (Section 1(3)).
Central Government: To apply provisions of the Act with modifications to certain aircraft (Section 9).
Central Government: To certify contracting parties to the Tokyo Convention (Section 10).
Central Government: To treat certain aircraft as registered in a Convention country (Section 11).
Commander of aircraft: To take reasonable measures, including restraint, against persons jeopardizing safety or committing offences (Section 5(1)).
Commander of aircraft: To require assistance from other crew members and request assistance from passengers for restraint (Section 5(2)).
Commander of aircraft: To disembark or deliver persons in certain circumstances (Section 5(5)).
Crew members or passengers: To take reasonable preventive measures without authorization when immediately necessary to protect safety (Section 5(3)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any act or omission taking place on board an Indian registered aircraft while in flight elsewhere than in or over India which, if taking place in India, would constitute an offence under any law in force in India, shall constitute that offence (Section 3(1)). A commander of an aircraft who, without reasonable cause, fails to comply with reporting requirements regarding disembarkation or delivery of persons shall be liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding one thousand rupees (Section 5(6)).

applies_to: Indian registered aircraft
aircraft in flight
persons on board aircraft
exemptions: military aircraft
aircraft belonging to, or exclusively employed in the service of, the State
special_provisions: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, direct that all or any of the provisions of this Act shall apply to an aircraft referred to in sub-clause (B) of clause (e) of sub-section (1) of section 2, subject to such modifications as may be specified in the notification.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the application of Indian criminal law to offences committed on aircraft, the exercise of powers by aircraft commanders to maintain order and safety, and the jurisdiction of Indian courts. It also includes provisions for the admissibility of evidence.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: a court in India; any court having jurisdiction in respect of piracy committed on the high seas

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Offences include holding/giving false declarations, carrying on business without registration, false representation as a registered dealer, failure to comply with registration cancellation provisions, failure to submit returns or submitting false returns, collecting tax illegally, failure to keep accounts, failure to issue cash memos, maintaining incorrect accounts, neglecting to furnish information, refusing to comply with requirements, obstructing officers, failure to comply with goods vehicle requirements, and aiding/abetting. Penalties for these offences can include rigorous imprisonment for up to six months or fine, or both, with daily fines for continuing offences (up to Rs. 200 or Rs. 300 for wilful offences). Specific penalties include up to twice the tax amount or Rs. 2000 for failure to furnish returns or pay tax, and up to two and a half times the tax avoided for concealment of sales, inaccurate particulars, or false representations. Wrongful collection of tax can incur a penalty of up to two and a half times the tax wrongly collected.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official name of the Act, its territorial application to the whole of India, and that its commencement date will be notified by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Duties specified in the Schedules to be levied.
key_sections.description: States that customs duties will be levied at the rates specified in the First and Second Schedules under the Customs Act, 1962.

key_sections.title: Levy of additional duty equal to excise duty, sales tax, local taxes and other charges.
key_sections.description: Provides for the levy of additional duties on imported articles, equivalent to domestic excise duty, sales tax, value added tax, local taxes, and goods and services tax compensation cess, to ensure a level playing field for domestic products.

key_sections.title: Levy of duty where standard rate and preferential rate are specified.
key_sections.description: Outlines the conditions under which a preferential rate of customs duty may be levied, typically for goods originating from a notified preferential area, and grants the Central Government power to alter these rates.

key_sections.title: Levy of a lower rate of duty under a trade agreement.
key_sections.description: Enables the Central Government to charge a lower rate of duty on articles from foreign countries or territories as per trade agreements, and to make rules for determining the origin of such articles.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to levy protective duties in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to impose protective duties on imported goods, based on recommendations from the Tariff Commission, to safeguard domestic industries.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to apply safefuard measures.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to impose safeguard measures, including safeguard duty or tariff-rate quotas, on imported articles causing or threatening serious injury to domestic industry, with specific exemptions for developing countries and export-oriented units.

key_sections.title: Countervailing duty on subsidized articles.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to impose a countervailing duty on imported articles that have benefited from subsidies in the exporting country, to offset the impact on domestic industry, and includes provisions for circumvention and absorption.

key_sections.title: Anti-dumping duty on dumped articles.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to impose anti-dumping duty on articles imported at less than their normal value, causing injury to domestic industry, and includes provisions for circumvention, absorption, and retrospective application.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Establishes the right to appeal against determinations or reviews related to subsidy, dumping, or safeguard duties to the Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Rules to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Mandates that all rules made under the Act must be laid before each House of Parliament for a specified period, allowing for parliamentary review and modification or annulment.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to amend First Schedule.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to amend the First Schedule in the public interest, provided such amendments do not alter the specified rates of customs duties, and requires parliamentary oversight.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Indian Tariff Act, 1934, and the Indian Tariff (Amendment) Act, 1949, while saving actions taken under those repealed Acts if consistent with the current Act.

key_sections.title: Consequential amendment of Act 52 of 1962.
key_sections.description: Amends the Customs Act, 1962, by substituting references to the 'Indian Tariff Act, 1934' with 'Customs Tariff Act, 1975'.

powers_conferred: Central Government: appoint date of commencement (S.1)
Central Government: specify rate of additional duty (S.3)

Central Government: direct an amendment of the First Schedule to be made so as to provide for discontinuance of, or increase or decrease in, the preferential rate (S.4)
Central Government: make rules for determining if any article is the produce or manufacture of such foreign country or territory under a trade agreement (S.5)
Central Government: decide if any trade agreement applies to any country or territory, or whether it has ceased to apply to India or any foreign country or territory (S.5)
Central Government: impose protective duties on any goods imported into India (S.6)
Central Government: increase or reduce protective duties (S.7)

Central Government: amend the First Schedule (S.11A)

regulatory_bodies: Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The provisions of the Customs Act, 1962 (52 of 1962) and the rules and regulations made thereunder, including those relating to drawbacks, refunds and exemption from duties, apply to duties chargeable under this Act.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (for appeals)

Details the Export Tariff, specifying rates of duties on goods exported from India.

act_identification.act_title: THE SMUGGLERS AND FOREIGN EXCHANGE MANIPULATORS (FORFEITURE OF PROPERTY) ACT, 1976

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to provide for the forfeiture of illegally acquired properties of smugglers and foreign exchange manipulators. Its main objective is to effectively prevent smuggling activities and foreign exchange manipulations by depriving individuals involved in such activities of their ill-gotten gains, which are often held through various means including in the names of relatives and associates.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Act's name, territorial application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Application.
key_sections.description: Defines the categories of persons to whom the Act applies, including those convicted of smuggling/FERA offenses, detainees, their relatives, and associates.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms like "Appellate Tribunal," "competent authority," and "illegally acquired property."

key_sections.title: Prohibition of holding illegally acquired property.
key_sections.description: Prohibits persons covered by the Act from holding illegally acquired property, making such property liable for forfeiture.

key_sections.title: Competent authority.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to authorize officers to act as competent authorities for the Act's functions.

key_sections.title: Notice of forfeiture.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for the competent authority to issue a show-cause notice for forfeiture of suspected illegally acquired properties.

key_sections.title: Forfeiture of property in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Details the process for the competent authority to declare property as illegally acquired and forfeited to the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Burden of proof.
key_sections.description: Places the burden of proving that property is not illegally acquired on the person affected.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of an Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals against orders made under the Act.

key_sections.title: Bar of jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: States that civil courts have no jurisdiction over matters determined by the Appellate Tribunal or competent authority under this Act.

key_sections.title: Competent authority and Appellate Tribunal to have powers of civil court.
key_sections.description: Grants civil court powers to the competent authority and Appellate Tribunal for certain matters.

key_sections.title: Power to take possession.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the competent authority to take possession of forfeited property.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the Act's provisions override inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_sections.title: Provisions of the Act not to apply to certain properties held in trust.
key_sections.description: Specifies exemptions for certain properties held by public, religious, or charitable trusts.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to implement the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Authorise officers as competent authority (S.5), constitute Appellate Tribunal (S.12), make rules (S.26).

Competent Authority: Serve notice of forfeiture (S.6), record finding on illegally acquired property (S.7), declare forfeiture (S.7), give option to pay fine (S.9), revoke forfeiture (S.9), take possession (S.19), require officers to exercise powers (S.18), require information (S.16), powers of civil court (S.15), rectify mistakes (S.20).
Appellate Tribunal: Hear appeals (S.12), confirm, modify or set aside orders (S.12), regulate its own procedure (S.12), powers of civil court (S.15), rectify mistakes (S.20).

Officers of Income-tax, Customs, Central Excise, Enforcement: Furnish information suo motu (S.16), assist competent authority and Appellate Tribunal (S.17), conduct inquiry/investigation/survey (S.18).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: This Act does not define new offences but provides for forfeiture of property based on convictions under other acts. Section 9 prescribes a fine equal to one and one-fifth times the value of the unproven part of income/earnings/assets, which can be paid in lieu of forfeiture.

repealed_acts: The Smugglers and Foreign Exchange Manipulators (Forfeiture of Property) Ordinance, 1975 (20 of 1975)
related_acts: Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of Smuggling Activities Act, 1974 (52 of 1974)
Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (61 of 1985)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint competent authorities and the Chairman and other members of the Appellate Tribunal.

applies_to: Every person convicted under the Sea Customs Act, 1878 or the Customs Act, 1962 for an offence involving goods exceeding one lakh rupees.
Every person convicted under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947 or the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973 for an offence involving an amount or value exceeding one lakh rupees.
Every person with subsequent convictions under the aforementioned Acts.

Every person in respect of whom an order of detention has been made under the Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of Smuggling Activities Act, 1974 (subject to provisos regarding revocation or setting aside of the order).
Every person who is a relative of a person referred to in the above categories.
Every associate of a person referred to in the above categories.

Any holder of property which was at any time previously held by a person referred to in the above categories, unless the present holder or any intermediate holder was a transferee in good faith for adequate consideration.
exemptions: Property held by a trust or an institution created or established wholly for public, religious or charitable purposes if such property has been held by them from a date prior to the commencement of this Act, or is wholly traceable to property held by them prior to the commencement of this Act.
special_provisions: Vide Notification No. S.O. 3912 (E), dated 30th October, 2019, this Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Competent Authority serves notices, conducts inquiries, determines illegally acquired property, orders forfeiture, and takes possession. The Appellate Tribunal hears appeals against the Competent Authority's orders. Various officers from Customs, Central Excise, Income-tax, and Enforcement Departments assist the Competent Authority and Appellate Tribunal.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil courts are barred from jurisdiction in matters determined by the Appellate Tribunal or Competent Authority under this Act. The Appellate Tribunal serves as the appellate body.

act_identification.act_title: THE SALES PROMOTION EMPLOYEES (CONDITIONS OF SERVICE) ACT, 1976
act_identification.act_short_title: The Sales Promotion Employees (Conditions of Service) Act, 1976

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate certain conditions of service of sales promotion employees in certain establishments.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the conditions of service for sales promotion employees. It covers aspects such as leave, appointment letters, and the application of other labour laws to these employees, ensuring their welfare and fair treatment.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical reach, effective date, and initial application to the pharmaceutical industry.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'establishment', 'notified industry', and 'sales promotion employees'.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to declare certain industries to be notified industries.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government authority to declare industries as 'notified industries' for the Act's application.

key_sections.title: Leave.
key_sections.description: Outlines the provisions for earned leave, medical leave, and cash compensation for sales promotion employees.

key_sections.title: Issue of appointment letter.
key_sections.description: Mandates employers to furnish appointment letters to sales promotion employees in a prescribed form.

key_sections.title: Application of certain Acts to sales promotion employees.
key_sections.description: Extends the applicability of several other labour laws (e.g., Workmen’s Compensation, Industrial Disputes, Minimum Wages) to sales promotion employees.

key_sections.title: Maintenance of registers.
key_sections.description: Requires employers to maintain prescribed registers and documents related to sales promotion employees.

key_sections.title: Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of Inspectors by the State Government and outlines their powers to ensure compliance with the Act.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for employers who contravene provisions of sections 4, 5, 7, or rules made under the Act.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Details the liability of companies and their officers for offences committed under the Act.

key_sections.title: Effect of laws and agreements inconsistent with this Act.
key_sections.description: States that the Act's provisions prevail over inconsistent laws or agreements, while allowing for more favourable benefits to employees.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government to declare certain industries to be notified industries (Section 3)
Central Government to apply provisions to other establishments (Section 1(5))
Central Government to make rules (Section 12)
State Government to appoint Inspectors (Section 8(1))
Inspectors to require information, enter establishments, examine persons, make copies of documents (Section 8(2))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Employers contravening sections 4, 5, 7, or rules made under the Act are punishable with a fine up to one thousand rupees. Offences by companies also incur liability for the company and responsible individuals. The State Amendment for Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh introduces compounding of offences with a payment not exceeding fifty thousand rupees.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government has the power to appoint Inspectors for the purposes of this Act (Section 8(1)).

applies_to: every establishment engaged in pharmaceutical industry
any other establishment engaged in any notified industry
sales promotion employees
exemptions: Sales promotion employees employed or engaged in a supervisory capacity drawing wages exceeding sixteen hundred rupees per mensem (Section 2(d)(i))
Sales promotion employees employed or engaged mainly in a managerial or administrative capacity (Section 2(d)(ii))
Sales promotion employees whose wages exceed the ceiling limit for application of other Acts (Section 6(7)(b))
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different States for the Act to come into force (Section 1(3))
Special provisions for compounding of offences for the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh (Section 9A)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through Inspectors appointed by the State Government, who have powers to inspect establishments, require information, and examine persons. Contraventions are subject to penalties, and offences by companies are also addressed. The Act specifies which courts can take cognizance of offences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act (Section 11(1)).

act_identification.act_title: THE ELECTION LAWS (EXTENSION TO SIKKIM) ACT, 1976
act_identification.act_short_title: The Election Laws (Extension to Sikkim) Act, 1976

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the extension of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Representation of the People Act, 1951, to the State of Sikkim.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to extend the application of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Representation of the People Act, 1951, to the State of Sikkim. It also makes necessary amendments to these Acts to accommodate the specific electoral requirements and representation of Sikkim.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its deemed commencement date.

key_sections.title: Extension and amendment of election laws.
key_sections.description: Extends the Acts mentioned in the Schedule to the State of Sikkim and specifies that they shall be amended as per the Schedule. It also provides for construction of references to laws or functionaries not in existence in Sikkim.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Election Laws (Extension to Sikkim) Ordinance, 1975, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

key_sections.section_number: Section 7A (of The Representation of the People Act, 1950)
key_sections.title: Total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of Sikkim and Assembly constituencies.
key_sections.description: Specifies the total number of seats (32) in the Legislative Assembly of Sikkim and that each constituency shall be a single member constituency, maintaining the extent and reservation of seats as before the Constitution (Thirty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1975.

key_sections.section_number: Section 25A (of The Representation of the People Act, 1950)
key_sections.title: Conditions of registration as elector in Sangha constituency in Sikkim.
key_sections.description: Defines the conditions for registration as an elector in the Sangha constituency in Sikkim, limiting it to Sanghas belonging to recognised monasteries.

key_sections.section_number: Section 5A (of The Representation of the People Act, 1951)
key_sections.title: Qualifications for membership of Legislative Assembly of Sikkim.
key_sections.description: Prescribes specific qualifications for membership in the Legislative Assembly of Sikkim based on origin (Bhutia-Lepcha, Nepali, Scheduled Castes) and for the Sangha constituency.

key_sections.section_number: Section 12A (of The Representation of the People Act, 1951)
key_sections.title: Notification for election to fill the seat allotted to the State of Sikkim in the Council of States.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for the President to call for the first election to fill the seat allotted to Sikkim in the Council of States.

key_sections.section_number: Section 14A (of The Representation of the People Act, 1951)
key_sections.title: Notification for electing the representative of the State of Sikkim to the existing House of the People.
key_sections.description: Details the process for the Election Commission to call for the election of a representative from Sikkim to the House of the People.

key_sections.section_number: Section 33 (of The Representation of the People Act, 1951)
key_sections.title: Nomination paper for election to the Legislative Assembly of Sikkim.
key_sections.description: Amends the requirements for nomination papers for elections to the Legislative Assembly of Sikkim, including specific proposer and seconder requirements for reserved seats.

powers_conferred: Central Government to decide as to who a corresponding functionary will be if not in existence in Sikkim.
Election Commission to direct the manner of preparation or revision of electoral rolls for Sangha constituency in consultation with the Government of Sikkim.
President to issue notification for election to fill the seat allotted to Sikkim in the Council of States.
Election Commission to call upon members of the Legislative Assembly of Sikkim to elect a representative to the House of the People.
