Qualifications for membership based on Scheduled Castes in Sikkim

schedules_summary.description: Contains specific amendments to THE REPRESENTATION OF THE PEOPLE ACT, 1950 and THE REPRESENTATION OF THE PEOPLE ACT, 1951, primarily concerning the State of Sikkim. These amendments include provisions for the total number of seats and constituencies in the Legislative Assembly of Sikkim, conditions for elector registration in the Sangha constituency, qualifications for membership in the Legislative Assembly based on origin and caste, and procedures for elections to the Council of States and House of the People for Sikkim.

act_identification.act_title: THE REGIONAL RURAL BANKS ACT, 1976

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the incorporation, regulation and winding up of Regional Rural Banks with a view to developing the rural economy by providing, for the purpose of development of agriculture, trade, commerce, industry and other productive activities in the rural areas, credit and other facilities, particularly to the small and marginal farmers, agricultural labourers, artisans and small entrepreneurs, and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: To provide for the incorporation, regulation, and winding up of Regional Rural Banks. Its main objective is to develop the rural economy by offering credit and other facilities for agriculture, trade, commerce, industry, and other productive activities in rural areas, specifically targeting small and marginal farmers, agricultural labourers, artisans, and small entrepreneurs.

chapter_titles: INCORPORATION AND CAPITAL OF REGIONAL RURAL BANKS
BUSINESS OF A REGIONAL RURAL BANK

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, and its deemed commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Board', 'Chairman', 'Regional Rural Bank', and 'Sponsor Bank'.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Regional Rural Banks.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to establish Regional Rural Banks as body corporates with perpetual succession, upon request from a Sponsor Bank.

key_sections.title: Authorised capital.
key_sections.description: Sets the authorised capital for each Regional Rural Bank and allows the Central Government to increase or reduce it.

key_sections.title: Issued capital.
key_sections.description: Determines the initial issued capital and specifies the subscription proportions by the Central Government, State Government, and Sponsor Bank.

key_sections.title: Management.
key_sections.description: Vests the general superintendence, direction, and management of a Regional Rural Bank in its Board of directors.

key_sections.title: Board of directors.
key_sections.description: Outlines the composition of the Board of directors, including nominated and elected members.

key_sections.title: Chairman.
key_sections.description: Details the appointment, term, duties, and removal of the Chairman of a Regional Rural Bank by the Sponsor Bank.

key_sections.title: Business which a Regional Rural Bank may transact.
key_sections.description: Defines the banking business and specific types of loans and advances that a Regional Rural Bank may undertake, particularly for rural development.

key_sections.title: Amalgamation of Regional Rural Banks.
key_sections.description: Provides for the amalgamation of two or more Regional Rural Banks by the Central Government in public interest, specifying the process and effects.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to give directions.
key_sections.description: States that Regional Rural Banks shall be guided by Central Government directions on policy matters involving public interest.

key_sections.title: Inspection, audit and scrutiny by the Sponsor Bank.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Sponsor Bank to monitor, inspect, audit, and scrutinize the Regional Rural Banks it sponsors.

key_sections.title: Obligations as to fidelity and secrecy.
key_sections.description: Requires Regional Rural Banks to observe fidelity and secrecy customary among bankers, with directors and employees making a declaration.

key_sections.title: Bar to liquidation of Regional Rural Bank.
key_sections.description: Prohibits liquidation of a Regional Rural Bank except by order of the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Act to override the provisions of other laws.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over conflicting provisions in other laws or contracts.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To establish Regional Rural Banks, specify local limits, increase/reduce authorised capital, fix issued capital, raise/reduce shareholding limits, appoint officers to the Board, approve Chairman appointments/removals, determine employee remuneration, specify accounting year, cause reports to be laid before Parliament, amalgamate Regional Rural Banks, give policy directions, order liquidation, make rules, and remove difficulties.

Sponsor Bank: To request establishment of Regional Rural Banks, aid and assist Regional Rural Banks, appoint/terminate/remove the Chairman, send officers on deputation, and conduct inspection, audit, and scrutiny of sponsored Regional Rural Banks.
Board of Directors: To exercise general superintendence, direction, and management of the Regional Rural Bank, constitute committees, and make regulations.
Regional Rural Bank: To transact banking business, grant loans and advances, and appoint officers and other employees.

related_acts: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981 (61 of 1981)
Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has powers to appoint officers to the Board and approve Chairman appointments. The Sponsor Bank appoints the Chairman.

applies_to: Regional Rural Banks
Small and marginal farmers
Agricultural labourers
Artisans
Small entrepreneurs

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government gives policy directions. The Sponsor Bank monitors, inspects, audits, and scrutinizes Regional Rural Banks. The Board of directors manages the affairs and business.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the form for the declaration of fidelity and secrecy to be made by directors, members of committees, officers, employees, or auditors of a Regional Rural Bank.

act_identification.act_title: THE BONDED LABOUR SYSTEM (ABOLITION) ACT, 1976

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the abolition of bonded labour system with a view to preventing the economic and physical exploitation of the weaker sections of the people and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The primary purpose of this Act is to abolish the bonded labour system throughout India. It aims to prevent the economic and physical exploitation of the weaker sections of society. The Act also addresses various matters connected with or incidental to the abolition of bonded labour.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II: ABOLITION OF BONDED LABOUR SYSTEM
CHAPTER III: EXTINGUISHMENT OF LIABILITY TO REPAY BONDED DEBT
CHAPTER VI: OFFENCES AND PROCEDURE FOR TRIAL

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, and its deemed commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'advance', 'bonded debt', 'bonded labour system', and 'nominal wages'.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other enactments.

key_sections.title: Abolition of bonded labour system.
key_sections.description: Declares the abolition of the bonded labour system and frees all bonded labourers from their obligations upon the Act's commencement.

key_sections.title: Agreement, custom, etc., to be void.
key_sections.description: Renders void any custom, tradition, contract, or agreement that requires a person to render service as a bonded labourer.

key_sections.title: Liability to repay bonded debt to stand extinguished.
key_sections.description: Extinguishes all obligations of a bonded labourer to repay bonded debts and provides for the restoration of property.

key_sections.title: Creditor not to accept payment against extinguished debt.
key_sections.description: Prohibits creditors from accepting payments against bonded debts that have been extinguished by the Act and prescribes punishment for contravention.

key_sections.title: Authorities who may be specified for implementing the provisions of this Act.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to confer powers and duties on District Magistrates for implementing the Act.

key_sections.title: Vigilance Committees.
key_sections.description: Mandates State Governments to constitute Vigilance Committees at district and sub-divisional levels and specifies their composition.

key_sections.title: Functions of Vigilance Committees.
key_sections.description: Outlines the duties of Vigilance Committees, including advising authorities, rehabilitating freed bonded labourers, and coordinating credit.

key_sections.title: Punishment for enforcement of bonded labour.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for compelling any person to render bonded labour after the Act's commencement.

key_sections.title: Offences to be tried by Executive Magistrates.
key_sections.description: Allows State Governments to confer powers of Judicial Magistrates on Executive Magistrates for the trial of offences under this Act.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of civil courts barred.
key_sections.description: Bars the jurisdiction of civil courts in matters to which the provisions of this Act apply.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Ordinance, 1975, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under the Ordinance.

powers_conferred: State Government may confer powers and impose duties on a District Magistrate (Section 10)
District Magistrate may specify officers subordinate to him (Section 10)
State Government shall constitute Vigilance Committees (Section 13)
Vigilance Committee may authorise one of its members to defend a suit (Section 14(2))
State Government may confer powers of a Judicial Magistrate on an Executive Magistrate (Section 21(1))
Central Government may make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act (Section 26(1))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes punishment for various offences, including accepting payment against extinguished bonded debt (imprisonment up to three years and fine), enforcement of bonded labour (imprisonment up to three years and fine up to two thousand rupees), advancement of bonded debt (imprisonment up to three years and fine up to two thousand rupees), extracting bonded labour under the bonded labour system (imprisonment up to three years and fine up to two thousand rupees, with payment to the labourer from the fine), and omission or failure to restore property to bonded labourers (imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both, with payment to the labourer from the fine). Abetment of any offence under the Act is also punishable with the same punishment as the abetted offence.

repealed_acts: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Ordinance, 1975 (17 of 1975)
related_acts: Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 (37 of 1970)
Inter-State Migrant Workmen (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1979 (30 of 1979)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The District Magistrate or Sub-Divisional Magistrate, as applicable, nominates the Chairman and other members (belonging to Scheduled Castes/Tribes, social workers, representatives of financial institutions) for Vigilance Committees. The State Government nominates representatives for official or non-official agencies in the district/sub-division.

applies_to: every bonded labourer
any person who makes advances under the bonded labour system
any person who compels another to render bonded labour
creditors

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through District Magistrates and officers specified by them, who are tasked with ensuring proper implementation, promoting the welfare of freed bonded labourers, and inquiring into and eradicating forced labour. Vigilance Committees are constituted to advise, rehabilitate, coordinate credit, and monitor offences. Offences under the Act are cognizable and bailable and are tried by Executive Magistrates, who may be conferred powers of Judicial Magistrates.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Executive Magistrates (for trial of offences); Civil courts (for executing orders of prescribed authority and determining mesne profits, but their jurisdiction is otherwise barred for matters covered by this Act).

act_identification.act_title: THE EQUAL REMUNERATION ACT, 1976

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Twenty-seventh Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the payment of equal remuneration to men and women workers and for the prevention of discrimination, on the ground of sex, against women in the matter of employment and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to ensure equal remuneration for men and women workers for the same work or work of a similar nature. It also aims to prevent discrimination against women in employment on the ground of sex and addresses related matters.

chapter_titles: PAYMENT OF REMUNERATION AT EQUAL RATES TO MEN AND WOMEN WORKERS AND OTHER MATTERS

key_definitions: same work or work of a similar nature

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent (whole of India), and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'employer', 'remuneration', and 'same work or work of a similar nature'.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in any other law, award, agreement, or contract of service.

key_sections.title: Duty of employer to pay equal remuneration to men and women workers for same work or work of a similar nature.
key_sections.description: Mandates employers to pay equal remuneration to men and women workers for the same work or work of a similar nature and prohibits reduction of remuneration to comply with this provision.

key_sections.title: No discrimination to be made while recruiting men and women workers.
key_sections.description: Prohibits discrimination on the ground of sex against women in recruitment and subsequent conditions of service, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Advisory Committee.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to constitute Advisory Committees to advise on increasing employment opportunities for women.

key_sections.title: Power of appropriate Government to appoint authorities for hearing and deciding claims and complaints.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the appropriate Government to appoint officers to hear and decide complaints regarding contravention of the Act and claims for non-payment of equal wages, granting them powers of a Civil Court.

key_sections.title: Duty of employers to maintain registers.
key_sections.description: Requires employers to maintain prescribed registers and documents related to their workers.

key_sections.title: Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Allows the appropriate Government to appoint Inspectors to investigate compliance with the Act, granting them powers of entry, examination, and evidence collection.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for employers who fail to maintain records, produce documents, give evidence, or contravene provisions regarding equal pay and non-discrimination.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Specifies liability for offences committed by companies, extending to persons in charge and officers, with provisions for proving lack of knowledge or due diligence.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply in certain special cases.
key_sections.description: Outlines specific situations where the Act does not apply, such as special treatment for women under other laws, in connection with childbirth, or terms related to retirement, marriage, or death.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Equal Remuneration Ordinance, 1975, while saving actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Appropriate Government to constitute Advisory Committees for increasing employment opportunities for women (Section 6(1))
Appropriate Government to issue directions regarding employment of women workers (Section 6(5))
Appropriate Government to appoint authorities for hearing and deciding claims and complaints (Section 7(1))
Appropriate Government to define local limits for authorities (Section 7(1))
Authorities appointed under Section 7 to hear and decide complaints and claims (Section 7(1))
Authorities appointed under Section 7 to decide if works are of same or similar nature (Section 7(3))
Authorities appointed under Section 7 to direct payment of wages or steps to prevent contravention (Section 7(4))
Authorities appointed under Section 7 to exercise powers of a Civil Court for taking evidence, enforcing attendance, and compelling document production (Section 7(5))
Appropriate Government to specify appellate authority for orders made under Section 7 (Section 7(6))
Appropriate Government to appoint Inspectors for investigating compliance (Section 9(1))
Appropriate Government to define local limits for Inspectors (Section 9(1))
Inspectors to enter premises, require documents, take evidence, examine persons, and make copies/extracts (Section 9(3))
Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions (Section 13(1))
Central Government to give directions to a State Government for execution of the Act (Section 14)
Appropriate Government to make a declaration that remuneration differences are based on factors other than sex (Section 16)
Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act (Section 17)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 10 prescribes penalties for employers. Offences include omitting or failing to maintain registers or documents, omitting or failing to produce documents, omitting or refusing to give evidence or information, making recruitment in contravention of the Act, making unequal payments of remuneration, making discrimination between men and women workers, or failing to carry out directions from the appropriate Government. Penalties range from simple imprisonment up to one month or fine up to ten thousand rupees (for record-keeping offences) to fine not less than ten thousand rupees but up to twenty thousand rupees or imprisonment not less than three months but up to one year (for discrimination/unequal pay offences), with higher imprisonment for subsequent offences. Failure to produce documents or give information to an Inspector carries a fine up to five hundred rupees. Section 11 details liability for offences committed by companies.

repealed_acts: The Equal Remuneration Ordinance, 1975 (12 of 1975)

authorities_established: authorities for hearing and deciding claims and complaints
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The appropriate Government has the power to appoint members of the Advisory Committee, authorities for hearing and deciding claims and complaints, and Inspectors.

applies_to: men and women workers
employers
establishments or employments
exemptions: Employment of women in work prohibited or restricted by law (Section 5)
Priority or reservation for Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes, ex-servicemen, retrenched employees or any other class or category of persons in recruitment (Section 5 proviso)
Cases affecting terms and conditions of a woman’s employment in complying with requirements of any law giving special treatment to women (Section 15(a))
Special treatment accorded to women in connection with birth or expected birth of a child (Section 15(b)(i))
Special treatment accorded to women in connection with terms and conditions relating to retirement, marriage or death or any provision made in connection therewith (Section 15(b)(ii))
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for commencement of the Act for different establishments or employments (Section 1(3))
State Amendment for Uttar Pradesh regarding composition of offences (Section 11A)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the appointment of Inspectors to investigate compliance, and authorities to hear and decide complaints and claims. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance, and the Central Government can issue directions to State Governments for execution.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE LEVY SUGAR PRICE EQUALISATION FUND ACT, 1976
act_identification.act_short_title: Levy Sugar Price Equalisation Fund Act, 1976

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment, in the interest of the general public, of a fund to ensure that the price of levy sugar may be uniform throughout India and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Levy Sugar Price Equalisation Fund. Its primary objective is to ensure a uniform price for levy sugar across India, serving the general public interest, and addresses related matters.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'controlled price', 'excess realisation', and 'producer'.

key_sections.title: Levy Sugar Price Equalisation Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Fund and outlines the types of amounts to be credited to it, including excess realisations by producers.

key_sections.title: Determination of questions as to making of excess realisations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to decide questions regarding whether a producer has made excess realisations on levy sugar.

key_sections.title: Right of buyer to claim refund.
key_sections.description: Grants buyers of levy sugar the right to claim a refund from the Fund for excess realisations made by producers or dealers, subject to certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Fund to vest in the Central Government.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that unclaimed money in the Fund vests in the Central Government and how it shall be utilized, while preserving the right to claim refunds.

key_sections.title: Power of entry, search and seizure.
key_sections.description: Confers powers on specified authorities to enter, search, and seize documents related to levy sugar if a contravention of the Act is suspected.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to recover excess realisations as arrears of land revenue.
key_sections.description: Enables the Central Government to recover any default in crediting excess realisations or interest to the Fund as arrears of land revenue.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for producers who default in crediting excess realisations or fail to maintain records or furnish information.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, covering various procedural and administrative matters.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to appoint commencement date (Section 1(3))
Central Government: to decide questions as to making of excess realisations (Section 4)
Central Government: to administer the Fund (Section 3(7))
Central Government: to make refunds from the Fund (Section 6(3))
Central Government: to utilise unclaimed money in the Fund (Section 8(1))
Central Government: to maintain or specify authority to maintain accounts for the Fund (Section 8(3))
Central Government: to require producers to maintain accounts and furnish information (Section 9)
Central Government: to authorise persons for entry, search, and seizure (Section 10(1))
Central Government: to recover excess realisations as arrears of land revenue (Section 11)
Central Government: to dissolve the Fund (Section 12)
Central Government: to remove difficulties by order (Section 14)
Central Government: to make rules for carrying out the Act (Section 16)
Authority specified by Central Government: to authorise entry and search (Section 10(1))
Person authorised: to seize accounts, books, registers, or other documents (Section 10(2))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Producers are punishable with imprisonment for up to two years, or a fine up to five thousand rupees, or both, for default in crediting excess realisations or interest to the Fund, or for failing to maintain/produce records, or furnishing incorrect/false information. No court shall take cognizance of an offence except on a complaint by the Central Government or its authorized officer/authority.

related_acts: Defence and Internal Security of India Rules, 1971
Levy Sugar Price Equalisation Fund (Amendment) Act, 1984 (54 of 1984)

applies_to: producers
buyers of levy sugar
exemptions: State of Jammu and Kashmir

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government administers the Fund, determines questions regarding excess realisations, recovers unpaid amounts as arrears of land revenue, and has powers of entry, search, and seizure. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance, with cognizance taken only upon complaint by the Central Government or its authorized officer.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Act except on the complaint in writing made by the Central Government or by any officer or authority authorized, in writing, by that Government in this behalf.

act_identification.act_title: THE DEPARTMENTALISATION OF UNION ACCOUNTS (TRANSFER OF PERSONNEL) ACT, 1976
act_identification.act_short_title: The Departmentalisation of Union Accounts (Transfer of Personnel) Act, 1976

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the transfer of officers serving in the Indian Audit and Accounts Department to any Ministry, Department or office of the Central Government for facilitating the efficient discharge by such Ministry, Department or office of the responsibility in connection with compiling the accounts thereof.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to facilitate the transfer of officers and employees from the Indian Audit and Accounts Department to various Ministries, Departments, or offices of the Central Government. This transfer aims to enable these government entities to efficiently discharge their responsibility for compiling their own accounts.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Transfer of officers and employees of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.
key_sections.description: Details the conditions and process for transferring officers and employees from the Indian Audit and Accounts Department to Ministries, Departments, or offices of the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Departmentalisation of Union Accounts (Transfer of Personnel) Ordinance, 1976, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To transfer officers and employees of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department to any Ministry, Department or office of the Central Government (Section 2(1)).
Central Government: To establish one or more Advisory Committees for assisting in the transfer of officers and employees (Section 2(2)).

repealed_acts: The Departmentalisation of Union Accounts (Transfer of Personnel) Ordinance, 1976 (2 of 1976)
related_acts: Comptroller and Auditor-General’s (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 (56 of 1971)

authorities_established: Advisory Committees (established by the Central Government)
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government has the power to establish Advisory Committees and specify designations for transferred officers/employees.

applies_to: Officers and employees serving in the Indian Audit and Accounts Department
exemptions: Officers or employees who intimate unwillingness to be transferred, unless the Central Government deems it necessary in the public interest (Section 2(1) proviso).
The right of any officer or employee to resign or retire from service in accordance with applicable rules (Section 2(1) second proviso).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through orders issued by the Central Government for the transfer of personnel, based on the advice of established Advisory Committees.

act_identification.act_title: THE HIGH COURT AT PATNA (ESTABLISHMENT OF A PERMANENT BENCH AT RANCHI) ACT, 1976
act_identification.act_short_title: High Court at Patna (Establishment of a Permanent Bench at Ranchi) Act, 1976

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Districts of Hazaribagh, Giridih, Dhanbad, Ranchi, Palamau and Singhbhum (for the bench's jurisdiction)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of a permanent bench of the High Court at Patna at Ranchi.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the establishment of a permanent bench of the High Court at Patna at Ranchi. It specifies the number of judges to sit at Ranchi and defines the districts over which this bench will exercise jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The High Court at Patna (Establishment of a Permanent Bench at Ranchi) Act, 1976'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of a permanent bench of High Court at Patna at Ranchi.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of a permanent bench of the High Court at Patna at Ranchi, to be staffed by at least three nominated Judges, exercising jurisdiction over cases from Hazaribagh, Giridih, Dhanbad, Ranchi, Palamau and Singhbhum districts, with a proviso for the Chief Justice to order cases to be heard at Patna.

powers_conferred: Chief Justice of the High Court at Patna may nominate not less than three Judges to sit at Ranchi.
Chief Justice of the High Court at Patna may, in his discretion, order that any case or class of cases arising in specified districts shall be heard at Patna.

authorities_established: a permanent bench of the High Court at Patna at Ranchi
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Chief Justice of the High Court at Patna has the power to nominate Judges to the permanent bench at Ranchi.

applies_to: Cases arising in the districts of Hazaribagh, Giridih, Dhanbad, Ranchi, Palamau and Singhbhum
exemptions: The Chief Justice of the High Court at Patna may, in his discretion, order that any case or class of cases arising in the specified districts shall be heard at Patna instead of Ranchi.

implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court at Patna (specifically its permanent bench at Ranchi)

act_identification.act_title: THE BETWA RIVER BOARD ACT, 1976

legislative_details.geographical_extent: inter-State Betwa River and River Valley, concerning the Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Board for the creation of a reservoir at Rajghat by construction, on behalf of the Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, of a dam on the Betwa river at Rajghat and for the regulation of such reservoir.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Betwa River Board to oversee the construction of a dam and reservoir at Rajghat on the Betwa river, on behalf of the Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. Its purpose is to regulate the reservoir and facilitate the development of the inter-State Betwa River and River Valley, including power generation.

chapter_titles: FUNCTIONS AND POWERS OF THE BOARD

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and the date of its commencement.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to expediency of control by the Union.
key_sections.description: Declares the expediency of Union control over the regulation and development of the inter-State Betwa River and River Valley.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of the Betwa River Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Betwa River Board as a body corporate with perpetual succession and defines its composition.

key_sections.title: Executive Committee.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of an Executive Committee and outlines its composition and functions.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Board.
key_sections.description: Details the various functions of the Board, including surveys, project preparation, construction of the dam and power house, and laying down operation rules.

key_sections.title: Conditions subject to which the Board may exercise its functions.
key_sections.description: Specifies the conditions, such as financial provisions and cooperation from State Governments, under which the Board can exercise its functions.

key_sections.title: Powers of the Board.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board general powers necessary for carrying out its functions, including acquiring property and publishing information.

key_sections.title: Betwa River Board Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Betwa River Board Fund and specifies how it shall be constituted and applied.

key_sections.title: Directions by Central Government.
key_sections.description: States that the Board shall be guided by directions and instructions on policy from the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Disputes between the Board and the State Governments.
key_sections.description: Mandates that disputes between the Board and the State Governments be referred to the Central Government, whose decision is final.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Board to make regulations with the Central Government's approval.

powers_conferred: Board: acquire, hold and dispose of property, both movable and immovable, and to contract and shall by the said name sue and be sued (S.4(2))
Board: associate with itself any person whose assistance or advice it may desire (S.4(5))
Board: appoint officers and employees (S.8(1))
Board: constitute one or more Advisory Committees (S.9)

Board: carry out surveys and investigations, prepare project reports, prepare detailed reports and estimates, draw up standards and specifications, construct the Rajghat Dam and Rajghat Power House, lay down rules of operation and management, perform supplemental functions (S.10)

Board: require the Governments of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh to furnish information (S.12(2)(c))
Central Government: appoint date of commencement (S.1(2))
Central Government: constitute an Executive Committee (S.5(1))
Central Government: appoint an Engineer (Chief Engineer), a Financial Adviser, and a Secretary to the Board (S.7(1))
Central Government: give directions and instructions on questions of policy to the Board (S.17)
Central Government: decide disputes between the Board and State Governments (S.18)
Central Government: make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act (S.22)
Executive Committee: manage the affairs of the Board (S.5(3))
Executive Committee: exercise any power and do any act or thing which may be exercised or done by the Board (S.5(4))

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints the Chief Engineer, Financial Adviser, and Secretary to the Board. The Board appoints other officers and employees.

applies_to: inter-State Betwa River and River Valley
Governments of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
special_provisions: Provisions for appointment of representatives to the Board by the Central Government when a proclamation under article 356 of the Constitution is in force in Madhya Pradesh or Uttar Pradesh (S.4(3) Proviso).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for rules), Board (for regulations with Central Government approval)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Board carries out its functions subject to conditions and directions from the Central Government. Disputes are resolved by the Central Government. Officers of the Board have powers of entry for works, surveys, and investigations.

schedules_summary.description: Provides a description of the Rajghat Dam, specifying its location across the Betwa river, its components (masonry section, earthen flanks), and the earth dam for reservoir creation.

act_identification.act_title: THE LIFE INSURANCE CORPORATION (MODIFICATION OF SETTLEMENTS) ACT, 1976
act_identification.act_short_title: Life Insurance Corporation (Modification of Settlements) Act, 1976

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the modification of the settlements arrived at between the Life Insurance Corporation of India and their workmen.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the modification of specific settlements made between the Life Insurance Corporation of India and its workmen. Specifically, it nullifies the provision for an annual cash bonus of fifteen percent of annual salary for Class III and Class IV employees from April 1, 1975.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Life Insurance Corporation (Modification of Settlements) Act, 1976.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Corporation', 'salary', and 'settlements'.

key_sections.title: Modification of settlements.
key_sections.description: Declares that provisions of certain settlements relating to the payment of an annual cash bonus to Class III and Class IV employees of the Corporation shall have no force or effect from April 1, 1975.

applies_to: Life Insurance Corporation of India and their workmen
Class III and Class IV employee of the Corporation

act_identification.act_title: THE DISTURBED AREAS (SPECIAL COURTS) ACT, 1976

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the speedy trial of certain offences in certain areas and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to provide for the speedy trial of specific offences committed in areas declared as 'disturbed areas'. It also addresses matters connected with such trials by establishing Special Courts and outlining their jurisdiction and procedure.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its application to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Code', 'disturbed area', 'scheduled offence', and 'Special Court'.

key_sections.title: Declaration of an area as disturbed area.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to declare an area as 'disturbed' due to extensive public peace and tranquillity disturbances, specifying the period of such declaration.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Special Courts.
key_sections.description: Authorizes State Governments to constitute Special Courts for speedy trial of scheduled offences in disturbed areas, with judges appointed by the High Court.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of Special Courts.
key_sections.description: States that scheduled offences committed in disturbed areas shall be triable only by Special Courts, and allows them to try connected non-scheduled offences.

key_sections.title: Procedure and powers of Special Courts.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for Special Courts, including taking cognizance of offences, powers akin to a Court of Session, and provisions for summary trials and tendering pardon.

key_sections.title: Power to transfer cases to regular courts.
key_sections.description: Allows Special Courts to transfer cases to regular courts if they determine the offence is not a scheduled offence.

key_sections.title: Appeal and revision.
key_sections.description: Grants the High Court powers of appeal and revision over Special Courts, treating them as Courts of Session.

key_sections.title: Overriding effect of Act.
key_sections.description: Declares that the Act's provisions override other laws, but the Code of Criminal Procedure applies where not inconsistent, deeming Special Courts as Courts of Session.

key_sections.title: Saving.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not affect the jurisdiction or procedure of courts under laws relating to armed forces, and Special Courts are deemed courts of ordinary criminal justice for such laws.

powers_conferred: State Government to declare an area as disturbed area (Section 3)
State Government to constitute Special Courts (Section 4)
High Court to appoint judges of Special Courts (Section 4)
Special Courts to try scheduled offences (Section 5)
Special Courts to take cognizance of offences (Section 6)
Special Courts to try offences summarily (Section 6)
Special Courts to tender pardon (Section 6)
Special Courts to transfer cases to regular courts (Section 7)
High Court to exercise powers of appeal and revision over Special Courts (Section 8)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines 'scheduled offence' as offences specified in the Schedule, forming part of or arising out of disturbances referred to in Section 3. These include various sections of the Indian Penal Code, Arms Act, 1959, and Indian Explosives Act, 1884. For summary trials, a Special Court may pass a sentence of imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: High Court appoints judges of Special Courts upon request by the State Government.

applies_to: scheduled offences committed in any disturbed area
exemptions: jurisdiction exercisable by, or the procedure applicable to, any court or other authority under any law relating to the naval, military or air forces or any other armed forces of the Union
special_provisions: Karnataka Amendment to Section 3: allows declaration of disturbed area due to 'any other reason'.

Manipur Amendment to Section 3: includes 'extensive and indiscriminate armed violence by members of an association declared as unlawful association under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967' as a reason for declaring disturbed area, and modifies period specification.
Manipur Amendment to Section 9: adds an explanation regarding evidence recorded by a predecessor of the Special Court.
Manipur Amendment to The Schedule: substitutes 'Section 120 B' with 'Sections 120 B, 121 to 130'.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for commencement date); State Government (for declaring disturbed areas and constituting Special Courts).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced through the constitution of Special Courts which try scheduled offences in disturbed areas, following procedures largely aligned with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Special Courts (primary jurisdiction), High Court (appeal and revision), regular courts (for transferred non-scheduled cases).

schedules_summary.description: Lists the 'scheduled offences' which include specific sections from the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860), the Arms Act, 1959 (54 of 1959), and the Indian Explosives Act, 1884 (4 of 1884).

act_identification.act_title: THE TERRITORIAL WATERS, CONTINENTAL SHELF, EXCLUSIVE ECONOMIC ZONE AND OTHER MARITIME ZONES ACT, 1976
act_identification.act_short_title: The Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Territorial waters, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone and other maritime zones of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for certain matters relating to the territorial waters continental shelf, exclusive economic zone and other maritime zones of India.
act_overview.purpose: This Act defines and regulates India's sovereign rights and jurisdiction over its territorial waters, contiguous zone, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone, and historic waters. It establishes limits, controls activities, and provides for the management and protection of resources within these maritime zones.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the official short title of the Act and specifies its commencement dates.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines the term 'limit' in relation to India's maritime zones.

key_sections.title: Sovereignty over, and limits of, territorial waters.
key_sections.description: Declares India's sovereignty over its territorial waters and defines their limits, with provisions for alteration by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Use of territorial waters by foreign ships.
key_sections.description: Grants foreign ships the right of innocent passage through territorial waters and specifies conditions for warships and submarines.

key_sections.title: Contiguous zone of India.
key_sections.description: Defines the contiguous zone, its limits, and the powers of the Central Government within this zone regarding security, immigration, sanitation, customs, and fiscal matters.

key_sections.title: Continental shelf.
key_sections.description: Describes India's continental shelf, its limits, and the Union's sovereign rights and exclusive jurisdiction over its resources and activities.

key_sections.title: Exclusive economic zone.
key_sections.description: Establishes India's exclusive economic zone, its limits, and the Union's sovereign rights and exclusive jurisdiction over its resources and activities, including freedom of navigation and overflight.

key_sections.title: Historic waters.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to specify limits of historic waters and declares India's sovereignty over them.

key_sections.title: Maritime boundaries between India and States having coasts opposite or adjacent to those of India.
key_sections.description: Provides for the determination of maritime boundaries with neighboring states through agreement or by an equidistant line.

key_sections.title: Offences.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of the Act or notifications issued thereunder.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Stipulates liability for offences committed by companies and their officers.

key_sections.title: Previous sanction of the Central Government for prosecution.
key_sections.description: Requires prior sanction from the Central Government for instituting prosecutions under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including regulation of conduct, resource management, and marine environment protection.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To alter the limit of territorial waters (Section 3(3)).
Central Government: To suspend entry of foreign ships into specified areas of territorial waters (Section 4(3)).
Central Government: To exercise powers and take measures in the contiguous zone for security, immigration, sanitation, customs, and fiscal matters (Section 5(4)).
Central Government: To extend enactments to the contiguous zone (Section 5(5)).

Union (India): Full and exclusive sovereign rights in respect of its continental shelf for exploration, exploitation, conservation, management of resources, construction of artificial islands, scientific research, and marine environment protection (Section 6(2), 6(3)).
Central Government: To declare designated areas in the continental shelf and make provisions for their regulation (Section 6(5)).
Central Government: To extend enactments to the continental shelf (Section 6(6)).

Union (India): Sovereign rights in the exclusive economic zone for exploration, exploitation, conservation, management of natural resources, energy production, construction of artificial islands, scientific research, marine environment protection, and other internationally recognized rights (Section 7(4)).
Central Government: To declare designated areas in the exclusive economic zone and make provisions for their regulation (Section 7(6)).
Central Government: To extend enactments to the exclusive economic zone (Section 7(7)).
Central Government: To specify the limits of historic waters (Section 8(1)).
Central Government: To cause publication of charts for baselines, limits of maritime zones, and maritime boundaries (Section 10).
Central Government: To grant licenses or letters of authority for activities in the continental shelf (Section 6(4)) and exclusive economic zone (Section 7(5)).
Central Government: To sanction prosecution for offences under the Act (Section 14).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 15).
Central Government: To remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act (Section 16).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever contravenes any provision of this Act or any notification thereunder shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. Offences committed by companies are also addressed, holding both the company and responsible individuals liable. Rules made under the Act may also provide for similar punishments.

applies_to: Territorial waters of India
Contiguous zone of India
Continental shelf of India
Exclusive economic zone of India
Historic waters of India
Foreign ships (other than warships including sub-marines and other underwater vehicles) for innocent passage
Foreign warships including submarines and other underwater vehicles for entry/passage with prior notice
Any person (including a foreign Government) for activities in the continental shelf and exclusive economic zone
Companies for offences under the Act
exemptions: Fishing by a citizen of India from the requirement of agreement, license, or letter of authority for exploring or exploiting resources of the exclusive economic zone (Section 7(5) proviso).
special_provisions: Foreign submarines and other underwater vehicles must navigate on the surface and show their flag while passing through territorial waters (Section 4(2) proviso).
The Central Government may suspend the entry of all or any class of foreign ships into specified areas of territorial waters (Section 4(3)).
Maritime boundaries between India and States having coasts opposite or adjacent to those of India shall be determined by agreement or by an equidistant line pending agreement (Section 9).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government is empowered to make rules, extend existing enactments to maritime zones, declare designated areas, and grant licenses for activities. Contravention of the Act or rules leads to penalties, and prosecution requires prior sanction from the Central Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any place in which the offender may be found or such other place as the Central Government may direct by order published in the Official Gazette (Section 13).

act_identification.act_title: THE SCHEDULED CASTES AND SCHEDULED TRIBES ORDERS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1976
act_identification.act_short_title: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Orders (Amendment) Act, 1976

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the inclusion in, and the exclusion from, the lists of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, of certain castes and tribes, for the re-adjustment of representation of parliamentary and assembly constituencies in so far as such re-adjustment is necessitated by such inclusion or exclusion and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to amend the lists of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes by including or excluding certain castes and tribes. It also provides for the re-adjustment of representation in parliamentary and assembly constituencies as a result of these changes, and outlines the procedures and powers of the Election Commission in this regard.

key_sections.title: Short title and Commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'census authority', 'Commission', and 'Scheduled Castes Order'.

key_sections.title: Determination of population of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for the census authority to ascertain or estimate the population of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes after the Act's commencement.

key_sections.title: Re-adjustment of constituencies by the Election Commission.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Election Commission to amend the Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1976, to ensure proper representation for Scheduled Castes and Tribes based on updated population figures.

key_sections.title: Procedure and powers of the Commission.
key_sections.description: Grants the Election Commission powers of a civil court for its functions under the Act, including summoning witnesses and requiring document production.

key_sections.title: Publication of amendments and their dates of operation.
key_sections.description: Requires the Election Commission to publish amendments in official gazettes, stating that such amendments will have the force of law and cannot be questioned in court.

key_sections.title: Certain other powers of Election Commission.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Election Commission to correct printing mistakes and make necessary amendments to the Delimitation Order due to altered boundaries or names of territorial divisions.

key_sections.title: Validation of acts done previous to the commencement of the Act.
key_sections.description: Validates actions taken by the census authority or Election Commission before the Act's commencement, provided they conform to the Act's provisions.

powers_conferred: Census authority to ascertain or estimate population of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Section 5).
Election Commission to make amendments in the Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1976 (Section 6).
Election Commission to determine its own procedure and exercise powers of a civil court (Section 7).
Election Commission to require any person to furnish information (Section 7).
Election Commission to publish amendments in official gazettes (Section 8).
Election Commission to correct printing mistakes and make necessary amendments to the Delimitation Order (Section 9).

amended_acts: Constitution (Andaman and Nicobar Islands) Scheduled Tribes Order, 1959
Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1976
Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
related_acts: Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
Constitution (Andaman and Nicobar Islands) Scheduled Tribes Order, 1959
Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1976

applies_to: Scheduled Castes
Scheduled Tribes
Parliamentary constituencies
Assembly constituencies
States included in the Scheduled Castes Order and Scheduled Tribes Orders
Union territory of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
special_provisions: The Union territory of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is included in the definition of 'State' for the purposes of this Act.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The census authority ascertains population figures, which are then notified in the Gazette of India. The Election Commission uses these figures to re-adjust constituencies, publishing its proposals and final amendments in official gazettes. These amendments gain the force of law upon publication.

schedules_summary.description: Repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1988.
Repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1988.

act_identification.act_title: THE SALARY AND ALLOWANCES OF LEADERS OF OPPOSITION IN PARLIAMENT ACT, 1977
act_identification.act_short_title: Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act, 1977

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the salary and allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the salary, allowances, residence, medical treatment, and other amenities for Leaders of Opposition in both Houses of Parliament. Its main objective is to enable them to discharge their official duties effectively and conveniently by providing necessary facilities and financial provisions.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines 'Leader of the Opposition' in relation to either House of Parliament.

key_sections.title: Salary, and daily, constituency and sumptuary allowances.
key_sections.description: Specifies the salary, daily, constituency, and sumptuary allowances for Leaders of Opposition.

key_sections.title: Residence for Leaders of Opposition.
key_sections.description: Provides for rent-free furnished residence for Leaders of Opposition and their families.

key_sections.title: Travelling and daily allowances to Leaders of Opposition.
key_sections.description: Outlines entitlement to travelling and daily allowances for Leaders of Opposition and their families.

key_sections.title: Medical treatment, etc., to Leaders of Opposition.
key_sections.description: Grants free medical treatment and accommodation in government hospitals to Leaders of Opposition and their families.

key_sections.title: Leaders of Opposition not to draw salary or allowances as Members of Parliament.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that Leaders of Opposition receiving benefits under this Act shall not draw salary or allowances as Members of Parliament.

key_sections.title: Amenities to Leaders of Opposition.
key_sections.description: Provides for telephone, secretarial facilities, and conveyance allowance to Leaders of Opposition.

key_sections.title: Advance to Leader of Opposition for purchase of motor car.
key_sections.description: Allows for a repayable advance for the purchase of a motor car for Leaders of Opposition.

key_sections.title: Exemption from liability to pay income-tax on certain perquisites received by a Leader of the Opposition.
key_sections.description: Exempts the value of rent-free furnished residence from income-tax computation for Leaders of Opposition.

key_sections.title: Power to make rule.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint the date of commencement of the Act.
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Chairman of the Council of States or the Speaker of the House of the People: To recognise the Leader of the Opposition.

related_acts: Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 (30 of 1954)
Salaries and Allowances of Ministers Act, 1952 (58 of 1952)
Salaries and Allowances of Officers of Parliament and Leaders of Opposition in Parliament (Second Amendment) Act, 2002

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Chairman of the Council of States or the Speaker of the House of the People for recognizing the Leader of the Opposition; Central Government for appointing the commencement date and making rules.

applies_to: Leaders of Opposition in Parliament (Council of States or House of the People)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Administered by the Central Government through rules and notifications, with recognition powers vested in the Chairman of the Council of States or the Speaker of the House of the People.

act_identification.act_title: THE PARLIAMENTARY PROCEEDINGS (PROTECTION OF PUBLICATION) ACT, 1977
act_identification.act_short_title: The Parliamentary Proceedings (Protection of Publication) Act, 1977

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to protect the publication of reports of proceedings of Parliament.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to protect the publication of substantially true reports of Parliamentary proceedings in newspapers from civil or criminal liability. It extends this protection to reports broadcast by wireless telegraphy, provided the publication is not malicious or against public good.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its geographical extent, and the date from which it is deemed to have come into force.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines the term 'newspaper' for the purposes of this Act.

key_sections.title: Publication of reports of Parliamentary proceedings privileged.
key_sections.description: Grants privilege against civil or criminal proceedings for publishing substantially true reports of Parliamentary proceedings in newspapers, unless published with malice or not for the public good.

key_sections.title: Act also to apply to Parliamentary proceedings broadcast by wireless telegraphy.
key_sections.description: Extends the application of the Act's provisions to reports or matters broadcast by wireless telegraphy.

applies_to: publication in a newspaper of a substantially true report of any proceedings of either House of Parliament
reports or matters broadcast by means of wireless telegraphy as part of any programme or service provided by means of a broadcasting station situate within the territories to which this Act extends
exemptions: publication is proved to have been made with malice
publication of any matter, the publication of which is not for the public good
special_provisions: except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: any court

act_identification.act_title: THE LADY HARDINGE MEDICAL COLLEGE AND HOSPITAL (ACQUISITION) AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS ACT, 1977
act_identification.act_short_title: Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital (Acquisition) and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1977

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the acquisition of the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital and for the management of the Kalavati Saran Hospital, with a view to ensuring better facilities for higher medical education for women and medical facilities for women and children in the Union territory of Delhi and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the acquisition of the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital and the management of the Kalavati Saran Hospital. Its primary purpose is to enhance facilities for higher medical education for women and improve medical services for women and children within the Union territory of Delhi.

chapter_titles: ACQUISITION OF LADY HARDINGE MEDICAL COLLEGE AND HOSPITAL
MANAGEMENT OF THE KALAVATI SARAN HOSPITAL

key_definitions: Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and provides for its commencement on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'Board of Administration', 'Kalavati Saran Hospital', and 'Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital'.

key_sections.title: Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital to vest in Central Government.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that on the appointed day, the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital, along with all its assets, properties, and liabilities, shall be transferred to and vest absolutely in the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Payment of amount.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to pay a sum of rupees one lakh to the Treasurer as compensation for the acquisition of the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital.

key_sections.title: Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital to be administered as Government institution.
key_sections.description: Declares that from the appointed day, the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital shall be administered by the Central Government as a Government institution.

key_sections.title: Kalavati Saran Hospital to be managed as Government institution.
key_sections.description: Provides that the Kalavati Saran Hospital shall be managed by the Central Government as a Government institution from the appointed day, and its Board of Management shall stand dissolved.

key_sections.title: Act to override all other enactments.
key_sections.description: Establishes that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws, instruments, or court orders.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to officers and other employees of Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital and Kalavati Saran Hospital.
key_sections.description: Details the transfer of employees of both institutions to the Central Government, ensuring continuity of service terms unless duly altered, with provisions for termination if alterations are not accepted.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both, for wrongful withholding, obtaining, retaining, removing, or using property, or failing to deliver documents related to the institutions.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act, requiring such rules to be laid before Parliament.

powers_conferred: Power to the Central Government to appoint the date of commencement of the Act (Section 1(2)).
Power to the Central Government to administer the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital as a Government institution (Section 5).
Power to the Central Government to manage the Kalavati Saran Hospital as a Government institution (Section 8(1)).
Power to the Central Government to alter the remuneration, terms, and conditions of employees transferred under the Act (Section 10(1)).
Power to the Central Government to terminate the employment of employees who do not accept altered terms (Section 10(1) proviso).
Power to the Central Government to specify substituted trustees for provident or gratuity funds (Section 10(3)).
Power to the Central Government to cancel or vary contracts entered into in bad faith or detrimental to the institutions' interests (Section 12(1)).
Power to the Central Government to authorize officers or persons to take delivery of property, books, and documents (Section 13(1)).
Power to the Central Government to take all necessary steps for taking possession of vested properties or properties under its management (Section 13(2)).
Power to the Central Government to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act (Section 19(1)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 14 defines offenses such as wrongfully withholding, obtaining, retaining, removing, or using property, or failing to deliver documents related to the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital or the Kalavati Saran Hospital. The penalty for such offenses is imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both. Section 15 extends liability for offenses to companies and their responsible persons.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to specify substituted trustees for provident or gratuity funds (Section 10(3)).

applies_to: Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital
Kalavati Saran Hospital
Officers and other employees of the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital and Kalavati Saran Hospital
exemptions: Any right accrued to, or any liability incurred by, the Board of Administration or any member thereof under the provisions of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, in respect of anything done or omitted to be done during any period preceding the appointed day (Section 6).
Officers or other employees who, within thirty days of the appointed day, intimate their intention of not becoming an officer or employee of the Central Government (Section 10(1) proviso).
special_provisions: The Act specifically targets institutions located in the Union territory of Delhi, aiming to improve medical education and facilities for women and children in that region (Preamble).
Provisions for employees whose terms and conditions are altered by the Central Government, allowing for termination with compensation if the alterations are not acceptable (Section 10(1) proviso).
Special provisions for the Central Government to cancel or vary contracts deemed to be in bad faith or detrimental to the institutions' interests, subject to a hearing (Section 12).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the vesting of the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital in the Central Government and the assumption of management of the Kalavati Saran Hospital by the Central Government. It includes provisions for the transfer of assets, liabilities, and employees. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance related to property and documents. The Central Government or an authorized officer is responsible for making complaints for offenses.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The principal court of civil jurisdiction within the local limits where the institutions are situated has jurisdiction for applications regarding the variation or reversal of orders cancelling or varying contracts (Section 12(2)). Cognizance of offenses under this Act by any court requires a written complaint from the Central Government or an authorized officer (Section 17).

act_identification.act_title: THE INTEREST ACT, 1978

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the allowance of interest in certain cases.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the law relating to the allowance of interest in certain cases, empowering courts to award interest on debts and damages, and specifying conditions for such awards.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Establishes the name, territorial application, and effective date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as "court," "current rate of interest," "debt," and "personal injuries."

key_sections.title: Power of court to allow interest.
key_sections.description: Grants courts the discretion to award interest on debts or damages in legal proceedings, specifying conditions and limitations.

key_sections.title: Interest payable under certain enactments.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that interest is payable where mandated by other enactments or rules of law, and outlines specific cases where courts shall allow interest.

key_sections.title: Section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to apply.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not affect the provisions of Section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Interest Act, 1839, and other corresponding laws, while providing saving clauses for pending legal proceedings.

powers_conferred: Power of court to allow interest in proceedings for recovery of debt or damages (Section 3)
Power to the Central Government to appoint the date of commencement of the Act (Section 1(3))

repealed_acts: the Interest Act, 1839 (32 of 1839)
any other law corresponding thereto in force in any State
related_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government

applies_to: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir
any proceedings for the recovery of any debt or damages
exemptions: any debt or damages upon which interest is payable as of right, by virtue of any agreement
any debt or damages upon which payment of interest is barred, by virtue of an express agreement
the compensation recoverable for the dishonour of a bill of exchange, promissory note or cheque, as defined in the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
the provisions of rule 2 of Order II of the First Schedule to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
special_provisions: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the judicial system, where courts exercise their power to allow interest in legal proceedings for debt or damages.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: court (includes a tribunal and an arbitrator)

act_identification.act_title: THE PUBLIC SECTOR IRON AND STEEL COMPANIES (RESTRUCTURING) AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS ACT, 1978
act_identification.act_short_title: The Public Sector Iron and Steel Companies (Restructuring) and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1978.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for restructuring of the iron and steel companies in the public sector so as to secure better management and greater efficiency in their working and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to restructure public sector iron and steel companies. Its primary objective is to enhance their management and improve operational efficiency. It also covers related and incidental matters concerning this restructuring.

chapter_titles: DISSOLUTION, TRANSFER AND VESTING OF UNDERTAKINGS OF CERTAIN COMPANIES
PROVISIONS RELATING TO OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: “Undertaking”— meaning of.
key_sections.description: Clarifies the meaning of 'undertaking' for the purposes of the Act, including assets, rights, liabilities, and obligations.

key_sections.title: Dissolution, transfer and vesting of undertakings of certain companies in Integral Company.
key_sections.description: States that companies specified in the First Schedule are dissolved and their undertakings vest in the Integral Company.

key_sections.title: Transfer of shares held by Bokaro Steel Limited to Central Government.
key_sections.description: Specifies the transfer of shares from Bokaro Steel Limited to the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Transfer of shares held by Integral Company to Central Government.
key_sections.description: Specifies the transfer of shares from the Integral Company to the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to modify amount of paid-up share capital of Integral Company, etc., and issue of shares.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to adjust the paid-up share capital of specified companies.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to officers and other employees of dissolved companies.
key_sections.description: Details the continuation of service terms for employees of dissolved companies.

key_sections.title: Compensation for transfer not payable.
key_sections.description: States that no compensation is payable for the transfer of services of officers or employees under this Act.

key_sections.title: Provisions with respect to income-tax and surtax.
key_sections.description: Outlines the tax implications, treating transfers as amalgamations for income-tax and surtax purposes.

key_sections.title: Taxes, fees and other charges not payable.
key_sections.description: Declares that no taxes, duties, or fees are payable in respect of any transfer under the provisions of this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.

key_sections.title: Act to override the provisions of other laws.
key_sections.description: Establishes the overriding effect of this Act over other laws, including the Companies Act.

key_sections.title: Power to amend memorandum and articles of association.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to amend company memorandums and articles of association to give effect to the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint commencement date (Section 1(2))
Central Government to modify amount of paid-up share capital of Integral Company, etc., and issue of shares (Section 13)
Integral Company or other transferee company to alter tenure and terms and conditions of service for employees (Sections 14, 15)
Central Government to remove difficulties (Section 25)
Central Government to amend memorandum and articles of association of Integral Company or other transferee company (Section 27)
