applies_to: Public sector iron and steel companies (dissolved companies, Integral Company, transferee companies, transferred companies, transferred units)
Officers and employees of these companies
special_provisions: Registered office of Bharat Refractories Limited may remain at Bokaro Steel City or be transferred to Ranchi (Section 6(2))
Specific provisions for income-tax and surtax treatment of transfers, deeming them as amalgamations (Section 21)
Exemption from taxes, duties, fees, or other charges for transfers under the Act (Section 22)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act dictates the dissolution, transfer, and vesting of undertakings and shares. Legal proceedings pending against dissolved companies can be continued by or against the Integral Company or other transferee company.

schedules_summary.description: Lists the companies that are deemed 'dissolved companies' under the Act, whose undertakings are transferred to the Integral Company.
Lists companies whose shares, held by the Integral Company, are transferred to the Central Government.

act_identification.act_title: An Act to provide for the constitution and regulation of an Armed Force of the Union for ensuring the security of the maritime zones of India with a view to the protection of maritime and other national interests in such zones and for matters connected therewith.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Any part of India as well as outside India (for members' service liability); maritime zones of India; inland area adjoining the coast of India; area in any maritime zone of India.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution and regulation of an Armed Force of the Union for ensuring the security of the maritime zones of India with a view to the protection of maritime and other national interests in such zones and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes and regulates the Coast Guard as an Armed Force of the Union. Its primary purpose is to ensure the security of India's maritime zones and protect national interests within these areas.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

chapter_titles: CONSTITUTION OF THE COAST GUARD AND CONDITIONS OF SERVICE OF THE MEMBERS OF THE COAST GUARD
DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS OF THE COAST GUARD
CHIEF LAW OFFICER AND LAW OFFICERS
JUDICIAL REVIEW OF PROCEEDINGS OF COAST GUARD COURTS
MODIFICATION OF FINDINGS AND SENTENCES, PARDONS, COMMUTATION AND REMISSION OF SENTENCES

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Coast Guard.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Coast Guard as an armed force of the Union for maritime security.

key_sections.title: Duties and functions of Coast Guard.
key_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities and functions of the Coast Guard, including protecting maritime interests, assisting fishermen, preventing marine pollution, and aiding anti-smuggling operations.

key_sections.title: Mutiny.
key_sections.description: Defines the offence of mutiny and prescribes punishment, including death.

key_sections.title: Civil offences.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that civil offences committed by persons subject to the Act can be tried by a Coast Guard Court.

key_sections.title: Punishments awardable by Coast Guard Courts.
key_sections.description: Lists the scale of punishments that can be inflicted by Coast Guard Courts.

key_sections.title: Power to convene a Coast Guard Court.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the Central Government, Director-General, or authorized officers to convene a Coast Guard Court.

key_sections.title: Choice between criminal court and Coast Guard Court.
key_sections.description: Determines the discretion of the Director-General or other specified officers in deciding whether an offence should be tried by a criminal court or a Coast Guard Court.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Chief Law Officer and Law Officers.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment and qualifications of the Chief Law Officer and Law Officers.

key_sections.title: Powers and duties conferrable and imposable on members of the Coast Guard.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to confer specific powers and duties on Coast Guard members under various Central and State Acts.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: General superintendence, direction and control of the Coast Guard (Section 5); dismiss or remove members from service (Section 11); order detention of lunatic accused (Section 88); release or transfer lunatic accused (Section 91); order delivery of lunatic accused to relatives (Section 92); make rules (Section 123); convene Coast Guard Courts (Section 64); pardon, commute, or remit sentences (Section 120); confer powers and duties on members of the Coast Guard (Section 121).

Director-General: Command and supervision of the Coast Guard (Section 5); appoint Inspectors-General, Deputy Inspectors-General, Commandant and other officers (Section 5); dismiss or remove persons other than officers (Section 11); appoint Coast Guard police officers (Section 63); convene Coast Guard Courts (Section 64); decide choice between criminal court and Coast Guard Court (Section 71); suspend sentences (Section 107); pardon, commute, or remit sentences (Section 120).

Commanding Officer: Duty regarding detention of offenders (Section 60); give information of desertion (Section 62); serve summons (Section 79); sign records in ship books (Section 86); award minor punishments (Section 57); suspend sentences (Section 107).
Coast Guard Courts: Power to try any person subject to this Act for any offence and pass authorised sentences (Section 67).
Officers: Order other officers into Coast Guard custody in case of quarrel, affray or disorder (Section 59(2)); appoint persons for discharging functions of Coast Guard police officers (Section 63).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines various offences including correspondence with offenders, deserting post, neglect of duty, mutiny (punishable by death), seducing personnel from allegiance, striking/threatening superior officers, disobedience, ill-treating subordinates, disorderly behaviour, disgraceful conduct, drunkenness, desertion, losing ship/aircraft, dangerous unauthorised flying, inaccurate certificates, low flying, disobedience of captain's command, false accusations, falsifying official documents, offences in respect of property, damage to property, taking unauthorised goods on board, offences relating to custody of vessels/aircraft, unlawful taking of ransom, offences relating to Coast Guard Courts, escape from custody, violation of rules, false answers on enrolment, and offences against good order and discipline. Penalties range from death, imprisonment (life or lesser term), dismissal from Coast Guard, detention in Coast Guard custody, reduction in rank, forfeiture of seniority/service, fine, mulcts of pay and allowances, to severe reprimand or reprimand.

related_acts: Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and other Maritime Zones Act, 1976 (80 of 1976)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints the Director-General, Inspectors-General, Deputy Inspectors-General, Commandant, other officers, Chief Law Officer, and Law Officers. The Director-General or any prescribed officer may appoint Coast Guard police officers.

applies_to: Officers
Subordinate officers and other persons enrolled under this Act
Persons required by Central Government order to serve in a ship
Persons ordered to be received, or being passengers, on board any ship or aircraft of the Coast Guard
exemptions: Civil offences of murder, culpable homicide not amounting to murder, or rape against a person not subject to this Act are not triable by a Coast Guard Court, unless committed outside India or in a specified place.
Officers are not subject to detention for any offence under this Act.
Subordinate officers shall not be sentenced to detention except for desertion.
special_provisions: The Act applies to a person sentenced to imprisonment or death by a Coast Guard Court during the term of their sentence, even if dismissed or no longer subject to the Act.
A Coast Guard Court may be held on shore or afloat.
Special rules for evidence apply to child witnesses under twelve years of age.
Certain documents are exempted from production, and specific procedures are outlined for their access.
Detailed provisions exist for cases where an accused person is found to be of unsound mind, including custody, detention, subsequent fitness for trial, release, and delivery to relatives.
Provisions for the custody and disposal of property related to an offence, both pending and after trial.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the establishment of the Coast Guard, defining duties and functions, specifying offences and corresponding punishments, outlining procedures for arrest and trial by Coast Guard Courts, and providing for the execution and suspension of sentences. It also includes provisions for judicial review of Coast Guard Court proceedings and powers of the Central Government and Director-General regarding findings and sentences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Coast Guard Courts, Criminal Courts, Magistrates, Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Court of Session, High Court.

act_identification.act_title: THE METRO RAILWAYS (CONSTRUCTION OF WORKS) ACT, 1978

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Metropolitan city of Calcutta; and may be extended by Central Government notification to the National Capital Region, such other metropolitan city and metropolitan area.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the construction of works relating to metro railways in the metropolitan cities and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides a legal framework for the construction of metro railways and associated works in metropolitan cities. It outlines procedures for land acquisition, construction, and administration of metro railway projects, ensuring their safe and efficient development.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER V INSPECTION OF METRO RAILWAY

key_sections.title: Short title, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its commencement date, and its initial application to Calcutta, with provisions for extension to other metropolitan areas.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'metro railway', 'competent authority', and 'metropolitan city'.

key_sections.title: Power to acquire land, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants metro railway administrations the power to apply to the Central Government for acquisition of land, buildings, streets, or rights of user for construction.

key_sections.title: Declaration of acquisition.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for the Central Government to declare acquisition of land or rights, leading to absolute vesting in the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Determination of amount payable for acquisition.
key_sections.description: Details how the amount payable for acquired land or rights of user is determined by the competent authority, with provisions for appeal.

key_sections.title: Competent authority and appellate authority.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to appoint a competent authority and an appellate authority for each metro railway, specifying their qualifications.

key_sections.title: Land Acquisition Act 1 of 1894 not to apply.
key_sections.description: States that the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, does not apply to acquisitions made under this Act.

key_sections.title: Functions of metro railway administration.
key_sections.description: Describes the various functions and construction activities that a metro railway administration can undertake for building metro railways.

key_sections.title: Power to prohibit or regulate construction of buildings and excavation.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to prohibit or regulate construction and excavation near metro alignments for safety and construction facilitation.

key_sections.title: Appointment and duties of commissioner.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to appoint commissioners of metro railway and defines their duties, including inspection for public carriage safety.

key_sections.title: Penalty for failure to comply with directions issued under section 21.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for non-compliance with directions regarding construction or evacuation issued under Section 21, including imprisonment or fine.

key_sections.title: Effect of Act and rules, etc., inconsistent with other enactments.
key_sections.description: Establishes that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in other enactments.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, specifying various matters for which rules can be made.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint General Manager (S.3), constitute Advisory Board (S.4), declare application to other cities (S.1(3)), issue notifications for acquisition (S.7), declare acquisition (S.10), appoint competent and appellate authorities (S.16), prohibit/regulate construction (S.21), appoint commissioners (S.27), approve disposal of surplus land (S.30), alter Schedule entries (S.32), make rules (S.44).

Metro Railway Administration: Apply for land acquisition (S.6), enter for survey (S.8), take possession of acquired land (S.11), enter land where right of user vested (S.12), construct works (S.18), enter contracts/leases, make rail tracks, open/divert/close utilities, burrow tunnels, lay signalling, regulate tubewells (S.19), underpin/strengthen buildings (S.23), enter for survey/inspection (S.24), dispose of surplus land (S.30).

Competent Authority: Hear objections (S.9), submit report for acquisition (S.10), direct owner to surrender possession (S.11), determine amount payable for acquisition (S.13), receive deposits (S.14), have powers of civil court (S.15), inspect property (S.15A), enforce orders (S.16C), enforce temporary evacuation (S.36(2A)).
Appellate Authority: Determine amount on appeal (S.13), have powers of civil court (S.16A), call in assessors (S.16A), enforce orders (S.16C).
Commissioner of Metro Railway: Inspect metro railway, make periodical inspections, perform duties (S.27), enter/inspect, make enquiry, require attendance/documents (S.28).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 36 prescribes punishment for wilful failure to comply with directions under section 21, with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both. Section 37 provides a general punishment for contravention of the Act or rules, if no other penalty is specified, with imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both. Offences by companies are also addressed in Section 38.

amended_acts: Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Amendment Act, 1982 (Act 41 of 1982)
Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Amendment Act, 1987 (Act 42 of 1987)
Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Amendment Act, 2009 (Act 34 of 2009)
related_acts: Bombay Municipal Corporation Act, 1888 (Bombay Act III 1888)
Calcutta Metropolitan Planning Area (Use and Development of Land) Control Act, 1965 (West Bengal Act XIV of 1965)
Madras City Municipal Act, 1919 (Madras Act IV of 1919)
National Capital Region Planning Board Act, 1985 (2 of 1985)
Requisitioning and Acquisition of Immovable Property Act, 1952 (30 of 1952)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the General Manager (S.3), members and Chairman of the Advisory Board (S.4), the Competent Authority (S.16), the Appellate Authority (S.16), and Commissioners of metro railway (S.27).

applies_to: The metropolitan city of Calcutta (initially)
The National Capital Region
Such other metropolitan city and metropolitan area as the Central Government may notify
Metro railway administrations and their officers/employees
Persons interested in land, buildings, streets, roads, or passages affected by metro railway construction or operations
special_provisions: The Act applies in the first instance to the metropolitan city of Calcutta, with provisions for extension to other metropolitan cities and areas by Central Government notification (S.1(3)).
Specific definitions are provided for the metropolitan cities of Bombay, Calcutta, Delhi, and Madras (S.2(l)-(o)).
A proviso to Section 42 limits the period for the Central Government to remove difficulties in relation to any metropolitan city.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The competent authority directs surrender of possession of acquired land (S.11), which can be enforced by the Commissioner of Police or Executive Magistrate (S.11(2)). Orders of the competent authority and appellate authority regarding amounts payable are enforceable as civil court decrees (S.16C). The metro railway administration can demolish or alter buildings if owners fail to comply with directions under Section 21 (S.36(2)). The competent authority can enforce temporary evacuation with police help (S.36(2A)). Penalties are prescribed for various offences (S.36, S.37).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The principal civil court of original jurisdiction has jurisdiction over disputes regarding the apportionment of amounts (S.14(4)) and for enforcing orders of the competent authority and appellate authority (S.16C). No suit or application for injunction lies in any court against the Central Government or metro railway administration for actions done in connection with metro railway construction (S.39).

schedules_summary.description: Contains the metro alignment in respect of a metropolitan city, metropolitan area and the National Capital Region, and can be altered by the Central Government.

act_identification.act_title: THE DELHI POLICE ACT, 1978

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of the Union territory of Delhi

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend and consolidate the law relating to the regulation of the police in the Union territory of Delhi.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to amend and consolidate the law relating to the regulation of the police in the Union territory of Delhi, establishing a unified police force, defining its organization, powers, duties, and prescribing regulations for public order and safety.

chapter_titles: ORGANISATION, SUPERINTENDENCE AND CONTROL OF THE POLICE FORCE
REGULATION, CONTROL AND DISCIPLINE OF THE DELHI POLICE
SPECIAL MEASURES FOR MAINTENANCE OF PUBLIC ORDER AND SECURITY OF STATE
EXECUTIVE DUTIES AND POWERS OF POLICE OFFICERS
POWERS IN RELATION TO UNCLAIMED PROPERTY
SPECIAL PROVISIONS RELATING TO EXERCISE OF POWERS UNDER THE CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE, 1973
SPECIAL POWERS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS ACT, 1960

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of the Union territory of Delhi, and its deemed commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Administrator', 'competent authority', 'Delhi police', 'public place', etc.

key_sections.title: One police force for the whole of Delhi.
key_sections.description: Establishes a single police force for Delhi and states that its members are liable for posting to any branch.

key_sections.title: Commissioner of Police.
key_sections.description: Mandates the appointment of a Commissioner of Police by the Administrator for direction and supervision of the police force.

key_sections.title: General powers of Commissioner of Police.
key_sections.description: Outlines the Commissioner of Police's general powers to direct and regulate various aspects of the police force's duties and administration.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations for regulating traffic and for preservation of order in public places, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants the Commissioner of Police power to make regulations concerning traffic, public order, licensing, and other public safety matters.

key_sections.title: Power to prohibit certain acts for prevention of disorder.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Commissioner of Police to prohibit carrying of arms, corrosive substances, public utterances, assemblies, and processions to preserve public peace and safety.

key_sections.title: Dispersal of gangs and bodies of persons.
key_sections.description: Allows the Commissioner of Police to direct gangs or bodies of persons to disperse and remove themselves from Delhi if they pose a danger or alarm.

key_sections.title: Removal of persons about to commit offences.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Commissioner of Police to order the removal of persons from Delhi who are likely to commit offences or are a hazard to the community.

key_sections.title: Duty of police officer to enforce provisions of the Act.
key_sections.description: Defines the duty of police officers to ensure compliance with the Act, including powers to warn, require desistance, arrest, and seize objects.

key_sections.title: Other duties of a police officer.
key_sections.description: Lists various other duties of police officers, such as serving summons, obtaining intelligence, preventing nuisances, aiding disabled persons, and regulating traffic.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to authorise Commissioner of Police and certain other officers to exercise powers of District Magistrates and Executive Magistrates under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to empower the Commissioner of Police and subordinate officers with powers of District and Executive Magistrates under the CrPC.

key_sections.title: Penalties for offences under sections 80 to 96.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for various minor offences related to public conduct, traffic, and nuisances.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Administrator the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering various administrative and procedural matters.

key_sections.title: Cesser of operation of certain enactments and savings.
key_sections.description: States that certain enactments specified in Schedule II cease to be in force in Delhi upon the commencement of this Act, with saving provisions for past actions.

powers_conferred: Administrator: Appoint Commissioner of Police, Additional Commissioner of Police, Deputy, Additional Deputy and Assistant Commissioners of Police, Principals of Police training institutions; specify powers and duties of various police officers; make general or special orders for subordinate ranks appointment; specify form of certificate of appointment; extend period of additional police employment; require recovery of cost of additional police; exempt persons from cost of additional police; declare essential service; empower Commissioner/other officers with District Magistrate/Executive Magistrate powers; make rules.

Commissioner of Police: Direct and regulate police force; investigate and regulate police accounts; appoint special police officers; appoint additional police officers; make regulations for administration of police; call for returns; award punishments; constitute police districts, sub-divisions and police stations; make regulations for traffic and public order; give directions to the public; prohibit certain acts for prevention of disorder; prohibit continuance of music, sound or noise; issue order for prevention of riot; take special measures for epidemic prevention; reserve street or public place; authorise erecting of barriers; make regulations prohibiting disposal of the dead; depute additional police; disperse gangs and bodies of persons; remove persons about to commit offences; remove persons convicted of certain offences; permit temporary entry; require measurements and photographs of persons; take charge of unclaimed property; dispose of unclaimed property; authorise police officers to take steps for compliance with court directions; make regulations regarding carrying weapons; exercise powers of District Magistrate under certain Acts.
Additional Commissioner of Police: Appoint Inspectors of Police; award punishments.
Deputy Commissioner of Police: Appoint Sub-Inspectors of Police and other officers of subordinate rank; award punishments.
Assistant Commissioner of Police: Award punishment of censure.
Inspector of Police: Suspend police officer below the rank of Sub-Inspector of Police.

Police Officer: Enforce provisions of the Act; warn persons; require persons to desist from contravening provisions; arrest persons contravening provisions; seize objects; serve summons and execute warrants; obtain intelligence concerning offences; prevent public nuisances; apprehend persons; aid other police officers; prevent breach of public peace; afford assistance to disabled/helpless persons; take charge of intoxicated persons and lunatics; procure necessary help for arrested persons; arrange for sustenance and shelter of arrested persons; refrain from needless rudeness in searches; act with regard to decency with women and children; prevent loss or damage by fire; avert accident or danger to the public; regulate and control traffic; keep order in public places; regulate resort to public bathing and washing places; enter places of public resort; search suspected persons; take temporary charge of unclaimed property; unsaddle or unload animals; arrest without warrant in case of certain offences under Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960.

Central Government: Empower Commissioner of Police and certain other officers to exercise powers of District Magistrates and Executive Magistrates under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973; remove difficulties.
District Collector: Award compensation.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter X defines numerous offences and their corresponding punishments. General offences include disregarding road rules, causing obstruction or mischief by animals, exposing animals for hire/sale in streets, causing obstruction in streets, obstructing footways, causing annoyance by performances, offensive acts in public, letting loose animals, bathing/washing in unapproved places, defiling public water sources, obstructing bathers, indecent public behaviour, obstructing/annoying passengers, misbehaviour to provoke breach of peace, flying kites dangerously, committing nuisance, and disregard of notices in public buildings. Penalties for these range from fines up to one hundred rupees or imprisonment up to eight days. More serious offences include failure to keep cattle confined (imprisonment up to 6 months, fine up to 500 rupees for subsequent offences), cruelty to animals (imprisonment up to 1 month, fine up to 100 rupees), wilful trespass (imprisonment up to 7 days, fine up to 100 rupees), false alarm of fire (imprisonment up to 3 months, fine up to 100 rupees), being found under suspicious circumstances (imprisonment up to 3 months), possession of suspected stolen property (imprisonment up to 3 months, fine up to 100 rupees), and various contraventions of orders and regulations made under the Act, which carry penalties ranging from fines to imprisonment for terms up to three years, often with minimum prescribed sentences for serious contraventions (e.g., 4 months to 1 year for contravening orders under sections 46, 47 or 48).

repealed_acts: The Delhi Police Ordinance, 1978 (Ord. 2 of 1978)
The Police Act, 1861 (V)
Section 40 of the Punjab Laws Act, 1872 (IV)
The provisions of the Bombay Police Act, 1951 (XXII)
related_acts: Delhi Public Gambling Act, 1955 (Delhi Act 9 of 1955)
Suppression of Immoral Traffic in Women and Girls Act, 1956 (104 of 1956)
Punjab Excise Act, 1955 (Punjab Act No. 18 of 1955)
Bombay Prevention of Begging Act, 1959 (Bombay Act No. 10 of 1960)
Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 (59 of 1960)
The Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867
The Madras Restriction of Habitual Offenders Act, 1948
The Punjab Security of State Act, 1953

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Administrator appoints the Commissioner of Police, Additional Commissioners of Police, Deputy, Additional Deputy and Assistant Commissioners of Police, and Principals of Police training institutions. The Additional Commissioner of Police appoints Inspectors of Police. Deputy Commissioners of Police, Additional Deputy Commissioners of Police, Principal of the Police Training College or of the Police Training School, or any other police officer of equivalent rank appoint Sub-Inspectors of Police and other officers of subordinate rank. The Commissioner of Police appoints special police officers and additional police officers.

applies_to: Whole of the Union territory of Delhi
Police force and its members
Persons and entities within Delhi
exemptions: Members of the Indian Police Service or the Delhi, Andaman and Nicobar Islands Police Service regarding recruitment, pay, allowances, and other conditions of service.
Persons exempted by the Administrator from liability to bear any portion of the cost of additional police.
Persons exempted by the District Collector from compensation amounts.
Performances granted suitability certificate by any State are exempted from prior scrutiny under Section 28(1)(y)(iii).
special_provisions: Special provisions for the Union territory of Delhi.
Special powers for police officers under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
Special powers for police officers under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Administrator has the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act. The Commissioner of Police has the power to make regulations for the administration of the police, regulating traffic, preserving public order, prohibiting certain acts, and regarding carrying weapons.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is primarily carried out by police officers who have duties to ensure compliance, prevent offences, apprehend offenders, and maintain public order. The Act provides for powers of arrest, search, and seizure. Contraventions of the Act, rules, regulations, and orders are subject to penalties, including fines and imprisonment, as detailed in Chapter X. Summary disposal of certain cases is also provided.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Metropolitan Magistrates, Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, and civil courts (for specific matters like challenging rules/orders).

schedules_summary.description: Lists Central Acts and Delhi Act and Acts Extended to Delhi under which the Commissioner of Police exercises powers and discharges functions.
Lists enactments that cease to be in force in Delhi upon the commencement of this Act.
Specifies the deemed appointments of officers of the Delhi police force, mapping their previous designations to new designations under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: An Act to establish a Press Council for the purpose of preserving the freedom of the Press and of maintaining and improving the standards of newspapers and news agencies in India.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish a Press Council for the purpose of preserving the freedom of the Press and of maintaining and improving the standards of newspapers and news agencies in India.
act_overview.purpose: To establish a Press Council for the purpose of preserving the freedom of the Press and of maintaining and improving the standards of newspapers and news agencies in India.

chapter_titles: POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE COUNCIL

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Press Council Act, 1978, and its applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'Chairman', 'Council', 'member', 'prescribed', 'editor', 'newspaper', and 'working journalist'.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of the Council.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Press Council of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, effective from a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Composition of the Council.
key_sections.description: Details the composition of the Council, including a Chairman and twenty-eight other members, specifying their nomination procedures from various categories like journalists, newspaper owners, news agency managers, and Members of Parliament.

key_sections.title: Objects and functions of the Council.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary objects of the Council to preserve Press freedom and improve standards, and lists various functions to achieve these objects, such as building a code of conduct, reviewing developments, and promoting functional relationships.

key_sections.title: Power to censure.
key_sections.description: Grants the Council the power to warn, admonish, censure, or disapprove the conduct of newspapers, news agencies, editors, or journalists for offending journalistic ethics or public taste, after an inquiry.

key_sections.title: General powers of the Council.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the Council powers equivalent to a civil court for conducting inquiries, including summoning witnesses, requiring document discovery, and receiving evidence, while protecting the source of news.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering aspects like nomination procedures, allowances, and financial matters, in consultation with the Council.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Council to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules, for regulating meetings, terms of service for employees, inquiry procedures, and delegation of powers.

powers_conferred: Power to censure newspapers, news agencies, editors, or journalists (Section 14)
General powers throughout India as are vested in a civil court for inquiries (Section 15)
Power to levy fees from registered newspapers and news agencies (Section 16)
Power to make regulations (Section 26)
Central Government has power to appoint date for establishment of Council (Section 4)
Central Government has power to notify nominations of members (Section 5)
Central Government has power to make rules (Section 25)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Council may, for offending against standards of journalistic ethics or public taste or professional misconduct, warn, admonish or censure the newspaper, news agency, editor or journalist or disapprove their conduct (Section 14).

amended_acts: Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Adaptation of Central Laws) Order, 2020
Union Territory of Ladakh Reorganisation (Adaptation of Central Laws) Order, 2020
repealed_acts: Act 25 of 1867 (by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1988 (19 of 1988))
related_acts: Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867 (25 of 1867)
Working Journalists and other Newspaper Employees (Conditions of Service) and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1955 (45 of 1955)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Chairman is nominated by a Committee consisting of the Chairman of the Council of States, the Speaker of the House of the People, and a person elected by the members of the Council. Other members are nominated by the Central Government after inviting panels of names from relevant associations. The Council appoints its Secretary and other employees.

applies_to: newspapers
news agencies
editors
working journalists
special_provisions: Rule of construction respecting enactments not extending to the State of Jammu and Kashmir or Sikkim (Section 3), with subsequent amendments for Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Council holds inquiries into complaints or otherwise, and if satisfied, may warn, admonish, censure, or disapprove the conduct of newspapers, news agencies, editors, or journalists. It has powers of a civil court for these inquiries.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The decision of the Council under Section 14(1) or (2) shall be final and shall not be questioned in any court of law. The Council itself has powers of a civil court for performing its functions or holding inquiries.

act_identification.act_title: THE BRITANNIA ENGINEERING COMPANY LIMITED (MOKAMEH UNIT) AND THE ARTHUR BUTLER AND COMPANY (MUZAFFARPORE) LIMITED (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKINGS) ACT, 1978
act_identification.act_short_title: the Britannia Engineering Company Limited (Mokameh Unit) and the Arthur Butler and Company (Muzaffarpore) Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1978
act_identification.date_of_commencement: Sections 27 and 28 came into force at once; remaining provisions deemed to have come into force on 01/04/1978.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the acquisition and transfer of the right, title and interest of the undertakings of Britannia Engineering Company in relation to the Mokameh unit owned by it and the right, title and interest of Arthur Butler and Company in relation to the undertakings owned by it, with a view to ensuring the continued manufacture of railway wagons and other goods essential to the needs of the country in general and the Railways in particular, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS Britannia Engineering Company at the Mokameh unit and Arthur Butler and Company were engaged in the manufacture of railway wagons and other goods; AND WHEREAS as a result of the closure of the wagon and other undertakings owned by the companies aforesaid, there was a substantial fall in the manufacture of railway wagons and other goods; AND WHEREAS for the purpose of bringing the closed works of the companies aforesaid into operation the management of the Mokameh unit of Britannia Engineering Company and the management of the undertakings of Arthur Butler and Company were taken over by the Central Government under the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 (65 of 1951); AND WHEREAS it is necessary to acquire the said wagon and other undertakings to ensure the continued manufacture of railway wagons and other goods which are essential to the needs of the country in general, and the Railways in particular;
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the acquisition and transfer of the Mokameh unit of Britannia Engineering Company and the undertakings of Arthur Butler and Company. The primary objective is to ensure the continued manufacture of railway wagons and other essential goods for the country, particularly for the Railways, following the closure and government takeover of their management.

chapter_titles: ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF MOKAMEH UNIT AND UNDERTAKINGS OF ARTHUR BUTLER AND COMPANY
MANAGEMENT, ETC., OF MOKAMEH UNIT AND THE UNDERTAKINGS OF ARTHUR BUTLER AND COMPANY
PROVISIONS RELATING TO EMPLOYEES OF MOKAMEH UNIT AND OF ARTHUR BUTLER AND COMPANY

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's official title and the dates of commencement for its various provisions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'Government company', and 'Mokameh unit'.

key_sections.title: Vesting in the Central Government of Mokameh unit and undertakings of Arthur Butler and Company.
key_sections.description: States that the Mokameh unit and the undertakings of Arthur Butler and Company, along with their rights, title, and interest, are transferred to and vested in the Central Government on the appointed day.

key_sections.title: General effect of vesting.
key_sections.description: Details the assets, rights, and properties included in the vesting and declares them free from encumbrances, attachments, or decrees.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of Mokameh unit and the undertakings of Arthur Butler and Company in a Government company.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to direct the vested undertakings to be transferred to a Government company under specified terms and conditions.

key_sections.title: Payment of amount.
key_sections.description: Stipulates the amount to be paid by the Central Government to Britannia Engineering Company and Arthur Butler and Company for the acquisition, as specified in the First Schedule.

key_sections.title: Employment of employees to continue.
key_sections.description: Ensures that employees of the acquired units continue their employment under the Central Government or Government company with existing rights and privileges.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Commissioner of Payments.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to appoint a Commissioner of Payments for disbursing the amounts payable to the companies.

key_sections.title: Priority of claims.
key_sections.description: Establishes the order of priorities for various claims against the acquired companies, as detailed in the Second Schedule.

key_sections.title: Act have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws or instruments.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for offences such as wrongful withholding, obtaining, or removal of property, or failure to furnish documents.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to the policy of the State.
key_sections.description: Declares that the Act is for giving effect to the policy of the State towards securing the principles specified in clause (b) of article 39 of the Constitution.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To direct vesting of undertakings in a Government company (Section 5).
Central Government: To appoint a Commissioner of Payments and other assisting persons (Section 15).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act (Section 31).
Central Government: To remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions (Section 32).
Central Government: To delegate powers (Section 30).
Commissioner of Payments: To authorise other persons to exercise powers (Section 15).

Commissioner of Payments: To regulate own procedure, summon and enforce attendance of witnesses, examine on oath, discover and produce documents, receive evidence on affidavits, issue commissions for examination of witnesses (Section 21(5)).
Government company: To exercise all such powers and do all such things as the original companies were authorised to do in relation to their units/undertakings (Section 9).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 27 defines offences including wrongfully withholding, obtaining, or retaining property; wilfully withholding or failing to furnish documents; failing to deliver assets/books; or wrongfully removing/destroying property, or making false claims. Such offences are punishable with imprisonment for a term up to two years, or with a fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both. Section 28 specifies provisions for offences committed by companies.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government shall appoint the Commissioner of Payments and may appoint other persons to assist the Commissioner.

applies_to: Britannia Engineering Company Limited (Mokameh Unit)
Arthur Butler and Company (Muzaffarpore) Limited
Employees of the Mokameh unit and undertakings of Arthur Butler and Company

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the vesting of the undertakings in the Central Government or a Government company, the payment of specified amounts, the management by the Government company or appointed persons, and the process of claims and disbursements handled by the Commissioner of Payments. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Principal court of original jurisdiction and High Court for appeals against decisions of the Commissioner of Payments.

schedules_summary.description: Specifies the amount payable to The Britannia Engineering Company and Arthur Butler and Company for the acquisition, in Rupees in lakhs.
Outlines the order of priorities for various claims against the companies, categorised from I to VI, including employees' dues, secured loans, government loans, revenue, taxes, and trade creditors.

act_identification.act_title: THE PRIZE CHITS AND MONEY CIRCULATION SCHEMES (BANNING) ACT, 1978
act_identification.act_short_title: The Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978

act_overview.preamble: An Act to ban the promotion or conduct of prize chits and money circulation schemes and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to ban the promotion or conduct of prize chits and money circulation schemes. It also covers matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, including penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'conventional chit', 'money circulation scheme', and 'prize chit'.

key_sections.title: Banning of prize chits and money circulation schemes or enrolment as members or participation therein.
key_sections.description: Prohibits any person from promoting, conducting, enrolling in, or participating in prize chits or money circulation schemes.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravening the provisions of section 3.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals who violate the ban on prize chits and money circulation schemes, including imprisonment and fine.

key_sections.title: Penalty for other offences in connection with prize chits or money circulation schemes.
key_sections.description: Outlines penalties for actions related to the promotion or conduct of banned schemes, such as printing, publishing, selling, or advertising materials for such schemes.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Specifies how offences committed by companies under this Act are to be handled, including liability for persons in charge and directors.

key_sections.title: Power to enter, search and seize.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to police officers and authorized State Government officers to enter, search, seize, and take persons into custody in connection with suspected illegal schemes.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply to certain prize chits or money circulation schemes.
key_sections.description: Lists specific types of prize chits or money circulation schemes that are exempt from the provisions of this Act, such as those promoted by State Governments or certain banking institutions.

key_sections.title: Transitional provisions.
key_sections.description: Provides for the winding up of existing prize chits or money circulation schemes at the commencement of the Act, including requirements for furnishing information and refunding monies.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the State Government, in consultation with the Reserve Bank, to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeals and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals specific State Acts related to money circulation schemes and includes saving provisions for actions taken under those repealed Acts.

powers_conferred: Police officers not below the rank of an officer in charge of a police station have power to enter, search, seize, and take into custody persons and things related to prize chits or money circulation schemes (Section 7(1)).

Officers authorised by the State Government have power to enter, search, examine persons, order production of documents, inspect and seize registers, books, and documents related to prize chits or money circulation schemes (Section 7(2)).
The State Government has power to declare forfeiture of newspapers and publications containing material or advertisements related to prize chits or money circulation schemes (Section 8).
The State Government has power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act, in consultation with the Reserve Bank (Section 13).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of the ban on prize chits and money circulation schemes (Section 3) is punishable with imprisonment up to three years, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both, with minimums of one year imprisonment and one thousand rupees fine (Section 4). Other offences related to promoting or conducting such schemes (e.g., printing, publishing, selling tickets or advertisements, using premises) are punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or fine up to three thousand rupees, or both, with minimums of one year imprisonment and one thousand rupees fine (Section 5). Failure to refund monies during transitional winding-up period (Section 12(4)) is punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or fine up to three thousand rupees, or both, with minimums of one year imprisonment and one thousand rupees fine (Section 12(5)). Offences committed by companies also incur liability for the company and responsible individuals (Section 6).

repealed_acts: The Andhra Pradesh Money Circulation Scheme (Prohibition) Act, 1965 (Andhra Pradesh Act 30 of 1956)
the Madhya Pradesh Dhan Parichalan Skeem (Pratishedh) Adhiniyam, 1975 (Madhya Pradesh Act 19 of 1975)
related_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
State Bank of India Act, 1955 (23 of 1955)
State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959 (38 of 1959)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 (5 of 1970)

applies_to: Any person promoting or conducting prize chits or money circulation schemes
Any person enrolling as a member or participating in such schemes
exemptions: Prize chits or money circulation schemes promoted by a State Government or any officer or authority on its behalf.
Prize chits or money circulation schemes promoted by a company wholly owned by a State Government which does not carry on any business other than the conducting of such a scheme.

Prize chits or money circulation schemes promoted by a banking company as defined in clause (c) of section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, or a banking institution notified by the Central Government under section 51 of that Act, or the State Bank of India, or a subsidiary bank, or a corresponding new bank, or a Regional Rural Bank, or a co-operative bank as defined in clause (bii) of section 2 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
Prize chits or money circulation schemes promoted by any charitable or educational institution notified in this behalf by the State Government, in consultation with the Reserve Bank.
special_provisions: Transitional provisions for persons conducting prize chits or money circulation schemes at the commencement of the Act, allowing them to continue for a period necessary for winding up, not exceeding two years, subject to furnishing information and a winding up plan (Section 12).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: State Government (in consultation with the Reserve Bank)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through penalties for contravention (Sections 4, 5, 12(5)), powers of police officers and authorized State Government officers to enter, search, seize, and take into custody (Section 7), and the declaration of offences as cognizable (Section 10).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, or as the case may be, Chief Judicial Magistrate, shall try any offence punishable under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE COCONUT DEVELOPMENT BOARD ACT, 1979

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the development under the control of the Union of the coconut industry and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish the Coconut Development Board to promote and develop the coconut industry under the control of the Union. It outlines measures for improving cultivation, marketing, processing, and research related to coconuts and their products.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II THE COCONUT DEVELOPMENT BOARD
CHAPTER III FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT
CHAPTER IV CONTROL BY CENTRAL GOVERNMENT

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.section_number: 2. Declaration as to expediency of control by the Union.
key_sections.title: Declaration as to expediency of control by the Union.
key_sections.description: Declares that it is expedient in the public interest for the Union to control the coconut industry.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Board', 'Chairman', 'coconut', and 'coconut industry'.

key_sections.section_number: 4. Establishment and constitution of the Board.
key_sections.title: Establishment and constitution of the Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Coconut Development Board as a body corporate and details its composition and membership.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the duties and measures the Board shall undertake for the development of the coconut industry, including marketing, technical advice, financial assistance, and research.

key_sections.section_number: 12. Grants and loans by the Central Government.
key_sections.title: Grants and loans by the Central Government.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to provide grants and loans to the Board for the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Coconut Development Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Coconut Development Fund and specifies sources of credit and application of funds.

key_sections.title: Directions by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Board to carry out directions issued to it from time to time by the Central Government for the efficient administration of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Board, with previous sanction of the Central Government, to make regulations for giving effect to the provisions of this Act.

powers_conferred: Power to the Central Government to appoint a non-executive Chairman, Chief Executive Officer, Chief Coconut Development Officer, Secretary, and various members to the Board (Section 4(4), Section 7).
Power to the Board to acquire, hold and dispose of property, both movable and immovable, and to contract (Section 4(2)).
Power to the Board to elect a Vice-Chairman from amongst its members (Section 4(5)).
Power to the Board to associate any person for assistance or advice (Section 4(8)).
Power to the Board to appoint committees for efficient discharge of duties (Section 9).
Power to the Board to promote the development of the coconut industry through various measures (Section 10).
Power to the Board to borrow money from the public, banks, or other institutions (Section 14).
Power to the Central Government to dissolve the Board (Section 11).
Power to the Central Government to make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act (Section 19).
Power to the Board to make regulations, with the previous sanction of the Central Government (Section 20).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints the Chairman, Chief Executive Officer, Chief Coconut Development Officer, Secretary, and various members of the Board. The Board appoints other officers and employees.

applies_to: whole of India
coconut industry
growers of coconut
dealers in coconut
manufacturers of coconut products
special_provisions: Representation of specific States (Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Nagaland, Odisha, Telengana, Tripura, West Bengal) and Union territories (Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Puducherry) on the Board (Section 4(4)(g), (h), (i)).
Special provisions for transfer of employees from the Directorate of Coconut Development to the Board (Section 8).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government has the power to make rules (Section 19). The Board has the power to make regulations with the previous sanction of the Central Government (Section 20).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Board performs its functions as outlined in Section 10. The Central Government issues directions to the Board for efficient administration (Section 16). The Board furnishes returns and reports to the Central Government (Section 17).

act_identification.act_title: THE UNION DUTIES OF EXCISE (DISTRIBUTION) ACT, 1979

legislative_details.geographical_extent: States to which the law imposing the duty extends

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the payment out of the Consolidated Fund of India of sums equivalent to a part of the net proceeds of certain Union duties of excise to the States to which the law imposing the duty extends and for the distribution of those sums among those States in accordance with the principles recommended by the Finance Commission in its[1][report dated the 25th day of November, 1994].
act_overview.purpose: To provide for the payment of a part of the net proceeds of Union duties of excise from the Consolidated Fund of India to the States. It also outlines the distribution of these sums among the States based on the Finance Commission's recommendations.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines the term 'distributable Union duties of excise' and 'net proceeds'.

key_sections.title: Payment to States of sums equivalent to a part of the net proceeds of Union duties of excise and distribution of sums among them.
key_sections.description: Mandates payment of sums equivalent to distributable Union duties of excise to States and specifies the distribution percentages among them through Table I and Table II.

key_sections.title: Payment to be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
key_sections.description: States that payments under Section 3 shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make rules for the time, manner, and adjustments of payments under the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Union Duties of Excise (Distribution) Act, 1962, from 1st April, 1979.

powers_conferred: Power to Central Government to make rules

repealed_acts: The Union Duties of Excise (Distribution) Act, 1962 (3 of 1962)
related_acts: Central Excises and Salt Act, 1944 (1 of 1944)

applies_to: States
special_provisions: Specific percentages for distribution of excise duties to various States for different financial years (1995-96 to 1999-2000) as detailed in Table I and Table II of Section 3.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Payment out of the Consolidated Fund of India; Central Government to make rules for time and manner of payments.

act_identification.act_title: THE INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN (REGULATION OF EMPLOYMENT AND CONDITIONS OF SERVICE) ACT, 1979
act_identification.act_short_title: The Inter-State Migrant Workmen (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1979.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the employment of inter-State migrant workmen and to provide for their conditions of service and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the employment of inter-State migrant workmen. It also seeks to provide for their conditions of service and address related matters concerning their welfare and protection.

chapter_titles: REGISTRATION OF ESTABLISHMENTS EMPLOYING INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN
WAGES, WELFARE AND OTHER FACILITIES TO BE PROVIDED TO INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's name, territorial reach, effective date, and to whom it applies (establishments/contractors employing 5+ inter-State migrant workmen).

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as "appropriate Government", "contractor", "establishment", "inter-State migrant workman", and "principal employer".

key_sections.title: Registration of certain establishments.
key_sections.description: Mandates principal employers to register establishments employing inter-State migrant workmen with a registering officer.

key_sections.title: Licensing of contractors.
key_sections.description: Requires contractors to obtain a licence for recruiting or employing inter-State migrant workmen across states.

key_sections.title: Duties of contractors.
key_sections.description: Outlines specific duties of contractors, including furnishing particulars, issuing pass books, and providing returns for migrant workmen.

key_sections.title: Wage rates and other conditions of service of inter-State migrant workmen.
key_sections.description: Specifies that wage rates, holidays, hours of work, and other conditions of service for migrant workmen should be comparable to local workmen or as prescribed, ensuring no less than Minimum Wages Act rates.

key_sections.title: Displacement allowance.
key_sections.description: Mandates contractors to pay a non-refundable displacement allowance to inter-State migrant workmen at recruitment.

key_sections.title: Other facilities.
key_sections.description: Lists other facilities contractors must provide, such as regular wage payment, equal pay, suitable working conditions, residential accommodation, medical facilities, protective clothing, and accident reporting.

key_sections.title: Responsibility for payment of wages.
key_sections.description: Makes contractors responsible for wage payment, with the principal employer liable in case of contractor default.

key_sections.title: Past liabilities.
key_sections.description: States that any loan given by a contractor or principal employer to a migrant workman becomes extinguished upon completion of employment.

key_sections.title: Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of inspectors and defines their powers to ensure compliance with the Act.

key_sections.title: Contravention of provisions regarding employment of inter-State migrant workmen.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravening provisions related to employment of inter-State migrant workmen or licence conditions.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the appropriate Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeals and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Orissa Dadan Labour (Control and Regulation) Act, 1975, and similar State laws.

powers_conferred: Appropriate Government: Appoint registering officers (Section 3), fix period for registration (Section 4), appoint licensing officers (Section 7), impose conditions on licences (Section 8), appoint inspectors (Section 20), exempt in special cases (Section 31), make rules (Section 35).
Registering Officer: Register establishments, issue certificates (Section 4), revoke registration (Section 5).
Licensing Officer: Grant licences (Section 9), revoke, suspend, amend licences (Section 10).
Central Government: Postpone/relax operation of Act (Section 1), give directions to State Governments (Section 33), remove difficulties (Section 34), make rules (Section 35).
Inspectors: Enter premises, examine persons/records, seize documents (Section 20).
State Government: May appoint persons to exercise inspector powers (Section 20(3)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Obstruction of inspector/authorised person or refusal to afford facility: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine up to two thousand rupees, or both (Section 24(1)). Refusal to produce documents or preventing examination: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine up to two thousand rupees, or both (Section 24(2)). Contravention of provisions regarding employment of inter-State migrant workmen or licence conditions: Imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both; continuing contravention with additional fine up to one hundred rupees per day (Section 25). Other contraventions for which no other penalty is provided: Imprisonment up to two years, or fine up to two thousand rupees, or both (Section 26). Offences by companies: Company and responsible persons deemed guilty, with provisions for proving lack of knowledge or due diligence, and liability for directors/managers/officers in case of consent/connivance/neglect (Section 27).

repealed_acts: The Orissa Dadan Labour (Control and Regulation) Act, 1975 (Orissa Act 42 of 1975)
any law corresponding to this Act, in force in any State
related_acts: Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (19 of 1952)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Appropriate Government: Appoints registering officers (Section 3), licensing officers (Section 7), inspectors (Section 20), and nominates appellate officers (Section 11). State Government: May appoint persons to exercise inspector powers (Section 20(3)).

applies_to: Every establishment in which five or more inter-State migrant workmen are employed or were employed on any day of the preceding twelve months.
Every contractor who employs or employed five or more inter-State migrant workmen on any day of the preceding twelve months.
exemptions: The Central Government may postpone or relax the operation of all or any provisions in any State(s) for up to one year (Section 1(3) Proviso).
The appropriate Government may exempt any establishment or class of establishments or any contractor or class of contractors or any inter-State migrant workmen in special cases (Section 31).
special_provisions: Central Government's power to postpone or relax operation of the Act in certain states (Section 1(3) Proviso).
Power of appropriate Government to exempt in special cases (Section 31).
Provisions for industrial disputes in relation to inter-State migrant workmen, allowing reference to authorities in either the establishment's state or the recruitment state (Section 22).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Registration of establishments (Chapter II), licensing of contractors (Chapter III), duties and obligations of contractors (Chapter IV), provision of wages, welfare, and facilities (Chapter V), appointment of inspecting staff (Chapter VI), penalties for contraventions (Chapter VII), and power to give directions by Central Government to State Governments (Section 33).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act.

schedules_summary.description: Lists enactments for the purposes of which an inter-State migrant workman is deemed to be employed from the date of recruitment. These include The Workmen’s Compensation Act, 1923, The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, The Employees’ State Insurance Act, 1948, The Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, and The Maternity Benefit Act, 1961.

act_identification.act_title: THE HARYANA AND UTTAR PRADESH (ALTERATION OF BOUNDARIES) ACT, 1979
act_identification.act_short_title: the Haryana and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1979

legislative_details.geographical_extent: States of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the alteration of boundaries of the States of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish fixed boundaries between the States of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, replacing the fluctuating deep stream line of the river Yamuna. It also addresses consequential matters such as the transfer of territories, representation in legislatures, jurisdiction of High Courts, apportionment of assets and liabilities, and other legal and miscellaneous provisions.

chapter_titles: PART III REPRESENTATION IN THE LEGISLATURES
PART VI APPORTIONMENT OF ASSETS AND LIABILITIES
PART VII LEGAL AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Haryana and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1979.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'fixed boundaries', and 'transferred territories'.

key_sections.title: Replacement of fluctuating boundaries by fixed boundaries.
key_sections.description: Mandates the replacement of fluctuating river boundaries between Haryana and Uttar Pradesh with fixed boundaries as from the appointed day, to be demarcated by a Central Government appointed authority.

key_sections.title: Transfer of territories.
key_sections.description: Specifies that territories lying on the Haryana side of the fixed boundaries shall be added to Haryana and cease to be part of Uttar Pradesh, and vice versa for Uttar Pradesh.

key_sections.title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Provides for the amendment of the First Schedule to the Constitution to reflect the altered territories of Uttar Pradesh and Haryana.

key_sections.title: Extension of jurisdiction of, and transfer of proceedings to, High Court of Punjab and Haryana.
key_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the High Court of Punjab and Haryana to territories transferred to Haryana and provides for the transfer of relevant pending proceedings from the High Court at Allahabad.

key_sections.title: Extension of jurisdiction of, and transfer of proceedings to, High Court at Allahabad.
key_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad to territories transferred to Uttar Pradesh and provides for the transfer of relevant pending proceedings from the High Court of Punjab and Haryana.

key_sections.title: Land and goods.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that all land, stores, articles, and goods belonging to the transferring State in the transferred territories shall pass to the receiving State.

key_sections.title: Contracts.
key_sections.description: Determines how contracts made by the transferring State before the appointed day will be apportioned between the States based on the purpose of the contract and its relation to the transferred territories.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to order allocation or adjustment in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to order allocation or adjustment of property, benefits, or liabilities between the States if deemed just and equitable, within three years from the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Power to adapt laws.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to make adaptations and modifications to laws for facilitating their application in relation to the altered States of Haryana or Uttar Pradesh.

key_sections.title: Construction of boundary pillars, etc.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the construction and maintenance of boundary pillars, provides for joint inspection, and prescribes penalties for wilfully removing or injuring boundary pillars.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the President the power to issue notified orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions, provided they are not inconsistent with the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules by notification to give effect to the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint the 'appointed day' (Sec 2(a)).
Central Government: To appoint an authority for demarcation of fixed boundaries (Sec 3(2)).
Central Government: To order allocation or adjustment of assets and liabilities between States (Sec 24).
Central Government: To remove difficulties by notified order (Sec 35).
Central Government: To make rules to give effect to the Act (Sec 36(1)).
State Governments (Haryana and Uttar Pradesh): To provide for the administration of transferred territories (Sec 4(2)).
State Governments (Haryana and Uttar Pradesh): To spend money from the Consolidated Fund for transferred territories (Sec 12(1)).
State Governments (Haryana and Uttar Pradesh): To make rules for joint inspection of boundary pillars (Sec 32(2)).
Governor of Haryana or Uttar Pradesh: To authorise expenditure from the Consolidated Fund for transferred territories (Sec 12(2)).

Authority appointed by Central Government: To demarcate fixed boundaries, decide on interpretation of boundary description, determine location of boundary pillars, specify State Government for construction/maintenance of pillars, and prepare maps (Sec 3).
Chief Justice of High Court of Judicature at Allahabad/Punjab and Haryana: To certify proceedings for transfer (Sec 8(2), 9(2)).
Chief Justice of High Court of Judicature at Allahabad/Punjab and Haryana: To order transfer of proceedings (Sec 8(3) Proviso, 9(3) Proviso).
Chief Justice of High Court of Punjab and Haryana/High Court of Judicature at Allahabad: To specify advocates entitled to practice (Sec 8(5), 9(5)).
Appropriate Government: To adapt and modify laws (Sec 28).
Any court, tribunal or authority: To construe laws for facilitating their application (Sec 29).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever wilfully removes or injures any boundary pillars shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both (Section 32(3)).

related_acts: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
The Bihar and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act, 1968 (24 of 1968)
The State Financial Corporations Act, 1951 (63 of 1951)
The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974)

authorities_established: An authority appointed by the Central Government for demarcation of fixed boundaries (Sec 3(2))
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the authority for demarcation of fixed boundaries (Sec 3(2)). The Chief Justices of the High Courts have the power to specify advocates entitled to practice (Sec 8(5), 9(5)).

applies_to: States of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh
Territories transferred between these states
Sitting members of Parliament and State Legislatures affected by boundary changes
High Courts of Punjab and Haryana and High Court at Allahabad
State Financial Corporations and State Electricity Boards of Haryana and Uttar Pradesh
special_provisions: Specific provisions for the High Court of Punjab and Haryana and the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad regarding jurisdiction and transfer of proceedings (Part IV).
Provisions for the administration of transferred territories by State Governments (Sec 4(2)).
Provisions for financial adjustments between the States regarding assets and liabilities (Part VI).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government (Sec 36(1)). The High Courts of Punjab and Haryana and High Court of Judicature at Allahabad can make rules or give directions regarding the practice of advocates (Sec 8(5), 9(5)).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the demarcation of boundaries by a Central Government-appointed authority, orders by State Governments for administration of transferred territories, transfer of legal proceedings between High Courts and other courts/tribunals, and penalties for damaging boundary pillars. The Central Government also has powers to remove difficulties.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court of Punjab and Haryana, High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, and courts in either Haryana or Uttar Pradesh for specific offences related to boundary pillars. High Courts also have jurisdiction over questions regarding transfer of proceedings.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the detailed description of the fixed boundaries between the Karnal and Sonepat districts of Haryana and the Saharanpur, Muzaffarnagar and Meerut districts of Uttar Pradesh (as the present deep stream line), and between the Gurgaon district of Haryana and the Bulandshahr and Aligarh districts of Uttar Pradesh, specifying village names and geographical features for demarcation.

act_identification.act_title: THE PREVENTION OF BLACKMARKETING AND MAINTENANCE OF SUPPLIES OF ESSENTIAL COMMODITIES ACT, 1980
act_identification.act_short_title: the Prevention of Blackmarketing and Maintenance of Supplies of Essential Commodities Act, 1980

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for detention in certain cases for the purpose of prevention of black marketing and maintenance of supplies of commodities essential to the community and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to prevent black marketing and ensure the maintenance of supplies of commodities essential to the community. It provides for the detention of persons involved in such activities to safeguard public interest and ensure availability of essential goods.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official name, territorial application, and effective date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appropriate Government' and 'detention order'.

key_sections.title: Power to make orders detaining certain persons.
