key_sections.description: Grants power to Central/State Governments and specified officers to issue detention orders to prevent black marketing and ensure essential supplies.

key_sections.title: Powers in relation to absconding persons.
key_sections.description: Outlines powers of the appropriate Government or officers regarding persons who abscond after a detention order has been made.

key_sections.title: Grounds of order of detention to be disclosed to person affected by the order.
key_sections.description: Mandates the disclosure of grounds for detention to the detained person within a specified period and allows for representation.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Advisory Boards.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of Advisory Boards by Central and State Governments to review detention orders.

key_sections.title: Reference to Advisory Boards.
key_sections.description: Requires detention orders and representations to be placed before Advisory Boards within three weeks.

key_sections.title: Action upon the report of Advisory Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the action to be taken by the appropriate Government based on the Advisory Board's report, either confirming or revoking the detention order.

key_sections.title: Maximum period of detention.
key_sections.description: Sets the maximum period of detention at six months, subject to the Government's power to revoke or modify.

key_sections.title: Revocation of detention orders.
key_sections.description: Allows for the revocation or modification of detention orders by the Central or State Government and permits fresh orders under new facts.

key_sections.title: Temporary release of persons detained.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to temporarily release detained persons under specified conditions and prescribes penalties for non-compliance.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Grants immunity from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Prevention of Black marketing and Maintenance of Supplies of Essential Commodities Ordinance, 1979, and includes saving provisions.

powers_conferred: Power to make orders detaining certain persons (Central Government, State Government, officers not below the rank of a Joint Secretary/Secretary, District Magistrates, Commissioners of Police) under Section 3.
Power to regulate place and conditions of detention (appropriate Government) under Section 5.

Power to make reports to a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class regarding absconding persons (appropriate Government or officer mentioned in sub-section (2) of section 3) under Section 7(1)(a).
Power to direct absconding persons to appear (appropriate Government or officer mentioned in sub-section (2) of section 3) under Section 7(1)(b).
Power to constitute Advisory Boards (Central Government and each State Government) under Section 9(1).
Power to confirm or revoke detention orders based on the report of the Advisory Board (appropriate Government) under Section 12.
Power to revoke or modify detention orders (Central Government or State Government) under Section 14.
Power to direct temporary release of persons detained (appropriate Government) under Section 15(1).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Failure to comply with a direction to appear for absconding persons is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine or with both (Section 7(1)(b)). Failure to surrender after temporary release is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both (Section 15(4)). Failure to fulfill conditions of temporary release or bond leads to forfeiture of the bond (Section 15(5)).

repealed_acts: The Prevention of Black marketing and Maintenance of Supplies of Essential Commodities Ordinance, 1979 (10 of 1979)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The appropriate Government appoints members of the Advisory Boards, who are or have been, or are qualified to be appointed as, Judges of a High Court. The appropriate Government also appoints one of these members as Chairman. For Union territories, the appointment of a High Court Judge from a State requires previous approval of the concerned State Government.

applies_to: Any person acting in any manner prejudicial to the maintenance of supplies of commodities essential to the community.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Detention orders are made by the Central Government, State Government, or specially empowered officers. These orders are executed at any place in India following the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Detention orders made by certain officers must be reported to the State Government for approval, and State Government orders must be reported to the Central Government. Grounds for detention must be disclosed to the detained person, who can make a representation. Advisory Boards are constituted to review detention orders, and the appropriate Government acts upon their report, either confirming or revoking the detention.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class (for matters related to absconding persons).

act_identification.act_title: THE BANKING COMPANIES (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKINGS) ACT, 1980
act_identification.act_short_title: The Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of certain banking companies, having regard to their size, resources, coverage and organisation, in order further to control the heights of the economy, to meet progressively, and serve better, the needs of the development of the economy and to promote the welfare of the people, in conformity with the policy of the State towards securing the principles laid down in clauses (b) and (c) of article 39 of the Constitution and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of certain banking companies. Its main objectives are to control the economy, meet the needs of economic development, and promote public welfare in line with constitutional principles.

chapter_titles: TRANSFER OF THE UNDERTAKINGS OF EXISTING BANKS AND SHARE CAPITALS OF THE CORRESPONDING NEW BANKS

key_definitions: words and expressions used herein and not defined but defined in the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (10 of 1949)
words and expressions used herein and not defined either in this Act or in the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (10 of 1949), but defined in the Companies Act, 1956

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its date of commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'banking company', 'corresponding new bank', 'Custodian', and 'existing bank'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of corresponding new banks and business thereof.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of corresponding new banks, their capital structure, and their business operations, including acting as agents for the Reserve Bank.

key_sections.title: Undertakings of existing banks to vest in corresponding new banks.
key_sections.description: States that the undertakings of existing banks are transferred to and vested in the corresponding new banks upon the Act's commencement.

key_sections.title: General effect of vesting.
key_sections.description: Details the scope of the vesting, including all assets, rights, liabilities, and obligations, and provisions for assets/liabilities outside India.

key_sections.title: Payment of amount.
key_sections.description: Outlines the method and options for payment of compensation by the Central Government to existing banks for the transfer of their undertakings.

key_sections.title: Head office and management.
key_sections.description: Specifies the location of the head office and the management structure, including the Board of Directors and the role of the Custodian.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make scheme.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make schemes for implementing the Act, covering capital structure, Board constitution, and amalgamation.

key_sections.title: Closure of accounts and disposal of profits.
key_sections.description: Mandates the closing and balancing of accounts, appointment of auditors, audit procedures, and reporting requirements for corresponding new banks.

key_sections.title: Vacation of office of Chairman, etc.
key_sections.description: Addresses the vacation of office by the Chairman of an existing bank and the transfer of employees to the corresponding new bank with existing terms and conditions.

key_sections.title: Obligations as to fidelity and secrecy.
key_sections.description: Imposes obligations on corresponding new banks and their personnel regarding fidelity and secrecy of information.

key_sections.title: Dissolution.
key_sections.description: States that no corresponding new bank shall be placed in liquidation except by order of the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Board of Directors of a corresponding new bank to make regulations for giving effect to the Act's provisions.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To specify head office location (Section 7(1))
Central Government: To constitute the first Board of Directors and appoint members (Section 7(3))
Central Government: To remove and appoint persons to the first Board of Directors (Section 7(3) Proviso)
Central Government: To appoint Custodian and specify emoluments (Section 7(5) Proviso)
Central Government: To give directions on policy matters involving public interest (Section 8)
Central Government: To make schemes for carrying out the Act's provisions (Section 9(1))
Central Government: To amend or vary schemes (Section 9(4))
Central Government: To increase or reduce authorised capital (Section 3(2A) Proviso)
Central Government: To contribute to paid-up capital (Section 3(2B)(b))
Central Government: To reduce paid-up capital (Section 3(2BB)(a))
Central Government: To appoint additional auditors (Section 10(9))
Central Government: To dissolve corresponding new banks (Section 18)
Central Government: To supersede the Board of Directors (Section 18A(1))
Central Government: To appoint an Administrator (Section 18A(2))
Reserve Bank: To appoint additional director (Section 9A)
Board of Directors of corresponding new bank: To exercise general superintendence, direction, and management (Section 7(2))
Board of Directors of corresponding new bank: To increase paid-up capital by transferring from reserve fund (Section 3(2B)(a))
Board of Directors of corresponding new bank: To raise paid-up capital by public issue, rights issue, bonus shares, preferential allotment or private placement (Section 3(2B)(c))
Board of Directors of corresponding new bank: To reduce paid-up capital by paying off excess capital (Section 3(2BB)(b))
Board of Directors of corresponding new bank: To reduce paid-up capital by resolution of shareholders (Section 3(2BBA))
Board of Directors of corresponding new bank: To make regulations (Section 19(1))
Custodian: To exercise all powers and do all acts as chief executive officer until first Board is appointed (Section 7(4))

repealed_acts: The Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Ordinance, 1980 (3 of 1980)
related_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 (5 of 1970)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints the first Board of Directors, Custodian, and Administrator. Reserve Bank may appoint additional directors.

applies_to: certain banking companies
existing bank
exemptions: foreign company within the meaning of section 591 of the Companies Act, 1956

assets, rights, powers, authorities and privileges and property, movable and immovable, cash balances and investments in any country outside India if, under the laws in force in that country, it is not permissible for a banking company, owned or controlled by Government, to carry on the business of banking there
special_provisions: Provisions for transfer of assets and liabilities situated outside India (Section 5(2), 5(3))
Restrictions on shareholding and voting rights for non-Central Government shareholders (Section 3(2D), 3(2E))
Arrangement with corresponding new bank on appointment of directors to prevail over other laws (Section 16A)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for schemes), Board of Directors of a corresponding new bank (for regulations)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Central Government directions, audit by auditors, administration by an Administrator in case of Board supersession.

schedules_summary.description: Lists the 'Existing bank' and its 'Corresponding New Bank'.
Specifies the 'Amount (in lakhs of rupees)' payable to each 'Name of existing bank'.
Contains the 'DECLARATION OF FIDELITY AND SECRECY' form to be made by various officials.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL COMPANY LIMITED (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKINGS) ACT, 1980
act_identification.act_short_title: The National Company Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980
act_identification.date_of_commencement: The provisions of sections 29 and 30 shall come into force at once and the remaining provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 27th day of April, 1980.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of Messrs. National Company Limited with a view to securing the proper management of such undertakings so as to subserve the interests of the general public by ensuring the continued manufacture, production and distribution of articles made of jute, which are essential to the needs of the economy of the country and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS Messrs. National Company Limited had been engaged in the manufacture and production of articles mentioned in the First Schedule to the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 (65 of 1951), namely, textiles made wholly or in part of jute; AND WHEREAS the management of the undertakings of Messrs. National Company Limited was taken over by the Central Government under section 18AA of the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 (65 of 1951); AND WHEREAS it is necessary to acquire the undertakings of Messrs. National Company Limited to ensure that the interests of the general public are served by the continuance, by the undertakings of the Company, of the manufacture, production and distribution of the aforesaid articles, which are essential to the needs of the economy of the country;
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of Messrs. National Company Limited. Its primary goal is to ensure the proper management of these undertakings to serve the general public interest by maintaining the manufacture, production, and distribution of essential jute articles for the country's economy.

chapter_titles: ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF THE UNDERTAKINGS OF THE COMPANY
MANAGEMENT, ETC., OF THE UNDERTAKINGS OF THE COMPANY
PROVISIONS RELATING TO THE EMPLOYEES OF THE COMPANY

key_definitions: words and expressions used herein and not defined but defined in the Companies Act, 1956 (1 of 1956)

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title and the staggered commencement dates for its provisions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as "appointed day," "Commissioner," and "Company."

key_sections.title: Transfer to, and vesting in, the Central Government of the undertakings of the Company.
key_sections.description: States that the undertakings of the Company, including all rights, title, and interest, are transferred to and vested in the Central Government on the appointed day.

key_sections.title: General effect of vesting.
key_sections.description: Details what the undertakings include (assets, rights, properties) and how they are freed from encumbrances upon vesting, and how pending legal proceedings are handled.

key_sections.title: Payment of amount.
key_sections.description: Stipulates the amount of compensation to be paid by the Central Government to the Company for the acquisition of its undertakings.

key_sections.title: Management, etc., of the undertakings of the Company.
key_sections.description: Outlines how the management of the acquired undertakings will be handled, either by an existing/new Government company or by appointed Custodians.

key_sections.title: Continuance of employees.
key_sections.description: Ensures the continuity of employment for the Company's employees, transferring them to the Central Government or the acquiring Government company with existing rights and privileges.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Commissioner of Payments.
key_sections.description: Mandates the appointment of a Commissioner of Payments for disbursing amounts to the Company and handling claims.

key_sections.title: Claims to be made to the Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Specifies the process and timeframe for persons to make claims against the Company to the Commissioner.

key_sections.title: Priority of claims.
key_sections.description: Establishes the order of priorities for claims made to the Commissioner, as detailed in the Schedule.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act will prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws or instruments.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for various wrongful acts related to the Company's property or documents.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the National Company Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Ordinance, 1980, while saving actions taken under it.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To direct vesting of undertakings in a Government company (Section 5), to declare transfer to a new Government company (Section 6), to appoint Custodians (Section 10), to issue directions to Government company/Custodians (Section 11), to take steps for securing possession of undertakings (Section 12), to appoint Commissioner of Payments (Section 15), to assume undischarged liabilities (Section 26), to delegate powers (Section 32), to make rules (Section 33), to remove difficulties (Section 34).

Commissioner of Payments: To appoint assistants (Section 15), to authorise assistants to exercise powers (Section 15), to regulate own procedure (Section 21), to summon witnesses, enforce attendance, discover/produce documents, receive evidence on affidavits, issue commissions for examination of witnesses (Section 21(5)).
Existing/New Government Company: To exercise powers and do things as the Company is authorised to do (Section 10).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 29 prescribes penalties for wrongful withholding or obtaining of property, failure to furnish documents, or making false claims, with imprisonment up to two years and a fine up to ten thousand rupees. Section 30 details that companies committing offences, along with responsible persons and officers, shall be deemed guilty and punished accordingly.

repealed_acts: The National Company Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Ordinance, 1980 (4 of 1980)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the Commissioner of Payments and Custodians. The Commissioner of Payments may also appoint and authorize other persons to assist him in exercising his powers under the Act.

applies_to: Messrs. National Company Limited
undertakings of Messrs. National Company Limited

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the vesting of undertakings in the Central Government or a Government company, with management overseen by these entities or appointed Custodians. A Commissioner of Payments is appointed to manage the disbursement of amounts and settlement of claims. Non-compliance with the Act's provisions, particularly regarding property and documents, is subject to penalties, and the Act's provisions have an overriding effect.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court (for appeals against Commissioner's decision), Civil Court (Commissioner has powers of a civil court for investigations).

schedules_summary.description: This Schedule outlines the order of priorities for claims made against the Company, categorizing them into five parts: Employees' dues (Category I), Secured loans from banks/financial institutions (Category II), Amounts due to trade/other creditors during post-take-over management (Category III), Revenue, taxes, cesses, or other dues to government/local authorities for pre-take-over period (Category IV), and Amounts due to trade/other creditors during pre-take-over management (Category V).

act_identification.act_title: THE ESSENTIAL SERVICES MAINTENANCE (ASSAM) ACT, 1980

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of the State of Assam

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the maintenance of certain essential services and the normal life of the community in Assam.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to ensure the continuous operation of essential services and maintain the normal life of the community in Assam by empowering the State Government to prohibit strikes and prescribing penalties for participation in illegal strikes.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical extent to the whole of the State of Assam.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'essential service', 'State Government', and 'strike'.

key_sections.title: Power to prohibit strikes in certain employments.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government power to prohibit strikes in essential services in Assam for public interest, with provisions for publication and duration of such orders.

key_sections.title: Dismissal of employees participating in illegal strikes.
key_sections.description: States that employees participating in illegal strikes are liable to disciplinary action, including dismissal.

key_sections.title: Penalty for illegal strikes.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for persons participating in illegal strikes, including imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.

key_sections.title: Penalty for instigation, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for persons who instigate or incite others to participate in illegal strikes, including imprisonment up to one year or a fine up to two thousand rupees, or both.

key_sections.title: Penalty for giving financial aid to illegal strikes.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for persons who knowingly provide financial aid to illegal strikes, including imprisonment up to one year or a fine up to two thousand rupees, or both.

key_sections.title: Power to arrest without warrant.
key_sections.description: Grants police officers the power to arrest without warrant any person reasonably suspected of committing an offence under this Act.

key_sections.title: Offences to be tried summarily.
key_sections.description: Mandates that all offences under this Act shall be tried summarily by a specially empowered Judicial Magistrate of the first class.

key_sections.title: Act to override other laws.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall have overriding effect over inconsistent provisions in other laws, including the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Essential Services Maintenance (Assam) Ordinance, 1980, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: State Government: Power to declare any service or employment as an essential service by notification in the official gazette (Section 2(1)(b)(v))
State Government: Power to prohibit strikes in any essential service in the State of Assam (Section 3(1))
State Government: Power to extend the period of strike prohibition orders (Section 3(3))
Police officer: Power to arrest without warrant any person suspected of having committed an offence under this Act (Section 8)
Judicial Magistrate of the first class: Power to try offences under this Act summarily (Section 9)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Participation in illegal strikes is punishable with imprisonment for up to six months or a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both. Instigation, incitement, or furtherance of illegal strikes, and knowingly providing financial aid to illegal strikes, are punishable with imprisonment for up to one year or a fine up to two thousand rupees, or both. Employees participating in illegal strikes are also liable to disciplinary action, including dismissal.

repealed_acts: The Essential Services Maintenance (Assam) Ordinance, 1980 (2 of 1980)

applies_to: persons employed in any essential service in the State of Assam
special_provisions: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Assam (Section 1(2)).
References to laws not in force in any area of the State of Assam shall be construed as references to corresponding laws in force in that area (Section 2(3)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the prohibition of strikes by the State Government, disciplinary actions against employees, and criminal penalties for participation, instigation, or financial aid to illegal strikes, with powers of arrest without warrant and summary trials.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Judicial Magistrate of the first class specially empowered by the State Government

act_identification.act_title: THE BRAHMAPUTRA BOARD ACT, 1980

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Board for the planning and integrated implementation of measures for the control of floods and bank erosion in the Brahmaputra Valley and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: To establish a Board for the planning and integrated implementation of measures for the control of floods and bank erosion in the Brahmaputra Valley and for matters connected therewith.

chapter_titles: FUNCTIONS AND POWERS OF THE BOARD

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to expediency of control by the Union.
key_sections.description: Declares the expediency of Union control over the regulation and development of the inter-State Brahmaputra river valley.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of the Brahmaputra Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Brahmaputra Board as a body corporate and outlines its composition and membership.

key_sections.title: Limits of the Brahmaputra Valley.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to demarcate the limits of the Brahmaputra Valley for the Act's purposes and specifies the Board's operational areas.

key_sections.title: Master Plan for the control of floods, etc., in the Brahmaputra Valley.
key_sections.description: Requires the Board to prepare a Master Plan for flood control, bank erosion, and drainage improvement, considering water resource development.

key_sections.title: Other functions of the Board.
key_sections.description: Details additional functions of the Board, including preparing reports, setting standards, constructing and maintaining dams, and preparing phased programmes.

key_sections.title: Conditions subject to which the Board may perform its functions.
key_sections.description: Lays down conditions for the Board's performance of functions, particularly concerning land availability and cost sharing with State Governments.

key_sections.title: Directions and instructions by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue directions and instructions to the Board for efficient administration of the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Brahmaputra Board Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Brahmaputra Board Fund and specifies its constitution and application for meeting expenses.

key_sections.title: Disputes between the Board and the State Governments.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for resolving disputes between the Board and State Governments, including reference to the Central Government and arbitration.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board the power to make regulations, with Central Government approval, consistent with the Act and rules.

powers_conferred: Board: To establish and incorporate, acquire, hold and dispose of property, contract, sue and be sued (Section 4).
Board: To carry out surveys and investigations and prepare a Master Plan for flood control, bank erosion, and drainage improvement (Section 12).
Board: To prepare detailed reports and estimates, draw up standards, construct, maintain, and operate multi-purpose dams and works (Section 13).
Board: To publish statistics or other information relating to flood control, bank erosion, and drainage (Section 15).
Board: To require State Governments to furnish information (Section 15).
Board: To make regulations with the previous approval of the Central Government (Section 29).
Central Government: To appoint Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and various members to the Board (Section 4).
Central Government: To appoint the General Manager and Financial Adviser of the Board (Sections 7, 8).
Central Government: To appoint Chief Engineers and the Secretary to the Board (Section 9).
Central Government: To demarcate the limits of the Brahmaputra Valley (Section 11).
Central Government: To approve the Master Plan prepared by the Board (Section 12).
Central Government: To approve the Board's construction of dams or projects (Section 13(2)).
Central Government: To specify conditions for the Board's performance of functions, including cost sharing (Section 14).
Central Government: To issue directions and instructions to the Board (Section 17).
Central Government: To pay grants and loans to the Board (Section 18).
Central Government: To resolve disputes between the Board and State Governments, including by arbitration (Section 23).
Central Government: To remove members from the Board and reconstitute the Board (Section 24).
Central Government: To make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (Section 28).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, various members, General Manager, Financial Adviser, Chief Engineers, and Secretary. The Board may appoint other officers and employees.

applies_to: Brahmaputra Valley
Governments of Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur and Tripura
Administrations of Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram
special_provisions: Central Government shall consult the Government of the State before specifying areas within the Brahmaputra Valley for the Board's functions (Section 11(2) Proviso).
State Governments are not required to consult the Board for urgently necessary works due to emergency or extraordinary circumstances (Section 16(3) Proviso).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Board performs its functions under the directions and instructions of the Central Government. Officers of the Board have the power to enter land or premises for carrying out works, surveys, or investigations. Disputes are resolved by the Central Government or through arbitration. Members, officers, and employees of the Board are deemed public servants.

act_identification.act_title: THE SREE CHITRA TIRUNAL INSTITUTE FOR MEDICAL SCIENCES AND TECHNOLOGY, TRIVANDRUM, ACT, 1980
act_identification.act_short_title: the Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology, Trivandrum, Act, 1980

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare the Sree Chitra Tirunal Medical Centre Society for Advanced Studies in Specialities, Trivandrum, in the State of Kerala, to be an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act declares the Sree Chitra Tirunal Medical Centre Society for Advanced Studies in Specialities, Trivandrum, as an institution of national importance and provides for its incorporation. Its main purpose is to promote biomedical engineering and technology, ensure high standards of patient care in advanced medical specialities, and develop top-quality post-graduate training programmes in these fields.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Declaration of the Sree Chitra Tirunal Medical Centre Society for Advanced Studies in Specialities, Trivandrum, as an institution of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the Sree Chitra Tirunal Medical Centre Society as an institution of national importance.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used within the Act.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of Institute.
key_sections.description: Constitutes the Sree Chitra Tirunal Medical Centre Society as a body corporate named Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology, Trivandrum.

key_sections.title: Composition of Institute.
key_sections.description: Outlines the members who shall constitute the Institute, including ex officio members and nominated members.

key_sections.title: Objects of Institute.
key_sections.description: Specifies the primary objectives of the Institute, including promoting biomedical engineering, patient care, and post-graduate training.

key_sections.title: Functions of Institute.
key_sections.description: Details the various functions the Institute may perform to achieve its objects, such as providing teaching, research facilities, and granting degrees.

key_sections.title: Grant of medical degrees, diplomas, etc., by Institute.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Institute to grant medical degrees, diplomas, and other academic distinctions.

key_sections.title: Recognition of medical qualifications granted by Institute.
key_sections.description: Ensures that medical degrees and diplomas granted by the Institute are recognized medical qualifications under the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956.

key_sections.title: Control by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the Institute shall comply with directions issued by the Central Government for efficient administration.

key_sections.title: Transfer of service of existing employees.
key_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of employees from the former Society to the newly incorporated Institute, maintaining their terms and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Institute the power to make regulations, with Central Government approval, to carry out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Institute: to acquire, hold and dispose of property and to contract, and to sue and be sued (Section 4)
Institute: to constitute a Governing Body and other committees (Section 10)
Institute: to appoint a Director (after the first) and other officers and employees (Section 11)

Institute: to provide for post-graduate teaching, research facilities, conduct experiments, prescribe courses, establish and maintain hospitals and research centers, hold examinations, grant degrees/diplomas, institute professorships, receive grants/gifts, deal with property, demand fees, and do other necessary acts (Section 13)
Institute: to maintain a Fund (Section 16)
Institute: to prepare budget (Section 17)
Institute: to maintain proper accounts and prepare annual statements (Section 18)
Institute: to prepare an annual report of its activities (Section 19)
Institute: to constitute pension and provident funds for its employees (Section 20)
Institute: to grant medical degrees, diplomas and other academic distinctions and titles (Section 23)
Institute: to make regulations (Section 32)
Central Government: to appoint the date of commencement of the Act (Section 1)
Central Government: to nominate members to the Institute (Section 5)
Central Government: to nominate the President of the Institute (Section 7)
Central Government: to appoint the first Director of the Institute (Section 11)
Central Government: to pay sums of money to the Institute after appropriation by Parliament (Section 15)
Central Government: to approve the manner of depositing or investing the Fund (Section 16)
Central Government: to prescribe the form and time for the Institute's budget (Section 17)
Central Government: to prescribe the form for the annual statement of accounts (Section 18)
Central Government: to issue directions to the Institute for efficient administration (Section 25)
Central Government: to make final decisions on disputes between the Institute and the Central Government (Section 26)
Central Government: to require reports, returns, and information from the Institute (Section 27)
Central Government: to approve alterations to the tenure, remuneration, and terms of service of transferred employees if to their disadvantage (Section 28)
Central Government: to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions (Section 30)
Central Government: to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (Section 31)
Central Government: to make the first regulations under the Act (Section 32)

authorities_established: Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology, Trivandrum
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government nominates members to the Institute, the President, and the first Director. The Institute appoints the Director (after the first), other officers and employees, and persons to professorships, readerships, and lecturerships.

applies_to: Sree Chitra Tirunal Medical Centre Society for Advanced Studies in Specialities, Trivandrum (now the Institute)
Employees of the Sree Chitra Tirunal Medical Centre Society for Advanced Studies in Specialities, Trivandrum
special_provisions: The Institute shall continue to provide facilities to the Government and people of the State of Kerala and the Central Government, not less favourable than before commencement of the Act (Section 29).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through rules made by the Central Government and regulations made by the Institute (with Central Government approval). The Central Government exercises control by issuing directions and resolving disputes. Accounts are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

act_identification.act_title: THE HOTEL-RECEIPTS TAX ACT, 1980

act_overview.preamble: An Act to impose a special tax on gross receipts of certain hotels.
act_overview.purpose: To impose a special tax on the gross receipts of certain hotels.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'assessee', 'hotel', 'chargeable receipts', and 'room charges'.

key_sections.title: Application of the Act.
key_sections.description: Defines the criteria for hotels to which the Act applies, based on room charges, and how room charges are determined.

key_sections.title: Tax authorities.
key_sections.description: Grants Income-tax authorities powers and functions under this Act similar to those under the Income-tax Act, and outlines their jurisdiction and adherence to Board instructions.

key_sections.title: Charge of tax.
key_sections.description: Imposes a tax at fifteen per cent on chargeable receipts of hotels, with a reduction for receipts in foreign exchange, and addresses arrangements to avoid tax.

key_sections.title: Scope of chargeable receipts.
key_sections.description: Defines what constitutes chargeable receipts, including charges for accommodation, food, drink, and other services, and amounts collected as various taxes, with specific exclusions.

key_sections.title: Computation of chargeable receipts.
key_sections.description: Specifies the deductions allowed when computing chargeable receipts, such as bad debts and certain taxes, and clarifies that no other deductions are permitted.

key_sections.title: Return of chargeable receipts.
key_sections.description: Mandates persons carrying on hotel business to furnish returns of chargeable receipts in the prescribed form and manner, with provisions for extensions and revised returns.

key_sections.title: Penalty for failure to furnish returns, comply with notices, concealment of receipts, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for various defaults including failure to furnish returns, non-compliance with notices, and concealment or inaccurate particulars of chargeable receipts.

key_sections.title: Application of provisions of Income-tax Act.
key_sections.description: States that specific sections and schedules of the Income-tax Act and Income-tax (Certificate Proceedings) Rules, 1962, apply with necessary modifications to this Act.

key_sections.title: Wilful attempt to evade tax, etc.
key_sections.description: Defines offences related to wilful attempts to evade tax, penalty, or interest, and prescribes rigorous imprisonment and fine as punishment.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board, subject to Central Government control, the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes, including specific matters like determining room charges and forms.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to exempt any hotel or class of hotels from the hotel-receipts tax under certain conditions, in public interest or due to peculiar circumstances.

powers_conferred: Income-tax Officer: to assess, re-assess, issue notices, determine room charges, impose penalties.
Commissioner (Appeals): to hear appeals, impose penalties.
Appellate Tribunal: to hear appeals.
Commissioner: to revise orders, institute proceedings, compound offences.
Board (Central Board of Direct Taxes): to make rules, issue orders, instructions and directions.
Central Government: to exempt hotels or classes of hotels, to remove difficulties.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties are prescribed for failure to furnish returns, comply with notices, or conceal receipts (Section 15), and for false estimates or failure to pay advance tax (Section 16). Offences include wilful attempt to evade tax (Section 26), failure to furnish returns (Section 27), failure to produce accounts and documents (Section 28), false statements in verification (Section 29), and abetment of false returns (Section 30). These offences are punishable with rigorous imprisonment (ranging from 3 months to 7 years) and/or fine, with varying degrees based on the amount of tax evaded or the nature of the offence.

related_acts: Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963 (54 of 1963)

applies_to: Every hotel wherein the room charges for residential accommodation provided to any person at any time during the previous year are seventy-five rupees or more per day per individual.
Every person carrying on the business of a hotel in relation to which this Act applies.
exemptions: Charges from persons within the purview of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961 or the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, 1963.
Any hotel or any class of hotels exempted by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Board, subject to the control of the Central Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through assessment by Income-tax Officers, self-assessment, advance payment of tax, and provisions for appeals to the Commissioner (Appeals) and Appellate Tribunal. It includes penalties for non-compliance and criminal prosecution for wilful evasion and other offences. The provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, are applied with necessary modifications for enforcement.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts for prosecution of offences (implied by punishment provisions). High Court or Supreme Court for revision orders.

act_identification.act_title: THE COMPANY SECRETARIES ACT, 1980

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make provision for the regulation and development of the profession of Company Secretaries.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the regulation and development of the profession of Company Secretaries. It establishes the Institute of Company Secretaries of India to manage the affairs of the profession, define membership, and address professional conduct.

chapter_titles: INSTITUTE OF COMPANY SECRETARIES OF INDIA
DISSOLUTION OF THE INSTITUTE OF COMPANY SECRETARIES OF INDIA REGISTERED UNDER THE COMPANIES ACT

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions and interpretation.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act and clarifies when a member is deemed 'to be in practice'.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of the Institute.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Institute of Company Secretaries of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and common seal.

key_sections.title: Entry of names in the Register of members.
key_sections.description: Outlines the eligibility criteria for individuals to have their names entered in the Register of members.

key_sections.title: Certificate of practice.
key_sections.description: Mandates that no member can practice as a Company Secretary without obtaining a certificate of practice from the Council.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Council of the Institute.
key_sections.description: Details the composition of the Council, including elected and nominated members, for managing the Institute's affairs.

key_sections.title: Functions of Council.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the duties and responsibilities of the Council, including approving courses, prescribing fees, and regulating professional standards.

key_sections.title: Register of members.
key_sections.description: Requires the Council to maintain a Register of members, specifying the particulars to be included therein.

key_sections.title: Disciplinary Directorate.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Disciplinary Directorate to investigate complaints and information regarding professional misconduct.

key_sections.title: Professional or other misconduct defined.
key_sections.description: Defines professional or other misconduct by referring to acts or omissions specified in the Schedules to the Act.

key_sections.title: Penalty for falsely claiming to be a member, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals falsely representing themselves as members or practicing without a certificate.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Quality Review Board.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of a Quality Review Board by the Central Government to review the quality of services provided by members.

key_sections.title: Dissolution of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India registered under the Companies Act.
key_sections.description: Provides for the dissolution of the previously registered Institute and the extinguishment of members' rights in it upon the commencement of this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Council the power to make regulations for carrying out the provisions of the Act, covering various aspects of the profession.

powers_conferred: The Institute shall have power to acquire, hold and dispose of property, movable or immovable and shall by its name sue or be sued (Section 3(2)).
The Council may confer on any person Honorary Fellow Membership (Section 4(5)).
The Council may cancel the certificate of practice (Section 6(3)).
The Council shall constitute a Board of Discipline (Section 21A(1)).

The Board of Discipline may reprimand the member, remove the name of the member from the Register up to a period of three months, or impose such fine as it may think fit which may extend to rupees one lakh (Section 21A(3)).
The Council shall constitute a Disciplinary Committee (Section 21B(1)).

The Disciplinary Committee may reprimand the member, remove the name of the member from the Register permanently or for such period, as it thinks fit, or impose such fine as it may think fit, which may extend to rupees five lakhs (Section 21B(3)).

The Authority, the Disciplinary Committee, Board of Discipline and the Director (Discipline) shall have the same powers as are vested in a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for inquiry purposes (Section 21C).
The Council may constitute such Regional Councils as and when it deems fit (Section 23(1)).
The Central Government may, from time to time, issue such directions to the Council as are conducive to the fulfilment of the objects of this Act (Section 35(1)).
The Central Government may, by notification, make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act (Section 38A(1)).
The Council may, by notification in the Gazette of India, make regulations for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of this Act (Section 39(1)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalty for falsely claiming to be a member or practicing without a certificate: fine up to one lakh rupees for first conviction, and imprisonment up to six months or fine up to five lakh rupees or both for subsequent conviction (Section 24). Penalty for using the Council's name or awarding a degree of Company Secretary: imprisonment up to six months or fine not less than one lakh rupees but up to five lakh rupees or both for first conviction, and imprisonment up to one year or fine not less than two lakh rupees but up to ten lakh rupees or both for subsequent conviction (Section 25). Companies engaging in Company Secretaryship: fine not less than two lakh rupees but up to ten lakh rupees for first conviction, and fine not less than four lakh rupees but up to twenty lakh rupees for subsequent conviction (Section 26). Unqualified persons signing documents: fine not less than one lakh rupees but up to five lakh rupees for first conviction, and imprisonment up to one year or fine not less than two lakh rupees but up to ten lakh rupees or both for subsequent conviction (Section 27).

related_acts: the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 (6 of 2009)
the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 (65 of 1951)
the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 (15 of 1992)
the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (42 of 1999)
the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (31 of 2016)
the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908)

authorities_established: Institute of Company Secretaries of India
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government nominates members to the Council, appoints the Presiding Officer and Members of the Tribunal, nominates members to the Disciplinary Committee, and appoints the Chairperson and members of the Quality Review Board. The Council elects the President and Vice-President, appoints the Secretary, Director (Discipline), and other officers/employees, and appoints auditors.

applies_to: Persons whose names are entered in the Register of members of the Institute
Company Secretaries in practice
exemptions: Persons not attaining the age of twenty-one years at the time of application for name entry in the Register of members (Section 8(a))
Persons of unsound mind adjudged by a competent court (Section 8(b))
Undischarged insolvents or undischarged bankrupts (Section 8(c), (ca))
Discharged insolvents who have not obtained a court certificate stating insolvency was caused by misfortune without misconduct (Section 8(d))
Persons convicted by a competent court of an offence involving moral turpitude or a non-technical professional offence, unless pardoned or disability removed by Central Government (Section 8(e))
Persons removed from membership of the Institute for professional or other misconduct (Section 8(f))

A Company Secretary in practice or firm of such Company Secretaries may be exempted by the Council from the requirement of having each branch office in separate charge of a member (Section 37 proviso).
special_provisions: The Central Government or the Council may impose further conditions for non-permanently residing individuals seeking name entry in the Register of members (Section 4(1) proviso).

Transitional provisions for complaints pending before the Council or inquiries initiated by the Disciplinary Committee or references/appeals made to a High Court prior to the commencement of the Company Secretaries (Amendment) Act, 2006 (Section 21D).
Transitional provisions for Regional Councils of the dissolved company to function as Regional Councils of the Institute for a specified period (Section 23(3)).

Provisions for the dissolution of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India registered under the Companies Act, including transfer of assets and liabilities to the new Institute and provisions respecting employees (Chapter IX, Sections 31, 32, 33).
Reciprocity provisions regarding membership and practice for subjects of countries that discriminate against Indian domiciled persons (Section 38).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the Council, which manages the Institute and regulates the profession. Disciplinary actions for professional or other misconduct are handled by the Disciplinary Directorate, Board of Discipline, Disciplinary Committee, and Appellate Authority. Penalties for various offences are prescribed in Chapter VII. The Central Government also has powers to issue directions to the Council and dissolve it in case of persistent default.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil courts (for powers of inquiry under Section 21C). High Courts (for appeals prior to the 2006 amendment, as per Section 21D).

schedules_summary.description: Details professional misconduct in relation to company secretaries in practice, members of the Institute in service, and members of the Institute generally. It also defines other misconduct in relation to members generally.

Details professional misconduct in relation to company secretaries in practice and members of the Institute generally. It also defines other misconduct in relation to members of the Institute generally, typically for more severe offenses.

act_identification.act_title: THE JUTE COMPANIES (NATIONALISATION) ACT, 1980

act_overview.preamble:
An Act to provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of the jute companies, specified in the First Schedule with a view to securing the proper management of such undertakings so as to subserve the interests of the general public by ensuring the continued manufacture, production and distribution of articles made of jute, which are essential to the needs of the economy of the country and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

WHEREAS the said jute companies had been engaged in the manufacture and production of articles
mentioned in the First Schedule to the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 (65 of 1951),
namely, textiles made wholly or in part of jute;

AND WHEREAS the management of the undertakings of each of the said jute companies was
taken over by the Central Government under the Industries (Development and Regulation)
Act, 1951 (65 of 1951);

AND WHEREAS it is necessary to acquire the undertakings of the said jute companies to ensure that the
interests of the general public are served by the continuance, by the undertakings of the said jute
companies, of the manufacture, production and distribution of the aforesaid articles which are essential to
the needs of the economy of the country;

BE it enacted by Parliament in the Thirty-first Year of the Republic of India as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of specified jute companies. This is done to ensure proper management, continued manufacture, production, and distribution of essential jute articles, thereby serving the interests of the general public and the country's economy.

chapter_titles: ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF THE UNDERTAKINGS OF THE JUTE COMPANIES
MANAGEMENT, ETC., OF THE UNDERTAKINGS OF THE JUTE COMPANIES
PROVISIONS RELATING TO EMPLOYEES OF THE JUTE COMPANIES

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Transfer to, and vesting in, the Central Government of the undertakings of the jute companies.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the undertakings of jute companies are transferred to and vested in the Central Government on the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of the undertakings of the jute companies in Jute Manufactures Corporation.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to vest the acquired undertakings in the Jute Manufactures Corporation.

key_sections.title: Payment of amount.

key_sections.title: Continuance of employees.
key_sections.description: Ensures the continued employment of persons working in the undertakings, either under the Central Government or the Jute Manufactures Corporation.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Commissioner of Payments.
key_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to appoint a Commissioner of Payments for disbursing amounts to jute companies.

key_sections.title: Claims to be made to the Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Specifies the procedure and timeframe for persons to make claims against jute companies to the Commissioner.

key_sections.title: Priority of Claims.
key_sections.description: Outlines the principles for prioritizing claims made to the Commissioner.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in other laws or instruments.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for various wrongful acts related to the undertakings of jute companies.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to direct vesting of undertakings in Jute Manufactures Corporation (Section 6)
Central Government: Power to make payments to jute companies (Sections 7 and 8)
Central Government: Power to issue directions to Jute Manufactures Corporation (Section 10)
Central Government: Power to appoint Commissioner of Payments and assistants (Section 14)
Central Government: Power to make rules for carrying out the Act (Section 32)
Central Government: Power to remove difficulties in implementing the Act (Section 33)
Central Government: Power to delegate its powers (Section 31)
Jute Manufactures Corporation: Power to manage affairs and business of vested undertakings (Section 9)
Jute Manufactures Corporation: Power to receive money due to jute companies (Section 16)

Commissioner of Payments: Power to regulate his own procedure and exercise powers of a Civil Court for investigations (Section 20(5))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who wrongfully withholds property, obtains possession, fails to furnish documents, fails to deliver assets, or removes/destroys property of the nationalised jute companies, or prefers a false claim, shall be punishable with imprisonment for up to two years and a fine up to ten thousand rupees. important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the Commissioner of Payments and other persons to assist the Commissioner.

implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court (for appeals against Commissioner's decisions); Commissioner of Payments has powers of a Civil Court for investigations.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL SECURITY ACT, 1980

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for preventive detention in certain cases and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: To provide for preventive detention in certain cases and for matters connected therewith.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, such as 'appropriate Government' and 'detention order'.

key_sections.title: Power to make orders detaining certain persons.
key_sections.description: Grants power to Central or State Governments, and in certain cases, District Magistrates or Commissioners of Police, to issue detention orders for preventive reasons.

key_sections.title: Grounds of detention severable.
key_sections.description: Ensures that a detention order based on multiple grounds remains valid even if some grounds are found to be invalid.

key_sections.title: Powers in relation to absconding persons.
key_sections.description: Outlines powers of the government or officers to deal with persons who abscond or conceal themselves to avoid detention orders.

key_sections.title: Grounds of order of detention to be disclosed to persons affected by the order.
key_sections.description: Mandates the disclosure of detention grounds to the detained person and provides an opportunity for representation.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Advisory Boards.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of Advisory Boards by Central and State Governments to review detention cases.

key_sections.title: Reference to Advisory Boards.
key_sections.description: Requires detention cases to be referred to Advisory Boards within a specified period.

key_sections.title: Action upon the report of the Advisory Board.
key_sections.description: Specifies the action to be taken by the appropriate Government based on the Advisory Board's report, either confirming or revoking the detention order.

key_sections.title: Maximum period of detention.
key_sections.description: Sets the maximum period for which a person may be detained under the Act, which is twelve months.

key_sections.title: Revocation of detention orders.
key_sections.description: Allows for the revocation or modification of detention orders by the Central or State Government.

key_sections.title: Circumstances in which persons may be detained for periods longer than three months without obtaining the opinion of Advisory Boards.
key_sections.description: Provides for extended detention without Advisory Board opinion in specific circumstances related to disturbed areas and terrorist activities.

key_sections.title: Temporary release of persons detained.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to temporarily release detained persons under specified conditions.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Grants immunity from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the National Security Ordinance, 1980, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Central Government or State Government: Power to make orders detaining certain persons (Section 3)
District Magistrate or Commissioner of Police: Power to make orders detaining certain persons (Section 3(3))
Appropriate Government: Power to regulate place and conditions of detention (Section 5)
Central Government or State Government or officer: Power to make report to Magistrate and direct absconding persons to appear (Section 7)
Central Government and each State Government: Power to constitute Advisory Boards (Section 9)
Appropriate Government: Power to confirm or revoke detention orders based on Advisory Board report (Section 12)
Appropriate Government: Power to revoke or modify detention orders (Section 14)
Appropriate Government: Power to direct temporary release of persons detained (Section 15)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Failure to comply with an order to appear under Section 7(1)(b) is punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both. Failure to surrender after temporary release under Section 15(1) is punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both. Failure to fulfill conditions of release or bond under Section 15(1) results in forfeiture of the bond.

repealed_acts: The National Security Ordinance, 1980 (11 of 1980)
related_acts: Prevention of Black marketing and Maintenance of Supplies of Essential Commodities Act, 1980 (7 of 1980)
Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Ordinance, 1987 (Ord. 2 of 1987)

foreigner
exemptions: Orders of detention made under any State law in force immediately before the commencement of the National Security Ordinance, 1980 (11 of 1980).
special_provisions: Special powers for District Magistrate or Commissioner of Police in certain areas (Section 3(3)).
Special provisions for detention periods longer than three months without Advisory Board opinion in disturbed areas (Section 14A).
Special provisions for Union territories regarding Advisory Board appointments (Section 9(3)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Detention orders are executed in the manner provided for warrants of arrest under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Advisory Boards review detention cases and report to the appropriate Government for confirmation or revocation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class (for reporting absconding persons).

act_identification.act_title: THE HIND CYCLES LIMITED AND SEN-RALEIGH LIMITED (NATIONALISATION) ACT, 1980
act_identification.act_short_title: the Hind Cycles Limited and Sen-Raleigh Limited (Nationalisation) Act, 1980

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the acquisition of the undertakings of Hind Cycles Limited and Sen-Raleigh Limited. This acquisition aims to ensure the proper management and continued manufacture, production, and distribution of bicycles and their components, which are essential for the country's economy and public interest.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its deemed date of commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'Commissioner', 'Custodian', and 'two companies'.

key_sections.title: Transfer to, and vesting in, the Central Government of the undertakings of the two companies.
key_sections.description: Mandates the transfer and vesting of the undertakings of Hind Cycles Limited and Sen-Raleigh Limited, including all rights, title, and interest, to the Central Government on the appointed day.

key_sections.title: General effect of vesting.
key_sections.description: Details what the undertakings include (assets, rights, properties, etc.) and specifies that vested properties are freed from encumbrances. It also addresses the continuation of licenses and pending legal proceedings.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of the undertakings of the two Companies in two Government Companies.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to direct that the vested undertakings and specified liabilities be transferred to and vest in Government companies instead of continuing to vest in the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Payment of amount.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the Central Government shall pay an amount, as specified in the First Schedule, to each of the two companies for the acquisition and vesting of their undertakings.

key_sections.title: Management, etc., of the undertakings of the two companies.
key_sections.description: Outlines how the management of the acquired undertakings will be handled, either by a specified Government company or by Custodians appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Continuance of employees.
key_sections.description: Ensures the continued employment of persons working in the undertakings, transferring them to the Central Government or the concerned Government company with existing rights and privileges.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Commissioner of Payments.
key_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to appoint a Commissioner of Payments for disbursing amounts payable to the two companies under the Act.

key_sections.title: Claims to be made to the Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Specifies that all claims against the two companies regarding matters in the Third Schedule must be preferred before the Commissioner within a stipulated period.

key_sections.title: Priority of claims.
key_sections.description: Establishes the principles for prioritizing and settling claims made under the Act, based on categories specified in the Third Schedule.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws, instruments, decrees, or orders.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for various offenses such as wrongfully withholding property, failing to furnish documents, or making false claims.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act and specifies matters for which rules may be made.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Hind Cycles Limited and Sen-Raleigh Limited (Nationalisation) Ordinance, 1980, and includes a saving clause for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

act_identification.act_title: THE BIRD AND COMPANY LIMITED (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKINGS AND OTHER PROPERTIES) ACT, 1980
act_identification.act_short_title: the Bird and Company Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings and Other Properties ) Act, 1980

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of the Bird and Company Limited for the purpose of ensuring the continuity of production of goods which are vital to the needs of the country and for the acquisition of shares held by the Bird and Company Limited in the specified companies for the purpose of securing to those undertakings the facilities and advantages derived by reason of such shareholding with respect to the operation and functioning of those undertakings and also to enable the Central Government to exercise such control over the affairs of the specified companies as is necessary to ensure that the affairs of those companies are not mismanaged and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS the Bird and Company Limited were engaged in the manufacture of E.O.T. cranes and other varieties of cranes; polystyrene based cation exchange resin; equipment for fertilizers, oil refineries, steel plants, petro-chemical and other industries; tanks and vessels of various shapes and sizes, water treatment equipment and other types of equipment for the control of water pollution and were also engaged in various other activities; AND WHEREAS the top management of the Bird and Company Limited had so mismanaged the affairs of that Company as to cause heavy losses to the Company and had also managed the affairs of the Company in a manner prejudicial to the interests of the Company and the public interest; AND WHEREAS in view of the mismanagement aforesaid, the Central Government had, in pursuance of the provisions of section 408 of the Companies Act, 1956 (1 of 1956), appointed six directors on the Board of directors of the Bird and Company Limited; AND WHEREAS investment of a large amount is necessary for the maintenance and development of the production of the undertakings of the Company; AND WHEREAS it is necessary in the public interest to acquire the undertakings of the Bird and Company Limited to enable the Central Government to have such investment made and to ensure that the interests of the general public are served by the continuance, by the undertakings of the Company, of the manufacture, production and distribution of goods or articles which are essential to the needs of the economy of the country; AND WHEREAS the Bird and Company Limited is holding shares in the specified companies which are either engaged in the production, distribution or marketing of goods which are vital to the needs of the country or are engaged in providing finance to other companies which are so engaged and it is expedient in the public interest to acquire the said shares to secure for the undertakings of the Company the facilities and advantages derived by reason of such shareholding with respect to the operation and functioning of such undertakings and also to enable the Central Government to exercise, through such shareholdings, such control on the affairs of those companies as may be necessary to prevent their mismanagement;
act_overview.purpose: The Act provides for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of Bird and Company Limited and shares held by it in specified companies. This is to ensure continuity of production of vital goods, secure operational advantages for the undertakings, and enable the Central Government to control the affairs of specified companies to prevent mismanagement, all in the public interest.

act_identification.act_title: THE VAN (SANRAKSHAN EVAM SAMVARDHAN) ADHINIYAM, 1980

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Thirty-first Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS, the importance of forests is to be realised to enable achievement of national targets of Net Zero Emission by 2070 and maintain or enhance the forest carbon stocks through ecologically balanced sustainable development; AND WHEREAS, [Nationally] Determined Contribution targets of the country envisage creating carbon sink of additional 2.5 to 3.0 billion tons of CO2 equivalent by 2030; AND WHEREAS, the country envisages an increase in the forest and tree cover to one-third of its land area, which is to be given impetus with an enhanced growth trajectory; AND WHEREAS, India has a rich tradition of preserving forests and their bio-diversity, and, therefore, enhancing forest based economic, social and environmental benefits, including improvement of livelihoods for forest dependent communities is envisaged; AND WHEREAS, it is necessary to provide for provisions relating to conservation management and restoration of forests, maintaining ecological security, sustaining cultural and traditional values of forests and facilitating economic needs and carbon neutrality.
act_overview.purpose: An Act to provide for the conservation of forests and for matters connected therewith or ancillary or incidental thereto.

act_identification.act_short_title: the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the prevention, control and abatement of air pollution, for the establishment, with a view to carrying out the aforesaid purposes, of Boards, for conferring on and assigning to such Boards powers and functions relating thereto and for matters connected therewith. WHEREAS decisions were taken at the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment held in Stockholm in June, 1972, in which India participated, to take appropriate steps for the preservation of the natural resources of the earth which, among other things, include the preservation of the quality of air and control of air pollution; AND WHEREAS it is considered necessary to implement the decisions aforesaid in so far as they relate to the preservation of the quality of air and control of air pollution;
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to prevent, control, and abate air pollution across India. It establishes Central and State Boards to carry out these functions, granting them powers to set standards, monitor emissions, and enforce compliance to preserve air quality.
