key_sections.description: Establishes the Act's name, geographical reach, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Central Pollution Control Board.
key_sections.description: Designates the CPCB (from Water Act) to also function under this Act for air pollution control.

key_sections.title: Constitution of State Boards.
key_sections.description: Outlines the formation and composition of State Boards for air pollution control.

key_sections.title: Functions of Central Board.
key_sections.description: Details the duties and responsibilities of the Central Board, including advising government, planning programs, and setting standards.

key_sections.title: Functions of State Boards.
key_sections.description: Specifies the duties of State Boards, such as planning programs, inspecting plants, and laying down emission standards.

key_sections.title: Power to give directions.
key_sections.description: Grants power to Central/State Governments and Central Board to issue binding directions.

key_sections.title: Power to declare air pollution control areas.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to designate and regulate air pollution control areas.

key_sections.title: Restrictions on use of certain industrial plants.
key_sections.description: Requires previous consent from the State Board to establish or operate industrial plants in air pollution control areas.

key_sections.title: Persons carrying on industry, etc., not to allow emission of air pollutants in excess of the standard laid down by State Board.
key_sections.description: Prohibits persons from discharging air pollutants in excess of standards set by the State Board.

key_sections.title: Power of Board to make application to court for restraining persons from causing air pollution.
key_sections.description: Allows Boards to seek court orders to prevent persons from causing air pollution exceeding standards.

key_sections.title: Power of entry and inspection.
key_sections.description: Authorizes empowered persons to enter and inspect premises for compliance with the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to give directions.
key_sections.description: Grants Boards power to issue binding directions, including for closure or regulation of industries.

key_sections.title: Failure to comply with the provisions of section 22 or section 31A.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for non-compliance with emission standards or Board directions.

key_sections.title: Offences for failure to comply with provisions of section 21 and for failure to pay penalty.
key_sections.description: Specifies punishments, including imprisonment and fines, for operating without consent or failing to pay penalties.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to frame rules for implementing the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to frame rules for implementing the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint commencement date (S.1(3)), give directions to Central Board (S.18(1)(a)), exempt industrial plants (S.21(1) Proviso), appoint adjudicating officers (S.39A(1)), make rules (S.53).

State Government: To constitute State Boards (S.5), declare air pollution control areas (S.19), prohibit use of certain fuels/materials (S.19(3),(5)), give instructions to motor vehicle registration authorities (S.20), supersede State Board (S.47), make rules (S.54).

Central Board: To advise Central Government (S.16(2)(a)), plan nationwide programmes (S.16(2)(b)), coordinate State Boards (S.16(2)(c)), provide technical assistance (S.16(2)(d)), lay down air quality standards (S.16(2)(h)), give directions to State Boards (S.18(1)(b)), exercise powers of State Board in Union territories (S.6), issue directions (S.31A).

State Board: To plan comprehensive programmes (S.17(1)(a)), advise State Government (S.17(1)(b)), inspect industrial plants/control equipment (S.17(1)(e)), lay down emission standards (S.17(1)(g)), grant/refuse consent for industrial plants (S.21), make application to court for restraining air pollution (S.22A), enter and inspect (S.24), obtain information (S.25), take samples (S.26), issue directions (S.31A).
Adjudicating Officer: To hold inquiry and impose penalties (S.39A).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 37 prescribes penalties for failure to comply with Section 22 or directions under Section 31A, ranging from ten thousand rupees to fifteen lakh rupees, with additional daily penalties for continuing contravention. Section 38 outlines penalties for acts like destroying Board property, obstructing officers, or failing to furnish information, with similar monetary penalties. Section 38A imposes penalties on Government Department heads and officers for contraventions. Section 39 covers general contraventions not otherwise specified, with penalties from ten thousand rupees to fifteen lakh rupees and additional daily penalties. Section 39D specifies punishments, including imprisonment (from one year six months up to seven years) and fines, for failure to comply with Section 21 (operating without consent) and for failure to pay imposed penalties.

repealed_acts: Section 50 (Power to amend the Schedule) by Act 47 of 1987
The Schedule by Act 47 of 1987
related_acts: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 (6 of 1974)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government nominates Chairman and members of State Boards, appoints member-secretary, appoints Government analysts, and appoints Appellate Authority. State Board appoints officers, employees, and consultants, and Board analysts. Central Government appoints adjudicating officers.

applies_to: Whole of India
Persons establishing or operating industrial plants in air pollution control areas
Persons carrying on industry or operating control equipment
Government Departments
Companies
exemptions: Central Government may exempt certain categories of industrial plants from consent requirement (S.21(1) Proviso).
Provisions of this Act do not apply to radioactive air pollution covered by the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 (S.52).
special_provisions: In Union territories, the Central Board exercises powers and functions of a State Board (S.6).
State Boards constituted under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, are deemed State Boards under this Act (S.4).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement involves the declaration of air pollution control areas, restrictions on industrial plants and emissions, issuance of directions by Boards, powers of entry, inspection, and sampling, analysis of samples by State Air Laboratories, and penalties/punishments for non-compliance. Adjudication of penalties is done by adjudicating officers, with appeals to the Appellate Authority and National Green Tribunal. State Boards can also be superseded by the State Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class (for restraining air pollution and cognizance of offences). Appellate Authority (for appeals against State Board orders). National Green Tribunal (for appeals against Appellate Authority orders and adjudicating officer orders). Civil courts are barred from jurisdiction on matters determinable by the Appellate Authority.

act_identification.act_title: THE HIGH COURT AT BOMBAY (EXTENSION OF JURISDICTION TO GOA, DAMAN AND DIU) ACT, 1981
act_identification.act_short_title: High Court at Bombay (Extension of Jurisdiction to Goa, Daman and Diu) Act, 1981

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the extension of the jurisdiction of the High Court at Bombay to the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu, for the establishment of a permanent bench of that High Court at Panaji and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to extend the jurisdiction of the High Court at Bombay to the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu. It also provides for the establishment of a permanent bench of the Bombay High Court at Panaji and addresses related matters.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Act's short title and specifies that its commencement date will be appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day' and 'Court of the Judicial Commissioner'.

key_sections.title: Extension of jurisdiction of Bombay High Court to Goa, Daman and Diu.
key_sections.description: Extends the jurisdiction of the High Court at Bombay to the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu, and abolishes the Court of the Judicial Commissioner.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of Bombay High Court.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the High Court at Bombay all jurisdiction, powers, and authority previously exercised by the Court of the Judicial Commissioner in the specified territories.

key_sections.title: Chapter VI of Part VI of the Constitution to apply to the Bombay High Court exercising jurisdiction over the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu.
key_sections.description: Applies provisions of Chapter VI of Part VI of the Constitution to the Bombay High Court's jurisdiction over Goa, Daman and Diu, with specified exceptions and modifications.

key_sections.title: Special provisions relating to advocates.
key_sections.description: Allows advocates entitled to practice in the Court of the Judicial Commissioner to practice in the High Court at Bombay.

key_sections.title: Transfer of pending proceedings from the Court of the Judicial Commissioner to the Bombay High Court.
key_sections.description: Mandates the transfer of all pending proceedings from the abolished Court of the Judicial Commissioner to the High Court at Bombay.

key_sections.title: Establishment of a permanent bench of Bombay High Court at Panaji.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of a permanent bench of the High Court at Bombay at Panaji, with judges nominated by the Chief Justice.

key_sections.title: Allocation of expenditure of the Bombay High Court.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the expenditure of the Bombay High Court will be allocated between the State of Maharashtra and the Union as determined by the President.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Power to adapt laws.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to adapt and modify laws to facilitate their application in the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to appoint the commencement date of the Act (Section 1(2))
Central Government: to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act (Section 13)
Central Government: to adapt and modify laws for application in the Union territory (Section 14)
President: to determine the proportion of expenditure allocation for the Bombay High Court (Section 10)
Chief Justice of the High Court at Bombay: to nominate judges for the permanent bench at Panaji (Section 9)
Chief Justice of the High Court at Bombay: to order any case or class of cases to be heard at Bombay (Section 9 proviso)
High Court at Bombay: to make rules or give directions regarding advocates' practice (Section 6)

amended_acts: Goa, Daman and Diu Act 16 of 1965

authorities_established: permanent bench of the High Court at Bombay at Panaji

applies_to: Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu
advocates entitled to practise in the Court of the Judicial Commissioner
special_provisions: Modifications to Chapter VI of Part VI of the Constitution for its application to the High Court at Bombay in relation to the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu (Section 5)
Discretion of the Chief Justice of the High Court at Bombay to order cases arising in the territory to be heard at Bombay (Section 9 proviso)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for removing difficulties and adapting laws); High Court at Bombay (for advocates)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government is empowered to issue orders to remove difficulties and adapt laws. The High Court at Bombay is vested with jurisdiction and powers over the specified territory.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court at Bombay

act_identification.act_title: THE EXPORT-IMPORT BANK OF INDIA ACT, 1981
act_identification.act_short_title: The Export-Import Bank of India Act, 1981

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish a corporation to be known as the Export-Import Bank of India for providing financial assistance to exporters and importers, and for functioning as the principal financial institution for co-ordinating the working of institutions engaged in financing export and import of goods and services with a view to promoting the country’s international trade and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: To establish the Export-Import Bank of India to provide financial assistance to exporters and importers. It also functions as the principal financial institution for coordinating institutions financing export and import, aiming to promote India's international trade.

chapter_titles: ESTABLISHMENT OF THE EXPORT-IMPORT BANK OF INDIA AND INCORPORATION THEREOF
TRANSFER OF PART OF BUSINESS OF DEVELOPMENT BANK

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its application to the whole of India, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Exim Bank', 'export', 'import', 'goods', and 'services'.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Export-Import Bank of India.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of the Export-Import Bank of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

key_sections.title: Management.
key_sections.description: Vests the general superintendence, direction, and management of the Exim Bank's affairs in the Board, guided by Central Government directions on policy matters.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Board.
key_sections.description: Details the composition of the Board of Directors, including the appointment of chairman, managing director, whole-time directors, and nominated directors.

key_sections.title: Business of Exim Bank.
key_sections.description: Outlines the various types of business the Exim Bank may conduct, including granting loans, underwriting issues, issuing guarantees, and financing international trade.

key_sections.title: Export Development Fund.
key_sections.description: Requires the Exim Bank to establish a special fund called the Export Development Fund.

key_sections.title: Transfer of part of business of Development Bank.
key_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of export financing functions, assets, and liabilities from the Industrial Development Bank of India to the Exim Bank.

key_sections.title: Obligation as to fidelity and secrecy.
key_sections.description: Imposes an obligation on the Exim Bank and its personnel to maintain fidelity and secrecy regarding its constituents' affairs, with exceptions for information sharing.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board the power to make regulations, with Central Government approval, for implementing the Act's provisions.

powers_conferred: Exim Bank may grant loans and advances by itself or in participation with any bank or financial institution for export or import purposes (Section 10(1)).
Exim Bank may underwrite the issue of stocks, shares, bonds or debentures of any company engaged in export or import (Section 10(2)(b)).
Exim Bank may issue bid bonds or guarantees in or outside India (Section 10(2)(c)).
Exim Bank may accept, collect, discount, re-discount, purchase, sell or negotiate bills of exchange or promissory notes arising out of export or import transactions (Section 10(2)(d)).
Exim Bank may grant lines of credit to foreign governments, financial institutions, or persons outside India for export or import (Section 10(2)(g)).
Exim Bank may borrow money from the Reserve Bank or other approved authorities/institutions and accept deposits (Section 12).
Exim Bank may borrow foreign currency with previous consent of the Central Government (Section 13).
Exim Bank may receive gifts, grants, donations or benefactions (Section 14).
Exim Bank shall establish an Export Development Fund (Section 15).
Exim Bank may appoint officers and other employees and determine their terms and conditions (Section 27(1)).
Board may delegate its powers and functions to any director, officer, or employee (Section 28).
Board may, with previous approval of the Central Government, make regulations (Section 39).

related_acts: Industrial Development Bank of India Act, 1964 (18 of 1964)
Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the chairman, managing director, whole-time directors, and nominated directors to the Board (Section 6). The Central Government appoints auditors for the Exim Bank and the Export Development Fund (Section 19(3), 24(1)).

applies_to: Whole of India
Exporters
Importers
Scheduled banks
Financial institutions
exemptions: The Exim Bank is exempt from the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, except for section 34A and section 36AD thereof (Section 36).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Board, with the previous approval of the Central Government (Section 39).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The general superintendence, direction, and management of the Exim Bank's affairs and business vest in the Board. The Central Government may give written directions in matters of policy involving public interest. Accounts are audited by appointed auditors and may be examined by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the form for the 'DECLARATION OF FIDELITY AND SECRECY' to be made by directors, committee members, auditors, officers, or other employees of the Exim Bank.
This schedule has been repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 1988.

act_identification.act_title: THE BRITISH INDIA CORPORATION LIMITED (ACQUISITION OF SHARES) ACT, 1981
act_identification.act_short_title: The British India Corporation Limited (Acquisition of Shares) Act, 1981

act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the acquisition of shares of the British India Corporation Limited by the Central Government to ensure proper management, continuity, and development of production of vital goods. It aims to facilitate further investment and secure effective control over the company's affairs.

chapter_titles: ACQUISITION OF THE SHARES OF THE COMPANY

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name and its deemed commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as "appointed day", "Commissioner", and "share".

key_sections.title: Transfer and vesting of shares of the Company in the Central Government.
key_sections.description: Mandates the transfer and vesting of all shares of the Company to the Central Government on the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Management of the Company.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make provisions for the Company to function as a Government company, including changes to its Board and articles of association.

key_sections.title: Payment of amounts.
key_sections.description: Stipulates the amount to be paid by the Central Government to shareholders for the acquired shares and the interest thereon.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Commissioner of Payments.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of a Commissioner to disburse payments to shareholders and outlines the Commissioner's powers and assistance.

key_sections.title: Claims to be made to the Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Requires shareholders to prefer claims for payment to the Commissioner within a specified period.

key_sections.title: Admission or rejection of claims.
key_sections.description: Details the Commissioner's procedure for examining, admitting, or rejecting claims, including powers of a civil court.

key_sections.title: Disbursement of money by the Commissioner to claimants.
key_sections.description: Specifies the rates at which the Commissioner shall pay for preference and ordinary shares and the discharge of government liability upon payment.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the Act's provisions shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in other laws or instruments.

key_sections.title: Penalties.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.

powers_conferred: Central Government: make provisions for company management (Section 4)
Central Government: appoint Commissioner of Payments (Section 6(1))
Central Government: make rules (Section 20)
Central Government: sanction cognizance of offences (Section 19)
Commissioner: appoint other persons to assist (Section 6(2))
Commissioner: authorise assistants to exercise powers (Section 6(2))
Commissioner: examine claims (Section 9)
Commissioner: admit or reject claims (Section 10)
Commissioner: regulate own procedure (Section 10(5))

Commissioner: refer disputes to civil court (Section 14)
Commissioner: deposit amount in court (Section 15)

A Commissioner of Payments is appointed to manage claims and disburse compensation to shareholders. The Act has overriding effect over other laws. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance and false claims.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Principal civil court of original jurisdiction (for appeals against Commissioner's decisions and for disputes referred by Commissioner). Courts for cognizance of offences.

act_identification.act_title: THE DALMIA DADRI CEMENT LIMITED (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKINGS) ACT, 1981

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of the Dalmia Dadri Cement Limited with a view to securing the proper management of such undertakings so as to subserve the interest of the general public by ensuring the continued manufacture, production and distribution of cement which is essential to the needs of the economy of the country and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS Messrs. Dalmia Dadri Cement Limited had been engaged in the manufacture and production of portland cement, an article mentioned in the First Schedule to the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 (65 of 1951); AND WHEREAS an order has been made for the winding up of the Company and proceedings for its liquidation are pending in the High Court of Punjab and Haryana; AND WHEREAS the undertakings of the Company have not been functioning since March, 1980; AND WHEREAS it is necessary to acquire the undertakings of the said Company to ensure that the interests of the general public are served by the continuance, by the undertakings of the said Company, of the manufacture, production and distribution of portland cement which is essential to the needs of the economy of the country;
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of Dalmia Dadri Cement Limited. Its main objective is to ensure the continued manufacture, production, and distribution of cement, which is vital for the economy, thereby serving the interest of the general public.

chapter_titles: ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF THE UNDERTAKINGS OF THE COMPANY
MANAGEMENT, ETC., OF THE UNDERTAKINGS OF THE COMPANY
PROVISIONS RELATING TO THE EMPLOYEES OF THE COMPANY

key_sections.title: Definitions.

key_sections.title: Transfer to, and vesting in, the Central Government of the undertakings of the Company.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Commissioner of Payments.

repealed_acts: The Dalmia Dadri Cement Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Ordinance, 1981 (6 of 1981)

act_identification.act_title: THE CINE-WORKERS WELFARE FUND ACT, 1981

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the financing of activities to promote the welfare of certain cine-workers.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the financing of activities aimed at promoting the welfare of cine-workers. It establishes a Cine-workers Welfare Fund to meet expenditures related to welfare measures, grants, loans, and other schemes for cine-workers.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.

key_sections.title: Definition.

key_sections.title: Cine-workers Welfare Fund.

key_sections.title: Application of Fund.

key_sections.title: Advisory Committees.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to constitute Advisory Committees to advise on matters related to the administration and application of the Fund.

key_sections.title: Central Advisory Committee.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Welfare Commissioners, etc., and their powers.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of Welfare Commissioners, Welfare Administrators, Inspectors, and other staff, and defines their powers and duties.

key_sections.title: Annual report of activities financed under the Act.
key_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to publish an annual report on activities financed by the Act and a statement of accounts.

key_sections.title: Power to call for information.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to appoint commencement date (Section 1(3))

act_identification.act_title: THE MARITIME ZONES OF INDIA (REGULATION OF FISHING BY FOREIGN VESSELS) ACT, 1981
act_identification.act_short_title: the Maritime Zones of India (Regulation of Fishing by Foreign Vessels) Act, 1981

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the regulation of fishing by foreign vessels in certain maritime zones of India and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate fishing activities conducted by foreign vessels within India's maritime zones, including its territorial waters and exclusive economic zone, and to address related issues.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II REGULATION OF FISHING BY FOREIGN VESSELS
CHAPTER III POWERS OF SEARCH AND SEIZURE

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement provisions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'exclusive economic zone of India', 'fish', 'fishing', 'foreign vessel', and 'maritime zones of India'.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of fishing in maritime zones of India by foreign vessels.
key_sections.description: Prohibits foreign vessels from fishing in India's maritime zones without a valid licence or permit.

key_sections.title: Grant of licences.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for applying for and granting licences to foreign vessel owners for fishing in Indian maritime zones.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of fishing by Indian citizens, etc., using foreign vessels.
key_sections.description: Specifies the requirement for Indian citizens or entities using foreign vessels for fishing to obtain a permit.

key_sections.title: Authorised officers and their powers
key_sections.description: Grants powers to officers of the Coast Guard or other authorised government officers to stop, board, search, seize vessels, and arrest persons for non-compliance.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of section 3.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for foreign vessels fishing in Indian maritime zones without a licence or permit.

key_sections.title: Confiscation of vessels, etc.
key_sections.description: Provides for the confiscation of foreign vessels, fishing gear, and catch upon conviction for certain offences.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Addresses liability for offences committed by companies, including directors and other officers.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable.
key_sections.description: Declares all offences under this Act to be cognizable.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government to grant licences and permits
Central Government to specify ports
Central Government to permit foreign vessels for scientific research, investigation, or experimental fishing
Central Government to make rules
Central Government to remove difficulties
Authorised officers (Coast Guard or other government officers) to stop, board, search, seize vessels, and arrest persons
Magistrates to order retention or custody of seized vessels/things and authorise sale of fish
Magistrates to impose enhanced penalties
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties include imprisonment up to three years or fine up to rupees fifteen lakhs for contravention of section 3 in territorial waters, and fine up to rupees ten lakhs in the exclusive economic zone. Contravention of licence provisions carries a fine up to rupees ten lakhs. Contravention of permit provisions carries a fine up to rupees five lakhs (for area/method) or rupees fifty thousand (for other cases). Contravention of section 7 (stowing gear) carries a fine up to rupees five lakhs. Obstruction of authorised officers carries imprisonment up to one year or fine up to rupees fifty thousand or both. Vessels, fishing gear, equipment, stores, cargo, and fish are liable to confiscation upon conviction.

related_acts: Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and other Maritime Zones Act, 1976

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government has the power to authorise officers for enforcement and to grant licences and permits.

owner of a foreign vessel
master of a foreign vessel
Indian citizens using foreign vessels
companies committing offences
exemptions: Foreign vessels permitted by the Central Government for scientific research, investigation, or experimental fishing.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced by authorised officers (from the Coast Guard or other government departments) who have powers of search, seizure, and arrest. Offences are cognizable and tried by Metropolitan Magistrates or Judicial Magistrates of the first class. The Central Government makes rules for implementation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate competent to try an offence under this Act, Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class

act_identification.act_title: THE ANTI-APARTHEID (UNITED NATIONS CONVENTION) ACT, 1981

act_overview.preamble: An Act to give effect to the International Convention on the Suppression and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid. WHEREAS an International Convention on the Suppression and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid was adopted by the General Assembly of the United Nations on the Thirtieth day of November, 1973; AND WHEREAS India, having acceded to the said Convention, should make provisions for giving effect to it;
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to implement the International Convention on the Suppression and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid in India. It criminalizes acts of apartheid and provides for their punishment and trial within the Indian legal framework.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Application of the International Convention on the Suppression and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid.
key_sections.description: Declares that provisions of the International Convention on the Suppression and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid, as set out in the Schedule, shall have the force of law in India.

key_sections.title: Punishment for international criminal responsibility.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for persons to whom international criminal responsibility applies under Article III of the Convention, including death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies, organisations or institutions.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that persons in charge of companies, organisations, or institutions are deemed guilty if an offence under the Act is committed by such entities, unless they prove lack of knowledge or due diligence.

key_sections.title: Place of trial.
key_sections.description: Allows for trial of an offence under section 3 in any place where the offender is found or as directed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Previous sanction of the Central Government for arrest or prosecution.
key_sections.description: Requires prior sanction from the Central Government or an authorised officer for arrest or prosecution in respect of any offence under section 3.

key_sections.title: Provisions as to Extradition Act.
key_sections.description: States that an offence under section 3 shall not be considered an offence of a political character for the purposes of the Extradition Act, 1962.

powers_conferred: Central Government may, from time to time, by notification in the Official Gazette, amend the Schedule
Central Government may, by general or special order, published in the Official Gazette, direct the place of trial
Central Government or such officer or authority as may be authorised by that Government by order in writing in this behalf has the power to sanction arrest or prosecution
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Every person to whom international criminal responsibility applies under article III of the said Convention, as set out in the Schedule, shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Offences can also be committed by companies, organisations or institutions.

applies_to: Every person to whom international criminal responsibility applies under article III of the said Convention
companies, organisations or institutions

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for amending the Schedule, directing place of trial, sanctioning prosecution)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through prosecution and punishment in Indian courts, with a requirement for prior sanction from the Central Government for arrest or prosecution.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any place in which the offender may be found or in such other place as the Central Government may direct.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the provisions of the International Convention on the Suppression and Punishment of the Crime of Apartheid which shall have force of law, specifically Article II defining 'the crime of apartheid' and Article III defining international criminal responsibility.

act_identification.act_title: THE CINE-WORKERS AND CINEMA THEATRE WORKERS (REGULATION OF EMPLOYMENT) ACT, 1981
act_identification.act_short_title: Cine-workers and Cinema Theatre Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1981

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the regulation of the conditions of employment of certain cine-workers and cinema theatre workers and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the conditions of employment for cine-workers and cinema theatre workers. It establishes mechanisms for resolving disputes and ensures certain benefits and protections for these workers.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II REGULATION OF EMPLOYMENT OF CINE-WORKERS
CHAPTER III REGULATION OF EMPLOYMENT OF CINEMA THEATRE WORKERS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its territorial extent, and the process for its commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'cine-worker', 'cinema theatre', and 'wages'.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of employment of cine-worker without agreement.
key_sections.description: Mandates a written and registered agreement for the employment of any cine-worker, detailing terms and conditions.

key_sections.title: Conciliation officers.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint conciliation officers to mediate and promote settlement of disputes between cine-workers and producers/contractors.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Tribunals.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of Cine-workers Tribunals by the Central Government for the adjudication of disputes.

key_sections.title: Procedure and powers of conciliation officers and Tribunals.

key_sections.title: Revision.
key_sections.description: Grants the High Court powers to revise awards made by a Tribunal, allowing for modification, annulment, or reversal of such awards.

key_sections.title: Application of Act 19 of 1952 to cine-workers.
key_sections.description: Extends the provisions of the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, to eligible cine-workers.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, primarily fines, for contravention of the requirement for written agreements for cine-workers.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.

key_sections.title: Application of Act 19 of 1952.
key_sections.description: Extends the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, to cinema theatres employing five or more workers.

key_sections.title: Application of Act 39 of 1972.
key_sections.description: Extends the provisions of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, to workers employed in cinema theatres with five or more workers.

Central Government to refer disputes to Tribunals
Central Government to make rules

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL BANK FOR AGRICULTURE AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT ACT, 1981
act_identification.act_short_title: the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981
act_identification.date_of_commencement: 1st May, 1982 (except sections 3, 16 and 18), 12th July, 1982 (in respect sections 3, 16 and 18)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish a development bank to be known as the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development for providing and regulating credit and other facilities for the promotion and development of agriculture, micro-enterprises, small enterprises and medium enterprises, cottage and village industries, handlooms handicrafts and other rural crafts and other allied economic activities in rural areas with a view to promoting integrated rural development and securing prosperity of rural areas and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) to provide and regulate credit and other facilities. Its primary objective is to promote and develop agriculture, micro, small, and medium enterprises, cottage and village industries, handicrafts, and other rural economic activities. The ultimate goal is to foster integrated rural development and ensure prosperity in rural areas.

key_sections.title: Power of Board to make regulations.

act_identification.act_title: THE AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT FUND ACT, 1982

act_overview.preamble: An Act to implement the African Development Fund Agreement and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to implement the African Development Fund Agreement in India. It provides for financial contributions to the Fund from the Consolidated Fund of India and designates the Reserve Bank of India as the depository for the Fund's Indian currency holdings. Furthermore, it confers specific status, immunities, exemptions, and privileges upon the African Development Fund and its personnel within India.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.

key_sections.title: Payments to Fund.

key_sections.title: Reserve Bank to be depository for Fund.
key_sections.description: Designates the Reserve Bank of India as the depository for the Indian currency holdings of the African Development Fund.

key_sections.title: Conferment of status and certain immunities, exemptions and privileges on Fund and conferment of certain immunities, exemptions and privileges on its officers and employees.
key_sections.description: Gives the provisions of the African Development Fund Agreement, as set out in the Schedule, the force of law in India, granting immunities, exemptions, and privileges, with certain provisos regarding customs duties and taxes.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act by notification in the Official Gazette.

key_sections.title: Notifications issued under section 5 and rules made under section 6 to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Requires all notifications and rules made under the Act to be laid before each House of Parliament for a specified period, allowing for modification or annulment.

Matters related to the African Development Fund Agreement

Fund's immunity from legal process, seizure, attachment, or execution (Schedule, Article 43, 44)
Immunity of governors, directors, President, and personnel from legal process for official acts (Schedule, Article 48(i))
Exemption from immigration restrictions, alien registration, national service obligations, and exchange regulations for non-local national personnel (Schedule, Article 48(ii))
Exemption from taxation for salaries and emoluments paid by the Fund to President and personnel (Schedule, Article 49(4))

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Payments from the Consolidated Fund of India (Section 3); Notifications and rules laid before Parliament for oversight (Section 7); Provisions of the Agreement having force of law (Section 5).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Court of competent jurisdiction (Schedule, Article 43)

schedules_summary.description: Contains provisions of the African Development Fund Agreement, specifically Chapter VIII, which details the status, immunities, exemptions, and privileges accorded to the Fund, its assets, archives, communications, and personnel, and the conditions for waiver of such immunities.

act_identification.act_title: THE SUGAR DEVELOPMENT FUND ACT, 1982

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the financing of activities for development of sugar industry and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Sugar Development Fund to provide financial assistance for the development of the sugar industry. The fund is used for making loans for rehabilitation, modernization, and sugarcane development, as well as grants for research, maintaining buffer stocks, promoting exports, and providing interest assistance on loans.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act.

key_sections.title: Sugar Development Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Sugar Development Fund and specifies how it is constituted by crediting amounts from the Sugar Cess Act, 1982.

key_sections.title: Application of Fund.
key_sections.description: Details the various purposes for which the fund can be utilized, including loans for modernization, grants for research, and expenditure for buffer stocks and exports.

key_sections.title: Applications for loans or grants.
key_sections.description: Specifies that applications for loans or grants under section 4 must be made to the Committee in the prescribed manner and form.

key_sections.title: Committee.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a committee by the Central Government to consider and dispose of applications and address administrative problems.

key_sections.title: Annual report of activities financed under the Act.
key_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to publish an annual report on activities financed under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to call for reports and returns.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to require sugar factories to furnish statistical and other information.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government authority to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions and specifies the procedure for laying rules before Parliament.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to appoint commencement date
Central Government: to determine cost of collection
Central Government: to apply the Fund
Central Government: to constitute a committee
Central Government: to publish annual report
Central Government: to call for reports and returns from sugar factories
Central Government: to make rules
Parliament: to make appropriation by law

applies_to: any sugar factory or any unit thereof
occupier of a sugar factory

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government applies the fund, constitutes a committee, and calls for reports and returns from sugar factories.

act_identification.act_title: THE CHAPARMUKH-SILGHAT RAILWAY LINE AND THE KATAKHAL-LALABAZAR RAILWAY LINE (NATIONALISATION) ACT, 1982
act_identification.act_short_title: the Chaparmukh-Silghat Railway Line and the Katakhal-Lalabazar Railway Line (Nationalisation) Act, 1982

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the acquisition of the undertakings of the Chaparmukh-Silghat Railway Company Limited in relation to the Chaparmukh-Silghat Railway Line and the undertakings of the Katakhal-Lalabazar Railway Company Limited in relation to the Katakhal-Lalabazar Railway Line with a view to securing the efficient operation of the said Railway lines so as to subserve the needs of the north-eastern areas of India and to protect the links of communication between the said areas and the rest of the country and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS the Chaparmukh-Silghat Railway Line owned by the Chaparmukh-Silghat Railway Company Limited and the Katakhal-Lalabazar Railway Line owned by the Katakhal-Lalabazar Railway Company Limited, are vital communication links between the north-eastern areas of India and the rest of the country; AND WHEREAS the said Railway Lines are integrated with the metre gauge system of the contiguous North-East Frontier Railway; AND WHEREAS the condition of assets of the aforesaid companies has reached such a stage that it may not be possible to operate train services for long on the railway lines owned by them; AND WHEREAS it is necessary to secure the efficient operation of the said Railway lines;
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the nationalisation (acquisition) of the Chaparmukh-Silghat Railway Line and the Katakhal-Lalabazar Railway Line. The primary objective is to ensure the efficient operation of these vital communication links, which serve the north-eastern areas of India and connect them to the rest of the country. This is deemed necessary due to the deteriorating condition of the assets of the owning companies.

chapter_titles: ACQUISITION OF THE UNDERTAKINGS OF THE TWO SPECIFIED COMPANIES
DUTY OF PERSONS IN CHARGE OF MANAGEMENT OF THE UNDERTAKINGS OF THE TWO SPECIFIED COMPANIES TO DELIVER ALL ASSETS, ETC.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.—In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,—
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'specified company', and 'undertakings'.

key_sections.title: Transfer to, and vesting in the Central Government of the undertakings of the two specified companies.
key_sections.description: Mandates the transfer and vesting of the undertakings of the two specified railway companies to the Central Government on the appointed day.

key_sections.title: General effect of vesting.
key_sections.description: Details what is included in the undertakings upon vesting, such as assets, rights, and properties, and declares them free from encumbrances.

key_sections.title: Owners of the two specified companies to be liable for certain prior liabilities.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that liabilities incurred by the specified companies prior to the appointed day remain their responsibility and are not enforceable against the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Payment of amount.
key_sections.description: Specifies the aggregate amounts to be paid by the Central Government to each of the two specified companies for their undertakings, with provisions for deductions.

key_sections.title: Duty of persons in charge of management of the undertakings of the two specified companies to deliver all assets, etc.
key_sections.description: Requires persons managing the undertakings to deliver all assets, books, and documents to the Central Government upon vesting.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws, instruments, decrees, or orders.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for various wrongful acts related to the property and documents of the nationalised undertakings.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Lays down provisions for holding companies and their responsible officers liable for offences committed under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act and mandates parliamentary oversight for such rules.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, with a time limit.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to acquire undertakings (Section 3).
Central Government: Power to deduct amounts from compensation (Section 6).
Central Government: Power to take steps for securing possession of undertakings (Section 9(2)).
Central Government: Power to specify persons to whom assets/documents are to be delivered (Section 9(1)).
Central Government: Power to allow time for furnishing inventory (Section 9(3)).
Central Government: Power to delegate powers (Section 14).
Central Government: Power to make rules (Section 15).
Central Government: Power to remove difficulties (Section 16).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 11 defines offences such as wrongfully withholding property, obtaining possession of property, wilfully withholding documents, failing to deliver assets, or wrongfully removing/destroying property, or making false claims. The penalty is imprisonment for up to two years, or a fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both. Section 12 deals with offences committed by companies.

applies_to: Chaparmukh-Silghat Railway Company Limited
Katakhal-Lalabazar Railway Company Limited
Undertakings of these two companies
Persons in charge of management of these undertakings

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act provides for the transfer and vesting of the undertakings of the specified railway companies in the Central Government. It mandates the payment of specified amounts as compensation and imposes a duty on persons in charge to deliver assets and account for them. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance or wrongful acts, and the Central Government is empowered to take necessary steps for securing possession.

act_identification.act_title: THE CHIT FUNDS ACT, 1982

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the regulation of chit funds and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the regulation of chit funds. It also addresses various matters connected with the establishment, operation, and termination of chit businesses.

chapter_titles: REGISTRATION OF CHITS, COMMENCEMENT AND CONDUCT OF CHIT BUSINESS
RIGHTS AND DUTIES OF NON-PRIZED SUBSCRIBERS
RIGHTS AND DUTIES OF PRIZED SUBSCRIBERS
MEETINGS OF GENERAL BODY OF SUBSCRIBERS
APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS AND LEVY OF FEES

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application across India, and that its commencement date will be notified by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'chit', 'foreman', 'subscriber', and 'approved bank'.

key_sections.title: Act to override other laws, memorandum, articles, etc.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act will prevail over any conflicting provisions in other laws or company documents.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of chits not sanctioned or registered under the Act.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the commencement or conduct of chits without prior sanction from the State Government and registration under the Act.

key_sections.title: Form of chit agreement.
key_sections.description: Details the mandatory particulars to be included in every chit agreement, such as subscriber details, instalment amounts, and discount terms.

key_sections.title: Minimum capital requirements for the commencement, etc., of a chit, and creation of a reserve fund, by a company.
key_sections.description: Sets minimum paid-up capital requirements for companies conducting chit business and mandates the creation and maintenance of a reserve fund.

key_sections.title: Commencement of chit.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for a foreman to file a declaration and obtain a certificate of commencement from the Registrar before starting a chit.

key_sections.title: Security to be given by foreman.
key_sections.description: Requires every foreman to furnish security, such as cash deposits or government securities, to the Registrar for the proper conduct of the chit.

key_sections.title: Rights of foreman.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the rights of a foreman, including entitlement to commission, interest, and the ability to demand security from prized subscribers.

key_sections.title: Duties of foreman.
key_sections.description: Specifies the duties of a foreman, such as paying the net chit amount to prized subscribers, depositing uncollected amounts, and distributing the share of discount.

key_sections.title: Circumstances under which chits may be wound up.
key_sections.description: Lists the conditions under which a chit may be wound up by the Registrar, either on his own motion or upon application.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Registrar and other officers.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to appoint a Registrar of Chits and other officers for the administration of the Act.

key_sections.title: Disputes relating to chit business.
key_sections.description: Provides for the referral of disputes touching the management of a chit business to the Registrar for arbitration, excluding Civil Court jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for contraventions of various provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules, in consultation with the Reserve Bank, for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: State Government: To sanction chits (Section 4), permit longer duration for chits (Section 6), extend periods for capital requirements (Section 8), extend period for winding up other business (Section 12), approve banking institutions (Section 2(a)), appoint Registrar and other officers (Section 61), prescribe fees (Section 63), hear appeals (Sections 59, 70, 74), delegate powers (Section 84), exempt persons/chits (Section 87), make rules (Section 89).

Registrar: To sanction/register chits (Sections 4, 7), grant certificate of commencement (Section 9), approve new places of business (Section 19), permit substitution of security (Section 20), order release of security (Section 20), arbitrate disputes (Sections 21, 28, 64), inspect records (Section 46), wind up chits (Section 48), appoint inspectors and chit auditors (Section 61), settle disputes (Section 66), exercise powers of Civil Court for dispute settlement (Section 67), order attachment before judgment (Section 68), make awards (Section 69), issue certificates for recovery of money (Section 71), give extension of time for filing documents (Section 75), enter and search places and seize documents (Section 82).

Reserve Bank: To inspect chit books and records of any foreman (Section 47), tender advice to State Governments on policy matters (Section 73), be consulted for exemptions (Section 87) and rule-making (Section 89).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention or abetment of contravention of Sections 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14, 19, 20, 22, 24, 30, 31, sub-section (4) of Section 33, Sections 46, 47 or sub-section (5) of Section 61 is punishable with imprisonment for up to two years or a fine up to five thousand rupees, or both. A foreman failing to file documents, comply with draw requirements, or other Act requirements is punishable with a fine up to three thousand rupees. Wilfully making a false statement in any required document is punishable with imprisonment for up to two years or a fine up to five thousand rupees, or both. For second and subsequent convictions under Section 76(1) or 76(3), the punishment is imprisonment for up to two years and a fine.

authorities_established: Additional, Joint, Deputy and Assistant Registrars
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government appoints the Registrar of Chits and other Registrars. The Registrar appoints inspectors of chits and chit auditors.

applies_to: The whole of India
Persons engaged in conducting chit business
exemptions: Any chit started before the commencement of this Act (Section 85(a)).

Any chit the amount of which, or where two or more chits were started or conducted simultaneously by the same foreman, the aggregate amount of which does not exceed such amount as may be specified by notification by the State Government (Section 85(b)).
Banks are prohibited from commencing or carrying on chit business after the commencement of this Act (Section 86(1)).
The State Government may, in consultation with the Reserve Bank, exempt any person or class of persons or any chit or class of chits from all or any of the provisions of this Act (Section 87).
special_provisions: The Central Government may appoint different commencement dates for different States (Section 1(3)).
The State Government may permit the duration of a chit up to a period of ten years under specific conditions (Section 6(2)).
The State Government may extend periods for companies to increase paid-up capital or wind up other businesses (Sections 8(2), 12(2)).
Where a person opens a new place of business in a State other than the State of origin, the Registrar of the new State may also exercise powers (Section 19(3)).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The State Government, in consultation with the Reserve Bank (Section 89).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through mandatory registration and sanction of chits, inspection of records by the Registrar and Reserve Bank, winding up proceedings for non-compliance or financial distress, and arbitration for disputes. Penalties are prescribed for contraventions, and powers of search and seizure are granted to the Registrar.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No Civil Court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or other proceedings in respect of disputes referred to the Registrar under Section 64. Offences under the Act are triable by a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class. Awards passed by the Registrar or nominee can be executed as decrees of a Civil Court. In cases of insolvency or company winding up, the insolvency court or the court winding up the company handles the distribution of chit assets.

act_identification.act_title: THE GOVERNORS (EMOLUMENTS, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) ACT, 1982
act_identification.act_short_title: The Governors (Emoluments, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1982

act_overview.preamble: An Act to determine the emoluments, allowances and privileges of Governors.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to determine the emoluments, allowances, and privileges granted to Governors of States in India. It outlines their financial benefits, residential entitlements, medical treatment, and other facilities necessary for discharging their duties.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its geographical extent to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'ex-Governor', 'Governor', 'maintenance', 'members of the family', 'official residences', 'rules', and 'State'.

key_sections.title: Emoluments.
key_sections.description: Determines the rate of emoluments payable to every Governor and specifies conditions under which these emoluments may be reduced, such as in receipt of a pension or contributory provident fund benefits.

key_sections.title: Leave allowance.
key_sections.description: Empowers the President to grant leave to a Governor and determine the rate of leave allowance, subject to rules made in this behalf.

key_sections.title: Use and maintenance of official residences.
key_sections.description: Entitles a Governor to the rent-free use of official residences throughout their term of office, with no personal charge for furnishing or maintenance.

key_sections.title: Medical treatment.
key_sections.description: Entitles a Governor and their family members to free medical attendance, accommodation, and treatment in government hospitals during and after the term of office, subject to rules.

key_sections.title: Traveling allowance on assumption or vacation of office.
key_sections.description: Entitles a Governor and their family to traveling allowance for journeys related to assuming or relinquishing office, including transport of effects, subject to rules.

key_sections.title: Other privileges and allowances.
key_sections.description: Provides for other privileges and allowances, such as entertainment allowance, hospitality grant, household establishment expenses, office expenses, and tour expenses, as determined by the President.

key_sections.title: Entitlement of ex-Governor to secretarial assistance.
key_sections.description: Grants ex-Governors secretarial assistance of one Personal Assistant on a reimbursement basis for the remainder of their life, with certain conditions for disqualification.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the President to make rules for giving effect to the provisions of the Act, specifying various matters that such rules may cover.

key_sections.title: Validation.
key_sections.description: Validates special orders issued by the President regarding allowances, expenses, or privileges of Governors (including the Governor of Nagaland) before the commencement of this Act, even if made retrospectively or inconsistently with general orders.

key_sections.title: Saving.
key_sections.description: Ensures that nothing in this Act or rules made thereunder shall diminish the emoluments and allowances of any Governor during their term of office.

powers_conferred: President: grant leave to a Governor (Section 4)
President: determine leave allowance (Section 4)
President: specify official residences (Section 2(d))
President: determine number of motor vehicles (Section 8)
President: determine allowances for renewing furnishings and maintenance of official residences (Section 10)
President: determine other privileges and allowances (Section 11)
President: increase allowances or sanction expenses by special order (Section 12)
President: make rules for the purpose of giving effect to the provisions of this Act (Section 13)
Central Government: appoint the date of commencement of the Act (Section 1)

applies_to: Governor
ex-Governor
members of the family of a Governor
special_provisions: Governor of Nagaland

act_identification.act_title: THE STATE BANK OF SIKKIM (ACQUISITION OF SHARES) AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS ACT, 1982
act_identification.act_short_title: the State Bank of Sikkim (Acquisition of Shares) and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1982

act_identification.act_title: THE SUPPRESSION OF UNLAWFUL ACTS AGAINST SAFETY OF CIVIL AVIATION ACT, 1982
act_identification.act_short_title: Suppression of Unlawful Acts against Safety of Civil Aviation Act, 1982

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India and, save as otherwise provided in this Act, it applies also to any offence under section 3 committed outside India by any person.

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to give effect to the Montreal Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Civil Aviation. It aims to make provisions for preventing and punishing unlawful acts that endanger civil aviation safety and for matters connected therewith.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, application and commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.

key_sections.title: Offence of committing violence on board an aircraft in flight, etc.

key_sections.title: Offence at airport.
key_sections.description: Defines offences involving violence, destruction, damage, or disruption at an airport, prescribing punishment of imprisonment for life and fine.

key_sections.title: Destruction of, or damage to, air navigation facilities.
key_sections.description: Defines offences related to destruction, damage, or interference with air navigation facilities, prescribing punishment of imprisonment for life and fine.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Establishes jurisdiction for offences committed outside India under specific conditions, such as aircraft registration or offender's nationality.

key_sections.title: Conferment of powers of investigation, etc.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to confer powers of arrest, investigation, and prosecution on its officers for the purposes of this Act.

key_sections.title: Designated Courts.
key_sections.description: Mandates the State Government to specify Courts of Session as Designated Courts for speedy trials of offences under this Act.

key_sections.title: Offences triable by Designated Courts.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that all offences under this Act shall be triable only by Designated Courts and outlines procedures for detention and cognizance.

key_sections.title: Provisions as to extradition.
key_sections.description: Deems offences under sections 3 and 4 as extraditable offences under existing treaties with Convention countries.

key_sections.title: Provision as to bail.
key_sections.description: Imposes limitations on granting bail for persons accused of offences under this Act, requiring public prosecutor's opportunity to oppose and court's satisfaction of innocence.

key_sections.title: Previous sanction necessary for prosecution.
key_sections.description: Requires the previous sanction of the Central Government for instituting any prosecution for an offence under this Act.

key_sections.title: Presumptions as to offences under sections 3, 3A and 4.
key_sections.description: Establishes presumptions in prosecution if arms, ammunition, explosives, or evidence of violence are proved, unless the contrary is shown.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Provides protection against legal proceedings for actions done or intended to be done in good faith under the provisions of this Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint commencement date (Section 1(3)).
Central Government: To confer powers of arrest, investigation and prosecution on any officer of the Central Government (Section 5A(1)).
Central Government: To certify contracting parties to the Montreal Convention (Section 7).
Central Government: To direct that certain aircraft be treated as registered in Convention countries (Section 8).
Central Government: To grant previous sanction for prosecution (Section 9).
State Government: To specify a Court of Session to be a Designated Court (Section 5B(1)).
Designated Courts: To hold trials on a day-to-day basis (Section 5B(2)).
Designated Courts: To try all offences under this Act (Section 5C(1)(a)).
Designated Courts: To exercise powers under section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Section 5C(1)(c)).
Designated Courts: To take cognizance of an offence upon a complaint (Section 5C(1)(d)).
Designated Courts: To try other offences along with offences under this Act (Section 5C(2)).
Magistrates: To authorise detention of accused persons (Section 5C(1)(b)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines offences such as committing violence on board an aircraft in flight, destroying or damaging an aircraft, placing destructive devices, communicating false information endangering aircraft safety (Section 3), committing violence or damaging facilities at an airport (Section 3A), and destroying or damaging air navigation facilities (Section 4). For all these offences, the punishment prescribed is imprisonment for life and liability to fine. Attempts to commit or abetment of these offences carry the same punishment.

applies_to: Whole of India
Offences under section 3 committed outside India by any person
Offences committed on board an aircraft registered in India
Offences committed on board an aircraft leased without crew to a lessee who has his principal place of business, or permanent residence in India
Alleged offender is a citizen of India or is on board the aircraft when it lands in India or is found in India
exemptions: Military aircraft
Aircraft used in customs or police service

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through investigation and prosecution by officers of the Central Government, with trials conducted by Designated Courts. Extradition provisions apply to specified offences. Prosecution requires previous sanction from the Central Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Designated Courts

act_identification.act_title: THE AFRICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK ACT, 1983

act_overview.preamble: An Act to implement the international agreement for the establishment and operation of the African Development Bank and for matters concerned therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act is enacted to give effect to the international agreement for the establishment and operation of the African Development Bank within India. It provides for the legal framework, financial contributions, and privileges necessary for the Bank's functioning.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its applicability to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms 'Agreement' and 'Bank' for the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Payments to Bank.
key_sections.description: Mandates payments from the Consolidated Fund of India for subscriptions and other sums payable to the Bank under the Agreement, and allows the Central Government to issue non-interest bearing notes.

key_sections.title: Reserve Bank to be depository for Bank.
key_sections.description: Designates the Reserve Bank of India as the depository for the Indian currency holdings of the African Development Bank.

key_sections.title: Conferment of status and certain immunities, exemptions and privileges on Bank and conferment of certain immunities, exemptions and privileges on its officers and employees.
key_sections.description: Grants the provisions of the Agreement set out in the Schedule the force of law in India, conferring immunities, exemptions, and privileges, with certain provisos regarding customs duties and taxes.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Notifications issued under section 5 and rules made under section 6 to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Requires notifications and rules made under the Act to be laid before each House of Parliament for a specified period.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint commencement date
Central Government to create and issue non-interest bearing notes or other obligations to the Bank
Central Government to amend the Schedule
Central Government to make rules
Parliament to make appropriation by law for payments to the Bank

related_acts: Agreement for the establishment of the African Development Bank

applies_to: whole of India
African Development Bank
officers and employees of the African Development Bank
exemptions: Bank from customs duties (with restrictions)
Bank from duties or taxes which form part of the price of goods sold
Bank from duties or taxes which are charges for services rendered
Bank, its property, other assets, income and its operations and transactions from all taxation and from all customs duties
Bank from any obligation relating to the payment, withholding or collection of any tax or duty
Salaries and emoluments paid by the Bank to directors, alternates, officers and other professional staff from tax
Obligations or securities issued by the Bank from tax (under specific conditions)
Obligations or securities guaranteed by the Bank from tax (under specific conditions)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Provisions of the Agreement set out in the Schedule shall have the force of law in India; Rules and notifications to be laid before Parliament.
