schedules_summary.description: Contains provisions of the Agreement Establishing the African Development Bank, specifically Chapter VII on Status, Immunities, Exemptions and Privileges (Articles 50-59), which are given the force of law in India.

act_identification.act_title: THE EMIGRATION ACT, 1983

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India and applies also to citizens of India outside India.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to emigration of citizens of India.
act_overview.purpose: This Act consolidates and amends the law concerning the emigration of Indian citizens. Its primary purpose is to regulate the process of recruitment and emigration for employment outside India, ensuring the protection and welfare of intending emigrants and emigrants.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical reach, applicability to Indian citizens abroad, and commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'emigrant', 'recruiting agent', and 'employment'.

key_sections.title: Protectors of Emigrants.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint a Protector General of Emigrants and Protectors of Emigrants, defining their authority and control.

key_sections.title: General duties of Protectors of Emigrants.
key_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities of Protectors of Emigrants, including protecting and aiding emigrants, ensuring compliance, and inquiring into their treatment.

key_sections.title: No person to function as recruiting agent without a valid certificate.
key_sections.description: Prohibits individuals from operating as recruiting agents without a valid registration certificate issued under the Act.

key_sections.title: Application for registration.
key_sections.description: Details the procedure for applying for a recruiting agent's registration, including required particulars, fees, and security.

key_sections.title: Cancellation, suspension, etc., of a certificate.
key_sections.description: Specifies the grounds and procedures for the registering authority or a court to cancel or suspend a recruiting agent's certificate.

key_sections.title: Recruitment by employers to be through recruiting agent or under permit.
key_sections.description: Mandates that employers recruit Indian citizens for overseas employment either through a competent recruiting agent or with a valid permit.

key_sections.title: Requirement, etc., as to emigration clearance.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that no citizen of India shall emigrate without obtaining an emigration clearance from the Protector of Emigrants.

key_sections.title: Offences and penalties.
key_sections.description: Defines various offences related to emigration, such as contravening provisions, furnishing false information, or cheating emigrants, and prescribes corresponding penalties.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Addresses the liability of companies and their officers when an offence under the Act is committed by a company.

key_sections.title: Power to prohibit emigration to any country in the interests of the general public, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to prohibit emigration to any country based on national interests, security, or public welfare.

key_sections.title: Power to prohibit emigration due to outbreak of epidemics, civil disturbances, etc., in a country.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to prohibit emigration to countries where emigrants might face serious risks due to epidemics, hostilities, or lack of diplomatic protection.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, covering various procedural and administrative matters.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Act 7 of 1922.
key_sections.description: Repeals the previous Emigration Act, 1922.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to appoint Protector General of Emigrants and Protectors of Emigrants (Sec 3).
Central Government: Power to set up emigration check-posts (Sec 6).
Central Government: Power to appoint registering authority (Sec 9).
Central Government: Power to appoint competent authority for permits (Sec 15).
Central Government: Power to exempt employers from permit requirements (Sec 21).
Central Government: Power to prohibit emigration to any country (Sec 30, 31).
Central Government: Power to prohibit emigration of any class or category of persons (Sec 32).
Central Government: Power to give directions to authorities (Sec 38).
Central Government: Power to delegate powers or functions (Sec 40).
Central Government: Power to exempt certain foreign entities, public undertakings, or government officers from the Act (Sec 41).
Central Government: Power to make rules (Sec 43).
Protectors of Emigrants: Power to protect and aid emigrants, inspect conveyances, inquire into treatment of emigrants (Sec 4).
Protectors of Emigrants: Power to determine if a person is an emigrant (Sec 29).
Protectors of Emigrants: Power to search, seize, and detain persons, conveyances, etc. (Sec 35).
Registering Authority: Power to issue, renew, suspend, or cancel certificates for recruiting agents (Sec 11, 13, 14).
Competent Authority: Power to issue, suspend, or cancel permits for recruitment by employers (Sec 17, 20).
Prescribed Authority: Power to forfeit security, require additional security or fresh security (Sec 33).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 24 outlines offences such as emigrating without conformity to the Act, contravening sections 10 or 16, furnishing false information, altering certificates, disobeying Protector's orders, collecting excess charges, or cheating emigrants. Penalties include imprisonment up to two years and a fine up to two thousand rupees, with a minimum of six months imprisonment and one thousand rupees fine for certain offences. Attempts and abetment are also punishable. Contravention of emigration clearance terms can lead to one year imprisonment or two thousand rupees fine or both. Repeat offenders face double penalties. Section 25 specifies that companies and responsible officers can be held liable for offences.

repealed_acts: The Emigration Act, 1922 (7 of 1922)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government

applies_to: citizens of India
recruiting agents
employers
exemptions: Any class or classes of employers (exempted by Central Government notification under Section 21)
Foreign dignitary or class of foreign employers, public undertaking, approved concern or Government officers (exempted by Central Government notification under Section 41)
Recruitment by such authorities, agencies or persons as may be specified in notification for implementing treaties, agreements or conventions (under Section 41(2))
Recruitment or emigration of any person who is not a citizen of India (Section 42(a))
Control of recruiting in India for the service of foreign States to which the Foreign Recruiting Act, 1874 applies (Section 42(b))

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the appointment of Protectors of Emigrants and other officers, establishment of emigration check-posts, mandatory registration and certification for recruiting agents and employers, and the requirement of emigration clearance for individuals. Authorities are vested with powers similar to civil courts for inquiries, and offences under the Act are cognizable, with prescribed penalties. The Central Government also has the power to issue directions and make rules for implementation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts (for conviction and cancellation of certificates), Appellate court or court exercising powers of revision (for cancellation of certificates), Civil court (for purposes of sections 195 and Chapter XXVI of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973).

act_identification.act_title: THE ARMED FORCES (PUNJAB AND CHANDIGARH) SPECIAL POWERS ACT, 1983
act_identification.act_short_title: The Armed Forces (Punjab and Chandigarh) Special Powers Act, 1983

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of the State of Punjab and the Union territory of Chandigarh

act_overview.preamble: An Act to enable certain special powers to be conferred upon members of the armed forces in the disturbed areas in the State of Punjab and the Union territory of Chandigarh.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to confer special powers upon members of the armed forces in disturbed areas within the State of Punjab and the Union territory of Chandigarh. These powers are intended to assist civil authorities in maintaining public order and addressing dangerous conditions.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its application to Punjab and Chandigarh, and its deemed commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms such as 'armed forces' and 'disturbed area' for the purpose of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to declare areas to be disturbed areas.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the Governor, Administrator, or Central Government to declare areas in Punjab or Chandigarh as 'disturbed areas' if necessary for aid to civil power.

key_sections.title: Special powers of the armed forces.
key_sections.description: Outlines the special powers granted to armed forces personnel in disturbed areas, including the power to use force, destroy structures, arrest without warrant, and search premises.

key_sections.title: Power of search to include powers to break open locks, etc.
key_sections.description: Confers the power to break open locks during a search if the key is withheld.

key_sections.title: Arrested person and seized property to be made over to the police.
key_sections.description: Mandates that arrested persons and seized property under the Act must be handed over to the nearest police station with a report of the circumstances.

key_sections.title: Protection of persons acting in good faith under this Act.
key_sections.description: Provides protection from prosecution, suit, or other legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act, requiring prior sanction of the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Armed Forces (Punjab and Chandigarh) Special Powers Ordinance, 1983, while saving actions taken under it.

Power to fire upon or use force against persons acting in contravention of public order laws (armed forces personnel)

Power to enter and search premises without warrant for arrest, recovery of wrongfully restrained persons, stolen property, or unlawful arms/ammunition/explosives (armed forces personnel)

State of Punjab
Union territory of Chandigarh

act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to make better provisions for the suppression of disorder and for the restoration and maintenance of public order in disturbed areas within the Union territory of Chandigarh.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Act's name, geographical reach, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Administrator' and 'disturbed area'.

key_sections.title: Powers to declare areas to be disturbed areas.
key_sections.description: Grants the Administrator the authority to officially designate areas as disturbed.

key_sections.title: Power to fire upon persons contravening certain orders.

key_sections.title: Powers to destroy arms dump, fortified positions, etc.

key_sections.title: Protection of persons acting under sections 4 and 5.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.

powers_conferred: Administrator: Power to declare areas to be disturbed areas by notification in the Official Gazette.

Magistrate or Police Officer (not below the rank of Sub-Inspector or Havildar in case of Armed Branch of Police): Power to fire upon, or otherwise use force, even to the causing of death, against persons contravening certain orders for maintenance of public order.

disturbed area

act_identification.act_title: THE ILLEGAL MIGRANTS (DETERMINATION BY TRIBUNALS) ACT, 1983
act_identification.act_short_title: the Illegal Migrants (Determination by Tribunals) Act, 1983

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of Tribunals for the determination, in a fair manner, of the question whether a person is an illegal migrant to enable the Central Government to expel illegal migrants from India and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS a good number of the foreigners who migrated into India across the borders of the eastern and north-eastern regions of the country on and after the 25th day of March, 1971, have, by taking advantage of the circumstances of such migration and their ethnic similarities and other connections with the people of India and without having in their possession any lawful authority so to do, illegally remained in India; AND WHEREAS the continuance of such foreigners in India is detrimental to the interests of the public of India; AND WHEREAS on account of the number of such foreigners and the manner in which such foreigners have clandestinely been trying to pass off as citizens of India and all other relevant circumstances, it is necessary for the protection of the citizens of India to make special provisions for the detection of such foreigners in Assam and also in any other part of India in which such foreigners may be found to have remained illegally;
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes Tribunals to fairly determine if a person is an illegal migrant. Its main objective is to enable the Central Government to identify and expel illegal migrants from India, particularly those who entered after March 25, 1971, and are detrimental to public interest.

chapter_titles: ENFORCEMENT OF THE ORDERS MADE BY THE TRIBUNALS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the Act's name, geographical application, and effective dates.

key_sections.title: Application.
key_sections.description: Specifies categories of persons to whom the Act does not apply.

key_sections.title: Definitions and construction of references.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms like 'illegal migrant' and 'foreigner'.

key_sections.title: Overriding effect of the Act.
key_sections.description: States that this Act's provisions prevail over certain other Acts.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Illegal Migrants (Determination) Tribunals.
key_sections.description: Details the establishment, composition, and jurisdiction of Tribunals.

key_sections.title: References or applications to Tribunals.
key_sections.description: Outlines how questions of illegal migration are referred or applied to Tribunals.

key_sections.title: Application to the Central Government for reference.
key_sections.description: Allows individuals to apply to the Central Government for a reference to a Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Powers of Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Grants Tribunals powers similar to a civil court for certain matters.

key_sections.title: Determination of the question as to whether a person is an illegal migrant.
key_sections.description: Describes the procedure for Tribunals to determine illegal migrant status.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals against Tribunal orders to the Appellate Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Details the establishment, composition, and functions of Appellate Tribunals.

key_sections.title: Expulsion of illegal migrants.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to order the expulsion of determined illegal migrants and outlines police powers for enforcement.

key_sections.title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts.
key_sections.description: Excludes civil courts from jurisdiction over matters covered by the Act.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of expulsion orders or harbouring illegal migrants.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make rules for implementing the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Establish Tribunals (Sec 5), establish Appellate Tribunals (Sec 15), refer questions to Tribunals (Sec 8), make rules (Sec 28), order expulsion (Sec 20), delegate powers (Sec 21), remove difficulties (Sec 27).

Tribunals: Determine illegal migrant status (Sec 12), summon witnesses, enforce attendance, discover documents, receive evidence, requisition public records, issue commissions (Sec 9), regulate own procedure (Sec 18).
Appellate Tribunals: Hear appeals (Sec 14, 16), superintendence over Tribunals (Sec 17), regulate own procedure (Sec 18).
Police Officer (not below SP): Obtain bond, arrest for failure to furnish bond (Sec 20(2), 21A).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who contravenes or attempts to contravene, or abets the contravention of, any order made under section 20; or fails to comply with any direction given by any such order; or harbours any person who has contravened any order made under section 20 or has failed to comply with any direction given by any such order, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to three years and with fine which shall not be less than two thousand rupees.

repealed_acts: The Illegal Migrants (Determination by Tribunals) Ordinance, 1983 (8 of 1983)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government

applies_to: persons in respect of whom each of the following conditions is satisfied, namely:— (i) he has entered into India on or after the 25th day of March, 1971, (ii) he is a foreigner, (iii) he has entered into India without being in possession of a valid passport or other travel document or any other lawful authority in that behalf
exemptions: any person who was in any State and who had been expelled from that State or India before the commencement of this Act in that State or in relation to whose expulsion from such State or India any order made before such commencement under any other law is in force
any person detected as a foreigner at the time of his entry across any border of India

any foreigner who, having entered into India under a valid passport or travel document, continued to remain therein after the expiry of the period for which he was authorised to remain in India under such passport or travel document
special_provisions: It shall be deemed to have come into force in the State of Assam on the 15th day of October, 1983
special provisions for the detection of such foreigners in Assam and also in any other part of India in which such foreigners may be found to have remained illegally

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Where a person has been determined by a Tribunal, or, as the case may be, by the Appellate Tribunal, to be an illegal migrant, the Central Government shall, by order served on such person, direct such person to remove himself from India. Any police officer not below the rank of a Superintendent of Police shall have such powers as may be necessary, including the power to obtain a bond from any person for the due compliance of an order and to arrest such person in the event of his failure to furnish such bond.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Tribunal or Appellate Tribunal

act_identification.act_title: THE PUBLIC FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS (OBLIGATION AS TO FIDELITY AND SECRECY) ACT, 1983

act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish and regulate the obligation of public financial institutions regarding fidelity and secrecy in their operations. It outlines the conditions under which information can be divulged or shared, and mandates a declaration of fidelity and secrecy from their personnel.

key_sections.title: Declaration of fidelity and secrecy.

act_identification.act_title: THE PREVENTION OF DAMAGE TO PUBLIC PROPERTY ACT, 1984
act_identification.act_short_title: The Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act, 1984

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for prevention of damage to public property and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to prevent damage to public property by defining specific offences related to mischief against such property. It prescribes penalties for individuals who cause damage to public property, including aggravated forms of mischief.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act, its geographical applicability, and the date it came into force.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, specifically 'mischief' and 'public property'.

key_sections.title: Mischief causing damage to public property.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for committing mischief that causes damage to public property, with enhanced penalties for damage to specific types of public property like utilities or transport.

key_sections.title: Mischief causing damage to public property by fire or explosive substance.
key_sections.description: Prescribes more severe punishment for committing mischief to public property using fire or explosive substances.

key_sections.title: Special provisions regarding bail.
key_sections.description: Stipulates conditions for granting bail to persons accused or convicted under sections 3 or 4, requiring the prosecution to have an opportunity to oppose.

key_sections.title: Saving.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act's provisions are in addition to, and not in derogation of, other existing laws.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Ordinance, 1984, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 3(1) prescribes imprisonment up to five years and fine for mischief causing damage to public property. Section 3(2) prescribes rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than six months but up to five years and fine for mischief causing damage to specific public properties (e.g., utilities, transport). Section 4 prescribes rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than one year but up to ten years and fine for mischief causing damage to public property by fire or explosive substance.

repealed_acts: The Prevention of Damage to Public Property Ordinance, 1984 (Ord. 3 of 1984)

applies_to: Whoever commits mischief by doing any act in respect of any public property

Any property (immovable or movable) owned by, in possession of, or under control of Central Government, State Government, local authority, corporations established by law, companies as defined in section 617 of the Companies Act, 1956, or specified institutions/concerns/undertakings.
special_provisions: Court may award a sentence of imprisonment for a term of less than six months under Section 3(2) for reasons to be recorded in its judgment.
Court may award a sentence of imprisonment for a term of less than one year under Section 4 for special reasons to be recorded in its judgment.
Central Government's power to specify institutions as 'public property' is subject to the condition that such institutions are financed wholly or substantially by government funds.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced through criminal proceedings, including investigation and prosecution, with specific provisions for punishment and bail.

act_identification.act_title: THE INCHEK TYRES LIMITED AND NATIONAL RUBBER MANUFACTURERS LIMITED (NATIONALISATION) ACT, 1984
act_identification.act_short_title: the Inchek Tyres Limited and National Rubber Manufacturers Limited (Nationalisation) Act, 1984

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of the Inchek Tyres Limited and the National Rubber Manufacturers Limited, with a view to securing the proper management of such undertakings so as to subserve the interests of the general public by ensuring the continued manufacture, production and distribution of tyres, tubes and other rubber goods which are essential to the needs of the economy of the country and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS the Inchek Tyres Limited and the National Rubber Manufacturers Limited had been engaged in the manufacture, production and distribution of articles mentioned in the First Schedule to the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 (65 of 1951), namely, tyres, tubes and other rubber goods; AND WHEREAS the management of the undertakings of the Inchek Tyres Limited and the management of the undertakings of the National Rubber Manufacturers Limited were taken over by the Central Government under the provisions of the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 (65 of 1951); AND WHEREAS for the purpose of securing the optimum utilisation of the available facilities for the manufacture, production and distribution of tyres, tubes and other rubber goods by the undertakings of the two companies, investment of a large amount is necessary; AND WHEREAS it is necessary to acquire the undertakings of the Inchek tyres Limited and the National Rubber Manufacturers Limited to enable the Central Government to have such investments made and to ensure that the interests of the general public are served by the continuance, by the undertakings of the companies, of the manufacture, production and distribution of the aforesaid articles which are essential to the needs of the economy of the country;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to acquire and transfer the undertakings of Inchek Tyres Limited and National Rubber Manufacturers Limited to the Central Government. This is done to ensure proper management, continued manufacture, production, and distribution of essential rubber goods like tyres and tubes, thereby serving the interests of the general public and the economy of the country.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN VETERINARY COUNCIL ACT, 1984

legislative_details.geographical_extent: in the first instance, to the whole of the States of Haryana, Bihar, Orissa, Himachal Pradesh and Rajasthan and to all Union territories; and it shall also extend to such other States as may adopt this Act by resolution passed in that behalf in pursuance of clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution. Extended to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh by Act 34 of 2019, s. 95 and the Fifth Schedule (w.e.f. 31-10-2019).

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate veterinary practice and to provide, for that purpose, for the establishment of a Veterinary Council of India and State Veterinary Councils and the maintenance of registers of the veterinary practitioners and for matters connected therewith. WHEREAS it is expedient to make provision for the regulation of veterinary practice and to provide, for that purpose, for the establishment of a Veterinary Council of India and State Veterinary Councils and the maintenance of registers of persons qualified to engage in veterinary practice for the whole of India and for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto; AND WHEREAS Parliament has no power to make laws for the States with respect to any of the matters aforesaid except as provided in articles 249 and 250 of the Constitution; AND WHEREAS in pursuance of clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution, resolutions have been passed by all the Houses of the Legislatures of the States of Haryana, Bihar, Orissa, Himachal Pradesh and Rajasthan to the effect that the matters aforesaid should be regulated in those States by Parliament by law;
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to regulate veterinary practice in India by establishing a Veterinary Council of India and State Veterinary Councils. It provides for the maintenance of registers for qualified veterinary practitioners and addresses related matters to ensure standardized veterinary services.

State Government: Establish State Veterinary Councils, nominate State Council members, decide election disputes, appoint Registrar, prepare State veterinary register, constitute Registration Tribunal, appoint authority for appeals, make rules, appoint Commission of Inquiry, permit persons to render minor veterinary services.

Veterinary Council of India: Acquire, hold, dispose of property, sue/be sued, elect President/Vice-President, appoint Secretary/officers, appoint Executive and other Committees, furnish reports to Central Government, enter negotiations for reciprocity, require information from veterinary institutions, appoint visitors, make representation to Central Government for withdrawal of recognition, specify minimum standards of veterinary education, maintain Indian veterinary practitioners register, issue certificate of registration, register additional qualifications, specify standards of professional conduct, approve restoration to State register, direct transfer of registration, make regulations.
State Veterinary Council: Maintain State veterinary register, elect President, appoint Registrar/officers, furnish reports to State Government, remove names from register, restore names to register.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 55: Falsely claiming to be registered - fine up to five hundred rupees on first conviction, imprisonment up to six months or fine up to one thousand rupees or both on subsequent conviction. Section 56: Misuse of titles by unregistered persons or those not possessing recognized qualifications - fine up to one thousand rupees on first conviction, imprisonment up to six months or fine up to five thousand rupees or both on subsequent conviction. Section 57: Practice by unregistered persons - fine up to one thousand rupees on first conviction, imprisonment up to six months or fine up to five thousand rupees or both on subsequent conviction. Section 58: Failure to surrender certificate of registration after removal from register - fine up to five hundred rupees, and additional fine up to ten rupees per day for continuing offence.

act_identification.act_title: THE HOOGHLY DOCKING AND ENGINEERING COMPANY LIMITED (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKINGS) ACT, 1984
act_identification.act_short_title: the Hooghly Docking and Engineering Company Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1984

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of the Hooghly Docking and Engineering Company Limited with a view to securing the better utilisation of the available infrastructure thereof, to modernise and increase the capacity for ship building and ship repairing so as to reduce the import of ships, vessels and craft and to augment the production of grey iron, non-ferrous and alloy castings by the said undertakings so as to subserve the interests of the general public by ensuring the continued supply of the said articles which are essential to the needs of the economy of the country, and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto. WHEREAS the Hooghly Docking and Engineering Company Limited is, through its undertakings, engaged in shipbuilding, ship repairing, general engineering and other activities; AND WHEREAS the Company has the capacity and infrastructure to effect an increase in the country’s capacity to manufacture ships and other vessels and craft; AND WHEREAS an increase in the production of such vessels and craft would reduce the need of the country to make imports of such vessels and craft and would thereby enable the country to save foreign exchange; AND WHEREAS the Company is also engaged in the production of grey iron, non-ferrous and alloy castings which are essential to the needs of the economy of the country; AND WHEREAS the Company had been suffering heavy losses for a number of years mainly due to lack of fresh investment and modernisation; AND WHEREAS further investment of substantial sums of money is needed to run and modernise the undertakings of the Company: but in view of the serious adverse financial condition of the Company it is not in a position to secure such investment; AND WHEREAS the liquidation of the Company, by reason of its inability to pay its debts, would prejudicially affect the country’s capacity to manufacture such ships, vessels and craft and would thereby be prejudicial to the public interest; AND WHEREAS in view of the position aforesaid it is necessary to acquire the undertaking of the said Company to enable the Central Government to make necessary investments for securing the proper utilisation of the available facilities for shipbuilding and ship repairing (including the production of vessels and craft) and also for the production of grey iron, non-ferrous and alloy castings which are essential to the needs of the economy of the country;
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of the Hooghly Docking and Engineering Company Limited. Its main objective is to ensure better utilization of infrastructure, modernize shipbuilding and repair capacity, reduce imports, and augment production of essential castings, thereby serving public interest and the economy. The acquisition was deemed necessary due to the company's financial distress and its importance to national economic needs.

Non-compliance is addressed through prescribed penalties.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Principal civil court of original jurisdiction for appeals against Commissioner's decisions; High Court if the Commissioner is a High Court Judge. The Commissioner has powers vested in a civil court for investigations.

schedules_summary.description: Details the order of priorities for the discharge of liabilities of the Company, categorizing claims into seven categories (I to VII) including wages, provident fund arrears, secured loans, statutory dues, unsecured loans, and other credits/dues.

act_identification.act_title: THE TERRORIST AFFECTED AREAS (SPECIAL COURTS) ACT, 1984
act_identification.act_short_title: The Terrorist Affected Areas (Special Courts) Act, 1984

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir*. *Vide notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019, this Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the speedy trial of certain offences in terrorist affected areas and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: To provide for the speedy trial of certain offences in terrorist affected areas and for matters connected therewith.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical extent, and the date it came into force.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Code', 'Special Court', 'scheduled offence', and 'terrorist affected area'.

key_sections.title: Declaration of terrorist affected area.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to declare an area as terrorist affected and constitute judicial zones for the purpose of this Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Special Courts.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of Special Courts and Additional Special Courts for the speedy trial of scheduled offences.

key_sections.title: Composition and appointment of Judges of Special Courts.
key_sections.description: Outlines the qualifications and appointment process for Judges and Additional Judges of Special Courts.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of Special Court.
key_sections.description: Defines the exclusive jurisdiction of Special Courts over scheduled offences committed in terrorist affected judicial zones.

key_sections.title: Procedure and powers of Special Courts.
key_sections.description: Details the procedural powers of Special Courts, including taking cognizance, summary trials, tendering pardon, and acting as a Court of Session.

key_sections.title: Protection of witnesses.
key_sections.description: Mandates in camera proceedings and empowers Special Courts to take measures to keep the identity and address of witnesses secret.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Establishes a right of appeal from Special Courts directly to the Supreme Court on facts and law.

key_sections.title: Modified application of certain provisions of the Code.
key_sections.description: Modifies the application of the Code of Criminal Procedure, including deeming scheduled offences as cognizable, altering bail provisions, and restricting anticipatory bail.

key_sections.title: Overriding effect of Act.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over the Code of Criminal Procedure or any other law, where inconsistent.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Act 1 of 1872.
key_sections.description: Inserts a new section 111A into the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, regarding presumptions as to certain offences.

powers_conferred: Central Government to declare terrorist affected area (Section 3)
Central Government to constitute judicial zones (Section 3)
Central Government to establish Special Courts (Section 4)
Central Government to appoint Judges of Special Courts with High Court concurrence (Section 5)
Central Government to appoint Public Prosecutors (Section 9)
Central Government to delegate powers to State Government (Section 17)
State Government to request establishment of Additional Special Court outside the State (Section 4)
Special Courts to try scheduled offences (Section 7)
Special Courts to try other connected offences (Section 8)
Special Courts to take cognizance of scheduled offences (Section 10)
Special Courts to try offences in a summary way (Section 10)
Special Courts to tender pardon to obtain evidence (Section 10)
Special Courts to exercise powers of a Court of Session (Section 10)
Special Courts to conduct proceedings in camera and protect witnesses (Section 12)
Special Courts to transfer cases to regular courts if not scheduled offences (Section 13)
Supreme Court to transfer cases between Special Courts (Section 11)
Supreme Court to hear appeals from Special Courts (Section 14)
Supreme Court to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act (Section 18)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for the trial of 'scheduled offences' as specified in the Schedule, which include offences under the Indian Penal Code (sections 121, 121A, 122, 123) and the Anti-Hijacking Act, 1982 (sections 4, 5), along with criminal conspiracy, attempt, and abetment. Section 12(4) prescribes a penalty for contravening witness protection directions: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.

amended_acts: The Terrorist Affected Areas (Special Courts) Amendment Act, 1985 (Act 45 of 1985)
repealed_acts: The Terrorist Affected Areas (Special Courts) Ordinance, 1984 (9 of 1984)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints Judges of Special Courts with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court. Central Government appoints Public Prosecutors, Additional Public Prosecutors, or Special Public Prosecutors.

applies_to: Scheduled offences committed in a judicial zone in a State declared as a terrorist affected area.
Persons who indulge in wanton killing, violence, disruption of essential services, or damaging property with specific intentions (terrorists).
exemptions: Jurisdiction or procedure applicable to any court or authority under any law relating to naval, military, air forces, or other armed forces of the Union.
special_provisions: The Act was made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh by notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019.
Provision for establishing Additional Special Courts outside the State under certain exigencies (Section 4(2)).
Period of declaration of a terrorist affected area may commence from a date earlier than the notification date (Section 3(2)).
Modified application of various provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Section 15).
No anticipatory bail for scheduled offences in a terrorist affected area (Section 15(4)).
Limitations on granting bail for persons accused of scheduled offences (Section 15(5)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the establishment of Special Courts and Additional Special Courts for the speedy trial of scheduled offences in terrorist affected areas, with modified procedures from the Code of Criminal Procedure, including provisions for witness protection and direct appeal to the Supreme Court.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Special Courts, Additional Special Courts, and the Supreme Court (for appeals and transfers).

schedules_summary.description: Lists the 'scheduled offences' which include specific sections of the Indian Penal Code (121, 121A, 122, 123) and the Anti-Hijacking Act, 1982 (sections 4, 5). It also includes criminal conspiracy, attempt to commit, or abetment of these offences, and commission by members of an unlawful assembly.

act_identification.act_title: THE FAMILY COURTS ACT, 1984

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of Family Courts with a view to promote conciliation in, and secure speedy settlement of, disputes relating to marriage and family affairs and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish Family Courts to promote conciliation and ensure speedy settlement of disputes related to marriage and family affairs. It also defines the jurisdiction, powers, and procedures for these courts.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its geographical extent to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on dates appointed by the Central Government for different States.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, such as 'Judge', 'notification', 'prescribed', and 'Family Court'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Family Courts.
key_sections.description: Mandates the State Government, in consultation with the High Court, to establish Family Courts for areas with populations exceeding one million and optionally for other areas.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Judges.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for the State Government to appoint Judges for Family Courts, their qualifications, and conditions of service, emphasizing selection of persons committed to family welfare and conciliation.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Confers upon Family Courts the jurisdiction exercisable by district or subordinate civil courts for disputes related to marriage, family status, property, maintenance, guardianship, and also powers of a Magistrate under CrPC Chapter IX.

key_sections.title: Exclusion of jurisdiction and pending proceedings.
key_sections.description: Excludes the jurisdiction of district courts, subordinate civil courts, and magistrates in areas where a Family Court is established, and mandates the transfer of pending proceedings to the Family Court.

key_sections.title: Duty of Family Court to make efforts for settlement.
key_sections.description: Requires Family Courts to make efforts to assist and persuade parties to arrive at a settlement in disputes, including adjourning proceedings for this purpose.

key_sections.title: Procedure generally.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, apply to proceedings before a Family Court, but allows the Family Court to lay down its own procedure for settlement.

key_sections.title: Right to legal representation.
key_sections.description: States that parties are not entitled as of right to legal representation, but the Family Court may seek assistance of a legal expert as amicus curiae.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals from judgments or orders of a Family Court to the High Court on facts and law, with certain exceptions like consent decrees or orders under CrPC Chapter IX.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_sections.title: Power of High Court to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the High Court the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including rules for working hours, sittings, and settlement procedures.

key_sections.title: Power of the Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for prescribing qualifications of Judges and mandates that such rules be laid before Parliament.

key_sections.title: Power of the State Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the State Government to make rules for implementing the Act, covering matters like Judges' salaries, counsellors' terms, and payment of experts and legal practitioners.

powers_conferred: State Government to establish Family Courts
State Government to appoint Judges of Family Courts
State Government to determine number and categories of counsellors, officers and other employees of Family Courts
State Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act
High Court to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act
Family Court to exercise jurisdiction of district court or subordinate civil court in family matters
Family Court to exercise jurisdiction of a Magistrate of the first class under Chapter IX of CrPC
Family Court to make efforts for settlement between parties
Family Court to lay down its own procedure with a view to arrive at a settlement or truth of facts
Family Court to secure services of medical and welfare experts
Family Court to receive certain reports, statements, documents, information or matter as evidence
Family Court to execute its own decrees and orders or send them for execution to other courts
Central Government to make rules prescribing qualifications for appointment of a Judge

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government, with the concurrence of the High Court, for Judges; State Government for counsellors, officers and other employees.

applies_to: disputes relating to marriage and family affairs
parties to a marriage
any person (for legitimacy)
any minor (for guardianship, custody, access)
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different States for the commencement of the Act.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: High Court, Central Government, State Government
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Decrees and orders (other than under CrPC Chapter IX) are executed as prescribed by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Orders under CrPC Chapter IX are executed as prescribed by that Code. Execution can be by the Family Court that passed the order or by another Family Court or ordinary civil court.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Family Courts (primary jurisdiction); High Court (for appeals and revisions).

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL CAPITAL REGION PLANNING BOARD ACT, 1985
act_identification.act_short_title: National Capital Region Planning Board Act, 1985

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution of a Planning Board for the preparation of a plan for the development of the National Capital Region and for co-ordinating and monitoring the implementation of such plan and for evolving harmonized policies for the control of land-uses and development of infrastructure in the National Capital Region so as to avoid any haphazard development of that region and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS it is expedient in the public interest to provide for the constitution of a Planning Board for the preparation of a plan for the development of the National Capital Region and for co-ordinating and monitoring the implementation of such plan and for evolving harmonized policies for the control of land-uses and development of infrastructure in the National Capital Region so as to avoid any haphazard development thereof; AND WHEREAS Parliament has no power to make laws for the States with respect of any of the matters aforesaid, except as provided in articles 249 and 250 of the Constitution; AND WHEREAS in pursuance of the provisions of clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution, resolutions have been passed by all the Houses of the Legislatures of the States of Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh to the effect that the matters aforesaid should be regulated in those States by Parliament by law;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to constitute a Planning Board for the National Capital Region to prepare, coordinate, and monitor a development plan. It aims to evolve harmonized policies for land-use control and infrastructure development to prevent haphazard growth in the region.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II THE NATIONAL CAPITAL REGION PLANNING BOARD
CHAPTER III FUNCTIONS AND POWERS OF THE BOARD AND OF THE COMMITTEE
CHAPTER V FUNCTIONAL PLANS, SUB-REGIONAL PLANS AND PROJECT PLANS
CHAPTER VI FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution and incorporation of the Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes the National Capital Region Planning Board as a body corporate and outlines its composition.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Board.
key_sections.description: Details the responsibilities of the Board, including preparing plans, coordinating implementation, and overseeing financing.

key_sections.title: Powers of the Board.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to the Board to call for reports, ensure conformity of plans, review implementation, and approve projects.

key_sections.title: Contents of the Regional Plan.
key_sections.description: Specifies the elements and matters to be included in the Regional Plan, such as land-use policy, settlement patterns, and infrastructure.

key_sections.title: Procedure to be followed for the preparation of Regional Plan.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for preparing the Regional Plan, including draft publication, inviting objections, and finalization.

key_sections.title: Date of coming into operation of the Regional Plan.
key_sections.description: States when the Regional Plan comes into effect after its final preparation and publication.

key_sections.title: Grants and loans by the Central Government.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to provide grants and loans to the Board for its functions and administrative expenses.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the National Capital Regional Planning Board Fund and specifies sources of credit and application of funds.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in other laws or instruments.

key_sections.title: Violation of Regional Plan.
key_sections.description: Prohibits development inconsistent with the Regional Plan and allows the Board to direct states to stop violations and withhold financial assistance.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the National Capital Region Planning Board Ordinance, 1984, and includes saving provisions.

powers_conferred: Power to constitute the Board (Central Government, Section 3)
Power to co-opt members (Board or Committee, Section 5)
Power to prepare Regional and Functional Plans (Board, Section 7)
Power to arrange for preparation of Sub-Regional and Project Plans (Board, Section 7)
Power to coordinate enforcement and implementation of plans (Board, Section 7)
Power to ensure proper programming and phasing of development (Board, Section 7)
Power to arrange for and oversee financing of projects (Board, Section 7)
Power to call for reports and information (Board, Section 8)
Power to ensure conformity of plans (Board, Section 8)
Power to indicate stages for implementation (Board, Section 8)
Power to review implementation of plans (Board, Section 8)
Power to select and approve comprehensive projects and provide assistance (Board, Section 8)
Power to select counter-magnet areas (Board, Section 8)
Power to entrust functions to the Committee (Board, Section 8)
Power to make modifications in the Regional Plan (Board, Section 14)
Power to review and revise the Regional Plan (Board, Section 15)
Power to cause surveys and studies (Board, Section 11)
Power to appoint officers and employees (Board, Section 31)
Power to delegate functions or powers (Board, Section 32)
Power of entry (Board authorized persons, Section 33)
Power to give directions (Central Government to Board, Section 28)
Power to make rules (Central Government, Section 36)

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Violation of Regional Plan (Section 29) may lead to the Board directing the concerned participating State or Union territory to stop such violation and, in case of omission or refusal, to withhold financial assistance.

repealed_acts: The National Capital Region Planning Board Ordinance, 1984 (Ord. 11 of 1984)
related_acts: clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution
section 21 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government nominates members to the Board. The Board constitutes the Planning Committee and appoints its officers and employees.

applies_to: National Capital Region
participating States
Union territory
special_provisions: The Central Government, with the consent of the concerned participating State and in consultation with the Board, may add or exclude areas from the National Capital Region by notification.

Acquisition of land or determination of rights in relation to land to give effect to plans shall be made by the Government of the concerned participating State or Union territory in accordance with their respective laws.
Reference to any district or tehsil in the Schedule is construed as the areas comprised on 27th August, 1984, the date the Bill was introduced.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Board coordinates enforcement and implementation of plans, monitors activities, and can direct participating States or Union territories to stop violations, with the power to withhold financial assistance.

schedules_summary.description: Lists the specific geographical areas that comprise the National Capital Region, including the whole of the Union territory of Delhi and designated districts/tehsils from the States of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan.

act_identification.act_title: THE CALCUTTA METRO RAILWAY (OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE) TEMPORARY PROVISIONS ACT, 1985
act_identification.act_short_title: Calcutta Metro Railway (Operation and Maintenance) Temporary Provisions Act, 1985

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Thirty-fifth Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make temporary provisions for the operation and maintenance of the Calcutta metro railway and for matters connected therewith, pending the making of regular arrangements for such operation and maintenance.
act_overview.purpose: This Act makes temporary provisions for the operation and maintenance of the Calcutta metro railway. It addresses matters connected with its functioning until regular arrangements for operation and maintenance are established.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II THE CALCUTTA METRO RAILWAY ADMINISTRATION
CHAPTER III SPECIAL PROVISIONS FOR THE RUNNING OF THE METRO RAILWAY

key_sections.title: Short title, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's name, effective date, and geographical scope.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Calcutta metro railway administration to be responsible for the operation and maintenance of the metro railway.
key_sections.description: Establishes the primary responsibility of the metro railway administration for operation and maintenance.

key_sections.title: Previous sanction of the Central Government required for the opening of metro railway.
key_sections.description: Mandates Central Government approval for public operation of the metro railway.

key_sections.title: Penalty for taking or causing to take offensive or dangerous goods upon the metro railway.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for carrying prohibited goods on the metro railway.

key_sections.title: Drunkenness or nuisance upon the metro railway.
key_sections.description: Defines offenses related to intoxication or nuisance on the metro railway and their penalties.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of demonstrations upon the metro railway.
key_sections.description: Prohibits demonstrations and unauthorized postings on metro property.

key_sections.title: Endangering the safety of passengers.
key_sections.description: Specifies penalties for metro railway officials whose actions endanger passenger safety.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Addresses liability for offenses committed by companies and their responsible personnel.

key_sections.title: Application of Act 9 of 1890 and the rules, etc., made thereunder to the metro railway.
key_sections.description: Extends the applicability of the Indian Railways Act, 1890, to the metro railway with modifications.

key_sections.title: Effect of Act and rules, etc., inconsistent with other enactments.
key_sections.description: Establishes the overriding effect of this Act over inconsistent enactments.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government authority to make rules for implementing the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals a previous Ordinance and includes saving provisions for actions taken under it.

powers_conferred: Power to appoint officers and employees (by Calcutta metro railway administration)
Power to remove persons from metro railway (by metro railway official)
Power to cause packages to be opened (by metro railway official)
Power to sanction opening of metro railway (by Central Government)
Power to remove difficulties (by Central Government)
Power to make rules (by Central Government)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines various offenses related to the operation and use of the metro railway. Penalties include fines ranging from fifty rupees to six thousand rupees, and imprisonment terms ranging from one month to five years, depending on the severity of the offense. Specific offenses include carrying dangerous or offensive goods, smoking, drunkenness or nuisance, holding demonstrations, travelling on the roof of a train, unlawfully entering or walking on the metro railway line, endangering passenger safety by metro railway officials, abandoning duty by metro railway officials, and obstructing train running. Companies and their responsible personnel can also be held liable for offenses.

repealed_acts: The Calcutta Metro Railway (Operation and Maintenance) Temporary Provisions Ordinance, 1984 (13 of 1984)
related_acts: Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Act, 1978 (33 of 1978)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Calcutta metro railway administration (for officers and other employees)

applies_to: metropolitan city of Calcutta
persons travelling in the metro railway
metro railway officials
companies

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through penalties (fines and imprisonment) for various offenses, and metro railway officials are authorized to remove individuals from trains or premises for contraventions.

act_identification.act_title: THE ADMINISTRATIVE TRIBUNALS ACT, 1985
act_identification.date_of_commencement: such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint

legislative_details.geographical_extent: in so far as it relates to the Central Administrative Tribunal, to the whole of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the adjudication or trial by Administrative Tribunals of disputes and complaints with respect to recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union or of any State or of any local or other authority within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India or of [1][any corporation or society owned or controlled by the Government in pursuance of article 323A of the Constitution] and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes Administrative Tribunals for the adjudication of disputes and complaints concerning recruitment and conditions of service for persons in public services and posts under the Union, States, local authorities, or government-controlled corporations/societies, in line with Article 323A of the Constitution.

chapter_titles: ESTABLISHMENT OF TRIBUNALS AND BENCHES THEREOF
JURISDICTION, POWERS AND AUTHORITY OF TRIBUNALS

key_definitions: service rules as to redressal of grievances

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application, and the dates for its commencement for Central and State Tribunals.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply to certain persons.
key_sections.description: Excludes members of armed forces, Supreme Court/High Court staff, and secretarial staff of Parliament/State Legislatures from the Act's applicability.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Administrative Member', 'Judicial Member', 'service matters', and 'appropriate Government'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Administrative Tribunals.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of the Central Administrative Tribunal and allows for the establishment of State and Joint Administrative Tribunals.

key_sections.title: Composition of Tribunals and Benches thereof.
key_sections.description: Details the composition of Tribunals with a Chairman and Judicial/Administrative Members, and how Benches are constituted and function.

key_sections.title: Qualifications for appointment as Chairman, Vice-Chairman and other Members.
key_sections.description: Outlines the eligibility criteria for appointment as Chairman, Administrative Member, and Judicial Member of the Tribunals.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction, powers and authority of the Central Administrative Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Defines the scope of jurisdiction, powers, and authority of the Central Administrative Tribunal over recruitment and service matters for Union public services and government-controlled entities.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction, powers and authority of State Administrative Tribunals.
key_sections.description: Defines the scope of jurisdiction, powers, and authority of State Administrative Tribunals over recruitment and service matters for State public services and state government-controlled entities.

key_sections.title: Power to punish for contempt.
key_sections.description: Grants Tribunals the same power to punish for contempt of themselves as a High Court, with modifications to references in the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971.

key_sections.title: Applications to tribunals.
key_sections.description: Allows aggrieved persons to make applications to Tribunals for redressal of grievances related to service matters, specifying the form and fee requirements.

key_sections.title: Applications not to be admitted unless other remedies exhausted.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that applications will ordinarily not be admitted unless the applicant has exhausted all available remedies under relevant service rules.

key_sections.title: Procedure and powers of Tribunals.
key_sections.description: States that Tribunals are not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure but are guided by natural justice, and outlines their powers, including those of a civil court.

key_sections.title: Execution of orders of a Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Declares that final orders of a Tribunal are final and not questionable in any court (including a High Court) and specifies their execution manner.

key_sections.title: Exclusion of jurisdiction of courts except the Supreme Court under article 136 of the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Excludes the jurisdiction of all courts (except the Supreme Court under Article 136 and certain industrial/labour courts) over matters falling under the Tribunal's jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Transfer of pending cases.
key_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of pending suits and proceedings from courts or other authorities to the newly established Tribunals.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws or instruments.

key_sections.title: Power of the Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, specifying various matters for which rules can be made.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To establish Administrative Tribunals (Section 4).
Central Government: To appoint Chairman and Members of Tribunals (Section 6).
Central Government: To make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act (Section 35).
Central Government: To remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act (Section 34).

State Government: To make rules for specific matters under the Act (Section 36).
President: To appoint Chairman and Members of Tribunals (Section 6).
President: To remove Chairman or Members on grounds of misbehaviour or incapacity (Section 9).

Tribunals: To punish for contempt of itself (Section 17).
Tribunals: To regulate their own procedure (Section 22(1)).
Tribunals: To exercise powers vested in a civil court for certain matters (Section 22(3)).
Chairman: To exercise financial and administrative powers over Benches (Section 12).
Chairman: To transfer cases from one Bench to another (Section 25).
