Chairman: To specify classes of cases for single Member Benches (Section 5(6)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Tribunals have the power to punish for contempt of themselves, similar to a High Court, as per the provisions of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The President appoints the Chairman and other Members of the Tribunals after consultation with the Chief Justice of India (for Central Tribunal) or the Governor of the concerned State (for State Tribunals). The appropriate Government may authorize a Member to act as Chairman in certain circumstances.

applies_to: Persons appointed to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union or of any State.
Persons appointed to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of any local or other authority within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India.
Persons appointed to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of any corporation or society owned or controlled by the Government.
Members of any All-India Service.
Civilians appointed to any defence services or a post connected with defence.
exemptions: Any member of the naval, military or air forces or of any other armed forces of the Union.
Any officer or servant of the Supreme Court or of any High Court or courts subordinate thereto.

Any person appointed to the secretarial staff of either House of Parliament or to the secretarial staff of any State Legislature or a House thereof or, in the case of a Union territory having a Legislature, of that Legislature.
special_provisions: The Act, in so far as it relates to the Central Administrative Tribunal, extends to the whole of India.
Provisions relating to an Administrative Tribunal for a State shall come into force in a State on such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint.
Two or more States may enter into an agreement for a Joint Administrative Tribunal.
References to "Union" in Section 14(1) shall be construed as including references also to a Union territory.

The jurisdiction, powers and authority of the Administrative Tribunal for a State shall not extend to, or be exercisable in relation to, any matter in relation to which the jurisdiction, powers and authority of the Central Administrative Tribunal extends or is exercisable.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Orders of a Tribunal finally disposing of an application or an appeal shall be final and executed in the same manner as any final order under relevant service rules. Tribunals possess powers vested in a civil court for discharging their functions.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The Supreme Court (under article 136 of the Constitution) and any Industrial Tribunal, Labour Court or other authority constituted under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 or any other corresponding law.

act_identification.act_title: THE HANDLOOMS (RESERVATION OF ARTICLES FOR PRODUCTION) ACT, 1985
act_identification.act_short_title: Handlooms (Reservation of Articles for Production) Act, 1985

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for reservation of certain articles for exclusive production by handlooms and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to protect and develop the handloom industry by reserving certain articles for exclusive production by handlooms, thereby prohibiting their production by other means, and provides for related enforcement and penalty mechanisms.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'handloom', 'power loom', 'manufacturer', 'processor', and 'producer'.

key_sections.title: Power to specify articles for exclusive production by handlooms.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to reserve articles for exclusive handloom production for protection and development of the industry.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Advisory Committee.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to constitute an Advisory Committee to recommend articles for reservation.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of production of articles exclusively reserved for handlooms.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the production of reserved articles by any loom other than handlooms, with a temporary exception for existing producers.

key_sections.title: Power to enter and impact.
key_sections.description: Grants authorised officers the power to enter premises, inspect records, and seek information related to manufacturing and storage of textile articles.

key_sections.title: Power to search and seize.
key_sections.description: Authorises officers to search and seize articles or power looms believed to be in contravention of reservation orders.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of orders made under section 3.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment, fine, and forfeiture, for producing articles in contravention of reservation orders.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Stipulates liability for offences committed by companies, including directors and other officers.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable.
key_sections.description: Declares all offences under this Act to be cognizable, notwithstanding the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to exempt certain articles from reservation for export, research, or market development purposes.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to specify articles for exclusive production by handlooms (Section 3)
Central Government: Power to constitute an Advisory Committee (Section 4)
Central Government: Power to require manufacturers to furnish information or samples (Section 6)
Authorised Officer: Power to enter and inspect premises, books of account, registers, records, and documents (Section 7)
Authorised Officer: Power to search and seize articles or power looms produced or used in contravention of orders (Section 8)
Central Government: Power to delegate its powers (except for making orders under section 3 or 18, or rules under section 19) to subordinate officers/authorities or State Governments (Section 15)
Central Government: Power to give directions to State Governments for carrying out the Act's provisions (Section 16)
Central Government: Power to exempt articles from reservation for specific purposes (Section 18)
Central Government: Power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 19)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever produces any article in contravention of a reservation order (Section 3) shall be punishable with imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to five thousand rupees per loom, with additional fines for continuing contravention, and forfeiture of articles/power loom (Section 10). Making false statements or failing to furnish information/samples/documents when required is punishable with imprisonment up to three months or a fine up to five thousand rupees (Section 11). Attempts and abetment of contravention are also deemed offences (Section 12). Offences committed by companies hold the company and responsible individuals liable (Section 13).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government constitutes the Advisory Committee and appoints its members.

applies_to: Manufacturers
Producers
Processors
Companies engaged in manufacturing activities
exemptions: Any person engaged in production of a reserved article by a non-handloom method immediately before the date of reservation may continue for three months (Proviso to Section 5).
The Central Government may exempt articles for export or research purposes (Section 18).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through orders issued by the Central Government, recommendations from the Advisory Committee, powers of authorised officers to inspect, search, and seize, and penalties for contravention. The Central Government can also give directions to State Governments for implementation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The Act refers to 'court' for forfeiture decisions (Section 10) and incorporates provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for search and seizure, implying jurisdiction of criminal courts.

act_identification.act_title: THE BHOPAL GAS LEAK DISASTER (PROCESSING OF CLAIMS) ACT, 1985

act_overview.preamble: An Act to confer certain powers on the Central Government to secure that claims arising out of, or connected with, the Bhopal gas leak disaster are dealt with speedily, effectively, equitably and to the best advantage of the claimants and for matters incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act confers powers on the Central Government to process and manage claims arising from the Bhopal gas leak disaster. Its objective is to ensure that these claims are handled efficiently, fairly, and to the benefit of the claimants.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its deemed date of commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Bhopal gas leak disaster', 'claim', 'claimant', and 'Commissioner'.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to represent claimants.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the exclusive right to represent and act on behalf of all claimants for purposes connected with their claims, including instituting suits or entering compromises.

key_sections.title: Claimant’s right to be represented by a legal practitioner.
key_sections.description: Ensures that claimants can have a legal practitioner of their choice associated with their claim, at their own expense, even while the Central Government represents them.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government.
key_sections.description: Confers powers of a civil court on the Central Government for discharging its functions under the Act, including summoning, discovery of documents, and receiving evidence.

key_sections.title: Commissioner and other officers and employees.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to appoint a Commissioner for the welfare of Bhopal gas leak disaster victims and other assisting officers, outlining their functions and powers.

key_sections.title: Power to delegate.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to delegate its powers under the Act (except the power to frame a Scheme) to the Government of Madhya Pradesh or specified officers.

key_sections.title: Power to frame a Scheme.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to frame a Scheme for carrying out the Act's purposes, detailing matters such as claim registration, processing, fund creation, and disbursal of compensation.

key_sections.title: Overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act and any Scheme framed under it shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in any other enactment.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Bhopal Gas Leak Disaster (Processing of Claims) Ordinance, 1985, while saving actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Central Government: exclusive right to represent and act in place of claimants (Section 3)
Central Government: powers of a civil court while trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Section 5)
Central Government: power to appoint a Commissioner and other officers/employees (Section 6)
Central Government: power to delegate its powers (except framing a Scheme) to the Government of Madhya Pradesh or specified officers (Section 7)
Central Government: power to frame a Scheme (Section 9)
Commissioner: to discharge functions assigned by the Scheme (Section 6(2))
Commissioner and authorised officers: to exercise powers of the Central Government under section 5 for discharging functions under the Scheme (Section 6(3))

repealed_acts: The Bhopal Gas Leak Disaster (Processing of Claims) Ordinance, 1985 (1 of 1985)

authorities_established: Commissioner for the welfare of the victims of the Bhopal gas leak disaster
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government has the power to appoint the Commissioner and other officers and employees to assist him (Section 6(1)).

applies_to: Every person who has made, or is entitled to make, a claim arising out of, or connected with, the Bhopal gas leak disaster

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (power to frame a Scheme under Section 9)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government represents claimants, exercises civil court powers, and frames a Scheme for claim registration, processing, and disbursal. A Commissioner and other officers assist in these functions. Government officers and authorities are required to aid the Commissioner.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The Central Government and the Commissioner (and authorised officers) are vested with powers of a civil court. The Act also refers to 'any court or other authority' for institution or withdrawal of suits or proceedings related to claims.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIRA GANDHI NATIONAL OPEN UNIVERSITY ACT, 1985
act_identification.act_short_title: The Indira Gandhi National Open University Act, 1985

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India and to the Study Centres outside India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate an open University at the national level for the introduction and promotion of the open university and distance education systems in the educational pattern of the country and for the co-ordination and determination of standards in such systems.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes and incorporates the Indira Gandhi National Open University at a national level. Its primary purpose is to introduce and promote open university and distance education systems, and to coordinate and determine standards within these systems across the country.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the official short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act and the Statutes made thereunder.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of the University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Indira Gandhi National Open University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with its headquarters at Delhi.

key_sections.title: The objects of the University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary goals of the University, including advancing knowledge, providing higher education opportunities, and promoting open and distance education systems.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers of the University, such as providing instruction, conferring degrees, establishing centres, and managing finances.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Specifies that the University's jurisdiction extends over the whole of India and to Study Centres outside India.

key_sections.title: The Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University and details the Visitor's powers of inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the designated officers of the University, including the Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellors, Directors, Registrars, and Finance Officer.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University
key_sections.description: Lists the principal authorities of the University, such as the Board of Management, Academic Council, and Planning Board.

key_sections.title: Statutes.
key_sections.description: Outlines the matters for which the Statutes may provide, including appointment of officers, constitution of authorities, and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Statutes how made.
key_sections.description: Describes the process for making, amending, or repealing Statutes, requiring approval from the Visitor.

key_sections.title: Tribunal of Arbitration.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Tribunal of Arbitration for resolving disputes arising from employment contracts between the University and its employees.

key_sections.title: Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Mandates the publication of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations in the Official Gazette and their presentation before both Houses of Parliament.

powers_conferred: Power to provide for instruction in various branches of knowledge, technology, vocations and professions and to make provision for research (University)
Power to plan and prescribe courses of study for degrees, diplomas, certificates or other purposes (University)
Power to hold examinations and confer degrees, diplomas, certificates or other academic distinctions (University)
Power to confer honorary degrees or other distinctions (University)
Power to determine the manner of organizing distance education (University)
Power to institute professorships, readerships, lecturerships and other academic positions and appoint persons thereto (University)
Power to co-operate with other universities and institutions (University)
Power to institute and award fellowships, scholarships, prizes and other awards (University)
Power to establish and maintain Regional Centres (University)
Power to establish, maintain or recognise Study Centres (University)
Power to provide for the preparation of instructional materials (University)
Power to organise and conduct refresher courses, workshops, seminars and other programmes (University)
Power to recognise examinations or periods of study from other institutions (University)
Power to make provision for research and development in educational technology (University)
Power to create administrative, ministerial and other necessary posts and make appointments (University)
Power to receive benefactions, donations and gifts and to acquire, hold, maintain and dispose of property (University)
Power to borrow money with Central Government approval (University)
Power to enter into, carry out, vary or cancel contracts (University)
Power to demand and receive fees and other charges (University)
Power to provide, control and maintain discipline among students and employees (University)
Power to recognise any institution of higher learning or studies (University)
Power to appoint visiting Professors, Emeritus Professors, Consultants, fellows, scholars, artists, course writers (University)
Power to recognise persons working in other universities as teachers of the University (University)
Power to determine standards and specify conditions for student admission (University)
Power to make arrangements for the promotion of general health and welfare of employees (University)
Power to confer autonomous status on a College or a Regional Centre (University)
Power to admit to its privileges any College in or outside India (University)
Power to take steps for the promotion of open university and distance education systems and for determination of standards (University)
Power to allocate and disburse grants to Colleges or other universities/institutions (University)
Power to cause an inspection or inquiry of the University and its components (Visitor)
Power to issue directions to the Board of Management (Visitor)
Power to annul any proceedings of the University not in conformity with the Act, Statutes or Ordinances (Visitor)
Power to exercise supervision and control over the affairs of the University and give effect to decisions of authorities (Vice-Chancellor)
Power to take immediate action on any matter and report to the authority (Vice-Chancellor)
Power to make new or additional Statutes or amend or repeal existing Statutes (Board of Management, with Visitor's approval)
Power to make new or additional Statutes or amend or repeal existing Statutes for three years after commencement (Visitor)
Power to direct the University to make provisions in the Statutes (Visitor)
Power to make Ordinances (Vice-Chancellor with Central Government approval, then Board of Management)
Power to make Regulations (Authorities of the University)
Power of management and administration of the revenue and property of the University (Board of Management)
Power to create teaching and other academic posts and define their functions and conditions of service (Board of Management)
Power to approve the appointment of teachers and academic staff (Board of Management)
Power to manage and regulate the finances, accounts, investments, property (Board of Management)
Power to invest money belonging to the University (Board of Management)
Power to create administrative, ministerial and other necessary posts (Board of Management)
Power to regulate and enforce discipline amongst employees (Board of Management)
Power to transfer or accept transfers of property (Board of Management)
Power to entertain, adjudicate upon, or redress grievances of employees and students (Board of Management)
Power to fix remuneration for course writers, counsellors, examiners, invigilators (Board of Management)
Power to delegate any of its powers (Board of Management)
Power to exercise general supervision over the academic policies of the University and give directions (Academic Council)
Power to design and formulate appropriate programmes and activities of the University (Planning Board)
Power to examine the accounts and scrutinise the expenditure (Finance Committee)
Power to fix the limits for the total recurring and non-recurring expenditure (Finance Committee)
Power to appoint Professors, Readers, Lecturers and other teachers (Vice-Chancellor, with Board of Management approval, as per Statutes)
Power to appoint course writers, script writers, counsellors, programmers, artists (Vice-Chancellor, as per Statutes)
Power to take disciplinary action against specified employees (Registrar, as per Statutes)
Power to maintain discipline amongst students and take disciplinary action (Vice-Chancellor)

authorities_established: the Indira Gandhi National Open University
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Vice-Chancellor. The Board of Management appoints Pro-Vice-Chancellors, Directors, Registrars, and the Finance Officer, and approves the appointment of Professors, Readers, Lecturers, and other teachers and academic staff. The Vice-Chancellor appoints course writers, script writers, counsellors, programmers, artists, and persons for short-term appointments.
regulatory_bodies: Indira Gandhi National Open University (for co-ordination and determination of standards in open university and distance education systems)
Board of Recognition (for admitting Colleges to the privileges of the University)
Academic Council (for control and general regulation of, and responsibility for, maintenance of standards of learning, education, instruction, evaluation and examination)

applies_to: Persons of either sex and of whatever race, creed, caste or class
Students pursuing any course of study of the University
Employees of the University
Colleges or other academic institutions established or maintained by, or admitted to the privileges of, the University
Regional Centres and Study Centres
special_provisions: Special provision for the appointment or admission of women or of persons belonging to the weaker sections of the society, and in particular, of persons belonging to the Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes.
The University may, with the prior approval of the Visitor, establish Study Centres outside India.
Transitional provisions for the appointment of the first Vice-Chancellor, Registrars, Finance Officer, and the constitution of the first Board of Management and Planning Board.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Statutes are made by the Board of Management with the approval of the Visitor, or by the Visitor directly under certain conditions. Ordinances are initially made by the Vice-Chancellor with Central Government approval, and subsequently by the Board of Management. Regulations are made by the authorities of the University.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor has powers of inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions to ensure compliance. The Vice-Chancellor exercises supervision and control over University affairs. The Board of Management manages and administers the University's property and enforces discipline. Disputes arising from employment contracts are referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration. Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations are published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.

schedules_summary.description: Details the objects of the University, including strengthening courses, providing access to higher education for disadvantaged groups, promoting knowledge acquisition, offering innovative education, improving the educational system, providing training in arts/crafts/skills, post-graduate courses, counselling, and promoting national integration.

Contains the first Statutes of the University, covering the appointment, term, emoluments, powers, and functions of the Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellors, Directors, Registrars, and Finance Officer. It also details the powers and functions of the Board of Management, Academic Council, Planning Board, Finance Committee, Selection Committees, special appointment modes, recognised teachers, committees, terms and conditions of service, and removal of employees.

act_identification.act_title: THE PONDICHERRY UNIVERSITY ACT, 1985

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of the Union territory of Pondicherry; may extend to the Union territory of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands or of the Union territory of Lakshadweep with prior Central Government approval.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University in the Union territory of Pondicherry and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to establish and incorporate the Pondicherry University as a teaching and affiliating body. It aims to disseminate and advance knowledge, provide instructional and research facilities, and make special provisions for studies in French, integrated courses, and inter-disciplinary research.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act and the Statutes.

key_sections.title: The University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Pondicherry University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, headquartered at Pondicherry.

key_sections.title: Objects.
key_sections.description: Outlines the objectives of the University, including knowledge dissemination, research, special provisions for French studies, integrated courses, and inter-disciplinary studies.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers of the University, such as providing instruction, granting degrees, establishing institutions, and managing its affairs.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Defines the geographical extent of the University's jurisdiction and conditions for affiliation of colleges and institutions.

key_sections.title: Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor and outlines his powers of inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the various officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Directors, Deans, Registrar, and Finance Officer.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities of the University, such as the Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Boards of Schools, and Planning Board.

key_sections.title: Power to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Statutes can be made, covering constitution of authorities, appointment of officers and staff, and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Details the matters for which Ordinances can be made, including student admission, courses of study, examinations, and conditions of residence.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees.
key_sections.description: Mandates written contracts for employees and provides for arbitration in disputes between the University and employees.

key_sections.title: Procedure of appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for students to appeal disciplinary actions and provides for arbitration in disputes.

key_sections.title: Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Requires publication of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations in the Official Gazette and their presentation before Parliament.

powers_conferred: University: To provide instruction and research facilities, grant diplomas/degrees, organize extra-mural studies, confer honorary degrees, institute teaching/academic posts, recognise institutions, appoint teachers, create administrative posts, co-operate with other institutions, establish campuses/centres, award fellowships/scholarships, maintain colleges/institutions, provide research/advisory services, admit colleges to privileges, declare autonomous colleges, determine admission standards, demand fees, supervise student residences, make special arrangements for women students, regulate discipline, promote employee welfare, receive donations, acquire/hold/manage/dispose of property, borrow money.

Visitor: To cause inspection or inquiry of the University and its institutions, issue directions to the Executive Council or management, annul proceedings of the University, appoint Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor (including first appointments).

Executive Council: To manage and administer the revenue and property of the University, conduct administrative affairs, create teaching/academic/administrative posts, appoint staff, grant leave, regulate employee discipline, manage finances/accounts/investments, fix expenditure limits, invest money, transfer property, provide infrastructure, enter into contracts, redress grievances, appoint examiners, select common seal, make special arrangements for women students, delegate powers, institute fellowships/scholarships.

Academic Council: To coordinate and exercise general supervision over academic policies, bring about inter-School coordination, establish committees/boards for projects, consider academic matters, frame regulations regarding academic functioning, discipline, admissions, fellowships, etc.

Vice-Chancellor: To be the principal executive and academic officer, exercise general supervision and control, take immediate action in emergencies, preside at convocations, be ex officio Chairman of Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, and Finance Committee, ensure observance of Act/Statutes/Ordinances/Regulations, convene meetings, take disciplinary action against students.
Registrar: To enter into agreements, sign documents, authenticate records, take disciplinary action against non-academic staff (with appeal to Vice-Chancellor).

Finance Officer: To exercise general supervision over University funds, advise on financial policy, hold and manage property/investments, ensure expenditure limits, prepare annual accounts and budget, monitor cash/bank balances, watch revenue collection, ensure asset registers are maintained, call for explanations for financial irregularities, call for information from departments.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for disciplinary actions against students, including expulsion, rustication, debarring from examinations, fines, and cancellation of results (Section 30). For teachers and academic staff, removal from service can occur on grounds of misconduct, requiring a two-thirds majority vote of the Executive Council (Statute 26). Other employees can also be removed for reasons like unsound mind, insolvency, conviction for moral turpitude, or misconduct (Statute 27).

authorities_established: Sri Aurobindo School of Eastern and Western Thought
Subramania Bharati School of Tamil Language and Literature
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and during transitional periods, the first Registrar, Finance Officer, and members of the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council. The Executive Council appoints Directors, Registrar, Finance Officer, Heads of Departments, Proctors, Librarians, Professors, Readers, Lecturers, other academic staff, and Principals of Colleges/Institutions. The Vice-Chancellor appoints Deans of Schools.

applies_to: Persons of either sex and of whatever race, creed, caste, or class.
French nationals of Indian origin residing in Pondicherry.
Colleges and institutions situated within the Union territory of Pondicherry.
exemptions: The University may make special provisions for the weaker sections of the people, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
special_provisions: Special provisions for studies in French and for integrated courses for humanity and science.
Establishment of Sri Aurobindo School of Eastern and Western Thought and Subramania Bharati School of Tamil Language and Literature.
Jurisdiction may be extended to Andaman and Nicobar Islands or Lakshadweep.
Special provisions for weaker sections, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
French nationals of Indian origin are eligible for admission.
Special arrangements for women students.
Transitional provisions for the appointment of first officers and constitution of authorities.
Provisions for students to complete courses from previously affiliated universities (University of Madras, University of Calicut, Andhra University).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Statutes are made by the Executive Council (with Visitor's assent) or the Visitor directly. Ordinances are initially made by the Vice-Chancellor (with Central Government approval) and subsequently by the Executive Council. Regulations are made by the authorities of the University.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor has powers of inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions. The Vice-Chancellor exercises general supervision and control. The Executive Council manages administration and finances. Disciplinary actions are taken by the Vice-Chancellor, Discipline Committee, Examination Committee, and Principals. Disputes involving employees and students can be referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration. Appeals against decisions of officers or authorities can be made to the Executive Council.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The Act specifies that no suit shall lie in any civil court for matters decided by the Tribunal of Arbitration (Section 31(2)) or for the Visitor's decision on disqualification (Statute 36(2)).

schedules_summary.description: Contains the detailed Statutes of the University, covering the powers and duties of the Vice-Chancellor, Directors, Registrar, Finance Officer, Deans of Schools, Heads of Departments, Proctors, and Librarians. It also outlines the constitution, powers, and functions of the Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Planning Board, Schools of Studies, Departments, Boards of Studies, Finance Committee, and Selection Committees. Further, it details provisions for special modes of appointment, recognised teachers, committees, terms and conditions of service for teachers and other employees, seniority lists, removal procedures, honorary degrees, withdrawal of degrees, maintenance of discipline among students, admission of colleges to privileges, convocations, resignation, disqualifications, and the process for making Ordinances and Regulations.

act_identification.act_title: THE INTELLIGENCE ORGANISATIONS (RESTRICTION OF RIGHTS) ACT, 1985
act_identification.act_short_title: The Intelligence Organisations (Restriction of Rights) Act, 1985

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the restriction of certain rights conferred by Part III of the Constitution in their application to the members of certain organisations established by the Central Government for purposes of intelligence or counter-intelligence so as to ensure the proper discharge of their duties and the maintenance of discipline among them.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to restrict certain fundamental rights of members of intelligence and counter-intelligence organizations established by the Central Government. Its purpose is to ensure the proper discharge of duties and the maintenance of discipline among these members.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its application to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Intelligence Organisation', 'member of an Intelligence Organisation', and 'prescribed'.

key_sections.title: Restrictions respecting right to form association, freedom of speech, etc.
key_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on members of Intelligence Organisations regarding forming associations, freedom of speech, communication with the press, and contact with persons on official matters.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of the provisions of section 3, including imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to two thousand rupees, or both.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable.
key_sections.description: Declares that all offences punishable under section 4 shall be cognizable, notwithstanding anything in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

key_sections.title: Power to amend Schedule.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to amend the Schedule by adding or removing organisations through notification in the Official Gazette.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act and mandates that such rules be laid before each House of Parliament.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint commencement date (Section 1(3))
Central Government to decide on the nature of societies/institutions (Section 3 Explanation)
Head of the Intelligence Organisation to grant prior permission for communication/publication (Section 3(1)(c))

act_identification.act_title: THE JUDGES (PROTECTION) ACT, 1985

act_overview.preamble: An Act for securing additional protection for Judges and others acting Judicially and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: The primary purpose of this Act is to provide additional legal protection to Judges and individuals performing judicial functions, safeguarding them from civil or criminal proceedings for actions undertaken in their official capacity. It also clarifies that this protection does not impede the disciplinary powers of the Central Government, State Government, Supreme Court, or High Courts against Judges.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Judges (Protection) Act, 1985, and specifies its applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines the term 'Judge' to include not only officially designated Judges but also persons empowered by law to give definitive judgments or part of a body empowered to do so.

key_sections.title: Additional protection to Judges.
key_sections.description: Provides that no court shall entertain civil or criminal proceedings against a person who is or was a Judge for acts done in discharge of official or judicial duty, but clarifies this does not affect the power of governments or higher courts to take action against Judges.

key_sections.title: Saving.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act are in addition to, and not in derogation of, other laws providing protection to Judges.

applies_to: every person who is officially designated as a Judge

every person who is empowered by law to give in any legal proceeding a definitive judgment, or a judgment which, if not appealed against, would be definitive, or a judgment which, if confirmed by some other authority, would be definitive
every person who is one of a body of persons which body of persons is empowered by law to give such a judgment as is referred to in clause (a)

act_identification.act_title: THE NARCOTIC DRUGS AND PSYCHOTROPIC SUBSTANCES ACT, 1985
act_identification.act_short_title: The Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India and it applies also— (a) to all citizens of India outside India; (b) to all persons on ships and aircrafts registered in India, wherever they may be

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to narcotic drugs, to make stringent provisions for the control and regulation of operations relating to narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances [, to provide for the forfeiture of property derived from, or used in, illicit traffic in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, to implement the provisions of the International Conventions on Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances] and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the law concerning narcotic drugs, establish stringent controls and regulations for operations involving narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, provide for the forfeiture of property linked to illicit drug traffic, and implement international conventions on narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.

chapter_titles: NATIONAL FUND FOR CONTROL OF DRUG ABUSE

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its application to the whole of India and citizens/vessels outside India, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'narcotic drug', 'psychotropic substance', 'illicit traffic', 'commercial quantity', and 'small quantity'.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of certain operations.
key_sections.description: Prohibits cultivation, production, manufacture, possession, sale, purchase, transport, use, etc., of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, except for medical or scientific purposes under specific conditions.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to permit, control and regulate.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make rules to permit and regulate various operations related to coca plant, opium poppy, opium, manufactured drugs, psychotropic substances, and their import/export.

key_sections.title: Punishment for contravention in relation to poppy straw.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishments, including rigorous imprisonment and fines, for contraventions involving poppy straw, with varying degrees based on quantity (small, lesser than commercial, commercial).

key_sections.title: Punishment for contravention in relation to manufactured drugs and preparations.
key_sections.description: Outlines punishments for illegal manufacture, possession, sale, purchase, transport, import, export, or use of manufactured drugs and preparations, scaled by quantity.

key_sections.title: Punishment for financing illicit traffic and harbouring offenders.
key_sections.description: Imposes rigorous imprisonment and substantial fines for financing illicit drug traffic or harbouring offenders involved in such activities.

key_sections.title: Death penalty for certain offences after previous conviction.
key_sections.description: Provides for the death penalty for specific serious drug-related offenses involving commercial quantities after a previous conviction for certain offenses.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Special Court.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Government to constitute Special Courts for speedy trial of offenses under the Act.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable and non-bailable.
key_sections.description: Declares all offenses under the Act as cognizable and specifies strict conditions for granting bail, especially for serious offenses.

key_sections.title: Power to issue warrant and authorisation.
key_sections.description: Grants Magistrates and authorized gazetted officers the power to issue warrants for arrest or search related to offenses under the Act, including for illegally acquired property.

key_sections.title: Power of entry, search, seizure and arrest without warrant or authorisation.
key_sections.description: Authorizes specific officers to enter, search, seize, and arrest without a warrant under certain conditions, particularly when there is a belief that evidence might be concealed or offenders might escape.

key_sections.title: Disposal of seized narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.
key_sections.description: Establishes a procedure for the speedy disposal of seized narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, controlled substances, or conveyances, including inventory, photography, and sampling before a Magistrate.

key_sections.title: Immunity from prosecution to addicts volunteering for treatment.
key_sections.description: Offers immunity from prosecution to addicts charged with certain offenses (consumption or small quantity offenses) who voluntarily seek and undergo medical treatment for de-addiction.

key_sections.title: Application.
key_sections.description: Defines the categories of persons to whom the provisions of Chapter VA (Forfeiture of Illegally Acquired Property) apply, including convicted persons, those detained, and their relatives/associates.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter IV details various offenses and their corresponding penalties. These include punishments for contravention in relation to poppy straw, coca plant, coca leaves, prepared opium, opium poppy, opium, embezzlement of opium by cultivator, cannabis plant, cannabis, manufactured drugs, psychotropic substances, illegal import/export/transhipment, external dealings in contravention of section 12, allowing premises to be used for an offense, contravention of orders under section 9A, certain acts by licensees or their servants, consumption of narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances, financing illicit traffic, harbouring offenders, contravention of section 8A, attempts to commit offenses, abetment and criminal conspiracy, and preparation. Penalties range from imprisonment (rigorous, up to one year, ten years, twenty years) and fines (up to ten thousand, one lakh, two lakh rupees), with enhanced punishments for repeat offenders and a death penalty for certain offenses involving commercial quantities after previous conviction. There are also provisions for offenses for which no specific punishment is provided, and factors for imposing higher than minimum punishment.

special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act and for different States for commencement.

Section 360 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 do not apply to persons convicted under this Act, unless they are under eighteen years of age or the offense is punishable under section 26 or section 27.
High Court retains special powers regarding bail under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
Transitional provisions for trial of offenses by Court of Session until Special Courts are constituted.

For persons accused of offenses under section 19, 24, 27A or involving commercial quantity, the detention period under section 167 of CrPC is extended to 180 days, extendable up to one year by Special Court.
Offenses punishable with imprisonment for not more than three years may be tried summarily.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through various authorities and officers of the Central and State Governments, including the Narcotics Commissioner. It involves measures for preventing and combating abuse and illicit traffic, and for ensuring medical/scientific use. Enforcement includes powers of arrest, search, seizure, and investigation by authorized officers, trial by Special Courts, and provisions for confiscation of illicit articles and forfeiture of illegally acquired property. The Act also provides for immunity from prosecution for addicts volunteering for treatment and for rule-making by governments.

act_identification.act_title: THE INLAND WATERWAYS AUTHORITY OF INDIA ACT, 1985
act_identification.act_short_title: the Inland Waterways Authority of India Act, 1985

legislative_details.geographical_extent: National waterways as declared by law

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution of an Authority for the regulation and development of inland waterways for purposes of shipping and navigation and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Inland Waterways Authority of India to regulate and develop inland waterways for shipping and navigation. Its primary objective is to ensure the safe and efficient use of these waterways and to provide necessary infrastructure and services.

chapter_titles: FUNCTIONS AND POWERS OF THE AUTHORITY

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Authority', 'national waterway', and 'infrastructure'.

key_sections.title: Constitution and incorporation of the Inland Waterways Authority of India.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Inland Waterways Authority of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, and outlines its composition.

key_sections.title: Transfer of assets and liabilities of the Central Government to the Authority.
key_sections.description: Details the transfer of properties, assets, liabilities, contracts, and employees from the Central Government's Inland Water Transport Directorate to the Authority.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Authority.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the core functions and powers of the Authority, including surveys, infrastructure provision, conservancy, regulation of navigation, and coordination of transport.

key_sections.title: Levy and collection of fees and charges.
key_sections.description: Grants the Authority the power to levy and collect fees and charges for services or benefits rendered in relation to the use of national waterways.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Inland Waterways Authority of India Fund, specifying sources of credit and purposes for which the fund shall be applied.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to issue directions.
key_sections.description: States that the Authority is bound by policy directions issued by the Central Government in the discharge of its functions and duties.

key_sections.title: Members, officers and employees of the Authority to be public servants.
key_sections.description: Declares all members, officers, and employees of the Authority to be public servants within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code when acting in pursuance of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, covering various administrative and procedural matters.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Authority, with Central Government approval, to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules, particularly concerning operational aspects of waterways.

act_identification.act_title: THE MUSLIM WOMEN (PROTECTION OF RIGHTS ON DIVORCE) ACT, 1986
act_identification.act_short_title: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986

act_overview.preamble: An Act to protect the rights of Muslim women who have been divorced by, or have obtained divorce from, their husbands and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to protect the rights of Muslim women who have been divorced by, or have obtained divorce from, their husbands. It provides for their maintenance, provision, and the return of their properties, and addresses related matters.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its geographical applicability.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, such as 'divorced woman', 'iddat period', 'Magistrate', and 'prescribed'.

key_sections.title: _Mahr or other properties of Muslim woman to be given to her at the time of divorce._
key_sections.description: Entitles a divorced Muslim woman to reasonable provision and maintenance, maintenance for children, mahr or dower, and properties received, to be paid/delivered by her former husband within the iddat period. Allows application to a Magistrate for enforcement.

key_sections.title: Order for payment of maintenance.
key_sections.description: Provides for maintenance for a divorced woman who has not re-married and cannot maintain herself after the iddat period, to be paid by her relatives who would inherit her property, or by the State Wakf Board if relatives are unable or non-existent.

key_sections.title: Option to be governed by the provisions of sections 125 to 128 of Act 2 of 1974.
key_sections.description: Allows a divorced woman and her former husband to jointly or separately declare their preference to be governed by sections 125 to 128 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Transitional provisions.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that applications by divorced women under sections 125 or 127 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, pending at the commencement of this Act, shall be disposed of in accordance with this Act, subject to section 5.

powers_conferred: Magistrate: To order payment of provision, maintenance, mahr, dower, or delivery of properties (Section 3(3)).
Magistrate: To issue a warrant for levying amounts and sentence to imprisonment for non-compliance (Section 3(4)).
Magistrate: To order relatives or the State Wakf Board to pay maintenance (Section 4).
Magistrate: To dispose of applications under the Act (Section 5, 7).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 6).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Failure to comply with a Magistrate's order for payment of maintenance or mahr/dower, or delivery of properties, may result in a warrant for levying the amount and imprisonment for a term up to one year, or until payment is made (Section 3(4)).

applies_to: Muslim women who have been divorced by, or have obtained divorce from, their husbands
special_provisions: Option for divorced woman and former husband to be governed by sections 125 to 128 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Section 5).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Applications are made to a Magistrate. The Magistrate can issue orders for payment/delivery, warrants for levying amounts, and impose imprisonment for non-compliance. (Sections 3, 4)
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate of the First class exercising jurisdiction under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Section 2(c))

act_identification.act_short_title: Coal Mines Labour Welfare Fund (Repeal) Act, 1986

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to repeal the Coal Mines Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1947. It also provides for the dissolution of the Coal Mines Labour Housing Board and outlines the consequential transfer of its rights, properties, liabilities, and ongoing legal matters to the Central Government or a Government company.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Act 32 of 1947 and dissolution of Housing Board.

key_sections.title: Consequential provisions.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of rights in a Government company.

related_acts: Coal Mines Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1947

act_identification.act_title: THE ENVIRONMENT (PROTECTION) ACT, 1986

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Thirty-seventh Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the protection and improvement of environment and for matters connected therewith. WHEREAS decisions were taken at the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment held at Stockholm in June, 1972, in which India participated, to take appropriate steps for the protection and improvement of human environment; AND WHEREAS it is considered necessary further to implement the decisions aforesaid in so far as they relate to the protection and improvement of environment and the prevention of hazards to human beings, other living creatures, plants and property;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the protection and improvement of the environment and for matters connected therewith. It aims to implement decisions from the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment, specifically concerning the protection and improvement of human environment and the prevention of hazards to human beings, other living creatures, plants, and property.

chapter_titles: GENERAL POWERS OF THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT
PREVENTION, CONTROL AND ABATEMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL POLLUCTION

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'environment', 'environmental pollutant', and 'hazardous substance'.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to take measures to protect and improve environment.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government broad powers to take necessary measures for environmental protection and improvement, including coordination, planning, setting standards, and restricting industrial activities.

key_sections.title: Power to give directions.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue binding directions to any person, officer, or authority, including directions for closure or regulation of industries.

key_sections.title: Appeal to National Green Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Allows persons aggrieved by directions under section 5 to appeal to the National Green Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Persons carrying on industry, operations, etc., not to allow emission or discharge of environmental pollutants in excess of the standards.
key_sections.description: Prohibits industries from discharging environmental pollutants beyond prescribed standards.

key_sections.title: Persons handling hazardous substances to comply with procedural safeguards.
key_sections.description: Requires compliance with prescribed procedures and safeguards for handling hazardous substances.

key_sections.title: Powers of entry and inspection.
key_sections.description: Grants empowered persons the right to enter and inspect premises for enforcement purposes, including examining equipment and seizing materials.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of section 7 or section 8.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravening provisions related to emission standards and handling hazardous substances.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of provisions of Act, rules, orders and directions.
key_sections.description: Stipulates penalties for general contraventions of the Act, rules, orders, and directions where no specific penalty is provided.

key_sections.title: Adjudicating officer.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of adjudicating officers by the Central Government to determine and impose penalties under the Act.

key_sections.title: Environmental Protection Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Environmental Protection Fund, detailing its credits and application for environmental protection activities.

key_sections.title: Cognizance of offences.
key_sections.description: Specifies who can make a complaint for an offence under the Act, including the Central Government or any person after giving notice.

key_sections.title: Power to delegate.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to delegate its powers and functions under the Act to officers, State Governments, or other authorities, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, covering various specific matters.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to take measures to protect and improve environment (Section 3)
Central Government: Power to appoint officers and entrust them with powers and functions (Section 4)
Central Government: Power to give directions to any person, officer or authority (Section 5)
Central Government: Power to make rules to regulate environmental pollution (Section 6)
Central Government: Power to establish or recognise environmental laboratories (Section 12)
Central Government: Power to appoint or recognise Government Analysts (Section 13)
Central Government: Power to appoint adjudicating officers (Section 15C)
Central Government: Power to establish an Environmental Protection Fund (Section 16)
Central Government: Power to require information, reports or returns (Section 20)
Central Government: Power to delegate its powers and functions (Section 23)
Central Government: Power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 25)

Adjudicating officer: Power to hold an inquiry and impose penalty (Section 15C)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for various contraventions: for contravention of section 7 or 8, a penalty of not less than one lakh rupees and up to fifteen lakh rupees, with an additional fifty thousand rupees per day for continuing contravention (Section 14A). For contravention of sections 9, 10, or 11, a penalty of not less than ten thousand rupees and up to five lakh rupees, with an additional ten thousand rupees per day for continuing contravention (Section 14B). For general contraventions of the Act, rules, orders, or directions where no specific penalty is provided, a penalty of not less than ten thousand rupees and up to fifteen lakh rupees, with an additional ten thousand rupees per day for continuing contravention (Section 15). Companies face a penalty of not less than one lakh rupees and up to fifteen lakh rupees, with an additional one lakh rupees per day for continuing contravention (Section 15A). Heads of Government Departments and other officers are liable to a penalty equal to one month of their basic salary for contraventions, with certain provisos (Section 15B). Failure to pay a penalty within ninety days may result in imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to twice the penalty amount, or both (Section 15F).

authorities_established: Authority or authorities constituted under Section 3(3)
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint officers (Section 4), Government Analysts (Section 13), and adjudicating officers (Section 15C).

Persons carrying on any industry, operation or process
Persons handling hazardous substances
Companies
Departments of the Central Government or the State Government

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government is empowered to take all necessary measures for environmental protection, including issuing directions, making rules, and appointing officers for enforcement. Enforcement involves inspections, sample collection, and imposition of penalties for contraventions. Adjudicating officers determine and impose penalties, with provisions for appeals to the National Green Tribunal. Offences can be cognized based on complaints from the Central Government, authorized officers, or private individuals after due notice.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: National Green Tribunal (for appeals against directions and orders of adjudicating officers). Civil courts are barred from having jurisdiction over actions taken under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE SWADESHI COTTON MILLS COMPANY LIMITED (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKINGS) ACT, 1986
act_identification.act_short_title: The Swadeshi Cotton Mills Company Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1986

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the acquisition and transfer of certain textile undertakings of the Swadeshi Cotton Mills Company Limited, with a view to securing the proper management of such undertakings so as to subserve the interests of the general public by ensuring the continued manufacture, production and distribution of different varieties of cloth and yarn and thereby to give effect to the policy of the State towards securing the principles specified in clauses (b) and (c) of article 39 of the Constitution and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS the Swadeshi Cotton Mills Company Limited has, through its six textile undertakings, been engaged in the manufacture and production of different varieties of cloth and yarn; AND WHEREAS the management of the said textile undertakings was taken over by the Central Government under section 18AA of the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951(65 of 1951); AND WHEREAS large sums of money have been invested with a view to making the said textile undertakings viable; AND WHEREAS further investment of very large sums of money is necessary for the purpose of securing the optimum utilisation of the available facilities for the manufacture, production and distribution of cloth and yarn by the said textile undertakings of the Company; AND WHEREAS such investment is also necessary for securing the continued employment of the workmen employed in the said textile undertakings; AND WHEREAS it is necessary in the public interest to acquire the said textile undertakings of the Swadeshi Cotton Mills Company Limited to ensure that the interests of the general public are served by the continuance by the said undertakings of the Company of the manufacture, production and distribution of different varieties of cloth and yarn which are vital to the needs of the country; AND WHEREAS such acquisition is for giving effect to the policy of the State towards securing the principles specified in clauses (a) and (b) of article 39 of the Constitution;
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the acquisition and transfer of the textile undertakings of Swadeshi Cotton Mills Company Limited. Its main objective is to ensure proper management, continued manufacture, production, and distribution of cloth and yarn, thereby serving public interest and securing employment, in line with constitutional principles.

chapter_titles: ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF THE TEXTILE UNDERTAKINGS
MANAGEMENT, ETC., OF THE TEXTILE UNDERTAKINGS
PROVISIONS RELATING TO EMPLOYEES OF THE TEXTILE UNDERTAKINGS

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and specifies the commencement dates for different provisions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'Commissioner', 'Company', and 'textile undertakings'.

key_sections.title: Transfer and vesting of the textile undertakings.
key_sections.description: Mandates the transfer and vesting of the Company's textile undertakings first in the Central Government and then immediately in the National Textile Corporation on the appointed day.

key_sections.title: General effect of vesting.
key_sections.description: Details the comprehensive nature of the vesting, including all assets, rights, and properties, and declares them free from encumbrances, while allowing mortgagees to claim from the specified amounts.

key_sections.title: Payment of amount.
key_sections.description: Specifies the amount of rupees twenty-four crores and thirty-two lakhs to be paid by the Central Government to the Company for the acquisition of its textile undertakings.

key_sections.title: Payment of further amounts.
key_sections.description: Provides for additional payments to the Company for the deprivation of management and retrospective operation of the Act, including interest.

key_sections.title: Management, etc., of the textile undertakings.
key_sections.description: Grants the National Textile Corporation or its specified person the powers of general superintendence, direction, control, and management of the acquired textile undertakings.

key_sections.title: Continuance of employees of the textile undertakings.
key_sections.description: Ensures that employees of the textile undertakings become employees of the National Textile Corporation with existing rights and privileges, without entitlement to compensation for transfer of services.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Commissioner of Payments.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to appoint a Commissioner of Payments for disbursing the amounts payable to the Company under the Act.

key_sections.title: Claims to be made to the Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Requires persons with claims against the Company related to the textile undertakings to prefer such claims before the Commissioner within a specified period.

key_sections.title: Priorities of claims.
key_sections.description: Establishes a hierarchical order of priorities (Category I, II, etc.) for the discharge of claims specified in the Schedule.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws, instruments, decrees, or orders.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for various offences such as wrongful withholding of property, failure to deliver assets, or making false claims.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act and specifies matters for which rules may be made.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Swadeshi Cotton Mills Company Limited (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Ordinance, 1986, while saving actions taken under it.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint Commissioner of Payments (S.15), pay amounts (S.16), assume undischarged liabilities (S.25), direct NTC to discharge liabilities (S.25), make rules (S.31), remove difficulties (S.32), delegate powers (S.30).

National Textile Corporation: To receive vested undertakings (S.3), manage undertakings (S.10), transfer undertakings to subsidiaries (S.6), receive money due to undertakings (S.17), make claims to Commissioner (S.17), ratify contracts (S.26), dispose of assets with Central Government sanction (S.10A).

Section 28 addresses offences committed by companies and specifies liability for persons in charge and directors/managers.

six textile undertakings of the Company
Employees of the textile undertakings

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the acquisition and vesting of undertakings, payment of amounts by the Central Government, a claims process managed by the Commissioner of Payments, and penalties for non-compliance.
