act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL SECURITY GUARD ACT, 1986

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Any part of India as well as outside India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed force of the Union for combating terrorist activities with a view to protecting States against internal disturbances and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes and regulates the National Security Guard, an armed force of the Union. Its primary purpose is to combat terrorist activities and protect States from internal disturbances.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

chapter_titles: CONSTITUTION OF THE SECURITY GUARD AND CONDITIONS OR SERVCE OF THE MEMBERS OF THE SECURITY GUARD
EXECUTION OF SENTENCES, PARDONS, REMISSIONS, ETC.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'active duty', 'civil offence', 'terrorist', and various ranks.

key_sections.title: Persons subject to this Act.
key_sections.description: Specifies the categories of persons appointed in the Security Guard who are subject to the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Security Guard.
key_sections.description: Establishes the National Security Guard as an armed force of the Union for combating terrorist activities.

key_sections.title: Control, direction, etc.
key_sections.description: Vests general superintendence, direction, and control of the Security Guard in the Central Government and command in the Director-General.

key_sections.title: Restrictions respecting right to form associations, freedom of speech, etc.
key_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on members of the Security Guard regarding forming associations, communicating with the press, and participating in political activities.

key_sections.title: Offences in relation to the terrorists and other persons in arms against the Union and punishable with death.
key_sections.description: Defines severe offences related to terrorist activities and actions against the Union, punishable by death.

key_sections.title: Civil offences.
key_sections.description: States that persons subject to the Act committing civil offences in or beyond India are deemed guilty under this Act and triable by a Security Guard Court.

key_sections.title: Civil offences not triable by a Security Guard Court.
key_sections.description: Specifies certain civil offences (murder, culpable homicide, rape) against non-subjects of the Act that are generally not triable by a Security Guard Court, with exceptions.

key_sections.title: Punishments awardable by Security Guard Courts.
key_sections.description: Lists the scale of punishments that can be inflicted by Security Guard Courts, including death, imprisonment, and dismissal.

key_sections.title: Kinds of Security Guard Courts.
key_sections.description: Identifies the three types of Security Guard Courts: General, Petty, and Summary.

key_sections.title: Choice between Criminal Court and Security Guard Court.
key_sections.description: Grants discretion to specified officers to decide whether an offence should be tried by a Criminal Court or a Security Guard Court.

key_sections.title: General rule as to evidence.
key_sections.description: States that the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, applies to proceedings before a Security Guard Court, subject to this Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Remedy against order, finding or sentence of Security Guard Court.
key_sections.description: Provides a mechanism for aggrieved persons to petition against orders, findings, or sentences of Security Guard Courts.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: General superintendence, direction, and control of Security Guard; dismiss or remove persons; sanction for associations/speech; order detention of lunatic accused; confirm findings/sentences of General Security Guard Courts; mitigate, remit, commute sentences; annul proceedings; pardon and remission; suspend sentences; make rules; confer powers/duties on members.

Director-General: Command and supervision of Security Guard; dismiss, remove, reduce non-officers; revise decisions on complaints; convene General Security Guard Courts; discretion for choice of court; annul proceedings; pardon and remission; suspend sentences.

Additional Director-General, Inspector-General, Deputy Inspector-General, Group Commander, Squadron Commander, Team Commander: Various powers related to dismissal, removal, reduction; minor punishments; convening courts; discretion for choice of court; confirming sentences; pardon and remission.
Security Guard Courts: Try offences and award punishments.
Commander: Duty regarding detention; give information of desertion; hold Summary Security Guard Court; award minor punishments.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines a wide range of offences in Chapter III, including those related to terrorist activities, mutiny, desertion, disobedience, assault, property offences, false accusations, and civil offences. Chapter IV outlines the punishments, which can be awarded by Security Guard Courts or other officers. Punishments include death, imprisonment (life or lesser term), dismissal from service, reduction in rank, forfeiture of seniority or service, severe reprimand, and deductions from pay and allowances. Minor punishments can also be awarded by Commanders.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government has the power to appoint the Director-General, Additional Directors-General, Inspectors-General, Deputy Inspectors-General, Group Commanders, and other officers of the Security Guard, as well as Judge Attorney-General and related positions.

applies_to: Officers and Assistant Commander appointed in the Security Guard
Rangers and combatised tradesmen appointed in the Security Guard
exemptions: A person subject to this Act who commits an offence of murder or of culpable homicide not amounting to murder against, or of rape in relation to, a person not subject to this Act shall not be deemed to be guilty of an offence under this Act and shall not be tried by a Security Guard Court, unless he commits any of the said offences, while on active duty; or at any place outside India.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the constitution of the National Security Guard, defining offences and prescribing punishments. Enforcement is carried out by Security Guard Courts, with provisions for arrest, detention, and trial procedures. Civil authorities also assist in apprehension and execution of sentences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Security Guard Courts (General, Petty, Summary) and Criminal Courts (for civil offences, with jurisdiction determined by specified officers).

act_identification.act_title: THE DOCK WORKERS (SAFETY, HEALTH AND WELFARE) ACT, 1986
act_identification.act_short_title: The Dock Workers (Safety, Health and Welfare) Act, 1986

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the safety, health and welfare of dock workers and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to ensure the safety, health, and welfare of dock workers. It also covers related matters concerning their working conditions and environment, including provisions for inspection, penalties, and rule-making.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, its commencement date, and non-application to ships of war.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'dock work', and 'dock worker'.

key_sections.title: Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to appoint a Chief Inspector of Dock Safety and other Inspectors, who are deemed public servants.

key_sections.title: Powers of Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Outlines the powers of Inspectors, including entry, examination, requiring documents, taking evidence, and inquiring into accidents.

key_sections.title: Powers of Inspectors where employment of dock workers are dangerous.
key_sections.description: Allows Inspectors to prohibit dock work in dangerous places until safety measures are taken.

key_sections.title: Advisory Committee.
key_sections.description: Enables the appropriate Government to constitute an Advisory Committee to advise on matters arising from the Act's administration.

key_sections.title: Obligations of dock workers.
key_sections.description: Defines the duties of dock workers regarding safety appliances and actions, and prescribes penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for various offences, including obstructing Inspectors, contravening regulations leading to accidents, and general contraventions.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Specifies the courts competent to try offences under the Act and sets limitations for prosecution.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the appropriate Government the power to make rules for the administration of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the appropriate Government the power to make regulations for the safety, health, and welfare of dock workers, detailing specific areas of regulation.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Act 9 of 1948.
key_sections.description: Amends specific clauses of the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948.

key_sections.title: Repeal.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Indian Dock Labourers Act, 1934.

key_sections.title: Savings.
key_sections.description: Provides for the continuation of existing regulations and schemes made under repealed or amended Acts until altered or repealed under this Act.

powers_conferred: Appropriate Government to appoint Chief Inspector and Inspectors (Section 3)
Appropriate Government to direct inquiry into accidents or diseases (Section 10)
Appropriate Government to exempt certain ports, premises, or ships from provisions (Section 12)
Appropriate Government to make rules (Section 20)
Appropriate Government to make regulations for safety, health and welfare of dock workers (Section 21)
Inspectors to enter, examine, require documents, take evidence, inquire into accidents, issue show cause notices, and prosecute (Section 4)
Inspectors to prohibit dangerous dock work (Section 5)
Chief Inspector to modify or cancel Inspector's order (Section 5)
Chief Inspector or specified authority to hear appeals against Inspector's orders (Section 8)
Courts to make orders requiring measures for remedying offences (Section 16)
Metropolitan magistrate or magistrate of the first class to pass sentence of fine exceeding five thousand rupees (Section 18)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Dock workers contravening obligations under Section 11 are punishable with imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to one hundred rupees, or both. Obstructing an Inspector, removing safety items, or failing to restore them is punishable with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both. Contravention of regulations resulting in fatal accidents carries imprisonment up to six months and a fine not less than two thousand rupees (up to five thousand), or both. Contravention resulting in incapacitating accidents carries imprisonment up to six months and a fine not less than five hundred rupees (up to five thousand), or both. Dock workers contravening duties under regulations are punishable with imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to two hundred rupees, or both. Subsequent convictions for the same offence within two years incur double the imprisonment. General contravention of the Act, where no other penalty is provided, is punishable with a fine up to five hundred rupees. Breach of regulations can be punishable with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both, with a further fine for continuing breaches.

repealed_acts: Indian Dock Labourers Act, 1934
related_acts: Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948 (9 of 1948)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Appropriate Government

applies_to: whole of India
dock workers
exemptions: any ship of war of any nationality
any port or place, dock, wharf, quay or similar premises (by appropriate Government)
any specified ship or class of ships (by appropriate Government)
special_provisions: Regulations may make special provision to meet the special requirement of any particular port or ports.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced by Inspectors who have powers to enter, examine, inquire, and prohibit dangerous work. Penalties are prescribed for contraventions, and courts can issue orders for compliance. The appropriate Government also has powers to make rules and regulations for implementation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Metropolitan magistrate or a magistrate of the first class

act_identification.act_title: THE DELHI APARTMENT OWNERSHIP ACT, 1986

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of the Union territory of Delhi

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the ownership of an individual apartment in a multi-storeyed building and of an undivided interest in the common areas and facilities appurtenant to such apartment and to make such apartment and interest heritable and transferable and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS with a view to securing that the ownership and control of the material resources of the community are so distributed as to sub-serve the common good, it is expedient to provide for the ownership of an individual apartment in a multi-storeyed building and of an undivided interest in the common areas and facilities appurtenant to such apartment, and to make such apartment and interest heritable and transferable and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto;
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the ownership of individual apartments in multi-storeyed buildings in Delhi, along with an undivided interest in common areas and facilities. It aims to make such apartments and interests heritable and transferable, ensuring proper distribution and control of material resources for the common good.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II OWNERSHIP, HERITABILITY AND TRASFERABILITY OF APARTMENTS
CHAPTER III DEED OF APARTMENT AND ITS REGISTRATION
CHAPTER IV ASSOCIATION OF APARTMENT OWNERS AND BYE-LAWS FOR THE REGULATION OF THE AFFAIRS OF SUCH ASSOCIATION
CHAPTER V COMMON PROFITS, COMMON EXPENSES AND OTHER MATTERS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application to the Union territory of Delhi, and commencement date to be appointed by the Administrator.

key_sections.title: Application.
key_sections.description: Defines the applicability of the Act to apartments in multi-storeyed buildings constructed for residential or commercial purposes, including provisions for buildings with two or three apartments.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'apartment', 'apartment owner', 'common areas and facilities', and 'Association of Apartment Owners'.

key_sections.title: Ownership of apartments.
key_sections.description: Establishes the exclusive ownership and possession rights of apartment owners, including their undivided interest in common areas and facilities, and prohibits partition of common areas.

key_sections.title: Apartment to be heritable and transferable.
key_sections.description: Declares apartments, along with their undivided interest in common areas, as heritable and transferable immovable property, subject to specific conditions for group housing cooperative societies.

key_sections.title: Right of re-entry.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for lessees to grant sub-leases, inspect for breaches of terms, impose composition fees, and exercise the right of re-entry in case of default, with provisions for appeal to the District Court.

key_sections.title: Benamidar of the apartment to be deemed to be the real owner.
key_sections.description: States that the acquirer of an apartment is deemed the real owner, even if consideration was paid by another person, overriding provisions of the Transfer of Property Act and Indian Trusts Act.

key_sections.title: Contents of Deed of Apartment.
key_sections.description: Mandates promoters to execute a Deed of Apartment containing specific particulars like land description, floor plans, apartment details, common areas, and value, within prescribed timelines.

key_sections.title: Registration of Deed of Apartment.
key_sections.description: Makes the Deed of Apartment and its endorsements compulsorily registrable documents under the Registration Act, 1908, and requires maintenance of a special register.

key_sections.title: Association of Apartment Owners and bye-laws relating thereto.
key_sections.description: Establishes the requirement for an Association of Apartment Owners for administration and management, and provides for the framing of model bye-laws by the Administrator.

key_sections.title: Common expenses to be a charge on the apartment.
key_sections.description: Declares unpaid common expenses assessed by the Association as a charge on the apartment, prior to all other charges except government/municipal taxes and first mortgages.

key_sections.title: Act to be binding on apartment owners, tenants, etc.
key_sections.description: States that the Act's provisions override inconsistent laws or contracts and are binding on all apartment owners, tenants, and other users of the property.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the Act's provisions, including specific matters like prescribed purposes, composition fees, and compensation scales.

powers_conferred: Administrator: To appoint commencement date (S.1(3)), frame model bye-laws (S.15(2)), approve departures from model bye-laws (S.15(2)).
Competent Authority: To permit extension for executing Deed of Apartment (S.13(1) Proviso), decide succession disputes (S.13(4)), record succession (S.13(5)).
Board or Manager (of Association): To have access to apartments for maintenance/repairs (S.4(8)), bring action on behalf of apartment owners (S.18(1)), obtain insurance (S.16(1)).
Central Government: To exempt stamp duty, registration fee, court fees, and refund amounts (S.25), make rules (S.27).

Lessee: To grant sub-leases (S.8(1)), inspect for breaches (S.8(2)), require defaulting owner to refrain or pay composition fees (S.8(3)), exercise right of re-entry (S.8(7)), make fresh allotment (S.8(10)).
Local Authority: To make suitable regulations for separate assessment of tax (S.22(1)).

related_acts: State Bank of India Act, 1955 (23 of 1955)
State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959 (38 of 1959)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 (5 of 1970)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980 (40 of 1980)

authorities_established: Board of Management of an Association of Apartment Owners
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Administrator: Appoints "competent authority" (S.3(m)). Members of Association of Apartment Owners: Elect "Board of Management" (S.15(3)(b)), "President" (S.15(3)(j)), "Secretary" (S.15(3)(k)), "Treasurer" (S.15(3)(l)). Board: Engages "Manager" (S.15(3)(g)).

applies_to: every apartment in a multi-storeyed building which was constructed mainly for residential or commercial or such other purposes as may be prescribed
Buildings constructed by "any group housing co-operative society" or "any other person or authority"
Buildings on "free hold land, or a lease hold land, if the lease for such land is for a period of thirty years or more"
Buildings with two or three apartments if the owner makes a declaration
all apartment owners, tenants of owners, employees of owners and tenants, or any other person who may, in any manner, use the property or any part thereof
exemptions: nothing contained in this sub-section shall affect the right, title or interest acquired by any allottee or other person in common areas and facilities from any promoter on or before the 28th day of February, 1986.
special_provisions: Union territory of Delhi

where the allotment, sale or other transfer of any apartment has been made by any group housing co-operative society in favour of any member thereof, the transferability of such apartment and all other matters shall be regulated by the law applicable to such group housing co-operative society.

where a building constructed, whether before or after the commencement of this Act, on any land contains only two or three apartments, the owner of such building may, by a declaration duly executed and registered... indicate his intention to make the provisions of this Act applicable to such building

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Compliance with bye-laws and Deed of Apartment covenants enforced by Manager or Board, or aggrieved apartment owner (S.7). Lessees can inspect for breaches, impose composition fees, and exercise re-entry rights (S.8). Lessor can take action if lessee fails (S.8(11)). Association of Apartment Owners manages common areas and facilities (S.15). Unpaid common expenses are a charge on the apartment (S.21). Competent authority decides succession disputes (S.13(4)).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Court of the District Judge having jurisdiction (hereinafter referred to as the District Court) for appeals against lessee's notice (S.8(4)) and compensation determination (S.8(9)). "higher court" for further appeals (S.8(7), S.8(8)). Competent authority has powers of a civil court for succession disputes (S.13(4)).

act_identification.act_title: THE CHILD AND ADOLESCENT LABOUR (PROHIBITION AND REGULATION) ACT, 1986
act_identification.act_short_title: the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986
act_identification.date_of_commencement: at once for most provisions; 26/05/1993 for Part III

act_overview.preamble: An Act to prohibit the engagement of children in all occupations and to prohibit the engagement of adolescents in hazardous occupations and processes and the matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act prohibits the employment of children in all occupations and processes. It also prohibits the engagement of adolescents in hazardous occupations and processes, while regulating their conditions of work in non-hazardous settings.

chapter_titles: PART II - PROHIBITION OF EMPLOYMENT OF CHILDREN IN CERTAIN OCCUPATIONS AND PROCESSES
PART III - REGULATION OF CONDITIONS OF WORK OF ADOLESCENTS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, and the dates of its commencement for different parts.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'adolescent', 'child', 'establishment', and 'appropriate Government'.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of employment of children in any occupation and process.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the employment of children in any occupation or process, with specific exceptions for family enterprises and entertainment industry under certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of employment of adolescents in certain hazardous occupations and processes.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the employment of adolescents in hazardous occupations or processes listed in the Schedule.

key_sections.title: Technical Advisory Committee.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to constitute a Technical Advisory Committee to advise on adding occupations and processes to the Schedule.

key_sections.title: Hours and period of work.
key_sections.description: Regulates the working hours, rest intervals, and spread-over for adolescents in establishments.

key_sections.title: Health and safety.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the appropriate Government to make rules for the health and safety of adolescents employed in establishments.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contraventions of the Act, including imprisonment and fines for employers, and fines for parents/guardians in certain cases.

key_sections.title: Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund.
key_sections.description: Mandates the appropriate Government to constitute a fund in every district for the rehabilitation of rescued children and adolescents, credited with fines and government contributions.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of Inspectors by the appropriate Government to ensure compliance with the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: District Magistrate to implement the provisions.
key_sections.description: Allows the appropriate Government to confer powers and duties on District Magistrates for the proper implementation of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the appropriate Government the power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Employment of Children Act, 1938, and includes savings provisions for actions taken under the repealed Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to amend the Schedule (Section 4)
Central Government: Power to constitute Technical Advisory Committee (Section 5)
Central Government: Power to make rules (Section 18)
Central Government: Power to remove difficulties (Section 21)
Appropriate Government: Power to make rules for health and safety of adolescents (Section 13)
Appropriate Government: Power to constitute Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund (Section 14B)
Appropriate Government: Power to appoint Inspectors (Section 17)
Appropriate Government: Power to confer powers and duties on District Magistrate (Section 17A)
Appropriate Government: Power to make rules (Section 18)
District Magistrate: Power to compound offences (Section 14D)
District Magistrate: Power to implement provisions (Section 17A)
Inspector: Power to inspect establishments and refer age disputes (Section 10)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Employing any child in contravention of Section 3 or any adolescent in contravention of Section 3A is punishable with imprisonment for 6 months to 2 years, or a fine of Rs. 20,000 to Rs. 50,000, or both. Parents/guardians are not punished for a first offence, but may be fined up to Rs. 10,000 for subsequent offences. Subsequent offences by employers carry imprisonment from 1 to 3 years. Other contraventions of the Act or rules are punishable with simple imprisonment up to 1 month or a fine up to Rs. 10,000, or both.

repealed_acts: The Employment of Children Act, 1938 (26 of 1938)
related_acts: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 (35 of 2009)

authorities_established: Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints Chairman and members of the Technical Advisory Committee. Appropriate Government appoints Inspectors.

applies_to: Children (prohibition of employment)
Adolescents (prohibition in hazardous occupations, regulation in others)
Occupiers of establishments, workshops, railway administrations, port authorities
exemptions: Children helping their family or family enterprise (non-hazardous, after school hours or during vacations)
Children working as artists in audio-visual entertainment industry (except circus), subject to prescribed conditions and safety measures
Establishments where any process is carried on by the occupier with the aid of his family (for sections 7, 8, and 9)
Schools established by, or receiving assistance or recognition from, Government (for sections 7, 8, and 9)
Parents or guardians for the first offence under Section 3 or 3A
special_provisions: Gujarat State Amendment: Increased fines for contravention of Section 3 and 3A to one lakh rupees.

Gujarat State Amendment: Expanded the authorities for compounding offences and implementing provisions to include Municipal Commissioner, Director of Labour, or Regional Commissioner of Municipalities, in addition to District Magistrate.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through Inspectors appointed by the appropriate Government. District Magistrates are empowered to implement provisions and compound certain offences. The appropriate Government is responsible for periodic inspection and monitoring. Offences committed by employers under Section 3 or 3A are cognizable. Complaints can be filed by any person, police officer, or Inspector.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class.

schedules_summary.description: Lists hazardous occupations and processes where the employment of adolescents is prohibited, including Mines, Inflammable substances or explosives, and Hazardous processes (as defined in the Factories Act, 1948).

act_identification.act_title: THE INDECENT REPRESENTATION OF WOMEN (PROHIBITION) ACT, 1986
act_identification.act_short_title: The Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act, 1986

act_overview.preamble: An Act to prohibit indecent representation of women through advertisements or in publications, writings, paintings, figures or in any other manner and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to prevent the depiction of women in a manner that is indecent, derogatory, or denigrating, or likely to deprave public morality, through advertisements, publications, and other forms of representation. It establishes prohibitions, powers of search and seizure, and penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used within the Act, such as 'advertisement' and 'indecent representation of women'.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of advertisements containing indecent representation of women.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the publication or exhibition of any advertisement containing indecent representation of women.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of publication or sending by post of books, pamphlets, etc., containing indecent representation of women.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the production, sale, distribution, or sending by post of materials containing indecent representation of women, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Powers to enter and search.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to authorized Gazetted Officers to enter, search, and seize materials believed to contravene the Act, subject to rules and the Code of Criminal Procedure.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for contravention of sections 3 or 4, with enhanced penalties for subsequent convictions.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies
key_sections.description: Stipulates liability for offences committed by companies, extending to persons in charge and, in certain cases, directors, managers, or other officers.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable and bailable.
key_sections.description: Declares that offences under this Act are cognizable and bailable, notwithstanding provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Provides protection from legal proceedings for the Central or State Government or their officers for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, including procedures for seizure and other matters.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to appoint commencement date
Central Government: Power to make rules
State Government: Power to authorise Gazetted Officers for entry and search
Gazetted Officer: Powers to enter, search, and seize materials
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person contravening section 3 or section 4 is punishable on first conviction with imprisonment up to two years and a fine up to two thousand rupees. For a second or subsequent conviction, imprisonment is not less than six months but may extend to five years, and a fine not less than ten thousand rupees but may extend to one lakh rupees. Offences committed by companies also incur liability for those in charge and, in some cases, directors or officers.

act_identification.act_title: THE JUTE PACKAGING MATERIALS (COMPULSORY USE IN PACKING COMMODITIES) ACT, 1987
act_identification.act_short_title: The Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory Use in Packing Commodities) Act, 1987

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the compulsory use of jute packaging material in the supply and distribution of certain commodities in the interests of production of raw jute and jute packaging material, and of persons engaged in the production thereof, and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to ensure the mandatory use of jute packaging material for the supply and distribution of specific commodities. This measure is intended to safeguard the production of raw jute and jute packaging material, thereby protecting the livelihoods of individuals involved in their production.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its applicability to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'commodity', 'essential commodity', 'jute packaging material', 'scheduled industry', and 'Standing Advisory Committee'.

key_sections.title: Power to specify commodities which are required to be packed in jute packaging material.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to mandate, by order, the compulsory packing of specified commodities or percentages thereof in jute packaging material, based on recommendations from the Standing Advisory Committee.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Standing Advisory Committee.
key_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to constitute a Standing Advisory Committee with expertise to advise on which commodities should use jute packaging material, considering factors like jute availability and industry interests.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of packing in any material other than the jute packaging material.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the supply or distribution of commodities in materials other than jute packaging material, once an order under section 3 is in effect, with a temporary exemption for existing practices.

key_sections.title: Power to call for information and samples.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to require persons using jute packaging material to furnish information and samples for the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to enter and inspect.
key_sections.description: Authorizes officers to enter and inspect places or vehicles where commodities packed in jute packaging material are stored, and to request related information.

key_sections.title: Power to search and seize.
key_sections.description: Grants authorized officers the power to search and seize commodities packed in contravention of section 5, with provisions for applying the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of section 5.
key_sections.description: Prescribes a fine for packing commodities in materials other than jute packaging material, in contravention of section 5, up to double the cost of the required jute material.

key_sections.title: Penalty for false statement, etc.
key_sections.description: Imposes a fine of up to five thousand rupees for failing to furnish information or samples, or for providing false information, when required under section 6.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that when an offence is committed by a company, both the company and individuals in charge are liable, with provisions for proving lack of knowledge or due diligence, and for offences committed with consent or connivance of officers.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable.
key_sections.description: Declares that all offences punishable under this Act are cognizable, notwithstanding the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to exempt, in public interest, any person or class of persons from the operation of an order made under section 3.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, with a requirement for such rules to be laid before Parliament.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to specify commodities for compulsory jute packaging (Section 3)
Central Government: Power to constitute a Standing Advisory Committee (Section 4)
Central Government: Power to call for information and samples (Section 6)
Central Government: Power to delegate its powers (excluding making orders under Section 3 or 16, or rules under Section 17) to subordinate officers/authorities or State Governments (Section 13)
Central Government: Power to give directions to State Governments for carrying out the Act (Section 14)
Central Government: Power to exempt persons or classes of persons from compulsory jute packaging (Section 16)
Central Government: Power to make rules for the purposes of the Act (Section 17)
Authorised Officer: Power to enter and inspect places, premises, or vehicles (Section 7)
Authorised Officer: Power to search and seize commodities packed in contravention of Section 5 (Section 8)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of section 5 (packing in material other than jute packaging material) is punishable with a fine up to double the cost of the jute packaging material that should have been used. Failure to furnish information or samples, or furnishing false information under section 6, is punishable with a fine up to five thousand rupees. Offences by companies hold both the company and persons in charge liable, with provisions for directors, managers, or other officers if the offence is attributable to their consent, connivance, or neglect.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government constitutes the Standing Advisory Committee and authorizes officers for inspection, search, and seizure.

applies_to: Any person required to pack commodities for supply or distribution in jute packaging material as per orders under Section 3
Companies committing offences under the Act
exemptions: The Central Government may exempt any person or class of persons from the operation of an order under Section 3 in the public interest (Section 16).

A temporary exemption for a period of three months from the specified date applies if, immediately before that date, the commodity was being packed in material other than jute packaging material (Proviso to Section 5).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government issues orders specifying commodities for compulsory jute packaging. Authorized officers are empowered to call for information and samples, enter and inspect premises, and search and seize goods. Penalties are prescribed for contraventions. The Central Government can also give directions to State Governments for implementation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Offences under this Act are cognizable, implying jurisdiction of criminal courts. The provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, apply to searches and seizures.

act_identification.act_title: THE GOA, DAMAN AND DIU MINING CONCESSIONS (ABOLITION AND DECLARATION AS MINING LEASES) ACT, 1987
act_identification.act_short_title: the Goa, Daman and Diu Mining Concessions (Abolition and Declaration as Mining Leases) Act, 1987

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the abolition of the mining concessions in operation in the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu and specified in the First and the Second Schedules, and for the declaration of such mining concessions as mining leases under the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957 with a view to the regulation of the mines to which such concessions relate and for the development of minerals under the control of the Union and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS certain mining concessions have been granted in perpetuity under the former Portuguese Mining Laws (Decree of 20th day of September, 1906) in the territories now included in the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu by the former Portuguese Government and by the Government of Goa, Daman and Diu: AND WHEREAS the aforesaid mining laws have ceased to be in force and doubts have been expressed as to whether such mining concessions are mining leases within the meaning of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act 1957 (67 of 1957): AND WHEREAS it is expedient in the public interest to abolish such mining concessions and declare them as mining leases under the aforesaid Act for the purpose of making the provisions of that Act applicable to the mines to which such concessions relate with a view to the regulation of such mines and for the development of minerals under the control of the Union so as to subserve the common good:
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to abolish existing mining concessions in Goa, Daman and Diu, granted under former Portuguese laws, and declare them as mining leases under the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957. The objective is to regulate these mines and develop minerals under Union control for the common good.

key_sections.title: Interest on delayed payment of expenditure-tax.
key_sections.description: Prescribes interest for delayed payment of expenditure-tax to the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Penalty for failure to collect or pay expenditure-tax.
key_sections.description: Specifies penalties for failure to collect expenditure-tax or failure to pay collected tax to the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Application of provisions of Income-tax Act.
key_sections.description: States that certain provisions and schedules of the Income-tax Act, 1961, and Income-tax (Certificate Proceedings) Rules, 1962, apply to this Act with necessary modifications.

key_sections.title: Wilful attempt to evade tax, etc.
key_sections.description: Defines the offence of wilful attempt to evade tax, penalty, or interest and prescribes punishment.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Board of Direct Taxes the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: appoint commencement date, remove difficulties by order.
Board (Central Board of Direct Taxes): make rules, issue orders, instructions, and directions.
Tax authorities (Director General of Income-tax, Chief Commissioner of Income-tax, etc.): exercise powers and perform functions similar to those under the Income-tax Act.
Assessing Officer: require production of accounts/documents, assess chargeable expenditure, make best judgment assessments, reassess escaped expenditure, serve notice of demand, direct penalties.
Commissioner: revise orders, direct Assessing Officer to appeal, sanction prosecution, compound offences.
Commissioner (Appeals): hear and determine appeals.
Appellate Tribunal: hear appeals.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes interest at 1% per month for delayed payment of expenditure-tax (Section 14). Penalties include a sum equal to the uncollected tax or Rs. 100-200 per day (up to the unpaid tax amount) for failure to collect or pay tax (Section 15), Rs. 100-200 per day for failure to furnish returns (Section 16), and 1 to 2 times the tax sought to be evaded for concealment of chargeable expenditure (Section 17). Failure to comply with a notice can result in a penalty of 10% to 50% of the tax avoided (Section 18). Wilful attempts to evade tax, failure to furnish returns, making false statements, and abetment of false returns are punishable with rigorous imprisonment for 3 months to 7 years and a fine (Sections 25-28).

related_acts: Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963 (54 of 1963)

applies_to: Expenditure incurred in hotels where room charges are three thousand rupees or more per day (before 1st June, 2003).
Expenditure incurred in restaurants (before 1st June, 1992).
Persons responsible for collecting expenditure-tax.
exemptions: Expenditure incurred in foreign exchange (before 1st October, 1992).
Expenditure incurred by persons within the purview of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961 or the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations, 1963.
Expenditure incurred in any shop or office not owned or managed by the hotel.
Expenditure by way of any tax, including tax under this Act.
Hotels referred to in clause (a) of sub-section (7) of section 80-IB of the Income-tax Act during specific periods (1st April, 1991 to 31st March, 2001 and 1st April, 1998 to 31st March, 2008).
special_provisions: Initially extended to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir, but later made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Board (Central Board of Direct Taxes), subject to the control of the Central Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through collection of tax by responsible persons, assessment by Assessing Officers, provisions for interest and penalties, and a system of appeals to the Commissioner (Appeals) and the Appellate Tribunal. Criminal proceedings can be instituted for wilful evasion and other offences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Appellate Tribunal, High Court, Supreme Court, National Tax Tribunal.

schedules_summary.description: The Act applies the provisions of the Second Schedule of the Income-tax Act, 1961, with necessary modifications, relating to procedure for recovery of tax.
The Act applies the provisions of the Third Schedule of the Income-tax Act, 1961, with necessary modifications, relating to procedure for recovery of tax.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL DAIRY DEVELOPMENT BOARD ACT, 1987
act_identification.act_short_title: The National Dairy Development Board Act, 1987

legislative_details.geographical_extent: throughout the country; in or outside India

act_overview.purpose: The Act declares the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) as an institution of national importance, incorporates it as a body corporate, and vests in it the undertakings of the Indian Dairy Corporation. Its purpose is to enable the NDDB to administer and carry out its functions more effectively across the country, promoting dairy development and related industries through a co-operative strategy for rural economic development.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II THE NATIONAL DAIRY DEVELOPMENT BOARD
CHAPTER III MANAGEMENT OF THE NATIONAL DAIRY DEVELOPMENT BOARD
CHAPTER IV POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE NATIONAL DAIRY DEVELOPMENT BOARD
CHAPTER V PROVISIONS RELATING TO DIRECTORS AND EMPLOYEES OF THE NATIONAL DAIRY DEVELOPMENT BOARD
CHAPTER VI FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Declaration of National Dairy Development Board as an institution of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the National Dairy Development Board at Anand, Gujarat, as an institution of national importance.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'Board', 'Chairman', 'Indian Dairy Corporation', and 'milk product'.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of National Dairy Development Board.
key_sections.description: Constitutes the National Dairy Development Board as a body corporate with perpetual succession, common seal, and powers to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.

key_sections.title: Vesting of undertakings of Indian Dairy Corporation in National Dairy Development Board and dissolution of Indian Dairy Corporation.
key_sections.description: Mandates the transfer of all undertakings of the Indian Dairy Corporation to the NDDB and the dissolution of the Indian Dairy Corporation from the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Management of National Dairy Development Board and composition of its Board of Directors.
key_sections.description: Vests the general superintendence, direction, control, and management of NDDB in a Board of Directors and specifies its composition.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of National Dairy Development Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the duties, functions, and responsibilities of the NDDB, including promoting dairy development, adopting co-operative strategies, and providing assistance to related industries.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to officers and other employees of society and of dissolved company.
key_sections.description: States that employees of the erstwhile society and dissolved company become employees of NDDB on the same terms and conditions, subject to alteration by the Board.

key_sections.title: Power of Board to restructure and streamline organisational and functional set-up of National Dairy Development Board to secure utmost efficiency in functioning.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board power to restructure and streamline its organizational and functional set-up, including declaring employees redundant, to ensure efficiency.

key_sections.title: National Dairy Development Board Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the National Dairy Development Board Fund, detailing what sums of money are to be credited to it and how it shall be applied.

key_sections.title: Special provisions for enforcement of claims by National Dairy Development Board.
key_sections.description: Provides special provisions for the NDDB to enforce claims against defaulters of loans or advances, including applying to court for sale of property or transfer of management.

key_sections.title: Mother Dairy to be a subsidiary unit of National Dairy Development Board.
key_sections.description: Declares Mother Dairy, Delhi, as a subsidiary unit of the National Dairy Development Board from the appointed day, while retaining its separate character.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over anything inconsistent in the Companies Act, Industrial Disputes Act, or any other law.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Board to make regulations for giving effect to the provisions of the Act, covering various procedural and administrative matters.

powers_conferred: Power to acquire, hold and dispose of property and to contract (Section 4)
Power to establish units, offices, branches or agencies (Section 4)
Power to promote, plan and organise programmes for dairy and agriculture-based industries (Section 16)
Power to facilitate research and promotional activities (Section 16)
Power to impart technological know-how (Section 16)
Power to design, plan, promote, develop, construct, sponsor and set up dairy industries (Section 16)
Power to provide consultancy and managerial services (Section 16)
Power to recommend maximum and minimum prices for milk (Section 16)
Power to function as a channelising agency for import/export of milk products and animals (Section 16)
Power to provide financial, technical, administrative, managerial assistance (Section 16)
Power to regulate dairy and allied industries (Section 16)
Power to collect and compile relevant data and statistics (Section 16)
Power to borrow money (Section 23)
Power to receive gifts, grants, donations (Section 25)
Power to make schemes and regulations regarding service matters retrospectively (Section 46)
Power to make regulations (Section 48)

related_acts: Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 (5 of 1970)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980 (44 of 1980)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government nominates Chairman and directors (Section 8). Board may appoint additional officers and employees (Section 36).
regulatory_bodies: National Dairy Development Board (as regulatory authority for dairy and allied industries)

applies_to: National Dairy Development Board
Indian Dairy Corporation
Society (National Dairy Development Board formed under Societies Registration Act, 1860)
Officers and other employees of the society and dissolved company
Organisations receiving assistance from NDDB
Mother Dairy, Delhi
special_provisions: Mother Dairy, Delhi, to be a subsidiary unit of National Dairy Development Board (Section 42)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Board (for regulations), Central Government (for schemes and approval of schemes)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Board exercises powers and functions, manages finances, and can enforce claims through courts. Central Government provides grants and loans and lays reports before Parliament.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Court (for enforcement of claims under Section 31)

schedules_summary.description: Contains the form for the 'Declaration of fidelity and secrecy' to be made by the Chairman, director, member of committee, auditor, officer or other employee of the National Dairy Development Board.

act_identification.act_title: THE LEGAL SERVICES AUTHORITIES ACT, 1987

act_overview.preamble: An Act to constitute legal services authorities to provide free and competent legal services to the weaker sections of the society to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities, and to organize Lok Adalats to secure that the operation of the legal system promotes justice on a basis of equal opportunity.
act_overview.purpose: To establish legal services authorities at national, state, district, and taluk levels to provide free and competent legal services to the weaker sections of society. The Act also aims to organize Lok Adalats and Permanent Lok Adalats for amicable settlement of disputes and to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied due to economic or other disabilities.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title, geographical extent, and commencement details of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'legal service', 'Lok Adalat', and various authorities.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the National Legal Services Authority.
key_sections.description: Establishes the National Legal Services Authority and outlines its composition and appointment process.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Central Authority.
key_sections.description: Details the responsibilities and functions of the National Legal Services Authority, including policy-making, scheme framing, and fund allocation.

key_sections.title: Constitution of State Legal Services Authority.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of State Legal Services Authorities and their composition.

key_sections.title: District Legal Services Authority.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of District Legal Services Authorities and specifies their structure.

key_sections.title: Criteria for giving legal services.
key_sections.description: Lays down the eligibility criteria for individuals to receive legal services under the Act, focusing on vulnerable groups and income levels.

key_sections.title: Organisation of Lok Adalats.
key_sections.description: Empowers various legal services authorities to organize Lok Adalats and defines their jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Cognizance of cases by Lok Adalats.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for Lok Adalats to take up cases, either by reference from courts or application from parties, for settlement.

key_sections.title: Award of Lok Adalat.
key_sections.description: States that awards made by Lok Adalats are deemed decrees of civil courts, are final and binding, and provides for refund of court fees.

key_sections.title: Powers of Lok Adalat or Permanent Lok Adalat.
key_sections.description: Confers powers on Lok Adalats and Permanent Lok Adalats similar to a Civil Court for conducting determinations.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Permanent Lok Adalats.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of Permanent Lok Adalats for public utility services and specifies their composition.

key_sections.title: Cognizance of cases by Permanent Lok Adalat.
key_sections.description: Details the process for Permanent Lok Adalats to take cognizance of pre-litigation disputes, including limitations on jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Award of Permanent Lok Adalat to be final.
key_sections.description: Declares that awards of Permanent Lok Adalats are final, binding, deemed civil court decrees, and not subject to challenge.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in other laws.

powers_conferred: Central Government to constitute National Legal Services Authority and make rules

Central Authority to lay down policies, frame schemes, allocate funds, undertake social justice litigation, organize legal aid camps, encourage settlement, promote research, monitor programs, provide grants-in-aid, develop clinical legal education, spread legal literacy, coordinate and monitor, and make regulations
State Government to constitute State Legal Services Authority and make rules
State Authority to give effect to Central Authority's policy, give legal service, conduct Lok Adalats, undertake preventive programs, and make regulations
District Authority to perform delegated functions of State Authority, coordinate activities, and organize Lok Adalats
Lok Adalat/Permanent Lok Adalat to determine and arrive at compromise/settlement, exercise powers of a Civil Court, and issue final and binding awards

related_acts: Persons With Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 (1 of 1996)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: President (for Supreme Court Judge as Executive Chairman of Central Authority, in consultation with CJI); Central Government (for other members of Central Authority, Member-Secretary, officers/employees of Central Authority and Supreme Court Legal Services Committee, in consultation with CJI); Chief Justice of India (for members of Supreme Court Legal Services Committee); Governor (for High Court Judge as Executive Chairman of State Authority, in consultation with CJ of HC); State Government (for other members of State Authority, Member-Secretary, officers/employees of State Authority, High Court Legal Services Committee, District Authority, Taluk Legal Services Committee, in consultation with CJ of HC); State Authority (for Secretary of District Authority, in consultation with Chairman of District Authority); Central Authority/State Authority (for Chairman and other persons of Permanent Lok Adalats)

applies_to: Weaker sections of the society
Members of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe
Victims of trafficking in human beings or begar
Women or children
Persons with disability as defined in clause (i) of section 2 of the Persons With Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995
Persons under circumstances of underserved want such as being a victim of a mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster
Industrial workmen
Persons in custody, including custody in a protective home, juvenile home, psychiatric hospital or psychiatric nursing home
Persons in receipt of annual income less than rupees nine thousand (or higher prescribed by State Government) if case is before a court other than Supreme Court
Persons in receipt of annual income less than rupees twelve thousand (or higher prescribed by Central Government) if case is before the Supreme Court
exemptions: Lok Adalats have no jurisdiction in respect of any case or matter relating to an offence not compoundable under any law
Permanent Lok Adalats have no jurisdiction in respect of any matter relating to an offence not compoundable under any law
Permanent Lok Adalats have no jurisdiction in the matter where the value of the property in dispute exceeds ten lakh rupees (subject to increase by Central Government notification)
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act and for different States for commencement.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government, State Government, Central Authority (for regulations), State Authority (for regulations)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Legal services are provided by various authorities and committees established under the Act. Disputes are resolved through Lok Adalats and Permanent Lok Adalats, whose awards are deemed decrees of civil courts, are final and binding, and can be executed by civil courts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil courts, Supreme Court, High Courts, District Courts, and other tribunals or authorities exercising judicial or quasi-judicial functions.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL HOUSING BANK ACT, 1987
act_identification.date_of_commencement: By notification of Central Government (different dates for different provisions, e.g., 09/07/1988 for most provisions and 01/06/1989 for Chapter V and Section 49(3))

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish a bank to be known as the National Housing Bank to operate as a principal agency to promote housing finance institutions both at local and regional levels and to provide financial and other support to such institutions and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: To establish the National Housing Bank as a principal agency to promote housing finance institutions at local and regional levels. Its purpose is to provide financial and other support to such institutions and address related matters.

chapter_titles: ESTABLISHMENT OF THE NATIONAL HOUSING BANK AND CAPITAL THEREOF
MANAGEMENT OF THE NATIONAL HOUSING BANK
BUSINESS OF THE NATIONAL HOUSING BANK
PROVISIONS RELATING TO HOUSING FINANCE INSTITUTIONS
OTHER PROVISIONS RELATING TO HOUSING FINANCE INSTITUTIONS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of National Housing Bank.
key_sections.description: Details the establishment, incorporation, and corporate structure of the National Housing Bank.

key_sections.title: Capital.
key_sections.description: Outlines the authorised and paid-up capital of the National Housing Bank and provisions for its increase.

key_sections.title: Board of Directors.
key_sections.description: Defines the composition and appointment process for the Board of Directors of the National Housing Bank.

key_sections.title: Business of the National Housing Bank.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various types of business activities the National Housing Bank is authorised to undertake.

key_sections.title: Borrowings and acceptance of deposits by National Housing Bank.
key_sections.description: Specifies the National Housing Bank's powers to borrow money and accept deposits for its operations.

key_sections.title: Requirement of registration and net owned fund.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration and a minimum net owned fund for housing finance institutions to operate as principal business.

key_sections.title: Power of Reserve Bank to determine policy and issue directions.
key_sections.description: Grants the Reserve Bank the authority to determine policy and issue directions to housing finance institutions in public interest.

key_sections.title: Power of Reserve Bank to prohibit acceptance of deposit and alienation of assets.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Reserve Bank to prohibit housing finance institutions from accepting deposits or alienating assets under certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of Housing Finance Institutions Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunals.

key_sections.title: Audit.
key_sections.description: Details the audit requirements and procedures for the accounts of the National Housing Bank.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for various offences and contraventions of the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power on the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of the Board to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board of the National Housing Bank the power to make regulations consistent with the Act.

powers_conferred: National Housing Bank: promoting, establishing, supporting housing finance institutions; making loans and advances; subscribing to securities; guaranteeing financial obligations; dealing in financial instruments; buying, selling or dealing in loans/advances; creating trusts; issuing and selling securities based on loans; setting up mutual funds; undertaking housing mortgage insurance; promoting companies/subsidiaries; undertaking research and surveys; formulating schemes; organising training programmes; providing guidelines and technical/administrative assistance; co-ordinating with other financial institutions; acting as agent of Central Government, State Government or Reserve Bank; borrowing money; accepting deposits; borrowing in foreign currency; transferring and acquiring rights; imposing conditions for accommodation; calling for repayment before agreed period; accessing records; inspecting institutions; collecting and publishing credit information; providing advisory services; appointing officers and employees; delegating powers; making regulations.

Central Government: appointing Chairman, Managing Director, and other directors of NHB; removing Chairman, Managing Director, or directors; terminating term of office of Chairman/Managing Director; giving directions to NHB in matters of policy involving public interest; guaranteeing bonds and debentures issued by NHB; guaranteeing foreign currency loans taken by NHB; establishing Appellate Tribunals; appointing Presiding Officer of Appellate Tribunal; appointing Recovery Officers; making rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

Reserve Bank: regulating or prohibiting issue of prospectus or advertisement soliciting deposits; determining policy and issuing directions to housing finance institutions; prohibiting acceptance of deposit and alienation of assets by housing finance institutions; inspecting housing finance institutions; appointing auditors for the National Housing Bank.

Recovery Officer: taking possession of property pledged, mortgaged, hypothecated or assigned as security; requesting Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or District Magistrate to assist in taking charge of property.
Appellate Tribunal: exercising jurisdiction, powers and authority to entertain appeals against orders of recovery officer.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties are prescribed for various offences including wilfully making false statements or omitting material statements (imprisonment up to 3 years and fine), contravening registration and net owned fund requirements (imprisonment 1-5 years and fine 1-5 lakh rupees), failing to comply with NCLT orders (imprisonment up to 3 years and fine of 50 rupees/day), receiving deposits in contravention of directions (imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to twice the deposit amount), and issuing unauthorised prospectus/advertisements (imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to twice the called-for deposit amount). The National Housing Bank or Reserve Bank can also impose administrative penalties on housing finance institutions and individuals for various contraventions and defaults, ranging from 25,000 rupees to 10 lakh rupees (or twice the amount involved if quantifiable), with additional daily penalties for continuing defaults. Specific penalties are also prescribed for auditors failing to comply with directions and for failure to produce documents or furnish information.

related_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
Voluntary Deposits (Immunities and Exemptions) Act, 1991 (47 of 1991)
Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993 (51 of 1993)

authorities_established: Housing Finance Institutions Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunals
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairman, Managing Director, and other directors of the National Housing Bank (excluding the director nominated by the Reserve Bank), the Presiding Officer of the Appellate Tribunal, and Recovery Officers. The Reserve Bank nominates one director to the NHB Board and appoints auditors for the NHB. The Board of the National Housing Bank appoints its officers and other employees.

applies_to: Whole of India
National Housing Bank
Housing finance institutions (especially those which are companies)
Borrowers of approved institutions
exemptions: Chapter V provisions do not apply to deposits accepted by housing finance institutions which are firms or unincorporated associations of individuals.
The Reserve Bank may exempt a housing finance institution or a group of such institutions from all or any provisions of Chapter V.
special_provisions: The head office of the National Housing Bank shall be at New Delhi or at such other place as the Central Government may specify.
The National Housing Bank may establish offices, branches or agencies at any place in India, and with previous approval of the Central Government, at any place outside India.
The Central Government may, by notification, increase the authorised capital of the National Housing Bank up to two thousand crore rupees or such other amount as may be determined by it.

The Central Government may, on the recommendation of the Reserve Bank, declare that the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 29C (regarding reserve fund) shall not be applicable to a housing finance institution for a specified period.

Transitional provisions state that till the establishment of an Appellate Tribunal under this Act, the Appellate Tribunal established under the Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993, shall exercise the jurisdiction.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for rules) and the Board of the National Housing Bank (for regulations).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through inspections by the National Housing Bank and the Reserve Bank, collection of credit information, powers to prohibit acceptance of deposits and alienation of assets, winding up petitions by the National Housing Bank, recovery of dues by Recovery Officers, appeals to Appellate Tribunals, and the imposition of penalties and fines for contraventions.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Principal civil courts (for penal interest and enforcement of penalties), National Company Law Tribunal (for certain orders and winding up), Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class or a court superior thereto (for cognizance of offences), and the Supreme Court and High Courts (exercising jurisdiction under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution).

schedules_summary.description: Contains the form for the Declaration of Fidelity and Secrecy to be made by directors, members of committees, auditors, advisors, officers, or other employees of the National Housing Bank.
Contains the form for the Declaration referred to in Section 16A of the National Housing Bank Act, 1987, for creating a charge on immovable property offered as security for financial assistance.

act_identification.act_title: THE RAILWAY CLAIMS TRIBUNAL ACT, 1987

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Railway Claims Tribunal for inquiring into and determining claims against a railway administration for loss, destruction, damage, deterioration or non-delivery of animals or goods entrusted to it to be carried by railway or for the refund of fares or freight or for compensation for death or injury to passengers occurring as a result of railway accidents [1][or untoward incidents] and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Railway Claims Tribunal to adjudicate claims against railway administrations. It covers claims for loss, damage, or non-delivery of goods, refund of fares or freight, and compensation for death or injury to passengers due to railway accidents or untoward incidents.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II ESTABLISHMENT OF RAILWAY CLAIMS TRIBUNAL AND BENCHES THEREOF
CHAPTER III JURISDICTION, POWERS AND AUTHORITY OF CLAIMS TRIBUNAL

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical applicability, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Railway Claims Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Composition of Claims Tribunal and Benches thereof.

key_sections.title: Qualifications for appointment as Chairman, Vice-Chairman or other Member.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction, powers and authority of Claims Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Application to Claims Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Procedure and powers of Claims Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.

Claims Tribunal to exercise jurisdiction, powers and authority relating to claims against railway administrations

Claims Tribunal to execute its orders as a decree of civil court

claims for the refund of fares or freight
claims for compensation for death or injury to passengers occurring as a result of railway accidents or untoward incidents
