act_identification.act_title: THE ALL INDIA COUNCIL FOR TECHNICAL EDUCATION ACT, 1987
act_identification.act_short_title: The All India Council for Technical Education Act, 1987.

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Human Resource Development of the Central Government

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of an All India Council for Technical Education with a view to the proper planning and co-ordinated development of the technical education system throughout the country, the promotion of qualitative improvement of such education in relation to planned quantitative growth and the regulation and proper maintenance of norms and standards in the technical education system and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the All India Council for Technical Education to ensure proper planning and coordinated development of technical education across India. Its main objectives include promoting qualitative improvement, regulating norms and standards, and fostering planned quantitative growth in the technical education system.

chapter_titles: POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE COUNCIL

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Commission', 'Council', 'technical education', and 'technical institution'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of the Council.
key_sections.description: Establishes the All India Council for Technical Education as a body corporate, specifies its head office, and details its composition.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Council.
key_sections.description: Outlines the comprehensive duties and powers of the Council, including coordinating development, allocating grants, formulating schemes, laying down norms and standards, and granting approvals for technical institutions.

key_sections.title: Inspection.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Council to inspect technical institutions and Universities to ascertain financial needs and standards of teaching, examination, and research.

key_sections.title: Executive Committee of the Council.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution and composition of the Executive Committee to discharge functions assigned by the Council.

key_sections.title: Boards of Studies.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of various Boards of Studies (e.g., Vocational Education, Technician Education, Engineering and Technology, Management Studies) to advise on academic matters.

key_sections.title: Regional Committees.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of Regional Committees (Northern, Southern, Western, Eastern) to advise and assist the Council in planning, promoting, and regulating technical education within their regions.

key_sections.title: Directions by the Central Government.
key_sections.description: States that the Council is bound by policy directions issued by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power to supersede the Council.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to supersede the Council under certain conditions, such as inability to perform duties or abuse of powers.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Council to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules for its functioning.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to appoint Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Member-Secretary, and other members of the Council (Section 3(4), 3(5)); Power to approve establishment of offices (Section 3(3)); Power to declare programmes/areas as technical education (Section 2(g)); Power to declare institutions as technical institutions (Section 2(h)); Power to give directions on policy (Section 20); Power to supersede the Council (Section 21); Power to make rules (Section 22); Power to remove difficulties (Section 25).

Council: Power to contract, sue and be sued (Section 3(2)); Power to establish offices (Section 3(3)); Power to associate persons (Section 7); Power to appoint officers and employees (Section 8); Power to undertake surveys, coordinate development, allocate grants, promote innovations, formulate schemes, evolve appraisal systems, formulate training schemes, lay down norms and standards, fix fees, grant approvals, advise Central Government, lay down autonomy norms, prevent commercialisation, provide admission guidelines, inspect institutions, withhold/discontinue grants, strengthen organisations, declare institutions fit for grants, advise Commission for deemed University status, set up National Board of Accreditation, perform other functions (Section 10); Power to cause inspection (Section 11); Power to constitute Executive Committee (Section 12); Power to establish Boards of Studies (Section 13); Power to establish Regional Committees (Section 14); Power to spend sums from Fund (Section 16(3)); Power to make regulations (Section 23).

authorities_established: All India Council for Technical Education
All India Board of Vocational Education
All India Board of Technician Education
All India Board of Under-graduate Studies in Engineering and Technology
All India Board of Post-graduate Education and Research in Engineering and Technology
All India Board of Management Studies
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government
regulatory_bodies: All India Council for Technical Education

applies_to: technical education system throughout the country
technical institutions
Universities imparting technical education
special_provisions: Appointment of members representing States and Union territories on the recommendation of the respective Government.
Specific initial appointments for the first Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and Member-Secretary of the Council.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Directions by the Central Government; Inspection by the Council; Withholding or discontinuing grants by the Council; Power to supersede the Council by the Central Government; Power to make regulations by the Council.

act_identification.act_title: THE CHANDIGARH (DELEGATION OF POWERS) ACT, 1987

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of the Union territory of Chandigarh

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the delegation of powers vested in the Administrator of the Union territory of Chandigarh.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to enable the Administrator of the Union territory of Chandigarh to delegate his powers, authority, jurisdiction, and duties to other officers or authorities. It also validates any such delegations made by officers or authorities prior to the commencement of this Act, ensuring their actions are deemed legally sound.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's official name and specifies its geographical application to the Union territory of Chandigarh.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Provides the definition of 'Administrator' as the administrator of the Union territory of Chandigarh appointed by the President under article 239 of the Constitution.

key_sections.title: Delegation of powers, etc., vested in Administrator.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Administrator to delegate any power, authority, jurisdiction, or duty to specified officers or authorities, and allows for the transfer or withdrawal of appeals and applications for revision.

key_sections.title: Validation.
key_sections.description: Validates actions taken by officers or authorities before the commencement of this Act, deeming them to have been validly exercised or discharged as if the delegation provisions were in force at the time.

powers_conferred: Administrator may exercise or discharge any power, authority, jurisdiction or duty under any law in force in the Union territory of Chandigarh.
Administrator may delegate powers, authority, jurisdiction or duties to such officer or other authority as may be specified by the Central Government or the Administrator by notification.
Administrator may transfer any appeal or application for revision or any other matter pending before him to a competent officer or authority.
Administrator may withdraw for disposal by himself any appeal or application for revision or any other matter pending before a competent officer or authority.
Central Government or Administrator may specify officers or authorities for the exercise or discharge of delegated powers.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: President under article 239 of the Constitution appoints the Administrator. Central Government or Administrator can specify officers or other authorities for delegation.

applies_to: Union territory of Chandigarh
Administrator of the Union territory of Chandigarh
officer or other authority specified by the Central Government or the Administrator

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government or the Administrator (by notification in the Official Gazette for specifying officers/authorities)

act_identification.act_title: THE COMMISSION OF SATI (PREVENTION) ACT, 1987

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to provide for the more effective prevention of the commission of sati and its glorification. It seeks to address the practice of sati, which involves the burning or burying alive of widows or women, by implementing stringent measures and punishments.

chapter_titles:
PART II

PUNISHMENTS FOR OFFENCES RELATING TO SATI

PART III

POWERS OF COLLECTOR OR DISTRICT MAGISTRATE TO PREVENT OFFENCES RELATING TO SATI

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, its application to the whole of India except Jammu and Kashmir, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Code', 'glorification', 'sati', 'Special Court', and 'temple'.

key_sections.title: Attempt to commit sati.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for attempting to commit sati, which may extend to six months imprisonment or fine or both.

key_sections.title: Abetment of sati.
key_sections.description: Mandates severe punishment, including death or life imprisonment, for abetting the commission of sati or an attempt to commit sati.

key_sections.title: Punishment for glorification of sati.
key_sections.description: Stipulates punishment for glorifying sati, with imprisonment ranging from one to seven years and a fine.

key_sections.title: Power to prohibit certain acts.
key_sections.description: Grants the Collector or District Magistrate power to prohibit acts leading to sati or its glorification in specified areas.

key_sections.title: Power to remove certain temples or other structures.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government or Collector/District Magistrate to order the removal of structures perpetuating the memory of a person in respect of whom sati was committed.

key_sections.title: Power to seize certain properties.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Collector or District Magistrate to seize funds or property collected for the glorification of sati.

key_sections.title: Trial of offences under this Act.
key_sections.description: Mandates that all offences under this Act shall be triable only by Special Courts constituted by the State Government.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Provides for an appeal as a matter of right to the High Court from any judgment, sentence, or order of a Special Court.

key_sections.title: Burden of proof.
key_sections.description: States that in a prosecution for abetment of sati under section 4, the burden of proving innocence lies on the accused.

key_sections.title: Person convicted of an offence under section 4 to be disqualified from inheriting certain properties.
key_sections.description: Disqualifies a person convicted of abetting sati from inheriting property of the person in respect of whom sati was committed.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent in any other enactment.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal of existing laws.
key_sections.description: Repeals all existing State laws concerning the prevention or glorification of sati upon the commencement of this Act in that State.

powers_conferred: Collector or District Magistrate: Power to prohibit certain acts (Section 6)
Collector or District Magistrate: Power to remove certain temples or other structures (Section 7)
Collector or District Magistrate: Power to seize certain properties (Section 8)
State Government: Power to constitute Special Courts (Section 9)
State Government: Power to appoint Special Public Prosecutors (Section 10)
Special Court: Power to take cognizance of offences, try offences, convict for other connected offences, and forfeit funds/property (Sections 11, 12, 13)
Central Government: Power to make rules (Section 21)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Attempt to commit sati (Section 3): Imprisonment for up to six months or fine or both. Abetment of sati (Section 4(1)): Death or imprisonment for life and fine. Abetment of attempt to commit sati (Section 4(2)): Imprisonment for life and fine. Glorification of sati (Section 5): Imprisonment for a term not less than one year but which may extend to seven years and fine not less than five thousand rupees but which may extend to thirty thousand rupees. Contravention of Collector/District Magistrate's order (Section 6(3)): Imprisonment for a term not less than one year but which may extend to seven years and fine not less than five thousand rupees but which may extend to thirty thousand rupees. Contravention of reporting obligation (Section 17(3)): Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and fine.

repealed_acts: All laws in force in any State immediately before the commencement of this Act in that State which provide for the prevention or the glorification of sati

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government appoints Judges of Special Courts (with concurrence of Chief Justice of High Court) and Special Public Prosecutors.

applies_to: Whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir
Any person committing or abetting sati or its glorification
exemptions: State of Jammu and Kashmir
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different States for the commencement of the Act.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced through powers conferred upon Collector or District Magistrate to prohibit acts and seize property, establishment of Special Courts for trial of offences, and obligations of government officers and village officers to report offences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Special Court, High Court (for appeals)

act_identification.act_title: THE SPECIAL PROTECTION GROUP ACT, 1988

legislative_details.geographical_extent: any part of India as well as outside India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed force of the Union for providing proximate security to the Prime Minister of India and the [1][former Prime Ministers of India and members of their immediate families] and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: To provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed force of the Union, known as the Special Protection Group, for providing proximate security to the Prime Minister of India, former Prime Ministers, and their immediate families.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'active duty', 'Director', 'Group', and 'proximate security'.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Group.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Special Protection Group as an armed force of the Union for providing proximate security to the Prime Minister and former Prime Ministers and their immediate families.

key_sections.title: Control, direction, etc.
key_sections.description: Vests the general superintendence, direction, and control of the Group in the Central Government and provides for the appointment of a Director.

key_sections.title: Liability for service in and outside India.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that every member of the Group is liable to serve both within and outside India.

key_sections.title: Members of the Group always on active duty.
key_sections.description: Declares that members of the Group, when not on leave or under suspension, are always on active duty.

key_sections.title: Tenure of service.
key_sections.description: Specifies that every member of the Group holds office during the pleasure of the President.

key_sections.title: Restrictions respecting right to from associations, freedom of speech, etc.
key_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on members of the Group regarding joining associations, freedom of speech, and publication without prior sanction.

key_sections.title: Assistance to Group.
key_sections.description: Mandates that various government ministries, departments, and authorities must assist the Director or any member of the Group when called upon.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken under this Act.
key_sections.description: Provides legal protection against suits, prosecution, or other legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Provision as to existing Special Protection Group.
key_sections.description: Deems the Special Protection Group existing at the commencement of the Act and its members to be constituted and appointed under this Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: general superintendence, direction and control of the Group (Section 5)
Central Government: appoint Director of the Group (Section 5)
Central Government: appoint Inspectors General, Deputy Inspectors General, Assistant Inspectors General and other officers (Section 5)
Central Government: appoint any person or member of any other armed force to the Group (Section 4(3))
Central Government: grant previous sanction for members to join associations, speak, or publish (Section 10)
Central Government: direct members of the Group to exercise specified powers or duties (Section 13)
Central Government: make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act (Section 16)
Prescribed authority: appoint members to the Group (Section 2(d))
Prescribed authority: grant previous permission for resignation or withdrawal from duties (Section 8)
Prescribed authority: terminate appointment of any member in public interest (Section 11)
Board (constituted by Central Government): hear appeals against termination orders (Section 12)
Board: regulate its own procedure (Section 12)

authorities_established: Board (to be constituted by the Central Government)
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (Director, other officers, persons to Group); Prescribed authority (members of the Group)

applies_to: Every member of the Group
Prime Minister of India
former Prime Ministers of India and members of their immediate families
exemptions: any former Prime Minister or any member of the immediate family of the Prime Minister or of a former Prime Minister may decline proximate security
special_provisions: where the level of threat faced by any member of the immediate family of a former Prime Minister warrants proximate security or any other security, such security shall be provided to that member

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The general superintendence, direction and control of the Group shall vest in, and be exercised by, the Central Government. Ministries, Departments, and other authorities are mandated to act in aid of the Director or any member of the Group.

act_identification.act_title: THE RELIGIOUS INSTITUTIONS (PREVENTION OF MISUSE) ACT, 1988
act_identification.act_short_title: The Religious Institutions (Prevention of Misuse) Act, 1988

act_overview.preamble: An Act to prevent the misuse of religious institutions for political and other purposes.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to prevent religious institutions from being used for political activities, harbouring criminals, storing arms, promoting disharmony, or any other unlawful acts. It also prescribes penalties for such misuse and disqualifies individuals involved in contraventions.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and the date of commencement of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'ammunition', 'arms', 'manager', 'political activity', 'political party', and 'religious institution'.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of use of religious institutions for certain purposes.
key_sections.description: Prohibits religious institutions or their managers from using premises for political activity, harbouring criminals, storing arms, keeping illegal goods, erecting unauthorized constructions, carrying on unlawful acts, promoting disharmony, or activities prejudicial to India's sovereignty, unity, and integrity, or contravening the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971.

key_sections.title: Restrictions on carrying arms and ammunition into a religious institution.
key_sections.description: Prohibits religious institutions or managers from allowing entry of arms or ammunition, with exceptions for Kirpans worn by Sikhs and arms used in religious ceremonies by custom.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of use of funds of religious institutions for certain activities.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the use of funds or properties of religious institutions for the benefit of any political party, for political activity, or for committing any offence.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of religious for a for propagating political ideas.
key_sections.description: Prohibits religious institutions or managers from allowing ceremonies, festivals, congregations, processions, or assemblies under their auspices to be used for political activity.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of sections 3, 4, 5, or 6, including imprisonment up to five years and a fine up to ten thousand rupees.

key_sections.title: Disqualification of persons convicted or charge-sheeted under this Act.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that managers or employees convicted under this Act will be removed from office and disqualified for appointment in any religious institution for six years. Courts can also restrain charge-sheeted persons from exercising duties pending trial.

key_sections.title: Certain persons bound to give information to police.
key_sections.description: Mandates managers and employees of religious institutions to inform the police of any contravention or impending contravention of the Act, with failure punishable under section 176 of the Indian Penal Code.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Religious Institutions (Prevention of Misuse) Ordinance, 1988, while saving actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Power to courts to restrain persons from exercising powers or discharging duties of office pending trial (Section 8(2))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of sections 3, 4, 5, or 6 is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees (Section 7). Failure to give information to police as required by Section 9 is punishable under section 176 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).

repealed_acts: The Religious Institutions (Prevention of Misuse) Ordinance, 1988 (Ord. 3 of 1988)
related_acts: Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 (69 of 1971)

applies_to: religious institution
manager of a religious institution
other employee of a religious institution
exemptions: wearing and carrying of a Kirpan by any person professing the Sikh religion
any arms which are used, as part of any religious ceremony or ritual of the institution as established by custom or usage

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced through police action (information to police, Section 9) and judicial proceedings in courts, leading to penalties (Section 7) and disqualifications (Section 8).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: any court

act_identification.act_title: THE BHARAT PETROLEUM CORPORATION LIMITED (DETERMINATION OF CONDITIONS OF SERVICE OF EMPLOYEES) ACT, 1988
act_identification.act_short_title: the Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (Determination of Conditions of Service of Employees) Act, 1988

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS for the purpose of making the conditions of service of the officers and employees of the Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited comparable with the conditions of service of the officers and employees of other public sector companies, it is necessary to empower the Central Government to determine the conditions of service of the officers and employees of the said Corporation;
act_overview.purpose: This Act empowers the Central Government to determine the conditions of service for officers and employees of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited. The main objective is to ensure their conditions of service are comparable with those in other public sector companies.

key_definitions: officers and employees of the Corporation

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall be deemed to have come into force on July 2, 1988.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Burmah Shell', 'Corporation', and 'public sector company'.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to frame schemes to determine conditions of service of officers and employees.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to frame schemes for determining the conditions of service of the Corporation's employees, including provisions for retrospective effect and amendments, overriding other laws or judgments.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (Determination of Conditions of Service of Employees) Ordinance, 1988, and includes a saving clause for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Power of Central Government to frame schemes to determine conditions of service of officers and employees.
Power to give retrospective effect to any such scheme or any provision thereof.
Power to amend, by way of addition, variation or repeal, any existing provisions determining the conditions of service of the officers and employees of the Corporation.

repealed_acts: The Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (Determination of Conditions of Service of Employees) Ordinance, 1988 (6 of 1988)
related_acts: Burmah Shell (Acquisition of Undertakings in India) Act, 1976 (2 of 1976)

applies_to: officers and employees of the Corporation

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government frames schemes which are then laid before each House of Parliament. Parliament has the power to modify or annul these schemes.

act_identification.act_title: THE PROHIBITION OF BENAMI PROPERTY TRANSACTIONS ACT, 1988
act_identification.act_short_title: The Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act, 1988
act_identification.date_of_commencement: Sections 3, 5 and 8 came into force at once; remaining provisions deemed to have come into force on 19/05/1988

act_overview.preamble: An Act to prohibit benami transactions and the right to recover property held benami and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to prohibit benami transactions and prevent the recovery of property held benami. It also provides for mechanisms to identify, adjudicate, and confiscate such properties, along with prescribing penalties for related offences.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official short title, geographical extent, and commencement dates of the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'benami property', 'benami transaction', 'benamidar', and various authorities.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of benami transactions.
key_sections.description: Prohibits any person from entering into benami transactions and prescribes penalties for such actions.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of the right to recover property held benami.
key_sections.description: Bars any suit, claim, or action to enforce rights in respect of property held benami by a person claiming to be the real owner.

key_sections.title: Property held benami liable to confiscation.
key_sections.description: States that any property involved in a benami transaction is liable to be confiscated by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Prohibition on re-transfer of property by benamidar.
key_sections.description: Prohibits a benamidar from re-transferring benami property to the beneficial owner or any other person acting on their behalf, declaring such re-transfers null and void.

key_sections.title: Authorities and jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Lists the authorities for the purposes of the Act, including the Initiating Officer, Approving Authority, Administrator, and Adjudicating Authority.

key_sections.title: Notice and attachment of property involved in benami transaction.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Initiating Officer to issue notices and provisionally attach property believed to be involved in a benami transaction.

key_sections.title: Adjudication of benami property.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for the Adjudicating Authority to determine whether a property is benami, including issuing notices, conducting inquiries, and passing orders.

key_sections.title: Confiscation and vesting of benami property.
key_sections.description: Provides for the confiscation of benami property by the Central Government and its vesting in the government, free of encumbrances, upon an order from the Adjudicating Authority.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to establish an Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals against orders of authorities under the Act.

key_sections.title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts.
key_sections.description: States that civil courts shall not have jurisdiction over matters that the authorities, Adjudicating Authority, or Appellate Tribunal are empowered to determine under this Act.

key_sections.title: Special Courts.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to designate Courts of Session as Special Courts for the trial of offences punishable under this Act.

key_sections.title: Penalty for benami transaction.
key_sections.description: Prescribes rigorous imprisonment and fine for persons found guilty of the offence of benami transaction.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Authorities (Initiating Officer, Approving Authority, Administrator, Adjudicating Authority) have powers of a civil court for discovery, enforcing attendance, compelling production of documents, issuing commissions, receiving evidence, etc.
Authorities have power to call for information from government officers, local bodies, or any person responsible for maintaining records.
Authorities have power to impound and retain documents for inquiry.
Initiating Officer, with Approving Authority's approval, has power to conduct inquiry or investigation.
Initiating Officer has power to issue notice and provisionally attach property involved in benami transaction.
Adjudicating Authority has power to adjudicate benami property, confirm attachment, and order confiscation.
Administrator has power to receive and manage confiscated property and dispose of property vested in the Central Government.
Central Government has power to establish an Appellate Tribunal.
Appellate Tribunal has powers of a civil court for summoning, discovery, receiving evidence, reviewing decisions, etc., and its orders are executable as civil court decrees.
Central Government has power to designate Special Courts for trial of offences.
Initiating Officer has power to tender immunity from prosecution with previous sanction of the competent authority.
Central Government has power to issue orders, instructions, or directions for the proper administration of the Act.
Central Government has power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Entering into any benami transaction (after 01/11/2016) is punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term of 1 to 7 years and a fine up to 25% of the fair market value of the property. Giving false information to any authority or furnishing false documents is punishable with rigorous imprisonment for 6 months to 5 years and a fine up to 10% of the fair market value of the property. Failure to comply with summons or furnish information is liable to a penalty of Rs. 25,000 for each such failure.

repealed_acts: Sections 81, 82 and 94 of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882 (2 of 1882)
Section 66 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908)
Section 281A of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (43 of 1961)
The Benami Transactions (Prohibition of the Right to Recover Property) Ordinance, 1988 (Ord. 2 of 1988)
related_acts: Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963 (54 of 1963)
Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (61 of 1985)
Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 (15 of 1992)
Smugglers and Foreign Exchange Manipulators (Forfeiture of Property) Act, 1976 (13 of 1976)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson and Members of the Appellate Tribunal. The Central Government designates Special Courts in consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court. The Central Government may appoint Public Prosecutors or Special Public Prosecutors.
regulatory_bodies: Securities and Exchange Board of India

applies_to: Whole of India
Persons entering into benami transactions
Beneficial owners
Benamidars
exemptions: Property held by a Karta or a member of a Hindu undivided family for their benefit or benefit of other members, with consideration from known HUF sources.
Property held by a person in a fiduciary capacity for the benefit of another person (e.g., trustee, executor, partner, director, depository participant).
Property held by an individual in the name of their spouse or child, with consideration from known sources of the individual.
Property held by an individual jointly with their brother, sister, lineal ascendant, or descendant, with consideration from known sources of the individual.

Transactions involving allowing possession of property in part performance of a contract under Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, if consideration is provided, stamp duty paid, and contract registered.
Property relating to charitable or religious trusts, if exempted by Central Government notification.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a multi-tiered system involving Initiating Officers, Approving Authorities, Administrators, and the Adjudicating Authority. It includes powers for inquiry, investigation, provisional attachment, adjudication, and confiscation of benami properties. Appeals can be made to the Appellate Tribunal and then to the High Court. Offences are tried by Special Courts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court (for appeals), Special Courts (for trial of offences)

act_identification.act_title: THE PREVENTION OF ILLICIT TRAFFIC IN NARCOTIC DRUGS AND PSYCHOTROPIC SUBSTANCES ACT, 1988
act_identification.act_short_title: THE PREVENTION OF ILLICIT TRAFFIC IN NARCOTIC DRUGS AND PSYCHOTROPIC SUBSTANCES ACT, 1988

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS illicit traffic in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances poses a serious threat to the health and welfare of the people and the activities of persons engaged in such illicit traffic have a deleterious effect on the national economy; ANDWHEREAS having regard to the persons by whom and the manner in which such activities are organised and carried on, and having regard to the fact that in certain areas which are highly vulnerable to the illicit traffic in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, such activities of a considerable magnitude are clandestinely organised and carried on, it is necessary for the effective prevention of such activities to provide for detention of persons concerned in any manner therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the preventive detention of persons involved in illicit traffic of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. Its objective is to counter the serious threat posed by such activities to public health, welfare, and the national economy, especially in vulnerable areas, by enabling the detention of individuals engaged in these clandestine operations.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application (whole of India except J&K), and the date it came into force.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'detention order', and 'illicit traffic'.

key_sections.title: Power to make orders detaining certain persons.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the Central or State Government, or their empowered officers, to issue detention orders against persons (including foreigners) to prevent them from engaging in illicit traffic.

key_sections.title: Execution of detention orders.
key_sections.description: States that detention orders can be executed anywhere in India, similar to warrants of arrest under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

key_sections.title: Advisory Boards.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of Advisory Boards by Central and State Governments to review detention orders and report on the sufficiency of cause for detention.

key_sections.title: Cases in which and circumstances under which persons may be detained for periods longer than three months without obtaining the opinion of Advisory Board.
key_sections.description: Allows for detention periods longer than three months (up to six months) without an Advisory Board opinion in specific circumstances related to highly vulnerable areas for illicit traffic.

key_sections.title: Maximum period of detention.
key_sections.description: Sets the maximum detention period at one year for general cases and two years for cases falling under Section 10, subject to confirmation by the appropriate Government.

key_sections.title: Revocation of detention orders
key_sections.description: Provides for the revocation or modification of detention orders by the Central or State Government, and clarifies that revocation does not bar making a new order.

key_sections.title: Temporary release of persons detaine
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central or State Government to direct temporary release of detained persons, with or without conditions, and outlines penalties for non-compliance.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith
key_sections.description: Grants immunity from legal proceedings to the Central or State Government and individuals for actions taken in good faith under this Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving
key_sections.description: Repeals the Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Ordinance, 1988, and includes a saving clause for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Central Government or a State Government, or any officer of the Central Government, not below the rank of a Joint Secretary, or any officer of a State Government, not below the rank of a Secretary: Power to make orders detaining certain persons (Section 3).
Appropriate Government: Power to regulate place and conditions of detention and to remove persons from one place of detention to another (Section 5).
Appropriate Government: Power to make a report to a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class regarding absconding persons and to direct such persons to appear (Section 8).
Central Government and each State Government: Power to constitute Advisory Boards (Section 9).
Appropriate Government: Power to confirm or revoke detention orders based on the Advisory Board's report (Section 9).
Central Government: Power to direct temporary release of any person detained (Section 13).
State Government: Power to direct temporary release of any person detained (Section 13).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Failure to comply with a direction to appear by an absconding person (Section 8(1)(b)) is punishable with imprisonment for up to one year, or fine, or both. Failure to surrender after temporary release (Section 13(5)) is punishable with imprisonment for up to two years, or fine, or both. Failure to fulfil conditions of temporary release (Section 13(6)) results in forfeiture of the bond.

repealed_acts: The Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Ordinance, 1988 (Ord. 7 of 1988)
related_acts: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (61 of 1985)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government and State Government (for Advisory Boards)

applies_to: any person (including a foreigner) engaging in illicit traffic in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances
special_provisions: The Act extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

Special provisions for detention for periods longer than three months without Advisory Board opinion apply to persons engaged in illicit traffic in 'area highly vulnerable to such illicit traffic' as defined in Section 10(1) Explanation 1.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Detention orders are made by authorized government officials (Section 3) and executed in the manner provided for warrants of arrest (Section 4). Detention orders are reviewed by Advisory Boards (Section 9), and the appropriate Government confirms or revokes them. Absconding persons can be reported to Magistrates (Section 8).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Metropolitan Magistrate or a Magistrate of the first class (for matters related to absconding persons under Section 8)

act_identification.act_title: THE PREVENTION OF CORRUPTION ACT, 1988

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India and it applies also to all citizens of India outside India.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the prevention of corruption and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws related to the prevention of corruption. Its main objective is to provide a comprehensive legal framework to combat corruption, particularly involving public servants.

chapter_titles: INVESTIGATION INTO CASES UNDER THE ACT
SANCTION FOR PROSECUTION AND OTHER MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its geographical applicability to the whole of India and to citizens outside India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'election', 'prescribed', 'public duty', 'public servant', and 'undue advantage'.

key_sections.title: Power to appoint special Judges.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central or State Government to appoint Special Judges to try offences under this Act.

key_sections.title: Offence relating to public servant being bribed.
key_sections.description: Defines the offence committed by a public servant who obtains, accepts, or attempts to obtain undue advantage for improper performance of public duty.

key_sections.title: Offence relating to bribing of a public servant.
key_sections.description: Defines the offence committed by any person who gives or promises to give undue advantage to induce or reward a public servant for improper performance of public duty.

key_sections.title: Offence relating to bribing a public servant by a commercial organisation.
key_sections.description: Specifies the offence committed by a commercial organisation if a person associated with it bribes a public servant to obtain or retain business or an advantage.

key_sections.title: Criminal misconduct by a public servant.
key_sections.description: Defines criminal misconduct by a public servant, including dishonest misappropriation of property or intentional illicit enrichment.

key_sections.title: Persons authorised to investigate.
key_sections.description: Stipulates the minimum rank of police officers authorized to investigate offences under this Act.

key_sections.title: Enquiry or Inquiry or investigation of offences relatable to recommendations made or decision taken by public servant in discharge of official functions or duties.
key_sections.description: Requires previous approval for inquiry or investigation into offences committed by public servants related to their official recommendations or decisions.

key_sections.title: Provisions of Criminal Law Amendment Ordinance, 1944 to apply to attachment under this Act.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of the Criminal Law Amendment Ordinance, 1944, apply to the attachment, administration, and execution of orders related to property procured by means of an offence under this Act.

key_sections.title: Previous sanction necessary for prosecution.
key_sections.description: Mandates previous sanction from the appropriate government or authority for the prosecution of public servants for certain offences under the Act.

key_sections.title: Presumption where public servant accepts any undue advantage.
key_sections.description: Establishes a legal presumption that a public servant who accepts or attempts to obtain undue advantage does so as a motive or reward for improper public duty.

key_sections.title: Act to be in addition to any other law.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act are in addition to, and not in derogation of, any other law in force.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, and the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1952, while providing for savings of actions taken under the repealed Acts.

powers_conferred: Central Government or State Government: Power to appoint Special Judges (Section 3).
Special Judge: Power to take cognizance of offences, follow procedure, tender pardon, pass sentences, and try summarily (Sections 5, 6).
Police Officer: Power to inspect bankers’ books for investigation (Section 18).
Central Government: Power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act (Section 29A).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines several offences related to corruption. For public servants, these include obtaining undue advantage (Section 7, punishable with imprisonment 3-7 years + fine), obtaining undue advantage without consideration (Section 11, imprisonment 6 months-5 years + fine), and criminal misconduct (Section 13, imprisonment 4-10 years + fine). For other persons, offences include bribing a public servant (Section 8, imprisonment up to 7 years or fine or both) and taking undue advantage to influence a public servant (Section 7A, imprisonment 3-7 years + fine). Commercial organisations are punishable with fine for bribing a public servant (Section 9), and persons in charge of such organisations can face imprisonment (3-7 years + fine) if the offence is committed with their consent or connivance (Section 10). Abetment of offences (Section 12), habitual offending (Section 14), and attempts to commit offences (Section 15) also carry specific punishments.

repealed_acts: The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (2 of 1947)
The Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1952 (46 of 1952)
related_acts: Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (15 of 2003)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government or the State Government has the power to appoint Special Judges.

applies_to: Whole of India and to all citizens of India outside India.
Public servants as defined in Section 2.
Commercial organisations and persons associated with them.
exemptions: Persons compelled to give undue advantage, provided they report the matter to law enforcement within seven days (Section 8).

Jurisdiction exercisable by, or procedure applicable to, any court or authority under the Army Act, 1950, the Air Force Act, 1950, the Navy Act, 1957, the Border Security Force Act, 1968, the Coast Guard Act, 1978, and the National Security Guard Act, 1986 (Section 25).
special_provisions: Special provisions for the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union Territory of Ladakh regarding the establishment of an Anti-Corruption Bureau and powers of attachment of property (Sections 17B to 17G, inserted by State Amendment).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Offences are investigated by authorized police officers (Section 17, 17A) and tried by Special Judges (Chapter II). Prosecution requires previous sanction (Section 19). The Act also provides for attachment and forfeiture of property (Chapter IVA).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Special Judges (for trial), High Court (for appeal and revision).

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the simplification of procedure for furnishing returns and maintaining registers in relation to establishments employing a small number of persons under certain labour laws.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to simplify the procedural requirements for employers in small and very small establishments regarding the furnishing of returns and maintenance of registers under various labour laws. It seeks to ease compliance by allowing a consolidated annual return and simplified registers.

key_sections.title: Exemption from furnishing or maintaining of returns and registers requires under certain labour laws.

key_sections.title: Penalty.

act_identification.act_title: THE AUROVILLE FOUNDATION ACT, 1988

act_identification.act_title: THE JAMIA MILLIA ISLAMIA ACT, 1988

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate a teaching University in the Union territory of Delhi and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS it is expedient to establish and incorporate a teaching University at New Delhi, to dissolve the “Jamia Millia Islamia Society, Delhi”, a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (21 of 1860) and to transfer to and vest in the said University all properties and rights of the said Society;
act_overview.purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching University in the Union territory of Delhi, dissolving the existing Jamia Millia Islamia Society and transferring its assets to the new University. The Act aims to disseminate and advance knowledge, promote educational innovations, inter-disciplinary studies, national integration, secularism, and international understanding.

Power to exercise any power conferred on any authority of the University in case of immediate action (Shaikh-ul-Jamia (Vice-Chancellor))
Power to manage and administer the revenue and property of the University and conduct administrative affairs (Majlis-i-Muntazimah (Executive Council))
Power to create teaching and academic posts, determine emoluments, and define duties and conditions of service (Majlis-i-Muntazimah (Executive Council))
Power to appoint Professors, Readers, Lecturers and other academic staff (Majlis-i-Muntazimah (Executive Council))
Power to exercise general supervision over the academic policies of the University and give directions (Majlis-i-Talimi (Academic Council))
Power to make new or additional Statutes or amend or repeal existing Statutes (Majlis-i-Muntazimah (Executive Council) and Visitor)
Power to make Ordinances (Majlis-i-Muntazimah (Executive Council))
Power to make Regulations (Authorities of the University)
Power to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act (Central Government)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for disciplinary actions against students, including expulsion, rustication, debarment from examinations, fines, and cancellation of results (Section 30, Statute 31). It also outlines procedures for the removal of teachers and other employees on grounds of misconduct or other specified reasons (Statutes 37, 38).

authorities_established: Board of Management for the Mass Communication Research Centre
Board of Management for Jamia Schools
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Shaikh-ul-Jamia (Vice-Chancellor). The Anjuman (Court) elects the Amir-i-Jamia (Chancellor). The Majlis-i-Muntazimah (Executive Council) appoints the Naib Shaikh-ul-Jamia (Pro-Vice-Chancellor), Musajjil (Registrar), Finance Officer, Librarian, Professors, Readers, Lecturers, other academic staff, and administrative/ministerial staff. The Shaikh-ul-Jamia (Vice-Chancellor) appoints Deans of Faculties and the Dean of Students’ Welfare. The Board of Management of the Mass Communication Research Centre and Jamia Schools appoint their respective teaching and administrative staff.

applies_to: The Jamia Millia Islamia University
Persons of either sex and of whatever race, creed, caste or class
Employees of the University
Students of the University
special_provisions: Appropriate provisions for reservation for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the physically handicapped persons and women (Section 7)
Transitional provisions for existing authorities, officers, and employees of Jamia Millia Islamia to continue in their roles until new bodies are constituted under the Act (Section 41)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Majlis-i-Muntazimah (Executive Council) has the power to make Statutes and Ordinances. The authorities of the University may make Regulations. The Visitor also has powers to make, amend, or repeal Statutes.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor has powers of inspection, inquiry, and annulment of University proceedings. The Shaikh-ul-Jamia (Vice-Chancellor) exercises general supervision and control. Annual reports and accounts are submitted to the Anjuman (Court), Visitor, and Parliament. Disputes involving employees or students are referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration. Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations are published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil courts are barred from hearing matters decided by the Tribunal of Arbitration concerning employee disputes. The Visitor's decision is final on disputes regarding the constitution of University authorities. No suit or legal proceedings lie against officers or employees for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the detailed Statutes of the University, covering the constitution, powers, and duties of various officers and authorities like the Amir-i-Jamia (Chancellor), Shaikh-ul-Jamia (Vice-Chancellor), Registrar, Finance Officer, Deans, Heads of Departments, Dean of Students' Welfare, Librarian, Anjuman (Court), Majlis-i-Muntazimah (Executive Council), Majlis-i-Talimi (Academic Council), Faculties, Departments, Boards of Studies, Mass Communication Research Centre, Jamia Schools, Finance Committee, Selection Committees, and provisions for service conditions, honorary degrees, withdrawal of degrees, discipline, and other administrative matters.

act_identification.act_title: THE MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to motor vehicles.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws concerning motor vehicles, covering aspects like licensing, registration, control of transport vehicles, construction, equipment, maintenance, traffic control, insurance, and claims tribunals.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II LICENSING OF DRIVERS OF MOTOR VEHICLES
CHAPTER III LICENSING OF CONDUCTORS OF STAGE CARRIAGES
CHAPTER IV REGISTRATION OF MOTOR VEHICLES
CHAPTER V CONTROL OF TRANSPORT VEHICLES
CHAPTER VI SPECIAL PROVISIONS RELATING TO STATE TRANSPORT UNDERTAKINGS
CHAPTER VII CONSTRUCTION, EQUIPMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF MOTOR VEHICLES
CHAPTER IX MOTOR VEHICLES TEMPORARILY LEAVING OR VISITING INDIA

CHAPTER XI INSURANCE OF MOTOR VEHICLES AGAINST THIRD PARTY RISKS
CHAPTER XIII OFFENCES, PENALTIES AND PROCEDURE

key_definitions: liability covered by the terms of the policy

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Necessity for driving licence.
key_sections.description: Mandates holding an effective driving licence to operate a motor vehicle in public places.

key_sections.title: Necessity for registration.
key_sections.description: Requires motor vehicles to be registered and display a registration mark to be driven in public places.

key_sections.title: Alteration in motor vehicle.
key_sections.description: Prohibits altering a motor vehicle from its manufacturer's specifications without approval, with provisions for specific modifications.

key_sections.title: Certificate of fitness of transport vehicles.
key_sections.description: Requires transport vehicles to have a certificate of fitness to be validly registered.

key_sections.title: Necessity for permits.
key_sections.description: Mandates permits for transport vehicles to be used in public places, with certain exemptions.

key_sections.title: Limits of speed.
key_sections.description: Sets maximum and minimum speed limits for motor vehicles.

key_sections.title: Limits of weight and limitations on use.
key_sections.description: Regulates the weight of motor vehicles and prohibits driving vehicles with unladen or laden weight exceeding specified limits.

key_sections.title: Wearing of protective headgear.
key_sections.description: Mandates wearing protective headgear for persons on motorcycles, with an exemption for Sikhs wearing turbans.

key_sections.title: Protection of Good Samaritans.
key_sections.description: Protects individuals who render emergency aid to accident victims from civil or criminal liability for negligence.

key_sections.title: Necessity for insurance against third party risks.
key_sections.description: Requires motor vehicles to have a policy of insurance against third-party risks to be used in public places.

key_sections.title: Special provisions as to compensation in case of hit and run motor accident.
key_sections.description: Provides for compensation from the Central Government for death or grievous hurt in hit and run accidents.

key_sections.title: Payment of compensation in case of death or grevious hurt, etc.
key_sections.description: Establishes fixed compensation amounts for death or grievous hurt in motor vehicle accidents, irrespective of fault.

key_sections.title: Claims Tribunals.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to constitute Motor Accidents Claims Tribunals for adjudicating compensation claims.

key_sections.title: General provision for punishment of offences.
key_sections.description: Prescribes general penalties for contraventions of the Act or rules where no specific penalty is provided.

key_sections.title: Driving by a drunken person or by a person under the influence of drugs.
key_sections.description: Penalizes driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

key_sections.title: Offences by juveniles.
key_sections.description: Holds guardians or owners liable for offences committed by juveniles and imposes penalties including driving licence restrictions for juveniles.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Make rules (Sections 27, 64, 75, 110, 118, 137, 139, 164C, 210C, 215C), specify age limits for motor vehicles (Section 59), register vehicles belonging to Central Government (Section 60), develop National Transportation Policy (Section 66A), make schemes for national/multimodal/inter-State transport (Section 88A), direct recall of motor vehicles (Section 110A), exempt certain vehicles from Chapter VII (Section 110(3)(a)), constitute National Road Safety Council (Section 215), constitute National Road Safety Board (Section 215B), delegate powers (Section 215A), remove difficulties (Section 216).

State Government: Make rules (Sections 28, 38, 65, 67, 95, 96, 107, 111, 138, 164D, 176, 210D, 215D), control road transport (Section 67), constitute Transport Authorities (Section 68), constitute State Transport Appellate Tribunals (Section 89), grant exemptions from hours of work for drivers (Section 91), formulate proposals for State transport undertakings (Section 99), modify approved schemes (Section 102), exempt certain vehicles from rules under Section 110(1) (Section 110(3)(b)), restrict speed of motor vehicles (Section 112), restrict use of vehicles (Section 115), determine parking places and halting stations (Section 117), authorise police officers for information/arrest (Sections 133, 158, 202, 206, 207), frame schemes for accident investigation/amenities (Section 135), ensure electronic monitoring of road safety (Section 136A), constitute Motor Accidents Claims Tribunals (Section 165), increase penalties (Section 210A), delegate powers (Section 215A), constitute State Road Safety Council/District Road Safety Committee (Section 215).

Licensing Authority: Grant learner's licence (Section 8), grant driving licence (Section 9), add classes to driving licence (Section 11), revoke driving licence (Section 16), disqualify from holding driving licence (Section 19), grant conductor's licence (Section 30), revoke conductor's licence (Section 32), disqualify from holding conductor's licence (Section 34).
Registering Authority: Register motor vehicles (Section 41), refuse registration/renewal (Section 45), assign new registration mark (Section 47), cancel registration (Sections 54, 55).

Transport Authority (Regional/State): Grant permits (Sections 72, 74, 76, 79, 80, 87, 88), transfer permits (Section 82), replace vehicles (Section 83), cancel/suspend permits (Section 86), countersign permits (Section 88).
Courts: Disqualify from holding driving licence (Section 20), set aside/vary disqualification orders (Section 20(5)), cancel/suspend driving licence on conviction (Section 22).
Claims Tribunals: Adjudicate compensation claims (Section 165), make awards (Section 168), enforce awards (Section 169(4)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter XIII details various offences and penalties. These include: General contravention of Act/rules (fine up to 1500 rupees); contravention of regulations under Section 118 (fine 500-1000 rupees); travelling without pass/ticket, conductor dereliction of duty, refusal to ply contract carriage (fine up to 500 rupees); disobedience of orders, obstruction, refusal of information (fine up to 2000 rupees or imprisonment up to one month or both); allowing unauthorised persons to drive (imprisonment up to three months or fine of 5000 rupees or both); driving without valid licence or under age (imprisonment up to three months or fine of 5000 rupees or both); driving while disqualified, obtaining licence by fraud (imprisonment up to three months or fine of 10000 rupees or both); offences relating to construction, maintenance, sale, alteration of vehicles/components (imprisonment up to one year or fines ranging from 1 lakh to 100 crore rupees or both); contravention of Section 62A (oversized vehicles) (fine 5000-10000 rupees); driving at excessive speed (fines from 1000 to 4000 rupees, driving licence impounded for subsequent offence); driving dangerously (imprisonment 6 months to 1 year or fine 1000-5000 rupees for first offence; imprisonment up to 2 years or fine of 10000 rupees for subsequent); driving under influence of alcohol/drugs (imprisonment up to 6 months or fine of 10000 rupees for first offence; imprisonment up to 2 years or fine of 15000 rupees for subsequent); driving when mentally/physically unfit (fine 1000 rupees for first offence; fine 2000 rupees for subsequent); offences relating to accident (failure to comply with duties) (imprisonment up to 6 months or fine of 5000 rupees for first offence; imprisonment up to 1 year or fine of 10000 rupees for subsequent); abetment of certain offences (same punishment as abetted offence); racing and trials of speed (imprisonment up to 3 months or fine of 5000 rupees for first offence; imprisonment up to 1 year or fine of 10000 rupees for subsequent); using vehicle in unsafe condition (fine of 1500 rupees, or imprisonment up to 3 months or fine of 5000 rupees if accident caused; subsequent offences have higher penalties); using vehicle without registration (fine up to 5000 rupees for first offence; imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to 10000 rupees for subsequent); using vehicle without permit (imprisonment up to 6 months and fine of 10000 rupees for first offence; imprisonment up to 1 year or fine of 10000 rupees for subsequent); offences relating to registration (false documents, failure to apply) (fines based on road tax, imprisonment up to 1 year); agents/canvassers/aggregators without proper authority (fines from 1000 to 1 lakh rupees, imprisonment up to 6 months); driving vehicle exceeding permissible weight (fine of 20000 rupees + 2000 rupees per tonne of excess load); carriage of excess passengers (fine of 200 rupees per excess passenger); not wearing safety belt/child restraint (fine of 1000 rupees); violation of safety measures for motor cycle drivers/pillion riders (fine of 1000 rupees and disqualification for 3 months); not wearing protective headgear (fine of 1000 rupees and disqualification for 3 months); failure to allow free passage to emergency vehicles (imprisonment up to 6 months or fine of 10000 rupees or both); improper use of horns/silence zones (fine of 1000 rupees for first offence; fine of 2000 rupees for subsequent); driving uninsured vehicle (imprisonment up to 3 months or fine of 2000 rupees for first offence; imprisonment up to 3 months or fine of 4000 rupees for subsequent); taking vehicle without authority (imprisonment up to 3 months or fine of 5000 rupees or both); unauthorised interference with vehicle (fine of 1000 rupees); failure to comply with road design/construction/maintenance standards (fine up to 1 lakh rupees); offences by companies (company and responsible persons liable); offences by juveniles (guardian/owner liable, imprisonment up to 3 years, fine of 25000 rupees, vehicle registration cancelled, juvenile disqualified from licence until 25 years); causing obstruction to free flow of traffic (penalty up to 500 rupees); penalty for offence committed by an enforcing authority (twice the penalty for that offence).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out by police officers and officers of the Motor Vehicles Department, who are empowered to seize documents, detain vehicles, conduct tests, and make arrests. act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL HIGHWAYS AUTHORITY OF INDIA ACT, 1988

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution of an Authority for the development, maintenance and management of national highways and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the constitution of an Authority for the development, maintenance and management of national highways and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

chapter_titles: THE NATIONAL HIGHWAYS AUTHORITY OF INDIA

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its applicability to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used within the Act, such as 'Authority', 'Chairman', 'member', and 'national highway'.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Authority.
key_sections.description: Establishes the National Highways Authority of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, and outlines its composition including a Chairman and members appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power of the Central Government to vest or entrust any national highway in the Authority.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to vest or entrust national highways or stretches thereof to the Authority via notification.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Authority.
key_sections.description: Details the primary functions of the Authority, including the development, maintenance, and management of national highways, and other related activities like surveying, construction, and providing facilities.

key_sections.title: Fund of the Authority.
key_sections.description: Establishes the National Highways Authority of India Fund, specifying what shall be credited to it (grants, loans, other sums) and how it shall be utilized.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Mandates the maintenance and audit of the Authority's accounts in consultation with the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, and requires submission of audited accounts to the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Employees of the Authority to be public servants.
key_sections.description: Declares that all members, officers, and employees of the Authority are deemed public servants under the Indian Penal Code when acting under this Act.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Provides protection against legal proceedings for the Authority, its members, officers, or employees for actions done in good faith under the Act or its rules/regulations.

key_sections.title: Power of the Central Government to supersede the Authority.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to supersede the Authority under certain circumstances, such as grave emergency or persistent default, for a specified period.

key_sections.title: Power of the Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, covering various aspects like terms of service, budget, and audit.

key_sections.title: Power of the Authority to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Authority the power to make regulations, not inconsistent with the Act or rules, to carry out its provisions, including meeting procedures, terms of service for employees, and highway management.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act establishes the National Highways Authority of India to develop, maintain, and manage national highways. Power to create teaching and academic posts, determine emoluments, and define duties and conditions of service (Executive Council, Statute 13(i)).
Power to appoint Professors, Readers, Lecturers, academic staff, and Principals (Executive Council, Statute 13(ii)).
Power to create administrative, ministerial and other necessary posts and make appointments (Executive Council, Statute 13(iii)).
Power to regulate and enforce discipline among employees (Executive Council, Statute 13(v)).
Power to manage and regulate the finances, accounts, investments, property, business (Executive Council, Statute 13(vi)).
Power to entertain, adjudicate upon, and redress grievances of employees and students (Executive Council, Statute 13(xii)).
Power to appoint examiners and moderators (Executive Council, Statute 13(xiii)).
Power to delegate any of its powers (Executive Council, Statute 13(xvi)).
Power to exercise general supervision over the academic policies of the University and give directions (Academic Council, Statute 15(a)).
Power to bring about inter-School co-ordination, establish or appoint committees or boards (Academic Council, Statute 15(b)).
Power to frame regulations and rules consistent with the Statutes and Ordinances regarding academic functioning (Academic Council, Statute 15(d)).
Power to advise on the development of the University and review the progress implementation of programmes (Planning Board, Statute 16(2)).
Power to take disciplinary action against employees (Registrar, Statute 5(5)).
Power to exercise general supervision over the funds of the University and advise on financial policy (Finance Officer, Statute 6(6)(a)).
Power to hold and manage the property and investments of the University (Finance Officer, Statute 6(7)(a)).
Power to ensure expenditure limits are not exceeded and prepare annual accounts (Finance Officer, Statute 6(7)(b), (c)).
Power to maintain discipline among students and take disciplinary action (Vice-Chancellor, Statute 31(1)).
Power to expel, rusticate, debar students, or cancel examination results (Vice-Chancellor, Statute 31(3)).
Power to make Regulations (Authorities of the University, Section 29, Statute 43).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes disciplinary actions for misconduct by employees, which may include suspension, censure, withholding of increment, or removal from service. For students, disciplinary actions can include removal from the rolls, debarment from examinations, fines, expulsion, rustication for a specified period, or cancellation of examination results.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, first Registrar, first Finance Officer, and nominates members for the first Court, Executive Council, Planning Board, and Academic Council. The Executive Council appoints Pro-Vice-Chancellors, the Registrar, the Finance Officer, Professors, Readers, Lecturers, other academic staff, Principals of Colleges/Institutions, administrative/ministerial/other posts, Proctors, and the Librarian. The Vice-Chancellor appoints Deans of Schools and makes temporary appointments for vacant posts.

applies_to: Persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class.
Colleges situated in the districts of Cachar, Karimganj, North Cachar Hills, Karbi Anglong and Hailakandi.
Employees and students of the University or of a College or Institution maintained by or admitted to its privileges.
exemptions: Special provisions for the employment or admission of women, physically handicapped, weaker sections of society, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Section 7 proviso).

Colleges and Institutions maintained by Government are exempt from certain rules regarding the constitution of their Governing Body and appointment procedures for teaching and administrative staff (Statute 33).
special_provisions: Special provisions for the employment or admission of women, physically handicapped, weaker sections, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Section 7).
Transitional provisions for initial appointments and constitution of authorities for a specified term (Section 43).
Provision for students of Gauhati University or Dibrugarh University to complete their courses if their colleges become affiliated to Assam University (Section 44).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Parliament enacts the Act. The Visitor has powers to make or direct the making of Statutes. The Executive Council is empowered to make Statutes and Ordinances. The Academic Council proposes Ordinances and makes Regulations. Other authorities of the University may make Regulations. The Central Government can issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is primarily through the Visitor's powers of review, inspection, inquiry, and issuing binding directions. The Vice-Chancellor, as the principal executive and academic officer, supervises and controls University affairs. The Executive Council manages administration, finances, and discipline. The Registrar and Finance Officer have specific duties related to records, correspondence, examinations, and financial oversight. Disputes concerning employee contracts and student disciplinary actions are subject to arbitration tribunals. Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations are published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament for oversight.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the detailed Statutes of the University, covering the appointment, powers, and duties of officers (Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, Deans, Heads of Departments, Proctors, Librarian), the constitution and functions of various authorities (Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Planning Board, Finance Committee, Boards of Schools, Selection Committees), conditions of service for employees, procedures for removal of employees, conferment and withdrawal of honorary degrees and academic distinctions, maintenance of discipline among students, admission of colleges to university privileges, convocations, resignation, disqualifications for membership, and procedures for making Ordinances and Regulations.

act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws pertaining to railways. Its primary objective is to regulate the construction, maintenance, operation, and safety of railways, as well as the carriage of passengers and goods, and to establish authorities for rate fixation and safety oversight.
