key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter XV details various offences and penalties. These include: fraudulently travelling without proper pass/ticket (imprisonment up to 6 months, fine up to 1000 rupees); levy of excess charge for travelling without proper pass/ticket (excess charge plus fare, or 250 rupees, with potential imprisonment for non-payment); needlessly interfering with means of communication (imprisonment up to 1 year, fine up to 1000 rupees); unauthorised business of procuring/supplying tickets (imprisonment up to 3 years, fine up to 10,000 rupees); hawking or begging (imprisonment up to 1 year, fine up to 2000 rupees); drunkenness or nuisance (imprisonment up to 6 months, fine up to 500 rupees); obstructing railway servant (imprisonment up to 6 months, fine up to 1000 rupees); trespass (imprisonment up to 6 months, fine up to 1000 rupees); making false statements/claims for compensation (imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both); maliciously wrecking or attempting to wreck a train (imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, or death/life imprisonment if death is caused); damage to railway properties (imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both); endangering safety of persons (imprisonment up to 5 years for wilful act, up to 1 year for rash/negligent act); travelling on roof/step/engine (imprisonment up to 3 months, fine up to 500 rupees); opening or breaking a level crossing gate (imprisonment up to 3-5 years); negligently crossing unmanned level crossing (imprisonment up to 1 year); unlawfully bringing dangerous goods (imprisonment up to 3 years, fine up to 1000 rupees); smoking (fine up to 100 rupees); intoxication of railway servant (fine up to 500 rupees, or imprisonment up to 1 year if safety endangered); abandoning train without authority (imprisonment up to 2 years, fine up to 1000 rupees); obstructing running of train (imprisonment up to 2 years, fine up to 2000 rupees); false returns/reports by railway servants (imprisonment up to 1-2 years, fine up to 500-1000 rupees).

act_identification.act_title: THE SCHEDULED CASTES AND THE SCHEDULED TRIBES (PREVENTION OF ATROCITIES) ACT, 1989
act_identification.act_short_title: Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989

act_overview.preamble: An Act to prevent the commission of offences of atrocities against the members of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes, to provide for Special Courts and the Exclusive Special Courts for the trial of such offences and for the relief and rehabilitation of the victims of such offences and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to prevent atrocities against members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. It establishes Special Courts for the speedy trial of such offenses and provides for the relief and rehabilitation of victims.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.description: Empowers Special Courts to order externment of persons likely to commit offenses under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes.

powers_conferred: State Government to confer powers on officers for prevention and coping with offenses (Section 9)
State Government to establish Special Courts and Exclusive Special Courts (Section 14)
State Government to specify Public Prosecutors or appoint advocates as Special Public Prosecutors (Section 15)

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 3(1) details various acts of atrocity by non-SC/ST members, punishable with imprisonment from six months to five years and fine. Section 3(2) specifies penalties for false evidence (including life imprisonment or death penalty if execution occurs), mischief by fire/explosive (including life imprisonment), IPC offenses with imprisonment of ten years or more against SC/ST persons/property (life imprisonment and fine), and offenses listed in the Schedule (punishment as per IPC and fine). Public servants committing offenses under Section 3 face imprisonment not less than one year. Section 4 prescribes punishment for public servants neglecting duties (six months to one year imprisonment). Section 5 mandates enhanced punishment for subsequent convictions (not less than one year imprisonment). Section 13 imposes imprisonment up to one year and fine for non-compliance with externment orders.

Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 (25 of 2013)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government has the power to specify a Public Prosecutor or appoint an advocate as a Special Public Prosecutor or Exclusive Special Public Prosecutor for Special Courts and Exclusive Special Courts.

applies_to: members of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (as victims)
persons not being a member of a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe (as offenders)
public servant (as offenders for neglect of duty or committing atrocities)
exemptions: Action taken in discharge of a public duty (from forcing a member of SC/ST to leave residence under Section 3(1)(z))
Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (anticipatory bail) does not apply to offenses under this Act
Section 360 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and the provisions of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 do not apply to persons above eighteen years found guilty of an offense under this Act
special_provisions: Special provisions for 'Scheduled Areas' or 'tribal areas' regarding externment orders (Section 10(1))
Special provisions for Districts with fewer cases, allowing the Court of Session to be specified as a Special Court (Section 14 proviso)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through investigation by police officers, trial by Special Courts and Exclusive Special Courts, and appeals to the High Court. State Governments are mandated to ensure effective implementation through measures like providing legal aid, covering witness expenses, victim rehabilitation, appointing prosecution officers, setting up committees, conducting periodic surveys, and identifying atrocity-prone areas. The Central Government coordinates these measures and reports to Parliament annually. Magistrates and police officers can take preventive action.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Special Court, Exclusive Special Court, High Court

schedules_summary.description: Lists specific sections from the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and their corresponding offenses and punishments. The listed offenses include criminal conspiracy, unlawful assembly, rioting, hurt, grievous hurt, various sexual offenses, criminal trespass, criminal intimidation, and insulting the modesty of a woman.

act_identification.act_title: THE SMALL INDUSTRIES DEVELOPMENT BANK OF INDIA ACT, 1989

act_overview.preamble: An Act to constitute a National Commission for Women and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the National Commission for Women. Its purpose is to empower this Commission to investigate matters relating to safeguards for women, review laws affecting women, address violations of women's rights, and advise the government on policies concerning women.

Commission to exercise powers and perform functions assigned under the Act.
Commission to appoint committees for special issues.
Commission to regulate its own procedure and that of its committees.
Commission to investigate and examine matters relating to safeguards for women.
Commission to present annual and other reports to the Central Government.
Commission to make recommendations for effective implementation of safeguards.
Commission to review existing laws affecting women and recommend amendments.
Commission to take up cases of violation of women's rights with appropriate authorities.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to enable certain special powers to be conferred upon members of the armed forces in the disturbed areas in the State of Jammu and Kashmir*.
act_overview.purpose: This Act enables the conferment of special powers upon members of the armed forces in disturbed areas within the State of Jammu and Kashmir. Its primary objective is to maintain public order and counter activities involving terrorist acts or those challenging India's sovereignty and territorial integrity. It grants armed forces personnel powers such as using force, making arrests without warrant, and conducting searches.

key_sections.title: Arrested persons and seized property to be made over to the police.

key_sections.title: Protection of persons acting in good faith under this Act.
key_sections.description: Provides immunity from prosecution, suit, or other legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act, subject to previous sanction of the Central Government.

Corporation may appoint such committees as may be necessary for the efficient performance, exercise and discharge of its functions, powers and duties.

Central Government may require the Corporation to furnish such information as that Government may consider necessary.
President may by notification supersede the Board for such period not exceeding six months as may be specified in the notification.

Corporation may, by general or special order, delegate to the Chairman or any other Member or to any officer of the Corporation, subject to such conditions and limitations, if any, as may be specified therein, such of its powers and duties under this Act as it may deem fit.
Central Government may, by notification, make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act.
Corporation may, by notification, make regulations not inconsistent with this Act and the rules made thereunder for enabling it to perform its functions under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE PUBLIC LIABILITY INSURANCE ACT, 1991

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for public liability insurance for the purpose of providing immediate relief to the persons affected by accident occurring while handling any hazardous substance and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: To establish a system of public liability insurance to provide immediate relief to individuals affected by accidents involving hazardous substances. It also covers related matters concerning the handling of such substances.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'accident', 'hazardous substance', and 'owner'.

key_sections.title: Liability to give relief in certain cases on principle of no fault.
key_sections.description: Establishes the owner's liability to provide relief for death, injury, or property damage from accidents involving hazardous substances, based on the principle of no-fault.

key_sections.title: Duty of owner to take out insurance policies.
key_sections.description: Mandates owners of undertakings handling hazardous substances to obtain insurance policies to cover their liability for relief, and specifies policy amounts and contributions to the Relief Fund.

key_sections.title: Application for claim for relief.
key_sections.description: Outlines who can make a claim for relief, the procedure for application to the Collector, and the time limit for filing claims.

key_sections.title: Award of relief.
key_sections.description: Details the Collector's process for inquiring into claims, making awards, and the payment mechanism involving insurers, the Relief Fund, and owners.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Environmental Relief Fund.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of an Environmental Relief Fund by the Central Government, specifying its sources of credit and utilization for relief payments.

key_sections.title: Power to give directions.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to issue directions to owners or other entities for the purposes of the Act, including regulating hazardous substance handling.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for owners who contravene provisions related to taking out insurance policies.

key_sections.title: Penalty for non-compliance of directions.
key_sections.description: Specifies penalties for non-compliance with directions issued under the Act, or for obstructing authorized persons.

key_sections.title: Adjudicating officer.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint adjudicating officers to determine and impose penalties for contraventions.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Allows aggrieved persons to appeal orders of the adjudicating officer to the National Green Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Offence for failure to pay penalty or additional penalty.
key_sections.description: Defines the failure to pay penalties as an offence, punishable with imprisonment or fine, or both.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint commencement date, specify quantity of hazardous substance, exempt owners from insurance, establish Environmental Relief Fund, make scheme for Relief Fund, authorise persons for information, authorise persons for entry/inspection, authorise persons for search/seizure, give directions, make application to Courts for restraining owners, appoint adjudicating officers, delegate powers, constitute Advisory Committee, make rules.
Collector: Verify and publish accident, receive applications for claim, hold inquiry and make award, exercise powers of Civil Court, grant temporary injunction.
Adjudicating Officer: Determine and impose penalties, summon and enforce attendance.
National Green Tribunal: Hear appeals against adjudicating officer's orders.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 14 prescribes penalties for contravention of insurance policy requirements, including an amount equal to the annual premium, potentially doubled, and additional penalties for continued contravention. Section 15 imposes penalties for non-compliance with directions, obstruction of officials, ranging from ten thousand rupees up to fifteen lakh rupees, with additional daily penalties for continued non-compliance. Section 17 outlines penalties for contravention by Government Departments, making the Head of Department or other officers liable to a penalty equal to one month of their basic salary. Section 17B makes failure to pay penalties an offence punishable with imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to fifteen lakh rupees, or both.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Collector verifies accidents, invites claims, holds inquiries, and makes awards. Insurers and owners are required to deposit award amounts, with unpaid amounts recoverable as arrears of land revenue. The Central Government can call for information, conduct entry/inspection, search/seizure, and issue directions. It can also apply to courts to restrain owners. Penalties are imposed by adjudicating officers, with appeals to the National Green Tribunal. Failure to pay penalties constitutes an offence.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts not inferior to a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate first class (for restraining orders), National Green Tribunal (for appeals), and Civil Courts (for Collector's powers).

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement dates of the Act.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to the religious character of certain places of worship and bar of jurisdiction of courts, etc.
key_sections.description: Declares that the religious character of a place of worship existing on August 15, 1947, shall remain the same, and bars courts from entertaining suits regarding conversion, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Act to override other enactments.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_sections.title: [Repealed.]

Any suit, appeal or other proceeding, with respect to any matter referred to in sub-section (2) of Section 4, finally decided, settled or disposed of by a court, tribunal or other authority before the commencement of this Act.
Any dispute with respect to any such matter settled by the parties amongst themselves before such commencement.
Any conversion of any such place effected before such commencement by acquiescence.

implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts, tribunals, or other authorities as per Section 4(2).

act_identification.act_title: THE REMITTANCES OF FOREIGN EXCHANGE AND INVESTMENT IN FOREIGN EXCHANGE BONDS (IMMUNITIES AND EXEMPTIONS) ACT, 1991
act_identification.act_short_title: The Remittances of Foreign Exchange and Investment in Foreign Exchange Bonds (Immunities and Exemptions) Act, 1991.

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Forty-second Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for certain immunities to persons receiving remittances in foregin exchange and to persons owning the Foreign Exchange Bonds and for certain exemptions from direct taxes in relation to such remittances and bonds and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS the position relating to balance of payments has become difficult and it is necessary to attract large inflow of foreign exchange; AND WHEREAS with a view to attracting such inflow of foreign exchange, it is expedient to provide for certain immunities and exemptions to render it possible for certain persons to receive the said remittances in foreign exchange and to own the said Bonds;
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to attract foreign exchange inflow into India by providing immunities and exemptions to individuals receiving foreign exchange remittances and those investing in Foreign Exchange Bonds. It seeks to address the difficult balance of payments situation by encouraging such financial inflows.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its geographical applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms for Chapter II, including 'recipient' and 'remittance'.

key_sections.title: Immunities.
key_sections.description: Grants immunities to recipients of foreign exchange remittances, protecting them from disclosure requirements and inquiries regarding the source of funds, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Remittances not to be taken into account in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Specifies that remittances are not considered for Income-tax or Wealth-tax purposes, with an explanation regarding income from remittances.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms for Chapter III, including 'Foreign Exchange Bonds', 'non-resident Indian', and 'overseas corporate body'.

key_sections.title: Immunities.
key_sections.description: Grants immunities to owners of Foreign Exchange Bonds (non-resident Indians or overseas corporate bodies) and their Indian gift recipients, protecting them from disclosure and inquiries regarding investment source, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Foreign Exchange Bonds not to be taken into account in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Specifies that provisions of Income-tax, Wealth-tax, and Gift-tax Acts do not apply to interest from, ownership of, or gifts of Foreign Exchange Bonds in certain cases.

powers_conferred: Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify in this behalf (later date for specified date)
Reserve Bank of India may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify for the purposes of receiving remittances (scheme for remittances)
Central Government shall cause the scheme notified under clause (a) of sub-section (1) to be laid, as soon as may be after it is notified, before each House of Parliament.

related_acts: State Bank of India Act, 1955 (28 of 1955)
Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (61 of 1985)
Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, 1987 (28 of 1987)

applies_to: persons receiving remittances in foreign exchange (recipient)
persons owning the Foreign Exchange Bonds (non-resident Indian or overseas corporate body)
person resident in India to whom a gift of such Bonds has been made by such non-resident Indian or overseas corporate body
exemptions: Immunities do not apply to foreign exchange required to be brought into India under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973 or the Income-tax Act, 1961 read with the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973, if the period for bringing it in has not expired.

Immunities do not apply to prosecution for any offence punishable under Chapter IX or Chapter XVII of the Indian Penal Code, the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, 1987, the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 or for the purpose of enforcement of any civil liability.
Nationals of Pakistan or Bangladesh shall not be deemed to be of Indian origin.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government, Reserve Bank of India

act_identification.act_title: THE GOVERNMENT OF NATIONAL CAPITAL TERRITORY OF DELHI ACT, 1991
act_identification.act_short_title: the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi Act, 1991

act_overview.preamble: An Act to supplement the provisions of the Constitution relating to the Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers for the National Capital Territory of Delhi and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers for the National Capital Territory of Delhi. It supplements constitutional provisions and addresses related matters for the governance of Delhi.

chapter_titles: CERTAIN PROVISIONS RELATING TO LIEUTENANT GOVERNOR AND MINISTERS
PROVISIONS RELATING TO THE MAINTENANCE OF THE DEMOCRATIC AND ADMINISTRATIVE BALANCE IN THE GOVERNANCE OF NATIONAL CAPITAL TERRITORY OF DELHI

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on dates appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Capital', 'Legislative Assembly', and 'Lieutenant Governor'.

key_sections.title: Legislative Assembly and its composition.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Legislative Assembly for Delhi, its total number of seats, and provisions for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes.

key_sections.title: Disqualifications for membership.
key_sections.description: Outlines conditions under which a person is disqualified from being a member of the Legislative Assembly, including holding an office of profit.

key_sections.title: Disqualification on ground of defection.
key_sections.description: Applies the provisions of the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution regarding disqualification on grounds of defection to members of the Legislative Assembly.

key_sections.title: Assent to Bills.
key_sections.description: Details the process for Bills passed by the Legislative Assembly to receive assent from the Lieutenant Governor or be reserved for the President's consideration.

key_sections.title: Annual financial statement.
key_sections.description: Requires the Lieutenant Governor to lay an annual financial statement (budget) before the Legislative Assembly, detailing estimated receipts and expenditure.

key_sections.title: Rules of procedure.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Legislative Assembly to make rules for regulating its procedure and business, with certain restrictions and provisions for rules made by the Lieutenant Governor.

key_sections.title: Matters in which Lieutenant Governor to act in his sole discretion.
key_sections.description: Specifies matters where the Lieutenant Governor acts in his sole discretion, including those outside the Assembly's purview or where required by law.

key_sections.title: Conduct of business.
key_sections.description: Mandates the President to make rules for the allocation and convenient transaction of business with Ministers, and states that executive action is taken in the Lieutenant Governor's name.

key_sections.title: Constitution of National Capital Civil Service Authority.
key_sections.description: Establishes the National Capital Civil Service Authority and defines its composition, including the Chief Minister, Chief Secretary, and Principal Home Secretary.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Authority.
key_sections.description: Grants the National Capital Civil Service Authority responsibility for recommending transfers, postings, and vigilance matters for Group 'A' officers and DANICS to the Lieutenant Governor.

key_sections.title: Consolidated Fund of the Capital.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Consolidated Fund of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, into which all revenues, grants, and loans are credited.

key_sections.title: Relation of Lieutenant Governor and his Ministers to President.
key_sections.description: States that the Lieutenant Governor and his Council of Ministers are under the general control of, and must comply with directions from, the President.

key_sections.title: Power of President to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the President power to make orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, particularly concerning the constitution of the Legislative Assembly.

powers_conferred: Legislative Assembly: To make laws (subject to restrictions), fix salaries and allowances of members, make rules for its procedure and conduct of business.

Lieutenant Governor: To summon, prorogue, and dissolve the Legislative Assembly; address and send messages to the Assembly; assent to Bills or reserve them for the President; recommend financial Bills; authorize expenditure; make rules (with President's approval) for financial matters and authentication of orders; act in sole discretion in specified matters; administer oaths to Ministers.

President: To extend the duration of the Legislative Assembly during an emergency; approve rules made by the Lieutenant Governor; make rules for the conduct of business with Ministers; remove difficulties in implementing the Act; authorize expenditure when the Assembly is dissolved or suspended.

Central Government: To appoint commencement dates for provisions of the Act; make rules under Part IV-A; determine the nature and categories of officers and employees for the National Capital Civil Service Authority.
Election Commission: To delimit constituencies and maintain delimitation orders up-to-date.

National Capital Civil Service Authority: To recommend transfers, postings, and vigilance matters for Group 'A' officers and DANICS to the Lieutenant Governor; recommend panels for constitution/appointment/nomination by the Lieutenant Governor for bodies established under laws made by the Legislative Assembly.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 17 prescribes a penalty of five hundred rupees for any person who sits or votes as a member of the Legislative Assembly before making an oath or affirmation, or when not qualified or disqualified.

repealed_acts: The Delhi Administration Act, 1966 (Act 19 of 1966)
related_acts: Representation of the People Act, 1951 (43 of 1951)
Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)
Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965
Delegation of the Financial Powers Rules, 1978

authorities_established: Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chief Secretary. The Lieutenant Governor appoints persons to administer oaths to members and determines salaries/allowances of Speaker/Deputy Speaker/Ministers (with President's approval). The Legislative Assembly chooses its Speaker and Deputy Speaker. The President appoints the administrator (Lieutenant Governor) and approves rules. The National Capital Civil Service Authority recommends panels for appointments by the Lieutenant Governor.

applies_to: National Capital Territory of Delhi
Members of the Legislative Assembly
Ministers of the National Capital Territory of Delhi
Officers and employees serving in the affairs of the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi
exemptions: Property of the Union is exempted from all taxes imposed by or under any law made by the Legislative Assembly or other law in force in the Capital, with a proviso for pre-Constitution taxes.

Officers serving in connection with specific subject matters (Entries 1, 2, and 18 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, and related entries 64, 65, 66) are excluded from certain provisions of Part IV-A regarding Group 'A', 'B', 'C' officials and the Authority's powers.
special_provisions: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes in the Legislative Assembly.
Special provisions regarding financial Bills, requiring the Lieutenant Governor's recommendation for introduction or consideration.
The Lieutenant Governor delivers a special address at the commencement of the first session after each general election and the first session of each year.
The Lieutenant Governor is required to act in his sole discretion in matters outside the Legislative Assembly's purview, or where required by law, or in discharge of functions under Part IV-A.
The duration of the Legislative Assembly may be extended by the President during a Proclamation of Emergency.
The provisions of the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution regarding disqualification on ground of defection apply to members of the Legislative Assembly.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Legislative Assembly may make rules for its procedure and business. The Lieutenant Governor may make rules for the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, form of accounts (with President's approval), and authentication of orders. The President makes rules for the allocation and conduct of business with Ministers. The Central Government may make rules for carrying out the provisions of Part IV-A.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the legislative process of the Legislative Assembly, the executive actions of the Lieutenant Governor and Council of Ministers, and the functions of established authorities like the Election Commission and the National Capital Civil Service Authority. Financial provisions are enforced through appropriation bills and audit reports. Disqualification provisions are enforced by the President based on the Election Commission's opinion or by the Speaker.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts are restricted from inquiring into the proceedings of the Legislative Assembly or the validity of orders authenticated in the Lieutenant Governor's name. The question of advice tendered by Ministers is not to be inquired into by any court. The Act mentions the High Court in relation to derogation of its powers and the Supreme Court of India in the context of matters affecting relations with it.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the forms of oaths or affirmations to be made by candidates for election to the Legislative Assembly, members of the Legislative Assembly, and members of the Council of Ministers (oath of office and oath of secrecy).

act_identification.act_title: THE DESTRUCTIVE INSECTS AND PESTS (AMENDMENT AND VALIDATION) ACT, 1992
act_identification.act_short_title: The Destructive Insects and Pests (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1992

act_overview.preamble: An Act further to amend the Destructive Insects and Pests Act, 1914.
act_overview.purpose: This Act further amends the Destructive Insects and Pests Act, 1914, and validates a notification and fees levied or collected for import, inspection, fumigation, disinfection, disinfestation, or supervision of articles or insects under the principal Act.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its deemed date of commencement.

key_sections.title: Amendment of section 3 of Act 2 of 1914.
key_sections.description: Originally amended section 3 of the principal Act, but was later repealed.

key_sections.title: Validation.
key_sections.description: Validates a specific notification and any fees levied or collected under the principal Act, overriding any court judgments, and provides for recovery of uncollected fees and clarifies rights regarding refunds.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Destructive Insects and Pests (Amendment and Validation) Ordinance, 1992, and saves actions taken under it.

powers_conferred: Power to levy or collect fees for making an application for a permit to import, or for making inspection, fumigation, disinfection, disinfestation or supervision of, any article or class of articles or any insect or class of insects under the principal Act.
Power to recover fees levied or purported to have been levied but not collected.

amended_acts: the Destructive Insects and Pests Act, 1914
repealed_acts: The Destructive Insects and Pests (Amendment and Validation) Ordinance, 1992 (Ord. 4 of 1992)

applies_to: Persons involved in the import of articles or insects, or subject to inspection, fumigation, disinfection, disinfestation, or supervision under the Destructive Insects and Pests Act, 1914.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Validation of past actions and fees, and provisions for recovery of uncollected fees under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE BOARD OF INDIA ACT, 1992
act_identification.act_short_title: The Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Board to protect the interests of investors in securities and to promote the development of, and to regulate, the securities market and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to safeguard the interests of investors in securities. It aims to promote the orderly development and regulation of the securities market, addressing matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II ESTABLISHMENT OF THE SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE BOARD OF INDIA
CHAPTER III TRANSFER OF ASSETS, LIABILITIES, ETC., OF THE EXISTING SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE BOARD TO THE BOARD
CHAPTER IV POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE BOARD
CHAPTER VA PROHIBITION OF MANIPULATIVE AND DECEPTIVE DEVICES, INSIDER TRADING AND SUBSTANTIAL ACQUISITION OF SECURITIES OR CONTROL
CHAPTER VI FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT
CHAPTER VIB ESTABLISHMENT, JURISDICTION, AUTHORITY AND PROCEDURE OF APPELLATE TRIBUNAL

key_definitions: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its application to the whole of India, and its deemed commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Board', 'Chairman', 'collective investment scheme', and 'securities'.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Board.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment and incorporation of the Securities and Exchange Board of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

key_sections.title: Management of the Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the composition of the Board, including the Chairman and other members, and vests general superintendence, direction, and management of affairs in the Board.

key_sections.title: Functions of Board.
key_sections.description: Details the duties and functions of the Board, including protecting investors, promoting market development, regulating securities markets, and prohibiting fraudulent practices.

key_sections.title: Board to regulate or prohibit issue of prospectus, offer document or advertisement soliciting money for issue of securities.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Board to regulate or prohibit the issue of prospectuses, offer documents, or advertisements for soliciting money for securities, for investor protection.

key_sections.title: Power to issue directions and levy penalty.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board power to issue directions to persons associated with the securities market and levy penalties to protect investors and ensure orderly market development.

key_sections.title: Investigation.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Board to direct investigations into the affairs of intermediaries or persons associated with the securities market if there are reasonable grounds to believe violations or detrimental transactions.

key_sections.title: Registration of stock-brokers, sub-brokers, share transfer agents, etc.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration with the Board for various intermediaries in the securities market, such as stock-brokers, sub-brokers, and share transfer agents.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of manipulative and deceptive devices, insider trading and substantial acquisition of securities or control.
key_sections.description: Prohibits persons from engaging in manipulative or deceptive devices, insider trading, or substantial acquisition of securities or control in contravention of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to adjudicate.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Board to appoint adjudicating officers to conduct inquiries and impose penalties for contraventions of specified sections of the Act.

key_sections.title: Factors to be taken into account while adjudging quantum of penalty.
key_sections.description: Specifies the factors that the Board or adjudicating officer must consider when determining the quantum of penalty, such as disproportionate gain, loss to investors, and repetitive nature of default.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Securities Appellate Tribunals.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of Securities Appellate Tribunals to exercise jurisdiction, powers, and authority conferred by the Act or other laws.

key_sections.title: Appeal to the Securities Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Allows any person aggrieved by an order of the Board or an adjudicating officer to prefer an appeal to the Securities Appellate Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Offences.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for contraventions or attempts to contravene the provisions of the Act or rules/regulations made thereunder.

key_sections.title: Recovery of amounts.
key_sections.description: Outlines the mechanism for the Recovery Officer to recover penalties, refund monies, disgorgement orders, or fees due to the Board through various modes.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Board to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Board: Establish and incorporate (Sec 3)
Board: Manage affairs (Sec 4)
Board: Appoint officers and employees (Sec 9)
Board: Protect investors, promote development, and regulate the securities market (Sec 11)
Board: Regulate or prohibit issue of prospectus, offer document or advertisement soliciting money for issue of securities (Sec 11A)
Board: Issue directions and levy penalty (Sec 11B)
Board: Conduct investigations (Sec 11C)
Board: Initiate cease and desist proceedings (Sec 11D)

Board: Register stock-brokers, sub-brokers, share transfer agents, depositories, foreign institutional investors, credit rating agencies, venture capital funds, collective investment schemes, alternative investment funds, and business trusts (Sec 12)
Board: Make regulations (Sec 30)
Central Government: Issue directions on policy to the Board (Sec 16)
Central Government: Supersede the Board under certain circumstances (Sec 17)
Central Government: Make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Sec 29)
Central Government: Establish or designate Special Courts (Sec 26A)
Adjudicating Officer: Adjudicate and impose penalties (Sec 15-I)
Securities Appellate Tribunal: Hear appeals against orders of the Board or adjudicating officers (Sec 15T)
Securities Appellate Tribunal: Regulate its own procedure and exercise powers of a civil court (Sec 15U)
Recovery Officer: Recover amounts due to the Board (Sec 28A)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes various penalties for contraventions. For failure to furnish information, return, redress grievances, or defaults by mutual funds, asset management companies, investment funds, investment advisers, research analysts, and stock brokers, penalties range from not less than one lakh rupees up to one crore rupees, or one lakh rupees per day of default, or five times the amount of brokerage, or three times the amount of gains, whichever is higher. For insider trading, fraudulent and unfair trade practices, non-disclosure of acquisition of shares and takeovers, and alteration/destruction of records, penalties range from not less than five lakh or ten lakh rupees up to twenty-five crore rupees or three times the amount of profits made. General offences under Section 24 can lead to imprisonment up to ten years, or a fine up to twenty-five crore rupees, or both. Failure to pay penalties or comply with directions can also result in imprisonment from one month to ten years, or a fine up to twenty-five crore rupees, or both.

repealed_acts: The Securities and Exchange Board of India Ordinance, 1992 (Ord. 5 of 1992)
Section 33
THE SCHEDULE
related_acts: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999 (41 of 1999)
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 2013 (23 of 2013)
Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (19 of 1952)
Cost and Works Accountants Act, 1959 (23 of 1959)
International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019

authorities_established: Securities and Exchange Board of India
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairman and members of the Board, the Presiding Officer and Judicial Members of the Securities Appellate Tribunal (in consultation with the Chief Justice of India or his nominee), and judges of Special Courts (with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court). Technical Members of the Securities Appellate Tribunal are appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of a Search-cum-Selection Committee.
regulatory_bodies: Securities and Exchange Board of India
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority

applies_to: Whole of India

Stock-brokers, sub-brokers, share transfer agents, bankers to an issue, trustees of trust deeds, registrars to an issue, merchant bankers, underwriters, portfolio managers, investment advisers, depositories, participants, custodians of securities, foreign institutional investors, credit rating agencies, venture capital funds, collective investment schemes, mutual funds, alternative investment funds, business trusts, investment advisers, research analysts
Companies issuing or dealing in securities
exemptions: Certain schemes or arrangements are not considered collective investment schemes, including those made by cooperative societies, deposits accepted by non-banking financial companies, insurance contracts, provident fund schemes, deposits under section 58A of the Companies Act, 1956, deposits accepted by Nidhi/Mutual Benefit Societies, chit business, and subscriptions to mutual funds (Sec 11AA(3)).
The Board's powers do not extend to an International Financial Services Centre (Sec 28C).
special_provisions: Provisions for the transfer of assets, liabilities, etc., of the existing Securities and Exchange Board to the newly established Board (Sec 10).

Special measures and powers for the Board concerning listed public companies or public companies intending to get their securities listed, particularly regarding insider trading or fraudulent practices (Sec 11(2A), 11(4) proviso, 11C(9) proviso, 11D proviso).
Establishment of Special Courts for speedy trial of offences under the Act (Sec 26A-26E).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), which has powers to regulate, investigate, issue directions, and levy penalties. Adjudicating Officers are appointed by the Board to conduct inquiries and impose penalties. Appeals against orders of the Board or adjudicating officers can be made to the Securities Appellate Tribunal, and further appeals to the Supreme Court. Recovery of amounts due to the Board is handled by a Recovery Officer. Offences under the Act are tried by Special Courts established by the Central Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Special Courts (Sec 26A, 26B), Court of Session (until Special Court is established) (Sec 26E), Supreme Court (for appeals from Securities Appellate Tribunal) (Sec 15Z). Civil courts are barred from jurisdiction in matters determinable by an adjudicating officer or the Securities Appellate Tribunal (Sec 15Y, 20A).

schedules_summary.description: This schedule was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 2001 (30 of 2001).

act_identification.act_title: THE CESS AND OTHER TAXES ON MINERALS (VALIDATION) ACT, 1992
act_identification.act_short_title: The Cess and Other Taxes on Minerals (Validation) Act, 1992

act_overview.preamble: An Act to validate the imposition and collection of cesses and certain other taxes on minerals under certain State laws.
act_overview.purpose: This Act validates the imposition and collection of cesses and other taxes on minerals under certain State laws, making such provisions and actions taken thereunder legally valid. It also repeals a related Ordinance and prevents suits for refund of taxes, with an exception for excess payments.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.

key_sections.title: Validation of certain State laws and actions taken and things done thereunder.

powers_conferred: Validation of powers exercised by State Governments to impose and collect cesses and other taxes on minerals under specified State laws.

repealed_acts: The Cess and Other Taxes on Minerals (Validation) Ordinance, 1992 (Ord. 7 of 1992)

The Karnataka (Mineral Rights) Tax Act, 1984 (Karnataka Act 32 of 1984)
The Madhya Pradesh Karadhan Adhiniyam, 1982 (M.P. Act 15 of 1982)
The Madhya Pradesh Upkar Adhiniyam, 1981 (M.P. Act 1 of 1982)

applies_to: Whole of India
State laws specified in the Schedule to this Act
Actions taken, things done, rules made, notifications issued, and cesses or other taxes on minerals realised under such laws
exemptions: Any person from claiming refund of any cess or tax paid by him in excess of the amount due from him under any such laws.
special_provisions: Validation of certain State laws and actions taken thereunder retrospectively.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Validation of past enforcement actions by State Governments under their respective laws.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No suit or other proceeding shall be maintained or continued in any court for the refund of the cesses or other taxes realised under any such laws, except for claims of excess payment.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR MINORITIES ACT, 1992
act_identification.act_short_title: The National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992

act_overview.preamble: An Act to constitute a National Commission for Minorities and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the National Commission for Minorities to safeguard the interests of minority communities, monitor their development, and address grievances. It outlines the Commission's constitution, powers, functions, and financial provisions.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Commission', 'Member', 'minority', and 'prescribed'.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the National Commission for Minorities.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to constitute the National Commission for Minorities and specifies its composition.

key_sections.title: Term of office and conditions of service of Chairperson and Members.
key_sections.description: Outlines the tenure, resignation process, and grounds for removal of the Chairperson and Members of the Commission.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Commission
key_sections.description: Details the various functions of the Commission, including evaluating development, monitoring safeguards, making recommendations, and looking into complaints regarding minorities.

key_sections.title: Grants by the Central Government.
key_sections.description: Provides for the Central Government to make grants to the Commission for the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Stipulates the maintenance of accounts by the Commission and their audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

key_sections.title: Chairperson, Members and staff of the Commission to be public servants.
key_sections.description: Declares the Chairperson, Members, and staff of the Commission as public servants under the Indian Penal Code.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, within a specified period.

powers_conferred: Central Government to constitute the National Commission for Minorities (Section 3)
Central Government to nominate Chairperson and Members (Section 3)
Central Government to remove Chairperson or Member (Section 4)
Central Government to provide Secretary and other officers/employees to the Commission (Section 5)
Commission to regulate its own procedure (Section 8)
Commission to perform functions related to minorities' development, safeguards, and complaints (Section 9)
Commission to have powers of a civil court for certain functions (Section 9(4))
Central Government to make grants to the Commission (Section 10)
Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions (Section 15)
Central Government to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act (Section 16)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government nominates the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and Members of the Commission. Central Government provides the Secretary and other officers and employees to the Commission.

applies_to: minority communities notified by the Central Government

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Commission performs its functions by evaluating progress, monitoring safeguards, making recommendations, looking into complaints, conducting studies, and submitting reports. The Central Government causes recommendations and reports to be laid before Parliament. The Commission has powers of a civil court for certain functions.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The Commission itself has powers of a civil court for specific matters under Section 9(4).

act_identification.act_title: THE FOREIGN TRADE (DEVELOPMENT AND REGULATION) ACT, 1992
act_identification.act_short_title: the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 1992

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the development and regulation of foreign trade by facilitating imports into, and augmenting exports from, India and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to develop and regulate foreign trade in India by facilitating imports and increasing exports. It also covers matters connected with or incidental to foreign trade.

chapter_titles: POWER OF CENTRAL GOVERNMENT TO MAKE ORDER AND ANNOUNCE FOREIGN TRADE POLICY
CONTROLS ON EXPORT OF SPECIFIED GOODS, SERVICES AND TECHNOLOGY

key_definitions: specified goods or services or technology

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement dates for different provisions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'import', 'export', 'licence', and 'Director General'.

key_sections.title: Powers to make provisions relating to imports and exports.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make provisions for the development and regulation of foreign trade, including prohibiting or restricting imports and exports.

key_sections.title: Foreign Trade Policy.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to formulate, announce, and amend the foreign trade policy from time to time.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Director General and his functions.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of the Director General of Foreign Trade and outlines their advisory and implementation functions regarding foreign trade policy.

key_sections.title: Importer-exporter Code Number.
key_sections.description: Mandates that no person shall make any import or export without an Importer-exporter Code Number granted by the Director General.

key_sections.title: Suspension and cancellation of Importer-exporter Code Number.
key_sections.description: Details the grounds and procedure for the Director General to suspend or cancel an Importer-exporter Code Number.

key_sections.title: Issue, suspension and cancellation of licence.
key_sections.description: Governs the levy of fees, issuance, renewal, refusal, suspension, and cancellation of import/export licenses and other financial benefits.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to impose quantitative restrictions.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to impose quantitative restrictions on imports if they cause or threaten serious injury to domestic industry.

key_sections.title: Power relating to search and seizure.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to empower persons to conduct searches, inspections, and seizures related to import and export activities.

key_sections.title: Contravention of provisions of this Act, rules, orders and foreign trade policy.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contraventions of the Act, rules, orders, or foreign trade policy, including fines and confiscation of goods.

key_sections.title: Controls on export of specified goods, services and technology.
key_sections.description: Establishes controls on the export of specified goods, services, and technology, linking them to the Weapons of Mass Destruction Act.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Provides for an appeal mechanism against decisions or orders made by the Adjudicating Authority.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, 1947, and the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Ordinance, 1992, with savings clauses.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To make provisions relating to imports and exports (Section 3).
Central Government: To formulate and announce foreign trade policy (Section 5).
Central Government: To appoint Director General of Foreign Trade (Section 6).
Central Government: To impose quantitative restrictions on imports (Section 9A).
Central Government: To authorize persons for search and seizure (Section 10).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act (Section 19).
Director General of Foreign Trade: To grant Importer-exporter Code Number (Section 7).
Director General of Foreign Trade: To suspend and cancel Importer-exporter Code Number (Section 8).
Director General of Foreign Trade: To issue, suspend, and cancel licences (Section 9).
Director General of Foreign Trade: To advise the Central Government in the formulation of foreign trade policy (Section 6).
Director General of Foreign Trade: To recover penalties (Section 11).
Adjudicating Authority: To impose penalties or adjudge confiscation (Section 13).
Adjudicating Authority: To determine settlement amounts (Section 11(4)).
Adjudicating Authority: To suspend Importer-exporter Code Number for non-payment of penalty (Section 11(7)).
Adjudicating Authority: To confiscate goods and conveyances (Section 11(8)).
Adjudicating Authority: To release confiscated items on payment of redemption charges (Section 11(9)).
Appellate Authority: To hear appeals against decisions or orders (Section 15).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of any provision of this Act, rules, orders, or foreign trade policy, or making false declarations, is liable to a penalty of not less than ten thousand rupees and not more than five times the value of the goods or services or technology. Goods and conveyances involved in contravention are liable to confiscation. For contraventions relating to specified goods, services, or technologies under Chapter IVA, penalties and imprisonment are in accordance with the Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, 2005.

repealed_acts: The Imports and Exports (Control) Act, 1947 (18 of 1947)
The Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Ordinance, 1992 (Ord. 11 of 1992)
related_acts: Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery System (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, 2005 (21 of 2005)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the Director General of Foreign Trade.

applies_to: Any person making import or export.
Service or technology providers availing benefits under the foreign trade policy or dealing with specified services or specified technologies.
exemptions: No permit or licence is necessary for import or export of any goods, nor are any goods prohibited, except as required under this Act or rules or orders made thereunder.

Quantitative restrictions shall not be imposed on goods originating from a developing country if its share of imports does not exceed three percent, or if the aggregate from multiple developing countries does not exceed nine percent.
special_provisions: The foreign trade policy may apply to goods, services, and technology in Special Economic Zones with specified exceptions, modifications, and adaptations.
Import and export in relation to Special Economic Zones or between two Special Economic Zones shall be governed by the Special Economic Zones Act, 2005.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through powers of search and seizure, imposition and recovery of penalties, confiscation of goods and conveyances, and an appeal and review process. Settlement of customs duty and interest as ordered by the Settlement Commission under the Central Excise Act, 1944, is deemed a settlement under this Act.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Authorities making adjudication or hearing appeals or exercising review powers under this Act have all the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and are deemed civil courts for purposes of sections 345 and 346 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. No court shall take cognizance of any offence under Chapter IVA without the previous sanction of the Central Government.

act_identification.act_title: THE SPECIAL COURT (TRIAL OF OFFENCES RELATING TO TRANSACTIONS IN SECURITIES) ACT, 1992
act_identification.act_short_title: the Special Court (Trial of Offences Relating to Transactions in Securities) Act, 1992

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Special Court for the trial of offences relating to transactions in securities and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes a Special Court for the trial of offences related to transactions in securities. It also provides for the appointment of a Custodian to attach and manage properties of persons involved in such offences, and outlines the jurisdiction and procedures of the Special Court.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Code', 'Custodian', 'securities', and 'Special Court'.

key_sections.title: Appointment and functions of Custodian.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint Custodians and outlines their functions, including notifying persons involved in securities offences and attaching their property.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Special Court.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to establish a Special Court and specifies the composition of its Judges.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of Special Court.
key_sections.description: Establishes the exclusive jurisdiction of the Special Court for prosecuting offences related to securities transactions and provides for transfer of pending cases.

key_sections.title: Procedure and powers of Special Court.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure to be followed by the Special Court for trials, equating it to a Court of Session, and grants it powers to pass sentences.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction, powers, authority and procedure of Special Court in civil matters.
key_sections.description: Confers civil jurisdiction, powers, and authority upon the Special Court concerning matters related to attached property and securities transactions, and outlines its procedure.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals from judgments, decrees, sentences, or orders of the Special Court directly to the Supreme Court.

key_sections.title: Discharge of liabilities.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Special Court to direct the Custodian for disposal of attached property and specifies the order of priority for discharging liabilities.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws or instruments.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Special Court (Trial of Offences Relating to Transactions in Securities) Ordinance, 1992, and includes savings provisions for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint Custodians (Section 3(1))
Central Government: Establish Special Court (Section 5(1))
Central Government: Make rules for carrying out provisions of the Act (Section 14(1))
Custodian: Notify names of persons involved in offences and attach their property (Section 3(2), 3(3))
Custodian: Deal with attached property as directed by the Special Court (Section 3(4))
Custodian: Cancel fraudulent contracts (Section 4(1))
Special Court: Take cognizance of and try cases (Section 6)
Special Court: Exercise exclusive jurisdiction over offences (Section 7)
Special Court: Try persons jointly (Section 8)
Special Court: Follow procedure prescribed by the Code of Criminal Procedure for warrant cases (Section 9(1))
Special Court: Act as a Court of Session and have all its powers (Section 9(2))
Special Court: Pass sentences authorized by law (Section 9(3))
Special Court: Adopt procedure consistent with natural justice in other matters (Section 9(4))
Special Court: Exercise civil jurisdiction, powers, and authority (Section 9A(1))
Special Court: Regulate its own procedure in civil matters (Section 9A(4))
Special Court: Have powers of a civil court for summoning, discovery, evidence, etc. (Section 9A(5))
Special Court: Have jurisdiction and powers of a Court under the Arbitration Act, 1940 (Section 9B(1))
Special Court: Direct the Custodian for disposal of property under attachment (Section 11(1))
Special Court: Punish for contempt (Section 11A)
Chief Justice of the High Court: Nominate sitting Judges for the Special Court (Section 5(2), 5(3))
Chief Justice of the High Court: Make provisions for distribution of cases amongst Judges of Special Court (Section 5A)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act deals with 'offence relating to transactions in securities' (Section 3(2)). The Special Court is empowered to pass 'any sentence authorised by law for the punishment of the offence' upon conviction (Section 9(3)).

amended_acts: Special Court (Trial of Offences Relating to Transactions in Securities) Amendment Act, 1994 (24 of 1994)
repealed_acts: The Special Court (Trial of Offences Relating to Transactions in Securities) Ordinance, 1992 (Ord. 10 of 1992)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government may appoint one or more Custodians. The Special Court Judges are nominated by the Chief Justice of the High Court with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of India.

applies_to: Any person involved in any offence relating to transactions in securities after 1st April, 1991 and on or before 6th June, 1992.
Matters or claims relating to any property standing attached under sub-section (3) of section 3.

Matters or claims arising out of transactions in securities entered into after 1st April, 1991, and on or before 6th June, 1992, in which a person notified under sub-section (2) of section 3 is involved.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Custodian is responsible for notifying persons involved in securities offences, attaching their property, and dealing with it as directed by the Special Court. The Special Court is established to try these offences and exercise civil jurisdiction over related matters, ensuring enforcement through judicial process and sentencing.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Special Court (for trials and civil matters), Supreme Court (for appeals)

act_identification.act_title: THE INDO-TIBETAN BORDER POLICE FORCE ACT, 1992

legislative_details.geographical_extent: any part of India as well as outside India, including the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed force of the Union for ensuring the security of the borders of India and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the constitution and regulation of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police Force, an armed force of the Union, to ensure the security of India's borders and perform other entrusted duties.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

chapter_titles: CONSTITUTION OF THE FORCE AND CONDITIONS OR SERVICE OF THE MEMBERS OF THE FORCE
EXECUTION OF SENTENCES, PARDONS, REMISSIONS, ETC.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Persons subject to this Act.
key_sections.description: Specifies who is subject to the Act and for how long.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Force.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Indo-Tibetan Border Police Force and its purpose.

key_sections.title: Offences in relation to the enemy or terrorist and punishable with death.
key_sections.description: Details severe offences related to the enemy or terrorists, punishable by death.

key_sections.title: Punishment awardable by Force Courts.
key_sections.description: Outlines the scale of punishments that can be inflicted by Force Courts.

key_sections.title: Kinds of Force Courts.
key_sections.description: Identifies the three types of Force Courts: General, Petty, and Summary.

key_sections.title: Choice between criminal court and Force Court.
key_sections.description: Grants discretion to senior officers to decide whether an offence should be tried by a criminal court or a Force Court.

key_sections.title: Finding and sentence not valid unless confirmed.
key_sections.description: States that findings and sentences of General and Petty Force Courts require confirmation to be valid.

key_sections.title: Pardon and remission.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government or Director-General to pardon, remit, mitigate, or commute punishments.

key_sections.title: Rank structure.
key_sections.description: Classifies the officers and other members of the Force according to their ranks.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Provisions as to existing Indo-Tibetan Border Police Force.
key_sections.description: Deems the existing ITBP Force and its members to be constituted and enrolled under this Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: entrust duties to the Force (Section 4), appoint Director-General and other officers (Section 5), dismiss or remove from service (Section 10), sanction for association/speech restrictions (Section 13), decide on social/recreational/religious nature of organizations (Section 13), order detention in lunatic asylum (Section 111), order release or transfer of lunatic accused (Section 114), order delivery of lunatic accused to relatives (Section 115), confirm findings and sentences of General Force Courts (Section 122), pardon, remit, mitigate, commute sentences, or release on parole (Section 142), cancel conditional pardon/release/remission (Section 143), suspend sentence of imprisonment (Section 144), make rules (Section 156), grant local rank (with confirmation) (Section 153), direct members of Force to exercise powers/duties under Central Act (Section 154), confer/impose powers/duties under State Act (Section 154), annul proceedings of Force Court (Section 132).

Director-General: command and supervision of the Force (Section 5), dismiss or remove from service or reduce rank (Section 11), revise decisions on complaints (Section 14), order withholding of pay/allowances of prisoner of war (Section 65), convene General Force Court (Section 77), decide between criminal court and Force Court trial (Section 92), pardon, remit, mitigate, commute sentences, or release on parole (Section 142), suspend sentence of imprisonment (Section 144), grant local rank (Section 153), annul proceedings of Force Court (Section 132).

Inspector-General: dismiss or remove from service or reduce rank (Section 11), proceed against officer of or below Commandant rank for punishment (Section 58), decide between criminal court and Force Court trial (Section 92).
Additional Director-General: dismiss or remove from service or reduce rank (Section 11), decide between criminal court and Force Court trial (Section 92).

Additional Deputy Inspector-General: dismiss or remove from service (Section 11), proceed against Subedar-Major or below for punishment (Section 58), decide between criminal court and Force Court trial (Section 92), confirm findings and sentences of Petty Force Court (Section 123), pardon, remit, mitigate, commute sentences, or release on parole (Section 142).

Commanding Officer: take care that person is not detained for more than 48 hours without investigation (Section 70), report detention beyond 48 hours (Section 70), make special report for delay in trial (Section 71), give information of desertion to civil authorities (Section 73), impose collective fine (Section 60), hold Summary Force Court (Section 82), tender pardon to accomplices (Section 119).

Force Courts: try any person for any offence (Section 84), pass any sentence authorized (Section 84), take judicial notice (Section 100), summon witnesses (Section 101), make orders for custody/disposal of property (Section 116, 117).

Force Police Officers: take charge of persons confined for any offence, preserve good order and discipline, prevent breaches (Section 75), arrest and detain for trial (Section 75), carry into effect punishment (Section 75).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines a wide range of offences, including those related to the enemy or terrorists (punishable by death or imprisonment up to 14 years), mutiny (death), desertion (death or imprisonment up to 7 years), absence without leave (imprisonment up to 3 years), striking or threatening superior officers (imprisonment up to 14 years), disobedience (imprisonment up to 14 years), insubordination and obstruction (imprisonment up to 10 years), false answers on enrolment (imprisonment up to 5 years), unbecoming or disgraceful conduct (dismissal or imprisonment up to 7 years), ill-treating subordinates (imprisonment up to 7 years), intoxication (imprisonment up to 6 months), permitting escape of persons in custody (imprisonment up to 10 years), irregularity in connection with arrest or confinement (imprisonment up to 1 year), escape from custody (imprisonment up to 3 years), offences in respect of property (imprisonment up to 10 years), extortion and exaction (imprisonment up to 10 years), making away with equipment (imprisonment up to 10 years), injury to property (imprisonment up to 10 years), false accusations (imprisonment up to 3 years), falsifying official documents and false declarations (imprisonment up to 10 years), signing in blank and failure to report (imprisonment up to 3 years), offences relating to Force Court (imprisonment up to 3 years), false evidence (imprisonment up to 7 years), unlawful detention of pay (imprisonment up to 5 years), violation of good order and discipline (imprisonment up to 7 years), miscellaneous offences (imprisonment up to 7 years), attempt (up to 14 years or half of original punishment), abetment (same as original offence or up to 14 years/half of original punishment), and civil offences (punishable as per law or imprisonment up to 7 years). Penalties awardable by Force Courts include death, imprisonment (life or lesser term), dismissal/removal from service, compulsory retirement, imprisonment in Force custody (up to 3 months), reduction in rank/grade, forfeiture of seniority/service, fine, severe reprimand/reprimand, forfeiture of pay/allowances, and stoppage of pay/allowances to make good loss. Minor punishments can be awarded by commanding officers without Force Courts, including imprisonment/detention/confinement to lines (up to 28 days), extra guards/duties, deprivation of special position/emoluments, severe reprimand/reprimand, fine (up to 14 days' pay), and deductions for loss/damage. Higher officers can award forfeiture of seniority/service, severe reprimand/reprimand, and deductions for loss/damage to officers of lower ranks.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Director-General, Additional Directors-General, Inspectors-General, Deputy Inspectors-General, Additional Deputy Inspectors-General, Commandants, and other officers, as well as Judge Attorney-General and other Judge Attorneys. The Director-General or any prescribed officer may appoint Force Police Officers.

applies_to: officers and subordinate officers
under-officers and other persons enrolled under this Act
Every person subject to this Act shall remain so subject until repatriated, retired, released, discharged, removed or dismissed from the Force
exemptions: A person subject to this Act who commits an offence of murder or culpable homicide not amounting to murder against, or of rape in relation to, a person not subject to this Act shall not be deemed to be guilty of an offence against this Act and shall not be tried by a Force Court, unless he commits any of the said offences— (a) while on active duty; or (b) at any place outside India; or (c) at any place specified by the Central Government by notification, in this behalf.
special_provisions: This Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act establishes a system of Force Courts (General, Petty, Summary) for the trial of offences and empowers various officers (e.g., commanding officers, Director-General) to award punishments or take disciplinary actions. It also outlines procedures for arrest, custody, and execution of sentences, including provisions for civil authorities' aid.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Force Courts and criminal courts

act_identification.act_title: THE REHABILITATION COUNCIL OF INDIA ACT, 1992

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution of the Rehabilitation Council of India for regulating [1][and monitoring the training of rehabilitation professionals and personnel, promoting research in rehabilitation and special education,] the maintenance of a Central Rehabilitation Register and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the constitution of the Rehabilitation Council of India. Its main purpose is to regulate and monitor the training of rehabilitation professionals and personnel, promote research in rehabilitation and special education, and maintain a Central Rehabilitation Register.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution and incorporation of Rehabilitation Council of India.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Rehabilitation Council of India as a body corporate and outlines its composition.

key_sections.title: Recognition of qualifications granted by University, etc., in India for rehabilitation professionals.
key_sections.description: Details the process for recognizing rehabilitation qualifications granted by Indian universities and institutions.

key_sections.title: Rights of persons possessing qualifications included in the Schedule to be enrolled.
