key_sections.description: Specifies the rights of registered rehabilitation professionals and restrictions on unregistered individuals, including penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Minimum standards of education.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Council to prescribe minimum standards of education for recognized rehabilitation qualifications.

key_sections.title: Registration in Register.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for registration of individuals in the Central Rehabilitation Register.

key_sections.title: Privileges of persons who are registered on Register.
key_sections.description: Grants registered persons the right to practice as rehabilitation professionals in India and recover fees.

key_sections.title: Professional conduct and removal of names from Register.
key_sections.description: Allows the Council to prescribe standards of professional conduct and remove names from the Register for misconduct.

key_sections.title: Register.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Member-Secretary to maintain and publish the Central Rehabilitation Register as a public document.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Council to make regulations for carrying out the purposes of the Act, with Central Government sanction.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint Chairperson and members of the Council (Section 3).
Central Government: To appoint the Member-Secretary of the Council (Section 8).
Central Government: To sanction employment of officers and employees by the Council and fix allowances/conditions of service (Section 8).
Central Government: To amend the Schedule to include or modify recognized qualifications (Section 11).
Central Government: To withdraw recognition of qualifications based on Council's representation (Section 17).
Central Government: To make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (Section 28).
Council: To constitute an Executive Committee and other committees (Section 7).
Council: To appoint Inspectors to inspect universities or institutions and recommend recognition of qualifications (Section 15).
Council: To appoint Visitors to inspect universities or institutions or attend examinations (Section 16).
Council: To prescribe minimum standards of education for recognized rehabilitation qualifications (Section 18).
Council: To prescribe standards of professional conduct and a code of ethics for rehabilitation professionals (Section 21).
Council: To order removal of names from the Register for specified reasons (Section 21).
Council: To make regulations to carry out the purposes of the Act, with previous sanction of the Central Government (Section 29).
Member-Secretary: To enter names in the Register upon application (Section 19).
Member-Secretary: To keep and maintain the Register, revise it, and publish it in the Official Gazette (Section 23).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person acting in contravention of sub-section (2) of Section 13 (practicing as a rehabilitation professional without recognized qualification and registration) shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

related_acts: Persons With Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 (1 of 1996)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson, certain members, and the Member-Secretary. The Council nominates members to the Executive Committee and appoints Inspectors and Visitors.

applies_to: rehabilitation professionals
persons with disabilities (indirectly, through services of professionals)
exemptions: Doctors or paramedics in physical medicine and rehabilitation, orthopaedics, ENT, ophthalmology or psychiatry, employed or working in hospitals owned or controlled by Central Government or a State Government or any other body funded by Central or State Government and notified by the Central Government, are exempt from certain restrictions under Section 13(2).
special_provisions: The Council shall register vocational instructors and other personnel working in vocational rehabilitation centres under the Ministry of Labour on recommendation of that Ministry and recognize such centres as manpower development centres.

The Council shall register personnel working in national institutes and apex institutions on disability under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment on recommendation of that Ministry and recognize such institutes as manpower development centres.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Council regulates professional standards, education, and registration. It appoints inspectors and visitors to monitor institutions. It can withdraw recognition of qualifications and remove names from the Register for professional misconduct. Contravention of professional practice rules can lead to imprisonment or fine. Courts can take cognizance of offences only upon a written complaint by a person authorized by the Council.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any court (for evidence as expert, Section 13(2)(d)); no court shall take cognizance of an offence under this Act except upon a complaint by the Council (Section 25).

schedules_summary.description: Lists recognized rehabilitation qualifications granted by Universities or Institutions in India, categorized by profession: Rehabilitation engineers/technicians, Audiologists and speech therapists, Teachers of special schools and integrated schools for the disabled, Multipurpose rehabilitation therapists technicians/assistant/worker, Vocational counsellors, and Diploma in communication disorders.

act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITY ACT, 1992

legislative_details.ministry_department: Central Government
legislative_details.geographical_extent: North-Eastern region comprising the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment and incorporation of a University for the North-Eastern region for the development of agriculture and for the furtherance of the advancement of learning and prosecution of research in agriculture and allied sciences in that region.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes and incorporates a Central Agricultural University for the North-Eastern region of India. Its main purpose is to foster the development of agriculture, advance learning, and promote research in agriculture and allied sciences within the specified region.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines various key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'agriculture', 'University', 'Statutes', and 'Ordinances'.

key_sections.title: The University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the 'Central Agricultural University' as a body corporate with perpetual succession and specifies its headquarters at Imphal, Manipur.

key_sections.title: Objects of the University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the University's objectives, including imparting education, advancing learning and research in agriculture, and undertaking extension education programmes.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Details the extensive powers of the University, such as providing instruction, conducting research, granting degrees, establishing colleges, and managing its finances and personnel.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Defines the geographical jurisdiction of the University for teaching, research, and extension education, covering specific North-Eastern states.

key_sections.title: The Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University and grants powers of inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions to ensure compliance with the Act.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the principal officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Deans, Directors, Registrar, and Comptroller.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the main governing authorities of the University, such as the Board, Academic Council, Finance Committee, and Board of Studies.

key_sections.title: Power to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Statutes can be made, covering the constitution of authorities, appointment of officers and staff, conditions of service, and discipline.

key_sections.title: Statutes how to be made.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the procedure for making, amending, or repealing Statutes, requiring the assent of the Visitor.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Outlines the matters for which Ordinances can be made, including student admission, courses of study, examinations, fees, and conditions of residence.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees.
key_sections.description: Mandates written contracts for employees and provides for arbitration in disputes arising from these contracts.

key_sections.title: Procedure of appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students.
key_sections.description: Establishes a right to appeal to the Board and provides for arbitration in disciplinary cases involving students.

key_sections.title: Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Requires the publication of all Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations in the Official Gazette and their presentation before both Houses of Parliament.

powers_conferred: University: To impart education, conduct research, undertake extension education, grant diplomas/certificates/degrees, confer honorary degrees, provide lectures for field workers, cooperate with other institutions, establish colleges/campuses/laboratories, create teaching/research/administrative posts, award fellowships/scholarships, determine admission standards, provide residential accommodation, supervise student residences, lay down conditions of service, regulate discipline, fix fees, borrow money, receive benefactions/donations/gifts, acquire/hold/manage/dispose of property.

Visitor: To cause inspection/inquiry, give notice to the University, consider representations, address the Vice-Chancellor with advice, issue directions, annul proceedings, appoint Chancellor/Vice-Chancellor/first members of Board/Academic Council, decide disputes regarding constitution of authorities, amend/repeal Statutes, direct the University to make provisions in Statutes.

Board: Principal executive body, management and administration of revenue/property, create teaching/academic/administrative posts, appoint staff, grant leave of absence, regulate discipline among employees, manage finances/accounts/investments, fix expenditure limits, invest money, transfer property, provide infrastructure, enter contracts, redress grievances of employees/students, appoint examiners/moderators, select common seal, make special arrangements for women students, delegate powers, institute fellowships/scholarships, appoint Visiting Professors/Consultants/Scholars, make/amend/repeal Statutes, make Ordinances, direct amendment/annulment of Regulations.

Vice-Chancellor: Principal executive and academic officer, exercise general supervision and control, take immediate action on any matter, review decisions of authorities, exercise powers and perform duties prescribed by Statutes/Ordinances, be ex officio Chairman of Board/Academic Council/Finance Committee, preside at convocations, ensure observance of Act/Statutes/Ordinances/Regulations, maintain discipline, convene meetings, appoint Deans of colleges, appoint persons to perform duties of Registrar/Comptroller when vacant/unable, take disciplinary action against employees (excluding teachers) as specified by Board, make recommendations to Visitor regarding decisions of authorities.

Central Government: Appoint date of commencement of the Act, receive annual reports/accounts, cause annual reports/accounts to be laid before Parliament, remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act, approve first Ordinances.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for disciplinary actions against students, including expulsion, rustication, debarment from examinations, fines, or cancellation of results. For employees, disciplinary actions can include suspension, censure, withholding of increment, or removal from service on grounds of misconduct. Disputes regarding employee contracts or student disciplinary actions can be referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and the first members of the Board and Academic Council. The Board appoints the Director Instruction, Director of Research, Director of Extension Education, Registrar, Comptroller, Librarians, and other teachers and academic staff. The Vice-Chancellor appoints Deans of colleges.

applies_to: North-Eastern region
States of Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura
persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class
employees of the University
students of the University
exemptions: Special provisions for the employment or admission of women, handicapped or of persons belonging to the weaker sections of the society and, in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.
special_provisions: The Act applies specifically to the North-Eastern region of India.
Special arrangements may be made for the residence and discipline of women students.
Transitional provisions are made for the appointment and term of office of the first Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Comptroller, and members of the Board and Academic Council.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Board, with the Visitor's assent, has the power to make, amend, or repeal Statutes. The Vice-Chancellor, with Central Government approval, makes the first Ordinances, which can then be amended or repealed by the Board. Authorities of the University may make Regulations for their own business.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is primarily through the Visitor's powers of inspection, inquiry, and issuing binding directions. The Board acts as the principal executive body, and the Vice-Chancellor exercises general supervision and control. Disciplinary actions against employees and students, along with provisions for arbitration, also serve as enforcement mechanisms.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The Act specifies that no suit shall lie in any civil court in respect of matters decided by the Tribunal of Arbitration concerning employee disputes. This implies that civil courts would otherwise have jurisdiction over matters not covered by such arbitration.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the Statutes of the University, detailing the appointment, powers, and duties of key officers like the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Deans, Directors, Registrar, and Comptroller. It also outlines the constitution, powers, and functions of the Board, Academic Council, Finance Committee, Board of Studies, and Selection Committees. Further provisions cover terms and conditions of service for employees, removal procedures, honorary degrees, withdrawal of degrees, maintenance of discipline among students, and the process for making Ordinances and Regulations.

act_identification.act_title: THE INFANT MILK SUBSTITUTES, FEEDING BOTTLES AND INFANT FOODS (REGULATION OF PRODUCTION, SUPPLY AND DISTRIBUTION) ACT, 1992
act_identification.act_short_title: The Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles and Infant Foods (Regulation of Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 1992

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the regulation of production, supply and distribution of infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles and infant foods with a view to the protection and promotion of breast-feeding and ensuring the proper use of infant foods and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the production, supply, and distribution of infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles, and infant foods. Its primary objective is to protect and promote breast-feeding and ensure the proper use of infant foods, thereby safeguarding infant health.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Certain prohibitions in relation to infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles and infant foods.
key_sections.description: Prohibits advertising, creating belief of equivalence to mother's milk, and promotion of infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles, and infant foods.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of incentives for the use or sale of infant milk substitutes or feeding bottles or infant foods.
key_sections.description: Prohibits supplying samples, contacting pregnant women/mothers, or offering other inducements to promote these products.

key_sections.title: Donations of infant milk substitutes or feeding or equipment or materials relating thereto.
key_sections.description: Restricts donations and distribution of infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles, and related materials, with an exception for orphanages and health care systems under certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Information on containers and labels of infant milk substitutes of infant foods.
key_sections.description: Mandates specific information and warnings on containers and labels of infant milk substitutes and infant foods, and prohibits certain imagery or words.

key_sections.title: Educational and other materials relating to feeding of infants to contain certain particulars.
key_sections.description: Requires educational materials on infant feeding to include information on the benefits of breast-feeding and hazards of substitutes, and prohibits their use for promotion.

key_sections.title: Health care system.
key_sections.description: Regulates the use of health care systems for promoting infant milk substitutes, prohibits payments to health workers for promotion, and specifies conditions for demonstration and distribution.

key_sections.title: Inducement to health worker for promoting use of infant milk substitutes, etc.
key_sections.description: Prohibits producers, suppliers, or distributors from offering financial inducements or gifts to health workers or their families for promotion.

key_sections.title: Standards of infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles or infant foods.
key_sections.description: Requires infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles, and infant foods to conform to specified standards and bear the Bureau of Indian Standards mark.

key_sections.title: Powers of entry and search.
key_sections.description: Grants Food Safety Officers or authorised officers powers to enter and search premises for contraventions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to seize infant milk substitutes, etc., or containers thereof.
key_sections.description: Empowers officers to seize products or containers believed to be in contravention of the Act.

key_sections.title: Confiscation.
key_sections.description: States that products or containers contravening the Act are liable to confiscation.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for contraventions of various provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to appoint commencement date (S.1(3)), make rules (S.26), specify limits for adjudication (S.17(b)), authorise voluntary organizations for complaints (S.21(1)(c)).
State Government: Power to authorise officers for entry and search (S.12(1)).
Food Safety Officer/Authorised Officer: Powers of entry and search (S.12), power to seize (S.13).
Courts: Power to adjudicate confiscation (S.14, S.17), order payment of cost in lieu of confiscation (S.15), hear appeals (S.19), take cognizance of offences (S.21).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of Sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10 or sub-section (2) of Section 11 and rules made under Section 26 is punishable with imprisonment up to three years, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both. Contravention of Section 6 or sub-section (1) of Section 11 and rules made under Section 26 is punishable with imprisonment not less than six months but up to three years and fine not less than two thousand rupees (with a proviso for lesser punishment under special reasons). Offences by companies are also covered, making the company and responsible persons liable. Offences are cognizable and bailable.

related_acts: The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (34 of 2006)
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 (63 of 1986)
Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (37 of 1954)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government (to authorise officers for entry and search); Central Government (to authorise other courts for adjudication, to authorise representatives of voluntary organisations for complaints).

applies_to: the whole of India
Any person involved in production, supply, distribution, or sale of infant milk substitutes, feeding bottles, and infant foods
Health care systems and health workers
exemptions: Donation or distribution of informational or educational equipment or material through the health care system, subject to prescribed conditions and restrictions (Proviso to S.5(b)).
Dissemination of scientific and factual information to a health worker (S.8(1)(b)).
Orphanages purchasing infant milk substitutes or feeding bottles at a price lower than their sale price (S.8(5)).
Health workers demonstrating feeding with infant milk substitutes or infant foods (S.8(3)).

Institutions or organisations engaged in health care for mothers, infants or pregnant women distributing infant milk substitutes or feeding bottles to a mother who cannot resort to breast-feeding and who cannot afford to purchase (S.8(4)).
special_provisions: Orphanages may purchase infant milk substitutes or feeding bottles at a price lower than their sale price (S.8(5)).
Specific provisions for companies regarding offences (S.22).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through prohibitions on certain activities (advertising, incentives, inducements), mandatory information requirements on products and educational materials, adherence to standards, powers of entry, search, and seizure by designated officers, confiscation of non-compliant products, and prescribed penalties including imprisonment and fines. Offences are cognizable and bailable, and complaints can be made by designated officers, authorised officers, or authorised voluntary organisations.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Principal civil court of original jurisdiction; other courts authorised by the Central Government (not below a civil court with pecuniary jurisdiction exceeding five thousand rupees); appellate courts.

act_identification.act_title: THE GOLD BONDS (IMMUNITIES AND EXEMPTIONS) ACT, 1993

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for certain immunities to the subscribers of the Gold Bonds and for certain exemptions from direct taxes in relation to such Bonds and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS with a view to mobilising the idle gold resources of residents in India, it is expedient to provide for certain immunities and exemptions to render it possible for such residents to subscribe to Gold Bonds;
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to mobilize idle gold resources in India by encouraging residents to subscribe to Gold Bonds. It achieves this by granting subscribers certain immunities from disclosure regarding the source of gold and exemptions from direct taxes related to these bonds.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its deemed date of commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Gold Bonds' and 'subscriber'.

key_sections.title: Gold Bonds Scheme.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to frame a scheme for subscription to Gold Bonds, 1998.

key_sections.title: Immunities.
key_sections.description: Grants immunities to subscribers from disclosure, inquiry, or investigation regarding the source of gold for Gold Bonds under various tax and regulatory acts, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Gold Bonds not to be taken into account in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Provides that provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, shall not apply to interest or long-term capital gains from Gold Bonds, and the Gift-tax Act, 1958, shall not apply to gifts of Gold Bonds to spouse, child, or parent.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Gold Bonds (Immunities and Exemptions) Ordinance, 1993, and includes savings provisions for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Central Government to frame a scheme for subscription to Gold Bonds (Section 3(1))

repealed_acts: The Gold Bonds (Immunities and Exemptions) Ordinance, 1993 (Ord. 22 of 1993)
related_acts: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (61 of 1985)
Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, 1987 (28 of 1987)

applies_to: subscribers of the Gold Bonds
residents in India
an individual, a Hindu undivided family, trustees of a trust, a firm or a company, being a resident or residents in India
exemptions: Immunities from disclosure, inquiry, or investigation regarding the nature and source of acquisition of gold subscribed for Gold Bonds under the Wealth-tax Act, 1957, Gift-tax Act, 1958, Income-tax Act, 1961, Customs Act, 1962, Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973, and Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 1976.
Exemption from the Income-tax Act, 1961, for any interest accruing to the subscriber from Gold Bonds and any long-term capital gains arising to the subscriber.
Exemption from the Gift-tax Act, 1958, where the gift of Gold Bonds is made by an individual subscriber to his spouse, child, or parent.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for framing the Gold Bonds scheme)

act_identification.act_title: THE MULTIMODAL TRANSPORTATION OF GOODS ACT, 1993

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the regulation of the multimodal transportation of goods, from any place in India to a place outside India, on the basis of a multimodal transport contract and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the multimodal transportation of goods from any place in India to a place outside India. It establishes a framework for multimodal transport contracts and addresses related matters.

chapter_titles: RESPONSIBILITIES AND LIABILITIES OF THE MULTIMODAL TRANSPORT OPERATOR

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: No person to carry on business without registration.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration for engaging in multimodal transportation business.

key_sections.title: Registration for multimodal transportation.
key_sections.description: Outlines the application process and conditions for registration as a multimodal transport operator.

key_sections.title: Issue of multimodal transport document.
key_sections.description: Requires the multimodal transport operator to issue a document upon taking charge of goods.

key_sections.title: Multimodal transport document to be regarded as document of title.
key_sections.description: Establishes the multimodal transport document as a document of title, conferring rights and liabilities.

key_sections.title: Contents of multimodal transport document.
key_sections.description: Details the mandatory particulars to be included in the multimodal transport document.

key_sections.title: Basis of liability of multimodal transport operator.
key_sections.description: Defines the circumstances under which a multimodal transport operator is liable for loss, damage, or delay.

key_sections.title: Limits of liability when the nature and value of the consignment have not been declared and stage of transport where loss or damage occurred is not known.
key_sections.description: Sets limits on liability when the value of goods is undeclared and the stage of loss is unknown.

key_sections.title: Limits of liability when the nature and value of the consignment have not been declared and stage of transport where loss or damage occurred is known.
key_sections.description: Sets limits on liability when the value of goods is undeclared and the stage of loss is known, referring to relevant law.

key_sections.title: Limitation on action.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the time limit within which legal action can be brought against a multimodal transport operator.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction for instituting action.
key_sections.description: Specifies the competent courts and locations for instituting legal actions under the Act.

key_sections.title: Multimodal transport contract to be made in accordance with this Act.
key_sections.description: Mandates that multimodal transport contracts comply with the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Act to override other enactments.
key_sections.description: States that the Act's provisions prevail over inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government authority to make rules for implementing the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government to authorize competent authority (Section 2(b))
Central Government to delegate powers (Section 27)
Central Government to make rules (Section 30)
Competent authority to register multimodal transport operators (Section 4)
Competent authority to cancel registration (Section 5)
Multimodal transport operator to issue multimodal transport document (Section 7)
Multimodal transport operator to have lien on goods and documents (Section 22)

repealed_acts: The Multimodal Transportation of Goods Ordinance, 1993 (Ord. 6 of 1993)
Repealing and Amending Act, 2001 (30 of 2001)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government

applies_to: multimodal transportation of goods, from any place in India to a place outside India
Any person carrying on or commencing the business of multimodal transportation
special_provisions: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a registration system for multimodal transport operators, provisions for multimodal transport documents, defined responsibilities and liabilities, and mechanisms for appeals and legal actions in competent courts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: a court which is competent and within the jurisdiction of which is situated one of the following places: the principal place of business or habitual residence of the defendant; the place where the multimodal transport contract was made (if defendant has a place of business there); the place of taking charge of goods or delivery thereof; or any other place specified in the multimodal transport contract.

schedules_summary.description: This Schedule was repealed by the Repealing and Amending Act, 2001 (30 of 2001).

act_identification.act_title: THE INDUSTRIAL FINANCE CORPORATION (TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKING AND REPEAL) ACT, 1993
act_identification.act_short_title: Industrial Finance Corporation (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Act, 1993

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Forty-fourth Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the transfer and vesting of the undertaking of the Industrial Finance Corporation of India to and in the Company to be formed and registered as a Company under the Companies Act, 1956, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto and also to repeal the Industrial Finance Corporation Act, 1948.
act_overview.purpose: This Act facilitates the transfer of the undertaking of the Industrial Finance Corporation of India to a new company, the Industrial Finance Corporation of India Limited, formed under the Companies Act, 1956. It also repeals the Industrial Finance Corporation Act, 1948, and addresses consequential matters such as employee provisions and tax implications.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its deemed commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Company', and 'Corporation'.

key_sections.title: Undertaking of the Corporation to vest in the company.
key_sections.description: Mandates the transfer and vesting of the undertaking of the Corporation in the Company on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: General effect of vesting of undertaking in the Company.
key_sections.description: Details the comprehensive effect of the vesting, including the transfer of all business, assets, liabilities, contracts, and legal proceedings to the Company.

key_sections.title: Concession, etc., to be deemed to have been granted to the Company.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that all fiscal and other concessions, licenses, benefits, privileges, and exemptions granted to the Corporation are deemed granted to the Company.

key_sections.title: Tax exemption or benefit to continue to have effect.
key_sections.description: Ensures that tax exemptions, assessments, or benefits available to the Corporation under the Income-tax Act, 1961, continue for the Company.

key_sections.title: Provisions in respect of officers and other employees of Corporation.
key_sections.description: Outlines the terms and conditions for the transfer of officers and employees from the Corporation to the Company, including their remuneration, rights, and benefits.

key_sections.title: Act 18 of 1891 to apply to the books of the Company.
key_sections.description: Deems the Company to be a bank for the purposes of the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 1891.

key_sections.title: Shares, bonds and debentures to be deemed to be approved securities.
key_sections.description: Declares shares, bonds, and debentures of the Company as approved securities for the purposes of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, and the Insurance Act, 1938.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving of Act 15 of 1948.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Industrial Finance Corporation Act, 1948, on the appointed day, with certain provisions for compliance related to annual accounts.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Industrial Finance Corporation (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Ordinance, 1993, and saves actions taken under it.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint the 'appointed day' for transfer and vesting (Section 3)

repealed_acts: Industrial Finance Corporation Act, 1948
Industrial Finance Corporation (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Ordinance, 1993 (Ord. 5 of 1993)

applies_to: Industrial Finance Corporation of India
the Company (Industrial Finance Corporation of India Limited)
shareholders of the Corporation
officers and other employees of Corporation

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Legal proceedings by or against the Company (Section 4(4))
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any court, tribunal or other authority (Section 4(4), Section 8(3))

act_identification.act_title: THE ACQUISITION OF CERTAIN AREA AT AYODHYA ACT, 1993
act_identification.act_short_title: The Acquisition of Certain Area at Ayodhya Act, 1993

legislative_details.geographical_extent: certain area at Ayodhya, in village Kot Ramchandra in Ayodhya, in Pargana Haveli Avadh, in tehsil Faizabad Sadar, in the district of Faizabad of the State of Uttar Pradesh, and other areas specified in the Schedule.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the acquisition of certain area at Ayodhya and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS there has been a long-standing dispute relating to the structure (including the premises of the inner and outer courtyards of such structure), commonly known as the Ram Janma Bhumi-Babri Masjid, situated in village Kot Ramchandra in Ayodhya, in Pargana Haveli Avadh, in tehsil Faizabad Sadar, in the district of Faizabad of the State of Uttar Pradesh; AND WHEREAS the said dispute has affected the maintenance of public order and harmony between different communities in the country; AND WHEREAS it is necessary to maintain public order and to promote communal harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst the people of India; AND WHEREAS with a view to achieving the aforesaid objectives, it is necessary to acquire certain areas in Ayodhya; BE it enacted by Parliament in the Forty-fourth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the acquisition of a specific area in Ayodhya to resolve a long-standing dispute related to the Ram Janma Bhumi-Babri Masjid structure. Its main objectives are to maintain public order, promote communal harmony, and facilitate the management of the acquired property.

chapter_titles: ACQUISITION OF THE AREA IN AYODHYA

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its deemed commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act.

key_sections.title: Acquisition of rights in respect of certain area.
key_sections.description: States that rights, title, and interest in the specified area are transferred to and vested in the Central Government upon commencement of the Act.

key_sections.title: General effect of vesting.
key_sections.description: Details the comprehensive nature of vesting, including assets, rights, and freedom from encumbrances, and abatement of pending suits.

key_sections.title: Duty of person or State Government in charge of the management of the area to deliver all assets, etc.
key_sections.description: Mandates delivery of assets, registers, and documents to the Central Government or authorized person upon vesting.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to direct vesting of the area in another authority or body or trust.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to transfer the vested rights, title, and interest to another authority, body, or trust under specified conditions.

key_sections.title: Management of property by Government.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the vested property shall be managed by the Central Government or by a person or body of persons or trustees of any trust authorised by that Government, ensuring the maintenance of the pre-commencement position of the Ram Janma Bhumi-Babri Masjid structure.

key_sections.title: Payment of amount.
key_sections.description: Provides for payment of market value as compensation to owners and establishes a Claims Commissioner for deciding claims.

key_sections.title: Act to override all other enactments.
key_sections.description: Establishes the overriding effect of this Act over other inconsistent laws, instruments, decrees, or orders.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for failure to deliver assets or documents by those in charge of management.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Acquisition of Certain Area at Ayodhya Ordinance, 1993, with specific saving provisions regarding plot No. 242.

powers_conferred: Central Government to take all necessary steps to secure possession of the area
Central Government to direct vesting of the area in another authority or body or trust
Central Government or authorised person to manage property
Central Government to appoint a Claims Commissioner
Central Government to make rules
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who is in charge of the management of the area and fails to deliver to the Central Government or the authorised person any asset, register or other document in his custody relating to such area or, as the case may be, authenticated copies of such register or document, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both.

repealed_acts: Acquisition of Certain Area at Ayodhya Ordinance, 1993 (Ord. 8 of 1993)

authorities_established: any authority or other body, or trustees of any trust, set up on or after the commencement of this Act
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (for Claims Commissioner)

applies_to: certain area at Ayodhya
the area (including all the buildings, structures or other properties comprised therein) specified in the Schedule
exemptions: plot No. 242 situated in village Kot Ramchandra specified against Sl. No. 1 of the Schedule to the said Ordinance
special_provisions: the position existing before the commencement of this Act in the area on which the structure (including the premises of the inner and outer courtyards of such structure), commonly known as the Ram Janma Bhumi-Babri Masjid, stood in village Kot Ramchandra in Ayodhya... is maintained.
Specific provisions in Section 13(2) regarding plot No. 242, ensuring it was never vested and related proceedings never abated.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government acquires the area, manages it directly or through an authorized person, and appoints a Claims Commissioner to handle compensation claims. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance with delivery duties.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: any court, tribunal or other authority (as mentioned in relation to abatement of suits and overriding effect)

schedules_summary.description: Contains the description of the area to be acquired, listing specific revenue (Khasra) plot numbers in villages Kot Ramchandra, Avadhkhas, and Jalwanpur, along with their area in Bigha, Biswa, and Biswansi, and some boundary descriptions for part plots.

act_identification.act_title: THE SAARC CONVENTION (SUPPRESSION OF TERRORISM) ACT, 1993
act_identification.act_short_title: the SAARC Convention (Suppression of Terrorism) Act, 1993

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India and, subject to the provisions of section 6, it applies also to any offence under this Act committed outside India by any person.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to give effect to the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation Convention on Suppression of Terrorism and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS a Convention on the Suppression of Terrorism was signed on behalf of the Government of India at Kathmandu on the 4th day of November, 1987; AND WHEREAS India, having ratified the said Convention, should make provisions for giving effect thereto and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto; BE it enacted by Parliament in the Forty-fourth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to give effect to the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation Convention on Suppression of Terrorism. It provides legal provisions for implementing the Convention and addresses related matters.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and application.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent to the whole of India, and its application to offences committed outside India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, specifically 'Convention' and 'Convention country'.

key_sections.title: Application of the Convention.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that Articles I to VIII of the Convention shall have the force of law in India, overriding other laws.

key_sections.title: Hostage-taking.
key_sections.description: Defines the offence of hostage-taking and prescribes the punishment for committing this offence.

key_sections.title: Provisions as to Extradition Act.
key_sections.description: Declares that certain offences under this Act or Article I of the Convention shall not be considered political offences for the purposes of the Extradition Act, 1962.

key_sections.title: Offences committed outside India.
key_sections.description: Establishes jurisdiction for offences committed outside India by Indian citizens, on Indian-registered conveyances, or in a Convention country, and allows the Central Government to direct inquiry or trial anywhere in India.

key_sections.title: Previous sanction necessary for prosecution.
key_sections.description: Mandates that no prosecution for an offence under this Act can be instituted without the previous sanction of the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Provides immunity from legal proceedings against any person or the Central Government for actions done or intended to be done in good faith under this Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government may, by general or special order published in the Official Gazette, direct that the offence under sub-section (1) of section 4 or any other offence specified in Article I of the Convention may be inquired into or tried at any place within India.
Central Government's previous sanction is necessary for prosecution for an offence under this Act.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever commits the offence of hostage-taking shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

related_acts: Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft, signed at the Hauge, on December 16, 1970
Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Act, against the Safety of Civil Aviations signed at Montreal, on September 23, 1971
Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of Crimes against Internationally Protected Persons, including Diplomatic Agents, signed at New York, on December 14, 1973

applies_to: the whole of India
any offence under this Act committed outside India by any person
a citizen of India, whether on the high seas or elsewhere
a person, not being such citizen, on any ship or aircraft, registered in India
a person, not being such citizen, in a Convention country

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Prosecution for offences under the Act requires previous sanction from the Central Government. The Act also incorporates provisions for extradition and jurisdiction over offences committed outside India as per the SAARC Convention.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the full text of the SAARC Regional Convention on Suppression of Terrorism, detailing its articles concerning terroristic offences, extradition principles, mutual assistance among contracting states, and procedures for its entry into force.

act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL LAWS (EXTENSION TO ARUNACHAL PRADESH) ACT, 1993
act_identification.act_short_title: The Central Laws (Extension to Arunachal Pradesh) Act, 1993

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the extension of certain Central laws to the State of Arunachal Pradesh. BE it enacted by Parliament in the Forty-fourth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the extension of specific Central laws, along with their associated rules, orders, regulations, and schemes, to the State of Arunachal Pradesh, making them enforceable within that region. It also includes provisions for the construction of references and removal of difficulties.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Central Laws (Extension to Arunachal Pradesh) Act, 1993' and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government by notification.

key_sections.title: Extension of certain laws.
key_sections.description: Declares that the Acts mentioned in the Schedule, along with all rules, orders, regulations, and schemes made thereunder, are extended to and shall be in force in the State of Arunachal Pradesh.

key_sections.title: Construction of references to laws not in force in Arunachal Pradesh.
key_sections.description: Provides that any reference in a Scheduled Act to a law not in force in Arunachal Pradesh shall be construed as a reference to the corresponding law in force in that State.

key_sections.title: Construction of references to authorities where new authorities have been constituted.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that references to existing authorities in Arunachal Pradesh laws shall, where a corresponding new authority is constituted under an extended law, be construed as references to the new authority.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make provisions or give directions to remove difficulties in giving effect to the extended Acts, including specifying corresponding authorities and providing for transfer of pending matters.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint the date of commencement of the Act (Section 1(2))
Central Government: To make provisions or give directions for the removal of difficulties in giving effect to the extended Acts (Section 5(1))
Central Government: To specify corresponding authorities (Section 5(2)(a))
Central Government: To provide for the transfer of matters pending before courts, tribunals, or other authorities (Section 5(2)(b))

related_acts: The Manoeuvres, Field Firing and Artillery Practice Act, 1938
The Coal Mines Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1948

applies_to: State of Arunachal Pradesh

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government via notification in the Official Gazette. The Central Government can also issue orders and directions to remove difficulties in its implementation.

schedules_summary.description: Lists various Central Acts by their year, number, and short title, which are extended to the State of Arunachal Pradesh by this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE TEZPUR UNIVERSITY ACT, 1993

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of the State of Assam

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate a teaching and residential University in the State of Assam at Tezpur and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: To establish and incorporate a teaching and residential University in the State of Assam at Tezpur. Its main purpose is to disseminate and advance knowledge, provide instructional and research facilities, promote integrated courses, and educate manpower for the development and welfare of the people of Assam.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act and its Statutes.

key_sections.title: The University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Tezpur University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with its headquarters at Tezpur.

key_sections.title: Objects of the University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary goals of the University, including knowledge dissemination, research, integrated courses, manpower training for Assam, and improving social and economic conditions in the State.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers of the University, such as providing instruction, granting degrees, conducting research, establishing campuses, and managing its affairs.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: States that the University's jurisdiction extends to the entire State of Assam.

key_sections.title: The Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor and details the Visitor's powers, including review, inspection, inquiry, issuing directions, and annulling proceedings.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the designated officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Deans, Registrar, and Finance Officer.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main governing authorities of the University, such as the Board of Management, Academic Council, and Finance Committee.

key_sections.title: Power to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Statutes can be made, covering the constitution of authorities, appointment of officers and staff, and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Outlines the matters for which Ordinances can be made, including student admission, courses of study, examinations, fees, and conditions of residence.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees.
key_sections.description: Mandates written contracts for employees and provides for arbitration in disputes between the University and its employees.

key_sections.title: Procedure of appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students.
key_sections.description: Establishes a right to appeal to the Board of Management and provides for arbitration in disciplinary cases involving students.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act for a period of three years from its commencement.

key_sections.title: Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Requires all Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and laid before both Houses of Parliament.

powers_conferred: University: to provide for instruction and research, grant diplomas/certificates/degrees, organise extra-mural studies, confer honorary degrees, provide distance education, institute teaching/academic positions, recognise institutions/persons for instruction, appoint staff, co-operate/collaborate with other institutions, establish campuses/centres, institute/award fellowships/scholarships/medals/prizes, establish/maintain Colleges/Institutions/Halls, make provision for research/advisory services, organise/conduct refresher courses/workshops/seminars, make special arrangements for women students, appoint visiting/emeritus professors/consultants/scholars, confer autonomous status, determine admission standards, demand fees, supervise student residences, make arrangements for health/welfare of students/employees, lay down conditions of service, regulate/enforce discipline, receive benefactions/donations/gifts, acquire/hold/manage/dispose of property, borrow money, do all other necessary/incidental acts.

Visitor: to appoint Vice-Chancellor, review work and progress of the University, inspect University buildings/laboratories/equipment/Colleges/Institutions, inquire into administration/finances, issue directions, annul proceedings not in conformity with the Act/Statutes/Ordinances, make new/additional Statutes or amend/repeal existing ones.

Vice-Chancellor: to be the principal executive and academic officer, exercise general supervision and control, give effect to decisions of authorities, take immediate action on matters, ask authorities to review decisions, exercise other powers/duties prescribed by Statutes/Ordinances.

Board of Management: to make new/additional Statutes or amend/repeal existing ones, manage and administer revenue and property, conduct administrative affairs, create teaching/academic/administrative/ministerial posts, appoint staff, grant leave of absence to officers (other than Chancellor/Vice-Chancellor), regulate/enforce discipline among employees, manage finances/accounts/investments, fix expenditure limits, invest University money, transfer property, provide infrastructure, enter into contracts, entertain/adjudicate grievances of employees/students, appoint/remove examiners/moderators, fix fees/emoluments, select common seal, make special arrangements for women students, delegate powers, institute fellowships/scholarships/studentships/medals/prizes, appoint visiting/emeritus professors/consultants/scholars.

Academic Council: to coordinate and exercise general supervision over academic policies, give directions regarding instruction methods/co-operative teaching/evaluation of research/academic standards, bring about inter-School co-ordination, establish committees/boards for projects, consider matters of general academic interest, frame regulations/rules.

Planning and Academic Committee: to advise the Board of Management on academic and development activities, oversee/review/monitor development, keep under review standards of education and research, exercise powers and functions of the Academic Council and Planning Board.

Registrar: to enter into agreements, sign documents, authenticate records, take disciplinary action against specified employees (excluding teachers/academic staff), suspend employees pending inquiry, administer warnings, impose censure/withholding of increment, be custodian of records/common seal/property, issue notices for meetings, keep minutes of meetings, conduct official correspondence, arrange/superintend examinations, supply agenda/minutes to Visitor, represent University in suits/proceedings.

Finance Officer: to exercise general supervision over funds, advise on financial policy, hold/manage property/investments, ensure expenditure limits are not exceeded, prepare annual accounts/budget, watch cash/bank balances/investments, watch revenue collection, ensure registers are maintained, bring unauthorised expenditure/financial irregularities to Vice-Chancellor's notice, call for information/returns from offices/centres/colleges/institutions.
Deans of Schools: to be Head of the School, responsible for conduct and maintenance of teaching/research standards.
Heads of Departments: to perform duties prescribed by Ordinances.
Proctors: to exercise powers and perform duties assigned by the Vice-Chancellor.
Librarian: to exercise powers and perform duties assigned by the Board of Management.
Authorities of the University: to make Regulations for the conduct of their own business and committees.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for disciplinary actions against employees for misconduct, including suspension, censure, withholding of increment, and removal from service. For students, disciplinary actions can include expulsion, rustication for a specified period, debarment from examinations, imposition of fines, or cancellation of examination results. Disputes arising from employee contracts or student disciplinary actions can be referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Vice-Chancellor, the first Vice-Chancellor, first Registrar, first Finance Officer, and members of the first Board of Management. The Board of Management appoints the Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, Heads of Departments, Proctors, Librarian, Professors, Readers, Lecturers, other academic staff, and Principals of Colleges/Institutions. The Vice-Chancellor appoints Deans of Schools.

applies_to: persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class
students of the University
employees of the University
teachers of the University
special_provisions: Special provisions for the employment or admission of women, physically handicapped or of persons belonging to the weaker sections of the society and, in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.
Special arrangements in respect of the residence, discipline and teaching of women students.
Transitional provisions for the appointment of the first Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, and the constitution of the first Board of Management, Academic Council, and Planning Board.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Statutes are made by the Board of Management (with Visitor's assent) or by the Visitor directly. Ordinances are made by the Vice-Chancellor (first Ordinances with Central Government approval) or by the Board of Management (for amendments/additions). Regulations are made by the authorities of the University.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor has powers of review, inspection, inquiry, issuing directions, and annulling proceedings. The Vice-Chancellor exercises general supervision and control. The Board of Management is the principal executive body. Disputes concerning employee service conditions and student disciplinary actions are subject to arbitration by a Tribunal.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No suit shall lie in any civil court in respect of matters decided by the Tribunal of Arbitration concerning employee disputes.

schedules_summary.description: Details the specific objects of the University, focusing on its role in the development of the North-Eastern Region, promoting culture, offering employment-oriented and inter-disciplinary courses, research in Science and Technology, national integration, utilizing distance education, and fostering innovative learning.

Contains the Statutes of the University, which prescribe the constitution, powers, and functions of various officers (Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, Deans, Heads of Departments, Proctors, Librarian) and authorities (Board of Management, Planning and Academic Committee, Academic Council, Planning Board, Schools of Studies, Departments, Board of Studies, Finance Committee, Selection Committees). It also covers terms and conditions of service, removal of employees, honorary degrees, withdrawal of degrees, student discipline, convocations, resignation, disqualifications, Alumni Association, Students' Council, and the process for making Ordinances and Regulations.

act_identification.act_title: THE EMPLOYMENT OF MANUAL SCAVENGERS AND CONSTRUCTION OF DRY LATRINES (PROHIBITION) ACT, 1993
act_identification.act_short_title: The Employment of Manual Scavengers and Construction of Dry Latrines (Prohibition) Act, 1993

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of the States of Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tripura and West Bengal and to all the Union territories and it shall also apply to such other State which adopts this Act by resolution passed in that behalf under clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the prohibition of employment of manual scavengers as well as construction or continuance of dry latrines and for the regulation of construction and maintenance of water-seal latrines and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS fraternity assuring the dignity of the individual has been enshrined in the Preamble to the Constitution; AND WHEREAS article 47 of the Constitution, inter alia, provides that the State shall regard raising the standard of living of its people and the improvement of public health as among its primary duties; AND WHEREAS the dehumanizing practice of manual scavenging of human excreta still continues in many parts of the country; AND WHEREAS the municipal laws by themselves as a measure for conversion of dry latrines into water-seal latrines and prevention of construction of dry latrines are not stringent enough to eliminate this practice; AND WHEREAS it is necessary to enact a uniform legislation for the whole of India for abolishing manual scavenging by declaring employment of manual scavengers for removal of human excreta an offence and thereby ban the further proliferation of dry latrines in the country; AND WHEREAS it is desirable for eliminating the dehumanising practice of employment of manual scavengers and for protecting and improving the human environment to make it obligatory to convert dry latrines into water-seal latrines or to construct water-seal latrines in new construction; AND WHEREAS Parliament has no power to make laws for the States with respect to the matters aforesaid, except as provided in articles 249 and 250 of the Constitution; AND WHEREAS in pursuance of clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution, resolutions have been passed by all the Houses of the Legislatures of the States of Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tripura and West Bengal that the matters aforesaid should be regulated in those States by Parliament by law;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to prohibit the employment of manual scavengers and the construction or continuance of dry latrines. It also aims to regulate the construction and maintenance of water-seal latrines to eliminate the dehumanizing practice of manual scavenging and improve public health and environmental conditions.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II PROHIBITION OF EMPLOYMENT OF MANUAL SCAVENGERS, ETC.
CHAPTER III IMPLEMENTING AUTHORITIES AND SCHEMES

key_sections.title: Short title, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its initial application to certain states and Union territories, and the date of its commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'manual scavenger', 'dry latrine', and 'water-seal latrine'.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of employment of manual scavengers, etc.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the engagement or employment of manual scavengers and the construction or maintenance of dry latrines, subject to certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government power to exempt certain areas, buildings, or persons from the Act's provisions under specific conditions.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Executive Authorities and their powers and functions.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to appoint Executive Authorities (District or Sub-Divisional Magistrates) to enforce the Act and rehabilitate manual scavengers.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to make schemes.
key_sections.description: Allows the State Government to formulate schemes for converting dry latrines, constructing water-seal latrines, and rehabilitating manual scavengers.

key_sections.title: Appointment of inspectors and their powers of entry and inspection.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the State Government to appoint inspectors with powers to enter and inspect premises to ensure compliance with the Act.

key_sections.title: Duty of HUDCO to extend financial assistance in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Mandates HUDCO to provide financial assistance for schemes related to the construction of water-seal latrines.

key_sections.title: Constitution of committees.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of Project Committees, Monitoring Committees by the Central Government and State Co-ordination Committees by the State Government.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of the provisions of the Act and rules, orders, directions and schemes.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for non-compliance or contravention of the Act's provisions, rules, orders, directions, and schemes.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Stipulates liability for offences committed by companies, including the company itself and responsible individuals.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable.
key_sections.description: Declares all offences under this Act to be cognizable.

key_sections.title: Provision in relation to jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Specifies the minimum court level for trying offences and the requirement for Executive Authority's sanction for prosecution.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions, particularly regarding committees.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions, particularly regarding committees.

powers_conferred: Power to exempt any area, category of buildings or class of persons from provisions of the Act (State Government)
Power to appoint Executive Authorities and confer powers and duties on them (State Government)
Power to make schemes for regulating conversion of dry latrines, construction of water-seal latrines, and rehabilitation of manual scavengers (State Government)
Power to issue directions to any person, officer or authority (State Government)
Power to appoint inspectors and define their local limits of jurisdiction (State Government)
Power of entry and inspection for inspectors
Power to prevent environmental pollution and direct remedial measures (Executive Authority)
Power to levy fees in respect of community latrines, shared latrines, supply of documents, licensing of contractors, etc. (State Government)
Power to constitute Project Committees, Monitoring Committees, and other committees (Central Government)
Power to constitute State Co-ordination Committees and other committees (State Government)
Power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act (Central Government)
Power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act (State Government)
Power to remove difficulties (Central Government)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever fails to comply with or contravenes any provisions of the Act, rules, orders, directions, or schemes shall be punishable with imprisonment for up to one year or with a fine up to two thousand rupees, or both. Additional fine of one hundred rupees per day for continuing contravention after conviction. Companies and responsible individuals are also liable for offences.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government appoints Executive Authorities and inspectors. Central Government constitutes Project Committees, Monitoring Committees, and other committees. State Government constitutes State Co-ordination Committees and other committees.
regulatory_bodies: HUDCO (Housing and Urban Development Corporation Limited)

applies_to: whole of the States of Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tripura and West Bengal and to all the Union territories
such other State which adopts this Act by resolution passed in that behalf under clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution
exemptions: any area
category of buildings
class of persons
special_provisions: Extended to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh by Act 34 of 2019, s. 95 and the fifth Schedule (w.e.f. 31-10-2019).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced through Executive Authorities and inspectors who have powers of entry and inspection. Contraventions are punishable with imprisonment and fines. Offences are cognizable, and prosecution requires sanction from the Executive Authority.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class

act_identification.act_title: THE RECOVERY OF DEBTS AND BANKRUPTCY ACT, 1993
act_identification.act_short_title: The Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of Tribunals for expeditious adjudication and recovery of debts due to banks and financial institutions [,insolvency resolution and bankruptcy of individuals and partnership firms] and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes Tribunals for the expeditious adjudication and recovery of debts owed to banks and financial institutions. It also covers insolvency resolution and bankruptcy for individuals and partnership firms, along with related incidental matters.

chapter_titles: ESTABLISHMENT OF TRIBUNAL AND APPELLATE TRIBUNAL
JURISDICTION, POWERS AND AUTHORITY OF TRIBUNALS
RECOVERY OF DEBT DETERMINED BY TRIBUNAL

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical extent, commencement date, and conditions for its application based on debt amount.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Appellate Tribunal', 'bank', 'debt', 'financial institution', and 'secured creditor'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to establish Debts Recovery Tribunals and specifies their jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to establish Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunals to hear appeals against Tribunal orders.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction, powers and authority of Tribunals.
key_sections.description: Outlines the jurisdiction, powers, and authority of Tribunals and Appellate Tribunals for debt recovery and insolvency matters.

key_sections.title: Bar of jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Bars other courts and authorities from exercising jurisdiction over matters specified in Section 17, with exceptions for the Supreme Court and High Courts.

key_sections.title: Application to the Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Details the procedure for banks and financial institutions to file applications for debt recovery, including requirements for disclosure of assets and interim orders.

key_sections.title: Filing of recovery applications, documents and written statements in electronic form.
key_sections.description: Allows for the electronic filing of applications, documents, and pleadings, and electronic service of notices, as prescribed by rules.

key_sections.title: Appeal to the Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals to the Appellate Tribunal against orders of the Tribunal, specifying filing period and procedure.

key_sections.title: Deposit of amount of debt due, on filing appeal.
key_sections.description: Requires a deposit of a percentage of the debt amount for an appeal to be entertained by the Appellate Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Procedure and powers of the Tribunal and the Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: States that Tribunals and Appellate Tribunals are not bound by the Civil Procedure Code but are guided by natural justice, and outlines their powers.

key_sections.title: Modes of recovery of debts.
key_sections.description: Specifies the methods a Recovery Officer can use to recover debts, including attachment and sale of property, taking possession of secured assets, and arrest.

key_sections.title: Transfer of pending cases.
key_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of suits and proceedings pending before other courts to the Tribunals upon their establishment.

key_sections.title: Priority to secured creditors.
key_sections.description: Establishes the priority of secured creditors in realizing secured debts over other debts and government dues, subject to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in other laws, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To establish Debts Recovery Tribunals (Section 3).
Central Government: To establish Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunals (Section 8).
Central Government: To appoint Presiding Officers of Tribunals (Section 4).
Central Government: To appoint Chairperson of Appellate Tribunals (Section 9).
Central Government: To provide staff for Tribunals (Section 7).
Central Government: To make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act (Section 36).
Central Government: To remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act (Section 35).
Tribunal: To exercise jurisdiction, powers, and authority for recovery of debts and insolvency matters (Section 17).
Tribunal: To regulate its own procedure (Section 22).
Tribunal: To summon and enforce attendance, require discovery, receive evidence, issue commissions, review decisions, dismiss/set aside orders (Section 22(2)).
Tribunal: To issue certificate of recovery (Section 19(22)).
Tribunal: To order attachment of property (Section 19(13)).
Tribunal: To appoint a receiver (Section 19(18)).
Appellate Tribunal: To exercise jurisdiction, powers, and authority to entertain appeals (Section 17(2)).
Chairperson of Appellate Tribunal: To exercise general power of superintendence and control over Tribunals (Section 17A).
Chairperson of Appellate Tribunal: To transfer cases from one Tribunal to another (Section 17A(2)).
Recovery Officer: To recover debt by attachment and sale of property, taking possession of secured property, arrest, or appointing a receiver (Section 25).
Recovery Officer: To require declaration of assets on affidavit (Section 28(4A)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes detention in civil prison for a term not exceeding three months for non-compliance with certain orders of the Presiding Officer or Tribunal (Section 19(5)(iii), Section 19(17)). It also states that a person making a false statement on oath regarding money due to the defendant, or discharging liability to the defendant after receiving a notice from the Recovery Officer, shall be personally liable to the Recovery Officer (Section 28(3)(vi), Section 28(3)(ix)).
