Enforcement of Security Interest and Recovery of Debts Laws (Amendment) Act, 2004 (30 of 2004)
Unit Trust of India Act, 1963 (52 of 1963)
Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India Act, 1984 (62 of 1984)
Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985 (1 of 1986)
Small Industries Development Bank of India Act, 1989 (39 of 1989)
Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions (Amendment) Act, 2000 (1 of 2000)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the Presiding Officer of a Tribunal, the Chairperson of an Appellate Tribunal, and Recovery Officers.

applies_to: Banks and financial institutions for recovery of debts.
Individuals and partnership firms for insolvency resolution and bankruptcy.
exemptions: Cases where the amount of debt due is less than ten lakh rupees or such other amount, being not less than one lakh rupees, as the Central Government may specify.
special_provisions: The Act extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
Multi-State co-operative banks have the option to initiate proceedings under the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002, instead of making an application under this Act.

Proceedings related to the recovery of debts due to any multi-State co-operative bank pending before the commencement of the Enforcement of Security Interest and Recovery of Debts Laws (Amendment) Act, 2012, under the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002, shall be continued under that Act.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through Debts Recovery Tribunals and Appellate Tribunals. Upon determination of debt, the Presiding Officer issues a certificate of recovery to a Recovery Officer. The Recovery Officer then proceeds to recover the amount through various modes, including attachment and sale of property, taking possession of secured assets, arrest, or appointing a receiver. Appeals against orders of the Recovery Officer can be made to the Tribunal.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Debts Recovery Tribunals and Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunals have jurisdiction. Other courts or authorities are barred from exercising jurisdiction, except the Supreme Court and High Courts exercising jurisdiction under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution.

act_identification.act_title: THE OIL AND NATURAL GAS COMMISSION (TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKING AND REPEAL) ACT, 1993
act_identification.act_short_title: The Oil and Natural Gas Commission (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Act, 1993

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the transfer and vesting of the undertaking of the Oil and Natural Gas Commission to and in the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited, a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto and also to repeal the Oil and Natural Gas Commission Act, 1959.
act_overview.purpose: This Act facilitates the transfer and vesting of the undertaking of the Oil and Natural Gas Commission to the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited. It also addresses related matters such as the continuation of existing rights, liabilities, and employee provisions, and repeals the original Oil and Natural Gas Commission Act, 1959.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its deemed date of commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used within the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'Corporation', and 'Commission'.

key_sections.title: Undertaking of Commission to vest in Corporation.
key_sections.description: States that the undertaking of the Oil and Natural Gas Commission shall be transferred to and vest in the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: General effect of vesting of undertaking in Corporation.
key_sections.description: Details the comprehensive transfer of all assets, rights, powers, authorities, privileges, properties, liabilities, and obligations from the Commission to the Corporation.

key_sections.title: Tax exemption or benefit to continue to have effect.
key_sections.description: Ensures that tax exemptions, assessments, or benefits granted to the Commission under the Income-tax Act, 1961, continue to apply to the Corporation.

key_sections.title: Provisions in respect of officers and other employees of Commission.
key_sections.description: Outlines the terms and conditions for the transfer of officers and employees from the Commission to the Corporation, ensuring continuity of service, remuneration, and benefits, with an option for employees not to join the Corporation.

key_sections.title: Power of entry.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to authorize Corporation officers to enter and inspect land for ascertaining the availability of oil or natural gas, with provisions for compensation for any damage caused.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, particularly concerning compensation for land damage.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Act 48 of 1959.
key_sections.description: States that the Oil and Natural Gas Commission Act, 1959, shall stand repealed on the appointed day, with a saving clause for annual accounts.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Oil and Natural Gas Commission (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Ordinance, 1993, and saves actions taken under the said Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint the 'appointed day' for vesting (Section 3).
Central Government: To authorise officers or employees of the Corporation for entry, inspection, survey, digging, and examination of documents for oil and natural gas purposes (Section 9).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, including for compensation (Section 10).

repealed_acts: Oil and Natural Gas Commission Act, 1959 (Act 43 of 1959)
Oil and Natural Gas Commission (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Ordinance, 1993 (Ord. 28 of 1993)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government has the power to appoint the 'appointed day' (Section 3) and to appoint a competent authority for determining compensation (Section 9(4)).

applies_to: Oil and Natural Gas Commission
Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited
Officers and other employees of the Commission
Persons having control of or connected with land where entry is made for exploration
exemptions: Transfer and vesting of the undertaking is not construed as a transfer for capital gains under the Income-tax Act, 1961 (Section 6(3)).
Members or chairman of the Commission are not entitled to compensation for loss of office or premature termination of contract (Section 8(6)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act itself effects the transfer and vesting of the undertaking. Compensation for land damage is to be determined by a competent authority appointed by the Central Government in a prescribed manner (Section 9(3), 9(4)).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any court, tribunal or other authority (mentioned in the context of not entertaining claims for compensation for transfer of service under Section 8(3)).

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR SAFAI KARAMCHARIS ACT, 1993
act_identification.act_short_title: The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis Act, 1993

act_overview.preamble: An Act to constitute a National Commission for Safai Karamcharis and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: To constitute a National Commission for Safai Karamcharis and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

chapter_titles: THE NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR SAFAI KARAMCHARIS
FUNCTION SAND POWERS OF THE COMMISSION

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, application, commencement, duration and savings.

key_sections.title: Definitions.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis.

key_sections.title: Term of office and conditions of service of Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and Members.

key_sections.title: Functions and powers of the Commission.

key_sections.title: Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and Members and staff of the Commission to be public servants.
key_sections.description: Declares the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Members, officers, and other employees of the Commission as public servants under the Indian Penal Code.

key_sections.title: Central Government to consult Commission.
key_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to consult the Commission on all major policy matters affecting Safai Karamcharis.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, including matters related to salaries, allowances, and annual reports.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint the date of commencement of the Act.
Central Government: To constitute the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis.
Central Government: To nominate the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and Members of the Commission.
Central Government: To remove the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, or a Member under specified conditions.
Central Government: To provide officers and employees to the Commission.
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Commission: To exercise powers and perform functions assigned under the Act.
Commission: To call for information from any Government or authority.
Commission: To regulate its own procedure.
Commission: To delegate its powers and duties to the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Member, or officer.

amended_acts: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis (Amendment) Act, 1997 (18 of 1997)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government

applies_to: Safai Karamcharis

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis is constituted to perform functions, investigate grievances, and make recommendations to the Central and State Governments regarding Safai Karamcharis. The Central Government is required to consult the Commission on major policy matters, and annual reports are laid before Parliament and State Legislatures.

act_identification.act_title: An Act to regulate the management, administration and preservation of public records of the Central Government, Union territory Administrations, public sector undertakings, statutory bodies and corporations, commissions and committees constituted by the Central Government or a Union territory Administration and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Central Government, Union territory Administrations, public sector undertakings, statutory bodies and corporations, commissions and committees constituted by the Central Government or a Union territory Administration. Extended to the Union territory Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the management, administration and preservation of public records of the Central Government, Union territory Administrations, public sector undertakings, statutory bodies and corporations, commissions and committees constituted by the Central Government or a Union territory Administration and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish a comprehensive framework for the management, administration, and preservation of public records belonging to the Central Government, Union Territory Administrations, and various public sector entities. Its objective is to ensure the systematic handling, storage, and accessibility of these vital records for future use and historical importance.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'public records' and 'records creating agency'.

key_sections.title: Power of the Central Government to coordinate, regulate and supervise operations connected with administration, management, etc., of public records.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government powers to coordinate, regulate, and supervise public records management and allows delegation of functions to the Director General or head of Archives.

key_sections.title: Prohibition against taking of public records out of India.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the removal of public records from India without prior Central Government approval, with an exception for official purposes.

key_sections.title: Records officer.
key_sections.description: Mandates every records creating agency to nominate a records officer to discharge functions under the Act and allows for setting up record rooms.

key_sections.title: Responsibilities of records officer.
key_sections.description: Outlines the duties of records officers, including arrangement, maintenance, preservation, review, appraisal, and destruction of public records.

key_sections.title: Destruction or disposal of public records.
key_sections.description: Specifies the conditions and manner for the destruction or disposal of public records, with a special provision for records created before 1892.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contraventions.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for contravening provisions of section 4 or section 8.

key_sections.title: Access to public records.
key_sections.description: Regulates access to unclassified public records older than thirty years for bona fide research scholars and allows agencies to grant access to records in their custody.

key_sections.title: Archival Advisory Board.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of an Archival Advisory Board by the Central Government and specifies its composition.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, detailing specific matters for which rules can be made.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To coordinate, regulate and supervise operations connected with administration, management, preservation, selection, disposal and retirement of public records.
Central Government: To authorise the Director General or the head of the Archives to carry out specified functions related to public records.
Central Government: To constitute an Archival Advisory Board.
Central Government: To make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

Director General/head of the Archives: To supervise, manage and control the Archives, accept public records, ensure maintenance and security, promote utilisation of space, tender advice, survey and inspect records, organise training, accept records from private sources, regulate access, receive records from defunct bodies, provide authenticated copies, destroy/dispose of records, and obtain documents of historical importance.
Director General: To lay down norms and standards for courses in archival science.
Records officer: To take appropriate action for the recovery or restoration of public records in the event of unauthorised removal, destruction, defacement or alteration.
Records officer: To seek assistance from any government officer or other person for recovery or restoration of public records.
National Archives of India or the Archives of the Union territory: To accept any record of historical or national importance from any private source by way of gift, purchase or otherwise.
National Archives of India or the Archives of any Union territory: To make records referred to in sub-section (1) of section 11 available to any bona fide research scholar.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever contravenes any of the provisions of section 4 (Prohibition against taking of public records out of India) or section 8 (Destruction or disposal of public records) shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Director General of Archives. The Central Government nominates members to the Archival Advisory Board. Every records creating agency nominates a records officer.

applies_to: Central Government
Union territory Administrations
public sector undertakings
statutory bodies and corporations
commissions and committees constituted by the Central Government or a Union territory Administration
Union territory Jammu and Kashmir
Union territory of Ladakh
special_provisions: This Act has been extended to the Union territory Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh by Act 34 of 2019, s. 95 and the Fifth Schedule (w.e.f. 31-10-2019).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the responsibilities assigned to records officers, the powers vested in the Central Government and the Director General/head of Archives, and the functions of the Archival Advisory Board. Contraventions of specific sections are subject to penalties.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL COUNCIL FOR TEACHER EDUCATION ACT, 1993
act_identification.act_short_title: The National Council for Teacher Education Act, 1993

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of a National Council for Teacher Education with a view to achieving planned and co-ordinated development of the teacher education system throughout the country, the regulation and proper maintenance of norms and standards in the teacher education system [1][including qualifications of school teachers] and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: To establish a National Council for Teacher Education for the planned and co-ordinated development of the teacher education system. It aims to regulate and maintain norms and standards, including qualifications of school teachers, across the country.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Council', 'institution', 'teacher education', and 'school'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of the Council.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of the National Council for Teacher Education as a body corporate, specifies its head office, and details its composition.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Council.
key_sections.description: Outlines the duties and powers of the Council, including undertaking surveys, making recommendations, coordinating teacher education, laying down norms and standards, and preventing commercialisation.

key_sections.title: Power of Council to determine minimum standards of education of school teachers.
key_sections.description: Grants the Council the power to determine qualifications for persons to be recruited as teachers in various types of schools and colleges.

key_sections.title: Recognition of institutions offering course or training in teacher education.
key_sections.description: Establishes the process for institutions to apply for and obtain recognition from the Regional Committee for offering teacher education courses.

key_sections.title: Contravention of provisions of the Act and consequences thereof.
key_sections.description: Details the procedure for withdrawing recognition from institutions that contravene the Act's provisions and specifies the consequences of such withdrawal, including invalidation of qualifications.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Provides for a mechanism for persons aggrieved by orders related to recognition or permission to prefer an appeal to the Council.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, specifying various matters that can be covered by such rules.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Council to make regulations, not inconsistent with the Act or rules, for generally carrying out the Act's provisions, including norms, guidelines, and standards.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Member-Secretary, and other members of the Council (Section 3); approve establishment of regional offices (Section 3); give directions on policy matters to the Council (Section 29); supersede the Council (Section 30); make rules (Section 31); remove difficulties (Section 34).

Council: Establish as a body corporate, having perpetual succession and a common seal with power to contract, sue and be sued (Section 3); undertake surveys and studies, make recommendations, coordinate and monitor teacher education, lay down guidelines for minimum qualifications, norms for courses, standards for examinations, guidelines for fees, promote research, examine implementation, formulate schemes, prevent commercialisation (Section 12); determine minimum standards of education for school teachers (Section 12A); cause inspection of institutions (Section 13); hear appeals against recognition/permission orders (Section 18); constitute Executive Committee (Section 19); establish Regional Committees (Section 20); terminate Regional Committees (Section 21); delegate powers and functions (Section 27); make regulations (Section 32).
Regional Committees: Grant or refuse recognition to institutions (Section 14); grant or refuse permission for new courses (Section 15); withdraw recognition of institutions (Section 17).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: If an institution offers teacher education courses after withdrawal of recognition or without obtaining recognition/permission, the qualification obtained from such an institution shall not be treated as a valid qualification for employment under the Central Government, any State Government, University, or any school, college or other educational body aided by the Central or State Government (Section 17(4)).

related_acts: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 (35 of 2009)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Member-Secretary, and other members of the Council. The Council appoints its officers and other employees. The Council nominates members for the Regional Committees.

applies_to: institutions
students and teachers of the institutions
schools imparting pre-primary, primary, upper primary, secondary or senior secondary education and colleges providing senior secondary or intermediate education
teachers for schools and colleges
special_provisions: Institutions funded by the Central Government, State Government or Union territory Administration, which offered a course or training in teacher education on or after the appointed day till the academic year 2017-2018 and fulfil specified conditions, shall be deemed to have been recognised/permitted (Section 14(1) Proviso, Section 15(1) Proviso).

The continuance of any person recruited as a teacher before the commencement of the National Council for Teacher Education (Amendment) Act, 2011, shall not be adversely affected solely on the ground of non-fulfilment of qualifications specified by the Council, provided minimum qualifications are acquired within a specified period (Section 12A Proviso).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Council ensures planned and co-ordinated development and maintenance of standards through its functions (Section 12), inspections (Section 13), recognition and permission processes (Sections 14, 15), and withdrawal of recognition for contraventions (Section 17). The Central Government can issue directions (Section 29) and supersede the Council (Section 30) to ensure compliance.

act_identification.act_title: THE KALAKSHETRA FOUNDATION ACT, 1993

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of the Central Government dealing with culture

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare Kalakshetra of Madras to be an institution of national importance to provide for the establishment and incorporation of a Foundation for its administration, to make provisions for further development of Kalakshetra in accordance with the aims and objects for which Kalakshetra was founded and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act declares Kalakshetra of Madras as an institution of national importance. Its purpose is to establish and incorporate a Foundation for the administration and further development of Kalakshetra, ensuring its aims and objects are upheld.
act_overview.act_category: Institutions of Natural and Cultural Importance

chapter_titles: ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF THE ASSETS AND PROPERTIES OF KALAKSHETRA

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.

key_sections.title: Declaration of Kalakshetra as an institution of national importance.

key_sections.title: Definitions.

key_sections.title: Transfer to, and vesting in, the Central Government of the assets and properties of Kalakshetra.
key_sections.description: States that the assets and properties of Kalakshetra shall be transferred to and vest in the Central Government upon commencement of the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Foundation.

key_sections.title: The objects of Foundation.

key_sections.title: The Governing Board.
key_sections.description: Details the composition of the Governing Board of the Foundation.

key_sections.title: Governing Board to be the supreme authority of Foundation.
key_sections.description: Declares the Governing Board as the supreme authority responsible for the general superintendence, direction, and management of the Foundation's affairs.

key_sections.title: Appointment and duties of Director.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit of the Foundation.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To direct vesting of assets (Section 6), appoint Director (Section 19), give grants (Section 21), approve investments (Section 22), give directions to Foundation (Section 27), dissolve Foundation (Section 28), make rules (Section 31), approve regulations (Section 32), remove difficulties (Section 34).
Foundation: To acquire, hold and dispose of property, contract, sue and be sued (Section 8), spend sums from Fund (Section 22), make regulations (Section 32).

Academic Committee: Responsible for maintenance of standards of education, training and examination (Section 16), exercise powers and perform functions assigned by Governing Board (Section 16).

related_acts: scheme writ approved by the Madras High Court in petition No. 716 of 1985

applies_to: Kalakshetra institution at Adyar, Madras
assets and properties of Kalakshetra
employees of Kalakshetra
Kalakshetra Foundation

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government has powers to give directions to the Foundation, make rules, and approve regulations. The Foundation's accounts are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, and reports are laid before Parliament.

schedules_summary.description: Lists the constituent units of Kalakshetra, including Kalakshetra College of Fine Arts, Craft Education and Research Centre, Besant Arundale Theosophical Senior Secondary School, Besant Theosophical High School, and Besant Cultural Centre Hostel.

Details the assets and properties of Kalakshetra, divided into Part A and Part B, including land parcels with document numbers, dates, villages, taluks, districts, survey numbers, paimash numbers, and extents, as well as buildings, institutions, bank balances, and cash.

act_identification.act_title: THE PROTECTION OF HUMAN RIGHTS ACT, 1993
act_identification.act_short_title: the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution of a National Human Rights Commission, State Human Rights Commissions in States and Human Rights Courts for better protection of human rights and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes a National Human Rights Commission, State Human Rights Commissions, and Human Rights Courts. Its main purpose is to ensure better protection of human rights and to address matters connected with or incidental to human rights.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II THE NATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION
CHAPTER III FUNCTIONS AND POWERS OF THE COMMISSION
CHAPTER V STATE HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSIONS
CHAPTER VII FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT

key_definitions: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
National Commission for the Scheduled Castes
National Commission for the Scheduled Tribes

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its application to the whole of India, and its deemed commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Human Rights', 'Commission', 'armed forces', etc.

key_sections.title: Constitution of a National Human Rights Commission.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to constitute the National Human Rights Commission and outlines its composition.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Commission.

key_sections.title: Powers relating to inquiries.

key_sections.title: Steps during and after inquiry.

key_sections.title: Constitution of State Human Rights Commissions.
key_sections.description: Allows State Governments to constitute State Human Rights Commissions and specifies their composition and jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Human Rights Courts.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.

key_sections.title: Power of Commission to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Commission the power to make regulations, with Central Government approval, to carry out the Act's provisions, including its own procedure.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.

related_acts: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (49 of 2016)

act_identification.act_title: THE MANIPUR PANCHAYATI RAJ ACT, 1994

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of the State of Manipur excepting any area to which the Manipur (Hill Areas) District Council Act, 1971 (Manipur Act 76 of 1971) or the Manipur (Village Authorities in Hill Areas) Act, 1956 (Manipur Act 80 of 1956) extends, or which has been or may hereafter be declared as, or included in, a municipality under any law for the time being in force, or which has been or may hereafter be declared as, or included in a cantonment under the Cantonment Act, 1924 (2 of 1924)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution and organisation of Panchayats as units of local self-Government in the rural areas of Manipur and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto. WHEREAS it is expedient to reorganise Panchayats in rural areas of Manipur by comprehensive enactment to establish a two-tier Panchayati Raj system in the State with elected bodies at the Gram and District levels, in keeping with the Constitutional provisions relating to Panchayats for greater participation of the people and more effective implementation of rural development programmes.

key_sections.title: Definitions.

Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950)

Gram Panchayat appoints Secretary (Section 45) and other employees (Section 47). Deputy Commissioner appoints Administrative Committee or Administrator (Section 22).

whole of the State of Manipur
persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of the Panchayat at the village level

The Government has powers of inquiry, inspection, issuing directions, and suspending unlawful orders. The Chief Executive Officer has powers to requisition records and recover money. act_identification.act_title: THE TRANSPLANTATION OF HUMAN ORGANS AND TISSUES ACT, 1994
act_identification.act_short_title: The Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of the States of Goa, Himachal Pradesh and Maharashtra and to all the Union territories and it shall also apply to such other State which adopts this Act by resolution passed in that behalf under clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution. Extended to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh by Act 34 of 2019, s. 95 and the Fifth Schedule (w.e.f. 31-10-2019).

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the regulation of removal, storage and transplantation of human organs and tissues for therapeutic purposes and for the prevention of commercial dealings in human organs and tissues and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the regulation of removal, storage and transplantation of human organs or tissues or both for therapeutic purposes and for the prevention of commercial dealings in human organs or tissues or both; AND WHEREAS in Parliament has no power to make laws for the States with respect to any of the matters aforesaid except as provided in articles 249 and 250 of the Constitution; AND WHEREAS in pursuance of clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution, resolutions have been passed by all the Houses of the Legislatures of the States of Goa, Himachal Pradesh and Maharashtra to the effect that the matters aforesaid should be regulated in those States by Parliament by law;
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the removal, storage, and transplantation of human organs and tissues for therapeutic purposes. It also seeks to prevent commercial dealings in human organs and tissues, and addresses related matters.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II AUTHORITY FOR THE REMOVAL OF HUMAN ORGANS OR TISSUES OR BOTH

key_sections.title: Short title, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, initial geographical application, and commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Authority for removal of human organs or tissues or both.
key_sections.description: Outlines conditions and procedures for authorising the removal of human organs or tissues from living donors or deceased persons.

key_sections.title: Restrictions on removal and transplantation of human organs or tissues or both.
key_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on organ/tissue removal and transplantation, especially concerning non-near relatives, foreign nationals, minors, and mentally challenged persons, requiring Authorisation Committee approval.

key_sections.title: Regulation of hospitals conducting the removal, storage or transplantation of human organs or tissues or both.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration for hospitals and Tissue Banks involved in organ/tissue activities and prohibits activities for non-therapeutic purposes.

key_sections.title: Appropriate Authority.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Appropriate Authority and outlines its functions, including registration, enforcement of standards, and investigation of complaints.

key_sections.title: Powers of Appropriate Authority.
key_sections.description: Grants the Appropriate Authority powers of a civil court for summoning, discovery, and issuing search warrants.

key_sections.title: Registration of hospitals engaged in removal, storage or transplantation of human organs or tissues or both.
key_sections.description: Details the requirements and process for hospitals to register for organ/tissue removal, storage, or transplantation activities.

key_sections.title: Punishment for removal of human organ without authority.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for unauthorised removal of human organs or tissues, including imprisonment and fines, and action against medical practitioners.

key_sections.title: Punishment for commercial dealings in human organs.
key_sections.description: Defines and penalises various forms of commercial dealings in human organs, including making/receiving payments, advertising, and abetting false documentation.

key_sections.title: Punishment for illegal dealings in human tissues.
key_sections.description: Defines and penalises various forms of illegal dealings in human tissues, similar to those for human organs.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes, covering various procedural and operational aspects.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Ear Drums and Ear Bones (Authority for Use for Therapeutic Purposes) Act, 1982 and the Eyes (Authority for Use for Therapeutic Purposes) Act, 1982, with savings for previous operations.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint Appropriate Authorities for Union territories, establish National Human Organs and Tissues Removal and Storage Network, maintain a national registry of donors and recipients, and make rules.
State Government: To appoint Appropriate Authorities for States, constitute Authorisation Committees, and constitute Advisory Committees.

Appropriate Authority: To grant, renew, suspend or cancel registration of hospitals and Tissue Banks; enforce standards; investigate complaints; inspect hospitals and Tissue Banks; and exercise powers of a civil court.
Authorisation Committee: To approve removal and transplantation of human organs or tissues or both in specific cases (e.g., non-near relatives, foreign nationals, swap donations).
Registered Medical Practitioner: To remove human organs or tissues or both for therapeutic purposes, certify brain-stem death, and explain effects to donor and recipient.
Person in charge of hospital or prison: To authorise removal of organs/tissues from unclaimed bodies.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Punishment for removal of human organ without authority (Section 18): Imprisonment up to ten years and fine up to twenty lakh rupees for services providers; for registered medical practitioners, removal from State Medical Council register for three years for first offence and permanently for subsequent offence. For human tissue without authority, imprisonment up to three years and fine up to five lakh rupees. Punishment for commercial dealings in human organs (Section 19): Imprisonment not less than five years but may extend to ten years, and fine not less than twenty lakh rupees but may extend to one crore rupees. Punishment for illegal dealings in human tissues (Section 19A): Imprisonment not less than one year but may extend to three years, and fine not less than five lakh rupees but may extend to twenty-five lakh rupees. Punishment for contravention of any other provision (Section 20): Imprisonment up to five years or fine up to twenty lakh rupees.

repealed_acts: The Ear Drums and Ear Bones (Authority for Use for Therapeutic Purposes) Act, 1982 (28 of 1982)
The Eyes (Authority for Use for Therapeutic Purposes) Act, 1982 (29 of 1982)
related_acts: Persons With Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Right and Full Participation) Act, 1995 (1 of 1996)

authorities_established: National Human Organs and Tissues Removal and Storage Network
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government: Appoints Appropriate Authorities for Union territories, constitutes Advisory Committees. State Government: Appoints Appropriate Authorities for States, constitutes Authorisation Committees, constitutes Advisory Committees. Registered medical practitioner in charge of hospital: Nominates independent medical practitioners for brain-stem death certification.

applies_to: States of Goa, Himachal Pradesh and Maharashtra.
All Union territories (including Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh).
Any other State which adopts this Act by resolution.
Hospitals, Tissue Banks, medical practitioners, donors, recipients, and any person involved in the removal, storage, or transplantation of human organs or tissues.
exemptions: Dealings with a deceased person's body or part thereof that would have been lawful if this Act had not been passed (Section 8(1)).
Removal of eyes or ears from a dead body for therapeutic purposes by a registered medical practitioner at any place (Section 10(2)).
special_provisions: Initial application to specific states and Union territories, with provision for adoption by other states.

Prior approval of Authorisation Committee required for foreign national donors/recipients who are near relatives, and prohibition if recipient is foreign national and donor is Indian national unless near relatives (Section 9(1A)).
Specific manner prescribed for removal of organs/tissues from a minor before death for transplantation (Section 9(1B)).
Prohibition of removal of organs/tissues from a mentally challenged person before death for transplantation (Section 9(1C)).
Provision for swap donations with prior approval of the Authorisation Committee (Section 9(3A)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Appropriate Authority is responsible for granting/renewing/suspending/cancelling registrations, enforcing standards, investigating complaints, and inspecting facilities. Offences are punishable with imprisonment and fines, and tried by Metropolitan Magistrates or Judicial Magistrates of the first class.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class

act_identification.act_title: THE MANIPUR MUNICIPALITIES ACT, 1994

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of the State of Manipur except the Hill Areas to which the Manipur (Hill Areas) District Council Act, 1971 (Manipur Act 76 of 1971) extends or any area which is included in a Cantonment under the Cantonment Act, 1924 (2 of 1924).

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for constitution and organisation of municipalities in the Urban areas of Manipur and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish and organize municipalities in the urban areas of Manipur. It also addresses various related matters concerning their functioning and administration.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Constitution of municipalities.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Governor to constitute Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils, and Municipal Corporations for different urban areas.

key_sections.title: Reservation of seats.
key_sections.description: Mandates reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women in municipalities.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of the Chairperson.
key_sections.description: Outlines the duties and authority of the Chairperson, including presiding over meetings, financial oversight, and emergency powers.

key_sections.title: Obligatory functions of the municipality.
key_sections.description: Lists essential services and duties that every municipality must provide, such as lighting, cleaning, road maintenance, and public health.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Executive Officers.

key_sections.title: Municipal property and vesting thereof.

key_sections.title: Finance Commission for municipalities.
key_sections.description: States that the State Finance Commission will review municipal finances and make recommendations to the Governor.

key_sections.title: Taxes which may be imposed.

key_sections.title: Powers of State Government to make rules.

key_sections.title: Election to the municipalities.

powers_conferred: Power to acquire, hold and dispose of property and to contract (Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council)
Power to determine strength of its employees (Nagar Panchayat and Council)
Power to appoint its officers and employees (Nagar Panchayat and Council)
Power to make rules (State Government, Section 48, 208)

Power to remove obstructions, encroachments and projections in or on public road, etc. (Nagar Panchayat or Council)
Power of the District Magistrate and Sub-Divisional Magistrate to remove encroachment summarily on requisition by the Government
Power to attach brackets for lamps (Nagar Panchayat or Council)
Power to require owners to clear noxious vegetation (Nagar Panchayat or Council)
Power to require owners to improve bad drainage (Nagar Panchayat or Council)
Power to require unwholesome tanks or private premises to be cleansed or drained (Nagar Panchayat or Council)
Power of Government to prohibit cultivation, use of manure, or irrigation injurious to health

Delegation of powers of State Government
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties are prescribed for various offenses including: Councillors/officers having interest in contracts (fine up to five thousand rupees); default in furnishing tax returns (fine up to five hundred rupees, further fifty rupees/day) or obstruction of assessor (fine up to two thousand rupees); keeping unlicensed carts/animals (fine not exceeding four times the fee plus licence fee); refusing to pay market rents/tolls/fees (fine up to five hundred rupees); disobeying public road use orders (fine up to two hundred rupees); encroachment on public roads (fine up to two thousand five hundred rupees, further two hundred rupees/day); unauthorized use of public roads by vendors (fine up to two thousand five hundred rupees, further five hundred rupees for subsequent offence); disobeying requisitions for obstruction removal (fine up to two thousand rupees, further one hundred rupees/day); destroying road names/building numbers (fine up to two hundred rupees); building without sanction (fine up to one thousand rupees, further two hundred rupees/day); disobedience of building construction orders (fine up to five hundred rupees, further one hundred rupees/day); using building unfit for human habitation (fine up to five hundred rupees, further one hundred rupees/day); disobeying requisitions for dangerous buildings/ruins (penalty up to one thousand rupees, further two hundred rupees/day); disobeying requisitions for noxious vegetation/bad drainage/unwholesome tanks (fine up to one thousand rupees, further two hundred rupees/day); allowing sewer water on public roads (fine up to two hundred rupees, daily fine up to fifty rupees); disobeying land drainage requisitions (fine up to two hundred rupees, further fifty rupees/day); placing rubbish on public roads (fine up to five hundred rupees); occupier not removing filth (fine up to five hundred rupees); throwing offensive matter on public roads (fine up to five hundred rupees); slaughtering animals at unauthorized places (fine up to five hundred rupees); using premises for offensive trades in contravention of notice (fine up to four hundred rupees/day); failing to close markets/stalls as ordered (fine up to five thousand rupees, attending such market fine up to five hundred rupees); failure to give information of infectious diseases (fine up to five hundred rupees); letting infected house (fine up to two thousand rupees); burying/burning corpses at unauthorized places (fine up to five hundred rupees); and general violation of Act provisions where no specific penalty is provided (fine not exceeding five hundred rupees for each day of continuing violation).

act_identification.act_title: THE NEW DELHI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL ACT, 1994

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes various offences and penalties, detailed in Chapter XX and the Tenth Schedule. Penalties include fines, which can be daily fines for continuing contraventions, and in some cases, simple imprisonment. For instance, erecting a building without sanction (Section 237(1)) can lead to simple imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to Rs. 5000, or both. Failure to give notice of transfer of property (Section 74) incurs a fine of Rs. 50. A general penalty for non-compliance with notices or contravention of the Act, where no specific penalty is provided, is a fine up to one hundred rupees, with an additional fine for continuing failure.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement involves issuing notices, bills, orders, and requisitions. Taxes are recovered as arrears through distress and sale of movable property, or attachment and sale of immovable property. Vehicles and animals can be seized for non-payment of tax. Police officers assist in arresting offenders. The Chairperson can execute work if a person fails to comply with a notice. The Central Government can issue directions to the Council for proper performance of duties.

Municipal magistrates are appointed to try offences and handle complaints concerning nuisances.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever unlawfully occupies any airport premises shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six years and with fine. Whoever fails to comply with any order of the eviction officer or the High Court under Chapter VA shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and with fine. If any person who has been evicted from any airport premises under Chapter VA again occupies the premises without authority, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years and with fine (Section 28N). Wilful failure to comply with any direction issued under Section 37 is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both (Section 37(3)). Contravention of certain regulations may be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees and in the case of a continuing contravention with an additional fine which may extend to twenty rupees for every day during which such contravention continues after conviction for the first such contravention (Section 42(3)).

act_identification.act_title: THE PRE-CONCEPTION AND PRE-NATAL DIAGNOSTIC TECHNIQUES (PROHIBITION OF SEX SELECTION) ACT, 1994
act_identification.act_short_title: the Pre-conception and Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry or Department of Family Welfare

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the prohibition of sex selection, before or after conception, and for regulation of pre-natal diagnostic techniques for the purposes of detecting genetic abnormalities or metabolic disorders or chromosomal abnormalities or certain congenital malformations or sex-linked disorders and for the prevention of their misuse for sex determination leading to female foeticide and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to prohibit sex selection before or after conception and to regulate pre-natal diagnostic techniques. Its primary objective is to prevent the misuse of these techniques for sex determination, which contributes to female foeticide, while allowing their legitimate use for detecting genetic abnormalities and disorders.

chapter_titles: REGULATION OF GENETIC COUNSELLING CENTRES, GENETIC LABORATORIES AND GENETIC CLINICS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Appropriate Authority', 'Genetic Clinic', 'sex selection', and 'pre-natal diagnostic techniques'.

key_sections.title: Regulation of Genetic Counselling Centres, Genetic Laboratories and Genetic Clinics.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration for Genetic Counselling Centres, Genetic Laboratories, and Genetic Clinics, and requires qualified personnel for their operation.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of sex selection.
key_sections.description: Explicitly prohibits any person, including specialists, from conducting or aiding in sex selection on a woman, man, or any related biological material.

key_sections.title: Prohibition on sale of ultrasound machine, etc., to persons, laboratories, clinics, etc., not registered under the Act.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the sale of ultrasound machines or other sex-detecting equipment to entities not registered under the Act.

key_sections.title: Regulation of pre-natal diagnostic techniques.
key_sections.description: Regulates the use of pre-natal diagnostic techniques, specifying the permissible purposes (e.g., detecting genetic abnormalities) and conditions under which they can be conducted, including record-keeping requirements.

key_sections.title: Written consent of pregnant woman and prohibition of communicating the sex of foetus.
key_sections.description: Requires written consent from the pregnant woman after explaining procedures and prohibits communicating the sex of the foetus to her or her relatives.

key_sections.title: Determination of sex prohibited.
key_sections.description: Prohibits Genetic Counselling Centres, Laboratories, Clinics, and any person from conducting pre-natal diagnostic techniques, including ultrasonography, for the purpose of determining or selecting the sex of a foetus.

key_sections.description: Prohibits all forms of advertisement related to pre-natal sex determination or sex selection and prescribes punishment for contravention.

key_sections.title: Offences and penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for medical practitioners, owners of centres, and individuals who contravene the Act's provisions, including those who seek sex selection, with varying punishments for first and subsequent offences.

Appropriate Authority: Grant, suspend or cancel registration, enforce standards, investigate complaints, take legal action against sex selection, create public awareness, supervise implementation, recommend modifications, take action on Advisory Committee recommendations, summon persons, demand production of documents, issue search warrants.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of advertisement prohibition (S.22): Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to 10,000 rupees. Contravention by medical geneticist, gynaecologist, registered medical practitioner, or owner/employee of Centre/Laboratory/Clinic (S.23(1)): Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to 10,000 rupees for first offence; up to 5 years and 50,000 rupees for subsequent conviction. Seeking aid for sex selection or prohibited pre-natal diagnostic techniques (S.23(3)): Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to 50,000 rupees for first offence; up to 5 years and 1 lakh rupees for subsequent offence. General contravention of Act/rules where no specific punishment is provided (S.25): Imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to 1,000 rupees or both; additional fine of 500 rupees per day for continuing contravention. Offences by companies (S.26): Company and responsible persons deemed guilty. Offences are cognizable, non-bailable, non-compoundable (S.27).
