key_sections.description: Outlines the primary goals of the University, including promoting advanced knowledge, integrated courses, and social justice.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers of the University, such as providing instruction, granting degrees, conducting research, and establishing campuses.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Defines the geographical area of the University's jurisdiction as the whole of Uttar Pradesh.

key_sections.title: The Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor and outlines the Visitor's powers of review, inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the designated officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and Registrar.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main governing bodies of the University, such as the Board of Management and Academic Council.

key_sections.title: Power to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Statutes can be made, covering constitution of authorities, appointments, and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Details the matters for which Ordinances can be made, including student admission, courses of study, and examinations.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees.
key_sections.description: Mandates written contracts for employees and provides for arbitration in case of disputes.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make provisions to remove difficulties in implementing the Act for a limited period.

key_sections.title: Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Requires publication of statutory instruments and their presentation to Parliament.

powers_conferred: University: To provide instruction and research facilities, grant degrees, organise extra-mural studies, confer honorary degrees, provide distance education, institute and appoint to academic positions, recognise institutions, create administrative posts, cooperate with other universities, establish campuses/centres, institute awards, maintain colleges/institutions, provide research/advisory services, organise courses, make special arrangements for women students, appoint visiting faculty, confer autonomous status, determine admission standards, fix quotas for SC/ST, demand fees, supervise student residences, lay down employee conditions, regulate discipline, promote employee welfare, receive donations, acquire/manage property, borrow money (with Central Government approval).
Visitor: To appoint Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor, review work and progress, cause inspection and inquiry, issue directions, annul proceedings not in conformity with the Act/Statutes/Ordinances.

Board of Management: To make new/amend/repeal Statutes (with Visitor's assent), manage and administer revenue/property, create teaching/academic/administrative posts, appoint staff, grant leave, regulate discipline, manage finances, invest money, transfer property, provide infrastructure, enter contracts, redress grievances, appoint examiners, select common seal, make special arrangements for women students, delegate powers, institute awards, appoint visiting faculty.
Academic Council: To coordinate and supervise academic policies, bring about inter-School coordination, consider academic matters, frame regulations.
Planning Board: To review educational programmes, organise education structure, create value-oriented atmosphere, develop teaching-learning processes, advise on development, monitor implementation.
Vice-Chancellor: To exercise general supervision and control, take immediate action, review decisions of authorities, maintain discipline, convene meetings.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Visitor: Appoints Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, first Vice-Chancellor, first Registrar, first Finance Officer, first Board of Management members, first Academic Council members, first Planning Board members. Board of Management: Appoints Pro-Vice-Chancellors (on VC's recommendation), Registrar (on Selection Committee recommendation), Finance Officer (on Selection Committee recommendation), other officers (as prescribed by Statutes), Heads of Departments (on VC's recommendation), Proctor (on VC's recommendation), Librarian (on Selection Committee recommendation), Professors, Readers, Lecturers, academic staff, Principals (on Selection Committee recommendation), administrative, ministerial and other posts. Vice-Chancellor: Appoints Deans of Schools, persons to perform duties of Registrar/Finance Officer when vacant, temporary teaching staff. Selection Committee: Recommends for appointment of Professor, Reader, Lecturer, Registrar, Finance Officer, Librarian, Principals.

applies_to: all persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race, class, place of domicile
employees of the University
students of the University
special_provisions: special provisions for the employment or promotion of educational interests of women, physically handicapped or of persons belonging to the weaker sections of the society and, in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.
adequate percentage of seats for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes
special arrangements in respect of the residence discipline and teaching of women students

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Board of Management (for Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations); Visitor (for Statutes in exceptional circumstances); Vice-Chancellor (for first Ordinances); Authorities of the University (for Regulations).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor has powers of review, inspection, inquiry, issuing directions, and annulment of non-conforming proceedings. The Vice-Chancellor exercises general supervision, control, and disciplinary powers. The Board of Management manages administrative and financial affairs and regulates employee discipline. Disputes involving employees or students are referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration.

schedules_summary.description: Details the objects of the University, including promoting advanced knowledge, integrated courses, social justice, national integration, and providing for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

Contains the Statutes of the University, which prescribe the manner of appointment, powers, duties, and terms of service for officers and authorities, constitution of committees, disciplinary procedures, and other administrative and academic regulations.

act_identification.act_title: THE CABLE TELEVISION NETWORKS (REGULATION) ACT, 1995

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the operation of cable television networks in the country and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the operation of cable television networks across the country and address matters connected with or incidental to such operations, ensuring proper functioning and adherence to prescribed codes.

chapter_titles:
CHAPTER II
REGULATION OF CABLE TELEVISION NETWORK

CHAPTER III
SEIZURE AND CONFISCATION OF CERTAIN EQUIPMENT

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Act's name, geographical reach (whole of India), and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as "authorised officer," "cable operator," "cable service," "programme," and "subscriber."

key_sections.title: Cable television network not to be operated except after registration.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration for any person operating a cable television network.

key_sections.title: Registration as cable operator.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for registration and renewal, including eligibility criteria, application procedures, and conditions.

key_sections.title: Transmission of programmes through digital addressable systems, etc.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to mandate digital addressable systems for programme transmission and specifies related provisions for channels and tariffs.

key_sections.title: Right of way for cable operators and permission by public authority.
key_sections.description: Grants cable operators the right to lay cables and erect posts on public property, subject to permission and conditions.

key_sections.title: Programme code.
key_sections.description: Requires all programmes transmitted via cable service to conform to a prescribed programme code.

key_sections.title: Advertisement code.
key_sections.description: Requires all advertisements transmitted via cable service to conform to a prescribed advertisement code.

key_sections.title: Compulsory transmission of certain channels.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to mandate the carriage of Doordarshan or Parliamentary channels by cable operators.

key_sections.title: Power to seize equipment used for operating cable television network.
key_sections.description: Authorizes officers to seize equipment for contravention of specific provisions related to operation, digital systems, codes, and standards.

key_sections.title: Confiscation.
key_sections.description: States that seized equipment is liable to confiscation if the operator does not register within thirty days from the date of seizure.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of provisions of this Act.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contraventions, including advisory, censure, warning, fines up to one lakh rupees, and suspension or revocation of registration.

key_sections.title: Power to prohibit transmission of certain programmes in public interest.
key_sections.description: Grants power to prohibit transmission of programmes that violate codes or promote disharmony, hatred, or disturb public tranquility.

key_sections.title: Power to prohibit operation of cable television network in public interest.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to prohibit cable network operations or regulate/prohibit channels/programmes in public interest, national security, or for other specified reasons.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power on the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions, covering various aspects like eligibility, application forms, codes, and interference standards.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To notify authorised officers and registering authorities.
Central Government: To prescribe eligibility criteria and conditions for cable operators.
Central Government: To suspend or revoke registration of cable operators.
Central Government: To make digital transmission obligatory and specify dates for implementation.
Central Government: To direct the Authority (TRAI) to specify free-to-air channels and fix tariffs for basic service tier.
Central Government: To lay down guidelines for State Governments regarding right of way for cable operators.
Central Government: To specify Doordarshan or Parliamentary channels for mandatory carriage by cable operators.
Central Government: To prescribe standards relating to interference with telecommunication systems.
Central Government: To inspect cable networks and services, or authorize officers/agencies to do so.
Central Government: To prohibit transmission of certain programmes in public interest.
Central Government: To prohibit operation of cable television networks in public interest.

Central Government: To regulate or prohibit transmission or re-transmission of any channel or programme in the interest of sovereignty, security, friendly relations, public order, decency or morality.
Central Government: To make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.
Authorised Officer: To seize equipment used for operating cable television network in contravention of provisions.
Authorised Officer: To prohibit transmission of certain programmes in public interest.
Authorised Officer: To make a complaint in writing for cognizance of offences.
Registering Authority: To register or renew registration of cable operators.
Registering Authority: To refuse registration or renewal for specified reasons.
Public Authority: To permit cable operators to lay and maintain cables and erect posts on property under its control or management.
Public Authority: To require removal or shifting of cables/posts.
Designated Officer (as prescribed by rules): To impose penalties for contravention of the Act.
Designated Officer (as prescribed by rules): To suspend or revoke registration in cases of repeated contraventions.
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Authority): To specify free-to-air channels and fix tariffs for basic service tier (if directed by Central Government).
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Authority): To specify information to be publicized by cable operators.
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Authority): To specify format and intervals for information from cable operators.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever contravenes any of the provisions of this Act shall be liable for the first contravention with advisory, censure, warning, or a penalty up to twenty thousand rupees, or both. For every subsequent contravention within a period of three years, the penalty may extend to one lakh rupees, or both. In cases of more than three contraventions over a period of three years, the designated officer may, in addition to the penalty, suspend or revoke the registration. Offences committed by companies are also addressed, holding persons in charge and the company liable, with provisions for directors, managers, etc., if the offence was committed with their consent, connivance, or negligence.

repealed_acts: The Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Ordinance, 1995 (Ord. 3 of 1995)
related_acts: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997 (24 of 1997)
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 (63 of 1986)
Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act, 1950 (12 of 1950)
Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 (21 of 1954)
Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (37 of 1954)
Trade and Merchandise Marks, Act, 1958 (43 of 1958)
Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act, 1986 (60 of 1986)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to notify officers to be 'authorised officers' and to specify the 'registering authority'.

applies_to: Any person who provides cable service through a cable television network
Every cable operator
special_provisions: Different dates may be specified for different States, cities, towns or areas for mandatory digital transmission.
Different numbers of free-to-air channels may be specified for different States, cities, towns or areas.
In areas where digital addressable system has not been introduced, the mandatory carriage of Doordarshan channels is limited to two terrestrial channels and one regional language channel.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is primarily through mandatory registration of cable operators, adherence to prescribed programme and advertisement codes, maintenance of registers, use of standard equipment, and non-interference with telecommunication systems. It includes powers of inspection, seizure, and confiscation of equipment for contraventions. Penalties range from advisory and fines to suspension or revocation of registration. The Central Government also has powers to prohibit transmission of certain programmes or operation of networks in public interest.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Act except upon a complaint in writing made by any authorised officer. Appeals against confiscation orders lie to the court to which an appeal lies from the decision of such court.

act_identification.act_title: THE TEXTILE UNDERTAKINGS (NATIONALISATION) ACT, 1995

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to acquire and transfer specified textile undertakings to the Central Government and then to the National Textile Corporation. This is done to augment the production and distribution of cloth and yarn, serve public interest, and ensure the continued employment of workmen in these undertakings.

chapter_titles: ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF THE TEXTILE UNDERTAKINGS
PROVISIONS RELATING TO EMPLOYEES OF TEXTILE UNDERTAKINGS

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its commencement dates, with sections 31 and 32 coming into force immediately and others retrospectively from April 1, 1994.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'Commissioner', 'National Textile Corporation', 'owner', and 'textile undertaking'.

key_sections.title: Acquisition of rights of owners and vesting of the textile undertakings.
key_sections.description: States that on the appointed day, the rights, title, and interest of owners in textile undertakings are transferred to and vest absolutely in the Central Government, and then immediately in the National Textile Corporation.

key_sections.title: General effect of vesting.
key_sections.description: Details what the textile undertakings include (assets, rights, liabilities) upon vesting, how they are freed from encumbrances, and the substitution of the National Textile Corporation in licenses and instruments.

key_sections.title: Owner to be liable for certain prior liabilities.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the owner remains liable for most prior liabilities, but specifies certain liabilities (e.g., government loans, employee dues after takeover) that become the Central Government's responsibility, discharged by NTC.

key_sections.title: Payment of amount to owners of textile undertakings.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to pay a specified amount to the owners of each textile undertaking for the transfer and vesting of their rights and interests.

key_sections.title: Employment of certain employees to continue.
key_sections.description: Ensures the continued employment of workmen and other employees of the textile undertakings by the National Textile Corporation with existing terms and conditions, subject to alteration or termination by NTC.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Commissioners of Payments.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of Commissioners of Payments by the Central Government to disburse amounts to owners and claimants, defining their powers and duties.

key_sections.title: Priority of claims.
key_sections.description: Establishes the order of priority for claims against the textile undertakings, as detailed in the Second Schedule, for the purpose of disbursement by the Commissioner.

key_sections.title: Act to override all other enactments.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws, instruments, or court orders.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for persons who wrongfully withhold property, obtain possession, or destroy assets of the textile undertakings, or make false claims.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, including specific matters like intimations and handling of provident funds.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Textile Undertakings (Nationalisation) Ordinance, 1995, while saving actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint Commissioners of Payments (Section 17).
Central Government: To make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act (Section 36).
Central Government: To remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions (Section 37).
Central Government: To delegate its powers under the Act (Section 35).
Central Government: To assume undischarged liabilities of owners (Section 27).
National Textile Corporation: To exercise powers of general superintendence, direction, control and management of textile undertakings (Section 10).
National Textile Corporation: To transfer textile undertakings or parts thereof to subsidiary textile corporations (Section 6).
National Textile Corporation: To transfer, mortgage, sell or otherwise dispose of assets of textile undertakings with Central Government sanction (Section 11).
National Textile Corporation: To receive money due to textile undertakings realised after the appointed day (Section 19).
National Textile Corporation: To discharge liabilities assumed by the Central Government (Section 27).
Commissioner of Payments: To appoint persons to assist him and authorise them to exercise powers (Section 17).
Commissioner of Payments: To regulate his own procedure and have powers of a civil court for investigation (Section 23).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who wrongfully withholds property, obtains possession of, or retains property, wilfully withholds or fails to furnish documents, fails to deliver assets/books/documents, wrongfully removes or destroys property, or prefers a false claim, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both. Companies committing offences are also liable, with provisions for directors/managers/officers.

repealed_acts: The Textile Undertakings (Nationalisation) Ordinance, 1995 (Ord. 6 of 1995)
related_acts: Textile Undertakings (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1983 (40 of 1983)
Laxmirattan and Atherton West Cotton Mills (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1976 (98 of 1976)
State Bank of India Act, 1955 (23 of 1955)
State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959 (38 of 1959)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 (5 of 1970)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980 (40 of 1980)
Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint Commissioners of Payments.

applies_to: Textile undertakings specified in the First Schedule
Owners of the specified textile undertakings
Employees of the specified textile undertakings
special_provisions: Lease-hold rights of textile undertakings shall continue to remain vested in the Central Government, with NTC discharging rents (Section 3(3)).
No court shall have jurisdiction to order divestment from the National Textile Corporation of property vested in it (Section 3(4)).
Discontinued textile operations, if revived, are deemed continued, and no suit can be maintained against NTC for discontinuance (Section 4(8)).
No proceeding for the winding up of a textile company or appointment of a receiver shall lie or be proceeded with in any court except with the consent of the Central Government (Section 34).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act provides for the acquisition and transfer of textile undertakings, payment of amounts to owners through Commissioners of Payments, and management by the National Textile Corporation. It also includes provisions for penalties for non-compliance and overriding other enactments.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Principal civil court of original jurisdiction (for appeals against Commissioner's decision and disputes over owner's right to payment), High Court (if Commissioner is a High Court Judge).

schedules_summary.description: Lists the names of textile undertakings, their respective owners, and the amount in rupees specified against each undertaking for payment.

Outlines the order of priorities for the discharge of liabilities in respect of a textile undertaking, categorized into 'Post-take-over management period' (Category I, II) and 'Pre-take-over management period' (Category III, IV, V, VI).

act_identification.act_title: THE WAQF ACT, 1995

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the better administration of [1][Auqaf] and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to ensure the proper administration, maintenance, control, and development of Auqaf (religious endowments) and their properties. It establishes regulatory bodies like the Central Waqf Council and State Waqf Boards, defines their powers and functions, and provides mechanisms for registration, financial oversight, dispute resolution, and protection against alienation and encroachment of waqf properties.

chapter_titles: ESTABLISHMENT OF BOARDS AND THEIR FUNCTIONS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Application of the Act.
key_sections.description: States that the Act applies to all auqaf, with an exception for Durgah Khawaja Saheb, Ajmer.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Preliminary survey of auqaf.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to appoint a Survey Commissioner for surveying auqaf and outlines the survey process and particulars to be collected.

key_sections.title: Establishment and constitution of Central Waqf Council.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment and composition of the Central Waqf Council to advise governments and Boards on waqf administration.

key_sections.title: Incorporation.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of a Board of Auqaf in each State as a body corporate.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of the Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the general superintendence powers and specific functions of the Waqf Board over auqaf.

key_sections.title: Registration.
key_sections.description: Requires every waqf to be registered at the Board's office and specifies the application process and particulars.

key_sections.title: Alienation of waqf property without sanction of Board to be void.
key_sections.description: Declares alienation (sale, gift, exchange, mortgage, transfer) of waqf property without Board sanction as void.

key_sections.title: Penalty for alienation of waqf property without sanction of Board.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including rigorous imprisonment and vesting of property in the Board, for unauthorized alienation of waqf property.

key_sections.title: Removal of encroachment from waqf property.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Chief Executive Officer to initiate proceedings for removal of encroachments on waqf property.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Specifies penalties for mutawallis failing to comply with various duties under the Act.

key_sections.title: Removal of mutawalli.
key_sections.description: Provides grounds and procedure for the Board to remove a mutawalli from office.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Tribunals, etc.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of Tribunals for determining disputes related to waqf or waqf property and outlines their composition and powers.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall override inconsistent provisions in other laws.

Central Government's power to make rules for Chapter III (Section 12)
District Magistrate, Additional District Magistrate or Sub-Divisional Magistrate's power to implement Board directions (Section 28)
Chief Executive Officer's power to inspect records, registers, etc. (Section 29)

Board's general superintendence, administration, scheme settlement, budget approval, mutawalli appointment/removal, property recovery, lease sanction, Waqf Fund administration, property inspection, waqf land development (Section 32)
Chief Executive Officer's power to inspect for mutawalli negligence/misappropriation (Section 33)
Board's power to appoint Executive Officers for auqaf (Section 38)
Board's power to inquire and re-appropriate funds of defunct auqaf (Section 39)
Board's power to direct or cause waqf registration and amend registers (Section 41)
Board's power to pay mutawalli's dues and recover from waqf property (Section 58)
Board's power to appoint mutawallis in case of vacancy or dispute (Section 63)
State Government's power to appoint/remove mutawallis where deed/decree specifies court/authority (Section 66)
Board's power to frame administration schemes for waqf (Section 69)
Chief Executive Officer's power to direct banks/persons to pay contributions from waqf funds (Section 73)
Board's power to borrow with State Government sanction (Section 75)
Central Government's power to regulate secular activities of auqaf (Section 96)
State Government's power to supersede the Board (Section 99)
Board and Chief Executive Officer's power to demand documents related to waqf (Section 105)
Central Government's power to establish common Boards for multiple States (Section 106)
State Government's power to make rules (Section 109)
Board's power to make regulations (Section 110)
Central Government's power to remove difficulties (Section 113)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 52A prescribes rigorous imprisonment up to two years for alienation or purchase of waqf property without Board sanction, with the property vesting in the Board. Section 61 outlines penalties for mutawallis, including fines up to ten thousand rupees for non-compliance with duties (e.g., registration, furnishing accounts) and imprisonment up to six months and/or fine up to fifteen thousand rupees for concealing waqf existence or providing false information. properties given or donated by persons not professing Islam for support of certain waqf
exemptions: Durgah Khawaja Saheb, Ajmer to which the Durgah Khawaja Saheb Act, 1955 (36 of 1955) applies.

Special provision for reorganisation of certain Boards (Section 102)

Application of Act to properties given or donated by persons not professing Islam for support of certain waqf (Section 104)
Special provision as to evacuee waqf properties (Section 108)

act_identification.act_title: THE TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT BOARD ACT, 1995

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution of a Board for payment of equity capital or any other financial assistance to industrial concerns and other agencies attempting development and commercial application of indigenous technology or adapting imported technology to wider domestic applications and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to establish the Technology Development Board to provide financial assistance, including equity capital, to industrial concerns and other agencies for the development and commercial application of indigenous technology or adaptation of imported technology for wider domestic use.

chapter_titles: APPLICATION FOR GRANT OF FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE

key_sections.title: Constitution and incorporation of the Board.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Board.

key_sections.title: Application for grant of financial assistance, etc.
key_sections.description: Details the process for applying for financial assistance and the Board's power to grant or refuse such applications.

key_sections.title: Fund for Technology Development and Application.

key_sections.title: Power of the Central Government to issue directions.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to supersede the Board.

key_sections.title: Members, officers and employees of the Board to be public servants.

Board: Appoint committees for efficient discharge of duties (Section 5(1)).

research and development institutions engaged in developing indigenous technology or adaptation of imported technology for commercial application

act_identification.act_title: THE DEPOSITORIES ACT, 1996

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for regulation of depositories in securities and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate depositories involved in securities and address related matters, including the rights and obligations of depositories, participants, issuers, and beneficial owners, and to establish mechanisms for enforcement and appeals.

chapter_titles: RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF DEPOSITORIES, PARTICIPANTS, ISSUERS AND BENEFICIAL OWNERS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'beneficial owner', 'depository', 'issuer', and 'security'.

key_sections.title: Certificate of commencement of business by depositories.
key_sections.description: Mandates that no depository can operate without a certificate of commencement of business from the Board, ensuring adequate systems and safeguards.

key_sections.title: Surrender of certificate of security.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for a person to surrender physical security certificates to an issuer to avail depository services, leading to dematerialisation.

key_sections.title: Securities in depositories to be in fungible form.
key_sections.description: States that all securities held by a depository must be dematerialised and fungible, and exempts certain Companies Act provisions.

key_sections.title: Rights of depositories and beneficial owner.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that a depository is the registered owner for transfer purposes, but the beneficial owner retains all rights and liabilities of the securities.

key_sections.title: Pledge or hypothecation of securities held in a depository.
key_sections.description: Allows beneficial owners to pledge or hypothecate their securities held in a depository, with intimation to and record by the depository.

key_sections.title: Depositories to indemnify loss in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Requires depositories to indemnify beneficial owners for losses caused by the negligence of the depository or its participants.

key_sections.title: Power of Board to call for information and enquiry.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board powers to call for information and conduct enquiries or inspections related to securities held in a depository.

key_sections.title: Power of Board to give directions in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Board to issue directions to depositories, participants, or issuers to protect investors or ensure orderly development of the securities market.

key_sections.title: Power to adjudicate.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Board to appoint adjudicating officers to conduct inquiries and impose penalties for contraventions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Offences.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for contravening the Act, rules, regulations, or bye-laws, or failing to comply with directions.

key_sections.title: Appeal to Securities Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals against orders of the Board or adjudicating officers to the Securities Appellate Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power on the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of Board to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Confers power on the Board to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules to carry out its purposes.

key_sections.title: Power of depositories to make bye-laws.
key_sections.description: Grants depositories the power to make bye-laws, with Board approval, covering various operational aspects.

powers_conferred: Power of Board to call for information and enquiry (Section 18)
Power of Board to give directions in certain cases (Section 19)
Power of Board to adjudicate and impose penalties (Section 19H)
Power of Central Government to make rules (Section 24)
Power of Board to make regulations (Section 25)
Power of depositories to make bye-laws (Section 26)
Power of Central Government to grant immunity from prosecution (Section 22B)
Power of Central Government to establish Special Courts (Section 22C)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines various failures as offences, including failure to furnish information, enter agreements, redress investor grievances, delay dematerialisation, reconcile records, comply with Board directions, or conduct business fairly. Penalties for these failures range from not less than one lakh rupees to one crore rupees, or up to twenty-five crore rupees or three times the gain for unfair business conduct. General contraventions of the Act, rules, regulations, or bye-laws, or failure to pay penalties or comply with directions, can lead to imprisonment for up to ten years, or a fine up to twenty-five crore rupees, or both.

Cost and Works Accountants Act, 1959 (23 of 1959)
International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019

regulatory_bodies: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Board)

applies_to: Depositories
Participants
Issuers
Beneficial owners
Persons making an issue of securities
Persons registered as intermediaries under SEBI Act, 1992

Powers of the Board do not extend to an International Financial Services Centre (Section 23G).
special_provisions: Powers of the Board do not apply to International Financial Services Centres, where the International Financial Services Centres Authority exercises regulatory powers (Section 23G).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for rules), Board (for regulations), Depositories (for bye-laws with Board approval).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Board has powers to call for information, conduct enquiries, issue directions, and appoint adjudicating officers to impose penalties. Recovery Officers are empowered to recover penalties and disgorgement amounts. Offences are triable by Special Courts, with provisions for appeals to the Securities Appellate Tribunal and Supreme Court.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Special Courts, Securities Appellate Tribunal, High Court (for appeal and revision from Special Courts), Supreme Court (for appeals from Securities Appellate Tribunal). Civil courts are barred from jurisdiction.

act_identification.act_title: THE ARBITRATION AND CONCILIATION ACT, 1996

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Forty-seventh Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL) has adopted the UNCITRAL Model Law on International Commercial Arbitration in 1985; ANDWHEREAS the General Assembly of the United Nations has recommended that all countries give due consideration to the said Model Law, in view of the desirability of uniformity of the law of arbitral procedures and the specific needs of international commercial arbitration practice; ANDWHEREAS the UNCITRAL has adopted the UNCITRAL Conciliation Rules in 1980; ANDWHEREAS the General Assembly of the United Nations has recommended the use of the said Rules in cases where a dispute arises in the context of international commercial relations and the parties seek an amicable settlement of that dispute by recourse to conciliation; ANDWHEREAS the said Model Law and Rules make significant contribution to the establishment of a unified legal framework for the fair and efficient settlement of disputes arising in international commercial relations; ANDWHEREAS it is expedient to make law respecting arbitration and conciliation, taking into account the aforesaid Model Law and Rules;
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the law relating to domestic arbitration, international commercial arbitration, and the enforcement of foreign arbitral awards. It also defines the law relating to conciliation and addresses matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, taking into account the UNCITRAL Model Law and Conciliation Rules.

chapter_titles: _Making of arbitral award and termination of proceedings_

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its applicability to the whole of India, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in Part I of the Act, such as 'arbitration', 'arbitration agreement', 'Court', and 'international commercial arbitration'.

key_sections.title: Arbitration agreement.
key_sections.description: Defines what constitutes an arbitration agreement, including its form and requirement to be in writing.

key_sections.title: Power to refer parties to arbitration where there is an arbitration agreement.
key_sections.description: Empowers a judicial authority to refer parties to arbitration if an arbitration agreement exists, upon application by a party.

key_sections.title: Interim measures, etc., by Court.
key_sections.description: Allows a party to apply to a Court for interim measures of protection before, during, or after arbitral proceedings.

key_sections.title: Appointment of arbitrators.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for appointing arbitrators, including party agreement, default procedures, and involvement of the Supreme Court or High Court.

key_sections.title: Grounds for challenge.
key_sections.description: Specifies the grounds on which an arbitrator may be challenged, primarily concerning independence, impartiality, and qualifications.

key_sections.title: Competence of arbitral tribunal to rule on its jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Establishes the principle of 'Kompetenz-Kompetenz', allowing the arbitral tribunal to rule on its own jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Interim measures ordered by arbitral tribunal.
key_sections.description: Grants the arbitral tribunal the power to order interim measures of protection during arbitral proceedings.

key_sections.title: Time limit for arbitral award.
key_sections.description: Prescribes time limits for making arbitral awards, especially for non-international commercial arbitrations, and provisions for extension.

key_sections.title: Application for setting aside arbitral awards.
key_sections.description: Details the limited grounds and procedure for a Court to set aside an arbitral award.

key_sections.title: Enforcement.
key_sections.description: Provides for the enforcement of arbitral awards as if they were decrees of the court, subject to applications for setting aside.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Arbitration Council of India.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Arbitration Council of India as a body corporate to promote and encourage arbitration and other alternative dispute resolution mechanisms.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines 'foreign award' for the purpose of enforcing New York Convention Awards.

key_sections.title: Application and scope.
key_sections.description: Specifies the application and scope of Part III concerning conciliation of disputes.

key_sections.title: Status and effect of settlement agreement.
key_sections.description: States that a settlement agreement reached through conciliation has the same status and effect as an arbitral award on agreed terms.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals previous arbitration acts and includes saving provisions for ongoing proceedings and rules.

Conciliation

act_identification.act_title: THE BUILDING AND OTHER CONSTRUCTION WORKERS’ WELFARE CESS ACT, 1996

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the levy and collection of a cess on the cost of construction incurred by employers with a view to augmenting the resources of the Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare Boards constituted under the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996.
act_overview.purpose: The Act provides for the levy and collection of a cess on the cost of construction incurred by employers. The objective is to augment the financial resources of the Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare Boards, which are constituted to provide welfare for construction workers.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's official name, its geographical application to the whole of India, and its deemed commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act such as “Board”, “Fund”, and “prescribed”.

key_sections.title: Levy and collection of cess.
key_sections.description: Mandates the levy and collection of a cess on construction costs at a rate specified by the Central Government, and outlines the collection mechanism.

key_sections.title: Furnishing of returns.
key_sections.description: Requires employers to furnish returns regarding construction costs to designated officers or authorities.

key_sections.title: Assessment of cess.
key_sections.description: Details the process for officers or authorities to assess the amount of cess payable by employers.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to exempt certain employers or classes of employers from cess payment under specific conditions.

key_sections.title: Power of entry.
key_sections.description: Authorizes officers or authorities of the State Government to enter construction sites for verification purposes.

key_sections.title: Interest payable on delay in payment of cess.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that employers must pay interest on delayed cess payments at a specified rate.

key_sections.title: Penalty for non-payment of cess within the specified time.
key_sections.description: Provides for the imposition of a penalty, not exceeding the cess amount, for failure to pay cess within the due date.

key_sections.title: Recovery of amount due under the Act.
key_sections.description: States that any amount due under the Act, including interest or penalty, can be recovered in the same manner as an arrear of land revenue.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Establishes a mechanism for employers to appeal against assessment orders or penalty orders to an appellate authority.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for furnishing false returns or wilfully evading cess.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Addresses the liability of companies and their responsible officers (directors, managers, etc.) for offences committed under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare Cess Third Ordinance, 1996, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under it.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To specify the rate of cess (Section 3(1))
Central Government: To exempt employers or classes of employers from cess payment (Section 6)
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act (Section 14)
Officer or authority: To assess the amount of cess payable by employers (Section 5)
Officer or authority of the State Government: To enter places for verification and discharge duties (Section 7)
Prescribed authority: To impose penalty for non-payment of cess (Section 9)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes interest for delayed payment of cess (Section 8) and a penalty for non-payment of cess within the specified time, which may not exceed the amount of cess (Section 9). It also defines offences such as furnishing false returns or wilfully evading cess, punishable with imprisonment up to six months, fine, or both (Section 12). Offences by companies are also addressed, holding responsible persons and the company liable (Section 13).

repealed_acts: The Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare Cess Third Ordinance, 1996 (Ord. 26 of 1996)
related_acts: Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996 (27 of 1996)

applies_to: Every employer incurring cost of construction
exemptions: Any employer or class of employers in a State where such cess is already levied and payable under any corresponding law in force in that State (by Central Government notification)
special_provisions: Explanation for cost of construction in Uttar Pradesh, excluding cost of land, compensation under Employees’s Compensation Act, 1923, expenditure on certain plant/equipment not part of construction activity, and specific medical machines (Uttar Pradesh Act 28 of 2018, s. 2)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the levy and collection of cess (Section 3), mandatory furnishing of returns by employers (Section 4), and assessment of cess by designated officers (Section 5). Recovery of unpaid amounts (including interest and penalty) can be done as an arrear of land revenue (Section 10). Officers have powers of entry for verification (Section 7). Penalties are imposed for non-payment or evasion (Sections 9, 12, 13), and an appeal mechanism is provided (Section 11).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under Section 12 save on a complaint made by or under the authority of the Central Government. Orders passed in appeal under Section 11 are final and shall not be called in question in any court of law.

act_identification.act_short_title: the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the employment and conditions of service of building and other construction workers and to provide for their safety, health and welfare measures and for other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the employment and conditions of service of building and other construction workers. It also provides for their safety, health, and welfare measures, and addresses other related matters.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, commencement and application.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'building worker', and 'establishment'.

key_sections.title: Central Advisory Committee.

key_sections.title: Registration of establishments.

key_sections.title: Registration of building workers as beneficiaries.
key_sections.description: Outlines the eligibility criteria and procedure for building workers to register as beneficiaries under the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution of State Welfare Boards.
key_sections.description: Requires State Governments to constitute Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare Boards to exercise powers and perform functions under the Act.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Boards.
key_sections.description: Details the welfare functions of the Boards, including providing assistance in case of accident, pension, loans for housing, and educational assistance.

key_sections.title: Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare Fund and its application.
key_sections.description: Establishes a welfare fund for each Board and specifies the sources of its credit and how it shall be applied.

key_sections.title: Power of appropriate Government to make rules for the safety and health of building workers.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the appropriate Government to make rules concerning safety and health measures for building workers.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Director-General, Chief Inspector and Inspectors.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of inspecting staff, including a Director-General, Chief Inspector, and Inspectors, to oversee the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Responsibility of employers.
key_sections.description: Holds employers responsible for constant and adequate supervision to ensure compliance with safety provisions and prevent accidents.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of provisions regarding safety measures.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for contravening rules related to safety measures.

key_sections.title: Cognizance of offences.
key_sections.description: Specifies the conditions under which courts can take cognizance of offences under the Act and the minimum court level.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, detailing specific matters that may be covered.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals a previous Ordinance and includes saving provisions for actions taken under it.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for various contraventions. Failure to give notice of commencement of work (Sec 48) carries similar penalties. Obstruction of an Inspector (Sec 49) is punishable with imprisonment up to three months or a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both. Other offences (Sec 50) where no express penalty is provided are punishable with a fine up to one thousand rupees, with additional fines for continuing contravention. Offences committed by companies (Sec 53) hold both the company and persons in charge liable.
