implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The appropriate Government, after consultation with the expert committee, has the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act. Both the Central Government and State Governments are empowered to make rules.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a system of registration of establishments and building workers, constitution of welfare boards, and regulation of working conditions, safety, and health measures. Inspecting staff, including a Director-General, Chief Inspector, and Inspectors, are appointed with powers to enter, examine, and seize records. Penalties are prescribed for contraventions, and mechanisms for recovery of penalties are in place. The Central Government can issue directions to State Governments or Boards for implementation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE PROVISIONS OF THE PANCHAYATS (EXTENSION TO THE SCHEDULED AREAS) ACT, 1996
act_identification.act_short_title: Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the extension of the provisions of Part IX of the Constitution relating to the Panchayats to the Scheduled Areas.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to extend the provisions of Part IX of the Constitution, which deals with Panchayats, to the Scheduled Areas. It introduces specific exceptions and modifications to ensure that the local self-governance structures respect the customary laws, social practices, and traditional management of community resources prevalent in these areas, while empowering Gram Sabhas and Panchayats with significant powers.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996'.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines 'Scheduled Areas' as referred to in clause (1) of article 244 of the Constitution.

key_sections.title: Extension of Part IX of the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Extends the provisions of Part IX of the Constitution relating to Panchayats to the Scheduled Areas, subject to exceptions and modifications in section 4.

key_sections.title: Exceptions and modifications to Part IX of the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Outlines specific features that State legislation on Panchayats in Scheduled Areas must adhere to, including consonance with customary law, powers of Gram Sabha, reservation for Scheduled Tribes, and powers of Panchayats regarding resources and social sectors.

key_sections.title: Continuance of existing laws and Panchayats.
key_sections.description: Provides for the continuance of existing laws and Panchayats in Scheduled Areas for a specified period, even if inconsistent with the Act, until amended or repealed.

powers_conferred: State Legislature to make laws on Panchayats in consonance with customary law, social and religious practices and traditional management practices of community resources.
Gram Sabha to safeguard and preserve traditions and customs, cultural identity, community resources and customary mode of dispute resolution.
Gram Sabha to approve plans, programmes and projects for social and economic development.
Gram Sabha to identify or select persons as beneficiaries under poverty alleviation and other programmes.
Panchayat at the village level to obtain certification of utilisation of funds from Gram Sabha.
State Government to nominate persons belonging to Scheduled Tribes in Panchayats.
Gram Sabha or Panchayats to be consulted before acquisition of land for development projects and before re-settling or rehabilitating persons.
Panchayats at the appropriate level to manage minor water bodies.
Gram Sabha or Panchayats to recommend prior to grant of prospecting licence or mining lease for minor minerals.
Gram Sabha or Panchayats to recommend prior to grant of concession for the exploitation of minor minerals by auction.
Panchayats at the appropriate level and Gram Sabha to enforce prohibition or to regulate or restrict the sale and consumption of any intoxicant.
Panchayats at the appropriate level and Gram Sabha to have ownership of minor forest produce.
Panchayats at the appropriate level and Gram Sabha to prevent alienation of land and restore unlawfully alienated land of a Scheduled Tribe.
Panchayats at the appropriate level and Gram Sabha to manage village markets.
Panchayats at the appropriate level and Gram Sabha to exercise control over money lending to the Scheduled Tribes.
Panchayats at the appropriate level and Gram Sabha to exercise control over institutions and functionaries in all social sectors.
Panchayats at the appropriate level and Gram Sabha to control over local plans and resources for such plans including tribal sub plans.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government may nominate persons belonging to such Scheduled Tribes as have no representation in the Panchayat at the intermediate level or the Panchayat at the district level.

applies_to: Scheduled Areas
Panchayats in Scheduled Areas
Gram Sabha in Scheduled Areas
State Legislature making laws under Part IX of the Constitution for Scheduled Areas
special_provisions: Reservation of seats in Panchayats in Scheduled Areas for Scheduled Tribes not less than one-half of total seats.
All seats of Chairpersons of Panchayats at all levels in Scheduled Areas reserved for Scheduled Tribes.
State Government may nominate persons belonging to Scheduled Tribes in Panchayats in Scheduled Areas.

Specific powers conferred on Gram Sabha and Panchayats in Scheduled Areas regarding prohibition, minor forest produce, land alienation, village markets, money lending, social sectors, and local plans.
State Legislature to endeavour to follow the pattern of the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution while designing administrative arrangements in Panchayats at district levels in Scheduled Areas.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: State legislation on Panchayats in Scheduled Areas must be in consonance with customary law and traditional practices. Gram Sabhas are empowered to approve plans, identify beneficiaries, and certify fund utilization. Recommendations of Gram Sabhas or Panchayats are mandatory for certain activities like mining leases and land acquisition.

act_identification.act_title: THE MAHATMA GANDHI ANTARRASHTRIYA HINDI VISHWAVIDYALAYA ACT, 1996
act_identification.act_short_title: Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya Act, 1996

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate a teaching University for the promotion and development of Hindi language and literature, through teaching and research, with a view to enabling Hindi to achieve greater functional efficiency and recognition as a major international language and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya to promote and develop Hindi language and literature through teaching and research. Its objective is to enhance Hindi's functional efficiency and international recognition, and to facilitate comparative studies, information dissemination, and training in related areas like translation and linguistics.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act and its Statutes.

key_sections.title: Establishment of the University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya as a body corporate with perpetual succession.

key_sections.title: Objects of the University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary goals of the University, including promotion of Hindi language and literature, research, and distance education.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Details the various powers vested in the University to achieve its objects, such as granting degrees, establishing institutions, and managing finances.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: States that the University's jurisdiction extends to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: University open to all classes, castes and creeds.
key_sections.description: Ensures the University is open to all persons without discrimination, with a proviso for special provisions for certain groups.

key_sections.title: The Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor and outlines the Visitor's powers of review, inspection, and direction.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the designated officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and Registrar.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities of the University, such as the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council.

key_sections.title: Power to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Grants the power to make Statutes for various matters concerning the University's constitution, administration, and academic functions.

key_sections.title: Powers to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Grants the power to make Ordinances for academic and administrative matters, subject to the Act and Statutes.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees.
key_sections.description: Mandates written contracts for employees and provides for arbitration in disputes arising from these contracts.

key_sections.title: Procedure of appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for appeals and arbitration in disciplinary cases involving students.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make provisions to remove difficulties in implementing the Act for a limited period.

key_sections.title: Transitional provisions.
key_sections.description: Provides for the initial appointment of officers and constitution of authorities during the transitional period after the Act's commencement.

powers_conferred: University: To provide instructions, grant diplomas/degrees, organize extra-mural studies, confer honorary degrees, provide distance education, institute teaching positions, recognise institutions, appoint teachers, create posts, cooperate with other institutions, establish campuses/centres/laboratories, institute awards, maintain institutions/halls, provide research/advisory services, organize courses, make special arrangements for women students, appoint visiting professors, confer autonomous status, determine admission standards, demand fees, supervise student residences, lay down conditions of service, regulate discipline, promote employee welfare, receive donations, borrow money, and other incidental acts (Section 5).
Visitor: To appoint persons to review work, issue directions, cause inspection/inquiry, annul proceedings, make/amend Statutes (Section 9, Section 27).
Vice-Chancellor: To exercise powers of any authority in immediate action, ask for review of decisions, exercise general supervision and control (Section 12).

Executive Council: To make new/amend/repeal Statutes (Section 27), make Ordinances (Section 28), manage and administer revenue/property, create teaching/academic/administrative posts, grant leave, regulate discipline, manage finances, invest money, transfer property, provide infrastructure, enter contracts, redress grievances, appoint examiners, select common seal, make special arrangements for women students, delegate powers, institute awards, invite writers-in-residence, appoint visiting professors (Statute 13).
Central Government: To appoint date of commencement (Section 1(2)), approve borrowing (Section 5(xxvi)), declare Provident Funds Act applicable (Section 35(2)), remove difficulties (Section 42).
Authorities of the University: To make Regulations (Section 29).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for disciplinary action against employees for misconduct (Section 26(f), Statute 26) and against students (Section 33, Statute 29). Penalties for students include expulsion, rustication, debarment from examinations, fines, and cancellation of results (Statute 29(3)). Specific offences are not detailed in the main Act text.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and initial members of the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council. The Executive Council appoints the Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, Librarian, Professors, Readers, Lecturers, other academic staff, Principals of Institutions, administrative/ministerial posts, and the Proctor. The Vice-Chancellor appoints Deans of Schools. Selection Committees recommend candidates for various posts.

applies_to: Persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class
Employees of the University
Students of the University
exemptions: Special provisions for the employment or admission of women, physically handicapped or of persons belonging to the weaker sections of the society and, in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.
special_provisions: Special provisions for the employment or admission of women, physically handicapped or of persons belonging to the weaker sections of the society and, in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Section 7 proviso).
Transitional provisions for initial appointments and constitution of authorities (Section 43).
Special arrangements for residence, discipline and teaching of women students (Section 5(xvi), Section 28(1)(i), Statute 13(xv)).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Executive Council has the power to make Statutes and Ordinances. The Academic Council proposes Ordinances and frames regulations. The Visitor can make or amend Statutes. The Vice-Chancellor makes the first Ordinances. Authorities of the University can make Regulations. Principals of Institutions, Deans of Schools of Studies, and Heads of teaching Departments can make supplementary rules of discipline.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor has powers of review, inspection, inquiry, issuing directions, and annulling proceedings. The Vice-Chancellor exercises general supervision and control, takes immediate action, and ensures observance of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations. The Executive Council manages and administers affairs and enforces discipline. Disciplinary actions are prescribed for employees and students, with provisions for arbitration in disputes. Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations are published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: For disputes arising out of contracts between the University and employees, or disciplinary actions against students, a Tribunal of Arbitration has final decision, and no suit shall lie in any civil court in respect of such matters.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the Statutes of the University, detailing provisions for the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, Deans of Schools of Studies, Heads of Departments, Proctor, Librarian, Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Schools of Studies and Departments, Finance Committee, Selection Committees, special modes of appointment, committees, terms and conditions of service and code of conduct for employees, seniority list, removal of employees, honorary degrees, withdrawal of degrees, maintenance of discipline among students, convocations, acting chairman of meetings, resignation, disqualification, residence condition for membership, membership of authorities by virtue of other bodies, and procedures for making Ordinances and Regulations.

act_identification.act_title: THE MAULANA AZAD NATIONAL URDU UNIVERSITY ACT, 1996
act_identification.act_short_title: The Maulana Azad National Urdu University Act, 1996

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate in University at the national level mainly to promote and develop Urdu language and to import vocational and technical education in Urdu medium through conventional teaching and distance education system and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to establish the Maulana Azad National Urdu University to promote and develop the Urdu language. It aims to impart vocational and technical education in Urdu medium through conventional teaching and distance education systems, providing wider access to higher education, with a focus on women's education.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act and the Statutes made thereunder.

key_sections.title: Establishment of the University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Maulana Azad National Urdu University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, headquartered at Hyderabad.

key_sections.title: Objects of the University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary goals of the University, including promoting Urdu language, imparting vocational/technical education in Urdu, and focusing on women's education.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers of the University, such as providing instruction, granting degrees, establishing institutions, and managing finances.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: States that the University's jurisdiction extends to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: University open to all classes, castes and creeds.
key_sections.description: Declares the University open to all persons regardless of sex, caste, creed, race or class, with a proviso for special provisions for certain groups.

key_sections.title: The Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University and outlines the Visitor's powers, including review, inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the designated officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and Registrar.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities of the University, such as the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council.

key_sections.title: Power to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Details the matters for which Statutes may be made, covering constitution of authorities, appointment of officers, and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinance.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Ordinances may be made, including admission of students, courses of study, and conduct of examinations.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees.
key_sections.description: Mandates written contracts for employees and provides for arbitration in disputes arising from such contracts.

key_sections.title: Procedure of appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students.
key_sections.description: Outlines the appeal process for students against disciplinary actions and provides for arbitration in disputes.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make provisions to remove difficulties in implementing the Act for a period of three years.

key_sections.title: Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Requires publication of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations in the Official Gazette and their presentation before Parliament.

powers_conferred: Power to provide for instructions and research (University)
Power to grant diplomas or certificates and confer degrees (University)
Power to organise and undertake extra-mural studies, training and extension services (University)
Power to confer honorary degrees (University)
Power to institute Professorships, Readerships, Lecturerships and other teaching or academic positions (University)
Power to appoint persons working in any other University or organisation as teacher (University)
Power to create administrative, ministerial and other posts and to make appointments thereto (University)
Power to co-operate or collaborate or associate with any other University or authority or institution of higher learning (University)
Power to establish, with prior approval of the Central Government, centres and specialised laboratories (University)
Power to institute and award fellowships, scholarships, studentships, medals and prizes (University)
Power to establish and maintain Institutions and Halls (University)
Power to make provision for research and advisory services (University)
Power to organise and conduct refresher courses, workshops, seminars and other programmes (University)
Power to make special arrangements in respect of the residence, discipline and teaching of women students (University)
Power to appoint, on contract or otherwise, visiting Professors, Emeritus Professors, Consultants, Scholars (University)
Power to confer autonomous status on a Department (University)
Power to determine standards of admission to the University (University)
Power to demand and receive payment of fees and other charges (University)
Power to supervise the residences of the students and make arrangements for their health and welfare (University)
Power to lay down conditions of service of all categories of employees (University)
Power to regulate and enforce discipline among students and employees (University)
Power to make arrangements for promoting the health and general welfare of the employees (University)
Power to receive benefactions, donations and gifts and to acquire, hold, manage and dispose of property (University)
Power to borrow, with the approval of the Central Government, money for the purposes of the University (University)
Power to organise suitable distance education programmes (University)
Power to establish maintain or recognise Study Centres for the delivery of the distance education system (University)
Power to provide for the preparation of instructional materials (University)
Power to devise and implement suitable schemes for promotion and dissemination of Urdu (University)
Power to do all such other acts and things as may be necessary, incidental or conducive to the attainment of its objects (University)
Power to review the work and progress of the University and submit a report (Visitor)
Power to cause an inspection or inquiry (Visitor)
Power to issue directions (Visitor)
Power to annul any proceeding of the University (Visitor)
Power to make new or additional Statutes or amend or repeal Statutes (Executive Council, Visitor)
Power to make Ordinances (Executive Council, Vice-Chancellor)
Power to make Regulations (Authorities of the University)
Power to remove difficulties (Central Government)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for disciplinary action against students, which may include expulsion, rustication for a specified period, debarring from examinations, imposition of fines, or cancellation of examination results. For employees, the Act allows for disciplinary action, including suspension, censure, withholding of increment, and removal from service on grounds of misconduct or for good cause after notice.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, first Registrar, first Finance Officer, and nominates members for the first Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council. The Executive Council appoints the Pro-Vice-Chancellor (on VC's recommendation), Registrar, Finance Officer, Librarian (on Selection Committee recommendation), Professors, Readers, Lecturers, other academic staff, Principals of Institutions (on Selection Committee recommendation), and administrative/ministerial posts. The Vice-Chancellor appoints Deans of Schools. The Executive Council, on the recommendation of the Vice-Chancellor, appoints Heads of Departments and the Proctor.

applies_to: The whole of India
Persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class
special_provisions: Special provisions for the employment or admission of women, physically handicapped or of persons belonging to the weaker sections of the society and, in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Statutes are made by the Executive Council (with Visitor's assent) or the Visitor. Ordinances are made by the Vice-Chancellor (first ordinances, with Central Government approval) or the Executive Council. Regulations are made by the authorities of the University.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor has powers of review, inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions, including annulling proceedings. The Vice-Chancellor exercises general supervision and control. The Executive Council manages and administers the University's affairs. Disciplinary actions are taken against employees and students. Disputes involving employees or students can be referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: For disputes arising out of employee contracts, no suit shall lie in any civil court in respect of matters decided by the Tribunal of Arbitration. For questions regarding the constitution of University authorities, the Visitor's decision is final. The Act also provides protection for actions taken in good faith, implying general civil court jurisdiction otherwise.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the detailed Statutes of the University, governing the appointment, powers, and duties of officers (Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, Deans, Heads of Departments, Proctor, Librarian), the constitution and functions of authorities (Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Finance Committee, Selection Committees), conditions of service for employees, procedures for honorary degrees, withdrawal of degrees, maintenance of discipline among students, and general provisions for resignations, disqualifications, and making of Ordinances and Regulations.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDUSTRIAL RECONSTRUCTION BANK (TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKINGS AND REPEAL) ACT, 1997
act_identification.act_short_title: Industrial Reconstruction Bank (Transfer of Undertakings and Repeal) Act, 1997

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the transfer and vesting of the undertakings of the Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India to and in the Company to be formed and registered as a Company under the Companies Act, 1956, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto and also to repeal the Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India Act, 1984.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to facilitate the transfer and vesting of the undertakings of the Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India into a new company. It also aims to repeal the Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India Act, 1984, and address related matters concerning the transfer and the new company.

chapter_titles: TRANSFER AND VESTING OF THE UNDERTAKING OF RECONSTRUCTION BANK IN COMPANY
AMENDMENT TO THE INDUSTRIAL RECONSTRATION BANK OF INDIA ACT, 1984

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its deemed date of commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used within the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'Company', and 'Reconstruction Bank'.

key_sections.title: Undertakings of the Reconstruction Bank to vest in company.
key_sections.description: Mandates the transfer and vesting of the undertakings of the Reconstruction Bank to the Company on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: General effect of vesting of undertaking in Company.
key_sections.description: Details the comprehensive effect of the vesting, including transfer of all business, assets, rights, liabilities, and the continuation of contracts and proceedings by or against the Company.

key_sections.title: Provisions in respect of officers and other employees of Reconstruction Bank.
key_sections.description: Outlines the terms and conditions for the transfer of employees from the Reconstruction Bank to the Company, including their remuneration, benefits, and options not to continue employment.

key_sections.title: Act 18 of 1891 to apply to the books of Company.
key_sections.description: Declares the Company to be a bank for the purposes of the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving of Act 62 of 1984.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India Act, 1984, on the appointed day, with certain saving provisions for compliance and enforcement of existing arrangements.

key_sections.title: Repeal and Saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Industrial Reconstruction Bank (Transfer of Undertakings and Repeal) Ordinance, 1997, and saves actions taken under it.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint a date for the transfer of undertakings (Section 3)
Company to act upon and enforce arrangements entered into by the Reconstruction Bank (Section 13(2)(b))
Company to appoint one or more directors to industrial or other concerns (Section 9(1))
Company to remove or substitute any director appointed by it (Section 9(2)(a))

repealed_acts: Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India Act, 1984
Industrial Reconstruction Bank (Transfer of Undertakings and Repeal) Ordinance, 1997 (Ord. 7 of 1997)
related_acts: Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India Act, 1984

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Company has the power to appoint directors to industrial or other concerns (Section 9).

applies_to: Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India
Company (Industrial Investment Bank of India Limited)
Officers and other employees of the Reconstruction Bank
Industrial concerns
exemptions: Officers or other employees opting not to continue employment with the Company are deemed to have resigned (Section 5(2))
Transfer of services of employees to the Company does not entitle them to compensation under this Act or any other law (Section 5(3))
Directors of the Board, Chairman and Managing Director of the Reconstruction Bank are not entitled to compensation for loss of office (Section 5(6))
Company is not liable to pay income-tax or any other tax for five years from the appointed day (Section 7(1))
Transfer and vesting of undertakings is not construed as a transfer for capital gains under the Income-tax Act, 1961 (Section 7(2))
Provisions regarding share qualification, age limit, number of directorships, removal from office, etc., do not apply to directors appointed by the Company (Section 9(1))

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Company shall continue to enforce existing contracts, deeds, bonds, guarantees, and other instruments (Section 4(3)). The Company can continue and enforce any pending proceedings or causes of action (Section 4(4)). The Company will be entitled to act upon and enforce arrangements under Chapter VIII of the repealed Act (Section 13(2)(b)).

act_identification.act_title: THE LALIT KALA AKADAMI (TAKING OVER OF MANAGEMENT) ACT, 1997
act_identification.act_short_title: The Lalit Kala Akadami (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1997

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the temporary taking over of the management of the Lalit Kala Akadami in the public interest due to serious difficulties and complaints regarding misuse of funds and mismanagement. It aims to secure proper management and prevent further detriment to the Akadami's interests and objectives.

chapter_titles: TAKING OVER OF THE MANAGEMENT OF THE LALIT KALA AKADAMI

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its deemed date of commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used within the Act, such as 'Administrator' and 'society'.

key_sections.title: Management of the society.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the management of the Lalit Kala Akadami shall vest in the Central Government for a limited period, including all assets and rights, and deems existing contracts and office-holders terminated.

key_sections.title: Administrator of society.
key_sections.description: Mandates the appointment of an Administrator by the Central Government to manage the society, outlining the Administrator's powers, duties, and remuneration, and requiring delivery of property and documents to them.

key_sections.title: No right to compensation for premature termination of a contract.
key_sections.description: States that no person is entitled to compensation for premature termination of contracts or loss of office due to the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Relinquishment of administration of the society.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to relinquish the management of the society if its purposes are fulfilled or it's no longer necessary, returning administration to the General Council.

key_sections.title: Application of Act 21 of 1860.
key_sections.description: Specifies how the Societies Registration Act, 1860, applies to the society while its management is vested in the Central Government, restricting certain actions by members or the General Council.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals who wrongfully withhold property or documents, or fail to account for them, in relation to the society's management.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws, instruments, or court orders.

key_sections.title: Contracts in bad faith may be cancelled or varied.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to cancel or vary contracts entered into in bad faith or detrimental to the society's interests, with a provision for appeal to the High Court at Delhi.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act and outlines the parliamentary procedure for such rules.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Lalit Kala Akadami (Taking Over of Management) Ordinance, 1997, and saves actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to continue management beyond three years (Section 3(1) Proviso)
Central Government: to appoint an Administrator (Section 4(1))
Central Government: to issue directions to the Administrator (Section 4(3))
Central Government: to fix remuneration for the Administrator (Section 4(8))
Central Government: to relinquish management of the society (Section 6(1))
Central Government: to approve resolutions of the society's General Council (Section 7(b))
Central Government: to consent to dissolution, merger, or appointment of Receiver for the society (Section 7(c))
Central Government: to cancel or vary contracts entered into in bad faith (Section 13(1))
Central Government: to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act (Section 15(1))
Administrator: to carry on the management of the society (Section 4(1))
Administrator: to exercise powers of the General Council or Executive Board, including disposing of property (Section 4(4))
Administrator: to terminate contracts of employment (Section 14)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who wrongfully withholds property from the Administrator, wrongfully obtains possession of such property, wilfully retains or fails to deliver property, removes or destroys it, wilfully withholds or fails to account for books/papers/documents, or fails to furnish information as required, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both (Section 8). Offences committed by companies are also addressed, holding persons in charge and the company liable, with provisions for proving lack of knowledge or due diligence, and for liability of directors/managers/officers in cases of consent, connivance, or neglect (Section 9).

repealed_acts: The Lalit Kala Akadami (Taking Over of Management) Ordinance, 1997 (Ord. 10 of 1997)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government shall appoint a person as the Administrator of the society (Section 4(1)).

applies_to: Lalit Kala Akadami (society)
special_provisions: The Societies Registration Act, 1860, is specified as in force in the National Capital Territory of Delhi for the purposes of this Act (Section 2(c)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The management of the Lalit Kala Akadami vests in the Central Government, which appoints an Administrator to carry out its functions. The Act provides for penalties for non-compliance with the Administrator's authority and for wrongful actions related to the society's property. It also grants the Central Government powers to cancel contracts and make rules for implementation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court at Delhi (for applications against cancellation or variation of contracts under Section 13(2))

act_identification.act_title: THE TELECOM REGULATORY AUTHORITY OF INDIA ACT, 1997
act_identification.act_short_title: the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of the [1][Telecom Regulatory Authority of India and the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal to regulate the telecommunication services, adjudicate disputes, dispose of appeals and to protect the interests of service providers and consumers of the telecom sector, to promote and ensure orderly growth of the telecom sector] and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India and the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal. Its primary purpose is to regulate telecommunication services, resolve disputes, handle appeals, protect the interests of service providers and consumers, and foster the orderly growth of the telecom sector in India.

chapter_titles: POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE AUTHORITY

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical applicability, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Authority.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India as a body corporate.

key_sections.title: Functions of Authority.
key_sections.description: Outlines the recommendations and functions of the Authority, including regulating services, ensuring compliance, and setting quality standards.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal to adjudicate disputes and hear appeals.

key_sections.title: Application for settlement of disputes and appeals to Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Details the process for applying for dispute settlement and filing appeals with the Appellate Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Civil court not to have jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Bars civil courts from having jurisdiction over matters determinable by the Appellate Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Procedure and powers of Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Describes the procedure and powers of the Appellate Tribunal, including its powers as a civil court.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to issue directions.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to issue directions to the Authority on matters of national interest and policy.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of directions of Authority.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for violating directions issued by the Authority.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Authority to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.

powers_conferred: Authority to make recommendations on new service providers, licence terms, revocation, competition, technological improvements, equipment, development of telecommunication technology, and spectrum management (Section 11(1)(a)).

Authority to ensure compliance of licence terms, fix interconnectivity terms, ensure technical compatibility, regulate revenue sharing, lay down quality standards, ensure time periods for circuits, maintain registers, and ensure universal service obligations (Section 11(1)(b)).
Authority to levy fees and other charges (Section 11(1)(c)).
Authority to notify rates for telecommunication services (Section 11(2)).
Authority to call for information, conduct investigations, and inspect books of account from service providers (Section 12(1)).
Authority to issue directions to service providers (Section 12(4), Section 13).
Central Government to appoint Chairperson and members of Authority (Section 3(3)).
Chairperson of Authority to have powers of general superintendence and directions (Section 6(1)).
Central Government to establish Appellate Tribunal (Section 14).
Appellate Tribunal to adjudicate disputes and hear appeals (Section 14).
Central Government to appoint Chairperson and Members of Appellate Tribunal (Section 14B(1)).
Appellate Tribunal to have powers of a civil court (Section 16(2)).
Central Government to issue directions to the Authority (Section 25).
Authority to delegate powers and functions (Section 33).
Central Government to make rules (Section 35).
Authority to make regulations (Section 36).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalty for wilful failure to comply with orders of Appellate Tribunal (Section 20): fine up to one lakh rupees, for second/subsequent offence up to two lakh rupees, and for continuing contravention additional fine up to two lakh rupees per day. Penalty for contravention of directions of Authority (Section 29): fine up to one lakh rupees, for second/subsequent offence up to two lakh rupees, and for continuing contravention additional fine up to two lakh rupees per day. Offences by companies (Section 30): persons in charge and the company deemed guilty, directors/managers/secretaries also guilty if committed with consent/connivance/neglect. Offences by Government Departments (Section 31): Head of Department deemed guilty, other officers also guilty if committed with consent/connivance/neglect.

repealed_acts: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Ordinance 1997 (Ord. 11 of 1997)
related_acts: Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969 (54 of 1969)
Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India Act, 2008 (27 of 2008)
Cost and Works Accountants Act, 1959 (23 of 1959)
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Amendment) Act, 2000 (2 of 2000)

authorities_established: Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (for Authority members); Central Government in consultation with the Chief Justice of India (for Appellate Tribunal members)
regulatory_bodies: Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal

applies_to: Whole of India
Service providers
Licensor and licensee
Group of consumers
Central Government or a State Government or a local authority or any person (for applications/appeals to Appellate Tribunal)
exemptions: Broadcasting services (unless notified by Central Government)

Matters relating to monopolistic trade practice, restrictive trade practice and unfair trade practice which are subject to the jurisdiction of the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Commission
Complaint of an individual consumer maintainable before a Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum or a Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission or the National Consumer Redressal Commission
Dispute between telegraph authority and any other person referred to in sub-section (1) of section 7B of the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885
special_provisions: Any reference in this Act to a law which is not in force in the State of Jammu and Kashmir shall in relation to that State be construed as a reference to the corresponding law, if any, in that State (Section 2(3)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Authority issues directions to service providers; penalties for contravention of Authority's directions; Appellate Tribunal adjudicates disputes and hears appeals; orders of Appellate Tribunal are executable as a civil court decree; penalties for wilful failure to comply with Appellate Tribunal orders; cognizance of offences by courts only on complaint by Authority.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Supreme Court (for appeals against Appellate Tribunal orders); Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or a Chief Judicial Magistrate of first class (for trying offences); Civil court (for executing Appellate Tribunal orders).

act_identification.act_title: THE VICE-PRESIDENT'S PENSION ACT, 1997

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the payment of pension and other facilities to retiring Vice-Presidents.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the payment of pension and other facilities to persons who cease to hold the office of Vice-President. It also extends benefits such as family pension, medical facilities, and accommodation to the spouse of a deceased or retiring Vice-President.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Vice-President’s Pension Act, 1997'.

key_sections.title: Pension to retiring Vice-Presidents.
key_sections.description: Mandates pension payment to retiring Vice-Presidents, family pension to their spouses, and facilities like furnished residence, telephone, secretarial staff, medical attendance, and travel.

key_sections.title: Medical facilities to the family of deceased Vice-President.
key_sections.description: Entitles the spouse of a Vice-President who dies in office to free medical attendance and treatment for life.

key_sections.title: Free accommodation to spouse of Vice-President.
key_sections.description: Entitles the spouse of a deceased or retiring Vice-President to the use of a furnished residence without licence fee for life.

key_sections.title: Pension to be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
key_sections.description: Declares that all sums payable under this Act shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, subject to parliamentary oversight.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, particularly as amended by the Vice-President’s Pension (Amendment) Act, 2008, for a period of two years from the Act's commencement.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To determine furnished residence and its maintenance (Section 2(2)(a))
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 5(1))
Central Government: To remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act (Section 6(1))

related_acts: Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 (30 of 1954)
President’s Emoluments and Pension Act, 1951 (30 of 1951)

applies_to: Every person who ceases to hold office as Vice-President
Spouse of a person who dies while holding the office of Vice-President
Spouse of a person who dies after ceasing to hold office as Vice-President
Spouse and minor children of a retiring Vice-President
exemptions: A person shall not receive pension if holding office as Prime Minister, Minister, or Member of Parliament and receiving salary/allowances from Consolidated Fund of India or a State.
A person or spouse re-elected as Vice-President is not eligible for benefits under Section 2 during the re-elected term.
A person or spouse elected as President of India is not eligible for benefits under Section 2.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Sums payable under this Act are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India. The Central Government is empowered to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act and to remove difficulties in its implementation.

act_identification.act_title: THE DOCK WORKERS (REGULATION OF EMPLOYMENT) (INAPPLICABILITY TO MAJOR PORTS) ACT, 1997

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.

key_sections.title: Inapplicability of the provisions of the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948 to major ports.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to declare, by notification, that the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948, ceases to apply to a major port after a settlement is reached.

key_sections.title: Transfer of assets and liabilities of the Dock Labour Board, etc., to the Board.

Central Government to direct, by notification, that the provisions of the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1948, shall cease to have effect in relation to a major port (Section 3)

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF PHARMACEUTICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH ACT, 1998

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare certain institutions of pharmaceutical education and research to be institutions of national importance and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish and declare certain institutions dedicated to pharmaceutical education and research as institutions of national importance. It provides for their establishment, incorporation, functions, governance, and other related matters to promote quality and excellence in the field.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Declaration of certain institutions as institutions of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares institutions mentioned in the Schedule and those established under section 4(2A) as institutions of national importance.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Institutes.

key_sections.title: Functions of Institutes.
key_sections.description: Outlines the various functions of the Institutes, including promoting education, research, granting degrees, and cooperating with other institutions.

key_sections.title: Powers of Board of an Institute.

key_sections.title: Visitor.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Council.

key_sections.title: Functions of Council.

key_sections.title: Grant of degrees, etc., by Institutes.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to issue directions.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue directions to the Institute for efficient administration of the Act.

key_sections.title: Statutes and Ordinances to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament.

act_identification.act_title: THE LOTTERIES (REGULATION) ACT, 1998

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the lotteries and to provide for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate lotteries across India, establishing conditions under which State Governments may organize them and prohibiting lotteries that contravene these provisions. It also defines penalties for violations.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, its applicability to the whole of India, and its deemed commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'bumper draw of a lottery', 'lottery', and 'prescribed'.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of lotteries.
key_sections.description: Prohibits State Governments from organizing, conducting, or promoting lotteries, except as provided in Section 4.

key_sections.title: Conditions subject to which lotteries may be organised, etc.
key_sections.description: Lays down specific conditions under which a State Government may organize, conduct, or promote a lottery, including rules on prize money, ticket printing, sale, draws, and unclaimed prizes.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of sale of ticket in a State.
key_sections.description: Allows a State Government to prohibit the sale of tickets of lotteries organized by other States within its own territory.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of organisation, etc., of lottery.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to prohibit lotteries organized or sold in contravention of Sections 4 or 5.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of the Act, including rigorous imprisonment or fine or both, for Heads of Departments, other officers, and agents/promoters/traders.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable and non-bailable.
key_sections.description: Declares offences under this Act as cognizable and non-bailable.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Stipulates liability for offences committed by companies, extending to persons in charge and responsible for the company's business, as well as directors, managers, or other officers.

key_sections.title: Power to give directions.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to State Governments for the execution of the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act and specifies the parliamentary oversight for such rules.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Authorizes State Governments to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, particularly concerning prize money claims and draw periods.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Lotteries (Regulation) Ordinance, 1998, and includes a saving clause for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: State Government may organise, conduct or promote a lottery, subject to conditions (Section 4)
State Government may prohibit the sale of tickets of a lottery organised by every other State within its own State (Section 5)

Central Government may prohibit a lottery organised, conducted or promoted in contravention of the provisions of section 4 or where tickets of such lottery are sold in contravention of the provisions of section 5 (Section 6)
Central Government may give directions to the State Government as to carrying into execution in the State of any of the provisions of this Act or of any rule or order made thereunder (Section 10)
Central Government may make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act (Section 11)
State Government may make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act (Section 12)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any Department of the State Government contravening the Act, the Head of the Department shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine or with both. Other officers, if involved, are also liable. Any person acting as an agent, promoter, or trader in a contravening lottery, or selling/distributing/purchasing its ticket, shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine or with both.

repealed_acts: The Lotteries (Regulation) Ordinance, 1998 (Ord. 6 of 1998)

applies_to: State Governments
Departments of the State Government
Head of the Department
Officers of a Department of Government
Any person acting as an agent or promoter or trader in any lottery
Companies (including firms or other associations of individuals)
exemptions: Head of the Department if he proves that the contravention was committed without his knowledge or that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such contravention (Section 7(1) proviso)

Any person in charge of a company if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he had exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence (Section 9(1) proviso)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government can give directions to State Governments. Offences are cognizable and non-bailable, with penalties prescribed for contraventions by government departments, officers, and individuals involved in lotteries.

act_identification.act_title: THE LEADERS AND CHIEF WHIPS OF RECOGNISED PARTIES AND GROUPS IN PARLIAMENT (FACILITIES) ACT, 1998

act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL INDUSTRIAL SECURITY FORCE (AMENDMENT AND VALIDATION) ACT, 1999

act_overview.preamble: An Act further to amend the Central Industrial Security Force Act, 1968, and to validate certain revision petitions disposed of under the rules made under the said Act.
act_overview.purpose: This Act amends the Central Industrial Security Force Act, 1968, to expand the functions of the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) to include providing technical consultancy services to private sector industrial establishments and protecting government-owned or funded organizations. It also introduces provisions for revision petitions for aggrieved members of the Force and validates past disposals of such petitions.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Central Industrial Security Force (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1999.

key_sections.title: Amendment of long title.
key_sections.description: Substitutes the long title of the principal Act to reflect the expanded scope of the Central Industrial Security Force, including protection of various undertakings and provision of technical consultancy services.

key_sections.title: Amendment of section 2.
key_sections.description: Inserts a new clause (ca) in sub-section (1) of section 2 of the principal Act, defining 'industrial establishment'.

key_sections.title: Amendment of section 3.
key_sections.description: Amends section 3 of the principal Act to include that the Force shall perform other duties as entrusted by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Amendment of section 8.
key_sections.description: Amends section 8 of the principal Act to include 'order for compulsory retirement of' as a disciplinary action and adds 'withholding of increment of pay', 'withholding of promotion', and 'censure' to the list of punishments.

key_sections.title: Amendment of section 9.
key_sections.description: Amends section 9 of the principal Act to introduce provisions for revision petitions by aggrieved enrolled members of the Force against appellate orders, and for an authority to call for records and pass orders on such petitions.

key_sections.title: Insertion of new section 14A.
key_sections.description: Inserts a new section 14A in the principal Act, enabling the Director-General to provide technical consultancy services relating to security to private sector industrial establishments for a fee.

key_sections.title: Amendment of section 22.
key_sections.description: Amends section 22 of the principal Act to include rule-making powers for prescribing authorities and procedures related to revision petitions and the manner and fee for technical consultancy services.

key_sections.title: Validation of the disposal of certain revision petitions.
key_sections.description: Validates the disposal of revision petitions under rule 49 of the Central Industrial Security Force Rules, 1969, retrospectively, notwithstanding any court judgment to the contrary.

powers_conferred: Director-General to direct members of the Force to provide technical consultancy services to industrial establishments in the private sector.
Central Government to entrust other duties to the Central Industrial Security Force.
Central Government to issue general directions regarding technical consultancy services.
Prescribed authority to dispose of revision petitions preferred by aggrieved enrolled members of the Force.
Prescribed authority to call for records of proceedings and make inquiry for revision petitions.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 5 amends the principal Act to include additional disciplinary actions that can be taken against members of the Force, such as compulsory retirement, withholding of increment of pay with or without cumulative effect, withholding of promotion, and censure.

amended_acts: Central Industrial Security Force Act, 1968 (50 of 1968)

authorities_established: authority as may be prescribed (for revision petitions)

Employees of all such undertakings

act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority to protect the interests of insurance policyholders. It aims to regulate, promote, and ensure the orderly growth of the insurance industry in India. Additionally, it amends existing insurance-related legislation.

key_sections.title: Duties, powers and functions of Authority.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Authority to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Act 4 of 1938.
key_sections.description: States that the Insurance Act, 1938, shall be amended as specified in the First Schedule.

Power to issue, renew, modify, withdraw, suspend or cancel registration (Authority, Section 14(2)(a))
Power to specify requisite qualifications, code of conduct and practical training for intermediary or insurance intermediaries and agents (Authority, Section 14(2)(c))

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The First Schedule amends the Insurance Act, 1938, to introduce new penalty provisions. Section 102 prescribes a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees and fine for defaults in furnishing documents, complying with directions, maintaining solvency margin, or complying with insurance treaties. Section 103 imposes a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees and imprisonment up to three years for false statements. Section 104 sets a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees for failure to comply with investment-related sections (27, 27A, 27B, 27C, 27D). Section 105 imposes a penalty not exceeding two lakh rupees for wrongfully obtaining or withholding property. Section 105A details offences by companies. Section 105B imposes a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees and imprisonment up to three years for failure to comply with obligations in the rural or social sector (Section 32B). Section 105C imposes a penalty not exceeding twenty-five lakh rupees and potential cancellation of registration for failure to comply with obligations for rural or unorganised sectors and backward classes (Section 32C).

Non-compliance with the Act or rules/regulations can lead to penalties, fines, and imprisonment as detailed in the amended Insurance Act, 1938.

act_identification.act_title: THE FOREIGN EXCHANGE MANAGEMENT ACT, 1999

legislative_details.geographical_extent: It extends to the whole of India. It shall also apply to all branches, offices and agencies outside India owned or controlled by a person resident in India and also to any contravention thereunder committed outside India by any person to whom this Act applies.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to foreign exchange with the objective of facilitating external trade and payments and for promoting the orderly development and maintenance of foreign exchange market in India.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to consolidate and amend the law concerning foreign exchange. Its primary objectives are to facilitate external trade and payments and to promote the orderly development and maintenance of the foreign exchange market in India.

chapter_titles: REGULATION AND MANAGEMENT OF FOREIGN EXCHANGE

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical and extra-territorial application, and commencement details.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Dealing in foreign exchange, etc.
key_sections.description: Prohibits unauthorized dealing in foreign exchange or securities, payments to non-residents, and certain financial transactions.

key_sections.title: Holding of foreign exchange, etc.
key_sections.description: Restricts persons resident in India from acquiring, holding, owning, possessing, or transferring foreign exchange, foreign security, or immovable property outside India, unless otherwise provided.

key_sections.title: Capital account transactions.
key_sections.description: Allows persons to deal in foreign exchange for capital account transactions, subject to Reserve Bank and Central Government specifications and restrictions.

key_sections.title: Realisation and repatriation of foreign exchange.
key_sections.description: Mandates persons resident in India to take steps to realise and repatriate foreign exchange due or accrued to them.

key_sections.title: Authorised person.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Reserve Bank to authorise persons to deal in foreign exchange and outlines conditions for such authorisation and their duties.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contraventions of the Act, including monetary fines, confiscation, and imprisonment for certain serious contraventions.

key_sections.title: Enforcement of the orders of Adjudicating Authority.
key_sections.description: Details provisions for civil imprisonment for non-payment of penalties imposed by the Adjudicating Authority.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Adjudicating Authority.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of Adjudicating Authorities by the Central Government to inquire into contraventions and impose penalties.

key_sections.title: Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Designates the Appellate Tribunal constituted under the Smugglers and Foreign Exchange Manipulators (Forfeiture of Property) Act, 1976, as the Appellate Tribunal for this Act.

key_sections.title: Directorate of Enforcement.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Directorate of Enforcement for the purposes of the Act, including a Director and other officers.

key_sections.title: Special provisions relating to assets held outside India in contravention of section 4.
key_sections.description: Allows for the seizure of value equivalent to foreign assets held in contravention of section 4 and outlines the process involving an Authorised Officer and Competent Authority.

key_sections.title: Powers of Reserve Bank not to apply to International Financial Services Centre.
key_sections.description: States that the Reserve Bank's powers under this Act do not extend to International Financial Services Centres, where regulation is handled by the International Financial Services Centres Authority.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under the repealed Act and pending appeals.

powers_conferred: Reserve Bank: To specify classes of capital account transactions and limits (Section 6(2)); To prohibit, restrict, or regulate establishment of branches by non-residents (Section 6(6)); To specify limits for possession of foreign currency/coins (Section 9(a)); To specify classes of persons and limits for foreign currency accounts (Section 9(b)); To specify limits for exempted foreign exchange (Section 9(d), 9(e)); To specify other exempted receipts (Section 9(f)); To authorise persons to deal in foreign exchange (Section 10(1)); To revoke authorisation (Section 10(3)); To issue directions to authorised persons (Section 11(1)); To direct authorised persons to furnish information (Section 11(2)); To impose penalty on authorised persons (Section 11(3)); To inspect authorised persons (Section 12); To make regulations (Section 47).

Central Government: To impose restrictions on current account transactions (Section 5 Proviso); To prescribe classes of capital account transactions not involving debt instruments and limits (Section 6(2A)); To appoint Adjudicating Authorities (Section 16(1)); To specify jurisdiction of Adjudicating Authorities (Section 16(2)); To authorise officers to make complaints for adjudication (Section 16(3)); To appoint Special Directors (Appeals) (Section 17(1)); To establish Directorate of Enforcement (Section 36(1)); To authorise Director/Additional Director/Special Director/Deputy Director of Enforcement to appoint officers (Section 36(2)); To authorise other officers (Customs, Central Excise, Police) to exercise powers (Section 38(1)); To suspend or relax operation of the Act (Section 40(1)); To give directions to the Reserve Bank (Section 41); To make rules (Section 46).

Adjudicating Authority: To impose penalties (Section 13(1), 13(1A)); To order confiscation (Section 13(2)); To enforce orders and commit defaulters to civil prison (Section 14); To recover arrears of penalty (Section 14A); To hold inquiry (Section 16(1)); To direct furnishing of bond or guarantee (Section 16(1) Proviso); To exercise powers of a civil court (Section 16(5)).
Director of Enforcement: To compound contraventions (Section 15(1)); To direct prosecution (Section 13(1B)); To investigate contraventions (Section 37(1)).
Authorised Officer (under Section 37A): To seize value equivalent of foreign exchange, foreign security, or immovable property held in contravention of Section 4 (Section 37A(1)).
Competent Authority (under Section 37A): To confirm or set aside seizure orders (Section 37A(3)); To pass appropriate directions regarding seizure (Section 37A(4)).

Appellate Tribunal: To hear appeals (Section 19); To dispense with penalty deposit (Section 19 Proviso); To examine legality, propriety, or correctness of orders (Section 19(6)); To regulate its own procedure (Section 28(1)); To exercise powers of a civil court (Section 28(2)); To execute orders as a decree of civil court (Section 28(3)).

Special Director (Appeals): To hear appeals (Section 17); To entertain appeals after expiry of period (Section 17(3) Proviso); To regulate its own procedure (Section 28(1)); To exercise powers of a civil court (Section 28(2)); To execute orders as a decree of civil court (Section 28(3)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person contravening provisions of the Act or rules/regulations/directions/orders, or conditions of authorisation, is liable to a penalty up to thrice the sum involved (if quantifiable) or up to two lakh rupees (if not quantifiable). For continuing contraventions, an additional penalty of up to five thousand rupees per day applies. For acquiring foreign exchange, foreign security, or immovable property outside India exceeding a prescribed threshold in contravention of section 4, a penalty up to three times the sum involved and confiscation of equivalent value in India applies. Such contravention may also lead to imprisonment for up to five years and a fine. The Adjudicating Authority may also order confiscation of currency, security, money, or property involved in the contravention. Failure to pay penalty within ninety days can lead to civil imprisonment.

repealed_acts: Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973 (46 of 1973)
related_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
Unit Trust of India Act, 1963 (52 of 1963)
Smugglers and Foreign Exchange Manipulators (Forfeiture of Property) Act, 1976 (13 of 1976)
International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints Adjudicating Authorities (Section 16), Special Directors (Appeals) (Section 17), the Director and other officers of Enforcement (Section 36), and the Competent Authority (Section 37A). The Director of Enforcement or an Additional/Special/Deputy Director of Enforcement may appoint officers of Enforcement below the rank of Assistant Director (Section 36(2)).

applies_to: Whole of India
All branches, offices and agencies outside India owned or controlled by a person resident in India
Any contravention thereunder committed outside India by any person to whom this Act applies
Persons resident in India
Exporters of goods and services
Authorised persons
Companies
exemptions: Possession of foreign currency or foreign coins up to specified limit (Section 9(a))
Foreign currency account held or operated by specified persons/classes up to specified limit (Section 9(b))
Foreign exchange acquired or received before 8th July, 1947, or income thereon, held outside India with RBI permission (Section 9(c))
Foreign exchange held by a person resident in India up to specified limit, acquired by gift or inheritance from a person referred to in Section 9(c) (Section 9(d))
Foreign exchange acquired from employment, business, etc., up to specified limit (Section 9(e))
Other receipts in foreign exchange as the Reserve Bank may specify (Section 9(f))
Powers of Reserve Bank not to apply to International Financial Services Centre (Section 44A)
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act (Section 1(4) Proviso).
Special provisions relating to assets held outside India in contravention of section 4 (Section 37A).
Powers of Reserve Bank not to apply to International Financial Services Centre (Section 44A).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through adjudication by Adjudicating Authorities, who can impose penalties and order confiscation. Non-payment of penalties can lead to civil imprisonment. The Directorate of Enforcement investigates contraventions, with powers of search and seizure. Special provisions exist for assets held outside India in contravention of the Act, involving an Authorised Officer and Competent Authority. Appeals against orders of Adjudicating Authorities can be made to the Special Director (Appeals) and further to the Appellate Tribunal. The Central Government can empower other officers (Customs, Central Excise, Police) for enforcement. The Reserve Bank also has powers to issue directions, inspect, and impose penalties on authorised persons.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Appeals from the Appellate Tribunal lie to the High Court (Section 35). Civil courts are barred from entertaining suits or proceedings in matters determined by the Adjudicating Authority, Appellate Tribunal, or Special Director (Appeals) (Section 34). Criminal complaints for certain offences under Section 13(1C) are filed by officers of the Directorate of Enforcement.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL TRUST FOR WELFARE OF PERSONS WITH AUTISM, CEREBRAL PALSY, MENTAL RETARDATION AND MULTIPLE DISABILITIES ACT, 1999

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Offences include falsifying trade marks (S.102(1)) and falsely applying trade marks to goods or services (S.102(2)). Penalties for applying false trade marks or trade descriptions (S.103) and for selling goods/providing services with false marks (S.104) involve imprisonment from six months to three years and a fine from fifty thousand to two lakh rupees. Enhanced penalties apply for second or subsequent convictions (S.105). Falsely representing a trade mark as registered (S.107) incurs a penalty based on sales/turnover or a fixed sum. Failure to comply with adjudication orders (S.112B(6)) can lead to an additional fine or imprisonment. The Act also provides for the forfeiture of goods involved in offences (S.111).

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the registration and better protection of geographical indications relating to goods.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the registration and enhanced protection of geographical indications related to goods, ensuring their proper identification and preventing misuse.

key_sections.title: Penalty for applying false geographical indications.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for falsifying or falsely applying geographical indications.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Establishes liability for offences committed by companies, including the company itself and responsible individuals.

key_sections.title: Suit for infringement, etc., to be instituted before district court.
key_sections.description: Specifies that suits for infringement of a registered geographical indication or passing off must be filed in a district court.

powers_conferred: Registrar: withdraw or transfer cases, classify goods, refuse or accept applications, withdraw acceptance, advertise applications, decide opposition, permit correction or amendment, register geographical indications and users, issue certificates, amend register, renew registration, remove or restore from register, cancel or vary registration, rectify register, correct register, alter registered geographical indications, adapt entries in register, appear in legal proceedings, adjudicate penalties, exercise powers of a civil court for evidence, make orders as to costs, review own decision, exercise discretionary power, take evidence, extend time, treat application as abandoned, keep indexes.
