key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Offences include falsifying geographical indications (Section 38), falsely applying geographical indications (Section 38), selling goods with false geographical indications (Section 40), and falsely representing a geographical indication as registered (Section 42). Penalties for applying false GIs or selling goods with false GIs (Sections 39, 40) include imprisonment for not less than six months (extendable to three years) and a fine of not less than fifty thousand rupees (extendable to two lakh rupees). Enhanced penalties for second or subsequent convictions (Section 41) involve imprisonment for not less than one year (extendable to three years) and a fine of not less than one lakh rupees (extendable to two lakh rupees). Falsely representing a GI as registered (Section 42) incurs a penalty equal to one-half percent of total sales/turnover or gross receipts, or five lakh rupees, whichever is less. Offences by companies are also covered (Section 49), and goods involved in offences may be forfeited (Section 46).

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide legal recognition for electronic transactions and communications, including electronic commerce, and to facilitate electronic filing of documents with government agencies. It also aims to amend existing laws like the Indian Penal Code and Indian Evidence Act to accommodate electronic records and addresses matters related to cyber security and cybercrimes.

key_sections.description: Allows for the compounding of contraventions under the Act by the Controller or adjudicating officer, subject to certain conditions.

key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for dishonestly or fraudulently committing acts referred to in Section 43.

key_sections.title: Punishment for cyber terrorism.
key_sections.description: Defines and punishes acts of cyber terrorism, including denial of access, unauthorized access, and introduction of contaminants with intent to threaten national security or cause terror.

key_sections.title: Punishment for publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form.

key_sections.description: Empowers the Central or State Government to direct interception, monitoring, or decryption of information for national security, public order, and investigation purposes.

key_sections.description: Provides conditions under which an intermediary is exempt from liability for third-party information, data, or communication links.

key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws, with a proviso for Copyright and Patents Acts.

Appropriate Government: Authorise service providers for delivery of services (Section 6A), declare computer resources as protected systems (Section 70), authorise persons to access protected systems (Section 70).

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties and compensation for various cyber-related contraventions and offences. These include liability to pay damages for damage to computer systems (Section 43) and failure to protect data (Section 43A). Penalties for failure to furnish information or maintain records can range up to fifteen lakh rupees (Section 44). Residuary penalties apply for other contraventions, up to one lakh rupees plus compensation (Section 45). Specific offences like tampering with computer source documents (Section 65), computer-related offences (Section 66), identity theft (Section 66C), cyber terrorism (Section 66F, punishable with life imprisonment), and publishing obscene or sexually explicit material (Sections 67, 67A, 67B) carry imprisonment and/or significant fines. Non-compliance with directions from the Controller or government agencies for interception, blocking, or cyber security data collection also attracts imprisonment and/or fines (Sections 68, 69, 69A, 69B). Misrepresentation (Section 71), breach of confidentiality (Section 72), and fraudulent publication of electronic signature certificates (Section 74) are also punishable. The Act also provides for confiscation of devices (Section 76).

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India, and it shall apply to— (a) citizens of India outside India; and (b) associates, branches or subsidiaries, outside India of companies or bodies corporate, registered or incorporated in India.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to give effect to the Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production, Stockpiling and Use of Chemical Weapons and on their Destruction and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS a Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production, Stockpiling and Use of Chemical Weapons and on their Destruction was signed on behalf of the Government of India at Paris on the 14th day of January, 1993; AND WHEREAS India, having ratified the said Convention, has to make provisions for giving effect thereto and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to implement the Convention on the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons in India, making provisions for its enforcement and related matters. It seeks to prohibit the development, production, stockpiling, and use of chemical weapons and ensure their destruction.

powers_conferred: Central Government: deny request for inspection (Section 4), declare cessation of Act (Section 5), establish National Authority (Section 6), constitute Committee (Section 11), appoint enforcement officers (Section 9), make rules (Section 56), delegate powers (Section 53).

National Authority: issue directions (Section 10), call for information (Section 12), submit declarations to Organization (Section 8), fulfil obligations under Convention (Section 7), monitor compliance (Section 7), regulate toxic chemicals (Section 7), manage inspections (Section 7), advise Central Government (Section 7), ensure data confidentiality (Section 7), approve small-scale facilities (Section 7), provide training (Section 7), ensure protection of environment/health/safety (Section 7), coordinate information exchange (Section 7), determine quantity limits (Section 7).

Inspector: inspect any person or place (Section 19), interview facility personnel (Section 19), request clarifications (Section 19), demand documentation (Section 19), take photographs (Section 19), draw samples (Section 19).

Enforcement officer: enter any building or place for verification/search (Section 20), accompany Inspector/Inspection Team (Section 20), seize goods (Section 23, 24), arrest persons (Section 23, 24), stop and search conveyance (Section 26).
Magistrates: issue warrant for arrest or search (Section 22).
Courts: decide on confiscation of goods (Section 36).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter VI details various punishments: Failure to register (Section 39) with fine up to one lakh rupees, or imprisonment up to three years, or both. Contravention related to Chemical Weapons (Section 40), Schedule 1 Toxic Chemicals (Section 41), transfer of Schedule 2 Toxic Chemicals (Section 42), export/import of Toxic Chemicals (Section 43), or disclosure of confidential information (Section 44), or denial of access/obstruction (Section 45) are punishable with imprisonment not less than one year, extendable to life, and fine up to one lakh rupees. Failure to furnish information/declaration/return (Section 46) is punishable with fine up to one lakh rupees, or imprisonment up to three years, or both. Offences by companies (Section 48) hold both the company and responsible persons liable.

Appeals from National Authority decisions are allowed to the Central Government.

It includes Articles I to XXIV of the Convention, and three Annexes: the Annex on Chemicals (listing and categorizing toxic chemicals and precursors), the Annex on Implementation and Verification (detailing verification measures for chemical weapons, production facilities, and scheduled chemicals, including challenge inspections), and the Annex on the Protection of Confidential Information (outlining rules for handling sensitive data).

key_sections.description: Defines the period for which a layout-design registration is valid.

key_sections.title: Rights conferred by registration.
key_sections.description: Details the exclusive rights granted to the registered proprietor.

key_sections.title: Infringement of layout-design.
key_sections.description: Describes actions that constitute infringement and certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Layout-Design Appellate Board.
key_sections.description: Mandates the creation of the Appellate Board to handle disputes and appeals.

key_sections.title: Penalty for infringement of layout-design.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the punishment for knowingly and wilfully infringing a layout-design.

key_sections.title: Convention countries.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to notify countries for reciprocal privileges regarding layout-designs.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government authority to make rules for implementing the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoints Registrar and other officers; establishes Registry offices; defines territorial limits of Registry; establishes Appellate Board; appoints Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and Members of Appellate Board; determines staff for Appellate Board; protects security of India; specifies convention countries; removes difficulties; makes rules.

Registrar of Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design: Transfers pending matters; accepts or refuses registration applications; withdraws acceptance; advertises applications; decides opposition to registration; corrects and amends applications/notices; registers layout-designs; amends register/certificates; cancels registered user registrations; calls for information on user agreements; rectifies the register; corrects the register; has powers of a civil court for evidence, oaths, attendance, production of documents, commissions; exercises discretionary power; gives preliminary advice.

Layout-Design Appellate Board: Determines royalty; cancels registration of layout-designs or assignments/transmissions; hears appeals against Registrar's orders/decisions; regulates its own procedure; has powers of a civil court for receiving evidence, issuing commissions, requisitioning public records; permits certain uses of layout-designs by government/authorized persons; grants certificates of validity.
Chairperson of Appellate Board: Transfers cases between Benches.
Registered Proprietor: Assigns layout-design; gives receipts for assignment; applies for royalty determination.
Registered User: Takes proceedings against infringement (subject to agreement).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 56 prescribes imprisonment up to three years or a fine between fifty thousand and ten lakh rupees, or both, for infringement of layout-design. Section 57 penalizes falsely representing a layout-design as registered with imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to fifty thousand rupees, or both. Section 58 imposes penalties for improperly describing a place of business as connected with the Registry. Section 59 penalizes falsification of entries in the register with imprisonment up to two years or a fine, or both. Section 60 allows for forfeiture of goods related to an offence. Section 63 deals with offences committed by companies, and Section 67 addresses abetment of offences outside India.

authorities_established: Registrar of Semiconductor Integrated Circuits Layout-Design
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Registrar and other officers. The President of India appoints the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and other Members of the Appellate Board after consultation with the Chief Justice of India for the Chairperson.

applies_to: Whole of India
Any person claiming to be the creator of a layout-design
Registered proprietor
Registered user
Government
Citizens of convention countries
exemptions: Layout-designs which are not original, commercially exploited (with a two-year grace period), not inherently distinctive, or not inherently distinguishable (Section 7).
Acts of reproduction for limited purposes of scientific evaluation, analysis, research or teaching (Section 18(2)).
Creation of an original layout-design based on scientific evaluation or analysis of a registered one (Section 18(3)).
Performance of acts by a person without knowledge or reasonable ground to know of infringement, with royalty payment for stock on hand after notice (Section 18(5)).
Purchasers of semiconductor integrated circuits or articles from persons referred to in Section 18(5) (Section 18(6)).
Acts performed with the written consent of the registered proprietor (Section 18(7)).
Identical layout-design created by independent intellect (Section 18(8)).
Certain persons employed in the ordinary course of business who meet specific conditions (Section 61).
Servants acting in good faith in obedience to master's instructions (Section 90).
special_provisions: A layout-design commercially exploited for not more than two years from application date is treated as not commercially exploited (Proviso to Section 7(1)).
A combination of common elements can be original if the combination as a whole is the result of intellectual efforts (Proviso to Section 7(2)).
Where validity of assignment/transmission is in dispute, Registrar may refuse registration until rights are determined by a competent court (Proviso to Section 23(1)).
Before cancelling registration of a registered user, the proprietor must be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard (Proviso to Section 26(3)).
If the ground for cancellation of registration is established for only a part of a layout-design, only that part is cancelled (Proviso to Section 41(2)).
An appeal may be admitted after the specified period if the appellant shows sufficient cause for delay (Proviso to Section 42(2)).

The Appellate Board may permit use of a registered layout-design by the Government or authorized persons for non-commercial public purposes, national emergency, or extreme public urgency, subject to conditions and royalty (Section 51).
No order to remove difficulties shall be made after five years from the commencement of the Act (Proviso to Section 95(1)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the registration process by the Registrar, adjudication of disputes and appeals by the Layout-Design Appellate Board, and criminal penalties for infringement and other offences. Orders of the Appellate Board are executable by civil courts, and appeals from the Board lie to the High Courts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil courts, High Courts, and competent criminal courts. The Appellate Board also possesses powers vested in a civil court for specific matters.

act_identification.act_title: THE COAL INDIA (REGULATION OF TRANSFERS AND VALIDATION) ACT, 2000
act_identification.act_short_title: The Coal India (Regulation of Transfers and Validation) Act, 2000

act_overview.preamble: An Act to empower the Central Government to direct the transfer of the land, or of the rights in or over land or of the right, title and interest in relation to a coal mine, coking coal mine or coke oven plant, vested in the Coal India Limited or in a subsidiary company to any subsidiary company of Coal India Limited or any other subsidiary company and to validate certain transfers of such land or rights.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to empower the Central Government to direct the transfer of land, rights, title, or interest related to coal mines, coking coal mines, or coke oven plants vested in Coal India Limited or its subsidiary companies. It also aims to validate certain past transfers of such land or rights, ensuring their legal effectiveness and preventing legal challenges.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Coal India (Regulation of Transfers and Validation) Act, 2000'.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Coal India' and 'subsidiary company'.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to direct transfer of land, rights, title or interest.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to direct the transfer of land, rights, title, or interest related to coal mines, coking coal mines, or coke oven plants vested in Coal India Limited or its subsidiary companies.

key_sections.title: Validation of certain transfers.
key_sections.description: Validates past transfers of land, rights, title, or interest related to coal mines, coking coal mines, or coke oven plants that occurred before the commencement of this Act, deeming them valid and effective.

powers_conferred: Power of Central Government to direct transfer of land, rights, title or interest

related_acts: Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 (67 of 1957)

applies_to: Coal India Limited
subsidiary company
coal mine
coking coal mine
coke oven plant

act_identification.act_title: THE IMMIGRATION (CARRIERS’ LIABILITY) ACT, 2000

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Home Affairs

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make the carriers liable in respect of passengers brought by them into India in contravention of the provisions of the Passport (Entry into India) Act, 1920 and the rules made thereunder and matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the liability of carriers for bringing passengers into India in contravention of the Passport (Entry into India) Act, 1920. It empowers the Competent Authority to impose penalties on such carriers and outlines the process for appeals and recovery of penalties.

key_sections.title: Short title and extent.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as The Immigration (Carriers' Liability) Act, 2000, and states its applicability to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'carrier', 'Competent Authority', and 'prescribed'.

key_sections.title: Liability of carriers for passengers brought into India.
key_sections.description: Establishes that a Competent Authority may impose a penalty of rupees one lakh on a carrier for bringing a person into India in contravention of the Passport (Entry into India) Act, 1920, after providing an opportunity of being heard.

key_sections.title: Power to exempt.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to exempt any carrier or class of carrier from the Act's provisions in the public interest or to fulfill international obligations, subject to conditions.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Provides for an appeal mechanism against orders made under section 3 to the Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Home Affairs, specifying the time limit and procedure for appeals.

key_sections.title: Recovery of penalty due to Government.
key_sections.description: Outlines the method for recovering unpaid penalties, allowing the Competent Authority to seize, detain, or sell the aircraft, ship, or goods belonging to the carrier.

key_sections.title: Bar of legal proceedings.
key_sections.description: Protects the Central Government, Competent Authority, and officers from legal proceedings for actions done in good faith under the Act.

key_sections.title: Application of Acts 16 of 1939, 34 of 1920 and 31 of 1946 not barred.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the provisions of this Act are in addition to, and not in derogation of, the Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939, the Passport (Entry into India) Act, 1920, and the Foreigners Act, 1946.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including prescribing fees for appeals.

key_sections.title: Rules to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Mandates that every rule made under the Act must be laid before each House of Parliament for a specified period, allowing for modification or annulment.

powers_conferred: Competent Authority: Impose a penalty of rupees one lakh on carriers (Section 3).
Competent Authority: Recover unpaid penalties by seizing, detaining, or selling the aircraft, ship, or goods belonging to the carrier (Section 5).
Central Government: Exempt any carrier or class of carrier from the operations of all or any of the provisions of this Act (Section 3A).
Central Government: Make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act (Section 8).
Central Government: Remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of this Act (Section 10).
Joint Secretary to the Government of India in the Ministry of Home Affairs (Appellate Authority): Hear appeals, make inquiry, and confirm, modify, or reverse orders appealed against (Section 4).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: A penalty of rupees one lakh can be imposed on carriers who bring a person into India in contravention of the provisions of the Passport (Entry into India) Act, 1920 and the rules made thereunder.

applies_to: Carriers engaged in the business of transporting passengers by water or air
Any association of persons, whether incorporated or not, by whom the aircraft or the ship is owned or chartered
exemptions: Any carrier or class of carrier may be exempted by the Central Government from the operations of all or any of the provisions of this Act.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Competent Authority imposes penalties. Appeals can be made to the Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Home Affairs. Unpaid penalties can be recovered by seizing, detaining, or selling the carrier's aircraft, ship, or goods.

act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL ROAD AND INFRASTRUCTURE FUND ACT, 2000
act_identification.act_short_title: Central Road and Infrastructure Fund Act, 2000

act_overview.preamble: An Act to give statutory status to [1][the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund for development and maintenance of National Highways, railway projects, improvement of safety in railways, State and rural roads and other infrastructure, and for these purposes to levy and collect by way of cess, a duty of excise and a duty of customs on motor spirit commonly known as petrol and high speed diesel oil] and for other matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: To give statutory status to the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund for the development and maintenance of National Highways, railway projects, improvement of safety in railways, State and rural roads, and other infrastructure. It also provides for the levy and collection of cess on motor spirit and high speed diesel oil to fund these purposes.

chapter_titles: MANAGEMENT OF CENTRAL ROAD AND INFRASTRUCTURE FUND

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Levy and collection of cess.
key_sections.description: Mandates the levy and collection of cess as a duty of excise and customs on motor spirit and high speed diesel oil.

key_sections.title: Crediting of cess to Consolidated Fund of India.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that cess proceeds are first credited to the Consolidated Fund of India and then to the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Central [4][Road and Infrastructure Fund].
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund and specifies what amounts are credited to it.

key_sections.title: Utilisation of the Fund.
key_sections.description: Outlines the purposes for which the Fund shall be utilised, including development and maintenance of various roads and infrastructure projects.

key_sections.title: Apportionment of share of fund by Committee.
key_sections.description: States that a Committee constituted by the Central Government will finalise the apportionment of the Fund's share to infrastructure projects.

key_sections.title: Powers of Central Government to administer the Fund.
key_sections.description: Confers powers on the Central Government to administer the Fund, including investment decisions and measures to raise funds.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Central Government.
key_sections.description: Details the responsibilities of the Central Government regarding the administration, management, coordination, and allocation criteria for the Fund.

key_sections.title: Administration of States’ share of the Fund.
key_sections.description: Describes how the share of the Fund for State roads is allocated and administered, including provisions for resuming funds.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Central Road Fund Ordinance, 2000, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Levy and collect cess (Central Government, Sec 3)
Specify rates of cess (Central Government, Sec 3)
Establish the Fund (Central Government, Sec 6)
Control the Fund (Central Government, Sec 6(2))
Make grants or loans to the Fund (Central Government, Sec 5)
Administer the Fund (Central Government, Sec 9)
Take decisions regarding investment on projects (Central Government, Sec 9(a))
Take measures to raise funds (Central Government, Sec 9(b))
Formulate criteria for allocation of funds (Central Government, Sec 10(iv), (vi))
Amend Schedule II (Central Government, Sec 7(2))
Make rules (Central Government, Sec 12)
Constitute a Committee for apportionment of funds (Central Government, Sec 7A)
Resume funds from States/UTs (Central Government, Sec 11(3))

repealed_acts: The Central Road Fund Ordinance, 2000 (Ord. 5 of 2000)
related_acts: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (16 of 2016)

authorities_established: Committee, constituted by the Central Government by notification published in the Official Gazette, headed by the Finance Minister (for apportionment of fund share)
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (for constituting the Committee under Section 7A)

applies_to: whole of India
motor spirit commonly known as petrol and high speed diesel oil (for cess levy)
development and maintenance of National Highways, railway projects, improvement of safety in railways, State and rural roads and other infrastructure (for fund utilization)
special_provisions: The Central Government may resume the whole or part of any sums held for expenditure in a State or Union territory if the respective government or administration fails to take recommended steps for motor vehicle regulation and control, or delays the application of allocated funds without reasonable cause (Section 11(3)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the levy and collection of cess, crediting of proceeds to the Consolidated Fund of India and then to the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund, and the utilization and administration of this Fund by the Central Government, with accounts audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

schedules_summary.description: Lists items on which cess is levied, specifically Motor spirit commonly known as petrol and High speed diesel oil.
Specifies categories of projects and Infrastructure Sub-Sectors for which the Fund can be utilized, including Transport, Energy, Water and Sanitation, Communication, and Social and Commercial Infra.

act_identification.act_title: THE MIZORAM UNIVERSITY ACT, 2000

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of the State of Mizoram

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University in the State of Mizoram and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The Act establishes a teaching and affiliating university in Mizoram to advance knowledge, provide instructional and research facilities, and offer integrated courses. Its purpose is also to promote innovation in teaching and research, train manpower for the state's development, and improve the social, economic, intellectual, academic, and cultural welfare of the people of Mizoram.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the official name of the Act and specifies its effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as "Academic Council," "employee," "University," and "Vice-Chancellor."

key_sections.title: Establishment of the University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the "Mizoram University" as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, headquartered at Aizawl.

key_sections.title: Objects of the University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary goals of the University, including knowledge dissemination, research, integrated courses, innovation, manpower training, and social/economic development in Mizoram.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the extensive powers of the University, such as granting degrees, instituting teaching positions, establishing colleges, and managing its finances.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Defines the geographical area of the University's authority as the whole of the State of Mizoram and details the transfer of affiliations from North-Eastern Hill University.

key_sections.title: The Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor, outlining powers related to review, inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions to the University.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the principal officers of the University, including the Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Deans, Registrar, Finance Officer, and Librarian.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Specifies the main governing bodies of the University, such as the Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, and Finance Committee.

key_sections.title: Powers to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Details the matters for which Statutes can be made, covering the constitution of authorities, appointment of officers and staff, conditions of service, and academic distinctions.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Ordinances can be made, including student admission, courses of study, examinations, fees, and conditions for awards.

key_sections.title: Transfer of services of certain employees of the North-Eastern Hill University.
key_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of employees from North-Eastern Hill University to Mizoram University on similar terms and conditions.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees.
key_sections.description: Mandates written contracts for employees and establishes a Tribunal of Arbitration for disputes arising from these contracts.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make provisions to remove difficulties in implementing the Act for a period of three years.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Act 24 of 1973.
key_sections.description: Amends the North-Eastern Hill University Act, 1973, to remove Mizoram from its jurisdiction.

powers_conferred: University: to provide for instructions, grant diplomas/certificates/degrees, organise extramural studies, confer honorary degrees, provide distance education, institute teaching positions, recognise institutions, appoint teachers, create administrative/ministerial posts, co-operate/collaborate with other institutions, establish Centres/laboratories, institute fellowships/scholarships/medals/prizes, establish/maintain Colleges/Institutions/Halls, make provision for research/advisory services, organise refresher courses/workshops/seminars, admit colleges to privileges, appoint visiting Professors/Emeritus Professors/Consultants/Scholars, confer autonomous status, determine admission standards, demand/receive fees, supervise student residence, make arrangements for student health/welfare, lay down conditions of service for employees, regulate/enforce discipline, make arrangements for employee health/welfare, receive benefactions/donations/gifts, acquire/hold/manage/dispose of property, borrow money, and do all other necessary acts.

Visitor: to appoint persons to review work, cause inspection/inquiry, issue directions, annul proceedings of the University, make new or additional Statutes or amend/repeal Statutes (during a transitional period), and direct the University to make provisions in Statutes.

Vice-Chancellor: to exercise general supervision and control over University affairs, give effect to decisions of authorities, exercise powers of any authority in immediate action cases, ask authorities to review decisions, and convene meetings of the Executive Council, Academic Council, and Finance Committee.

Executive Council: to manage and administer the revenue and property of the University, conduct administrative affairs, create teaching/academic posts, appoint Professors/Readers/Lecturers/academic staff/Principals, create administrative/ministerial posts, grant leave of absence to officers, regulate/enforce discipline among employees, manage/regulate finances/accounts/investments/property/business, fix expenditure limits, invest money, transfer property, provide buildings/premises/furniture/apparatus, enter into contracts, entertain/adjudicate grievances of employees/students, appoint examiners/moderators, select common seal, make special arrangements for women students, delegate powers, institute fellowships/scholarships/studentships/medals/prizes, provide for inviting Writers-in-Residence, and provide for appointment of Visiting Professors/Emeritus Professors/Consultants/Scholars.

Registrar: to enter into agreements, sign documents, authenticate records, take disciplinary action against specified employees (excluding teachers/academic staff), suspend employees pending inquiry, administer warnings, impose penalties (censure, withholding increment), be custodian of records/common seal, issue notices for meetings, keep minutes of meetings, conduct official correspondence, arrange for/superintend examinations, supply agenda/minutes to Visitor, represent University in suits, sign powers of attorney, and verify pleadings.

Finance Officer: to exercise general supervision over University funds, advise on financial policy, hold/manage property/investments, ensure expenditure limits are not exceeded, prepare annual accounts/budget, watch cash/bank balances, watch revenue collection, ensure registers are maintained, bring unauthorised expenditure/financial irregularities to Vice-Chancellor's notice, and call for information/returns from offices/centres/colleges/institutions.

Academic Council: to exercise general supervision over academic policies, give directions regarding instruction methods, coordinate teaching, evaluate research, improve academic standards, bring about inter-School coordination, establish committees/boards for inter-School projects, consider matters of general academic interest, and frame regulations/rules regarding academic functioning, discipline, residences, admissions, fellowships, fees, concessions, corporate life, and attendance.
College Development Council: to admit Colleges to the privileges of the University.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act outlines disciplinary actions for students, including expulsion, rustication, debarment from examinations, fines, and cancellation of results. For employees, it provides for disciplinary actions such as suspension, removal, censure, and withholding of increments for misconduct.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Vice-Chancellor and has powers for initial appointments of the first Registrar, Finance Officer, Court, Executive Council, College Development Council, and Academic Council. The Executive Council appoints the Pro-Vice-Chancellor (on VC's recommendation), Registrar (on Selection Committee's recommendation), Finance Officer (on Selection Committee's recommendation), Librarian (on Selection Committee's recommendation), Heads of Departments (on VC's recommendation), Proctor (on VC's recommendation), Professors, Readers, Lecturers, other academic staff, and Principals of Colleges/Institutions (on Selection Committee's recommendation), and creates administrative/ministerial posts. The Vice-Chancellor appoints Deans of Schools.

applies_to: persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class
Colleges, Institutions, Schools and Departments affiliated to, or admitted to the privileges of, or maintained by, the University
exemptions: The University may make special provisions for the employment or admission of women, physically handicapped persons, persons belonging to weaker sections of society, and Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
special_provisions: The University may make special provisions for the employment or admission of women, physically handicapped persons, persons belonging to weaker sections of society, and Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

Transitional provisions for the appointment of the first Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, and the nomination of members to the first Court, Executive Council, College Development Council, and Academic Council by the Visitor for a specified term.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Statutes are made by the Executive Council (with Visitor's assent) or directly by the Visitor. Ordinances are initially made by the Vice-Chancellor with Central Government approval and subsequently by the Executive Council. Regulations are made by the authorities of the University.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act establishes various authorities and officers (e.g., Vice-Chancellor, Executive Council, Academic Council) with powers to manage, administer, regulate, and enforce discipline within the University. Disputes concerning employee contracts and student disciplinary actions are referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the initial Statutes of the University, detailing the constitution, powers, and functions of various officers (e.g., Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, Deans, Heads of Departments, Proctor, Librarian) and authorities (e.g., Executive Council, Academic Council, Finance Committee, Selection Committee). It also includes provisions for special appointments, recognized teachers, committees, terms and conditions of service, removal of employees, honorary degrees, withdrawal of degrees, maintenance of discipline among students, admission of colleges, convocations, resignation, disqualification, residence conditions, Alumni Association, Students' Council, and the process for making Ordinances and Regulations.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN COUNCIL OF WORLD AFFAIRS ACT, 2001
act_identification.act_short_title: THE INDIAN COUNCIL OF WORLD AFFAIRS ACT, 2001

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of External Affairs

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare the Indian Council of World Affairs to be an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act declares the Indian Council of World Affairs as an institution of national importance. It provides for its incorporation, the transfer of assets and liabilities from the existing society, and establishes its structure, powers, and functions. The primary objective is to promote the study of Indian and international affairs, foster India's relations with other countries through research and discussion, and serve as a knowledge hub on world affairs.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its deemed date of commencement.

key_sections.title: Declaration of the Indian Council of World Affairs as institution of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the Indian Council of World Affairs as an institution of national importance.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of the Council.
key_sections.description: Constitutes the Indian Council of World Affairs as a body corporate with perpetual succession and common seal.

key_sections.title: Transfer of assets and liabilities of the existing Council to the Council.
key_sections.description: Details the vesting of properties, assets, debts, obligations, and employees from the existing Council to the newly incorporated Council.

key_sections.title: Composition of the Council.
key_sections.description: Outlines the members constituting the Council, including ex officio members and nominated members, and disqualifications for membership.

key_sections.title: Objects of Council.
key_sections.description: Specifies the objectives of the Council, including promoting the study of Indian and international affairs, fostering relations, and serving as an information clearing house.

key_sections.title: Governing Body and other committees of Council.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Governing Body as the executive committee and allows for the constitution of other standing and ad hoc committees.

key_sections.title: Staff of Council.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of a Director-General as the chief executive officer and other officers and employees of the Council.

key_sections.title: Fund of Council.
key_sections.description: Describes the establishment and management of the Council's fund, including sources of credit and application of moneys.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Mandates the maintenance of accounts and their audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, with reports to Parliament.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Council the power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Indian Council of World Affairs (Second) Ordinance, 2001, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: Council: to acquire, hold and dispose of property, both movable and immovable, and to contract and shall by that name sue and be sued (Section 4)
Council: to establish branches at other places in India with Central Government approval (Section 4)
Council: to constitute a Governing Body and other committees (Section 14)
Council: to appoint officers and employees (Section 15)
Council: to make regulations (Section 26)
President: to exercise such powers and discharge such functions as laid down in the Act or prescribed by rules (Section 9)
Vice-Presidents: to exercise such powers and perform such functions of the President as prescribed by rules or delegated by the President (Section 10)
Central Government: to appoint date for Council composition (Section 7)
Central Government: to remove members of the Council (Section 8)
Central Government: to appoint time and place for the first meeting of the Council (Section 12)
Central Government: to prescribe other functions for the Council (Section 16)
Central Government: to pay sums to the Council after due appropriation by Parliament (Section 17)
Central Government: to approve the manner of depositing or investing the Fund of the Council (Section 18)

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the efficient use and conservation of energy. It also covers matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to enforce efficient use of energy and its conservation.

key_sections.title: Issuance of carbon credit certificate.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To enforce efficient use of energy and its conservation (Section 14), issue energy savings certificates (Section 14A), issue carbon credit certificates (Section 14AA), specify value of energy (Section 14B), issue directions to any person, officer, authority or designated consumer (Section 18, 46, 55), supersede the Bureau (Section 47), exempt designated consumers (Section 53), make rules (Section 56), and remove difficulties (Section 62).

State Government: To enforce certain provisions for efficient use of energy and its conservation (Section 15), establish a State Energy Conservation Fund (Section 16), issue directions to any person, officer, authority or designated consumer (Section 18), exempt designated consumers (Section 53), and make rules (Section 57).

Bureau of Energy Efficiency: To coordinate with designated consumers and agencies, recommend norms and standards, recommend particulars for labels, recommend designated consumers, prescribe guidelines for building codes, create awareness, organize training, strengthen consultancy, promote R&D, develop testing and certification, formulate pilot projects, promote energy efficient processes, promote innovative financing, give financial assistance, levy fees, maintain a list of accredited energy auditors, specify qualifications and procedures for accreditation, specify energy audit intervals, specify certification procedures for energy auditors/managers, prepare educational curriculum, conduct examinations, implement international co-operation programmes, collaborate with international institutions, authorise agencies, test samples, empanel technical experts, recommend carbon credit scheme requirements, recommend minimum share of non-fossil sources (Section 13), and make regulations (Section 58).

Specific penalties apply for non-conforming equipment/appliances/vehicles/vessels/industrial units, and for non-compliance with carbon credit scheme related directions. Misuse of the Bureau's name or failure to provide information also attracts penalties.

act_identification.act_title: THE PROTECTION OF PLANT VARIETIES AND FARMERS’ RIGHTS ACT, 2001
act_identification.act_short_title: the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001

legislative_details.ministry_department: Department of Agriculture and Cooperation

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of an effective system for protection of plant varieties, the rights of farmers and plant breeders and to encourage the development of new varieties of plants. WHEREAS it is considered necessary to recognise and protect the rights of the farmers in respect of their contribution made at any time in conserving, improving and making available plant genetic resources for the development of new plant varieties; AND WHEREAS for accelerated agricultural development in the country, it is necessary to protect plant breeders' rights to stimulate investment for research and development, both in the public and private sector, for the development of new plant varieties; AND WHEREAS such protection will facilitate the growth of the seed industry in the country which will ensure the availability of high quality seeds and planting material to the farmers; AND WHEREAS, to give effect to the aforesaid objectives, it is necessary to undertake measures for the protection of the rights of farmers and plant breeders; AND WHEREAS India, having ratified the Agreement on Trade Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights should, inter alia, make provision for giving effect to sub-paragraph (b) of paragraph 3 of article 27 in Part II of the said Agreement relating to protection of plant varieties.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish a system for the protection of plant varieties and the rights of farmers and plant breeders. It seeks to encourage the development of new plant varieties, recognize farmers' contributions to genetic resources, stimulate investment in plant breeding research, and facilitate the growth of the seed industry in India.

act_identification.act_title: THE HAJ COMMITTEE ACT, 2002

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish a Haj Committee of India and State Haj Committees for making arrangements for the pilgrimage of Muslims for Haj, and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes a Haj Committee of India and State Haj Committees to make arrangements for the pilgrimage of Muslims for Haj. It aims to facilitate and manage all matters connected with the Haj pilgrimage.

key_sections.title: Constitution and incorporation of Haj Committee of India.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Haj Committee of India as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, headquartered at Mumbai.

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to implement international agreements, specifically the Convention on International Civil Aviation, by providing for the exemption from taxes and duties on fuel and lubricants supplied to foreign aircraft in India.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to co-operative societies, with objects not confined to one State and serving the interests of members in more than one State, to facilitate the voluntary formation and democratic functioning of co-operatives as people’s institutions based on self-help and mutual aid and to enable them to promote their economic and social betterment and to provide functional autonomy and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend laws for co-operative societies operating across multiple states. Its primary objective is to facilitate the voluntary formation and democratic functioning of co-operatives, promoting members' economic and social betterment through self-help and mutual aid, while ensuring functional autonomy.

key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of a Co-operative Election Authority by the Central Government to conduct elections for multi-State co-operative societies.

key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Registrar to conduct inquiries into the constitution, working, and financial condition of a multi-State co-operative society under specified circumstances.

key_sections.description: Stipulates that disputes touching the constitution, management, or business of a multi-State co-operative society shall be referred to arbitration.

key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of a Co-operative Ombudsman by the Central Government to inquire into and adjudicate complaints from members.

powers_conferred: Central Registrar: Registration of societies and bye-laws (Sec 7, 11), appoint officers to assist (Sec 4), prepare amalgamation schemes (Sec 18), cancel registration (Sec 21, 93), convene general meetings (Sec 39, 40), appoint auditors (Sec 70), direct special audit (Sec 77), hold inquiry (Sec 78), inspect societies (Sec 79, 80), apportion costs (Sec 81), make winding up orders (Sec 86), appoint liquidator (Sec 89), execute decisions (Sec 94), recover sums due to Government (Sec 98), review decisions (Sec 98A).

Board of Directors: Exercise powers for functions under Act (Sec 49), admit members, elect Chairperson/President, interpret objectives, appraise operations, appoint/remove Chief Executive and other employees, approve annual reports/budgets, acquire/dispose of property, raise funds, sanction loans.

Chief Executive: Day-to-day management, operate accounts, sign documents, maintain records, convene meetings, make appointments, assist board, furnish information, appoint person to sue/be sued, present annual report/financial statement (Sec 52).
Co-operative Election Authority: Conduct elections, supervise electoral rolls, other functions (Sec 45-I), issue directions (Sec 45L).
Co-operative Ombudsman: Inquire into complaints, adjudicate, issue directions (Sec 85A).

Liquidator: Take custody of property, carry on business, institute/defend suits, determine contributions, investigate claims, pay claims, determine costs, determine membership, give directions for asset collection/distribution, compromise with creditors/persons (Sec 90).

Central Government: Appoint Central Registrar (Sec 4), give directions to specified multi-State co-operative societies (Sec 122), supersede board (Sec 123), make rules (Sec 124), remove difficulties (Sec 125), amend Schedules (Sec 116).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 104 outlines various offences and penalties. These include fines for wilfully making false returns or information, failing to file returns, disobeying summons, or not furnishing required information (fine not less than 5,000 rupees, may extend to 1 lakh rupees). Employers failing to pay deducted amounts under Section 60 face a fine up to 10,000 rupees. Officers or custodians wilfully failing to hand over records or property are punishable with a fine up to 5,000 rupees, with a further fine up to 10,000 rupees per day for continuing breaches. Fraudulent acts related to elections (e.g., defacing nomination papers, tampering with ballot papers, offering/receiving gratification) are punishable with imprisonment up to six months or fine or both, and debarment from contesting elections for three years. The board of directors or responsible officers of a multi-State co-operative society can face imprisonment (1 month to 1 year) or fine (5,000 to 1 lakh rupees) or both for destroying/falsifying documents, making contravening investments, or causing unlawful loss to assets or depositors. Unlawful gains by directors or officers are also punishable with imprisonment and fine, with proceeds recovered.

Lists schemes and plans that constitute the 'undertaking' (excluding the specified undertaking) to be vested in the specified company.

act_identification.act_title: THE SECURITISATION AND RECONSTRUCTION OF FINANCIAL ASSETS AND ENFORCEMENT OF SECURITY INTEREST ACT, 2002
act_identification.act_short_title: The Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate securitisation and reconstruction of financial assets and enforcement of security interest and to provide for a Central database of security interests created on property rights, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act regulates the securitisation and reconstruction of financial assets and the enforcement of security interests by banks and financial institutions. It also establishes a central database for security interests created on property rights to facilitate recovery of debts.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II REGULATION OF SECURITISATION AND RECONSTRUCTION OF FINANCIAL ASSETS OF BANKS AND FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS
CHAPTER III ENFORCEMENT OF SECURITY INTEREST
CHAPTER IVA REGISTRATION BY SECURED CREDITORS AND OTHER CREDITORS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Short title, extent and commencement of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Registration of asset reconstruction companies.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration for asset reconstruction companies with the Reserve Bank.

key_sections.title: Measures for assets reconstruction.
key_sections.description: Outlines measures an asset reconstruction company can take for asset reconstruction, including management takeover and debt conversion.

key_sections.title: Enforcement of security interest.
key_sections.description: Empowers secured creditors to enforce security interests without court intervention in case of borrower default.

key_sections.title: Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or District Magistrate to assist secured creditor in taking possession of secured asset.
key_sections.description: Provides for assistance from Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or District Magistrate to secured creditors for taking possession of secured assets.

key_sections.title: Application against measures to recover secured debts.
key_sections.description: Allows aggrieved persons (including borrowers) to apply to the Debts Recovery Tribunal against measures taken by secured creditors.

key_sections.title: Appeal to Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals to the Appellate Tribunal against orders of the Debts Recovery Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Central Registry.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Central Registry for registration of securitisation, reconstruction, and security interest transactions.

key_sections.title: Registration by secured creditors and other creditors.
key_sections.description: Extends registration provisions of Chapter IV to other creditors and mandates filing of attachment orders.

key_sections.title: Priority to secured creditors.
key_sections.description: Establishes priority for debts due to secured creditors after registration of security interest.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for defaults in filing particulars of transactions, modifications, or intimations of satisfaction.

key_sections.title: Provisions of this Act not to apply in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Lists specific cases and types of security interests to which the Act does not apply.

key_sections.title: Civil court not to have jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Bars civil courts from having jurisdiction over matters determinable by Debts Recovery Tribunal or Appellate Tribunal under this Act.

key_sections.title: The provisions of this Act to override other laws.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act override other inconsistent laws.

powers_conferred: Reserve Bank: To determine policy and issue directions (Section 12), call for statements and information (Section 12A), carry out audit and inspection (Section 12B), impose penalty (Section 30A).

Central Government: To set up Central Registry (Section 20), appoint Central Registrar (Section 21), make rules (Section 38), remove difficulties (Section 40), exempt banks/financial institutions (Section 31A).

Secured Creditor: To enforce security interest without court intervention (Section 13), take possession of secured assets (Section 13(4)), take over management (Section 13(4)), appoint manager (Section 13(4)), require payment from debtors of borrower (Section 13(4)).
Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or District Magistrate: To assist secured creditor in taking possession of secured asset (Section 14).

Asset Reconstruction Company: To acquire financial assets (Section 5), issue security receipts (Section 7), provide for asset reconstruction measures (Section 9), act as agent/manager/receiver (Section 10).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 27 prescribes penalties for default in filing particulars of transactions, modification, or intimation of satisfaction, with fines up to five thousand rupees per day. Section 29 outlines offences for contravening the Act or rules, punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both. Section 30A empowers the adjudicating authority (Reserve Bank) to impose penalties on asset reconstruction companies or persons for non-compliance with directions, up to one crore rupees or twice the amount involved, plus daily penalties for continuing failure.

amended_acts: Enforcement of Security Interest and Recovery of Debts Laws (Amendment) Act, 2004
Enforcement of Security Interest and Recovery of Debts Laws (Amendment) Act, 2013
Enforcement of Security Interest and Recovery of Debts Laws and Miscellaneous Provisions (Amendment) Act, 2016

Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959

applies_to: Banks
Financial Institutions
Asset Reconstruction Companies
Borrowers
Secured Creditors
Debenture Trustees
Qualified Buyers
exemptions: A lien on any goods, money or security given by or under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 or the Sale of Goods Act, 1930 or any other law for the time being in force.
A pledge of movables within the meaning of section 172 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
Creation of any security in any aircraft as defined in clause (1) of section 2 of the Aircraft Act, 1934.
Creation of security interest in any vessel as defined in clause (55) of section 3 of the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958.
Any rights of unpaid seller under section 47 of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930.

Any properties not liable to attachment (excluding the properties specifically charged with the debt recoverable under this Act) or sale under the first proviso to sub-section (1) of section 60 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

Power to exempt a class or classes of banks or financial institutions by Central Government notification (Section 31A).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Secured creditors can enforce security interests without court intervention, taking measures such as possession of assets or management takeover. Chief Metropolitan Magistrates or District Magistrates assist in possession. Disputes are resolved by conciliation or arbitration. Applications against measures are made to the Debts Recovery Tribunal, with appeals to the Appellate Tribunal. The Central Registry facilitates registration of transactions. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Debts Recovery Tribunal, Appellate Tribunal, Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class (for offences), Principal civil court (for recovery of penalties). Civil courts are barred from jurisdiction in matters covered by the Act.

schedules_summary.description: Specifies amendments to other enactments, including the Companies Act, 1956, the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, and the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985.

act_identification.act_title: THE METRO RAILWAYS (OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE) ACT, 2002
act_identification.act_short_title: the Metro Railways (Operation and Maintenance) Act, 2002

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of the Government of India dealing with Railways
legislative_details.geographical_extent: National Capital Region, metropolitan city and metropolitan area

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the operation and maintenance and to regulate the working of the metro railway in the [1][National Capital Region, metropolitan city and metropolitan area] and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the operation, maintenance, and regulation of metro railways in the National Capital Region, metropolitan cities, and metropolitan areas. It covers aspects like administration, safety, fare fixation, accident inquiries, and penalties for offences.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II: GOVERNMENT METRO RAILWAY ADMINISTRATION
CHAPTER III: FUNCTIONS AND POWERS OF THE METRO RAILWAY ADMINISTRATION
CHAPTER IV: COMMISSIONER OF METRO RAILWAY SAFETY
CHAPTER V: OPENING OF METRO RAILWAY
CHAPTER VI: WORKING OF THE METRO RAILWAY
CHAPTER X: LIABILITY OF METRO RAILWAY ADMINISTRATION DUE TO ACCIDENTS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Functions of metro railway administration.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary duties of metro railway administrations, including operation and maintenance.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety.
key_sections.description: Establishes the position of Commissioner for Metro Railway Safety to oversee safety aspects.

key_sections.title: Sanction of Central Government to the opening of metro railway.
key_sections.description: Requires previous sanction from the Central Government for opening metro railways for public carriage of passengers.

key_sections.title: Prohibition against travelling without pass or ticket.
key_sections.description: Prohibits any person from travelling in a metro railway carriage without a proper pass or ticket.

key_sections.title: Fixation of fare for carriage of passengers.
key_sections.description: Mandates the metro railway administration to fix passenger fares based on recommendations from the Fare Fixation Committee.

key_sections.title: Notice of metro railway accident.
key_sections.description: Requires immediate notice of metro railway accidents involving loss of life, grievous hurt, collisions, or derailments.

key_sections.title: Claims Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of a Claims Commissioner to adjudicate compensation claims arising from metro railway accidents.

key_sections.title: Extent of liability.
key_sections.description: Defines the metro railway administration's liability to pay compensation for death or bodily injury caused by accidents.

key_sections.title: Drunkenness or nuisance on metro railway.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for persons in a state of intoxication or committing nuisance on metro railways, and for intoxicated officials.

key_sections.title: Maliciously wrecking a train or causing sabotage.
key_sections.description: Defines severe offences related to damaging metro railway property with intent to endanger safety, including sabotage, and prescribes penalties.

key_sections.title: Power of arrest without warrant.
key_sections.description: Grants metro railway officials and police officers the power to arrest without warrant for certain specified offences.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers general power on the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Delhi Metro Railway (Operation and Maintenance) Ordinance, 2002, and includes savings provisions for actions taken under it.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Sanction opening of metro railway (Sec 14), appoint General Manager (Sec 4), appoint Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety (Sec 7), make rules (Sec 22, 32, 47, 56, 100), issue directions (Sec 86), remove difficulties (Sec 99).

Metro Railway Administration: Maintain and operate metro railway (Sec 5), acquire/hold/dispose of property (Sec 6), develop land (Sec 6), levy and collect penalties (Sec 6), employ agents/contractors (Sec 6), display commercial advertisements (Sec 29), fix fares (Sec 33), make regulations (Sec 101), constitute and maintain security staff (Sec 97).

Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety: Inspect metro railway (Sec 8), inquire into accidents (Sec 8, 39), require attendance of officials and production of documents (Sec 9), close metro railway or discontinue rolling stock use (Sec 18, via Central Government direction).
Claims Commissioner: Adjudicate claims for compensation (Sec 48), powers of a civil court (Sec 53).
Metro Railway Official: Remove persons from train/premises (Sec 26, 30, 31, 62, 63, 67), arrest without warrant (Sec 82, 83).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter XI details various offences and corresponding penalties, including: drunkenness or nuisance (fine up to 500 rupees, forfeiture of fare/ticket; for officials, penalty up to 10,000 rupees or imprisonment up to 2 years or both); taking offensive material (fine up to 500 rupees); taking dangerous material (imprisonment up to 4 years and fine up to 5,000 rupees); prohibition of demonstrations (imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both); travelling on roof (penalty up to 5,000 rupees); unlawfully entering or remaining on metro railway or walking on track (imprisonment up to 3/6 months, or fine up to 250/500 rupees, or both); endangering safety by metro railway official (imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine up to 30,000 rupees, or both); abandoning train (imprisonment up to 4 years, or fine up to 5,000 rupees, or both); obstructing running of train (imprisonment up to 4 years, or fine up to 5,000 rupees, or both); obstructing metro railway official (imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both); travelling without proper pass or ticket (excess charge); needlessly interfering with communication means (penalty up to 10,000 rupees); altering, defacing or counterfeiting pass or ticket (imprisonment up to 6 months); defacing public notices (imprisonment up to 2 months, or fine up to 250 rupees, or both); unauthorised sale of articles (fine up to 500 rupees, or imprisonment up to 6 months); maliciously wrecking a train or causing sabotage (imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, or death if intent to cause death); unauthorised sale of tickets (imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to 500 rupees, or both); maliciously hurting persons (imprisonment for life or up to 10 years); endangering safety by rash or negligent act (imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both); damage to metro railway properties (imprisonment up to 10 years); endangering safety by wilful act or omission (imprisonment up to 7 years). Section 80 regarding false claims for compensation has been omitted.

related_acts: National Capital Region Planning Board Act, 1985 (2 of 1985)
Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Act, 1978 (33 of 1978)
Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023 (18 of 2023)

Metro railways in metropolitan cities and metropolitan areas (as extended by notification)
