implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate shall try an offence under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE SUPPRESSION OF UNLAWFUL ACTS AGAINST SAFETY OF MARITIME NAVIGATION AND FIXED PLATFORMS ON CONTINENTAL SHELF ACT, 2002
act_identification.act_short_title: THE SUPPRESSION OF UNLAWFUL ACTS AGAINST SAFETY OF MARITIME NAVIGATION AND FIXED PLATFORMS ON CONTINENTAL SHELF ACT, 2002

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of India including the limit of the territorial waters, the continental shelf, the exclusive economic zone or any other maritime zone of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to give effect to the International Maritime Organisation Convention for Suppression of Unlawful Acts Against the Safety of Maritime Navigation and the Protocol for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts Against the Safety of Fixed Platforms Located on the Continental Shelf and for matters connected therewith. WHEREAS a Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts Against the Safety of Maritime Navigation and the Protocol for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts Against the Safety of Fixed Platforms Located on the Continental Shelf were signed at Rome on the 10th day of March, 1988; AND WHEREAS India, having acceded to the said Convention and the Protocol, should make provisions for giving effect thereto and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to give effect to the International Maritime Organisation Convention for Suppression of Unlawful Acts Against the Safety of Maritime Navigation and the Protocol for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts Against the Safety of Fixed Platforms Located on the Continental Shelf. It provides for the suppression of unlawful acts against the safety of maritime navigation and fixed platforms, and for matters connected therewith, in accordance with India's international commitments.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's name, geographical scope, conditions of applicability, and commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Offences against ship, fixed platform, cargo of a ship, maritime navigational facilities, etc.
key_sections.description: Details various unlawful acts against maritime safety and fixed platforms, including violence, destruction, seizure, damage, and false communication, along with their corresponding punishments.

key_sections.title: Conferment of powers of investigation.
key_sections.description: Grants powers of arrest, investigation, and prosecution to gazetted officers of the Coast Guard or Central Government.

key_sections.title: Designated Courts.
key_sections.description: Provides for the State Government to specify Courts of Session as Designated Courts for speedy trials of offences under the Act.

key_sections.title: Offence triable by Designated Court.
key_sections.description: Specifies that all offences under this Act are triable only by Designated Courts and outlines procedures for detention and cognizance.

key_sections.title: Provision as to bail.
key_sections.description: Lays down special conditions for granting bail to persons accused of offences under this Act, overriding certain provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

key_sections.title: Provisions as to extradition.
key_sections.description: Deems offences under Section 3 as extraditable offences under existing treaties and clarifies jurisdiction for extradition purposes.

key_sections.title: Previous sanction necessary for prosecution.
key_sections.description: Requires prior sanction from the Central Government for instituting prosecution for an offence under this Act.

key_sections.title: Presumptions as to offences under section 3.
key_sections.description: Establishes presumptions of guilt in certain circumstances for offences under Section 3, based on evidence like recovery of arms or use of force.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Provides immunity from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the provisions of this Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to appoint commencement date (S.1(5)), designate authority to take persons into custody (S.3(6)), confer powers of investigation on officers (S.4(1)), certify Convention/Protocol States (S.10), treat ships as registered in Convention States (S.11), grant sanction for prosecution (S.12).
State Government: Power to specify Designated Courts (S.5(1)).
Designated Courts: Power to try offences under the Act (S.6), exercise powers of a Magistrate regarding detention (S.6(1)(c)), take cognizance of offences (S.6(1)(d)).
Gazetted officers of Coast Guard/Central Government: Powers of arrest, investigation, and prosecution (S.4(1)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 3 defines various unlawful acts against ships, fixed platforms, cargo, and maritime navigational facilities. Penalties include imprisonment for terms extending up to ten or fourteen years, life imprisonment, and in cases causing death, the death penalty. Fines are also applicable for some offences. Attempting or abetting such offences is punishable as if the offence itself was committed.

related_acts: Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and other Maritime Zones Act, 1976 (80 of 1976)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government can designate authorities for custody (S.3(6)) and confer investigation powers on gazetted officers (S.4(1)). State Government specifies Designated Courts (S.5(1)).

applies_to: The whole of India including the limit of the territorial waters, the continental shelf, the exclusive economic zone or any other maritime zone of India (S.1(2)).
Any offence under section 3 committed outside India by any person (S.1(3)(a)).

A ship, if that ship is navigating or scheduled to navigate into, through or from waters beyond the outer limits of the territorial waters of India, or the lateral limits of its territorial waters with adjacent States (S.1(3)(b)).
Offences committed on board a ship in the territorial waters of India or against a fixed platform located on the Continental Shelf of India (S.1(3)(c)).
Offences committed by an offender or alleged offender when found in the territory of a Convention State, Protocol State, or any other State (S.1(4)).
Indian ships, any ship in the territory of India, and stateless persons (S.3(4)).
Alleged offenders who are citizens of India or found in India (S.3(8)(c)).
special_provisions: The Act applies only to offences committed by an offender or alleged offender when such an offender is found in the territory of a Convention State, Protocol State, or a State other than those referred to (S.1(4)).

No court shall take cognizance of an offence committed outside India unless specific conditions are met, such as the offence being on an Indian-flagged ship, a ship chartered to an Indian lessee, or if the alleged offender is an Indian citizen or found in India (S.3(8)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through investigation by designated officers (S.4), trial by Designated Courts (S.5, S.6), specific provisions for bail (S.8), and extradition procedures (S.9). Prosecution requires previous sanction from the Central Government (S.12).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Designated Courts

act_identification.act_title: THE COMPETITION ACT, 2002

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir. Vide notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019, this Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide, keeping in view of the economic development of the country, for the establishment of a Commission to prevent practices having adverse effect on competition, to promote and sustain competition in markets, to protect the interests of consumers and to ensure freedom of trade carried on by other participants in markets, in India, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to establish a Commission to prevent practices that harm competition, promote and sustain competition in markets, protect consumer interests, and ensure freedom of trade for market participants in India. It also covers matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

chapter_titles: PROHIBITION OF CERTAIN AGREEMENTS, ABUSE OF DOMINANT POSITION AND REGULATION OF COMBINATIONS
DUTIES, POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF COMMISSION

key_definitions: words and expressions used but not defined in this Act and defined in the Companies Act, 2013 (18 of 2013)

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its geographical extent to the whole of India (with specific mention of J&K/Ladakh), and that it comes into force on dates appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act, such as 'acquisition', 'agreement', 'cartel', 'Commission', 'consumer', 'enterprise', 'relevant market', etc.

key_sections.title: Anti-competitive agreements.
key_sections.description: Prohibits enterprises or persons from entering into agreements that cause or are likely to cause an appreciable adverse effect on competition within India, detailing types of agreements presumed to be anti-competitive and certain exemptions.

key_sections.title: Abuse of dominant position.
key_sections.description: Prohibits any enterprise or group from abusing its dominant position, outlining specific actions that constitute such abuse, including imposing unfair conditions or prices, limiting production, or denying market access.

key_sections.title: Combination.
key_sections.description: Defines what constitutes a 'combination' based on thresholds of assets or turnover for acquisitions, mergers, or amalgamations, and includes explanations for 'control', 'group', 'turnover', and 'value of transaction'.

key_sections.title: Regulation of combinations.
key_sections.description: Prohibits combinations that cause or are likely to cause an appreciable adverse effect on competition and mandates notice to the Commission for proposed combinations, with provisions for deemed approval or voidance.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Commission.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the 'Competition Commission of India' as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, and specifies its head office and power to establish other offices.

key_sections.title: Duties and functions of Commission.
key_sections.description: Outlines the Commission's duties to eliminate anti-competitive practices, promote competition, protect consumers, and ensure freedom of trade in Indian markets, including entering into arrangements with foreign agencies or statutory authorities.

key_sections.title: Inquiry into certain agreements and dominant position of enterprise.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Commission to inquire into alleged contraventions of anti-competitive agreements or abuse of dominant position, either suo motu or upon information/reference, and specifies factors for determining adverse effects or dominant position.

key_sections.title: Procedure for inquiry under section 19.
key_sections.description: Details the procedure for inquiries, including directing the Director General to investigate, closing matters if no prima facie case exists, and handling reports from the Director General.

key_sections.title: Orders by Commission after inquiry into agreements or abuse of dominant position.
key_sections.description: Specifies the types of orders the Commission can pass after finding contraventions of anti-competitive agreements or abuse of dominant position, including directing discontinuance, imposing penalties, or modifying agreements.

key_sections.title: Orders of Commission on combinations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Commission to approve, prohibit, or approve with modifications, combinations based on their effect on competition, and sets timelines for such decisions.

key_sections.title: Acts taking place outside India but having an effect on competition in India.
key_sections.description: Grants the Commission power to inquire into agreements, abuse of dominant position, or combinations occurring outside India if they have an appreciable adverse effect on competition within India.

key_sections.title: Contravention of orders of Commission.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for failure to comply with the Commission's orders or directions, including daily penalties and potential imprisonment or higher fines for non-payment.

key_sections.title: Power to impose penalty for non-furnishing of information on combinations.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Commission to impose penalties for failure to give notice of combinations or for contravening regulations related to combinations, with penalties based on turnover, assets, or transaction value.

key_sections.title: Power to impose lesser penalty.
key_sections.description: Allows the Commission to impose a lesser penalty on cartel members who make full, true, and vital disclosures about violations, subject to certain conditions and continued cooperation.

key_sections.title: Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Designates the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal as the Appellate Tribunal for this Act, specifying its functions to hear appeals against Commission orders and adjudicate compensation claims.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969, and includes saving provisions for past actions, rights, and pending cases, transferring them to the Appellate Tribunal or National Commission.

Commission: issue interim orders (Section 33)
Commission: regulate its own procedure (Section 36)

Commission: call upon experts to assist in inquiry (Section 36(3))

Commission: impose penalty for non-furnishing of information on combinations (Section 43A)
Commission: impose penalty for false statements or omission of material information (Section 44, 45)
Commission: impose lesser penalty (Section 46)
Commission: make regulations (Section 64)
Commission: issue guidelines (Section 64B)
Central Government: appoint Chairperson and Members of Commission (Section 8, 9)
Central Government: approve appointment of Director General (Section 16)
Central Government: issue directions to the Commission on policy matters (Section 55)
Central Government: supersede Commission (Section 56)
Central Government: make rules (Section 63)
Central Government: exempt from application of Act (Section 54)
Central Government: remove difficulties (Section 65)
Appellate Tribunal: hear and dispose of appeals (Section 53A, 53B)
Appellate Tribunal: adjudicate on claims for compensation (Section 53A, 53N)

Appellate Tribunal: punish for contempt (Section 53U)

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for various contraventions. Failure to comply with orders or directions of the Commission (under sections 6, 27, 28, 31, 32, 33, 42A, 43, 43A, 44 and 45) can result in a penalty up to rupees one lakh per day, with a maximum of rupees ten crore. Non-payment of such penalties can lead to imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to rupees twenty-five crore, or both. Failure to comply with directions of the Commission or Director General (under sections 36(2), (4) or 41(2)) can incur a penalty up to rupees one lakh per day, with a maximum of rupees one crore. Non-furnishing of information on combinations (under section 6(2) or 6(4) or 20(1)) or contravening section 6(2A) can lead to a penalty up to one percent of the total turnover, assets, or value of transaction, whichever is higher. Making false statements or omitting material information (Section 44) carries a penalty between rupees fifty lakhs and rupees five crore. Contraventions in furnishing information (Section 45) can result in a penalty up to rupees one crore. The Act also provides for a 'lesser penalty' scheme for cartel members who make vital disclosures (Section 46) and addresses contraventions by companies, imposing penalties on persons in charge or officers responsible (Section 48). Revocation of settlement or commitment orders can lead to liability for legal costs and restoration of inquiry (Section 48C).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) is established to enforce the Act. It conducts inquiries into anti-competitive agreements and abuse of dominant position, and regulates combinations. The Director General assists the CCI in investigations. The CCI can issue orders, impose penalties, and direct modifications. The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) acts as the Appellate Tribunal, hearing appeals against CCI orders and adjudicating compensation claims. The Supreme Court hears appeals against Appellate Tribunal decisions. Penalties can be recovered by the CCI or referred to income-tax authorities. Certain offences can be compounded by the Appellate Tribunal or a court.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (as Appellate Tribunal), Supreme Court, Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Delhi (for certain penalties), Civil Courts (jurisdiction excluded for matters determinable by CCI/Appellate Tribunal, but can execute Appellate Tribunal orders).

act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the control of land within National Highways, including the right of way, and regulates traffic moving on these highways. It also establishes mechanisms for the prevention and removal of unauthorized occupation on highway land.

act_identification.act_title: THE OFFSHORE AREAS MINERAL (DEVELOPMENT AND REGULATION) ACT, 2002
act_identification.act_short_title: The Offshore Areas Mineral (Development and Regulation) Act, 2002

legislative_details.geographical_extent: territorial waters, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone and other maritime zones of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for development and regulation of mineral resources in the territorial waters, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone and other maritime zones of India and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate and facilitate the development of mineral resources found in India's offshore areas, including its territorial waters, continental shelf, and exclusive economic zone. It establishes a framework for granting operating rights for reconnaissance, exploration, and production of these minerals, while also addressing environmental protection, safety, and revenue collection.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to expediency of Union control.
key_sections.description: Declares that it is in the public interest for the Union to control the regulation of mines and development of minerals in offshore areas.

key_sections.title: Application.
key_sections.description: States that the Act applies to all minerals in offshore areas, excluding mineral oils and related hydrocarbons, and is in addition to other laws.

key_sections.title: Reconnaissance, exploration or production to be under permit, licence or lease.
key_sections.description: Mandates that all reconnaissance, exploration, or production operations in offshore areas must be conducted under a valid permit, licence, or lease, with exceptions for government agencies.

key_sections.title: Grant of operating right.
key_sections.description: Sets eligibility criteria for granting operating rights, requiring the applicant to be an Indian national or a company, and specifies conditions for atomic minerals.

key_sections.title: Termination of operating right.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to prematurely terminate operating rights in public or strategic interest, and outlines conditions for lapsing of rights due to non-commencement or discontinuation of operations.

key_sections.title: Grant of composite licence.
key_sections.description: Details the procedure for granting composite licences through competitive bidding for areas where mineral resources are not yet adequately established, including exploration and subsequent production phases.

key_sections.title: Grant of production lease.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for granting production leases through competitive bidding for areas with established mineral resources, specifying the lease period and operational requirements.

key_sections.title: Royalty.
key_sections.description: Requires lessees to pay royalty to the Central Government on minerals removed or consumed, at rates specified in the First Schedule, with provisions for amendment of rates.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Offshore Areas Mineral Trust.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of a non-profit trust to use accrued funds for research, environmental mitigation, disaster relief, exploration, and benefit of affected persons.

key_sections.title: Safety of persons and property.
key_sections.description: Makes holders of operating rights responsible for ensuring safety and health of persons and property, and allows the Central Government to declare safety zones and prescribe norms.

key_sections.title: Prevention and control of pollution and protection of marine environment.
key_sections.description: Obligates operating right holders to comply with pollution control laws and makes them liable for compensation for marine pollution or damage caused by their activities.

key_sections.title: Offences.
key_sections.description: Defines various offences under the Act, including undertaking operations without proper authorization, failure to furnish data, illegal handling of minerals, and obstruction of officers, prescribing corresponding penalties.

key_sections.title: Civil liability and adjudication.
key_sections.description: Establishes civil liability for contravention of terms and conditions of permits, licences, or leases, and designates an authorised officer for adjudication of such cases.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for various purposes under the Act, including terms and conditions of operating rights, data furnishing, safety, and environmental protection.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Undertaking reconnaissance, exploration, or production operations without a valid permit, licence, or lease is punishable with imprisonment up to five years, or a fine of five lakh rupees which may extend to ten lakh rupees, or both, per standard block. Failure to furnish required data or information is punishable with imprisonment up to three years, or a fine of five lakh rupees which may extend to ten lakh rupees, or both, per standard block. Vessels and associated equipment used in violation of Section 5, along with recovered minerals, shall be confiscated. Shipping, transporting, selling, purchasing, importing, exporting, or possessing illegally recovered minerals is punishable with imprisonment up to three years, or a fine of twenty-five lakh rupees which may extend to fifty lakh rupees, or both. Obstructing authorised officers, failing to provide facilities, or interfering with lawful apprehension is punishable with imprisonment up to five years, or a fine of two lakh rupees which may extend to five lakh rupees, or both. Repeat offenders face an additional fine of up to one lakh rupees per day. Other contraventions of the Act or rules are punishable with imprisonment up to five years, or a fine of fifty lakh rupees which may extend to one crore rupees, or both, with an additional fine of five lakh rupees per day for continuing contravention.

act_identification.act_title: THE BIOLOGICAL DIVERSITY ACT, 2002

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the conservation of biological diversity, promote the sustainable use of its components, and ensure the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilization of biological resources and associated knowledge. It also aims to give effect to India's obligations under the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity and the Nagoya Protocol.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its applicability to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on dates appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.description: Mandates prior approval from the National Biodiversity Authority for non-citizens, non-resident Indian citizens, and foreign-controlled companies to access biological resources or associated knowledge for research, commercial utilisation, or bio-survey/bio-utilisation.

key_sections.title: Application for intellectual property rights not to be made without approval of National Biodiversity Authority.
key_sections.description: Requires prior approval from the National Biodiversity Authority for certain persons/entities applying for intellectual property rights based on Indian biological resources or traditional knowledge, with provisions for benefit sharing.

key_sections.title: Prior intimation to State Biodiversity Board for accessing biological resource for certain purposes.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that persons other than those covered by Section 3(2) must give prior intimation to the State Biodiversity Board for accessing biological resources for commercial utilisation, with certain exemptions.

key_sections.title: Establishment of National Biodiversity Authority.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the National Biodiversity Authority as a body corporate, outlining its composition and head office location.

key_sections.title: Functions and powers of National Biodiversity Authority
key_sections.description: Outlines the functions and powers of the National Biodiversity Authority, including regulating access, advising governments, and taking measures against IPR grants outside India.

key_sections.title: Determination of fair and equitable benefit sharing by National Biodiversity Authority.
key_sections.description: Empowers the National Biodiversity Authority to determine fair and equitable benefit sharing from the use of biological resources, including mechanisms like joint ownership of IPR, technology transfer, and monetary compensation.

key_sections.title: Establishment of State Biodiversity Board.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of State Biodiversity Boards by State Governments, detailing their corporate status and composition, and specifying NBA's role in Union Territories.

key_sections.title: Central Government to develop national strategies and plans for conservation, promotion and sustainable use of biological diversity.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to develop national strategies and plans for biodiversity conservation, sustainable use, and to issue directives to State Governments for ameliorative measures.

key_sections.title: Biodiversity heritage sites.
key_sections.description: Allows State Governments to notify areas of biodiversity importance as biodiversity heritage sites based on State Biodiversity Board recommendations, and to frame rules for their management and conservation.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Biodiversity Management Committee.
key_sections.description: Requires local bodies to constitute Biodiversity Management Committees for promoting conservation, sustainable use, and documentation of biological diversity, and allows them to levy collection fees.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of sections 3, 4, 6, or 7 by specified persons/entities, ranging from one lakh to fifty lakh rupees, with additional penalties for continuous contravention.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, specifying various matters that such rules may cover.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint Chairperson, members, and Member-Secretary of the National Biodiversity Authority (Section 8).
Central Government: To appoint adjudicating officers for penalties (Section 55A).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 62).
Central Government: To give directions to the National Biodiversity Authority on policy matters (Section 48).
Central Government: To notify threatened species (Section 38).
Central Government: To designate repositories for biological resources (Section 39).
Central Government: To remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act (Section 65).
Central Government: To give directions to State Governments regarding implementation (Section 60).
National Biodiversity Authority: To regulate access to biological resources and traditional knowledge (Section 18).
National Biodiversity Authority: To grant or reject approvals for certain activities (Section 19).
National Biodiversity Authority: To determine fair and equitable benefit sharing (Section 21).
National Biodiversity Authority: To make regulations for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 64).
National Biodiversity Authority: To delegate powers and functions (Section 16).
State Government: To establish State Biodiversity Boards (Section 22).
State Government: To appoint Chairperson, ex officio members, and non-official members of State Biodiversity Boards (Section 22).
State Government: To make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 63).
State Government: To give directions to the State Biodiversity Board on policy matters (Section 49).
State Government: To notify biodiversity heritage sites (Section 37).
State Biodiversity Board: To restrict certain activities violating conservation objectives (Section 24).
Biodiversity Management Committees: To levy charges by way of collection fees for accessing biological resources for commercial purposes (Section 41(3)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 55 prescribes penalties for persons or entities covered under sub-section (2) of section 3 or section 7 who contravene or attempt to contravene sections 3, 4, 6, or 7. The penalty shall not be less than one lakh rupees, but may extend to fifty lakh rupees, or be commensurate with the damage caused if it exceeds the penalty amount. For continuous contravention, an additional penalty not exceeding one crore rupees may be imposed. Section 56 specifies penalties for contravention of directions or orders issued by the Central Government, State Government, National Biodiversity Authority, or State Biodiversity Boards, with a fine up to one lakh rupees for the first offence, up to two lakh rupees for a second or subsequent offence, and an additional fine of up to two lakh rupees per day for continuous contravention.

related_acts: United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity
Nagoya Protocol on access to genetic resources and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from their utilisation to the convention on Biological Diversity
Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976 (80 of 1976)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson, members, and Member-Secretary of the National Biodiversity Authority, and adjudicating officers. The State Government appoints the Chairperson, ex officio members, and non-official members of the State Biodiversity Board.

applies_to: The whole of India.
Persons who are not citizens of India.
Citizens of India who are non-residents as defined in the Income-tax Act, 1961.
Body corporates, associations, or organisations not incorporated or registered in India.
Body corporates, associations, or organisations incorporated or registered in India but controlled by a foreigner.
Any person accessing biological resources and associated knowledge for commercial utilisation (with prior intimation to State Biodiversity Board).
exemptions: Collaborative research projects involving transfer or exchange of biological resources or traditional knowledge between Indian and foreign institutions, if they conform to Central Government policy guidelines and are approved by the Central Government (Section 5).
Applications for rights under any law relating to protection of plant varieties (Section 6(3)).

Codified traditional knowledge, cultivated medicinal plants and their products, local people and communities of the area (including growers and cultivators of biodiversity), and vaids, hakims, and registered AYUSH practitioners practicing indigenous medicines for sustenance and livelihood (Section 7 proviso).
Biological resources when normally traded as commodities or items derived from them, including agricultural wastes, as notified by the Central Government.
Cultivated medicinal plants and their products for entities covered under section 7, registered as per regulations or prescribed (Section 40).

Any person who has been given any approval or granted any right under any law relating to protection of plant varieties enacted by Parliament, to the extent that such approvals or rights do not require similar approval under this Act (Section 59A).
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act to come into force (Section 1(3) proviso).
For Union territories, the National Biodiversity Authority shall exercise the powers and perform the functions of a State Biodiversity Board, or may delegate these powers/functions (Section 22(2)).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government has the power to make rules (Section 62). The State Government has the power to make rules (Section 63). The National Biodiversity Authority has the power to make regulations with the previous approval of the Central Government (Section 64).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a system of approvals and intimations required for accessing biological resources and associated knowledge, and for applying for intellectual property rights. The National Biodiversity Authority and State Biodiversity Boards regulate these activities. Contraventions are subject to penalties, which are adjudicated by officers appointed by the Central Government. Authorities are empowered to enter, inspect, survey, and seize materials. The Central and State Governments can issue directions to the respective Biodiversity Authorities/Boards. Disputes between authorities are settled by the Central Government or National Biodiversity Authority.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Appeals against determinations or orders of the National Biodiversity Authority or a State Biodiversity Board could be filed with the High Court (before the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010). After the commencement of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010, appeals are filed with the National Green Tribunal. Orders and determinations are deemed decrees of a civil court and are executable as such. No court can take cognizance of offences under this Act except on a written complaint by the Central Government or an authorized officer, or by a benefit claimer after giving due notice.

act_identification.act_title: THE CIGARETTES AND OTHER TOBACCO PRODUCTS (PROHIBITION OFADVERTISEMENT AND REGULATION OF TRADE AND COMMERCE, PRODUCTION, SUPPLY AND DISTRIBUTION) ACT, 2003
act_identification.act_short_title: The Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003.
act_identification.date_of_commencement: on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to prohibit the advertisement of, and to provide for the regulation of trade and commerce in, and production, supply and distribution of, cigarettes and other tobacco products and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS, the Resolution passed by the 39th World Health Assembly (WHO), in its Fourteenth Plenary meeting held on the 15th May, 1986 urged the member States of WHO which have not yet done so to implement the measures to ensure that effective protection is provided to non-smokers from involuntary exposure to tobacco smoke and to protect children and young people from being addicted to the use of tobacco; AND WHEREAS, the 43rd World Health Assembly in its Fourteenth Plenary meeting held on the 17th May, 1990, reiterated the concerns expressed in the Resolution passed in the 39th World Health Assembly and urged Member States to consider in their tobacco control strategies plans for legislation and other effective measures for protecting their citizens with special attention to risk groups such as pregnant women and children from involuntary exposure to tobacco smoke, discourage the use of tobacco and impose progressive restrictions and take concerted action to eventually eliminate all direct and indirect advertising, promotion and sponsorship concerning tobacco; AND WHEREAS, it is considered expedient to enact a comprehensive law on tobacco in the public interest and to protect the public health; AND WHEREAS, it is expedient to prohibit the consumption of cigarettes and other tobacco products which are injurious to health with a view to achieving improvement of public health in general as enjoined by article 47 of the Constitution; AND WHEREAS, it is expedient to prohibit the advertisement of, and to provide for regulation of trade and commerce, production, supply and distribution of, cigarettes and other tobacco products and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto:
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to prohibit the advertisement of cigarettes and other tobacco products and to regulate their trade, commerce, production, supply, and distribution. It aims to protect public health by discouraging tobacco use, especially among children and vulnerable groups, and to provide protection to non-smokers from involuntary exposure to tobacco smoke.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its applicability to the whole of India, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'advertisement', 'cigarette', 'public place', and 'specified warning'.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of smoking in a public place.
key_sections.description: Prohibits smoking in public places, with provisions for designated smoking areas in certain establishments.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of advertisement of cigarettes and other tobacco products.
key_sections.description: Prohibits direct and indirect advertisement, promotion, and sponsorship of cigarettes and other tobacco products.

key_sections.title: Prohibition on sale of cigarette or other tobacco products to a person below the age of eighteen years and in particular area.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the sale of tobacco products to minors and within a hundred-yard radius of educational institutions.

key_sections.title: Restrictions on trade and commerce in, and production, supply and distribution of cigarettes and other tobacco products.
key_sections.description: Mandates specified warnings and disclosure of nicotine and tar contents on packages of tobacco products.

key_sections.title: Power of entry and search.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to police officers and other authorized officers to enter and search premises suspected of contravening the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to seize.
key_sections.description: Authorizes officers to seize packages or advertisement material contravening the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Punishment for failure to give specified warning and nicotine and tar contents.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for manufacturing, producing, selling, or distributing tobacco products without specified warnings and content information.

key_sections.title: Punishment for smoking in certain places.
key_sections.description: Stipulates punishment for smoking in public places.

key_sections.title: Punishment for advertisement of cigarettes and tobacco products.
key_sections.description: Outlines penalties for contravening the prohibition on advertisement of tobacco products.

key_sections.title: Punishment for sale of cigarettes or any other tobacco products in certain places or to persons below the age of eighteen years.
key_sections.description: Sets forth penalties for selling tobacco products to minors or near educational institutions.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply to cigarettes of other tobacco products which are exported.
key_sections.description: Exempts exported tobacco products from the Act's provisions, with a caveat regarding destination country laws.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Cigarettes (Regulation of Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 1975, and includes savings provisions.

powers_conferred: Power to enter and search premises (Section 12)
Power to seize packages or advertisement material (Section 13)
Power to give option to pay costs in lieu of confiscation (Section 15)
Power to add any tobacco products in the Schedule (Section 30)
Power of Central Government to make rules (Section 31)
Power to authorize officers for prevention, detention, and trial of offences (Section 25)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes punishments for various offences including failure to provide specified warnings and nicotine/tar contents (Section 20), smoking in public places (Section 21), advertisement of tobacco products (Section 22), and sale of tobacco products to minors or in prohibited areas (Section 24). Penalties range from fines (e.g., up to two hundred rupees for smoking in public) to imprisonment (e.g., up to five years for repeat advertisement offences or failure to warn).

repealed_acts: The Cigarettes (Regulation of Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 1975 (49 of 1975)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government or State Government may authorize police officers or other officers for entry, search, seizure, and enforcement (Sections 12, 13, 25).

applies_to: Whole of India
Persons engaged in production, supply, distribution, advertisement, or sale of cigarettes and other tobacco products
Any person smoking in a public place
exemptions: Cigarettes or other tobacco products which are exported
special_provisions: Provisions for separate smoking areas in hotels, restaurants, and airports (Section 4 proviso)
State amendments introducing 'hookah bar' definition and prohibition (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement involves powers of entry, search, and seizure by authorized police officers or other officers. Contraventions lead to confiscation of packages/advertisement material and various punishments. Offences can be compounded or tried summarily.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Principal civil court of original jurisdiction, other courts authorized by the Central Government (not below a civil court having pecuniary jurisdiction exceeding rupees five thousand), Magistrate, appellate court.

schedules_summary.description: Lists the tobacco products to which the Act applies, including cigarettes, cigars, beedis, various forms of tobacco, pan masala with tobacco, gutka, and tooth powder containing tobacco.

act_identification.act_title: THE ELECTRICITY ACT, 2003

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate the laws relating to generation, transmission, distribution, trading and use of electricity and generally for taking measures conducive to development of electricity industry, promoting competition therein, protecting interest of consumers and supply of electricity to all areas, rationalisation of electricity tariff, ensuring transparent policies regarding subsidies, promotion of efficient and environmentally benign policies, constitution of Central Electricity Authority, Regulatory Commissions and establishment of Appellate Tribunal and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act consolidates laws concerning electricity generation, transmission, distribution, trading, and use. Its main objectives include developing the electricity industry, promoting competition, protecting consumer interests, ensuring electricity supply to all areas, rationalizing tariffs, and establishing regulatory bodies like the Central Electricity Authority, Regulatory Commissions, and an Appellate Tribunal.

chapter_titles: PART II NATIONAL ELECTRICITY POLICY AND PLAN
PART XI APPELLATE TRIBUNAL FOR ELECTRICITY

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical reach, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: National Electricity Policy and Plan.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to prepare national electricity and tariff policies and the Authority to prepare a National Electricity Plan.

key_sections.title: Authorised persons to transmit, supply, etc., electricity.
key_sections.description: States that a licence is required for transmitting, distributing, or trading electricity, unless exempted.

key_sections.title: Duties of distribution licensee and open access.
key_sections.description: Outlines the duties of distribution licensees and introduces the concept of open access for consumers.

key_sections.title: Duty to supply on request.
key_sections.description: Obligates distribution licensees to supply electricity to premises within one month of application, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Tariff regulations.
key_sections.description: Directs the Appropriate Commission to specify terms and conditions for tariff determination, guided by commercial principles, consumer interest, and promotion of renewable energy.

key_sections.title: Constitution, etc., of Central Electricity Authority.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Central Electricity Authority and details its composition and continuity.

key_sections.title: Functions of Central Commission.
key_sections.description: Defines the regulatory functions of the Central Commission, including tariff regulation, licensing, and dispute adjudication for inter-State operations.

key_sections.title: Functions of State Commission.
key_sections.description: Defines the regulatory functions of the State Commission, including tariff determination, licensing, and dispute adjudication for intra-State operations.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity to hear appeals against orders of adjudicating officers or Appropriate Commissions.

key_sections.title: Theft of electricity.
key_sections.description: Defines the offence of electricity theft and prescribes penalties.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Special Courts.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to constitute Special Courts for speedy trial of electricity-related offences.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the Act's provisions generally override other inconsistent laws, except as provided in Section 173.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals previous electricity acts and includes saving provisions for actions taken under them.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To prepare National Electricity Policy and Plan (Section 3), notify Central Transmission Utility (Section 38), establish National Load Despatch Centre (Section 26), establish Regional Load Despatch Centre (Section 27), issue directions to generating companies (Section 11), make rules (Section 176), remove difficulties (Section 183).

State Government: To prepare national policy on stand alone systems for rural areas (Section 4), national policy on electrification in rural areas (Section 5), notify State Transmission Utility (Section 39), establish State Load Despatch Centre (Section 31), constitute State Commissions (Section 82), make rules (Section 180), constitute Special Courts (Section 153), appoint Chief Electrical Inspector and Electrical Inspector (Section 162).

Appropriate Commission (Central/State): To grant/revoke licences (Sections 14, 19), amend licences (Section 18), issue directions to licensees (Section 23), suspend distribution licence (Section 24), determine tariff (Section 62), adjudicate disputes (Sections 79, 86), investigate affairs of generating companies/licensees (Section 128), issue orders for securing compliance (Section 129), appoint adjudicating officers (Section 143), make regulations (Sections 178, 181).

Authority (Central Electricity Authority): To prepare National Electricity Plan (Section 3), specify technical standards (Section 73), specify safety requirements (Section 73), specify Grid Standards (Section 73), specify conditions for meters (Section 73), make regulations (Section 177).
Appellate Tribunal for Electricity: To hear appeals (Section 111), issue orders/instructions/directions to Appropriate Commissions (Section 121).
Licensee: To open up streets, railways etc. for works (Section 67), enter premises (Section 163).
Assessing Officer: To provisionally assess electricity charges for unauthorised use (Section 126).
Police Officer: To investigate offences punishable under the Act (Section 151A).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Part XIV (Sections 135-152) defines various offences and prescribes penalties. Offences include theft of electricity (Section 135), theft of electric lines and materials (Section 136), receiving stolen property (Section 137), interference with meters or works of licensee (Section 138), negligently breaking or damaging works (Section 139), intentionally injuring works (Section 140), and extinguishing public lamps (Section 141). Penalties range from fines to imprisonment, with higher penalties for repeat offenders and specific conditions. Non-compliance with directions or orders from the Appropriate Commission also attracts penalties (Sections 142, 146). The Act also covers offences by companies (Section 149) and abetment (Section 150), and provides for compounding of offences (Section 152).

the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948 (54 of 1948)

State Governments appoint the Chairperson and Members of State Commissions, Judges of Special Courts, and Electrical Inspectors. The Appropriate Commission appoints its Secretary, officers, employees, and adjudicating officers.

Generating companies
transmission licensees
distribution licensees
electricity traders
consumers

Appropriate Government (deemed licensee, not required to obtain licence under Section 14).
Damodar Valley Corporation (deemed licensee, not required to obtain licence under Section 14).
Government company or companies created in pursuance of Acts in Schedule (deemed licensee, not required to obtain licence under Section 14).

Inconsistency with Consumer Protection Act, Atomic Energy Act, Railways Act (Section 173).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through licensing and regulation by Central and State Commissions, issuance of directions by various authorities, investigation of entities, assessment of charges for unauthorized electricity use, and imposition of penalties and imprisonment for offences. Special Courts are constituted for speedy trials, and an Appellate Tribunal handles appeals. Dispute resolution can also occur through arbitration. Penalties are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Special Courts (Sections 153, 154, 155), High Court (for appeal and revision from Special Courts, Section 156), Supreme Court (for appeal from Appellate Tribunal, Section 125). Civil courts' jurisdiction is barred for matters determinable by assessing officers, appellate authorities, or adjudicating officers (Section 145).

schedules_summary.description: Lists various State Electricity Reform Acts, including those from Orissa, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Rajasthan, Delhi, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat. These enactments are relevant for transitional provisions and for entities deemed to be licensees under the Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE FISCAL RESPONSIBILITY AND BUDGET MANAGEMENT ACT, 2003
act_identification.act_short_title: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the responsibility of the Central Government to ensure inter-generational equity in fiscal management and long-term macro-economic stability by removing fiscal impediments in the effective conduct of monetary policy and prudential debt management consistent with fiscal sustainability through limits on the Central Government borrowings, debt and deficits, greater transparency in fiscal operations of the Central Government and conducting fiscal policy in a medium-term framework and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to ensure inter-generational equity in fiscal management and long-term macro-economic stability for the Central Government. It seeks to achieve this by setting limits on borrowings, debt, and deficits, enhancing transparency in fiscal operations, and conducting fiscal policy within a medium-term framework. The goal is to remove fiscal impediments for effective monetary policy and prudential debt management.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'fiscal deficit' and 'gross domestic product'.

key_sections.title: Fiscal policy statements to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to present various fiscal policy statements, including Medium-term Fiscal Policy and Macro-economic Framework Statements, to Parliament annually.

key_sections.title: Fiscal management principles.
key_sections.description: Outlines the fiscal management principles for the Central Government, including targets for fiscal deficit and debt limits, and conditions for deviation.

key_sections.title: Borrowing from Reserve Bank.
key_sections.description: Restricts the Central Government's ability to borrow from the Reserve Bank, with specific exceptions for temporary advances and subscription to securities.

key_sections.title: Measures for fiscal transparency.
key_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to take steps to ensure greater transparency in its fiscal operations and make necessary disclosures with financial statements.

key_sections.title: Measures to enforce compliance.
key_sections.description: Details mechanisms for reviewing fiscal trends, taking corrective measures for revenue shortfalls or expenditure excesses, and explaining deviations to Parliament.

key_sections.title: Laying of review reports.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to entrust the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India to review compliance with the Act, with reports to be laid before Parliament.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of civil courts barred.
key_sections.description: States that civil courts do not have jurisdiction to question the legality of actions or decisions made by the Central Government under this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions, within a specified timeframe.

Central Government: to lay fiscal policy statements before Parliament (Section 3)
Central Government: to take appropriate measures to limit fiscal deficit and debt (Section 4(1))
Central Government: to prescribe annual targets for reduction of fiscal deficit (Section 4(2))
Central Government: to borrow from the Reserve Bank by way of advances to meet temporary excess of cash disbursement over cash receipts (Section 5(2))
Central Government: to take suitable measures to ensure greater transparency in its fiscal operations (Section 6(1))
Central Government: to make disclosures in prescribed form (Section 6(2))
Central Government: to take appropriate measures for increasing revenue or for reducing expenditure (Section 7(2))
Central Government: to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act (Section 8(1))
Central Government: to entrust the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India to review compliance (Section 7A)
Central Government: to remove difficulties by order (Section 13(1))
Minister-in-charge of the Ministry of Finance: to review trends in receipts and expenditure and place outcome before Parliament (Section 7(1))
Minister-in-charge of the Ministry of Finance: to make a statement in both Houses of Parliament explaining deviations (Section 7(3)(b))
Reserve Bank: to subscribe to the primary issues of Central Government Securities due to specified grounds (Section 5(3))
Reserve Bank: to buy and sell the Central Government securities in the secondary market or convert them (Section 5(4))
Comptroller and Auditor-General of India: to review periodically the compliance of the provisions of this Act (Section 7A)

related_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)

applies_to: Central Government
whole of India

expenditure which is required to be incurred under any agreement or contract
expenditure which cannot be postponed or curtailed
special_provisions: Exceeding annual fiscal deficit target due to ground or grounds of national security, act of war, national calamity, collapse of agriculture severely affecting farm output and incomes, structural reforms in the economy with unanticipated fiscal implications, decline in real output growth of a quarter by at least three per cent. points below its average of the previous four quarters.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Laying of fiscal policy statements before Parliament; half-yearly review of receipts and expenditure by the Minister-in-charge of the Ministry of Finance; taking appropriate measures for increasing revenue or reducing expenditure; making statements to Parliament explaining deviations; periodic review of compliance by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL VIGILANCE COMMISSION ACT, 2003

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution of a Central Vigilance Commission to inquire or cause inquiries to be conducted into offences alleged to have been committed under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 by certain categories of public servants of the Central Government, corporations established by or under any Central Act, Government companies, societies and local authorities owned or controlled by the Central Government and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Central Vigilance Commission to investigate corruption allegations against public servants of the Central Government and related entities. It aims to ensure transparency and accountability in the vigilance administration of these bodies by conducting inquiries and exercising superintendence.

chapter_titles: FUNCTIONS AND POWERS OF THE CENTRAL VIGILANCE COMMISSION

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Central Vigilance Commissioner', 'Commission', and 'Delhi Special Police Establishment'.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Central Vigilance Commission.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Central Vigilance Commission, outlining its composition (Chairperson and Members) and the qualifications for appointment.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners.
key_sections.description: Details the process for appointing the Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners by the President, based on the recommendation of a committee.

key_sections.title: Terms and other conditions of service of Central Vigilance Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Specifies the term of office, age limits, oath, resignation, and ineligibility for reappointment or further employment for the Commissioners.

key_sections.title: Removal of Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioner.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for removal of Commissioners by the President on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, involving a Supreme Court inquiry.

key_sections.title: Functions and powers of Central Vigilance Commission.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the core functions and powers of the Commission, including superintendence over the Delhi Special Police Establishment, conducting inquiries, and tendering advice.

key_sections.title: Power relating to inquiries.

act_identification.act_title: THE REPATRIATION OF PRISONERS ACT, 2003

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the transfer of certain prisoners from India to country or place outside India and reception in India of certain prisoners from country or place outside India.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides a legal framework for the transfer of prisoners between India and other countries (contracting States). It outlines procedures for Indian prisoners to be transferred out of India and for foreign prisoners to be transferred into India to serve their sentences.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date, to be appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act such as 'contracting State', 'prescribed', 'prisoner', and 'warrant'.

key_sections.title: Application of Act.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to apply the Act to specific countries or places outside India through notification, potentially with modifications to align with treaties.

key_sections.title: Application for transfer by a prisoner.
key_sections.description: Allows a prisoner who is a citizen of a contracting State to apply to the Central Government for transfer of custody from India.

key_sections.title: Consideration of request by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Outlines the conditions under which the Central Government may forward a prisoner's transfer application to a contracting State, including no pending inquiry, no death penalty, and no conviction under military law.

key_sections.title: Consideration of request by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Details the Central Government's power to issue a warrant for a prisoner's transfer out of India upon receiving willingness and undertaking from the contracting State.

key_sections.title: Provision to issue warrant for transfer.
key_sections.description: Authorizes an officer to issue a warrant for the delivery of a prisoner to the authorized person of a contracting State, along with records and personal effects.

key_sections.title: Transfer into India.
key_sections.description: Enables the Central Government to accept the transfer of an Indian citizen prisoner from a contracting State, subject to agreed terms and conditions, and to issue a warrant for their detention in India.

key_sections.title: Determination of prison and issue of warrant for receiving transfer in India.
key_sections.description: Provides for the Central Government to determine the prison and officer for receiving a transferred prisoner in India and outlines the process for issuing the warrant and dealing with the prisoner.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, including forms for warrants and means for forwarding applications.

key_sections.title: Laying of rules, etc.
key_sections.description: Mandates that all notifications and rules made under the Act be laid before each House of Parliament for review.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, provided such orders are not inconsistent with the Act and are made within two years of its commencement.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Direct application of Act to countries (Section 3), consider and forward transfer requests (Section 5), issue warrants for transfer out of India (Section 7), requisition and send records (Section 10), accept transfer of prisoners into India (Section 12), determine prison and authorize officers for receiving transfers (Section 13), make rules (Section 14), remove difficulties (Section 16).
Officer not below the rank of a Joint Secretary to a State Government: Issue warrants for transfer out of India (Section 8).
Officer not below the rank of a Joint Secretary to the Central Government: Issue warrants for receiving transfer in India (Section 13(2)).
Officer in charge of the prison: Furnish information for transfer (Section 5), deliver custody of prisoner (Section 8).
Officer referred to in Section 13(1): Receive and hold prisoner in custody (Section 13(3)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act specifies that if a prisoner escapes custody within India during transfer, they are liable for an offence under section 224 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) and are subject to the remaining sentence in India.

applies_to: A country or place outside India as may be specified by notification (Section 3(1))
A prisoner who is a citizen of a contracting State (Section 4)
A prisoner who is a citizen of India (Section 12)
exemptions: Prisoners against whom an inquiry, trial or any other proceeding is pending (Section 5(2)(a))
Prisoners to whom death penalty has been awarded (Section 5(2)(b))
Prisoners convicted for an offence under military law (Section 5(2)(c))
special_provisions: The Central Government may modify the application of the Act to a country to give effect to a treaty (Section 3(3)).
The Central Government may adapt the sentence of a prisoner transferred into India if it is incompatible with Indian law (Section 13(6)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through notifications, treaties, warrants issued by the Central Government or authorized officers, and agreements with contracting States. The Central Government plays a central role in approving and facilitating transfers.

act_identification.act_title: THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM (REPEAL) ACT, 2004
