act_identification.act_title: THE PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS REGULATORY BOARD ACT, 2006
act_identification.act_short_title: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board Act, 2006

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board to regulate the refining, processing, storage, transportation, distribution, marketing and sale of petroleum, petroleum products and natural gas excluding production of crude oil and natural gas so as to protect the interests of consumers and entities engaged in specified activities relating to petroleum, petroleum products and natural gas and to ensure uninterrupted and adequate supply of petroleum, petroleum products and natural gas in all parts of the country and to promote competitive markets and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The Act establishes the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board to regulate various aspects of the petroleum and natural gas industry, excluding production. Its main objectives are to protect consumer and entity interests, ensure uninterrupted and adequate supply of petroleum products and natural gas across the country, and promote competitive markets in the sector.

chapter_titles: PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS REGULATORY BOARD
FUNCTIONS AND POWERS OF THE BOARD

key_definitions: city or local natural gas distribution network
notified petroleum, petroleum products and natural gas

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its applicability to the whole of India, its commencement date, and the activities it covers (refining, processing, storage, transportation, distribution, marketing, and sale of petroleum, petroleum products, and natural gas, excluding production).

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Board', 'entity', 'common carrier', 'natural gas', 'petroleum', and various types of petroleum products.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of the Board.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board as a body corporate with perpetual succession, outlining its composition and head office location.

key_sections.title: Functions of the Board.
key_sections.description: Details the primary functions of the Board, including protecting consumer interests, registering and authorising entities, regulating access and transportation rates for carriers, ensuring adequate supply, monitoring prices, and laying down technical and safety standards.

key_sections.title: Powers regarding complaints and resolution of disputes by the Board.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board jurisdiction to adjudicate disputes between entities or between an entity and other persons, and to receive and investigate complaints related to contraventions of the Act or its regulations.

key_sections.title: Registration of entities.
key_sections.description: Requires entities engaged in marketing, operating LNG terminals, or establishing large storage facilities to register with the Board, with provisions for existing entities and suspension/cancellation of registration.

key_sections.title: Authorisation.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that no entity shall lay, build, operate, or expand common/contract carriers or city/local natural gas distribution networks without obtaining authorisation under the Act.

key_sections.title: Transportation tariff.
key_sections.description: Directs the Board to lay down regulations for transportation tariffs for common carriers, contract carriers, or city/local natural gas distribution networks, guided by factors like competition, efficiency, consumer interest, and cost recovery.

key_sections.title: Board to settle disputes.
key_sections.description: Empowers a Bench of the Board to settle disputes arising among entities or between an entity and any other person concerning refining, processing, storage, transportation, distribution, marketing, and sale of petroleum and natural gas.

key_sections.title: Civil penalty for contravention of directions given by the Board.
key_sections.description: Prescribes civil penalties for contravention of Board directions, including failure to provide access, adhere to transportation rates, display retail prices, or comply with registration/authorisation terms, with penalties up to one crore rupees and additional daily penalties.

key_sections.title: Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Designates the Appellate Tribunal established under the Electricity Act, 2003, as the Appellate Tribunal for this Act, with specific provisions for a Technical Member (Petroleum and Natural Gas).

key_sections.title: Appeals to Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Allows any person aggrieved by an order or decision of the Board to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal, specifying the time limit, fee, and conditions for such appeals.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to issue directions.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to issue directions to the Board in matters of national interest, security, or public order, and policy directives for maintaining supplies and equitable distribution, which are binding on the Board.

key_sections.title: Punishment for unauthorised activities.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment, including imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to twenty-five crore rupees (or both), for entities marketing notified petroleum products or natural gas without valid registration or authorisation.

key_sections.title: Power of Board to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Board to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules to carry out its provisions, covering aspects like meetings, powers of the Secretary, storage capacity, open access, marketing obligations, fees, and technical standards.

powers_conferred: Board: To protect consumer interests, foster fair trade and competition (Section 11(a)).
Board: To register entities for marketing, operating LNG terminals, and establishing storage facilities (Section 11(b)).
Board: To authorise entities for laying, building, operating, or expanding common/contract carriers and city/local natural gas distribution networks (Section 11(c)).
Board: To declare pipelines as common carrier or contract carrier (Section 11(d)).
Board: To regulate access to common/contract carriers and city/local natural gas distribution networks, and transportation rates (Section 11(e)).

Board: To ensure adequate availability, monitor prices, prevent restrictive trade practices, and enforce retail/marketing service obligations for notified petroleum, petroleum products, and natural gas (Section 11(f)).
Board: To levy fees and other charges (Section 11(g)).
Board: To maintain a data bank of information (Section 11(h)).
Board: To lay down technical standards and specifications, including safety standards (Section 11(i)).
Board: To adjudicate and decide disputes between entities or an entity and any other person (Section 12(1)(a), Section 24).
Board: To receive complaints and conduct inquiries/investigations (Section 12(1)(b)).
Board: To pass orders and issue directions (Section 12(2)).

Board: To exercise powers of a civil court for summoning, enforcing attendance, requisitioning records, receiving evidence, issuing commissions, granting interim relief, reviewing decisions (Section 13(1)).
Board: To suspend or cancel a certificate of registration (Section 15(4)).
Board: To suspend or cancel authorisation (Section 23).
Board: To appoint Investigating Officers (Section 26(1)).
Board: To make regulations (Section 61).
Board: To delegate powers and functions (Section 58).
Central Government: To appoint Chairperson and other members of the Board (Section 3(3), Section 4(1)).
Central Government: To constitute a Search Committee for selecting Chairperson, members, and Technical Member (Section 4(2)).
Central Government: To appoint a Secretary to the Board (Section 10(1)).
Central Government: To approve the number, nature, and categories of other officers and employees of the Board (Section 10(2)).
Central Government: To issue directions to the Board in national interest, security, or public order (Section 42(1)).
Central Government: To issue policy directives to the Board in public interest or for maintaining supplies and equitable distribution (Section 42(2)).
Central Government: To take over control and management of facilities and business premises of any entity and retail outlets in public interest during emergencies (Section 43(1)).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act (Section 60).
Appellate Tribunal: To hear appeals against orders/decisions of the Board (Section 33).
Appellate Tribunal: To make rules regarding its conduct and procedure (Section 35).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes civil penalties and criminal punishments. Civil penalties include an amount not exceeding one crore rupees for each contravention of Board directions, with an additional penalty of ten lakh rupees per day for continuing failure. For restrictive trade practices, the civil penalty can extend to five times the unfair gains or ten crore rupees, whichever is higher (Section 28). Criminal punishments include fines up to twenty-five crore rupees and additional daily fines for contravention of Board directions (Section 44), wilful failure to comply with Appellate Tribunal orders (fine up to one crore, two crore for subsequent, and daily fines) (Section 45), and imprisonment up to three years or fine up to twenty-five crore rupees (or both) for unauthorised activities like marketing without registration, operating LNG terminals without registration, or laying/operating common carriers without authorisation (Sections 46, 47, 48). Wilful damages to common carriers also carry similar imprisonment and fines (Section 49). Offences by companies are also addressed, holding responsible persons in charge and the company liable (Section 50).

related_acts: Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 (63 of 1986)
Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946 (25 of 1946)

authorities_established: Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson and other members of the Board (Section 3(3), Section 4(1)). The Central Government also appoints the Secretary to the Board (Section 10(1)). A Search Committee, constituted by the Central Government, prepares a panel for the appointment of the Technical Member (Petroleum and Natural Gas) of the Appellate Tribunal (Section 4(2), Section 31(1)).
regulatory_bodies: Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board
Appellate Tribunal (established under the Electricity Act, 2003, but exercising jurisdiction under this Act)

applies_to: Refining, processing, storage, transportation, distribution, marketing and sale of petroleum, petroleum products and natural gas.
Entities (persons, associations, firms, companies, co-operative societies) engaged or intending to be engaged in the specified activities.
exemptions: Production of crude oil and natural gas (Section 1(4)).

Entities carrying on activities referred to in Section 15(1)(a), (b), or (c) immediately before the appointed day are not required to register, but must inform the Board within six months (Section 15(1) Proviso).
Complaints of individual consumers maintainable before a consumer disputes redressal forum under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 (Section 25(1) Proviso).
special_provisions: Transitional arrangements for existing agreements between oil companies for sharing petroleum products or infrastructure facilities, and for monitoring the setting up of dealerships and distributorships during a three-year transition period (Section 63).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (Section 60), Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (Section 61), Appellate Tribunal (Section 35).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Board issues directions, registers and authorises entities, regulates tariffs, and settles disputes. It has powers akin to a civil court for inquiries and investigations. Contraventions of Board directions or Appellate Tribunal orders lead to civil penalties or criminal punishments, including fines and imprisonment. The Central Government can issue binding policy directives and take over facilities in public interest. The Act also mandates maintenance of data banks and obligations for entities to comply with Board directions and provide information.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Appellate Tribunal (for appeals against Board orders/decisions) (Section 30, 33). Supreme Court (for appeals against Appellate Tribunal orders) (Section 37). Courts inferior to a Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or Chief Judicial Magistrate cannot try offences under Chapter IX (Section 57(2)). Civil courts are explicitly barred from jurisdiction over matters the Board or Appellate Tribunal are empowered to determine (Section 56).

unauthorised development with regard to mixed land use not conforming to the Master Plan

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Fifty-seventh Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate the National Institute of Fashion Technology for the promotion and development of education and research in fashion technology and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes and incorporates the National Institute of Fashion Technology. Its primary purpose is to promote and develop education and research in fashion technology, along with addressing related and incidental matters.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment of the Institute.
key_sections.description: Establishes the National Institute of Fashion Technology as a body corporate and outlines its composition.

key_sections.title: Functions of Institute.
key_sections.description: Details the various functions and objectives of the Institute, including education, research, and promotion of fashion technology.

key_sections.title: Powers of Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the general superintendence, direction, and control powers of the Board of Governors over the Institute's affairs.

key_sections.title: Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the Institute.

key_sections.title: Authorities of Institute.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities governing the Institute, including the Board of Governors and the Senate.

key_sections.title: Director-General.
key_sections.description: Describes the appointment, role, and responsibilities of the Director-General as the principal executive officer.

key_sections.title: Fund of Institute.
key_sections.description: Specifies the maintenance and sources of the Institute's fund and its application.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Mandates proper accounts, annual statements, and audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

key_sections.title: Statutes.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the matters for which Statutes may provide, governing various aspects of the Institute's administration and academic life.

key_sections.title: Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Lists the matters for which Ordinances may provide, covering student admission, courses, examinations, and discipline.

key_sections.title: Power of Institute to grant degrees, etc.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the Institute the power to grant degrees, diplomas, and certificates equivalent to those from other universities.

powers_conferred: Institute: To acquire, hold and dispose of property and to contract, and to sue or be sued (Sec 3(2)); to grant degrees, diplomas, certificates and other academic distinctions (Sec 31).

Board: General superintendence, direction and control of the affairs of the Institute; to exercise all powers not otherwise provided for by this Act, the Statutes and the Ordinances; to review the acts of the Senate; to take decisions on questions of policy; to establish new campuses; to fix, demand and receive fees; to establish, maintain and manage halls and hostels; to supervise and control students; to institute academic and other posts; to frame Statutes and Ordinances; to institute and award fellowships, scholarships, prizes and medals; to consider and pass resolutions on annual reports, accounts and budget estimates; to receive gifts, grants, donations or benefactions; to appoint committees (Sec 7).

Central Government: To appoint date of commencement of the Act (Sec 1(2)); to appoint date of establishment of the Institute (Sec 3(1)); to approve disposal of immovable property by the Board (Sec 7(4)); to appoint persons to review work and progress of the Institute and hold inquiries (Sec 7(5)); to issue directions to the Institute (Sec 7(6)); to remove members of the Board (Sec 7(8)); to approve appointment of Director-General (Sec 15(1)); to remove Director-General (Sec 15(5)); to direct setting up of endowment fund (Sec 20); to issue general directions for accounts (Sec 21(1)); to declare Provident Funds Act, 1925 applicable (Sec 22(2)); to approve first Statutes (Sec 25(1)); to remove difficulties (Sec 32).

Visitor: To nominate Chairperson and two eminent experts to the Board (Sec 3(3)(a), (h)); to remove Chairperson or other nominated members of the Board (Sec 7(7)); to approve new Statutes or amendments (Sec 25(1), (3), (4)); to appoint umpire for Tribunal of Arbitration (Sec 28(1)).
Senate: To control and generally regulate, and be responsible for the maintenance of standards of instruction, education and examination in the Institute; to make Ordinances (Sec 13, 27(1)).

Director-General: To be the principal executive officer of the Institute; to be responsible for proper administration, imparting of instruction and maintenance of discipline; to submit annual reports and accounts to the Board; to appoint staff in certain cases (Sec 15, 23(b)).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Visitor: Nominates Chairperson and two eminent experts to the Board (Sec 3(3)(a), (h)). Speaker of Lok Sabha: Nominates two Members of Parliament from Lok Sabha to the Board (Sec 3(3)(b)). Chairman of Rajya Sabha: Nominates one Member of Parliament from Rajya Sabha to the Board (Sec 3(3)(b)). Central Government: Nominates five persons representing States to the Board (Sec 3(3)(g)); approves the appointment of the Director-General by the Board (Sec 15(1)). Board: Appoints the Director-General (with Central Government approval) (Sec 15(1)); appoints academic staff (Assistant Professor or above) and non-academic staff (high pay-scale) (Sec 23(a)). Chairperson (in consultation with Director-General): Nominates three persons (educationists) and one alumnus to the Senate (Sec 12(c), (d)). Director-General: Appoints staff in other cases not covered by the Board (Sec 23(b)).

applies_to: The National Institute of Fashion Technology (body corporate)
persons of either sex and of whatever race, creed, caste or class (for admission/appointment to Institute)
employees of the Institute
special_provisions: Representation on the Board for States in which the campus of the Institute is located (Sec 3(3)(g))

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Board: Frames Statutes and Ordinances (Sec 7(2)(g)). Senate: Makes Ordinances (Sec 27(1)). Central Government: Can issue directions (Sec 7(6), 21(1), 32(1)).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (Sec 21); review of work and progress by the Central Government and issuance of directions (Sec 7(5), 7(6)); resolution of disputes between the Institute and its employees by a Tribunal of Arbitration (Sec 28).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Tribunal of Arbitration for disputes between the Institute and its employees (Sec 28). No suit or proceeding shall lie in any court in respect of matters required to be referred to the Tribunal of Arbitration (Sec 28(3)).

act_identification.act_title: THE FOOD SAFETY AND STANDARDS ACT, 2006
act_identification.act_short_title: the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate the laws relating to food and to establish the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India for laying down science based standards for articles of food and to regulate their manufacture, storage, distribution, sale and import, to ensure availability of safe and wholesome food for human consumption and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate food-related laws and establish the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India. Its main objective is to set science-based standards for food articles and regulate their manufacture, storage, distribution, sale, and import to ensure the availability of safe and wholesome food for human consumption.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II FOOD SAFETY AND STANDARDS AUTHORITY OF INDIA
CHAPTER III GENERAL PRINCIPLES OF FOOD SAFETY
CHAPTER IV GENERAL PROVISIONS AS TO ARTICLES OF FOOD
CHAPTER V PROVISIONS RELATING TO IMPORT
CHAPTER VI SPECIAL RESPONSIBILITIES AS TO FOOD SAFETY
CHAPTER VII ENFORCEMENT OF THE ACT
CHAPTER X ADJUDICATION AND FOOD SAFETY APPELLATE TRIBUNAL
CHAPTER XI FINANCE, ACCOUNTS, AUDIT AND REPORTS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to establish the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India.

key_sections.title: Duties and functions of Food Authority.
key_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities and functions of the Food Authority, including regulating food, setting standards, and providing scientific advice.

key_sections.title: General principles to be followed in administration of Act.
key_sections.description: Lays down the guiding principles for the administration of the Act, focusing on consumer protection, risk management, and transparency.

key_sections.title: All imports of articles of food to be subject to this Act.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that all food imports into India must comply with the provisions of this Act.

key_sections.title: Responsibilities of the food business operator.
key_sections.description: Defines the duties of food business operators to ensure food safety at all stages of their operations.

key_sections.title: Authorities responsible for enforcement of Act.
key_sections.description: Identifies the Food Authority and State Food Safety Authorities as primary bodies for enforcing the Act.

key_sections.title: Licensing and registration of food business.
key_sections.description: Requires food businesses to obtain a licence or register, with exemptions for petty manufacturers and vendors.

key_sections.title: Powers of Food Safety Officer.
key_sections.description: Details the powers of Food Safety Officers, including taking samples, seizing food, and inspecting premises.

key_sections.title: Procedure for launching prosecution.
key_sections.description: Establishes the process for initiating prosecution based on food analysis reports.

key_sections.title: Punishment for unsafe food.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for manufacturing, storing, selling, distributing, or importing unsafe food, varying with the severity of injury or death caused.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Food Safety Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of tribunals to hear appeals against decisions of Adjudicating Officers.

key_sections.title: Overriding effect of this Act over all other food related laws.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in other food-related laws.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Specifies the repeal of previous food-related enactments and orders, with saving clauses for past actions and existing licences.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint Chairperson and Members of Food Authority, constitute Selection Committee, approve number of officers and employees, issue directions to Food Authority, give directions to State Governments, make rules, establish Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, appoint Public Prosecutor, remove difficulties.

Food Authority: Establish, specify standards and guidelines, establish scientific panels, constitute Scientific Committee, make regulations, notify food laboratories, recognise organisations for food safety audit.

Commissioner of Food Safety: Prohibit manufacture/storage/sale of food, sanction prosecution, delegate powers, appoint Designated Officer, appoint Food Safety Officers, appoint Food Analysts, empower Designated Officer to compound offences, approve prosecution within extended period.
Designated Officer: Grant/refuse/cancel licence, issue improvement notices, prohibit sale of food, sanction/launch prosecutions, investigate complaints.
Food Safety Officer: Take samples, seize articles of food, enter and inspect premises, seize adulterants/documents, launch prosecution.
Courts: Impose prohibitions, try cases summarily, impose enhanced punishment, implead manufacturer.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter IX details various offences and penalties. Penalties range from fines (e.g., up to five lakh rupees for sub-standard food, ten lakh rupees for misleading advertisement, two lakh rupees for possessing non-injurious adulterant, ten lakh rupees for injurious adulterant, two lakh rupees for general contraventions, ten lakh rupees for false information, ten lakh rupees for business without licence) to imprisonment (e.g., for unsafe food: three months to life imprisonment depending on injury/death, six months for interfering with seized items, three months for obstructing Food Safety Officer). Subsequent offences attract double punishment and licence cancellation. Compensation for injury or death of consumer is also provided.

amended_acts: Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles and Infant Foods (Regulation of Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 1992 (41 of 1992)
repealed_acts: The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (37 of 1954)
The Fruit Products Order, 1955
The Meat Food Products Order, 1973
The Vegetable Oil Products (Control) Order, 1947
The Edible Oils Packaging (Regulation) Order, 1998
The Solvent Extracted Oil, De oiled Meal, and Edible Flour (Control) Order, 1967
The Milk and Milk Products Order, 1992
Any other order issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (10 of 1955) relating to food
related_acts: Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles and Infant Foods (Regulation of Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 1992 (41 of 1992)
Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (61 of 1985)
Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 1992 (22 of 1992)

authorities_established: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints Chairperson and Members of Food Authority, Chief Executive Officer, Presiding Officer of Tribunal, and Public Prosecutor. Commissioner of Food Safety appoints Designated Officer, Food Safety Officers, and Food Analysts. Food Authority appoints members of Scientific Committee and Scientific Panel.
regulatory_bodies: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (Food Authority)

applies_to: Whole of India
Food business operators
Manufacturers, packers, wholesalers, distributors, sellers
Importers of articles of food
exemptions: Petty manufacturer, petty retailer, hawker, itinerant vendor, temporary stall holder, small scale or cottage or such other industries relating to food business or tiny food business operator (though they must register)

Farmer or fisherman or farming operations or crops or livestock or aquaculture, and supplies used or produced in farming or products of crops produced by a farmer at farm level or a fisherman in his operations
special_provisions: The Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.
Different dates of commencement may be appointed for different provisions of the Act.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government, Food Authority (for regulations), State Government
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforced by the Food Authority and State Food Safety Authorities, involving Commissioner of Food Safety, Designated Officers, and Food Safety Officers. Mechanisms include licensing, inspections, sampling, analysis, improvement notices, prohibition orders, and prosecution, with adjudication by Adjudicating Officers or the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts of ordinary jurisdiction, Special Courts, Judicial Magistrate of the first class or Metropolitan Magistrate (for summary trials), High Court (for appeals), Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, Adjudicating Officer

schedules_summary.description: Lists five Zones with States and Union Territories for the purpose of appointing members to the Food Authority by rotation.
Lists the enactments and Orders that are repealed by this Act, including The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, and various food-related orders.

act_identification.act_title: THE ACTUARIES ACT, 2006

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for regulating and developing the profession of Actuaries and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Institute of Actuaries of India to regulate and develop the profession of Actuaries. It sets standards for professional education, practice, and conduct, and provides for disciplinary actions and penalties for misconduct.

chapter_titles: DISSOLUTION OF THE ACTUARIAL SOCIETY OF INDIA REGISTERED UNDER THE SOCIETIES REGISTRATION ACT

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, including 'Actuary' and 'in practice'.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of Institute.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Institute of Actuaries of India as a body corporate.

key_sections.title: Objects of Institute.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary goals of the Institute, including promoting standards and regulating the profession.

key_sections.title: Entry of names in register.
key_sections.description: Details the eligibility criteria for individuals to have their names entered in the Institute's register.

key_sections.title: Certificate of practice.
key_sections.description: Mandates that members must obtain a certificate of practice to practice as an Actuary.

key_sections.title: Disqualifications.
key_sections.description: Lists conditions under which a person is not entitled to be a member of the Institute.

key_sections.title: Composition of Council of Institute.
key_sections.description: Describes the structure and membership of the governing Council of the Institute.

key_sections.title: Functions of Council.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the duties and responsibilities of the Council, including examinations, regulation, and disciplinary powers.

key_sections.title: Register.
key_sections.description: Requires the Council to maintain a register of members with specified particulars.

key_sections.title: Member to be afforded opportunity of being heard.
key_sections.description: Ensures due process for members accused of misconduct, outlining possible actions by the Council.

key_sections.title: Professional or other misconduct defined.
key_sections.description: States that professional or other misconduct includes acts or omissions listed in the Schedule.

key_sections.title: Penalty for falsely claiming to be a member, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals falsely representing themselves as members or practicing without a certificate.

key_sections.title: Functions of Board.
key_sections.description: Defines the responsibilities of the Quality Review Board, including setting standards and reviewing service quality.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government authority to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Council authority to make regulations with Central Government approval.

powers_conferred: Council: To constitute the Institute, manage affairs, hold examinations, specify qualifications, grant/refuse certificates of practice, maintain register, levy fees, remove/restore names, regulate standards, issue guidelines, receive/give grants, cooperate with institutions, award fellowships, conduct research, maintain library, exercise disciplinary powers, establish regional councils, make regulations.

Central Government: To appoint commencement date, nominate members to Council, establish Tribunal, issue directions to Council, dissolve Council, make rules, issue directions for making/amending regulations, remove difficulties.
Disciplinary Committee: To conduct inquiries.
Prosecution Director: To assist Disciplinary Committee in inquiries.
Authority (Appellate): To hear appeals, confirm/modify/set aside orders, impose/reduce/enhance penalties.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 37: Penalty for falsely claiming to be a member or practicing without a certificate (fine up to one lakh rupees for first conviction, imprisonment up to one year or fine up to two lakh rupees or both for subsequent conviction). Section 38: Penalty for using the Institute's name/seal, awarding similar degrees, or regulating the profession without authority (fine up to fifty thousand rupees for first conviction, imprisonment up to one year or fine up to one lakh rupees or both for subsequent conviction). Section 39: Companies engaging in actuarial practice (fine up to ten thousand rupees for first conviction, up to twenty-five thousand rupees for subsequent conviction). Section 40: Unqualified person signing documents (fine up to fifty thousand rupees for first conviction, imprisonment up to one year or fine up to one lakh rupees or both for subsequent conviction). Section 30(c): Council may impose a fine up to five lakh rupees for professional or other misconduct.

related_acts: Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950 (Bombay Act No XXXIX of 1950)
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999 (41 of 1999)
Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (nominates members to Council, establishes Tribunal, appoints Chairperson and Members of Quality Review Board); Council (appoints Executive Director, Treasurer, other officers/employees; elects President, Vice-President, Honorary Secretary; constitutes Disciplinary Committee; appoints Prosecution Director).

applies_to: all persons whose names are entered in the register of the Actuarial Society at the commencement of this Act
all persons who may thereafter have their names entered in the register to be maintained under this Act
members of the Institute
Actuaries in practice
companies
exemptions: Any University or other institution established by law or to any body affiliated to the Institute (from penalties related to using name/awarding degrees under Section 38(3)).
Any Actuary in practice or firm of such Actuaries may be exempted by the Council from the requirement of having a fellow member in charge of each office (Section 50(1) proviso).
special_provisions: Central Government or the Council may impose further conditions on non-permanently residing persons for entry in the register (Section 6(1) proviso).

Reciprocity clause for subjects of countries that prevent persons of Indian domicile from becoming members of similar institutions or practicing the profession of Actuaries or subject them to unfair discrimination (Section 51).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (Section 55); Council (Section 56, with previous approval of Central Government).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Disciplinary Committee conducts inquiries into misconduct. Prosecution Director assists in inquiries. Council takes action on Disciplinary Committee's report, including reprimand, removal from register, or fine. Appellate Authority hears appeals against Council's orders. Penalties (fines, imprisonment) for various offences. Quality Review Board reviews service quality and guides members.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil court (for powers of inquiry by Authority, Disciplinary Committee, Prosecution Director); Civil or criminal court (for holding members guilty of offences, as mentioned in Part IV of the Schedule); Courts for prosecution under penalties chapter.

schedules_summary.description: Defines professional misconduct in relation to members of the Institute in practice (Part I), professional misconduct in relation to members of the Institute in service (Part II), professional misconduct in relation to members of the Institute generally (Part III), and other misconduct in relation to members of the Institute generally (Part IV).

act_identification.act_title: THE GOVERNMENT SECURITIES ACT, 2006

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of the States, except the State of Jammu and Kashmir, and to all the Union territories and it shall also apply to the State of Jammu and Kashmir which adopts this Act by resolution passed in that behalf under clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Government securities and its management by the Reserve Bank of India and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS it is expedient to consolidate and amend the law relating to Government securities and its management by the Reserve Bank of India; AND WHEREAS Parliament has no power to make laws for the States with respect to any of the matters aforesaid except as provided in articles 249 and 250 of the Constitution; AND WHEREAS in pursuance of clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution, resolutions have been passed by the Houses of the Legislatures of all the States, except the Legislature of the State of Jammu and Kashmir, to the effect that the matters aforesaid should be regulated in those States by Parliament by law;
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws concerning Government securities and their management by the Reserve Bank of India. It seeks to provide a comprehensive legal framework for the creation, issue, transfer, and management of these securities, and to address related matters.

key_sections.title: Short title, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's name, applicability, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act.

key_sections.title: Forms of Government securities.
key_sections.description: Specifies the various forms in which Government securities may be issued.

key_sections.title: Transfer of Government securities.
key_sections.description: Outlines the rules and manner for transferring Government securities.

key_sections.title: Recognition of title to Government security of deceased sole holder or joint holders.
key_sections.description: Deals with the recognition of title to securities upon the death of holders.

key_sections.title: Nomination by holders of Government securities.
key_sections.description: Provides for the nomination facility for holders of Government securities.

key_sections.title: Issue of duplicate securities and of new securities on conversion, consolidation, sub-division, renewal, stripping or reconstruction.
key_sections.description: Governs the issuance of duplicate or new securities under various circumstances.

key_sections.title: Summary determination by Bank of title to Government security in case of dispute.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Bank to summarily determine title in case of disputes.

key_sections.title: Misuse of subsidiary general ledger account facility.
key_sections.description: Addresses the misuse of SGL accounts and the Bank's power to debar holders.

key_sections.title: Power to call for information, cause inspection and issue directions.
key_sections.description: Confers powers on the Bank to gather information, inspect, and issue directions.

key_sections.title: Contravention and penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contraventions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Certain laws not to apply to Government securities.
key_sections.description: Specifies the non-applicability of certain other laws to Government securities.

key_sections.title: Powers of Bank not to apply to International Financial Services Centre.
key_sections.description: Limits the Bank's powers in relation to International Financial Services Centres.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Bank the power to make regulations to carry out the Act's purposes.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Indian Securities Act, 1920, and includes saving provisions.

powers_conferred: Power of the Bank to specify terms and conditions for forms of Government securities (Section 3).
Power of the Bank to open and maintain subsidiary general ledger accounts (Section 4).
Power of the Bank to recognise title to Government security of deceased holders (Section 7).
Power of the Bank to make orders for vesting Government securities belonging to minor or insane persons (Section 10).
Power of the Bank to issue duplicate or new securities (Section 11).
Power of the Bank to summarily determine title to Government security in case of dispute (Section 12).
Power of the Bank to suspend payments or postpone registration of transfers (Section 14).
Power of the Bank to require indemnity bonds (Section 15).
Power of the Bank to publish notices in Official Gazette (Section 16).
Power of the Bank to cancel vesting proceedings (Section 20).
Power of the Bank to specify securities for interest payment after limitation period (Section 23).
Power of the Bank to debar holders from SGL account facility (Section 27).
Power of the Bank to call for information, cause inspection and issue directions (Section 29).
Power of the Bank to impose penalties (Section 30).
Power of the Bank to make regulations (Section 32).
Power of the Central Government to fix higher amounts for deceased holders/minors (Section 7(3), 10(2)).
Power of the Central Government to appoint date of commencement (Section 1(4)).
Power of the Central Government to remove difficulties (Section 34).
Power of the International Financial Services Centre Authority to exercise powers in IFSC (Section 31A).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: If any person makes a false statement for obtaining title to a Government security, the Bank may impose a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees or twice the amount involved, whichever is higher, and a further penalty of up to five thousand rupees per day for continuing contravention. The Bank may also impose a penalty not exceeding five lakh rupees for contravention of any provision of this Act, regulations, notifications, directions, or violation of SGL account terms, with a further penalty of up to five thousand rupees per day for continuing contravention.

amended_acts: Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization (Adaptation of Central Laws) Order, 2020
Union Territory of Ladakh Reorganisation (Adaptation of Central Laws) Order, 2020
repealed_acts: The Indian Securities Act, 1920 (10 of 1920)
related_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019

applies_to: Government securities created and issued whether before or after the commencement of this Act by the Central Government or a State Government.
whole of the States, except the State of Jammu and Kashmir, and to all the Union territories
the State of Jammu and Kashmir which adopts this Act by resolution passed in that behalf under clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution.
exemptions: State of Jammu and Kashmir (initially, until adoption)
International Financial Services Centre set up under sub-section (1) of section 18 of the Special Economic Zones Act, 2005 (for powers of the Bank)
special_provisions: State of Jammu and Kashmir (special adoption mechanism)
International Financial Services Centre (Bank's powers are exercisable by IFSC Authority)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Bank (Reserve Bank of India), with the previous approval of the Central Government
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Bank has powers to determine title in disputes, suspend payments, postpone transfers, require indemnity bonds, publish notices, debar from SGL account facility, call for information, cause inspection, issue directions, and impose penalties for contraventions.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts of India, competent court, Court of competent jurisdiction, District Magistrate, Executive Magistrate

act_identification.act_title: THE PONDICHERRY (ALTERATION OF NAME) ACT, 2006

act_overview.preamble: An Act to alter the name of the Union territory of Pondicherry.
act_overview.purpose: The primary purpose of this Act is to change the name of the Union territory of Pondicherry to Puducherry. It mandates consequential amendments to the Constitution and other relevant laws to reflect this alteration, ensuring legal consistency across all applicable statutes and documents.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'appropriate Government', and 'law'.

key_sections.title: Alteration of name of the Union territory of Pondicherry.
key_sections.description: States that the Union territory of Pondicherry shall be known as the Union territory of Puducherry from the appointed day.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Part VIII of the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Substitutes the word 'Pondicherry' with 'Puducherry' in Part VIII of the Constitution.

key_sections.title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Substitutes the word 'Pondicherry' with 'Puducherry' in entry 6 under 'II. THE UNION TERRITORIES' in the First Schedule to the Constitution.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Fourth Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Substitutes the word 'Pondicherry' with 'Puducherry' in entry 30 under 'TABLE' in the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution.

key_sections.title: Amendment of section 2 of Act 20 of 1963.
key_sections.description: Substitutes the word 'Pondicherry' with 'Puducherry' in section 2, sub-section (1), clause (h) of the Government of Union Territories Act, 1963.

key_sections.title: Power to adapt laws.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the appropriate Government to make adaptations and modifications to existing laws to give effect to the name alteration.

key_sections.title: Power to construe laws.
key_sections.description: Allows courts, tribunals, or authorities to construe laws in a necessary or proper manner even if adaptations under section 8 are insufficient.

key_sections.title: Legal proceedings.
key_sections.description: Provides that references to the administrator of the Union territory of Pondicherry in pending legal proceedings shall be construed as references to the administrator of the Union territory of Puducherry.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint the date of commencement of the Act.
Appropriate Government to make adaptations and modifications of any law.
Parliament or Legislative Assembly of the Union territory of Puducherry or other competent authority to repeal or amend adapted or modified laws.

Specific penalties include: fine up to ten thousand rupees for failure to comply with notice of transfer (Sec 81); fine up to five thousand rupees or ten times tax for failure to give notice of building erection (Sec 82); fine up to ten times tax or two thousand five hundred rupees for tax evasion (Sec 91); fine up to one thousand rupees for failure to report infectious disease (Sec 155); fine up to one lakh rupees for contravention of building use restrictions (Sec 244); fine up to fifty thousand rupees for illegal building erection (Sec 247); imprisonment up to six months or fine up to twenty thousand rupees for removing seal on unauthorized construction (Sec 249); fine up to five thousand rupees or imprisonment up to six months for unauthorized sale of spirituous liquor (Sec 285); imprisonment up to three months or fine up to five thousand rupees for loitering for prostitution (Sec 300); and a general penalty of fine up to five thousand rupees for non-compliance with notices or contravention of provisions (Sec 333).

act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to consolidate and amend the law governing the Assam Rifles, an Armed Force of the Union. key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter IV (Sections 21-56) defines various offences, including those in relation to the enemy, mutiny, desertion, absence without leave, striking or threatening superior officers, disobedience, insubordination, fraudulent enrolment, false answers, unbecoming conduct, disgraceful conduct, ill-treating subordinates, intoxication, permitting escape, irregularity in arrest, escape from custody, offences in respect of property, extortion and corruption, making away with equipment, injury to property, false accusations, falsifying official documents, signing in blank, offences relating to Assam Rifles Courts, false evidence, unlawful detention of pay, violation of good order and discipline, miscellaneous offences, attempt, abetment, and civil offences. Penalties (Chapter V, Sections 57-67) include death, imprisonment (life or lesser term), dismissal from service, compulsory retirement, imprisonment in Force custody, reduction to lower rank, forfeiture of seniority/service, fine, severe reprimand or reprimand, forfeiture of pay and allowances, stoppage of pay and allowances, and collective fines. The severity of punishment varies based on the offence and circumstances, with imprisonment terms ranging from six months to fourteen years, and death for grave offences.

act_identification.act_title: THE SCHEDULED TRIBES AND OTHER TRADITIONAL FOREST DWELLERS (RECOGNITION OF FOREST RIGHTS) ACT, 2006
act_identification.act_short_title: the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Environment and Forests, Ministry of Tribal Affairs

act_overview.preamble: An Act to recognise and vest the forest rights and occupation in forest land in forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers who have been residing in such forests for generations but whose rights could not be recorded; to provide for a framework for recording the forest rights so vested and the nature of evidence required for such recognition and vesting in respect of forest land. WHEREAS the recognised rights of the forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers include the responsibilities and authority for sustainable use, conservation of biodiversity and maintenance of ecological balance and thereby strengthening the conservation regime of the forests while ensuring livelihood and food security of the forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers; AND WHEREAS the forest rights on ancestral lands and their habitat were not adequately recognised in the consolidation of State forests during the colonial period as well as in independent India resulting in historical injustice to the forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers who are integral to the very survival and sustainability of the forest ecosystem; AND WHEREAS it has become necessary to address the long standing insecurity of tenurial and access rights of forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers including those who were forced to relocate their dwelling due to State development interventions.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to recognize and vest forest rights and occupation in forest land for Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers whose rights were previously unrecorded. It seeks to rectify historical injustices by providing a framework for recording these rights, ensuring their livelihood, food security, and participation in forest conservation.

chapter_titles: RECOGNITION, RESTORATION AND VESTING OF FOREST RIGHTS AND RELATED MATTERS
AUTHORITIES AND PROCEDURE FOR VESTING OF FOREST RIGHTS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's official name, geographical application, and the date it comes into force.

key_sections.title: Definitions.

key_sections.description: Enumerates various individual and community forest rights recognized for forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers, including rights to hold land, collect minor forest produce, and access biodiversity.

key_sections.title: Recognition of, and vesting of, forest rights in forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers.
key_sections.description: Details the process and conditions for the recognition and vesting of forest rights, including provisions for critical wildlife habitats, heritability, and restrictions on land area.

key_sections.title: Duties of holders of forest rights.
key_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities of forest rights holders, Gram Sabha, and village-level institutions to protect wildlife, forests, biodiversity, and ensure sustainable practices.

key_sections.description: Establishes the multi-tier authority structure (Gram Sabha, Sub-Divisional Level Committee, District Level Committee, State Level Monitoring Committee) and the procedure for initiating, verifying, and vesting forest rights.
