key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, including procedural details for implementation.

powers_conferred: Gram Sabha: To initiate the process for determining the nature and extent of individual or community forest rights, receive claims, consolidate and verify them, prepare maps, pass resolutions, and recommend diversion of forest land.

Gram Sabha and village level institutions: To protect wildlife, forest and biodiversity, ensure protection of ecological sensitive areas, preserve habitat, and regulate access to community forest resources.
Sub-Divisional Level Committee: To examine Gram Sabha resolutions, prepare the record of forest rights, and dispose of petitions.
District Level Committee: To consider and finally approve the record of forest rights and dispose of petitions.
State Level Monitoring Committee: To monitor the process of recognition and vesting of forest rights.
Central Government: To determine and notify critical wildlife habitat, issue directions to authorities, and make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
State Government: To constitute Sub-Divisional Level Committee, District Level Committee, and State Level Monitoring Committee.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any authority or Committee or officer or member contravening any provision of this Act or rules concerning recognition of forest rights shall be guilty of an offence and liable to a fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.

related_acts: Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (40 of 1996)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government constitutes the Sub-Divisional Level Committee, District Level Committee, and State Level Monitoring Committee. Panchayati Raj Institutions appoint three members to these committees. The Central Government appoints experts to the Expert Committee.

applies_to: Forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes
Other traditional forest dwellers
Members or communities who primarily reside in and depend on the forests or forest lands for bona fide livelihood needs
Those who occupied forest land before the 13th day of December, 2005
exemptions: The traditional right of hunting or trapping or extracting a part of the body of any species of wild animal
special_provisions: Forest rights recognized in critical wildlife habitats may be modified or resettled under specific conditions, including free informed consent of Gram Sabhas and a secure resettlement package.
The land under individual or family or community occupation for habitation or self-cultivation shall not exceed an area of four hectares.
Rights conferred are heritable but not alienable or transferable.
No member shall be evicted or removed from forest land until the recognition and verification procedure is complete.
Diversion of forest land for certain government facilities (e.g., schools, hospitals) is allowed under specific conditions, including Gram Sabha recommendation and land being less than one hectare.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a multi-tier system involving the Gram Sabha, Sub-Divisional Level Committee, District Level Committee, and State Level Monitoring Committee, which process claims, verify rights, and monitor implementation. Aggrieved persons can prefer petitions to higher committees.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts can take cognizance of offences under Section 7 if a forest dwelling Scheduled Tribe or Gram Sabha gives 60 days' notice to the State Level Monitoring Committee and the Committee fails to act.

act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS (RESERVATION IN ADMISSION) ACT, 2006
act_identification.act_short_title: The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the reservation in admission of the students belonging to the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes and the Other Backward Classes of citizens, to certain Central Educational Institutions established, maintained or aided by the Central Government, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to implement reservations in admissions for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes in Central Educational Institutions. It covers institutions established, maintained, or aided by the Central Government, along with related matters.

key_definitions: teaching or instruction in any branch of study

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'academic session', 'Central Educational Institution', 'appropriate authority', 'Other Backward Classes', 'Scheduled Castes', and 'Scheduled Tribes'.

key_sections.title: Reservation of seats in Central Educational Institutions.
key_sections.description: Mandates reservation of seats in Central Educational Institutions for Scheduled Castes (15%), Scheduled Tribes (7.5%), and Other Backward Classes (27%). Includes provisos for State seats in tribal areas and specific north-eastern regions.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Specifies cases where the provisions of section 3 do not apply, including institutions of excellence, research institutions, Minority Educational Institutions, and high-level specialisation courses.

key_sections.title: Mandatory increase of seats.
key_sections.description: Requires Central Educational Institutions to increase the number of seats to accommodate reservations without reducing the number of unreserved seats. Allows for phased increase over a maximum period of six years with Central Government approval.

key_sections.title: Reservation of seats in admissions to begin in calendar year, [3][2008].
key_sections.description: Directs Central Educational Institutions to implement the reservation provisions for academic sessions commencing from the calendar year 2008.

key_sections.title: Laying of notifications before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that all notifications made under this Act must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for review and potential modification or annulment.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To amend the Schedule (Section 4(b) proviso).
Central Government: To specify courses or programmes at high levels of specialisation for exemption (Section 4(d)).
Central Government: To permit institutions to increase annual permitted strength over a maximum period of six years (Section 5(2)).
Appropriate authority: To give prior approval for increasing the number of seats in a branch of study or faculty (Section 5(1)).
State Government: To specify reservation policy for State seats in tribal areas by notification (Section 3 proviso).

related_acts: National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions Act, 2004

regulatory_bodies: All India Council for Technical Education

applies_to: students belonging to the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes and the Other Backward Classes of citizens
certain Central Educational Institutions established, maintained or aided by the Central Government
exemptions: institutions of excellence, research institutions, institutions of national and strategic importance specified in the Schedule
a Minority Educational Institution as defined in this Act
a course or programme at high levels of specialisation, including at the post-doctoral level, within any branch of study or faculty
special_provisions: State seats, if any, in a Central Educational Institution situated in the tribal areas referred to in the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution
Central Educational Institutions in the specified north-eastern region

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Central Educational Institutions shall take all necessary steps to give effect to the provisions of the Act for reservation of seats in admissions.

schedules_summary.description: Lists names of Institutions of Excellence, research institutions, and institutions of national and strategic importance that are exempt from the provisions of Section 3 of the Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE ENGLISH AND FOREIGN LANGUAGES UNIVERSITY ACT, 2006
act_identification.act_short_title: the English and Foreign Languages University Act, 2006

legislative_details.geographical_extent: The jurisdiction of the University shall extend to the whole of India.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate a teaching University for promotion and development of English and other Foreign Languages and their Literature, and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS it is expedient to establish and incorporate a teaching University at Hyderabad, to dissolve the "Central Institute of English and Foreign Languages, Hyderabad", a Society registered under the Hyderabad Societies Registration Act, 1350(Act 1 of 1350 Fasli) and to transfer to and vest in the said University all properties and rights of the said Society;
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to establish and incorporate a teaching University named The English and Foreign Languages University. It aims to promote and develop English and other Foreign Languages and their Literature, provide instructional, research, and extension facilities, train language teachers, and foster inter-disciplinary studies and research in Literary and Cultural Studies.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines various terms used throughout the Act, Statutes, and Ordinances.

key_sections.title: Establishment of the University.
key_sections.description: Establishes "The English and Foreign Languages University" in Andhra Pradesh, specifying its headquarters and potential campuses.

key_sections.title: Dissolution of the Central Institute of English and Foreign Languages, Hyderabad Society and transfer of all the properties and effect of establishment of the University.
key_sections.description: Details the dissolution of the previous society and the transfer of its properties, rights, liabilities, and employees to the newly established University.

key_sections.title: Objects of the University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary objectives of the University, including dissemination of knowledge, teacher training, and inter-disciplinary studies in languages and literature.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the extensive powers of the University, such as granting degrees, establishing campuses, conducting research, and managing its affairs.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: States that the University's jurisdiction extends to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University and defines his powers, including review, inspection, and issuing directions.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the various officers who shall govern the University, such as the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and Registrar.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main governing authorities of the University, including the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council.

key_sections.title: Powers to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Statutes can be made, covering constitution of authorities, appointments, and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Details the matters for which Ordinances can be made, such as student admission, courses of study, and examinations.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees.
key_sections.description: Mandates written contracts for employees and provides for arbitration in disputes between the University and its employees.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Requires publication of statutory instruments in the Official Gazette and their laying before both Houses of Parliament.

powers_conferred: University: To provide for instructions, grant diplomas/certificates/degrees, organize extramural studies, confer honorary degrees, provide distance education, institute teaching positions, recognise institutions, appoint teachers, create administrative/ministerial posts, co-operate with other institutions, establish campuses/centres, institute awards, establish colleges/institutions/halls, conduct research, organize courses, supervise student residences, lay down conditions of service, regulate discipline, receive benefactions/donations/gifts, acquire/hold/manage/dispose of property, borrow money, and other incidental acts.

Visitor: To appoint persons to review work, cause inspection/inquiry, issue directions, annul proceedings of the University, assent to Statutes, make new/additional Statutes or amend/repeal existing ones, direct the University to make provisions in Statutes.

Central Government: To appoint the commencement date of the Act, approve the establishment of campuses/centres, approve the first Ordinances, receive annual reports and accounts, require returns or information, declare the Provident Funds Act applicable, remove difficulties in implementing the Act, and appoint the first Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council.

Executive Council: To manage and administer revenues and property, conduct administrative affairs, create teaching/academic/administrative posts, appoint staff, grant leave of absence, regulate and enforce discipline among employees, manage finances/accounts/investments, fix expenditure limits, invest money, transfer property, provide infrastructure, enter into contracts, entertain/adjudicate grievances, appoint examiners, select common seal, make special arrangements for women students, institute awards, appoint visiting professors, and make/amend/repeal Statutes and Ordinances.

Vice-Chancellor: To be the principal executive and academic officer, exercise general supervision and control, exercise powers of any authority in emergency, ask for review of decisions, be ex officio Chairman of the Executive Council, Academic Council, and Finance Committee, preside at Convocations/Court meetings, ensure observance of the Act/Statutes/Ordinances/Regulations, maintain discipline, convene meetings, and make first Ordinances with Central Government approval.
Registrar: To take disciplinary action against specified employees (excluding teachers and academic staff), suspend pending inquiry, administer warnings, or impose censure/withholding of increment.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for disciplinary action against students, which may include removal from rolls, debarment from examinations, fines, expulsion, or rustication. It also allows for the removal of employees on grounds of misconduct.

related_acts: Hyderabad Societies Registration Act, 1350 (Act 1 of 1350 Fasli)

authorities_established: The English and Foreign Languages University
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and an umpire for employee arbitration. The Executive Council appoints the Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, Librarian, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, teachers, academic staff, administrative/ministerial posts, and the Proctor. The Central Government appoints the first Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, and nominates members for the first Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council. The Vice-Chancellor appoints Deans of Schools and persons to fill temporary vacancies in certain offices. The Academic Council nominates students to the Students' Council.

applies_to: The English and Foreign Languages University
Persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class
Employees and students of the University
special_provisions: Special provisions for the employment or admission of women, persons with disabilities or of persons belonging to the weaker sections of the society and, in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.

Transitional provisions for the appointment of the first Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, and the constitution of the first Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council by the Central Government.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Statutes are made by the Executive Council (amend/repeal/add) with the assent of the Visitor, who can also make or direct changes. Ordinances are initially made by the Vice-Chancellor with Central Government approval, then amended/repealed/added to by the Executive Council based on proposals from the Academic Council. Regulations are made by the authorities of the University.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is primarily through the Visitor's powers of review, inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions; the Vice-Chancellor's role as the principal executive and academic officer with powers to ensure observance of rules and maintain discipline; the Executive Council's management and administrative powers; and specific disciplinary actions against employees and students. Disputes are subject to arbitration, with judicial remedies preserved under the Constitution.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: While arbitration decisions are generally final and no suit lies in civil courts, judicial remedies available under Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution are preserved, implying the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and High Courts.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the detailed Statutes of the University, including provisions for the appointment, terms, and powers of the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Deans of Schools, Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, and Librarian. It also outlines the constitution, powers, and functions of the Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Schools of Studies, Finance Committee, Selection Committees, and provisions for recognized teachers, committees, terms of service, removal of employees, honorary degrees, withdrawal of degrees, maintenance of discipline among students, convocations, resignation, disqualification, residence conditions for membership, Alumni Association, and Students' Council.

act_identification.act_title: THE RAJIV GANDHI UNIVERSITY ACT, 2006

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of the State of Arunachal Pradesh

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University in the State of Arunachal Pradesh and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The objects of the University shall be to disseminate and advance knowledge by providing instructional and research facilities in such branches of learning as it may deem fit; to make provisions for integrated courses in humanities, natural and physical sciences, social sciences, forestry and other allied disciplines in the educational programmes of the University; to take appropriate measures for promoting innovations in teaching-learning process, inter-disciplinary studies and research; to educate and train manpower for the development of the State of Arunachal Pradesh; and to pay special attention to the improvement of the social and economic conditions and welfare of the people of that State, their intellectual, academic and cultural development.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment of the University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Rajiv Gandhi University as a body corporate and specifies its headquarters.

key_sections.title: Effect of establishment of the University.
key_sections.description: Details the transfer of assets, liabilities, and employees from the previous Rajiv Gandhi University to the new one.

key_sections.title: Objects of the University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary goals and objectives of the University, including knowledge dissemination, research, and regional development.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers of the University, such as granting degrees, conducting research, and establishing institutions.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Defines the geographical extent of the University's jurisdiction to the whole of Arunachal Pradesh and restricts other universities' operations there.

key_sections.title: The Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor and outlines their powers of review, inspection, and direction.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the various officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and Registrar.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main governing bodies of the University, such as the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council.

key_sections.title: Power to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Grants the power to make Statutes for various administrative and academic matters.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Grants the power to make Ordinances for academic and operational details.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions of service for employees, including arbitration for disputes.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Arunachal Pradesh Act 1 of 1984.
key_sections.description: Repeals the previous Rajiv Gandhi University Act, 1984, while providing for transitional provisions.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Act 24 of 1973.
key_sections.description: Amends the North-Eastern Hill University Act, 1973, to reflect the new University's jurisdiction.

powers_conferred: to provide for instructions in such branches of learning as the University may, from time to time, determine and to make provisions for research and for the advancement and dissemination of knowledge

to grant, subject to such conditions as the University may determine, diplomas or certificates to, and confer degrees or other academic distinctions on the basis of examinations, evaluation or any other method of testing, on persons, and to withdraw any such diplomas, certificates, degrees or other academic distinctions for good and sufficient cause
to organise and to undertake extramural studies, training and extension services
to confer honorary degrees or other distinctions in the manner prescribed by the Statutes
to provide facilities through the distance education system to such persons as it may determine

to institute Principalships, Professorships, Readerships, Lecturerships and other teaching or academic positions, required by the University and to appoint persons to such Principalships, Professorships, Readerships, Lecturerships or other teaching or academic positions
to recognise an Institution of higher learning for such purposes as the University may determine and to withdraw such recognition
to recognise persons for imparting instructions in any College or Institution admitted to the privileges of the University
to appoint persons working in any other University or educational institution as teachers of the University for a specified period
to create administrative, ministerial and other posts and to make appointments thereto
to co-operate or collaborate or associate with any other University or authority or Institution of higher learning in such manner and for such purposes as the University may determine

to establish, with the prior approval of the Central Government, such Centres and specialised laboratories or other units for research and instruction as are, in the opinion of the University, necessary for the furtherance of its objects
to institute and award fellowships, scholarships, studentships, medals and prizes
to establish and maintain Colleges, Institutions and Halls

to make provision for research and advisory services and for that purpose to enter into such arrangements with other institutions, industrial or other organisations, as the University may deem necessary
to organise and conduct refresher courses, workshops, seminars and other programmes for teachers, evaluators and other academic staff

to admit to its privileges Colleges and Institutions within the State of Arunachal Pradesh not maintained by the University; to withdraw all or any of those privileges in accordance with such conditions as may be prescribed by the Statutes; torecognise, guide, supervise, and control Halls not maintained by the University and other accommodation for students, and to withdraw any such recognition
to appoint on contract or otherwise visiting Professors, Emeritus Professors, Consultants, Scholars and such other persons who may contribute to the advancement of the objects of the University
to confer autonomous status on a College or an Institution or a Department, as the case may be, in accordance with the Statutes
to determine standards of admission to the University, which may include examination, evaluation or any other method of testing
to demand and receive payment of fees and other charges
to supervise the residences of the students of the University and to make arrangements for promoting their health and general welfare
to lay down conditions of service of all categories of employees, including their code of conduct
to regulate and enforce discipline among the students and the employees, and to take such disciplinary measures in this regard as may be deemed by the University to be necessary
to make arrangements for promoting the health and general welfare of the employees

to receive benefactions, donations and gifts and to acquire, hold and manage, and to dispose of, with the previous approval of the Central Government, any property, movable or immovable, including trust and endowment properties for the purposes of the University
to borrow, with the approval of the Central Government, on the security of the property of the University, money for the purposes of the University
to do all such other acts and things as may be necessary, incidental or conducive to the attainment of all or any of its objects
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for disciplinary action against students, including removal from rolls, debarment from examinations, fines, expulsion, or rustication (Section 37, Statute 30). For employees, it allows for disciplinary action including suspension, censure, withholding increment, and removal on grounds of misconduct (Statute 6, Statute 27).

amended_acts: The North-Eastern Hill University Act, 1973 (Act 24 of 1973)
repealed_acts: The Rajiv Gandhi University Act, 1984 (Arunachal Pradesh Act 1 of 1984)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Visitor (for Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and to approve Statutes), Executive Council (for Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, Librarian, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Deans of Faculties, teachers, academic staff, other employees), Central Government (for first Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, and members of initial authorities).

applies_to: Educational institutions within the State of Arunachal Pradesh
persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class
employees of the University
students of the University
exemptions: Educational institutions within the State of Arunachal Pradesh may be exempted by Central Government order from being associated only with this University (Section 7(2) proviso)
Special provisions for employment or admission of women, persons with disabilities, weaker sections of society, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Section 8 proviso)
special_provisions: Special provisions for employment or admission of women, persons with disabilities, weaker sections of society, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Section 8 proviso)
Central Government may exempt educational institutions from exclusive affiliation (Section 7(2) proviso)
Transitional provisions for initial appointments and functioning of authorities (Section 47)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Visitor (for Statutes), Executive Council (for Statutes and Ordinances), Academic Council (proposes Ordinances, frames Regulations), Vice-Chancellor (makes first Ordinances), University authorities (for Regulations).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor has powers of review, inspection, and issuing directions (Section 9). The Vice-Chancellor is the principal executive and academic officer, responsible for general supervision and control, and ensuring observance of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations (Section 13, Statute 3). The Executive Council manages and regulates finances and administrative affairs (Statute 12). Disciplinary actions are prescribed for employees and students (Sections 36, 37, Statutes 6, 27, 30, 31).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Disputes between the University and employees are referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration, whose decision is final, but employees retain the right to judicial remedies under Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution (Section 36).

schedules_summary.description: Contains the Statutes of the University, detailing the constitution, powers, and duties of the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Deans of Faculties, Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, and Librarian. It also covers the functioning of the Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Finance Committee, Selection Committees, appointment procedures, terms of service, removal of employees, honorary degrees, withdrawal of degrees, maintenance of discipline among students, admission of colleges to privileges, and general provisions regarding meetings, resignations, disqualifications, and delegation of powers.

act_identification.act_title: THE TRIPURA UNIVERSITY ACT, 2006

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of the State of Tripura

act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to establish a teaching and affiliating university in Tripura to disseminate and advance knowledge through instruction and research. implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Executive Council has the power to make, amend, or repeal Statutes and Ordinances. The Academic Council proposes Ordinances and frames Regulations. Other authorities of the University may make Regulations. The Visitor assents to Statutes and can make, amend, or repeal Statutes, and direct the University to make Statutes. The Vice-Chancellor makes the first Ordinances with the Central Government's approval. The Central Government can issue orders to remove difficulties.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor has powers to review, inspect, issue directions, and annul proceedings. The Vice-Chancellor ensures the observance of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations. Disciplinary actions are prescribed for employees and students. Disputes arising from contracts or disciplinary actions are subject to arbitration. Annual reports and accounts are submitted to the Court, Visitor, and Central Government, and laid before Parliament. Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations are published in the Official Gazette.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil courts are generally excluded for matters decided by the Tribunal of Arbitration, but employees retain the right to avail judicial remedies under Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution (i.e., High Courts and Supreme Court).

schedules_summary.description: Contains the detailed Statutes of the University, covering the appointment, powers, and duties of officers (Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Deans, Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, Librarian), the constitution and functions of authorities (Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Finance Committee), selection committees for appointments, terms and conditions of service for employees, provisions for honorary degrees and withdrawal of degrees, maintenance of discipline among students, admission of colleges to university privileges, convocations, disqualifications for membership, alumni association, students' council, and procedures for making Ordinances and Regulations.

act_identification.act_title: THE PROHIBITION OF CHILD MARRIAGE ACT, 2006
act_identification.act_short_title: THE PROHIBITION OF CHILD MARRIAGE ACT, 2006

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India; and it applies also to all citizens of India without and beyond India: Provided that nothing contained in this Act shall apply to the Renoncants of the Union territory of Pondicherry.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the prohibition of solemnisation of child marriages and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to prohibit the solemnisation of child marriages across India. It provides legal provisions for declaring child marriages voidable or void, ensures maintenance and custody for affected parties and children, and prescribes punishments for those involved in promoting or conducting such marriages.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, its geographical application to the whole of India and to Indian citizens abroad, and the process for its commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'child', 'child marriage', 'contracting party', 'Child Marriage Prohibition Officer', 'district court', and 'minor'.

key_sections.title: Child marriages to be voidable at the option of contracting party being a child.
key_sections.description: Declares child marriages voidable at the option of the party who was a child at the time of marriage, allowing them to file a petition for annulment.

key_sections.title: Provision for maintenance and residence to female contracting party to child marriage.
key_sections.description: Empowers the district court to order maintenance and residence for the female contracting party to a child marriage until her remarriage.

key_sections.title: Punishment for male adult marrying a child.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for a male adult above eighteen years of age who contracts a child marriage.

key_sections.title: Punishment for solemnising a child marriage.
key_sections.description: Stipulates punishment for individuals who perform, conduct, direct, or abet any child marriage.

key_sections.title: Punishment for promoting or permitting solemnisation of child marriages.
key_sections.description: Defines punishment for persons, including parents or guardians, who promote, permit, or negligently fail to prevent the solemnisation of child marriages.

key_sections.title: Marriage of a minor child to be void in certain circumstances.
key_sections.description: Declares a child marriage null and void if the minor child was taken, enticed, compelled, induced, or sold for the purpose of marriage or trafficked thereafter.

key_sections.title: Power of court to issue injunction prohibiting child marriages.
key_sections.description: Grants power to Judicial Magistrates or Metropolitan Magistrates to issue injunctions prohibiting child marriages, including _suo motu_ cognizance and powers for District Magistrates in mass child marriage prevention.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable and non-bailable.
key_sections.description: States that offences punishable under this Act are cognizable and non-bailable, overriding provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

key_sections.title: Child Marriage Prohibition Officers.
key_sections.description: Mandates the appointment of Child Marriage Prohibition Officers by the State Government and outlines their duties, including preventing child marriages, collecting evidence, and creating awareness.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Act No. 25 of 1955.
key_sections.description: Amends Section 18 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, to align penalties for contravention of marriage conditions with this Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929, while providing for the continuation and disposal of pending cases under the repealed Act.

powers_conferred: District court: to grant a decree of nullity for child marriages (Section 3)
District court: to make interim or final orders for maintenance and residence for female contracting parties (Section 4)
District court: to make appropriate orders for custody and maintenance of children born of child marriages (Section 5)
District court: to add to, modify or revoke any order made under section 4 or section 5 (Section 7)
Judicial Magistrate of the first class or a Metropolitan Magistrate: to issue injunctions prohibiting child marriages (Section 13)
Judicial Magistrate of the first class or a Metropolitan Magistrate: to take _suo motu_ cognizance of child marriage arrangements (Section 13(3))
District Magistrate: to be deemed Child Marriage Prohibition Officer for preventing mass child marriages and to take appropriate measures including minimum force (Section 13(4), (5))
State Government: to appoint Child Marriage Prohibition Officers (Section 16(1))
State Government: to invest Child Marriage Prohibition Officers with powers of a police officer (Section 16(4))
State Government: to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act (Section 19)

Child Marriage Prohibition Officer: to prevent solemnisation of child marriages, collect evidence, advise, create awareness, sensitize community, furnish returns, and discharge assigned duties (Section 16(3))
Child Marriage Prohibition Officer: to move the Court for an order under sections 4, 5 and 13 and along with the child under section 3 (Section 16(5))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Punishment for male adult marrying a child (Section 9): rigorous imprisonment up to two years or fine up to one lakh rupees or both. Punishment for solemnising a child marriage (Section 10): rigorous imprisonment up to two years and fine up to one lakh rupees. Punishment for promoting or permitting solemnisation of child marriages (Section 11): rigorous imprisonment up to two years and fine up to one lakh rupees (no imprisonment for women). Punishment for disobeying an injunction (Section 13(10)): imprisonment up to two years or fine up to one lakh rupees or both (no imprisonment for women).

repealed_acts: The Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929 (19 of 1929)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government has the power to appoint Child Marriage Prohibition Officers.

applies_to: whole of India
all citizens of India without and beyond India
exemptions: Renoncants of the Union territory of Pondicherry
special_provisions: Karnataka State Amendments for sections 3, 9, 10, 11, 13, and insertion of new section 15A.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through Child Marriage Prohibition Officers, who prevent marriages, collect evidence, and raise awareness. Judicial Magistrates, Metropolitan Magistrates, and District Magistrates have powers to issue injunctions. Offences are cognizable and non-bailable, and police officers may take _suo motu_ cognizance in Karnataka.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District court, Judicial Magistrate of the first class, Metropolitan Magistrate

act_identification.act_title: THE SIKKIM UNIVERSITY ACT, 2006

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of the State of Sikkim

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University in the State of Sikkim and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University in the State of Sikkim. Its primary objectives include disseminating and advancing knowledge, providing instructional and research facilities, promoting integrated courses and inter-disciplinary studies, and educating manpower for the development and welfare of the people of Sikkim.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act and in Statutes made thereunder.

key_sections.title: Establishment of the University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the 'Sikkim University' in the State of Sikkim with its headquarters at Gangtok, constituting it as a body corporate.

key_sections.title: Objects of the University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the University's objectives, including disseminating knowledge, providing instructional and research facilities, promoting integrated and inter-disciplinary studies, training manpower for Sikkim's development, and improving social, economic, intellectual, academic, and cultural conditions in the State.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers of the University, such as granting degrees, organizing studies, instituting teaching positions, establishing centers, awarding scholarships, and managing property.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: States that the University's jurisdiction extends to the whole of the State of Sikkim and restricts other universities from affiliating institutions within the State.

key_sections.title: The Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University, outlining powers to review work, inspect, inquire, issue directions, and annul proceedings.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the key officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Deans, Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, and Librarian.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities of the University, such as the Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, College Development Council, Board of Studies, and Finance Committee.

key_sections.title: Power to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Details the matters for which Statutes may provide, covering constitution of authorities, appointments, conditions of service, and academic matters.

key_sections.title: Statutes how to be made.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the procedure for making, amending, or repealing Statutes, requiring the assent of the Visitor.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Ordinances may provide, including admission, courses of study, examinations, fees, and conditions of residence.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees.
key_sections.description: Mandates written contracts for employees and provides for arbitration in disputes arising from such contracts, with constitutional remedies preserved.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act for a period of three years from commencement.

key_sections.title: Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Requires all Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and laid before both Houses of Parliament.

powers_conferred: University: To provide instruction, grant degrees, organize extramural studies, confer honorary degrees, provide distance education, institute teaching positions, recognize institutions, appoint teachers, create administrative posts, cooperate with other institutions, establish centres and laboratories, institute and award fellowships/scholarships/medals/prizes, establish and maintain colleges/institutions/halls, make provisions for research and advisory services, organize refresher courses/workshops/seminars, admit colleges to privileges, appoint visiting professors/consultants/scholars, confer autonomous status, determine admission standards, demand fees, supervise student residences, lay down conditions of service for employees, regulate and enforce discipline, promote employee welfare, receive benefactions/donations/gifts, acquire/hold/manage/dispose of property, borrow money.

Visitor: To appoint the Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor, appoint persons to review the work and progress of the University, issue directions, cause inspections and inquiries, annul proceedings not in conformity with the Act/Statutes/Ordinances, make new or additional Statutes or amend/repeal existing ones, direct the University to make provisions in Statutes.

Executive Council: To manage and administer the revenues and property of the University, conduct administrative affairs, create teaching and academic posts, appoint academic staff, recognize teachers, create administrative/ministerial posts, grant leave of absence to officers, regulate and enforce discipline among employees, manage finances/accounts/investments, fix expenditure limits, invest University money, transfer property, provide infrastructure, enter into contracts, entertain/adjudicate employee/student grievances, appoint examiners and moderators, select a common seal, make special arrangements for women students, institute fellowships/scholarships/medals/prizes, appoint visiting professors/consultants/scholars, make/amend/repeal Ordinances (after initial ones), appoint Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, Librarian, Proctor.

Vice-Chancellor: To be the principal executive and academic officer, exercise general supervision and control, give effect to decisions of authorities, take immediate action in necessary matters (reporting to authority), review decisions of authorities, ensure observance of Act/Statutes/Ordinances/Regulations, maintain discipline, convene meetings of Executive Council/Academic Council/Finance Committee, make first Ordinances (with Central Government approval), appoint Deans of Schools.

Central Government: To appoint date of commencement, approve establishment of centres/laboratories, approve disposal of property, approve borrowing of money, declare Provident Funds Act applicable, make orders to remove difficulties, cause annual report/accounts to be laid before Parliament.

Registrar: To take disciplinary action against specified employees (excluding teachers/academic staff), enter into agreements, sign documents, authenticate records, be custodian of records/seal/property, issue notices, keep minutes, conduct official correspondence, supply information to Visitor, represent University in suits.

Finance Officer: To exercise general supervision over funds, advise on financial policy, manage property and investments, ensure expenditure limits are not exceeded, prepare annual accounts and budget, watch cash/bank balances and investments, watch revenue collection, ensure maintenance of registers, report unauthorised expenditure/financial irregularities.

Academic Council: To coordinate and exercise general supervision over academic policies, give directions regarding instruction methods, evaluation, and academic standards, promote inter-School coordination, establish committees, consider academic matters, frame Regulations and rules regarding academic functioning.
College Development Council: To admit Colleges to the privileges of the University.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for disciplinary actions against employees for misconduct, including suspension, censure, withholding increment, and removal from service (Statute 26). For students, disciplinary actions include removal from rolls, debarment from examinations, fines, expulsion, or rustication (Section 36, Statute 29). Disputes related to employee contracts and student disciplinary actions can be referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Visitor: Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, first Registrar, first Finance Officer, members of the first Court, Executive Council, College Development Council, and Academic Council. Executive Council: Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, Librarian, teachers, academic staff, administrative staff, Proctor. Vice-Chancellor: Deans of Schools.

applies_to: Educational institutions within the State of Sikkim
Persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class
Employees of the University
Students of the University
exemptions: Educational institutions within the State of Sikkim specified by the Central Government order from the restriction of associating with other universities
Special provisions for employment or admission of women, persons with disabilities, or persons belonging to weaker sections of society, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
special_provisions: Special provisions for employment or admission of women, persons with disabilities, or persons belonging to weaker sections of society, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Section 7 proviso)
Transitional provisions for the appointment of first officers and constitution of initial authorities for a specified term (Section 46).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Statutes: Executive Council (with Visitor's assent), Visitor. Ordinances: Vice-Chancellor (first Ordinances with Central Government approval), Executive Council. Regulations: Authorities of the University.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor has powers to review, inspect, inquire, issue directions, and annul proceedings. The Vice-Chancellor is responsible for ensuring the observance of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations. The Executive Council manages and administers the University's affairs. Disputes concerning employee contracts and student disciplinary actions are resolved through a Tribunal of Arbitration.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Civil courts are generally excluded for matters decided by the Tribunal of Arbitration, but employees retain the right to avail judicial remedies under Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution (Supreme Court and High Courts).

schedules_summary.description: Contains the initial Statutes of the University, detailing the constitution, powers, and functions of various officers and authorities like the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Deans, Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, Librarian, Executive Council, Academic Council, Finance Committee, and Selection Committees. It also covers terms and conditions of service, removal of employees, honorary degrees, withdrawal of degrees, maintenance of discipline, admission of colleges, and procedures for making Ordinances and Regulations.

act_identification.act_title: THE SPORTS BROADCASTING SIGNALS (MANDATORY SHARING WITH PRASAR BHARATI) ACT, 2007
act_identification.act_short_title: The Sports Broadcasting Signals (Mandatory Sharing with Prasar Bharati) Act, 2007

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide access to the largest number of listeners and viewers, on a free to air basis, of sporting events of national importance through mandatory sharing of sports broadcasting signals with Prasar Bharati and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to ensure that a wide audience can access sporting events of national importance on a free-to-air basis. It achieves this by mandating the sharing of sports broadcasting signals with Prasar Bharati, along with related provisions.

chapter_titles: MANDATORY SHARING OF SPORTS BROADCASTING SIGNALS WITH PRASAR BHARATI
POWERS OF THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT TO ISSUE GUIDELINES

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its application to the whole of India, and its deemed commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'broadcaster', 'broadcasting', 'Prasar Bharati', and 'sporting events of national importance'.

key_sections.title: Mandatory sharing of certain sports broadcasting signals.
key_sections.description: Mandates content rights owners and broadcasters to share live broadcasting signals of national importance sporting events with Prasar Bharati, including revenue sharing terms.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to specify penalties, including licence suspension or revocation, for violations, with a pecuniary penalty limit of one crore rupees.

key_sections.title: Power of the Central Government to issue Guidelines.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to issue Guidelines for mandatory sharing of broadcasting signals with Prasar Bharati.

key_sections.title: Validation.
key_sections.description: Validates previously issued Guidelines for Downlinking and Uplinking of Television Channels regarding mandatory sharing of sports broadcasting signals.

key_sections.title: Power of the Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act.

key_sections.title: Rules and Guidelines to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Requires all rules and Guidelines made under the Act to be laid before each House of Parliament for review and potential modification or annulment.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Sports Broadcasting Signals (Mandatory Sharing with Prasar Bharati) Ordinance, 2007, while saving actions taken under it.

powers_conferred: Power of the Central Government to issue Guidelines (Section 5)
Power of the Central Government to make rules (Section 7)
Power of the Central Government to specify penalties (Section 4)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Central Government may specify penalties, including suspension or revocation of licence, permission or registration, for violation of terms and conditions under section 3. Pecuniary penalty shall not exceed one crore rupees. No penalty shall be imposed without giving a reasonable opportunity. No act or omission between 11th November, 2005 and the promulgation of the Sports Broadcasting Signals (Mandatory Sharing with Prasar Bharati) Ordinance, 2007, shall be subjected to penalties.

repealed_acts: The Sports Broadcasting Signals (Mandatory Sharing with Prasar Bharati) Ordinance, 2007 (Ord. 4 of 2007)
related_acts: Prasar Bharati (Broadcasting Corporation of India) Act, 1990
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997

applies_to: content rights owner or holder
television or radio broadcasting service provider
exemptions: No act or omission on the part of any person after the 11th November, 2005 and before the date of promulgation of the Sports Broadcasting Signals (Mandatory Sharing with Prasar Bharati) Ordinance, 2007 (Ord. 4 of 2007) shall be subjected to penalties.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Through the issuance of Guidelines by the Central Government, specification of terms and conditions for signal sharing, and imposition of penalties for violations, including licence suspension or revocation.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL RURAL EMPLOYMENT GUARANTEE (EXTENSION TO JAMMU AND KASHMIR) ACT, 2007
act_identification.act_short_title: National Rural Employment Guarantee (Extension to Jammu and Kashmir) Act, 2007

legislative_details.geographical_extent: State of Jammu and Kashmir, Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the extension of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 to the State of Jammu and Kashmir*.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to extend the provisions of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, along with all its rules, orders, and schemes, to the State of Jammu and Kashmir. It also amends the principal Act to remove the exclusion of Jammu and Kashmir.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government, with different dates possible for different areas.

key_sections.title: Extension and amendment of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005.
key_sections.description: Extends the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, and its associated rules, orders, and schemes to the State of Jammu and Kashmir, and amends Section 1(2) of the principal Act to omit the exclusion of Jammu and Kashmir.

key_sections.title: Construction of reference to a law not in force in Jammu and Kashmir.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that any reference in the principal Act to a law not in force in Jammu and Kashmir shall be construed as a reference to the corresponding law in force in that State.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint the date of commencement of the Act by notification in the Official Gazette.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government

applies_to: State of Jammu and Kashmir
Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir
Union territory of Ladakh
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different areas in the State for the commencement of the Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF TECHNOLOGY, SCIENCE EDUCATION AND RESEARCH ACT, 2007
act_identification.act_short_title: National Institutes of Technology, Science Education and Research Act, 2007

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Human Resource Development
legislative_details.geographical_extent: Institutions of national importance listed in the First, Second and Third Schedules

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare [1][certain institutions of technology, science education and research] to be Institutions of national importance and to provide for instructions and research in branches of engineering, technology, management, education, sciences and arts and for the advancement of learning and dissemination of knowledge in such branches and for certain other matters connected with such institutions.
act_overview.purpose: To declare certain institutions of technology, science education and research as Institutions of national importance. It aims to provide for instruction and research in various branches like engineering, technology, management, education, sciences, and arts, and for the advancement and dissemination of knowledge in these fields.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Declaration of certain Institutions as Institutions of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares institutions mentioned in the Schedules as Institutions of national importance.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of Institutes.
key_sections.description: Establishes each Institute as a body corporate with perpetual succession and common seal.

key_sections.title: Effect of incorporation of Institutes.
key_sections.description: Outlines the legal consequences of incorporation, including vesting of property, transfer of liabilities, and employee terms.

key_sections.title: Powers of Institutes.
key_sections.description: Details the powers and duties of the Institutes, such as providing instruction, granting degrees, and managing property.

key_sections.title: Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of every Institute and outlines the Visitor's powers.

key_sections.title: Board of Governors.
key_sections.description: Specifies the composition of the Board of Governors for Institutes mentioned in the First Schedule.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Board.

key_sections.title: Senate.

key_sections.title: Grants by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Provides for financial grants from the Central Government to Institutes.

key_sections.title: Statutes.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Council.

key_sections.title: Functions of Council.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.

powers_conferred: Institutes: To provide for instruction and research, hold examinations and grant degrees, confer honorary degrees, fix fees, establish and manage halls and hostels, supervise and control students, maintain National Cadet Corps units, institute academic posts, frame Statutes and Ordinances, deal with property, receive gifts and grants, cooperate with other institutions, institute fellowships and scholarships, undertake consultancy.

Central Government: To make rules to carry out the purposes of Chapter III.

National Institutes of Technology, Science Education and Research (Amendment) Act, 2014 (9 of 2014)

Chairperson nominates members to the Senate. Senate nominates professor/assistant professor to the Board.

All India Council for Technical Education

act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to make provisions for the development and regulation of warehouses, facilitate the negotiability of warehouse receipts, and establish a Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority to oversee these functions and related matters.

chapter_titles: THE WAREHOUSING DEVELOPMENT AND REGULATORY AUTHORITY

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Requirement of registration for warehouses issuing negotiable warehouse receipts.

key_sections.title: Liabilities of warehousemen.
