key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority as a body corporate.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Authority.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the powers and functions of the Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority, including regulation and promotion of warehousing business.

key_sections.title: Offences and penalties.
key_sections.description: Defines various offences related to warehousing business and warehouse receipts, prescribing penalties including imprisonment and fines.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government authority to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of Authority to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Authority power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the Act's provisions shall prevail over anything inconsistent in any other law.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Act 2 of 1899.
key_sections.description: Amends the Stamp Act, 1899, to exempt negotiable warehouse receipts from stamp duty.

powers_conferred: Central Government to issue directions to the Authority (Section 40)
Central Government to supersede the Authority (Section 41)
Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act (Section 50)
Central Government to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act (Section 54)
Authority to issue, renew, modify, withdraw, suspend or cancel registration certificates for warehouses (Section 35(2)(a))
Authority to regulate the registration and functioning of accreditation agencies (Section 35(2)(b))
Authority to regulate the process of pledge, creation of charges and enforcement thereof in respect of goods deposited (Section 35(2)(d))
Authority to make regulations (Section 51)
Authority to appoint officers and other employees (Section 33)
Authority to delegate powers (Section 48)
Warehouseman to deal with perishable and hazardous goods (Section 9)
Warehouseman to sell goods by public auction or other specified manner to recover lien (Section 10(5))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 43 defines offences such as knowingly issuing a negotiable warehouse receipt without actual physical delivery of goods, issuing duplicate negotiable warehouse receipts without proper procedure, delivering goods when a negotiable warehouse receipt is outstanding, failing to deliver goods upon surrender of receipt and payment of charges, and depositors declaring false value of goods. Penalties include imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and/or fines which may extend to four times the value of the goods or one lakh rupees, depending on the offence.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson and other members of the Authority (Section 25). The Authority appoints its officers and other employees (Section 33).

applies_to: Persons carrying on warehousing business
Warehousemen
Accreditation agencies
Depositors
Holders of warehouse receipts
exemptions: Warehouses which do not propose to issue negotiable warehouse receipts (Section 3)
The Authority from tax on wealth and income (Section 49)
special_provisions: The Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh by notification (Footnote to Section 1(2)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Authority regulates warehousing business, registers warehousemen and accreditation agencies, specifies standards, and conducts inspections and enquiries. Offences are punishable with imprisonment and fines, with cognizance taken by specific courts upon a complaint made by the Authority or an authorized officer.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class (Section 45(2))

act_identification.act_title: THE CARRIAGE BY ROAD ACT, 2007

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Fifty-eighth Year of the Republic of India
legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry or Department of the Central Government dealing with road transport and highways
legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India, except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the regulation of common carriers, limiting their liability and declaration of value of goods delivered to them to determine their liability for loss of, or damage to, such goods occasioned by the negligence or criminal acts of themselves, their servants or agents and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate common carriers operating on roads, defining and limiting their liability for loss or damage to goods. It establishes a framework for registration, declaration of goods' value, and addresses issues arising from negligence or criminal acts of carriers, their servants, or agents.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application, and the date it comes into force.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'common carrier', 'consignee', and 'consignment'.

key_sections.title: Persons not to engage in business of common carrier without registration.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration for persons engaged in the business of a common carrier after the Act's commencement.

key_sections.title: Application for grant or renewal of registration.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for applying for and renewing a certificate of registration for common carriers.

key_sections.title: Suspension or cancellation of registration.
key_sections.description: Details the conditions and procedures under which a common carrier's registration may be suspended or cancelled.

key_sections.title: Goods receipt.
key_sections.description: Requires common carriers to issue a goods receipt upon acceptance of goods, serving as prima facie evidence of particulars.

key_sections.title: Liability of common carrier.
key_sections.description: Limits the liability of common carriers for loss or damage to consignments, unless a higher risk rate is agreed upon.

key_sections.title: Provision for carriage of goods of dangerous or hazardous nature to human life.
key_sections.description: Regulates the carriage of dangerous or hazardous goods, requiring specific procedures, safeguards, and insurance.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to prohibit carriage of certain class of goods.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to prohibit the carriage of specific goods or classes of goods in public interest.

key_sections.title: General responsibility of common carrier.
key_sections.description: Defines the general responsibility of common carriers for loss, destruction, damage, or non-delivery, with specified exceptions.

key_sections.title: Punishment for contravention in relation to non-registration, carrying goods of dangerous or hazardous nature, or prohibited goods.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contraventions related to registration, carriage of dangerous goods, or prohibited goods.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Carriers Act, 1865, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under the repealed Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to appoint commencement date (Section 1(3))
Central Government: to specify goods of dangerous or hazardous nature and labels (Section 13(2))
Central Government: to prohibit carriage of certain class of goods (Section 14)
Central Government: to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act (Section 20)
Central Government: to remove difficulties by order (Section 21)
Registering authority: to grant or renew certificate of registration (Section 4(5))
Registering authority: to grant or refuse permission for shifting main office (Section 4(7)(b))
Registering authority: to suspend or cancel registration (Section 5)
State Government: to specify officers or authorities for compounding offences (Section 19(1))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever contravenes the provisions of section 3 (non-registration), section 13 (carrying dangerous/hazardous goods), or a notification issued under section 14 (prohibited goods) shall be punishable for the first offence with a fine up to five thousand rupees, and for the second or subsequent offence with a fine up to ten thousand rupees. Companies and their responsible officers can also be held liable.

repealed_acts: The Carriers Act, 1865 (3 of 1865)

regulatory_bodies: Transport Research Wing of the Ministry or Department of the Central Government dealing with road transport and highways

applies_to: persons engaged in the business of a common carrier
consignor
consignee
exemptions: Government (from the definition of common carrier)
special_provisions: The Act extends to the whole of India, except the State of Jammu and Kashmir (as per Section 1(2) before amendment).
Vide notification No. S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019, this Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Requires registration of common carriers; provides for suspension or cancellation of registration; prescribes penalties for contraventions; allows for compounding of offences.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL CAPITAL TERRITORY OF DELHI LAWS (SPECIAL PROVISIONS) ACT, 2007
act_identification.act_short_title: The National Capital Territory of Delhi Laws (Special Provisions) Act, 2007

act_overview.purpose: This Act makes special provisions for the National Capital Territory of Delhi for a further period up to 31st December, 2008. Its main purpose is to provide temporary relief and minimise hardships to the people of Delhi against punitive action for encroachment or unauthorised developments, allowing the Central Government time to finalise relevant policies and strategies.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, commencement and duration.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Act's name, geographical reach, effective date, and expiry date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Enforcement to be kept in abeyance.
key_sections.description: Directs the Central Government to finalise policies and mandates a status quo, suspending punitive actions against certain unauthorised developments until 31st December, 2008.

key_sections.title: Provisions of this Act not to apply in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Specifies exceptions where the relief provided by Section 3 does not apply.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to give directions.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government authority to issue directions to local authorities for implementing the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals a previous Ordinance and includes savings provisions for actions taken under it.

powers_conferred: Power of Central Government to give directions to local authorities (Section 5)
Power of Central Government to withdraw exemption by notification (Section 3(4))

repealed_acts: The National Capital Territory of Delhi Laws (Special Provisions) Second Ordinance, 2007 (Ord.7 of 2007)
related_acts: New Delhi Municipal Council Act, 1994 (44 of 1994)
National Capital Territory of Delhi Laws (Special Provisions) Ordinance, 2007 (Ord. 6 of 2007)

applies_to: National Capital Territory of Delhi
Slum dwellers and Jhuggi-Jhompri clusters
Hawkers and urban street vendors
Unauthorised colonies, village abadi area and its extension
Existing farm houses involving construction beyond permissible building limits

Schools, dispensaries, religious institutions, cultural institutions, storages, warehouses and godowns used for agricultural inputs or produce (including dairy and poultry) in rural areas built on agricultural land
exemptions: Encroachment on public land except in cases covered under clauses (a), (b) and (c) of sub-section (1) of section 3

Removal of slums and Jhuggi-Jhompri dwellers, hawkers and urban street vendors, unauthorised colonies or part thereof, village abadi area and its extension, in accordance with relevant policies approved by the Central Government for clearance of land required for specific public projects
special_provisions: Maintenance of status quo as on 1st January, 2006, for encroachment or unauthorised development.
Maintenance of status quo for unauthorised colonies, village abadi area and its extension, which existed on 31st March, 2002, and where construction took place up to 8th February, 2007.
Suspension of all notices for punitive action against encroachment or unauthorised development until 31st December, 2008.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Central Government is to finalise norms, policy guidelines, and feasible strategies. Local authorities are to comply with directions from the Central Government. Punitive actions are kept in abeyance for a specified period.

act_identification.act_title: THE TYRE CORPORATION OF INDIA LIMITED (DISINVESTMENT OF OWNERSHIP) ACT, 2007
act_identification.act_short_title: The Tyre Corporation of India Limited (Disinvestment of Ownership) Act, 2007

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for disinvestment of Government's equity in the Tyre Corporation of India Limited and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS the Inchek Tyres Limited and the National Rubber Manufacturers Limited, engaged in the manufacture, production and distribution of articles mentioned in the First Schedule to the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951, namely, tyres, tubes and other rubber goods, were nationalised under the Inchek Tyres Limited and National Rubber Manufacturers Limited (Nationalisation) Act, 1984 and transferred to, and vested in, the Tyre Corporation of India Limited, Calcutta from the 5th day of March, 1984; AND WHEREAS for the purpose of securing optimum utilisation of the available facilities for the manufacture, production and distribution of tyres, tubes and other rubber goods, investment of large amount is necessary; AND WHEREAS it is expedient to disinvest the Government's equity in the Tyre Corporation of India Limited, Kolkata to enable the private sector to have investment made to ensure that the interest of general public are served by the continuance of the manufacture, production and distribution of the aforesaid articles which are essential to the needs of the economy of the country. BE it enacted by Parliament in the Fifty-eighth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the disinvestment of the Government's equity in the Tyre Corporation of India Limited. Its objective is to secure optimum utilisation of facilities and ensure continued manufacture, production, and distribution of essential rubber goods by enabling private sector investment.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as The Tyre Corporation of India Limited (Disinvestment of Ownership) Act, 2007.

key_sections.title: Disinvestment in the company.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to order disinvestment of shares in the Tyre Corporation of India Limited based on recommendations from the Board for Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprises.

key_sections.title: Payment of consideration for disinvestment in the company.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that consideration for the transfer of shares shall be given to the Central Government, determined by optimum valuation of assets and liabilities.

key_sections.title: Manner of disinvestment.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to specify methods for disinvestment, including public offer, preferential allotment, or private placement.

key_sections.title: Provision in respect of officers and other employees of the company.
key_sections.description: Ensures continuity of employment for officers and employees (excluding Chairman and Directors) for three years post-disinvestment, with an option to resign.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in the Inchek Tyres Limited and National Rubber Manufactures, Limited (Nationalisation) Act, 1984 or any other law.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To pass an order providing for transfer, exchange or relinquishment of shares in the company (Section 2).
Central Government: To specify the valuation method for consideration (Section 3).
Central Government: To specify the methods of disinvestment of shares (Section 4).

related_acts: Inchek Tyres Limited and National Rubber Manufacturers Limited (Nationalisation) Act, 1984 (17 of 1984)

regulatory_bodies: Board for Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprises

applies_to: Tyre Corporation of India Limited
Officers and other employees of the company
Any person or company acquiring shares

act_identification.act_title: THE PAYMENT AND SETTLEMENT SYSTEMS ACT, 2007
act_identification.act_short_title: The Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the regulation and supervision of payment systems in India and to designate the Reserve Bank of India as the authority for that purpose and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: To regulate and supervise payment systems in India and to designate the Reserve Bank of India as the authority for this purpose, along with addressing related and incidental matters.

chapter_titles: REGULATION AND SUPERVISION BY THE RESERVE BANK
RIGHTS AND DUTIES OF A SYSTEM PROVIDER

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its applicability to the whole of India, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Designated authority.
key_sections.description: Designates the Reserve Bank as the authority for regulation and supervision of payment systems and establishes the Payments Regulatory Board.

key_sections.title: Payment system not to operate without authorisation.
key_sections.description: Mandates that no person, other than the Reserve Bank, can operate a payment system without authorisation, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Issue or refusal of authorisation.
key_sections.description: Outlines the conditions and considerations for the Reserve Bank to issue or refuse an authorisation for operating a payment system.

key_sections.title: Revocation of authorisation.
key_sections.description: Details the grounds and procedure for the Reserve Bank to revoke an authorisation given to a system provider.

key_sections.title: Power to determine standards.
key_sections.description: Grants the Reserve Bank power to prescribe standards for payment instructions, timings, transfer methods, membership criteria, and participant rights/obligations.

key_sections.title: Bank, etc., not to impose charge for using electronic modes of payment.
key_sections.description: Prohibits banks or system providers from imposing charges for using prescribed electronic modes of payment.

key_sections.title: Power to issue directions.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Reserve Bank to issue directions to payment systems or participants to address systemic risk or impact on monetary/credit policy.

key_sections.title: Settlement and netting.
key_sections.description: Governs the determination of payment obligations and settlement instructions, including the finality and irrevocability of settlements.

key_sections.title: Protection of funds collected from customers.
key_sections.description: Allows the Reserve Bank to require system providers to protect customer funds by depositing them in separate accounts or maintaining liquid assets.

key_sections.title: Dishonour of electronic funds transfer for insufficiency, etc., of funds in the account.
key_sections.description: Defines the offence of dishonouring electronic funds transfers due to insufficient funds and prescribes penalties.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Specifies various penalties for contraventions of the Act, including operating without authorisation, making false statements, and non-compliance with directions.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply to stock exchanges or clearing corporations of stock exchanges.
key_sections.description: Exempts stock exchanges and their clearing corporations from the applicability of this Act.

key_sections.title: Power of Reserve Bank to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Reserve Bank the power to make regulations to carry out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Reserve Bank: to determine standards (Section 10)
Reserve Bank: to call for returns, documents or other information (Section 12)
Reserve Bank: to access information (Section 13)
Reserve Bank: to enter and inspect (Section 14)
Reserve Bank: to carry out audit and inspection (Section 16)
Reserve Bank: to issue directions (Section 17, Section 18)
Reserve Bank: to impose penalties (Section 30)
Reserve Bank: to make regulations (Section 38)
Central Government: to appoint commencement date (Section 1(3))
Central Government: to hear appeals against refusal or revocation of authorisation (Section 9)
Central Government: to remove difficulties (Section 37)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Operating a payment system without authorisation or non-compliance with conditions (Section 26(1)) is punishable with imprisonment (1 month to 10 years) or fine (up to 1 crore rupees, with further fine of 1 lakh/day for continuing contravention) or both. Making false statements or omissions in applications/returns (Section 26(2)) is punishable with imprisonment (up to 3 years) and fine (10 lakh to 50 lakh rupees). Failure to produce information/returns (Section 26(3)) or general contravention/default (Section 26(6)) is liable to penalty under Section 30. Disclosure of confidential information (Section 26(4)) is punishable with imprisonment (up to 6 months) or fine (up to 5 lakh rupees or twice damages) or both. Non-compliance with directions or non-payment of penalty (Section 26(5)) is punishable with imprisonment (1 month to 10 years) or fine (up to 1 crore rupees, with further fine of 1 lakh/day for continuing contravention) or both. Dishonour of electronic funds transfer for insufficiency of funds (Section 25) is an offence punishable with imprisonment (up to 2 years) or fine (up to twice the amount) or both.

related_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government nominates three members to the Payments Regulatory Board. The Central Board of the Reserve Bank nominates one officer to the Payments Regulatory Board.

applies_to: Payment systems in India
Designated trade repository
Issuer
exemptions: Existing payment systems for a period not exceeding six months from commencement, if applying for authorisation
Any person acting as the duly appointed agent of another person to whom the payment is due
A company accepting payments either from its holding company or any of its subsidiary companies or from any other company which is also a subsidiary of the same holding company
Any other person whom the Reserve Bank may, by notification, exempt
Stock exchanges or the clearing corporations of the stock exchanges
International Financial Services Centre set up under sub-section (1) of section 18 of the Special Economic Zones Act, 2005
special_provisions: Not less than fifty-one per cent. of the equity of a company or corporation authorised to operate or regulate clearing houses shall be held by public sector banks.
The Act applies to a designated trade repository or issuer with specific modifications regarding references to 'payment system'/'system provider' and 'commencement of this Act'.
Powers of Reserve Bank do not apply to an International Financial Services Centre, where they are exercisable by the International Financial Services Centres Authority.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Reserve Bank has the power to make regulations. The Central Government has the power to make orders to remove difficulties.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the Reserve Bank's powers of authorisation, regulation, supervision, inspection, audit, and issuance of directions. Contraventions are subject to penalties, and disputes are settled through specified mechanisms. Penalties can be recovered by the Reserve Bank.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class for offences under the Act. Principal civil court for recovery of penalty.

act_identification.act_title: An Act to provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed force of the Union for ensuring the security of the borders of India and for matters connected therewith.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: any part of India as well as outside India. This Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the constitution and regulation of an armed force of the Union for ensuring the security of the borders of India and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the establishment and governance of the Sashastra Seema Bal, an armed force of the Union. Its primary objective is to ensure the security of India's borders and to address all related matters concerning its constitution, service conditions, discipline, and legal framework.
act_overview.act_category: Defence of India and Armed Forces

chapter_titles: CONSTITUTION OF THE FORCE AND CONDITIONS OF SERVICE OF THE MEMBERS OF THE FORCE
EXECUTION OF SENTENCES, PARDONS, REMISSIONS, ETC.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Persons subject to this Act.
key_sections.description: Specifies who is subject to the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Constitution of the Force.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Sashastra Seema Bal as an armed force of the Union and outlines its purpose.

key_sections.title: Restrictions respecting right to form association, freedom of speech, etc.
key_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on members of the Force regarding associations, speech, and publications.

key_sections.title: Offences in relation to enemy and punishable with death.
key_sections.description: Details severe offences related to the enemy, punishable by death.

key_sections.title: Mutiny.
key_sections.description: Defines mutiny-related offences and their severe penalties.

key_sections.title: Civil offences.
key_sections.description: Addresses the trial of civil offences by Force Courts, subject to certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Punishment by Force Courts.
key_sections.description: Lists the scale of punishments that can be inflicted by Force Courts.

key_sections.title: Kinds of Force Courts.
key_sections.description: Categorizes the types of Force Courts established under the Act.

key_sections.title: Powers of a General Force Court.
key_sections.description: Outlines the powers of a General Force Court to try offences and pass sentences.

key_sections.title: Choice between criminal court and Force Court.
key_sections.description: Determines the discretion of senior officers in deciding whether an offence is tried by a criminal court or a Force Court.

key_sections.title: General rule as to evidence.
key_sections.description: States that the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, applies to Force Court proceedings.

key_sections.title: Pardon and remission.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to the Central Government and other authorities to pardon, remit, or commute sentences.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power on the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions.

powers_conferred: Central Government: General superintendence, direction and control of the Force (Section 5); appoint Director-General and other officers (Section 5); dismiss or remove from service (Section 10); sanction for associations/speech (Section 13); order detention of lunatic accused (Section 111); confirm findings/sentences of General Force Courts (Section 122); pardon, remit, commute sentences (Section 142); suspend sentences (Section 144); make rules (Section 155); confer powers/duties on members of the Force (Section 153).

Director-General: Command and supervision of the Force (Section 5); assisted by other officers (Section 5); dismiss, remove, reduce in rank (Section 11); revise grievance decisions (Section 14); appoint Force Police (Section 75); convene General Force Courts (Section 77); decide choice between criminal court and Force Court (Section 92); pardon, remit, commute sentences (Section 142); suspend sentences (Section 144); annul proceedings (Section 132).
Inspector-General: Dismiss, remove, reduce in rank (Section 11); proceed against officers of or below Commandant rank (Section 58); decide choice between criminal court and Force Court (Section 92).

Commanding Officer: Duty in regard to detention (Section 70); make report for delay in Force Court (Section 71); give information of desertion (Section 73); appoint court of inquiry for absence (Section 74); hold Summary Force Court (Section 82); impose collective fines (Section 60).
Force Courts: Try offences and award punishments (Sections 84, 85, 86).
Presiding Officer of Force Court: Casting vote (Section 98); summon witnesses (Section 101).
Judge Attorney-General: Issue commission for examination of witnesses (Section 103).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines a wide range of offences, categorized into: Offences in relation to enemy (Sections 16, 17, 18); Mutiny (Section 19); Desertion and absence without leave (Sections 20, 21); Insubordination and obstruction (Sections 22, 23, 24); Conduct unbecoming (Sections 26, 27, 28, 29); Offences related to custody and property (Sections 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36); False accusations and falsifying documents (Sections 37, 38, 39, 41); Offences relating to Force Courts (Section 40); Miscellaneous offences (Sections 42, 43, 44); Attempt and Abetment (Sections 45, 46, 47, 48); Civil offences (Section 49). Penalties range from death, imprisonment (life or lesser terms), dismissal/removal from service, compulsory retirement, reduction in rank, forfeiture of seniority/pay/allowances, fines, severe reprimand, to stoppage of pay. Specific terms of imprisonment vary widely depending on the offence, from a few months to fourteen years or life.

related_acts: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974)
The National Security Guard Act, 1986 (47 of 1986)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints Director-General, Additional Directors-General, Inspectors-General, Deputy Inspectors-General, Additional Deputy Inspectors-General, Commandants and other officers (Section 5). Director-General or any prescribed officer appoints Force Police (Section 75). Judge Attorney-General or officer authorised by him approves officers to attend Force Court (Section 95).

applies_to: officers and subordinate officer
under-officers and other persons enrolled under this Act
Every person subject to this Act shall remain so subject until repatriated, retired, released, discharged, removed or dismissed from the Force
any person subject to this Act who commits any civil offence
exemptions: A person subject to this Act who commits an offence of murder or culpable homicide not amounting to murder against, or of rape in relation to, a person not subject to this Act shall not be deemed to be guilty of an offence under this Act and shall not be tried by a Force Court, unless he commits any of the said offences— (a) while on active duty; or (b) at any place outside India; or (c) at any place specified by the Central Government by notification, in this behalf.
special_provisions: In this Act, references to any law not in force in the State of Jammu and Kashmir* shall be construed as references to the corresponding law in force in that State.
This Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government may, by notification, make rules for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of this Act.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement involves Force custody and detention, trials by various Force Courts, confirmation and revision of proceedings, and execution of sentences including death, imprisonment, and fines. It also includes provisions for pardon, remission, and suspension of sentences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Force Courts (General, Petty, Summary) and Criminal Courts.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIRA GANDHI NATIONAL TRIBAL UNIVERSITY ACT, 2007
act_identification.act_short_title: the Indira Gandhi National Tribal University Act, 2007

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University at Amarkantak in the State of Madhya Pradesh to facilitate and promote avenues of higher education and research facilities for the tribal population in India and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Indira Gandhi National Tribal University to provide higher education and research facilities, primarily for the tribal population of India. It aims to disseminate knowledge in tribal art, culture, and related fields, and to promote the social, educational, and economic conditions of Scheduled Tribes.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act and its Statutes.

key_sections.title: Establishment of University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Indira Gandhi National Tribal University in Madhya Pradesh and outlines its headquarters and corporate status.

key_sections.title: Objects of University.
key_sections.description: Details the primary objectives of the University, focusing on higher education and research for tribal populations and related cultural studies.

key_sections.title: Powers of University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers of the University, including granting degrees, establishing centers, and making special provisions for Scheduled Tribes.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: States that the jurisdiction of the University extends to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: University open to all classes, castes and creed.
key_sections.description: Declares the University open to all persons regardless of sex, race, creed, caste, or class, with a proviso for special provisions for certain groups.

key_sections.title: The Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University and outlines the Visitor's powers of review, inspection, and direction.

key_sections.title: Officers of University.
key_sections.description: Lists the designated officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and Registrar.

key_sections.title: Authorities of University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities of the University, such as the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council.

key_sections.title: Power to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Grants the power to make Statutes and specifies the matters they may provide for.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Grants the power to make Ordinances and specifies the matters they may provide for.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees.
key_sections.description: Outlines conditions of service for employees, including provisions for arbitration in disputes.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act for a limited period.

key_sections.title: Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Mandates publication of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations in the Official Gazette and their presentation before Parliament.

powers_conferred: To provide for instruction in various branches of learning and for research and dissemination of knowledge.
To grant diplomas, certificates, degrees, or other academic distinctions.
To organise and undertake extra-mural studies, training, and extension services.
To confer honorary degrees.
To provide facilities through the distance education system.
To institute and appoint persons to Directorships, Principalships, Professorships, Readerships, Lecturerships, and other teaching/academic positions.
To recognise and withdraw recognition from institutions of higher learning.
To recognise persons for imparting instructions in Colleges or Institutions.
To appoint persons from other Universities/educational institutions as teachers for a specified period.
To create administrative, ministerial, and other posts and make appointments thereto.
To co-operate, collaborate, or associate with other Universities or institutions of higher learning.
To establish Campuses, special centres, specialised laboratories (with prior Central Government approval).
To institute and award fellowships, scholarships, studentships, medals, and prizes.
To establish and maintain Colleges, Institutions, and Halls.
To make provision for research and advisory services and enter into arrangements with other institutions/organisations.
To organise and conduct refresher courses, workshops, seminars, and other programmes for academic staff.
To make special arrangements for the residence and teaching of women students.
To appoint visiting professors, Emeritus Professors, Consultants, Scholars.
To confer autonomous status on a College, Institution, or Department.
To admit Colleges and Institutions located in India to its privileges and withdraw them; to recognise, guide, supervise, and control Halls and other student accommodation.
To determine standards of admission to the University.
To demand and receive payment of fees and other charges.
To supervise student residences and promote their health and general welfare.
To lay down conditions of service of all categories of employees, including their code of conduct.
To regulate and enforce discipline among students and employees.
To make arrangements for promoting the health and general welfare of employees.
To receive benefactions, donations, gifts, and to acquire, hold, manage, and dispose of property (with previous Central Government approval for disposal).
To borrow money (with prior Central Government approval).
To establish Regional Centres in various tribal areas.
To make special provisions for the promotion of educational, economic interests, and welfare of Scheduled Tribes by providing adequate percentage of seats in admission and posts in employment.
To do all other acts necessary, incidental, or conducive to the attainment of its objects.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for disciplinary action against employees and students, including suspension, removal, debarment from examinations, and fines for students, and withdrawal of degrees or academic distinctions for good and sufficient cause. Specific criminal offences and penalties are not defined.

related_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 (5 of 1970)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980 (40 of 1980)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor, and an umpire for employee disputes. The Executive Council appoints Pro-Vice-Chancellors, Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, Librarian, teachers, academic staff, and administrative staff, often based on recommendations from Selection Committees. The Central Government appoints the first set of key officers and members of initial authorities.

applies_to: Tribal population of India (primarily)
Persons seeking higher education and research facilities in India
Students and employees of the University, its Colleges, and Institutions
Colleges and Institutions admitted to the privileges of the University
exemptions: Nothing in Section 7 prevents special provisions for employment or admission of women, persons with disabilities, weaker sections of society, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes.

Government-maintained Colleges and Institutions are exempt from certain conditions regarding Governing Body constitution, appointment of teaching staff/Principal, and service conditions of non-academic staff.
special_provisions: Special provisions for the promotion of educational, economic interests, and welfare of Scheduled Tribes by providing adequate percentage of seats in admission and posts in employment.

The Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, College Development Council, Boards of Studies, Academic Boards, Management Boards, Finance Committee, and other authorities shall have adequate number of members from amongst the Scheduled Tribes.
Special arrangements for the residence and teaching of women students.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Statutes are made by the Executive Council (with Visitor's assent) or directly by the Visitor. Ordinances are made by the Executive Council (on Academic Council's proposal) or the Vice-Chancellor (first Ordinances with Central Government approval). Regulations are made by the authorities of the University.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor has powers to review work, inspect, issue directions, and annul proceedings. The Vice-Chancellor exercises general supervision and control. The Executive Council manages and administers the University's affairs. Disputes between the University and employees are subject to arbitration. Disciplinary actions against students and employees have appeal mechanisms to the Executive Council.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Disputes arising from employee contracts are referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration, whose decision is final, precluding civil court suits, though judicial remedies under Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution are preserved. The Act does not specify other competent courts for general enforcement.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the initial Statutes of the University, detailing the appointment, powers, and duties of the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Deans of Faculties, Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, and Librarian. It also outlines the constitution, powers, and functions of the Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Finance Committee, Selection Committees, and provisions for the maintenance of discipline, admission of colleges, and other administrative matters.

act_identification.act_title: THE RAJIV GANDHI INSTITUTE OF PETROLEUM TECHNOLOGY ACT, 2007
act_identification.act_short_title: The Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology Act, 2007

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare the institution known as the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology to be an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act declares the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology as an institution of national importance. It provides for its incorporation as a body corporate and outlines its functions, powers, and governance structure. The Act aims to regulate the administration, academic activities, and financial management of the Institute.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Declaration of Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology as an institution of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology as an institution of national importance due to its objects.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Board', 'Director', 'Institute', 'General Council', and 'Statutes'.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of Institute.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Board of Governors.
key_sections.description: Details the composition and constitution of the Board of Governors, including the President, Director, and various nominated members.

key_sections.title: Functions of Institute.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary functions of the Institute, including promoting education and research in petroleum and hydrocarbons, granting degrees, and fostering industry interaction.

key_sections.title: Powers of Board.
key_sections.description: Confers powers upon the Board for general superintendence, direction, and control of the Institute's affairs, including policy decisions, framing Statutes, and establishing campuses.

key_sections.title: Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the Institute, with powers to review its work and issue directions.

key_sections.title: Establishment of General Council.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment and composition of the General Council, including ex officio members from various government and industry bodies.

key_sections.title: Grants by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to provide financial grants to the Institute for its efficient functioning.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Institute to maintain proper accounts and specifies that its accounts shall be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

key_sections.title: Statutes.
key_sections.description: Lists the matters for which Statutes may provide, such as formation of departments, classification of posts, and terms and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Tribunal of Arbitration.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Tribunal of Arbitration for resolving disputes arising out of contracts between the Institute and its employees, with its decisions being final.

key_sections.title: Grant of degrees, etc., by Institute.
key_sections.description: Confers power on the Institute to grant degrees and other academic distinctions, notwithstanding other laws like the University Grants Commission Act.

powers_conferred: Institute: Nurture and promote quality and excellence in education and research in petroleum and hydrocarbons (Section 9(i)).
Institute: Provide for programmes and courses of instruction and research leading to degrees (Section 9(ii)).
Institute: Grant degrees, diplomas, certificates or other academic distinctions (Section 9(iii)).
Institute: Confer honorary degrees and award fellowships, scholarships, prizes (Section 9(iv)).
Institute: Lay down standards of admission (Section 9(v)).
Institute: Fix, demand and receive fees and other charges (Section 9(vi)).
Institute: Manage academic and research programmes (Section 9(vii)).
Institute: Promote research and development for oil, gas and petrochemical industry (Section 9(viii)).
Institute: Foster close educational and research interaction (Section 9(ix)).
Institute: Co-operate with educational and research institutions (Section 9(x)).
Institute: Organise national and international symposia, seminars and conferences (Section 9(xi)).
Institute: Establish, maintain and manage halls, residences and hostels for students (Section 9(xii)).
Institute: Create academic, administrative, technical and other posts and make appointments (Section 9(xiii)).
Institute: Lay down conditions of service including code of conduct for teachers and employees (Section 9(xiv)).
Institute: Supervise, control and regulate discipline of employees and students (Section 9(xv), (xvi)).
Institute: Frame Statutes and Ordinances (Section 9(xvii)).
Institute: Deal with property belonging to or vested in it (Section 9(xviii)).
Institute: Receive gifts, grants, donations or benefactions (Section 9(xix)).
Institute: Borrow money for its purposes (Section 9(xx)).
Institute: Integrate new technology in the classroom (Section 9(xxi)).
Institute: Develop and maintain an information resource centre (Section 9(xxii)).
Institute: Provide for further education to working professionals (Section 9(xxiii)).
Board: General superintendence, direction and control of the affairs of the Institute (Section 10(1)).
Board: Take decisions on questions of policy (Section 10(2)(a)).
Board: Lay down policy regarding duration of courses, nomenclature of degrees (Section 10(2)(b)).
Board: Institute courses of study and lay down standards of proficiency (Section 10(2)(c)).
Board: Lay down policy regarding cadre structure, qualification, recruitment and conditions of service (Section 10(2)(d)).
Board: Guide resource mobilisation and lay down policies for investment (Section 10(2)(e)).
Board: Consider and approve proposals for taking loans (Section 10(2)(f)).
Board: Frame Statutes and alter, modify or rescind them (Section 10(2)(g)).
Board: Consider and pass resolutions on annual report, accounts and budget estimates (Section 10(2)(h)).
Board: Appoint committees (Section 10(3)).
Board: Establish campus and academic centres at any place within or outside India (with Central Government approval for outside India) (Section 10(4)).
Board: Delegate any of its powers and duties (Section 10(6)).
Visitor (President of India): Appoint persons to review work and hold inquiries (Section 13(2)).
Visitor: Issue directions based on reports, which the Institute is bound to comply with (Section 13(3)).
General Council: Review broad policies and programmes of the Institute and suggest improvements (Section 16(a)).
General Council: Consider annual statement of accounts and audit report (Section 16(b)).
General Council: Review and evaluate overall quality and effectiveness of the Institute (Section 16(c)).
General Council: Advise the Institute and its Board on advanced technology and other matters (Section 16(e)).
Senate: Control and general regulation, and responsibility for maintenance of standards of instruction, education and examination (Section 18).
Central Government: Appoint the date of commencement of the Act (Section 1(2)).
Central Government: Constitute the Board of Governors (Section 5(1)).
Central Government: Appoint the President of the Board (Section 5(1)(a)).
Central Government: Appoint the Director of the Institute (Section 20(1)).
Central Government: Pay grants to the Institute (Section 23).
Central Government: Frame the first Statutes of the Institute (Section 30(1)).
Central Government: Remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act (Section 38(1)).

authorities_established: Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints the President of the Board, the Director, and certain members of the Board. The General Council nominates eminent experts to the Board and persons representing private entities to the General Council. The Senate nominates Professors of the Institute to the Board. The Executive Committee of the Alumni Association nominates a representative of graduates to the Board. The Board appoints academic staff (Assistant Professor or above) and non-academic staff of equivalent pay scale. The Director appoints other staff. The Visitor appoints an umpire for the Tribunal of Arbitration.

applies_to: Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Petroleum Technology
Board of Governors
General Council
Senate
Employees of the Institute
Students of the Institute
special_provisions: Provisions for the appointment of the first President of the Board for a limited period (Section 5(1)(a) Proviso).
Provisions for the terms of employment for existing employees of the Society upon incorporation of the Institute (Section 8(c) Proviso).
Requirement for prior approval of the Central Government for establishing a campus or academic centre outside India (Section 10(4) Proviso).
Requirement for prior approval of the Central Government for disposing of immovable property of the Institute (Section 10(5)).
Provisions for the appointment of the first Director for a limited period (Section 20(1) Proviso).
Provisions for the transfer of unutilised funds from sponsored schemes to the endowment fund (Section 37 Proviso).
Power of the Central Government to remove difficulties for a period of two years from the appointed day (Section 38(1) Proviso).
Transitional provisions for the continuation of the existing Board of Governors and the Statutes and Ordinances of the Society until new ones are constituted/made under this Act (Section 39).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government frames the first Statutes and can issue orders to remove difficulties. The Board has the power to make new or additional Statutes, or amend/repeal existing ones, subject to General Council approval. The Senate makes Ordinances, subject to Board review. The authorities of the Institute may have their own rules of procedure.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act establishes a governance structure including the Board of Governors, General Council, Senate, Director, and Registrar, each with defined powers and duties to administer the Institute. Financial accounts are subject to audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India. Disputes between the Institute and its employees are resolved by a Tribunal of Arbitration.

act_identification.act_title: THE ARMED FORCES TRIBUNAL ACT, 2007

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the adjudication or trial by Armed Forces Tribunal of disputes and complaints with respect to commission, appointments, enrolment and conditions of service in respect of persons subject to the Army Act, 1950, the Navy Act, 1957 and the Air Force Act, 1950 and also to provide for appeals arising out of orders, findings or sentences of court martial held under the said Acts and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes an Armed Forces Tribunal to adjudicate disputes and complaints concerning commission, appointments, enrolment, and conditions of service for personnel subject to the Army, Navy, and Air Force Acts. It also provides a mechanism for appeals against orders, findings, or sentences issued by court martials under these Acts.

chapter_titles: ESTABLISHMENT OF TRIBUNAL AND BENCHES THEREOF
JURISDICTION, POWERS AND AUTHORITY OF THE TRIBUNAL

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Applicability of the Act.
key_sections.description: Defines to whom the provisions of the Act apply, including serving and retired personnel of the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used within the Act, such as 'service matters' and 'court martial'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Armed Forces Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to establish the Armed Forces Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction, powers and authority in service matters.
key_sections.description: Outlines the Tribunal's jurisdiction, powers, and authority over service matters, excluding certain courts and granting powers similar to a Civil Court.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction, powers and authority in matters of appeal against court martial.
key_sections.description: Details the Tribunal's jurisdiction and powers to hear appeals against orders, decisions, findings, or sentences of court martials, including powers to grant bail and modify sentences.

key_sections.title: Power to punish for contempt.
key_sections.description: Grants the Tribunal the power to punish individuals for contempt, with provisions similar to the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971.

key_sections.title: Application not to be admitted unless other remedies exhausted.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that applications to the Tribunal generally require exhaustion of other available remedies under the respective service Acts.

key_sections.title: Procedure and powers of the Tribunal.
key_sections.description: States that the Tribunal is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure but is guided by natural justice, and can regulate its own procedure.

key_sections.title: Appeal to Supreme Court.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals to the Supreme Court against final decisions or orders of the Tribunal, with specific time limits.

key_sections.title: Exclusion of jurisdiction of civil courts.
key_sections.description: Excludes the jurisdiction of civil courts in relation to service matters once the Tribunal's jurisdiction commences.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in any other law.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Tribunal to exercise jurisdiction, powers and authority in service matters (Section 14).
Tribunal to exercise jurisdiction, powers and authority in appeals against court martial (Section 15).
Tribunal to grant bail to accused persons in military custody (Section 15(3)).
Tribunal to substitute findings, remit, mitigate, commute, or enhance sentences, release on parole, or suspend sentences (Section 15(6)).
Tribunal to quash conviction and order re-trial (Section 16).
Tribunal to order production of documents, attendance of witnesses, receive evidence, obtain reports, order reference for inquiry, appoint assessors, and determine necessary questions (Section 17).
Tribunal to punish for contempt (Section 19).
Tribunal to lay down and regulate its own procedure (Section 23).
Chairperson to transfer Members, issue general or special orders for Benches, and exercise financial and administrative powers (Section 5(3), Section 12, Section 27).
Central Government to establish the Tribunal, appoint Members, determine staff, make rules, and remove difficulties (Section 4, Section 7, Section 13, Section 40, Section 41).
President to appoint Chairperson and Members of the Tribunal (Section 7).
President to remove Chairperson or Members on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity (Section 9).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person guilty of contempt of the Tribunal by using insulting or threatening language, or causing interruption or disturbance in proceedings, shall be liable to suffer imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years (Section 19(1)).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The President, after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, appoints the Chairperson and other Members of the Tribunal (Section 7).

applies_to: All persons subject to the Army Act, 1950, the Navy Act, 1957 and the Air Force Act, 1950 (Section 2(1)).

Retired personnel subject to the Army Act, 1950, the Navy Act, 1957 or the Air Force Act, 1950, including their dependants, heirs and successors, in so far as it relates to their service matters (Section 2(2)).
exemptions: Matters relating to orders issued under section 18 of the Army Act, 1950, sub-section (1) of section 15 of the Navy Act, 1957 and section 18 of the Air Force Act, 1950 (Section 3(o)(i)).
Transfers and postings including the change of place or unit on posting (Section 3(o)(ii)).
Leave of any kind (Section 3(o)(iii)).
Summary court martial except where the punishment is of dismissal or imprisonment for more than three months (Section 3(o)(iv)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Tribunal's orders are final and executable (Section 29). The Tribunal possesses powers of a Civil Court for adjudicating applications (Section 14(4)) and can punish for contempt (Section 19).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Supreme Court (for appeals against final decisions or orders of the Tribunal, Section 30, Section 31).

act_identification.act_title: THE MAINTENANCE AND WELFARE OF PARENTS AND SENIOR CITIZENS ACT, 2007
act_identification.act_short_title: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and SeniorCitizens Act, 2007
act_identification.date_of_commencement: in a State on such date as the State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Fifty-eighth Year of the Republic of India
legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India and it applies also it citizens of India outside India.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for more effective provisions for the maintenance and welfare of parents and senior citizens guaranteed and recognised under the Constitution and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to provide more effective provisions for the maintenance and welfare of parents and senior citizens. It seeks to guarantee and recognize their rights under the Constitution and addresses matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

chapter_titles: MAINTENANCE OF PARENTS AND SENIOR CITIZENS
PROVISIONS FOR MEDICAL CARE OF SENIOR CITIZEN
PROTECTION OF LIFE AND PROPERTY OF SENIOR CITIZEN

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, its applicability to the whole of India and citizens outside India, and its commencement date as appointed by State Governments.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'children', 'maintenance', 'parent', 'senior citizen', and 'property'.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other enactments.

key_sections.title: Maintenance of parents and senior citizens.
key_sections.description: Outlines the entitlement of senior citizens and parents to maintenance from their children or relatives if they are unable to maintain themselves.

key_sections.title: Application for maintenance.
key_sections.description: Details who can apply for maintenance, the procedure for application, interim maintenance, and disposal timelines.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Maintenance Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Mandates the State Government to constitute Maintenance Tribunals for adjudicating maintenance orders.

key_sections.title: Order for maintenance.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Tribunal to order children or relatives to pay a monthly allowance for the maintenance of senior citizens, up to a prescribed maximum.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Allows the State Government to constitute Appellate Tribunals to hear appeals against orders of the Maintenance Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Establishment of old age homes.
key_sections.description: Requires the State Government to establish and maintain old age homes for indigent senior citizens.

key_sections.title: Medical support for senior citizens.
key_sections.description: Mandates the State Government to ensure medical support for senior citizens, including beds in hospitals, separate queues, and expanded treatment facilities.

key_sections.title: Transfer of property to be void in certain circumstances.
key_sections.description: Declares that property transfers made by senior citizens, subject to conditions of basic amenities, can be declared void if the transferee fails to provide such amenities.

key_sections.title: Exposure and abandonment of senior citizen.
key_sections.description: Defines the offence of abandoning a senior citizen under one's care and prescribes punishment.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of civil courts barred.
key_sections.description: Bars the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in matters covered by this Act and prohibits injunctions against actions taken under the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including procedures for inquiry, maintenance allowance, and old age home management.

powers_conferred: State Government to constitute Maintenance Tribunals (Section 7)
State Government to constitute Appellate Tribunals (Section 15)
State Government to establish and maintain old age homes (Section 19)
State Government to ensure medical support for senior citizens (Section 20)
State Government to take measures for publicity and awareness (Section 21)
State Government to confer powers and impose duties on District Magistrates (Section 22)
State Government to make rules (Section 32)
Tribunal to adjudicate and decide on maintenance orders (Section 7)
Tribunal to order monthly allowance for maintenance (Section 9)
Tribunal to enforce maintenance orders (Section 11)
Tribunal to take evidence on oath and enforce attendance of witnesses (Section 8)
Tribunal to refer applications to Conciliation Officer (Section 6)
Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals (Section 15)
Appellate Tribunal to allow or reject appeals (Section 16)
Central Government to specify authority for serving summons outside India (Section 6)
Central Government to give directions to State Governments (Section 30)
Central Government to review and monitor implementation (Section 31)
District Magistrate to ensure provisions of the Act are carried out (Section 22)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever, having the care or protection of a senior citizen, leaves such senior citizen in any place with the intention of wholly abandoning them, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or fine which may extend to five thousand rupees or with both (Section 24).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government for Maintenance Tribunals, Appellate Tribunals, and Maintenance Officers.

applies_to: parents
senior citizens
children (son, daughter, grandson, grand-daughter)
relatives (legal heir of childless senior citizen)
citizens of India outside India
exemptions: minor (from definition of children)
transferee for consideration and without notice of right (in property transfer cases)
special_provisions: Commencement in a State on such date as the State Government may, by notification, appoint (Section 1(3))

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through Maintenance Tribunals and Appellate Tribunals constituted by the State Government. Maintenance orders can be enforced by Tribunals, similar to Chapter IX of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. District Magistrates are empowered to ensure proper implementation. Maintenance Officers assist parents/senior citizens in proceedings. Public media, sensitization training for officers, and inter-departmental coordination are also mandated for awareness and implementation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Maintenance Tribunal, Appellate Tribunal

act_identification.act_title: THE JAWAHARLAL INSTITUTE OF POST-GRADUATE MEDICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH, PUDUCHERRY ACT, 2008
act_identification.act_short_title: the Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry Act, 2008

legislative_details.ministry_department: Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare the Institution known as the Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry, to be an institution of national importance and to provide for its incorporation and matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to declare the Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry, as an institution of national importance. It provides for its incorporation as a body corporate and outlines its objectives, functions, and administrative framework to promote high standards in medical education and research.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Declaration of Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry, as an institution of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry, as an institution of national importance.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Fund', 'Governing Body', and 'Institute'.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of Institute.
key_sections.description: Constitutes the Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry, as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

key_sections.title: Composition of Institute.
key_sections.description: Details the composition of the Institute, including ex officio members and nominated/elected members.

key_sections.title: Objects of Institute.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary objectives of the Institute, focusing on developing high standards in medical education, training, and achieving self-sufficiency in postgraduate medical education.

key_sections.title: Functions of Institute.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various functions the Institute may perform to promote its objects, including providing teaching, research facilities, establishing colleges and hospitals, and granting degrees.

key_sections.title: Grant of medical degrees, diplomas, etc., by Institute.
key_sections.description: Confers the power upon the Institute to grant medical, dental, nursing degrees, diplomas, and other academic distinctions.

key_sections.title: Recognition of medical qualifications granted by Institute.

key_sections.title: Control by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the Institute shall comply with directions issued by the Central Government for efficient administration.

key_sections.title: Transfer of service of existing employees.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint commencement date (S.1(2)), nominate members (S.5(1)(i), (j)), accept resignation of members (S.6(7)), appoint first Director (S.11(1) Proviso), approve fees and charges (S.13(l)), make payments to Institute (S.15), approve investment of funds (S.16(2)), prescribe budget form (S.17), prescribe accounts form (S.18(1)), require reports (S.19, S.27), issue directions for administration (S.25), resolve disputes (S.26), make rules (S.29), make first regulations (S.30(2)), remove difficulties (S.32).

Institute: To acquire, hold, dispose of property, contract, sue and be sued (S.4), constitute Governing Body and committees (S.10), appoint Director and other staff (S.11), develop teaching patterns, train personnel, attain self-sufficiency (S.12), provide teaching, research facilities, establish colleges, hospitals, grant degrees, institute professorships, receive grants, deal with property, demand fees, reserve seats, provide free treatment, construct quarters, borrow money (S.13), maintain Fund (S.16), prepare budget (S.17), maintain accounts (S.18), prepare annual report (S.19), constitute pension and provident funds (S.20), authenticate orders (S.21), grant degrees, diplomas (S.23), make regulations (S.30).
President of Institute: To exercise powers and discharge functions as prescribed (S.7(2)), be Chairperson of Governing Body (S.10(3)).
Director of Institute: To act as Secretary to Institute and Governing Body (S.11(2)), exercise powers and discharge functions as specified or delegated (S.11(4)).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government nominates President, nominates members, and appoints the first Director. The Institute appoints the Director and other officers and employees.

applies_to: Jawaharlal Institute of Post-Graduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry
officers, teachers and other employees of the Institute
students of the Institute
local applicants for undergraduate courses
poor patients

Free treatment to poor patients in the same manner as provided by a medical Institute of the Central Government (S.13(n)).
The first Director of the Institute shall be appointed by the Central Government (S.11(1) Proviso).
