act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN MARITIME UNIVERSITY ACT, 2008

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways (Department of Shipping)

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate a teaching and affiliating University at the national level to facilitate and promote maritime studies and research and to achieve excellence in areas of marine science and technology, marine environment and other related fields, and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Indian Maritime University to promote maritime studies, training, research, and extension work, focusing on emerging areas like oceanography, maritime law, and marine technology. It aims to provide institutional and research facilities, foster innovation in teaching, and contribute to national development through education in marine sciences.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: The University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Indian Maritime University, its headquarters, and legal status.

key_sections.title: Objects of the University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary goals and objectives of the University, including promoting maritime studies and research.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Details the various powers vested in the University, such as providing instruction, granting degrees, and establishing facilities.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: States that the University's jurisdiction extends to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: The Visitor.
key_sections.description: Defines the role and powers of the President of India as the Visitor of the University, including inspection and direction.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the designated officers of the University.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities governing the University.

key_sections.title: Power to make statutes.
key_sections.description: Grants the power to make Statutes and specifies the matters they may cover.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Grants the power to make Ordinances and specifies the matters they may cover.

key_sections.title: Tribunal of Arbitration.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Tribunal of Arbitration for resolving disputes between the University and its employees.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.

key_sections.title: Transfer of assets and options of the employees.
key_sections.description: Addresses the transfer of assets and employee options from institutions merged into the University.

powers_conferred: To provide for instruction in various branches of learning and for research.
To establish and maintain campuses, colleges, institutions, departments, laboratories, libraries, museums, centres of research, training and specialised studies.
To grant diplomas and confer degrees and other academic distinctions.
To confer honorary degrees or other distinctions.
To institute Directorships, Principalships, Professorships, Associate Professorships, Assistant Professorships and other teaching or academic positions and appoint persons thereto.
To provide for the terms and conditions of service of Directors, Principals, teachers, academic staff, and other employees.
To recognise and withdraw recognition from institutions of higher learning.
To organise and conduct refresher courses, workshops, seminars and other programmes.
To appoint visiting Professors, Emeritus Professors, Consultants, Scholars on contract or otherwise.
To create teaching, non-teaching, administrative, ministerial and other posts and make appointments thereto.
To co-operate or collaborate or associate with any other University or authority or institution of higher learning within India or abroad.
To inspect recognised institutions and ensure proper standards.
To prescribe fees and other charges.
To coordinate the work of different colleges and institutions.
To set up central facilities like computer centre, training centre, instrumentation centre, library, simulators.
To set up curriculum development centres.
To admit to its privileges colleges and institutions not maintained by the University and withdraw such privileges.
To recognise, guide, supervise and control Halls and other accommodation for students.
To make provision for research and advisory services.
To determine standards of admission to the University.
To institute and award fellowships, scholarships, studentships, assistantships, medals and prizes.
To demand and receive payment of fees and other charges.
To supervise the residences of students and make arrangements for their health and welfare.
To regulate the conduct of students and employees.
To prescribe code of conduct for managements of recognised colleges and institutions.
To receive benefactions, donations and gifts.
To acquire, hold, manage and dispose of any property.
To borrow money with Central Government approval.
To assess needs of students and initiate necessary programmes.
To initiate measures to enlist co-operation of industry.
To provide for instruction through “distance learning” and “open approach”.
To establish such campuses, special centres, specialised laboratories or other units for research and instruction.
To confer autonomous status on a college or an institution or a Department.
To arrange for training to upgrade maritime standard of employees of industry and institutes and levy fees.
To establish Off-shore Campus at any place outside the Country.
Visitor: To review work and progress, inspect University/colleges, issue directions, annul proceedings, make/amend Statutes.
Vice-Chancellor: To exercise general supervision and control, take immediate action, review decisions of authorities, cause inspections, convene meetings, make short-term appointments.

Executive Council: Management and administration of revenue and property, create posts, appoint staff, regulate discipline, manage finances, invest money, enter contracts, redress grievances, appoint examiners, delegate powers.
Academic Council: Control and supervision over standards of instruction, education and examination, advise Executive Council on academic matters.
Board of Affiliation and Recognition: Responsible for admitting colleges and institutions to University privileges.
Planning Board: Principal planning body, responsible for monitoring development, advising on educational programmes.
Registrar: To enter into agreements, sign documents, authenticate records, take disciplinary action against certain employees.
Finance Officer: Exercise general supervision over funds, advise on financial policy, manage property/investments, prepare annual accounts/budget.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act outlines disciplinary actions against students (expulsion, rustication, fine, debarment from exams, cancellation of results) under Section 32. It also provides for the removal of employees for misconduct under Statute 29. No specific criminal offences or penalties for the general public are defined.

authorities_established: The Board of Affiliation and Recognition
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and nominates members to various authorities. The Executive Council appoints Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Registrars, Finance Officer, teachers, academic staff, Principals, Proctors, and the Librarian. The Vice-Chancellor appoints Deans of Schools, Heads of Departments, and makes temporary appointments.

applies_to: Persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class (for admission/employment)
Employees of the University
Students of the University
Colleges and institutions within the jurisdiction of the University
exemptions: The University may make special provisions for the employment or promotion of educational interests of women, physically handicapped, or persons belonging to the weaker sections of society, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Section 7 proviso).
Government-maintained colleges and institutions are exempt from certain conditions regarding Governing Body constitution and appointment of teaching staff (Statute 34).
special_provisions: Transitional provisions for initial appointments and constitution of authorities (Section 46).
Provisions for students to complete their courses of studies in colleges or institutions affiliated to the University (Section 48).

Specific provisions for the transfer of assets and employee options from merged institutions (Training Ship Chanakya, Marine Engineering and Research Institute, Lal Bahadur Shastri College of Advance Maritime Studies, National Maritime Academy, Indian Institute of Port Management, National Ship Design and Research Centre) (Section 49).
Recommendations of an 'Equivalence Committee' for recognition of existing teaching posts in Government Maritime Institutes (Statute 46).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Parliament (for Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations to be laid before it), Executive Council (for Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations), Academic Council (for Regulations, proposing Ordinances), Visitor (for Statutes), Vice-Chancellor (for first Ordinances with Central Government approval).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor has powers of inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions to ensure compliance. The Vice-Chancellor exercises general supervision and control, including disciplinary powers over students and employees. Disputes between the University and employees are resolved by a Tribunal of Arbitration. The Executive Council regulates and enforces discipline among employees.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Tribunal of Arbitration (for specific disputes between the University and employees). Civil courts are impliedly excluded for certain matters referred to the Visitor (Section 38(2)).

schedules_summary.description: Contains the detailed Statutes of the University, covering the constitution, powers, and functions of various officers and authorities (e.g., Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Executive Council, Academic Council), appointment procedures, terms and conditions of service, disciplinary matters, admission of colleges, and other operational aspects of the University.

act_identification.act_title: THE AIRPORTS ECONOMIC REGULATORY AUTHORITY OF INDIA ACT, 2008
act_identification.act_short_title: the Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India Act, 2008

legislative_details.geographical_extent: all airports whereat air transport services are operated or are intended to be operated, other than airports and airfields belonging to or subject to the control of the Armed Forces or paramilitary Forces of the Union; all private airports and leased airports; all civil enclaves; all major airports.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Airports Economic Regulatory Authority to regulate tariff and other charges for the aeronautical services rendered at airports and to monitor performance standards of airports and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to establish an Airports Economic Regulatory Authority. This Authority is tasked with regulating tariffs and other charges for aeronautical services provided at airports, as well as monitoring the performance standards of these airports.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II THE AIRPORTS ECONOMIC REGULATORY AUTHORITY
CHAPTER III POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE AUTHORITY
CHAPTER V FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT

key_sections.title: Short title, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its commencement date, and the types of airports and areas to which it applies.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'aeronautical service', 'airport', 'Authority', and 'major airport'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Authority.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of the Airports Economic Regulatory Authority by the Central Government to exercise powers and functions under the Act.

key_sections.title: Composition of Authority.
key_sections.description: Details the composition of the Authority, including a Chairperson and two Members, and their qualifications and appointment process.

key_sections.title: Functions of Authority.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary functions of the Authority, including determining tariffs for aeronautical services, development fees, passenger service fees, and monitoring performance standards at major airports.

key_sections.title: Powers of Authority to call for information, conduct investigations, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants the Authority powers to request information, conduct inquiries, and inspect documents of service providers to assess their performance.

key_sections.title: Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Designates the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal as the Appellate Tribunal for this Act, defining its jurisdiction to adjudicate disputes and hear appeals against Authority's orders.

key_sections.title: Application for settlement of disputes and appeals to Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Describes the procedure for making applications for dispute settlement and appeals to the Appellate Tribunal, including timelines and parties who can apply.

key_sections.title: Penalty for wilful failure to comply with orders of Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including fines, for individuals who wilfully fail to comply with orders issued by the Appellate Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Punishment for non-compliance of orders and directions under this Act.
key_sections.description: Specifies punishments, including fines, for non-compliance with any order or direction given under this Act or contravention of its provisions, rules, or regulations.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, covering various administrative and procedural matters.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Authority the power to make regulations, with prior Central Government approval, to implement the purposes of the Act, particularly concerning internal procedures and engagement of experts.

powers_conferred: Power to establish the Airports Economic Regulatory Authority (Central Government, Section 3)
Power to appoint Chairperson and Members of the Authority (Central Government, Section 4)
Power to determine tariff for aeronautical services (Authority, Section 13(1)(a))
Power to determine development fees (Authority, Section 13(1)(b))
Power to determine passenger service fee (Authority, Section 13(1)(c))
Power to monitor performance standards (Authority, Section 13(1)(d))
Power to call for information, conduct investigations, and inspect documents (Authority, Section 14)
Power to issue directions to service providers (Authority, Section 15)
Power of seizure (Authority or authorised officer, Section 16)
Power to make rules (Central Government, Section 51)
Power to make regulations (Authority, Section 52)
Power to supersede Authority (Central Government, Section 49)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter VI outlines penalties for various offences. Section 37 imposes a fine up to one lakh rupees for wilful failure to comply with Appellate Tribunal orders, with increased fines for subsequent or continuing offences. Section 38 specifies fines up to one lakh rupees for non-compliance with orders/directions under the Act, also with increased penalties for repeat or continuing contraventions. Section 39 provides similar penalties for non-compliance with orders of the Authority or Appellate Tribunal. Sections 40 and 41 address offences committed by companies and Government Departments, respectively, holding responsible individuals and entities accountable.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Authority determines tariffs, fees, and monitors performance. It has powers to call for information, conduct investigations, issue directions, and seize documents. The Appellate Tribunal adjudicates disputes and hears appeals, with its orders being executable as civil court decrees. Chapter VI prescribes penalties for non-compliance, and the Authority can initiate complaints for cognizance of offences.

schedules_summary.description: Contains amendments to the Aircraft Act, 1934 and the Airports Authority of India Act, 1994, specifically modifying provisions related to tariff and development fees.

act_identification.act_title: THE UNORGANISED WORKERS’ SOCIAL SECURITY ACT, 2008
act_identification.act_short_title: the Unorganised Workers’ Social Security Act, 2008

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Labour and Employment

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the social security and welfare of unorganised workers and for other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to provide social security and welfare benefits to unorganised workers across India. It facilitates the formulation of schemes by both Central and State Governments and establishes boards to oversee their implementation and administration.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER III NATIONAL SOCIAL SECURITY BOARD FOR UNORGANISED WORKERS
CHAPTER IV STATE SOCIAL SECURITY BOARD FOR UNORGANISED WORKERS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, its applicability to the whole of India, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'employer', 'unorganised worker', 'National Board', etc.

key_sections.title: Framing of scheme.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central and State Governments to formulate and notify welfare schemes for unorganised workers covering various benefits.

key_sections.title: Funding of Central Government Schemes.
key_sections.description: Outlines the funding mechanisms for schemes notified by the Central Government, including wholly, partly, or beneficiary-contributed funding.

key_sections.title: National Social Security Board.

key_sections.title: State Social Security Board.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of State Social Security Boards by State Governments, detailing their composition, term, and functions.

key_sections.title: Eligibility for registration and social security benefits.
key_sections.description: Sets out the eligibility criteria for unorganised workers to register and receive social security benefits, including age and self-declaration.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to give directions.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to issue directions to the National Board, State Governments, or State Boards regarding the Act's implementation.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, specifying various matters.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules by State Government.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, specifying various matters.

key_sections.title: Saving of certain laws.
key_sections.description: States that the Act does not affect more beneficial welfare schemes provided by corresponding State laws.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, with a two-year limitation.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To formulate and notify welfare schemes (Section 3(1)), amend Schedules (Section 3(3)), fund schemes (Section 4), constitute National Board (Section 5(1)), give directions (Section 11), make rules (Section 13), remove difficulties (Section 17).

State Government: To formulate and notify welfare schemes (Section 3(4)), fund schemes (Section 7), constitute State Board (Section 6(1)), set up Workers' facilitation centres (Section 9), make rules (Section 14).

National Social Security Board: To recommend schemes, advise Central Government, monitor schemes, review registration progress, review record keeping, review expenditure, undertake other assigned functions (Section 5(8)).

State Social Security Board: To recommend schemes, advise State Government, monitor schemes, review record keeping, review registration progress, review expenditure, undertake other assigned functions (Section 6(8)).
District Administration: To perform record keeping functions (Section 8), register workers and issue identity cards (Section 10(3)).

related_acts: The Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government nominates thirty-four members to the National Board (Section 5(2)(c)). State Government nominates twenty-eight members to the State Board (Section 6(2)(c)).

applies_to: Unorganised workers
Home-based workers
Self-employed workers
Wage workers in the unorganised sector
Workers in the organised sector who are not covered by any of the Acts mentioned in Schedule II
exemptions: Workers in the organised sector who are covered by the Acts mentioned in Schedule II
special_provisions: Adequate representation shall be given to persons belonging to the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Minorities and Women in the National and State Boards.
The Act does not affect the operation of any corresponding law in a State providing welfare schemes which are more beneficial to the unorganised workers.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Formulation and notification of schemes by Central and State Governments; monitoring and advisory functions by National and State Social Security Boards; record keeping, registration, and identity card issuance by District Administration; facilitation by Workers' facilitation centres.

schedules_summary.description: Lists social security schemes for unorganised workers, including Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme, National Family Benefit Scheme, Janani Suraksha Yojana, Handloom Weavers’ Comprehensive Welfare Scheme, Handicraft Artisans’ Comprehensive Welfare Scheme, Pension to Master craft persons, National Scheme for Welfare of Fishermen and Training and Extension, Janshree Bima Yojana, Aam Admi Bima Yojana, and Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana.

Lists Acts that define workers in the organised sector, including The Workmen’s Compensation Act, 1923, The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, The Employees’ State Insurance Act, 1948, The Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, The Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, and The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL INVESTIGATION AGENCY ACT, 2008

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India and it applies also— (a) to citizens of India outside India; (b) to persons in the service of the Government wherever they may be; (c) to persons on ships and aircrafts registered in India wherever they may be and (d) to persons who commit a Scheduled Offence beyond India against the Indian citizens or affecting the interest of India.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to constitute an investigation agency at the national level to investigate and prosecute offences affecting the sovereignty, security and integrity of India, security of State, friendly relations with foreign States and offences under Acts enacted to implement international treaties, agreements, conventions and resolutions of the United Nations, its agencies and other international organisations and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes a national-level investigation agency to investigate and prosecute offences that threaten India's sovereignty, security, and integrity, as well as offences related to international treaties and organizations. It also provides for the constitution of special courts for the trial of such offences.

chapter_titles: INVESTIGATION BY THE NATIONAL INVESTIGATION AGENCY

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and application of the Act, including extraterritorial jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution of National Investigation Agency.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to constitute the National Investigation Agency (NIA) for investigation and prosecution of Scheduled Offences.

key_sections.title: Investigation of Scheduled Offences.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for investigation of Scheduled Offences, including the role of State and Central Governments and the NIA.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to designate Court of Session as Special Courts.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to designate Courts of Session as Special Courts for the trial of Scheduled Offences.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of Special Courts.
key_sections.description: Defines the jurisdiction of Special Courts and provides for transfer of cases by the Supreme Court or High Court.

key_sections.title: Public Prosecutors.
key_sections.description: Details the appointment and qualifications of Public Prosecutors, Additional Public Prosecutors, and Special Public Prosecutors for Special Courts.

key_sections.title: Procedure and powers of Special Courts.
key_sections.description: Describes the procedure and powers of Special Courts, including taking cognizance, summary trials, and powers akin to a Court of Session.

key_sections.title: Protection of witnesses.
key_sections.description: Allows Special Courts to hold proceedings in camera and take measures to protect the identity and address of witnesses.

key_sections.title: Appeals.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals from Special Courts to the High Court and specifies the procedure and time limits for such appeals.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to designate Court of Session as Special Courts.
key_sections.description: Enables State Governments to designate Courts of Session as Special Courts for Scheduled Offences and outlines modifications to Chapter IV for such courts.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To constitute the National Investigation Agency (Sec 3), exercise superintendence over the Agency (Sec 4), appoint the Director-General (Sec 4), direct the Agency to investigate Scheduled Offences (Sec 6), designate Courts of Session as Special Courts (Sec 11), appoint Public Prosecutors (Sec 15), grant sanction for prosecution against Agency members (Sec 18), make rules (Sec 25), and remove difficulties (Sec 24).

National Investigation Agency (NIA): To investigate Scheduled Offences throughout India and outside India (Sec 3, 6), investigate connected offences (Sec 8), and with Central Government approval, transfer cases to State Government for investigation and trial (Sec 7).

Special Courts: To try Scheduled Offences (Sec 13), try other connected offences (Sec 14), take cognizance of offences without commitment (Sec 16), try certain offences summarily (Sec 16), exercise powers of a Court of Session (Sec 16), hold proceedings in camera and protect witnesses (Sec 17), and transfer cases to regular courts if not triable by them (Sec 20).
State Government: To investigate and prosecute any Scheduled Offence (Sec 10), extend assistance and co-operation to the Agency (Sec 9), and designate Courts of Session as Special Courts (Sec 22).

High Courts: To make rules relating to Special Courts within their territory (Sec 23), hear appeals from Special Courts (Sec 21), and transfer cases pending before a Special Court within the State to another Special Court within the State (Sec 13).
Supreme Court: To transfer any case pending before a Special Court to any other Special Court within that State or in any other State (Sec 13).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act primarily deals with the investigation and prosecution of 'Scheduled Offences' which are offences specified in the Schedule and are defined under other Acts. A specific penalty is prescribed in Section 17(4) for contravention of witness protection measures: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.

related_acts: The Suppression of Unlawful Acts against Safety of Civil Aviation Act, 1982
The SAARC Convention (Suppression of Terrorism) Act, 1993
The Suppression of Unlawful Acts Against Safety of Maritime Navigation and Fixed Platforms on Continental Shelf Act, 2002
The Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, 2005

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the Director-General of the National Investigation Agency and Public Prosecutors. The appointing authority, in consultation with the Central Government, may direct a Sessions Judge to continue as a judge of the Special Court.

applies_to: whole of India
citizens of India outside India
persons in the service of the Government wherever they may be
persons on ships and aircrafts registered in India wherever they may be
persons who commit a Scheduled Offence beyond India against the Indian citizens or affecting the interest of India
special_provisions: The Act extends to the whole of India and applies extraterritorially to Indian citizens, government servants, persons on Indian-registered ships and aircrafts, and persons committing Scheduled Offences abroad affecting India's interest (Section 1(2)).

Chapter IV provisions apply to Special Courts designated by State Governments with specific modifications, such as references to 'Central Government' being construed as 'State Government' and 'Agency' as 'investigation agency of the State Government' (Section 22(2)).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The High Courts (for matters relating to Special Courts within their territory) and the Central Government (for carrying out the general provisions of the Act).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the investigation of Scheduled Offences by the National Investigation Agency and their prosecution in designated Special Courts. State Governments are mandated to extend assistance and cooperation to the Agency, and they also retain powers to investigate and prosecute Scheduled Offences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Special Courts (for trial), High Courts (for appeals and case transfers), and the Supreme Court (for case transfers).

schedules_summary.description: Lists the Acts and specific sections of Acts under which offences are designated as 'Scheduled Offences' for the purpose of this Act. These include The Explosive Substances Act, The Atomic Energy Act, The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, The Anti-Hijacking Act, Acts related to safety of civil aviation and maritime navigation, The Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Act, and specific sections of the Indian Penal Code, The Arms Act, and The Information Technology Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP ACT, 2008

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make provisions for the formation and regulation of limited liability partnerships and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to provide for the formation and regulation of limited liability partnerships. It covers all matters connected with or incidental to the establishment and operation of such partnerships.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II NATURE OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP
CHAPTER III INCORPORATION OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND MATTERS INCIDENTAL THERETO
CHAPTER IV PARTNERS AND THEIR RELATIONS
CHAPTER V EXTENT AND LIMITATION OF LIABILITY OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP AND PARTNERS
CHAPTER VIII ASSIGNMENT AND TRANSFER OF PARTNERSHIP RIGHTS
CHAPTER X CONVERSION INTO LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP
CHAPTER XI FOREIGN LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIPS
CHAPTER XII COMPROMISE, ARRANGEMENT OR RECONSTRUCTION OF LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIPS
CHAPTER XIII WINDING UP AND DISSOLUTION

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Limited liability partnership to be body corporate.
key_sections.description: Declares a limited liability partnership as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a separate legal entity from its partners.

key_sections.title: Non-applicability of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, generally do not apply to limited liability partnerships.

key_sections.title: Designated partners.
key_sections.description: Mandates every limited liability partnership to have at least two designated partners, with specific requirements for their residency and consent.

key_sections.title: Incorporation document.
key_sections.description: Outlines the requirements for the incorporation document, including subscription by persons, filing with the Registrar, and a statement of compliance.

key_sections.title: Relationship of partners.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that mutual rights and duties of partners are governed by the limited liability partnership agreement, or by the First Schedule in its absence.

key_sections.title: Extent of liability of partner.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that a partner is not personally liable for the obligations of the limited liability partnership solely by being a partner, but is liable for their own wrongful acts.

key_sections.title: Unlimited liability in case of fraud.
key_sections.description: Imposes unlimited liability on the limited liability partnership and partners for acts carried out with intent to defraud creditors or for any fraudulent purpose.

key_sections.title: Maintenance of books of account, other records and audit, etc.
key_sections.description: Requires limited liability partnerships to maintain proper books of account, prepare a Statement of Account and Solvency, and have accounts audited.

key_sections.title: Investigation of the affairs of limited liability partnership.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint inspectors to investigate the affairs of a limited liability partnership under specified circumstances.

key_sections.title: Conversion from firm into limited liability partnership.
key_sections.description: Provides for the conversion of a firm into a limited liability partnership in accordance with the Second Schedule.

key_sections.title: Conversion from private company into limited liability partnership.
key_sections.description: Provides for the conversion of a private company into a limited liability partnership in accordance with the Third Schedule.

key_sections.title: Conversion from unlisted public company into limited liability partnership.
key_sections.description: Provides for the conversion of an unlisted public company into a limited liability partnership in accordance with the Fourth Schedule.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Special Courts.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to establish or designate Special Courts for the speedy trial of offences under this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint inspectors to investigate affairs of LLP (Section 43).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act (Section 79).
Central Government: To alter any of the provisions contained in any of the Schedules (Section 78).
Central Government: To remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act (Section 80).
Central Government: To establish or designate Special Courts for speedy trial of offences (Section 67A).
Central Government: To appoint Registrars, Additional Registrars, Joint Registrars, Deputy Registrars and Assistant Registrars (Section 68A).
Central Government: To prescribe accounting and auditing standards in consultation with NFRA (Section 34A).
Central Government: To direct application of provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, to LLPs (Section 67).
Registrar: To register incorporation documents and issue certificates (Section 12).
Registrar: To reserve names for proposed LLPs (Section 16).
Registrar: To obtain information from persons related to LLPs (Section 38).
Registrar: To strike defunct limited liability partnerships off the register (Section 75).
Tribunal: To declare that affairs of LLP ought to be investigated (Section 43).
Tribunal: To enforce compromise or arrangement (Section 61).
Tribunal: To order winding up of a limited liability partnership (Section 61, Section 64).
Special Court: To try offences under this Act (Section 67B).
Adjudicating Officer: To impose penalties and direct rectification of defaults (Section 76A).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes various penalties and punishments for contraventions. These include penalties for contravention of designated partner requirements (Section 10), false statements in incorporation documents (imprisonment up to two years and fine up to five lakh rupees, Section 11(3)), default in registered office requirements (penalty, Section 13(4)), improper use of 'LLP' words (fine, Section 20), contravention of publication requirements (penalty, Section 21(2)), default in registration of changes in partners (penalty, Section 25(4), (5)), fraudulent conduct (imprisonment up to five years and fine up to five lakh rupees, plus compensation, Section 30(2), (3)), false statements in returns/documents (imprisonment up to two years and fine up to five lakh rupees, Section 37), failure to comply with Registrar's requisitions (fine, Section 38(3)), defaults in financial disclosures and annual returns (penalties/fines, Section 34(5), (6), Section 35(2)), failure to assist inspectors (fine, Section 47(5)), and general penalties for unspecified contraventions (penalty, Section 74). Enhanced punishment is provided for second or subsequent offences (Section 70). Offences committed by LLPs can also lead to liability for partners/designated partners (Section 76). Failure to comply with orders of Adjudicating Officers can result in fines or imprisonment (Section 76A(8), (9)).

related_acts: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint inspectors (Section 43), judges for Special Courts (Section 67A), Registrars and other officers for registration offices (Section 68A), and Adjudicating Officers (Section 76A).
regulatory_bodies: National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (Appellate Tribunal)
Institute of Chartered Accountants of India

applies_to: Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs)
Partners of LLPs
Designated partners of LLPs
Individuals
Body corporates
Firms (for conversion)
Private companies (for conversion)
Unlisted public companies (for conversion)
Foreign limited liability partnerships (for establishing place of business in India)
exemptions: Central Government may exempt any class or classes of limited liability partnerships from audit requirements (Section 34(4) Proviso).
Certain entities like corporation sole, co-operative societies, and other specified body corporates are excluded from the definition of 'body corporate' for the purpose of this Act (Section 2(d)).
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act to come into force (Section 1(3) Proviso).
Special provisions for 'small limited liability partnership' and 'start-up limited liability partnership' regarding reduced penalties (Section 76A Proviso).
Specific provisions and schedules for conversion of firms, private companies, and unlisted public companies into limited liability partnerships (Chapters X, Second, Third, and Fourth Schedules).
Establishment of Special Courts for speedy trial of offences under the Act (Section 67A).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through registration and filing requirements with the Registrar, inspections and investigations by Central Government appointed inspectors, adjudication of penalties by Adjudicating Officers, and judicial proceedings before the Tribunal, Appellate Tribunal, and Special Courts. Penalties, fines, and imprisonment are prescribed for non-compliance and offences. The Central Government also has powers to make rules, alter schedules, and remove difficulties for effective implementation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Tribunal (National Company Law Tribunal), Appellate Tribunal (National Company Law Appellate Tribunal), Special Courts (established or designated by Central Government), Judicial Magistrate of the first class, Metropolitan Magistrate, and High Court (for appeals/revisions from Special Courts).

schedules_summary.description: Contains provisions regarding the mutual rights and duties of partners and the limited liability partnership, applicable in the absence of any specific agreement on such matters.
Outlines the process and requirements for the conversion of a firm into a limited liability partnership, including eligibility, statements to be filed, registration, and effects of conversion.

Details the procedure and conditions for the conversion of a private company into a limited liability partnership, covering eligibility, filing requirements, registration, and the legal effects of such conversion.

Specifies the provisions for the conversion of an unlisted public company into a limited liability partnership, including interpretation, eligibility criteria, statements for filing, registration process, and the consequences of conversion.

act_identification.act_title: THE GRAM NYAYALAYAS ACT, 2008

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Nagaland, the State of Arunachal Pradesh, the State of Sikkim and to the tribal areas

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of Gram Nyayalayas at the grass roots level for the purposes of providing access to justice to the citizens at their doorsteps and to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of social, economic or other disabilities and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: To establish Gram Nyayalayas at the grass roots level to provide access to justice to citizens at their doorsteps and ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied due to social, economic, or other disabilities.

chapter_titles: JURISDICTION, POWERS AND AUTHORITY OF GRAM NYAYALAYA

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Gram Nyayalayas.
key_sections.description: Empowers State Governments to establish Gram Nyayalayas in consultation with the High Court.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Nyayadhikari.
key_sections.description: Mandates the appointment of a presiding officer (Nyayadhikari) for each Gram Nyayalaya by the State Government in consultation with the High Court.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of Gram Nyayalaya.
key_sections.description: Grants Gram Nyayalayas both civil and criminal jurisdiction, overriding other laws.

key_sections.title: Criminal jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Details the types of criminal offences Gram Nyayalayas can try, as specified in the First Schedule.

key_sections.title: Civil jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Details the types of civil suits and disputes Gram Nyayalayas can try, as specified in the Second Schedule.

key_sections.title: Power to amend Schedules.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to the Central and State Governments to amend the First and Second Schedules.

key_sections.title: Overriding effect of Act in criminal trial.
key_sections.description: States that the Act's provisions override the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, but the Code applies where not inconsistent.

key_sections.title: Gram Nyayalaya to follow summary trial procedure.
key_sections.description: Mandates Gram Nyayalayas to follow summary trial procedures for offences.

key_sections.title: Overriding effect of Act in civil proceedings.
key_sections.description: States that the Act's provisions override the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, but the Code applies where not inconsistent.

key_sections.title: Duty of Gram Nyayalaya to make efforts for conciliation and settlement of civil disputes.
key_sections.description: Requires Gram Nyayalayas to attempt conciliation and settlement in civil disputes.

key_sections.title: Appeal in criminal cases.
key_sections.description: Outlines the provisions for appeals in criminal cases from Gram Nyayalayas to the Court of Session.

key_sections.title: Appeal in civil cases.
key_sections.description: Outlines the provisions for appeals in civil cases from Gram Nyayalayas to the District Court.

key_sections.title: Power of High Court to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the High Court to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions.

powers_conferred: State Government: Establish Gram Nyayalayas, specify local limits of jurisdiction, appoint Nyayadhikari, determine nature and categories of officers and employees, make rules, notify State Acts for jurisdiction.

High Court: Consulted for establishment of Gram Nyayalayas, consulted for appointment of Nyayadhikari, specify pecuniary limits of Gram Nyayalayas, make rules, authorize inspection of Gram Nyayalayas.
Central Government: Add to or omit items in Part I or Part II of the First Schedule or Part II of the Second Schedule.

Gram Nyayalaya: Exercise civil and criminal jurisdiction, take cognizance of offences, try offences, grant relief, follow summary trial procedure, dispose of plea bargaining applications, conduct trials and proceedings in villages (mobile courts), execute decrees and orders, make efforts for conciliation and settlement of civil disputes.
District Court: Transfer civil disputes, prepare panel of Conciliators, hear appeals in civil cases.
Court of Session: Hear appeals in criminal cases.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Gram Nyayalayas try offences specified in Part I of the First Schedule (IPC offences not punishable with death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment exceeding two years; specific theft, receiving stolen property, assisting concealment, house-trespass, insult, criminal intimidation with specific limits) and offences/grant relief under enactments in Part II of the First Schedule (Cattle-trespass Act, Payment of Wages Act, Minimum Wages Act, Protection of Civil Rights Act, maintenance under CrPC, Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, Equal Remuneration Act, Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act). They also try offences under State Acts notified by the State Government.

related_acts: Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 (22 of 1955)
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (43 of 2005)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government in consultation with the High Court appoints Nyayadhikari. District Court in consultation with the District Magistrate prepares a panel of Conciliators.

applies_to: Whole of India
citizens
exemptions: State of Nagaland
State of Arunachal Pradesh
State of Sikkim
tribal areas
special_provisions: Explanation for 'tribal areas' meaning areas specified in Parts I, II, IIA and III of the Table below paragraph 20 of the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution within the State of Assam, the State of Meghalaya, the State of Tripura and the State of Mizoram, respectively.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Gram Nyayalayas exercise civil and criminal jurisdiction, follow summary trial procedures, conduct plea bargaining, make efforts for conciliation, and execute decrees. Police officers are bound to assist Gram Nyayalayas.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Gram Nyayalayas (first instance), Court of Session (criminal appeals), District Court (civil appeals)

schedules_summary.description: Lists offences under the Indian Penal Code and other Central Acts that Gram Nyayalayas can try, and provides for State Acts to be notified.
Lists suits of a civil nature (civil disputes, property disputes, other disputes) within the jurisdiction of Gram Nyayalayas, and provides for Central and State Acts to be notified.

act_identification.act_title: THE COLLECTION OF STATISTICS ACT, 2008

act_overview.preamble: An Act to facilitate the collection of statistics on economic, demographic, social, scientific and environmental aspects, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to facilitate the collection of statistics on economic, demographic, social, scientific, and environmental aspects. It establishes a framework for the collection, security, and disclosure of statistical information, and defines the duties of informants and powers of statistics officers.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER III DISCLOSURE OF INFORMATION IN CERTAIN CASES AND RESTRICTIONS OF THEIR USE
CHAPTER V POWER IN RESPECT OF CORE STATISTICS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'agency', 'appropriate Government', 'informant', 'statistics officer', etc.

key_sections.title: Collection of statistics.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to direct the collection of statistics on various aspects through notification, with provisos regarding Union List matters and overlapping collections.

key_sections.title: Nodal officer.
key_sections.description: Mandates the designation of a nodal officer by Central or State Governments/UT Administrations to coordinate and supervise statistical activities.

key_sections.title: Powers of appropriate Government to appoint statistics officer, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants the appropriate Government powers to appoint statistics officers, agencies, or persons for collecting statistics and to delegate such powers.

key_sections.title: Duty of informants.
key_sections.description: Obligates informants to furnish required information to the best of their knowledge or belief, even if part of a sampling procedure.

key_sections.title: Security of information.
key_sections.description: Ensures the security and confidentiality of information collected, restricting its use and disclosure to statistical purposes and preventing identification of informants.

key_sections.title: Penalty for neglect or refusal to supply particulars.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including fines, for individuals or companies who neglect or refuse to supply required particulars or answer questions.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that persons in charge of a company's business are deemed guilty of offences committed by the company, with provisions for proving lack of knowledge or due diligence.

key_sections.title: Cognizance of offences.
key_sections.description: States that courts can only take cognizance of offences based on a complaint by the appropriate Government or authorized officer, and specifies the competent courts.

key_sections.title: Power in respect of core statistics.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to declare subjects as 'core statistics' of national importance and make arrangements for their collection and dissemination.

key_sections.title: Overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the Act's provisions override inconsistent provisions in other laws, except for human population census under the Census Act, 1948.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions, including coordination, terms for engaging agencies, and manner of information use.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Collection of Statistics Act, 1953, while saving actions taken and rules made under the repealed Act.

powers_conferred: Power of appropriate Government to appoint statistics officer, etc. (Section 4)
Power of statistics officer to call for information (Section 5)
Power of appropriate Government to disclose certain information (Section 10)
Power of appropriate Government to disclose information schedules for bona fide research or statistical purposes (Section 11)
Power of appropriate Government to release historical documents (Section 12)
Power of Central Government in respect of core statistics (Section 27)
Power of Central Government to give directions to State/UT/local governments (Section 28)
Power of Central Government to make rules (Section 33)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for various offences including neglect or refusal to supply particulars (fine up to one thousand rupees, or five thousand for companies, with daily fines for continued failure), making false statements (simple imprisonment up to six months or fine up to one thousand rupees, or five thousand for companies, or both), mutilation or defacement of information schedules (simple imprisonment up to six months or fine up to two thousand rupees, or ten thousand for companies, or both), obstruction of employees (simple imprisonment up to six months or fine up to two thousand rupees, or ten thousand for companies, or both), other contraventions (simple imprisonment up to six months or fine up to two thousand rupees, or ten thousand for companies, or both), failure of employees to carry out duties or divulging information (simple imprisonment up to six months or fine up to two thousand rupees, or ten thousand for companies, or both), and impersonation of an employee (simple imprisonment up to six months or fine up to two thousand rupees, or ten thousand for companies, or both). A general penalty is also provided for offences not specifically covered.

repealed_acts: The Collection of Statistics Act, 1953 (32 of 1953)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The appropriate Government may appoint statistics officers and agencies. The Central Government or a State Government or Union territory Administration shall designate a nodal officer.

applies_to: informants
agencies
persons engaged in collection of statistics
special_provisions: State Governments or Union territory Administrations or local governments are not authorised to collect statistics on matters in the Union List (List I of Seventh Schedule to the Constitution).
Restrictions on similar directions for statistics collection by different levels of government to avoid duplication.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through statistics officers who can call for information. Non-compliance or other offences are subject to penalties, prosecution initiated by the appropriate Government or statistics officer, and summary trials by Judicial Magistrates of the first class or Metropolitan Magistrates.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class

act_identification.act_title: THE SOUTH ASIAN UNIVERSITY ACT, 2008

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India and to campuses and centres established outside India in the SAARC region

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to give effect to the Agreement for the establishment of the South Asian University. It aims to incorporate the University, define its objectives, powers, and governance structure, and provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, including promoting knowledge, regional peace, and capacity building in South Asian nations.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its geographical extent, and the commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Provisions of Agreement to have force of law.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of the Agreement set out in the Schedule shall have the force of law in India.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of South Asian University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the South Asian University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, with its headquarters in Delhi.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Defines the geographical jurisdiction of the University, extending to India and campuses/centres in the SAARC region.

key_sections.title: Governing Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Governing Board of the University, its composition, and responsibilities for policies and management.

key_sections.title: Objectives of University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary objectives of the University, including dissemination of knowledge, promoting innovation, capacity building, fostering civic sense, and strengthening regional consciousness.

key_sections.title: Powers of University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers of the University, such as providing instruction, conducting research, granting degrees, establishing centres, and managing its affairs.

key_sections.title: University open to all persons.
key_sections.description: Declares the University open to all persons irrespective of gender, caste, creed, disability, ethnicity or socio-economic background, prohibiting religious tests.

key_sections.title: Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the Foreign Minister of the current Chair of SAARC as the Visitor of the University and outlines their powers.

key_sections.title: President and its powers.
key_sections.description: Details the appointment process and powers of the President as the Chief Executive Officer of the University.

key_sections.title: Privileges and immunities of President and academic staff.
key_sections.description: Grants privileges and immunities to the University, President, and academic staff as notified under the United Nations (Privileges and Immunities) Act, 1947.

key_sections.title: Authorities of University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities of the University, including the Executive Council and Academic Council.

key_sections.title: Statutes.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Statutes may provide, including powers of authorities, appointment of staff, and establishment of faculties.

key_sections.title: Reference to SAARC Arbitration Council.
key_sections.description: Mandates that differences arising from the interpretation or application of the Agreement shall be referred to the SAARC Arbitration Council.

powers_conferred: To provide for instruction in such branches of learning as the University may, from time to time, determine and to make provisions for research and for the advancement and dissemination of knowledge
To establish such special centres and specialised laboratories and such other units for research and instruction as are necessary for the furtherance of its objects
To plan and prescribe courses of study for degrees, diplomas, certificates or for any other purpose
To grant, subject to such conditions as the University may determine, diplomas or certificates and confer degrees or other academic distinctions
To confer honorary degrees or other distinctions
To organise and to undertake open learning programmes, extramural studies, training and extension services
To institute Chairs, principalships, professorships, readerships and lecturerships and other teaching and academic positions, required by the University and to appoint persons to such positions
To appoint visiting professors, Emeritus professors, consultants, scholars and such other persons who may contribute to the advancement of the objects of the University
To recognise persons as Professors, Readers or Lecturers or otherwise as teachers of the University
To create administrative and other posts as the University may deem necessary from time to time and to make appointments thereto
To lay down conditions of service of all categories of employees, including their code of conduct
To establish and maintain campuses, Centres, Regional Centres as may be determined from time to time
To admit to its privileges institutions situated within its jurisdiction as the University institutions and to withdraw all or any of those privileges
To co-operate or collaborate or associate with any other University or authority or institution of higher learning or any other public or private body
To determine standards of admission, including examination, evaluation or any other method of testing, to the University
To demand and receive payment of fees and other charges as may be prescribed
To establish Halls and to recognise, guide, supervise and control Halls not maintained by the University and other accommodation for students
To make arrangements for promoting health and general welfare of students and employees of the University
To regulate and enforce discipline among the students and the employees
To institute and award Fellowships, Scholarships, Studentships and prizes

To receive benefactions, donations and gifts and to acquire, hold, manage and dispose of any property, movable or immovable, including trust and endowment properties, for the purposes or objects of the University and to invest funds
To borrow, with the approval of the Governing Board, on the security of the University property, money for purposes of the University
To recognise for any purpose, either in whole or in part, any institution or members or students thereof
To enter into any agreement for the incorporation of any other institution in the University and for taking its rights, properties and liabilities
To make provision for research and advisory services and for that purpose to enter into such arrangements with other institutions or bodies
To provide for the printing, reproduction and publication of research and other work which may be issued by the University
To exercise such other powers accorded to it under the Agreement
To do all such other acts as may be necessary, incidental or conducive to the promotion of all or any of the objects of the University

related_acts: United Nations (Privileges and Immunities) Act, 1947 (46 of 1947)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Governing Board (President); University (teachers, academic staff, other employees)

applies_to: Whole of India
Campuses and centres established outside India in the SAARC region
All persons irrespective of gender, caste, creed, disability, ethnicity or socio-economic background
special_provisions: Privileges and immunities for President and academic staff under the United Nations (Privileges and Immunities) Act, 1947
University and its campuses/centres exempted from direct and indirect taxes and duties in the state where located
Employees from countries other than the host country will be governed by income-tax laws of their home countries and not taxed by the host country

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Governing Board (Statutes, Regulations); Chief Executive Officer of the Project Office (First Regulations); Authorities of the University (Bye-laws); Central Government (Power to remove difficulties)
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Statutes, Regulations, and bye-laws to be published in Official Gazette and laid before Parliament. Central Government has power to remove difficulties.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: SAARC Arbitration Council (for Agreement interpretation/application); Tribunal for Arbitration (for employee/student disputes)

schedules_summary.description: Contains the provisions of the Agreement for the establishment of the South Asian University that have the force of law in India. It details the establishment, objectives, funding, fiscal status (tax exemptions), governance structure, visa and resident permit provisions, and recognition of degrees.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL JUTE BOARD ACT, 2008

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Textiles

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of a National Jute Board for the development of the cultivation, manufacture and marketing of jute and jute products and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the establishment of a National Jute Board. Its primary purpose is to promote the development of the cultivation, manufacture, and marketing of jute and jute products. This includes measures to improve quality, enhance productivity, stabilize prices, and develop markets for jute.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution and incorporation of Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes the National Jute Board as a body corporate and outlines its composition and head office.

key_sections.title: Functions of Board.
key_sections.description: Details the duties and measures the Board may undertake to promote the development of jute and jute products.

key_sections.title: The Council and Society to vest in Board.
key_sections.description: Stipulates the transfer and vesting of the Jute Manufactures Development Council and the National Centre for Jute Diversification in the newly constituted Board.

key_sections.title: Provisions in respect of officers and other employees of Council and Society.
key_sections.description: Outlines the terms and conditions for the transfer of employees from the erstwhile Council and Society to the Board.

key_sections.title: Directions by Central Government.
key_sections.description: States that the Board shall be bound by policy directions issued by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Supersession of Board.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to supersede the Board under certain circumstances.

key_sections.title: Grants and loans by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Provides for grants and loans from the Central Government to the Board and establishes the Jute Board Fund.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Board to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Act 28 of 1983.
key_sections.description: Details specific amendments made to the Jute Manufactures Cess Act, 1983.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Jute Manufactures Development Council Act, 1983, and includes savings provisions.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint Secretary and other officers/employees for the Board (Section 4).
Central Government: To give directions on questions of policy to the Board (Section 12).
Central Government: To supersede the Board under specific conditions (Section 13).
Central Government: To make grants and loans to the Board (Section 14).
Central Government: To make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (Section 21).
Central Government: To remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions (Section 24).
Board: To acquire, hold, and dispose of property, both movable and immovable, and to contract, and to sue and be sued (Section 3).
Board: To promote the development of jute and jute products through various measures (Section 5).
Board: To make regulations consistent with the Act and rules (Section 22).
Chairperson: To preside over Board meetings and exercise powers and duties assigned by the Board or as prescribed (Section 3(7)).
Vice-Chairperson: To exercise powers and perform functions as prescribed or delegated by the Chairperson (Section 3(8)).

repealed_acts: Jute Manufactures Development Council Act, 1983 (27 of 1983)
related_acts: Jute Manufactures Development Council Act, 1983 (27 of 1983)
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 (27 of 2006)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government has the power to appoint the Secretary and other officers and employees of the Board (Section 4). The Central Government also nominates various members to the Board (Section 3(4)(e), (f), (g), (h), (i), (j), (k), (l), (m)). The Board elects a Vice-Chairperson from among its members (Section 3(8)).

applies_to: Whole of India
Persons and entities involved in the cultivation, manufacture, and marketing of jute and jute products.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the functions and duties of the National Jute Board, which is bound by directions from the Central Government. The Central Government also has powers of supersession over the Board.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL CAPITAL TERRITORY OF DELHI LAWS (SPECIAL PROVISIONS) ACT, 2009
act_identification.act_short_title: National Capital Territory of Delhi Laws (Special Provisions) Act, 2009

act_overview.purpose: The Act makes special provisions for the National Capital Territory of Delhi for a temporary period up to December 31, 2009. Its main objective is to provide temporary relief and minimize hardships to people against punitive action for encroachment or unauthorized development, while the Central Government finalizes policies and strategies for orderly urban development and regularization.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, commencement and duration.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, deemed commencement date, and the temporary duration of the Act until December 31, 2009.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'building bye-laws', 'encroachment', 'local authority', 'Master Plan', and 'unauthorised development'.

key_sections.title: Enforcement to be kept in abeyance.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to finalize policies and strategies for various types of unauthorized developments and keeps punitive action in abeyance until December 31, 2009, maintaining status quo as on January 1, 2006, or March 31, 2002, for specific cases.

key_sections.title: Provisions of this Act not to apply in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Specifies categories of encroachment or unauthorized development for which the temporary relief under Section 3 will not be available, such as certain public land encroachments and clearances for specific public projects.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to give directions.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue directions to local authorities for giving effect to the provisions of this Act, making it a duty for local authorities to comply.

key_sections.title: Validation of acts done or omitted to be done, etc., during 1st January, 2009 up to the date of commencement of this Act.
key_sections.description: Validates all actions taken or omitted between January 1, 2009, and the Act's commencement date, deeming them to be in conformity with the Act's provisions as if they were in force during that period.

powers_conferred: Central Government to take all possible measures to finalise norms, policy guidelines, feasible strategies and make orderly arrangements to deal with the problem of encroachment or unauthorised development (Section 3(1)).
Central Government to withdraw the exemption by notification in respect of encroachment or unauthorised development (Section 3(4)).
Central Government to issue directions to the local authorities for giving effect to the provisions of this Act (Section 5).

related_acts: New Delhi Municipal Council Act, 1994 (44 of 1994)
National Capital Territory of Delhi Laws (Special Provisions) Act, 2007 (43 of 2007)

applies_to: National Capital Territory of Delhi
Slum dwellers and Jhuggi-Jhompri clusters
Hawkers and urban street vendors
Unauthorised colonies
Village abadi area (including urban villages) and its extension
Existing farm houses involving construction beyond permissible building limits

Schools, dispensaries, religious institutions, cultural institutions, storages, warehouses and godowns used for agricultural inputs or produce (including dairy and poultry) in rural areas built on agricultural land
exemptions: Encroachment on public land except in those cases covered under clauses (a), (b) and (c) of sub-section (1) of section 3.

Removal of slums and Jhuggi-Jhompri dwellers, hawkers and urban street vendors, unauthorised colonies or part thereof, village abadi area (including urban villages) and its extension in accordance with relevant policies approved by the Central Government for clearance of land required for specific public projects.
special_provisions: Temporary relief and abeyance of punitive action against encroachment or unauthorised development until December 31, 2009.

Maintenance of status quo as on January 1, 2006, for encroachment or unauthorised development, and as on March 31, 2002 (with construction up to February 8, 2007) for unauthorised colonies and village abadi areas.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act suspends punitive action by local authorities against specified unauthorized developments. The Central Government is responsible for finalizing policies and issuing directions to local authorities for implementation.

act_identification.act_title: THE PREVENTION AND CONTROL OF INFECTIOUS AND CONTAGIOUS DISEASES IN ANIMALS ACT, 2009
act_identification.act_short_title: The Prevention and Control of Infectious and Contagious Diseases in Animals Act, 2009

legislative_details.geographical_extent: all the States and Union territories except the State of Uttar Pradesh

act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to prevent, control, and eradicate infectious and contagious diseases in animals across India. It seeks to prevent the inter-state spread of such diseases, mitigate economic losses, and fulfill international obligations related to the import and export of animals and animal products. The legislation emphasizes a national approach with active State Government involvement and adherence to international animal health standards.

chapter_titles: PRECAUTIONARY MEASURES ON CAUSATIVE ORGANISM, ETC.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application, and the process for its commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'animal', 'scheduled disease', 'Veterinary Officer', etc.

key_sections.title: Reporting scheduled diseases obligatory.
key_sections.description: Mandates owners, NGOs, public bodies, and village panchayats to report suspected scheduled diseases to Veterinarians and Village Officers.

key_sections.title: Notification of controlled areas and free areas.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to declare controlled areas for disease prevention and free areas when diseases are no longer prevalent, requiring compulsory vaccination in controlled areas.

key_sections.title: Entry and exit of animals into controlled area and free area.
key_sections.description: Regulates the movement of animals into and out of controlled and free areas, with specific provisions for vaccinated animals and railway carriage.

key_sections.title: Declaration of infected areas.
key_sections.description: Allows a Veterinary Officer to declare an area as infected if an animal is found or suspected to be infected with a scheduled disease.

key_sections.title: Resort to euthanasia for infected animals.
key_sections.description: Authorizes a Veterinary Officer to order euthanasia for infected animals to prevent disease spread or protect public health.

key_sections.title: Penalty for issuing vaccination certificate without authority or administering defective vaccine.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals who issue unauthorized or defective vaccination certificates.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Outlines general penalties for contravening the Act's provisions or obstructing Competent Officers.

key_sections.title: Penalty for placing infected animal or carcass in river, etc.
key_sections.description: Imposes penalties for disposing of infected animal carcasses in water bodies.

key_sections.title: Prevention of escape of causative organism.
key_sections.description: Requires institutions involved in vaccine/diagnostic research to take precautionary measures to prevent the escape of causative organisms and mandates euthanasia for certain animals.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for implementing the Act, including specifics on vaccination certificates, carcass disposal, and post-mortem procedures.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
