key_sections.description: Repeals the Glanders and Farcy Act, 1899, and the Dourine Act, 1910, along with inconsistent State laws, while providing for savings of previous actions.

powers_conferred: State Government to appoint Veterinarians and Veterinary Officers (Section 3)
State Government to declare controlled areas and free areas (Section 6)
Director to prohibit movement of animals (Section 7)
Director to establish Quarantine Camps and Check Posts (Section 14)
Competent Officer to relax prohibition on markets/fairs (Section 12)
Veterinary Officer or Competent Officer to enter and inspect land, building, vessel or vehicle (Section 19)
Veterinary Officer to declare infected areas (Section 20)
Veterinarian to direct segregation and treatment of infected animals (Section 23)
Veterinary Officer to draw samples from animals (Section 24)
Veterinary Officer to direct euthanasia for infected animals (Section 25)
Veterinary Officer or Veterinarian to hold post-mortem examinations (Section 27)
Veterinary Officer or Competent Officer to seize and remove certain animals (Section 28)
Central Government to amend the Schedule (Section 38)
Central Government to issue directions to State Government or other authorities (Section 39)
Central Government to remove difficulties (Section 41)
Central Government to make rules (Section 42)
State Government to make rules (Section 43)
State Government to delegate powers (Section 36)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for various offences, including issuing vaccination certificates without authority or with defective vaccine (fine of five thousand rupees or one month imprisonment for first offence, ten thousand rupees or three months for subsequent offences), general contravention of the Act or obstruction of officers (fine up to one thousand rupees or one month imprisonment for first offence, two thousand rupees or two months for subsequent offences), and placing infected animal carcasses in water bodies (fine of two thousand rupees or one month imprisonment for first offence, five thousand rupees or three months imprisonment or both for subsequent conviction). Companies committing offences are also liable, with provisions for directors, managers, etc., to be held responsible.

repealed_acts: The Glanders and Farcy Act, 1899 (13 of 1899)
The Dourine Act, 1910 (5 of 1910)
any other corresponding law of any State

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government appoints Veterinarians and Veterinary Officers (Section 3) and Competent Officers (Section 17).

applies_to: Owners or persons in charge of animals
Non-governmental organisations
Public bodies
Village panchayats
Veterinarians
Veterinary Officers
Common carriers (vessels, vehicles)
Institutions, laboratories, or clinics engaged in vaccine/diagnostic manufacture, testing, or research
exemptions: Movement of animals for vaccination purposes (Section 7(3)(a))
Movement of animals accompanied by a valid vaccination certificate (Section 7(3)(b))
Carriage by railway of animals through a controlled or infected area, provided the animal is not unloaded within that area (Section 10(4))
special_provisions: The Act shall come into force in all the States and Union territories except the State of Uttar Pradesh.
Different dates may be appointed for different States or for different areas therein as well as for different provisions of this Act.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement involves mandatory reporting of scheduled diseases, segregation of infected animals, declaration of controlled and infected areas, compulsory vaccination, regulation of animal movement through check posts and quarantine camps, inspection powers, euthanasia for infected animals, proper carcass disposal, and post-mortem examinations. Village officers and various government departments are mandated to assist. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The Act refers to recovery of costs in the manner provided by the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for recovery of fines imposed by a Court, and mentions 'conviction' for certain offences, implying jurisdiction of criminal courts.

schedules_summary.description: Lists various scheduled diseases, categorized by the species they affect, including multiple species diseases, cattle diseases, sheep and goat diseases, equine diseases, swine diseases, avian diseases, lagomorph diseases, bee diseases, fish diseases, mollusc diseases, crustacean diseases, amphibian disease, and other diseases like Camel pox and Leishmaniosis.

act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL UNIVERSITIES ACT, 2009

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Various States and Union Territories of India, establishing universities with territorial jurisdictions as specified in the First Schedule, including 'Whole of India' for Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya, 'Whole of the State' for others, and specific divisions for some.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate universities for teaching and research in the various States and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to establish and incorporate universities across various States for teaching and research. Its primary objectives include disseminating knowledge, promoting innovation in education, training manpower, fostering industry linkages, and improving the social, economic, intellectual, academic, and cultural welfare of the people.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act and its Statutes.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Universities.
key_sections.description: Details the establishment of various universities, including the conversion of existing ones and the creation of new ones, specifying their names and territorial jurisdictions.

key_sections.title: Objects of University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the core objectives of the universities, such as knowledge dissemination, research, innovation in teaching, manpower training, and social welfare.

key_sections.title: Powers of University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers vested in the University, including granting degrees, conducting research, establishing academic positions, and managing finances.

key_sections.title: University open to all castes, creed, race or class.
key_sections.description: Ensures non-discrimination in admission and employment based on caste, creed, race, or class, while allowing special provisions for certain disadvantaged groups.

key_sections.title: Visitor of University.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor and defines the Visitor's powers, including review, inspection, and issuing directions.

key_sections.title: Officers of University.
key_sections.description: Lists the designated officers of the University, such as Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, and Finance Officer.

key_sections.title: Authorities of University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities governing the University, including the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council.

key_sections.title: Powers to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Statutes can be made, covering the constitution of authorities, appointment of officers, and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Details the matters for which Ordinances can be made, such as student admission, courses of study, examinations, and fees.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees, etc.
key_sections.description: Mandates written contracts for employees and provides for arbitration in disputes between the University and its employees.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act within a specified period.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Central Universities Ordinance, 2009, and includes savings clauses for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

powers_conferred: University: To provide instruction, grant degrees, organize extramural studies, confer honorary degrees, provide distance education, institute teaching positions, recognize institutions, appoint teachers, create administrative posts, cooperate with other institutions, establish centers, award fellowships, maintain colleges, conduct research, organize refresher courses, appoint visiting professors, confer autonomous status, determine admission standards, demand fees, supervise student residences, lay down service conditions, regulate discipline, promote employee welfare, receive benefactions, borrow money.

Visitor (President of India): To review work and progress, issue directions, cause inspections or inquiries, annul proceedings, appoint Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor (as per Statutes), appoint first officers and members of authorities during transition.

Executive Council: To manage and administer revenues and property, create teaching and academic posts, appoint staff, grant leave, regulate discipline, manage finances, fix expenditure limits, invest money, transfer property, provide infrastructure, enter contracts, redress grievances, appoint examiners, select common seal, make special arrangements for women students, institute fellowships, appoint visiting professors, enter partnerships, make/amend/repeal Statutes and Ordinances.

Vice-Chancellor: To act as principal executive and academic officer, exercise general supervision, take immediate action in emergencies, review decisions of authorities, maintain discipline, convene meetings, make first Ordinances (with Executive Council approval).

Central Government: To specify headquarters of universities, receive annual reports and accounts, cause them to be laid before Parliament, require returns and information, declare Provident Funds Act applicable, remove difficulties.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act primarily deals with internal disciplinary actions against students and employees, including removal from rolls, debarment from examinations, suspension, censure, withholding of increment, and termination of employment for misconduct. It does not define specific criminal offences or prescribe monetary penalties in the typical sense of a penal code.

amended_acts: Madhya Pradesh Vishwavidyalaya Adhiniyam, 1973 (Madhya Pradesh Act 22 of 1973)
Uttar Pradesh State Universities Act, 1973 (President’s Act 10 of 1973)
repealed_acts: Central Universities Ordinance, 2009 (Ord. 3 of 2009)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor (President of India) appoints the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and during transitional periods, the first Registrar, Finance Officer, and members of the Court, Executive Council, and Academic Council. The Executive Council appoints the Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, Librarian, teachers, academic staff, administrative/ministerial posts, and Proctor. The Vice-Chancellor appoints Deans of Schools.

applies_to: Universities established and incorporated under this Act
Officers, employees, and students of these Universities
Existing universities converted under this Act (Guru Ghasidas Vishwavidyalaya, Doctor Harisingh Gour Vishwavidyalaya, Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University)
special_provisions: Special provision with respect to the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir (Section 3A)
Special provision with respect to State of Bihar (Section 3B)
Establishment of Central University of Andhra Pradesh (Section 3C)
Establishment of Central Tribal University of Andhra Pradesh (Section 3D)
Establishment of Sindhu Central University (Section 3E)
Establishment of Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya in Gujarat (Section 3F)
Establishment of Sammakka Sarakka Central Tribal University (Section 3G)

Special provision for the employment or admission of women, persons with disabilities, or persons belonging to the weaker sections of the society, and in particular, of the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes and the other socially and educationally backward classes of citizens (Section 7 proviso)
Transitional provisions for the appointment of first officers and constitution of first authorities (Section 44)

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Executive Council, Academic Council, and other authorities of the University have powers to make Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations. The Visitor also has powers to assent to, withhold assent from, or direct the making of Statutes. The Vice-Chancellor makes the first Ordinances with Executive Council approval.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through the various authorities of the University, including the Visitor, Executive Council, Academic Council, and Vice-Chancellor. It involves review of work, inspections, inquiries, issuing directions, disciplinary actions against employees and students, and arbitration for disputes.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: While civil courts are generally excluded for matters decided by arbitration tribunals, judicial remedies available under Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution are preserved. No specific courts are given exclusive jurisdiction for all matters under the Act.

schedules_summary.description: Lists the names of States, the names of the Universities established under the Act, and their respective territorial jurisdictions.

Contains the initial Statutes of the University, detailing the appointment, powers, and duties of various officers (Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, etc.) and the constitution, powers, and functions of authorities (Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Finance Committee, Selection Committees, etc.). It also covers conditions of service, discipline, and other administrative matters.

act_identification.act_title: THE RIGHT OF CHILDREN TO FREE AND COMPULSORY EDUCATION ACT, 2009
act_identification.act_short_title: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years.
act_overview.purpose: To provide for free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years.

chapter_titles: RIGHT TO FREE AND COMPULSORY EDUCATION
DUTIES OF APPROPRIATE GOVERNMENT, LOCAL AUTHORITY AND PARENTS
CURRICULUM AND COMPLETION OF ELEMENTARY EDUCATION

key_definitions: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
State Commission for Protection of Child Rights

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical extent, application, and commencement date, with exemptions for religious institutions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'child', 'elementary education', and 'school'.

key_sections.title: Right of child to free and compulsory education.
key_sections.description: Establishes the right of every child aged six to fourteen years to free and compulsory education in a neighbourhood school, including provisions for children with disabilities.

key_sections.title: Duties of appropriate Government.
key_sections.description: Outlines the responsibilities of the appropriate Government, including providing free and compulsory education, ensuring neighbourhood schools, and providing infrastructure.

key_sections.title: Duty of parents and guardian.
key_sections.description: Mandates that every parent or guardian admit their child or ward to an elementary education in the neighbourhood school.

key_sections.title: Extent of school’s responsibility for free and compulsory education.
key_sections.description: Details the responsibilities of different types of schools (government, aided, specified category, unaided) in providing free and compulsory elementary education, including admission quotas for disadvantaged groups.

key_sections.title: No capitation fee and screening procedure for admission.
key_sections.description: Prohibits schools from collecting capitation fees or subjecting children/parents to screening procedures for admission, and prescribes penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Examination and holding back in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Mandates regular examinations in fifth and eighth classes, provides for re-examination, and allows appropriate Government to permit holding back a child in certain cases, while prohibiting expulsion till elementary education completion.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of physical punishment and mental harassment to child.
key_sections.description: Prohibits physical punishment and mental harassment of children and specifies disciplinary action for contravention.

key_sections.title: No school to be established without obtaining certificate of recognition.
key_sections.description: Requires schools (other than government-owned) to obtain a certificate of recognition and outlines procedures for granting and withdrawing recognition, with penalties for non-compliance.

key_sections.title: Norms and standards for school.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that schools must fulfill norms and standards specified in the Schedule for establishment or recognition, with provisions for existing schools to comply within a timeframe.

key_sections.title: School Management Committee.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of School Management Committees (SMCs) in certain schools, specifying their composition and functions, including monitoring and preparing development plans.

key_sections.title: Qualifications for appointment and terms and conditions of service of teachers.
key_sections.description: Sets minimum qualifications for teachers, allows for relaxation by the Central Government, and addresses salary, allowances, and service conditions.

key_sections.title: Monitoring of child’s right to education.
key_sections.description: Assigns monitoring functions related to the right to education to the National and State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights.

key_sections.title: Power of appropriate Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the appropriate Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, detailing specific matters for which rules can be made.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To amend the Schedule (Section 20).
Central Government: To remove difficulties in implementing the Act (Section 39).
Central Government: To issue guidelines to appropriate Government or local authority (Section 35(1)).
Central Government: To authorize an academic authority for laying down minimum qualifications for teachers (Section 23(1)).
Central Government: To relax minimum qualifications for teachers for a specified period (Section 23(2)).
Appropriate Government: To establish schools (Section 6).
Appropriate Government: To provide free and compulsory elementary education (Section 8).
Appropriate Government: To provide for pre-school education (Section 11).
Appropriate Government: To make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act (Section 38).
Appropriate Government: To issue guidelines and directions to local authority or School Management Committee (Section 35(2)).
Appropriate Government: To specify an academic authority for laying down curriculum and evaluation procedure (Section 29(1)).
Local Authority: To establish schools (Section 6).
Local Authority: To provide free and compulsory elementary education (Section 9).
Local Authority: To issue guidelines and directions to the School Management Committee (Section 35(3)).
Prescribed authority (under Section 18): To issue or withdraw certificate of recognition for schools.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Collection of capitation fee (fine up to ten times the fee charged) or subjecting a child to screening procedure (fine up to twenty-five thousand rupees for first contravention, fifty thousand for subsequent) under Section 13(2). Establishing or running a school without recognition or continuing after withdrawal of recognition is punishable with a fine up to one lakh rupees, and ten thousand rupees for each day of continuing contravention under Section 18(5) and Section 19(5). Physical punishment or mental harassment to a child leads to disciplinary action under service rules applicable to the person under Section 17(2).

related_acts: Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 (1 of 1996)
National Trust for Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and Multiple Disabilities Act, 1999 (44 of 1999)
Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005 (4 of 2006)
Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act, 1886 (6 of 1886)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints members of the National Advisory Council. State Government appoints members of the State Advisory Council. An academic authority authorized by the Central Government lays down minimum qualifications for teachers. The appropriate Government specifies the academic authority for curriculum and evaluation procedure.
regulatory_bodies: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
State Commission for Protection of Child Rights

applies_to: All children of the age of six to fourteen years
exemptions: Madrasas
Vedic Pathsalas
Educational institutions primarily imparting religious instruction
special_provisions: Special provisions for children not admitted to, or who have not completed, elementary education (Section 4).
Special provisions for children with disability (Section 3(3)).
Proportionate representation for parents/guardians of children belonging to disadvantaged group and weaker section in School Management Committee (Section 21(1)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Monitoring by National and State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (Section 31). Grievance redressal by local authority with appeal to State Commission (Section 32). Disciplinary action against teachers for contravention of duties or physical punishment/mental harassment (Sections 17(2), 24(2)). Fines for collecting capitation fees, screening procedures, or operating schools without recognition (Sections 13, 18, 19). Prosecution for certain offences requires previous sanction of an authorized officer (Section 36).

schedules_summary.description: Contains norms and standards for a school, including: numbers of teachers (Pupil-Teacher Ratio) for different classes, building requirements (all-weather building, barrier-free access, separate toilets, drinking water, kitchen, playground, boundary wall), minimum number of working days/instructional hours in an academic year, minimum working hours per week for teachers, teaching learning equipment, library, and play material, games and sports equipment.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL CAPITAL TERRITORY OF DELHI LAWS (SPECIAL PROVISIONS) SECOND ACT, 2009
act_identification.act_short_title: The National Capital Territory of Delhi Laws (Special Provisions) Second Act, 2009

act_overview.purpose: This Act makes special provisions for the National Capital Territory of Delhi for a further period up to December 31, 2010. Its main purpose is to provide temporary relief and minimize hardships to the people of Delhi against punitive actions by agencies concerning unauthorized developments, while the Central Government finalizes policies for regularization and planned development.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, commencement and duration.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official name, geographical applicability, effective date, and limited duration of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'building bye-laws', 'Delhi', 'encroachment', 'local authority', 'Master Plan', 'punitive action', and 'unauthorised development'.

key_sections.title: Enforcement to be kept in abeyance.
key_sections.description: Directs the Central Government to finalize policies for various unauthorized developments and mandates that punitive actions against such developments be suspended, maintaining status quo until December 31, 2010.

key_sections.title: Provisions of this Act not to apply in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Outlines specific types of encroachment or unauthorized development, including certain public land encroachments and removals for public projects, for which the relief provided by Section 3 will not be available.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to give directions.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to issue directions to local authorities for the effective implementation of the Act, making it mandatory for local authorities to comply.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To take all possible measures to finalise norms, policy guidelines, feasible strategies and make orderly arrangements to deal with the problem of encroachment or unauthorised development (Section 3(1)).
Central Government: To withdraw the exemption by notification in respect of encroachment or unauthorised development (Section 3(4)).
Central Government: To issue directions to the local authorities for giving effect to the provisions of this Act (Section 5).
Local authorities: Duty to comply with such directions issued by the Central Government (Section 5).

related_acts: National Capital Territory of Delhi Laws (Special Provisions) Act, 2007 (43 of 2007)
National Capital Territory of Delhi Laws (Special Provisions) Act, 2009 (24 of 2009)
New Delhi Municipal Council Act, 1994 (44 of 1994)

Slum dwellers and Jhuggi-Jhompri clusters
Hawkers and urban street vendors
Unauthorised colonies

Schools, dispensaries, religious institutions, cultural institutions, storages, warehouses and godowns used for agricultural inputs or produce (including dairy and poultry) in rural areas built on agricultural land

Removal of slums and Jhuggi-Jhompri dwellers, hawkers and urban street vendors, unauthorised colonies or part thereof, village abadi area (including urban villages) and its extension in accordance with relevant policies approved by the Central Government for clearance of land required for specific public projects.

act_identification.act_title: THE LEGAL METROLOGY ACT, 2009

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and enforce standards of weights and measures, regulate trade and commerce in weights, measures and other goods which are sold or distributed by weight, measure or number and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to establish and enforce standards of weights and measures. It aims to regulate trade and commerce involving weights, measures, and other goods sold or distributed by weight, measure, or number, ensuring accuracy and public guarantee.

chapter_titles: APPOINTMENT AND POWERS OF DIRECTOR, CONTROLLER AND LEGAL METROLOGY OFFICERS
VERIFICATION AND STAMPING OF WEIGHT OR MEASURE

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, and its commencement date as appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Controller', 'Director', 'Legal Metrology', 'manufacturer', 'pre-packaged commodity', and 'weight or measure'.

key_sections.title: Units of weights and measures to be based on metric system.
key_sections.description: Mandates that all units of weight or measure must conform to the metric system based on the international system of units.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of quotation, etc., otherwise than in terms of standard units of weight, measure or numeration.
key_sections.description: Prohibits quoting prices, issuing price lists, or indicating net quantity of pre-packaged commodities in terms other than standard units of weight, measure, or numeration, with an exception for exports.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Director, legal metrology officers and other employees.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to appoint a Director and other legal metrology officers for inter-State trade and commerce, defining their powers and duties.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Controller, legal metrology officers and other employees.
key_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to appoint a Controller and other legal metrology officers for intra-State trade and commerce, defining their powers and duties.

key_sections.title: Power of inspection, seizure, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to the Director, Controller, or legal metrology officers to inspect premises, search, and seize non-compliant weights, measures, or related documents.

key_sections.title: Declarations on prepackaged commodities.
key_sections.description: Requires manufacturers, packers, sellers, and importers to ensure pre-packaged commodities are in standard quantities and bear prescribed declarations and particulars.

key_sections.title: Prohibition on manufacture, repair or sale of weight or measure without licence.
key_sections.description: Prohibits manufacturing, repairing, or selling any weight or measure without a valid licence issued by the Controller.

key_sections.title: Verification and stamping of weight or measure.
key_sections.description: Mandates verification and stamping of weights and measures used in transactions or for protection, on payment of prescribed fees, and allows for verification through Government approved Test Centres.

key_sections.title: Penalty for use of non-standard weight or measure.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including fines, for using or keeping for use any weight or measure that does not conform to the specified standards.

key_sections.title: Compounding of offences.
key_sections.description: Allows for the compounding of certain offences under the Act, either before or after prosecution, upon payment of a prescribed sum.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies and power of court to publish name, place of business, etc., for companies convicted.
key_sections.description: Addresses offences committed by companies, holding responsible the nominated person or those in charge, and allows courts to publish details of convicted companies.

key_sections.title: Power of the Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, covering various specific matters.

key_sections.title: Repeal of the Standards of Weights and Measures Act, 1976 and Standards of Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1985.
key_sections.description: Repeals the previous Standards of Weights and Measures Act, 1976 and the Standards of Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1985, while ensuring continuity of existing notifications, rules, and orders.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint Director and legal metrology officers, specify their local limits, delegate powers, make rules, prepare objects or equipments for deriving unit values, prescribe specifications for units, notify Government approved Test Centres.
State Government: Appoint Controller and legal metrology officers, specify their local limits, make rules, notify Government approved Test Centres.

Director/Controller/Legal Metrology Officer: Inspect premises, search, seize weights, measures, goods, records, registers, or documents, require production of documents, dispose of perishable seized goods.
Controller: Issue licences for manufacturing, repairing, or selling weights or measures.
Appellate Authority: Hear appeals against decisions or orders made under the Act.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines various offences including using or keeping non-standard weights/measures, altering weights/measures to deceive, manufacturing/selling non-standard weights/measures, making transactions in contravention of standards, quoting non-standard units, delivering less quantity or rendering less service, non-production of documents, failure to get models approved, using unverified weights/measures, selling non-standard packages, contraventions by Government approved Test Centres, non-registration by importers, importing non-standard weights/measures, obstructing officers, giving false information, and counterfeiting seals/stamps. Penalties range from fines (up to five lakh rupees) to imprisonment (up to five years), with enhanced penalties for second and subsequent offences.

repealed_acts: The Standards of Weights and Measures Act, 1976 (60 of 1976)
Standards of Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1985 (54 of 1985)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Director of legal metrology, Additional Director, Joint Director, Deputy Director, Assistant Director and other employees. The State Government appoints the Controller of legal metrology, Additional Controller, Joint Controller, Deputy Controller, Assistant Controller, Inspector and other employees.

applies_to: Whole of India
Persons involved in inter-State trade and commerce of weights and measures
Persons involved in intra-State trade and commerce of weights and measures
Manufacturers of weights or measures
Repairers of weights or measures
Dealers of weights or measures
Importers of weights or measures
Persons manufacturing, packing, selling, importing, distributing, delivering, offering, exposing or possessing for sale any pre-packaged commodity
exemptions: Manufacture of weights or measures exclusively for export or for scientific investigation or research (from standard conformity for manufacture/import)
Export of any goods, things or service (from prohibition of non-standard unit quotation)
Weights or measures used in any factory exclusively engaged in the manufacture of arms, ammunition or both, for the use of the Armed Forces of the Union (from verification and stamping)
Weights or measures used for scientific investigation or for research (from verification and stamping)
Weights or measures manufactured exclusively for export (from verification and stamping)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through inspection, search, and seizure powers granted to the Director, Controller, and legal metrology officers. The Act prescribes various penalties for contraventions, allows for compounding of certain offences, and outlines procedures for offences committed by companies. Appeals against decisions or orders can be made to the Director, Central Government, Controller, or State Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts are empowered to deal with offences, including publishing names of convicted companies. Searches and seizures are to be carried out in accordance with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Appellate authorities are specified for appeals against decisions of legal metrology officers, Director, and Controller.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL GREEN TRIBUNAL ACT, 2010

act_overview.preamble:
An Act to provide for the establishment of a National Green Tribunal for the effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources including enforcement of any legal right relating to environment and giving relief and compensation for damages to persons and property and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
AND WHEREAS India is a party to the decisions taken at the United Nations Conference on the Human
Environment held at Stockholm in June, 1972, in which India participated, calling upon the States to take
appropriate steps for the protection and improvement of the human environment;
AND WHEREAS decisions were taken at the United Nations Conference on Environment and
Development held at Rio de Janeiro in June, 1992, in which India participated, calling upon the States to
provide effective access to judicial and administrative proceedings, including redress and remedy and to
develop national laws regarding liability and compensation for the victims of pollution and other
environmental damage;
AND WHEREAS in the judicial pronouncement in India, the right to healthy environment has been
construed as a part of the right to life under article 21 of the Constitution;
AND WHEREAS it is considered expedient to implement the decisions taken at the aforesaid
conferences and to have a National Green Tribunal in view of the involvement of multi-disciplinary
issues relating to the environment.
act_overview.purpose: To establish a National Green Tribunal for the effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection, conservation of forests and other natural resources. It aims to enforce legal rights related to the environment and provide relief and compensation for damages to persons and property.

chapter_titles: JURISDICTION, POWERS AND PROCEEDINGS OF THE TRIBUNAL

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines various terms used throughout the Act, such as 'accident', 'environment', 'hazardous substance', and 'Tribunal'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to establish the National Green Tribunal by notification.

key_sections.title: Qualifications for appointment of Chairperson, Judicial Member and Expert Member.
key_sections.description: Lays down the eligibility criteria for the appointment of the Chairperson, Judicial Members, and Expert Members of the Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Tribunal to settle disputes.
key_sections.description: Grants the Tribunal jurisdiction over all civil cases involving a substantial question relating to the environment arising from enactments specified in Schedule I.

key_sections.title: Relief, compensation and restitution.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Tribunal to provide relief and compensation to victims of pollution and environmental damage, and for restitution of damaged property or environment.

key_sections.title: Tribunal to have appellate jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Confers appellate jurisdiction on the Tribunal to hear appeals against orders or decisions made under various specified environmental acts.

key_sections.title: Procedure and powers of Tribunal.
key_sections.description: States that the Tribunal is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure or the Indian Evidence Act but is guided by natural justice, and outlines its powers as a civil court.

key_sections.title: Tribunal to apply certain principles.
key_sections.description: Directs the Tribunal to apply the principles of sustainable development, the precautionary principle, and the polluter pays principle in its decisions.

key_sections.title: Appeal to Supreme Court.
key_sections.description: Allows any person aggrieved by an award, decision, or order of the Tribunal to file an appeal to the Supreme Court.

key_sections.title: Penalty for failure to comply with orders of Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for individuals and companies failing to comply with the Tribunal's orders, awards, or decisions.

key_sections.title: Bar of jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Bars civil courts from entertaining matters that the Tribunal is empowered to determine under its appellate or original jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall have overriding effect over any inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995, and the National Environment Appellate Authority Act, 1997, and includes savings provisions.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Establish the Tribunal (Section 3), appoint Chairperson, Judicial Members and Expert Members (Section 6), determine nature and categories of staff (Section 12), make rules (Section 35), amend Schedule I (Section 34), remove difficulties (Section 37).

Tribunal: Settle disputes (Section 14), provide relief, compensation and restitution (Section 15), exercise appellate jurisdiction (Section 16), regulate its own procedure (Section 19), exercise powers of a civil court (Section 19), execute awards or orders or decisions (Section 25).
Chairperson: Exercise financial and administrative powers (Section 13), delegate financial and administrative powers (Section 13), recruit officers and other employees (Section 12).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Failure to comply with any order, award or decision of the Tribunal is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine which may extend to ten crore rupees, or with both. In case of continuing failure, an additional fine of twenty-five thousand rupees per day applies after conviction. For companies, the fine may extend to twenty-five crore rupees, with an additional fine of one lakh rupees per day for continuing contravention. Offences by companies and Government Departments are also addressed, holding responsible persons accountable.

amended_acts: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 (6 of 1974)
The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977 (36 of 1977)
The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 (14 of 1981)
repealed_acts: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 (27 of 1995)
The National Environment Appellate Authority Act, 1997 (22 of 1997)
related_acts: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 (6 of 1974)
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977 (36 of 1977)
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 (14 of 1981)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson, Judicial Members, and Expert Members. The Chairperson is appointed in consultation with the Chief Justice of India. Judicial and Expert Members are appointed on the recommendations of a Selection Committee.

applies_to: All civil cases where a substantial question relating to environment is involved, arising out of the implementation of enactments specified in Schedule I.
Victims of pollution and other environmental damage arising under the enactments specified in Schedule I.
Any person aggrieved by orders or decisions made under specific environmental acts listed in Section 16.
exemptions: Accidents by reason only of war or civil disturbance are excluded from the definition of 'accident'.

The two-year post-tenure employment restriction for Tribunal members does not apply to employment under the Central Government, a State Government, local authority, statutory authority, corporation, or a Government company.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Awards, orders, or decisions of the Tribunal are executable as a decree of a civil court. The Tribunal has the powers of a civil court for this purpose and may transmit orders to a civil court for execution. Unpaid amounts can be recovered as arrears of land revenue or public demand. Non-compliance with Tribunal orders is an offence punishable with imprisonment and/or fine.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Supreme Court (for appeals against Tribunal's orders). No civil court has jurisdiction over matters the Tribunal is empowered to determine. No court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act.

schedules_summary.description: Lists seven enactments under which the National Green Tribunal has jurisdiction for civil cases and environmental damage claims. These include The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977, The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981, The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, The Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991, and The Biological Diversity Act, 2002.

Specifies the various heads under which compensation or relief for damage may be claimed. These include death, permanent/temporary disability or injury, loss of wages, medical expenses, damages to private property, expenses incurred by government/local authority for relief and rehabilitation, compensation for environmental degradation and restoration, loss to government/local authority, harm to fauna and flora, damage to environment (pollution), loss of property, loss of business or employment, and other claims related to handling hazardous substances.

Details amendments to six specific enactments: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974; The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977; The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980; The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981; The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986; and The Biological Diversity Act, 2002. These amendments primarily involve inserting new sections to provide for appeals to the National Green Tribunal.

act_identification.act_title: THE CLINICAL ESTABLISHMENTS (REGISTRATION AND REGULATION) ACT, 2010
act_identification.act_short_title: The Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010.
act_identification.date_of_commencement: It shall come into force at once in the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Mizoram and Sikkim and the Union territories, on such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint and in any other State which adopts this Act under clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution, on the date of such adoption

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole of the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Mizoram and Sikkim and the Union territories; and it shall apply to such other State which adopts this Act by resolution passed in that behalf under clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the registration and regulation of clinical establishments in the country and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS, it is considered expedient to provide for the registration and regulation of clinical establishments with a view to prescribe minimum standards of facilities and services which may be provided by them so that mandate of article 47 of the Constitution for improvement in public health may be achieved; ANDWHEREAS, Parliament has no power to make laws for the States with respect to any of the matters aforesaid except as provided in articles 249 and 250 of the Constitution; ANDWHEREAS, in pursuance of clause (1) of article 252 of the Constitution, resolutions have been passed by all the Houses of the Legislatures of the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Mizoram and Sikkim to the effect that the matters aforesaid should be regulated in those States by Parliament by law;
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the registration and regulation of clinical establishments across the country. Its main objective is to prescribe minimum standards for facilities and services offered by these establishments to improve public health, in line with Article 47 of the Constitution.

chapter_titles: THE NATIONAL COUNCIL FOR CLINICAL ESTABLISHMENTS
REGISTRATION AND STANDARDS FOR CLINICAL ESTABLISHMENTS

key_definitions: to stabilise (with its grammatical variations and cognate expressions)

key_sections.title: Short title, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its initial geographical application, and conditions for its commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'clinical establishment', 'National Council', and 'recognised system of medicine'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of National Council.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of the National Council for clinical establishments and outlines its composition.

key_sections.title: Functions of National Council.

key_sections.title: State Council of clinical establishments.

key_sections.title: Registration for clinical establishments.
key_sections.description: Makes it mandatory for all clinical establishments to be duly registered in accordance with the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Condition for registration.
key_sections.description: Lays down the essential conditions for registration and continuation of clinical establishments, including minimum standards, personnel, records, and emergency medical care.

key_sections.title: Application for provisional certificate of registration.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for applying for a provisional certificate of registration for clinical establishments.

key_sections.title: Application for permanent registration.

key_sections.title: Cancellation of registration.

key_sections.title: Monetary penalty for non-registration.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to make rules.

powers_conferred: National Council: Compile and publish National Register, classify establishments, develop standards, collect statistics (Section 5).
National Council: Seek advice or assistance (Section 6).
State Government: Constitute State Council (Section 8).
State Government: Set up district registering authority (Section 10).

Authority: Issue duplicate certificates (Section 19).
Authority: Cancel registration (Section 32).

Serving in unregistered establishment: Monetary penalty up to twenty-five thousand rupees (Section 41(2)). Disobedience of direction, obstruction, refusal of information: Monetary penalty up to five lakh rupees (Section 42). Minor deficiencies: Fine up to ten thousand rupees (Section 43). Contravention by companies: Company and persons in charge liable to fine; directors/managers/officers also liable if with consent/connivance/neglect (Section 44). act_identification.act_title: THE LAND PORTS AUTHORITY OF INDIA ACT, 2010
act_identification.act_short_title: Land Ports Authority of India Act, 2010

legislative_details.geographical_extent: designated points along the international borders of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Land Ports Authority of India to put in place systems which address security imperatives and for the development and management of facilities for cross border movement of passengers and goods at designated points along the international borders of India and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Land Ports Authority of India to develop, sanitize, and manage facilities for cross-border movement of passengers and goods at designated points along India's international borders. Its primary objective is to address security imperatives and facilitate efficient border operations.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II THE LAND PORTS AUTHORITY OF INDIA

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Authority.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Land Ports Authority of India as a body corporate and details its composition, including the Chairperson and various members.

key_sections.title: Functions of Authority.

key_sections.title: Assets and liabilities to vest in Authority.

key_sections.title: Compulsory acquisition of land for Authority.

key_sections.title: Power of Authority to charge fees, rent, etc.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.

act_identification.act_title: THE NALANDA UNIVERSITY ACT, 2010

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of External Affairs, Ministry of Human Resource Development
legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India and to centres established within or outside India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to implement the decisions arrived at the Second East Asia Summit held on the 15th January, 2007, at Philippines and subsequently at the Fourth East Asia Summit held on the 25th October, 2009, at Thailand for the establishment of the Nalanda University in the State of Bihar as an international institution for pursuit of intellectual, philosophical, historical and spiritual studies and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS, the Second East Asia Summit held on the15th January, 2007 in the city of Cebu, Republic of Philippines, agreed to strengthen regional educational co-operation by tapping the East Asia Region’s centres of excellence in education and for the revival of the Nalanda University located in the State of Bihar to improve regional understanding and the appreciation of one another’s heritage and history; AND WHEREAS, the Fourth East Asia Summit held on the 25th October, 2009 in Hua Hin, Thailand, supported the establishment of the Nalanda University and encouraged the networking and collaboration between the proposed Nalanda University and existing centres of excellence in the East Asia Summit so as to participating countries to build a community of learning where students, scholars, researchers and academicians can work together symbolising the spirituality that unites all mankind; AND WHEREAS, it is considered expedient to make provision for implementing the decisions arrived at in the aforesaid East Asia Summits for establishment of the Nalanda University in the State of Bihar and declare it to be an institution of national importance.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to establish the Nalanda University in Bihar as an international institution for intellectual, philosophical, historical, and spiritual studies, implementing decisions from the East Asia Summits. It seeks to strengthen regional educational cooperation, improve understanding of heritage, and foster a community of learning among East Asian countries.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement.

key_sections.title: Declaration of Nalanda University as an institution of national importance.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Nalanda University.
key_sections.description: Establishes and incorporates the Nalanda University as a body corporate in the State of Bihar.

key_sections.title: Effect of establishment of University.
key_sections.description: Details the legal consequences of the University's establishment, including transfer of property, rights, liabilities, and continuity of employment.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Specifies that the University's jurisdiction extends to the whole of India and to centres established within or outside India.

key_sections.title: Governing Board.
key_sections.description: Constitutes the Governing Board of the University and outlines its composition.

key_sections.title: Objectives of University.
key_sections.description: Lays down the primary objectives of the University, including imparting education, research, and promoting regional peace.

key_sections.title: Powers of University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers vested in the University to achieve its objectives, such as granting degrees, establishing centres, and appointing staff.

key_sections.title: Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor and outlines the Visitor's powers to review, inspect, and issue directions.

key_sections.title: Officers of University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and Registrar.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities of the University, such as the Governing Board and Academic Council.

key_sections.title: Statutes.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which the Statutes of the University may provide.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees.
key_sections.description: Details the conditions of service for employees and provides for arbitration in case of disputes.

key_sections.title: Repeal of University of Nalanda Act.
key_sections.description: Repeals the University of Nalanda Act, 2007, and provides for transitional arrangements.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor has powers of review, inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions. The Vice-Chancellor has emergency powers. Disputes between the University and employees are referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration. Disciplinary cases against students have a procedure for appeal and arbitration. Employees and students have a right to appeal to the Governing Board. Annual reports and accounts are submitted to the Visitor and Parliament.

act_identification.act_title: THE CIVIL LIABILITY FOR NUCLEAR DAMAGE ACT, 2010
act_identification.act_short_title: The Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Extends to the whole of India, and also applies to nuclear damage suffered in or over the maritime areas beyond the territorial waters of India, in or over the exclusive economic zone of India, on board or by a ship registered in India, on board or by an aircraft registered in India, and on or by an artificial island, installation or structure under the jurisdiction of India. It applies only to nuclear installations owned or controlled by the Central Government either by itself or through any authority or corporation established by it or a Government company.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for civil liability for nuclear damage and prompt compensation to the victims of a nuclear incident through a no-fault liability regime channeling liability to the operator, appointment of Claims Commissioner, establishment of Nuclear Damage Claims Commission and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes a no-fault liability regime for nuclear damage, ensuring prompt compensation to victims of nuclear incidents. It provides for the appointment of a Claims Commissioner and the establishment of a Nuclear Damage Claims Commission to adjudicate claims and manage compensation.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II LIABILITY FOR NUCLEAR DAMAGE
CHAPTER V NUCLEAR DAMAGE CLAIMS COMMISSION

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's short title, geographical extent, application scope, and commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Liability of operator.
key_sections.description: Establishes the strict and no-fault liability of the operator for nuclear damage.

key_sections.title: Operator not liable in certain circumstances.
key_sections.description: Specifies circumstances under which an operator is not liable for nuclear damage.

key_sections.title: Limits of liability.
key_sections.description: Sets the maximum limits of liability for nuclear incidents.

key_sections.title: Liability of Central Government.
key_sections.description: Defines the liability of the Central Government for nuclear damage.

key_sections.title: Operator to maintain insurance or financial securities.
key_sections.description: Mandates operators to maintain insurance or financial securities to cover their liability.

key_sections.title: Compensation for nuclear damage and its adjudication.
key_sections.description: Establishes the right to claim compensation and provides for the appointment of Claims Commissioners.

key_sections.title: Operator's right of recourse.
key_sections.description: Outlines the operator's right of recourse against other parties after paying compensation.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Nuclear Damage Claims Commission.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the Nuclear Damage Claims Commission.

key_sections.title: Exclusion of jurisdiction of civil courts.
key_sections.description: Excludes the jurisdiction of civil courts in matters adjudicated by the Claims Commissioner or Commission.

key_sections.title: Offences and penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes offences and penalties for non-compliance with the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Act to be in addition to any other law.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act is in addition to, and not in derogation of, other laws.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To specify higher liability amount (Section 6(1)), assume full liability (Section 7(1) Proviso), establish Nuclear Liability Fund (Section 7(2)), appoint Claims Commissioners (Section 9(2)), establish Nuclear Damage Claims Commission (Section 19), provide officers and employees to Commission (Section 30(1)), dissolve Commission (Section 38(1)), issue directions (Section 43), call for information (Section 44), exempt nuclear installations (Section 45), make rules (Section 48), remove difficulties (Section 49).
Atomic Energy Regulatory Board: To notify nuclear incident (Section 3(1)), cause wide publicity (Section 3(2)).

Claims Commissioner: To adjudicate claims, follow prescribed procedure (Section 12(1)), associate experts (Section 12(2)), have powers of a civil court (Section 12(4)), invite applications for claims (Section 13), make awards (Section 16).

Nuclear Damage Claims Commission: To adjudicate claims (Section 32(1)), constitute benches (Section 32(3)), regulate its own procedure (Section 32(4)), have powers of a civil court (Section 32(5)), make awards (Section 32(6)).
Chairperson of Commission: Power of superintendence in general administration (Section 29).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever contravenes any rule or direction, fails to comply with insurance provisions (Section 8), or fails to deposit amount (Section 36) shall be punishable with imprisonment up to five years or fine or both. Whoever fails to comply with directions (Section 43) or obstructs authorities shall be punishable with imprisonment up to one year or fine or both. The Act also covers offences by companies (Section 40) and Government Departments (Section 41).

related_acts: Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976 (80 of 1976)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints Claims Commissioner (Section 9(2)), and the Chairperson and Members of the Commission (Section 20(1)).

applies_to: the whole of India
in or over the maritime areas beyond the territorial waters of India
in or over the exclusive economic zone of India
on board or by a ship registered in India
on board or by an aircraft registered in India
on or by an artificial island, installation or structure under the jurisdiction of India
nuclear installation owned or controlled by the Central Government either by itself or through any authority or corporation established by it or a Government company
exemptions: Operator not liable for damage caused by a grave natural disaster of an exceptional character or an act of armed conflict, hostility, civil war, insurrection or terrorism (Section 5(1)).

Operator not liable for damage to the nuclear installation itself, any other nuclear installation on the same site, any property on the same site used in connection with such installation, or the means of transport (Section 5(2)).
Operator not liable if nuclear damage is suffered by a person on account of their own negligence or acts of commission or omission (Section 5(3)).
Central Government may exempt any nuclear installation from the application of this Act if the risk involved is insignificant due to small quantity of nuclear material (Section 45).
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act to come into force (Section 1(5)).
The Central Government may, by notification, assume full liability for a nuclear installation not operated by it if it is deemed necessary in public interest (Section 7(1) Proviso).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through adjudication of claims by the Claims Commissioner and the Nuclear Damage Claims Commission. Unpaid award amounts are recoverable as arrears of land revenue. The Central Government has powers to issue directions and call for information. Offences are subject to penalties as prescribed in Chapter VI.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No civil court (except the Supreme Court and a High Court exercising jurisdiction under articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution) has jurisdiction over matters adjudicated under this Act. Offences under this Act shall be tried by a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class (Section 42).

act_identification.act_title: THE FOREIGN CONTRIBUTION (REGULATION) ACT, 2010

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India, and it shall also apply to— (a) citizens of India outside India; and (b) associate branches or subsidiaries, outside India, of companies or bodies corporate, registered or incorporated in India.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate the law to regulate the acceptance and utilisation of foreign contribution or foreign hospitality by certain individuals or associations or companies and to prohibit acceptance and utilisation of foreign contribution or foreign hospitality for any activities detrimental to the national interest and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act consolidates the law to regulate the acceptance and utilisation of foreign contribution and hospitality by individuals, associations, or companies. It aims to prohibit such acceptance and utilisation for any activities deemed detrimental to the national interest.

chapter_titles: REGULATION OF FOREIGN CONTRIBUTION AND FOREIGN HOSPITALITY
ACCOUNTS, INTIMATION, AUDIT AND DISPOSAL OF ASSETS, ETC.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, application to citizens and entities outside India, and the commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act, such as 'foreign contribution', 'foreign source', 'association', and 'political party'.

key_sections.title: Prohibition to accept foreign contribution.
key_sections.description: Prohibits certain persons, including candidates for election, public servants, judges, government servants, members of Legislature, and political parties, from accepting foreign contribution.

key_sections.title: Persons to whom section 3 shall not apply.
key_sections.description: Outlines specific circumstances under which the prohibition in Section 3 does not apply, such as acceptance of salary, payments in ordinary course of business, or gifts from relatives.

key_sections.title: Restriction on acceptance of foreign hospitality.
key_sections.description: Restricts members of Legislature, office-bearers of political parties, judges, and government servants from accepting foreign hospitality without prior Central Government permission.

key_sections.title: Prohibition to transfer foreign contribution to other person.
key_sections.description: Prohibits any person who has received foreign contribution under registration or prior permission from transferring it to any other person.

key_sections.title: Restriction to utilise foreign contribution for administrative purpose.
key_sections.description: Restricts the amount of foreign contribution that can be used for administrative expenses to not exceeding twenty per cent, with exceptions for prior Central Government approval.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to prohibit receipt of foreign contribution, etc., in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to prohibit or require prior permission for foreign contribution or hospitality if it is likely to affect prejudicially the sovereignty, public interest, or friendly relations of India.

key_sections.title: Registration of certain persons with Central Government.
key_sections.description: Mandates that persons with definite cultural, economic, educational, religious or social programmes must obtain a certificate of registration or prior permission from the Central Government to accept foreign contribution.

key_sections.title: Grant of certificate of registration.
key_sections.description: Details the application process, conditions, and timelines for granting a certificate of registration or prior permission by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to require Aadhaar number, etc., as identification document.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to require Aadhaar number, Passport, or OCI Card as identification for office bearers/directors for prior permission, registration, or renewal.

key_sections.title: Suspension of certificate.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to suspend a certificate of registration for up to one hundred and eighty days, or further period, pending inquiry for cancellation.

key_sections.title: Cancellation of certificate.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to cancel a certificate of registration under specific conditions, such as making false statements, violating terms, or acting against public interest.

key_sections.title: Foreign contribution through scheduled bank.
key_sections.description: Requires all foreign contributions to be received in a designated 'FCRA Account' at a specified branch of the State Bank of India, with provisions for other scheduled bank accounts for utilisation.

key_sections.title: Punishment for contravention of any provision of the Act.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment of imprisonment up to five years, or fine, or both, for accepting or assisting in accepting foreign contribution in contravention of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 1976, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under the repealed Act.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines offences such as making false statements (Section 33) punishable with imprisonment up to six months or fine or both. Contravention of prohibitory orders under Section 10 (Section 34) carries imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both, plus an additional fine. General contravention of any provision of the Act (Section 35) is punishable with imprisonment up to five years, or fine, or both. Additional fines can be imposed if seized articles are not available for confiscation (Section 36). Offences without separate penalties (Section 37) are punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine or both. Subsequent conviction for certain offences leads to a five-year prohibition from accepting foreign contribution (Section 38). Offences by companies hold responsible both the company and persons in charge (Section 39).

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL CAPITAL TERRITORY OF DELHI LAWS (SPECIAL PROVISIONS) ACT, 2011

act_identification.act_title: THE COINAGE ACT, 2011

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate the laws relating to coinage and the Mints, the protection of coinage and to provide for the prohibition of melting or destruction of coins and prohibit the making or the possession thereof for issue and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate laws concerning coinage and Mints, protect coinage, and prohibit the melting, destruction, making, or unlawful possession of coins for issue. It also covers matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, territorial application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to establish and abolish Mints.
key_sections.description: Grants the Government authority to establish or abolish Mints and authorize minting by other organizations.

key_sections.title: Coin when a legal tender.
key_sections.description: Defines the conditions under which coins of various denominations are considered legal tender.

key_sections.title: Power to call in coin.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Government to declare any coin as no longer legal tender by notification.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of making or melting or destruction of coins.
key_sections.description: Prohibits various activities related to the unlawful use, melting, destruction, or excessive possession of coins.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of section 12.
key_sections.description: Prescribes imprisonment up to seven years and fine for contravening Section 12.

key_sections.title: Prohibition and penalty for unlawful making, issue or possession of pieces of metal to be used as money.
key_sections.description: Prohibits unlawful making, issue, or possession of metal pieces intended as money and sets penalties.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Specifies liability for offences committed by companies and their officers.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable, bailable and non-compoundable.
key_sections.description: Classifies offences under the Act for criminal procedure purposes.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Government power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Lists the enactments repealed by this Act and includes saving provisions.

powers_conferred: Power to establish and abolish Mints (Government, Section 3).
Power to authorize minting of coins by foreign countries/organizations (Government, Section 3).
Power to prescribe denominations, dimensions, designs, and composition of coins (Government, Section 4).
Power to prescribe standard weight and remedy for coins (Government, Section 5).
Power to designate units for decimal system of coinage (Government, Section 7).
Power to call in coin (Government, Section 8).
Power to authorize persons to cut diminished, defaced, or counterfeit coins (Government, Sections 9, 10).
Power of Mint to delegate functions for melting withdrawn coins (Mint, Section 11).
Power to make rules (Government, Section 24).
Power to remove difficulties (Government, Section 23).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prohibits unlawful making, melting, destruction, or excessive possession of coins (Section 12), unlawful making, issue, or possession of metal pieces as money (Section 14), and bringing metal pieces into India for use as coin without authority (Section 15). Penalties include imprisonment up to seven years and fine for contravention of Section 12 and Section 15, and imprisonment up to one year or fine or both for contravention of Section 14, with enhanced penalties for repeat offenders under Section 14. Offences committed by companies also incur liability for responsible persons and officers.

Companies

act_overview.preamble: An Act to alter the name of the State of Orissa.
act_overview.purpose: To alter the name of the State of Orissa to the State of Odisha, and to make consequential amendments to the Constitution of India and provide for adaptation and construction of existing laws.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.

key_sections.title: Alteration of name of State of Orissa.

key_sections.title: Amendment of article 164.

key_sections.title: Amendment of article 273.
key_sections.description: Substitutes the word 'Orissa' with 'Odisha' in article 273 of the Constitution.

key_sections.title: Amendment of First Schedule to the Constitution.
key_sections.description: Substitutes the word 'Orissa' with 'Odisha' in entry 10 under the heading 'I. THE STATES' in the First Schedule to the Constitution.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Fourth Schedule to the Constitution.

key_sections.title: Power to adapt laws.
key_sections.description: Grants power to the appropriate Government to make adaptations and modifications to existing laws within one year from the appointed day to give effect to the name alteration.

key_sections.title: Power to construe laws.
key_sections.description: Allows any court, tribunal, or authority to construe laws in a necessary or proper manner, without affecting substance, even if no or insufficient adaptation has been made under section 8.

key_sections.title: Legal proceedings.

Appropriate Government to adapt and modify laws (Section 8(1))
Competent Legislature or other competent authority to repeal or amend adapted/modified laws (Section 8(2))
Any court, tribunal or authority to construe laws (Section 9)

Laws relating to the State of Orissa
