implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any court, tribunal or authority required or empowered to enforce laws

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL CAPITAL TERRITORY OF DELHI LAWS (SPECIAL PROVISIONS) SECOND ACT, 2011

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS there has been phenomenal increase in the population of the National Capital Territory of Delhi owing to migration and other factors resulting in tremendous pressure on land and infrastructure leading to encroachment or unauthorised developments which are not in consonance with the concept of planned development as provided in the Master Plan for Delhi, 2001 and the relevant Acts and building bye-laws made thereunder; AND WHEREAS the Master Plan for Delhi, 2001 was extensively modified and notified by the Central Government on the 7th day of February, 2007 with the perspective for the year 2021 keeping in view the emerging new dimensions in urban development vis-a-vis the social, financial and other ground realities; AND WHEREAS the Master Plan for Delhi with the perspective for the year 2021 specifically provides for strategies for housing for urban poor as well as to deal with the informal sector; AND WHEREAS the exercise to formulate the Master Plan for Delhi with the perspective for the year 2041 is under progress; AND WHEREAS the National Capital Territory of Delhi (Recognition of Property Rights of Residents in Unauthorised Colonies) Act, 2019 (45 of 2019) was enacted to recognize and confer rights of ownership or transfer or mortgage to the residents of unauthorized colonies as one time special measure; AND WHEREAS in supersession of the Regulations for Regularisation of Unauthorised Colonies in Delhi notified on 24th March, 2008, the National Capital Territory of Delhi (Recognition of Property Rights of Residents in Unauthorised Colonies) Regulations, 2019 notified in the Gazette of India on 29th October, 2019; AND WHEREAS the Development Control Norms for unauthorised colonies as provided in the National Capital Territory of Delhi (Recognition of Property Rights of Residents in Unauthorised Colonies) Regulations, 2019, have been notified on the 8th day of March, 2022; AND WHEREAS the process of conferring the ownership rights to the residents of unauthorised colonies and action as per the Development Control Norms for unauthorised colonies is under progress and will take time; AND WHEREAS based on the policy finalised by the Central Government regarding village abadi area and their extensions, the Building Regulations for Special Area, Unauthorised Regularised Colonies and Village Abadis, have been made by the Delhi Development Authority under sub-section (1) of section 57 of the Delhi Development Act, 1957 (61 of 1957) notified in the Gazette of India vide S.O. 97(E), dated the 17th January, 2011; AND WHEREAS more time is required for completion of action envisaged for unauthorised colonies, village abadi area and their extension and special areas; AND WHEREAS the revised policy for proper arrangements for relocation and rehabilitation of slum dwellers and jhuggi-jhompri clusters in the National Capital Territory of Delhi has been formulated and accordingly, the Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board Act, 2010 (Delhi Act 7 of 2010) has been enacted by the Legislature of the National Capital Territory of Delhi and notified with effect from the 1st July, 2010 to provide for implementation of schemes for improvement of slums and jhuggi-jhompri clusters with a view to bring improvement in environment and living conditions, and to prepare housing scheme for such persons; AND WHEREAS the Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board has identified about six hundred and eighty-five jhuggi-jhompri clusters in the National Capital Territory of Delhi and relocation thereof is likely to take considerable time; AND WHEREAS the revised policy regarding farm houses is being prepared by the Delhi Development Authority and its finalisation is likely to take more time; AND WHEREAS pursuant to the Master Plan, the Zonal Development Plans in respect of various Zones have been notified which provides for regularisation of schools, dispensaries, religious institutions and cultural institutions established on or before the 1st January, 2006 in non-conforming areas; AND WHEREAS the policy with respect to storages, warehouses and godowns used for agricultural inputs or produce (including dairy and poultry) in rural areas built on agricultural land and guidelines for redevelopment of existing godown clusters in non-conforming areas (including those for a storage of non-agricultural goods) required to cater to the needs of the people of the National Capital Territory of Delhi are under consideration of the Central Government in consultation with the Delhi Development Authority; AND WHEREAS the policy with respect to the norms for godown clusters existing in non-conforming areas has been notified by the Central Government on 21st June, 2018; AND WHEREAS with respect to special areas (being the areas consisting of walled city, walled city extension and area known as Karol Bagh and as such other areas as may be designated as special area) referred to in clause (vi) of regulation 2 of the Building Regulations for Special Area, Unauthorised Regularised Colonies and Village Abadis, 2010 notified in the Gazette of India vide S.O. 97(E), dated the 17th January, 2011, is being taken for formulation of redevelopment plan and schemes by concerned local authority which is likely to take considerable time; AND WHEREAS in view of the foregoing paragraphs, it is expedient and in public interest that no hardship be caused (whether by way of sealing or demolition of the structures or otherwise), to the public until the revision of Master Plan as stated in the preceding paragraph is undertaken to facilitate the smooth review of the Master Plan; AND WHEREAS the National Capital Territory of Delhi Laws (Special Provisions) Act, 2007 (43 of 2007) was enacted on the 5th day of December, 2007 to make special provisions for the areas of National Capital Territory of Delhi for a period of up to the 31st day of December, 2008 which ceased to operate after the 31st December, 2008; AND WHEREAS the National Capital Territory of Delhi Laws (Special Provisions) Act, 2009 (24 of 2009) was enacted in continuation of the aforesaid Act for a period up to the 31st day of December, 2009 to make special provisions for the areas of the National Capital Territory of Delhi and that Act ceased to operate after the 31st day of December, 2009; AND WHEREAS the National Capital Territory of Delhi Laws (Special Provisions) Second Act, 2009 (40 of 2009) was enacted in continuation of the aforesaid Act for a period up to the 31st day of December, 2010 to make special provisions for the areas of National Capital Territory of Delhi and that Act ceased to operate after the 31st day of December, 2010; AND WHEREAS the National Capital Territory of Delhi Laws (Special Provisions) Act, 2011 (5 of 2011) has been enacted to give continued effect to provisions of the enactment specified in the preceding paragraph for a period up to the 31st day of December, 2011 and to make special provisions for the areas of the National Capital Territory of Delhi and that Act, shall cease to operate after the 31st day of December, 2011; AND WHEREAS it is expedient to have a law in terms of the Master Plan, in continuation of the said Acts for a period up to the 31st day of December, 2026 to provide for relief and to minimise avoidable hardships and irreparable loss to the people of the National Capital Territory of Delhi against any punitive action by any agency in respect of the persons covered by the policies referred to above.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to provide temporary relief from punitive actions (like demolition or sealing) against unauthorized developments and encroachments in the National Capital Territory of Delhi. This is to allow the Central Government and local authorities sufficient time to finalize policies, strategies, and orderly arrangements for regularization, relocation, and rehabilitation in areas like unauthorized colonies, slum clusters, village abadi areas, and special areas, in consonance with the Master Plan.

act_identification.act_title: THE FACTORING REGULATION ACT, 2011
act_identification.date_of_commencement: Different dates appointed by Central Government: 1st February, 2012 for most provisions; 2nd April, 2012 for Sections 19, 20, 21, 32.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for and regulate assignment of receivables by making provision for registration there for and rights and obligations of parties to contract for assignment of receivables and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to provide a legal framework for the assignment of receivables, regulating the registration of such assignments and defining the rights and obligations of all parties involved in factoring contracts. It also covers related and incidental matters concerning factoring business.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER IV RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF PARTIES TO CONTRACT FOR ASSIGMENT OF RECEIVABLES

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Registration of factors.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration with the Reserve Bank for entities to commence or carry on factoring business.

key_sections.title: Powers of Reserve Bank to give directions and to collect information from factors.
key_sections.description: Grants the Reserve Bank powers to issue directions and collect information from factors regarding their business.

key_sections.title: Assignment of receivables.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process and conditions for assigning receivables by an assignor to a factor.

key_sections.title: Notice to debtor and discharge of obligation of such debtor.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that notice of assignment must be given to the debtor before payment can be demanded by the assignee.

key_sections.title: Liability of debtor in case of an assignor being micro or small enterprises.
key_sections.description: Addresses the debtor's liability and assignee's rights regarding delayed payments when the assignor is a micro or small enterprise.

key_sections.title: Principle of debtor protection.
key_sections.description: Ensures that assignment of receivables does not affect the debtor's rights and obligations without their express written consent.

key_sections.title: Registration of certain assignments of receivables transactions.
key_sections.description: Requires factors to register particulars of assignment transactions with the Central Registry.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for default in filing particulars of assignment transactions and realization of receivables.

key_sections.title: Penalties for non-compliance of direction by Reserve Bank.
key_sections.description: Specifies penalties for factors failing to comply with directions issued by the Reserve Bank.

key_sections.title: Provisions of this Act to override other laws.
key_sections.description: Declares that the Act's provisions shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Reserve Bank the power to make regulations to carry out the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Amendments to certain enactments.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties are prescribed for default in filing particulars of assignment transactions and realization of receivables (Section 21), and for non-compliance with directions issued by the Reserve Bank (Section 22). These penalties can extend to five lakh rupees, with additional daily penalties for continuing offences. General contravention of the Act or rules, for which no specific penalty is provided, is punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both (Section 23). Offences committed by factors can lead to liability for the factor and responsible officers (Section 25).

act_identification.act_title: THE ACADEMY OF SCIENTIFIC AND INNOVATIVE RESEARCH, 2011
act_identification.act_short_title: the Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research Act, 2011

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Science and Technology, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research, Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish an Academy for furtherance of the advancement of learning and prosecution of research in the field of science and technology in association with Council of Scientific and Industrial Research and to declare the institution known as the Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research, to be an institution of national importance to provide for its incorporation and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research as an institution of national importance. Its primary purpose is to advance learning and research in science and technology, particularly in emerging and inter-disciplinary areas, in collaboration with the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research. The Act aims to provide high-quality education and research facilities, fostering innovation and developing leaders in scientific and technological fields.

key_definitions: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its geographical extent, and the date(s) of its commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Academy', 'Board', 'Director', and 'Council of Scientific and Industrial Research'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of the Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

key_sections.title: Object of Academy.
key_sections.description: Outlines the objectives of the Academy, including disseminating advanced knowledge, undertaking inter-disciplinary studies, conducting courses, promoting research, and establishing linkages with industries.

key_sections.title: Relationship of Academy with Council of Scientific and Industrial Research.
key_sections.description: Details how the Academy will utilize the infrastructure and manpower of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research and the requirement for a Memorandum of Understanding for affiliation.

key_sections.title: Declaration of Academy as an institution of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research as an institution of national importance.

key_sections.title: Transfer of assets, liabilities, etc., of existing Academy to Academy established under this Act and other provisions, etc.
key_sections.description: Provides for the transfer of all assets, liabilities, rights, and employees from the existing Academy to the newly established Academy.

key_sections.title: Functions and powers of Academy.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the extensive functions and powers of the Academy, including providing instruction, conducting research, conferring degrees, framing Statutes, and managing its finances.

key_sections.title: Authorities of Academy.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities of the Academy, including the Board, Senate, Director, and Boards of Studies.

key_sections.title: Composition of Board of Governors.
key_sections.description: Specifies the composition of the Board of Governors, including ex officio members and nominated members.

key_sections.title: Powers of Board.
key_sections.description: Defines the powers of the Board, including general superintendence, direction, control of the Academy's affairs, making Statutes, and approving budget estimates.

key_sections.title: Senate.
key_sections.description: Details the composition of the Senate, which includes the Director, Associate Directors, Deans, and various nominated scientists and educationists.

key_sections.title: Funds of Academy.
key_sections.description: Outlines the sources of funds for the Academy and how these funds shall be maintained and applied.

key_sections.title: Statutes.
key_sections.description: States that the Statutes of the Academy shall be enacted by the Board and can be amended or repealed by it.

key_sections.title: Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Provides for the making of Ordinances by the Senate, covering matters like student admission, courses of study, and examinations.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make provisions to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act, within a three-year period from commencement.

powers_conferred: To provide for instructions and conduct research in various branches of learning, particularly inter-disciplinary and multi-disciplinary areas.
To lay administrative standards and structures, decide on creation of posts, recruitment standards, compensation packages, and contractual arrangements.
To design curriculum and pedagogy for award of diplomas or certificates and confer degrees or other academic distinctions.

act_identification.act_title: THE PROTECTION OF CHILDREN FROM SEXUAL OFFENCES ACT, 2012
act_identification.act_short_title: the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Sixty-third Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to protect children from offences of sexual assault, sexual harassment and pornography and provide for establishment of Special Courts for trial of such offences and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS clause (3) of article 15 of the Constitution, inter alia, empowers the State to make special provisions for children; AND WHEREAS, the Government of India has acceded on the 11th December, 1992 to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, adopted by the General Assembly of the United Nations, which has prescribed a set of standards to be followed by all State parties in securing the best interests of the child; AND WHEREAS it is necessary for the proper development of the child that his or her right to privacy and confidentiality be protected and respected by every person by all means and through all stages of a judicial process involving the child; AND WHEREAS it is imperative that the law operates in a manner that the best interest and well being of the child are regarded as being of paramount importance at every stage, to ensure the healthy physical, emotional, intellectual and social development of the child; AND WHEREAS the State parties to the Convention on the Rights of the Child are required to undertake all appropriate national, bilateral and multilateral measures to prevent— (a)the inducement or coercion of a child to engage in any unlawful sexual activity; (b)the exploitative use of children in prostitution or other unlawful sexual practices; (c)the exploitative use of children in pornographic performances and materials; AND WHEREAS sexual exploitation and sexual abuse of children are heinous crimes and need to be effectively addressed.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to protect children from sexual assault, sexual harassment, and pornography. It also provides for the establishment of Special Courts to ensure speedy trial of such offences and addresses related matters.

Penalties range from imprisonment for a term not less than 3 years up to life imprisonment (remainder of natural life) or death, depending on the severity and nature of the offence. Fines are also prescribed, often to be paid to the victim for medical expenses and rehabilitation. The Act also penalizes abetment (S.16), attempt to commit an offence (S.18), failure to report or record a case (S.21), making false complaints (S.22), and contravention of media procedures (S.23).

act_overview.preamble:
WHEREAS sexual harassment results in violation of the fundamental rights of a woman to equality
under articles 14 and 15 of the Constitution of India and her right to life and to live with dignity under
article 21 of the Constitution and right to practice any profession or to carry on any occupation, trade or
business which includes a right to a safe environment free from sexual harassment;
AND WHEREAS the protection against sexual harassment and the right to work with dignity are
universally recognised human rights by international conventions and instruments such as Convention on
the Elimination of all Forms of Discrimination against Women, which has been ratified on the 25th June,
1993 by the Government of India;
AND WHEREAS it is expedient to make provisions for giving effect to the said Convention for
protection of women against sexual harassment at workplace.
act_overview.purpose: An Act to provide protection against sexual harassment of women at workplace and for the prevention and redressal of complaints of sexual harassment and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

Local Committee handles complaints where Internal Committee not constituted (less than ten workers) or if the complaint is against the employer himself (S.6(1)).
District Officer to designate one nodal officer in every block, taluka and tehsil in rural or tribal area and ward or municipality in the urban area (S.6(2)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the constitution of Internal Complaints Committees (ICC) at workplaces and Local Committees (LC) at the district level. Aggrieved women can file complaints with these committees, which then conduct conciliation or inquiry proceedings. The committees submit inquiry reports with recommendations to the employer or District Officer, who are mandated to act upon them. The Appropriate Government monitors implementation, maintains data, and publicises the Act. Non-compliance by employers attracts penalties. Appeals against recommendations can be made to a court or tribunal.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence under this Act. Appeals can be preferred to the court or tribunal.

act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to consolidate and amend the existing laws governing companies in India. key_sections.title: Formation of company.

key_sections.description: Regulates the acceptance of deposits by companies from the public, with specific conditions and prohibitions.

key_sections.title: Annual return.
key_sections.description: Mandates every company to prepare and file an annual return containing specified particulars about its structure, shareholding, and management.

key_sections.title: Declaration of dividend.
key_sections.description: Governs the declaration and payment of dividends by companies, including sources of funds and conditions.

key_sections.title: Corporate Social Responsibility.
key_sections.description: Requires certain companies to constitute a CSR Committee and spend a specified percentage of their profits on CSR activities.

key_sections.title: Appointment of auditors.
key_sections.description: Lays down the provisions for the appointment and re-appointment of auditors for companies, including tenure limits and procedures.

key_sections.title: Company to have Board of Directors.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the minimum and maximum number of directors for companies, including requirements for women and independent directors.

key_sections.title: Duties of directors.
key_sections.description: Outlines the statutory duties of directors, including acting in good faith, exercising due care, and avoiding conflicts of interest.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to appoint commencement dates, specify body corporate for application, approve name changes, revoke license for charitable companies, prescribe accounting standards, constitute NFRA, give directions for CSR, appoint Official Liquidators, make rules, remove difficulties.
Securities and Exchange Board: Power to regulate issue and transfer of securities, specify information in prospectus, make regulations for sweat equity shares, buy-back.

Tribunal (NCLT): Power to call annual general meeting, order re-opening of accounts, approve voluntary revision of financial statements, sanction compromise/arrangement, enforce compromise/arrangement, order winding up, assess damages, declare dissolution void.

Board of Directors: Power to form company, alter share capital, issue further share capital, declare interim dividend, appoint first auditor, appoint additional/alternate/nominee director, exercise general powers, contribute to charitable funds.
Registrar: Power to register companies, remove name of company, keep register of charges, conduct inspections and inquiries.
Company Liquidator: Power to carry on business for winding up, sell property, institute legal proceedings, invite claims, inspect records.
Official Liquidator: Exercise powers of Company Liquidator, conduct inquiries/investigations, dispose of assets, settle claims.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes various penalties and punishments for non-compliance, including fines for companies and officers in default, imprisonment for serious offences like fraud, personation, and fraudulent conduct of business, and personal liability for directors and officers in certain cases. Specific penalties are outlined for defaults related to incorporation, share capital, deposits, charges, annual returns, dividends, financial statements, audits, director duties, related party transactions, and winding up proceedings. Fraudulent activities are often punishable under Section 447, which includes imprisonment and substantial fines.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL FOOD SECURITY ACT, 2013

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for food and nutritional security in human life cycle approach, by ensuring access to adequate quantity of quality food at affordable prices to people to live a life with dignity and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to ensure food and nutritional security for people throughout their life cycle by providing access to adequate quantities of quality food at affordable prices. It aims to enable people to live a life with dignity and addresses related incidental matters.

key_sections.title: Right to receive foodgrains at subsidised prices by persons belonging to eligible households under Targeted Public Distribution System.

key_sections.title: Nutritional support to pregnant women and lactating mothers.
key_sections.description: Ensures nutritional support, including free meals and maternity benefits, for pregnant women and lactating mothers, subject to certain exclusions.

key_sections.title: Nutritional support to children.
key_sections.description: Outlines entitlements for nutritional needs of children up to fourteen years, including meals through anganwadis and mid-day meals in schools.

key_sections.title: Right to receive food security allowance in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Establishes the right of entitled persons to receive a food security allowance from the concerned State Government in cases of non-supply of foodgrains or meals.

key_sections.title: State Government to prepare guidelines and to identify priority households.
key_sections.description: Mandates State Governments to identify priority households and those under Antyodaya Anna Yojana based on Central Government guidelines and update the list.

key_sections.title: Reforms in Targeted Public Distribution System.
key_sections.description: Requires Central and State Governments to undertake reforms in the Targeted Public Distribution System, including doorstep delivery, ICT application, Aadhaar linkage, and diversification of commodities.

key_sections.description: Designates the eldest woman of eighteen years or above as the head of the household for ration card purposes, promoting women empowerment.

key_sections.title: District Grievance Redressal Officer.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of a District Grievance Redressal Officer in each district to address complaints related to foodgrain distribution and enforce entitlements.

key_sections.title: State Food Commission.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of a State Food Commission to monitor and review the implementation of the Act, inquire into violations, and advise the State Government.

key_sections.title: Central Government to allocate required quantity of foodgrains from central pool to State Governments.
key_sections.description: Outlines the Central Government's obligation to allocate foodgrains from the central pool to State Governments for the Targeted Public Distribution System and other schemes.

key_sections.title: Implementation and monitoring of schemes for ensuring food security.
key_sections.description: Defines the State Government's responsibility for implementing and monitoring food security schemes, including delivery of foodgrains and payment of food security allowance.

key_sections.title: Penalties.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties not exceeding five thousand rupees for public servants or authorities found guilty of failing to provide recommended relief or wilfully ignoring recommendations by the District Grievance Redressal Officer.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, in consultation with State Governments, covering various aspects like schemes and allowances.

key_sections.title: Power of State Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to make rules consistent with the Act and Central Government rules, for matters including identification of households, grievance redressal, and Vigilance Committees.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the National Food Security Ordinance, 2013, while saving actions taken and rights accrued under it.

act_identification.act_title: THE PROHIBITION OF EMPLOYMENT AS MANUAL SCAVENGERS AND THEIR REHABILITATION ACT, 2013
act_identification.act_short_title: the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the prohibition of employment as manual scavengers, rehabilitation of manual scavengers and their families, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS promoting among the citizens fraternity assuring the dignity of the individual is enshrined as one of the goals in the Preamble to the Constitution; AND WHEREAS the right to live with dignity is also implicit in the Fundamental Rights guaranteed in Part III of the Constitution; AND WHEREAS article 46 of the Constitution, inter alia, provides that the State shall protect the weaker sections, and, particularly, the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes from social injustice and all forms of exploitation; AND WHEREAS the dehumanising practice of manual scavenging, arising from the continuing existence of insanitary latrines and a highly iniquitous caste system, still persists in various parts of the country, and the existing laws have not proved adequate in eliminating the twin evils of insanitary latrines and manual scavenging; AND WHEREAS it is necessary to correct the historical injustice and indignity suffered by the manual scavengers, and to rehabilitate them to a life of dignity.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to prohibit the employment of manual scavengers and the construction of insanitary latrines. It also seeks to provide for the identification and comprehensive rehabilitation of manual scavengers and their families, ensuring their right to live with dignity.

Contravention of Section 7 (prohibition of hazardous cleaning of sewers/septic tanks): First contravention - imprisonment up to two years or fine up to two lakh rupees or both. key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Authority.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority as a body corporate.

key_sections.title: Extent and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies to which pension systems and schemes the Act applies and lists exemptions.

key_sections.title: Duties, powers and functions of Authority.
key_sections.description: Outlines the Authority's responsibilities, powers, and functions, including regulation, protection of subscribers, and investigation.

key_sections.title: National Pension System.
key_sections.description: Deems the contributory pension system as the National Pension System and defines its basic features.

key_sections.title: Registration of central recordkeeping agency, pension fund, point of presence, etc.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration for intermediaries and outlines the process for granting, suspending, or cancelling registration.

key_sections.title: Penalty for failure by an intermediary or any other person to comply with provisions of this Act, rules, regulations and directions.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for various failures to comply with the Act, rules, regulations, and directions.

key_sections.title: Offences.
key_sections.description: Defines offences under the Act and specifies imprisonment and fine penalties.

key_sections.title: Appeal to Securities Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals against orders of the Authority or adjudicating officer to the Securities Appellate Tribunal.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Pension Regulatory and Development Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Pension Regulatory and Development Fund and specifies its sources and application.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Subscriber Education and Protection Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Subscriber Education and Protection Fund and specifies its sources and utilization for subscriber protection.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Authority power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.

powers_conferred: Power to regulate, promote and ensure orderly growth of the National Pension System and pension schemes (Section 14(1)).
Power to approve schemes and lay down norms for the management of the corpus of the pension funds (Section 14(2)(b)).
Power to register and regulate intermediaries (Section 14(2)(c)).
Power to issue, renew, modify, withdraw, suspend or cancel registration certificates (Section 14(2)(d)).
Power to establish mechanism for redressal of grievances of subscribers (Section 14(2)(f)).
Power to adjudicate disputes between intermediaries and between intermediaries and subscribers (Section 14(2)(h)).
Power to collect data, undertake studies, educate subscribers and standardize information (Section 14(2)(i), (j), (k)).
Power to levy fees or other charges (Section 14(2)(m)).
Power to call for information, undertake inspection, conduct inquiries and investigations (Section 14(2)(o)).
Powers of a civil court for discovery, summoning, inspection, issuing commissions (Section 14(3)).
Power to issue directions to intermediaries or entities (Section 15).
Power of investigation into the affairs of intermediaries (Section 16).
Power of search and seizure (Section 17).
Power to ensure compliance and issue cease and desist orders (Section 18).
Power to appoint an Administrator to manage the affairs of the central recordkeeping agency or pension fund (Section 19(2)).
Power to make rules (Central Government) (Section 51).
Power to make regulations (Authority) (Section 52).
Power to supersede Authority (Central Government) (Section 44).
Power to establish Pension Advisory Committee (Authority) (Section 45).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties for non-compliance include: failure to obtain registration (up to one crore rupees or one lakh per day), failure to comply with registration terms (up to one crore rupees or one lakh per day), failure to furnish information/documents (up to one crore rupees or five times profits/losses avoided), failure to maintain books/records (up to five times profits/losses avoided or one lakh per day), failure to enter client agreements (up to five times profits/losses avoided or one lakh per day), failure to redress subscriber grievances (up to one crore rupees or five times profits/losses avoided), failure to segregate client moneys (up to one crore rupees or five times profits/losses avoided), and general non-compliance (up to one crore rupees or five times profits/losses avoided). Offences related to investigation (Section 16(7)) carry imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to twenty-five crore rupees, or both, with additional daily fines. General contravention or abetment of the Act/rules/regulations (Section 32(1)) is punishable with imprisonment up to ten years, or fine up to twenty-five crore rupees, or both. Failure to pay penalty or comply with directions (Section 32(2)) is punishable with imprisonment from one month to ten years, or fine up to twenty-five crore rupees, or both.

authorities_established: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints the Chairperson and members of the Authority.
regulatory_bodies: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority

applies_to: the National Pension System
any other pension scheme not regulated by any other enactment
exemptions: schemes or funds under the Coal Mines Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1948
schemes or funds under the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
schemes or funds under the Seamen’s Provident Fund Act, 1966
schemes or funds under the Assam Tea Plantations Provident Fund and Pension Fund Scheme Act, 1955
schemes or funds under the Jammu and Kashmir Employees’ Provident Funds Act, 1961
contracts referred to in sub-section (11) of section 2 of the Insurance Act, 1938
any other pension scheme, which the Central Government may, by notification, exempt

special_provisions: Any State Government or administrator of a Union territory may extend the National Pension System to its employees (Section 12(4)).
The Central Government may extend the Act to any other pension scheme, including exempted ones (Section 12(5)).
Persons governed by exempted schemes may optionally join the National Pension System (Section 12(6)).
Powers of Authority do not apply to International Financial Services Centre (Section 50A).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Authority regulates, promotes, and ensures orderly growth of the National Pension System. It has powers to issue directions, investigate, conduct search and seizure, ensure compliance, and adjudicate penalties. Violations can lead to penalties, and offences are punishable by imprisonment and fines.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Securities Appellate Tribunal, Supreme Court, Court of Session, Judicial Magistrate of first class

act_identification.act_title: THE RAJIV GANDHI NATIONAL AVIATION UNIVERSITY ACT, 2013
act_identification.act_short_title: Rajiv Gandhi National Aviation University Act, 2013

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Civil Aviation

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate a national aviation University to facilitate and promote aviation studies and research to achieve excellence in areas of aviation management, policy, science and technology, aviation environment, training in governing fields of safety and security regulations on aviation and other related fields to produce quality human resources to cater to the needs of the aviation sector and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Rajiv Gandhi National Aviation University to promote aviation studies, research, and training. Its main objective is to develop quality human resources for the aviation sector by focusing on emerging areas like aviation management, policy, science, technology, environment, safety, and security regulations.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it will come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines various terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Academic Council', 'University', 'Executive Council', etc.

key_sections.title: Establishment of University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the 'Rajiv Gandhi National Aviation University' with its headquarters at Fursatganj, Raebareli, Uttar Pradesh, and outlines its perpetual succession and common seal.

key_sections.title: Objects of University.
key_sections.description: Lays down the primary objectives of the University, including promoting aviation studies, research, training, and achieving excellence in various aviation-related fields.

key_sections.title: Powers of University.
key_sections.description: Details the extensive powers of the University, such as providing instruction, establishing campuses, granting degrees, collaborating with other institutions, and managing its property.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: States that the jurisdiction of the University shall extend to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: The Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University and outlines the Visitor's powers, including review, inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions.

key_sections.title: Officers of University.
key_sections.description: Lists the key officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Deans of Schools, Registrar, Finance Officer, and Controller of Examinations.

key_sections.title: Authorities of University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities of the University, such as the Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Board of Affiliation and Recognition, Boards of Schools, and Finance Committee.

key_sections.title: Power to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Statutes can be made, covering the constitution and functions of authorities, appointment of officers and employees, and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Ordinances can be made, including admission of students, courses of study, examinations, and fees.

key_sections.title: Tribunal of Arbitration.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Tribunal of Arbitration for resolving disputes between the University and its employees, making its decision final and binding.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act for a period of three years from its commencement.

key_sections.title: Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Mandates the publication of all Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations in the Official Gazette and their laying before both Houses of Parliament.

key_sections.title: Role of Central Government.
key_sections.description: States that the University is bound by the Central Government's directions on questions of policy, and the Central Government's decision on what constitutes a policy question is final.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Disciplinary actions against students include removal from rolls and debarment from examinations. Disputes arising from such actions can be referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration. No specific criminal offences or monetary penalties are defined for general public or employees.

authorities_established: The Board of Affiliation and Recognition

The Executive Council appoints the Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, and other officers as prescribed by Statutes.

applies_to: persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class
teachers
students
employees

Transitional provisions are made for the appointment and term of the first Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, Court, and Executive Council.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Executive Council has the power to make, amend, or repeal Statutes. The Vice-Chancellor, with Central Government approval, makes the first Ordinances, which the Executive Council can later amend. The Visitor can also make or amend Statutes. Authorities of the University can make Regulations.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor has powers to review the University's work, cause inspections and inquiries, and issue binding directions. The Vice-Chancellor can also initiate inspections and inquiries. The Central Government can issue binding policy directions. Disputes between the University and its employees or students are resolved through a Tribunal of Arbitration.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The decision of the Tribunal of Arbitration is final and binding, precluding suits in civil courts for matters decided by it. However, employees retain the right to avail judicial remedies under Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution.

act_identification.act_title: THE RIGHT TO FAIR COMPENSATION AND TRANSPARENCY IN LAND ACQUISITION, REHABILITATION AND RESETTLEMENT ACT, 2013
act_identification.act_short_title: the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013

act_overview.preamble: An Act to ensure, in consultation with institutions of local self-government and Gram Sabhas established under the Constitution, a humane, participative, informed and transparent process for land acquisition for industrialisation, development of essential infrastructural facilities and urbanisation with the least disturbance to the owners of the land and other affected families and provide just and fair compensation to the affected families whose land has been acquired or proposed to be acquired or are affected by such acquisition and make adequate provisions for such affected persons for their rehabilitation and resettlement and for ensuring that the cumulative outcome of compulsory acquisition should be that affected persons become partners in development leading to an improvement in their post acquisition social and economic status and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: To ensure a humane, participative, informed, and transparent process for land acquisition. It aims to provide just and fair compensation, rehabilitation, and resettlement to affected families, ensuring their improved social and economic status post-acquisition.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II: DETERMINATION OF SOCIAL IMPACT AND PUBLIC PURPOSE
CHAPTER III: SPECIAL PROVISION TO SAFEGUARD FOOD SECURITY
CHAPTER V: REHABILITATION AND RESETTLEMENT AWARD
CHAPTER VI: PROCEDURE AND MANNER OF REHABILITATION AND RESETTLEMENT
CHAPTER VII: NATIONAL MONITORING COMMITTEE FOR REHABILITATION AND RESETTLEMENT
CHAPTER VIII: ESTABLISHMENT OF LAND ACQUISITION, REHABILITATION AND RESETTLEMENT AUTHORITY
CHAPTER XI: TEMPORARY OCCUPATION OF LAND

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Application of Act.
key_sections.description: Outlines the circumstances and purposes for which the Act's provisions on land acquisition, compensation, rehabilitation, and resettlement apply, including for public sector undertakings, public-private partnerships, and private companies.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Administrator', 'affected family', 'appropriate Government', 'Collector', 'land owner', and 'public purpose'.

key_sections.title: Preparation of Social Impact Assessment study.
key_sections.description: Mandates the appropriate Government to conduct a Social Impact Assessment study before acquiring land for a public purpose, detailing its scope and publication requirements.

key_sections.title: Publication of preliminary notification and power of officers thereupon.
key_sections.description: Requires the appropriate Government to publish a preliminary notification for land acquisition, detailing the land and public purpose, and restricts transactions on such land.

key_sections.title: Land acquisition process under Act No. 1 of 1894 shall be deemed to have lapsed in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Stipulates conditions under which land acquisition proceedings initiated under the repealed Land Acquisition Act, 1894, are deemed to have lapsed, particularly if possession was not taken or compensation not paid for five years or more.

key_sections.title: Determination of market value of land by Collector.
key_sections.description: Sets out the criteria and parameters for the Collector to assess and determine the market value of land for compensation purposes, including sale deeds, average sale price, and consented amounts.

key_sections.title: Award of solatium.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Collector to impose a solatium amount equivalent to one hundred percent of the compensation, in addition to market value and interest.

key_sections.title: Rehabilitation and Resettlement Award for affected families by Collector.
key_sections.description: Requires the Collector to pass R&R Awards for each affected family, detailing entitlements as per the Second Schedule, including monetary and non-monetary benefits.

key_sections.title: Power to take possession of land to be acquired.
key_sections.description: Specifies that the Collector can take possession of land only after ensuring full payment of compensation and R&R entitlements within prescribed periods.

key_sections.title: Special powers in case of urgency to acquire land in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Grants the appropriate Government special powers to acquire land urgently for specific purposes like national security or natural calamities, allowing for immediate possession after notice and advance compensation.

key_sections.title: Special provisions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
key_sections.description: Outlines special safeguards and entitlements for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes during land acquisition, including prior consent of Gram Sabha, development plans, and additional compensation.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of an Authority to ensure speedy disposal of disputes related to land acquisition, compensation, rehabilitation, and resettlement.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of civil courts barred.
key_sections.description: Bars civil courts from entertaining disputes related to land acquisition under this Act, reserving jurisdiction for the Authority, High Courts (under Articles 226/227), and the Supreme Court.

key_sections.title: Return of unutilised land.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that land acquired under this Act, if unutilised for five years from taking possession, shall be returned to the original owner or their heirs, or to the Land Bank.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, while providing for saving clauses regarding the effect of repeals.

powers_conferred: Appropriate Government: To notify affected area (Section 3(b)), specify public purpose (Section 2), exempt Social Impact Assessment (Section 9), extend period for Social Impact Assessment report (Section 14), extend period for award (Section 25), direct Collector in urgency cases (Section 40), make rules (Section 109), amend schedules (Section 106), remove difficulties (Section 113).

Collector: To conduct preliminary survey (Section 12), pay for damage (Section 13), hear objections (Section 15), make land acquisition award (Section 23), determine market value (Section 26), determine compensation (Section 27), award solatium (Section 30), pass Rehabilitation and Resettlement awards (Section 31), correct awards (Section 33), adjourn enquiry (Section 34), summon witnesses (Section 35), take possession of land (Section 38), enforce surrender (Section 91).
Administrator: To conduct survey and census for Rehabilitation and Resettlement scheme (Section 16).

Authority: To dispose of disputes relating to land acquisition, compensation, rehabilitation and resettlement (Section 51), summon witnesses, enforce production of documents, receive evidence, requisition public records, issue commissions, review decisions (Section 60).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Punishment for false information or mala fide action (Section 84) includes imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to one lakh rupees, or both, with disciplinary proceedings for Government servants. Penalty for contravention of Act provisions (Section 85) is imprisonment from six months to three years, or a fine, or both. Offences by companies (Section 86) hold persons in charge and responsible, or directors/managers/officers, liable. Offences by Government departments (Section 87) hold the head of the department liable.

repealed_acts: The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (1 of 1894)
related_acts: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (2 of 2007)
Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (40 of 1996)
Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 (35 of 2009)
The Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958 (24 of 1958)
The Damodar Valley Corporation Act, 1948 (14 of 1948)
The Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Act, 1978 (33 of 1978)
The Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962 (50 of 1962)
The Requisitioning and Acquisition of Immovable Property Act, 1952 (30 of 1952)
The Resettlement of Displaced Persons (Land Acquisition) Act, 1948 (60 of 1948)
The Coal Bearing Areas Acquisition and Development Act, 1957 (20 of 1957)

authorities_established: Rehabilitation and Resettlement Committee at project level
National Monitoring Committee for rehabilitation and resettlement
State Monitoring Committee for rehabilitation and resettlement
Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority
important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government appoints Administrator (Section 43), Commissioner (Section 44), and Presiding Officer of Authority (Section 52, 53). Appropriate Government also appoints Presiding Officer of Authority (Section 52, 53).

applies_to: When appropriate Government acquires land for its own use, hold and control, including for Public Sector Undertakings and for public purpose (Section 2(1)).

For strategic purposes relating to naval, military, air force, and armed forces of the Union, including central paramilitary forces or any work vital to national security or defence of India or State police, safety of the people (Section 2(1)(a)).
For infrastructure projects (Section 2(1)(b)).
For project affected families (Section 2(1)(c)).
For housing for such income groups, as may be specified (Section 2(1)(d)).
For planned development or improvement of village sites or urban areas or provision of land for residential purposes for weaker sections (Section 2(1)(e)).
For residential purposes to the poor or landless or to persons residing in areas affected by natural calamities, or displaced by Government schemes (Section 2(1)(f)).
For public private partnership projects, where ownership of land continues to vest with the Government (Section 2(2)(a)).
For private companies for public purpose (Section 2(2)(b)).
When a private company purchases land, equal to or more than prescribed limits, through private negotiations (Section 2(3)(a)).
When a private company requests the appropriate Government for acquisition of a part of an area for a public purpose (Section 2(3)(b)).
exemptions: Exemption from Social Impact Assessment study when invoking urgency provisions under Section 40 (Section 9).
Provisions relating to Social Impact Assessment shall not apply to irrigation projects where Environment Impact Assessment is required under other laws (Section 6(2) proviso).
No irrigated multi-cropped land shall be acquired, save for exceptional circumstances as a demonstrable last resort (Section 10(1), (2)).

Provisions of Section 10 (food security) shall not apply in the case of projects that are linear in nature such as railways, highways, major district roads, irrigation canals, power lines (Section 10 proviso).
Provisions of this Act shall not apply to the enactments relating to land acquisition specified in the Fourth Schedule, subject to sub-section (3) of Section 105.
special_provisions: Special provisions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Section 41): Acquisition in Scheduled Areas only as a demonstrable last resort, prior consent of Gram Sabha/Panchayats/Autonomous District Councils, preparation of Development Plan for involuntary displacement, one-third of compensation paid as first instalment, resettlement preferably in the same Scheduled Area, land for community and social gatherings, fishing rights in reservoir areas, additional 25% R&R benefits and one-time 50,000 rupees if relocated outside district.

State Amendments (Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Haryana) introduce specific exemptions or modifications for certain projects or procedures within their respective states, such as exempting certain projects from Chapter II and III provisions or modifying definitions and procedures.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through various authorities: the Collector conducts surveys, enquiries, makes awards, and takes possession; the Administrator prepares rehabilitation and resettlement schemes; the Commissioner supervises these schemes; National and State Monitoring Committees review implementation; and the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority adjudicates disputes. Magistrates can enforce surrender of land.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority (for references from Collector), High Court (for appeals against Authority's awards and under Articles 226/227 of the Constitution), Supreme Court (under Articles 226/227 of the Constitution). For offences, no court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall be competent to try.

schedules_summary.description: Details the components of minimum compensation package for land owners, including market value determination, multiplication factors for rural/urban areas, value of assets, solatium, and final award calculation.

Lists the elements of rehabilitation and resettlement entitlements for all affected families, such as provision of housing units, land for land, developed land, choice of annuity or employment, subsistence grant, transportation cost, cattle shed/petty shops cost, one-time grant to artisans/small traders, fishing rights, one-time resettlement allowance, and stamp duty/registration fee exemptions.

Specifies the infrastructural facilities and basic minimum amenities to be provided in resettlement areas to ensure a reasonable standard of community life for resettled populations, including roads, drainage, drinking water, grazing land, fair price shops, schools, health centres, and community centres.
Provides a list of other Central enactments regulating land acquisition and rehabilitation and resettlement, to which the provisions of this Act may not apply or may apply with certain modifications.

act_identification.act_title: THE LOKPAL AND LOKAYUKTAS ACT, 2013

act_overview.purpose: To establish a body of Lokpal for the Union and Lokayukta for States to inquire into allegations of corruption against certain public functionaries. Its purpose is to ensure justice, implement the United Nations Convention Against Corruption, and provide for prompt and fair investigation and prosecution in cases of corruption.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical extent, application to public servants, and commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Lokpal', 'public servant', 'competent authority', and 'complaint'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Lokpal.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the Lokpal body, its composition, and eligibility criteria for its Chairperson and Members.

key_sections.title: Inquiry Wing.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Lokpal to constitute an Inquiry Wing for conducting preliminary inquiries into corruption allegations.

key_sections.title: Prosecution Wing.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Lokpal to constitute a Prosecution Wing for prosecuting public servants based on Lokpal's findings.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of Lokpal to include Prime Minister, Ministers, members of Parliament, Groups A, B, C and D officers and officials of Central Government.
key_sections.description: Outlines the Lokpal's jurisdiction over various public functionaries, including the Prime Minister, Ministers, MPs, and Central Government officers, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to complaints and preliminary inquiry and investigation.
key_sections.description: Details the procedure for handling complaints, conducting preliminary inquiries, and initiating investigations, including timelines and referral to other agencies.

key_sections.title: Power of Lokpal to grant sanction for initiating prosecution.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the Lokpal the power to grant sanction for prosecution of public servants, overriding other laws.

key_sections.title: Supervisory powers of Lokpal.
key_sections.description: Grants the Lokpal supervisory powers over the Delhi Special Police Establishment and the Central Vigilance Commission in matters referred by it.

key_sections.title: Provisional attachment of assets.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Lokpal to provisionally attach assets believed to be proceeds of corruption.

key_sections.title: Special Courts to be constituted by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Requires the Central Government to constitute Special Courts for hearing cases arising under this Act and the Prevention of Corruption Act.

key_sections.title: Removal and suspension of Chairperson and Members of Lokpal.
key_sections.description: Lays down the procedure for removal and suspension of the Chairperson and Members of the Lokpal on grounds of misbehaviour or other specified reasons.

key_sections.title: Declaration of assets.
key_sections.description: Mandates public servants to declare their assets and liabilities in a prescribed form and manner.

key_sections.title: Prosecution for false complaint and payment of compensation, etc., to public servant.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for making false and frivolous complaints and provides for compensation to public servants falsely accused.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in other enactments.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Lokayukta.
key_sections.description: Requires every State to establish a Lokayukta body to deal with corruption complaints against public functionaries at the State level.

powers_conferred: Lokpal to constitute an Inquiry Wing (Section 11)
Lokpal to constitute a Prosecution Wing (Section 12)
Lokpal to inquire or cause an inquiry into allegations of corruption (Section 14)
Lokpal to order preliminary inquiry or investigation (Section 20)
Lokpal to grant sanction for prosecution (Section 23)
Lokpal to have supervisory powers over Delhi Special Police Establishment (Section 25)
Lokpal to authorize search and seizure of documents (Section 26)
Lokpal to have powers of a civil court in certain cases (Section 27)
Lokpal to utilize services of officers or organizations of Central or State Government (Section 28)
Lokpal to provisionally attach assets (Section 29)
Lokpal to recommend transfer or suspension of public servant (Section 32)
Lokpal to give directions to prevent destruction of records (Section 33)
Lokpal to delegate administrative or financial powers (Section 34)
Central Government to constitute Special Courts (Section 35)
Central Government to make rules (Section 59)
Lokpal to make regulations (Section 60)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever makes any false and frivolous or vexatious complaint under this Act shall, on conviction, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees. Societies, associations, or trusts committing such offences are also liable. The Act also deals with offences punishable under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

amended_acts: THE COMMISSIONS OF INQUIRY ACT, 1952 (60 OF 1952)
THE DELHI SPECIAL POLICE ESTABLISHMENT ACT, 1946 (25 OF 1946)
THE PREVENTION OF CORRUPTION ACT, 1988 (49 OF 1988)
THE CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE, 1973 (2 OF 1974)
THE CENTRAL VIGILANCE COMMISSION ACT, 2003 (45 OF 2003)
related_acts: Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946 (25 of 1946)
Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993 (51 of 1993)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: President appoints Chairperson and Members of Lokpal. Chairperson of Lokpal appoints Secretary, Director of Inquiry, Director of Prosecution, and other officers/staff of Lokpal. Central Government appoints Director of Prosecution for Delhi Special Police Establishment and Director of Inquiry for Central Vigilance Commission.

applies_to: Whole of India
Public servants in and outside India
Prime Minister, Ministers, members of Parliament, Groups A, B, C and D officers and officials of Central Government

Chairperson or member or officer or employee in any body or Board or corporation or authority or company or society or trust or autonomous body established by an Act of Parliament or wholly or partly financed by the Central Government or controlled by it
Director, manager, secretary or other officer of every other society or association of persons or trust wholly or partly financed by the Government

Director, manager, secretary or other officer of every other society or association of persons or trust in receipt of any donation from any foreign source under the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 in excess of ten lakh rupees in a year
Any person involved in the act of abetting, bribe giving or bribe taking or conspiracy relating to any allegation of corruption against a public servant
exemptions: Public servants in respect of whom jurisdiction is exercisable by any court or other authority under the Army Act, 1950, the Air Force Act, 1950, the Navy Act, 1957 and the Coast Guard Act, 1978
Prime Minister in so far as it relates to international relations, external and internal security, public order, atomic energy and space
Any member of either House of Parliament in respect of anything said or a vote given by him in Parliament or any committee thereof covered under clause (2) of article 105 of the Constitution
Persons holding office in pursuance of the provisions of the Constitution in respect of which a procedure for removal of such person has been specified therein (regarding sanction for prosecution)
Complaints made in good faith
special_provisions: Inquiry into allegations against the Prime Minister requires approval of at least two-thirds of a full bench of the Lokpal and shall be held in camera.
Jurisdiction over officers working in connection with the affairs of a State or State-controlled bodies requires consent of the concerned State Government.
No action under Section 14(3) shall be taken in case of a person serving in connection with the affairs of a State, without the consent of the State Government.
Every State shall establish a body to be known as the Lokayukta.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Lokpal, through its Inquiry Wing and Prosecution Wing, conducts preliminary inquiries and investigations into corruption allegations. It can utilize agencies like the Delhi Special Police Establishment and Central Vigilance Commission. Special Courts are constituted to hear and decide cases, including trials, confiscation of assets, and recovery of losses. The Lokpal also has powers of search, seizure, and provisional attachment of assets.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Special Courts

schedules_summary.description: Contains amendments to various enactments, including the Commissions of Inquiry Act, 1952, the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946, the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, and the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.

act_identification.act_title: THE ANDHRA PRADESH REORGANISATION ACT, 2014

legislative_details.geographical_extent: The existing State of Andhra Pradesh, which is reorganized into the State of Telangana and the State of Andhra Pradesh.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the reorganisation of the existing State of Andhra Pradesh and for matters connected therewith.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to reorganize the existing State of Andhra Pradesh into two separate successor states, namely the State of Andhra Pradesh and the State of Telangana. It also addresses various connected matters such as the division of assets, liabilities, services, and legislative representation between the new states.

PART VII: PROVISIONS AS TO CERTAIN CORPORATIONS
PART VIII: PROVISIONS AS TO SERVICES
PART IX: MANAGEMENT AND DEVELOPMENT OF WATER RESOURCES
PART X: INFRASTRUCTURE AND SPECIAL ECONOMIC MEASURES

key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Formation of Telangana State.
key_sections.description: Details the formation of the new State of Telangana and its territorial composition.

key_sections.title: State of Andhra Pradesh and territorial divisions thereof.
key_sections.description: Defines the territories comprising the successor State of Andhra Pradesh.

key_sections.title: Hyderabad to be common capital for States of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
key_sections.description: Designates Hyderabad as the common capital for both successor states for a period not exceeding ten years.

key_sections.title: Expert Committee for setting up of a capital for Andhra Pradesh.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to constitute an expert committee to recommend a new capital for Andhra Pradesh.

key_sections.title: Governor of existing State of Andhra Pradesh to be common Governor.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the Governor of the existing State of Andhra Pradesh shall serve as the common Governor for both successor states.

key_sections.title: Representation in House of the People.
key_sections.description: Allocates seats in the House of the People (Lok Sabha) to the successor States of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

key_sections.title: High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad to be common High Court till establishment of High Court of Andhra Pradesh.
key_sections.description: Declares the High Court of Judicature at Hyderabad as the common High Court until a separate High Court for Andhra Pradesh is established.

key_sections.title: Application of Part.
key_sections.description: Outlines the general principles for the apportionment of assets and liabilities of the existing State of Andhra Pradesh.

key_sections.title: Public Debt.
key_sections.description: Specifies how the public debt of the existing State of Andhra Pradesh shall be apportioned between the successor states.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to All-India Services.
key_sections.description: Addresses the creation of separate cadres for All-India Services for the successor states and allocation of officers.

key_sections.title: Apex Council for Godavari and Krishna river water resources and their Management Boards.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of an Apex Council for the supervision of river management boards for Godavari and Krishna rivers.

key_sections.title: Polavaram Irrigation Project to be a national project.
key_sections.description: Declares the Polavaram Irrigation Project as a national project and outlines the Central Government's role in its execution.

key_sections.title: Equal opportunities for quality higher education to all students.
key_sections.description: Ensures continuation of existing admission quotas and common admission processes in higher education institutions for a period of ten years.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the President the power to make orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions.

act_identification.act_title: THE RANI LAKSHMI BAI CENTRAL AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITY ACT, 2014
act_identification.act_short_title: Rani Lakshmi Bai Central Agricultural University Act, 2014

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole country with priority on issues related to Bundelkhand region, covering six districts in Madhya Pradesh (Chhatarpur, Damoh, Datia, Panna, Sagar and Tikamgarh) and seven districts in Uttar Pradesh (Banda, Chitrakoot, Hamirpur, Jalaun, Jhansi, Lalitpur and Mahoba).

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment and incorporation of a University in the Bundelkhand region for the development of agriculture and for the furtherance of the advancement of learning and pursuit of research in agriculture and allied sciences and declare it to be an institution of national importance.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes and incorporates the Rani Lakshmi Bai Central Agricultural University in the Bundelkhand region. Its main purpose is to develop agriculture, advance learning, and conduct research in agriculture and allied sciences, declaring it an institution of national importance.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Declaration of Rani Lakshmi Bai Central Agricultural University as an institution of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the Rani Lakshmi Bai Central Agricultural University as an institution of national importance due to its objects.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines various terms used within the Act and its Statutes, such as 'agriculture', 'Bundelkhand', 'University', and its authorities and officers.

key_sections.title: The University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Rani Lakshmi Bai Central Agricultural University, specifies its headquarters at Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, and outlines its corporate status and power to establish colleges.

key_sections.title: Objects of the University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the University's objectives, including imparting education, advancing learning and research in agriculture, undertaking extension education, and promoting partnerships.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Details the University's powers, such as providing instructions, conducting research, granting degrees, establishing colleges, creating posts, and managing its finances and property.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Specifies the University's jurisdiction for teaching, research, and extension education across the whole country, with a priority on the Bundelkhand region.

key_sections.title: The Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University and defines the Visitor's powers of inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the key officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Deans, Directors, Registrar, and Comptroller.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities of the University, such as the Board of Management, Academic Council, Research Council, Extension Education Council, Finance Committee, Faculties, and Board of Studies.

key_sections.title: Power to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Grants the power to make Statutes and specifies the matters they may cover, including the constitution of authorities, appointment of officers and employees, and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Grants the power to make Ordinances and specifies the matters they may cover, such as student admission, courses of study, examinations, and fees.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees.
key_sections.description: Mandates written contracts for employees and establishes a Tribunal of Arbitration for disputes arising from these contracts, making its decision final.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make provisions to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act, within three years of its commencement.

key_sections.title: Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and to be laid before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Requires all Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations to be published in the Official Gazette and laid before both Houses of Parliament for review.
