Power to further the advancement of learning and conducting of research in agricultural and allied sciences
Power to undertake programmes of extension education
Power to promote partnership and linkages with national and international educational institutions

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for disciplinary actions against employees and students for misconduct. For employees, this includes suspension, termination of service, and disciplinary action, with disputes referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration. For students, disciplinary actions can include removal from rolls, debarment from examinations, expulsion, rustication, fines, or cancellation of examination results. Disputes arising from student disciplinary actions are also referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration.

related_acts: Central Civil Services (Commutation of Pension) Rules, 1981

authorities_established: Rani Lakshmi Bai Central Agricultural University
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor, and the first members of the Board and Academic Council. The Board of Management appoints Deans of colleges, Directors, Registrar, Comptroller, teachers, academic staff, and other employees. The Vice-Chancellor nominates Heads of Departments and co-opts members to various councils and committees.

applies_to: The University and its constituent colleges
Employees of the University (teachers, academic staff, other staff)
Students enrolled in the University
Persons of either sex and of whatever caste, creed, race or class
special_provisions: Special provisions for the employment or admission of women, persons with disabilities, or persons belonging to the weaker sections of society, including Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other socially and educationally backward classes of citizens (Section 8 proviso).
Mandate to establish two colleges in the State of Madhya Pradesh and two colleges at Jhansi in the State of Uttar Pradesh within the Bundelkhand Region (Section 4(2) proviso).
Jurisdiction extends to the whole country with priority on issues related to the Bundelkhand region (Section 7(1)).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Board of Management has the power to make, amend, or repeal Statutes and Ordinances. The Academic Council proposes drafts for Ordinances and frames Regulations. Other University authorities may make Regulations for their business. The Vice-Chancellor makes the first Ordinances with Central Government approval. The Visitor assents to Statutes and can direct the University to make provisions in Statutes.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Visitor exercises oversight through inspections, inquiries, issuing directions, and annulling non-conforming proceedings. The Vice-Chancellor is the principal executive and academic officer, responsible for general supervision, control, and discipline. The Board of Management manages the University's administration and finances. Disputes regarding employee contracts and student disciplinary actions are resolved through a Tribunal of Arbitration.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the detailed Statutes of the University. These Statutes govern the appointment, powers, and duties of officers (Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Deans, Directors, Registrar, Comptroller, Heads of Departments, Librarians). They also define the constitution, powers, and functions of the University's authorities (Board of Management, Academic Council, Board of Studies, Finance Committee, Research Council, Extension Education Council). Additionally, the Statutes cover selection committees, terms and conditions of service, removal of employees, honorary degrees, withdrawal of degrees, maintenance of discipline among students, convocations, resignations, disqualifications, residence conditions for membership, the Alumni Association, Students' Council, and procedures for making Ordinances and Regulations.

key_sections.title: Plan for street vending.

key_sections.title: Town Vending Committee.

key_sections.title: Prevention of harassment by police and other authorities.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contraventions.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.

key_sections.title: Scheme for street vendors.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF DESIGN ACT, 2014
act_identification.act_short_title: the National Institutes of Design Act, 2014

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare [1][certain institutions of design to be institutions of national importance] for the promotion of quality and excellence in education, research and training in all disciplines relating to Design and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to declare certain institutions of design as institutions of national importance. Its primary purpose is to promote quality and excellence in education, research, and training across all disciplines related to Design, along with addressing connected or incidental matters.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Declaration of certain institutions as institutions of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the institutions mentioned in the Schedule as institutions of national importance due to their objects.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Chairperson', 'design', 'Director', 'Institute', 'Governing Council', and 'Senate'.

key_sections.title: Incorporation of Institute.
key_sections.description: States that each Institute shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and powers to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.

key_sections.title: Effect of incorporation of the Institute.
key_sections.description: Details the legal consequences of the Institute's incorporation, including vesting of property, transfer of liabilities, and continuity of employment for staff.

key_sections.title: Powers of Institute.
key_sections.description: Outlines the extensive powers of each Institute, including providing instruction, research, training, granting degrees, managing funds, and establishing campuses.

key_sections.title: Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of each Institute and grants powers to review work, hold inquiries, and issue directions.

key_sections.title: Authorities of Institute.
key_sections.description: Lists the primary authorities of each Institute, namely the Governing Council and the Senate, along with other authorities declared by Statutes.

key_sections.title: Governing Council.
key_sections.description: Specifies the composition of the Governing Council for every Institute, including the Chairperson, Director, and various nominated members.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Governing Council.
key_sections.description: Defines the responsibilities of the Governing Council for general superintendence, direction, and control of the Institute's affairs, including policy decisions and making Statutes.

key_sections.title: Functions of Senate.
key_sections.description: Assigns the Senate control and general regulation over instruction, education, and examination standards within the Institute.

key_sections.title: Director.
key_sections.description: Details the appointment, tenure, and responsibilities of the Director as the principal executive officer of the Institute, including administration and coordination.

key_sections.title: Fund of Institute.
key_sections.description: Establishes the requirement for each Institute to maintain a Fund, specifying sources of credit and how moneys are to be deposited and applied.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Mandates proper accounts and annual statements, with audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, and submission to the Central Government and Parliament.

key_sections.title: Power of Institute to grant degrees, etc.
key_sections.description: Confers upon each Institute the power to grant degrees, diplomas, certificates, and other academic distinctions equivalent to those granted by universities or other institutes.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, specifying matters such rules may cover.

powers_conferred: To provide for instructions, research and training in design disciplines (Institute)
To develop courses leading to graduate and post-graduate degrees, doctoral and post-doctoral distinctions (Institute)
To hold examinations and grant degrees, diplomas and other academic distinctions or titles (Institute)
To confer honorary degrees, awards or other distinctions (Institute)
To institute and award fellowships, scholarships, exhibitions, prizes and medals (Institute)
To fix, demand and receive fees and other charges (Institute)
To establish, maintain and manage halls and hostels for students (Institute)
To supervise and control the residence and regulate the discipline of students (Institute)
To institute academic and other posts and to make appointments thereto (Institute)
To frame Statutes and Ordinances and to alter, modify or rescind the same (Institute)
To co-operate with educational or other institutions globally (Institute)
To act as a nucleus for interaction between academia and industry (Institute)
To establish, equip and maintain workshops or laboratories or studios (Institute)
To acquire any patent or licence relating to invention, improvement or design (Institute)
To undertake consultancy in design areas (Institute)
To deal with any property belonging to, or vested in, the Institute (Institute)
To receive gifts, grants, donations or benefactions from Government and others (Institute)
To encourage and improve education by grant of loans, scholarships or other monetary assistance (Institute)
To prepare, print, publish, issue, acquire and circulate books, papers, periodicals, etc. (Institute)
To establish, form and maintain museums, libraries and collections (Institute)
To nominate designers, engineers, architects, craftsmen, technicians or investigators to study (Institute)
To retain or employ skilled professional, technical advisers, consultants, workers or craftsmen (Institute)
To encourage artisans, technicians and others with inventive skill (Institute)
To construct buildings and alter, extend, improve, repair, enlarge or modify (Institute)
To borrow and raise moneys (Institute)
To review the work and progress of the Institute or any Institute campus and to hold inquiries (Visitor)
To take action and issue directions based on inquiry reports (Visitor)
To exercise general superintendence, direction and control of the affairs of the Institute (Governing Council)
To take decisions on questions of policy relating to administration and working (Governing Council)
To take decision on the establishment of new Institute campus (Governing Council)
To institute courses of study (Governing Council)
To make Statutes (Governing Council)
To consider and modify or cancel Ordinances (Governing Council)
To consider and pass resolutions on annual report, accounts and budget estimates (Governing Council)
To appoint such committees as it considers necessary (Governing Council)
To enter into arrangements for securing and accepting endowments, grants, donations or gifts (Governing Council)
To take over and acquire by purchase, gift or otherwise movable and immovable properties, endowments or other funds (Governing Council)
To delegate to the Chairperson such of its powers for the conduct of business (Governing Council)
To control and generally regulate, and be responsible for the maintenance of standards of instruction, education and examination (Senate)
To appoint Director (Central Government)
To remove Director before expiry of tenure (Central Government)
To direct any Institute to set up an Endowment Fund and any other Fund (Central Government)
To issue directions to any Institute for effective administration of this Act (Central Government)
To make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act (Central Government)
To regulate its own procedure (Arbitral Tribunal)

amended_acts: National Institute of Design (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act 38 of 2019)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor nominates the Chairperson of the Governing Council, an outstanding Designer to the Governing Council, and the umpire for the Arbitral Tribunal. The Central Government nominates professionals and a representative of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises to the Governing Council, and appoints the Director. The Secretary of relevant Ministries/Departments nominates representatives to the Governing Council. The State Government nominates a representative to the Governing Council. The Chairperson nominates a management expert to the Governing Council and persons to the Senate. The Senate nominates persons to the Governing Council. The Governing Council makes appointments for academic and other posts and staff. The Director makes appointments for other staff. The Institute and the employee each appoint a member to the Arbitral Tribunal.

applies_to: National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad
National Institute of Design, Madhya Pradesh
National Institute of Design, Assam
National Institute of Design, Haryana
National Institute of Design, Andhra Pradesh
special_provisions: The commencement of this Act for the National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad, is deemed to be 16th September, 2014.

The commencement of this Act for the National Institutes of Design in Madhya Pradesh, Assam, Haryana, and Andhra Pradesh, is construed as the date on which the provisions of the National Institute of Design (Amendment) Act, 2019 come into force.

Transitional provisions allow the existing Governing Council and Policy and Planning Committee (deemed Senate) to continue functioning until new ones are constituted, and existing rules/regulations to apply until new Statutes and Ordinances are made.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government has the power to make rules. The Governing Council has the power to make Statutes. The Senate has the power to make Ordinances.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the administration and governance by the Institutes' authorities (Governing Council, Senate, Director). The Central Government provides grants, issues directions, and oversees the Institutes. Accounts are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India. Disputes between an Institute and its employees are referred to an Arbitral Tribunal.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No suit or proceeding shall lie in any court in respect of any matter which is required to be referred to the Arbitral Tribunal under Section 32(1).

act_identification.act_title: THE COAL MINES (SPECIAL PROVISIONS) ACT, 2015

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for allocation of coal mines and vesting of the right, title and interest in and over the land and mine infrastructure together with mining leases to successful bidders and allottees with a view to ensure continuity in coal mining operations and production of coal, and for promoting optimum utilisation of coal resources consistent with the requirement of the country in national interest and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS the Supreme Court vide judgment dated 25th August, 2014 read with its order dated 24th September, 2014 has cancelled the allocation of coal blocks and issued directions with regard to such coal blocks and the Central Government in pursuance of the said directions has to take immediate action to implement the said order; AND WHEREAS it is expedient in public interest for the Central Government to take immediate action to allocate coal mines to successful bidders and allottees keeping in view the energy security of the country and to minimise any impact on core sectors such as steel, cement and power utilities, which are vital for the development of the nation; AND WHEREAS Parliament is competent to legislate under entry 54 of List I of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution for regulation of mines and mineral development to theextent to which such regulation and development under the control of Union is declared by Parliament by law to be expedient in the public interest.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the allocation of coal mines and vesting of rights to successful bidders and allottees to ensure continuity in coal mining operations and production. Its objective is to promote optimum utilisation of coal resources in the national interest, especially after the Supreme Court cancelled prior coal block allocations.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER III TREATMENT OF RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF PRIOR ALLOTTEES
CHAPTER IV POWERS OF THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT AFTER THE APPOINTED DATE

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Short title, extent and commencement of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Eligibility to participate in auction and payment of fees.
key_sections.description: Outlines eligibility criteria for participating in coal mine auctions and associated fees.

key_sections.title: Allotment of mines to Government companies or corporations.
key_sections.description: Provides for the allotment of coal mines to Government companies or corporations.

key_sections.description: Specifies the priority for disbursal of proceeds from coal mine allocations.

key_sections.description: Details the liabilities of prior allottees and limits the liabilities of successful bidders/allottees.

key_sections.title: Commissioner of payments to be appointed and his powers.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of a Commissioner of payments to disburse amounts to prior allottees.

key_sections.title: Valuation of compensation for payment to prior allottee.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the method for valuing compensation payable to prior allottees for land and mine infrastructure.

key_sections.title: Responsibility of Central Government after appointed date.
key_sections.description: Outlines the Central Government's responsibility for Schedule II coal mines after the appointed date.

key_sections.title: Penalties for certain offences.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for specific offences related to obstruction, misuse, or failure to deliver documents.

key_sections.title: Dispute settlement and Bar of Jurisdiction of civil courts.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Tribunal under the Coal Bearing Areas Act for dispute settlement and bars civil court jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the Act's provisions override inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Second Ordinance, 2014 and includes saving provisions.

Central Government: To appoint a nominated authority (Section 6).
Central Government: To approve certain arrangements (Section 20).
Central Government: To make rules (Section 31).

Nominated Authority: To terminate vesting order or allotment order (Section 8(13)).
Designated Custodian: To manage and operate coal mines (Section 18).
Designated Custodian: To take control and possession of lands and mine infrastructure (Section 19).
Designated Custodian: To direct prior allottees for manpower (Section 19(2)).
Designated Custodian: To receive monies due to Schedule II coal mines (Section 19(3)).
Designated Custodian: To call for information, records and documents (Section 19(4)).
Designated Custodian: To appoint consultants or experts (Section 19(5)).
Designated Custodian: To transfer management and operation of coal mines (Section 19(6)).
Commissioner of Payments: To disburse amounts payable to prior allottees (Section 15).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalties for obstructing possession/management, failing to deliver documents, destroying/misusing mine infrastructure or coal stock, or retaining/removing/destroying property include imprisonment up to two years, or a minimum fine of one lakh rupees per day (up to two lakh rupees per day for continuing failure), or both (Section 23). Failure to comply with directions of the Central Government, nominated authority, or designated custodian is punishable with a fine of one lakh rupees (up to two lakh rupees per day for continuing failure) (Section 24).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the nominated authority, officers and staff to assist the nominated authority, the Commissioner of payments, officers and staff to assist the Commissioner, and the designated custodian.
regulatory_bodies: Tribunal constituted under the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957

applies_to: Successful bidders and allottees of coal mines
Government companies or corporations
Joint venture companies
Prior allottees (for liabilities, compensation, etc.)
Persons involved in coal mining operations
exemptions: Prior allottees are ineligible to participate in auction if additional levy is not paid or if convicted for an offence relating to coal block allocation with imprisonment for more than three years (Section 4(4), 4(5)).
No allotment to a prior allottee if the additional levy has not been paid (Section 5(2)).
Successful bidder or allottee is not bound by liabilities or obligations arising out of ownership or contractual rights related to movable property not vested in them (Section 10(2)).
Contracts not adopted or continued by a successful bidder or allottee cease to be enforceable against them (Section 11(2)).

No proceedings, orders of attachment, distress, receivership, execution, suits for recovery of money, or enforcement of security/guarantee (except as provided) shall lie or be proceeded against the successful bidder, allottee, or the land/mine infrastructure for liabilities prior to the Act's commencement (Section 14(1)).

No claim for wages, bonus, royalty, taxes, provident fund, pension, gratuity, or other dues related to a Schedule I coal mine for any period prior to the vesting or allotment order shall be enforceable against the Central Government, successful bidder, or allottee (Section 14(6)(a)).

No award, decree, attachment, or order of any court/tribunal related to Schedule I coal mines prior to the Act's commencement shall be enforceable against the Central Government, successful bidder, or allottee (Section 14(6)(b)).

No liability for contravention of any law for acts or omissions prior to the vesting or allotment order shall be enforceable against the successful bidder, allottee, or the Central Government (Section 14(6)(c)).
special_provisions: The powers of the State Government to prematurely terminate a prospecting licence or mining lease stand suspended for one year from the date of commencement of this Act, or such other period as notified, in relation to Schedule I coal mines (Section 17(3)).
Specific provisions for the allocation, management, and liabilities concerning Schedule I, Schedule II, and Schedule III coal mines are detailed throughout the Act.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, has the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act (Section 31(1)).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a process of public auction and allotment of coal mines, issuance of vesting and allotment orders by a nominated authority, and the management of certain mines by a designated custodian. It includes provisions for the collection of an additional levy, penalties for offences, and a dispute settlement mechanism through a specialized Tribunal. The Central Government provides policy directions to the nominated authority and designated custodian.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any dispute arising out of actions of the Central Government, nominated authority, Commissioner of payment, or designated custodian, or disputes between successful bidders/allottees and prior allottees, shall be adjudicated by the Tribunal constituted under the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957. The jurisdiction of civil courts is barred, except for the Supreme Court and High Courts (Section 27).

act_identification.act_title: THE BLACK MONEY (UNDISCLOSED FOREIGN INCOME AND ASSETS) AND IMPOSITION OF TAX ACT, 2015
act_identification.act_short_title: the Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make provisions to deal with the problem of the Black money that is undisclosed foreign income and assets, the procedure for dealing with such income and assets and to provide for imposition of tax on any undisclosed foreign income and asset held outside India and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to address the issue of undisclosed foreign income and assets, commonly referred to as 'Black Money'. It establishes procedures for dealing with such income and assets and provides for the imposition of tax on them when held outside India.

chapter_titles:
CHAPTER VI
TAX COMPLIANCE FOR UNDISCLOSED FOREIGN INCOME AND ASSETS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Charge of tax.
key_sections.description: Imposes tax on undisclosed foreign income and assets at a specified rate.

key_sections.title: Scope of total undisclosed foreign income and asset.
key_sections.description: Defines what constitutes total undisclosed foreign income and asset for taxation purposes.

key_sections.title: Assessment.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for the Assessing Officer to make an assessment or reassessment of undisclosed foreign income and assets.

key_sections.title: Penalty in relation to undisclosed foreign income and asset.
key_sections.description: Prescribes a penalty equal to three times the tax computed on undisclosed foreign income and asset.

key_sections.title: Punishment for failure to furnish return in relation to foreign income and asset.
key_sections.description: Stipulates rigorous imprisonment and fine for wilful failure to furnish income tax returns related to foreign income and assets.

key_sections.title: Punishment for wilful attempt to evade tax.
key_sections.description: Prescribes rigorous imprisonment and fine for wilful attempts to evade tax, penalty, or interest under this Act.

key_sections.title: Declaration of undisclosed foreign asset.
key_sections.description: Allows persons to make a declaration of undisclosed foreign assets under a tax compliance scheme.

key_sections.title: Charge of tax.
key_sections.description: Specifies the tax rate for undisclosed foreign assets declared under the compliance scheme.

key_sections.title: Penalty.
key_sections.description: Prescribes a penalty for undisclosed foreign assets declared under the compliance scheme.

key_sections.title: Agreement with foreign countries or specified territories.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to enter into agreements with foreign countries for information exchange and tax recovery.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Board of Direct Taxes the power to make rules for implementing the Act.

powers_conferred: Tax authorities (discovery and production of evidence, impounding books, rectification, imposing penalty, issuing notices)
Assessing Officer (assessment, reassessment, inquiry, recovery of tax dues, direct assessment)
Commissioner (Appeals) (hear and determine appeals, confirm, reduce, enhance or annul assessment, confirm, cancel or vary penalty)
Appellate Tribunal (hear and make orders on appeals)
High Court (hear appeals on substantial questions of law, execute Supreme Court orders)
Supreme Court (hear appeals from High Court judgments)
Principal Commissioner or Commissioner (revision of orders, sanction for prosecution, approval of valuer)
Board (Central Board of Direct Taxes) (control of tax authorities, issue orders/instructions/directions for appeals, make rules)
Central Government (notify dates for declaration/payment, enter into agreements with foreign countries, make rules, remove difficulties)
Tax Recovery Officer (draw up statement of tax arrears, recover tax dues, extend time for payment, rectify mistakes)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter IV outlines penalties including three times the tax for undisclosed foreign income/asset (Section 41), ten lakh rupees for failure to furnish returns or inaccurate particulars (Sections 42, 43), and an amount equal to tax arrear for default in payment (Section 44), and fifty thousand to two lakh rupees for other defaults (Section 45). Chapter V defines offences such as wilful failure to furnish returns (Section 49), failure to furnish information about foreign assets (Section 50), wilful attempt to evade tax (Section 51), false statements (Section 52), and abetment (Section 53), prescribing rigorous imprisonment ranging from three months to ten years, along with fines, with enhanced penalties for second and subsequent offences (Section 58).

It also includes a tax compliance scheme for voluntary declaration of undisclosed foreign assets.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court, Supreme Court, and for cognizance of offences, a metropolitan magistrate or a magistrate of the First Class.

act_identification.act_title: THE JUVENILE JUSTICE (CARE AND PROTECTION OF CHILDREN) ACT, 2015
act_identification.act_short_title: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to children alleged and found to be in conflict with law and children in need of care and protection by catering to their basic needs through proper care, protection, development, treatment, social re-integration, by adopting a child-friendly approach in the adjudication and disposal of matters in the best interest of children and for their rehabilitation through processes provided, and institutions and bodies established, herein under and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS, the provisions of the Constitution confer powers and impose duties, under clause (3) [of article 15, clauses (e) and (f) of article 39, article 45 and article 47, on the State to ensure that all the] needs of children are met and that their basic human rights are fully protected; AND WHEREAS, the Government of India has acceded on the 11th December, 1992 to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, adopted by the General Assembly of United Nations, which has prescribed a set of standards to be adhered to by all State parties in securing the best interest of the child; AND WHEREAS, it is expedient to re-enact the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000 (56 of 2000) to make comprehensive provisions for children alleged and found to be in conflict with law and children in need of care and protection, taking into consideration the standards prescribed in the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Administration of Juvenile Justice, 1985 (the Beijing Rules), the United Nations Rules for the Protection of Juveniles Deprived of their Liberty (1990), the Hague Convention on Protection of Children and Co-operation in Respect of Inter-country Adoption (1993), and other related international instruments.
act_overview.purpose: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to children in conflict with law and children in need of care and protection. Its main purpose is to ensure their basic needs, proper care, protection, development, treatment, and social re-integration through a child-friendly approach, focusing on their best interests and rehabilitation.

chapter_titles: GENERAL PRINCIPLES OF CARE AND PROTECTION OF CHILDREN
PROCEDURE IN RELATION TO CHILDREN IN CONFLICT WITH LAW
PROCEDURE IN RELATION TO CHILDREN IN NEED OF CARE AND PROTECTION

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'child', 'child in conflict with law', 'child in need of care and protection', 'Board', 'Committee', and various types of institutions.

key_sections.title: General principles to be followed in administration of Act.
key_sections.description: Outlines fundamental principles like presumption of innocence, dignity and worth, participation, best interest of the child, family responsibility, safety, non-stigmatising semantics, non-waiver of rights, equality, privacy, institutionalisation as a last resort, repatriation, fresh start, diversion, and natural justice.

key_sections.title: Juvenile Justice Board.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of Juvenile Justice Boards in every district for children in conflict with law, specifying their composition, qualifications of members, and training requirements.

key_sections.title: Powers, functions and responsibilities of the Board.
key_sections.description: Details the exclusive powers of the Board to deal with children in conflict with law, including ensuring child rights, providing legal aid, conducting social investigations, adjudicating cases, and inspecting residential facilities.

key_sections.description: Prescribes the procedure and timelines for inquiries conducted by the Board concerning children alleged to be in conflict with law, including provisions for petty, serious, and heinous offences.

key_sections.title: Preliminary assessment into heinous offences by Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for the Board to conduct a preliminary assessment for children aged sixteen years or above who are alleged to have committed heinous offences, to determine their mental and physical capacity and understanding of consequences.

key_sections.title: Orders regarding child found to be in conflict with law.
key_sections.description: Specifies various orders the Board may pass for children found to be in conflict with law, ranging from advice and counselling to community service, probation, or placement in special homes.

key_sections.title: Powers of Children’s Court.
key_sections.description: Defines the powers of the Children's Court, particularly in cases of heinous offences where a child is to be tried as an adult, and its role in ensuring rehabilitation and follow-up.

key_sections.title: Child Welfare Committee.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of Child Welfare Committees in every district for children in need of care and protection, detailing their composition, qualifications, and functioning.

key_sections.title: Functions and responsibilities of Committee.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the duties of the Committee, including taking cognizance of children, conducting inquiries, directing social investigations, ensuring rehabilitation, certifying surrender deeds, and declaring children legally free for adoption.

key_sections.title: Procedure for declaring a child legally free for adoption.
key_sections.description: Establishes the process for the Committee to declare orphan, abandoned, or surrendered children legally free for adoption after due inquiry and tracing efforts.

key_sections.title: Registration of child care institutions.
key_sections.description: Requires all child care institutions, whether government or NGO-run, to be registered under this Act, specifying the registration process, capacity determination, and consequences of non-compliance.

key_sections.title: Adoption.
key_sections.description: States that adoption is for ensuring the right to family for orphan, abandoned, and surrendered children, and specifies that inter-country adoptions must follow this Act, while exempting adoptions under the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956.

key_sections.title: Prohibition on disclosure of identity of children.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the disclosure of the identity of children involved in legal proceedings in media, with exceptions for the child's best interest, and prescribes penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Punishment for cruelty to child.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for persons in charge of a child who assault, abandon, abuse, expose, or wilfully neglect the child, with enhanced penalties for institutional employees or if the child is severely harmed.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000, while saving actions taken under the repealed Act.

powers_conferred: Juvenile Justice Board: Deal exclusively with proceedings relating to children in conflict with law, ensure child rights, legal aid, social investigation, adjudicate cases, transfer matters to Committee, order registration of FIRs, inspect jails.
Children's Court: Exercise powers of Board, decide need for trial as adult, conduct inquiry, ensure individual care plan, send child to place of safety.

Child Welfare Committee: Dispose of cases for care, protection, treatment, development, rehabilitation of children in need of care and protection, take cognizance, conduct inquiry, direct social investigation, declare fit persons, direct foster care, ensure restoration, certify surrender deeds, declare children legally free for adoption, take suo motu cognizance, coordinate with other agencies.

Central Adoption Resource Authority: Promote in-country adoptions, regulate inter-country adoptions, frame regulations, carry out Hague Convention functions, issue instructions to agencies, recommend action against non-compliant officials/institutions.

State Government: Establish and maintain observation homes, special homes, places of safety, children's homes, open shelters, register institutions, make rules, create juvenile justice fund, constitute Child Protection Society and District Child Protection Unit, constitute Special Juvenile Police Units, order transfer of children.
District Magistrate: Review pendency of inquiry, grievance redressal authority for Committee, direct remedial measures for pendency, grant adoption orders, inspect institutions, evaluate functioning.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter IX defines various offences against children and prescribes penalties. These include: prohibition on disclosure of identity of children (imprisonment up to six months or fine up to two lakh rupees); cruelty to child (imprisonment up to three years or fine of one lakh rupees, with higher penalties for institutional employees or severe harm); employment of child for begging (imprisonment up to five years and fine of one lakh rupees, with rigorous imprisonment for 7-10 years and fine of five lakh rupees if child is maimed); giving intoxicating liquor/narcotic drug/psychotropic substance to a child (rigorous imprisonment up to seven years and fine up to one lakh rupees); using a child for vending/peddling/smuggling such substances (rigorous imprisonment up to seven years and fine up to one lakh rupees); exploitation of a child employee (rigorous imprisonment up to five years and fine of one lakh rupees); adoption without following prescribed procedures (imprisonment up to three years or fine of one lakh rupees, plus withdrawal of agency recognition); sale and procurement of children (rigorous imprisonment up to five years and fine of one lakh rupees, with higher imprisonment for persons in charge of the child); corporal punishment (fine for first offence, imprisonment/fine for subsequent, dismissal from service, and imprisonment/fine for management non-cooperation); use of child by militant groups or other adults (rigorous imprisonment up to seven years and fine of five lakh rupees); and double penalty for offences committed on disabled children. Offences are classified as cognizable/non-cognizable and bailable/non-bailable based on punishment term, and are triable by the Children's Court.

repealed_acts: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000 (56 of 2000)
related_acts: Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005 (4 of 2006)
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (32 of 2012)
Hague Convention on Protection of Children and Co-operation in Respect of Inter-country Adoption (1993)
Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (61 of 1985)
Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956 (78 of 1956)
Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 (35 of 2009)
Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 (1 of 1996)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government has the power to appoint members of the Juvenile Justice Board and the Child Welfare Committee.
regulatory_bodies: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
State Commission for Protection of Child Rights

applies_to: children in need of care and protection
children in conflict with law
all matters concerning children
exemptions: adoption of children made under the provisions of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956 (78 of 1956)
special_provisions: Special provisions for children below or above sixteen years of age in conflict with law for heinous offences.
Preference for children with physical and mental disability, siblings, and children above five years of age in inter-country adoption.
Special provisions for offences committed on disabled children.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: State Government (for general rules); Central Government (for model rules and certain regulations like adoption regulations by Authority).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out by the police (Special Juvenile Police Unit, Child Welfare Police Officer), Juvenile Justice Boards, Child Welfare Committees, and Children's Courts. Child care institutions, observation homes, special homes, and places of safety provide care and rehabilitation. Probation officers and Child Welfare Officers conduct social investigations and supervision. The Central Adoption Resource Authority and State Adoption Resource Agency manage adoption processes. Inspection committees monitor institutions, and the District Magistrate provides review and grievance redressal.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Juvenile Justice Board, Children's Court, High Court, District Magistrate, Divisional Commissioner.

act_identification.act_title: THE BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS ACT, 2016
act_identification.act_short_title: The Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of a national standards body for the harmonious development of the activities of standardisation, conformity assessment and quality assurance of goods, articles, processes, systems and services and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: To establish a national standards body, the Bureau of Indian Standards, to promote and regulate standardisation, conformity assessment, and quality assurance for goods, articles, processes, systems, and services. It aims to ensure quality and protect consumer interests through a structured framework for standards and certification.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS
CHAPTER III INDIAN STANDARDS, CERTIFICATION AND LICENCE
CHAPTER IV FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its applicability to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act, such as 'article', 'Bureau', 'Indian Standard', 'Standard Mark', 'licence', and 'precious metal article'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Bureau and Constitution of Governing Council.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Bureau of Indian Standards as a national body corporate and outlines the constitution of its Governing Council, including its members and their roles.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Bureau.
key_sections.description: Details the extensive powers and functions of the Bureau, including establishing branches, recognising international marks, enforcing provisions, providing services, publishing standards, and promoting quality.

key_sections.title: Indian Standards.
key_sections.description: States that standards established by the Bureau are Indian Standards and outlines the Bureau's powers to establish, publish, review, promote, and adopt standards, and to constitute technical committees.

key_sections.title: Grant of licence or certificate of conformity.
key_sections.description: Describes the process for applying for and granting a licence or certificate of conformity for goods, articles, processes, systems, or services that meet an Indian Standard, and related conditions.

key_sections.title: Certification of Standard Mark of jewellers and sellers of certain specified goods or articles.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to notify precious metal articles or other goods for compulsory marking with a Hallmark or Standard Mark, and outlines the certification process for jewellers and sellers.

key_sections.title: Central Government to direct compulsory use of Standard Mark.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to mandate the compulsory use of a Standard Mark for certain goods, articles, processes, systems, or services in the public interest or for protection of health, safety, or environment.

key_sections.title: Prohibition to manufacture, sell, etc., certain goods without Standard Mark.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the manufacture, import, distribution, or sale of goods, articles, processes, systems, or services specified under Section 16 without a valid Standard Mark or licence, or if they do not conform to the relevant standard.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for contraventions of various provisions of the Act, such as misuse of the Bureau's name, selling non-conforming goods, or manufacturing without a Standard Mark.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act by notification in the Official Gazette.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Executive Committee the power to make regulations, with the Central Government's approval, consistent with the Act and rules, to carry out the Act's purposes.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986, and includes savings clauses to ensure continuity of actions taken under the repealed Act.

powers_conferred: Power to establish branches, offices or agencies in India or outside (Bureau)
Power to recognise marks of international bodies or institutions (Bureau)
Power to seek recognition of the Bureau and Indian Standards outside India (Bureau)
Power to enter into and search places, premises or vehicles, and inspect and seize goods or articles and documents (Bureau)
Power to provide services to manufacturers and consumers for compliances of standards (Bureau)
Power to provide training services in relation to quality management, standards, conformity assessment, laboratory testing and calibration (Bureau)
Power to publish Indian Standards and sell publications (Bureau)
Power to authorise agencies in India or outside India for carrying out activities of the Bureau (Bureau)
Power to obtain membership in regional, international and foreign bodies (Bureau)
Power to undertake testing of samples for purposes other than for conformity assessment (Bureau)
Power to undertake activities relating to legal metrology (Bureau)
Power to issue directions on questions of policy to the Bureau (Central Government)
Power to direct compulsory use of Standard Mark (Central Government)
Power to appoint Director General (Central Government)
Power to make rules (Central Government)
Power to make regulations (Executive Committee with Central Government approval)
Power to appoint certification officers (Bureau)
Power to inspect operations and take samples (Certification Officer)
Power to search and seizure (Certification Officer)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalty for contravention of Section 11 (prohibition to publish/reproduce without authorisation) or Section 26 (restriction on use of Bureau's name/Indian Standard) is a fine up to five lakh rupees. Contravention of Section 14(6) or (8) (unauthorised use of Standard Mark/Hallmark by testing centres) or Section 15 (prohibition to import/sell without certification) is punishable with imprisonment up to one year or a fine not less than one lakh rupees but up to five times the value of goods, or both. Contravention of Section 17 (prohibition to manufacture/sell certain goods without Standard Mark) is punishable with imprisonment up to two years or a fine not less than two lakh rupees for the first contravention and not less than five lakh rupees for subsequent contraventions, up to ten times the value of goods, or both. The offence under Section 17(3) is cognizable.

repealed_acts: The Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 (63 of 1986)
related_acts: Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937 (1 of 1937)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Director General of the Bureau and certain members of the Governing Council. The Bureau may appoint other officers and employees, and certification officers.

applies_to: Whole of India
Manufacturers, importers, distributors, retailers, sellers, lessors of goods or articles
Providers of services
Jewellers and sellers of precious metal articles
Testing and marking centres, assaying and hallmarking centres
Any person dealing with goods, articles, processes, systems, or services subject to Indian Standards or compulsory marking
exemptions: Individual making a copy of Indian Standard for personal use

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Bureau, through its certification officers, has powers of inspection, search, and seizure. Offences are cognizable by courts, and penalties are prescribed. The Director General can compound certain offences. Appeals can be made to the Director General and then to the Central Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class, specially empowered in this behalf.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL WATERWAYS ACT, 2016

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make provisions for existing national waterways and to provide for the declaration of certain inland waterways to be national waterways and also to provide for the regulation and development of the said waterways for the purposes of shipping and navigation and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to make provisions for existing national waterways and to declare certain inland waterways as national waterways. It also aims to regulate and develop these waterways for shipping and navigation and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date, which is to be appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Existing national waterways and declaration of certain inland waterways as national waterways.
key_sections.description: Continues existing national waterways and declares additional inland waterways specified in the Schedule as national waterways for shipping and navigation.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to expediency of control and development by Union of waterways specified in Schedule for certain purposes.
key_sections.description: Declares that it is expedient for the Union to control and develop the specified waterways for shipping and navigation, as provided in the Inland Waterways Authority of India Act, 1985.

key_sections.title: Amendment of section 2 of Act 82 of 1985.

key_sections.title: Repeal of certain enactments and saving.

powers_conferred: Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint the date of commencement of the Act.
Union should take under its control the regulation and development of the waterways specified in the Schedule for the purposes of shipping and navigation.

amended_acts: Inland Waterways Authority of India Act, 1985 (82 of 1985)

the National Waterway (Kakinada-Puducherry Stretch of Canals and the Kaluvelly Tank, Bhadrachalam-Rajahmundry Stretch of River Godavari and Wazirabad-Vijayawada Stretch of River Krishna) Act, 2008 (24 of 2008)

certain inland waterways

act_identification.act_title: THE AADHAAR (TARGETED DELIVERY OF FINANCIAL AND OTHER SUBSIDIES, BENEFITS AND SERVICES) ACT, 2016
act_identification.act_short_title: Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for, as a good governance, efficient, transparent, and targeted delivery of subsidies, benefits and services, the expenditure for which is incurred from the Consolidated Fund of India, [1][or the Consolidated Fund of the State] to individuals residing in India through assigning of unique identity numbers to such individuals and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to ensure good governance, efficient, transparent, and targeted delivery of subsidies, benefits, and services funded by the Consolidated Fund of India or a State. This is achieved by assigning unique identity numbers (Aadhaar) to individuals residing in India.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical application, and commencement provisions.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Aadhaar number.
key_sections.description: Establishes the entitlement of residents to obtain an Aadhaar number and the process of its issuance.

key_sections.title: Properties of Aadhaar number.
key_sections.description: Describes the characteristics of an Aadhaar number, including its non-reassignability, randomness, and voluntary use for identity establishment.

key_sections.title: Proof of Aadhaar number necessary for receipt of certain subsidies, benefits and services, etc.
key_sections.description: Mandates Aadhaar authentication or proof for receiving certain government subsidies, benefits, or services.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Authority.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI).

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Authority.
key_sections.description: Outlines the comprehensive powers and functions of the Unique Identification Authority of India.

key_sections.title: Security and confidentiality of information.
key_sections.description: Ensures the security and confidentiality of identity information and authentication records held by the Authority.

key_sections.title: Restriction on sharing information.
key_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on sharing core biometric information and other identity information.

key_sections.title: Disclosure of information in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which identity information or authentication records may be disclosed, such as by court order or in national security interest.

key_sections.title: Penalty for failure to comply with provisions of this Act, rules, regulations and directions.
key_sections.description: Prescribes civil penalties for entities in the Aadhaar ecosystem failing to comply with the Act, rules, regulations, or directions.

key_sections.title: Penalty for impersonation at time of enrolment.
key_sections.description: Defines and penalizes impersonation during the Aadhaar enrolment process.

key_sections.title: Penalty for unauthorised access to the Central Identities Data Repository.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for unauthorized access, data manipulation, or other malicious activities related to the Central Identities Data Repository.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power of Authority to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the Unique Identification Authority of India the power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to notify commencement dates, notify categories of individuals for Aadhaar, appoint Chairperson/Members/CEO of the Authority, remove Chairperson/Members, make grants to the Authority, supersede the Authority, issue directions to the Authority, and make rules.

Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI): Power to issue Aadhaar numbers, take special measures for certain persons, require updates to information, perform authentication, establish and maintain the Central Identities Data Repository (CIDR), issue directions, ensure security and confidentiality of information, alter demographic/biometric information, maintain authentication records, appoint Adjudicating Officers, and make regulations.
Adjudicating Officer: Power to hold inquiries and impose civil penalties.
Appellate Tribunal: Power to hear appeals against decisions of the Adjudicating Officer.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes civil penalties for non-compliance by entities in the Aadhaar ecosystem, which can extend up to one crore rupees for each contravention and additional penalties for continuing failures. Criminal penalties are defined for various offences including impersonation at enrolment (imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to 10,000 rupees), impersonation of an Aadhaar holder (imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to 10,000 rupees), unauthorized disclosure of identity information (imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to 10,000 rupees, or 1 lakh for companies), unauthorized access to or tampering with the Central Identities Data Repository (imprisonment up to 10 years and fine not less than 10 lakh rupees), unauthorized use by requesting entities (imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to 10,000 rupees, or 1 lakh for companies), and non-compliance with intimation requirements (penalty up to 1 lakh rupees, or 10 lakh for companies). A general penalty is also provided for other offences.

related_acts: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997 (24 of 1997)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the Chairperson, Members, and Chief Executive Officer of the Unique Identification Authority of India. The Authority itself has the power to appoint an Adjudicating Officer.
regulatory_bodies: Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal

applies_to: individuals residing in India
Every resident
any offence or contravention thereunder committed outside India by any person
exemptions: Children shall not be denied any subsidy, benefit or service for failure to establish identity by authentication or furnishing Aadhaar proof.
Individuals to whom no Aadhaar number has been assigned shall be offered alternate and viable means of identification for delivery of subsidy, benefit or service.
Requesting entities shall not deny any service to an Aadhaar number holder for refusing to, or being unable to, undergo authentication.
special_provisions: Special measures for issuance of Aadhaar number to women, children, senior citizens, persons with disability, unskilled and unorganised workers, nomadic tribes or other persons without permanent dwelling house.
Provisions for Aadhaar number of children, including parental consent and option to cancel at eighteen years of age.
Exemption from tax on income for the Unique Identification Authority of India.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through directions issued by the Authority, civil penalties adjudicated by an Adjudicating Officer with appeals to an Appellate Tribunal and the Supreme Court, and criminal penalties for offences investigated by police officers not below the rank of Inspector of Police. Cognizance of offences is taken by courts based on complaints from the Authority or an Aadhaar number holder.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts not inferior to that of a Judge of a High Court for disclosure orders; Supreme Court for appeals from the Appellate Tribunal; and no court inferior to that of a Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or a Chief Judicial Magistrate shall try any offence punishable under this Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE REAL ESTATE (REGULATION AND DEVELOPMENT) ACT, 2016
act_identification.act_short_title: The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish the Real Estate Regulatory Authority for regulation and promotion of the real estate sector and to ensure sale of plot, apartment or building, as the case may be, or sale of real estate project, in an efficient and transparent manner and to protect the interest of consumers in the real estate sector and to establish an adjudicating mechanism for speedy dispute redressal and also to establish the Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals from the decisions, directions or orders of the Real Estate Regulatory Authority and the adjudicating officer and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish a Real Estate Regulatory Authority to regulate and promote the real estate sector, ensuring transparency and efficiency in the sale of real estate projects. It seeks to protect the interests of consumers, provide a speedy dispute redressal mechanism through an adjudicating officer, and establish an Appellate Tribunal for appeals.

chapter_titles: REGISTRATION OF REAL ESTATE PROJECT AND REGISTRATION OF REAL ESTATE AGENTS

key_definitions: estimated cost of real estate project

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's name, geographical scope, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Prior registration of real estate project with Real Estate Regulatory Authority.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration of real estate projects with the Authority, with certain exemptions.

key_sections.title: Application for registration of real estate projects.
key_sections.description: Details the application process and required documents for project registration.

key_sections.title: Grant of registration.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for granting or rejecting project registration by the Authority.

key_sections.title: Registration of real estate agents.
key_sections.description: Requires real estate agents to register with the Authority.

key_sections.title: Functions and duties of promoter.

key_sections.title: Return of amount and compensation.
key_sections.description: Deals with the promoter's liability to return amounts and pay compensation in case of failure to complete or give possession.

key_sections.title: Rights and duties of allottees.
key_sections.description: Enlists the rights and responsibilities of allottees in a real estate project.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Real Estate Regulatory Authority.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the Real Estate Regulatory Authority.

key_sections.title: Functions of Authority.
key_sections.description: Describes the key functions of the Real Estate Regulatory Authority, including registration, regulation, and database maintenance.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Real Estate Appellate Tribunal.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the Real Estate Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals.

key_sections.title: Punishment for nonregistration under section 3.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for promoters failing to register projects.

key_sections.title: Power to adjudicate.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.

powers_conferred: Real Estate Regulatory Authority: To register and regulate projects and agents, call for information and conduct investigations, issue interim orders, issue directions, impose penalty or interest, rectify orders.
Appropriate Government: To establish Authority and Appellate Tribunal, supersede Authority, issue directions to Authority, make rules.
Adjudicating Officer: To adjudicate compensation, summon and enforce attendance.
Central Government: To make grants and loans to Authority, establish Central Advisory Council, remove difficulties.
State Government: To make grants and loans to Authority.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter VIII details offences and penalties. Promoters face penalties up to 10% of estimated project cost for non-registration, and imprisonment up to 3 years for continued violation or failure to comply with Appellate Tribunal orders. False information or contravention of other provisions incurs penalties up to 5% of project cost. Real estate agents face daily penalties up to 5% of the property cost for non-registration or contravention of duties, and imprisonment up to 1 year for non-compliance with Appellate Tribunal orders. Allottees face penalties up to 5% of property cost for non-compliance with Authority orders, and imprisonment up to 1 year for non-compliance with Appellate Tribunal orders. Offences by companies hold both the company and responsible individuals liable. Imprisonment punishments may be compounded by the court.

amended_acts: The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Removal of Difficulties Order, 2016
The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization (Adaptation of Central Laws) Order, 2020
The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization (Adaptation of Central Laws) Third Order, 2020

Cost and Works Accountants Act, 1959 (23 of 1959)

Real estate agents
Allottees (buyers) of plots, apartments, or buildings
Real estate projects in planning areas

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The appropriate Government (for rules), the Central Government (for removing difficulties), and the Authority (for regulations).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through mandatory registration of projects and agents, a complaint mechanism with the Authority or adjudicating officer, investigation powers of the Authority, imposition and recovery of penalties and interest, adjudication for compensation, and a two-tier appeal process to the Appellate Tribunal and then to the High Court. Offences are tried by Metropolitan Magistrates or Judicial Magistrates of the first class.

act_identification.act_title: THE REPEALING AND AMENDING ACT, 2016

act_overview.preamble: An Act to repeal certain enactments and to amend certain other enactments.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to repeal certain existing enactments and to amend certain other enactments as specified in its schedules. It streamlines the body of law by removing obsolete acts and making necessary changes to others.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Repealing and Amending Act, 2016'.

key_sections.title: Repeal of certain enactments.
key_sections.description: Provides for the repeal of enactments specified in the First Schedule to the extent mentioned therein.

key_sections.title: Amendment of certain enactments.
key_sections.description: Provides for the amendment of enactments specified in the Second Schedule to the extent and manner mentioned therein.

key_sections.title: Savings.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the repeal of any enactment by this Act shall not affect other enactments, validity of past actions, acquired rights, liabilities, remedies, or revive non-existing matters.
