act_identification.act_title: An Act to give effect to the Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft and for matters connected therewith.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India and, save as otherwise provided in this Act, it applies also to any offence thereunder committed outside India by any person.

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to give effect to the Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft (Hague Convention, 1970) and its Supplementary Protocol (Beijing, 2010). It aims to effectively address unlawful acts of seizure or control of aircraft that jeopardize the safety of persons and property by making suitable legal provisions.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II HIJACKING AND CONNECTED OFFENCES

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its geographical extent to the whole of India and extraterritorial application, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Agency', 'aircraft', 'Hague Convention', and 'hostage'.

key_sections.title: Hijacking.
key_sections.description: Defines the offence of hijacking, including direct seizure, threats, attempts, abetment, organisation, direction, and accomplice participation.

key_sections.title: Punishment for hijacking.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for hijacking, which can be death (if death of a person results) or imprisonment for life, along with fine and confiscation of property.

key_sections.title: Punishment for acts of violence connected with hijacking.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that acts of violence committed during hijacking will be punished as if committed in India under existing laws.

key_sections.title: Conferment of powers of investigations, etc.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to confer powers of arrest, investigation, and prosecution on its officers or officers of the National Investigation Agency.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Outlines the jurisdiction of Indian courts over offences committed outside India, including those involving Indian aircraft, citizens, or stateless persons residing in India.

key_sections.title: Designated Court.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of Designated Courts by State Governments for speedy trial of offences under the Act, and specifies the Special Court under the NIA Act as a Designated Court in certain cases.

key_sections.title: Provisions as to extradition.
key_sections.description: Declares hijacking offences as extraditable and not political offences, ensuring cooperation with Convention countries for extradition.

key_sections.title: Provision as to bail.
key_sections.description: Imposes strict conditions for granting bail to persons accused under this Act, requiring public prosecutor's opportunity to oppose and court's satisfaction of innocence.

key_sections.title: Previous sanction necessary for prosecution.
key_sections.description: Mandates prior sanction from the Central Government before instituting any prosecution for an offence under this Act.

key_sections.title: Presumption as to offences under sections 3 and 5.
key_sections.description: Establishes legal presumptions in prosecution if arms, ammunition, explosives are recovered or evidence of force/threat exists, placing the burden of proof on the accused.

key_sections.title: Powers of investigating officers to seize or attach property.
key_sections.description: Grants investigating officers the power to seize or attach property believed to be related to the commission of an offence, subject to confirmation by the Designated Court.

key_sections.title: Confiscation and forfeiture of property.
key_sections.description: States that property ordered for confiscation by the Designated Court under Section 4 shall stand forfeited to the Government free from encumbrances.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Anti-Hijacking Act, 1982, while including savings clauses for previous operations, rights, liabilities, penalties, and ongoing legal proceedings.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Confer powers of arrest, investigation and prosecution on officers (Section 6(1))
Central Government: Certify contracting parties to the Hague Convention (Section 13)
Central Government: Direct certain aircraft to be treated as registered in Convention countries (Section 14(1))
Central Government: Grant previous sanction for prosecution (Section 15)
Central Government: Make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act (Section 20(1))
State Government: Specify a Court of Sessions to be a Designated Court (Section 8(1))
Officers of Central Government or Agency: Powers of arrest, investigation and prosecution (Section 6(1))
Officers of Central Government or Agency: Seize or attach property (Section 18(1))
Designated Court: Hold trial on a day-to-day basis (Section 8(3))
Designated Court: Try all offences under this Act and other connected offences (Section 9)
Designated Court: Exercise powers of a Magistrate under section 167 of CrPC (Section 9(1)(c))
Designated Court: Take cognizance of offence without accused being committed for trial (Section 9(1)(d))
Designated Court: Confirm or revoke order of seizure or attachment (Section 18(3))
Designated Court: Order confiscation and forfeiture of property (Section 19)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines the offence of hijacking (Section 3) which includes unlawful and intentional seizure or control of an aircraft, threats, attempts, abetment, organisation, direction, and accomplice participation. Punishment for hijacking (Section 4) is death where it results in the death of a hostage, security personnel, or any person not involved in the offence, or imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life) and fine, with property liable to confiscation. Acts of violence connected with hijacking (Section 5) are punishable with the same punishment as if committed in India under any other law.

repealed_acts: The Anti-Hijacking Act, 1982 (65 of 1982)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The State Government, with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court, specifies a Court of Sessions to be a Designated Court (Section 8(1)). The Central Government may confer powers of arrest, investigation, and prosecution on any officer of the Central Government or the Agency (Section 6(1)).

applies_to: Whole of India
Any offence committed outside India by any person
Offences committed against or on board an aircraft registered in India
Offences committed on board an aircraft that lands in India with the alleged offender
Offences committed against or on board an aircraft leased without crew to a lessee with principal place of business or permanent residence in India
Offences committed by or against a citizen of India
Offences committed by a stateless person whose habitual residence is in the territory of India
exemptions: Military aircraft
Aircraft used in customs or police service

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through investigation and prosecution by officers of the Central Government or the National Investigation Agency, trial by Designated Courts, and provisions for extradition. It also includes powers for seizure, attachment, confiscation, and forfeiture of property related to the offence. Previous sanction of the Central Government is required for prosecution.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Designated Court; High Court (for special bail powers)

act_identification.act_title: THE DR. RAJENDRA PRASAD CENTRAL AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITY ACT, 2016
act_identification.act_short_title: The Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University Act, 2016.

legislative_details.ministry_department: Department of Agricultural Research and Education, Government of India
legislative_details.geographical_extent: the whole country with special reference to the State of Bihar.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment and incorporation of a University by conversion of the existing Rajendra Agricultural University, Pusa, Bihar to Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University for the development of agriculture and for the furtherance of the advancement of learning and pursuit of research in agriculture and allied sciences and to declare it to be an institution of national importance.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes and incorporates the Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University by converting the existing Rajendra Agricultural University. Its main purpose is to develop agriculture, advance learning, and conduct research in agricultural and allied sciences, and to declare it an institution of national importance.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Declaration of Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University as an institution of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the University as an institution of national importance.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act and its Statutes.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the University as a body corporate, specifies its headquarters, and details its perpetual succession and common seal.

key_sections.title: Objects of the University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary goals of the University, including education, research, and extension education in agriculture and allied sciences.

key_sections.title: Powers of the University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers of the University, such as providing instruction, conducting research, granting degrees, and establishing colleges.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Defines the geographical and subject matter jurisdiction of the University, extending to the whole country with special reference to Bihar.

key_sections.title: The Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor and outlines the Visitor's powers of inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions.

key_sections.title: Officers of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the various officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Deans, and Registrar.

key_sections.title: Authorities of the University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities governing the University, such as the Board of Management and Academic Council.

key_sections.title: Power to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Specifies the matters for which Statutes can be made, covering governance, appointments, and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Details the matters for which Ordinances can be made, including student admission, courses of study, and examinations.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees.
key_sections.description: Addresses the conditions of service for University employees, including contract, dispute resolution, and arbitration.

key_sections.title: Effect of establishment of University.
key_sections.description: Describes the transitional effects of the University's establishment, including vesting of property, transfer of liabilities, and employment of existing staff.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Bihar Agricultural University Act.
key_sections.description: Repeals the relevant parts of the Bihar Agricultural University Act, 1987, concerning the Rajendra Agricultural University.

act_identification.act_title: THE INSOLVENCY AND BANKRUPTCY CODE, 2016

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the laws relating to reorganisation and insolvency resolution of corporate persons, partnership firms and individuals in a time bound manner for maximisation of value of assets of such persons, to promote entrepreneurship, availability of credit and balance the interests of all the stakeholders including alteration in the order of priority of payment of Government dues and to establish an Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to consolidate and amend laws related to reorganisation and insolvency resolution for corporate persons, partnership firms, and individuals. It aims to achieve this in a time-bound manner to maximize asset value, promote entrepreneurship, ensure credit availability, and balance stakeholder interests, including altering the priority of government dues. It also establishes the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India.

chapter_titles: FAST TRACK CORPORATE INSOLVENCY RESOLUTION PROCESS
BANKRUPTCY ORDER FOR INDIVIDUALS AND PARTNERSHIP FIRMS
ADMINISTRATION AND DISTRIBUTION OF THE ESTATE OF THE BANKRUPT

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Code, its applicability to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on dates appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides general definitions for terms used throughout the Code, such as 'Board', 'creditor', 'debt', 'default', 'financial information', 'insolvency professional', 'information utility', and 'property'.

key_sections.title: Application of this Part.
key_sections.description: States that Part II (Insolvency Resolution and Liquidation for Corporate Persons) applies to corporate debtors with a minimum default amount of one crore rupees, subject to Central Government notification.

key_sections.title: Persons who may initiate corporate insolvency resolution process.
key_sections.description: Identifies financial creditors, operational creditors, or the corporate debtor itself as persons who may initiate the corporate insolvency resolution process upon default.

key_sections.title: Moratorium.
key_sections.description: Declares a moratorium on the insolvency commencement date, prohibiting legal actions, asset transfers, and enforcement of security interests against the corporate debtor.

key_sections.title: Committee of creditors.
key_sections.description: Outlines the constitution of the committee of creditors, comprising financial creditors, and specifies their voting rights and representation.

key_sections.title: Person not eligible to be resolution applicant.
key_sections.description: Lists criteria that disqualify a person or entity from being eligible to submit a resolution plan, such as being an undischarged insolvent, wilful defaulter, or having non-performing asset accounts.

key_sections.title: Approval of resolution plan.
key_sections.description: States that the Adjudicating Authority shall approve a resolution plan if it meets specified requirements, making it binding on all stakeholders, or reject it if it does not conform.

key_sections.title: Initiation of liquidation.
key_sections.description: Details the circumstances under which the Adjudicating Authority shall pass a liquidation order for a corporate debtor, such as failure to receive a resolution plan or rejection of a plan.

key_sections.title: Distribution of assets.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the order of priority for the distribution of proceeds from the sale of liquidation assets among various creditors and stakeholders.

key_sections.title: Corporate debtors eligible for pre-packaged insolvency resolution process.
key_sections.description: Specifies the eligibility criteria for corporate debtors, particularly micro, small or medium enterprises, to initiate a pre-packaged insolvency resolution process.

key_sections.title: Adjudicating Authority for corporate persons.
key_sections.description: Designates the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) as the Adjudicating Authority for insolvency resolution and liquidation of corporate persons and personal guarantors.

key_sections.title: Appeals and Appellate Authority.
key_sections.description: Allows appeals against orders of the Adjudicating Authority to the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) and specifies grounds for appeal against a resolution plan.

key_sections.title: Punishment for concealment of property.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for officers of a corporate debtor who wilfully conceal property, fraudulently remove assets, or falsify records before or after the insolvency commencement date.

key_sections.title: Application.
key_sections.description: States that Part III (Insolvency Resolution and Bankruptcy for Individuals and Partnership Firms) applies to fresh start, insolvency, and bankruptcy matters for individuals and firms with a minimum default amount.

key_sections.title: Application by debtor to initiate insolvency resolution process.
key_sections.description: Allows a debtor (individual or firm) who commits a default to apply for initiating the insolvency resolution process, subject to certain conditions and in a prescribed manner.

key_sections.title: Bankruptcy order.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Adjudicating Authority to pass a bankruptcy order within fourteen days of receiving confirmation or nomination of a bankruptcy trustee.

key_sections.title: Adjudicating authority for individuals and partnership firms.
key_sections.description: Designates the Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT) as the Adjudicating Authority for insolvency matters of individuals and partnership firms.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Board.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment and incorporation of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) as a body corporate with perpetual succession.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the extensive powers and functions of the IBBI, including registration and regulation of insolvency professionals, agencies, and information utilities, and making regulations.

key_sections.title: Provisions of this Code to override other laws.
key_sections.description: Establishes the overriding effect of the Code's provisions over any inconsistent provisions in other laws.

powers_conferred: Adjudicating Authority: Admit/reject applications (Sec 7, 9, 10, 54C), declare moratorium (Sec 13, 54E), appoint Interim Resolution Professional/Resolution Professional (Sec 13, 16, 54E), approve/reject resolution plan (Sec 31, 54L), order liquidation (Sec 33, 54N), replace liquidator (Sec 34), pass orders for preferential/undervalued/extortionate transactions (Sec 44, 48, 51), dissolve corporate debtor (Sec 54), hear appeals (Sec 61), impose penalties (Sec 65, 67A), pass bankruptcy orders (Sec 126), modify/recall bankruptcy orders (Sec 142).

Resolution Professional: Manage affairs of corporate debtor (Sec 17), perform duties (Sec 18, 25, 54F), raise interim finance (Sec 20, 28), prepare information memorandum (Sec 29), submit resolution plan (Sec 30), supervise repayment plan (Sec 116).
Liquidator: Verify claims (Sec 35), take custody of assets (Sec 35), sell property (Sec 35), investigate financial affairs (Sec 35), apply for dissolution (Sec 54).

Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (Board): Register/regulate Insolvency Professionals, Insolvency Professional Agencies, Information Utilities (Sec 196), specify standards (Sec 196), conduct inspections/investigations (Sec 196, 218), make regulations (Sec 240).

Central Government: Appoint commencement date (Sec 1), notify bodies for application (Sec 2), specify minimum default amount (Sec 4), issue directions to Board (Sec 225), supersede Board (Sec 226), notify financial service providers (Sec 227), make rules (Sec 239), enter agreements with foreign countries (Sec 234).
Committee of Creditors: Propose Resolution Professional (Sec 22), replace Resolution Professional (Sec 27), propose Bankruptcy Trustee (Sec 145).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Code prescribes various offences and penalties. For corporate persons (Part II, Chapter VII), offences include concealment of property (Sec 68), transactions defrauding creditors (Sec 69), misconduct by officers (Sec 70), falsification of books (Sec 71), wilful omissions (Sec 72), false representations (Sec 73), contravention of moratorium or resolution plan (Sec 74), false information in applications (Sec 75, 77), non-disclosure by operational creditors (Sec 76), and offences related to pre-packaged insolvency (Sec 77A). Penalties generally involve imprisonment ranging from one to five years, and/or fines from one lakh to one crore rupees. For individuals and partnership firms (Part III, Chapter VII), offences include false information by creditors (Sec 184), contravention by insolvency professionals (Sec 185), false information/concealment by bankrupts (Sec 186), and certain actions by bankruptcy trustees (Sec 187). Penalties typically involve imprisonment up to two years and/or fines up to five lakh rupees (or multiples of loss/gain). Additionally, Section 235A provides for a general punishment of a fine between one lakh and two crore rupees for contraventions where no specific penalty is provided.

exemptions: Financial service providers are not included in the definition of 'corporate person'.
Certain transactions, agreements, or arrangements may be notified by the Central Government in consultation with financial sector regulators as exempt from moratorium provisions.
A surety in a contract of guarantee to a corporate debtor is exempt from moratorium provisions.
Assets owned by a third party in possession of the corporate debtor (e.g., under trust or bailment) are excluded from the liquidation estate.
Assets of any Indian or foreign subsidiary of the corporate debtor are excluded from the liquidation estate.
Personal assets of any shareholder or partner of a corporate debtor are excluded from the liquidation estate, unless they are avoidance transactions.

Certain persons are not entitled to make an application to initiate corporate insolvency resolution process (e.g., corporate debtors undergoing a process, those who completed a process within 12 months, those who violated a resolution plan, or those against whom a liquidation order has been made).

Certain persons are not eligible to be resolution applicants (e.g., undischarged insolvents, wilful defaulters, those with NPA accounts, convicted persons, disqualified directors, those prohibited by SEBI, or those involved in fraudulent transactions).

For individuals and partnership firms, 'excluded assets' (e.g., unencumbered tools, books, vehicles, household equipment, personal ornaments, life insurance, single dwelling unit of prescribed value) are not included in the estate of the bankrupt.
For individuals and partnership firms, 'excluded debts' (e.g., fines, damages for negligence, maintenance, student loans) are not considered bankruptcy debts.
The Central Government may direct that certain provisions of the Code shall not apply to micro, small and medium enterprises, or apply with modifications.
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Code to come into force.
The Code includes specific provisions for a 'pre-packaged insolvency resolution process' for corporate debtors, particularly micro, small or medium enterprises.
The Code includes specific provisions for a 'fast track corporate insolvency resolution process' for certain categories of corporate debtors.
Special provisions are made for the Adjudicating Authority and Appellate Authority for corporate persons (NCLT/NCLAT) and for individuals and partnership firms (DRT/DRAT).
Provisions for personal guarantors to corporate debtors are included, with the NCLT having jurisdiction over their insolvency/liquidation if the corporate debtor's process is pending before it.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Code is enforced through a structured process involving various authorities and professionals. Insolvency Resolution Professionals, Liquidators, and Bankruptcy Trustees are appointed to manage the insolvency, liquidation, and bankruptcy processes. The Adjudicating Authorities (National Company Law Tribunal for corporate persons and Debt Recovery Tribunal for individuals and firms) admit applications, declare moratoriums, approve resolution plans, and pass liquidation or bankruptcy orders. Appeals against these orders can be made to the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal and further to the Supreme Court. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) regulates insolvency professionals, insolvency professional agencies, and information utilities, setting standards and conducting investigations. The Code also defines various offences and prescribes penalties, with trials conducted by Special Courts.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) for corporate persons and personal guarantors (Section 60); Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT) for individuals and partnership firms (Section 79, 179); National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) for appeals from NCLT (Section 61); Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunal (DRAT) for appeals from DRT (Section 181); Supreme Court for appeals from NCLAT/DRAT on questions of law (Section 62, 182); Special Court for trial of offences under the Code (Section 236).

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of an institution of national importance to be known as Regional Centre for Biotechnology and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS an agreement for the establishment and operation of the Regional Centre for Biotechnology Training and Education in India was entered into between the Government of India and the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation on the 14th day of July, 2006; AND WHEREAS in pursuance of the said agreement, the Central Government through an executive order dated the 20th April, 2009, established the Regional Centre for Biotechnology Training and Education at Faridabad, Haryana; AND WHEREAS it is expedient to make provisions for strengthening and to make the Regional Centre for Biotechnology an institution of national importance for imparting education, training and conducting research in the areas of Biotechnology and related multi disciplinary areas.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the establishment of the Regional Centre for Biotechnology as an institution of national importance. Its main purpose is to impart education, training, and conduct research in biotechnology and related multidisciplinary areas, fostering capacity-building and international cooperation for sustainable development.

The primary objective is to utilize these funds for artificial and natural regeneration, forest protection, infrastructure development, wildlife protection, and other related activities to compensate for forest loss.

act_identification.act_title: THE RIGHTS OF PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES ACT, 2016
act_identification.act_short_title: the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016

act_overview.preamble: An Act to give effect to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS the United Nations General Assembly adopted its Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities on the 13th day of December, 2006. AND WHEREAS the aforesaid Convention lays down the following principles for empowerment of persons with disabilities,— (a) respect for inherent dignity, individual autonomy including the freedom to make one's own choices, and independence of persons; (b) non-discrimination; (c) full and effective participation and inclusion in society; (d) respect for difference and acceptance of persons with disabilities as part of human diversity and humanity; (e) equality of opportunity; (f) accessibility; (g) equality between men and women; (h) respect for the evolving capacities of children with disabilities and respect for the right of children with disabilities to preserve their identities; AND WHEREAS India is a signatory to the said Convention; AND WHEREAS India ratified the said Convention on the 1st day of October, 2007; AND WHEREAS it is considered necessary to implement the Convention aforesaid.
act_overview.purpose: To give effect to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. It aims to empower persons with disabilities by ensuring their rights to equality, non-discrimination, and full participation in society by providing for their education, employment, social security, healthcare, and establishing mechanisms for protection and enforcement of their rights.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Union territories of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu, Ladakh, Chandigarh and other territory.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make a provision for levy and collection of tax on intra-State supply of goods or services or both by the Union territories and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the levy and collection of tax on intra-State supply of goods or services or both within the Union territories. It also covers administrative provisions, payment of tax, transitional arrangements, and the application of provisions from the Central Goods and Services Tax Act to Union territories.

key_definitions: words and expressions used and not defined in this Act but defined in the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, the State Goods and Services Tax Act, and the Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date(s) of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Levy and collection.
key_sections.description: Outlines the levy and collection of Union territory tax on intra-State supplies of goods or services or both, including provisions for reverse charge and electronic commerce operators.

key_sections.title: Power to grant exemption from tax.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to exempt goods or services or both from tax in the public interest.

key_sections.title: Payment of tax.
key_sections.description: Details the utilisation of input tax credit available in the electronic credit ledger for payment of integrated tax and Union territory tax.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Authority for Advance Ruling.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of an Authority for Advance Ruling by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Appellate Authority for Advance Ruling.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of an Appellate Authority for Advance Ruling to hear appeals against advance rulings.

key_sections.title: Migration of existing tax payers.
key_sections.description: Deals with the migration of existing taxpayers registered under previous laws to the new GST regime.

key_sections.title: Transitional arrangements for input tax credit.
key_sections.description: Specifies provisions for carrying forward and utilising input tax credit from the existing laws.

key_sections.title: Application of provisions of Central Goods and Services Tax Act.
key_sections.description: States that various provisions of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to this Act with specified modifications.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Removal of difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions.

powers_conferred: Administrator may appoint Commissioners and other officers for carrying out the purposes of this Act (Section 3).
Administrator may authorise any officer to appoint officers of Union territory tax below the rank of Assistant Commissioner (Section 4).
An officer of the Union territory tax may exercise powers and discharge duties conferred or imposed under this Act, subject to conditions and limitations (Section 5).
Commissioner may delegate his powers to any other officer subordinate to him (Section 5).
Central Government may appoint the date(s) of commencement for the Act (Section 1).
Central Government may specify categories of supply for reverse charge mechanism (Section 7).
Central Government may specify categories of services for electronic commerce operator liability (Section 7).
Central Government may grant exemption from tax (Section 8).
Central Government shall constitute an Authority for Advance Ruling (Section 15).
Central Government shall constitute an Appellate Authority for Advance Ruling (Section 16).
Central Government may make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act (Section 22).
Central Government may make orders for removal of difficulties (Section 26).
Government may specify a class of registered persons for reverse charge from unregistered suppliers (Section 7).
Government may prescribe the order and manner of utilisation of input tax credit (Section 9B).
Board may make regulations consistent with this Act and rules (Section 23).
Commissioner may issue orders, instructions or directions for uniformity in implementation (Section 25).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 22(4) states that rules made under the Act may provide for a penalty not exceeding ten thousand rupees for contravention thereof. Section 21(xxii) also indicates that provisions relating to 'offences and penalties' from the Central Goods and Services Tax Act shall apply mutatis mutandis.

related_acts: Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act
Central Goods and Services Tax Act
State Goods and Services Tax Act
Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act
Central Sales Tax (Registration and Turnover) Rules, 1957

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Administrator may appoint Commissioners and other officers (Section 3). The Administrator may authorise any officer to appoint officers of Union territory tax below the rank of Assistant Commissioner (Section 4). The Central Government appoints members of the Authority for Advance Ruling (Section 15).

applies_to: Union territories of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu, Ladakh, Chandigarh and other territory.
Every person registered under any of the existing laws.
Taxable persons.
exemptions: Supply of alcoholic liquor for human consumption (Section 7(1)).
Exempt supply (as defined in Section 2(4)).
Goods or services or both exempted by the Central Government under Section 8.
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act (Section 1(3) proviso).
Each of the territories specified in sub-clauses (i) to (vi) of Section 2(8) shall be considered to be a separate Union territory (Section 2 Explanation).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced by officers appointed under this Act (Section 3), including officers of central tax authorised as proper officers (Section 6). Officers of Police, Railways, Customs, land revenue, central tax, and State tax are required to assist proper officers (Section 11). Recovery of tax can be made as an arrear of central tax (Section 13). Various provisions of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act apply mutatis mutandis for enforcement (Section 21).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Appellate Authority for Advance Ruling is established for appeals against advance rulings (Section 16). Provisions for appeals and revision from the Central Goods and Services Tax Act apply (Section 21(xx)).

act_identification.act_title: THE GOODS AND SERVICES TAX (COMPENSATION TO STATES) ACT, 2017
act_identification.act_short_title: Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act, 2017

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for compensation to the States for the loss of revenue arising on account of implementation of the goods and services tax in pursuance of the provisions of the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the compensation to States for the loss of revenue incurred due to the implementation of the goods and services tax. It establishes a mechanism for calculating and releasing this compensation, funded through a cess levied on specified goods and services. The Act aims to ensure financial stability for States during the transition to the GST regime.

State Goods and Services Tax Act
Union Territories Goods and Services Tax Act

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.description: Specifies the nominal growth rate of revenue subsumed for a State during the transition period.

key_sections.title: Base year.
key_sections.description: Designates the financial year for calculating compensation.

key_sections.title: Levy and collection of cess.
key_sections.description: Mandates the levy and collection of a cess on specified supplies to fund compensation.

key_sections.title: Returns, payments and refunds.

key_sections.title: Crediting proceeds of cess to Fund.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Goods and Services Tax Compensation Fund and details how cess proceeds are credited and utilized.

key_sections.title: Other provisions relating to cess.
key_sections.description: States that provisions of the CGST Act and IGST Act, including those on assessment, input tax credit, offences, and penalties, apply to the cess.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for implementing the Act, based on Council recommendations.

key_sections.title: Laying of rules before Parliament.
key_sections.description: Requires rules made under the Act to be laid before Parliament.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to appoint the commencement date of the Act (Section 1(3))
Central Government: to specify the rate of cess on goods and services (Section 8(2))
Central Government: to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act (Section 12)
Central Government: to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act (Section 14)
Council (Goods and Services Tax Council): to make recommendations for rules (Section 2(j), Section 12(1))
Council (Goods and Services Tax Council): to make recommendations for the period of cess imposition (Section 8(1))
Council (Goods and Services Tax Council): to make recommendations for the rate of cess (Section 8(2))
Council (Goods and Services Tax Council): to make recommendations for other amounts to be credited to the Fund (Section 10(1))
Council (Goods and Services Tax Council): to make recommendations for the transfer of unutilised amounts in the Fund (Section 10(3A))
Council (Goods and Services Tax Council): to make recommendations for removing difficulties (Section 14(1))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Offences and penalties are governed by the provisions of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act and the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, as applied mutatis mutandis by this Act (Section 11).

related_acts: Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016
Central Goods and Services Tax Act
Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act
Union Territories Goods and Services Tax Act

authorities_established: Goods and Services Tax Compensation Fund
regulatory_bodies: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs

applies_to: any State during the transition period
taxable person, making a taxable supply of goods or services or both
exemptions: supplies made by a taxable person who has decided to opt for composition levy under section 10 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act
special_provisions: For the State of Jammu and Kashmir, base year revenue includes tax collected on sale of services by the State Government during the base year (Section 5(2)).
For States mentioned in article 279A(4)(g) of the Constitution, revenue foregone due to exemptions/remissions for industrial investment is included in base year revenue (Section 5(3)).
The Act is made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government, on the recommendations of the Council (Section 12(1)).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the levy and collection of cess (Section 8), calculation and release of compensation to States (Section 7), and crediting proceeds to the Goods and Services Tax Compensation Fund (Section 10). Provisions of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act and Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act apply mutatis mutandis for assessment, input tax credit, non-levy, short-levy, interest, appeals, offences and penalties (Section 11). Accounts of the Fund are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (Section 10(4)).

schedules_summary.description: Lists specific goods and services (e.g., Pan Masala, Tobacco, Coal, Aerated waters, Motor vehicles) on which the goods and services tax compensation cess may be collected, along with their tariff items/headings and the maximum rates of cess. It also includes an Explanation defining 'retail sale price' for the purposes of this Schedule.

act_identification.act_title: THE INTEGRATED GOODS AND SERVICES TAX ACT, 2017
act_identification.act_short_title: the Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017

act_overview.preamble: An Act to make a provision for levy and collection of tax on inter-State supply of goods or services or both by the Central Government and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the levy and collection of integrated goods and services tax (IGST) on inter-State supplies of goods or services or both. It covers administrative aspects, determination of supply nature, place of supply, refunds, and apportionment of tax between the Central and State Governments.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's official name, its geographical application across India (with an exception), and the mechanism for its commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides comprehensive definitions for various terms used throughout the Act, ensuring clarity and consistent interpretation.

key_sections.title: Levy and collection.
key_sections.description: Outlines the levy and collection of integrated goods and services tax on inter-State supplies, including provisions for reverse charge and electronic commerce operators.

key_sections.title: Power to grant exemption from tax.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Government to grant exemptions from integrated tax, either generally or in specific cases, based on public interest and Council recommendations.

key_sections.title: Inter-State supply.
key_sections.description: Defines the criteria for classifying a supply of goods or services as an inter-State supply, crucial for determining the applicability of IGST.

key_sections.title: Intra-State supply.
key_sections.description: Defines the criteria for classifying a supply of goods or services as an intra-State supply, distinguishing it from inter-State supplies.

key_sections.title: Place of supply of services where location of supplier and recipient is in India.
key_sections.description: Establishes rules for determining the place of supply for various services when both the supplier and recipient are located within India.

key_sections.title: Place of supply of services where location of supplier or location of recipient is outside India.
key_sections.description: Sets out rules for determining the place of supply for services when either the supplier or the recipient is located outside India.

key_sections.title: Special provision for payment of tax by a supplier of online information and database access or retrieval services.
key_sections.description: Specifies the liability and registration requirements for suppliers of online information and database access or retrieval services located in non-taxable territories.

key_sections.title: Zero rated supply.
key_sections.description: Defines zero-rated supplies, including exports and supplies to Special Economic Zone units, and provides for claiming refund of unutilised input tax credit.

key_sections.title: Apportionment of tax and settlement of funds.
key_sections.description: Details the mechanism for apportioning integrated tax collected by the Central Government to the Central and State Governments.

key_sections.title: Application of provisions of Central Goods and Services Tax Act.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that various provisions of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Government the authority to make rules for the effective implementation and administration of the Act.

key_sections.title: Removal of difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Government to issue orders to remove any difficulties encountered in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Board may appoint such central tax officers as it thinks fit for exercising the powers under this Act.
Government shall, on the recommendations of the Council, by notification, specify exceptions and conditions for authorisation of officers of State tax or Union territory tax as proper officer.
Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, by notification, specify categories of supply of goods or services or both, the tax on which shall be paid on reverse charge basis.
Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, by notification, specify a class of registered persons who shall pay tax on reverse charge basis.
Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, by notification, specify categories of services, the tax on inter-State supplies of which shall be paid by the electronic commerce operator.

Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, by notification, exempt generally, either absolutely or subject to such conditions as may be specified therein, goods or services or both of any specified description from the whole or any part of the tax leviable thereon.
Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, by special order in each case, exempt from payment of tax any goods or services or both.

Government may, if it considers necessary or expedient so to do for the purpose of clarifying the scope or applicability of any notification or order, insert an Explanation in such notification or order.
Government shall have the power to notify any description of services or circumstances in which the place of supply shall be the place of effective use and enjoyment of a service.
Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, by notification, make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act.
Board may, by notification, make regulations consistent with this Act and the rules made thereunder to carry out the provisions of this Act.

Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, by a general or a special order published in the Official Gazette, make such provisions not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act or the rules or regulations made thereunder, as may be necessary or expedient for the purpose of removing the said difficulty.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The provisions of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act relating to offences and penalties apply to this Act. A contravention of rules made under this Act may be liable to a penalty not exceeding ten thousand rupees. Where penalty is leviable under CGST Act and SGST Act or UTGST Act, the penalty under this Act shall be the sum total of said penalties.

key_sections.title: Definitions.

key_sections.title: Levy and collection.
key_sections.description: Outlines the levy and collection mechanism for central goods and services tax, including provisions for reverse charge and electronic commerce operators.

key_sections.description: Allows certain registered persons with aggregate turnover below a specified limit to opt for a composition scheme with a lower tax rate.

key_sections.description: Defines the eligibility and conditions for registered persons to avail input tax credit on goods or services used in business.

key_sections.description: Lists categories of persons who are mandatorily required to register under the Act, irrespective of their turnover.

key_sections.title: Cancellation or suspension of registration.
key_sections.description: Details the circumstances and procedures under which a registration can be cancelled or suspended by the proper officer.

key_sections.title: Tax invoice.
key_sections.description: Prescribes the requirements for issuing tax invoices by registered persons for taxable supplies of goods or services.

key_sections.title: Credit and debit notes.
key_sections.description: Governs the issuance of credit and debit notes by registered persons for adjustments to taxable value or tax charged.

key_sections.title: Furnishing of returns.
key_sections.description: Mandates registered persons to furnish periodic returns electronically, detailing inward and outward supplies, input tax credit, and tax payments.

key_sections.title: Payment of tax, interest, penalty and other amounts.
key_sections.description: Outlines the methods and order of payment for tax, interest, penalty, and other amounts, including the use of electronic cash and credit ledgers.

key_sections.description: Empowers the Government to mandate certain entities to deduct tax at source from payments made to suppliers.

key_sections.title: Collection of tax at source.
key_sections.description: Requires electronic commerce operators to collect tax at source on taxable supplies made through their platform by other suppliers.

key_sections.title: Refund of tax.
key_sections.description: Provides the mechanism and conditions for claiming refunds of tax and interest, including unutilised input tax credit.

key_sections.title: Power of inspection, search and seizure.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to proper officers to inspect business premises, search for and seize goods, documents, or things in cases of suspected tax evasion.

key_sections.title: Power to arrest.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Commissioner to order the arrest of persons who have committed certain specified offences under the Act.

key_sections.title: Determination of tax not paid or short paid or erroneously refunded or input tax credit wrongly availed or utilised for any reason other than fraud or any wilful-misstatement or suppression of facts.
key_sections.description: Lays down the procedure for determining and recovering tax dues in cases not involving fraud or wilful misstatement.

key_sections.title: Determination of tax not paid or short paid or erroneously refunded or input tax credit wrongly availed or utilised by reason of fraud or any wilful-misstatement or suppression of facts.

key_sections.title: Recovery of tax.
key_sections.description: Details various modes for the proper officer to recover unpaid amounts due to the Government under the Act.

key_sections.title: Tax to be first charge on property.
key_sections.description: Establishes that any amount payable to the Government under the Act is a first charge on the property of the taxable person.

key_sections.title: Appeals to Appellate Authority.
key_sections.description: Provides for appeals against decisions or orders of adjudicating authorities to the Appellate Authority.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Appellate Tribunal and Benches thereof.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment and constitution of the Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal and its benches for hearing appeals.

key_sections.title: Penalty for certain offences.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for various specific offences committed by taxable persons or electronic commerce operators.

key_sections.title: Punishment for certain offences.
key_sections.description: Specifies imprisonment and fine as punishments for serious offences like tax evasion, fraudulent input tax credit, and dealing with confiscable goods.

key_sections.title: Anti-profiteering measure.
key_sections.description: Mandates that benefits from tax rate reduction or input tax credit must be passed on to recipients through reduced prices and provides for an authority to examine compliance.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Details the repeal of several existing indirect tax laws and saving provisions for past actions and proceedings.

powers_conferred: Government: Appoint officers (Section 3), grant exemption from tax (Section 11), specify categories of supply for reverse charge (Section 9(3)), specify categories of services for electronic commerce operator tax payment (Section 9(5)), increase composition levy limit (Section 10), prescribe modes of electronic payment (Section 31A), constitute Consumer Welfare Fund (Section 57), establish Appellate Tribunal (Section 109), appoint President and Members of Appellate Tribunal (Section 110), make rules (Section 164), make regulations (Section 165), extend time limit in special circumstances (Section 168A), constitute Anti-profiteering Authority (Section 171(2)), remove difficulties (Section 172).
Board: Appoint officers (Section 4), impose conditions/limitations on officers' powers (Section 5), make regulations (Section 165), issue orders/instructions/directions (Section 168).

Commissioner: Delegate powers (Section 5), extend time limit for furnishing details (Section 37), extend time limit for furnishing returns (Section 39), extend time limit for provisional assessment (Section 60), authorise audit (Section 65), approve special audit (Section 66), authorise inspection, search, seizure (Section 67), authorise arrest (Section 69), summon persons (Section 70), sanction prosecution (Section 134), compound offences (Section 138), extend period for job work (Section 141), extend period for goods returned (Section 142), notify common portal (Section 146), notify deemed exports (Section 147), notify special procedures (Section 148), call for information (Section 151), publish information (Section 159), delegate powers (Section 167).

Proper Officer: Assess tax liability (Section 62, 63, 64, 73, 74), recover tax (Section 79), attach property provisionally (Section 83), cancel registration (Section 29), revoke cancellation (Section 30), issue tax invoice (Section 31), issue notice to return defaulters (Section 46), scrutinize returns (Section 61), detain/seize goods (Section 129).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 122 prescribes penalties for various offences such as supplying without invoice, collecting tax but failing to pay, fraudulent refund claims, taking input tax credit without actual receipt, falsifying records, obstructing officers, and transporting goods without documents. Penalties range from ten thousand rupees or the tax evaded/wrongly availed/refunded (whichever is higher) for certain offences, to specific amounts for others. Section 123 imposes a late fee for failure to furnish information returns. Section 124 specifies fines for failure to furnish statistics. Section 125 provides a general penalty for contraventions not specifically covered. Section 129 details penalties for detention, seizure, and release of goods and conveyances in transit. Section 130 covers confiscation of goods or conveyances and associated penalties. Section 132 outlines punishments, including imprisonment (up to five years) and fines, for serious offences like tax evasion and fraudulent input tax credit, with varying degrees based on the amount of tax involved.
