Every person supplying online money gaming from a place outside India to a person in India (Section 24(xia)).
exemptions: Any person engaged exclusively in the business of supplying goods or services or both that are not liable to tax or wholly exempt from tax (Section 23(1)(a)).
An agriculturist, to the extent of supply of produce out of cultivation of land (Section 23(1)(b)).
The Government may, by notification, specify categories of persons who may be exempted from obtaining registration (Section 23(2)).
Input tax credit is not available for certain motor vehicles, vessels, aircraft, and related services (Section 17(5)(a), (aa), (ab)).

Input tax credit is not available for certain goods or services like food and beverages, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, health services, club membership, and travel benefits to employees (with exceptions) (Section 17(5)(b)).
Input tax credit is not available for works contract services for immovable property (other than plant and machinery) (Section 17(5)(c)).
Input tax credit is not available for goods or services received by a taxable person for construction of immovable property on his own account (Section 17(5)(d)).
Input tax credit is not available for goods or services on which tax has been paid under section 10 (composition levy) (Section 17(5)(e)).
Input tax credit is not available for goods or services received by a non-resident taxable person, except on goods imported by him (Section 17(5)(f)).
Input tax credit is not available for goods or services used for corporate social responsibility (Section 17(5)(fa)).
Input tax credit is not available for goods or services used for personal consumption (Section 17(5)(g)).
Input tax credit is not available for goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off or disposed of by way of gift or free samples (Section 17(5)(h)).
Input tax credit is not available for any tax paid in accordance with the provisions of sections 74, 129 and 130 (Section 17(5)(i)).
special_provisions: Special category States have a lower aggregate turnover threshold for registration (Section 22(1) proviso).
Special provisions apply to casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons regarding registration validity and advance tax deposit (Section 27).
The Government may notify special procedures for certain classes of registered persons regarding registration, returns, payment of tax, and administration (Section 148).
Special provisions regarding liability to pay tax, interest or penalty in cases of death, partition of HUF, dissolution of firm, or termination of guardianship/trust (Section 93).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Government, on the recommendations of the Council, has the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act (Section 164(1)).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a hierarchy of officers (Sections 3, 4, 5) who have powers of inspection, search, seizure, and arrest (Chapter XIV). It includes mechanisms for assessment (Chapter XII), demands and recovery of tax (Chapter XV), and penalties and prosecution for offences (Chapter XIX). Officers of Police, Railways, Customs, State tax, and Union territory tax are required to assist in its implementation (Section 72).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate (for arrest, recovery of fine, cognizance of offences), High Court (for appeals), Supreme Court (for appeals), and Civil Courts (for summoning persons, powers of Authority/Appellate Authority/Appellate Tribunal, but with bar on jurisdiction for certain matters).

schedules_summary.description: Lists activities to be treated as supply even if made without consideration, such as permanent transfer of business assets where input tax credit has been availed, supply between related persons or distinct persons, supply of goods by/to an agent, and import of services from a related person or establishment outside India.

Categorizes activities or transactions to be treated as either supply of goods or supply of services. This includes transfers of title or rights in goods, land and building transactions (lease, tenancy, construction), treatment or process on another's goods, transfer of business assets, and various services like renting immovable property, intellectual property rights, IT software, and composite supplies like works contracts and food/drink supply.

Specifies activities or transactions which shall be treated neither as a supply of goods nor a supply of services. This includes services by an employee to the employer, services by courts or tribunals, functions performed by elected representatives and constitutional office holders, funeral services, sale of land and certain sales of buildings, actionable claims (other than specified), and certain offshore/warehoused goods transactions.

act_identification.act_title: THE HUMAN IMMUNODEFICIENCY VIRUS AND ACQUIRED IMMUNE DEFICIENCY SYNDROME (PREVENTION AND CONTROL) ACT, 2017
act_identification.act_short_title: The Human Immunodeficiency Virus and Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to prevent and control the spread of HIV and AIDS, protect the human rights of affected persons, ensure effective care, support, and treatment, and safeguard the rights of healthcare providers. It also aims to give effect to the Declaration of Commitment on HIV and AIDS (2001) adopted by the United Nations General Assembly.

chapter_titles: ANTI-RETROVIRAL THERAPY AND OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTION MANAGEMENT FOR PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV
WELFARE MEASURES BY THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT AND STATE GOVERNMENT
PROMOTION OF STRATEGIES FOR REDUCTION OF RISK

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official title, geographical extent (whole of India), and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as AIDS, HIV, discrimination, protected person, informed consent, and significant-risk.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of discrimination.
key_sections.description: Prohibits discrimination against protected persons on various grounds including employment, healthcare, education, access to public services, housing, and insurance.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of certain acts.
key_sections.description: Prohibits publishing, propagating, or communicating hatred or discrimination against protected persons or groups.

key_sections.title: Informed consent for undertaking HIV test or treatment.
key_sections.description: Mandates informed consent from a person or their representative for HIV testing or medical treatment, interventions, or research, including pre-test and post-test counselling.

key_sections.title: Disclosure of HIV status.
key_sections.description: Establishes strict rules for the confidentiality of HIV status, generally prohibiting compelled disclosure except by court order or with informed consent, with specific exceptions for healthcare providers and government monitoring.

key_sections.title: Disclosure of HIV-positive status to partner of HIV-positive person.
key_sections.description: Allows a physician or counsellor to disclose an HIV-positive person's status to their partner under specific conditions, including counselling the HIV-positive person and ensuring no risk of violence to a woman.

key_sections.title: Central Government and State Government to take measures.
key_sections.description: Obligates the Central and State Governments to take necessary measures for the prevention and control of HIV or AIDS.

key_sections.title: Antiretroviral Therapy and Opportunistic Infection Management by Central Government and State Government.
key_sections.description: Requires governments to provide diagnostic facilities, Anti-retroviral Therapy (ART), and Opportunistic Infection Management to people living with HIV or AIDS, and for the Central Government to issue related guidelines.

key_sections.title: Obligation of establishments to provide safe working environment.
key_sections.description: Mandates healthcare and other high-risk establishments to provide Universal Precautions, training, and Post Exposure Prophylaxis to prevent occupational HIV exposure.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Ombudsman.
key_sections.description: Requires every State Government to appoint one or more Ombudsmen to inquire into violations of the Act, particularly discrimination and healthcare service issues.

key_sections.title: Right of residence.
key_sections.description: Grants protected persons the right to reside in a shared household and not be excluded or discriminated against in its use.

key_sections.title: Suppression of identity.
key_sections.description: Allows courts to order the suppression of identity of protected persons in legal proceedings, including using pseudonyms, in-camera proceedings, and restraining publication of identifying information.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for contravention of Section 4 (prohibition of hate speech against protected persons), including imprisonment and/or fine.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint date of commencement, issue guidelines, take measures for prevention and control of HIV/AIDS, provide diagnostic facilities, ART, and OI management, frame welfare schemes, lay down guidelines for care, support and treatment of children, specify guidelines for pre-marital information, make rules, and remove difficulties.

State Government: To appoint Ombudsman, make rules, take measures for prevention and control of HIV/AIDS, provide diagnostic facilities, ART, and OI management, frame welfare schemes, and take steps to protect property of children affected by HIV/AIDS.
Ombudsman: To inquire into violations of the Act, require persons to furnish information, and pass orders on complaints.

Courts: To order HIV tests, order disclosure of HIV status, suppress identity of protected persons in legal proceedings, consider maintenance applications, and consider HIV-positive status during sentencing for custodial placement.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Penalty for contravention of Section 4 (prohibition of certain acts) is imprisonment for a term not less than three months but which may extend to two years, and/or a fine up to one lakh rupees. Failure to comply with Ombudsman's orders incurs a fine up to ten thousand rupees, with an additional fine of five thousand rupees per day for continued failure. Breach of confidentiality in legal proceedings is punishable with a fine up to one lakh rupees. Victimisation of persons taking action under the Act is prohibited.

related_acts: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (43 of 2005)
Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000 (56 of 2000)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: State Government has the power to appoint one or more Ombudsmen.

applies_to: Whole of India
Protected persons (HIV-positive, or living/residing/cohabiting with HIV-positive persons)

Establishments (body corporate, co-operative society, organization, institution, or two or more persons carrying out systematic activity; specifically those with 100 or more persons, or 20 or more for healthcare establishments)
Healthcare providers
Testing or diagnostic centres, pathology laboratories, blood banks
Persons in care or custody of the State
exemptions: Medically advised safeguards and precautions to minimise the risk of infection shall not amount to discrimination.

Certain exposures are excluded from the definition of "significant-risk" (e.g., urine, faeces, human bites without blood contact, intact skin exposure, occupational centres using Universal Precautions).

Informed consent for HIV tests is not required in cases of court orders, procuring human body parts for medical research/therapy (with donor counselling), anonymous epidemiological/surveillance purposes, and screening in licensed blood banks.
Healthcare providers are not liable for criminal or civil action for disclosure or non-disclosure of confidential HIV-related information to a partner under specific conditions.
The duty to prevent transmission of HIV does not apply to a woman in cases where disclosure may result in violence, abandonment, or severe negative effects on her or her family's health or safety.

Disclosure of HIV-related information without informed consent is permitted for healthcare providers involved in care, by court order, in legal proceedings, for statistical information not identifying the person, and to government officers for monitoring/evaluation.
special_provisions: Special procedure in court for protected persons, including suppression of identity, in-camera proceedings, and priority disposal of cases.
Consideration of medical expenses and HIV-related costs in maintenance applications for protected persons.
HIV-positive status as a relevant factor in sentencing to determine appropriate custodial place with healthcare services.
Recognition of guardianship of older siblings (12-18 years) for children affected by HIV/AIDS for specific purposes.
Provision for living wills for guardianship and testamentary guardianship by parents/legal guardians of children affected by HIV/AIDS.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the prohibition of discrimination and certain acts, mandatory informed consent, confidentiality of HIV status, obligations on establishments, provision of ART and welfare measures by governments, establishment of an Ombudsman to inquire into complaints, and penalties for contraventions and non-compliance. Establishments are required to have a grievance redressal mechanism.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Court of a Judicial Magistrate First Class for trying offences under this Act. Other courts have jurisdiction for legal proceedings, maintenance applications, and sentencing related to protected persons.

act_identification.act_title: THE FOOTWEAR DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT INSTITUTE ACT, 2017
act_identification.act_short_title: The Footwear Design and Development Institute Act, 2017.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and declare the Footwear Design and Development Institute as an institution of national importance for the promotion and development of quality and excellence in education, research and training in all disciplines relating to footwear and leather products design and development and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the Footwear Design and Development Institute as an institution of national importance. Its main objective is to promote and develop quality and excellence in education, research, and training in all disciplines related to footwear and leather products design and development. The Act also covers matters connected with or incidental to these primary goals.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies the mechanism for its commencement.

key_sections.title: Declaration of Footwear Design and Development Institute as an institution of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the Footwear Design and Development Institute as an institution of national importance.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Institute.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Footwear Design and Development Institute as a body corporate and outlines the composition of its Governing Council.

key_sections.title: Functions of Institute.
key_sections.description: Details the core functions of the Institute, including education, research, skill development, and collaboration.

key_sections.title: Powers of Governing Council.
key_sections.description: Defines the general superintendence, direction, and control powers of the Governing Council over the Institute's affairs.

key_sections.title: Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the Institute.

key_sections.title: Functions of Senate.
key_sections.description: Outlines the academic functions, powers, and responsibilities of the Senate as the principal academic body.

key_sections.title: Managing Director.
key_sections.description: Describes the appointment, powers, and duties of the Managing Director as the principal executive officer of the Institute.

key_sections.title: Grants by Central Government.
key_sections.description: Provides for financial grants from the Central Government to enable the Institute to discharge its functions.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Mandates the maintenance of proper accounts and their audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

key_sections.title: Statutes.
key_sections.description: Specifies the various matters that may be provided for by the Statutes of the Institute.

key_sections.title: Power of Institute to grant degree, etc.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the Institute the power to grant degrees, diplomas, certificates, and other academic distinctions.

key_sections.title: Institute to be public authority under the Right to Information Act, 2005.
key_sections.description: Declares the Institute as a public authority for the purposes of the Right to Information Act, 2005.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

powers_conferred: Institute: To acquire, hold, and dispose of property, to contract, and to sue or be sued (Section 4(2)).

Institute: To nurture and promote quality in education and research, develop courses, grant degrees, institute fellowships, cooperate with other institutions, conduct research, provide consultancy, conduct skill development programs, acquire patents, maintain museums/libraries, function as a National resource centre, and frame Statutes/Ordinances (Section 7).
Institute: To grant degrees, diplomas, certificates, and other academic distinctions (Section 33).

Governing Council: General superintendence, direction, and control of the Institute's affairs, review acts of the Senate, take policy decisions, institute academic and other posts, frame Statutes and Ordinances, consider annual reports and budgets, receive gifts/grants/donations, and appoint committees (Section 8).
Central Government: To nominate the Chairperson and certain members of the Governing Council (Section 4(3)).
Central Government: To approve the disposal of immovable property by the Governing Council (Section 8(4)).
Central Government: To review the work and progress of the Institute, hold inquiries, and issue directions (Section 8(5), (6)).
Central Government: To remove the Chairperson or other Members or reconstitute the Governing Council (Section 8(7)).
Central Government: To appoint the Managing Director, Secretary, and Executive Director (Section 16(1), 17(1), 18(1)).
Central Government: To remove the Managing Director (Section 16(5)).
Central Government: To provide grants to the Institute (Section 20).
Central Government: To direct the Institute to set up an endowment fund and other funds (Section 22).
Central Government: To make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act (Section 35).
Central Government: To remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act (Section 39).

Senate: To act as the principal academic body, control and regulate standards of instruction, education, and examinations, specify admission criteria, recommend creation of academic posts and new programmes, specify academic contents and calendar, and approve grant of degrees (Section 14).
Senate: To make Ordinances (Section 29(1)).
Chairperson: To preside at meetings of the Governing Council and Convocations, review work and progress, and order enquiries (Section 15).
Managing Director: To be the principal executive officer, responsible for administration, instruction, and discipline, and to implement decisions of the Governing Council and Senate (Section 16).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson, certain members of the Governing Council, the Managing Director, Secretary, and Executive Director. The Governing Council appoints academic staff (Assistant Professor or above) and non-academic staff with equivalent pay scales. The Managing Director appoints other staff. The Chairperson, in consultation with the Managing Director, nominates certain members to the Senate.

applies_to: The Footwear Design and Development Institute (as a body corporate)
Persons employed by the Society (transferred to the Institute)
Persons pursuing academic or research courses in existing Institute campuses
Students of the Institute (for admission, courses, examinations, discipline)
Officers, teachers, and other staff of the Institute
Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other backward categories of persons (for reservation)
special_provisions: Provisions for employees of the Society regarding continuation of tenure, remuneration, terms, and conditions, with a mechanism for termination if alterations are not acceptable (Section 6(c)).
Provisions for students of existing Institute campuses regarding deemed migration and registration (Section 6(d)).
No test or condition as to religious belief or profession for admission or appointment (Section 9(1)).
The Governing Council shall not dispose of any immovable property without the prior approval of the Central Government (Section 8(4)).

Special provisions for sponsored schemes, requiring funds to be kept separately, staff recruitment as per sponsoring organization's terms, and unutilised money to be transferred to the endowment fund (Section 32).
Retrospective effect for Statutes or Ordinances is permissible with Central Government approval, but not to prejudicially affect the interests of any person (Section 38(3)).

Any student who joined classes on or after the academic year 2012-2013 or completed the course on or after the academic year 2013-2014 shall be deemed to have pursued a course of study in the existing Institute if not already awarded a degree or diploma (Section 37(c)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Governing Council is responsible for the general superintendence, direction, and control of the Institute's affairs. The Managing Director is the principal executive officer responsible for administration, instruction, and discipline. The Central Government has powers to review the Institute's work, hold inquiries, and issue directions. Accounts are subject to audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Tribunal of Arbitration (for disputes arising out of contracts between the Institute and its employees, Section 30)

schedules_summary.description: Lists the names and addresses of the existing Institute campuses located in various states, including Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Telangana, Gujarat, and Punjab.

act_identification.act_title: THE ADMIRALTY (JURISDICTION AND SETTLEMENT OF MARITIME CLAIMS) ACT, 2017
act_identification.act_short_title: The Admiralty (Jurisdiction and Settlement of Maritime Claims) Act, 2017

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Sixty-eighth Year of the Republic of India
legislative_details.geographical_extent: Applies to every vessel, irrespective of the place of residence or domicile of the owner, and jurisdiction is exercisable over the waters up to and including the territorial waters of their respective jurisdictions, extendable by notification.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate the laws relating to admiralty jurisdiction, legal proceedings in connection with vessels, their arrest, detention, sale and other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act consolidates laws related to admiralty jurisdiction, legal proceedings concerning vessels, their arrest, detention, and sale, and other connected matters, aiming to provide a comprehensive framework for the settlement of maritime claims.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II ADMIRALTY JURISDICTION AND MARITIME CLAIMS

key_sections.title: Short title, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its applicability to vessels, and the commencement date to be notified by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'admiralty jurisdiction', 'maritime claim', and 'vessel'.

key_sections.title: Admiralty jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Vests admiralty jurisdiction in High Courts for all maritime claims, exercisable over territorial waters, with potential extension by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Maritime claim.
key_sections.description: Enumerates various types of maritime claims over which High Courts may exercise jurisdiction, including disputes, mortgages, loss/damage, and services.

key_sections.title: Arrest of vessel in rem.
key_sections.description: Empowers High Courts to order the arrest of a vessel within its jurisdiction to secure a maritime claim under specific conditions.

key_sections.title: Admiralty jurisdiction in personam.
key_sections.description: Allows High Courts to exercise admiralty jurisdiction through actions in personam for any specified maritime claim.

key_sections.title: Inter se priority on maritime lien.
key_sections.description: Establishes the order of priority among different types of maritime liens and specifies their duration and commencement.

key_sections.title: Order of priority of maritime claims.
key_sections.description: Determines the inter se priority of maritime claims in admiralty proceedings, categorizing them into maritime liens, registered mortgages, and other claims.

key_sections.title: Application of Code of Civil Procedure.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, shall apply to proceedings before the High Court under this Act, unless inconsistent.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Provides for an appeal from a single Judge of the High Court to a Division Bench of the High Court under this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act, including matters related to assessors and procedure.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals several older admiralty enactments and includes savings provisions for pending proceedings and actions taken under repealed laws.

powers_conferred: High Court: exercise admiralty jurisdiction, hear and determine maritime claims, order arrest of vessel, exercise jurisdiction in personam, order sale of vessel, impose obligation for security, adjudicate pending proceedings.
Central Government: extend jurisdiction of High Court, notify vessels for Act purposes, appoint assessors, make rules, remove difficulties.
Supreme Court: transfer proceedings.

repealed_acts: the Admiralty Court Act, 1840 (3 and 4 Vict., c. 65)
the Admiralty Court Act, 1861 (24 and 25 Vict., c. 10)
the Colonial Courts of Admiralty Act, 1890 (53 and 54 vict., c. 27)
the Colonial Courts of Admiralty (India) Act, 1891 (16 of 1891)
the provisions of the Letters Patent, 1865 in so far as they apply to the admiralty jurisdiction of the Bombay, Calcutta and Madras High Courts
related_acts: Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976 (80 of 1976)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government has the power to appoint assessors.

applies_to: every vessel, irrespective of the place of residence or domicile of the owner
exemptions: an inland vessel defined in clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Inland Vessels Act, 1917 (1 of 1917)
a vessel under construction that has not been launched unless it is notified by the Central Government
a warship, naval auxiliary or other vessel owned or operated by the Central or a State Government and used for any non-commercial purpose
a foreign vessel which is used for any non-commercial purpose as may be notified by the Central Government

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: High Courts exercise admiralty jurisdiction, hear and determine maritime claims, and can order the arrest and sale of vessels. The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, applies to proceedings. The Central Government can make rules for implementation.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: High Court (specifically Calcutta, Bombay, Madras, Karnataka, Gujarat, Orissa, Kerala, Hyderabad for Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, or any other notified by Central Government); Supreme Court for transfer of proceedings.

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN INSTITUTES OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP) ACT, 2017
act_identification.act_short_title: The Indian Institutes of Information Technology (Public-private Partnership) Act, 2017

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Human Resource Development, Department of Higher Education
legislative_details.geographical_extent: Applies to the Indian Institutes of Information Technology established under public-private partnership as listed in the Schedule, located across various states of India.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to declare certain Indian Institutes of Information Technology established under public-private partnership as institutions of national importance, with a view to develop new knowledge in information technology and to provide manpower of global standards for the information technology industry and to provide for certain other matters connected with such institutions or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to declare specific Indian Institutes of Information Technology, established through public-private partnerships, as institutions of national importance. Its primary objectives are to foster new knowledge in information technology, supply globally competent manpower for the IT industry, and address related institutional matters.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER III AUTHORITIES OF INDIAN INSTITUTES OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY ESTABLISHED IN PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies its commencement.

key_sections.title: Declaration of certain institutions as institutions of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the Institutes mentioned in the Schedule as institutions of national importance.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Objects of Institute.
key_sections.description: Lays down the objectives for every Institute, focusing on information technology, innovation, and transparency.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Institute.
key_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of each Institute, including providing instruction, conducting research, granting degrees, and managing property.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Institute by Central Government, State Government and industry partners.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process and criteria for establishing new Institutes under public-private partnership.

key_sections.title: Visitor.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor and defines the Visitor's powers to review and issue directions.

key_sections.title: Board of Governors.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Board as the principal policy-making and executive body and details its composition.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Board.
key_sections.description: Specifies the powers and functions of the Board, including policy-making, budget approval, and Statute framing.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Senate.
key_sections.description: Details the academic powers of the Senate, including admission criteria, course design, and examination conduct.

key_sections.title: Director.
key_sections.description: Defines the role, appointment, and removal of the Director as the principal executive officer.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Mandates proper accounts, annual statements, and audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

key_sections.title: Tribunal of Arbitration.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Tribunal for resolving disputes between an Institute and its employees or students.

key_sections.title: Co-ordination Forum.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment and composition of a central body for better co-ordination among the Institutes.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions.

powers_conferred: Institute: To provide instructions, conduct research, grant degrees, create posts, appoint faculty, disseminate knowledge, create website, determine fees, deal with property, receive gifts, cooperate with other institutions, establish infrastructure, award fellowships (Section 7).

Board of Governors: To frame, amend, modify or rescind Statutes and Ordinances; decide policy questions; establish departments; approve budgets; approve development plans; create posts; approve fees; grant degrees; exercise other powers conferred by Act/Statutes (Section 17).

Senate: To enact, amend or modify Ordinances governing academic matters; specify admission criteria; recommend creation of academic posts; recommend new programs; specify academic content; specify academic calendar; approve degrees; appoint examiners; recognise diplomas/degrees; suggest departmental coordination; make recommendations to Board (Section 19).

Central Government: To appoint date of commencement (Section 1(2)); specify name of new Institute (Section 4(2)); examine proposals for new Institutes (Section 11(2)); suggest modifications to proposals (Section 11(3)); communicate decisions on proposals (Section 11(4)); enter into MoU/agreement for establishment (Section 11(5)); establish Co-ordination Forum (Section 38(1)); make rules (Section 41); issue directions (Section 44); remove difficulties (Section 47).

Visitor: To appoint Director (Section 23(2)); remove Director (Section 23(7)); appoint persons to review work and hold inquiries (Section 12(2)); take action and issue directions based on reports (Section 12(3)).
Co-ordination Forum: To advise Central Government on inclusion/exclusion of institutions from Schedule; deliberate on common interests; promote coordination; recommend scholarships (Section 40).

related_acts: Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Visitor appoints Director (Section 23(2)). Board appoints three eminent persons, two eminent academicians, and one person from SC/ST (Section 14(2)(c), (d), (h)). Central Government notifies the First Board of Governors (Section 14(4)). Senate nominates two faculty members to the Board (Section 14(2)(g)).
regulatory_bodies: All India Council of Technical Education

applies_to: certain Indian Institutes of Information Technology established under public-private partnership
Institutes mentioned in the Schedule
all citizens irrespective of gender, caste, creed, disability, domicile, ethnicity, social or economic background
special_provisions: The ratio of investment of capital required for establishing the proposed Institute in North Eastern States shall be 57.5:35:7.5 (Section 11(2)(a)).
Every Institute shall be open to all citizens irrespective of gender, caste, creed, disability, domicile, ethnicity, social or economic background (Section 8(1)).
Every such Institute shall be a Central Educational Institution for the purposes of the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 (5 of 2007) (Section 8(3)).

act_identification.act_title: THE FUGITIVE ECONOMIC OFFENDERS ACT, 2018

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Sixty-ninth Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for measures to deter fugitive economic offenders from evading the process of law in India by staying outside the jurisdiction of Indian courts, to preserve the sanctity of the rule of law in India and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to deter fugitive economic offenders from evading legal processes in India by remaining outside the jurisdiction of Indian courts. Its primary objective is to preserve the sanctity of the rule of law in India by providing for the declaration of such individuals as fugitive economic offenders and the confiscation of their properties.

chapter_titles: DECLARATION OF FUGITIVE ECONOMIC OFFENDERS AND CONFISCATION OF PROPERTY

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical application, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, including 'fugitive economic offender' and 'Scheduled Offence'.

key_sections.title: Application of Act.
key_sections.description: States that the Act applies to individuals who are or become fugitive economic offenders on or after its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Application for declaration of fugitive economic offender and procedure therefor.

key_sections.title: Attachment of property.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to the Director or authorized officers to attach property, including provisional attachment, under certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Declaration of fugitive economic offender.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Special Court to declare an individual as a fugitive economic offender and order the confiscation of their properties, including proceeds of crime.

key_sections.title: Power to disallow civil claims.
key_sections.description: Allows courts or tribunals to disallow civil claims by individuals declared as fugitive economic offenders or by companies/LLPs linked to such offenders.

key_sections.title: Management of properties confiscated under this Act.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of an Administrator to manage and dispose of properties confiscated under the Act.

key_sections.title: Appeal.
key_sections.description: Establishes the right to appeal judgments or orders of a Special Court to the High Court.

key_sections.title: Bar of jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Excludes civil courts from jurisdiction over matters determinable by the Special Court under this Act.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to amend Schedule.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to add or omit offences from the Schedule by notification.

key_sections.title: Overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Fugitive Economic Offenders Ordinance, 2018, while saving actions taken under it.

powers_conferred: Director or any other officer not below the rank of Deputy Director: File application for declaration of fugitive economic offender (Section 4).
Director or any other officer not below the rank of Deputy Director: Attach property (Section 5).
Director or any other officer: Conduct survey (Section 7).
Director or any other officer not below the rank of Deputy Director: Search and seizure (Section 8).
Authority authorized by Central Government: Search persons (Section 9).
Special Court: Declare individual as fugitive economic offender (Section 12).
Special Court: Order confiscation of property (Section 12).
Special Court: Issue letter of request to a Court or authority in a contracting State for execution of confiscation order (Section 12).
Court or tribunal in India: Disallow civil claims by a declared fugitive economic offender or related entities (Section 14).
Central Government: Appoint Administrator (Section 15).
Central Government: Amend the Schedule of offences (Section 20).
Central Government: Make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act (Section 23).
Central Government: Remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of this Act (Section 25).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines 'Scheduled Offence' as an offence specified in the Schedule with a total value of one hundred crore rupees or more. It does not prescribe new penalties for these offences but provides for the declaration of individuals as 'fugitive economic offenders' and the confiscation of their property, including proceeds of crime, if they evade criminal prosecution in India.

repealed_acts: The Fugitive Economic Offenders Ordinance, 2018 (Ord. 1 of 2018)
related_acts: Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act, 1988 (45 of 1988)
Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016 (18 of 2016)
Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 (15 of 1992)
Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015 (22 of 2015)
Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (12 of 2017)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints the Administrator.

applies_to: Any individual who is, or becomes, a fugitive economic offender on or after the date of coming into force of this Act.

Companies or limited liability partnerships, in relation to disallowing civil claims, if an individual filing the claim on their behalf, or any promoter, key managerial personnel, or majority shareholder, or an individual with controlling interest, has been declared a fugitive economic offender.
exemptions: Any property which is a proceed of crime in which any person, other than the fugitive economic offender, has an interest, if such interest was acquired bona fide and without knowledge of the fact that the property was proceeds of crime.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Director or authorized officers file applications in the Special Court for declaration of individuals as fugitive economic offenders. The Special Court hears these applications, declares individuals as FEOs, and orders confiscation of their properties. An Administrator is appointed by the Central Government to manage and dispose of confiscated properties. Powers of survey, search, and seizure are granted to officers for investigation.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir. Now applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh by vide notification No. S.O. 3912 (E), dated 30th October, 2019.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for a comprehensive mechanism to ban the unregulated deposit schemes, other than deposits taken in the ordinary course of business, and to protect the interest of depositors and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to establish a comprehensive mechanism to ban unregulated deposit schemes. It aims to protect the interests of depositors by regulating deposit-taking activities and providing for restitution.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II BANNING OF UNREGULATED DEPOSIT SCHEMES.
CHAPTER IV INFORMATION ON DEPOSIT TAKERS
CHAPTER VII INVESTIGATION, SEARCH AND SEIZURE

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the official name, geographical applicability, and effective date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'deposit', 'deposit taker', 'Competent Authority', and 'Unregulated Deposit Scheme'.

key_sections.title: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes.
key_sections.description: Prohibits Unregulated Deposit Schemes and prevents deposit takers from promoting or accepting deposits under such schemes.

key_sections.title: Competent Authority.
key_sections.description: Mandates the appointment of a Competent Authority by the appropriate Government to oversee the Act's provisions, including provisional attachment of deposits.

key_sections.title: Designated Court.
key_sections.description: Requires the constitution of Designated Courts with exclusive jurisdiction for matters under this Act, presided over by a District and Sessions Judge or Additional District and Sessions Judge.

key_sections.title: Central database.
key_sections.description: Enables the Central Government to designate an authority to create and maintain an online database of deposit takers operating in India.

key_sections.title: Priority of depositors’ claim.
key_sections.description: Establishes that claims of depositors have priority over other debts, taxes, and cesses payable to the government or local authority, with exceptions for certain other Acts.

key_sections.title: Confirmation of attachment by Designated Court.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for the Designated Court to confirm, vary, or cancel provisional attachment orders made by the Competent Authority.

key_sections.title: Powers of Designated Court.
key_sections.description: Details the extensive powers of the Designated Court regarding the assessment of dues, valuation of assets, sale of attached assets, and equitable distribution of funds to depositors.

key_sections.title: Punishment for contravention of section 3.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for soliciting or accepting deposits in contravention of the ban on Unregulated Deposit Schemes.

key_sections.title: Offences to be cognizable and non-bailable.
key_sections.description: Declares most offences under the Act as cognizable and non-bailable, except for those under sections 22 and 26.

key_sections.title: Power to enter, search and seize without warrant.
key_sections.description: Grants police officers, with authorization, the power to enter, search, and seize property related to illegal deposit schemes without a warrant under certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any other law for the time being in force, unless expressly provided otherwise.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Ordinance, 2019, while saving actions taken under it.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines several offences and prescribes penalties: soliciting deposits in contravention of Section 3 (imprisonment 1-5 years, fine 2-10 lakh rupees); accepting deposits in contravention of Section 3 (imprisonment 2-7 years, fine 3-10 lakh rupees); accepting deposits in contravention of Section 3 and fraudulently defaulting (imprisonment 3-10 years, fine 5 lakh - twice aggregate funds); fraudulent default in Regulated Deposit Schemes (imprisonment up to 7 years, fine 5 lakh - 25 crore rupees or 3 times profits); wrongful inducement in relation to Unregulated Deposit Schemes (imprisonment 1-5 years, fine up to 10 lakh rupees); punishment for repeat offenders (imprisonment 5-10 years, fine 10 lakh - 50 crore rupees); and failure to give intimation or furnish information under Section 10 (fine up to 5 lakh rupees). Offences by deposit takers other than individuals also hold responsible those in charge and the entity itself.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government and the State Government or Union territory Government (in consultation with the Central Government) have the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes, establishment of Competent Authorities for provisional attachment of assets, and Designated Courts for confirmation of attachments, sale of property, and restitution to depositors. A central database for deposit takers is maintained. Offences are cognizable and non-bailable, with investigation powers granted to police and the Central Bureau of Investigation, including powers of search and seizure.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Designated Courts have exclusive jurisdiction for matters under this Act. Appeals from the Designated Court lie with the High Court. The Supreme Court has the power to transfer cases between Designated Courts.

act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to repeal certain existing enactments that are no longer necessary or relevant. Additionally, it aims to amend specific provisions within other enactments to update or correct them. This legislative action streamlines the body of Indian law by removing obsolete statutes and refining current ones.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL MEDICAL COMMISSION ACT, 2019

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for a medical education system that improves access to quality and affordable medical education, ensures availability of adequate and high quality medical professionals in all parts of the country; that promotes equitable and universal healthcare that encourages community health perspective and makes services of medical professionals accessible to all the citizens; that promotes national health goals; that encourages medical professionals to adopt latest medical research in their work and to contribute to research; that has an objective periodic and transparent assessment of medical institutions and facilitates maintenance of a medical register for India and enforces high ethical standards in all aspects of medical services; that is flexible to adapt to changing needs and has an effective grievance redressal mechanism and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to establish a medical education system that ensures quality, affordability, and availability of medical professionals across India. It seeks to promote equitable healthcare, encourage research, ensure transparent assessment of medical institutions, maintain a medical register, and enforce high ethical standards.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Defines the Act's name, geographical reach, and effective date.

key_sections.title: Constitution of National Medical Commission.
key_sections.description: Establishes the National Medical Commission as a body corporate to exercise powers and perform functions under the Act.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Commission.
key_sections.description: Outlines the Commission's responsibilities including policy-making for medical education, regulation of institutions and professionals, and ensuring ethical standards.

key_sections.title: Constitution and composition of Medical Advisory Council.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Medical Advisory Council as an advisory body for States and Union territories to interact with the Commission.

key_sections.title: National Eligibility cum-Entrance Test.
key_sections.description: Mandates a uniform National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test for admission to undergraduate and postgraduate super-speciality medical education.

key_sections.title: National Exit Test.
key_sections.description: Introduces a common final year undergraduate medical examination for granting licence to practice and for admission to postgraduate broad-speciality medical education.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Autonomous Boards.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of four Autonomous Boards (Under-Graduate, Post-Graduate, Medical Assessment and Rating, Ethics and Medical Registration) under the Commission's supervision.

key_sections.title: Permission for establishment of new medical college.
key_sections.description: Details the process and requirements for obtaining permission to establish new medical colleges, start postgraduate courses, or increase seats.

key_sections.title: National Register and State Register.
key_sections.description: Requires the Ethics and Medical Registration Board to maintain a National Register and State Medical Councils to maintain State Registers of licensed medical practitioners.

key_sections.title: Community Health Provider.
key_sections.description: Allows the Commission to grant limited licences to practice medicine at mid-level as Community Health Providers under specified criteria.

key_sections.title: Rights of persons to have licence to practice and to be enrolled in National Register or State Register and their obligations thereto.
key_sections.description: Specifies the conditions for obtaining a licence to practice medicine and enrollment in the National or State Register, including for foreign medical qualifications.

key_sections.title: Bar to practice.
key_sections.description: Prohibits any person not enrolled in the State or National Register from practicing medicine and prescribes penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Recognition of medical qualifications granted by Universities or medical institutions in India.
key_sections.description: Governs the process for recognition of medical qualifications granted by Universities or medical institutions within India.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956, and includes saving provisions for previous actions and existing qualifications.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Power to constitute National Medical Commission, Autonomous Boards, Medical Advisory Council; appoint Chairperson and Members; give directions to Commission, Autonomous Boards, and State Governments; supersede Commission; make rules; remove difficulties.

National Medical Commission: Lay down policies and regulations for medical education, institutions, and professionals; assess healthcare requirements; coordinate Autonomous Boards and State Medical Councils; exercise appellate jurisdiction over Autonomous Boards; lay down ethics codes; frame guidelines for fees; make regulations.

Autonomous Boards (Under-Graduate Medical Education Board, Post-Graduate Medical Education Board, Medical Assessment and Rating Board, Ethics and Medical Registration Board): Perform specific functions related to their respective areas, including curriculum development, standard setting, assessment, rating, registration, and ethics.
Medical Assessment and Rating Board: Grant permission for establishment of new medical institutions, courses, or seat increases; carry out inspections; assess and rate institutions; impose penalties.

Ethics and Medical Registration Board: Maintain National Registers; regulate professional conduct and promote medical ethics; exercise appellate jurisdiction with respect to State Medical Council actions.
State Medical Councils: Take disciplinary actions in respect of professional or ethical misconduct; maintain and update State Registers.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who contravenes the provisions of Section 34 (Bar to practice without enrollment) shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to five lakh rupees or with both.

repealed_acts: the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956 (102 of 1956)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson, certain part-time Members, and the Secretary of the Commission, as well as the President and Members of the Autonomous Boards, based on recommendations from a Search Committee. The Search Committee recommends a panel of names for these positions.

applies_to: Medical education system in India
Medical institutions (within or outside India for recognition)
Medical professionals/practitioners
Health Universities
Community Health Providers
exemptions: Veterinary medicine and surgery (from the definition of 'medicine')
The Central Government (from the definition of 'person' for establishing new medical colleges)
special_provisions: Relaxation of criteria for medical colleges in specified areas.
Temporary registration for foreign citizens as medical practitioners.
Provisions for students already studying and for existing recognitions to continue under the new Act.
Joint sittings with Central Councils of Homoeopathy and Indian medicine to enhance interface between systems.
State Governments to promote primary healthcare in rural areas.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the National Medical Commission and its Autonomous Boards, which lay down policies, regulations, and standards. The Medical Assessment and Rating Board can impose penalties, reduce intake, or recommend withdrawal of recognition. The Ethics and Medical Registration Board regulates professional conduct and maintains registers. State Medical Councils handle disciplinary actions. An appellate mechanism exists from Autonomous Boards to the Commission, and from the Commission to the Central Government. Penalties are prescribed for unauthorized practice.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under this Act except upon a complaint in writing made by an officer authorized by the Commission, the Ethics and Medical Registration Board, or a State Medical Council.

schedules_summary.description: Lists categories of medical qualifications granted by statutory or other bodies in India, including those from Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research, All India Institutes of Medical Sciences, Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro-Sciences, and National Board of Examination.

act_identification.act_title: THE CODE ON WAGES, 2019
act_identification.date_of_commencement: on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette appoint; and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Code

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend and consolidate the laws relating to wages and bonus and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to amend and consolidate existing laws related to wages and bonus. Its objective is to streamline regulations concerning employee remuneration and bonus payments, and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

chapter_titles: PAYMENT OF DUES CLAIMS AND AUDIT

key_definitions: same work or work of a similar nature

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date notified by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Code, such as 'employee', 'employer', 'wages', 'appropriate Government', etc.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of discrimination on ground of gender.
key_sections.description: Prohibits discrimination based on gender in wage matters for same or similar work and in recruitment, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Fixation of minimum wages.
key_sections.description: Mandates the appropriate Government to fix minimum rates of wages for time work or piece work, considering skill, geographical area, and arduousness of work.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to fix floor wage.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to fix a floor wage, which minimum wages fixed by appropriate Governments cannot be less than.

key_sections.title: Wages for overtime work.
key_sections.description: Requires employers to pay at least twice the normal rate of wages for overtime work.

key_sections.title: Mode of payment of wages.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that wages shall be paid in current coin, currency notes, cheque, bank transfer, or electronic mode.

key_sections.title: Time limit for payment of wages.
key_sections.description: Sets deadlines for payment of wages based on wage periods (daily, weekly, fortnightly, monthly) and for employees leaving service.

key_sections.title: Deductions which may be made from wages.
key_sections.description: Authorizes specific types of deductions from wages, such as fines, absence from duty, damage or loss, and recovery of advances/loans.

key_sections.title: Eligibility for bonus, etc.
key_sections.description: Defines eligibility for annual minimum bonus for employees, its calculation, and maximum limits, including provisions for allocable surplus.

key_sections.title: Central Advisory Board and State Advisory Boards.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of Central and State Advisory Boards to advise on minimum wages, women's employment, and other matters under the Code.

key_sections.title: Claims under Code and procedure thereof.
key_sections.description: Empowers the appropriate Government to appoint authorities to hear and determine claims arising under the Code, including compensation and recovery procedures.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Inspector-cum-Facilitators and their powers.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the appropriate Government to appoint Inspector-cum-Facilitators with powers to advise, inspect, and investigate compliance with the Code.

key_sections.title: Penalties for offences.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for various offences such as paying less than due wages, contravening provisions, and improper record maintenance.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals four previous Acts related to wages and bonus, while providing for savings of actions taken under those repealed enactments.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To fix floor wage (Section 9).
Central Government: To make rules for carrying out provisions of the Code (Section 67).
Central Government: To give directions to State Governments for execution of provisions (Section 65).
Central Government: To remove difficulties in giving effect to the Code (Section 68).
Appropriate Government: To fix minimum rates of wages (Section 6).
Appropriate Government: To appoint authorities to hear and determine claims (Section 45).
Appropriate Government: To appoint Inspector-cum-Facilitators and define their powers (Section 51).
Appropriate Government: To make rules for carrying out provisions of the Code (Section 67).
Appropriate Government: To delegate its powers under the Code (Section 62).
Inspector-cum-Facilitators: To advise employers and workers, inspect establishments, search, seize or take copies of records (Section 51).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines offences such as paying less than the amount due, contravening other provisions of the Code, and non-maintenance or improper maintenance of records. Penalties include fines up to fifty thousand rupees for initial offences, and imprisonment up to three months or higher fines for repeat offences. Officers of the appropriate Government may impose penalties in certain cases.

authorities_established: Authorities to hear and determine claims (under Section 45)
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government nominates members to the Central Advisory Board and appoints its Chairperson. The State Government constitutes State Advisory Boards and appoints its Chairperson. The appropriate Government appoints authorities for claims, appellate authorities, Inspector-cum-Facilitators, and officers to impose penalties.

applies_to: Whole of India
Employees

Establishments
exemptions: Government establishments (from Chapter III, unless notified)

special_provisions: Different floor wage may be fixed for different geographical areas (Section 9(1) Proviso).

Chapter IV (Payment of Bonus) applies to public sector establishments if they compete with private sector and income from such competition is not less than twenty per cent. of gross income (Section 40(1)).
Chapter III (Payment of Wages) does not apply to Government establishments unless the appropriate Government, by notification, applies such provisions (Section 25).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The appropriate Government (Section 67(1)) and the Central Government (Section 67(3)) have the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Code.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through Inspector-cum-Facilitators who inspect establishments and investigate compliance. Authorities appointed by the appropriate Government hear and determine claims, with powers to order compensation and recover dues as arrears of land revenue. Offences are cognizable by courts based on complaints, and officers of the appropriate Government can impose penalties.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall try offences under this Code. Authorities and appellate authorities under the Code have powers of a civil court for taking evidence and enforcing attendance of witnesses.

act_identification.act_title: THE JAMMU AND KASHMIR REORGANISATION ACT, 2019
act_identification.act_short_title: the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019

legislative_details.geographical_extent: existing State of Jammu and Kashmir, Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir, Union territory of Ladakh

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the reorganisation of the existing State of Jammu and Kashmir and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the reorganisation of the existing State of Jammu and Kashmir into two new Union territories: the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir with a legislature, and the Union territory of Ladakh without a legislature. It also addresses the representation in legislatures, administration, financial matters, services, and legal provisions related to this reorganisation.

key_definitions: existing State of Jammu and Kashmir

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appointed day', 'Election Commission', 'existing State of Jammu and Kashmir', 'Legislative Assembly', and 'Lieutenant Governor'.

key_sections.title: Formation of Union territory of Ladakh without Legislature.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Union territory of Ladakh, comprising Kargil and Leh districts, without a legislature.

key_sections.title: Formation of Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir with Legislature.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir, comprising the remaining territories of the existing State, with a legislature.

key_sections.title: Legislative Assembly for the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and its composition.
key_sections.description: Provides for a Legislative Assembly for the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir, specifying its composition, total seats, reservation for Scheduled Castes and Tribes, and provisions for vacant seats.

key_sections.title: Extent of legislative power.
key_sections.description: Defines the legislative powers of the Legislative Assembly of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir, excluding 'Public Order' and 'Police'.

key_sections.title: Council of Ministers.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Council of Ministers for the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir, with the Chief Minister at its head, to aid and advise the Lieutenant Governor.

key_sections.title: Abolition of Legislative Council of the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
key_sections.description: Abolishes the Legislative Council of the existing State of Jammu and Kashmir.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Lieutenant Governor of Union territory of Ladakh.
key_sections.description: Provides for the administration of the Union territory of Ladakh by a Lieutenant Governor appointed by the President, and the President's power to make regulations for its governance.

key_sections.title: Delimitation of constituencies.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for delimitation of constituencies for the Legislative Assembly of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir by the Election Commission.

key_sections.title: High Court of Jammu and Kashmir to be common High Court.
key_sections.description: Declares the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir as the common High Court for both the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh.

key_sections.title: Provisions relating to All India Services.
key_sections.description: Specifies that members of All India Services for the existing Jammu and Kashmir cadre will become part of the Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Mizoram and Union territories cadre.

key_sections.title: Territorial extent of laws.
key_sections.description: States that Central laws and other specified laws will apply to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and Union territory of Ladakh as provided in the Fifth Schedule.

key_sections.title: Effect of provisions of the Act inconsistent with other laws.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Grants the President the power to make orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the Act, within a period of five years from the appointed day.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint 'appointed day', to specify associate members for Delimitation Commission, to publish orders for readjustment of constituencies, to establish Advisory Committee(s), to make rules for apportionment of losses/profits for income-tax, to make modifications in cadre allocation rules for All India Services, to determine successor Union territory for employees, to review orders under Section 89, to adapt and modify laws.

President: To appoint Election Commission, to appoint Lieutenant Governor, to determine period for common Lieutenant Governor, to extend duration of Legislative Assembly during emergency, to direct reservation of Bills, to assent or withhold assent to Bills, to authorise expenditure, to make regulations for Ladakh, to make reference to Union territories Finance Commission and Fifteenth Finance Commission, to approve UPSC serving Ladakh, to remove difficulties.

Lieutenant Governor: To summon, prorogue, dissolve Legislative Assembly, to determine salaries/allowances of Speaker/Deputy Speaker, to address and send messages to Legislative Assembly, to appoint person for oath/affirmation, to decide disqualification questions, to determine salaries/allowances of members, to recommend financial Bills, to assent or withhold assent to Bills, or reserve for President, to cause annual financial statement to be laid, to recommend demands for grants, to promulgate Ordinances, to act in discretion, to appoint Chief Minister and other Ministers, to administer oaths to Ministers, to determine Ministers' salaries/allowances, to make rules for conduct of business, to authenticate orders, to appoint Advocate-General, to authorise expenditure, to cause audit reports to be laid, to declare expenditure authorised, to specify authority for statutory functions.

Legislative Assembly: To choose Speaker and Deputy Speaker, to remove Speaker/Deputy Speaker, to make laws, to determine salaries/allowances of members, to make rules of procedure, to adopt official language(s), to regulate recruitment/conditions of service for secretariat staff, to determine sums for Contingency Fund, to fix limits for borrowing.
Election Commission: To conduct elections, to determine delimitation of constituencies, to publish proposals and orders, to maintain Delimitation Orders up-to-date.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 29 prescribes a penalty of five hundred rupees per day for any person who sits or votes as a member of the Legislative Assembly before making oath or affirmation, or when not qualified or disqualified.
