act_identification.act_title: THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for protection of the interests of consumers and for the said purpose, to establish authorities for timely and effective administration and settlement of consumers' disputes and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: To provide for the protection of consumer interests, establish authorities for timely and effective administration, and facilitate the settlement of consumer disputes.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, geographical extent, commencement process, and general applicability to goods and services.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act, such as 'consumer', 'complaint', 'unfair trade practice', and 'product liability'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Central Consumer Protection Authority.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of the Central Consumer Protection Authority to regulate consumer rights violations, unfair trade practices, and false advertisements.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Central Authority.
key_sections.description: Outlines the Central Authority's powers to protect consumer rights, prevent unfair trade practices, ensure no false advertising, and conduct inquiries/investigations.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Authority to recall goods, etc.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Authority power to order the recall of dangerous goods, withdrawal of unsafe services, reimbursement of prices, and discontinuation of unfair practices.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Authority to issue directions and penalties against false or misleading advertisements.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Authority to issue directions to discontinue or modify false/misleading advertisements and impose penalties on manufacturers, endorsers, or publishers.

key_sections.title: Establishment of District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
key_sections.description: Requires State Governments to establish District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions in each district.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of District Commission.
key_sections.description: Defines the pecuniary and territorial jurisdiction of the District Commission for entertaining complaints.

key_sections.title: Manner in which complaint shall be made.
key_sections.description: Specifies who can file a complaint with the District Commission and the manner of filing, including electronically.

key_sections.title: Findings of District Commission.
key_sections.description: Details the types of orders the District Commission can issue upon finding defects in goods, deficiencies in services, or unfair trade practices, including compensation and punitive damages.

key_sections.title: Appeal against order of District Commission.
key_sections.description: Allows appeals against District Commission orders to the State Commission within a specified period, with a requirement to deposit 50% of the awarded amount.

key_sections.title: Establishment of National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to establish the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of National Commission.
key_sections.description: Defines the pecuniary and appellate jurisdiction of the National Commission, including complaints exceeding ten crore rupees and appeals against State Commission and Central Authority orders.

key_sections.title: Enforcement of orders of District Commission, State Commission and National Commission.
key_sections.description: States that orders of the Commissions shall be enforced as if they were decrees of a Civil Court.

key_sections.title: Penalty for non-compliance of order.
key_sections.description: Prescribes imprisonment and/or fine for failure to comply with orders of the District, State, or National Commission.

key_sections.title: Application of Chapter.
key_sections.description: States that the Product Liability Chapter applies to claims for compensation due to harm caused by defective products.

key_sections.title: Liability of product manufacturer.
key_sections.description: Outlines the conditions under which a product manufacturer is liable in a product liability action, including manufacturing defects, design defects, and non-conformity to express warranty.

key_sections.title: Penalty for non-compliance of direction of Central Authority.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for non-compliance with directions issued by the Central Authority under sections 20 and 21.

key_sections.title: Punishment for false or misleading advertisement.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment, including imprisonment and fine, for manufacturers or service providers causing false or misleading advertisements.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, while providing for savings of actions taken under the repealed Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To establish Central Consumer Protection Council (Section 3), Central Consumer Protection Authority (Section 10), make rules (Section 101), give directions on policy (Section 99), remove difficulties (Section 106).
State Government: To establish State Consumer Protection Councils (Section 6), District Consumer Protection Councils (Section 8), make rules (Section 102).

Central Consumer Protection Authority: To protect, promote, and enforce consumer rights; prevent unfair trade practices; ensure no false or misleading advertisements; inquire/investigate violations; file complaints; intervene in proceedings; review consumer rights safeguards; recommend international practices; undertake research; spread awareness; encourage NGOs; mandate unique goods identifiers; issue safety notices; advise Ministries; issue guidelines (Section 18); refer matters for investigation or to other Regulators (Section 19); recall goods or withdraw services; order reimbursement; discontinue unfair practices (Section 20); issue directions and penalties against false or misleading advertisements (Section 21); make regulations (Section 104).

District Collector: To inquire into or investigate complaints regarding violation of consumer rights, unfair trade practices, and false or misleading advertisements within his jurisdiction (Section 16).

District Commission, State Commission, National Commission: To entertain complaints; hear appeals; enforce orders; review orders; summon witnesses; require discovery and production of documents; receive evidence on affidavits; requisition reports from laboratories; issue commissions for examination of witnesses/documents (Chapter IV).
National Commission: To make regulations (Section 103); lay down standards and have administrative control over State Commissions (Section 70).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines several offences and prescribes penalties: non-compliance with directions of the Central Authority (Section 88) punishable with imprisonment up to six months or fine up to twenty lakh rupees, or both; false or misleading advertisement (Section 89) punishable with imprisonment up to two years and fine up to ten lakh rupees, with higher penalties for subsequent offences; manufacturing, storing, selling, distributing, or importing products containing adulterant (Section 90) with penalties ranging from imprisonment up to six months and fine up to one lakh rupees for no injury, to imprisonment for life and fine not less than ten lakh rupees for death; manufacturing, storing, selling, distributing, or importing spurious goods (Section 91) with penalties ranging from imprisonment up to one year and fine up to three lakh rupees for non-grievous injury, to imprisonment for life and fine not less than ten lakh rupees for death; vexatious search by Director General or other officer (Section 93) punishable with imprisonment up to one year or fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both; and non-compliance with orders of the District, State, or National Commission (Section 72) punishable with imprisonment from one month to three years, or fine from twenty-five thousand rupees to one lakh rupees, or both.

related_acts: Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (34 of 2006)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints Chief Commissioner and Commissioners of the Central Authority (Section 10(2)), and Director-General and other officers of the Investigation Wing (Section 15(2)). National Commission, State Commission, or District Commission prepare a panel of mediators (Section 75(1)).

applies_to: Whole of India
all goods and services
consumers
exemptions: Goods obtained for resale or for any commercial purpose (Section 2(7)(i))
Services availed for any commercial purpose (Section 2(7)(ii))
Harm caused to a product itself or any damage to property on account of breach of warranty conditions or any commercial or economic loss (Section 2(22))
Seller of immovable property, unless engaged in the sale of constructed house or in the construction of homes or flats (Section 2(37)(a))
Provider of professional services where the sale or use of a product is only incidental thereto (Section 2(37)(b))

Persons acting only in a financial capacity with respect to product sale, not being a manufacturer, wholesaler, distributor, retailer, direct seller or an electronic service provider (Section 2(37)(c)(I), (II))
Lessor of a product without reasonable opportunity to inspect and discover defects, under certain lease arrangements (Section 2(37)(c)(III))
Rendering of any service free of charge or under a contract of personal service (Section 2(42))
Product liability action cannot be brought against the product seller if, at the time of harm, the product was misused, altered, or modified (Section 87(1))

Product manufacturer not liable for failure to provide adequate warnings/instructions if product purchased by employer for workplace and warnings provided to employer; or product sold as component and warnings given to purchaser of component; or product meant for expert use and warnings given to expert; or complainant was under influence of alcohol/prescription drug not prescribed by medical practitioner (Section 87(2))
Product manufacturer not liable for failure to instruct or warn about a danger which is obvious or commonly known to the user or consumer (Section 87(3))
special_provisions: Initially extended to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir, but later made applicable to the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Ladakh by notification.
Different dates may be appointed for commencement for different States and for different provisions of the Act (Section 1(3)).
State Government may establish more than one District Commission in a district (Proviso to Section 28(1)).
State Government may establish regional benches of the State Commission (Proviso to Section 42(2)).
Central Government may establish regional Benches of the National Commission (Proviso to Section 53(2)).

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act establishes a multi-tiered system for enforcement: Consumer Protection Councils (Central, State, District) for advisory roles; the Central Consumer Protection Authority to regulate, investigate, issue directions, and impose penalties for consumer rights violations, unfair trade practices, and false/misleading advertisements; and Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions (District, State, National) to adjudicate consumer complaints, pass orders, and enforce them. Mediation is provided as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance with orders and for specific offences like false advertising or selling adulterated/spurious goods.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District Commission, State Commission, National Commission (quasi-judicial bodies). Appeals against National Commission orders lie with the Supreme Court. For certain offences, the Commissions are deemed Judicial Magistrates of first class, and cognizance can be taken by a competent court.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL CAPITAL TERRITORY OF DELHI (RECOGNITION OF PROPERTY RIGHTS OF RESIDENTS IN UNAUTHORISED COLONIES) ACT, 2019
act_identification.act_short_title: the National Capital Territory of Delhi (Recognition of Property Rights of Residents in Unauthorised Colonies) Act, 2019

legislative_details.geographical_extent: the National Capital Territory of Delhi

act_overview.preamble: WHEREAS there has been phenomenal increase in the population of the National Capital Territory of Delhi in the last few decades owing to migration and other factors but development of planned housing colonies have not kept pace with the requirements of a burgeoning population resulting in the increase of unauthorised colonies; AND WHEREAS number of unauthorised colonies have been identified in the National Capital Territory of Delhi on the basis of applications made by the Residents Welfare Associations for regularisation in pursuance to notification number S.O. 683(E), dated the 24th March, 2008 of the Delhi Development Authority, published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub-section (ii), dated the 24th March, 2008; AND WHEREAS the properties in these colonies are not being registered by registering authority and thereby the residents do not have any title documents in respect of such properties and the Banks and financial institutions do not extend any credit facilities in respect of said properties; AND WHEREAS the ownership of the properties in unauthorised colonies have been transferred several times through registered or un-registered or notarised Power of Attorney, Agreement to Sale, Will, possession letter and other documents including documents evidencing payment of consideration and stamp duty on these multiple transactions have neither assessed nor been paid; AND WHEREAS the stamp duty on the conveyance deed or authorisation slip, as the case may be, is leviable as per minimum rates (circle rates) specified in the notification of the Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi published vide number F.1(953) Regn. Br./ Div. Com/HQ/2014, dated the 22nd September, 2014 or the sale consideration mentioned in the conveyance deed or authorisation slip, as the case may be, whichever is higher; AND WHEREAS the Supreme Court in the case of Suraj Lamp & Industries (P) Ltd. Vs. State of Haryana & others vide its judgment dated the 11th October, 2011 had held that sale agreement/general Power of Attorney or Will transactions are not “transfers” or “sales” and that such transactions cannot be treated as completed transfers or conveyances and they can continue to be treated as existing agreement of sale; AND WHEREAS keeping in view the socio-economic conditions of the residents of these unauthorised colonies and ground realities, it is desirable to recognise and confer rights of ownership or transfer or mortgage to the residents of such colonies on the basis of Power of Attorney, Agreement to Sale, Will, possession letter and other documents including documents evidencing payment of consideration and to facilitate development or re-development that may improve existing infrastructure, civic and social amenities which may lead to better quality of life; AND WHEREAS it is expedient to have a law to recognise and confer rights of ownership or transfer or mortgage to the residents of unauthorised colonies as one time special measure.
act_overview.purpose: An Act to provide special provisions for the National Capital Territory of Delhi for recognising the property rights of resident in unauthorised colonies by securing the rights of ownership or transfer or mortgage in favour of the residents of such colonies who are possessing properties on the basis of Power of Attorney, Agreement to Sale, Will, possession letter or any other documents including documents evidencing payment of consideration and for the matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

key_sections.description: Establishes the Act's official title and its geographical application to the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

key_sections.title: Recognition of property rights.

act_identification.act_title: THE PROHIBITION OF ELECTRONIC CIGARETTES (PRODUCTION, MANUFACTURE, IMPORT, EXPORT, TRANSPORT, SALE, DISTRIBUTION, STORAGE AND ADVERTISEMENT) ACT, 2019
act_identification.act_short_title: The Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes (Production, Manufacture, Import, Export, Transport, Sale, Distribution, Storage and Advertisement) Act, 2019.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to prohibit the production, manufacture, import, export, transport, sale, distribution, storage and advertisement of electronic cigarettes in the interest of public health to protect the people from harm and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to prohibit all activities related to electronic cigarettes, including their production, manufacture, import, export, transport, sale, distribution, storage, and advertisement. Its primary objective is to safeguard public health by protecting people from the harm associated with electronic cigarettes.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the official name of the Act and specifies its deemed date of commencement.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to expediency of control by Union.
key_sections.description: Declares that it is expedient in the public interest for the Union to control the electronic cigarettes industry.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'advertisement', 'authorised officer', and 'electronic cigarette'.

key_sections.title: Prohibition on production, manufacturing, import, export, transport, sale, distribution, advertisement of electronic cigarettes.
key_sections.description: Prohibits any person from directly or indirectly engaging in the production, manufacture, import, export, transport, sale, distribution, or advertisement of electronic cigarettes.

key_sections.title: Prohibition on storage of electronic cigarettes.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the storage of electronic cigarettes and outlines the procedure for disposing of existing stock.

key_sections.title: Power to enter, search and seize without warrant.
key_sections.description: Grants authorised officers the power to enter, search, and seize property or records related to contraventions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Punishment for contravention of section 4.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for violating the prohibitions specified in section 4.

key_sections.title: Punishment for contravention of section 5.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fine, for violating the prohibition on storage specified in section 5.

key_sections.title: Offences by companies.
key_sections.description: Stipulates the liability of companies and their officers for offences committed under this Act.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes (Production, Manufacture, Import, Export, Transport, Sale, Distribution, Storage and Advertisement) Ordinance, 2019, and includes savings provisions.

powers_conferred: Power to enter, search and seize without warrant (authorised officer)
Power to dispose of stock seized (authorised officer)
Power to remove difficulties (Central Government)
Power to authorise officers (Central Government or State Government)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Contravention of section 4 (production, manufacture, import, export, transport, sale, distribution, advertisement) is punishable with imprisonment for up to one year or a fine up to one lakh rupees, or both; for subsequent offences, imprisonment up to three years and a fine up to five lakh rupees. Contravention of section 5 (storage) is punishable with imprisonment for up to six months or a fine up to fifty thousand rupees, or both.

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Ships registered in India (wherever they may be), ships entering a port, shipyard or off-shore terminal or a place in India or within the Exclusive Economic Zone or territorial waters of India, warships/naval auxiliaries destined for recycling in a ship recycling facility operating in or within the territorial jurisdiction of India, and ship recycling facilities operating in India or within any area falling under the exclusive territorial jurisdiction of India.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the regulation of recycling of ships by setting certain standards and laying down the statutory mechanism for enforcement of such standards and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS, the International Maritime Organisation adopted the Hong Kong International Convention for the Safe and Environmentally Sound Recycling of Ships, 2009 which ensures that ships, when being recycled after the end of their operational lives, do not pose any unnecessary risk to the environment and to human health and safety; AND WHEREAS, the said Convention was developed with inputs from International Maritime Organisation Member States, Non-Governmental Organisations and in co-operation with the International Labour Organisation and the Parties to the Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and their Disposal, 1989; AND WHEREAS, the Hong Kong Convention lays down the aspects relating to design, construction, operation and preparation of ships so as to facilitate safe and environmentally sound recycling, without compromising the safety and operational efficiency of ships and the establishment of an appropriate enforcement mechanism for recycling of ships; AND WHEREAS, the said Convention contains the provisions which are not covered in the Shipbreaking Code (Revised), 2013 notified by the Government of India to regulate the recycling of ships in India; AND WHEREAS, the said Convention lays down the multilateral framework to be followed internationally by countries which become a party to it; AND WHEREAS, India, being a Member-State of the International Maritime Organisation, had participated in the said Convention and expressed views for the protection of environment and human health and safety during the process of recycling of ships; AND WHEREAS, it is considered expedient to accede to the aforesaid Convention now and to have an appropriate legislation on issues relating to the recycling of ships.
act_overview.purpose: To provide for the regulation of recycling of ships by setting certain standards and laying down the statutory mechanism for enforcement of such standards. It aims to ensure that ships, when recycled, do not pose unnecessary risks to the environment, human health, and safety, in line with the Hong Kong International Convention for the Safe and Environmentally Sound Recycling of Ships, 2009.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II: AUTHORITIES UNDER THE ACT
CHAPTER V: PROCESS OF RECYCLING OF SHIPS
CHAPTER VIII: POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF NATIONAL AUTHORITY, COMPETENT AUTHORITY AND CENTRAL GOVERNMENT
CHAPTER IX: OFFENCES, PENALTIES AND COMPENSATION

key_definitions: certificate of authorisation of ship recycling facility
certificate on inventory of hazardous materials

key_sections.title: Short title, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its commencement date, and the scope of its application to various ships and recycling facilities.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, including 'hazardous material', 'ship recycling', 'National Authority', and 'Competent Authority'.

key_sections.title: Designation of National Authority.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to designate a National Authority to administer, supervise, and monitor ship recycling activities.

key_sections.title: Designation of Competent Authority.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to designate a Competent Authority for performing duties within specified geographical areas or areas of expertise.

key_sections.title: Controls on hazardous materials.
key_sections.description: Prohibits the installation or use of notified hazardous materials on ships and requires compliance with prescribed restrictions and conditions.

key_sections.title: Certificate on inventory of hazardous materials.
key_sections.description: Requires ship owners to obtain and maintain a certificate on inventory of hazardous materials, which must be updated throughout the ship's operational life.

key_sections.title: Authorisation of ship recycling facility.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that no Ship Recycler shall recycle a ship without proper authorisation of the ship recycling facility.

key_sections.title: Ship recycling facility management plan and procedure for authorisation of ship recycling facility.
key_sections.description: Outlines the requirements for a ship recycling facility management plan and the procedure for obtaining authorisation from the Competent Authority.

key_sections.title: Workers safety, training and insurance.
key_sections.description: Mandates Ship Recyclers to provide adequate measures for worker safety, health, training, and insurance, applying provisions of the Factories Act, 1948.

key_sections.title: Ready for recycling certificate.
key_sections.description: Requires ship owners intending to recycle their ship to apply for a 'ready for recycling certificate' from the National Authority.

key_sections.title: Ship recycling plan.
key_sections.description: Prohibits ship recycling without a ship recycling plan prepared according to National Authority guidelines and approved by the Competent Authority.

key_sections.title: Safe and environmentally sound management of hazardous materials.
key_sections.description: Obligates Ship Recyclers to ensure safe and environmentally sound removal and management of hazardous materials and comply with infrastructure requirements.

key_sections.title: Power to inspect, dismiss, exclude or detain a ship.
key_sections.description: Grants the National Authority or Administration the power to inspect, dismiss, exclude, or detain ships for non-compliance with certificate requirements or hazardous material controls.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of provisions of Act or rules or regulations.
key_sections.description: Prescribes specific penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for various contraventions of the Act, rules, or regulations.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers upon the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Designate National/Competent Authority (S. 3, 4), notify prohibited hazardous materials (S. 6), authorise persons/organisations for surveys (S. 7), notify Surveyor (S. 2(1)(s)), exempt ships/facilities/recyclers (S. 29), specify categories of Indian ships to which Act doesn't apply (S. 30), nominate adjudicating officer (S. 39), delegate powers (S. 40), make rules (S. 42), remove difficulties (S. 46).

National Authority: Administer, supervise, monitor ship recycling (S. 3), carry out surveys (S. 7), issue/renew/suspend/cancel certificate on inventory of hazardous materials (S. 8, 9, 10), specify guidelines for ship recycling plan (S. 17), dismiss, exclude or detain a ship (S. 28), search and seize records (S. 27), delegate powers (S. 40), make regulations (S. 43).

Competent Authority: Perform duties within geographical area/expertise (S. 4), authorise ship recycling facility (S. 11, 12), suspend/cancel authorisation (S. 13), approve ship recycling plan (S. 17), grant permission for ship recycling (S. 18, 20), serve notice for oil spill (S. 22), receive statement of completion (S. 23), report to National Authority (S. 24), search and seize records (S. 27), delegate powers (S. 40).
Surveyor: Inspect ships (S. 28).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter IX (Sections 31-39) details offences, penalties, and compensation. Penalties for specific contraventions (e.g., using prohibited hazardous materials, operating without authorization, failing to manage hazardous materials, not responding to oil spill notices) include imprisonment up to one year and/or fines up to ten lakh rupees. A general penalty for other contraventions is imprisonment up to three months and/or a fine up to two lakh rupees, with additional fines for continuing contraventions. Offences by companies are also covered, holding responsible persons in charge. Offences are non-cognizable, bailable, and compoundable. The Act also provides for compensation for unduly detained or delayed ships.

related_acts: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 (6 of 1974)
Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976 (80 of 1976)
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 (14 of 1981)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government designates the National Authority and the Competent Authority.

applies_to: Any existing ship which is registered in India wherever it may be.
Any new ship which is required to be registered in India, wherever it may be.

Ships, other than those referred to in clauses (a) and (b), that enter a port, shipyard or off-shore terminal or a place in India or within the Exclusive Economic Zone or territorial waters of India or any marine areas adjacent thereto over which India has, or may have, exclusive jurisdiction.

Any warship, naval auxiliary or other ship owned or operated by an Administration and used on Government non-commercial service, and which is destined for recycling in a ship recycling facility operating in or within the territorial jurisdiction of India.
Ship recycling facilities operating in India or within any area falling under the exclusive territorial jurisdiction of India.
exemptions: Warships, naval auxiliaries, or other ships owned or operated by the Government and used for Government non-commercial purpose (from Chapter III provisions).
Ships of less than five hundred gross tonnage (from Chapter III provisions).
Certain class or category of ships from the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 6 (prohibited hazardous materials) as notified by the Central Government.
Any vessel or any class thereof, ship recycling facility or Ship Recycler from any specified requirement, as exempted by the Central Government.
Such category of Indian ships as the Central Government may, from time to time, by notification specify.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the designation of National and Competent Authorities, mandatory surveys and certification of ships (e.g., Inventory of Hazardous Materials, Ready for Recycling Certificate), authorization and annual audits of ship recycling facilities, approval of ship recycling plans, inspections, search and seizure powers, detention of non-compliant ships, and a system of penalties for contraventions. An appeals mechanism is also provided.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any Court which the Central Government may, by notification, direct in this behalf, or in any Court in which an offender might be tried under any other law for the time being in force. Cognizance of offences can only be taken on a complaint made by the Central Government, National Authority, or Competent Authority.

act_identification.act_title: THE INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL SERVICES CENTRES AUTHORITY ACT, 2019
act_identification.act_short_title: the International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019

legislative_details.geographical_extent: International Financial Services Centres in India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Authority to develop and regulate the financial services market in the International Financial Services Centres in India and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes an Authority to develop and regulate the financial services market within International Financial Services Centres in India. Its primary objective is to oversee financial products, services, and institutions operating in these special economic zones.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government, with different dates possible for different provisions.

key_sections.title: Application.
key_sections.description: States that the Act applies to International Financial Services Centres established under section 18 of the Special Economic Zones Act, 2005.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Authority', 'financial product', 'financial service', and 'International Financial Services Centre'.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Authority.
key_sections.description: Mandates the establishment of the International Financial Services Centres Authority as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

key_sections.title: Composition of Authority.
key_sections.description: Details the composition of the Authority, including a Chairperson and members nominated by various financial regulators and the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Functions of Authority.
key_sections.description: Outlines the duty of the Authority to develop and regulate financial products, financial services, and financial institutions in International Financial Services Centres.

key_sections.title: Powers of Authority in relation to financial products, financial services and financial institutions.
key_sections.description: Grants the Authority powers exercisable by other appropriate regulators in IFSCs, effectively superseding them in these specific areas.

key_sections.title: Power to issue directions.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue directions on policy matters to the Authority.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to supersede Authority.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to supersede the Authority under certain circumstances, such as inability to discharge functions or persistent default.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Authority to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules for its implementation.

key_sections.title: Overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent in any other law.

key_sections.title: Power to modify provisions of other enactments in relation to International Financial Services Centres.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to modify or exempt the application of provisions of other Central Acts, rules, or regulations to financial products, services, or institutions in IFSCs.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint Members, decide head office, approve offices, remove Members, make grants, issue directions to Authority, supersede Authority, make rules, modify provisions of other enactments, remove difficulties.

Authority: To enter into and execute contracts, acquire, hold and dispose of property, sue and be sued, appoint officers and employees, develop and regulate financial products, services and institutions, exercise powers of appropriate regulators in IFSCs, constitute Performance Review Committee, maintain website, make regulations, delegate powers.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act specifies that the procedures for prosecution of offences, adjudication of penalties, and recovery of fines and penalties, as laid down in the respective Acts specified in the First Schedule, shall apply mutatis mutandis to financial products, services, and institutions under this Act. Penalties, fines, fees, and settlement amounts are to be collected or realised in foreign currency equivalent.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government
regulatory_bodies: Securities and Exchange Board of India
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority

applies_to: International Financial Services Centres set up under section 18 of the Special Economic Zones Act, 2005
financial products, financial services and financial institutions in the International Financial Services Centres
exemptions: The Authority is exempt from income-tax or any other tax or duty with respect to its income, services or profits or gains.
special_provisions: Power to modify provisions of other enactments in relation to International Financial Services Centres.
Transactions in financial services in an International Financial Services Centre shall be in foreign currency.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Authority is responsible for developing and regulating the financial services market in IFSCs, exercising powers that would otherwise be held by other financial regulators. The Central Government has powers of direction and supersession over the Authority.

schedules_summary.description: Lists the 'Appropriate Regulators' (e.g., Reserve Bank of India, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA) and the specific Acts administered by each, indicating which regulatory powers are transferred to the International Financial Services Centres Authority within IFSCs.

Details amendments to various Central Acts (e.g., RBI Act, Insurance Act, Banking Regulation Act, SEBI Act) to clarify that the powers of the respective regulatory bodies under those Acts do not extend to International Financial Services Centres, where such powers are instead exercisable by the International Financial Services Centres Authority.

act_identification.act_title: THE TRANSGENDER PERSONS (PROTECTION OF RIGHTS) ACT, 2019
act_identification.act_short_title: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019

legislative_details.enacted_by: Parliament in the Seventieth Year of the Republic of India

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for protection of rights of transgender persons and their welfare and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to provide for the protection of rights of transgender persons and ensure their welfare. It addresses various matters connected with and incidental to the protection and welfare of transgender individuals.

chapter_titles: RECOGNITION OF IDENTITY OF TRANSGENDER PERSONS
OBLIGATION OF ESTABLISHMENTS AND OTHER PERSONS
EDUCATION, SOCIAL SECURITY AND HEALTH OF TRANSGENDER PERSONS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appropriate Government', 'establishment', 'inclusive education', and 'transgender person'.

key_sections.title: Prohibition against discrimination.
key_sections.description: Prohibits discrimination against transgender persons by any person or establishment on various grounds, including in education, employment, healthcare, and access to public services.

key_sections.title: Recognition of identity of transgender person.
key_sections.description: Establishes the right of a transgender person to be recognized as such and to have a self-perceived gender identity.

key_sections.title: Application for certificate of identity.
key_sections.description: Allows a transgender person to apply to the District Magistrate for a certificate of identity.

key_sections.title: Issue of certificate of identity.
key_sections.description: Mandates the District Magistrate to issue a certificate of identity as a transgender person and ensures its recording in official documents.

key_sections.title: Change in gender.
key_sections.description: Provides for the process of obtaining a revised certificate of identity if a transgender person undergoes surgery to change gender, and the right to change their first name in official documents.

key_sections.title: Obligation of appropriate Government.
key_sections.description: Requires the appropriate Government to take steps for the full and effective participation, inclusion, welfare, protection, and rehabilitation of transgender persons.

key_sections.title: Non-discrimination in employment.
key_sections.description: Prohibits discrimination against transgender persons in all matters related to employment, including recruitment and promotion.

key_sections.title: Right of residence.
key_sections.description: Ensures that no child is separated from their family on the ground of being transgender and guarantees transgender persons the right to reside in their household without discrimination.

key_sections.title: Obligation of educational institutions to provide inclusive education to transgender persons.
key_sections.description: Mandates educational institutions to provide inclusive education and opportunities for sports, recreation, and leisure activities to transgender persons without discrimination.

key_sections.title: Healthcare facilities.
key_sections.description: Requires the appropriate Government to take measures for healthcare, including setting up Sero-surveillance Centres, providing medical care for sex reassignment surgery and hormonal therapy, and ensuring insurance coverage.

key_sections.title: National Council for Transgender Persons.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a National Council for Transgender Persons by the Central Government to exercise powers and perform functions under the Act.

key_sections.title: Offences and penalties.
key_sections.description: Defines specific offences against transgender persons, such as forced labour, denial of public access, forced displacement, and various forms of abuse, and prescribes penalties.

key_sections.title: Power of appropriate Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the appropriate Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, covering various procedural and implementation aspects.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint commencement date
Central Government to constitute National Council for Transgender Persons
Central Government to make rules
Central Government to remove difficulties
Central Government to provide grants to the National Council
Appropriate Government to take welfare measures and formulate schemes
Appropriate Government to make rules
District Magistrate to issue certificate of identity
District Magistrate to issue revised certificate of identity
Competent court to order placement of transgender person in rehabilitation centre
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Whoever compels or entices a transgender person to indulge in forced/bonded labour, denies passage to a public place, forces them to leave their household, or harms/injures/endangers their life, safety, health, or well-being (including physical, sexual, verbal, emotional, and economic abuse) shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than six months but which may extend to two years and with fine.

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government has the power to nominate members to the National Council for Transgender Persons.

applies_to: transgender persons
establishments
educational institutions

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through prohibitions against discrimination, obligations on establishments and educational institutions, establishment of a grievance redressal mechanism, and provisions for offences and penalties. The National Council for Transgender Persons also monitors and evaluates policies and redresses grievances.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: competent court (for matters related to child separation/rehabilitation)

act_identification.act_title: THE DIRECT TAX VIVAD SE VISHWAS ACT, 2020
act_identification.act_short_title: Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas Act, 2020

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for resolution of disputed tax and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide a mechanism for the resolution of disputed direct tax cases. It aims to reduce pending litigation and provide an opportunity for taxpayers to settle their tax disputes by paying a specified amount.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act as 'The Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas Act, 2020'.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'appellant', 'disputed tax', 'designated authority', and 'tax arrear'.

key_sections.title: Amount payable by declarant.
key_sections.description: Specifies the amount payable by a declarant for tax arrear, based on the nature of the arrear and the date of payment, with various provisos for specific scenarios.

key_sections.title: Filing of declaration and particulars to be furnished.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for filing a declaration, the deemed withdrawal of pending appeals, and the requirement for the declarant to withdraw other proceedings and furnish an undertaking.

key_sections.title: Time and manner of payment.
key_sections.description: Details the process for the designated authority to determine the payable amount, issue a certificate, and the declarant's subsequent payment and intimation, making the order conclusive.

key_sections.title: Immunity from initiation of proceedings in respect of offence and imposition of penalty in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Grants immunity to the declarant from initiation of proceedings for an offence, imposition of penalty, or charging of interest under the Income-tax Act in respect of the tax arrear.

key_sections.title: No refund of amount paid.
key_sections.description: States that any amount paid under a declaration shall not be refundable, with an explanation clarifying refund of excess payment made before declaration.

key_sections.title: No benefit, concession or immunity to declarant.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not confer any general benefit, concession, or immunity on the declarant beyond what is expressly provided in sections 5(3) and 6.

key_sections.title: Act not to apply in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Lists specific cases where the provisions of this Act shall not apply, including certain tax arrears, persons with detention orders, or those prosecuted under specific serious laws.

key_sections.title: Power of Board to issue directions, etc.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Board of Direct Taxes to issue directions or orders to income-tax authorities, but not to dictate the disposal of a particular case.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to issue orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions, within a period of two years from its commencement.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, including prescribing forms and manners for declarations, undertakings, certificates, and payment intimations.

powers_conferred: Central Board of Direct Taxes to issue directions or orders to income-tax authorities (Section 10)
Central Government to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of this Act (Section 11)
Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act (Section 12)
Designated authority to determine the amount payable by the declarant and grant a certificate (Section 5)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act grants immunity from initiation of proceedings in respect of an offence, imposition or levy of any penalty, or charging of any interest under the Income-tax Act in respect of tax arrear (Section 6). However, the Act does not apply in cases where prosecution has already been instituted for certain serious offences under other Acts like the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, Prevention of Corruption Act, Prevention of Money Laundering Act, Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act, or the Indian Penal Code (Section 9).

related_acts: Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of Smuggling Activities Act, 1974 (52 of 1974)
Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (61 of 1985)
Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (15 of 2003)
Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act, 1988 (45 of 1988)
Special Court (Trial of Offences Relating to Transactions in Securities) Act, 1992 (27 of 1992)

applies_to: Persons who file a declaration under section 4 (declarants) for resolution of disputed tax.
exemptions: Tax arrear relating to an assessment based on search if the amount of disputed tax exceeds five crore rupees.
Tax arrear relating to an assessment year in respect of which prosecution has been instituted.
Tax arrear relating to any undisclosed income or asset located outside India.
Tax arrear relating to an assessment or reassessment made based on information received under international agreements (sections 90 or 90A of the Income-tax Act).
Any person in respect of whom an order of detention has been made under the Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of Smuggling Activities Act, 1974, under certain conditions.

Any person in respect of whom prosecution for offences under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, or the Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act, 1988, has been instituted or who has been convicted.
Any person in respect of whom prosecution has been initiated by an Income-tax authority for offences under the Indian Penal Code or for enforcement of civil liability, or who has been convicted.
Any person notified under section 3 of the Special Court (Trial of Offences Relating to Transactions in Securities) Act, 1992.
special_provisions: Specific calculation of amount payable (one-half) if an appeal or writ petition is filed by the income-tax authority on any issue.
Specific calculation of amount payable (one-half) if the appellant has a favorable decision from ITAT or High Court on an issue before Commissioner (Appeals) or Dispute Resolution Panel.
Specific calculation of amount payable (one-half) if the appellant has a favorable decision from High Court on an issue before Income Tax Appellate Tribunal.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Declarants file declarations with a designated authority. The designated authority determines the payable amount and issues a certificate. The declarant pays the amount and withdraws any pending appeals, writ petitions, or arbitration proceedings. The designated authority then passes an order confirming payment.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The Act refers to existing appellate forums such as the Supreme Court, High Court, Income Tax Appellate Tribunal, and Commissioner (Appeals) for pending disputes, but does not establish new courts.

act_identification.act_title: THE CENTRAL SANSKRIT UNIVERSITIES ACT, 2020

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Human Resource Development

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and incorporate Universities for teaching and research in Sanskrit, to develop all-inclusive Sanskrit promotional activities and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to establish and incorporate Central Universities dedicated to teaching and research in Sanskrit. Its primary objectives include promoting Sanskrit language and related branches of learning, fostering innovation in teaching and inter-disciplinary studies, and training manpower for the overall development, preservation, and research in Sanskrit and traditional Sanskrit subjects.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it will come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines various terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Academic Council', 'Campus', 'Chancellor', 'Vice-Chancellor', 'Executive Council', 'Sanskrit', 'Statutes', and 'Ordinances'.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Universities.
key_sections.description: Establishes three separate Central Universities: The Central Sanskrit University, Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University, and The National Sanskrit University, by converting existing deemed universities.

key_sections.title: Effect of establishment of University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the consequences of the establishment of the Universities, including the dissolution of previous societies, transfer of properties, rights, liabilities, and continuity of employment and affiliations.

key_sections.title: Objects of University.
key_sections.description: States the primary objectives of the University, which include disseminating and advancing knowledge in Sanskrit, promoting research, and providing integrated courses.

key_sections.title: Powers of University.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the various powers of the University, such as providing instruction, granting degrees, establishing teaching positions, conducting research, and cooperating with other institutions.

key_sections.title: University to be open to all caste, creed, race or class.
key_sections.description: Ensures that the University is open to all persons without discrimination based on caste, creed, race, or class, while allowing for special provisions for disadvantaged groups.

key_sections.title: Visitor of University.
key_sections.description: Designates the President of India as the Visitor of the University and details the Visitor's powers, including review, inspection, inquiry, and issuing directions.

key_sections.title: Officers of University.
key_sections.description: Lists the key officers of the University, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Deans, Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, and Librarian.

key_sections.title: Authorities of University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities of the University, such as the Court, Executive Council, Academic Council, Board of Studies, Finance Committee, and Planning and Monitoring Board.

key_sections.title: Power to make Statutes.
key_sections.description: Grants the power to make Statutes for various matters, including the constitution and functions of authorities, appointment and conditions of service of employees, and management of colleges.

key_sections.title: Power to make Ordinances.
key_sections.description: Grants the power to make Ordinances for matters such as student admission, courses of study, examinations, fees, and conditions of residence.

key_sections.title: Conditions of service of employees, etc.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that employees shall be appointed under a written contract and provides for a Tribunal of Arbitration to resolve disputes between the University and its employees.

key_sections.title: Procedure of appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases against students.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for appeal and arbitration in disciplinary cases involving students, allowing appeals to the Executive Council and referral to a Tribunal of Arbitration.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to make provisions to remove any difficulties in implementing the Act, within three years of its commencement.

powers_conferred: University: To provide for instructions in various branches of learning including Sanskrit, grant diplomas/certificates/degrees, organize extramural studies, confer honorary degrees, provide distance education, establish teaching positions, recognize institutions, cooperate with other universities, establish colleges/centers, award fellowships, conduct research and consultancy, organize refresher courses, appoint visiting faculty, confer autonomous status, determine admission standards, demand fees, supervise residences, lay down service conditions, regulate discipline, make special arrangements for women/persons with disabilities, accept benefactions/donations, acquire/manage/dispose of property, borrow money, establish new campuses in India and abroad.

Visitor (President of India): To appoint persons to review work and progress, cause inspection/inquiry, issue directions, annul proceedings not in conformity with the Act/Statutes/Ordinances, appoint Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor.

Central Government: To appoint the date of commencement of the Act, approve disposal of University property, approve borrowing by the University, permit establishment of off-shore campuses, nominate members to the first Court, nominate members to Selection Committees, and make provisions to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.

Executive Council: To make/amend/repeal Statutes, manage and administer University revenues and property, create teaching and administrative posts, appoint staff, grant leave of absence to officers (other than Chancellor/Vice-Chancellor), regulate employee discipline, manage finances/accounts/investments, fix expenditure limits, invest University money, transfer property, provide infrastructure, enter into contracts, redress grievances of employees/students, appoint examiners/moderators, select common seal, make special arrangements for women students, institute awards, appoint visiting faculty, approve award of degrees/diplomas, raise/borrow money, enter into partnerships with industry.

Vice-Chancellor: To exercise general supervision and control over University affairs, take immediate action on matters, review decisions of authorities, make the first Ordinances, appoint Deans of Schools of Studies, appoint Director of Campus, appoint temporary staff, and maintain discipline in the University.

Academic Council: To coordinate and supervise academic policies, promote inter-School coordination, consider academic matters, frame Regulations and rules for academic functioning, prescribe courses of study, and make recommendations to the Executive Council on academic standards and institution of awards.

Registrar: To enter into agreements, sign documents, authenticate records, take disciplinary action against non-academic staff, act as custodian of records, issue notices for meetings, keep minutes, conduct official correspondence, supply information to the Visitor, and represent the University in legal proceedings.

Finance Officer: To exercise general supervision over University funds, advise on financial policy, manage property and investments, ensure expenditure limits are not exceeded, prepare annual accounts and budget, monitor cash/bank balances, watch revenue collection, maintain asset registers, report financial irregularities, and call for information from departments.
Controller of Examinations: To arrange for and superintend the examinations of the University.
Authorities of the University: To make Regulations for the conduct of their own business and that of their committees.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act provides for disciplinary action against employees for misconduct, including suspension and removal from service, with provisions for notice or payment in lieu. For students, disciplinary actions can include removal from rolls, debarment from examinations for a specified period, fines, or withholding/cancellation of examination results. Disputes arising from disciplinary actions against employees or students can be referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration.

authorities_established: Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Visitor appoints the Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor. The Executive Council appoints the Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, Librarian, Professors, Associate Professors, Assistant Professors, other academic staff, administrative/ministerial/other posts, and the Proctor. The Vice-Chancellor appoints Deans of Schools of Studies, Director of Campus, and temporary staff.

applies_to: All persons of either sex and whatever caste, creed, race or class
Employees of the University
Students of the University
Colleges, Institutions, Schools of Studies, and Departments affiliated to, or admitted to the privileges of, or maintained by, the University
special_provisions: Special provisions for the employment or admission of women, persons with disabilities, weaker sections of the society, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, other socially and educationally backward classes of citizens, economically weaker section of the unreserved class, and other special categories as stipulated by the Central Government.
Transitional provisions for existing officers, employees, and students of the deemed to be Universities upon the commencement of this Act.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Visitor, Executive Council, Academic Council, Vice-Chancellor, and other authorities of the University are empowered to make Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations. The Visitor has the power to assent to, withhold assent from, or remit Statutes for reconsideration, and can also make or amend Statutes directly under certain conditions. The Executive Council can amend, repeal, or add to Ordinances, and the Academic Council proposes Ordinances. All Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations must be published in the Official Gazette and laid before Parliament.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is primarily through the Visitor's powers of review, inspection, inquiry, and issuing binding directions, as well as the Vice-Chancellor's general supervision and disciplinary authority. The Executive Council manages and administers the University's affairs. Disputes concerning employees and students are resolved through a Tribunal of Arbitration. The Act also mandates the publication of rules and their submission to Parliament for oversight.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: A Tribunal of Arbitration is established for disputes between the University and its employees or students. While civil courts are generally barred from hearing matters decided by the Tribunal, employees retain the right to avail judicial remedies under Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution (Supreme Court and High Courts).

schedules_summary.description: Lists the names of States and their corresponding Campuses that will be part of the Central Sanskrit University.

Contains the Statutes of the University, detailing the constitution, powers, and duties of various officers and authorities like the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, Librarian, Executive Council, Academic Council, Planning and Monitoring Board, Schools of Studies, Departments, Board of Studies, Finance Committee, and Selection Committees, as well as provisions for terms of service, discipline, honorary degrees, and other administrative matters.

act_identification.act_title: THE MARINE AIDS TO NAVIGATION ACT, 2021
act_identification.act_short_title: The Marine Aids to Navigation Act, 2021

legislative_details.geographical_extent: whole of India including the maritime zones of India as specified in the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976 (80 of 1976).

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the development, maintenance and management of aids to navigation in India; for training and certification of operator of aids to navigation, development of its historical, educational and cultural value; to ensure compliance with the obligation under the maritime treaties and international instruments to which India is a party and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS India is signatory to maritime treaties and international instruments such as International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea, 1974, as amended; and International Association of Marine Aids and Lighthouse Authorities Maritime Buoyage System; AND WHEREAS it is considered necessary to give effect to the said treaties and instruments which, _inter alia, provide for aids to navigation, vessel traffic services and marking of wrecks;_ AND WHEREAS it is necessary to provide for and create a framework for the development, maintenance and management of vessel traffic services in India; training and certification of operators of aids to navigation; and the development of the historical educational and cultural value of aids to navigation; AND WHEREAS it is further necessary to create a framework for the levy and collection of marine aids to navigation dues to discharge the sovereign functions of development, maintenance and management of aids to navigation and vessel traffic services in India by Government, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to provide for the development, maintenance, and management of marine aids to navigation and vessel traffic services in India. It also establishes a framework for training and certification of operators, development of heritage lighthouses, and the levy and collection of marine aids to navigation dues to fulfill India's international maritime obligations.

act_identification.act_short_title: The National Commission for Homoeopathy Act, 2020

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of AYUSH

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for a medical education system that improves access to quality and affordable medical education, ensures availability of adequate and high quality Homoeopathy medical professionals in all parts of the country; that promotes equitable and universal healthcare that encourages community health perspective and makes services of Homoeopathy medical professionals accessible and affordable to all the citizens; that promotes national health goals; that encourages Homoeopathy medical professionals to adopt latest medical research in their work and to contribute to research; that has an objective periodic and transparent assessment of medical institutions and facilitates maintenance of a Homoeopathy medical register for India and enforces high ethical standards in all aspects of medical services; that is flexible to adapt to the changing needs and has an effective grievance redressal mechanism and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes a comprehensive medical education system for Homoeopathy in India. Its main objectives are to ensure quality and affordable education, adequate availability of Homoeopathy medical professionals, equitable healthcare access, and high ethical standards. It also aims to promote research and maintain a robust registration mechanism for practitioners.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To constitute Commission, appoint Chairperson/Members, give directions to Commission/Boards, give directions to State Governments, supersede Commission, make rules, remove difficulties.

Commission: To lay down policies for education, institutions, professionals; assess healthcare requirements; frame guidelines; exercise appellate jurisdiction; conduct National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test, National Exit Test, Post-Graduate National Entrance Test, National Teachers’ Eligibility Test; make regulations.

Homoeopathy Education Board: To determine standards of education, develop curriculum, frame guidelines for institutions, determine minimum requirements for courses/exams, grant recognition to medical qualifications.
Board of Ethics and Registration for Homoeopathy: To maintain National Register, regulate professional conduct, promote medical ethics, exercise appellate jurisdiction.

Medical Assessment and Rating Board for Homoeopathy: To determine assessment/rating process, grant permission for new institutions/courses/seats, carry out inspections, assess/rate institutions, take measures against non-compliant institutions.
State Medical Councils: To take disciplinary actions.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who practices Homoeopathy without being enrolled in the State Register or National Register, or contravenes other provisions of Section 34, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to five lakh rupees, or with both.

Board of Ethics and Registration for Homoeopathy
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson and President of Autonomous Boards based on recommendations from a Search Committee. The Central Government also appoints ex officio and part-time Members of the Commission, and the Secretary. The Search Committee recommends panels for these appointments.
regulatory_bodies: Medical Assessment and Rating Board for Homoeopathy
Board of Ethics and Registration for Homoeopathy

applies_to: Whole of India
Medical institutions governed under this Act
Persons with recognised medical qualification in Homoeopathy
Practitioners of Homoeopathy
exemptions: Teachers appointed prior to the notified date for National Teachers’ Eligibility Test.
Persons enrolled on a State Register as practitioner of Homoeopathy who do not possess a recognised medical qualification as on the commencement date of this Act.
Persons who have been practicing Homoeopathy for not less than five years in a State where a State Register of Homoeopathy is not maintained as on the commencement date of this Act.
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act to come into force.
Criteria for approving or disapproving schemes for medical institutions may be relaxed for institutions set up in specified areas with prior Central Government approval.
Students studying for a degree or diploma in any medical institution before the commencement of this Act shall continue their studies and be awarded degrees/diplomas under this Act.
Medical institutions whose recognition has lapsed must continue to maintain minimum standards until all candidates complete their study.
Foreign citizens may be permitted temporary registration in India for a specified period and manner.

The Central Government may, by notification, direct that certain Homoeopathy qualifications granted by medical institutions outside India shall be recognized, subject to conditions including qualifying the National Exit Test.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through notifications by the Central Government, regulations made by the Commission, and guidelines framed by the Commission. It includes provisions for appeals against decisions of Autonomous Boards and the Commission. The Medical Assessment and Rating Board conducts inspections and takes measures against non-compliant institutions. Penalties are prescribed for contraventions. The Central Government can issue directions to the Commission, Autonomous Boards, and State Governments.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No Court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under this Act except upon a complaint in writing made by an officer authorised by the Commission, the Ethics and Registration Board, or a State Medical Council.

act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to establish a comprehensive medical education system for the Indian System of Medicine. It focuses on ensuring quality and affordable education, producing skilled professionals, promoting equitable healthcare, and maintaining high ethical standards. act_identification.act_title: THE JAMMU AND KASHMIR OFFICIAL LANGUAGES ACT, 2020
act_identification.act_short_title: THE JAMMU AND KASHMIR OFFICIAL LANGUAGES ACT, 2020

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir

An Act to provide for the languages to be used for the official purposes of the Union
territory of Jammu and Kashmir and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the designation of Kashmiri, Dogri, Urdu, Hindi, and English as official languages for the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir. It also mandates steps for the promotion and development of regional languages like Gojri, Pahari, and Punjabi.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Administrator' and 'Union territory'.

key_sections.title: Official languages of Union territory.

key_sections.title: Promotion and development of regional languages.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Administrator to take steps for the promotion and development of regional languages, specifically mentioning Gojri, Pahari, and Punjabi.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint the date of commencement of the Act.
Administrator to appoint different dates for different areas for commencement of the Act.
Administrator to appoint the date from which specified languages become official languages.
Administrator to take necessary steps for the promotion and development of regional languages.
