act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL FORENSIC SCIENCES UNIVERSITY ACT, 2020
act_identification.act_short_title: The National Forensic Sciences University Act, 2020

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish and declare an institution to be known as the National Forensic Sciences University as an institution of national importance to facilitate and promote studies and research and to achieve excellence in the field of forensic science in conjunction with applied behavioural science studies, law, criminology and other allied areas and technology and other related fields, and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act establishes the National Forensic Sciences University as an institution of national importance. Its main purpose is to promote studies, research, and excellence in forensic science, applied behavioural science, law, criminology, and related fields. It aims to strengthen criminal justice institutions and provide advanced education and training in these areas.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Declaration of National Forensic Sciences University as an institution of national importance.
key_sections.description: Declares the National Forensic Sciences University as an institution of national importance due to its objects.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of University.
key_sections.description: Establishes the National Forensic Sciences University by incorporating the Gujarat Forensic Sciences University and the Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Narayan National Institute of Criminology and Forensic Sciences, making it a body corporate.

key_sections.title: Objects of University.
key_sections.description: Outlines the primary objectives of the University, including promoting academic learning, research, skill development in forensic science, and strengthening criminal justice institutions.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of University.
key_sections.description: Details the various powers and functions of the University, such as providing studies, granting degrees, conducting research, establishing campuses, and managing its affairs.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of University.
key_sections.description: States that the University's jurisdiction extends to the whole of India.

key_sections.title: University to be open to all races, creeds and classes.
key_sections.description: Ensures that the University is open to all persons irrespective of gender, race, caste, creed, disability, domicile, ethnicity, social or economic background, and includes provisions for reservation.

key_sections.title: Authorities of University.
key_sections.description: Lists the main authorities of the University, including the Chancellor, Court, Board of Governors, Academic Council, Board for Affiliation and Recognition, and Finance Committee.

key_sections.title: Powers of Board of Governors.
key_sections.description: Defines the general superintendence, direction, and control powers of the Board of Governors over the University's affairs, including making Statutes and creating posts.

key_sections.title: Powers of Vice Chancellor.
key_sections.description: Describes the powers of the Vice-Chancellor as the principal academic and executive officer, including causing inspections, presiding over meetings, and financial powers.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Mandates the University to maintain proper accounts and specifies that its accounts shall be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

key_sections.title: Statutes.
key_sections.description: Outlines the matters for which Statutes may provide, such as the constitution of authorities, appointment of officers, and conditions of service.

key_sections.title: Tribunal of Arbitration.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Tribunal of Arbitration for resolving disputes arising from contracts between the University and its employees.

key_sections.title: Repeal of Gujarat Act 17 of 2008.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Gujarat Forensic Sciences University Act, 2008, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under the repealed Act.

powers_conferred: University: To provide for studies, training, skill-development, research and extension work in forensic science and allied areas.
University: To establish and maintain campuses, colleges, institutions, schools, departments, laboratories, libraries, and research centres.
University: To plan and prescribe courses of study, hold examinations, and grant degrees, diplomas, and certificates.
University: To confer honorary degrees and withdraw academic distinctions for good cause.
University: To provide facilities through distance education and introduce semester system, continuous evaluation, and choice-based credit system.
University: To make provisions for research and advisory services and enter into arrangements with other institutions.
University: To receive grants-in-aid and undertake projects for Central and State Governments.
University: To determine and receive fees and other charges for instruction and services.
University: To establish, maintain, and manage University buildings, halls, hostels, and other campuses.

University: To create academic and other teaching posts and make appointments thereto (except Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor).
University: To appoint visiting professors, emeritus professors, consultants, and scholars.
University: To create non-teaching, administrative, ministerial, and other posts and make appointments thereto.

University: To initiate measures to enlist industry cooperation.
University: To establish off-shore campuses.
University: To provide for printing, reproduction, and publication of research.
University: To provide, control, and maintain discipline among students and employees, and lay down conditions of service.
University: To conduct innovative experiments and develop new methods and technologies for criminal justice systems.
University: To admit students on an all-India basis and foreign students.
University: To purchase or lease land or buildings and construct, alter, and maintain them.
University: To raise and borrow moneys on bonds, mortgages, promissory notes, or other obligations.
University: To invest the funds of the University.
Board of Governors: General superintendence, direction, and control of University affairs.
Board of Governors: To take decisions on policy relating to administration and working of the University.
Board of Governors: To institute courses of study.
Board of Governors: To make, modify, or cancel Statutes.
Board of Governors: To create posts and appoint persons to academic and other posts, and determine salary structure and terms.
Board of Governors: To consider and pass resolutions on annual reports, accounts, and budget estimates.

Board of Governors: To delegate any of its power to officers or authorities.

Vice-Chancellor: To have all financial powers of the Secretary to the Government of India.

Central Government: To appoint the Chancellor.
Central Government: To appoint the Vice-Chancellor.

Central Government: To issue directions on questions of policy to the University.
Central Government: To remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

related_acts: Gujarat Forensic Sciences University Act, 2008 (Gujrat Act 17 of 2018)
Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 (5 of 2007)

The Board of Governors appoints academic staff (Assistant Professor or above) and non-academic staff (equivalent to Group ‘A’ and above). The Vice-Chancellor appoints Campus Directors (with Board approval), Deans, and other employees. The University appoints the Executive Registrar and Finance Officer.

All persons irrespective of gender, race, caste, creed, disability, domicile, ethnicity, social or economic background
Students of the University and its affiliated colleges

Existing employees and students of the Gujarat Forensic Sciences University and Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Narayan National Institute of Criminology and Forensic Sciences have transitional provisions for their service and academic continuity.

Disputes between the University and employees or students are referred to a Tribunal of Arbitration. The Central Government can issue directions on policy matters.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Tribunal of Arbitration (for specific disputes), with judicial remedies available under Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution (Supreme Court and High Courts).

act_identification.act_title: THE BILATERAL NETTING OF QUALIFIED FINANCIAL CONTRACTS ACT, 2020
act_identification.act_short_title: The Bilateral Netting of Qualified Financial Contracts Act, 2020

act_overview.preamble: An Act to ensure financial stability and promote competitiveness in Indian financial markets by providing enforceability of bilateral netting of qualified financial contracts and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to enhance financial stability and foster competitiveness within Indian financial markets. Its primary objective is to ensure the enforceability of bilateral netting for qualified financial contracts, along with addressing related and incidental matters.

chapter_titles: LIMITATIONS ON POWERS OF ADMINISTRATION PRACTITIONER

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as "administration", "close-out netting", "qualified financial contract", and "qualified financial market participant".

key_sections.title: Applicability of Act.
key_sections.description: States that the Act applies to qualified financial contracts entered into bilaterally between qualified financial market participants, where at least one is regulated by an authority specified in the First Schedule.

key_sections.title: Powers of authority.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to the relevant authority to designate bilateral agreements as qualified financial contracts and specify entities as qualified financial market participants.

key_sections.title: Enforceability of netting.
key_sections.description: Declares that netting of qualified financial contracts is enforceable, either under a netting agreement or as per Section 6, and is binding against insolvent parties.

key_sections.title: Invocation of close-out netting.
key_sections.description: Describes how close-out netting may be commenced upon an event of default or termination event, and how obligations are reduced to a single net amount.

key_sections.title: Net amount.
key_sections.description: Specifies that the net amount is determined by the netting agreement, or through arbitration if no agreement exists.

key_sections.title: Limitations on powers of administration practitioner.
key_sections.description: Restricts administration practitioners from rendering ineffective certain transfers, substitutions, or payment obligations under a netting agreement.

key_sections.title: Power to amend Schedules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to amend the First and Second Schedules by notification.

key_sections.title: Provisions of this Act to override other laws.
key_sections.description: States that the Act's provisions override inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act for a period of three years from commencement.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint commencement date (Section 1(2))
Central Government: To specify parties/terms for non-qualified contracts (Section 4(a)(i))
Central Government: To amend Schedules (Section 9)
Central Government: To remove difficulties (Section 11)
Authority: To designate qualified financial contracts (Section 4(a))
Authority: To specify qualified financial market participants (Section 4(b))
Reserve Bank of India: To specify other banks as banking institutions (Section 2(d)(ii))

related_acts: Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980
Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 2013
International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019

regulatory_bodies: Securities and Exchange Board of India
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority

applies_to: Qualified financial contracts entered into on a bilateral basis between qualified financial market participants, where at least one of such participants shall be an entity regulated by an authority specified in the First Schedule.
exemptions: Contracts entered into between such parties and on such terms as the Central Government may, by notification, specify.
Contracts entered into on multilateral basis in accordance with the provisions of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 and the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Netting of qualified financial contracts is enforceable in accordance with the terms of the netting agreement or the provisions of Section 6. Close-out netting is applicable and binding, even against an insolvent party, and is not affected by stays, injunctions, or other orders. If parties fail to agree on the net amount without a netting agreement, it shall be determined through arbitration.

schedules_summary.description: Lists the regulatory authorities that are considered 'authority' under the Act and whose regulated entities can be qualified financial market participants.
Lists various enactments whose provisions are overridden by this Act in matters of close-out netting for qualified financial market participants.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend and consolidate the laws relating to social security with the goal to extend social security to all employees and workers either in the organised or unorganised or any other sectors and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

chapter_titles: SOCIAL SECURITY AND CESS IN RESPECT OF BUILDING AND OTHER CONSTRUCTION WORKERS
SOCIAL SECURITY FOR UNORGANISED WORKERS, GIG WORKERS AND PLANTFORM WORKERS

key_sections.title: Short title extent, commencement and application.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Code, such as 'employee', 'employer', 'gig worker', 'platform worker', 'social security', and 'wages'.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Board of Trustees of Employees’ Provident Fund.
key_sections.description: Details the constitution, powers, and functions of the Central Board of Trustees for the Employees' Provident Fund, including its composition and corporate status.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Employees’ State Insurance Corporation.

key_sections.title: National Social Security Board and State Unorganised Workers’ Board.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of National and State Social Security Boards for unorganised workers, specifying their composition, functions, and term of office.

key_sections.title: Schemes.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to frame and modify schemes for Employees' Provident Fund, Pension, and Deposit Linked Insurance, and other social security benefits for various workers.

key_sections.title: All employees to be insured.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that every employee in an applicable establishment shall be insured under Chapter IV, defining an 'Insured Person' as one for whom contributions are payable.

key_sections.title: Benefits.
key_sections.description: Enumerates the benefits available to Insured Persons and their dependants under Chapter IV, including sickness, maternity, disablement, dependants' benefits, medical treatment, and funeral expenses.

key_sections.title: Payment of gratuity.
key_sections.description: Establishes the conditions for payment of gratuity to an employee upon termination of employment, including eligibility criteria, calculation methods, and forfeiture conditions.

key_sections.title: Right to payment of maternity benefit.
key_sections.description: Grants women employees the right to maternity benefit, specifying the rate, eligibility period, maximum duration, and special provisions for adoption and commissioning mothers.

key_sections.title: Employer’s liability for compensation.
key_sections.description: Defines an employer's liability to pay compensation for personal injury or occupational disease arising out of and in the course of employment, with specific exceptions.

key_sections.title: Levy and collection of cess.
key_sections.description: Provides for the levy and collection of a cess on the cost of construction for the social security and welfare of building workers, specifying rates and collection methods.

key_sections.title: Framing of schemes for unorganised workers.
key_sections.description: Empowers Central and State Governments to frame welfare schemes for unorganised workers covering various benefits like life, disability, health, maternity, and old age protection, and outlines funding mechanisms.

key_sections.title: Schemes for gig works and platform workers.
key_sections.description: Authorises the Central Government to frame social security schemes for gig workers and platform workers, detailing potential benefits, administration, funding sources, and the role of aggregators.

key_sections.title: Application of Aadhaar.
key_sections.description: Mandates the use of Aadhaar number for establishing identity for registration, seeking benefits, availing career centre services, or receiving payments under the Code.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals several existing enactments related to social security and includes savings provisions for actions taken under those repealed laws and for the continuation of certain schemes and exemptions.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint commencement date (S.1(3)), notify establishments (S.1(6)), appoint Central Provident Fund Commissioner (S.14(1)), frame schemes (S.15), establish funds (S.16), appoint Director General of Corporation (S.24(1)), frame schemes for other beneficiaries (S.44), frame schemes for unorganised/gig/platform workers (S.45, S.109, S.114), amend schedules (S.152(1)), make rules (S.155), give directions (S.149), remove difficulties (S.163).
Appropriate Government: To appoint competent authority (S.58, S.91), exempt establishments (S.46, S.143), make rules (S.154), delegate powers (S.162).

State Government: To constitute Employees' Insurance Court (S.48), constitute State Unorganised Workers' Board (S.6(9)), constitute State Building Workers' Welfare Boards (S.7(1)), amend schedules (S.152(2)), make rules (S.156).
Corporation: To promote measures for health (S.33), make regulations (S.157).
Inspector-cum-Facilitator: To advise employers/employees, inspect establishments, examine persons, require documents, search/seize, bring defects to notice (S.122(5), (6)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Section 133 prescribes penalties for various failures, including failure to pay contributions (imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine up to 1 lakh rupees, depending on the nature of default), failure to pay gratuity (imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to 50,000 rupees, or both), and other contraventions (imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to 50,000 rupees, or both, or fine up to 50,000 rupees). Section 134 provides for enhanced punishment for repeat offenders, with imprisonment up to 2 years and fine of 2 lakh rupees, or up to 3 years and fine of 3 lakh rupees for certain payment defaults.

amended_acts: The Act is to amend and consolidate the laws relating to social security, implying amendments to various existing social security laws.
repealed_acts: The Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 (8 of 1923)
The Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 (34 of 1948)
The Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (19 of 1952)
The Employment Exchanges (Compulsory Notification of Vacancies) Act, 1959 (31 of 1959)
The Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 (53 of 1961)
The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 (39 of 1972)
The Cine-Workers Welfare Fund Act, 1981 (33 of 1981)
The Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Cess Act, 1996 (28 of 1996)
The Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008 (33 of 2008)
related_acts: Metro Railways (Operation and Maintenance) Act, 2002 (60 of 2002)
Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971 (34 of 1971)
Sales Promotion Employees (Conditions of Service) Act, 1976 (11 of 1976)
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999 (41 of 1999)
Aadhaar (The Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016 (18 of 2016)
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 (5 of 1970)

authorities_established: Board of Trustees of Employees’ Provident Fund (Central Board)
National Social Security Board for Unorganised Workers
State Unorganised Workers’ Social Security Board
important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and members of the Central Board and ESI Corporation, Director General and Financial Commissioner of the Corporation, and Central Provident Fund Commissioner. Central Board appoints Additional/Deputy/Regional/Assistant Provident Fund Commissioners and other officers/employees. Corporation appoints other officers and employees. State Government appoints Judges of Employees' Insurance Court, Chairperson and members of Building Workers' Welfare Board, and Secretary and other officers/employees of the Building Workers' Welfare Board.
regulatory_bodies: Board of Trustees of Employees’ Provident Fund (Central Board)
National Social Security Board for Unorganised Workers
State Unorganised Workers’ Social Security Board

applies_to: Chapter III (Employees' Provident Fund): Every establishment in which twenty or more employees are employed.

Chapter IV (Employees’ State Insurance Corporation): Every establishment in which ten or more persons are employed (other than a seasonal factory); establishments with hazardous occupations (even single employee); plantations (optional, if benefits are better).

Chapter V (Gratuity): Every factory, mine, oilfield, plantation, port and railway company; every shop or establishment in which ten or more employees are employed, or were employed, on any day of the preceding twelve months; and such other shops or establishments as may be notified by the appropriate Government.

Chapter VI (Maternity Benefit): Every establishment being a factory, mine or plantation (including Government establishments); every shop or establishment in which ten or more employees are employed, or were employed, on any day of the preceding twelve months; and such other shops or establishments notified by the appropriate Government.
Chapter VII (Employee's Compensation): Employers and employees to whom Chapter IV does not apply, subject to the provisions of the Second Schedule.
Chapter VIII (Social Security and Cess in respect of Building and Other Construction Workers): Every establishment which falls under the building and other construction work.
Chapter IX (Social Security for Unorganised Workers, Gig Workers and Platform Workers): Unorganised sector, unorganised workers, gig workers, platform workers.
Chapter XIII (Employment Information and Monitoring): Career centres, vacancies, persons seeking services of career centres and employers.
exemptions: Chapter III: Establishments registered under Co-operative Societies Act, 1912, employing less than fifty persons and working without aid of power; Government/State Government establishments with similar provident fund/pension benefits; establishments under other laws with similar benefits; employees already receiving PF benefits under other Central/State enactments (S.20). Central Government may exempt classes of establishments (S.20(2)).
Chapter IV: Government or local authority factories/establishments if employees receive substantially similar or superior benefits (S.46).
General: Appropriate Government may grant exemption to an establishment or class of establishments or employees from any or all provisions of the Code or schemes, subject to conditions (S.143).
special_provisions: Opt-in/opt-out for Chapter III and IV applicability by agreement between employer and majority of employees (S.1(5), S.1(7)).
Continued applicability of Chapters even if employee count falls below threshold (S.1(8)).
Special provisions for accidents occurring outside Indian territory for masters of ships, seamen, crew of aircraft, and persons working abroad (S.83).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Appropriate Government (S.154), Central Government (S.155), State Government (S.156), and Employees' State Insurance Corporation (S.157).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Code is enforced through various Social Security Organisations (Central Board, ESI Corporation, National/State Social Security Boards, Building Workers' Welfare Boards). Inspector-cum-Facilitators are appointed to advise, inspect, and ensure compliance (S.122). Dues from employers are assessed and determined by Authorised Officers (S.125) and recovered by Recovery Officers (S.129-132). Offences and penalties are prescribed in Chapter XII, with provisions for prosecution and compounding of offences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Tribunal (for appeals related to Chapter III - S.23), Employees' Insurance Court (for disputes related to Chapter IV - S.48, S.49), High Court (for appeals from Employees' Insurance Court and competent authority - S.52, S.99), and Competent Authority (for disputes related to Gratuity and Employee's Compensation - S.56, S.58, S.90, S.91).

schedules_summary.description: Specifies the applicability of various Chapters (III, IV, V, VI, VII, VIII, IX, XIII) of the Code to different types of establishments and workers based on employee numbers or nature of work.

Lists specific categories of persons who are considered 'employees' for the purposes of Chapter VII (Employee's Compensation), covering various occupations in railways, factories, mines, shipping, construction, and other sectors.
Provides a list of occupational diseases, categorized into Part A, Part B, and Part C, along with the corresponding employments where there is a particular risk of contracting such diseases.
Lists injuries deemed to result in Permanent Total Disablement (Part I) and Permanent Partial Disablement (Part II), specifying the percentage of loss of earning capacity for each injury.
Details the matters that may be provided for in the Employees' Provident Fund Scheme (Part A), the Employees' Pension Scheme (Part B), and the Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme (Part C).
Contains a table of 'Factors' used for working out the lump sum equivalent of compensation amounts in cases of permanent disablement and death, based on the employee's age.

Classifies different types of aggregators, such as ride-sharing services, food and grocery delivery services, logistics services, e-marketplaces, professional services, healthcare, travel and hospitality, and content and media services.

act_identification.act_title: THE MAJOR PORT AUTHORITIES ACT, 2021

legislative_details.geographical_extent: Major Ports of Chennai, Cochin, Deendayal (Kandla), Jawaharlal Nehru (Nhava Sheva), Kolkata, Mormugao, Mumbai, New Mangalore, Paradip, V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin) and Visakhapatnam

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for regulation, operation and planning of Major Ports in India and to vest the administration, control and management of such ports upon the Boards of Major Port Authorities and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the regulation, operation, and planning of Major Ports across India. Its primary objective is to vest the administration, control, and management of these ports in newly constituted Boards of Major Port Authorities, along with addressing related and incidental matters.

key_definitions: Major Port or Major Port Authority

key_sections.title: Short title, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: Short title, commencement and application of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines various terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Constitution and composition of Board of Major Port Authority.
key_sections.description: Establishes the constitution and composition of the Board of Major Port Authority for each Major Port.

key_sections.title: Board to be deemed as successor of Board of Trustees of Major Port.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the new Board is the successor to the erstwhile Board of Trustees, inheriting assets and liabilities.

key_sections.title: Master Plan.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Board to create a Master Plan for development within port limits, superseding local regulations.

key_sections.title: Powers of Board in respect of planning and development.
key_sections.description: Outlines the Board's powers regarding planning and development, including undertaking works, providing services, and developing infrastructure.

key_sections.title: Scale of rates for assets and services available at Major Port.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Board to frame scales of rates and conditions for services and usage of port assets.

key_sections.title: Power to raise loans and issue securities.
key_sections.description: Grants the Board power to raise loans and issue securities for capital expenditure and working capital.

key_sections.title: Accounts and audit.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Board to prepare budgets, maintain accounts, and undergo audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to take over management of Board.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to take over the management of a Board under specific circumstances like inability to perform duties or persistent defaults.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Adjudicatory Board.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of an Adjudicatory Board to exercise specific jurisdiction, powers, and authority.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Adjudicatory Board.
key_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the Adjudicatory Board, including dispute resolution and review of PPP projects.

key_sections.title: Bar of jurisdiction of any court.
key_sections.description: Bars the jurisdiction of other courts for matters falling within the Adjudicatory Board's scope, with an exception for arbitration.

key_sections.title: General provision for punishment of offences.
key_sections.description: Establishes general punishment for offences, prescribing a fine for contravention of the Act, rules, or regulations.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963, and includes savings clauses for actions taken under the repealed Act.

powers_conferred: Board of Major Port Authority: To acquire, hold or dispose of property, both movable and immovable, and to contract (Section 3(2)).
Board of Major Port Authority: To make appointments (Section 18).
Board of Major Port Authority: To use its property, assets and funds (Section 22(1)).
Board of Major Port Authority: To erect, construct or build civil structures for port development (Section 22(3)).
Board of Major Port Authority: To declare availability and readiness of port assets (Section 22(4)).
Board of Major Port Authority: To enter into and perform contracts (Section 24(1)).
Board of Major Port Authority: To create specific master plan (Section 25).
Board of Major Port Authority: To make regulations for planning and development (Section 26(1)).
Board of Major Port Authority: To frame scale of rates and conditions for services and port assets (Section 27(1)).
Board of Major Port Authority: To raise loans and issue securities (Section 33(1)).
Board of Major Port Authority: To repay loans to Government before due date (Section 39).
Board of Major Port Authority: To establish and apply sinking fund (Section 40).
Board of Major Port Authority: To make regulations (Section 72).
Central Government: To appoint Chairperson, Deputy Chairperson, and Members of the Board (Section 4(1), 4(2), 4(3)).
Central Government: To remove Chairperson, Deputy Chairperson and Members (Section 9).
Central Government: To fix amount for pay scale for certain posts (Section 18(1)(a)(iii)).
Central Government: To specify posts regarded as Head of Department (Section 18(2)).
Central Government: To order survey or examination of works of Board (Section 46).
Central Government: To restore or complete works at cost of Board (Section 47).
Central Government: To take over management of Board (Section 48).
Central Government: To exempt from obligation to use port assets (Section 50).
Central Government: To issue directions to the Board (Section 53).
Central Government: To constitute Adjudicatory Board (Section 54).
Central Government: To appoint Presiding Officer and members of Adjudicatory Board (Section 55).
Central Government: To remove and suspend Presiding Officer and members of Adjudicatory Board (Section 57).
Central Government: To make rules (Section 71).
Central Government: To remove difficulties (Section 74).
Adjudicatory Board: To perform functions related to erstwhile Tariff Authority for Major Ports (Section 58(1)(a)).
Adjudicatory Board: To receive and adjudicate disputes, differences, or claims (Section 58(1)(b)).
Adjudicatory Board: To appraise, review stressed Public Private Partnership projects (Section 58(1)(c)).
Adjudicatory Board: To look into complaints from port users (Section 58(1)(d)).
Adjudicatory Board: To look into other matters referred by Central Government or Board (Section 58(1)(e)).
Adjudicatory Board: To have powers of a civil court (Section 58(3)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person who contravenes any of the provisions of this Act or any rule, regulation or order made thereunder, shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees (Section 62). Offences by companies are also addressed (Section 63).

repealed_acts: The Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 (38 of 1963)
related_acts: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (30 of 2013)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government appoints Chairperson, Deputy Chairperson, and Members of the Board (Section 4). Central Government appoints Presiding Officer and members of the Adjudicatory Board (Section 55). The Board may appoint officers and employees for the Adjudicatory Board with Central Government approval (Section 61(1)).

applies_to: Major Ports of Chennai, Cochin, Deendayal (Kandla), Jawaharlal Nehru (Nhava Sheva), Kolkata, Mormugao, Mumbai, New Mangalore, Paradip, V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin) and Visakhapatnam
Any person contravening provisions of the Act
Companies
Employees of Board or Adjudicatory Board
Allottee or employee or other person from premises of Board
exemptions: Central Government may exempt certain specified vessels or classes of vessels or goods or classes of goods from obligation to use port assets in the interest of security or grave emergency (Section 50).
special_provisions: The application of this Act to the port of Mumbai, the Bombay Port Trust Act, 1879 and the port of Kolkata, the Calcutta Port Act, 1890, in so far as the said Acts apply to municipal assessment of the properties of the port of Mumbai and port of Kolkata and matters connected therewith, shall continue to so apply (Section 75(2)(i)).

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for rules, Section 71(1)); Board (for regulations, Section 72(1)).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Board has a lien for rates, can seize and detain goods (Section 28), sell goods (Section 30), and recover rates by distraint of vessel (Section 31). The Adjudicatory Board resolves disputes and handles complaints (Section 58). Contravention of the Act, rules, or regulations is punishable by fine (Section 62). The Board can evict persons from its premises (Section 68) and recover dues by suit (Section 69).
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Adjudicatory Board (Section 58(3), 59); Supreme Court of India (for appeals from Adjudicatory Board, Section 60(2)); Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the first class (for trying offences, Section 64).

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL BANK FOR FINANCING INFRASTRUCTURE AND DEVELOPMENT ACT, 2021

act_overview.preamble: An Act to establish the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development to support the development of longterm non-recourse infrastructure financing in India including development of the bonds and derivatives markets necessary for infrastructure financing and to carry on the business of financing infrastructure and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: To establish the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development to support the development of long-term non-recourse infrastructure financing in India. This includes fostering the bonds and derivatives markets necessary for infrastructure financing and carrying on the business of financing infrastructure.

chapter_titles: GOVERNMENT GRANTS, GUARANTEES AND OTHER CONCESSIONS

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its applicability to the whole of India, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Institution', 'Board', 'infrastructure', and 'Reserve Bank'.

key_sections.title: Establishment and incorporation of Institution
key_sections.description: Establishes the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and powers to acquire property and sue/be sued, with its head office in Mumbai.

key_sections.title: Purposes and objectives of Institution
key_sections.description: Outlines the developmental objective to facilitate long-term non-recourse infrastructure financing and the financial objective to lend or invest in infrastructure projects in India.

key_sections.title: Board of Directors
key_sections.description: Details the composition of the Board of Directors, including the Chairperson, Managing Director, Deputy Managing Directors, government nominees, shareholder-elected directors, and independent directors.

key_sections.title: Functions and powers of Institution
key_sections.description: Enumerates the wide range of functions and powers of the Institution, including forming subsidiaries, coordinating with other institutions, setting up trusts, developing bond markets, lending/investing in infrastructure projects, borrowing money, issuing guarantees, and converting debt to equity.

key_sections.title: Prohibited business
key_sections.description: Specifies business activities that the Institution is prohibited from undertaking, such as making loans on the security of its own bonds or to entities where its directors hold substantial interest, with certain exceptions.

key_sections.title: Related party transactions
key_sections.description: Regulates contracts or arrangements between the Institution and related parties, requiring Board consent and sometimes shareholder approval, with provisions for voidability and penalties for non-compliance.

key_sections.title: Audit
key_sections.description: Mandates the audit of the Institution's accounts by qualified auditors, outlines their duties, access rights, and reporting requirements to the Central Government and Reserve Bank.

key_sections.title: Powers of Central Government to make rules
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, covering various specific matters.

key_sections.title: Power of Board to make regulations
key_sections.description: Empowers the Board, with Central Government approval and Reserve Bank consultation, to make regulations consistent with the Act for its effective implementation.

key_sections.title: Sanction for enquiry, inquiry, investigation and prosecution
key_sections.description: Requires prior approval from the Central Government or Managing Director for any enquiry, inquiry, investigation, or prosecution against officials of the Institution for actions taken in official capacity.

key_sections.title: Overriding effect of this Act
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws or instruments.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Act 2 of 1934
key_sections.description: Specifies that the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, shall be amended as detailed in the Second Schedule.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Act 10 of 1949
key_sections.description: Specifies that the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, shall be amended as detailed in the Third Schedule.

powers_conferred: Institution: form subsidiaries or joint ventures or branches, in India or outside India, for carrying out its functions

Institution: enter into any arrangement with such subsidiary company or joint venture or branch including for financing any such subsidiary company or joint venture or branch or guaranteeing any of their liabilities or make any other arrangement which may seem desirable to the Board

Institution: co-ordinate its operations and the operations of various institutions engaged in the field of infrastructure finance and maintain expert staff to study problems relating to infrastructure finance and be available for consultation to the Central Government, the Reserve Bank and the other institutions engaged in the field of infrastructure finance

Institution: set up trusts under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882 for establishment of funds for such nature as would assist in financing of infrastructure projects located in India, or partly in India and partly outside India, including real estate investment trusts and infrastructure investment trusts

Institution: support the development of a deep and liquid market for bonds, loans and derivatives for infrastructure financing including facilitating electronic and negotiated markets infrastructure, investor protection, adjudication infrastructure, etc.

Institution: lend and invest in infrastructure projects located in India, or partly in India and partly outside India, including by underwriting credit, securitisation of its receivables, including by way of any pass through certificate or direct assignment, transfer or novation, or by means of innovative financial tools including transactions secured by receivables from project

Institution: extend loans and advances to any company or statutory corporation or trust or any financial institution funding infrastructure, for the purposes of providing financial assistance for infrastructure projects located in India, or partly in India and partly outside India
Institution: take over or refinance existing loans extended by a lender for infrastructure projects located in India, or partly in India and partly outside India
Institution: transfer loans and advances granted by it, with or without the securities, to trusts, for consideration

Institution: set aside loans or advances held by the Institution and issue and sell securities based upon such loans or advances so set aside in the form of debt obligations, trust certificates of beneficial interest or other instruments, by whatever name called, and act as a trustee for the holders of such securities
Institution: assign securities issued to the Institution

Institution: subscribe to or purchase, underwrite, acquire, hold or sell stocks, shares, bonds, debenture stocks, debt securities, obligations and securities, commercial papers, certificates of deposit or debentures issued or guaranteed by any company or trust or registered society or co-operative society or association or the Central Government or any State Government or any financial institution funding infrastructure, to facilitate financing of infrastructure projects in India, or partly in India and partly outside India, or to facilitate deepening of bond market for infrastructure financing

Institution: borrow or raise money by way of loans or otherwise both in rupees and foreign currencies or secure the payment of money by the issue and sale of debentures, debenture stocks, bonds, obligations, mortgages and securities of all kinds

Institution: borrow money from the Central Government, scheduled banks, financial institutions, mutual funds, any class of persons, and from any other institution or authority or organisation notified by the Central Government
Institution: buy or sell, or enter into such other dealings in foreign exchange as may be necessary for the discharge of its functions

Institution: issue participation certificates or debt securities, and promote and facilitate securitisation of loan portfolio of companies and other entities engaged in the development and financing of infrastructure and create and develop a secondary market for the securitised receivables including by way of acting as an intermediary

Institution: lend money with or without security and make advances upon, hold in trust, issue, buy, sell or otherwise acquire or dispose of on commission or otherwise any of the securities or investments or act as an agent for any of the like purpose
Institution: lend to or invest in or acquire professional or technical services of companies operating in the infrastructure domain across the life cycle of projects

Institution: act as an intermediary in respect of transactions or services relating to debt securities issued by infrastructure companies and financial institutions for financing infrastructure projects located in India, or partly in India and partly outside India, including by way of extension of credit enhancement facilities
Institution: take an active role in negotiations and discussions with various Government authorities and stakeholders for effective dispute resolution in the field of infrastructure financing
Institution: apply for, receive, accept, administer and manage grants, aids, subsidies, funds or donations, etc., from national and international sources

Institution: issue guarantee, letters of comfort, or letters of credit for loans or credit arrangements made, or, debentures or bonds issued, by any financial institution funding infrastructure projects in India, or partly in India and partly outside India

Institution: borrow money from the Reserve Bank repayable on demand or on the expiry of fixed periods not exceeding ninety days from the date on which the money is so borrowed against the security of stocks, funds or securities

Institution: borrow money from the Reserve Bank against bills of exchange or promissory notes arising out of bona fide commercial or trade transactions maturing within five years from the date of the borrowing
Institution: convert any debt it has extended to a borrower into equity
Institution: any other kind of business or undertake any other kind of activity which the Central Government in consultation with the Reserve Bank may authorise
Board: increase or reduce the nominal or face value of the shares, and divide the authorised capital into such denomination as it may decide
Board: increase or reduce the authorised capital (in consultation with the Central Government)
Board: reduce its share capital, including by way of buy-back of shares (with prior approval of the Central Government)
Board: general superintendence, direction and management of the affairs and business of the Institution
Board: delegate powers and functions to any director or committee or officer or employee of the Institution
Board: make regulations (with previous approval of the Central Government and in consultation with the Reserve Bank)
Central Government: appoint Chairperson (in consultation with the Reserve Bank)
Central Government: nominate two directors who shall be officials of the Central Government
Central Government: determine procedure and clearances for appointment of Managing Director and Deputy Managing Directors
Central Government: prescribe terms and conditions of induction of independent directors
Central Government: remove directors from office under specified conditions
Central Government: terminate the term of office of Chairperson, Managing Director, Deputy Managing Directors or directors (in consultation with the Reserve Bank)
Central Government: guarantee the bonds, debentures and loans issued by the Institution
Central Government: authorise any other kind of business or activity for the Institution (in consultation with the Reserve Bank)
Central Government: make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act
Central Government: issue directions on questions of policy to the Institution
Central Government: order liquidation of the Institution
Central Government: remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of this Act
Reserve Bank: grant licence for setting up other development financial institutions (in consultation with the Central Government)
Reserve Bank: specify criteria, terms and conditions for such licences
Reserve Bank: approve panel of auditors for the Institution and fix their remuneration
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Directors or employees contravening disclosure of interest provisions (Section 16) are liable to a penalty of up to one lakh rupees. Directors or employees contravening related party transaction provisions (Section 19) are liable to a penalty of up to twenty-five lakh rupees.

amended_acts: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Act 2 of 1934)
related_acts: Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002 (54 of 2002)
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 2013 (23 of 2013)
Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934)
Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 (15 of 1992)
Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993 (51 of 1993)

authorities_established: National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (Institution)
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson (in consultation with the Reserve Bank) and nominates two directors. The Board appoints the Managing Director and Deputy Managing Directors (on recommendations of the Bureau) and independent directors (on recommendations of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee). Shareholders elect certain directors.

applies_to: National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (Institution)
Financial institutions (for refinancing)
Companies, statutory corporations, trusts, financial institutions funding infrastructure (for loans/investments)
Borrowing entities (for director appointments)
exemptions: Directors nominated by the Institution or Central Government, or elected by virtue of shares held by the Institution, are exempt from certain prohibited business rules.

Transactions entered into by the Institution in its ordinary course of business (other than non-arm's length transactions) are exempt from Board consent/shareholder approval for related party transactions.
Transactions between the Institution and its wholly owned subsidiary (if consolidated financials are presented to shareholders) are exempt from shareholder approval for related party transactions.
No fees are payable to directors who are officers of the Central Government.
special_provisions: The Act extends to the whole of India.
The head office of the Institution shall be in Mumbai.
The Institution may establish offices, branches or agencies at any place within or outside India.
The Institution's activities cover infrastructure projects located in India, or partly in India and partly outside India.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Board of Directors has general superintendence, direction, and management. The Board can delegate powers. The Institution's performance is reviewed by an external agency every five years. Accounts are audited by qualified auditors. The Institution furnishes returns and reports to the Central Government and Reserve Bank. The Central Government can issue policy directions. An adjudication mechanism is established for penalties. Sanction is required for inquiry/investigation/prosecution against officials.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: The Act implies that courts will take cognizance of offences after due sanction, but does not specify particular courts.

schedules_summary.description: Contains the form for the Declaration of Fidelity and Secrecy to be made by directors, auditors, officers, or other employees of the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development.

Details the amendments to be made to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, primarily by inserting references to the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development and other development financial institutions in various sections.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR ALLIED AND HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONS ACT, 2021

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for regulation and maintenance of standards of education and services by allied and healthcare professionals, assessment of institutions, maintenance of a Central Register and State Register and creation of a system to improve access, research and development and adoption of latest scientific advancement and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to regulate and maintain standards of education and services for allied and healthcare professionals. It aims to establish a system for assessment of institutions, maintain central and state registers, and foster research, development, and adoption of scientific advancements in the field.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Secretary of Commission (on recommendation of Search-cum-Selection Committee), Part-time Members of Commission, Secretary to Interim Commission, make rules, issue directions, amend Schedule.

Commission: Constitute Professional Councils, frame policies and standards, regulate professional conduct, maintain Central Register, provide scope of practice, set education standards, conduct examinations, delegate functions, make regulations.
State Government: Constitute State Councils, make rules, appoint Chairperson and Members of State Council, appoint President and members of Autonomous Boards.

State Council: Constitute Autonomous Boards, regulate allied and healthcare professionals, enforce professional conduct, ensure minimum education standards, inspect institutions, register professionals, approve courses, impose fines.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter VII outlines several offences and their corresponding penalties. Section 56 imposes a fine up to fifty thousand rupees for falsely claiming registration, with subsequent convictions leading to imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to one lakh rupees or both. Section 57 penalizes misuse of titles with a fine up to one lakh rupees for first conviction, and imprisonment up to one year or a fine up to two lakh rupees or both for subsequent convictions. Section 58 prescribes a fine up to fifty thousand rupees for failure to surrender a certificate of registration, with an additional fine of five thousand rupees per day for continuing offences. Section 59 states that contravention of any provisions of the Act or rules/regulations made thereunder shall be punishable with imprisonment of not less than one year but up to three years, or a fine of not less than one lakh rupees but up to five lakh rupees, or both.

act_identification.act_title: THE INLAND VESSELS ACT, 2021

act_overview.preamble: An Act to promote economical and safe transportation and trade through inland waters, to bring uniformity in application of law relating to inland waterways and navigation within the country, to provide for safety of navigation, protection of life and cargo, and prevention of pollution that may be caused by the use or navigation of inland vessels, to ensure transparency and accountability of administration of inland water transportation, to strengthen procedures governing the inland vessels, their construction, survey, registration, manning, navigation and such other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to promote economical and safe transportation and trade through inland waters in India. It aims to bring uniformity in laws relating to inland waterways and navigation, ensuring safety, protection of life and cargo, and prevention of pollution. The Act also seeks to strengthen administrative procedures for inland vessels, covering their construction, survey, registration, manning, and navigation.

chapter_titles: DECLARATION OF INLAND WATER AREA INTO ZONES
MANNING, QUALIFICATION, TRAINING, EXAMINATION AND CERTIFICATION

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's title, its application to the whole of India, and its commencement date(s).

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Registration
key_sections.description: Specifies the types of entities and vessels eligible for registration under the Act, including Indian-owned vessels and foreign vessels on bareboat charter-cum-demise.

key_sections.title: Training and minimum age for employment.
key_sections.description: Sets standards for qualification, training, examination, and certification for crew, and prohibits employment of persons under eighteen years on mechanically propelled inland vessels.

key_sections.title: Special category vessels.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to specify criteria for identifying special category vessels and outlines additional requirements for them.

key_sections.title: Chemicals, etc., to be designated as pollutants.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to designate pollutants and mandates standards for sewage and garbage disposal to prevent pollution by inland vessels.

key_sections.title: Prohibition against intentionally causing wreck.
key_sections.description: Prohibits intentional abandonment, dumping, or jettisoning of vessels or cargo to cause wreck.

key_sections.title: Liability under Act.
key_sections.description: Establishes liability for owners, operators, masters, crew, or insurers for contraventions of the Act and pecuniary penalties.

key_sections.title: Insurance to cover.
key_sections.description: Mandates insurance coverage for mechanically propelled vessels, including liability for death, injury, property damage, and pollution, as well as for dangerous goods.

key_sections.title: Reporting of casualty, accident, wreck, etc.
key_sections.description: Requires reporting of marine incidents to designated authorities and police, leading to preliminary inquiries and investigations.

key_sections.title: Offences and penalties.
key_sections.description: Lists specific contraventions of the Act and the corresponding fines or imprisonment penalties.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To make rules for various aspects (classification, survey, registration, manning, pollution, liability, insurance, trade, general powers), appoint officers for central database, give directions to State Governments, suspend/alter application of Act, designate pollutants, specify pilotage requirements for national waterways.

State Government: To declare inland water area into Zones, appoint designated authorities, appoint surveyors, grant certificate of survey, appoint ports/places of registry, appoint Registrars, appoint examiners, grant certificate of competency/service, identify special category vessels, appoint officers for special category vessels, appoint officers for detention, constitute Development Fund, appoint courts for trials, administer non-mechanically propelled vessels, make rules, specify pilotage requirements for state waterways.
Competent Authority (Inland Waterways Authority of India): To exercise powers and discharge duties conferred by or under this Act.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act specifies various offences for contravention of its provisions, categorized by section. Penalties range from fines (e.g., ten thousand rupees for not having a valid certificate of survey, up to fifty thousand rupees for pollution or operating foreign vessels without permission) to imprisonment (e.g., up to one year for illegal transfer of ownership, up to three years for intentionally causing wreck or certain pilotage violations), or both. A general penalty clause provides for fines up to three lakh rupees or imprisonment up to three years, or both, for contraventions not specifically listed. Magistrates can order fines to be levied by distress and sale of the vessel.

Inland Waterways Authority of India Act, 1985 (82 of 1985)
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (30 of 2013)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government and State Governments have powers to appoint various officers, authorities, and examiners under this Act.

applies_to: All inland vessels plying within inland waters of India (Chapters I, III, X, XVI and XVIII)
Mechanically propelled vessels registered under this Act (Chapters IV, V, VI, VIII, IX, X, XI, XII, XIII and XIV)
Vessels registered under other Indian laws or foreign laws but endorsed or recognised under this Act for plying within inland waterways (Chapters VIII, IX, X, XI, XII and XIII)
Special category vessels plying or using inland waterways (Chapters IV, V, VI, VII, VIII, IX, X, XI, XII, XIII and XIV)
Non-mechanically propelled inland vessels (Chapter XVII)
exemptions: Fishing vessels registered under the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 or the Marine Products Export Development Authority Act, 1972.
Any vessel specified as not to be inland vessels by notification by the Central Government.

The Central Government may declare that all or any of the provisions (other than those for safety, manning, and pollution) shall not apply to any specified class or category of mechanically propelled inland vessels.
special_provisions: Different dates may be appointed for bringing into force different provisions of this Act in different States or Union territories.

For the administration of non-mechanically propelled inland vessels (Chapter XVII), the Central Government shall have no powers of administration and shall only provide assistance to the respective State Government on official request.
The Central Government may suspend or relax the operation of all or any of the provisions of this Act for specified periods or indefinitely.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (general powers, specific chapters), State Government (general powers, specific chapters).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Enforcement is carried out through surveys, registration, certification, inspections, detention of vessels, inquiries into casualties and pollution incidents, and the imposition of penalties for contraventions. Designated authorities, Registrars, surveyors, and examiners play key roles.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Any civil court, revenue court or High Court having jurisdiction over matters of liabilities and offences. Courts not inferior to that of a Magistrate of the first class for trials. High Court for constituting limitation funds.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for surveillance, inspection, operation and maintenance of the specified dam for prevention of dam failure related disasters and to provide for institutional mechanism to ensure their safe functioning and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to provide for the surveillance, inspection, operation, and maintenance of specified dams. It aims to prevent dam failure related disasters and establish an institutional mechanism to ensure the safe functioning of these dams.

EMEGENCY ACTION PLAN AND DISASTER MANAGEMENT

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.

key_sections.title: Declaration as to expediency of Union control.
key_sections.description: Declares the expediency of Union control over the regulation of uniform dam safety procedures for specified dams.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'dam', 'specified dam', 'dam failure', and various authorities.

key_sections.title: Establishment of National Dam Safety Authority.

key_sections.title: Functions of Authority.
key_sections.description: Outlines the functions of the National Dam Safety Authority, including implementing policies, resolving disputes, and enforcing attendance/information requests.

key_sections.title: Constitution of State Committee on Dam Safety.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of a State Committee on Dam Safety and specifies its composition.

key_sections.title: Establishment of State Dam Safety Organisation.
key_sections.description: Requires State Governments to establish a State Dam Safety Organisation within a specified timeframe and details its leadership.

key_sections.title: Surveillance and inspection.
key_sections.description: Obligates State Dam Safety Organisations to conduct perpetual surveillance, inspections, and monitor operation/maintenance of specified dams.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of State Dam Safety Organisation and Authority.
key_sections.description: Defines the jurisdiction of State Dam Safety Organisations over dams within their State and specifies cases where the Authority acts as the State Dam Safety Organisation.

key_sections.title: Responsibility of owner of specified dam.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not absolve dam owners of their duties, obligations, or liabilities related to dam construction, operation, maintenance, and supervision.

key_sections.title: Obligation of owner of specified dam.
key_sections.description: Details the obligations of dam owners regarding hydro-meteorological networks, flood warning systems, technical instruments, information dissemination, and risk assessment studies.

key_sections.title: Emergency action plan.
key_sections.description: Requires dam owners to prepare and regularly update emergency action plans for dam failure scenarios, including procedures for protection and mitigation.

key_sections.title: Punishment for obstruction, etc.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for obstructing officers or refusing to comply with directions under the Act, with enhanced penalties if it results in loss of life or imminent danger.

key_sections.title: Act to have overriding effect.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions in other laws.

key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Punishment for obstruction of officers or non-compliance with directions under the Act, with imprisonment up to one year or fine, or both. If such obstruction or refusal results in loss of lives or imminent danger, imprisonment may extend to two years (Section 41). Heads of Government Departments and responsible persons in companies are deemed guilty for offences committed by their respective entities, unless they prove lack of knowledge or due diligence (Sections 42, 43).

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the head and members of the National Dam Safety Authority and members of the National Committee. The Central Government also provides officers and employees for the Authority. The State Government appoints members of the State Committee on Dam Safety and provides officers and employees for the State Dam Safety Organisation.

In States having more than thirty specified dams, the State Dam Safety Organisation shall be headed by an officer not below the rank of Chief Engineer or equivalent; in all other cases, by an officer not below the rank of Superintendent Engineer or equivalent (Section 14(1) proviso).
Special measures for dams located outside the territory of India if their failure may endanger life and property in India (Section 47).

act_identification.act_title: THE ASSISTED REPRODUCTIVE TECHNOLOGY (REGULATION) ACT, 2021

act_overview.preamble: An Act for the regulation and supervision of the assisted reproductive technology clinics and the assisted reproductive technology banks, prevention of misuse, safe and ethical practice of assisted reproductive technology services for addressing the issues of reproductive health where assisted reproductive technology is required for becoming a parent or for freezing gametes, embryos, embryonic tissues for further use due to infertility, disease or social or medical concerns and for regulation and supervision of research and development and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate and supervise assisted reproductive technology (ART) clinics and banks in India. Its primary objectives include preventing misuse, ensuring safe and ethical practices in ART services, and addressing reproductive health issues for individuals seeking parenthood or gamete/embryo preservation due to infertility, disease, or other concerns. The Act also provides for the regulation and supervision of research and development in ART.

chapter_titles: AUTHORITIES TO REGULATE ASSISTED REPRODUCTIVE TECHNOLOGY

key_sections.description: Provides the short title, extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'assisted reproductive technology', 'clinic', 'bank', 'commissioning couple', and 'gamete'.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of National Board.
key_sections.description: Outlines the advisory, review, monitoring, and supervisory powers and functions of the National Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Board.

key_sections.title: Functions of appropriate authority.
key_sections.description: Details the functions of the appropriate authority, including granting, suspending, or cancelling registration of clinics/banks, enforcing standards, and investigating complaints.

key_sections.title: Registration of assisted reproductive technology clinic or assisted reproductive technology bank.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration for any clinic or bank undertaking assisted reproductive technology procedures and sets conditions for application.

key_sections.title: General duties of assisted reproductive technology clinics and banks.
key_sections.description: Specifies general duties including ensuring eligibility of couples/donors, obtaining informed consent, maintaining confidentiality, and providing counselling.

key_sections.title: Written informed consent.
key_sections.description: Requires written informed consent for any treatment or procedure and mandates insurance coverage for oocyte donors.

key_sections.title: Sex selection.
key_sections.description: Prohibits sex selection in assisted reproductive technology procedures, aligning with existing laws.

key_sections.title: Sourcing of gametes by assisted reproductive technology banks.
key_sections.description: Regulates the sourcing, screening, and storage of gametes by ART banks, including age limits for donors and donation frequency.

key_sections.title: Rights of child born through assisted reproductive technology.
key_sections.description: Declares a child born through ART as the biological child of the commissioning couple, with all associated rights, and states that donors relinquish parental rights.

key_sections.title: Sex selective assisted reproductive technology.
key_sections.description: Prohibits advertisements for sex-selective ART and prescribes penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Offences and penalties.
key_sections.description: Lists various offences related to ART, such as abandoning children, selling gametes/embryos, or exploiting couples/donors, and specifies corresponding penalties.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Grants the National Board the power to make regulations with prior Central Government approval.

key_sections.title: Application of other laws not barred.
key_sections.description: Clarifies that this Act's provisions are in addition to, and not in derogation of, other specified laws.

Power to review and monitor implementation of the Act, rules and regulations (National Board)

Power to search any place suspected of violating the Act (Appropriate Authority)

Power to remove difficulties (Central Government)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prohibits sex-selective assisted reproductive technology, with penalties of imprisonment for 5 to 10 years or a fine of 10 to 25 lakh rupees, or both. It also criminalizes abandoning or exploiting children born through ART, selling human embryos or gametes, importing embryos/gametes, exploiting commissioning couples/donors, transferring embryos to males or animals, selling embryos for research, or using intermediaries for gamete donors. The penalty for these offences is a fine of 5 to 10 lakh rupees for the first contravention, and for subsequent contraventions, imprisonment for 3 to 8 years and a fine of 10 to 20 lakh rupees. Any other contravention of the Act or rules for which no specific punishment is provided is punishable as per the penalties for subsequent contraventions mentioned above.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Appoint appropriate authorities for Union Territories, make rules, approve regulations, remove difficulties.
State Government: Appoint appropriate authorities for States, hear appeals.

National Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Board: Advise Central Government, review and monitor implementation, lay down code of conduct, set minimum standards, oversee performance of bodies, supervise State Boards, make regulations.

Appropriate Authority: Grant, suspend or cancel registration of surrogacy clinics; enforce standards; investigate complaints and take legal action; supervise implementation; recommend modifications to rules and regulations; consider and grant or reject applications; summon persons; demand production of documents; search places.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Prohibition of commercial surrogacy, exploitation of surrogate mothers/children, selling human embryo/gametes, importing human embryo/gametes for surrogacy, and sex selection is punishable with imprisonment up to ten years and a fine up to ten lakh rupees (Section 38). Contravention of other provisions by medical practitioners or clinic owners is punishable with imprisonment up to five years and a fine up to ten lakh rupees, with subsequent offences leading to suspension of registration for five years (Section 39). Not following altruistic surrogacy (i.e., commercial surrogacy) is punishable with imprisonment up to five years and a fine up to five lakh rupees for the first offence, and up to ten years and ten lakh rupees for subsequent offences (Section 40). General contravention of the Act, rules, or regulations for which no specific penalty is provided, is punishable with imprisonment up to three years and a fine up to five lakh rupees, with additional daily fines for continuing contravention (Section 41).
