key_sections.title: Resistance to allow taking of measurements.
key_sections.description: States that resistance or refusal to allow measurements is lawful for police/prison officers to overcome and constitutes an offence under section 186 of the Indian Penal Code.

key_sections.title: Bar of suit.
key_sections.description: Provides immunity from legal action for anything done in good faith under this Act or rules made thereunder.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government and State Governments to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including specific matters like the manner of taking measurements.

key_sections.title: Power to remove difficulties.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to make orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, within three years of its commencement.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920, and includes saving provisions for actions taken under the repealed Act.

powers_conferred: Power to take measurements by a police officer or a prison officer (Section 3)
Power of Magistrate to direct a person to give measurements (Section 5)
Power of National Crime Records Bureau to collect, store, preserve, process, share, disseminate, destroy records of measurements (Section 4(1))
Power of State Government and Union territory Administration to notify an appropriate agency to collect, preserve and share measurements (Section 4(3))
Power to make rules by the Central Government or the State Government (Section 8)
Power to remove difficulties by the Central Government (Section 9)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Resistance to or refusal to allow the taking of measurements under this Act shall be deemed to be an offence under section 186 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).

repealed_acts: The Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920 (33 of 1920)

authorities_established: National Crime Records Bureau (assigned specific functions)
appropriate agency (to be notified by State Government and Union territory Administration)

applies_to: Any person convicted of an offence punishable under any law
Any person ordered to give security for good behaviour or maintaining peace
Any person arrested in connection with an offence or detained under any preventive detention law
Any person directed by a Magistrate to give measurements
exemptions: Any person arrested for an offence (except for an offence committed against a woman or a child or for any offence punishable with imprisonment for a period not less than seven years) may not be obliged to allow taking of his biological samples under the provisions of section 3.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government or the State Government
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Measurements are taken by police officers or prison officers. Magistrates can direct measurements. The National Crime Records Bureau is responsible for collecting, storing, preserving, processing, sharing, disseminating, and destroying records. Resistance to taking measurements is an offence.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Magistrate

act_identification.act_title: THE INDIAN ANTARCTIC ACT, 2022

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Earth Sciences
legislative_details.geographical_extent: Antarctica, comprising of: (i) the continent of Antarctica, including its ice-shelves; (ii) all islands south of 60° South Latitude, including their ice-shelves; (iii) all areas of the continental shelf that are adjacent to that continent or to those islands that are south of 60° South Latitude; (iv) all sea and air space south of 60° South Latitude; and (v) the area specified in Article I of the Convention on the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources.

act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to implement national measures for protecting the Antarctic environment and its associated ecosystems. It gives effect to international agreements like the Antarctic Treaty, the Convention on the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources, and the Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty, regulating various activities in Antarctica.

chapter_titles: COMMITTEE ON ANTARCTIC GOVERNANCE AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION
GRANT, SUSPENSION OR CANCELLATION OF PERMIT
PREVENTION OF MARINE POLLUTION AND LIABILITY FOR ENVIRONMENTAL EMERGENCY

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Application.
key_sections.description: Defines to whom and to what geographical area the Act applies.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Permit for Indian expedition to Antarctica.
key_sections.description: Requires a permit for any person in an Indian expedition to enter or remain in Antarctica.

key_sections.title: Permit for mineral resource activities.
key_sections.description: Prohibits mineral resource activities without a permit, allowing them only for scientific research or station maintenance.

key_sections.title: Prohibition of nuclear explosion or disposal of radioactive waste material in Antarctica.
key_sections.description: Strictly prohibits nuclear explosions or disposal of radioactive waste in Antarctica.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Committee.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Committee on Antarctic Governance and Environmental Protection and outlines its composition.

key_sections.title: Functions of Committee.
key_sections.description: Details the responsibilities of the Committee, including monitoring compliance, advisory roles, and record keeping.

key_sections.title: Application for permit.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for applying for a permit, including environmental impact assessment requirements.

key_sections.title: Waste disposal.
key_sections.description: Mandates the cleanup of waste disposal sites and abandoned worksites by waste generators and users.

key_sections.title: Duties and liabilities of Operator in case of environmental emergency.
key_sections.description: Specifies the duties and liabilities of an Operator in the event of an environmental emergency in Antarctica.

key_sections.title: Penalty for contravention of certain provisions of Act by person.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for individuals contravening specific provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Designated Court and jurisdiction.
key_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of Designated Courts for speedy trial of offences under the Act and defines their jurisdiction.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government: to give directions to the Committee (Section 26)
Central Government: to establish the Committee on Antarctic Governance and Environmental Protection (Section 23)
Central Government: to designate officers as Inspectors (Section 30)
Central Government: to confer powers of arrest, investigation, search, seizure, and prosecution on officers (Section 50)
Central Government: to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act (Section 55)
Central Government: to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act (Section 56)
Committee: to grant, suspend, or cancel permits (Chapter V)
Committee: to monitor, implement, and ensure compliance of international laws and rules (Section 25)
Committee: to undertake advisory, supervisory, or enforcement activities (Section 25)
Committee: to establish a waste classification system and prepare waste management plans (Section 34)
Committee: to ensure compliance of international obligations by permit holders (Section 38)
Inspector: to enter and search places, examine substances, open receptacles, examine documents, take samples, conduct tests, and confiscate samples (Section 30)
Inspection Team: to inspect stations, vessels, and aircraft in Antarctica (Section 31)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Chapter IX outlines offences and penalties. Persons contravening certain provisions face imprisonment up to 2 years and/or fine of 10-50 lakh rupees (e.g., Sections 4, 5, 8, 12, 18, 19, 20, 21, 29(4), 36, 37); or imprisonment up to 7 years and fine of 10-50 lakh rupees (e.g., Sections 7, 9, 10); or imprisonment of 20 years to life and fine of 50 crore rupees for nuclear explosion, or 14 years to life and fine of 25 crore rupees for radioactive waste disposal (Section 17); or imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine of 15-75 lakh rupees (e.g., Sections 11, 16, 33, 35); or imprisonment up to 1 year and/or fine of 5-20 lakh rupees (e.g., Sections 14, 32). Operators of vessels face imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine of 1-5 crore rupees (e.g., Sections 6, 11, 12, 13, 18, 19, 21, 22) or imprisonment up to 7 years and fine of 2-10 crore rupees (e.g., Sections 7, 9, 39). Operators of aircraft face similar penalties (Sections 6, 9, 11, 12, 19, 21). A general penalty for other contraventions is a fine up to 10 lakh rupees. Offences by companies are also covered, holding both the company and responsible individuals liable.

related_acts: Convention on the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources
Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty

authorities_established: Committee on Antarctic Governance and Environmental Protection
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to establish the Committee and nominate its members, including the Chairperson and experts. It also designates officers as Inspectors and Analysts, and constitutes inspection teams. The Committee appoints waste management officers.
regulatory_bodies: Committee on Antarctic Governance and Environmental Protection

applies_to: A citizen of India
A citizen of any other country (if part of an Indian expedition to Antarctica under a permit)
A company, body corporate, corporation, partnership firm, joint venture, an association of persons or any other entity incorporated, established or registered under any law in force in India

Any vessel or aircraft registered in India or outside India (if part of an Indian expedition to Antarctica under a permit, or registered in India but chartered by any other Party for entering into Antarctica)
Antarctica, as defined in Section 2(e)
exemptions: Persons travelling through, on or above the high seas, to an immediate destination outside Antarctica (Sections 4, 6)
Food other than poultry or live animals from the prohibition of introducing non-native animals and plants (Section 9)

Emergencies involving the safety of a person, protection of the environment, or safety of any vessel, aircraft, equipment or facility that has significant value (Sections 4, 5, 6, 11, 12, 13 are not applicable) (Section 15)
Removal of any structure or waste material if it may result in greater adverse environmental impact than leaving it (Section 33)
Waste that is incinerated, autoclaved, or otherwise treated to be made sterile (Section 35(2))
Waste whose removal would result in greater adverse environmental impact than leaving it (Section 35(2))
Substances generated by stations located on ice shelves or grounded ice-sheets, if disposed of after treatment in deep ice pits (Section 35(4))

Operator not liable for environmental emergency caused by an act or omission necessary to protect human life, a natural disaster, an act of terrorism, or an act of war aimed at the Operator's activity (Section 40)

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a permit system for various activities in Antarctica, prohibitions on harmful activities, inspections by designated Inspectors and inspection teams, and penalties for contraventions. The Committee on Antarctic Governance and Environmental Protection monitors compliance and advises the Central Government. Designated Courts are established for the speedy trial of offences.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Designated Court

act_identification.act_title: THE MARITIME ANTI-PIRACY ACT, 2022

act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to implement the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, specifically concerning the repression of piracy on the high seas. It establishes legal provisions for defining piracy, prescribing punishments, and setting up a framework for the arrest, investigation, and trial of piracy-related offences.

key_sections.title: Short title, commencement and application.
key_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its commencement date, and its application to the high seas.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'authorised personnel', 'high seas', and 'piracy'.

key_sections.title: Punishment for piracy.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for committing any act of piracy, including imprisonment for life, fine, or death in cases causing death or attempt thereof.

key_sections.title: Punishment for attempt to commit piracy, etc.
key_sections.description: Stipulates punishment for attempting, aiding, abetting, conspiring, or procuring the commission of piracy.

key_sections.title: Punishment for organising or directing others to participate in an act of piracy.
key_sections.description: Defines punishment for individuals who organise or direct others to participate in an act of piracy.

key_sections.title: Conferment of power of arrest, investigation, etc.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to confer powers of arrest, investigation, and prosecution on its officers or State Government officers for the purposes of this Act.

key_sections.title: Arrest of persons and seizure of ship and property.
key_sections.description: Empowers authorised personnel to board ships, arrest persons, and seize pirate ships and property on suspicion of piracy on the high seas.

key_sections.title: Designated Court.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to specify Courts of Sessions as Designated Courts for speedy trial of offences under this Act, in consultation with the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court.

key_sections.title: Jurisdiction of Designated Court.
key_sections.description: Outlines the territorial and personal jurisdiction of the Designated Court, including for persons apprehended, Indian citizens, resident foreign nationals, and stateless persons, with exemptions for warships and government ships.

key_sections.title: Trial of offences by Designated Court.
key_sections.description: Details the trial procedures for offences under this Act by the Designated Court, including powers regarding detention, cognizance, and concurrent trial of other offences.

key_sections.title: Presumption.
key_sections.description: Establishes presumptions against an accused person in certain circumstances, such as recovery of arms or evidence of force/threat, unless proven otherwise.

key_sections.title: Provisions as to bail.
key_sections.description: Sets conditions for granting bail to persons accused of offences under this Act, requiring the Public Prosecutor's opportunity to oppose and the court's satisfaction of innocence and unlikelihood of further offence.

key_sections.title: Application of Code in proceedings before Designated Court.
key_sections.description: States that the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, shall apply to proceedings before a Designated Court, unless otherwise provided in this Act.

key_sections.title: Provision as to extradition.
key_sections.description: Declares offences under this Act as extraditable and applicable to existing extradition treaties, or on the basis of reciprocity, and extends the jurisdiction for ships registered in other States.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Provides protection from legal proceedings for authorised personnel, the Central Government, or State Government for actions taken in good faith under this Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint commencement date (Section 1)
Central Government to confer powers of arrest, investigation, and prosecution on officers (Section 6)
Authorised personnel to board ships, arrest persons, and seize pirate ships and property (Section 7)
Central Government to specify Designated Courts (Section 8)
Designated Court to try offences (Section 9, 10)
Designated Court to authorise detention (Section 10)
Designated Court to take cognizance of offences (Section 10)
Designated Court to try offences under any other law concurrently (Section 10)
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Punishment for piracy (Section 3): Imprisonment for life or fine or both; or death or imprisonment for life if death or an attempt thereof is caused, along with restitution or forfeiture of property. Punishment for attempt to commit piracy, or aiding, abetting, conspiring, or procuring the commission of such offence (Section 4): Imprisonment up to ten years or fine or both. Punishment for organising or directing others to participate in an act of piracy (Section 5): Imprisonment up to fourteen years or fine or both.

related_acts: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, 1982
Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976 (80 of 1976)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: Central Government (for specifying Designated Courts and conferring powers of arrest, investigation, and prosecution)

applies_to: the high seas
persons apprehended by, or in the custody of, the authorized personnel or the police, regardless of nationality or citizenship
citizens of India
resident foreign nationals in India
any stateless person
exemptions: warship or its auxiliary ship
Government owned ship employed for non-commercial service and is under the control of Government authorities at the time of commission of the offence of piracy

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the conferment of powers of arrest, investigation, and prosecution by the Central Government on its officers or State Government officers. Authorised personnel can arrest persons and seize ships. Offences are tried by Designated Courts established by the Central Government.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Designated Court; High Court (for special powers regarding bail)

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL DENTAL COMMISSION ACT, 2023
act_identification.date_of_commencement: It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint; and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act.

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the profession of dentistry in the country, to provide for quality and affordable dental education, to make accessible high quality oral healthcare and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to regulate the profession of dentistry in India, ensuring quality and affordable dental education. It also seeks to make high-quality oral healthcare accessible to the public by establishing a regulatory framework.

chapter_titles: STATE DENTAL COUNCIL OR JOINT DENTAL COUNCIL

key_definitions: Under-Graduate and Post-Graduate Dental Education Board

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's short title, its applicability to the whole of India, and that its commencement date(s) will be appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Commission', 'dentistry', 'dental institution', and various boards.

key_sections.title: Constitution of National Dental Commission.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to constitute the National Dental Commission as a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, headquartered in New Delhi.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Commission.
key_sections.description: Outlines the comprehensive powers and functions of the Commission, including laying down policies, regulating standards for dental education, regulating institutions, and exercising appellate jurisdiction over Autonomous Boards.

key_sections.title: National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that all admissions to undergraduate dental courses (BDS) shall be through the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) and specifies provisions for postgraduate admissions until the National Exit Test (Dental) is operational.

key_sections.title: National Exit Test (Dental).
key_sections.description: Establishes a common final year undergraduate dental examination, the 'National Exit Test (Dental)', for granting a licence to practice dentistry and for enrolment in registers, also applicable to foreign dental qualification holders.

key_sections.title: Constitution of Autonomous Boards.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Central Government to constitute three Autonomous Boards: the Under-Graduate and Post-Graduate Dental Education Board, the Dental Assessment and Rating Board, and the Ethics and Dental Registration Board.

key_sections.title: Permission for establishment of new dental college or to start postgraduate course or to increase number of seats.
key_sections.description: Requires prior permission from the Dental Assessment and Rating Board for establishing new dental colleges, starting postgraduate courses, or increasing seats, with an appeal mechanism to the Commission and Central Government.

key_sections.title: State Dental Council or Joint Dental Council.
key_sections.description: Requires State Governments to establish State Dental Councils, outlining their composition, corporate status, term of office, and functions, including disciplinary actions and appellate jurisdiction of the Ethics and Dental Registration Board.

key_sections.title: National Register and State Register.
key_sections.description: Mandates the Ethics and Dental Registration Board to maintain online National Registers for dentists and dental auxiliaries, and requires State Dental Councils to maintain and update State Registers, ensuring electronic synchronization.

key_sections.title: Rights of persons to have licence to practice and to be enrolled in National Register or State Register and their obligations thereto.
key_sections.description: Grants the right to practice dentistry and be enrolled in registers to those who qualify the National Exit Test (Dental), with provisions for existing registrants and foreign qualification holders.

key_sections.title: Bar to practice.
key_sections.description: Prohibits any person not enrolled in the State or National Register from practicing dentistry, holding dental office, signing dental certificates, or giving expert evidence, and prescribes penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Dentists Act, 1948, dissolves the Dental Council of India, and includes saving provisions for previous operations, rights, penalties, and the continuation of existing orders, licences, and registrations.

powers_conferred: Commission: Lay down policies and regulate standards for dental education, examination and training; promote additional degrees/diplomas; regulate dental institutions, researches, dentists and dental auxiliaries; ensure admissions through NEET; identify and regulate dental auxiliaries; collaborate with industry for technology; assess dental healthcare requirements; frame guidelines for functioning of various bodies; ensure compliance by State Dental Councils; exercise appellate jurisdiction over Autonomous Boards; promote preventive dental care; lay down ethics policies; frame guidelines for fee determination (50% of seats in private institutions); enhance skills for global mobility.

Central Government: Appoint Chairperson, Members, Secretary of Commission and President, Members of Autonomous Boards; give directions to Commission and Autonomous Boards on policy matters; give directions to State Governments on policy matters; supersede the Commission; make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

Autonomous Boards: Perform functions assigned under the Act; Under-Graduate and Post-Graduate Dental Education Board determines minimum requirements and standards for dental education, develops curriculum, frames guidelines for institutions, determines standards for courses/examinations, specifies norms for disclosures, grants recognition to dental qualifications; Dental Assessment and Rating Board determines assessment procedures, grants permission for new colleges/courses/seats, conducts inspections, assesses and rates institutions, takes measures against non-compliant institutions; Ethics and Dental Registration Board maintains National Registers, regulates professional conduct and ethics, approves/rejects/suspends/cancels registration/licence, interacts with State Dental Councils, exercises appellate jurisdiction over State Dental Councils.
State Government: Establish State Dental Councils; make rules related to State Dental Councils and rural dental care; promote preventive and promotive dental care in rural areas.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person contravening the provisions of Section 32 (Bar to practice without enrollment) shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to five lakh rupees or with both. The Dental Assessment and Rating Board may impose a monetary penalty on a dental institution for failure to maintain minimum essential standards, ranging from not less than one-tenth to not more than five times the total amount charged for one full batch of students.

repealed_acts: Dentists Act, 1948 (16 of 1948)
related_acts: National Commission for Indian System of Medicine
National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions

authorities_established: Under-Graduate and Post-Graduate Dental Education Board
important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government appoints the Chairperson, part-time Members of the Commission, the Secretary, and the President and Members of Autonomous Boards based on recommendations from a Search-cum-Selection Committee. State Governments appoint the Chairperson and nominate members for State Dental Councils.
regulatory_bodies: Under-Graduate and Post-Graduate Dental Education Board
National Commission for Indian System of Medicine
National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions

applies_to: Profession of dentistry in the country
Dental education and oral healthcare
Dentists and dental auxiliaries
Dental institutions (within or outside India for recognition)
Universities granting dental qualifications
State Dental Councils
special_provisions: Temporary registration for foreign citizens enrolled as dentists in their country for a specified period and manner.
Transitory provisions for students studying before the Act's commencement, allowing them to complete their courses under previous regulations.
Transitory provisions for existing educational standards, requirements, and State Councils until new ones are established under this Act.
State Governments are encouraged to promote preventive and promotive dental care in rural areas and enhance the capacity of dental professionals for public dentistry.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: The Central Government has the power to make rules. The Commission has the power to make regulations. State Governments have the power to make rules concerning State Dental Councils and rural dental care.
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act establishes the National Dental Commission and three Autonomous Boards (Under-Graduate and Post-Graduate Dental Education Board, Dental Assessment and Rating Board, Ethics and Dental Registration Board) to regulate dental education, practice, and ethics. It mandates National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) for admissions and a National Exit Test (Dental) for licensure. The Ethics and Dental Registration Board maintains National Registers and regulates professional conduct, with appellate jurisdiction over State Dental Councils. The Dental Assessment and Rating Board grants permissions for new institutions/courses and conducts inspections, imposing penalties for non-compliance. The Central Government provides oversight through directions and the power to supersede the Commission. Appeals against decisions of Autonomous Boards and State Dental Councils are provided.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: No court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under this Act except upon a complaint in writing made by an officer authorized by the Commission or the Ethics and Dental Registration Board or a State Dental Council.

schedules_summary.description: Lists categories of dental qualifications granted by statutory or other dental bodies in India, specifically mentioning All India Institutes of Medical Sciences, Oral Health Sciences Centre (PGIMER), and Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry.

act_identification.act_title: THE NATIONAL NURSING AND MIDWIFERY COMMISSION ACT, 2023
act_identification.act_short_title: the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission Act, 2023

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for regulation and maintenance of standards of education and services by nursing and midwifery professionals, assessment of institutions, maintenance of a National Register and State Registers and creation of a system to improve access, research and development and adoption of latest scientific advancement and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The primary purpose of this Act is to establish a comprehensive regulatory framework for nursing and midwifery education and professional services in India. It aims to ensure high standards, facilitate institutional assessment, maintain professional registers, and promote advancements in the field, thereby improving healthcare access and quality.

chapter_titles: RECOGNITION OF NURSING AND MIDWIFERY QUALIFICATIONS

key_definitions: Nursing and Midwifery Assessment and Rating Board
Nursing and Midwifery Ethics and Registration Board
Nursing and Midwifery Undergraduate and Postgraduate Education Board

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the Act's official title and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms and expressions used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: National Nursing and Midwifery Commission.
key_sections.description: Establishes the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission as a body corporate.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of National Commission.
key_sections.description: Outlines the broad regulatory, policy-making, and oversight powers of the National Commission.

key_sections.title: Autonomous Boards.
key_sections.description: Mandates the constitution of three specialized Autonomous Boards under the National Commission.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Nursing and Midwifery Undergraduate and Postgraduate Education Board.
key_sections.description: Details the functions related to setting education standards, curriculum development, and regulating scope of practice.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Nursing and Midwifery Assessment and Rating Board.
key_sections.description: Describes functions related to assessing and rating institutions, granting permissions, and taking corrective measures.

key_sections.title: Powers and functions of Nursing and Midwifery Ethics and Registration Board.
key_sections.description: Covers the maintenance of professional registers, regulation of conduct, and ethical standards.

key_sections.title: Permission for establishment of new nursing or midwifery institution.
key_sections.description: Sets out the procedure for obtaining permission to establish new institutions, courses, or increase seats.

key_sections.title: Constitution and composition of State Nursing and Midwifery Commission.
key_sections.description: Provides for the constitution and composition of State-level Nursing and Midwifery Commissions.

key_sections.title: National Register and State Register.
key_sections.description: Details the maintenance of online National and State Registers for nursing and midwifery professionals.

key_sections.title: Rights of persons to have licence to practice and to be enrolled in National Register or State Register for Nursing and Midwifery Professionals and their obligations thereto.
key_sections.description: Grants rights to qualified persons for licensure and enrollment in professional registers.

key_sections.title: Bar to practice.
key_sections.description: Prohibits unauthorized practice of nursing or midwifery and prescribes penalties for contravention.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Indian Nursing Council Act, 1947, and includes saving provisions for previous actions and existing qualifications.

powers_conferred: National Commission: Frame policies and regulate standards for education and training; regulate institutions, researches, professionals, and associates; identify and regulate other categories of the profession; provide basic standards for education, facilities, assessment, examination, training, research, continuing professional education, and tuition fees; provide standards for faculty and clinical facilities; provide uniform admission mechanism; ensure competence for enrollment and licensure; collaborate with industry for innovation and research; integrate soft skills and elective courses; assess nursing and midwifery requirements and advise Central Government; ensure professional ethics; promote, coordinate, and frame guidelines for various bodies; ensure coordination among Autonomous Boards; ensure compliance by State Commissions; exercise appellate jurisdiction over Autonomous Boards; delegate functions (except rule-making) to Autonomous Boards; delegate administrative and financial powers to its Secretary; constitute sub-committees.
Autonomous Boards: Perform functions assigned under the overall supervision of the National Commission.

Nursing and Midwifery Undergraduate and Postgraduate Education Board: Determine minimum requirements and standards of education and examination; develop competency-based curriculum; prescribe qualifications; prescribe standards for setting up institutions; determine standards and norms for infrastructure, faculty, and quality of education; facilitate faculty development and exchange programs; specify norms for compulsory annual disclosures; regulate standards and scope of practice of registered professionals; regulate limited prescribing authority for nurse practitioners.

Nursing and Midwifery Assessment and Rating Board: Determine procedure for assessing and rating institutions; grant permission for establishment of new institutions, courses, or increase of seats; conduct inspections of institutions; empanel independent rating agencies; make assessment and ratings public; take measures including warnings, monetary penalties, reducing intake, stoppage of admissions, and recommending withdrawal of recognition against non-compliant institutions.

Nursing and Midwifery Ethics and Registration Board: Maintain the National Register; approve or reject applications for registration; regulate professional conduct and promote ethics; develop mechanisms for continuous interaction with State Commissions; exercise appellate jurisdiction over State Commission actions; provide mechanisms for complaints and grievance redressal.

State Nursing and Midwifery Commission: Enforce professional conduct, code of ethics, and etiquette; take disciplinary action including removal from State Register; ensure standards of education, courses, curricula, facilities, staff, quality instruction, assessment, examination, training, research, and continuing professional education; maintain State Registers; issue certification of specialisation; conduct common counselling; provide skill-based examination for associates; ensure compliance with National Commission directives; meet with college principals; perform other functions entrusted by State Government, Union territory Administration, or National Commission.

Central Government: Give directions to National Commission, Autonomous Boards, and Nursing and Midwifery Advisory Council on policy matters; give directions to State Governments for carrying out provisions of the Act; supersede the National Commission; make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
State Government: Make rules for carrying out provisions related to State Commissions and public health nursing/midwifery practice in rural areas.
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: Any person practicing nursing or midwifery as a qualified professional or associate without being enrolled in the National Register or State Register, or giving expert evidence in court without such enrollment, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to five lakh rupees, or with both.

The Chairperson of the Advisory Council nominates Heads of national level professional nursing and midwifery associations.

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government, National Commission (for regulations), State Government
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the regulatory powers of the National Commission and its Autonomous Boards, including setting standards, assessing institutions, conducting inspections, imposing penalties, and withdrawing recognition. Appeals mechanisms are provided to the National Commission and Central Government. The Central Government can issue directions to the National Commission, Autonomous Boards, Advisory Council, and State Governments.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: Courts of law, subject to a complaint in writing made by an officer authorized by the National Commission, the Nursing and Midwifery Ethics and Registration Board, or a State Commission.

act_identification.act_title: THE INTER-SERVICES ORGANISATIONS (COMMAND, CONTROL AND DISCIPLINE) ACT, 2023
act_identification.act_short_title: The Inter-services Organisations (Command, Control and Discipline) Act, 2023

act_overview.preamble: An Act to empower the Commander-in-Chief or the Officer-in-Command of Inter-services Organisations in respect of service personnel who are subject to the Air Force Act, 1950, the Army Act, 1950 and the Navy Act, 1957, who are serving under or attached to his command, for the maintenance of discipline and proper discharge of their duties, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to empower the Commander-in-Chief or Officer-in-Command of Inter-services Organisations with disciplinary and administrative powers over service personnel from the Air Force, Army, and Navy. Its primary objective is to ensure the maintenance of discipline and proper discharge of duties within these integrated commands.

key_sections.description: Delineates the command, control, and disciplinary powers of the Commander-in-Chief or Officer-in-Command over personnel.

key_sections.title: Commanding Officer.
key_sections.description: Outlines the duties and powers of a Commanding Officer within an Inter-services Organisation, including initiating disciplinary or administrative actions.

key_sections.title: Superintendence of Central Government.

key_sections.title: Power to declare persons to be on active service.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government power to declare service personnel on active service for the purpose of this Act and the Service Acts.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the Act's provisions.

key_sections.title: Overriding effect of this Act.
key_sections.description: Establishes that this Act's provisions prevail over inconsistent provisions in any other law for the time being in force.

key_sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
key_sections.description: Provides legal protection against suit, prosecution, or other legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

act_identification.act_title: THE MEDIATION ACT, 2023

act_overview.preamble: An Act to promote and facilitate mediation, especially institutional mediation, for resolution of disputes, commercial or otherwise, enforce mediated settlement agreements, provide for a body for registration of mediators, to encourage community mediation and to make online mediation as acceptable and cost effective process and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to promote and facilitate mediation, including institutional and online mediation, for resolving commercial and other disputes. It provides for the enforcement of mediated settlement agreements, establishes a body for mediator registration, and encourages community mediation.

key_sections.title: Online mediation.

key_sections.description: Establishes the Mediation Council of India as a body corporate to perform duties under the Act.

key_sections.description: Details the responsibilities of the Mediation Council of India, including promoting mediation, setting standards, and recognizing institutes.

key_sections.title: Community mediation.
key_sections.description: Introduces community mediation for disputes affecting peace and harmony, to be facilitated by Legal Services Authorities or Magistrates.

key_sections.title: Provisions of Act to have overriding effect on mediation or conciliation contained in other laws.
key_sections.description: Declares the Act's overriding effect on mediation or conciliation provisions in other laws, subject to the Second Schedule.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to Post Office in India and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The main purpose of this Act is to consolidate and amend the existing laws related to the Post Office in India. It also aims to provide for matters connected with or incidental to the functioning of the Post Office.

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Post Office Act, 2023, and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Director General', 'item', 'Post Office', and 'regulations'.

key_sections.title: Services to be provided by Post Office.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to prescribe services provided by the Post Office and the Director General to make regulations regarding activities, charges, and terms and conditions for these services.

key_sections.title: Exclusive privilege in respect of postage stamps.
key_sections.description: Grants the Post Office exclusive privilege for issuing postage stamps and allows the Director General to make regulations for their supply and sale.

key_sections.title: Recovery of sums due in respect of services provided by Post Office.
key_sections.description: States that charges for Post Office services are recoverable as arrears of land revenue if not paid.

key_sections.title: Power to intercept, open or detain any item or deliver item to customs authority.
key_sections.description: Authorizes the Central Government to empower officers to intercept, open, or detain items in transmission for security, public order, or contravention of law, and to deliver items to customs authorities.

key_sections.title: Exemption from liability.
key_sections.description: Limits the liability of the Post Office and its officers for services provided, except for prescribed liabilities or fraudulent/wilful acts by officers.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make regulations.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Director General, with Central Government approval, to make regulations for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Indian Post Office Act, 1898, and includes savings provisions for rules, notifications, and orders made under the repealed Act.

act_overview.preamble: An Act to amend and consolidate the law relating to development, expansion and operation of telecommunication services and telecommunication networks; assignment of spectrum; and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to amend and consolidate the existing laws governing the development, expansion, and operation of telecommunication services and networks. It also provides for the assignment of spectrum and addresses related matters.

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the Act's name, geographical applicability, and the mechanism for its commencement.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Authorisation.
key_sections.description: Mandates authorisation from the Central Government for providing telecommunication services, establishing networks, or possessing radio equipment, and outlines conditions and exemptions.

key_sections.title: Assignment of spectrum.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Central Government's role as owner of spectrum and outlines procedures for its assignment, including auction and administrative processes.

key_sections.title: Right of way for telecommunication network in public property.
key_sections.description: Details the process for facility providers to obtain right of way for telecommunication networks on public property.

key_sections.title: Provisions for public emergency or public safety.
key_sections.description: Grants powers to the Central or State Government to take temporary possession of telecommunication services/networks or intercept messages during public emergencies or for public safety.

key_sections.title: Measures for national security, etc.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Central Government to take measures, including issuing directions, in the interest of national security or in the event of war.

key_sections.title: Establishment of Digital Bharat Nidhi.
key_sections.description: Establishes the Digital Bharat Nidhi, succeeding the Universal Service Obligation Fund, for funding telecommunication objectives.

key_sections.title: Measures for users.
key_sections.description: Allows the Central Government to prescribe measures for user protection, including consent for messages and grievance redressal mechanisms.

key_sections.title: Breach of terms and conditions of authorisation or assignment.
key_sections.description: Outlines the process for adjudicating breaches of authorisation or assignment terms, including civil penalties and recommendations for suspension/revocation.

key_sections.title: General provisions relating to offences.
key_sections.description: Defines various offences under the Act, such as operating without authorisation, unauthorised access, and tampering with identifiers, and prescribes penalties.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal of certain Acts and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885, and the Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933, while providing for savings clauses.

powers_conferred: Central Government: Grant authorisation (Section 3(1)), provide exemption from authorisation (Section 3(3)), allot telecommunication identifiers (Section 3(8)), assign spectrum (Section 4(1)), amend First Schedule (Section 4(5)), exempt from spectrum assignment (Section 4(6)), re-farm or harmonise frequency range (Section 5), enable technologically neutral use of spectrum (Section 6), promote optimal utilisation of spectrum (Section 7(1)), terminate unutilised spectrum assignment (Section 7(2)), establish monitoring and enforcement mechanism (Section 8(1)), permit sharing, trading, leasing and surrender of assigned spectrum (Section 8(2)), establish common ducts and cable corridors (Section 15(1)), notify standards and conformity assessment measures (Section 19), take temporary possession of telecommunication service/network for public emergency/safety (Section 20(1)), direct interception/suspension of messages/services for public emergency/safety (Section 20(2)), take measures for national security (Section 21), make rules for cyber security (Section 22(1)), declare Critical Telecommunication Infrastructure (Section 22(3)), make rules for standards/security practices for Critical Telecommunication Infrastructure (Section 22(4)), give directions to authorised entities (Section 23), control and administer Digital Bharat Nidhi (Section 24(1), 26), create regulatory sandboxes (Section 27), make rules for user protection (Section 28(2)), establish/approve online dispute resolution mechanisms (Section 30(1)), appoint Adjudicating Officers (Section 35(1)), appoint Designated Appeals Committee (Section 36(1)), provide for security interests (Section 45), grant certification for radio equipment operation (Section 46), make rules for amateur station operator certification (Section 47), permit use of equipment blocking telecommunication (Section 48), make rules (Section 56), amend Schedules (Section 57), remove difficulties (Section 58).
Adjudicating Officer: Conduct inquiry, pass orders, direct actions, impose civil penalties (Section 32(1), 33(1)), accept voluntary undertakings (Section 34(7)).
Designated Appeals Committee: Hear appeals against Adjudicating Officer orders (Section 36(1)).

District Magistrate: Determine disputes under Chapter III (Section 18(1)), approve/reject relocation/alteration of network (Section 16(5)), order persons to abstain from damaging property (Section 17(4)).
Officer authorised by Central/State Government: Take temporary possession of telecommunication service/network, intercept/detain/disclose messages, suspend services (Section 20).
Officer authorised by Central Government for search: Search and take possession of unauthorised equipment (Section 43).
Officer authorised by Central Government for information: Direct authorised entity/assignee to furnish information (Section 44).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes both criminal offences and civil penalties. Criminal offences include providing telecommunication services or establishing networks without authorisation, causing damage to critical telecommunication infrastructure, unauthorised access to networks or data, unlawful interception of messages, possessing or using equipment that blocks telecommunication, using unallotted telecommunication identifiers, tampering with identifiers, possessing radio equipment with excess SIM capacity, obtaining SIMs by fraud, and wilfully contravening national security measures. Penalties for these offences range from imprisonment up to three years, or fines up to two crore rupees, or both. Damaging non-critical telecommunication networks incurs compensation and a fine up to fifty lakh rupees. Abetment, attempt, or conspiracy to commit an offence is punishable as the offence itself. All offences are cognizable and non-bailable, triable by a Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or Chief Judicial Magistrate of first class. Civil penalties are categorised as Severe (up to Rs. 5 Crore), Major (up to Rs. 1 Crore), Moderate (up to Rs. 10 lakh), Minor (up to Rs. 1 lakh), and Non-severe (Written warning) for breach of terms and conditions of authorisation or assignment. Specific contraventions, such as possessing radio equipment without authorisation, using telecommunication services without required authorisation, or contravening user protection measures, also carry civil penalties ranging from fifty thousand rupees to ten lakh rupees, with increased penalties for subsequent offences or daily penalties for continuing contraventions.

exemptions: The Central Government may provide exemption from the requirement of authorisation.

special_provisions: Press messages of correspondents accredited to the Central Government or a State Government, intended to be published in India, shall not be intercepted or detained unless their transmission has been prohibited.

Rights in Continental Shelf and Exclusive Economic Zone are subject to the Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and other Maritime Zones Act, 1976, and applicable international laws.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through a monitoring and enforcement mechanism established by the Central Government for spectrum utilisation. Contraventions are adjudicated by an Adjudicating Officer, with appeals heard by a Designated Appeals Committee. The Act also defines various criminal offences with prescribed penalties, and grants powers of search to authorised officers. The Central Government can also direct authorised entities to furnish information. The implementation of the Act is intended to be digital by design.
implementation_and_enforcement.competent_courts: District Magistrate, District Judge, Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT), Civil Court (for specific appeals), Chief Metropolitan Magistrate or Chief Judicial Magistrate of first class (for offences). Civil court jurisdiction is barred for matters determined by the Adjudicating Officer, Designated Appeals Committee, Central Government, or TDSAT.

schedules_summary.description: Lists 19 categories of spectrum usage that can be assigned through an administrative process (without auction), including national security, law enforcement, public broadcasting, disaster management, scientific research, safety of transport systems, meteorological services, amateur stations, and certain satellite-based services.
Outlines the categorisation of civil penalties for breach of terms and conditions under Sections 32 and 34, ranging from 'Non-severe' (Written warning) to 'Severe' (Up to Rs. 5 Crore).

Specifies civil penalties for certain contraventions, such as possessing radio equipment without authorisation, using telecommunication services without required authorisation, contravention of user protection measures, and general contraventions of the Act or rules, with varying penalty amounts for first and subsequent offences.

key_sections.title: Punishments.
key_sections.description: Lists the types of punishments offenders are liable to under the Act, including death, imprisonment, forfeiture, fine, and community service.

key_sections.title: Act done by a person bound, or by mistake of fact believing himself bound, by law.
key_sections.description: Establishes that an act done by a person legally bound or mistakenly believing to be bound by law is not an offence.

key_sections.title: Things done in private defence.
key_sections.description: States that acts done in exercise of the right of private defence are not offences.

key_sections.title: Abetment of a thing.
key_sections.description: Defines what constitutes abetment, including instigation, conspiracy, and intentional aid.

key_sections.title: Criminal conspiracy.
key_sections.description: Defines criminal conspiracy as an agreement between two or more persons to do an illegal act or an act by illegal means.

key_sections.title: Rape.
key_sections.description: Defines rape based on various forms of penetration and circumstances where consent is absent or vitiated.

key_sections.title: Murder.
key_sections.description: Defines murder as a form of culpable homicide with specific intentions or knowledge, and lists exceptions.

key_sections.title: Organised crime.
key_sections.description: Defines organised crime as continuing unlawful activity by a syndicate, including various criminal acts for material benefit.

key_sections.title: Terrorist act.
key_sections.description: Defines terrorist acts as actions intended to threaten India's unity, integrity, sovereignty, security, or economic security, or to strike terror.

key_sections.title: Waging, or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war, against Government of India.
key_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for acts of war against the Government of India.

key_sections.title: Unlawful assembly.
key_sections.description: Defines an unlawful assembly as a gathering of five or more persons with a common illegal object.

key_sections.title: Theft.
key_sections.description: Defines theft as dishonestly taking movable property out of another's possession without consent.

key_sections.title: Defamation.
key_sections.description: Defines defamation as making or publishing imputations intended to harm a person's reputation, with several exceptions.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and includes savings clauses for previous operations, rights, penalties, and investigations.

key_sections.title: Short title, application and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, scope of application to judicial proceedings and Courts-martial, and the commencement date to be appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Adhiniyam, such as 'Court', 'document', 'evidence', 'fact', 'proved', and 'relevant'.

key_sections.title: Evidence may be given of facts in issue and relevant facts.
key_sections.description: States that evidence can be given for the existence or non-existence of facts in issue and relevant facts, and no others.

key_sections.title: Admission defined.
key_sections.description: Defines an admission as a statement (oral, documentary, or electronic) suggesting an inference about a fact in issue or relevant fact, made by specified persons under certain circumstances.

key_sections.title: Confession caused by inducement, threat, coercion or promise, when irrelevant in criminal proceeding.
key_sections.description: Declares confessions made under inducement, threat, coercion, or promise from a person in authority as irrelevant in criminal proceedings, with provisos for relevancy under certain conditions.

key_sections.title: Confession to police officer.
key_sections.description: States that confessions made to a police officer or while in police custody (unless before a Magistrate) cannot be proved against an accused, with an exception for facts discovered from such information.

key_sections.title: Opinions of experts.
key_sections.description: Makes opinions of specially skilled persons (experts) on foreign law, science, art, handwriting, finger impressions, and electronic evidence relevant facts.

key_sections.title: Facts of which Court shall take judicial notice.
key_sections.description: Lists facts of which the Court shall take judicial notice, including laws in force, international treaties, proceedings of legislatures, seals of courts, and public offices.

key_sections.title: Oral evidence to be direct.
key_sections.description: Mandates that oral evidence must be direct, meaning from a witness who directly perceived the fact, with exceptions for expert opinions in treatises.

key_sections.title: Admissibility of electronic records.
key_sections.description: Provides for the admissibility of electronic records as documents, specifying conditions for their production and the requirement of a certificate.

key_sections.title: Public and private documents.
key_sections.description: Classifies documents into public documents (acts/records of sovereign authority, official bodies, public officers, public records of private documents) and private documents.

key_sections.title: Burden of proof.
key_sections.description: Defines the burden of proof, stating that whoever desires a Court to give judgment based on asserted facts must prove those facts.

key_sections.title: Estoppel.
key_sections.description: Establishes the principle of estoppel, preventing a person from denying a truth they intentionally caused another to believe and act upon.

key_sections.title: Who may testify.
key_sections.description: Declares all persons competent to testify unless the Court finds them unable to understand questions or give rational answers due to age, disease, or similar causes.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, but includes savings provisions for pending applications, trials, inquiries, investigations, proceedings, or appeals under the old Act.

key_sections.title: Trial and proceedings to be held in electronic mode.
