act_identification.act_title: THE CHIEF ELECTION COMMISSIONER AND OTHER ELECTION COMMISSIONERS (APPOINTMENT, CONDITIONS OF SERVICE AND TERM OF OFFICE) ACT, 2023
act_identification.act_short_title: Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023

legislative_details.ministry_department: Ministry of Law and Justice

act_overview.preamble: An Act to regulate the appointment, conditions of service and term of office of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners, the procedure for transaction of business by the Election Commission and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act regulates the appointment, conditions of service, and term of office for the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners. It also establishes the procedure for the transaction of business by the Election Commission and addresses related matters.

chapter_titles: APPOINTMENT AND TERM OF CHIEF ELECTION COMMISSIONER AND OTHER ELECTION COMMISSIONERS
SALARY, ALLOWANCES AND OTHER CONDITIONS OF SERVICE OF CHIEF ELECTION COMMISSIONER AND OTHER ELECTION COMMISSIONERS
TRANSACTION OF BUSINESS OF ELECTION COMMISSION

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Central Government.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Defines key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'Chief Election Commissioner', 'Election Commission', 'Search Committee', and 'Selection Committee'.

key_sections.title: Appointment of Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.
key_sections.description: States that the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners are appointed by the President by warrant.

key_sections.title: Qualifications of Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.
key_sections.description: Outlines the qualifications required for appointment, including holding a post equivalent to Secretary to the Government of India and having knowledge/experience in election management.

key_sections.title: Search Committee.
key_sections.description: Establishes a Search Committee headed by the Minister of Law and Justice to prepare a panel of persons for consideration.

key_sections.title: Selection Committee.
key_sections.description: Constitutes a Selection Committee, chaired by the Prime Minister, to recommend appointments, and specifies its members.

key_sections.title: Term of office.
key_sections.description: Sets the term of office for the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners as six years or until age sixty-five, whichever is earlier, and prohibits re-appointment.

key_sections.title: Salary, etc.
key_sections.description: Stipulates that the salary of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners shall be equal to that of a Supreme Court Judge and details other allowances and conditions.

key_sections.title: Resignation and removal.
key_sections.description: Outlines the procedures for resignation and removal from office, including that the Chief Election Commissioner can only be removed like a Supreme Court Judge, and other Election Commissioners on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.

key_sections.title: Protection of Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.
key_sections.description: Provides protection against civil or criminal proceedings for acts done in the discharge of official duty.

key_sections.title: Disposal of business.
key_sections.description: Describes how the Election Commission shall transact and dispose of its business, including unanimous decisions and majority opinion in case of difference.

key_sections.title: Repeal and saving.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991, and includes saving provisions.

powers_conferred: President: Appoints Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Sec 4), fixes number of other Election Commissioners (Sec 3), grants/refuses/revokes leave (Sec 12(2)), receives resignations (Sec 11(1)), determines other conditions of service by rules (Sec 15).
Central Government: Appoints the date of commencement of the Act (Sec 1(2)), removes difficulties in giving effect to the Act (Sec 19).
Search Committee: Prepares a panel of five persons for consideration for appointment as Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Sec 6).

Selection Committee: Recommends appointment of Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Sec 7), regulates its own procedure (Sec 8(1)), may consider persons not included in the panel by the Search Committee (Sec 8(2)).
Election Commission: Regulates the procedure for transaction of its business and allocation of business among its members (Sec 18(1)).
Chief Election Commissioner: Recommends the removal of other Election Commissioners (Sec 11(3)).

repealed_acts: The Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991 (11 of 1991)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The President appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners on the recommendation of the Selection Committee. The Prime Minister chairs the Selection Committee and nominates one Union Cabinet Minister to it. The Minister of Law and Justice heads the Search Committee.

applies_to: Chief Election Commissioner
Election Commissioners
Election Commission

implementation_and_enforcement.rule_making_authority: Central Government (for commencement and removing difficulties), President (for other conditions of service), Selection Committee (for its own procedure), Election Commission (for its business transaction).
implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced through the adherence to its provisions by the President, Central Government, Election Commission, and the established Search and Selection Committees in matters of appointment, service conditions, and business transaction.

act_identification.act_title: THE PROVISIONAL COLLECTION OF TAXES ACT, 2023
act_identification.act_short_title: The Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 2023

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for the immediate effect for a limited period of provisions in Bills relating to the imposition or increase of duties of customs or excise.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to allow provisions in Bills related to the imposition or increase of customs or excise duties to take immediate effect for a limited period. It ensures that such provisions have the force of law quickly, subject to certain conditions and durations.

key_sections.title: Short title.
key_sections.description: States the official short title of the Act as The Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 2023.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines the term 'declared provision' as a provision in a Bill for which a declaration has been made under section 3.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make declaration.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the power to insert a declaration in a Bill, stating that provisions related to imposition or increase of customs or excise duty shall have immediate effect.

key_sections.title: Effect of declarations under this Act, and duration thereof.
key_sections.description: Specifies that a declared provision has the force of law immediately upon introduction of the Bill and outlines conditions under which it ceases to have force of law, including enactment, notification by Central Government, or expiry of seventy-fifth day.

key_sections.title: Refunds to be made in certain cases.
key_sections.description: Mandates refunds of duties collected if a declared provision is enacted in an amended form or ceases to have the force of law, specifying the conditions and limits for such refunds.

key_sections.title: Repeal.
key_sections.description: Repeals The Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931.

powers_conferred: Power of Central Government to make declaration

repealed_acts: The Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931 (16 of 1931)

applies_to: provisions in Bills relating to the imposition or increase of duties of customs or excise

act_identification.act_title: THE PRESS AND REGISTRATION OF PERIODICALS ACT, 2023
act_identification.act_short_title: Press and Registration of Periodicals Act, 2023

act_overview.preamble: An Act to provide for press, registration of periodicals and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the regulation of the press, the registration of periodicals, and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. It establishes a framework for the printing, publication, and registration of various types of periodicals in India, and defines the roles of authorities like the Press Registrar General.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II PRINTING PRESS AND PERIODICAL

key_sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement.
key_sections.description: Specifies the short title, geographical extent, and commencement date of the Act.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act.

key_sections.title: Printer to furnish intimation.
key_sections.description: Requires every printer of a periodical to furnish intimation to the Press Registrar General and specified authority.

key_sections.title: Publication of periodical.
key_sections.description: Outlines who may bring out a periodical and requirements for printing information, with restrictions for certain individuals.

key_sections.title: Press Registrar General and other officers.
key_sections.description: Provides for the appointment of the Press Registrar General and other officers, and lists their functions.

key_sections.title: Powers of Press Registrar General.
key_sections.description: Details the powers of the Press Registrar General, including obtaining statements, verifying circulation, and revising/suspending/cancelling registration.

key_sections.title: Registration of periodical.
key_sections.description: Mandates registration for periodicals and outlines the application process for obtaining a certificate of registration.

key_sections.title: Suspension or cancellation of registration.
key_sections.description: Empowers the Press Registrar General to suspend or cancel the certificate of registration under specified circumstances.

key_sections.title: Annual statement to be furnished by periodical.
key_sections.description: Requires publishers to furnish annual statements and deliver copies of newspapers to the Press Registrar General and State Government.

key_sections.title: Power of Press Registrar General to impose penalty.
key_sections.description: Grants the Press Registrar General the power to impose penalties for non-compliance with registration and annual statement requirements.

key_sections.title: Press and Registration Appellate Board.
key_sections.description: Establishes an Appellate Board to hear appeals against orders of refusal, suspension, cancellation, or penalty.

key_sections.title: Power of Central Government to make rules.
key_sections.description: Confers power upon the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

key_sections.title: Repeal and savings.
key_sections.description: Repeals the Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867, and includes savings provisions for actions taken under the repealed Act.

powers_conferred: Central Government to appoint Press Registrar General and other officers (Section 5)

Press Registrar General to issue certificate of registration, maintain register, collect fees, prepare annual report, verify circulation, revise/suspend/cancel registration, impose penalty (Section 5, 6, 14)
Central Government to issue directions on policy matters to Press Registrar General (Section 16)
Central Government to make rules (Section 19)
Central Government to remove difficulties (Section 20)
State Government to specify officers as 'specified authority' (Section 2(p))
State Government to make rules (Section 19(3))
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act prescribes penalties for publishing a periodical without obtaining a certificate of registration, which can be up to five lakh rupees, along with a direction to cease publication. Failure to furnish annual statements incurs a penalty of ten thousand to twenty thousand rupees for the first default, and up to two lakh rupees for subsequent defaults. Additionally, failure to cease publication after a direction or publishing any other periodical without registration can lead to imprisonment for up to six months.

repealed_acts: The Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867 (25 of 1867)

important_authorities.appointment_powers: The Central Government has the power to appoint the Press Registrar General of India and such other officers as necessary. The Press and Registration Appellate Board consists of the Chairperson, Press Council of India, and two members nominated by the Press Council of India from among its members.

applies_to: Every citizen of India or a person, being an entity incorporated and registered in India under any law for the time being in force, who brings out a periodical
Every periodical printed in India
exemptions: Persons convicted by any court for an offence involving terrorist act or unlawful activity or for having done anything against the security of the State
special_provisions: Facsimile edition of a foreign periodical may be printed in India only with previous approval of the Central Government
No-objection of the specified authority not required for periodicals published by Central Government or a State Government or any authority under such Government

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: The Act is enforced primarily by the Press Registrar General, who is responsible for issuing and managing registrations, verifying circulation, and imposing penalties. The Press Registrar General can also suspend or cancel registrations. An Appellate Board is established to hear appeals against orders issued by the Press Registrar General.

act_identification.act_title: THE PUBLIC EXAMINATIONS (PREVENTION OF UNFAIR MEANS) ACT, 2024
act_identification.act_short_title: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024

act_overview.preamble: An Act to prevent unfair means in the public examinations and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
act_overview.purpose: This Act aims to prevent the use of unfair means in public examinations. It also provides for related and incidental matters concerning the integrity and conduct of such examinations.

chapter_titles: CHAPTER II UNFAIR MEANS AND OFFENCES
CHAPTER VI AMENDMENT TO THE CRIMINAL LAW (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1944

key_definitions: person associated with a service provider

key_sections.title: Short title and commencement.
key_sections.description: Establishes the official short title of the Act and specifies its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definitions.
key_sections.description: Provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Act, such as 'candidate', 'public examination', and 'service provider'.

key_sections.title: Unfair means.
key_sections.description: Lists various acts and omissions that constitute unfair means in relation to public examinations, including leakage of question papers and tampering with answer sheets.

key_sections.title: Conspiracy for unfair means.
key_sections.description: Prohibits any person, group, or institution from colluding or conspiring to facilitate unfair means.

key_sections.title: Disruption to conduct public examination.
key_sections.description: Addresses offences related to unauthorized entry into examination centers or actions by authorized persons to disrupt or leak information before an examination.

key_sections.title: Offences in respect of service providers and other persons.
key_sections.description: Defines offences committed by service providers or persons associated with them, including assisting in unfair means or failing to report incidents.

key_sections.title: Cognizable offences.
key_sections.description: Declares all offences under this Act as cognizable, non-bailable, and non-compoundable.

key_sections.title: Punishment for offences under this Act.
key_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for individuals and service providers involved in unfair means, including imprisonment and fines, with higher penalties for senior management.

key_sections.title: Organised crimes.
key_sections.description: Specifies severe punishments for organised crimes related to public examinations, including imprisonment and fines, and provisions for property attachment and forfeiture for institutions.

key_sections.title: Officers empowered to investigate.
key_sections.description: Designates officers not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police or Assistant Commissioner of Police to investigate offences, and allows the Central Government to refer investigations to a Central Investigating Agency.

key_sections.title: Members, officers and employees of public examination authority to be public servants.
key_sections.description: Deems the personnel of public examination authorities as public servants for actions taken under this Act.

key_sections.title: Power to make rules.
key_sections.description: Grants the Central Government the authority to make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act.

key_sections.title: Amendment of Ordinance 38 of 1944.
key_sections.description: Amends the Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance, 1944, to include offences punishable under this Act in its Schedule.

powers_conferred: Central Government: To appoint the commencement date of the Act (Section 1(2)).
Central Government: To notify other authorities for conducting public examinations (Section 2(k)).
Central Government: To notify public examination authorities from time to time (Section 2(l)).
Central Government: To refer investigation of any offence under this Act to any Central Investigating Agency (Section 12(2)).
Central Government: To make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act (Section 16).
Central Government: To make orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of this Act (Section 18).
Service provider: To report offences to concerned police authorities and public examination authority (Section 6).
Public examination authority: To report offences if the service provider resorts to unfair means (Section 6 proviso).
Officers not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police or Assistant Commissioner of Police: To investigate any offence under this Act (Section 12(1)).
key_provisions.offences_and_penalties: The Act defines various offences including unfair means (e.g., leakage of question papers, tampering with answer sheets), conspiracy for unfair means, disruption of public examinations, using unauthorized premises, and offences by service providers or associated persons. Organised crimes are also specifically addressed. Penalties for individuals range from imprisonment of 3 to 5 years and a fine up to ten lakh rupees. Service providers face fines up to one crore rupees, recovery of examination costs, and a four-year ban from conducting public examinations. Directors or senior management involved in offences can face imprisonment from 3 to 10 years and a fine of one crore rupees. Organised crimes carry imprisonment from 5 to 10 years and a fine of not less than one crore rupees, with provisions for attachment and forfeiture of property for institutions.

applies_to: Persons who have been granted permission by the public examination authority to appear in public examination (candidates).
Persons authorised to act as a scribe on behalf of a candidate in the public examination.
Any agency, organisation, body, association of persons, business entity, company, partnership or single proprietorship firm (institutions and service providers).
Any examination conducted by the public examination authority, as specified in the Schedule, or conducted by such other authority as may be notified by the Central Government.

Examinations conducted by: Union Public Service Commission, Staff Selection Commission, Railway Recruitment Boards, Institute of Banking Personnel Selection, Ministries or Departments of the Central Government and their attached and subordinate offices for recruitment of staff, National Testing Agency, and such other authority as may be notified by the Central Government.

implementation_and_enforcement.enforcement_mechanism: Offences are to be reported by service providers or public examination authorities to the police. Investigation is to be conducted by officers not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police or Assistant Commissioner of Police, or by a Central Investigating Agency if referred by the Central Government. Punishments include imprisonment, fines, and barring service providers from future assignments. Property attachment and forfeiture are applicable for institutions involved in organised crime.

schedules_summary.description: Lists the specific authorities whose examinations are covered under the Act. These include the Union Public Service Commission, Staff Selection Commission, Railway Recruitment Boards, Institute of Banking Personnel Selection, Ministries or Departments of the Central Government and their attached and subordinate offices for recruitment of staff, National Testing Agency, and any other authority as may be notified by the Central Government.

act_identification.act_title: THE POWERS-OF-ATTORNEY ACT, 1882

An Act to amend the law relating to Powers-of-Attorney.

For the purpose of amending the law relating to Powers-of-Attorney. It is hereby enacted as follows: —
act_overview.purpose: The Act aims to amend the law relating to Powers-of-Attorney. It defines the instrument, validates acts performed by an attorney in good faith even after the donor's death or incapacity, provides for the deposit of such instruments in courts, and grants married women the power to appoint attorneys.

key_sections.title: Short title. Local extent. Commencement.
key_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its geographical application to the whole of India, and its commencement date.

key_sections.title: Definition.
key_sections.description: Defines 'Power-of-Attorney' as any instrument empowering a specified person to act for and in the name of the person executing it.

key_sections.title: Execution under power-of-attorney.
key_sections.description: Allows the donee of a power-of-attorney to execute instruments or acts in their own name and signature, which shall be as effectual as if done by the donor.

key_sections.title: Payment by attorney under power, without notice of death, etc., good.
key_sections.description: Protects persons making payments or acts in good faith under a power-of-attorney from liability, even if the donor had died, become of unsound mind, or revoked the power, provided the fact was unknown at the time.

key_sections.title: Deposit of original instruments creating powers-of-attorney.
key_sections.description: Allows for the deposit of instruments creating powers-of-attorney in High Courts or District Courts, provides for inspection, certified copies, and rule-making power for the High Court.

key_sections.title: Power-of-attorney of married women.
key_sections.description: Grants married women of full age the power to appoint an attorney by a non-testamentary instrument for executing acts they might themselves perform.

act_overview.purpose: This Act provides for the establishment of two distinct Central Boards: one for Direct Taxes and another for Indirect Taxes and Customs. Its main objective is to confer powers and impose duties on these new Boards by amending existing enactments, replacing the former Central Board of Revenue.
